[Defi defipk of arXiv:2412.09471, 'On the moderate deviation principles in the sparse multi-type Erd\H{o}s R\'enyi random gra'] For each $k \in \mathbb{N}^d$, consider a random graph with $d$ vertex types whose type set is $\mathcal{S}$. 
The graph contains $k_r$ vertices of type-$r$ for every $r \in \mathcal{S}$, and each pair consisting of a type-$r$ vertex and a type-$s$ vertex is connected independently with probability $\kappa(r,s)/n$. 
Let $p_n(k)$ denote the connection probability of this graph.

[Definition 4 (Hermite process {\citep[Def.~4.2.1) of arXiv:2606.04179, 'Functional Scaling Limits of Interpolated Correlated Random Walks in Hölder Topology'] {pipirasLongRangeDependenceSelfSimilarity2017}}]
    
    The rank \(\hermRank\) Hermite process with Hurst index \(\hurst \in (\frac12, 1)\) is defined as
    \[
        Z^{\hermRank,\hurst}_t \coloneq A_{\hermRank, \hurst} \int_{\real^\hermRank}' \int_0^t \prod_{j=1}^\hermRank (s-x_j)_+^{-(\frac12 + \frac{1-\hurst}{\hermRank})} ds W(dx_1)\cdots W(dx_\hermRank),
    \]
    where \(W\) is the Wiener Gaussian white noise measure and \(\int'_{\real^\hurst}\) is the Itô integral that
    disregards the hyperplanes \(x_j = x_k\) for \(j \neq k\). The normalizing
    constant \(A_{\hermRank, \hurst}\) is selected such that
    \(\Exp{(Z^{\hermRank,\hurst}_1)^2} = 1\) and is known explicitly \citep[(4.2.7)]{pipirasLongRangeDependenceSelfSimilarity2017}.
    Equivalent representations are given in \citep[Cor.~4.2.11]{pipirasLongRangeDependenceSelfSimilarity2017}.

[Lemma local bridge4 of arXiv:2507.20324, 'Non-existence of several random fractals in Brownian motion and Brownian loop soup'] For $i=2,4$, let $E^{i}$ stand for the event that $X^{i}$ intersects $\mathcal{C}_{-K-L}(S)$, and for $i=1,3$, let $E^{i}$ stand for the event that $X^{i}$ intersects $\mathcal{C}_{-n+L}(S)$. Then there exist $c,c'>0$, such that for any $i=1,2,3,4$, we have:
\[\mathbb{P}(S\in\mathfrak{S}_{n},E^{i})\leq ce^{-c'\sqrt{n}}2^{-2n}.\]
Consequently, let $B_{4}$ be the union of $E^{i}$, then there exists $c''>0$, such that
\[\mathbb{P}(B_{4}|S\in\mathfrak{S}_{n})\leq c''e^{-c'\sqrt{n}}.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma local bridge4 of arXiv:2507.20324

body: [Theorem 82 (Stochastic orders) of arXiv:2608.07239, 'Unified framework for asymptotically uniform iterative construction of generalised random '] Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be negatively associated random variables, and let $Y_1,\ldots,Y_n$ be independent random variables, such that $X_i$ and $Y_i$ have the same distribution for all $i$. Then for any supermodular function $\phi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, we have $\mathbb{E}(\phi(X_1,\ldots,X_n))\leq\mathbb{E}(\phi(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n))$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: In mathematical analysis, a function of bounded variation, also known as BV function, is a real-valued function whose total variation is bounded (finite): the graph of a function having this property is well behaved in a precise sense. For a continuous function of a single variable, being of bounded variation means that the distance along the direction of the y-axis, neglecting the contribution of motion along x-axis, traveled by a point moving along the graph has a finite value. For a continuous function of several variables, the meaning of the definition is the same, except for the fact that the continuous path to be considered cannot be the whole graph of the given function, but can be every intersection of the graph itself with a hyperplane parallel to a fixed x-axis and to the y-axis.
title: Bounded variation

[Theorem thm:dim_free_unbounded of arXiv:2411.07878, 'Bernstein-type and Bennett-type inequalities for unbounded matrix martingales'] Let $\mathbf{X}_1, \dots, \mathbf{X}_n \in \mathbb{H}(d)$ be a martingale difference sequence adapted to a filtration $(\mathscr{F}_i)^n_{i=0}$ with $\mathscr{F}_0 = \{\varOmega, \varnothing\}$. 
    Fix $\alpha > 0$ and set for all $i \in [n]$
    \[
    \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i \coloneqq \E\lrs{\mathbf{X}^2_i \middle| \mathscr{F}_{i-1}},
    \quad
    U_i \coloneqq \norm*{\lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{X}_i)_+ \big| \mathscr{F}_{i-1}}_{\psi_{\alpha}}.
    \]
    
    Fix $\boldsymbol{\Sigma} \succcurlyeq 0$, $U \ge K > 0$ and define the event
    \begin{equation}
    
        E \coloneqq \lrc{\sum^n_{i = 1} \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i \preccurlyeq \boldsymbol{\Sigma},
        \quad
        \sum^n_{i = 1} U^{2}_i \le U^2,
        \quad
        \max_{i \in [n]} U_i \le K}.
    \end{equation}
    Let $\sigma^2 \coloneqq \lambda_{\max}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma})$, and $z$ be as in (equation eq:def_z of the paper). Then for any $\mathrm{x} > 0$ with probability at least $\mathbb{P}(E) - (e\cdot r(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}) +1) e^{-\mathrm{x}} - e^{-\mathrm{x}} \ind[\alpha < 1]$, it holds for any $0 < \varepsilon\le 1$
    \begin{align}
        \max_{k \in [n]} \lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{S}_k) \le& (1 + \varepsilon)\sigma \sqrt{2\mathrm{x}} + \frac{7 \lr{\ln \frac{8}{\varepsilon}}^{1/\alpha} Kz \mathrm{x}}{\min\lrc{2 \alpha z^{\alpha}, \hspace{0.2em}\underline{\log}\hspace{0.2em}\lr{\lr{\frac{K z}{\sigma}}^2 \mathrm{x}} }} \nonumber \\
        &+ \frac{3 K}{\alpha} \left(2 \mathrm{x} + 2\ln\lr{\frac{4 U}{K}}
        + \frac{4}{\alpha}\ln \lr{\frac{4}{\alpha e}} \right)^{\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha}} \ind[\alpha < 1] ,
    \end{align}
    and moreover,
    \begin{align}
       \max_{k \in [n]} \lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{S}_k) \le& (1 + \varepsilon)\sigma \sqrt{2 \mathrm{x}} + 2 \lr{\ln \frac{8}{\varepsilon}}^{1/\alpha} Kz \mathrm{x} \nonumber \\
       &+ \frac{3 K}{\alpha} \left(2 \mathrm{x} + 2\ln\lr{\frac{4 U}{K}}
        + \frac{4}{\alpha}\ln \lr{\frac{4}{\alpha e}} \right)^{\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha}} \ind[\alpha < 1] .
    \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unbounded case

Classical L1 half-snowflake / squared-Hilbert embedding, the method invoked before Yang-Duan-Hu-Salman-Razenshteyn-Li Appendix J Fact J.9 (arXiv:2002.08118v5, PDF p.47). Let (Omega,Sigma,mu) be a sigma-finite measure space and let L1(mu) denote real-valued integrable functions modulo equality almost everywhere. There is a map F:L1(mu)->L2(mu tensor Lebesgue_R), generally nonlinear, such that ||F(f)-F(g)||_2^2=||f-g||_1 for every f,g in L1(mu). Thus the metric ||f-g||_1^(1/2) embeds isometrically into a real Hilbert space. In particular, for probability densities p,q relative to mu, Psi(p)=F(p)/sqrt(2) satisfies ||Psi(p)-Psi(q)||_2^2=TV(p*mu,q*mu), under TV(P,Q)=sup_U |P(U)-Q(U)|=(1/2)int|p-q|dmu. Consequently, let (A,d_A) be a metric input space, let 0<s1<s2 and 0<a<b<infinity, and let x->q_x be a family of probability densities relative to this same mu. If d_A(x,y)<=s1 implies TV(q_x*mu,q_y*mu)<=a and d_A(x,y)>=s2 implies TV(q_x*mu,q_y*mu)>=b, then x->Psi(q_x) is an (s1,s2,sqrt(a),sqrt(b))-threshold map into Hilbert space.
(Omega,Sigma,mu) is sigma-finite; functions are real-valued elements of L1(mu)
For the TV specialization, p,q are nonnegative mu-densities with integral one; TV is the supremum-over-events convention
For the threshold-map consequence: a metric input space (A,d_A), 0<s1<s2, 0<a<b<infinity, and all q_x densities relative to the same mu

Let X be a continuous random vector in R^n with finite variance and let Z ~ N(0, I_n) be independent of X. Let X_t = X + sqrt(t) * Z. Let h(X_t) = - int p_t(x) log p_t(x) dx be the differential entropy of X_t. Then d/dt h(X_t) = (1/2) * J(X_t), where J(X_t) = int ||nabla log p_t(x)||^2 p_t(x) dx is the Fisher information of X_t.
X has finite second moments
Z ~ N(0, I_n) is independent of X
t > 0

body:
[Definition def:above_below_waterfall of arXiv:2507.22011, 'Random Lozenge Waterfall:\\Dimensional Collapse of Gibbs Measures'] Denote by $\mathcal{W}^{\pm}$ the regions above and below the waterfall, that is,
	\begin{equation*}
		\mathcal{W}^{+}\coloneqq
		\begin{cases}
			\{(\mathsf{t},\mathsf{x})\in \mathcal{H}\colon
			\mathsf{x}>\mathsf{N}+(\mathsf{t}-\mathsf{T}+\mathsf{S})^+\},&\textnormal{if $\mathsf{N}>\mathsf{T}$};\\
				\{(\mathsf{t},\mathsf{x})\in \mathcal{H}\colon
			\mathsf{t}_l<\mathsf{t}<\mathsf{t}_r,\ \mathsf{x}>\tfrac12(\mathsf{S+\mathsf{t}+\mathsf{N}})
		\}\\\hspace{20pt}
			\cup
				\{(\mathsf{t},\mathsf{x})\in \mathcal{H}\colon
					\mathsf{t}\le \mathsf{t}_l,\
					\mathsf{x}>\mathsf{N}
			\}\mathbf{1}_{\mathsf{N}>\mathsf{S}}
			\\\hspace{20pt}
			\cup
				\{(\mathsf{t},\mathsf{x})\in \mathcal{H}\colon
					\mathsf{t}\ge \mathsf{t}_r,\
					\mathsf{x}>\mathsf{S}+\mathsf{N}+\mathsf{t}-\mathsf{T}
				\}\mathbf{1}_{\mathsf{S}+\mathsf{N}>\mathsf{T}}
		,
		&\textnormal{if $\mathsf{N}<\mathsf{T}$},\\
		\end{cases}
	\end{equation*}
	and
	\begin{multline*}
		\mathcal{W}^{-}\coloneqq
				\{(\mathsf{t},\mathsf{x})\in \mathcal{H}\colon
			\mathsf{t}_l<\mathsf{t}<\mathsf{t}_r,\ \mathsf{x}<\tfrac12(\mathsf{S+\mathsf{t}-\mathsf{N}})
		\}
			\\
			\cup
				\{(\mathsf{t},\mathsf{x})\in \mathcal{H}\colon
					\mathsf{t}\le \mathsf{t}_l,\
					\mathsf{x}<\mathsf{t}
			\}\mathbf{1}_{\mathsf{N}<\mathsf{S}}
			\cup
				\{(\mathsf{t},\mathsf{x})\in \mathcal{H}\colon
					\mathsf{t}\ge \mathsf{t}_r,\
					\mathsf{x}<\mathsf{S}
				\}\mathbf{1}_{\mathsf{S}+\mathsf{N}<\mathsf{T}}.
	\end{multline*}
	Here the indicator $\mathbf{1}_{\mathsf{N}>\mathsf{S}}$ means that the
	subset in the union is present only if $\mathsf{N}>\mathsf{S}$, and similarly for all
	other indicators.
	In the samples in (fig:waterfall_region of the paper), right,
	the regions $\mathcal{W}^{\pm}$ are the lighter-colored ones. They consist solely of the horizontal lozenges
	\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline = (current bounding
		box.south),scale=.25]
	\draw[thick] (0,0)--++(1,1)--++(1,0)--++(-1,-1)--cycle;
	\end{tikzpicture}.\footnote{The below region $\mathcal{W}^-$ exists only if
	$\mathsf{N}<\mathsf{T}$. In (sec:asymptotic_clustering_of_nonintersecting_paths of the paper) below,
	we show that for
	$\mathsf{N}>\mathsf{T}$, the nonintersecting paths stay
	as low as they can: First, they go straight with
	slope $0$ until $\mathsf{t}=\mathsf{T}-\mathsf{S}$, and then
	continue diagonally with slope $1$.}

	Also denote $\mathcal{P}\coloneqq \mathcal{H}\setminus(\mathcal{W}^+\cup \mathcal{W}^-)$,
	this is the region inside the hexagon where we expect the nonintersecting paths to cluster together.
	We call $\mathcal{P}$ the \emph{saturation band}. It has constant width~$\mathsf{N}$
	and includes the waterfall region.
title: Definition def:above_below_waterfall of arXiv:2507.22011

[Lemma 7 (Joint score orthogonality and Fisher-energy decomposition) of arXiv:2608.21709, 'Posterior Information Dynamics of Diffusion Models for Linear Inverse Problems'] Under the joint law of $(X_t,R)$, assume the relevant squared scores are
integrable and that differentiation may be passed under the \(\nu\)-integral
in \(p_t(x)=\int p_t(x,r)\,\dd\nu(r)\).  Write
$s_t^R(X_t)=s_t^r(X_t)|_{r=R}$.  Then
\begin{equation}

\E[g_t(X_t,R)\mid X_t]=0,
\end{equation}
and therefore the score second-moment matrices obey
\begin{equation}

\E\!\left[s_t^R(X_t)s_t^R(X_t)^\top\right]
=
\E\!\left[s_t^{\rm prior}(X_t)s_t^{\rm prior}(X_t)^\top\right]
+
\E\!\left[g_t(X_t,R)g_t(X_t,R)^\top\right].
\end{equation}
Taking the trace gives
\begin{equation}

\E\|s_t^R(X_t)\|^2
=
\E\|s_t^{\rm prior}(X_t)\|^2
+
\E\|g_t(X_t,R)\|^2,
\end{equation}
and, for every deterministic vector $v$,
\begin{equation}

\E|v^\top s_t^R(X_t)|^2
=
\E|v^\top s_t^{\rm prior}(X_t)|^2
+
\E|v^\top g_t(X_t,R)|^2.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Joint score orthogonality and Fisher-energy decomposition

[Corollary 3 of arXiv:2609.03506, 'Divergence of decreasing rearranged Fourier series\\ on every infinite compact abelian gro'] Let \(f\in\D(G)\). There is a full-measure set \(X_f\subseteq G\)
such that, for every enumeration \((\gamma_n)_{n\geq1}\) of
\(\supp\widehat f\) satisfying
\[
 |\widehat f(\gamma_{n+1})|\leq|\widehat f(\gamma_n)|,
\]
the partial sums \(\sum_{n=1}^M\widehat f(\gamma_n)\gamma_n(x)\)
are unbounded for every \(x\in X_f\). Unboundedness already holds
along the indices at the ends of complete coefficient-magnitude levels.

[Proposition 19 of arXiv:2608.05931, 'Effective Lagrangian regularity and the uniqueness threshold for random H\"older velocity '] Fix $\alpha\in(0,1)$, $\beta>0$, $\lambda>0$, $p\geq 1$ and let, for all $j\geq 0$, $u^j$ be defined by~\eqref{eq:refreshing poisson}. Suppose there exists $M\geq 1$ such that for all $j\geq 0$, $n\in\{0,1,2\}$, and $s\in[0,1]$,
\[\|\nabla^n f^j_s\|_{L^p_\omega C^0_{t,x}}\leq M 2^{(n-\alpha-\beta /p)j}.\]
Then 
\begin{enumerate}
\item the $u^j$ are mutually independent with $\E u^j =0$,
\item for each $j\geq 1$, $u^j$ has a finite temporal range of dependence $2^{-\beta j}$,
\item and there exists a constant $C>0$ such that for all $j\geq 0$ and $n\in\{0,1,2\}$,
\[\|\nabla^n u^j\|_{L^p_\omega C^0_{t,x}}\leq CM(\lambda+p)2^{(n-\alpha)j}.\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 19 of arXiv:2608.05931

Let A0,A1 be real Hurwitz 2x2 matrices. Fix lambda in (0,1) such that Alambda=(1-lambda)A0+lambda A1 has real eigenvalues -lambda_minus<0<lambda_plus. For beta>0 let I switch 0->1 at rate beta*lambda and 1->0 at rate beta*(1-lambda), and let Xdot=AI X. For every initial probability law assigning no mass to X=0, t^-1 log||Xt|| converges almost surely to an initial-law-independent real chi(beta). There exist 0<beta1<=beta2<infinity such that chi(beta)<0 for beta<beta1 and chi(beta)>0 for beta>beta2. Consequently the norm tends respectively to zero or infinity. The theorem does not assert beta1=beta2, monotonicity, or a single instability interval. Source: Benaim, Le Borgne, Malrieu and Zitt, arXiv:1204.1921, Section 1 standing Hurwitz assumption, Assumption 1.1, rates preceding Theorem 1.6, Theorem 1.6, PDF pp.1-2.
Real 2x2 Hurwitz matrices A0,A1
lambda in (0,1)
The stationary weighted average (1-lambda)A0+lambda A1 has one positive and one negative real eigenvalue
Rates beta*lambda and beta*(1-lambda), beta>0
Initial law gives no mass to X=0

[Lemma Planar two-disk logarithmic capacity and
boundary-layer profile, \(d = 2\) of arXiv:2606.23025, 'Spectral-Capacitary Bounds for Homological Recovery from Reflected Brownian Trajectories'] For
\(0 < \varepsilon \ll \delta\) the logarithmic capacity of the
union of two disks of radius \(\varepsilon\) whose centers are at
distance \(2\delta\) is
\(\operatorname{cap}_{\log} = \sqrt{2\varepsilon\delta}\,\left( 1 + o(1) \right)\).
Consequently, writing
\(\delta_{\varepsilon} = \operatorname{dist}\left( x_{\varepsilon},\partial M \right)\)
and assuming
\(\log\delta_{\varepsilon}/\log\varepsilon \rightarrow \theta \in \lbrack 0,1\rbrack\),
the reflected half-plane condenser energy of
\(B\left( x_{\varepsilon},\varepsilon \right) \cap M\) is
\(E_{H} = B(\theta)\, E_{0}\,\left( 1 + o(1) \right)\) with the
planar profile

\[B(\theta) = \frac{1}{1 + \theta},\quad\quad B(1) = \frac{1}{2},\quad B(0) = 1.\]

[Theorem thm:lower of arXiv:2608.23638, 'Replicable Conformal Prediction'] Fix an integer $n\ge1$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$, $0<\varepsilon\le\min(\alpha,1-\alpha)/4$, $0<\rho\le1$, $0\le\delta\le\tfrac1{16}$. Let $\mathcal{A}:[0,1]^n\times\mathsf R\to\mathbb{R}$ be jointly measurable, with a shared seed $r\sim\nu$ independent of the data. If, for \emph{every} atomless Borel law $P$ on $[0,1]$ with CDF $F_P$, $\mathcal{A}$ is $\rho$-replicable and $\mathbb{P}[F_P(\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{D};r))\in[1-\alpha\pm\varepsilon]]\ge1-\delta$, then
$n\;\ge\;\tfrac{9(1-8\delta)^{2}}{4096}\,\tfrac{\alpha(1-\alpha)}{\varepsilon^{2}\rho^{2}}\;\ge\;\tfrac{9}{16384}\,\tfrac{\alpha(1-\alpha)}{\varepsilon^{2}\rho^{2}}$.
The proof is self-contained, incurs no logarithmic loss, and uses accuracy only at the two endpoints of the hard family, each satisfying Assumption~(ass:margin of the paper) with $\kappa=1$, $\Delta=\varepsilon$, constant density in $[2\min(\alpha,1-\alpha),2]$; the whole family satisfies it with $\Delta=\tfrac14$, $f_{\min}=\min(\alpha,1-\alpha)$, $f_{\max}=2$. The bound concerns exact replication of the scalar threshold; Appendix~(app:lower of the paper) states the exact scope (set-map-only replicability is not automatically covered). (Proof: Appendix~(app:lower of the paper).) (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let $n\ge1$, $\mathbf{x}=(x_1,...,x_n)$ and $\varepsilon>0$. Let $U=\{(y_1,y_2,\mathbf{x}):|y_1-u|<\varepsilon, 0\le y_2-y_1<\varepsilon,\|\mathbf{x}-{\bf x}_0\|<\varepsilon\}$, and $\Delta=\{(y_1,y_2,\mathbf{x})\in U:y_1=y_2\}$. For $\rho,\tau,\sigma\in\mathbbm{R}$, consider the differential operator
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{M}=\frac{1}{2}\partial_{y_1}^2+\left(\frac{\rho}{y_1-y_2}+a(y_1,y_2,\mathbf{x})\right)\partial_{y_1}+\left(\frac{\tau}{2(y_2-y_1)}+b(y_1,y_2,\mathbf{x})\right)\partial_{y_2}+{\bf X}+\left(-\frac{\tau \sigma}{2(y_1-y_2)^2}+\frac{d(y_1,y_2,\mathbf{x})}{y_2-y_1}\right)
\end{equation}
where ${\bf X}:=\sum_{i=1}^nc_i(y_1,\mathbf{x})\partial_{x_i}$, and $a,b,c,d$ are smooth on $U$. Suppose $\alpha_-<\alpha_+$ are the two roots of the indicial equation $\alpha(\alpha-1)+(\tau+2\rho)\alpha-\tau \sigma=0$.

Suppose $f$ is a real-valued smooth function on $U\setminus\Delta$ such that $\mathcal{M} f=0$ and $f=O((y_2-y_1)^{\alpha_-+\delta})$ for some $\delta>0$. Further, assume that for ${\bf Y}:=\partial_{y_1}$ and ${\bf Y},{\bf X}$ satisfies the H\"ormander's condition on $U\setminus\Delta$. Then there exists a smooth function $g$ on $U$ such that $f=(y_2-y_1)^{\alpha_+}g$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 5 (Localized cutoff heat-kernel bound) of arXiv:2607.19752, 'Weak Equilibrium Measures and Capacity--Hitting Identities\\ for the Hypoelliptic Third-Or'] Let $\mathsf O\subset\R^{3d}$ be a bounded smooth open set, and let
$Z^{\delta,\mathsf O}$ denote the cutoff process constructed in
Lemma~\ref{lem:chain-compatible-cutoffs}.  After the reordering
\[
    X^1=r,\qquad X^2=p,\qquad X^3=\theta,
\]
the cutoff drifts preserve Pigato's triangular dependence structure
\[
    B_j=B_j\left(x^{j-1},\ldots,x^3\right),\qquad j=2,3.
\]
Then, for every $0<t_0<M<\infty$ and compact sets
$K_0,K_1\subset\mathsf O$, the transition laws of
$Z^{\delta,\mathsf O}$ admit densities
$p_\delta^{\mathsf O}(t,z,y)$ satisfying
\[
    \sup_{\substack{
        0\le\delta\le1\\
        t\in[t_0,M]\\
        z\in K_0,\ y\in K_1}}
    p_\delta^{\mathsf O}(t,z,y)<\infty .
\]
The same estimate holds for the adjoint cutoff family.

[Prop upscale of arXiv:2609.03033, 'An Overview of Einstein $4$-Manifolds'] Let $(M^4,g)$ be a smooth compact oriented Riemannian manifold,
 and suppose, for a fixed spin$^c$ structure $\mathfrak{c}$,  that there is a solution of the unperturbed Seiberg-Witten equations  ((drc of the paper)--(sd of the paper))  for every 
 metric $\widehat{g}$ in the conformal class of  $g$.  
Then the scalar curvature 
$s$ and self-dual Weyl curvature $W_+$ of $g$ must satisfy
\begin{equation}

\int_M \left(s-\sqrt{6}|W_+|\right)^{2}d\mu_g  \geq  72\pi^2 [c_1^+]^2 .
\end{equation}
 Moreover, if $c_1^+:= c_1(L)^+$ is non-zero, equality can only occur  if $g$ is an almost-K\"ahler metric for which $s-\sqrt{6}|W_+|$ is a  negative constant,  for which the 
 symplectic form everywhere belongs to the bottom eigenspace of $W_+$,  and for which the two highest eigenvalues of $W_+$ are everywhere equal.

[Prop 6 of arXiv:2608.20552, 'One-point fluctuations for exponential last passage percolation under upper-tail condition'] Fix an integer $m\ge1$. Let $\bM=(M_1,\ldots,M_m)\in\N^m$, $\bN=(N_1,\ldots,N_m)\in\N^m$, and $\bT=(T_1,\ldots,T_m)\in\R_+^m$. Assume that $0<T_1\le\cdots\le T_m$ and that $(N_1,T_1),\ldots,(N_m,T_m)$ are all distinct. Then
\beq
	\prob\left(\LPP(M_1,N_1)>T_1,\ldots,\LPP(M_m,N_m)>T_m\right)=\QQ_m(\bM,\bN,\bT),
\eeq
where
\beq 
	\QQ_m(\bM,\bN,\bT):=\sum_{\bn\in\N^m}\frac{1}{(\bn!)^2}\QQ^{(\bn)}_m(\bM,\bN,\bT),
\eeq
with $\bn!:=n_1!\cdots n_m!$ for $\bn=(n_1,\ldots,n_m)$, and
\beq 
	\QQ^{(\bn)}_m(\bM,\bN,\bT):=\frac{(-1)^{|\bn|+m}}{(2\pi\ii)^{m-1}}\oint_{>1}\cdots\oint_{>1}\DD^{(\bn)}_{\bM,\bN,\bT}(\bz)\prod_{i=1}^{m-1}\frac{(z_i+1)^{n_i-n_{i+1}-1}}{z_i^{n_{i+1}+1}}\dd z_i.
\eeq
The function $\DD^{(\bn)}_{\bM,\bN,\bT}(\bz)$ is defined in \eqref{eq:D_hat_n}, and the contours are circles centered at the origin with radii greater than $1$.

body: The hairy ball theorem of algebraic topology (formally, the Sphere Vector Field Theory, sometimes called the hedgehog theorem) states that there is no non-vanishing continuous tangent vector field on even-dimensional n-spheres. For the ordinary sphere, or 2‑sphere, if f is a continuous function that assigns a vector in ℝ3 to every point p on a sphere such that f(p) is always tangent to the sphere at p, then there is at least one pole, a point where the field vanishes (a p such that f(p) = 0).
title: Hairy ball theorem

The unique strictly positive finite entrance has u0=0 and q(0+)=1/c^2; u0>0 gives q(0+)=0 and q_t/t^2->1/(2u0^2). For ReLU c=sqrt(2)/(3pi), the positive entrance is 9pi^2/2. # Positive entrances for the rescaled-correlation SDE

Status: proof draft (unaudited), Target1 architecture step. This is a theorem about a specified SDE, not a correction to Li-Nica Theorem4.1 and not a proof of finite-width network convergence. The result includes both disputed constant drifts, so it does not require deciding C012's source correction.

Let c>0, gamma be real, and B be standard Brownian motion on [0,T] with B_0=0 on a usual filtered probability space. Consider finite, continuous, adapted processes q_t>0 for t>0 satisfying on every compact positive-time interval

    dq_t = 2q_t[(1-c sqrt(q_t))/t+gamma]dt+2sqrt(2)q_t dB_t.   (Q)

Put a=c/sqrt(2), b=3-gamma. Every such solution corresponds to a finite nonnegative F_0-measurable variable u_0 through

    E_t=exp((b-1)t-sqrt(2)B_t),
    U_t=E_t[u_0+a integral_0^t E_s^(-1)ds],
    q_t=t^2/(2U_t^2), t>0.                                  (R)

Conversely every finite u_0>=0 in F_0 gives a strictly positive solution on positive times by (R). For u_0=0 its unique continuous entrance is q_0=1/c^2. For u_0>0 its continuous entrance is q_0=0, and q_t/t^2->1/(2u_0^2). Thus the unique solution having a strictly positive finite entrance value has necessarily q_0=1/c^2 and is pathwise unique for a given B. Merely assigning the value q_0=0 does not select a unique positive solution.

For the ReLU coefficient c=sqrt(2)/(3pi), the positive entrance is q_0=9pi^2/2. The source's displayed Eq4.7 has gamma=-1 (b=4); its displayed log equation4.8 corresponds to gamma=+1 (b=2). The entrance classification above applies separately to both. C004's checked compact generator selects gamma=+1 in its coordinate transformation, but the source-theorem correction remains for the Claude reviewer.

## Reciprocal transformation and classification

For t>0 define U=t/sqrt(2q). Its derivatives are U_t=U/t, U_q=-U/(2q), U_qq=3U/(4q^2). Ito's formula gives

    dU=[U/t-U((1-c sqrt(q))/t+gamma)+3U]dt-sqrt(2)U dB
       =[a+bU]dt-sqrt(2)U dB.                                (U)

The constant term uses U c sqrt(q)/t=c/sqrt(2)=a. The coefficients of (U) are globally Lipschitz, and its integrating factor is E_t as above. On any positive-time interval the variation-of-constants identity says E_t^-1 U_t-a integral_0^t E_s^-1 ds is constant in t. Evaluating at one positive time shows that this constant u_0 is finite. Since E is continuous, positive, and E_0=1, it follows that U_t->u_0 as t decreases to zero. Positivity of U at every positive time forces u_0>=0. Its measurability at zero follows from the usual right-continuity of the filtration and adaptedness of U_t. This proves that every positive solution must have representation (R).

Conversely the representation solves (U), is positive at every t>0 since a>0, and is finite on every finite interval. Applying Ito to t^2/(2U^2) away from t=0 proves (Q). Thus the representation covers exactly the positive solutions.

If u_0>0, U_t->u_0 immediately gives the stated q_t/t^2 limit. If u_0=0, continuity of B implies uniformly for 0<=s<=t that E_t/E_s->1 as t->0. Consequently

    U_t/(a t)=(1/t) integral_0^t E_t/E_s ds ->1 almost surely,
    q_t ->1/(2a^2)=1/c^2 almost surely.

This also proves continuity and strict positivity at the canonical entrance. Uniqueness follows from the integrating-factor formula, with no choice of an initial Brownian correlation or independent marginal limits.

## Integral interpretation through the singular time

The canonical extension also satisfies the integral SDE from time0; its singular drift is locally integrable. To see this directly without an unstated regularity assumption, set M_t=sup_(s<=t)|B_s|. On a fixed Brownian path and finite T, the exponential-ratio estimate gives

    |U_t/(at)-1| <= C(omega)(t+M_t)

near zero. Since the ratio tends to1, it follows that |q_t-1/c^2|<=C(omega)(t+M_t). The function q(1-c sqrt(q)) is locally Lipschitz and vanishes at 1/c^2, so the absolute singular drift is bounded by C(omega)(1+M_t/t). Doob's L2 inequality gives E M_t<=2sqrt(t), and therefore

    E integral_0^T M_t/t dt <=4sqrt(T)<infinity.

Tonelli's theorem makes the latter integral finite almost surely. The remaining drift is continuous and the noise coefficient q is bounded near zero on each path. Localize by these path bounds and let the lower integration endpoint decrease to zero; the stochastic integral has a continuous extension. Thus the integral equation is well defined with q_0=1/c^2. For u_0>0, q_t=O(t^2), making the drift integrable even more directly.

## Why this is not a full q-chain convergence statement at time0

For the network observable q_l=l^2(1-rho_l), the literal value at l=0 is0. The canonical positive-time limit instead has continuous extension 1/c^2>0. Hence the unmodified q_floor(nt) paths cannot converge in the usual Skorohod topology on [0,T] to that continuous extension: evaluation at0 preserves the value0 under Skorohod convergence. Changing only the value at the first time point also does not address the whole shrinking initial layer.

The natural continuous entrance variable is U_n=1/(n theta_floor(nt)), whose initial value tends to0. Once its network convergence is established, q_t=t^2/(2U_t^2) on positive times selects u_0=0 and thus the canonical q entrance. C005-C006 attempt precisely that network step but remain unaudited. The theorem above resolves the SDE entrance classification, while keeping this separate finite-width obligation explicit.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:bbfefc84f0aff1c56b907affa58118298696f5d8fa98c4a718e5143fbbc07351","revision_digest":"sha256:2fa51fbd0025d4dc64b7f47ed1cef1245d82a4ba78081dcc6205e9fbc7e5b21e","source_id":"own-work:T244-w691-C014:v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20-v1-unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body: In the random recursive tree, the layer of a vertex is the number of rounds of leaf-stripping until it is a leaf, and l_k is the limiting fraction of vertices at layer k. Conjecture 1 of arXiv:2608.04303, l_k = exp[-k/e - (3/(2e)) log k - O(1)], holds: the paper's recursion s_0 = 1, s_i(y) = 1 - exp(-int_0^y s_{i-1}) is exactly the Poisson product formula P(M_i <= y) for the generation-i minimum M_i of the branching random walk on the Poisson-weighted infinite tree, so lbar_k = E[e^{-M_k}], and the velocity 1/e with the (3/(2e)) log k correction is Addario-Berry and Ford (Ann. Appl. Probab. 2013, Theorem 1.1). With Aidekon (2013) the O(1) is a genuine limit: lbar_k e^{k/e} k^{3/(2e)} -> C* ~ 1.42 and l_k / lbar_k -> 1 - e^{-1/e} ~ 0.3078. The layer half of Conjecture 2 also holds: the maximum layer is floor(diameter/2), so L_n = e log n - 1.5 log log n + O_P(1).

[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2608.28528, 'Strong solutions of SDEs with critical discontinuities in diffusion coefficients'] Define occupation measures: for a Borel measurable set $A \subset [s,t] \times \mathbb R^d$, set
$$
\mu_m^{s,x}(A):=\mathbf{E}\int_s^t \mathbf{1}_A(r,X_{s,r}^{x,m})dr, \quad m=1,2,\dots
$$
and
$$
\mu^{s,x}(A):=\mathbf{E}\int_s^t \mathbf{1}_A(r,X_{s,r}^{x})dr.
$$
The following are true:
\begin{itemize}
\item[{\rm (\textit{i})}] For every function $0 \leq F \in C_c([s,t] \times \mathbb R^d) \cap \mathbf{F}_\mu$,
\begin{align*}
\int F d\mu_m^{s,x} & = \mathbf{E}\int_s^t F(r,X_{s,r}^{x,m})dr \\
& \rightarrow \int_s^t \int_{\mathbb R^d} F d\mu^{s,x} = \mathbf{E}\int_s^t F(r,X_{s,r}^{x})dr \text{ as } m \rightarrow \infty
\end{align*}
and
\begin{equation}

\mathbf{E}\int_s^t F(r,X_{s,r}^{m,x})dr,\;\; \mathbf{E}\int_s^t F(r,X_{s,r}^{x})dr \leq C \|F\|_{L^2([s,t], L^2_{\rho}(\mathbb R^d))}^{\frac{2}{q}},
\end{equation}
where constant $C$ depends on $\mu$, but does not depend on the smoothness or the support of $F$.

\item[{\rm (\textit{ii})}] The limiting occupation measure $\mu^{s,x}$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the weighted Lebesgue measure $dr \times \rho(x)dx$ on $[s,t] \times \mathbb R^d$.

\smallskip

\item[{\rm (\textit{iii})}] For every function $0 \leq F \in L^2([s,t] \times L^2_{\rho}(\mathbb R^d)) \cap \mathbf{F}_\mu$,
$$
\mathbf{E}\int_s^t F(r,X_{s,r}^{x})dr \leq C \|F\|_{L^2([s,t], L^2_{\rho}(\mathbb R^d))}^{\frac{2}{q}}.
$$ 
\end{itemize}

body:
[Corollary 18 (Unitriangular standard-monomial Wick--Jacobi gauge) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] On a fixed standard-monomial stratum, fix a monomial order and let
\[
 b_1,\ldots,b_\mu
\]
be the standard monomials for the quotient by the initial ideal of
\((\partial_1P_m,\ldots,\partial_dP_m)\), and put
\[
 \mathcal W
 =
 \exp\!\left(-\frac12\Delta\right),
 \qquad
 \Delta=\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_{x_j}^2.
\]
Choose the section \(\iota\) in
\cref{thm:jacobi-normal-form-transfer} to be their standard polynomial
representatives.
The classes represented by
\[
 \mathcal Wb_1,\ldots,\mathcal Wb_\mu
\]
form a Jacobi-enriched Wick basis of the twisted de Rham module.  Relative
to \(b_1,\ldots,b_\mu\), its algebraic comparison matrix is triangular by
increasing polynomial degree, has diagonal equal to one, and therefore
\begin{equation}
 \det B_{\mathrm{Jac}}^{\mathrm{std}}=1.
 
\end{equation}
Its inverse is induced by
\(\exp(\Delta/2)\), the positive finite sum over Wick pairings.
For a nonquadratic phase, \(\mathcal W\) is here a triangular change of
cohomology frame; it is not asserted to be a chain map for
\(\nabla_{P,t}\).
The equality of the determinant to one belongs to this specified gauge;
the invariant statement under arbitrary rational frame changes is the
nonvanishing in \cref{cor:jacobi-comparison-determinant}.

[Lemma lem:moment_bound of arXiv:2411.03609, 'Asymptotically optimal Wasserstein couplings for the small-time stable domain of attractio'] Let $\bm{X}$ be a L\'evy process with 
generating triplet $(\bm{\gamma_X},\bm{\Sigma_X}\bm{\Sigma_X}^{\scalebox{0.6}{$\top$}},\nu_{\bm{X}})$.
 Recall the Blumenthal--Getoor index $\beta$ from~(equation eq:BG of the paper) and the associated quantity $\beta_+\in [\beta,2]$. Assume that, for some $p>0$, we have
$\int_{\mathbb{R}^d\setminus B_{\bm{0}}(1)}|\bm{w}|^p\nu_{\bm{X}}(\mathrm{d}\bm{w})<\infty$.
 Then there exist constants $C_i\in[0,\infty)$, $i=1,\ldots,4$, such that
\[
\mathds{E}\bigg[\sup_{s\in[0,t]}|\bm{X}_s|^p\bigg]
\leqslant \1_{\{\bm{\Sigma_X}\neq\bm{0}\}}C_1 t^{p/2} 
+C_2 t^p + C_3 t^{\min\{1,p/\beta_+\}},
\quad \text{ for } t\in[0,1].
\]
If $\int_{B_{\bm{0}}(1)\setminus\{\bm{0}\}}|\bm{w}|\nu_{\bm{X}}(\mathrm{d}\bm{w})< \infty$ and $\bm{X}$ has zero natural drift, i.e. $\bm{\gamma_X}=\int_{B_{\bm{0}}(1)\setminus\{\bm{0}\}}\bm{w}\nu_{\bm{X}}(\mathrm{d}\bm{w})$, then $C_2=0$ in the inequality above. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:fourier of arXiv:2607.12564, 'Power-law and log-periodic degree tails for a family of probability generating function eq'] Let $\chi:=2\pi/\log\lambda$, $s_m:=\rho+1+i\chi m$, and
$\mathcal{M}_j(s):=\int_0^\infty w_j(x)x^{s-1}dx=\mathbb{E}[V_j^{\,s-1}]$, finite and analytic for
$\operatorname{Re}s>1$. Then the continuous period-$1$ function $\Psi_j$ has Fourier coefficients
\begin{equation}
  \widehat\Psi_j(m):=\int_0^1\Psi_j(u)e^{2\pi i m u}\,du=\frac{2p}{a\log\lambda}\,\mathcal{M}_j(s_m).
\end{equation}
In particular $\widehat\Psi_j(0)=\overline\Psi_j=\frac{2p}{a\log\lambda}\mathbb{E}[V_j^{\,\rho}]>0$.

[Theorem thm.odlyzko_richmond of arXiv:2603.11043, 'An asymptotically optimal bound for the concentration function of a sum of independent int'] If $\{p_j\}$ is a discrete distribution with $p_j = 0$ for $j < 0$ and $j > d$, while $p_0 > 0, p_d > 0$, and
    \[
        \gcd\{j: p_j \ne 0\} = 1,
    \]
    then for any $\delta > 0$ there is an $n_0^{OR} = n_0^{OR}(\delta)$ such that if $a_{k,n}$ denotes the value of the
    $n$-fold convolution $\{p_j\}^{*_n}$ at $k$ then for $n \ge n_0^{OR}$,
    \[
        a_{k,n}^2 \ge a_{k-1,n} a_{k+1,n}
    \]
    for $\delta n \le k \le (d-\delta) n$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Proposition 3.3 (Proposition 2.1, [PR19]) of arXiv:2604.02746, 'Zero-Freeness of the Hard-Core Model with Bounded Connective Constant'] Fix $\Delta\geq 3$. body:
[Lem 159 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}\ref{i:IAMP-main-chaotic}, in the limiting regime \eqref{eq:eta-delta-eps} we have
  \[
    \sup_{\upp \in [0,1]}
    \lt|
      \lim_{N\to\infty} \chi_{\breve{\cA}_N}(\upp) - \plim_{N\to\infty} \frac{(\hat{\by}^{\ubl},\tilde{\by}^{\ubl})}{N}
    \rt| \le \iota'\,,
  \]
  where $\hat{\by}^{\ubl},\tilde{\by}^{\ubl}$ are the outputs of $\IAMP_{\chaos,N}(p,\sigma,b,w,\delta,\eta)$ on $\upp$-correlated $\bz, \tilde{\bz}$.
\begin{proof}
  For each $\upp \in [0,1]$, we have
  \[
    \chi_{\breve{\cA}_N}(\upp)
    = \frac{\bbE (\breve{\cA}_N(\bz), \breve{\cA}_N(\tilde \bz) )}{N}
    = \frac{N}{\bbE_{\bz'}[\|\bar\cA_N(\bz')\|^2]} \cdot \frac{\bbE (\bar{\cA}_N(\bz), \bar{\cA}_N(\tilde \bz) )}{N}\,.
  \]
  As argued in the \hyperlink{proof:t.IAMP.main.main}{proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}\ref{i:IAMP-main-main}},
  \[
    \bigg|\frac{N}{\bbE_{\bz'}[\|\bar\cA_N(\bz')\|^2]} - 1\bigg| \le \iota'\,.
  \]
  We can write
  \[
    \frac{(\bar{\cA}_N(\bz), \bar{\cA}_N(\tilde \bz))}{N}
    = \frac{\|\bar{\cA}_N(\bz) + \bar{\cA}_N(\tilde \bz)\|^2}{2N} 
    - \frac{\|\bar{\cA}_N(\bz)\|^2}{2N} 
    - \frac{\|\bar{\cA}_N(\tilde\bz)\|^2}{2N}
  \]
  Since $\bar{\cA}$ is a $C(L,\epsilon)$-Lipschitz function of standard gaussians, each of the terms on the right-hand side has variance $O(1/N)$.
  Thus $(\bar{\cA}_N(\bz), \bar{\cA}_N(\tilde \bz)) / N$ has variance $O(1/N)$, which implies
  \[
    \lim_{N\to\infty} \frac{\bbE (\bar{\cA}_N(\bz), \bar{\cA}_N(\tilde \bz) )}{N}
    = \plim_{N\to\infty} \frac{(\bar{\cA}_N(\bz), \bar{\cA}_N(\tilde \bz) )}{N}\,.
  \]
  Finally, because $\bar{\cA}_N(\bz)$ agrees with $\tilde{\cA}_N(\bz)$ with probability $1-e^{-cN}$,
  \[
    \plim_{N\to\infty} \frac{(\bar{\cA}_N(\bz), \bar{\cA}_N(\tilde \bz) )}{N}
    = \plim_{N\to\infty} \frac{(\tilde{\cA}_N(\bz), \tilde{\cA}_N(\tilde \bz) )}{N}
    = \plim_{N\to\infty} \frac{(\hat{\by}^{\ubl},\tilde{\by}^{\ubl})}{N}\,. 
  \]
  This concludes the proof.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 159 of arXiv:2608.29416

body:
[Proposition 20 of arXiv:2608.19976, 'Random valuations'] Let $\Phi$ be a non-trivial $\sigma$-continuous non-negative ID valuation with
  independent increments and vanishing deterministic part. Assume that
  the distribution of $\Phi$ is determined by the measure $\nu$ on
  $\sC\times(0,\infty)$, see Theorem~\ref{thr:2}.
  \begin{enumerate}
  \item[(i)] $\Phi$ is $\alpha$-stable in argument if and only if
    \begin{equation}
      
      \nu(t^{1/\alpha}\sM\times A)=t \nu(\sM\times A)

    \end{equation}
    for all rational $t>0$, measurable $\sM\subset\sC$ and Borel
    $A\subset(0,\infty)$, and then $\alpha\in(0,\infty)$. Here the
    scaling of $\sM$ is applied to all its elements. 
  \item[(ii)] $\Phi$ is $\alpha$-stable in value if and only if 
    \begin{equation}
      
      \nu(\sM\times tA)=t^{-\alpha}\nu(\sM\times A)
    \end{equation}
    for all $t>0$, measurable $\sM\subset\sC$ and Borel
    $A\subset(0,\infty)$,
    and then $\alpha\in(0,1)$.
  \item[(iii)] $\Phi$ is $\beta$-homogeneous if and only if 
    $\nu(t\sM\times A)=\nu(\sM\times (t^{-\beta} A))$ for all $t>0$,
    measurable $\sM\subset\sC$ and Borel $A\subset(0,\infty)$.
  \end{enumerate}
  In each assertion, it suffices to verify the corresponding identity for 
  $\sM=\sC_L$, where $L$ ranges over finite unions of compact convex sets
  and $A\subset[\eps,\infty)$ for any $\eps>0$.
title: Proposition 20 of arXiv:2608.19976

[Lem lyapunovg of arXiv:2605.06488, 'Continuous-state branching processes with L\'evy-Khintchine drift-interaction: Laplace dua'] Consider a (sub)critical branching mechanism $\Sigma$ and a supercritical one, $\hat{\Psi}=\hat{\Sigma}-\hat{\Phi}$, such that $\int_0^1\frac{\mathrm{d} u}{\hat\Phi(u)}<\infty$. Set $g(x):=\int_0^{x}\frac{\mathrm{d} u}{\hat\Phi(u)}$ for $x\in [0,\infty)$. The function $g$ takes the following Bernstein form
	\begin{equation}g(x)=\int_0^{\infty}(1-e^{-xz})\frac{\hat{U}(\mathrm{d} z)}{z}, \ x\in [0,\infty),\end{equation} and denoting by $\mathcal{X}$ the generator of the minimal $\mathrm{CBDI}(\Sigma,\hat\Psi)$, see (equation genX of the paper), one has
\begin{equation} \mathcal{X}g(x)=1-xG(x)-\eta(x), \ x\in [0,\infty),
\end{equation}
where $G$ is given by (equation eq:G of the paper) and $\eta(x):=\frac{\hat{\Sigma}(x)}{\hat{\Phi}(x)}\underset{x\rightarrow 0}{\longrightarrow} 0$.

body:
Let M>=1 finite linear-regression tasks have matrices X_m in R^(n_m by d) and labels y_m. Suppose X_m*w_star=y_m for every m, put R=max_m||X_m||_2>0, and define L(w;m)=||X_m*w-y_m||^2/2 and L(w)=M^(-1)*sum_m L(w;m). Initialize w_0=0 and sample tau_1,...,tau_k independently and uniformly from{1,...,M}, with replacement. Scheme1 performs the exact update w_t=argmin_w {L(w;tau_t)+(lambda_t/2)*||w-w_(t-1)||^2}. Write D2=||w_0-w_star||^2. For a known integer horizon k>=2, use lambda_t=(13*R^2/3)*(k+1)/(k-t+2), t=1,...,k. Then E L(w_k)<=20*D2*R^2/(k+1). The regularizer penalizes movement from the preceding iterate; its coefficient grows through the run. The bound concerns the full-collection population loss L defined above.
Finite jointly realizable linear tasks; R is the largest task-matrix operator norm and R>0.
Independent uniform task indices sampled with replacement; exact Scheme1 updates; w_0=0.
Known horizon k>=2 and the displayed increasing coefficient schedule.

[Prop 7 of arXiv:2606.30349, 'Attenuated Poisson Dirichlet approximations for divisibility configurations'] Let $\vec{C}(n)=(\alpha_p(H_n):p\le n)$ and $\vec{\xi}(n)=(\xi_p:p\le n)$. Then for all $n\geq  21$
\begin{align}
\PP[A_n]
  &=
\mathfrak{l}_n\prod_{p\le n}(1-p^{-1})\ge \frac12 , 
\\
\mathcal{L}(\vec{C}(n))
  &=\mathcal{L}(\vec{\xi}(n)\mid A_n).

\end{align}
In particular, for any additive arithmetic function $\psi$,
\begin{align}
\mathcal{L}(\psi(H_n))
=
\mathcal{L}\big(
\sum_{p\le n}\psi(p^{\xi_p}) \,\big|\, A_n
\big).
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 7 of arXiv:2606.30349

[Lemma lem:phase-pair of arXiv:2609.02544, 'A finiteness theorem for geodesic Leech wheels'] Let $\alpha,\beta,\Gamma,V>0$ with $\Gamma>V$, and set
\[
  \tau=\frac{\alpha}{2\sqrt{\Gamma-V}}.
\]
Assume also
\[
  0<\tau<\beta,
  \qquad
  \Gamma(\beta-\tau)\ge V(2\beta-\tau).
\]
If complex numbers $z,w$ satisfy
\[
  |z^2-w|\le \Gamma,
  \qquad
  |w|\le V,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
  \alpha\operatorname{Im}z+
  \beta\operatorname{Re}w
  \le
  \alpha\sqrt{\Gamma-V}+\beta V.
\end{equation}

body:
[Definition 7 (Canonical version of $W^\ell$) of arXiv:2511.09517, 'From Cannings model to Brownian motion conditioned on local time profile'] Let $\ell$ be a continuous profile with $h(\ell)<\infty$.
Set
\[
\tilde{\ell}(s):= I(\ell)^{-\frac12}\,\ell\big(I(\ell)^{\frac12}s\big),\qquad s\ge 0,
\]
so that \(I(\tilde{\ell})=1\).  
Let \(W^{\tilde{\ell}}\) denote the version of the conditioned reflected Brownian motion associated with the normalized profile \(\tilde{\ell}\) constructed above.  
We then define
\[
W^\ell_t:= I(\ell)^{\frac12}\, W^{\tilde{\ell}}_{I(\ell)^{-1}t}\,,\qquad 0\le t\le I(\ell).
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:scale}, this defines a version of conditional law, which will serve as our \emph{canonical version} of \(W^\ell\) throughout the paper.
title: Canonical version of $W^\ell$

body:
[Lem 72 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For all $q_0 \in [0,1)$, we have 
\begin{align*}
\sM^{\sx}(\alpha,q_0) 
&\subseteq \sM^{\sxii}(\alpha,q_0)\,,\\
\sM^{\six}(\alpha,q_0) 
&\subseteq \sM^{\sidealast}(\alpha,q_0)\,.
\end{align*}

\begin{proof}
We repeat the most relevant part of Definition~\ref{d:SDE.classification} for this proof:
	\begin{center}
	\begin{tabular}[h]{r|cccccccc}
	\MSRheader\\
	\hline
	\PRFTWOdefn\\
	\PRFFOURdefn\\
	\PRFONEHALFdefn\\
	\SUPERPERFECTASTdefn
	\end{tabular}
	\end{center}
The classes only differ in the conditions on the function $p$.

    Consider any $\mu \in \cM^{\sx}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon)$ where $\epsilon < 1/2$. 
    Then $\mu$ is of the form $\mu = \mu(q_*=q_0,b,\sigma,p,\zeta = \delta_0)$ for some $(q_*=q_0,b,\sigma,w,p,\zeta = \delta_0,\zeta^\Ising) \in \Adm^{\sx}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon)$.
    Since $p$ satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.1}, $p$ is twice differentiable and therefore continuous, and further satisfies $p(q_0) \le \epsilon$.
    So we can find $q' \in (q_0,1)$ such that $p(q') = 2\epsilon$, and define $\tilde p \in \incr([q_0,1];[0,1])$ by
    \[
        \tilde p(t) = \begin{cases}
            2\epsilon (t - q_0) / (q' - q_0) & t \in [q_0,q')\,, \\
            p(t) & t \in [q',1]\,.
        \end{cases}
    \]
    In particular $\tilde p(q_0) = 0$, so $\tilde p$ satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.5withzero}, as required for the $\sxii$ class.
    Since $p$ and $\tilde p$ agree on $[q',1]$, we have
    \[
        \|p'-\tilde p'\|_1
        = \int_{q_0}^{q'} |p'(t) - \tilde p'(t)|\,dt
        \le \int_{q_0}^{q'} (p'(t) + \tilde p'(t))\,dt
        \le p(q') + \tilde p(q')
        = 4\epsilon\,.
    \]
Recalling Definition~\ref{d:X.adm}, we have $\mu \in \cM(q_0;p,f)$ for budget function
$f(t) = (\E w_t)^2 / \alpha$. Applying
    Proposition~\ref{p:continuity.in.p} gives the existence of a measure
    \[
        \tilde\mu \in \cM(q_0;\tilde p,f)
        \subseteq \cM^{\sxii}(\alpha,q_0)
    \]
    with $\bbW_2(\mu,\tilde \mu)^2 \le 6(1+1/\alpha) \cdot 4\epsilon$.
    Since this holds for all $\mu \in \cM^{\sx}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon)$ with $\epsilon < 1/2$, we conclude
    \[
        \cM^{\sx}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon) \subseteq \cB_{\tilde\epsilon}\Big(\cM^{\sxii}(\alpha,q_0)\Big)
    \]
    for some $\tilde\epsilon$ tending to $0$ with $\epsilon$.
    By adjusting $\tilde\epsilon$ we can also ensure
    \[
        \cB_{\epsilon}\Big(\cM^{\sx}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon)\Big) \subseteq \cB_{\tilde\epsilon}\Big(\cM^{\sxii}(\alpha,q_0)\Big)\,.
    \]
 Recall \eqref{e:measure.classes.simplification.without.L0}: taking a union over $L$ and an intersection over $\epsilon$ proves the first assertion, $\sM^{\sx}(\alpha,q_0) \subseteq \sM^{\sxii}(\alpha,q_0)$.

    The proof of the second assertion $\sM^{\six}(\alpha,q_0) \subseteq \sM^{\sidealast}(\alpha,q_0)$ is very similar, so we only describe the differences.
    Consider any $\mu \in \cM^{\six}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon)$ where $\epsilon < 1/2$, realized by controls $(q_*=q_0,b,\sigma,w,p,\zeta = \delta_0,\zeta^\Ising) \in \Adm^{\six}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon)$.
    In this case $p$ satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.1concave}, so $p$ is concave in addition to the properties of condition~\ref{it:3.1} used above.
    Let $q'$ and $\tilde p$ be defined as above.
    Since $p(q_0) \ge 0$ and $p(q') = 2\epsilon$, the concavity of $p$ implies $p(t) \ge \tilde p(t)$ for all $t\in [0,q']$.
    Thus $\tilde p$ is also concave, and in particular satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.3}, as required for the $\sidealast$ class.
Then, arguing identically as above completes the proof.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 72 of arXiv:2608.29416

body:
[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2609.02169, '2609.02169'] Let $L$ be an ample line bundle of type $(1,d)$, where $d\geq2$, on an
abelian surface $S$.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item The linear system $|L|$ has a fixed component if and only if there
are elliptic curves $E_1,E_2$, line bundles $L_i$ with
$\deg L_1=1$ and $\deg L_2=d$, and an isomorphism of polarized abelian
varieties
$(S,L)\simeq(E_1\times E_2,p_1^*L_1\otimes p_2^*L_2)$.
\item If $|L|$ has no fixed component, then it is base-point-free for
$d\geq3$, while for $d=2$ its base scheme consists of four points.  A
general member is smooth when $d\geq2$.  When $d=2$ and $L$ is symmetric, the four base
points are four-division points.
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma 16 (Conditional occupation after a small-$r$ boundary hit) of arXiv:2607.19752, 'Weak Equilibrium Measures and Capacity--Hitting Identities\\ for the Hypoelliptic Third-Or'] Let $\Sigma\in\{\partial A,\partial B,\partial\calD\}$ and let
$\tau=\tau_\Sigma$.  There exist constants $c,q,C>0$ such that, for all
sufficiently small $b\in(0,1)$, on the event
$\{\tau<\infty,\ |r_\tau|\le b\}$,
\[
    \Pbb_z\left(
    Z_{\tau+s}\in
    \{y:\dist(y,\Sigma)\le Cb^2,\ |r(y)|\le2b\}
    \text{ for all }0\le s\le cb^2
    \middle|\mathcal F_\tau
    \right)\ge q .
\]
On the same event one may also require
\[
    \sup_{0\le s\le cb^2}
    \left(|p_{\tau+s}-p_\tau|+|\theta_{\tau+s}-\theta_\tau|\right)
    \le Cb^2 .
\]
For the regularized process, the same statement holds uniformly whenever
$0<\delta\le b^2$.  The constants are common to the three boundary components,
the forward and adjoint processes, the hitting point, and
$0\le\delta\le b^2$.

body:
[Theorem of arXiv:2411.19433, 'Singular mean-field backward stochastic Volterra integral equations in infinite dimensiona'] Assume condition \((A_{1})\) holds. Then for any \(\Psi(\cdot) \in L^2_{\mathcal{F}_T}(0, b; H)\), equation (equation r3 of the paper) has a unique adapted \(M\)-solution within \(H^2[0, b]\). Additionally, the subsequent bound is satisfied:

\[
\mathbb{E} \left\{ \int_0^b |X(t)|_H^2 \, dt + \int_0^b \int_0^b |\aleph(t,s)|_{L^2_0}^2 \, ds \, dt \right\} \leq C \mathbb{E} \int_0^b |\Psi(t)|_H^2 \, dt.
\]

Assume $\bar{F}$ also meets condition $(A_{1})$, and let $\bar{\Psi}(\cdot) \in L^2_{\mathcal{F}_{b}}(0, b; H)$. If \((\bar{Y}(\cdot), \bar{\aleph}(\cdot, \cdot)) \in H^2[0, b]\) represents the adapted \(M\)-solution of (equation r3 of the paper) with \(F\) and \(\Psi(\cdot)\) replaced by \(\bar{F}\) and \(\bar{\Psi}(\cdot)\), respectively, then the subsequent stability estimate is valid:

\begin{align*}
&\quad\mathbb{E} \left\{ \int_0^b |X(t) - \bar{X}(t)|_H^2 \, dt + \int_0^b \int_0^b |\aleph(t,s) - \bar{\aleph}(t,s)|_{L^2_0}^2 \, ds \, dt \right\} \\
&\leq C \bigg\{ \mathbb{E} \int_0^b |\Psi(t) - \bar{\Psi}(t)|_H^2 \, dt \\
& + \mathbb{E} \int_0^b \int_t^b |P(t,s, \bar{X}(s), \bar{\aleph}(t,s), \bar{\aleph}(s,t), \mathbb{E}\bar{X}(s), \mathbb{E}\bar{\aleph}(t,s), \mathbb{E}\bar{\aleph}(s,t)) \\
& - \bar{F}(t,s, \bar{X}(s), \bar{\aleph}(t,s), \bar{\aleph}(s,t), \mathbb{E}\bar{X}(s), \mathbb{E}\bar{\aleph}(t,s), \mathbb{E}\bar{\aleph}(s,t))|_H^2 \, ds \, dt \bigg\}.
\end{align*}

[Corollary 9 of arXiv:2606.11068, '2606.11068'] Assume \eqref{eq:right-edge} and let \(\beta=1/\gamma\). Set
 \(v:=|2r-1|\).
 \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item If \(\E(\eta)<\infty\) and
 \[
   \Gamma(1/\gamma)v\,
   \limsup_{n\to\infty} L(n^\gamma)
   <
   \frac{1}{2\E(\eta)},
 \]
 then the frog model dies out almost surely.
 \item If \(\Pbb(\eta=0)<1\) and
 \[
   \Gamma(1/\gamma)v\,
   \liminf_{n\to\infty} L(n^\gamma)
   >
   \frac{1}{\E(\eta)},
 \]
 where \(1/\E(\eta):=0\) when \(\E(\eta)=\infty\), then the frog model survives
 with positive probability in the direction of the drift. More precisely, the
 survival occurs to the right if \(r>1/2\), and to the left if \(r<1/2\).
 \end{enumerate}

    $$\begin{bmatrix}

        x_2 & \vdots & \ddots & &\vdots\\
        \vdots & \vdots & & \ddots & \vdots \\
        x_{m/2} & x_{m/2+1} & \cdots & \cdots & x_{m}
    \end{bmatrix}$$

body: Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem: every bounded sequence in R^n has a convergent subsequence. Equivalently, a subset of R^n is sequentially compact exactly when it is closed and bounded. Both formulations fail in infinite-dimensional normed spaces, where the closed unit ball is closed and bounded but not sequentially compact.
title: Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem

\(\pi_1(M)\cong \mathbb Z\), and \emph{secondary} otherwise.
A primary Hopf surface is said to be of \emph{class \(1\)} if
\(\lambda=0\), and of \emph{class \(0\)} otherwise. A \emph{class \(1\)} Hopf surface is called diagonal, if $\vert\alpha\vert=\vert\beta\vert$.
title: Definition 7 of arXiv:2608.30638

[Mtheorem 5 of arXiv:2609.00254, 'On the geometry and cohomology of almost abelian solvmanifolds'] Let $G_A$ be a $6$-dimensional almost abelian Lie group whose Lie algebra
$\mathfrak g_A=\mathbb Re_0\ltimes_A\mathbb R^5$ admits no left-invariant complex or symplectic
structure. Then the existence of a left-invariant generalized complex structure of type $1$ or $2$ on
$G_A$, the existence of a generalized Calabi--Yau one, and an explicit pure spinor realizing each are
completely determined by the Jordan form of $A$, as recorded in Tables \ref{tab:spectral} and
\ref{tab:forms}. In particular, $G_A$ admits no left-invariant generalized complex structure of any
type when
$$A=J_5(\lambda)\ (\lambda\neq0),\qquad
A=J_4(\lambda) \oplus J_1(\mu)\ (\lambda\neq0),\qquad
A=J_3(\lambda) \oplus J_2(\mu)\ (\lambda\neq\pm\mu).$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Mtheorem 5 of arXiv:2609.00254

body:
[Theorem thm:main-simple of arXiv:2604.15146, 'Renormalised two-point functions of CLE$_4$ gaskets'] Let $D$ be a simply-connected domain and $z_1 \neq z_2 \in D$. Let $E^{\rm simp}_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}(z_1,z_2)$ denote the event that the  CLE$_4$ gasket comes $\varepsilon_1$-close to $z_1$ and $\varepsilon_2$-close to $z_2$. Then we have
$$
\lim_{\max(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2)\to 0}
\varepsilon_1^{-1/8}\varepsilon_2^{-1/8}
\mathbb{P}(E^{\rm simp}_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}(z_1,z_2))
=
C_1\CR(z_1,D)^{-1/8}\CR(z_2,D)^{-1/8}
\sqrt{\frac{\theta_3(q^{1/4})}{\theta_2(q^{1/4})}},
$$
where $C_1$ is an absolute constant, and the nome $q$ is uniquely determined by
$$
\exp\!\left(\pi G_D(z_1,z_2)\right)
=
\frac{\theta_3(q^{1/2})}{\theta_2(q^{1/2})}.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Two-point correlations of the simple CLE$_4$

body:
[Proposition 1 (Orbital bivariate chromatic polynomial) of arXiv:2609.01866, 'The Multiorbital Bivariate Chromatic Polynomial'] Let $\Gamma$ be a finite graph and let $G\leq\Aut(\Gamma)$. For admissible
parameters $(\lambda,\mu)$, the orbital bivariate chromatic polynomial
satisfies
\[
OP_{\Gamma,G}(\lambda,\mu)
=
\frac{1}{|G|}
\sum_{g\in G}
P_{\Gamma/g}(\lambda,\mu).
\]
In particular, the polynomial $P_{\Gamma/g}$ is the fixed-point
contribution of the element $g$ in the corresponding Burnside average. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Orbital bivariate chromatic polynomial

\pi^{MF1}_\lambda \sim \operatorname{Geom}\bigl(1 - x^*(\lambda)\bigr),
\]

body: [Theorem 5 of arXiv:2609.00448, 'Equivariant formality and representation theory'] Let $G$ be a compact connected Lie group and $S$ a torus subgroup, and $\pi: G/S\to\text{pt}$ be the collapsing map. Denote by $A$ the subring of $K_S^*(G/S)\otimes\mathbb{Q}$ generated by $S$-equivariant line bundles $G\times_S\mathbb{C}_\mu$ where $\mu\in\mathfrak{s}^*$. Define $\mathcal{L}_S$ to be the $R(S; \mathbb{Q})$-submodule of $K_S^*(G/S)\otimes\mathbb{Q}$ generated by the odd equivariant $K$-theory classes of $G/S$ defined by the $\delta$-construction (see Definitions \ref{deltaconstruction} and \ref{equivsamelson}). Then $(G, S)$ is isotropy formal if and only if there exist $a\in A$ and $b\in\bigwedge\nolimits_{R(S; \mathbb{Q})}^{\text{rank }G-\text{rank }S}\mathcal{L}_S$ such that $\pi_*(ab)\notin I(S; \mathbb{Q})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 5 of arXiv:2609.00448

body:
[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2609.03191, 'On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes '] Let $\mathcal B$ be a field of characteristic $0$. Let $\mathcal C$ be a $\mathcal B[H]$-module. Then the following statement are equivalent.

\medskip
{\bf (1)} The  $\mathcal B[H]$-module $\mathcal C$ is rational.

\smallskip
{\bf (2)} The monic characteristic polynomial of the $\mathcal B$-linear map $\tau:\mathcal C\rightarrow \mathcal C$ belongs to $\mathbb Q[x]$.

\smallskip
{\bf (3)} For each $i\in\llbracket1,p^s\rrbracket$, the trace of  the $\mathcal B$-linear map $\tau^i:\mathcal C\rightarrow \mathcal C$ is a rational number.

\smallskip
{\bf (4)} For each $i\in\llbracket1,p^s-1\rrbracket$, the trace of  the $\mathcal B$-linear map $\tau^i:\mathcal C\rightarrow \mathcal C$ is a rational number.

[Lemma 2 of arXiv:2605.30321, 'A Bayesian Proof and Interpretation \\ of Talagrand's Majorizing Measure Theorem'] Let $T$ be finite and let $(G_t)_{t\in T}$ be a centered Gaussian process. For $N=|T|,$ there exist $N$ \emph{distinct} vectors $(h_t)_{t\in T}$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$ such that, for $Z\sim N(0,I_N)$,
\[
    (G_t)_{t\in T}\stackrel{d}= (\langle Z,h_t\rangle)_{t\in T},
\]
and
\[
    d(s,t)=\|h_s-h_t\|_2.
    \]

[Definition 9 (Unstable dual coordinate) of arXiv:2607.20882, 'An Eyring--Kramers Law for the Hypoelliptic Third-Order\\ Langevin Diffusion'] Let $\ell_\sigma=(\alpha_\sigma,\beta_\sigma,\zeta_\sigma)$ be the left
eigenvector of $\mathsf A_\sigma$ for $\mu_\sigma$, normalized by
$\beta_\sigma=1$, so that (Appendix~\ref{app:local-saddle-analysis})
\[
\alpha_\sigma=\frac{\lambda_\sigma}{L\mu_\sigma},\qquad
\beta_\sigma=1,\qquad
\zeta_\sigma=\frac{\gamma}{\mu_\sigma+\gamma}.
\]
Define the unstable dual coordinate
\[
\Lambda_\sigma(\theta,p,r)
=
\alpha_\sigma\langle\theta-\sigma,e_\sigma\rangle
+\langle p,e_\sigma\rangle
+\zeta_\sigma\langle r,e_\sigma\rangle
=\ell_\sigma\cdot X_1 .
\]
Along the linearized flow
$\frac{d}{dt}(\ell_\sigma\cdot X_{1,t})
=\mu_\sigma(\ell_\sigma\cdot X_{1,t})$.
title: Unstable dual coordinate

body: A function f : U -> C on an open set U in C is holomorphic if the complex derivative f'(z) = lim_{h->0} (f(z+h) - f(z))/h exists at every z in U (the limit taken over complex h). Writing f = u + iv, differentiability at z implies the Cauchy-Riemann equations u_x = v_y and u_y = -v_x; conversely continuous partials satisfying Cauchy-Riemann on U give holomorphy.
title: Holomorphic Function

[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2609.02610, 'The frame set of the first Hermite function'] Let $a,b>0$, and set $\delta=ab$ and $\beta=b^2$. Further let $0<\delta<1$ and assume that $\cG(\phi_1,a,b)$ is not a frame. 
    Then then there exist
    $x_*\in\R$ and a nonzero sequence
    $c=(c_k)_{k\in\Z}\in\ell^\infty(\Z)$ such that the series
    \begin{equation}
        F(z)=\sum_{k\in\Z}c_k\e^{-\pi(z-k)^2/\beta},
        \quad  \text{ for } z\in\C,
    \end{equation} 
    converges locally uniformly on $\C$, defines a nonzero entire
    function, and satisfies
    \begin{equation}
        F'(x_*+n\delta)=0
        \quad\text{for all }n\in\Z.
    \end{equation}
title: Proposition 7 of arXiv:2609.02610

body:
[Theorem 224 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Consider the master Riemann--Hilbert problem with sources $(D_h(z))_{h = 1}^H$. In addition, choose $\boldsymbol{\kappa} \in \amsmathbb{C}$ and rational functions $(L_h(z))_{h=1}^H$ that can have poles at $z = \alpha_h,\beta_h$ and such that $L_h(z) = O(\frac{1}{z})$ as $z \rightarrow \infty$ for each $h\in[H]$.

Then there exists a unique solution $(F_h(z))_{h = 1}^H$ to the master Riemann--Hilbert problem such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\displaystyle \left(F_h(z) - \sigma_h^{-1}(z) L_h(z) - \frac{1}{2\theta_{h,h}}D_h(z)\right)_{h = 1}^H$ is tame with exponent $1$; and
\item $\displaystyle\oint_{\gamma_h} \frac{\dd z}{2\ii\pi}\,F_h(z) = \kappa_h$ for all $h\in[H]$.
\end{enumerate}
The solution is given by the formula:
\[
F_h(z) = \sum_{g = 1}^H \big(\kappa_g \mathfrak{c}^{\textnormal{1st}}_{h;g}(z) - r(\alpha_g)\mathfrak{c}_{h;g}^{\textnormal{3rd}}(z;\alpha_g) - r(\beta_g)\mathfrak{c}^{\textnormal{3rd}}_{h;g}(\z;\beta_g)\big) - \sum_{\textnormal{J} \in \{\textnormal{I},\textnormal{II},\textnormal{III}\}} \mathfrak{F}_h^{\textnormal{J}}[\boldsymbol{f}^{\textnormal{J}}](z).
\]
The $H$-tuple of functions $\boldsymbol{f}^{\textnormal{J}}$ and the constants $(r(\alpha_g),r(\beta_g))_{g = 1}^{H}$ are determined by
\[
\forall g \in [H]\qquad f_g^{\textnormal{II}}(z) = \frac{2}{\sigma_g(z)} \int_{z}^{\infty} \frac{L_g(\zeta)}{\sigma_g(\zeta)}\dd \zeta,
\]
and the (unique up to addition of a constant to $f^{\textnormal{I}}_g$) decomposition of the source
\begin{equation}

\forall g \in [H]\qquad D_g(z) = \partial_z f^{\textnormal{I}}_g(z) + \frac{r(\alpha_g)}{z - \alpha_g} + \frac{r(\beta_g)}{z -\beta_g} + \partial_z f^{\textnormal{III}}_g(z),
\end{equation}
where the function $f_g^{\textnormal{I}}(z)$ is holomorphic in a complex neighborhood of $\overline{\amsmathbb{B}}_g$ and $f^{\textnormal{III}}_g(z)$ is a rational function with possible poles at $\alpha_g,\beta_g$ and such that $f^{\textnormal{III}}_g(z) = O(\frac{1}{z})$ as $z \rightarrow \infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theo th:rho'_survival of arXiv:2505.12127, 'Generalised principal eigenvalues and global survival of branching Markov processes'] The following holds.
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item Let $x\in E$. If ${\mathbb P}_x(\ensuremath{\mathrm{glSurv}}) > 0$, then $\rho'_{c,x}(m) \ge 1$.
    \item Suppose there exists $u\in pB_b(E)$, $\rho\ge 1$ and $\delta>0$, such that 
      \begin{equation}
        
        \forall x\in E: {\mathbb E}_x\left[\sum_{i\in{\mathbb N}} u(X_i) \exp\left(-\delta\sum_{i\in{\mathbb N}} u(X_i)\right)\right] \ge \rho u(x).
      \end{equation}
      Then for all $x\in E$, we have that $u(x)>0$ implies
      \[
      {\mathbb P}_x(\liminf_{n\to\infty} \rho^{-n}N_n > 0) > 0,
      \]
      and, in particular, ${\mathbb P}_x(\ensuremath{\mathrm{glSurv}}) > 0$.

    \item 
      Suppose the following holds:
      \begin{itemize}
        \item[(B)]
      there exists a constant $K<\infty$ such that $N_1 \le K$, ${\mathbb P}_x$-a.s. for all $x\in E$. 
  \end{itemize}
  Then for every $\rho < \rho'_{c,x}(m)$, there exists $u\in pB_b(E)$ and $\delta>0$, such that (equation eq:assumption_u_discrete of the paper) is verified with this value of $\rho$ and $u(x) > 0$. In particular,
  \[
    \text{$\rho'_{c,x}(m) > 1$ implies ${\mathbb P}_x(\ensuremath{\mathrm{glSurv}})>0$ and }\forall \rho < \rho'_{c,x}:{\mathbb P}_x\left(\liminf_{n\to\infty} N_n^{1/n} \ge \rho\right) > 0.
  \]

    \item We have for every $x\in E$,
      \[
        {\mathbb P}_x\left(\limsup_{n\to\infty} N_n^{1/n} \le \rho''_{c,x}\right) = 1.
      \]
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 1 of arXiv:2609.03875, 'Measure theory without infinities'] Let $\mathcal Q$ be a $\delta$-ring. Then the following statements hold:
  \begin{itemize}
  \item [(i)] Let $B\in\mathcal Q$ and $\mb A\colon I\to \mathcal Q$ be a countable family such that $\mb A(i)\subset B$ for all $i\in I$. Then $\bigcup_{i\in I} \mb A(i) \in \mathcal Q$.
  \item [(ii)] $\sigma(\mathcal Q) = \sigma_0(\mathcal{Q})$.
  \item [(iii)] If $A\in \sigma(\mathcal Q)$ and $A\subset B$ for some $B\in \mathcal Q$, then $A\in \mathcal Q$.
  \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 43 (Simultaneous finite compression of the four flattenings) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Let $2\le r<\infty$ and suppose that the four flattenings of $\mathbf H$
belong to $\Sch_r$.  Let
$P_{\mathcal A}^{(m)},P_{\mathcal C_1}^{(m)},
 P_{\mathcal C_0}^{(m)},P_{\mathcal E}^{(m)}$
be increasing finite-rank orthogonal projections converging strongly to the
identity on the corresponding Hilbert spaces, and define
\[
 \mathbf H_m(x,y,z,w)
 :=\mathbf H(P_{\mathcal A}^{(m)}x,
 P_{\mathcal C_1}^{(m)}y,
 P_{\mathcal C_0}^{(m)}z,
 P_{\mathcal E}^{(m)}w).
\]
Then the four flattenings of $\mathbf H_m$ are
\begin{align*}
 F_{1,m}&=P_{\mathcal E}^{(m)}F_1
 (P_{\mathcal A}^{(m)}\otimes P_{\mathcal C_1}^{(m)}
 \otimes P_{\mathcal C_0}^{(m)}),\\
 F_{2,m}&=P_{\mathcal C_0}^{(m)}F_2
 (P_{\mathcal A}^{(m)}\otimes P_{\mathcal C_1}^{(m)}
 \otimes P_{\mathcal E}^{(m)}),\\
 F_{3,m}&=(P_{\mathcal C_1}^{(m)}\otimes P_{\mathcal E}^{(m)})F_3
 (P_{\mathcal A}^{(m)}\otimes P_{\mathcal C_0}^{(m)}),\\
 F_{4,m}&=(P_{\mathcal A}^{(m)}\otimes P_{\mathcal E}^{(m)})F_4
 (P_{\mathcal C_1}^{(m)}\otimes P_{\mathcal C_0}^{(m)}).
\end{align*}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \|F_{\varkappa,m}-F_{\varkappa}\|_{\Sch_r}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad 1\le\varkappa\le4.
\end{equation}
The same conclusion holds for a difference of two forms.

independent copies of Brownian motion, we use the notation ${_1}B,{_2}B,{_3}B,\ldots$
(in particular, we use ${_i}B^{x_i}$ and ${_i}B^{x_i,y_i}_t$, $i\geq1$, to denote independent Brownian motions
started at $x_i$ and independent Brownian bridges from $x_i$ to $y_i$ on the time interval $[0,t]$).

body:
[Prop log-concave of arXiv:2605.10908, 'On Talagrand's Convexity Conjecture'] Let $\mu=\sum\limits_{i=1}^{m} p_i \delta_{x_i}$ be a finitely supported centered probability measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and let $\nu$ be a centered  probability measure  on $\mathbb{R}^n$ absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure, and with finite first moments. Assume that $\mu\preceq_{\text{cx}}\nu$.
    Then there exists a natural bijection between the set of martingale couplings $(X,Y)$ of $\mu$ and $\nu$, and the collection $\mathcal{C}$ of tuples of nonnegative functions $(f_1,\ldots, f_m)$ (defined up to $\nu$-null sets) where the $f_{i} \colon \mathbb{R}^{n} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $$ \sum\limits_{i=1}^{m}p_if_i(x)=1,\ \mathbb{E}\left[f_i(Y)\right]=1,\ \mathbb{E} \left[Yf_i(Y)\right]=x_i.$$ 

 Moreover, we have $X\preceq_{\text{cx}}(1-\varepsilon) Y$ for some $\varepsilon>0$ if and only if there exist $(f_1^*,\ldots, f_m^*)$ in $\mathcal{C}$ such that each $f_i^*$ is of the form
 $$f_i^*(x)=\dfrac{e^{U_i+\langle V_i,x\rangle}}{\sum\limits_{j=1}^{m} p_j e^{U_j+\langle V_j,x\rangle}}$$
 for some $U_i\in \mathbb{R},\ V_i\in \mathbb{R}^n$. Note that each $f_i^*$ is log-concave. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop log-concave of arXiv:2605.10908

[Proposition 44 (The tower) of arXiv:2609.02267, 'Locally Conformally Flat Manifolds with Positive Scalar Curvature: Kleinian Groups, Moduli'] There are closed regular neighborhoods $V_j\subset\operatorname{int}B$ of
embedded rank-two roses $\Gamma_j$ whose petals are oriented and labeled
$a$ and $b$, a common wedge point
$x\in\bigcap_j\operatorname{int}V_j$, finite ball families
$\mathcal{U}_j=\{U_{j,\ell}\}$, and markings
$\mathfrak{m}_j:F_2\xrightarrow{\cong}\pi_1(V_j,x)$ such that for all
$j\ge1$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $V_{j+1}\Subset\operatorname{int}V_j$;
\item $\operatorname{cap}(V_j)<2^{-j}$;
\item $V_j\subset\bigcup_\ell U_{j,\ell}$ with
$\operatorname{diam}U_{j,\ell}<2^{-j}$ and
$\sum_\ell(\operatorname{diam}U_{j,\ell})^{1+1/j}<2^{-j}$;
\item $(i_j)_*\circ\mathfrak{m}_{j+1}=\mathfrak{m}_j\circ\omega$ for
$i_j:V_{j+1}\hookrightarrow V_j$;
\item $\mathfrak{m}_j(a)$ and $\mathfrak{m}_j(b)$ are represented by the
corresponding oriented petal loops of $\Gamma_j$ based at $x$;
\item there are a triangulation $\mathcal{T}_j$ of $S^n$ in which
$\Gamma_j$ is the polyhedron of a nonempty, proper, full subcomplex, the simplicial map
$f_j:|\mathcal{T}_j|\to[0,1]$ taking value $0$ on the vertices of this
subcomplex and value $1$ on all other vertices, and a number
$t_j\in(0,1)$ such that
\[
f_j^{-1}(0)=\Gamma_j,\qquad V_j=f_j^{-1}([0,t_j]),
\]
and, for every $c\in(0,1)$, $f_j^{-1}([0,c])$ is a closed regular
neighborhood of $\Gamma_j$ with
\[
\partial\bigl(f_j^{-1}([0,c])\bigr)=f_j^{-1}(c).
\]
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, for $k>j$ the inclusion $V_k\hookrightarrow V_j$
induces $\mathfrak{m}_j\circ\omega^{\,k-j}\circ\mathfrak{m}_k^{-1}$ on $\pi_1$; in
particular it is injective. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 148 (Homeomorphism and diffeomorphism properties of $\Upsilon$) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] The change of variables map $\Upsilon(t,u,x^2,x^3) = (t,x^1,x^2,x^3)$
		is \textbf{injective} on the compact set
		$\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot]}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}$
		and satisfies: 
		\begin{align} 
		\| \Upsilon \|_{C_{\textnormal{geo}}^{3,1}\left(\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot]}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]} \right)}
		\leq C.
		\end{align}
		In particular, $\Upsilon$ is a homeomorphism from 
		$\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot]}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}$
		onto its image.
		
		Moreover, with $d_{\textnormal{geo}} \Upsilon$ denoting the Jacobian matrix of $\Upsilon$,
		we have:
		\begin{align} 
			\mydet d_{\textnormal{geo}} \Upsilon
			& = 
				  \frac{\upmu  X^1}{1 - \Yvfsmallcoeff{A} X^A} 
				\approx
				- 
				\upmu.
		\end{align}
		
		In addition, if $\ubarboot < 0$, then $\Upsilon$ is a diffeomorphism from
		$\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot]}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}$ onto its image.

body: [Prop 2 of arXiv:2411.06571, 'Moment-based approach for two erratic KPZ scaling limits'] Let $\tilde Z_{s,t}(x,y)$ be the continuous modification from Proposition (mr0 of the paper). Fix some $x,s\in \Bbb R$. Then for all $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\Bbb R)$ the process $$M_t(\phi) := (\tilde Z_{s,t}(x,\bullet),\phi)_{L^2(\Bbb R)}-\frac12 \int_s^t (\tilde Z_{s,u}(x,\bullet),\phi'')_{L^2(\Bbb R)}du,\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\; t\ge s$$ is a continuous martingale in the filtration $(\mathcal F_{s,t})_{t\ge s}$ where $\mathcal F_{s,t}:=\sigma(\tilde Z_{a,b}(x,y): s<a<b<t,x,y\in\Bbb R\}$. body: TYPEWRITER (L^p convergence does not imply almost-everywhere convergence). On [0,1] write n = 2^k + j with 0 <= j < 2^k and let f_n be the indicator of [j 2^{-k}, (j+1) 2^{-k}). Then ||f_n||_p^p = 2^{-k} -> 0, so f_n -> 0 in L^p for every p < infinity and in measure. But for every x in [0,1) and every k there is exactly one j with f_{2^k + j}(x) = 1, so f_n(x) equals 1 for infinitely many n and 0 for infinitely many n: the sequence converges at NO point. This is why one extracts an a.e. convergent subsequence rather than hoping for the full sequence. SLIDING BUMP (pointwise convergence does not imply L^1 convergence). On [0,1] let g_n = n 1_{(0, 1/n)}. Then g_n(x) -> 0 for every x in (0,1], indeed the convergence is pointwise everywhere on (0,1], yet integral g_n = 1 for every n. The mass does not disappear, it concentrates. The dominated convergence theorem excludes exactly this: no integrable g dominates all g_n, since any such g would satisfy g >= n on (0,1/n) for every n, forcing integral_{(0,1/n)} g >= 1 for all n and contradicting absolute continuity of the integral. ESCAPING MASS is the third, distinct failure and lives on infinite measure spaces: h_n = 1_{[n, n+1]} on R is uniformly bounded, converges to 0 everywhere, and has ||h_n||_1 = 1. Three different mechanisms, three different repairs: a subsequence, a dominating function, and a tightness condition. [standard; the typewriter sequence is sometimes attributed to Kolmogorov]

For complex matrices A (n by n) and B (m by m), S(X) = AX - XB on n by m matrices X, and the Frobenius separation is sep_F(A, B) = min over ||X||_F = 1 of ||AX - XB||_F. If A and B are normal, sep_F(A, B) = min over lambda in spec A and mu in spec B of |lambda - mu|. Repeated eigenvalues within A or within B are allowed; only overlap between the two spectra makes the separation vanish.
A is n by n and B is m by m, complex

body:
[Proposition 8 of arXiv:2606.31455, 'Discrete time-multidimensional renewal theory and applications'] The renewal function $M$ satisfies the discrete multi-time renewal equation
\begin{equation}
M = F + f*M,
\end{equation}
i.e.\ for all $k\in\mathbb{N}^d$,
\[
M(k)=F(k)+\sum_{\ell\le_d k} f(\ell)\,M(k-\ell).
\]

[Definition 4 (\(\delta\)-hyperbolic metric spaces,~\cite{BH13}) of arXiv:2607.08632, 'Uncountably many extremal Series--Sinai states for the Ising model on Lobachevsky lattices'] Let \(\delta > 0\).
    A geodesic triangle in a metric space is said to be \emph{\(\delta\)-thin} \textiff{} each of its sides is contained in the \(\delta\)-neighbourhood of the union of the other two sides, \ie~every point on a side of the triangle is at distance at most \(\delta\) from the union of the other two sides.
    A geodesic metric space \(X\) is said to be \emph{\(\delta\)-hyperbolic} \textiff{} every geodesic triangle in \(X\) is \(\delta\)-thin.
    Moreover, if \(X\) is \(\delta\)-hyperbolic for some \(\delta > 0\), then \(X\) is said to be \emph{hyperbolic}.
title: \(\delta\)-hyperbolic metric spaces,~\cite{BH13}

[Theorem thm:signed-wedge-count-for-gaussian-points of arXiv:2602.14998, 'Random geometric graphs with smooth kernels: sharp detection threshold and a spectral conj'] Let $P$ denote the model of the random geometric graph with conditionally independent edges $A_{ij} \sim \widetilde K(x_i, x_j)$ given the latent points $x_1, \dots, x_n \sim {\mathcal{N}}(0, \frac 1d I_d)$. Let $p \triangleq \mathbb{E}_P[A_{ij}]$ and $\bar A_{ij} = A_{ij} - p$. 
Let $Q = G(n,p)$. 
Define the signed wedge count to be 
$$
W(A) \triangleq \sum_{H \subset K_n, \, H \cong \mathrm{wedge}} \prod_{e \in H} \bar A_e.
$$
If $1 \ll d \ll n^{3/2}$, then ${\rm TV}(P,Q) = 1-o(1)$, and thresholding the signed wedge count $W(A)$ is a consistent test. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:signed-wedge-count-for-gaussian-points of arXiv:2602.14998

[Proposition 23 of arXiv:2511.04938, 'Uniform dimension theorems for parabolic SPDEs'] Suppose $p \ge 4$, $\mathcal{M}(b) < \infty$, $\mathcal{M}(\sigma)<\infty$ 
	and $\inf_{v\in\R^p}\lambda(v)>0$.
	Fix $T > 0$ and $\delta \in (0\,,1)$.
	Then, there exists $L = L(p\,,\delta\,, T\,, b\,,\sigma\,, u_0) > 0$ such that
	\[
		\P\left\{\mathcal{N}^\delta_n(t\,, B(\nu\,, 2^{-n})) \ge 2^{2np\delta}\right\} 
		\le L^n n^{3pn} 2^{-\delta pn^2},
	\]
	uniformly for all $\nu \in \R^p$, $t \in (0\,, T]$ and $n \in \Z_+$ 
	such that $2^{-n} \le t/2$.
title: Proposition 23 of arXiv:2511.04938

body:
[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2605.17296, 'Zero correlations and averaged fields of orthonormal Gaussian Functions'] Fix $z_0 \in \C$ and a compact set $K \subset \C$. Then
\[
\cG_N^{(z_0)} \inlawto \cG
\qquad
\text{in } C(K),
\]
where $\cG$ is a centered real Gaussian process on $\C$ with covariance
\[
\E\bigl[\cG(\xi)\cG(\eta)\bigr] = \kappa(|\xi-\eta|).
\]
The limit covariance is the normalized overlap area of two unit
disks,
\[
\kappa(r) := \frac{|B(0,1)\cap B(r,1)|}{\pi},
\qquad
r\ge 0,
\]
where $B(z, \rho)$ is the disk of radius $\rho \ge 0$
centered at $z \in \C$. Equivalently,
\[
\kappa(r)=
\begin{cases}
\disp \frac{2}{\pi}\arccos \frac{r}{2}
-
\frac{r}{\pi}\sqrt{1-\frac{r^2}{4}},
&
0\le r\le 2,
\\[1ex]
0,
&
r\ge 2.
\end{cases}
\]
Moreover, for every $0<\alpha<\frac{1}{2}$, the family
$\{\cG_N^{(z_0)}\}_{N\ge 1}$ is tight in $C^{0,\alpha}(K)$, and $\cG$ admits a
version with sample paths in $C^{0,\alpha}(K)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 4 of arXiv:2605.17296

[Definition maindefi of arXiv:2412.06701, 'Matsumoto-Yor processes on Jordan algebras'] Let $(w_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of i.i.d. random variables on $E_+$ distributed according to $\mathrm{GIG}_{E_+}\left( p ; e, e \right)$. 

Let on the one hand, $L := (L_n \ ; \ n\ge 0)$ be the Markov chain defined by 
$$L_{n+1}=\mathrm{P}(w_{n+1})(L_n)+w_{n+1}, \, n\ge 0,$$
and $L_0=0$. 

On the other hand, the random process $\Lambda := (\Lambda_n \ ; \ n\ge 1)$ is defined by
$$ \Lambda_{n+1}=\mathrm{P}(w_{n+1}+L_n^{-1})(\Lambda_{n}), \, n\ge 1, $$
and $\Lambda_1=e$.
title: Definition maindefi of arXiv:2412.06701

body:
[Proposition prop:passive-active of arXiv:2605.02104, '\textbf{Chart-Generated Probability Geometry\\and Kolmogorov Expectations}'] Let $G,H:I\to(0,1)$ be probability coordinate charts on the same interval and
set
\[
T:=H\circ G^{-1}:(0,1)\to(0,1).
\]
Then $H=T\circ G$ and
\[
d_H(x,y)=\bigl|T(G(x))-T(G(y))\bigr|.
\]
If $G$ and $H$ are continuously differentiable with strictly positive
derivatives, then
\[
ds_H^2=\bigl(T'(G(x))\bigr)^2ds_G^2.
\]
By contrast, if $v=H(x)$ is used merely as a new coordinate in which to express
the already fixed geometry $d_G$, then
\[
ds_G^2
=
\left((G\circ H^{-1})'(v)\right)^2dv^2,
\]
not $dv^2$ in general.

[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2609.00680, 'Sharp embeddings between quasi-Banach Besov spaces and shallow ReLU Variation spaces'] Let $0<p,q\leq\infty$ and $s>0$, with the convention $d/\infty=0$.
There exist $x_0\in\Omega$ and
$\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ such that, for all sufficiently small
$h>0$, define
\[
\psi_h(x):=\psi\left(\frac{x-x_0}{h}\right).
\]
The following two-sided estimates hold:
\begin{equation}
\|\psi_h\|_{B_{p,q}^s(\mathbb R^d)}\simeq h^{d/p-s},\qquad
\|\psi_h\|_{\mathcal L_1(\D)}\simeq h^{-k}.
\end{equation}

[Proposition 3 (\cite{Li}) of arXiv:2605.15781, 'Mean-Field Backward Stochastic Differential Equations with Nonlinear Resistance and Double'] Suppose that $(l^i,r^i)$ satisfy Assumption $\ref{asslr}$, $i=1,2$.
Given  $s^i\in C[0,T]$, let $(x^i,K^i)$ be the solution to the Skorokhod problem $\mathbb{SP}_{l^i}^{r^i}(s^i)$. Then, we have
\begin{equation}
\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\left|K^1_t-K^2_t\right|
\leq \frac{C}{c}\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\left|s^1_t-s^2_t\right|+\frac{1}{c}(\bar{L}_T\vee\bar{R}_T),

where
\begin{align*}
\bar{L}_T=\sup_{(t,x)\in[0,T]\times \mathbb{R}}\left|{l}^1(t,x)-{l}^2(t,x)\right|,\
\bar{R}_T=\sup_{(t,x)\in[0,T]\times \mathbb{R}}\left|{r}^1(t,x)-{r}^2(t,x)\right|.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition Convexity gap of arXiv:2606.27073, 'Retention Profiles and KL Contraction Bounds in Finite Markov Chains'] For a distribution $\mu$ on $S$, define
\[
  \Delta(\mu)
  := \sum_{x\in S}\mu(x)\,D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P(x,\cdot)\|\pi)
     - D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu P\|\pi).
\]
By the convexity of $\nu\mapstoD_{\mathrm{KL}}(\nu\|\pi)$ (Jensen's inequality),
$\Delta(\mu)\ge 0$.
title: Convexity gap

body:
[Corollary cor:phase-prob of arXiv:2608.07410, 'Extreme least singular values of random row submatrices\\ with bounded-density subgaussian'] Let $A_m\in\mathbb R^{(2m-1)\times m}$ have independent entries distributed as a random variable $\xi$
satisfying the assumptions of \hyperref[thm:main]{Theorem~\ref*{thm:main}}. Then
\[
\frac1m\log\omega(A_m)\xrightarrow{\mathbb P}-\log4,
\qquad
\omega(A_m)=4^{-m+o_{\mathbb P}(m)}.
\]
Let $R_m:=\max_{1\le i\le2m-1}\|a_i\|_2$, where $a_i$ are the rows of $A_m$. Then, for every
$b>1/4$,
\[
\mathbb P\{\omega(A_m)\le R_m b^m\}\longrightarrow1,
\]
whereas for every $0<b<1/4$ and every fixed $C>0$,
\[
\mathbb P\{\omega(A_m)\le C R_m b^m\}\longrightarrow0.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Balan--Wang base for bounded-density subgaussian frames

body: [Lemma lem:smoothing_asymptotic_flows of arXiv:2506.12171, 'The multinomial dimer model'] Suppose that $(R,b)\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ and that $b$ is extendable outside and fix $\varepsilon>0$ small enough. Any asymptotic flow $\omega\in \mathrm{AF}(\Lambda,R,b)$ can be approximated in $d_W$ by a smooth flow $\omega_{\mathrm{sm}}\in \mathrm{AF}(\Lambda,R)$, where $\omega_{\mathrm{sm}}$ is constructed by mollifying $\omega$ with a bump function $\phi$ supported in $B_\varepsilon(0)$, and  has $d_W(\omega,\omega_{\mathrm{sm}}) < C \varepsilon^{1/2}$ for some constant $C>0$. Further we can assume that $\omega_{\mathrm{sm}}$ is valued strictly in the interior of $\mathcal{N}(\Lambda)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:smoothing_asymptotic_flows of arXiv:2506.12171

body:
[Theorem thm:multiclass-destruction of arXiv:2608.20480, 'When Clean Data Hurts: Learning with Monotone \\ Corruptions Beyond Binary Classification'] There are countable discrete spaces $\mathcal{X},\mathcal{Y}$ and a countable class
$\mathcal{H}\subseteq\mathcal{Y}^{\mathcal{X}}$ with $d_{\mathrm{DS}}(\mathcal{H})=2$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2em]
    \item A deterministic proper learner satisfies, for every clean sample
    size $N\ge2$,
    \[
        \Pr[L_D(\widehat h,h^\star)>\varepsilon]
        \le
        N^2e^{-\varepsilon(N-2)}.
    \]
    In particular, $\mathcal{H}$ is properly PAC learnable from clean i.i.d.\ data
    with sample complexity
    $O((\log(1/\varepsilon)+\log(1/\delta))/\varepsilon)$.

    \item For every $n\ge1$ and every learner $A_n$, permitted to be
    randomized and/or improper, there are a target $h^\star\in\mathcal{H}$, a
    finitely supported marginal $D$, and a deterministic adaptive monotone
    adversary adding exactly $n$ examples such that
    \[
        \mathbb{E} L_D(A_n(T),h^\star)\ge\frac14,
        \qquad
        \Pr\!\left[
            L_D(A_n(T),h^\star)>\frac18
        \right]
        \ge
        \frac17.
    \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:multiclass-destruction of arXiv:2608.20480

body: [Definition 70 of arXiv:2604.01685, 'Probability with Measure\footnote{Lecture notes. University of Ljubljana.}'] Let $(\Omega,\FF,\mu)$ be a measure space, $p\in [1,\infty)$ and $f\in \FF/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$. We put $$\Vert f\Vert_{p_\mu}:=\left(\int \vert f\vert^p\dd \mu\right)^{1/p}$$ and set $\LL^p(\mu):=\{g\in \FF/\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{R}}:\Vert g\Vert_{p_\mu}<\infty\}$ (this has already been defined for $p=1$); in addition we set $\Vert f\Vert_{\infty_\mu}:=\inf \{M\in [0,\infty]:\vert f\vert\leq M\text{ a.e.-$\mu$}\}$ and put $\LL^\infty(\mu):=\{g\in \FF/\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{R}}:\Vert g\Vert_{\mu_\infty}<\infty\}$. For $q\in [1,\infty]$, a sequence  $(f_n)_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ in $\LL^q(\mu)$ and $f_0\in \LL^q(\mu)$: $\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n=f_0$ in $\LL^q(\mu)$ \deff $\Vert f_n-f_0\Vert_{q_\mu}\to 0$ as $n\to\infty$, in which case $f_0$ is  called the $\LL^q(\mu)$-limit of $(f_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$. One also defines  $\langle f,g\rangle_\mu:=\mu[fg]$ for $\{f,g\}\subset\LL^2(\mu)$.
title: Definition 70 of arXiv:2604.01685
