body:
# Moitra-Risteski: relevant decomposition, uncovered phase-retrieval hypotheses

T321 Target 2. Literature applicability finding, not a new proof of Target 2.
Source: Fast Convergence for Langevin Diffusion with Manifold Structure,
arXiv:2002.05576, primary PDF saved under papers/.

Section 2, PDF page 3, requires the matrix-sensing operator to satisfy
(19/20)||M||_F^2 <= ||A(M)||_2^2 <= (21/20)||M||_F^2
for every matrix M of rank at most 2k. This is an operator-wide assumption,
not concentration for a fixed deterministic M.

For phase retrieval take k=1 and A_ph(M)_j=(a_j^T M a_j)/sqrt(m), so the
squared residual is precisely the normalized empirical quartic loss.
For every nonzero measurement a_i, set u=a_i/||a_i|| and M=uu^T. Then
rank(M)=1, ||M||_F=1 and

 ||A_ph(M)||_2^2=(1/m)sum_j(a_j.u)^4 >= ||a_i||^4/m.

Thus the upper RIP inequality would force
m >= (20/21)max_i||a_i||^4. The witness is allowed to depend on the sample,
because RIP quantifies over EVERY rank-one matrix. This is the exact
deterministic fourth-moment obstruction already relevant to this row,
applied to the paper's stated hypothesis; it is not presented as new.
For Gaussian measurements, ||a_1||^2/d tends to 1 in probability. Therefore
for m=C d log^3 d with fixed C, this necessary inequality fails with
probability tending to 1 as d grows. Multiplication by any fixed scalar
normalization of A_ph does not remove the growing d/log^3 d obstruction.
No claim is made here about operators obtained by data-dependent weighting,
truncation or a changed loss; those require their own arguments.

Section 4.1, Theorem 4, PDF page 7, is nevertheless a relevant generic
decomposition framework: along-level and across-level Poincare control,
control of changing conditional density/Jacobian, and finite-time retention
near the minimizer manifold combine into convergence to a restricted law.
These are hypotheses to establish, not consequences of benign landscape
alone. Our C007 is a different polar decomposition with the same unresolved
need for one conditional spectral-gap estimate.

Section 4.2, Theorem 5, PDF pages 7-8, assumes the matrix measurement
conditions above, a sufficiently large beta, and an absolutely continuous
initial law supported near one minimizer component. The target p_i is
defined just before the theorem as the Gibbs law restricted to points
closer to component E_i than the other component. The theorem's displayed
TV error includes an additive epsilon, as well as a decaying chi-square
term. It is not a statement of the full unrestricted even Poincare constant
for the empirical rank-one measurement model at beta~d/epsilon_loss.
The TV accuracy epsilon in the paper must not be identified silently with
the row's optimization/loss tolerance epsilon_loss.

The discussion on PDF page 9 explicitly leaves reaching the prescribed
initialization by unmodified Langevin for future work, while explaining
that optimization can supply such an initialization in the stated models.
Even if a warm-start sampling guarantee were imported, an additive-error
TV guarantee alone is not a variational Poincare inequality for the full law.

NEXT: adapt the near-well decomposition and retention estimates using the
actual rank-one measurement geometry, without imposing false global RIP;
then control the rest of the quotient to obtain the full polynomial gap.
No claim of a solved parameter range or a scored frontier move is made.
The rank-one diagnostic is analytic and unaudited, not a numerical bound
or a Lean-certified assertion.
Primary-source scope record, not a new polynomial-gap theorem
Matrix sensing application assumes 1/20-RIP on all rank-at-most-2k matrices
The actual row has iid Gaussian rank-one measurements and m at least C d log^3 d

[Theorem l.CLT-Cumulants of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Let $(\mathfrak{m}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$  be a sequence of purely
 atomic random signed measures and assume they admit  correlation functions $m^{\bk k1{p}}(\bk x1{p})= m^{\bk k1{p}}(\bk x1{p};n)$ defined as at (equation eqn:mixedmoment-general of the paper).   Assume  there exist fast decreasing functions $\tilde\phi_{k}$,
 and constants $M_{k}$,	$\tilde C_k$, 
 such that for all $p\ge 2$, $k_1,\ldots,k_p\in \mathbb{N}$, $k_1+\ldots+k_p=k$
 \begin{equation}
   \sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}}\sup_{\bk x1p\in\mathbb{R}^{dp}}m^{\bk k1{p}}(\bk x1{p};n)\le M_{k}<\infty
 \end{equation}
 and statement (i) of Lemma~(l.moments-cumulants of the paper) holds for
 the functions $\tilde\phi =\tilde\phi_k$ and constants  $\tilde C=\tilde C_k$ (uniformly in $n \in \mathbb{N}$).
 If the sequence  $(g_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of real-valued, measurable functions on $ \mathbb{R}^d$, 
 is uniformly  bounded in $n$ (i.e., $\sup_{n \geq 1}  \|g_n\|_\infty\le M<\infty$) and  satisfies
$\|g_n\|_1 := \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}|g_n(x)|\,\mathrm{d} x=O(n^\kappa)$ for some $\kappa<\infty$, and
  ${\rm Var}[\langle g_n,\mathfrak{m}_n\rangle] = \Omega(n^{\nu})$ for some $\nu > 0$, then

$$
({\rm Var}[\langle g_n,\mathfrak{m}_n\rangle])^{-1/2} ( \langle g_n,\mathfrak{m}_n\rangle - \mathbb {E} [\langle g_n,\mathfrak{m}_n\rangle]) \stackrel{d}{\Rightarrow} Z
$$
where $Z$ denotes a standard normal random variable.

[Cor corPhaseTransitionGnp of arXiv:2411.18563, 'Lower tails for triangles inside the critical window'] A phase transition for triangle-freeness in  $G(n,p)$  occurs at $p=c^\ast/\sqrt{n}$ for some $c^\ast \in [1/\sqrt{e}, 4.342)$ in the sense that the function $\varphi_0(c)$ is non-analytic at $c=c^\ast$.
 

   More generally, there exists $\eta_\ell \approx .0091$ so that for every $\eta \in [0, \eta_\ell)$, there exists $c^\ast_\eta \in (0,\infty)$ so that a phase transition occurs in the lower-tail problem at  $c^\ast_{\eta}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:BESQflow of arXiv:2411.04773, 'Meeting of squared Bessel flow lines and application to the skew Brownian motion'] Let $\delta \in {\mathbb R}$.  We call ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow  driven by $\mathcal W$ a collection ${\mathcal S}$ of continuous processes $({\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a),\, x\ge r)_{r\in {\mathbb R},a\ge 0}$ such that: 
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item
for each $(a,r)\in {\mathbb R}_+\times {\mathbb R}$, the process $({\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a),\, x\ge r)$ is almost surely the strong solution of the following SDE  
\begin{equation}
{\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a) = 
a + 2 \int_r^x  {\mathcal W}([0,{\mathcal S}_{r,s}(a)], \, \mathrm{d} s) + 
\delta (x-r) 
,\, x\ge r
\end{equation}
 and which, in the case $\delta<0$, is absorbed when hitting $0$.
 \item Almost surely,
 \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
 \item for all $r\in {\mathbb R}$ and $a\ge 0$, $ {\mathcal S}_{r,r}(a)=a$,
 \item for all $r\le x$, $a\mapsto  {\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a)$ is c\`adl\`ag,
 \item (Perfect flow property) for any $r\le x \le y$ and $a\ge 0$, $\mathcal S_{r,y}(a)=\mathcal S_{x,y}\circ \mathcal S_{r,x}(a)$. 
\end{enumerate} 
\end{enumerate}

We call killed ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow driven by $\mathcal W$ the flow obtained from the ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow by absorbing at $0$ the flow line $\mathcal S_{r,\cdot}(a)$ at time $\inf\{x>r\,:\,\mathcal S_{r,x}(a)=0\}$. 

We call general ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow  a  ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow or a  killed ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow.
title: Definition def:BESQflow of arXiv:2411.04773

[Corollary positive condition for CONTINUOUS of arXiv:2605.02226, 'Finitely Dependent Processes on Subshifts'] Let $ \mathcal{R}$ be a collection of boxes in $ \mathbb{R}^d$ with integer sidelengths such that for every partition $\mathcal{R}=A_1\sqcup\dots\sqcup A_d$, there is $1\le j\le d$ such that

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.23960, 'Learning from Uncertainty-dependent Missing Labels for Semi-supervised Classification'] Let \((Y,Z)\) have joint density \(p_\theta(Y,Z)\), and let
\(M\in\{0,1\}\) denote the label-missingness indicator, with \(M=1\) if the
label is missing and \(M=0\) if it is observed. Suppose that
\[
  M\perp Z\mid Y
\]
and that the missingness mechanism has the form
\[
  r_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)
  =
  \Pr(M=1\mid Y;\theta,\boldsymbol\xi)
  =
  h\{\eta_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)\},
\]
where \(h\) is a smooth inverse link function and
\(\eta_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)\) may depend on \(\theta\). Then, for known
\(\boldsymbol\xi\), the observed-data Fisher information for \(\theta\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}(\theta)
  =
  \mathcal I_{CC}(\theta)
  -
  \mathcal I_{CC}^{(\mathrm{miss},r)}(\theta,\boldsymbol\xi)
  +
  \mathcal I_{\mathrm{mech}}(\theta,\boldsymbol\xi).

\end{equation}
Equivalently,
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}(\theta)
  =
  \mathcal I_{UC}(\theta)
  +
  E_\theta\!\left[
    \{1-r_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)\}
    \operatorname{Var}_\theta\{S_c(Y,Z;\theta)\mid Y\}
  \right]
  +
  \mathcal I_{\mathrm{mech}}(\theta,\boldsymbol\xi).

\end{equation}
The mechanism-curvature term is positive semidefinite. For the logistic inverse
link,
\[
  w_h\{\eta_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)\}
  =
  r_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)
  \{1-r_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)\}.
\]
If \(r_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)\equiv\gamma\), then
\[
  \mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}(\theta)
  =
  \mathcal I_{CC}(\theta)
  -
  \gamma\,\mathcal I_{CC}^{(\mathrm{miss})}(\theta)
  +
  \mathcal I_{\mathrm{mech}}(\theta,\boldsymbol\xi).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.23960

[Theorem th:sec-order-main of arXiv:2412.09290, 'Asymptotics of Harish-Chandra transform and infinitesimal freeness'] Let $A$ be a random Hermitian matrix of size $N$ and assume that for every
  finite $r$ one has
  \begin{equation} 
  \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} N^2 \left( \frac{1}{N} \log \mathbb{E}[H
     \text{} C (x_1, \ldots, x_r, 0^{N - r} ; \lambda_1 (A), \ldots, \lambda_N
     (A))] - \sum_{i = 1}^r \Psi (x_i) - \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i = 1}^r \Phi (x_i)
     \right) = \sum_{i = 1}^r \mathrm{T} (x_i), 
     \end{equation} 
  where $\Psi, \Phi, \mathrm{T}$ are smooth functions in a complex neighborhood of $0$ and
  the above convergence is uniform in a complex neighborhood of $0^r$. Then the $1 /
  N^2$ correction of the average empirical distribution of $N^{- 1} \cdot A$
  is given by
  \[ \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} N^2 \left( \frac{1}{N^{k + 1}}
     \mathbb{E}[\ensuremath{\operatorname{Tr}} (A^k)] -\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_k - \frac{1}{N}
     \ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}'_k \right) =\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}''_k
     +\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\nu}}''_k, \]
  where $(\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}, (\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}'_k)_{k \in
  \mathbb{N}}$ are given by ((topg of the paper)),((G of the paper)) respectively. The sequences
  $(\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}''_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}, (\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\nu}}''_k)_{k \in
  \mathbb{N}}$ are given by
  \[ \ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}''_k = \sum_{m = 0}^{k - 1} \frac{k!}{m! (m + 1) ! (k -
     m - 1) !}  \left. \frac{\mathrm{d}^m}{\mathrm{d} x^m} ((\Psi' (x))^{k - m - 1}
     \mathrm{T}' (x)) \right|_{x = 0} \]
  \begin{equation}
    \text{{\hspace{10em}}} + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{m = 0}^{k - 2} \frac{k!}{m! (m
    + 1) ! (k - m - 2) !}  \left. \frac{\mathrm{d}^m}{\mathrm{d} x^m} ((\Psi'
    (x))^{k - m - 2} (\Phi' (x))^2) \right|_{x = 0} 
  \end{equation}
  and
  \[ \ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\nu}}''_k = \frac{1}{24} \sum_{m = 0}^{k - 3} \frac{k!}{m! (m
     + 1) ! (k - m - 3) !}  \left. \frac{\mathrm{d}^m}{\mathrm{d} x^m} ((\Psi'
     (x))^{k - m - 3} \Psi''' (x)) \right|_{x = 0} \]
  \[ \text{{\hspace{4em}}} + \frac{1}{12} \sum_{m = 0}^{k - 3} \frac{k!}{m! (m
     + 2) ! (k - m - 3) !}  \left. \frac{\mathrm{d}^m}{\mathrm{d} x^m} ((\Psi'
     (x))^{k - m - 3} \Psi''' (x)) \right|_{x = 0} \]
  \begin{equation}
    \text{{\hspace{10em}}} + \frac{1}{12} \sum_{m = 0}^{k - 4} \frac{k!}{m! (m
    + 2) ! (k - m - 4) !}  \left. \frac{\mathrm{d}^m}{\mathrm{d} x^m} ((\Psi'
    (x))^{k - m - 4} (\Psi'' (x))^2) \right|_{x = 0} . 
  \end{equation}

[Theorem theo:main of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions on co-evolutionary networks'] Assume that the interaction kernel \(K\) and the plasticity function \(\Gamma\) satisfy Assumptions
	(assump:interaction-kernel of the paper) and (assump:plasticity-function of the paper). Let 
	\((X_{i}^N,w_{ij}^N)_{1\leq i,j\leq N}\) be the unique strong
	solution to the discrete system (equation eq:multi-agent-discrete of the paper), starting from independent initial states and
	weights \((X_{i,0}^N,w_{ij,0}^N)_{1\leq i,j\leq N}\) that satisfy Assumptions (assump:weights of the paper) and
	(assump:initial-data of the paper). Define the (random) extended empirical measure for the states and empirical probability-graphon for the weights:
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
	\mu^{N,\xi}_{[0,t]} &:= \sum_{i=1}^{N} \mathds{1}_{I_i^N}(\xi) \delta_{X_{i,[0,t]}^N}, \quad && t\in [0,T],\,\xi\in [0,1], \\

	\end{aligned}

[Defn of arXiv:2412.04527, 'Critical Drift for Brownian Bees and a Reflected Brownian Motion Invariance Principle'] Let $A=(a_1,\ldots,a_m)\in \mathbb{R}^m$ and $B=(b_1,\ldots, b_n)\in \mathbb{R}^n$. Then $A\preccurlyeq B$ (we say that ``$A$ lies to the left of $B$'', or ``$A$ is less than $B$ in the sense of $\preccurlyeq$'') if and only if
$$|\{i:a_i \geq c\}| \leq |\{i: b_i \geq c\}| \; \forall c\in \mathbb{R}.$$
When $m=n$, this means that the empirical cumulative distribution functions are pointwise ordered.

[Theorem eq:coeffs-assumption of arXiv:2602.14998, 'Random geometric graphs with smooth kernels: sharp detection threshold and a spectral conj'] Suppose that the standardized kernel
\[
\kappa(t)
\triangleq
\frac{K(t)-p}{\sqrt{p(1-p)}} 
\]
is a polynomial $\kappa(t) = \sum_{\ell=0}^L b_\ell t^\ell$, where the coefficients satisfy 
\begin{equation}
|b_\ell| \le \frac{B r^{\ell}}{\sqrt{\ell!}} \ \forall \, 1 \le \ell \le L, 
\quad |b_0| \le \frac{B r^2}{d} ,
    
\end{equation}
for some $B>0$.
Assume that 
$$d \gg n^{3/4} r^{3/2}, $$
$n^{-1/2 + \epsilon} \le r \le d^{1/3 - \epsilon}$, and $L \le d^{1/6 - \epsilon}$.

Then ${\rm TV}(P_A, Q_A) = o(1)$.

In the special case of linear kernel, i.e., $\kappa(t) = b_1 t$, if $d \gg n^{3/4} b_1^{3/2}$ 

and $b_1\gtrsim n^{-1/2} \log n$, then ${\rm TV}(P_A, Q_A) = o(1)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem eq:coeffs-assumption of arXiv:2602.14998

[Prop 13 ({\cite[Theorem 2.6) of arXiv:2608.30415, 'On generalized complex projective product spaces'] {Naskar}}]
Let $F\hookrightarrow{} E\stackrel{p}{\longrightarrow} B$ be a fibre bundle, where  $F$, $E$ and $B$ are path-connected, Hausdorﬀ, second countable topological spaces. Suppose that $E$ is completely normal. 
Let $\{U_1,\dots,U_{m} \}$ be a categorical cover of $B$
such that $\phi_i \colon \overline{p^{-1}(U_i)}\to \overline{U_i}\times F$ is a homeomorphism for $1\leq i\leq m$. Moreover, there is a categorical cover  $\{V_1,\dots,V_{n}\}$ of $F$ such that $(U_{i'}\cap U_i)\times V_j$ are invariant under $\phi_{i'}\phi_{i}^{-1}$ for all $\{i,i'\}\subseteq \{1,\dots,m\}$ and $j\in\{1,\dots,n\}$. Then $\mathrm{cat}(E)\leq \mathrm{cat}(F)+\mathrm{cat}(B)-1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma p:mppmixcl_double of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Fix $p,q \in \mathbb{N}$ and $r \in (0, \infty)$.
Assume that we are given
\begin{enumerate}[wide,label=(\roman*),labelindent=0pt,partopsep=0pt,topsep=0pt,parsep=0pt]
\item  a marking function $\xi: \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K} \times \mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K}} \to \mathbb{K}'$, and
\item  
a marked point process $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{K}$ having  $\mathbb{B} $-mixing  correlations
as in  Definition (B-omega-mixing of the paper)(Bmixing of the paper)
with correlation decay functions $\omega_{k}(s) = C_k  \phi(s)$, $k \in \mathbb{N}$, 
where $(C_k)_{k \geq 1}$ is a non-decreasing sequence such that for some fixed $\epsilon \in (0,1)$, we have

\begin{equation}  
\sum_{l = 1}^{\infty}  \frac{ ({w}_0(1 + \epsilon)\kappa_0^{1 + \epsilon})^l }{l!} C_{l + p + q}  < \infty,
\end{equation}

with  ${w}_0= 4(p+q)\theta_d r^d$ and where $\kappa_0 = \max\{1, \sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}\rho^{(1)}(x)\}$ is related to the ground process $\mathcal{P}$.
\end{enumerate}

\vskip.2cm
Then for  all $f \in \mathbb{B} ((\mathbb{K}')^p),$   $g \in \mathbb{B} ((\mathbb{K}')^q)$ and for almost all $\bk x1{p+q}\in\mathbb{R}^{d(p+q)}$ such that $s:=d(\bk x1p,\bk x{p+1}{p+q}) >4r$ we have

\begin{align} \nonumber
& \Big| \mathbb {E} _{\bk x1{p+q}}[f(\bk{{\xi}^{\cup(r)}}{1}{p}(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}}))g(\bk{{\xi}^{\cup(r)}}{p+1}{p+q}(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}}))]\rho^{(p+q)}(\bk x1{p+q})  \\
&  \qquad - \,
\mathbb {E} _{\bk x1p}[f(\bk{{\xi}^{\cup(r)}}{1}{p}(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}}))] \rho^{(p)}(\bk x1{p}) \; \mathbb {E} _{\bk x{p+1}{p+q}}[g(\bk{{\xi}^{\cup(r)}}{p+1}{p+q}(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}}))]\rho^{(q)}(\bk x{p+1}{p+q}) \Big|  \nonumber \\
& \le 
\phi( \frac{s}{2})\sum_{l=1}^\infty \frac{w_0^l}{l!}  C_{l+p+q}
=:\phi( \frac{s}{2})\hat{C}_{p+q}<\infty.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: A mixing correlation bound for union-restricted marks

Let M>=1 finite linear-regression tasks have matrices X_m in R^(n_m by d) and labels y_m. Suppose X_m*w_star=y_m for every m, put R=max_m||X_m||_2>0, and define L(w;m)=||X_m*w-y_m||^2/2 and L(w)=M^(-1)*sum_m L(w;m). Initialize w_0=0 and sample tau_1,...,tau_k independently and uniformly from{1,...,M}, with replacement. Scheme1 performs the exact update w_t=argmin_w {L(w;tau_t)+(lambda_t/2)*||w-w_(t-1)||^2}. Write D2=||w_0-w_star||^2. Use the same coefficient lambda_t=lambda>0 in every round, and set a=R^2/(R^2+lambda), so0<a<1. For each integer k>=1, E L(w_k)<=e*D2*R^2/[2*a*(2-a)*k^(1-a*(1-a/4))]. The expectation is over the random task ordering and the loss averages over the full collection of M tasks.
Finite jointly realizable linear tasks; R is the largest task-matrix operator norm and R>0.
Independent uniform task indices sampled with replacement; exact Scheme1 updates; w_0=0.
The coefficient lambda>0 stays fixed within the entire run.

Let $X = Z\Sigma^{1/2}$ be $n \times p$ with $Z$ having i.i.d. entries of mean $0$ and variance $1$, $\Sigma$ positive semidefinite, and let $S = \frac{1}{n}X^T X$. Assume $p/n \to c \in (0, \infty)$ and that the empirical spectral distribution of $\Sigma$ converges weakly to a probability measure $H$ on $[0, \infty)$. Then almost surely the empirical spectral distribution of $S$ converges weakly to a nonrandom probability measure $F = F^{c, H}$, characterised as follows: with $\underline F = (1 - c)\delta_0 + cF$ (the limiting spectral distribution of the $n \times n$ companion $\frac{1}{n}XX^T$) and $\underline m(z) = \int \frac{d\underline F(t)}{t - z} = -\frac{1 - c}{z} + c\,m_F(z)$, for every $z \in \mathbb{C}^+$ the value $\underline m(z)$ is the unique solution in $\mathbb{C}^+$ of $$z = -\frac{1}{\underline m} + c\int \frac{\tau\, dH(\tau)}{1 + \tau\,\underline m}.$$ Equivalently, $m_F$ solves $m_F(z) = \int \frac{dH(\tau)}{\tau\,(1 - c - c z\, m_F(z)) - z}$. For $H = \delta_1$ (identity population covariance) the equation reduces to the quadratic $z\,\underline m^2 + (z + 1 - c)\,\underline m + 1 = 0$ for the companion transform (equivalently $c z\, m_F^2 + (z - 1 + c)\, m_F + 1 = 0$ for $m_F$ itself), whose solution is the Stieltjes transform of the Marchenko-Pastur law with ratio $c$; the support of $F$ and its density are read off by Stieltjes inversion, and the density is analytic inside the support and vanishes like a square root at each edge of the support other than $0$: for $c = 1$ the left edge is the hard edge $0$, where the density blows up like $x^{-1/2}$, and for $c > 1$ the measure $F$ also carries an atom of mass $1 - 1/c$ at $0$.
entries of Z i.i.d., mean zero, variance one (finite second moment suffices for the almost-sure convergence in the Bai-Silverstein form)
the spectral distribution of Sigma converges weakly to H; p/n -> c in (0, infinity)
Sigma and Z independent (Sigma may be random)

Let $\mathcal{Y} = (\mathsf{X}, \mathsf{W})$ be a state-weight structure on $(\Omega, \mathcal{A}, \pi)$ with $\mathsf{X} \in L^2(\Omega)$ and $\mathsf{W} \in L^\infty(\Omega \times \Omega)$. Let $\bm{\xi}_1, \dots, \bm{\xi}_N$ be independent latent variables whose laws $\pi_i$ satisfy $\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N \pi_i = \pi$. Let $\bm{\mathcal{Y}}_N = ((\mathsf{X}(\bm{\xi}_i))_{i \in [N]}, (\mathsf{W}(\bm{\xi}_i, \bm{\xi}_j))_{i, j \in [N]})$ be the sampled structure. Then there exists a universal constant $C > 0$ such that $\mathbb{E}[ \delta_{W_1, \square}(\bm{\mathcal{Y}}_N, \mathcal{Y}) ] \le \frac{C (\|\mathsf{X}\|_{L^2} + \|\mathsf{W}\|_{L^\infty})}{\sqrt{\log N}}$.
\mathsf{X} \in L^2(\Omega)
\mathsf{W} \in L^\infty(\Omega \times \Omega)
\frac{1}{N} \sum \pi_i = \pi

Own-work draft, T419-C029 v2, proof (unaudited), novelty unresolved. Fix r>=1, m,p>=r, 0<mu<=1 and 0<rho<1. For each real rank-r target Delta with largest singular value1 and all positive singular values >=mu, there exist a finite deterministic S=S(r,p,mu,rho) and a deterministic step eta(s)>0, constant along a trajectory and independent of requested accuracy, such that with probability >=1-rho over iid N(0,1) G in R^(r by p), ordinary simultaneous squared-loss GD from B0=0,A0=sG converges to Delta simultaneously for every s>=S. After a deterministic entry count N(s), the proof gives ||B_k A_k-Delta||F<=sqrt(r) exp[-eta(s)mu^2(k-N)/(32K(s))], K(s)=sqrt(r)(s^2(4rp/rho)+1+4sqrt(r)). The uniform spectral entry-time quantile is finite by Dini's theorem. That quantile is nonconstructive, so this does not provide an explicit condition-number hitting-time bound. The reduced-flow saddle exclusion uses a local stable-center theorem.
Noiseless exact-rank-r population Frobenius squared loss
Ordinary simultaneous factor GD, B0=0,A0=sG
Largest target singular value normalized1; arbitrary positive-spectrum condition number <=1/mu
Sufficiently large s; steps may be extremely small
Unaudited C014 boundedness/descent and C024 ordinary-operator contraction
Finite but nonconstructive reduced-flow entry quantile; no middle-scale or positive-noise statement

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:8213e9c69f82336711b29b4ecf778031a404ae6da57b57e1990726e83b449871","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/82/8213e9c69f82336711b29b4ecf778031a404ae6da57b57e1990726e83b449871.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:a18d33b892138867bf1ab0b6a4c877f2103aaa17e059e56ddef2993b655674cc","bundle_entry_key":"lora-large","bundle_id":"population.t419-large-scale-slow-flow-and-primary-scopes-015","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"matrix factorization and gradient dynamics","draft":"w705/bundle_015.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.lowrank:lora-large-gaussian-scale-arbitrary-spectrum-slow-flow-bridge","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T419-C029 v2: arbitrary spectra at sufficiently large Gaussian scales

Kind: moved. Target1. Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty unresolved.

This is a qualitative large-scale extension with a rigorously defined but nonconstructive uniform entry-time quantile. It does **not** supply the target's requested explicit condition-number complexity. It depends on the unaudited C014 and C024. The hardest remaining quantitative piece is an effective bound on T below. No independent audit or full-target solution is claimed.

## Statement and deterministic quantities

Let Delta be a real m-by-p matrix of exact rank r>=1, m,p>=r, with largest singular value1 and smallest positive singular value at least mu, 0<mu<=1. Let 0<rho<1. There are finite positive deterministic numbers S=S(r,p,mu,rho) and a positive step function eta(s), independent of requested accuracy, such that with probability at least1-rho over a single r-by-p standard Gaussian G, **simultaneously for every s>=S**, ordinary simultaneous population GD from B0=0,A0=sG converges to Delta. The step eta(s) is constant along each trajectory. A hitting-time bound is given below in terms of the implicit T.

Define a= (rho/4)/(10 r^(3/2)), b=sqrt(4rp/rho), m0=a^2 and

v=sqrt(2)b, u=sqrt(2)b/m0, R=sqrt(r)+uv, w=uR,
alpha=1/m0+2v^2/m0^2, c=1+2uv, L=c alpha+u^2.

For each spectrum lambda in [mu,1]^r, put H_lambda=diag(lambda_1^2,...,lambda_r^2,0,...,0) on R^p. For full-row-rank G set M=GG^T and let Y'=M^(-1)Y H_lambda(I-Y^TY), Y(0)=M^(-1/2)G. Define

F_j(lambda)=E_G tr[H_lambda(I-Y(j)^TY(j))].

Let T be the least positive integer for which sup_lambda F_T(lambda)<=rho mu^2/64. Section1 proves that T exists. This is a definition of a finite deterministic quantile, **not a numerical estimate or an effective formula for T**.

Set C_V=c exp(LT)(u+alpha wT)/m0 and
C_E=v alpha w/m0+(alpha v+u)C_V.
Let

epsilon0=min{1,m0^2/2,mu/(8C_E), m0 T/log(max{e,8vu/mu})},
S=epsilon0^(-1/4).

For s>=S put t*=s^2 T,
K=sqrt(r)(s^2 b^2+1+4sqrt(r)),
Z=s v+u/s, R0=Z+1, M_f=(sqrt(r)+R0^2)R0,
L_f=3R0^2+1, zeta=min{1/2,mu/(4R0)}, and

h=min{1/(1+r),1/(6K+1),1/[2(K+sqrt(r))],
      2zeta/[M_f(exp(L_f t*)-1)]}.

Choose N=ceil(t*/h)>=1 and eta(s)=t*/N. These are mathematical real-valued definitions; no floating-point computation of the enormous exponentials is proposed.

On the probability event specified below, all k>=N obey

||B_k A_k-Delta||F <= sqrt(r) exp[-eta(s) mu^2 (k-N)/(32K)].

Thus N+ceil((32K/[eta(s)mu^2]) max{0,log(sqrt(r)/eps)}) suffices. The scale, step and time depend on the implicit T and can be extremely poor. For a target of largest singular value d>0, apply this statement to Delta/d, scale s/sqrt(d), step d eta_original and tolerance eps/d.

## 1. Reduced flow: metric, convergence, and the uniform quantile

The row-Stiefel manifold St={Y:YY^T=I_r} is compact and smooth. Fix SPD M. Its metric g_M(X,Z)=tr(X^T M Z) is positive definite. For f(Y)=.5trH-.5tr(Y H Y^T), the vector field -grad_M f=M^(-1)Y H(I-P), P=Y^TY. It is tangent because Y'Y^T=0. To verify the metric formula, for tangent Z the matrix ZY^T is skew symmetric and Y H Y^T is symmetric; hence tr(Y H Y^T ZY^T)=0. This removes precisely the P term when evaluating g_M(-grad f,Z)=-df[Z]. It follows that f decreases and f'=-||grad_M f||_M^2.

Critical row spaces are exactly the H-invariant r-planes. Decompose R^p into the finitely many distinct eigenspaces of H. A critical component chooses a dimension in each eigenspace with total r, together with an orthonormal row frame. There are finitely many compact smooth components. At a critical frame, choose coordinates diagonalizing H and separating selected from unselected directions. Vertical frame rotations have zero Hessian. A horizontal rotation from a selected eigenvector of eigenvalue h_i to an unselected eigenvector of eigenvalue h_j has second variation h_i-h_j. Equal-eigenvalue rotations and vertical rotations are exactly the tangent space of the critical component; all remaining normal coefficients are nonzero. Thus f is Morse-Bott, including repeated positive eigenvalues. A positive metric changes neither the Hessian kernel nor its inertia.

For completeness, the needed convergence consequence follows locally rather than being assumed for arbitrary smooth functions. Compactness and the energy identity imply grad f tends to zero: its squared norm is integrable, and its derivative is uniformly bounded on compact St; separated positive-height peaks would contradict integrability. Every cluster point is critical. Near a compact Morse-Bott component C, tubular coordinates and the nonsingular normal Hessian give |f-f(C)|<=C1 dist(Y,C)^2 and ||grad_M f||_M>=C2 dist(Y,C). These follow by Taylor expansion, the uniform least normal Hessian singular value, and a sufficiently small tubular neighborhood. The finitely many components and finitely many critical values imply the trajectory eventually remains in the neighborhood of one component with value f_infty. Consequently ||grad_M f||_M>=c sqrt(f-f_infty). Differentiating sqrt(f-f_infty) shows that the remaining trajectory length is finite. If f=f_infty is reached then the energy identity makes the trajectory stationary. In all cases Y(t) converges to a single critical point.

If that point is nonglobal, its selected r-plane omits a positive eigendirection and contains a zero eigendirection: H has exactly r positive eigenvalues. The corresponding second variation is negative. The time-one flow map is a smooth diffeomorphism of compact St, with an eigenvalue >1 at every nonglobal critical point. Apply the local stable-center manifold theorem in a chart: there are a neighborhood U_x and a disk W_x of positive codimension containing every orbit that stays in U_x at all nonnegative integer times. The source form is Lee–Simchowitz–Jordan–Recht, arXiv1602.04915, Theorem4.4, PDF p.5 (it applies to local diffeomorphisms, not just GD). Take smaller open neighborhoods V_x with closure inside U_x and a countable subcover of the nonglobal critical set. Any orbit converging to a point in V_x eventually stays in U_x and therefore belongs to some inverse iterate of W_x. The countable union over neighborhoods and entry integers is volume-null. This addresses uncountably many critical points; no countability assumption on the points is used. Thus a full-density initial frame converges to the global row space range(H) almost surely.

The polar map G <-> (M,Y) with G=M^(1/2)Y is a smooth diffeomorphism from full-row-rank r-by-p matrices to SPD_r times St (also when p=r, using its two frame components). The Gaussian law has a positive smooth density. Smooth coordinate changes and Fubini therefore give almost-sure convergence for the joint Gaussian polar initialization, even though M and the flow are linked. It is unnecessary to assert independence. Rank-deficient G has probability zero.

Hence F_j(lambda) tends to zero for each lambda. It is nonincreasing in j and bounded by trH<=r. Continuous dependence of the compact smooth reduced flow on lambda, for each full-rank G, and dominated convergence show that F_j is continuous on compact [mu,1]^r. Dini's theorem yields uniform convergence. Explicitly, for any positive threshold the nested open sets {lambda:F_j(lambda)<threshold} cover the spectral cube; a finite subcover and nesting give a single covering index. This proves the existence of T as defined above. The case p=r has identically zero reduced residual and is included.

Orthogonal invariance of Gaussian G shows that the same T works for arbitrary target singular vectors. Output dimension does not enter H. Markov's inequality gives probability at most rho/4 that the reduced residual squared at T exceeds mu^2/16.

## 2. Uniform finite-time tracking of the true gradient flow

For actual population gradient flow write B=U/s,A=sV, epsilon=s^(-4), theta=t/s^2. Exactly

epsilon U'=(Delta-UV)V^T, V'=U^T(Delta-UV),
VV^T-epsilon U^TU=GG^T.

On the Gaussian event lambda_min(GG^T)>=m0, ||G||F<=b, let epsilon<=m0^2/2. The inward bound

(epsilon/2)(||U||F^2)' <= ||U||F sqrt(b^2+epsilon||U||F^2)-m0||U||F^2

shows ||U||F<=u from U0=0, because at u the right side is <=0. A first-crossing argument, or an arbitrarily enlarged barrier followed by a limit, handles equality. The imbalance then gives ||V||F<=v and VV^T>=m0 I. These bounds preclude finite-time escape. The equilibrium U_*(V)=Delta V^T(VV^T)^(-1) also has norm <=u, and ||V'||F<=w.

On this bounded full-row-rank domain, direct inverse-difference algebra gives ||U_*(V1)-U_*(V2)||F<=alpha||V1-V2||F; this does not require their intervening straight segment to remain full rank. The derivative bound along actual V is the same. For W=U-U_*(V),

epsilon W'=-W(VV^T)-epsilon DU_*(V)[V'],
||W(theta)||F <= u exp(-m0 theta/epsilon)+epsilon alpha w/m0.

The reduced vector field F(V)=U_*^T(Delta-U_*V) is L-Lipschitz between any two points in this domain. Indeed, dependence on U has constant c=1+2uv, dependence on V for fixed U has constant u^2, and the equilibrium map has constant alpha. Its discrepancy from the actual V field is at most c||W||F. Gronwall gives, on [0,T],

||V_actual(theta)-V_reduced(theta)||F <= epsilon C_V.

The reduced V has constant Gram GG^T and hence lies in the same domain. The product error at T is bounded by

||U_actual V_actual-U_*(V_reduced)V_reduced||F
 <= vu exp(-m0 T/epsilon)+epsilon C_E.

The definition of epsilon0 makes the two terms <=mu/8 each. Thus, when the reduced residual at T is <=mu/4, the actual gradient-flow residual at physical time t*=s^2 T is <=mu/2.

## 3. Transfer to ordinary simultaneous GD and a linear tail

The continuous factor-pair norm up to t* is at most Z. In the ball of radius R0=Z+1, the gradient vector field has norm <=M_f and Lipschitz constant <=L_f. The Hessian bound follows from

d^2 loss[(dB,dA)] = ||dB A+B dA||F^2+2<BA-Delta,dB dA>,

whose absolute value is <=(1.5 R0^2+1)||(dB,dA)||^2; L_f is a conservative bound. The usual local Euler remainder is <=eta^2 L_f M_f/2. Iterating the error recursion gives <=eta M_f(exp(L_f t*)-1)/2 at every grid point up to N, since N eta=t*. A bootstrap keeps every discrete point in the radius-R0 ball: the upper bound is at most zeta<=1/2, leaving distance to its boundary. This is an estimate for ordinary simultaneous GD, with no splitting or preconditioning.

At time N the product error relative to the flow is at most (Z+zeta/2)zeta<R0 zeta<=mu/4. Hence ||B_N A_N-Delta||op<=3mu/4.

C014, with q0<=r/2 and initial imbalance Frobenius norm <=s^2 b^2, gives ||A_k||F^2+||B_k||F^2<=K and residual Frobenius norm <=sqrt(r) for every k. The chosen eta meets all of its step conditions. It also ensures eta(||residual||op+||B||op^2+||A||op^2)<=1/2, so C024 makes the ordinary residual operator norm nonincreasing from N onward.

The known output-span invariance (credited to LoRA-One in C019) gives B_k=U_D R_k, with U_D an orthonormal basis of range(Delta), and R_k square r-by-r. Weyl's inequality on the reduced r-by-p product yields sigma_min(R_k A_k)>=mu/4. Thus sigma_min(R_k)>=mu/(4sqrt(K)). Since the error also lies in range(U_D), the A-gradient satisfies ||grad_A loss||F^2>=mu^2||error||F^2/(16K). C014 descent gives the squared-error contraction 1-eta mu^2/(16K), establishing the claimed tail.

Finally, the elementary Gaussian event from C004 gives sigma_min(G_first_r_columns)>=a with failure at most rho/4 and ||G||F<=b with failure at most rho/4. Since GG^T dominates the first-block Gram matrix, its least eigenvalue is >=m0. Combine these two events with the reduced residual event by a union bound: total failure <=3rho/4<rho. No independence product is used. The event is independent of s, making the statement simultaneous over s>=S.

## Provenance and limitations

The stable-center theorem is classical; Lee et al. Theorem4.4 is the inspected primary locator. The critical-manifold geometry and elementary finite-time bounds are written above rather than imported from an unchecked generic convergence assertion. Dini's theorem and change of smooth coordinates are classical compactness/measure facts. The singular perturbation is proved by the displayed energy and Gronwall estimates; no unverified Tikhonov theorem is needed.

This proof is unaudited. In particular, the reviewer should check the weighted metric identity, Morse-Bott critical-manifold argument, countable cover, uniform spectral Dini step, and tracking constants before relying on it. S and the entry count remain nonconstructive through T. body:
[Proposition prop:V of arXiv:2411.08018, 'Last passage percolation in hierarchical environments'] For all $n\ge1$ large enough such that ${M}\ge1$, there exist random sets of vertices
    \[
        \mathscr{V}^{(1)}\subset \mathscr{V}^{(2)}\subset \cdots\subset\mathscr{V}^{({M})}\subset\llbracket 0,n\rrbracket^2
    \]
    with the following properties.
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item  
        There exists an up-right directed lattice path from $(0,0)$ to $(n,n)$ that passes through every vertex in $\mathscr{V}^{({M})}$.
        Equivalently,  $\mathscr{V}^{({M})}$ is totally ordered with respect to $\prec$.
        \item  
        For all $\ell\in\llbracket1,{M}\rrbracket$, the set $\mathscr{V}^{(\ell)}\setminus\mathscr{V}^{(\ell-1)}$ consists entirely of vertices of scale $\ell{\zeta}$ (see Definition (def:kscale of the paper)).
        Here, we write $\mathscr{V}^{(0)} \coloneqq \bigl\{(0,0), (n,n)\bigr\}$.
        \item  There exists $c>0$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$,
        \[
            \mathbb{P}\left(
                \bigl|\mathscr{V}^{(\ell)}\setminus\mathscr{V}^{(\ell-1)}\bigr| \ge c\frac{2^{\ell{\zeta}}}{{\lambda}}\ \textup{for all}\ \ell\in\llbracket1,{M}\rrbracket
            \right)
            \ge 1-e^{-(\log n)^{97}}.
        \]
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Explicit model calculation and hypothesis obstruction Result: For an edgeless graph and fixed fugacity zeta>0, the stationary coordinates are independent Bernoulli(p), p=zeta/(1+zeta). Under rate-one refreshes and initial all ones, q_t=p+(1-p)*e^-t. A one-coordinate chi-square calculation gives (q_t-p)^2/[p*(1-p)] and hence full chi-square distance [1+((1-p)/p)*e^-2t]^N-1. An occupancy-sum Chebyshev lower bound matches the scale (log N)/2, yielding the familiar product cutoff. Check: The expression changes if one starts at all zeros, replacing (1-p)/p by p/(1-p); for fixed p both give the same leading time and bounded window. On a graph with edges the all-one configuration is inadmissible, so this is explicitly an edgeless baseline. Obstruction: Exclusion of adjacent particles creates long dependent update histories. Spectral independence and O(N log N) discrete-time mixing do not alone prove a vanishing relative window. No matching information-percolation or local-variance estimate in the full phase is established here.

body:
[Theorem 39 of arXiv:2604.09365, 'Cotlar martingale transforms and related singular integrals'] For $m=1, \cdots n$, set 
\begin{align}
Z^m=C_m*(M+iN) 
\end{align} 
and 
\begin{align}
Z=(Z^1, Z^2, \dots Z^n)\in \bC^n. 
\end{align}
$Z$ is a conformal martingale with the orthogonal property. Furthermore, the vector operator defined for $F:\R^d\to \bC$ by 
\[ 
\cB(d)F=\left(\cB_1(d)F, \dots, \cB_n(d)F\right)
\]
satisfies
\begin{align}
\|\cB(d)\|_{L^p(\R^d; \bC)}\leq 2(p^*-1), 
\quad 1<p<\infty. 
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

The output of Algorithm~\ref{alg:multi-horizon-sweep} satisfies

    \leq
    W_\star
    \min_{s\in\llbracket\ell\rrbracket}
      \delta(\mathcal O^{(s)})
    -g_\star\delta_k^*.

If at least one candidate is a $\rho$-approximation for weighted
$k$-means, so that
\[
    \min_{s\in\llbracket\ell\rrbracket}
      \delta(\mathcal O^{(s)})
    \leq\rho\delta_k^*,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
    F_\star(\widehat{\mathcal O}_\star)-F_{\star,k}^*
    \leq(\rho W_\star-g_\star)\delta_k^*.
    
\end{equation}

[Lemma of arXiv:2411.09075, 'Weak Poincar{\'e} Inequalities, Simulated Annealing, and Sampling from Spherical Spin Glas'] Let $\mu = \mu_0$ be a measure, and let $(\mu_t)_{t \in \Z_{\ge 0}}$ be a linear-tilt localization process defined by
    \[ \mu_{t+1}(x) = \mu_t(x) \left( 1 + \langle x-\mean(\mu_t) , Z_t\rangle \right) \]
    for some random variable $Z_t$ with $\E[Z_t | \mu_t] = 0$.
    Let $T > 0$ be an arbitrary stopping time and $0 \le K_t < 1$ for each $t \ge 0$, and consider the stopping time
    \[ \tau = T \land \inf_{t \ge 0} \left\{ \opnorm{\Cov(Z_t | \mu_t)^{1/2} \cdot \Cov(\mu_t) \cdot \Cov(Z_t | \mu_t)^{1/2}} \ge K_t \right\}. \]
    Then, for any function $\varphi$,
    \[ \frac{\E \Var_{\mu_{\tau}}[\varphi]}{\Var_{\mu}[\varphi]} \ge \prod_{t \ge 0} (1 - K_t). \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered lemma of arXiv:2411.09075, 'Weak Poincar{\'e} Inequalities, Simulated Annealing, and Sam'

A family \{X_i : i \in I\} of real-valued random variables is uniformly integrable if \lim_{M \to \infty} \sup_{i \in I} \mathbb{E}[|X_i| \mathbf{1}_{\{|X_i| > M\}}] = 0. body:
[Lem FixedPointsfsquared of arXiv:2603.17858, 'Decay of correlations and zeros for the hard-core model'] Let $d\in\mathbb{N}_{>0}$ and $\lambda>0$. Then $x_d(\lambda)$ is the unique fixed point of $f_{d,\lambda}$ in the interval $[-1,\infty]$ and:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item If $\lambda\le\lambda_{c}(d+1)$, then the entire interval $[-1,\infty]$
        lies in the basin of the attracting or parabolic fixed point $x_{d}(\lambda)$.
        \item If $\lambda>\lambda_{c}(d+1)$, then $f_{d,\lambda}$ has an attracting
        $2$-cycle $(x_{1},x_{2})=(x_{d,1}(\lambda),x_{d,2}(\lambda))\in(0,\lambda)^{2}$ (i.e. $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$
        are attracting fixed points of $f_{d,\lambda}^{2}$ with $f_{d,\lambda}(x_{1})=x_{2}$)
        and the entire interval $[-1,\infty]$ except the fixed point $x_{d}(\lambda)$
        lies inside the basin of the attracting cycle.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem FixedPointsfsquared of arXiv:2603.17858

[Proposition erasedmassdef of arXiv:2608.09856, '\bf Mass erasure on measured $\bbR$-trees,\\ applications to L\'evy forests'] Let $(T, d, \rho, \mu)$ be a rooted finitely measured Polish $\mathbb{R}$-tree and let $h \! \in \!  \mathbb{R}^*_+$. Then 
$\nu \! := \! \mathtt{P}_{T_{\! \mu, h}} \mu + h \varpi_{T_{\! \mu, h}}$ is the unique positive Borel measure on $T$ such that 
\begin{equation}

 \nu ( \theta_\sigma T) = \big( \mu (\theta_\sigma T)\!  -\! h \big)_{\! +} \; , \quad \sigma \! \in \!  T \; . 
 \end{equation}
Moreover, $\nu \! = \! \mathtt{P}_{T_{\! \mu, h+}} \mu + h \varpi_{T_{\! \mu, h+}}$, where we recall that $T_{\! \mu, h+}$ is the closure of $\, \bigcup_{h^\prime >h} T_{\! \mu , h^\prime} $. 

We call $\nu$ the \emph{$h$-erasure of $\mu$} and we use notation $\mathcal{E}_h \mu \! = \!   \nu$. 
We also adopt the convention ${\cal E}_0 \mu \! = \!  \mu$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition erasedmassdef of arXiv:2608.09856

[Proposition return probability of arXiv:2603.09008, 'On the statistics of random-to-top shuffles'] Let $W_{r,k}$ be the event that, after $r$ random-to-top shuffles, card $k$ is in position $k$, i.e. $k$ is a fixed point of the permutation corresponding to the shuffled deck. Then
\[
\mathbb{P}(W_{r,k})=\left(\frac{k-1}{n}\right)^r+\frac{\mathbb{P}(K_{r,n}\ge k)}{n},
\]
where $K_{r,n}$ is the number of occupied boxes when $r$ balls are thrown independently and uniformly into $n$ boxes.

[Lemma lem:hsupdif of arXiv:2507.08757, 'Strong existence and uniqueness of the tilt-indexed Busemann process in the planar corner '] \textup{[Jan-Ras-20-aop]}
A generalized Busemann function ${\widehat B} \in \widehat{\mathcal{K}}$ has the following properties: 
\begin{enumerate}[label={\rm(\alph*)}, ref={\rm\alph*}]   \itemsep=3pt  
\item $-\mathbf{h}({\widehat B})$ takes values in $\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U)$, $\widehat\mathbb{P}$-almost surely.
\item If $-\widehat\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{h}({\widehat B})]\in\partial\textup{g}(\xi)$ for some $\xi \in \mathcal U$, then $-\mathbf{h}({\widehat B})\in\partial\textup{g}(\xi)$ $\widehat\mathbb{P}$-almost surely.
\item If $-\widehat\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{h}({\widehat B})] \in\{\nabla \textup{g}(\xi+),\nabla\textup{g}(\xi-)\}$ for some $\xi \in \mathcal U$, then $\mathbf{h}({\widehat B}) = \widehat\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{h}({\widehat B})]$ $\widehat\mathbb{P}$-almost surely. \qedhere
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let Ω ⊂ R^n be open and u ∈ C(Ω). For x0 ∈ Ω define the superdifferential D^+u(x0) = { p ∈ R^n : limsup_{x→x0} ( u(x) - u(x0) - p·(x-x0) ) / |x - x0| ≤ 0 } and the subdifferential D^-u(x0) = { p : liminf_{x→x0} ( u(x) - u(x0) - p·(x-x0) ) / |x-x0| ≥ 0 }. Then: (a) p ∈ D^+u(x0) if and only if there exists φ ∈ C^1(Ω) with Dφ(x0) = p such that u - φ has a local maximum at x0; symmetrically for D^-u(x0) and local minima. (b) Hence, for continuous F, u is a viscosity subsolution of F(x,u,Du) = 0 iff F(x, u(x), p) ≤ 0 for every x ∈ Ω and every p ∈ D^+u(x), and a viscosity supersolution iff F(x,u(x),p) ≥ 0 for every x ∈ Ω and every p ∈ D^-u(x). (c) u is differentiable at x0 if and only if D^+u(x0) and D^-u(x0) are both nonempty, and in that case D^+u(x0) = D^-u(x0) = {Du(x0)}.

u continuous on Ω
F continuous on Ω × R × R^n (for part (b))

body:
[Thm 18 of arXiv:2609.00758, 'Deformations of Compact Calabi--Yau and Fano Varieties with Isolated Singularities'] Let $X,S$ be complex spaces and $X\to S$ a flat morphism of complex spaces with reduced fibres. Let $o\in S$ be a point such that the fibre $X_o$ over it has an isolated singularity $x.$ Then there exist, after making $X$ smaller if necessary, finitely many disjoint subsets $S_0,\dots,S_m\sb S$ with $S_0\sqcup\dots\sqcup S_m=S$ and such that the following hold. 

For every $i=0,\dots,m$ the stratum $S_i\sb S$ is a Zariski locally closed, non-singular and of pure dimension. We have $\dim S_0<\dots<\dim S_m;$ the first stratum $S_0$ contains the origin $o\in S$ and the last stratum $S_m\sb S$ is a Zariski open subset. For $i>0$ the closure of $S_i$ is equal to $S_0\sqcup\dots\sqcup S_{i-1}.$ For every $i$ there exists a good resolution of the projection $S_i\times_S X\to S_i.$

body:
[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2607.18862, 'Tamed Euler Schemes for Singular SDEs with Multiplicative L\'{e}vy Noise'] Assume that Conditions $\sH_\sigma^g$, $\sH_b$ and $\widehat{\sH}_\sigma^g$ hold. 
	Let $(X_t^n)_{t\in[0,1]}$ be the solution to Eq. \eqref{EulerAPP3.81}, and let $(X_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ be the solution to Eq. \eqref{EQU1}. 
	Let
	\ce
	\bar p\in(1,p)\cap\left(1,\frac{2}{d}\left(	p_0\wedge p\wedge \sqrt{pd)}	\right)\right),
	\qquad
	\theta\in(0,1).
	\de
	Assume further that
	\ce
	\varGamma_{0,\bar p}^{0,R}|g|,
	\ \varGamma_{1,\bar p}^{0,R}|g|,
	\in
	\mL_\infty^q([0,1]),
	\qquad
	\varGamma_{1,1}^{0,R}|g|
	\in
	\mL_p^q([0,1]).
	\de
	Define the jump-dependent constants
	\ce
	C_J^{(m)}
	:=
	\|\varGamma_{1,\bar p}^{0,R}|g|\|_{\mL_\infty^q([0,1])}^{\bar p}
	+
	\|\varGamma_{1,2}^{0,R}|g|\|_{\mL_\infty^q([0,1])}^{\bar p},
	\de
	and
	\ce
	C_J^{(c)}
	:=
	\|\varGamma_{1,1}^{0,R}|g|\|_{\mL_p^q([0,1])}^{\bar p}.
	\de
	
	If $\bar p\ge2$, set
	\ce
	\mathcal E_{B,n}
	:=
	\left(
	n^{-\alpha/2}
	+
	n^{-1/2}\log n
	\right)^{\bar p}
	+
	n^{-\alpha(1-\frac1q)},
	\de
	\ce
	\mathcal E_{J,m,n}
	:=
	C_J^{(m)}n^{-(1-\frac1q)},
	\qquad
	\mathcal E_{J,c,n}
	:=
	C_J^{(c)}n^{-(1-\frac1q)(1-\frac dp)},
	\de
	and
	\ce
	\mathcal E_n
	:=
	\mE |x_0-x_0^n|^{\bar p}
	+
	\big(\varpi_b^n(\bar p)\big)^{\bar p}
	+
	\mathcal E_{B,n}
	+
	\mathcal E_{J,m,n}
	+
	\mathcal E_{J,c,n}.
	\de
	Then there exists a finite positive constant
	\ce
	N=N(c_0,c_1,c_2,\alpha,\beta,\theta,p,q,p_0,q_0,\bar p,d)>0
	\de
	such that
	\begin{equation}
		\mE\left[
		\sup_{t\in[0,1]}|X_t^n-X_t|^{\theta\bar p}
		\right]
		\le
		N\mathcal E_n^\theta .
	\end{equation}
	
	If $1<\bar p<2$, set
	\ce
	\mathcal E_{B,n}^{<2}
	:=
	\left(
	n^{-\alpha/2}
	+
	n^{-1/2}\log n
	\right)^{\bar p}
	+
	n^{-\alpha(1-\frac1q)},
	\de
	\ce
	\mathcal E_{J,m,n}^{<2}
	:=
	C_J^{(m)}n^{-\bar p/2},
	\qquad
	\mathcal E_{J,c,n}^{<2}
	:=
	C_J^{(c)}n^{-\frac{\bar p}{2}(1-\frac dp)},
	\de
	and
	\ce
	\mathcal E_n^{<2}
	:=
	\mE |x_0-x_0^n|^{\bar p}
	+
	\big(\varpi_b^n(\bar p)\big)^{\bar p}
	+
	\mathcal E_{B,n}^{<2}
	+
	\mathcal E_{J,m,n}^{<2}
	+
	\mathcal E_{J,c,n}^{<2}.
	\de
	Then
	\begin{equation}
		\mE\left[
		\sup_{t\in[0,1]}|X_t^n-X_t|^{\theta\bar p}
		\right]
		\le
		N\left(\mathcal E_n^{<2}\right)^\theta .
	\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Thm RT<-->s-cycle of arXiv:2606.29829, ''] Let $s$ be an even integer satisfying $2<s\ll n$. Then a Boolean function is noise sensitive (respectively stable) with respect to the interchange process on $K_n$ if and only if it is noise sensitive (respectively stable) with respect to the continuous-time random walk on $S_n$ generated by all $s$-cycles. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Corollary 21 of arXiv:2608.26662, 'Boundary–Moment Universality and Curvature Corrections in Random Geometric Graphs on Riema'] As $r\downarrow0$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\E N_2(r)
=\binom{n}{3} r^{2d}\Bigg[&6A_2(d)\int_M f^3\,d\mathrm{vol}_g \\
&-6C_2(d)r^2
\left\{
\int_M f\|\grad f\|_g^2\,d\mathrm{vol}_g
+\frac16\int_M f^3\Scal_g\,d\mathrm{vol}_g
\right\}
+o(r^2)\Bigg].
\end{aligned}
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\E N_2(r)
={}&n^3r^{2d}\Bigg[A_2(d)\int_M f^3\,d\mathrm{vol}_g \\
&\hspace{4.5em}-C_2(d)r^2
\left\{
\int_M f\|\grad f\|_g^2\,d\mathrm{vol}_g
+\frac16\int_M f^3\Scal_g\,d\mathrm{vol}_g
\right\}
+o(r^2)\Bigg]\\
&+O(n^2r^{2d}).
\end{aligned}
\]

body:
[Theorem thm:harmonic of arXiv:2609.02155, 'Exact Limits of Random Projections for Preserving Geometry:\\ Distance Recovery, Nearest-N'] Let $P_L=G_L\cdots G_1$ be a chain of independent Gaussian stages
$G_\ell\in\mathbb{R}^{n_\ell\times n_{\ell-1}}$ with entries $N(0,1/n_\ell)$, where
$n_0=d$. Apply the chain to $Z\sim\mathcal N(0,2\sigma^2I_d)$. With correlation
taken jointly over $Z$ and the stages,
\[
\Corr^2\bigl(\left\lVertZ\right\rVert^2,\left\lVertP_LZ\right\rVert^2\bigr)
=\frac{2/d}{\prod_{\ell=0}^{L}(1+2/n_\ell)-1}
\]
at every finite size. A single stage of width $m$ therefore gives
$\Corr=\sqrt{m/(m+d+2)}$. For a typical sampled map,
\[
r_2(P_L^\top P_L)
=(1+o_{\mathbb P}(1))
\left(\sum_{\ell=0}^{L}\frac1{n_\ell}\right)^{-1}.
\]
For one stage, the deterministic equivalent is $(1/m+1/d)^{-1}$. The finite
ratio of moments is $md/(m+d+1)$ because $\E\tr M=d$ and
$\E\tr M^2=d(m+d+1)/m$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Gaussian chains

body:
[Lemma lem:zakexpr of arXiv:2609.00481, 'The frameset of the second-order B-spline along $ab=1/q$'] For $\gamma\in(0,1)$ and $x\in[0,1)$,
\begin{align}
    (Z_{1/b}Q_2)(x,\gamma) &= b^{-3/2}\Bigg[\frac{(b+x+\ell)\,\omega^{\ell} - 2x\, - (b-x-n)\,\omega^{n}}{1-\omega}+ \frac{\omega\,(\omega^{\ell} - 2 + \omega^{n})}{(1-\omega)^2}\Bigg], 
 \end{align}
where $\omega=e^{-2\pi i\gamma}$, and $\ell$ and $n$ are functions of $x$ given by
\[
    \ell(x) = \left\lceil -(x+b)\right\rceil, \qquad
    n(x) = \left\lceil b-x\right\rceil.
\]

[Lemma 29 of arXiv:2507.06186, '2507.06186'] Let $t>0$ and $x_1,x_2\in\mbb R^2$ be fixed.
Suppose that the pair $(Z_1,Z_2)$ is either $({_1}B^{x_1},{_2}B^{x_2})$
or $({_1}B^{x_1,x_1}_t,{_2}B^{x_2,x_2}_t)$.
Given a positive $\theta>0$,
let us denote the event
\[\mf O_{t,\theta}(Z_1,Z_2)=\left\{\inf_{(r_1,r_2)\in[0,t]^2}\|Z_1(r_1)-Z_2(r_2)\|\geq\theta\right\}.\]
Almost surely, $\al_t(Z_1,Z_2)\mbf 1_{\mf O_{t,\theta}(Z_1,Z_2)}=0.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own-work draft. Status: independently checked proof, T232-w704-C003 v2; reviewer urn:mb-agent:d6ca7a10ae76247b PASS, 21 Oct 2026. Deterministic 2x2 variational transport: along any nonzero balanced rank-one first path for C(P)=tr((P-M)Sigma(P-M)^T)/2, with invertible M and positive-definite Sigma and a nonzero critical endpoint, an independent variational vector spanning with the active vector a maximal J-null plane in orthogonal-graph component delta=sign det M asymptotically aligns with the next POSITIVE-growth residual eigenvector. Its normalized unstable projection tends to plus or minus one and log norm/t tends to s=sigma_1(G_endpoint)>0. If the first path converges exponentially, its exp(-s t) norm has a nonzero finite limit. The two positive origin singular modes automatically have this J-null orientation. Scope: No gap in the independently checked C003 v2 deterministic theorem. Finite-alpha matching and the complete nonlinear second-step claims are separate, still unaudited results. C003 alone is not an unconditional Gaussian second-step theorem. Novelty/priority remains unverified. Audit evidence: urn:mb-local:ed593d341268f44f and AUDIT_RECEIPTS.jsonl. The attached proof_text retains its historical pre-review status header verbatim; the current status is the independently checked v2 verdict recorded here. Brain ingestion is unverified.
Square input/output dimensions both two
Sigma positive definite; M invertible
Active rank-one balanced nonzero flow converges to a nonzero critical point
Independent solution of frozen-path variational ODE has zero J-norm and zero J-inner product with the active solution
Orthogonal-graph determinant is sign det M, as for the two positive origin modes
Exponential endpoint convergence needed only for a nonzero finite amplitude coefficient, not for limiting direction or growth exponent

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:aef446b599556efe6eade3db7749dcf36b97cd0a86b0b142ea77a1dcee3d2b33","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/ae/aef446b599556efe6eade3db7749dcf36b97cd0a86b0b142ea77a1dcee3d2b33.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:cdffb74e247ea38af9a95c8f87f6b93e9ec3c9eb3e821280b787574508c2e968","bundle_entry_key":"transport-orientation-two","bundle_id":"population.t232-conditional-endpoint-and-variational-transport-20261020","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"deep linear networks; saddle-to-saddle gradient flow","draft":"w704/bundle_002.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.deep_linear_networks:t232-square-two-null-plane-variational-transport","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T232 target 1: 2x2 deterministic variational transport avoids the bad branch

Rung: proof (unaudited), independent reviewer PASS not received. This is a deterministic variational transport statement; it is not a theorem about the full finite-alpha random trajectories.

## Precise theorem
Let Sigma be a positive-definite real 2-by-2 matrix and M an invertible real 2-by-2 target. Consider C(P)=tr((P-M)Sigma(P-M)^T)/2. Suppose a(t),b(t) in R^2 form a nonzero balanced rank-one trajectory on an interval [T,infinity),
  a'=-G(t)^T b,  b'=-G(t) a,  G(t)=(b(t)a(t)^T-M)Sigma,
  ||a(t)||=||b(t)||>0,
and converge to nonzero vectors a*,b* forming a critical point: G* a*=0, G*^T b*=0.

Let x(t)=(v(t);u(t)) be an independent solution of the frozen first-path variational equation
  v'=-G(t)u, u'=-G(t)^T v.
Put z(t)=(b(t);a(t)) and J=diag(I2,-I2). Assume at one finite time (and therefore all times):
  x^T J x=z^T J z=z^T J x=0,
  x,z are linearly independent,
and their two-plane is the graph v=O(t)u of an orthogonal map with determinant
  det O(t)=delta=sign det M.
Then G* has rank one with a positive singular value s. The transported vector satisfies
  x(t)/||x(t)|| -> sign(y(T)) (delta l_perp*; r_perp*)/sqrt(2),
where l*=b*/||b*||, r*=a*/||a*||, l_perp*=J2 l*, r_perp*=J2 r*, J2=[[0,-1],[1,0]]. The vector on the right is a unit POSITIVE-growth eigenvector of [[0,-G*],[-G*^T,0]], with eigenvalue s. In particular the normalized projection of x onto the next unstable direction tends to plus or minus one, not zero. Also log||x(t)||/t -> s.

If the active path approaches its endpoint exponentially, then exp(-s t)||x(t)|| tends to a finite strictly positive limit. More generally this conclusion holds when the scalar coefficient difference in Section 4 is absolutely integrable.

## Why the orientation assumption is the one supplied by the two positive origin modes
If this active path and variational solution extend to t->minus infinity, with leading terms proportional to exp(s1 t)(p1;q1) and exp(s2 t)(p2;q2), where s1>s2>0 and p_i,q_i are the two positive singular pairs of M Sigma, then the assumptions above follow automatically. Both solutions tend to zero, so the constant J-inner products are zero. They are independent because their leading singular directions are different. Their graph approaches [p1,p2][q1,q2]^T, whose determinant is sign det(M Sigma)=sign det M since Sigma is positive definite. This last statement is about these ideal variational solutions, not an assertion that the finite-alpha Gaussian remnant has already been approximated by them with a uniform error.

## 1. The preserved two-plane and its graph
Write H=[[0,G],[G^T,0]]. Then H^T J+JH=0, so differentiating any J-inner product of solutions of x'=-H(t)x gives zero. Independence is preserved by the invertible finite-time fundamental matrix (this use is only to preserve independence, not to infer any unstable projection).

A two-dimensional J-null plane has an injective projection onto its input R^2: if a vector on it has input zero, nullity gives ||output||^2=0, hence the vector is zero. Equal finite dimensions make that projection an isomorphism. Therefore the plane is a graph of a map O; nullity of every graph vector gives ||Ou||=||u||, so O is orthogonal. Its determinant is plus or minus one and is continuous in time, hence constant. The active vector lies on the plane, so O a=b.

## 2. An exact moving-frame scalar equation
Put rho=||a||=||b||>0 and write rhat=a/rho, lhat=b/rho. Set rperp=J2 rhat, lperp=J2 lhat, R=[rhat,rperp], L=[lhat,lperp]. Both R,L have determinant +1. Since O rhat=lhat and det O=delta,
  O=L diag(1,delta) R^T.
There are unique scalar coordinates c,y with
  u=c rhat+y rperp,  v=c lhat+delta y lperp.
Independence of x and z is exactly y!=0. Put gij=(L^T G R)ij. The angular velocities of rhat,lhat are respectively -g12 and -g21 (obtained by projecting the active equations onto rperp,lperp). Differentiating u and v and cancelling the active-coordinate terms gives the EXACT equations
  y'=-delta g22 y,
  c'=-g11 c-(g12+delta g21)y.
The symbolic check expands both equations against both original vector ODEs for delta=+1 and delta=-1. No asymptotic approximation has been made in this reduction.

## 3. The endpoint determinant selects the unstable sign
At the nonzero critical endpoint, G* kills a* and its transpose kills b*. In the oriented frames L*,R*, this means
  L*^T G* R*=diag(0,gamma).
Since M is invertible and b*a*^T has rank one, G* cannot be zero. Thus gamma!=0 and s=|gamma| is the only positive singular value of G*.

The identity M=b*a*^T-G* Sigma^(-1) yields
  det M = -rho*^2 gamma h22,
where h22=(R*^T Sigma^(-1) R*)22>0. This follows by taking the determinant of diag(rho*^2,0)-diag(0,gamma)(R*^T Sigma^(-1)R*); the two oriented frame determinants are +1. Therefore sign det M=-sign gamma, and the selected component satisfies
  -delta gamma=|gamma|=s>0.
The matrix [[0,-G*],[-G*^T,0]] sends (delta lperp*;rperp*) to s times itself. The other graph component would instead select the stable eigenvector. Positive definiteness, invertibility of M and nonzero endpoint norms are each used explicitly in this sign calculation.

## 4. Nonzero transmission, growth rate, and direction
Let k(t)=-delta g22(t). The exact scalar solution is
  y(t)=y(T) exp(integral_T^t k(tau) d tau).
It never vanishes and keeps its sign. As the active path converges, k(t)->s>0, so log|y(t)|/t->s by the elementary Cesaro limit. The ratio q=c/y obeys
  q'=-(g11+k)q-(g12+delta g21).
The coefficient g11+k tends to s>0 and the forcing term tends to zero. Variation of constants with a late-time lower bound s/2 gives q(t)->0: the initial term decays exponentially; split the forcing integral into a fixed old part and a tail where its supremum is arbitrarily small. Since ||x||^2=2(c^2+y^2), the asserted direction and growth exponent follow.

If integral_T^infinity |k(t)-s|dt is finite, exp(-st)y(t) converges to the nonzero number y(T) exp(-sT+integral_T^infinity(k-s)). The c/y limit gives exp(-st)||x||->sqrt(2) times its absolute value. Exponential convergence of a,b to nonzero a*,b* implies this integrability because all the moving frames and G are smooth near that endpoint.

## Relation to target 1 and the still-open transfer step
For the ideal rank-one first path with two distinct positive origin singular values, this proves that its SECOND positive variational mode cannot be transported into the stable residual branch for any positive-definite 2x2 covariance and invertible target, including nonwhitened and noncommuting data. The conclusion is a deterministic obstruction reduction on an infinite data class. It does not assert that every nonlinear perturbation of the first path has this transport asymptotic.

To turn it into an unconditional Gaussian second step, one must still prove that the actual finite-alpha transverse remainder, after the correct alpha^(1-s2/s1) normalization and active hidden rotation, converges to this variational solution on the matching window, with errors small enough through the subsequent saddle passage. One must also compare stable/neutral corrections with its squared Gram amplitude at a suitable arrival time. Independent Gaussian positive-mode coefficients at initialization alone do not prove this uniform tracking. This theorem must not be relabeled an unconditional T232 solution.

## Checks and scope boundaries
scripts/check_transport_square_two.py verifies both moving-frame equations for both components, H^TJ+JH=0, the exact endpoint determinant, and a rational nonwhitened/noncommuting example (with algebraic normalization of its balanced factor). For M=diag(3,2), Sigma=I, a*=b*=sqrt(3)e1, the opposite component x=(-e2;e2) is null and J-orthogonal to the active vector but is a stable solution with exponent -2. Hence the orientation hypothesis cannot be omitted. An indefinite covariance flips the sign implication: with Sigma=diag(1,-1), P*=diag(3,0), G*=diag(0,2), M=P*-G*Sigma^(-1)=diag(3,2), the component delta=+1 has growth -2. This lies outside the covariance hypothesis and only checks its necessity for this argument.

The maximal-null-plane graph argument uses square dimension two on both sides. It is not a result for arbitrary rectangular inputs or all depths. The proof is mathematical and unaudited; exact finite algebra checks do not certify its analytic limit or its transfer to the random nonlinear flow. [Lemma 12 (KL fixed-point recursion for projected Bellman updates) of arXiv:2608.24858, 'Bellman Calibration for Marginalized Importance Weighting in Offline Reinforcement Learnin'] Under the conditions of
Lemma~\ref{lem:calibration-adjoint-kl-contraction}, let
\(\omega,\omega^+\) be normalized. If, for some \(\varepsilon\ge0\),
\begin{equation}

  D_{\nu}^{\rm KL}(\omega^+\|w_\pi)
  \le
  D_{\nu}^{\rm KL}(\mathcal B_\pi^\star\omega\|w_\pi)
  +
  \varepsilon,
\end{equation}
then
\[
  D_{\nu}^{\rm KL}(\omega^+\|w_\pi)
  \le
  \gamma D_{\nu}^{\rm KL}(\omega\|w_\pi)+\varepsilon .
\]
Consequently, if iterates \(\omega^{(k+1)}\) satisfy
\eqref{eq:kl-projection-one-step} with
\(\omega=\omega^{(k)}\) and errors \(\varepsilon_k\), then
\begin{equation}

  D_{\nu}^{\rm KL}(\omega^{(K)}\|w_\pi)
  \le
  \gamma^K D_{\nu}^{\rm KL}(\omega^{(0)}\|w_\pi)
  +
  \sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\gamma^{K-1-k}\varepsilon_k .
\end{equation}
If \(\varepsilon_k\le\varepsilon\) for all \(k\), the summation term in
\eqref{eq:kl-projection-recursion} is at most
\((1-\gamma)^{-1}\varepsilon\).

body: [Lemma rigidity given slope 1 of arXiv:2605.02226, 'Finitely Dependent Processes on Subshifts'] Let $ H$ be a four cycle free simple graph. Let $ X \subset \textit{Hom}(\mathbb{Z}^d, H)$ be a subshift where $ d \geq 2$. Suppose that for some $1 \leq i \leq d$, $|c_{H}(x, re_i)|=r$ for all $ x \in X$ and $ r \in \mathbb{N}$. Then for any $k \in \mathbb{N}$, any two allowed patterns $ a, b \in L(X, \mathbf{B}(k))$ which agree on the boundary of $ \mathbf{B}(k)$ (i.e. $ a|_{\partial \mathbf{B}(k)} = b|_{\partial \mathbf{B}(k)})$ must agree on entire $ \mathbf{B}(k)$ (i.e. $ a=b$). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
REFUTED ROUTE. The proposed statement that every rectangular sign skeleton with flat kernel and flat orthonormal singular directions obeys Q_sign(D,r)<=Q_Gaussian(D,r)+exp(-cn) uniformly for some c>0 is false. The Hadamard family gives a positive threshold with excess >=3/[4(n+1)]. Orthogonal sign projections are not generally independent, because their squared norms sum to the deterministic value n.
This is a failed proof route, not an accepted theorem

body:
[Lemma L:LB_t_phi of arXiv:2602.05317, 'Strong local nondeterminism for stochastic time-fractional\\ slow and fast diffusion equat'] Suppose that $\gamma \ge 0$ and $\beta\in (0,2)$.
  \begin{enumerate}[\rm (i)]

    \item If $\alpha>0$ satisfies~(equation E:Rationals of the paper), then there exists a
          compactly supported smooth function $\phi: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ such that
          \begin{align}
            L_\phi \coloneqq \liminf_{\tau \to \infty} \left\lvert\int_0^\tau \ensuremath{\mathrm{d} } s\, e^{is} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \ensuremath{\mathrm{d} } y\, \phi(y) G(s, y)\right\rvert^2 > 0.
          \end{align}
          In particular, the above $\liminf$ is taken over all $\tau > 0$ when
          $\beta + \gamma - 1 - \beta \left(\frac{d}{\alpha} \wedge 1\right) \ne
            0$, and along the set $\bigcup_{k=0}^\infty \left[(2k+1/3)\pi - \theta,
              \left(2k+4/3\right) \pi - \theta\right]$ when $\beta + \gamma - 1 - \beta
            \left(\frac{d}{\alpha} \wedge 1\right) = 0$ for some $\theta \in (-\pi/2,
            \pi/2]$.

    \item Otherwise if $\alpha>0$ satisfies~(equation E:alpha-Q of the paper),
          then~(equation E:LB_t_phi of the paper) still holds.

  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma L:LB_t_phi of arXiv:2602.05317

\[{\mathds{E}}_{\mu\times \mu_k}[M_k(S)]=|S|+ O(\rho^k).
\]

[Theorem thm.nguyenvu2011 of arXiv:2603.11043, 'An asymptotically optimal bound for the concentration function of a sum of independent int'] Let $\varepsilon < 1$ and $C$ be positive constants. Let
    $V = \{v_1, \dots, v_n\}$ be a multiset from a torsion-free group $G$. Let
$X_1, \dots, X_n$ be independent Rademacher random variables $(\mathbb P(X_i=1) = \mathbb P(X_i=-1) = \frac 1 2)$.
Assume that
\[ \rho(V):=\mathcal{Q}(v_1 X_1 + \dots + v_n X_n) \ge n^{-C}.\]
Then, there exists a proper symmetric GAP $A$ of rank $r = O_{C,\varepsilon}(1)$ that contains all but at most $\varepsilon n$ elements of $V$ (counting multiplicity), where
    \[|A| = O_{C,\varepsilon} (\rho(V)^{-1} n^{-\frac r 2}).\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem~2.1 of Nguyen and Vu~\cite{nguyenvu2011}

body: [Lemma 6 (Existence and regularity of the CDF solution) of arXiv:2608.27156, 'Traveling Waves in Equity Markets with\\Rank-Based Entry and Exit'] Let $w_0(y) = u_0(e^y)$ be a continuous CDF with finite first moment. Then \eqref{eq:pde-general} has an admissible solution $w$ in the sense of Lemma~\ref{lem:uniqueness}, with $w$ and $\pp_y w$ continuous for $t > 0$. Moreover, $w(t, \cdot)$ is a continuous CDF for every $t$, and the map $t \mapsto w(t, \cdot)$ is continuous in the supremum norm; in particular $w$ is jointly continuous. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 31 of arXiv:2607.14948, 'Graph alignment in sparse inhomogeneous models via self-overlap'] Let $\delta, \eps > 0$. There exist constants $c = c_\eps \goesto{\eps \to 0} 0$, $C = C_\eps > 0$, $\gamma = \gamma_{\eps, \delta} > 0$ and a random subset $\Neg_2(\delta, \eps) \subseteq \Sym_n$, such that $\Proba(\pi^* \in \Neg_2) = o(1)$, and the following property holds.
    
    For any $\pi \notin \Neg_2$, $|V_{\leq(1 - \eps)}(\pi)| \geq x_{sparse}n (1 - c)$; furthermore, for any $A \subseteq V_{\leq(1 - \eps)}(\pi)$ with $|A| \geq \delta n$ and such that no edges of $I(\pi)$ link $A$ to $A^c$, the graph $I(\pi)[V_{\leq(1 - \eps)}(\pi)]$ has at least $\exp(\gamma n \log n)$ automorphisms $(\sigma_i)$, verifying $A^c \subseteq \Fix \sigma_i$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 31 of arXiv:2607.14948

body:
[Lemma thm:BL of arXiv:2606.19763, 'Optimal Sparsification of Gaussian Processes'] Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\R^n$ with density $d\mu(x) \propto e^{-V(x)}\,dx$ where $V\in C^2$ and $\nabla^2 V(x)\succeq I$ for every $x\in\R^n$. 
	Then, for any differentiable function $f:\R^n\to\R$, we have
	\[
		\Varx_{\bx\sim\mu}\sbra{f(\bx)}
		\leq 
		\Ex_{\bx\sim\mu}\sbra{\|\nabla f(\bx)\|_2^2}\,.
	\]
	In particular, for every $u\in\R^n$,
	\[
		\Varx_{\bx\sim\mu}\sbra{\bx\cdot u}
		\leq 
		\|u\|_2^2\,.
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 67 (Simultaneous dyadic realization and full cutoff convergence) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Fix the physical localizers and the four index triples
$(a;b,c)\in\mathfrak L$.  Assume the fixed-profile estimate
\eqref{eq:centered-block-profile}, with $\sup_{\Lambda\in\Dyd}$ inside every
finite $L^p(\Omega)$ norm.  There is one event
$\Omega_{\mathrm{cen}}$ of probability one such that, simultaneously for all
index triples, all dyadic triples, and every $\eta'>0$,
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{\Lambda\in\Dyd}
 \|\mathcal B_{\Lambda,N,Q,M}^{a;b,c}\|_{
 C(\Delta_{T_0};\mathcal L(L_q^2,L_n^2))}
 \le C_{\eta'}(\omega)
 N^{-3/2+\beta_{b,c}+\eta'}(Q^{3/2+\eta'}+M^{3/2+\eta'}).
\end{equation}
On this event, for every $0<s<1-\beta_{b,c}$ and $\beta_{b,c}<\sigma<1-\beta_{b,c}$, the entire fixed-profile dyadic
cutoff sequence converges, without passage to a subsequence, in the assembled
operator topology whenever $\eta'$ is chosen below the strict margins in
\eqref{eq:assembly-strict-margin}.
title: Simultaneous dyadic realization and full cutoff convergence

Proof: condition on the other coordinates X_R; t = L + beta has density <= 1/|w_i| and X_i is affine in t, so the hub value is x* = alpha/(2t) + c_0 - sigma t/2 and the one-variable bathtub of Proposition 3.14 applies; alpha (the numerator at t = 0) is a quadratic in X_R whose square direction u_R = v_R - (v_i/w_i) w_R has |u_R|^2 = 1 + v_i^2/w_i^2 >= 1 (from <v, w> = 0), so a Fresnel-Hoelder small-ball bound (or, if one coordinate carries over half of |u_R|^2, a one-variable quadratic bound) gives E log(1 + 2/|alpha|) <= 2 + log(1 + 4 pi^4/|lambda|). Consequence: on m light coordinates (max |w_i| >= m^{-1/2}) the density is <= 1/2 + m^{1/2} (27.9 + 0.5 log(1 + m|lambda| + 4 m^{1/2}|q_i|)) for |lambda| >= 1, uniformly as eps -> 0. Proposition 3.14 needed v = 0 on its block; on a single coordinate that hypothesis is unnecessary. body: [Lemma area-after-loop-operation-original of arXiv:2505.16585, 'Expanded regimes of area law for lattice Yang--Mills theories'] Let $s \in \mc{S}_\Lambda$ be non-null, and $\mbf{e}$ be an edge of $s$. For all $s' \in \mbb{S}_{\pm}(s, \mbf{e}) \cup \mbb{M}_{\pm}(s, \mbf{e})$, we have that $\underbar{area}(s') = \underbar{area}(s)$. For $s' \in \mbb{D}_{\pm}(s, \mbf{e})$, we have that $\underbar{area}(s) \leq \underbar{area}(s') + 1$. Lastly, if $(s',K',Q') \in \mc{R}(s,K,Q)$, then $\underbar{area}(s) \leq \underbar{area}(s')+8(d-1)(|Q'|-|Q|)$.

body: [Definition 44 of arXiv:2608.27630, 'Oriented planar maps and \\ annular mating of trees'] For $x\in\partial \cA_\tau$, let $x'\in\cS_\tau$ such that $p(x')=x$. With slight abuse of notation, we define the west-going flow line $\eta_x^\rmW$ of $h^{\mathrm{A}}$ started from $x$ to be equal to $p(\eta_{x'}^\rmW)$ where  $\eta_{x'}^\rmW$ is the west-going flow line of $h^\rmS$ started from $x'$, and the east-going flow line  $\eta_x^\rmE$ of $h^{\mathrm{A}}$ started from $x$ to be equal to $p(\eta_{x'}^\rmE)$ where  $\eta_{x'}^\rmE$ is the east-going flow line of $h^\rmS$ started from $x'$. Let $E^\cros$ be the event where the west-going flow line of $h^{\mathrm{A}}$ started from $1$ hits $C_\tau$. Conditioned on  the event $E^\cros$, we define the counterclockwise space-filling $\SLE_{\kappa'}$ loop associated with $h^{\mathrm{A}}$ by taking the projection under $p$ of the space-filling curve $\eta'$ for $h^\rmS$ on $\cS_\tau$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:ig-def-SLEloop}, and write $\SLE_{\kappa',\tau}^{\mathrm{loop}}$ for its law. We write $\IG^*_\tau$ for the law of $h^{\mathrm{A}}$ conditioned on the positive probability event $E^\cros$.

 $$

[Proposition 10 (Principal curvatures of $\partial K_n$) of arXiv:2605.11995, 'Intrinsic volumes of \(\ell_p\)-balls and a continuum of Maxwell--Poincar\'e--Borel laws f'] Fix a point $x\in \partial K_n$ such that $x_i\neq 0$ for all $i=1,\ldots,n$.
Then $\partial K_n$ is a $C^2$-hypersurface in the neighborhood of $x$ and
the principal curvatures $\lambda_1(x),\dots,\lambda_{n-1}(x)$  are precisely the solutions (in the variable $\lambda$) of the equation
\begin{equation}
\sum_{i=1}^n \bigl(\varphi_i'(x_i)\bigr)^2
\prod_{\substack{j=1\\ j\neq i}}^n
\left(\varphi_j''(x_j)-|\nabla F(x)|\,\lambda\right) = 0.
\end{equation}
The degree of the polynomial on the right-hand side is exactly $n-1$.

AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT, unaudited; novelty is unestablished. Explicit limiting cubic high-noise expansion for one non-Gaussian factor, proof unaudited. U in R^(N by M) has iid entries from a fixed centered variance-one real law with E exp(tu)<=exp(K^2t^2/2) for all real t,K>=1. Independently V in R^(P by M) is iid standard Gaussian, X=UV^T/sqrt(N), and Z is independent standard Gaussian. Let i_N(s)=I(X;sqrt(s)X+Z)/(NP), alpha_N=P/N<=alpha_star, beta_N=M/N<=beta_star, and v_N=1+s beta_N. Set L=8K sqrt(1+beta_star), D=L^2+beta_star, J=sqrt(beta_star^2+16K^4 beta_star), s_star=min(1/(2D),1/sqrt(8 alpha_star K^2 D)), A=D^4/3+40K^4 alpha_star beta_star D^2, q_N=2exp(-5N), delta_N^2=2J sqrt(q_N)+4 beta_star q_N, E_N(s)=2q_N/(NP)+sqrt(s)delta_N+s(beta_star q_N+J sqrt(q_N))/v_N. For0<s<=s_star, 0<=log(v_N)/2-i_N(s)<=A s^4+E_N(s). The error tends to zero exponentially with N uniformly on this SNR interval; E_N(s)/s^4 is not uniformly bounded near zero. If beta_N->beta, all limiting information envelopes have beta s/2-beta^2s^2/4+beta^3s^3/6 with remainder at most(A+beta_star^4/8)s^4. Limit existence/uniqueness is not asserted. A companion bound for0<s<=s_star/2 gives 0<=beta_N/v_N-m_N(s)<=32A exp(2 beta_star s)s^3+2exp(2 beta_star s)E_N(2s)/s, where m_N is scaled-product MMSE. The proof pays operator-norm conditioning with Gaussian entropy coupling006 and cites the unconditional Gaussian-reference obstruction033. Both-general-factor priors, finite-moment-only laws, and the first prior-dependent limiting coefficient remain open. Novelty unestablished.
Positive integer dimensions; independent arrays and noise
Fixed iid centered variance-one U law with the stated all-real MGF proxy K>=1
V entries standard real Gaussian
Aspect ratios bounded above by fixed positive alpha_star,beta_star
0<s<=s_star for MI,0<s<=s_star/2 for risk
Limiting expansion assumes beta_N converges; no prior MI-limit hypothesis
