[Corollary cor:lattice-transfer of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Let $G$ be any nontrivial torsion-free abelian group.  For all $h,k\geq1$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal R_G(h,k)=\mathcal R(h,k).
\end{equation}
Consequently the spectrum-only conclusions
(equation eq:endpoint-local of the paper), (equation eq:ambient-exponent of the paper), and
(equation eq:localmain of the paper), together with the four-point positive-density
conclusion, hold with $\mathcal R$ replaced by $\mathcal R_G$.  The diameter-filtered
integer-witness assertion (equation eq:quantmain of the paper) is not asserted for an
abstract group $G$.  In particular,
$|\mathcal R_G(h,k)|=h^{k-1+o_k(1)}$ for every fixed $k\geq4$, and
$|\mathcal R_G(h,4)|=\Theta(h^3)$ with positive lower density.

Let f_n, g_n, g be measurable with |f_n| <= g_n almost everywhere, f_n -> f a.e., g_n -> g a.e., every g_n and g in L^1(mu), and integral g_n dmu -> integral g dmu. Then f is in L^1, integral |f_n - f| dmu -> 0, and in particular integral f_n dmu -> integral f dmu. The classical dominated convergence theorem is the case g_n = g constant in n. The hypothesis that the integrals of the dominators CONVERGE (not merely that the dominators converge pointwise) is essential: with g_n = 1_{[n,n+1]} on R one has g_n -> 0 = g pointwise, but integral g_n = 1 does not converge to integral g = 0, and taking f_n = g_n shows the conclusion fails. [Pratt (1960), 'On interchanging limits and integrals', Ann. Math. Statist. 31, 74-77]

body: [Proposition 12 of arXiv:2604.01852, 'The on/off Brownian snake'] Let $(E',d')$ be a complete and separable metric space and $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P})$ a probability space on which we have random variables $\mathcal{Q}_t: \Omega \rightarrow E'$, $t \geq 0$. Suppose further that there is another probability space $(\Omega', \mathcal{F}', \mathbb{P}')$ on which random variables $\mathcal{Q}'_t: \Omega' \rightarrow E'$ form a path-continuous process with the same finite-dimensional distributions as $\mathcal{Q} = (\mathcal{Q}_t, t \geq 0)$. Then $(\mathcal{Q}_t, t \geq 0)$ has a modification $(\Tilde{\mathcal{Q}}_t, t \geq 0)$ with continuous paths, i.e. for each fixed $t \geq 0$ we have $\mathbb{P}(\Tilde{\mathcal{Q}}_t = \mathcal{Q}_t) = 1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 12 of arXiv:2604.01852

[Thm MainRes1 of arXiv:2607.19037, 'Semiclassical analysis for Yang--Mills \\ random connections on compact surfaces'] For $\alpha<\frac12$, $p\geqslant 2$, $\ell<0$, and $s<-1$, the Yang--Mills measure can be realized as a Borel probability measure on~$\mathcal{B}_{\mathsf{YM}}^{\alpha,p,s,\ell}$. Moreover, it admits the decomposition
\[
A_{\Sigma,\sigma}=A_{\mathcal{N},\Sigma,\sigma}+\sum_{a=1}^{2g}x_aU_a,
\]
where $A_{\mathcal{N},\Sigma,\sigma}\in \mathcal{W}^{\alpha,p,s,\ell}$ is the noise component, with regularity comparable to that of the Gaussian free field, each $U_a\in\mathcal{F}$ is an integration current on some unstable curve of a Morse gradient flow on~$\Sigma$, and almost surely
\[
\forall a=1,\dots,2g, \quad x_a\in B_{\mathfrak{g}}\bigl(0,\mathsf{diam}(G)\bigr).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm MainRes1 of arXiv:2607.19037

body:
[Definition def:restriction-to-a-subset of arXiv:2411.06195, 'Restrictions of some reinforced processes to subgraphs'] \mbox{}\\
  Let $(X_n,T_n)_{n\in{\mathbb N}_0}$ be a continuous-time jump process on $G$.
  Recursively, we take $\sigma_0:=0$ and for $n\in{\mathbb N}$, on the event
  $\{\sigma_{n-1}<\infty\}$, we define 
  $\sigma_n:=\inf\{l>\sigma_{n-1}:X_l\neq X_{\sigma_{n-1}}\}$ to be the index
  of the next jump to a different location. 
  The process with self-loops removed is defined by 
  $(X^{\neq},T^{\neq})=(X^{\neq}_n,T^{\neq}_n)_{n\in{\mathbb N}_0}:=(X_{\sigma_n},\sum_{l=\sigma_n}^{\sigma_{n+1}-1}T_l)_{n\in{\mathbb N}_0}$
  on the event $\{\sigma_n<\infty\text{ for all }n\in{\mathbb N}\}$. 

  Let $\emptyset\neq J\subseteq\Lambda$. We set recursively $\tau_0=0$, 
  $\tau_n=\inf\{ l>\tau_{n-1}: X_l\in J\}$
  for $n\in{\mathbb N}$. In other words, on the event $\{X_0\in J\}$, 
  $\tau_n$ denotes the number of jumps up to the $n$-th return to $J$. 
  The restriction of the process to $J$ is defined
  on the event $\{\tau_n<\infty\text{ for all }n\in{\mathbb N}\}$ by
  $(X^J,T^J)=(X_n^J,T_n^J)_{n\in{\mathbb N}_0}:=(X_{\tau_n},T_{\tau_n})_{n\in{\mathbb N}_0}$.

  The notation $(X^{J\neq},T^{J\neq})$ means that both operations have
  been applied to the process $(X,T)$, first the restriction to $J$ and
  then self-loop removal.
title: Removal of self-loops and restriction to a subset: process

[Corollary col: k simplex density of arXiv:2505.09839, '\textbf{Density Frankl–Rödl on the Sphere}'] Fix any \( r \in \left(-\frac{1}{k - 1}, 1\right) \). For any measurable set \( A \subseteq \mathbb{S}^{n-1} \) with \( \sigma(A) \geq \omega_{k,r}(n^{-\epsilon_{k,r}}) \), the probability that a uniformly random tuple \( (x_1, \dots, x_k) \in \Delta_k(n, r) \) lies entirely in \( A \) satisfies
\[
\mathop{\bf Pr\/}_{(x_1, \dots, x_k) \in \Delta_k(n, r)}(x_1 \in A, \dots, x_k \in A) \geq \Omega_{k,r}(\sigma(A)^{C_{k,r}}),
\]
as \( n \to \infty \). The constants \( C_{k,r},\ \epsilon_{k,r} \) are given by
\[
C_{k,r} = \sum_{i = 1}^{k - 1} \frac{2}{1 - |c_i|} \prod_{j = 1}^{i - 1} \frac{1 + |c_j|}{1 - |c_j|}
\qquad
\epsilon_{k,r}=\prod_{i=1}^{k-1}\frac{1-|c_i|}{1+|c_i|},
\]
where
\[
c_i = \frac{r}{1 + (i - 1)r}, \quad \text{for } i = 1, \dots, k - 1.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary col: k simplex density of arXiv:2505.09839

body:
For probability measures P and Q on one space, TV(P, Q) = sup_A |P(A) - Q(A)| and D = D(P || Q) is the Kullback-Leibler divergence in nats (+infinity unless P << Q). Then TV(P, Q) <= min(sqrt(D/2), sqrt(1 - exp(-D))). The two bounds cross at the unique positive root D* = 1.59362426004004... of D/2 = 1 - exp(-D): Pinsker's bound is the smaller for 0 < D < D* and the Bretagnolle-Huber bound for D > D*.
P and Q are probability measures on one measurable space

[Theorem cor020104-21 of arXiv:2606.07353, 'The Gaussian structure of a perturbed KPZ'] Suppose that $F\in C_b (  D_+(\mathbb{T}))$ and $\mu\in {\mathcal
  M}_1( D_+(\mathbb{T}))$, then there exists a unique measure  $\pi_\infty\in {\mathcal
  M}_1( D(\mathbb{T}))$  such that
\begin{equation}

\lim_{t\to+\infty}\int_{ D_+(\mathbb{T})}\tilde {\mathcal
    U}_t^VFd\mu= \int_{  D_+(\mathbb{T})}F d\pi_\infty .
\end{equation}
The measure $\pi_\infty$ is invariant under  $\big(\tilde
\mathcal{U}^V_t\big)$.

In addition,  for any $\delta>0$, $p\in[1,+\infty)$
there exist constants $C,\lambda>0$, depending only on
$\|V\|_{L^2(\mathbb{T})}$, $\delta$ and $p$,
such that
\begin{equation}

\sup_{\rho_1,\rho_2\in
  D_+(\mathbb{T})}\mathbf{E}\big\|\rho^V(t;\rho_1)-\rho^V(t;\rho_2)\big\|^p_\infty\leq
C e^{-\lambda t},\quad t\ge \delta.
\end{equation}
 

Furthermore,    there exists $C>0$, depending
only on $\|V\|_{L^2(\mathbb{T})}$, $\delta$ and $p$ such that  
\begin{equation}

\sup_{t\ge \delta,\,{\mu\in {\mathcal
    M}_1(\mathbb{T})}}\mathbf{E}_{\mu}\Big[{\|\rho^V(t;\mu)\|_\infty^p+\|\rho^V(t;\mu)^{-1}\|_\infty^{p}}\Big]\le C.
\end{equation}
In  consequence, for any $p\ge1$,
\begin{equation}

\int_{ D_+(\mathbb{T})}\big(\|\rho\|^p_\infty +{\|\rho^{-1}\|^{p}_\infty}\big) \pi_\infty (d\rho)<+\infty.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem cor020104-21 of arXiv:2606.07353

body:
[Corollary 44 (Convergence after $n(x)$ steps, stated with a reference measure) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] Let $(\XX,\XXA)$ be a measurable space and $\lambda$ a $\sigma$-finite measure on
it. Let $p : \XX \to [0,\infty)$ be measurable with $\int_{\XX} p \dd\lambda = 1$, let
$\tau : \XX\times\XX \to [0,\infty)$ be $\XXA\otimes\XXA$-measurable with
$\int_{\XX} \tau(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y) = 1$ for every $x \in \XX$, and define
\[
  \pi(A) := \int_{A} p \dd\lambda, \qquad T(A \mid x) := \int_{A}\tau(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y)
  \qquad (A \in \XXA,\ x \in \XX),
\]
and $\Xp := \{p > 0\} \in \XXA$. Let $\tau_{n} : \XX\times\XX \to [0,\infty)$ be given
by the Chapman--Kolmogorov recursion
\[
  \tau_{1} := \tau, \qquad
  \tau_{n+1}(y \mid x) := \int_{\XX} \tau_{n}(y \mid z)\,\tau(z \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd z)
  \qquad (n \in \N).
\]
Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep,topsep=3pt]
  \item \emph{(invariance)} $\displaystyle\int_{\XX} \tau(y \mid x)\,p(x)\,\lambda(\dd x) = p(y)$ for $\lambda$-almost every $y \in \XX$;
  \item \emph{(eventual positivity)} for every $x \in \XX$ there is a number $n \in \N$ with
        \[
          \lambda\bigl(\{ y \in \XX\setminus\Xp : \tau_{n}(y \mid x) > 0 \}\bigr) = 0
          \qquad\text{and}\qquad
          \lambda\bigl(\{ y \in \Xp : \tau_{n}(y \mid x) = 0 \}\bigr) = 0 .
        \]
\end{enumerate}
Then $\pi$ is the unique invariant probability measure of $T$, and
$\tv{T^{n}\circ\mu - \pi} \to 0$ for every $\mu \in \Prob$.

[Theorem thm-kk of arXiv:2412.03067, 'Geodesic Trees and Exceptional Directions in FPP on Hyperbolic Groups'] [kapovich-kleiner]
	Let $G$ be a one-ended torsion-free hyperbolic group with 1 dimensional boundary, and trivial JSJ decomposition. Then ${\partial G}$ is exactly one of the following:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item a circle $S^1$,
		\item  a Sierpinski carpet
		\item  a Menger curve.
	\end{enumerate}
	If $G$ does not split over ${\mathbb Z}$, ${\partial G}$ is either  a Sierpinski carpet or  a Menger curve. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm-kk of arXiv:2412.03067

[Defi 25 (Gaussian Process) of arXiv:2608.01860, 'A Variational Characterization of a Gibbs Measure related to the Aviles-Giga Functional'] A stochastic process $(X_t)_{t\in T}$, where $T$ is some index set, not necessarily countable or finite-dimensional, is called centered Gaussian process if for any finite set $t_1<t_2<...<t_n$ the vector random variable $(X_{t_1},X_{t_2},...,X_{t_n})$ is Gaussian with mean zero. The covariance is given by $c(t_1,t_2)=\mathbb{E}[X_{t_1}X_{t_2}]$.\\
 It is common to call $X$ a random field if $T\not\subset \R$.
title: Gaussian Process

body:
[Theorem 41 of arXiv:2607.28578, 'On two differing geometric descriptions of the passage from microscopy to macroscopy in Ma'] Let $M$ be a connected closed Riemannian manifold, let $\Prob^{\infty}_+(M)$ be its Fr\'echet manifold of smooth positive probability densities and let $\Hspace_k\hookrightarrow C^1(M;TM)$ be a vector-valued reproducing kernel Hilbert space.
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
		\item The continuity operator $\Aop_{\rho}v=-\Div(\rho v)$ is the differential of the pushforward action, is surjective from smooth vector fields onto $C^{\infty}_0(M)$ and identifies a smooth density tangent with a particle velocity modulo $\Ker\Aop_{\rho}$.
		\item The weighted form $\int_M\rho\langle\grad f,\grad h\rangle_g\,\dd{\mathrm{vol}}$ defines the Otto cotangent $\dot H^1_{\rho}$, tangent $\dot H^{-1}_{\rho}$ and Riesz isomorphism $\Kop^{\Wass}_{\rho}f=-\Div(\rho\grad f)$.
		\item The quotient range $T_{\rho,\Stein}=\Aop_{\rho}(\Hspace_k)$ with its minimum-$\Hspace_k$ norm is Hilbert. The kernel form $\langle\Iop_{\rho}^{*}\grad f,\Iop_{\rho}^{*}\grad h\rangle_{\Hspace_k}$ defines, after quotienting its full nullspace and completing, a Stein cotangent. The map $\Kop^{\Stein}_{\rho}f=-\Div(\rho\Iop_{\rho}^{*}\grad f)$ is an isometric isomorphism from this cotangent onto the full quotient tangent.
		\item The hierarchy associated with a differentiable functional is
		\[
			\mathcal F\longmapsto\dd{\mathcal F}(\rho)=[f]\longmapsto\grad f\longmapsto-\Bop^{\bullet}_{\rho}f\longmapsto-\Aop_{\rho}\Bop^{\bullet}_{\rho}f.
		\]
		The four arrows respectively pass from a functional to a density covector, from the covector to a sample space force, from the force to a selected particle velocity, and from the velocity to the law tangent.
		\item Let $\Mop_{\rho}=\mathsf{P}^{\mathrm{hor}}_{\rho}\Iop_{\rho}\Iop_{\rho}^{*}$ on the Otto horizontal space. Then $\Kop^{\Stein}_{\rho}f=\Aop_{\rho}\Mop_{\rho}\grad f$. Equality $\Mop_{\rho}\grad f=\grad f$ is equivalent to equality of the law tangents; equality $\Iop_{\rho}\Iop_{\rho}^{*}\grad f=\grad f$ is equivalent to equality of the particle fields; positive proportionality gives the same unparametrised law curve. Formula \eqref{prescribed-equivalence-eq} characterises equality under any prescribed differentiable observation, whilst $\Mop_{\rho}=\id$ on a closed force space characterises equality of the law geometries on all of its directions.
		\item The exact defect is given by \eqref{tangent-defect-eq}. Spectral bounds on $\Mop_{\rho}$ give the cotangent and tangent comparisons \eqref{cotangent-comparison-eq} and \eqref{tangent-metric-comparison-eq}. Every positive self-adjoint response on a finite dimensional smooth horizontal force space is realised by a finite rank vector-valued kernel.
		\item Relative entropy has regular cotangent $[\log(\rho/\pi)]$. Its Wasserstein and Stein descents agree precisely under Corollary \ref{entropy-equivalence-cor}. A regular minimal exponential family admits smooth Stein solutions which realise any prescribed Fisher mirror covector descent; exact membership in a chosen kernel space is the remaining range condition.
	\end{enumerate}
	All assertions concerning Hilbert pairs are fibrewise. Smooth variation of the Stein fibres, a connection or a globally well posed gradient flow requires additional uniform range and regularity hypotheses.

[Thm 3 of arXiv:2609.03061, '2609.03061'] Fix the reference Lagrangian $L_0=( \mathbb{R}^n \oplus 0) \subset \mathbb{R}^{2n}$.
Let $M_1, M_2: [a,b] \rightarrow  Sp(2n, \mathbb{R})$ be a pair of continuous, piecewise
smooth mappings.

Let the eigenvalues of $G[M_k(t)] \in U(n), k=1, \ 2$ be written in the form
$$
\{ \lambda_1(t)_k, \cdots, \lambda_n(t)_k\}
$$ where $\lambda_j(t)_k =  \pm \ e^{ i \theta_j(t)_k} $ with $0 \le \theta_j(t)_k < \pi$;
i.e., equivalently $\lambda_j(t)_k^2 = e^{ i (2 \theta_j(t)_k)}$ with $0 \le 2 \theta_j(t)_k < 2 \pi$
for $k=1, \ 2$ respectively.

Let the eigenvalues of $G[M_k(t)] \cdot G[M_k(t)]^t \in U(n)$ be written in the form
$$
\{ \lambda'_1(t)_k, \cdots,\lambda'_n(t)_k\}
$$
where $\lambda'_j(t)_k = e^{i \phi_j(t)_k}$ with $0 \le \phi_j(t)_k < 2 \pi$

Then the Maslov index of the path of pairs of Lagrangians  \cite{CLM},
$$
\mu_{CLM}( \ \{ \ \ t \mapsto (M_1(t) \cdot L_0,  M_2(t) \cdot L_0) \  \})
 = \mu_{CLM}( \{\  t \mapsto (K(G[M_1(t)]) \cdot L_0, \ K(G[M_2(t)]) \cdot L_0) \ \ \} \ )
$$
is equal to
$$ \begin{array}{l}
\int_a^b \ ( t \mapsto det(G[M_2(t)])^2 \in S^1)^\star \ ( \frac{d \theta}{2\pi})
- \int_a^b \ ( t \mapsto det(G[M_1(t)])^2 \in S^1)^\star \ ( \frac{d \theta}{2\pi})\\
 + \Sigma_{j=1}^n \ ( \ \frac{2\theta_j(a)_2 - 2\theta_j(b)_2}{2\pi} \ )
 -  \Sigma_{j=1}^n \ ( \   \frac{2\theta_j(a)_1 - 2\theta_j(b)_1}{2\pi} \ )
 + ( h_2(a)- h_2(b)) - (h_1(a) - h_1(b))\\ \\
 and \ also \ equal \ to \\ \\
 \int_a^b \ ( t \mapsto det(G[M_2(t)])^2 \in S^1)^\star \ (\frac{d \theta}{2\pi})
 - \int_a^b \ ( t \mapsto det(G[M_1(t)])^2 \in S^1)^\star \ (\frac{d \theta}{2\pi}) \\
 + \Sigma_{j=1}^n ( \ \frac{\phi_j(a)_2 - \phi_j(b)_2}{2\pi} \ )
 -  \Sigma_{j=1}^n ( \ \frac{\phi_j(a)_1 - \phi_j(b)_1}{2\pi} \ ) + ( h_2(a)- h_2(b))-( h_1(a)- h_1(b))\\
 \end{array}
 $$
 where $h_k(t)$ is the number of $j$ with $(\lambda_j(t)_k)^2=+1$, or equivalently
 the number of $j$ with $\lambda'_j(t)_k= +1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 5 (Euclidean shell trichotomy) of arXiv:2609.02362, '\textbf{Farthest-cell triplet entropy: high-dimensional shell limits and hyperbolic curvat'] Under the preceding assumptions:

\begin{enumerate}
  \item if $\lambda_d\to0$, then
  \[
    H_3(P_d,d_{\mathrm{Euc}})\longrightarrow\log 3;
  \]

  \item if $\lambda_d\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)$, then
  \[
    H_3(P_d,d_{\mathrm{Euc}})
    \longrightarrow
    H_\infty(\lambda;F);
  \]

  \item if $\lambda_d\to\infty$ and $F$ is continuous, then
  \[
    H_3(P_d,d_{\mathrm{Euc}})\longrightarrow0.
  \]
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Lem 25 of arXiv:2506.17979, '\large\bf A remark on subharmonicity for symmetric Dirichlet forms'] We consider a function $g\in L^1(E;{\m})$ with $0<g\leq 1$ ${\m}$-a.e.~on $E$. Let $\check{\bf X}$ be the time changed process  by $A_t^g$ and 
 $(\check{\mathscr{E}},D(\check{\mathscr{E}}))$ on $L^2(E;g{\m})$ the  Dirichlet form associated with $\check{\bf X}$.   
 The following hold. 
 \begin{enumerate}
 \item[\rm(1)] For $u\in D(\mathscr{E})_{e,\loc}$ {\rm(}resp.~$u\in D(\mathscr{E})_{e,\loc}^{\dag}$, $u\in D(\mathscr{E})_{e,\loc}^{\diamond}${\rm)}, there exists 
 $g\in L^1(E;{\m})$ satisfying $0<g\leq 1$ ${\m}$-a.e.~such that 
 $u\in D(\check{\mathscr{E}})_{\loc}$ {\rm(}resp.~$u\in D(\check{\mathscr{E}})_{\loc}^{\dag}$, $u\in D(\check{\mathscr{E}})_{\loc}^{\diamond}${\rm)} holds for the Dirichlet form $(\check{\mathscr{E}}, D(\check{\mathscr{E}}))$ on $L^2(E;g{\m})$ associated with the time changed process $\check{\bf X}$. In particular, for $u\in D(\mathscr{E})_{e,\loc}^{\diamond}$, $\mathscr{E}$-subharmonicity of $u$ in $D$ is equivalent to the 
 $\check{\mathscr{E}}$-subharmonicity of $u$ in $D$.  
 \item[\rm(2)] For a nearly Borel $\overline{\R}$-valued function $u$, 
 the subharmonicity of $u$ in $D$ with respect to ${\bf X}$ is equivalent to 
 the subharmonicity of $u$ in $D$ with respect to $\check{\bf X}$.
 \item[\rm(3)] For a nearly Borel $\overline{\R}$-valued function $u$, 
 the subharmonicity of $u$ in $D$ in the weak sense with respect to ${\bf X}$ is equivalent to  the subharmonicity of $u$ in $D$ in the weak sense with respect to $\check{\bf X}$.
 \end{enumerate}

body: [Abstract of arXiv:2609.03728, 'Moments for self-normalized partial sums'] We consider a \regvary\ stationary \seq\ of random variables $(X_t)$ with tail index $\a<2$. For these \seq s we study the joint \con\ of sums, $\ell^p$-type moduli and maxima. We focus on ratio statistics, including the studentized sums and sums normalized by the corresponding maxima, and study the existence of moments for the limit ratios. We consider particular examples of processes $(X_t)$ whose limit ratios possess all moments. But, in contrast to the latter situation, there also exist \seq s $(X_t)$ where certain moments of the limit ratio are infinite. This phenomenon results from extremal clusters in the \seq .
title: Abstract of arXiv:2609.03728: Moments for self-normalized partial sums

[Lemma 115 (Exhaustion of the three-frequency configurations) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Assume
$N_0=\langle\xi\rangle$, $N_1=\langle\eta\rangle$, and
$N_2=\langle\xi-\eta\rangle$ are all at least two.  After enlarging the
fixed comparability constants, the dyadic frequency space is the union of the
following four regions, with only finite overlap:
\begin{align*}
 &N_0\sim N_1\sim N_2,\\
 &N_0\sim N_2\gg N_1,\\
 &N_0\sim N_1\gg N_2,\\
 &N_1\sim N_2\gg N_0.
\end{align*}
In the first three regions the sublevel estimates of
\cref{lem:continuous-phase-layers} apply to every sign vector
$\bm\eps\in\{\pm1\}^3$.  In the last region the pointwise estimate of
\cref{lem:first-picard-low-output-gap} applies to every sign vector.

[Proposition prop:finite-time-concentration-scale of arXiv:2609.02829, 'Quantitative explosion and percolation of the divisible sandpile'] Assume that $(\zeta(z))_{z\in\mathbb{Z}^d}$ are i.i.d. For each $x$ and
		$t$, the map $\zeta\mapsto u_t(x)$ is convex and satisfies
		\[
			|u_t(x;\zeta)-u_t(x;\eta)|
			\leq
			\left(\sum_{z\in\mathbb{Z}^d}g_t(x,z)^2\right)^{1/2}
			\|\zeta-\eta\|_{\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}^d)}\, .
		\]
		For every $p\geq2$ with $\mathbb{E}|\zeta(0)|^p<\infty$ there is
		$C=C(p,\mathcal L(\zeta(0)))<\infty$ such that
		\[
			\mathbb{E}\bigl|u_t(x)-\mathbb{E} u_t(x)\bigr|^p
			\leq C \Var(V_t(0))^{p/2}\, .
		\]
		In particular, if $\Var(\zeta(0))<\infty$, then
		$\Var(u_t(x))\leq C\Var(V_t(0))$.
		If $0<\Var(\zeta(0))<\infty$, then, for every $m,n\geq0$ and
		$x,y\in\mathbb{Z}^d$,
		\begin{equation}
			0\leq\Cov(u_n(x),u_m(y))
			\leq
			2\Var(\zeta(0))
			\sum_{z\in\mathbb{Z}^d}g_n(x,z)g_m(y,z)\, .
		\end{equation}

[Lemma 18 of arXiv:2609.01574, 'A linear bound for Fujita's freeness conjecture'] Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a pair with $X$ smooth projective. Assume that $(X,\Delta)$ is log canonical near a closed point $x$ and is not klt at $x$, and let $W:=W_x(X,\Delta)$. Assume that $d:=\dim W\geq2$, and let $\nu\colon Z=W^\nu\to W$ be the normalization. Let $\mathcal I_x\subset\mathcal O_Z$ be the ideal sheaf of $x$, and let $f\colon Y\to Z$ be its normalized blow-up. Write $\mathcal I_x\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_Y(-E)$ and $H:=-E$. Let $\mathbf B$ be the discriminant $b$-divisor from Proposition~\ref{prop:adjunction-data} for the subadjunction of $(X,\Delta)$ along $W$, and let $B_Y$ be the trace of $\mathbf B$ on $Y$. Then
\[
 -\sum_F\mult_F B_Y\bigl(F\cdot H^{d-1}\bigr)
 \leq K_Y\cdot H^{d-1},
\]
where the sum runs over the prime components of $E$.

[Proposition prop:uniform-ranges of arXiv:2609.02544, 'A finiteness theorem for geodesic Leech wheels'] In a geodesic Leech wheel $W_{m+1}$ with $h$ large spokes, the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item If $h=0$, then $m\le39$, that is, $n\le40$.
\item If $h=1$, then $m\le40$, that is, $n\le41$.
\item If $h=2$, then $m\le41$, that is, $n\le42$.

body: [Lemma lemma cv CLE in the rectangles of arXiv:2609.04138, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ I:\\ subsequential limits of the non-simple C'] On the event that there is a loop of $\Gamma$ crossing $A_{s,t}(z)$ and that there are $k\ge 1$ conformal rectangles $R_1, \ldots, R_k$, for all $j \in [1, k]_\BZ$, let $\Gamma'_{R^n_j}$ be the non-nested $\CLE_{\kappa'}$ associated with the $\cwBCLE_{\kappa^\prime}(0)$/$\ccwBCLE_\kappa(-\kappa/2)$ iteration construction (see~(A025 of the paper)) in the connected component of the unexplored region $R^n_j$ containing $R_j$. For all $x\in R_j \cap \BQ^2$, consider the loop $\SCL_j^n(x)$ of $\Gamma'_{R^n_j}$ surrounding $x$. Then, for all simply connected open subset $U \subset R_j$ such that $\overline{U} \subset R_j$ there exists a sequence $(U_n)_{n\ge 1}$ of simply connected open subsets such that $\overline{U_n} \to \overline{U}$ a.s.\@ in the Hausdorff topology, $U_n \to U$ a.s.\@ in the Carathéodory sense, and such that the conditional laws given $R^n_j$ of the $\overline{U_n}\cap \SCL^n_j(x)$'s for $x\in R_j \cap \BQ^2$ converge a.s.\ weakly, in the Hausdorff topology, to the conditional law given $R_j$ of the $\overline{U} \cap \SCL_j(x)$'s for $x \in R_j \cap \BQ^2$, where the $\SCL_j(x)$'s are the loops of a $\CLE_{\kappa'}$ in $R_j$.

Let $x\in\bbR$. There exists a unique coupling between $(h^\rmS,\eta)$ where $\eta$ is a curve starting from $x$,  and stopped until either hitting $\bbR+i\tau$ or one of its translates $\eta+k$ where $k\in\bbZ$, such that the following holds:
    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
        \item For each stopping time $\sigma$ of $\eta$ before its duration, $\eta([0,\sigma])$ is a local set of $h^\rmS$, in the sense that the conditional law of $h^\rmS$ given $\eta|_{[0,\sigma]}$ has the following description. Let $\cS_{\eta,\sigma} = \cS_\tau\backslash \cup_{k\in\bbZ}(k+\eta([0,\sigma]))$, and $\cA_{\eta,\sigma}$ be the annulus such that there is a conformal map $\varphi_{\eta,\sigma}$ with $\cA_{\eta,\sigma} = p\circ\varphi_{\eta,\sigma}\circ \cS_{\eta,\sigma}$. Let $\mathfrak{h}_{\eta,\sigma}$ be the harmonic function on $\cS_{\eta,\sigma}$ whose boundary values agrees with $h^\rmS$ on $\partial\cS_\tau$ and is given by the flow line boundary conditions on $ \cup_{k\in\bbZ}(k+\eta([0,\sigma]))$ as in Figure~\ref{fig: flow line boundary data} and~\cite[Figure 1.10]{ImagGeo1}. Then $h^\rmS|_{\cS_{\eta,\sigma}} =  {h}_{\eta,\sigma}\circ p\circ \varphi_{\eta,\sigma} + \mathfrak{h}_{\eta,\sigma}$, where ${h}_{\eta,\sigma}$ is a zero boundary GFF in $\cA_{\eta,\sigma}$ independent from $\mathfrak{h}_{\eta,\sigma}$.
        \item The curve $\eta$ is measurable with respect to $h^\rmS$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[1 14 of arXiv:2607.12303, 'Marginal Stationary Distributions and Convergence Rates of Higher Order Markov Chains'] Suppose that the transition tensor ${\cal P}$ of  an $(m-1)$th order Markov chain $\{X_t\}_{t=1}^{\infty}$ on state space
$S$ is positive, that is, ${\cal P}>0$. Let $Q$ be the transition matrix of its reduced first order chain.  Then the $(m-1)$th power of $Q$ is a positive matrix,  that is,  
$$
Q^{m-1} >0.
$$
This implies that $Q$ itself is regular. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Prp 35 of arXiv:2511.21496, 'Optimal local central limit theorems on Wiener chaos'] Let $k \in \N_0$ and $M \in \N$. 
Take $p,q \in (1,\infty)$ such that $s_{k+M} = s_{k+M}[p,q] > 1$, where $\{s_i\}_{i \in \N}$ is defined by \eqref{def s_j}. 
Assume that $F \in \bW^{\infty}$ and $\Delta_F^{-1} \in L^q(\Omega)$.
Then, for every $j \in \{0, \ldots, k\}$ and $a \in \R$, we have
\begin{align}
    \rho^{(j)}_{\cN}(a) - \rho^{(j)}_{F}(a)
    &= \sum_{i=0}^{M-1} \frac{\kappa_{i+1}(F)}{i!}\dpair{\bW^{-j-i, s_{j+i}}}{(\sD^{i}f_{a,j})(F)}{1}{\bW^{j+i, s_{j+i}'}}\\
    &\quad + \dpair{\bW^{-j-M, s_{j+M}}}{(\sD^{M}f_{a,j})(F)}{\Gamma_M(F)}{\bW^{j+M, s_{j+M}'}}\\
    &\quad - \dpair{\bW^{-j-1, s_{j+1}}}{(\sD f_{a,j})(F)}{1}{\bW^{j+1,s_{j+1}'}},
\end{align}
where $\dpair{\bW^{0, s_0}}{f_{a,0}(F)}{1}{\bW^{0,s_0'}}$ is understood as $\E[f_{a,0}(F)]$.
In particular, if in addition $\E[F] = 0$ and $\E[F^2] = 1$, then $\kappa_1(F) = 0$ and $\kappa_2(F) = 1$, and consequently  
\begin{align}
    \rho^{(j)}_{\cN}(a) - \rho^{(j)}_{F}(a) 
    &= \sum_{i=2}^{M-1} \frac{\kappa_{i+1}(F)}{i!}\dpair{\bW^{-j-i, s_{j+i}}}{(\sD^{i}f_{a,j})(F)}{1}{\bW^{j+i, s_{j+i}'}}\\
    &\quad + \dpair{\bW^{-j-M, s_{j+M}}}{(\sD^{M}f_{a,j})(F)}{\Gamma_M(F)}{\bW^{j+M, s_{j+M}'}}.
\end{align}

For every fixed c>0, the maximum-cut size divided by n converges in probability to a deterministic constant H(c) in the independent-edge-endpoint multigraph with floor(cn) edges. H is nondecreasing and 1-Lipschitz in c. For each fixed integer d>=1, MaxCut/n also converges in probability to a deterministic constant in the d-regular configuration model along nd even, and hence in the uniform simple labelled d-regular graph. The sparse simple Erdos-Renyi graph G(n,d/n) has the same limit as the fixed-edge model at c=d/2: couple edge counts and use that changing one edge changes MaxCut by at most one. These results prove existence, not the value of the fixed-degree limit.
c>0 fixed in the fixed-edge model
d>=1 fixed integer in the regular model and nd even
For G(n,d/n), d>0 fixed and n large enough that d/n<=1

[Lem 6 of arXiv:2607.06242, 'Exponential mixing and Freidlin--Wentzell large deviation principle for Markov cocycles'] Let $(\Sigma,\theta,m)$ be an ergodic measure preserving dynamical system. Suppose that $A,F>0$ are measurable, $\log A\in L^1, \log^+F\in L^1$, and 
      \[\int_\Sigma \log A(\s)m(d\s)<\log q\]
      for some $q\in(0,1)$. Then
      \[N(\sigma):=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}q^{-(n+1)}
      F(\theta^n\sigma)\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}A(\theta^j\sigma)\]
      is finite for \(m\)-a.e. $\sigma$ and satisfies
      \[qN(\sigma)=F(\sigma)+A(\sigma)N(\theta\sigma).\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition of arXiv:2604.22130, 'Reflected Stochastic Differential Equations Driven by $G$-Brownian Motion with Nonlinear C'] (i) A progressively measurable process $\eta:[0,T]\times \Omega_T\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is called quasi-continuous (q.c. for short), if for each $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a progressively measurable open set $G$ in $[0,T]\times \Omega_T$ such that $\hat{c}(G)<\varepsilon$ and $\eta|_{G^c}$ is continuous.

    Fix $(s,x;t,y)\in\mathbb{R}^{4}_{\uparrow}$ and fix $s',t'$ satisfying $s<s'<t'<t$.
    Define the following $\sigma$-algebras on path space $C([s,t])$:
    \begin{align*}
        \mathcal{G}_{s,s'} \coloneqq  \sigma\left(
            X|_{[s,s']}:X\in C([s,t])
        \right),
        \qquad
        \mathcal{G}_{t',t} \coloneqq  \sigma\left(
            X|_{[t',t]}:X\in C([s,t])
        \right).
    \end{align*}
    Then almost surely,
    for all bounded  measurable functions $F:C([s',t'])\to\mathbb{R}$,  we have
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbb{E}^\xi_{1,(s,x),(t,y)}\left[

            F(X)
        \right]
        \qquad\quad
        \textup{$\mathbb{P}^\xi_{1,(s,x),(t,y)}$-a.s.,}
    \end{align*}

Own work, proof (unaudited), W719-T295-C006 v1. Standard-conditioning specialization for the Target 3 obstruction; neither novelty nor escape is asserted. Let d>=3, m>=1, eta>0, A have iid real N(0,1) entries, x_* a deterministic unit signal, and independently x0~N(0,I_d/d). For f(x)=(1/(4m)) sum_i ((a_i^T x)^2-(a_i^T x_*)^2)^2 run unmodified GD. Put e1=x_*, q0=<e1,x0>, rho0=||x0-q0*e1||, e2=(x0-q0*e1)/rho0, E an orthonormal basis of their perpendicular space, g=A*e1, h=A*e2, B=A*E, zt=A*xt, vt=zt*(zt^2-g^2) coordinatewise, qt=<e1,xt>, pt=<e2,xt>. Excluding null events rho0*||v0||*||B^T v0||=0, define u=v0/||v0||, P=I-u*u^T, w=B^T*u, W=||w||^2, Q=I-w*w^T/W, b=B*w, r=P*b, a=P*v1, L=||a||^2, nu=Q*B^T*v1, gamma=eta*||v0||/m, kappa=-gamma-(eta/m)*(u^T*v1+r^T*v1/W). Observe in order w, then b (equivalently z1), then nu. Let F2=sigma(x0,g,h,w,b), F3=sigma(F2,nu). Conditional on F2, nu has Gaussian law with covariance L*Q. If L>0, B|F3 has mean M3=u*w^T+r*w^T/W+a*nu^T/L and residual law (P-a*a^T/L)*Z*Q for a fresh standard Gaussian matrix Z. Consequently z2|F3 is Gaussian with mean q2*g+p2*h+kappa*b-eta*||nu||^2*a/(m*L) and covariance (eta^2*||nu||^2/m^2)*(P-a*a^T/L). The conditional law of ||nu||^2/L given F2 is chi-square with d-3 degrees of freedom, including the point mass at zero for d=3. If L=0, nu=0 and z2=q2*g+p2*h+kappa*b is already F2-measurable. Thus the next response is in the adaptively chosen direction P*v1; it cannot be omitted merely by citing fresh Gaussian noise. Bounds on accumulated responses and initial-scale overlap fluctuations remain open.

body: [Thmc1 54 (contraction at the nut-type stratum, i.e. zero-section; Theorem \ref{thm:contracting_Q0}) of arXiv:2609.03332, 'Singularity Models of Finite-Time K\"ahler-Ricci Flows'] Let $\widehat{M}$ be the compactification of $(0,\ell) \times P$ such that $Q_0 := N' = N_2 \times \cdots \times N_r$ is adjoined at $\{s = 0\}$, and $Q_\ell := \mathbb{CP}^m \times N'$ is adjoined at $\{s = \ell\}$. Suppose the total volume of $\widehat{M}$ stays positive at the first singular time $T < \infty$, and the singularity occurs at $Q_0$. Let $\mathcal{I}_0$ be the subset of $\{2, \cdots, r\}$ such that $i_0 \in \mathcal{I}_0$ if and only if the $N_{i_0}$-factor of $Q_0$ contracts to a point at $T$. Then, the blow-up limit splits as $( \operatorname{Tot} ( E_{\mathcal{I}_0} ), g_{\mathrm{sol}} ( t ) ) \times \mathbb{C}^k$, where $k = \sum_{i_0 \not\in \mathcal{I}_0,\, i_0 \not= 1} \dim_{\mathbb{C}} N_{i_0}$, $E_{\mathcal{I}_0} = \mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{I}_0}^{\oplus ( m + 1 )} \to \prod_{i_0 \in \mathcal{I}_0} N_{i_0}$ is the vector bundle obtained by restricting the normal bundle of $Q_0 \subset \widehat{M}$ to $\prod_{i_0 \in \mathcal{I}_0} N_{i_0}$, with $c_1 ( \mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{I}_0} ) = - \sum_{i_0 \in \mathcal{I}_0} q_{i_0} [\omega_{i_0}]$, and $g_{\mathrm{sol}}$ is a complete gradient shrinking K\"ahler--Ricci soliton of ansatz form on $\operatorname{Tot} ( E_{\mathcal{I}_0} )$ --- i.e. a higher-rank, multi-factor generalization by Dancer--Wang in \cite{DW2011} of the Feldman--Ilmanen--Knopf shrinker in \cite{FIK}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: contraction at the nut-type stratum, i.e. zero-section; Theorem \ref{thm:contracting_Q0}

[Proposition 65 (Sharp denominator growth) of arXiv:2608.29585, '2608.29585'] For every $d\ge0$, the polynomials
$\gamma_0^{4_1},\ldots,\gamma_d^{4_1}$ form an $R$-basis of the $R$-module of
polynomials in $\Bbbk[Y]$ of degree at most $d$ that take values in $R$
at every node
$Y=Q^n$, $n\ge2$.  The leading coefficient of $\gamma_k^{4_1}(Y)$ is
\begin{equation}
 \frac{(-1)^kQ^{k(k-3)/2}}{(Q;Q)_k}.
\end{equation}
In particular, it has a pole of order $k$ along $Q=1$, so the
quantum-factorial denominator length is unbounded.

[Definition RP of arXiv:2411.06089, '{\Large \bf Averaging principle for semilinear slow-fast rough partial differential equati'] {\rm (Rough Path)} For $\gamma \in (1/3, 1/2]$, a pair $\mathbf{X} =(X, X^2)$ is called $\gamma$-H\"{o}lder rough path $($over $\mathbb R^d)$.
	 If $X \in C^\gamma ([0,T]; \mathbb R^d)$, $X^2 \in C_2^{2\gamma}([0,T]; \mathbb R^d \otimes \mathbb R^d)$ and satisfy Chen's relation
	 \begin{equation}
	 	X^2_{t,s}-X^2_{t,u}-X^2_{u,s}= \delta X_{t,u} \otimes \delta X_{u,s}, ~~\text{for all}~~0\leq s \leq u \leq t \leq T.
	 \end{equation}
Denote by $ \mathscr{C}^\gamma ([0,T]; \mathbb R^d)$ the space of $\gamma$-H\"{o}lder rough paths
and the distance between two $ \gamma$-H\"{o}lder rough paths $\mathbf X=(X, X^2)$ and $\widetilde{\mathbf X}=(\widetilde{X}, \widetilde{X}^2)$ is defined by
$$d_\gamma(\mathbf X,\widetilde{\mathbf X})=|X-\widetilde{X}|_\gamma +|X^2-\widetilde{X}^2|_{2\gamma}.$$
We write $d_\gamma(\mathbf X)=d_\gamma(0, \mathbf X)$ for simplicity.

[Cor 19 of arXiv:2608.30380, 'Morita Induction and Geometric Ideals in $\ell^p$ Roe-Type Algebras'] Let $\{J_\lambda\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ and
$\{I_\lambda\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ be families of closed ideals of
$A$ and $B$, respectively.  Suppose that, for every
$\lambda\in\Lambda$,
\[
 \overline{J_\lambda E^{>}}
 =
 \overline{E^{>}I_\lambda}.
\]
Then
\[
 \Ind_A^B(J_\lambda)=I_\lambda
 \qquad(\lambda\in\Lambda).
\]

Suppose moreover that $\Lambda$ is a partially ordered set and that
the assignments
\[
 \lambda\longmapsto J_\lambda,
 \qquad
 \lambda\longmapsto I_\lambda
\]
are order isomorphisms from $\Lambda$ onto the two respective
families.  Then Morita induction restricts to an order isomorphism
between these families.

If, in addition, $\Lambda$ is a lattice, the two families are
sublattices of the respective ideal lattices, and the above
parametrizations are lattice isomorphisms, then the restricted
induction map is a lattice isomorphism.

[Thm corners_nomarkov_intro of arXiv:2412.05999, 'Non-Archimedean GUE corners and Hecke modules'] Let $t=1/q$, and let $n\ge 1$ be an integer.
\begin{enumerate}[left=0pt]
\item(Alternating case) Let $A_{2n}$ be a random element of $\Alt_{2n}(\mathfrak{o})$ with above-diagonal entries $a_{i,j}, 1 \leq i < j \leq 2n$ i.i.d. and distributed by the additive Haar measure on $\mathfrak{o}$. For $k=1,\ldots,2n$, let $A_k$ be the top-left $k \times k$ submatrix of $A_{2n}$. Then the joint distribution of their singular numbers is given by
\begin{multline}
    \mathbf{P}(\SN^{\alt}(A_2)=\lambda^{(2)},\SN^{\alt}(A_3)=\nu^{(3)},\ldots,\SN^{\alt}(A_{2n})=\lambda^{(2n)}) \\ 
    = \frac{P_{\lambda^{(2)}}(t^{2n-2};t^2)Q_{\lambda^{(2)}/\nu^{(3)}}(t^{3-2n};t^2)P_{\lambda^{(4)}/\nu^{(3)}}(t^{2n-4};t^2)\cdots P_{\lambda^{(2n)}/\nu^{(2n-1)}}(1;t^2)Q_{\lambda^{(2n)}}(t,t^3,\ldots)}{\Pi_{t^2}(1,1,t^2,1,t^2,t^4,\ldots,1,t^2,\ldots,t^{2n-2};t,t^3,\ldots)},
\end{multline}
with the normalizing constant $\Pi_t(\cdots)$ defined in (equation eq: Cauchy kernel of the paper).

\item(Hermitian case) Let $A_n\in\Her_n(\mathfrak{o})$ be random with i.i.d entries above the diagonal, distributed according to the additive Haar measure on $\mathfrak{o}$, and i.i.d entries on the diagonal independent of these, distributed according to the additive Haar measure on $\mathfrak{o}\cap F_0$. Then letting $A_1,\ldots,A_n$ be its top-left submatrices as before, the joint distribution of their singular numbers is given by

\begin{multline}
\mathbf{P}(\SN^{\her}(A_1)=\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\SN^{\her}(A_n)=\lambda^{(n)})=\frac{1}{\Pi}\sum_{\nu^{(1)}\in\Sig_1^+,\ldots,\nu^{(n-1)}\in\Sig_{n-1}^+} P_{\lambda^{(1)}}((-t)^{n-1};-t)
\\\times \left(\prod_{i=1}^{n-1}Q_{\lambda^{(i)}/\nu^{(i)}}(-(-t)^{i+1-n};-t)P_{\lambda^{(i+1)}/\nu^{(i)}}((-t)^{n-i-1};-t)\right)Q_{\lambda^{(n)}}(t,-t^2,\ldots;-t)
\end{multline}
with the normalizing constant $\Pi$ given by 
$$\Pi=\Pi_{-t}(1,1,-t,1,-t,t^2,\ldots,1,-t,\ldots,(-t)^{n-1};t,-t^2,\ldots).$$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm corners_nomarkov_intro of arXiv:2412.05999

A random variable $X: \Omega \to K$ taking values in a real separable Hilbert space $K$ is called Gaussian if for every $v \in K$, the real-valued random variable $\langle X, v \rangle_K$ is Gaussian. $X$ is centered if $\mathbb{E}[\langle X, v \rangle_K] = 0$ for all $v \in K$, and non-degenerate if $\operatorname{Var}(\langle X, v \rangle_K) > 0$ for every $v \neq 0$.
K is a real separable Hilbert space

body:
[Proposition 12 (Consistency of the Lipschitz-case powers) of arXiv:2608.17540, 'Pathwise stability for one-dimensional SDEs driven by Brownian motion and a symmetric stab'] Let $p=\alpha-1\in(0,1)$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \textup{Initial value perturbation.} Let
\[
  X_t=x_0+W_t+Z_t,
  \qquad
  \wt X_t=\wt x_0+W_t+Z_t.
\]
Then
\[
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-\wt X_t|^p=|x_0-\wt x_0|^p.
\]
Thus the initial error exponent $p=\alpha-1$ is exact.

\item \textup{Drift perturbation.} Let
\[
  X_t=bt,
  \qquad
  \wt X_t=\wt b t.
\]
Then
\[
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-\wt X_t|^p=T^p|b-\wt b|^p.
\]
Since $B=T|b-\wt b|$, this is exactly $B^p$.

\item \textup{Brownian diffusion perturbation.} Let
\[
  X_t=aW_t,
  \qquad
  \wt X_t=\wt a W_t.
\]
Then
\[
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-\wt X_t|^p
  =m_p T^{p/2}|a-\wt a|^p,
\]
where $m_p=\E|N(0,1)|^p$. Since $A=T^{1/2}|a-\wt a|$, this is $m_p A^p$.

\item \textup{Stable jump coefficient perturbation.} Let
\[
  X_t=\sigma Z_t,
  \qquad
  \wt X_t=\wt\sigma Z_t.
\]
Then
\[
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-\wt X_t|^p
  =\E|Z_1|^p T^{p/\alpha}|\sigma-\wt\sigma|^p.
\]
Since $S=T^{1/\alpha}|\sigma-\wt\sigma|$, this is $\E|Z_1|^pS^p$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, when $\wt\eta=1$, the powers $|x_0-\wt x_0|^{\alpha-1}$, $B^{\alpha-1}$, $A^{\alpha-1}$ and $S^{\alpha-1}$ agree with the exact scaling of the four elementary perturbation mechanisms.

body: [Lem 26 of arXiv:2605.26664, 'Mixing times for Glauber dynamics of lozenge tilings of the hexagon'] There exists a constant $\varepsilon > 0$ such that, for any $q \in (-\varepsilon, \varepsilon)$ and $a, b, c \in (1-\varepsilon, 1 + \varepsilon)$, the arctic boundary $\mathfrak{A}_{q;a,b,c}$ is a smooth, convex curve, whose curvature is bounded below by a positive constant $\kappa=\kappa(a,b,c)>0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 1 (Pointwise Gaussian majorizing-measure bound) of arXiv:2606.07931, 'Pointwise Complexity for Gaussian Fields:\\Upper Envelopes, Algorithmic Lower Bounds, and '] Assume \(0<R_\ast<\infty\) and \(\Phi_{\mu,\ast}<\infty\). There exists an absolute constant \(C>0\) such that, for every ambient prior \(\mu\in\Delta(T)\), every \(r_0>0\), every \(s_0\in(0,R_\ast]\), and every \(\delta\in(0,1)\), with probability at least \(1-\delta\),
\begin{equation}
\forall x\in T:\qquad
X_x\le C\,\mathcal E_{\mu,r_0,s_0}(x;\delta).
\end{equation}
Consequently, applying the same bound to \(X\) and \(-X\) and taking a union bound, with probability at least \(1-\delta\),
\begin{equation}
\forall x\in T:\qquad
|X_x|\le A_{\mu,r_0,s_0}(x;\delta),
\qquad
A_{\mu,r_0,s_0}(x;\delta):=
C\,\mathcal E_{\mu,r_0,s_0}(x;\delta/2).
\end{equation}
When \(r_0,s_0\) are fixed, we abbreviate \(A_{\mu,r_0,s_0}\) to \(A_\mu\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Pointwise Gaussian majorizing-measure bound

body:
[Prop 7 of arXiv:2607.21759, 'Marchenko--Pastur law for tensor powers of exchangeable unconditional vectors'] Assume $\mathbf X$ is isotropic, exchangeable, unconditional, with the component satisfying $\sup_{n} \E X_1^4 < \infty$. Assume in addition that $\nm{\mathbf X}_2$ and $\nm{\mathbf X}_4$ are both subexponential with uniformly bounded proxy variance $2\sigma^2$, i.e., for $k = 2,4$ and $ \lambda^2 \leq 1/\sigma^2$, \[
    \E\exp\bigl(\lambda (\nm{\mathbf X}_k - \E \nm{ \mathbf X}_k)\bigr) \leq \exp(\lambda^2 \sigma^2).
\] Then given $d = o(n^{1/3})$, we have $\ESD(K_{\PrincipalT}) \wkconv \mu_{\MP(c)}$ with probability $1$. 

    
    
    Assume furthermore that $\nm{\mathbf X}_4$ is sub-Gaussian with uniformly bounded proxy variance $2\sigma^2$, i.e., for all $\lambda \in \R$, \[
        \E\exp\bigl(\lambda (\nm{\mathbf X}_4 - \E \nm{ \mathbf X}_4)\bigr) \leq \exp(\lambda^2 \sigma^2).
    \] Then given $d = o(n^{1/2})$, we have $\ESD(K_{\PrincipalT}) \wkconv \mu_{\MP(c)}$ with probability $1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 7 of arXiv:2607.21759

[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2607.20714, 'High Minima of Gaussian Processes: Overshoots and Minimizer Locations'] Let $B_H$ and $\nu_H$ be as in Example~\ref{ex:fbm}.  Then $\nu_H$ is
the unique optimal measure for the covariance-energy problem on $[a,b], 0< a<b<\infty$.
For $0<H<1/2$, its density $\rho_H$ satisfies
\[
 \inf_{a<t<b}\rho_H(t)>0,\qquad \supp(\nu_H)=[a,b],
\]
and its potential is constant and positive on $[a,b]$.
For every $H\in(0,1)$, the covariance kernel $R_H$ is integrally strictly
positive definite on $[a,b]$.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Transform asymptotics, exact special case, coupling reduction or identifiability check Result: For a stable M/M/1 benchmark let a=P(W>0)=lambda/mu and b=E W=a/(mu-lambda). Inversion gives mu=a/[b*(1-a)] and lambda=a^2/[b*(1-a)]. Empirical busy fraction and mean workload therefore yield a consistent estimator on a fixed sampling grid by ergodicity. Its asymptotic covariance, when the joint CLT holds, is J*Sigma*J^T, where J is the Jacobian of this inversion and Sigma=sum over integer lags of Cov((1{W_0>0},W_0),(1{W_l>0},W_l)). The off-zero lags are part of the information calculation. Check: Substitution of the inverted parameters returns both a and b exactly. At lambda=1,mu=2 one gets a=1/2,b=1/2 and recovers both rates. Treating Sigma as a one-observation variance would discard the dependence at every finite grid spacing. Obstruction: The estimator is a benchmark only. Neither an efficiency bound for general input families nor an estimator attaining it has been proved here.

body: Zorn's lemma: if P is a NONEMPTY partially ordered set in which every chain - every totally ordered subset - has an upper bound in P, then P contains at least one maximal element. Over ZF it is equivalent to the axiom of choice and to the well-ordering theorem; it is the standard tool for existence proofs (maximal ideals, bases of vector spaces, Hahn-Banach).
title: Zorn's lemma

[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2607.22470, 'A Logarithmic Fluctuation Hierarchy for Sequential Interacting Diffusions'] Fix \(n\ge0\) and let \(\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\R^d)\). Set
\[
M_t^{N,n}(\varphi)
:=
\frac1{\sqrt N}\sum_{i=1}^N h_n(i/N)
\int_0^t\nabla\varphi(X_s^i)\cdot\dd B_s^i.
\]
Then
\begin{align}
\langle Y_t^{N,n},\varphi\rangle
&=
\langle Y_0^{N,n},\varphi\rangle
+
\int_0^t
\langle Y_s^{N,n},L_s\varphi\rangle\,\dd s\notag\\
&\quad+
\int_0^t I_s^{N,n}(\varphi)\,\dd s
+
\int_0^t
\mathcal B_s^{N,n}(\varphi)\,\dd s
+
M_t^{N,n}(\varphi),

\end{align}
where
\(L_s\varphi=\frac12\Delta\varphi+
\bigl(b(s,\cdot)+K*\bar\rho_s\bigr)\cdot\nabla\varphi\),
\begin{equation}
I_s^{N,n}(\varphi)
=
\frac1{\sqrt N}
\sum_{i=2}^N
h_n(i/N)
\nabla\varphi(X_s^i)\cdot
(K*(\mu_s^{i-1}-\bar\rho_s))(X_s^i),
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\mathcal B_s^{N,n}(\varphi)
=
-\frac{h_n(1/N)}{\sqrt N}
\nabla\varphi(X_s^1)\cdot(K*\bar\rho_s)(X_s^1).
\end{equation}
Moreover, as \(N\to\infty\),
\begin{equation}
\mathbb E\int_0^T |\mathcal B_s^{N,n}(\varphi)|\,\dd s\to0.
\end{equation}

body:
[Lemma lem:local of arXiv:2609.03448, 'Prime-power Diophantine tuples'] Assume that the triple is not regular.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $p$ is odd, then exactly one of $e,\bar e$ is divisible by $N^2$.
\item If $p=2$ and $r\ge3$, then
\[
 \{v_2(e),v_2(\bar e)\}=\{2,2r-2\}.
\]
In particular, exactly one of $e,\bar e$ is divisible by $N^2/4$.
\end{enumerate}

body:
Let T be an infinite locally finite rooted tree, and let |e| be the depth of the endpoint of e farther from the root. Define br(T)=sup{a>0: inf over root-to-infinity edge cutsets Pi of sum_{e in Pi} a^{-|e|}>0}, and assume br(T)>1. Fix beta>0 and delta>0. Start the walk at the root; at each step choose an incident edge proportionally to its current weight. The weight of e is beta^{-|e|} before its first traversal, and delta beta^{-|e|} thereafter. If 0<beta<=1, the walk is transient for every delta>0. If beta>1, it is transient when delta<(br(T)-1)/(beta-1), and recurrent when delta>(br(T)-1)/(beta-1). No conclusion at equality is asserted. In particular, at delta=1 (no reinforcement) the conductance walk with c(e)=beta^{-|e|} is transient for beta<br(T) and recurrent for beta>br(T), under the stated br(T)>1 hypothesis. Transient means positive probability of never returning to the root; the paper also proves the corresponding almost-sure finite-visit alternative. Source: The branching-ruin number and the critical parameter of once-reinforced random walk on trees, Corollary 6, pp.7-8; proof Section 4, pp.14-15; cutset definition eq. (2.2), p.6.
T infinite, locally finite and rooted
br(T)>1
beta>0
delta>0
edge weights change only after the first traversal

[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2607.13379, 'Quantitative Propagation of Chaos and Fluctuations for Kinetic McKean--Vlasov SDEs with Si'] Let $\mH$ be a separable Hilbert space, let $E$ be a measurable space, and
let $\xi$ be an $E$-valued random variable. For each $m\ge2$, let
$\xi_1,\dots,\xi_m$ be i.i.d. random variables with the same law as
$\xi$. Let $h:E\times E\to \mH$ be a measurable kernel satisfying the two
centering conditions
$$
    \mE h(z,\xi)=0,\qquad
    \mE h(\xi,z')=0
$$
for every frozen pair $z,z'\in E$. Assume that, for some $a>0$ and
$K<\infty$,
$$
    \sup_z\mE\exp\bigl(a\norm{h(z,\xi)}_\mH^2\bigr)
    +
    \sup_{z'}\mE\exp\bigl(a\norm{h(\xi,z')}_\mH^2\bigr)
    \le K .
$$
Then there is a constant $c_0=c_0(a,K)>0$,
independent of $m$, such that, for every $m\ge2$,
\begin{align}
    \mE\exp\left(
        \frac{c_0}m
        \norm{
        \sum_{i\ne j}h(\xi_i,\xi_j)
        }_{\mH}
    \right)
    \le 2 .
\end{align}

[Lemma lower_bound_on_the_expected_total_size_of_worms_hitting_one_vertex of arXiv:2505.07145, 'Nonamenable Poisson zoo'] Let us consider a nonamenable graph $G$ with a subgroup of its automorphisms $\Gamma \leq \mathrm{Aut}(G)$ that acts transitively on $G$. Let $\eta \, : \, \mathbb{N}_{>0} \rightarrow [0,1]$ be a probability mass function and $\mathcal{X} = \sum_{i \in I} \delta_{(x,H)_i} \sim \mathcal{P}_{\eta}^\lambda$.
Given some $R \in \mathbb{N}_{>0}$, a finite connected set $A \subset \subset V(G)$ and a vertex from its exterior boundary, $x \in \partial_{\mathrm{ext}} A$, let us consider
the total occupation measure $\check{ \Sigma }_{A, \{ x\}}^R$ corresponding to the restricted process introduced in (equation eq:point_measure_restricted_to_hit_B_but_not_the_closure_of_A of the paper).
For any $\varepsilon > 0$, with the constant $c(\varepsilon) > 0$ from Corollary~(coro:number_of_steps_and_size_of_trace_of_SRW_are_comparable_on_nonamenable_graphs of the paper), we have
\begin{equation}
	
	\mathbb{E} \big[ \check{ \Sigma }_{A, \{ x \}}^R \big] \geq c(\varepsilon) \cdot
	\lambda \cdot 
	\mathbb{E} \left[ \mathcal{L}^2 \, \mathds{1} \left[ \mathcal{L} \leq R \right] \right] \cdot  
	P_x \left( T_{\overline{A}}^+ = +\infty \right) \cdot 
	\left( P_x \left( T_{\overline{A}}^+ = +\infty \right) - \varepsilon \right),
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal{L}$ denotes a random variable that has law $\eta$.

For fixed n>=2, deterministic initial coordinates x0!=0 and y0, and fixed nonnegative variances s1,s2 with s1+s2>0, consider the fresh-RR common-Hessian finite sum f_i(x,y)=x^2/2+kappa_T*y^2/2+b_i*x+c_i*y with zero-sum linear terms and mean squares s1,s2 fixed across horizons T=nK. Assume kappa_T>=1 and kappa_T*log(T)/T ->0. Set B_T=n(n+1)(s1+kappa_T^2*s2)/48 and H_T=log(T^3/B_T). Every globally optimal constant step obeys T*eta_T/H_T ->1/2 and the optimal last-epoch expected function error is asymptotic to B_T*H_T^3/(8T^3). The result holds over all eta>=0 or over 0<=eta<=c/kappa_T for any fixed c>0. It includes s2=0. If s2>0 and kappa_T=T^alpha, 0<alpha<1, the step constant relative to log T is (3-2alpha)/2 and optimal error is asymptotic to n(n+1)*s2*(3-2alpha)^3*T^(2alpha-3)*log(T)^3/384. This completes a growing-parameter regime of named target 1; no full-row solution or priority claim is made.

Status: proof draft, unaudited. This extends C001's fixed-kappa limit. The exact epoch recursion is settled ground and is not re-proved. No priority claim or full-row solution is asserted.

## Statement

Fix n>=2, deterministic x0!=0 and y0, and s1,s2>=0 with s1+s2>0. For each T=nK, let kappa=kappa_T>=1 and use the target-1 common-Hessian instance

    f_i(x,y)=x^2/2+kappa*y^2/2+b_i*x+c_i*y,
    sum b_i=sum c_i=0, mean b_i^2=s1, mean c_i^2=s2.

The vectors (b_i),(c_i), n and initialization remain fixed. Each epoch has a fresh independent uniform permutation, shared by the two coordinates. No independence between coordinate noises is assumed; the objective has no mixed quadratic term. Suppose

    kappa_T*log(T)/T -> 0.

Put C=n(n+1)/48, B_T=C*(s1+kappa_T^2*s2), and H_T=log(T^3/B_T). Then H_T->infinity. For EVERY global minimizer eta_T of the expected last-epoch objective over eta>=0,

    T*eta_T/H_T -> 1/2,
    min_eta E[F_T(X_K)-F_T*] ~ B_T*H_T^3/(8*T^3).                 (1)

The same result holds if steps are restricted to 0<=eta<=c/kappa_T for any fixed c>0. No uniqueness or unimodality of the optimizer is assumed. This includes noise only on the flat coordinate (s2=0), the literal b_i-only construction in the target, as well as noise on the stiff coordinate.

For s2>0 and kappa_T=T^alpha, 0<alpha<1, (1) becomes

    min error ~ [n(n+1)*s2*(3-2alpha)^3/384]
                  *T^(2alpha-3)*log(T)^3,
    T*eta_T/log T -> (3-2alpha)/2.                              (2)

Thus replacing a fixed kappa by a growing kappa inside C001 while keeping its 3/2 step constant would be incorrect when the stiff-coordinate variance dominates.

## A uniform finite-n variance sandwich

For a coordinate of curvature h>0 and optimum variance s>=0, write a=1-h*eta. The settled recursion gives

    V_h = s/(n-1) * sum_{0<=i<j<n}(a^i-a^j)^2,
    B_h(eta) = (h/2)*eta^2*V_h/(1-a^(2n)),

where B_h is the stationary contribution to the expected objective. If 0<q=h*eta<1, then

    [s*h^2*n(n+1)/48]*eta^3*(1-q)^(2n-4)
       <= B_h(eta)
       <= [s*h^2*n(n+1)/48]*eta^3*(1-q)^(-(2n-1)).             (3)

Proof of (3). Set m=j-i. The identity

    a^i-a^j = q*a^i*sum_{r=0}^{m-1}a^r

lies between m*q*a^(j-1) and m*q. Since j-1<=n-2 and 0<a<1, it therefore lies between m*q*a^(n-2) and m*q. Square and sum; use sum_{i<j}(j-i)^2=n^2(n^2-1)/12. Also

    2n*q*a^(2n-1) <= 1-a^(2n) <= 2n*q.

All denominators are positive. Substituting the lower numerator and upper denominator gives the lower bound in (3); the opposite choices give the upper bound. The case s=0 is identically zero and requires no division by s. The exponent 2n-4 is nonnegative even at n=2.

For the two coordinates, whenever q=kappa*eta<1, summing (3) gives

    B_T*eta^3*(1-q)^(2n-4) <= B_1(eta)+B_kappa(eta)
       <= B_T*eta^3*(1-q)^(-(2n-1)).                           (4)

This uses 1-h*eta>=1-q and nonnegative coefficients; it remains valid when kappa=1, counting both coordinates. The actual finite-horizon variance is the sum of B_h(eta)*(1-(1-h*eta)^(2T)). In this range it is between (1-(1-eta)^(2T)) times the left side of (4) and the right side of (4).

## Global optimization proof

1. There are constants b0,b1>0, depending only on n,s1,s2, such that b0<=B_T<=b1*kappa^2. The assumption kappa*log T/T->0 implies eventually kappa<=T/log T. Hence

       log T + 2log log T - log b1 <= H_T <= 3log T - log b0.

   In particular H_T->infinity, H_T=O(log T), and kappa*H_T/T->0.

2. Use the candidate eta_c=H_T/(2T). Its q_c=kappa*eta_c tends to zero, so (4) applies. The deterministic contribution of the flat coordinate is at most x0^2*exp(-H_T)/2. That of the stiff coordinate is at most kappa*y0^2*exp(-kappa*H_T)/2. For H>=1 and kappa>=1,

       log kappa <= kappa-1 <= (kappa-1)*H,
       kappa*exp(-kappa*H)<=exp(-H).

   Thus the entire deterministic contribution is O(exp(-H_T)), with a constant independent of kappa. Since exp(-H_T)=B_T/T^3, and H_T->infinity, it is negligible relative to B_T*H_T^3/T^3. Equation (4) gives

       inf_eta P_T(eta) <= (1+o(1))*B_T*H_T^3/(8T^3).          (5)

   This tends to zero: B_T<=b1*kappa^2 and kappa*H_T/T->0 imply B_T*H_T^3/T^3 <= b1*(kappa*H_T/T)^2*(H_T/T)->0.

3. Existence of a minimizer holds because the exact error is a continuous coercive polynomial. In any noisy coordinate, the pair (i,j)=(0,1) alone and the final epoch alone give, for ALL eta>=0,

       P_T(eta) >= s*h^3*eta^4/[2(n-1)].                     (6)

   No step-size restriction is used in (6): the geometric variance multiplier is a sum of even powers and is at least one.

4. First suppose s2>0. With q_T=kappa*eta_T, (6) and (5) imply

       q_T^4 <= [2(n-1)/s2]*kappa*P_T(eta_T)
              <= O(kappa*B_T*H_T^3/T^3)
              <= O((kappa*H_T/T)^3) ->0.

   Thus q_T->0 and eta_T->0. If t_T=T*eta_T were bounded along a subsequence, then

       (1-eta_T)^(2T)=exp(-2t_T+O(T*eta_T^2))

   would stay bounded away from zero there. The flat deterministic contribution x0^2/2 times this quantity contradicts the vanishing optimum. Therefore t_T->infinity.

5. If s2=0 instead, s1>0 and B_T=C*s1 is constant. Using h=1 in (6) first gives eta_T->0. The same flat transient argument gives t_T->infinity. For the NOISY FLAT coordinate, (3) with q=eta_T, together with 1-(1-eta_T)^(2T)->1, yields

       P_T(eta_T)>=(1-o(1))*B_T*eta_T^3.

   Combining with (5) gives t_T=O(H_T), hence q_T=kappa*t_T/T->0 by step 1. This argument does not presuppose small q_T for the stiff coordinate.

6. Now in either case q_T->0 and t_T->infinity. The finite-horizon sandwich following (4) gives

       total variance = (1+o(1))*B_T*t_T^3/T^3.               (7)

   Its error is uniform along ANY sequence of minimizers: the factors in (4) depend only on q_T and fixed n, and the finite-horizon factor is at least 1-exp(-2t_T)->1. From (5) and (7), t_T=O(H_T). Thus T*eta_T^2=O(H_T^2/T)->0, and the flat transient equals

       A*exp(-2t_T+o(1)), A=x0^2/2>0.

   Comparing it with (5), and using B_T/T^3=exp(-H_T), gives

       2t_T >= H_T-3log H_T-O(1).

   Hence liminf t_T/H_T>=1/2. Equations (5) and (7) give limsup t_T/H_T<=1/2. Substitution into (7) and comparison with the candidate upper bound prove (1).

7. For the capped interval eta<=c/kappa, the candidate is eventually admissible since kappa*eta_c->0. Coercivity is replaced by compactness, and all lower bounds remain valid, so the same proof gives (1). Formula (2) follows from B_T~n(n+1)*s2*T^(2alpha)/48 and H_T~(3-2alpha)log T.

## Returning to an arbitrary fixed mu>0

Apply the theorem to f_i/mu with curvatures 1,kappa=L/mu, variances s1/mu^2,s2/mu^2, and normalized step mu*eta. Then

    B'_T=n(n+1)*(s1+kappa^2*s2)/(48mu^2),
    H'_T=log(T^3/B'_T),
    mu*T*eta_T/H'_T ->1/2,
    min original error ~ n(n+1)*(s1+kappa^2*s2)*(H'_T)^3/(384mu*T^3).

Here mu, n, s1, s2 and the initial point are fixed; only kappa grows. No assertion is made when kappa*log T/T fails to tend to zero, when n grows, or when x0=0. [Theorem 26 of arXiv:2605.25715, '2605.25715'] Let
\[
G=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\ c&d\end{pmatrix},\qquad
A=\begin{pmatrix}\alpha&\beta\\ \beta&\gamma\end{pmatrix}
\quad(\alpha>0,\ \delta:=\det A=\alpha\gamma-\beta^{2}>0).
\]
Then, there exists a symmetric matrix $S=\begin{pmatrix}s_{11}& s_{12}\\ s_{12}& s_{22}\end{pmatrix}$ satisfying \eqref{SOHHDlinalg1}, and given as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)]
If $\gamma b -\alpha c + \beta(a-d) =0$, then $S = A^{-1}G$, and in particular,
\[
s_{11} = \frac{\gamma a - \beta c}{\alpha\gamma - \beta^2}, \qquad
s_{12} = \frac{\gamma b - \beta d}{\alpha\gamma - \beta^2}, \qquad
s_{22} = \frac{\alpha d - \beta b}{\alpha\gamma - \beta^2}.
\]

\item[(ii)]
If $a+d=0$, then $S=0$, that is,
\[
s_{11} = 0, \qquad s_{12} = 0, \qquad s_{22} = 0.
\]

\item[(iii)] If $a+d \neq 0$ and $\gamma b- \alpha c + \beta(a-d) \neq 0$, then
\begin{align*}
s_{11} &= \frac{a+d}{ (\alpha \gamma-\beta^2) (a+d)^2 +\big( \gamma b - \alpha c + \beta(a-d)\big)^2} \Big( \gamma a(a+d) + \alpha c^2 - \gamma bc - 2\beta ac \Big), \\[8pt]
s_{12} &= \frac{a+d}{ (\alpha \gamma-\beta^2) (a+d)^2 +\big( \gamma b - \alpha c + \beta(a-d)\big)^2} \Big( \alpha cd + \gamma ab - 2\beta ad \Big), \\[8pt]
s_{22} &= \frac{a+d}{ (\alpha \gamma-\beta^2) (a+d)^2 +\big(\gamma b - \alpha c + \beta(a-d)\big)^2} \Big(\alpha d(a+d) + \gamma b^2 - \alpha bc - 2\beta bd \Big).
\end{align*}
\end{itemize}
title: Theorem 26 of arXiv:2605.25715

\[
q^{AMF2}_i(0) \sim q^{(MF1,1)}_i(0)

\mathbb{E}\bigl[q^{AMF2}_i(0)\bigr] < \infty.

Q^{AMF2} \leq_{st} Q^{(MF1,1)}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition prop:cdbm-properties of arXiv:2507.12502, 'Quantitative Edge Eigenvector Universality for Random Regular Graphs: Berry-Esseen Bounds '] The constrained Dyson Brownian motion satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Constraint preservation.} If $\tilde{H}_0\mathbf{e} = 0$, then $\tilde{H}_t\mathbf{e} = 0$ for all $t \geq 0$ [biane2004littelmann,journee2010low].
\item \emph{Invariant measure.} The stationary distribution is the constrained GOE ensemble on $\mathcal{M}_0$.
\item \emph{Eigenvalue evolution.} The eigenvalues $\lambda_i(t)$ evolve by non-intersecting diffusions with drift toward the origin [grabiner1999brownian,katori2004symmetry].
\item \emph{Eigenvector dynamics.} For $i \geq 2$, the eigenvector $\mathbf{u}_i(t)$ remains orthogonal to $\mathbf{e}$ for all $t$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Properties of CDBM

body:
[Prop 16 (Airy-time coefficient and the row-column correlation window) of arXiv:2608.15137, '2608.15137'] Let $p,q,P,Q$ be positive integers satisfying
\[
 p\leq q,\qquad P\leq Q,\qquad p\leq P,\qquad q\leq Q.
\]
Put
\[
 A=P-p,\qquad B=Q-q,\qquad r_0=q-p,\qquad r=Q-P.
\]
For $0\leq n\leq m$, define
\[
 \varphi_{n,m}(x)
 =
 \sqrt{\frac{n!}{m!}}\,
 \ee^{-x/2}x^{(m-n)/2}L_n^{(m-n)}(x).
\]
For $1\leq\ell\leq p$, define
\[
 c_\ell
 =
 \sqrt{
 \frac{(P-\ell)!(Q-\ell)!}
 {(p-\ell)!(q-\ell)!}
 }.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 &\sum_{\ell=1}^p
 \frac{(P-\ell)!}{(q-\ell)!}
 L_{P-\ell}^{(r)}(x)L_{p-\ell}^{(r_0)}(y)\\
 &\quad=
 \ee^{(x+y)/2}x^{-r/2}y^{-r_0/2}
 \sum_{\ell=1}^p
 c_\ell
 \varphi_{P-\ell,Q-\ell}(x)
 \varphi_{p-\ell,q-\ell}(y).
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
Moreover, with
\[
 c_0=\sqrt{\frac{P!Q!}{p!q!}},
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
 \frac{c_\ell}{c_0}
 =
 \left\{
 \prod_{h=0}^{\ell-1}
 \frac{(p-h)(q-h)}{(P-h)(Q-h)}
 \right\}^{1/2}.
\end{equation}

Define
\[
 \delta_{p,q}
 =
 \frac{(\sqrt p+\sqrt q)^{2/3}}{(pq)^{1/3}},
 \qquad
 \tau_{p,q;A,B}
 =
 \frac{A/p+B/q}{2\delta_{p,q}}.
\]
Fix $c_{\mathrm{box}}>0$ and $C_{\mathrm{box}}<\infty$. There is a constant $C$ depending only on them such that, whenever
\[
 c_{\mathrm{box}}N\leq p,q\leq C_{\mathrm{box}}N,
 \qquad
 A+B\leq\frac{c_{\mathrm{box}}N}{4},
 \qquad
 1\leq\ell\leq\frac{c_{\mathrm{box}}N}{2},
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
 \left|
 \log\frac{c_\ell}{c_0}
 +
 \tau_{p,q;A,B}\delta_{p,q}\ell
 \right|
 \leq
 C\frac{(A+B)\ell^2+(A^2+B^2)\ell}{N^2}.
\end{equation}
If $D_N>0$ satisfies
\[
 \frac{\log D_N}{\log N}\to0,
 \qquad
 A+B\leq N^{2/3}D_N,
 \qquad
 \ell\leq N^{1/3}D_N,
\]
then uniformly over these $\ell$,
\begin{equation}
 \frac{c_\ell}{c_0}
 =
 \exp(-\tau_{p,q;A,B}\delta_{p,q}\ell)(1+o(1)).
\end{equation}
If
\[
 \frac pN\to a>0,\qquad
 \frac qN\to b>0,\qquad
 \frac A{N^{2/3}}\to\alpha,\qquad
 \frac B{N^{2/3}}\to\beta,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
 \tau_{p,q;A,B}
 \longrightarrow
 \frac{\alpha/a+\beta/b}{2d_{a,b}},
 \qquad
 d_{a,b}
 =
 \frac{(\sqrt a+\sqrt b)^{2/3}}{(ab)^{1/3}}.
\end{equation}
Thus $\tau$ tends to zero when $A+B=o(N^{2/3})$, remains of order one when $A+B$ is of order $N^{2/3}$, and tends to infinity when
\[
 \frac{A+B}{N^{2/3}}\to\infty,
 \qquad
 A+B=o(N).
\]

For the nested rectangles $(M_N,N)$, assume
\[
 \frac{M_N}{N}\to\gamma\in(0,\infty),
 \qquad
 0\leq M_{N+1}-M_N\leq K.
\]
Compare $(M_N,N)$ with $(M_{N+H},N+H)$, where $1\leq H=o(N)$, and sort their dimensions into $(p,q)$ and $(P,Q)$. Then there are constants $0<c<C<\infty$, depending only on $\gamma$ and $K$, such that
\begin{equation}
 c\frac{H}{N^{2/3}}
 \leq
 \tau_{p,q;P-p,Q-q}
 \leq
 C\frac{H}{N^{2/3}}
\end{equation}
for all sufficiently large $N$.
title: Airy-time coefficient and the row-column correlation window

[Prop 8 of arXiv:2603.27433, 'The $k$-cycle shuffling with repeated cards'] Suppose that $r:=n-\l_1\in[n^{5/6},0.499n]$. Furthermore, suppose $2\le k\le 6\log n$. Moreover, suppose that $t':=t-\frac{n\log n}{k}$ satisfies $|t'|\le \frac{n(\log\log n-\omega(1))}{2k}$. Then, for sufficiently large $n$, we have
$$|s_\l(k)|^{2t}\le\exp(-2r\log n+(2/3+o(1))r\log r).$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Let X_1..X_4 be independent with densities at most 1, S_1 = X_1 + X_2, S_2 = X_3 + X_4, and let u, v be the orthonormal pair (1,1,1,1)/2, (1,1,-1,-1)/2 rotated by the angle theta with tan theta = sqrt 2, so that every coordinate has u_i^2 + v_i^2 = 1/2. Then U = <u, X>, V = <v, X> are linear combinations of the independent S_1, S_2 with determinant -1/2, and the pair argument (condition on nothing; the two quadratic curves along the parabola have separated critical points) bounds the density of U + cV^2 by 8 for every real c and all laws. For comb laws (each X_i uniform on N teeth [j, j + 1/N]) the maximal functional M_2 = int sup_u rho_{U,V}(u, v) dv grows linearly in N, because the coefficient ratio of V is the quadratic irrational (1 + sqrt 2)^2 and the lines V = v meet a bump of height at least 1/18 for a set of v of measure of order N. Consequence for the bounded-density quadratic-form conjecture: the leverage (spread) condition does not make maximal functionals bounded, so the curved-slice statements (CS), (VD), (P2) must use the curvature of the section.

body:
[Theorem 21 of arXiv:2609.03098, 'Standing waves for Schr\"odinger equations with Kato class potentials and $L^\infty$-bound'] Let $F$ be the mapping given by \eqref{Nemytzki_f}, and let $W\subset H^1(\R^N)$ be bounded in $L^\infty(\R^N)$. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item[$(i)$] If the condition $(LL)_+$ holds, then there exist $R > 0$ and $\nu>0$ such that 
$$
\langle F(v + w), v\rangle_{L^2} > \nu
$$
for all $w\in W$ and $v\in X_0$ with $\|v\|_{L^2} \ge R$.
\item[$(ii)$] If the condition $(LL)_-$ holds, then there exist $R > 0$ and $\nu>0$ such that
$$
\langle F(v + w), v\rangle_{L^2} < -\nu
$$
for all $w\in W$ and $v\in X_0$ with $\|v\|_{L^2} \ge R$.
\end{enumerate}

Let $u_{\theta,x_0}^\Psi$ be the mild solution of \eqref{PDE1Psi} with $\psi_R$ replaced by $\psi_{R,x_0}$. It is the log-Laplace cumulant associated with the weighted occupation time
$$
\theta\int_0^t\langle \psi_{R,x_0},X_s\rangle\dd s.
$$
Since $\overline{B(x_0,R)}\subset \overline{B(0,L)}$, Condition \ref{con_localize} gives
$$
\Psi(x,u)\geq \Phi_L(u),
\qquad x\in\overline{B(x_0,R)},\quad u\geq0.
$$
The shifted version of the local parabolic barrier in Lemma \ref{le:localBarrierPsi} gives
$$
0\leq u_{\theta,x_0}^\Psi(x,t)\leq u_{R,\Phi_L}(|x-x_0|),
\qquad x\in B(x_0,R),\quad t\geq0.
$$

and
\[

[Proposition P:CQCLT of arXiv:2606.23865, 'Uniform-in-time Gaussian fluctuations for multiscale nonlinear stochastic systems via Mall'] [bour_spilio_2025]
Let $T>0$ be fixed, $\theta_t^\varepsilon \triangleq \frac{X_t^\varepsilon-\bar{X}_t}{\sqrt{\varepsilon}}$ and $N \sim \mathscr{N}(0, \sigma_t^2).$ For sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ and $\eta,$ and $0<\xi < \frac{1}{2},$ there exists a time-dependent positive constant $C$ such that
\begin{multline*}
\sup_{t \in [0,T]}d_W \left( \theta_t^\varepsilon,N \right) \le C \left[ \eta^{\frac{1}{4}} + \varepsilon^{\frac{1}{4}} + \left( \frac{\eta}{\varepsilon}- \frac{1}{\gamma^2} \right)^{\frac{1}{2}}  + \left( \frac{\eta}{\varepsilon} \right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \eta^{\frac{1}{2}-\xi} + \varepsilon^{\frac{1}{2}-\xi} \right]\\
+ C \left( \left( \frac{\eta}{\varepsilon} \right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \eta^{\frac{1}{4}} + \left( \frac{\eta}{\varepsilon} \right) \eta^{\frac{1}{4}} + \left( 1+ \frac{\eta}{\varepsilon} \right)e^{-\frac{CT}{\eta}} \right).
\end{multline*}
where, $\sigma_t^2$ represents the limiting variance and is defined in equation (equation E:Limiting-Variance of the paper) below. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 25 of arXiv:2608.19976, 'Random valuations'] Let $\Phi$ be a $\sigma$-continuous non-negative stationary
  isotropic ID valuation with independent increments and vanishing
  deterministic part. Then there exist a non-negative infinitely
  divisible random variable $\xi$ and independent non-negative
  stationary isotropic ID valuations $\Psi_m$, $m=1,\dots,d$, with
  independent increments, such that
  \begin{displaymath}
    \Psi(K)
    =
    \xi\1_{K\neq\emptyset}
    +
    \sum_{m=1}^d\Psi_m(K),
    \qquad K\in\Kd,
  \end{displaymath}
  is weakly equivalent to $\Phi$. Moreover, $\Psi_m$ is
  $m$-stable in argument for every $m=1,\dots,d$.
  
  More precisely, there exist non-negative measures
  $b_0,\dots,b_d$ on $(0,\infty)$ satisfying \eqref{eq:theta-levy}
  such that
  \begin{equation}
    
    \nu(\sC_K\times A)
    =
    \sum_{m=0}^d V_m(K)b_m(A),
    \qquad K\in\Kd,
  \end{equation}
  for every Borel $A\subset(0,\infty)$, where
  $V_0(K)=\1_{K\neq\emptyset}$.
title: Theorem 25 of arXiv:2608.19976

[Lemma lem:square of arXiv:2609.03676, 'Quadratic Scalar Curvature Decay and Uniform Positivity in Dimensions Four through Seven'] Let $X\in L^\infty(TW)$ with $\operatorname{div} X\in L^\infty(W)$. Then for every $u\in H^1(W)$,
\begin{align}
  E_g(u)
  ={}&\frac{4(n-1)}{n-2}\int_W|\nabla u+Xu|^2\,dV_g\notag\\
  &+\int_W\bigl(R_g+\frac{4(n-1)}{n-2}(\operatorname{div} X-|X|^2)\bigr)u^2\,dV_g\notag\\
  &+\int_{\partial W}\bigl(2H_g-\frac{4(n-1)}{n-2}[X,\nu]\bigr)u^2\,dA_g.
  
\end{align}

[Lemma 129 (Finite-seminorm local functional calculus) of arXiv:2606.29292, 'Intrinsic Gaussian Tensor Geometry and Random Operator Spectra'] Let $I\Subset(0,\infty)$ be a compact interval.  Fix integers
$A\ge1$ and $s_-,s_+,B\ge0$ with $A\ge s_-+s_+$.  There is an integer
$K_{\mathrm{fc}}$ such that, for every chart $\nu$, every $0<h\le1$, and
every $\vartheta_h\in\mathscr X_I$, the symbols
\[
  a_{\nu,\ell,h}:=a_{\nu,\ell}[\vartheta_h]
\]
and the remainder
$\mathcal R_{\nu,A,h}:=\mathcal R_{\nu,A,h}[\vartheta_h]$ satisfy
\begin{equation}

  (\chi_\nu\vartheta_h(P_h)u)\circ\varkappa_\nu
  =\sum_{\ell=0}^{A-1}h^\ell
       a_{\nu,\ell,h}(z,hD_z)
       ((\widetilde\chi_\nu u)\circ\varkappa_\nu)
    +\mathcal R_{\nu,A,h}u
\end{equation}
for $u\in C^\infty(M)$, and
\begin{align}

 &\max_{0\le\ell<A}
   \max_{|\alpha|+|\beta|\le B}
   \sup_{z,\xi}
   |\partial_z^\alpha\partial_\xi^\beta
       a_{\nu,\ell,h}(z,\xi)|
 \le C_{\mathrm{fc}}p_{K_{\mathrm{fc}}}(\vartheta_h),\\

 &\|\mathcal R_{\nu,A,h}u\|_{H^{s_+}(\R^d)}
 \le C_{\mathrm{fc}}h^{A-s_--s_+}
       p_{K_{\mathrm{fc}}}(\vartheta_h)
       \|u\|_{H^{-s_-}(M)}.
\end{align}
The integer $K_{\mathrm{fc}}$ and the constant $C_{\mathrm{fc}}$ may depend
on $A,s_-,s_+,B,I$, the fixed atlas and cutoffs, and $(M,g)$, but not on
$\nu,h$, or $\vartheta_h$.  Moreover,
\begin{equation}

  \operatorname{supp}a_{\nu,\ell,h}
  \subset
  \bigl\{(z,\xi):
     \varkappa_\nu(z)\in\operatorname{supp}\chi_\nu,
     \ p_\nu(z,\xi)\in\operatorname{supp}\vartheta_h\bigr\}.
\end{equation}
In particular, the symbols are supported in a fixed compact subset of
$U_\nu\times\{\xi:c_I\le|\xi|\le C_I\}$.
title: Finite-seminorm local functional calculus

[Theorem thm:regularity-deweighting of arXiv:2608.16119, 'Fully nonlinear parabolic equations under a fixed reference diffusion: weighted \texorpdfs'] Let $w$ be a regular weight of order $\alpha$, where $0\leq\alpha<1$.  Assume
Assumptions~(ass:reference-diffusion of the paper),
(ass:drift-multiplier of the paper), (ass:lipschitz-driver of the paper), and
(ass:differentiable-driver of the paper) at the same order $\alpha$.  Suppose
$C_w(X)<\infty$, $\delta_{\mathrm{sg}}>0$, $\psi\in H^2(\mu_T)$, and
$f_0\in L_0^2$.  Then the unique order-$\alpha$ weighted Sobolev solution
$u^*$ and its source $F^*=F_{u^*}$ satisfy
\begin{equation}
 u^*,D_xu^*,D_x^2u^*,F^*
 \in L_0^2.
 
\end{equation}
The following estimate holds with
$C=C\bigl(T,\lambda,\Lambda,M_1(a),\operatorname{osc}_\alpha(w),C_w(X),
\Lambda_b,L_x^{\mathrm{gr}},\mathbf L_f,
\delta_{\mathrm{sg}}^{-1}\bigr)>0$:
\begin{equation}
 \left\lVert F^*\right\rVert_0+\sum_{j=0}^2\left\lVert D_x^ju^*\right\rVert_0
 \leq C\left(1+\sqrt{\frac{T^{1-\alpha}}{1-\alpha}}\right)
 \left[\left\lVert m_x\right\rVert_\alpha
 +\max\{1,T^{\alpha/2}\}
   \left(\left\lVert f_0\right\rVert_0+\norm\psi_{H^2(\mu_T)}\right)\right].
 
\end{equation}
The coefficient bounds also give $\mathsf Z u^*,\mathsf G u^*\in L_0^2$, and $u^*$ is
the unique unweighted Sobolev solution.
title: Theorem thm:regularity-deweighting of arXiv:2608.16119

[Lemma 28 (Support of $\bd_k^{(j)}$ and $\bu_k^{(j)}$) of arXiv:2608.28991, 'Jigsaw-CRL: Recovering Global Latent Causal Order from Fragmented Multi-Client Interventio'] Under the setup of Proposition~\ref{prop:margin Z}, for each client $k\in[K]$ and intervention $j\in\cJ_k$ targeting $t_j\in O_k$, let $r=\rho_k(t_j)$. Then the vectors $\bd_k^{(j)}$ and $\bu_k^{(j)}$ defined in Assumption~\ref{ass:non-degeneracy} satisfy
\[
\supp(\bd_k^{(j)}) \subseteq \rho_k\bigl(pa_k(t_j)\bigr),
\qquad
\supp(\bu_k^{(j)}) \subseteq \rho_k\bigl(sp_k(t_j)\bigr).
\]
Equivalently, for any $v\in O_k$,
\[
v\notin pa_k(t_j)\quad \Longrightarrow\quad [\bd_k^{(j)}]_{\rho_k(v)}=0,
\qquad
v\notin sp_k(t_j)\quad \Longrightarrow\quad [\bu_k^{(j)}]_{\rho_k(v)}=0.
\]

[Definition 5 ($\Omega$-isotypic summand) of arXiv:2609.03736, '2609.03736'] For $\Omega\subset\Irr(\mathsf G)$ let $z_\Omega$ be the central projection
onto the corresponding isotypic summands and put
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal I_{E,\Omega}=z_\Omega\mathcal I_E,
 \qquad
 \mathcal H_{E,\Omega}
 =\End_{\mathsf G}(\mathcal I_{E,\Omega})
 \cong z_\Omega\mathcal H_Ez_\Omega
 =\bigoplus_{\pi\in\Omega}\End(M_\pi).
 
\end{equation}
Because $z_\Omega$ is central, $\mathcal H_{E,\Omega}$ is a central direct
summand of $\mathcal H_E$, with unit $z_\Omega$.  Equivalently, it is the
Hecke algebra of the $\Omega$-isotypic submodule $\mathcal I_{E,\Omega}$.

[Prop dimension-free-identity of arXiv:2608.30847, 'An Almgren-type formula for planar $p$-harmonic functions'] Assume that $u$ is smooth and $Du\neq 0$ in an annulus containing
$\partial B_r(x_0)$. Then
$$
  D'(r)=\frac{n-p}{r}D(r)+pG(r),
$$
and
$$
   H'(r) = \frac{n-1}{r}H(r)+2D(r)+K(r).
$$
Consequently, at every such radius for which $H(r)>0$,
$$
  N_\ast'(r)+N_\ast(r)\Theta(r)  =  \frac{pr}{H(r)}
 \int_{\partial B_r(x_0)}  A \left(  \partial_\nu u-\frac{N_\ast(r)}{r}v \right)^2   \,dS .
$$
In particular,
$$
  N_\ast'(r)+N_\ast(r)\Theta(r)\ge 0.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop dimension-free-identity of arXiv:2608.30847

For independent bond percolation on the infinite d-regular tree with d>=3, p_c=1/(d-1), theta(p)=0 for p<=p_c, and theta(p)=[2d(d-1)/(d-2)](p-p_c)+O((p-p_c)^2) as p decreases to p_c from above. The positive descendant-survival solution u obeys 1-u=(1-pu)^(d-1); division by u and the implicit-function theorem give the expansion, and theta=1-(1-pu)^d. This is an exact tree analogue, not a high-dimensional lattice solution.

The intake route writes beta=gamma-Delta while substituting gamma=1 and Delta=2; that displayed subtraction cannot produce beta=1. We do not accept the claimed equivalence or differentiation of a singular limit as proved.

For bond percolation on the infinite d-regular tree, d>=3, p_c=1/(d-1) and

    theta(p) = [2d(d-1)/(d-2)] (p-p_c)+O((p-p_c)^2).

Let k=d-1 and u be the probability that a vertex with its parent edge removed has an infinite descendant cluster. It solves 1-u=(1-pu)^k. For p>1/k it is the positive branching-process survival solution. Dividing by u and expanding gives kp-1=binom(k,2)p^2 u+O(u^2). The divided equation has nonzero u derivative at (u,p)=(0,1/k), so its positive branch is analytic. With epsilon=p-1/k, u=2k^2 epsilon/(k-1)+O(epsilon^2), and theta=1-(1-pu)^d gives the claimed coefficient. This is a tree analogue, not a proof on Z^d. Nine small numerical checks for d=3,4,8 approach the predicted slopes.

Bounded-ratio exponent information and monotonicity alone are insufficient: F(epsilon)=epsilon(2+sin(log epsilon)), epsilon>0 small, lies between epsilon and 3epsilon and is strictly increasing because F'=2+sin(log epsilon)+cos(log epsilon)>=2-sqrt(2)>0. Nevertheless F(epsilon)/epsilon has no limit, while log F/log epsilon ->1. A lattice-percolation proof therefore needs an additional mechanism ruling out oscillation; this example is not a percolation counterexample.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:077cf63b0b28a58efb68f5be0ce6751bb5a7b70b5be125f907444102f63f36ea","revision_digest":"sha256:385eb1eea1dbc07806be0af7ddaf128d0ab39ce0fe0b86ae374635904d5deffa","source_id":"owner-w344-open-problems-20261010:regular-tree-percolation-linear-critical-amplitude","source_revision":"2026-10-10 worker result; proof; independent audit pending w346; novelty unverified","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2609.02169, '2609.02169'] Let $S$ be a complex abelian surface.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item Every effective divisor on $S$ is nef.
\item If $N$ is nef and $N^2>0$, then $N$ is ample,
      $H^i(S,N)=0$ for $i>0$, and
      $h^0(S,N)=\chi(N)=N^2/2$.
\item If $N$ is nonzero and effective with $N^2=0$, there are an elliptic
      quotient $q:S\to C$,
      a line bundle $N_0$ of positive degree $r$ on the elliptic curve
      $C$, and an elliptic fiber class $F$ such that
      $N\simeq q^*N_0$, $N\equiv rF$, and $h^0(S,N)=r$.
\item If $H$ is a polarization and $F\subset S$ is an elliptic curve with
      $H\cdot F=1$, then $S$ is isomorphic to a product of two elliptic
      curves.
\end{enumerate}

[Proposition 12 of arXiv:2607.29534, 'Expected signatures via partial integration, coordinate change and symmetrization'] For $w,v\in\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{A}}$,
$r,q\in\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{A}^{\prime\prime}}$, and
$\blue{i},\blue{j}\in\mathcal{A}^{\prime}$,
\begin{equation}
\left\{\begin{aligned}
r\gammashuffle q
&=
r\shuffle q,
\\
(w\blue{i}r)\gammashuffle q
&=
w\blue{i}(r\shuffle q),
\\
r\gammashuffle(v\blue{j}q)
&=
v\blue{j}(r\shuffle q),
\\
(w\blue{i}r)\gammashuffle(v\blue{j}q)
&=
\bigl((w\blue{i})\gammashuffle v\bigr)
\blue{j}(r\shuffle q)
+
\bigl(w\gammashuffle(v\blue{j})\bigr)
\blue{i}(r\shuffle q).
\end{aligned}\right.
\end{equation}
These identities uniquely determine $\gammashuffle$.

[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2608.22636, 'Q-Learning with Stable Infinite-Dimensional \\Linear Function Approximation'] Fix real numbers $\alpha\ge 1$ and $T>0$, and integers $n\ge0$ and $n_0>0$.  Set $\alpha_k=\alpha/(k+n_0)$,
$\tau(n,m)=\sum_{k=n}^{m-1}\alpha_{k+1}$, and
$\cW(n,T)=\setcond{m\ge n}{\tau(n,m)\le T}$.  Then, for every $m\in\cW(n,T)$,
\begin{equation}
        m+n_0+1
        \le
        e^{T/\alpha}(n+n_0+1).
        
\end{equation}

If $m_\vee=\max\cW(n,T)$ and $\alpha_{n+1}\le T/2$, then the end time satisfies
\begin{equation}
        \frac{T}{2}
        \le
        \tau(n,m_\vee)
        \le
        T.
        
\end{equation}

If either $T=1/4$ and $n+n_0\ge8$, or
$T=1/5$ and $n+n_0\ge10$, then
\begin{equation}
        m+n_0
        \le
        \frac32(n+n_0),
        \quad \forall m\in\cW(n,T).
        
\end{equation}

Let f be a smooth convex transpose-invariant real matrix loss, with sufficient differentiability for the local flow theorem (C-infinity suffices), and suppose its PSD flow Phi satisfies Wprime=-W grad f(W)-grad f(W) W and is defined at all real times. Let Wbar be a critical point, a local minimum of f on PSD matrices of rank at most r, r>=1, but not a global PSD minimum. Write the eigenvalues of -grad f(Wbar) as mu1>=mu2>=... and assume mu1>mu2 (then mu1>0); let v1 be a unit top eigenvector. For PSD initial matrices Walpha suppose arrival times Talpha give Ealpha=Phi(Walpha,Talpha)->Wbar and liminf (v1^T Ealpha v1)/||Ealpha-Wbar||_F>0. Then, for each fixed real t, Phi(Walpha,Talpha+log(1/(v1^T Ealpha v1))/(2mu1)+t) converges to the canonical escape orbit WG(t)=lim_(epsilon down to 0) Phi(Wbar+epsilon v1 v1^T,log(1/epsilon)/(2mu1)+t). This limit solves the same flow and has rank at most r+1. The statement does not assert that alignment follows from a Gaussian initialization, nor that the canonical orbit ends at a rank-(r+1) local minimum. Source: arXiv:2012.09839, Theorem G.2, PDF p.33; global-flow convention in Section 3, p.3; genericity limitations in Appendix H, pp.34-35.

Let (X,d,mu) be a metric space with a Borel probability measure. Assume every Borel set A has measurable distance expansions A_r={x:d(x,A)<=r} for r>=0, with empty-set expansion empty. Put alpha(r)=1-inf{mu(A_r): A Borel, mu(A)>=1/2}. For a Borel error region E={x:h(x)!=c(x)}, let epsilon=mu(E) and R(r)=mu(E_r). Fix finite budgets b1,b2>=0 and assume epsilon>alpha(b1). Then (i) R(b1+delta)>1/2 for every delta>0, hence R(b1)>=1/2; and (ii) R(b1+b2)>=1-alpha(b2), and consequently R(b1+b2)>=1-gamma whenever gamma>=alpha(b2). If, additionally, the distance from any point to every nonempty Borel subset is attained, then R(b1)>1/2 without slack; finite metric spaces satisfy this additional condition. R here uses the distance-enlargement convention. Its identification with existence of an error point within the exact closed budget requires attainment of distances to E, and is not silently assumed in the general statement. Labels in the error region are evaluated at the perturbed point, not against the original label. This gives the source Theorem3.2 near-one distance-enlargement conclusion on its general measurable metric-space scope; it does not assert the printed strict half-risk conclusion at exact radius without the added attainment assumption.
