body:
[The 20 of arXiv:2609.02879, 'On the cut locus of Hamilton--Jacobi equations I: structure and propagation via the touchi'] Let $H:\T^n\times\R^n\to\R$ be a Tonelli Hamiltonian and
	$\phi\in\SCL(\T^n)$. Then there exist positive constants
	$C_{1,1},C_{1,2},C_{2,1},C_{2,2}$
	(depending on the local $C^2$ modulus and the Tonelli modulus of $H$ and the Lipschitz and semiconcavity constants of $\phi$) such that
	\begin{enumerate}[\rm (1)]
		\item $R_\phi(x)\leqslant\max\Big\{\, \frac{C_{1,1}}{\tau_{\phi,H}(x)},\ C_{1,2}\ \Big\},\quad \forall x\in \T^n,$
		\item $\tau_{\phi,H}(x) \geqslant \min\Big\{\, \frac{C_{2,1}}{R_\phi(x)},\ C_{2,2}\ \Big\},\quad \forall x\in \T^n,$
	\end{enumerate}
where we let $\frac{1}{0}=+\infty$ and $\frac{1}{+\infty}=0$.

with $\mu([-1])=\mu([+1])=1/2$. Then there exists a sequence

\log\int \e^{g_L-\mu(g_L)}\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\mu
=
\infty .
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Proposition prop-pointed-cone of arXiv:2411.19810, 'Radial conformal welding in Liouville quantum gravity'] Let $W >0$. Sample $(z, \psi_0) \sim \mathcal{A}_{\psi_0}(dz) P_W(d\psi_0)$ and let $\psi$ be the field on $\mathbb{C}$ such that $(\mathbb{C}, \psi, 0, 1, \infty)/{\sim_\gamma} = (\mathbb{C}, \psi_0, 0, z, \infty)/{\sim_\gamma}$. Then the law of $\psi$ is $\frac1{2\pi(Q-\alpha)}\mathrm{LF}_{\mathbb{C}}^{(\alpha, 0), (\gamma, 1), (2Q-\alpha, \infty)}$, where $\alpha = Q - \frac W{2\gamma}$.

body:
[Theorem 22 (Localized continuous centered second-chaos operator) of arXiv:2606.26065, 'Localized Centered Second-Chaos Operators'] Assume the continuous Gaussian setup of Section~\ref{sec:setup}, the order-zero symbol bound~\eqref{eq:m-size}, covariance bounds~\eqref{eq:S-size}, and the time-regularity and cutoff-convergence assumptions in Assumption~\ref{ass:time}.  Assume also the power-law envelope~\eqref{eq:power-envelope}.  Let $\lambda>0$ and let $s,\sigma\in\R$ satisfy the strict window~\eqref{eq:lambda-window}.  Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.4em]
\item For every finite $p\ge2$, the localized centered Galerkin operators
\[
 \cB^\circ_\Lambda:
 \Xspace_T^\sigma
 \longrightarrow
 C_TH^{s-\lambda}\cap L_T^1B^{\sigma-\lambda}_{2,\infty}
\]
are uniformly bounded in $L^p(\Omega)$ and converge in $L^p$ operator norm.  More precisely, after choosing $\eps>0$ below the strict margins in~\eqref{eq:lambda-window},
\[
 \sup_{\Lambda\in\Dyd\cup\{\infty\}}
 \left\|
 \norm{\cB^\circ_\Lambda}_{\Xspace_T^\sigma\to C_TH^{s-\lambda}\cap L_T^1B^{\sigma-\lambda}_{2,\infty}}
 \right\|_{L^p(\Omega)}<\infty,
\]
and
\[
 \cB^\circ_\Lambda\to\cB^\circ
 \quad\text{in }L^p\bigl(\Omega;\cL(\Xspace_T^\sigma,
 C_TH^{s-\lambda}\cap L_T^1B^{\sigma-\lambda}_{2,\infty})\bigr).
\]
\item Under the finite-state Galerkin condition in Assumption~\ref{ass:time}, there is one full-probability event $\Omega_*$ on which the whole Galerkin sequence converges pathwise in the same operator norm.  The same event controls all dyadic blocks simultaneously.
\end{enumerate}
The result applies to independent Gaussian legs and to same-family Wick squares after complete Wick centering and decoupling.  The finite-state hypothesis is used only in item~\textup{(ii)}.

body:
[Proposition 9 of arXiv:2608.26692, 'Many Facets in Random Polytopes from Product and Log-Concave Measures'] Fix $\alpha>0$ and let $N=\lfloor e^{\alpha n}\rfloor$.  There exists a
symmetric isotropic probability measure $\nu_n$ on $\R^n$ with
$\operatorname{supp}\nu_n=\R^n$, which is not log-concave, such that for
independent $X_1,\ldots,X_N$ with law $\nu_n$ and
\[
 P_N=\conv\{X_1,\ldots,X_N\},
\]
one has
\[
 \E f_{n-1}(P_N)=(1+o(1))2^n.
\]
In particular,
\[
 \E f_{n-1}(P_N)=e^{O(n)}
 \ll n^{n/2}e^{-Cn}
\]
for every fixed $C>0$.

[Theorem thm:PoissonApproximation2 of arXiv:2607.22291, 'Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declum'] Assume that $\mu$ is critical and belongs to the domain of
attraction of an $\alpha$-stable law for some $\alpha\in(1,2]$. Let $(G_k)$
be a sequence of $\{0,1\}$-valued functions on finite plane trees,  let
$(k_n)$ be a sequence of integers and let $(M_n)$ be a cutoff sequence. Set
$$
  \pi_n=\P(G_{k_n}(\mathcal T)=1).
$$
Let $B\subset\mathbb Z_+$ be such that
$$
  c_B
  =
  \mathbb{E}\left[
    k_\varnothing(\mathcal T)
    \mathbbm{1}_{\{k_\varnothing(\mathcal T)\in B\}}
  \right]
  \in(0,\infty).
$$
Define
$$
  \widehat{G}_k(T)
  =
  \mathbbm{1}_{\{k_\varnothing(T)\in B\}}
  \mathbbm{1}_{\{\exists u\in\Gamma_\varnothing(T):G_k(T_u)=1\}}.
$$
Assume that $(G_k)$ satisfies Assumption
(hyp:S of the paper) along $(k_n)$ with respect to $(M_n)$, and that
$(\widehat G_k)$ satisfies Assumption (hyp:C of the paper) along $(k_n)$ with respect
to the same cutoff sequence $(M_n)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] If $(n\pi_n)$ is bounded, then
$
  d_{\mathrm{TV}} \big(
    \#\{u\in\mathcal T^n:\widehat{G}_{k_n}(\mathcal T^n_u)=1\},
    \mathrm{Poisson}(c_B n\pi_n)
  \big)
  \to 0$.
\item[(ii)] If $n\pi_n\to\infty$, then
$
{
\#\{u\in\mathcal T^n:
\widehat G_{k_n}(\mathcal T^n_u)=1\}
}
\to \infty$ in probability.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:PoissonApproximation2 of arXiv:2607.22291

body:
[Ppn 256 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] In both the spherical and Ising settings, there exists $c>0$ and $C = C(\alpha) > 0$ such that the following holds.
    Let $\cA^\circ$ be a $L$-Lipschitz algorithm with $L\ge 1$.
    Let $\chi^\circ \equiv \chi_{\cA^\circ}$ and $q_0 \equiv \chi^\circ(0)$, and suppose $q_0 < 1$.
    Then, there exists an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm $\cA$ such that the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item $\chi \equiv \chi_{\cA}$ satisfies $\chi(0) = q_0$ and
    \[
        \chi'(0) \ge  \frac1{L^2}\,.
    \]
In fact, we can take
    \[
        \chi(p) = \bigg(1-\frac{1}{(1-q_0)L^2}\bigg) \chi^\circ(p)+ \frac{q_0 + (1-q_0)p}{(1-q_0)L^2}\,.
    \]

\item 
The perturbed algorithm $\cA$ approximates the original algorithm $\cA^\circ$ in the sense that
    \[
        \frac{1}{N} \E\Big[\|\cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux}) - \cA(\bG,\bg^{\aux})\|^2\Big]
        \le \frac{2}{(1-q_0)L^2}\,.
    \]

\end{enumerate}
We remark that the above error should be considered small, since we will prove later in Lemma~\ref{l:sM.Lip.1.trivial} that a sequence of algorithms with $q_0$ tending to one can only achieve the gaussian distribution.

\begin{proof} 
Let $\dot{\bg}$ be a standard gaussian in $\bbR^N$ independent of $\bg^{\aux}$, and
let $\bv$ be a deterministic element of $S_N$ with 
 $(\bv,\bbE \cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux})) = 0$. The perturbed algorithm $\cA$ is defined by
    \[\cA(\bG, (\bg^{\aux}, \dot{\bg} )) 
        = \bigg\{1-\frac{1}{(1-q_0)L^2}
            \bigg\}^{1/2}
        \cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux}) 
        + \bigg(\frac{q_0}{1-q_0}\bigg)^{1/2} \frac{\bv}{L}
        + \frac{\dot{\bg}}{L} \,.
    \]
Then the gradient of $\cA$ can be bounded as
    \begin{align*}
        \|\nabla\cA
            (\bG,(\bg^{\aux}, \dot{\bg})) \|^2
        &= \|\nabla_{\bG,\bg^{\aux}}
            \cA(\bG,(\bg^{\aux}, \dot{\bg} )) \|^2
        + \|\nabla_{\dot{\bg}} 
            \cA(\bG,(\bg^{\aux},\dot{\bg})) \|^2 \\
        &\le \bigg\{1-\frac{1}{(1-q_0) L^2}   \bigg\} L^2 
            + \frac1{L^2}
        \le L^2\,.
    \end{align*}
Since $\bv$ is deterministic and orthogonal to $\bbE \cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux})$,
 $\dot{\bg}$ is independent of $(\bG,\bg^{\aux})$, and $\bbE[\|\dot{\bg}\|^2] = N$, we have
    \[\frac{\bbE[
             \|\cA(\bG,(\bg^{\aux},\dot{\bg}))\|^2]}{N}
    =\bigg\{ 1-\frac1{(1-q_0)L^2}\bigg\}
    	+\frac{q_0}{(1-q_0)L^2}
	+\frac{1}{L^2}
    = 1\,,
    \]
where the last step follows from the trivial inequality $1-q_0\le1\le L^2$.  The above two displays show that $\cA$ is an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm in the sense of Definition~\ref{d:Lip}. Moreover, recalling the abbreviations $\chi\equiv\chi_\cA$ and $\chi^\circ\equiv\chi_{\cA^\circ}$, for any $0\le p\le1$ we have
    \[\chi(p) 
    = \bigg(1-\frac1{(1-q_0)L^2}\bigg) \chi^\circ(p) + \frac{q_0+(1-q_0)p}{(1-q_0)L^2}\,,
    \]
which implies $\chi(0)=q_0$.
   As noted above, $\chi^\circ$ is nondecreasing, which implies $\chi'(0)\ge 1/L^2$. This proves part~\eqref{it:wlogable.PERTURBED.CHI}. 

Next, since $|a^{1/2}-b^{1/2}| \le |a-b|^{1/2}$ for all $a,b\ge0$, we can bound
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{1}{N} \E\bigg[\Big\|\cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux}) - \cA(\bG,\bg^{\aux})\Big\|^2\bigg]
        &= \bigg(1 - \bigg(1-\frac{1}{(1-q_0)L^2}\bigg)^{1/2}\bigg)^2
        + \frac{q_0}{(1-q_0)L^2} + \frac{1}{L^2} \\
        &\le \frac{1}{(1-q_0)L^2} + \frac{q_0}{(1-q_0)L^2} + \frac{1}{L^2}
        = \frac{2}{(1-q_0)L^2}\,.
    \end{align*}
This proves part~\eqref{it:wlogable.PERTURBED.APPX}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 71 (Localization remainder) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Let $\mathcal R^{a;b,c}_{\Lambda,N,R,Q,M}(t,s)$ denote the sum over the
finitely many outer stochastic shells $L\sim_{\mathrm{ap}}R$ of a centered
block in one of the following two sectors:
\begin{equation}
 R\not\sim_{\mathrm{tr}}N,
 \qquad\text{or}\qquad
 R\sim_{\mathrm{tr}}N\ \text{ and }\ M>C_{\mathrm{out}}N.
\end{equation}
For every $2\le p<\infty$, every $A>0$, and every
$0<\theta\le1/2$,
\begin{align}
 \|\mathcal R^{a;b,c}_{\Lambda,N,R,Q,M}(t,s)\|_{
 L^p_\omega\mathcal L(L_q^2,L_n^2)}
 &\lesssim_{p,A}\la N+R+M\ra^{-A},
 \\
 \|\mathcal R^{a;b,c}_{\Lambda,N,R,Q,M}(t,s)
 -\mathcal R^{a;b,c}_{\Lambda,N,R,Q,M}(t',s')\|_{
 L^p_\omega\mathcal L(L_q^2,L_n^2)}
 &\lesssim_{p,A,\theta}\la N+R+M\ra^{-A}
 (|t-t'|+|s-s'|)^\theta.
 
\end{align}
The estimates are uniform in the spectral cutoff.  Cutoff differences obey
the same majorants and converge on every fixed block.  For a fixed-profile
dyadic family, the supremum over all cutoff levels may be placed inside each
finite $L^p(\Omega)$ norm in \eqref{eq:localization-tail-block} and
\eqref{eq:localization-tail-increment}.  Consequently, the sum of the
remainder blocks converges after the insertion of arbitrary fixed polynomial
Sobolev or Besov weights, in particular in every operator topology used in
Theorem~\ref{thm:localized-centered}.  Along a fixed-profile dyadic family,
the full remainder sequence converges almost surely, without a subsequence,
on a probability-one event that may be intersected with
$\Omega_{\mathrm{cen}}$.  For every interval $I\subset[0,T_0]$, its
zero-history restriction is causal and maps $E_{I,0}^{2,\sigma}$ to
$L^1(I;B_{2,\infty}^{\sigma-1})$ with norm $O_\omega(|I|^2)$, uniformly over
the limit and all cutoff levels on that event.  In particular, its
initial-interval operator norm tends to zero as $T\downarrow0$.

[Lemma lem:hypE of arXiv:2412.01381, 'Ergodicity and mixing for locally monotone stochastic evolution equations'] If $A=A_0+F$ where $A_0=-\partial \Phi$ is the subgradient of a lower semi-continuous convex functional $\Phi:V\to \mathbb{R}$ such that $\inf_{u\in V}\Phi(u)>-\infty$, and $F:V\to V^\ast$ is a strongly measurable (nonlinear) operator.
Suppose that
for some constants $\kappa_1\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$, $K_1\in\mathbb{R}$
that for every $u\in V$,
\begin{equation}\|F (u)\|_{V^\ast}\le \kappa_1\langle A_0 u,u\rangle+K_1.\end{equation}
Furthermore, suppose that for some constants $K_2,\kappa_2\in\mathbb{R}$, for every $u\in V$, 
\begin{equation}2\langle F(u),u\rangle\le\kappa_2\|F (u)\|_{V^\ast}+K_2,\end{equation}
or that
\begin{equation}2\langle F(u),u\rangle\le\kappa_2\langle A_0 u,u\rangle+K_2,\end{equation}
where, in the second case, we additionally assume that $\kappa_2\in (-2,\infty)$, whenever $\kappa_1<0$.
Then $A$ satisfies Hypothesis~(hyp:angle of the paper).

body: [Corollary c:spec-manifold of arXiv:2609.03731, 'Weightings and Lie groupoids'] Let $M$ be a manifold, $\ensuremath{\mathcal{A}}$ a sheaf of $C^\infty_M$-algebras, $\ensuremath{\mathcal{S}}=\ensuremath{\textnormal{Spec}}(\ensuremath{\mathcal{A}})$, and let $\pi\colon \ensuremath{\mathcal{S}}\rightarrow \textnormal{Id}$ be the corresponding natural transformation. Let $S=\ensuremath{\mathcal{S}}(M)$. Let $\{U_i\}$ be a countable open cover of $M$ such that $\ensuremath{\mathcal{S}}(U_i)$ admits local coordinates. Then $S$ is a manifold with sheaf of smooth functions $C^\infty_S$, obtained by gluing together the smooth manifolds $\{\ensuremath{\mathcal{S}}(U_i)\}$ along the open subsets $\{\ensuremath{\mathcal{S}}(U_i\cap U_j)\}$, and equipped with a smooth map $\pi_M\colon S\rightarrow M$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary c:spec-manifold of arXiv:2609.03731

[Defn def:F-s-iota-n of arXiv:2609.03751, 'Sparse bounds for maximal rough singular integrals'] Set \(F_{s,\iota}^0:=\widetilde Q_0^{\vec w}\), and define
\[
    F_{s,\iota}^1
    :=
    \left\{
      x\in\mathbb R^d:
      \sum_{K\in\mathscr K_s^{\vec w}}
          \mathbf 1_{K^\iota}(x)>u_0
    \right\}.
\]
Recursively, for \(n\geq2\), let
\[
    F_{s,\iota}^n
    :=
    \left\{
      x\in\mathbb R^d:
      \sum_{\substack{K\in\mathscr K_s^{\vec w}\\
                      K^\iota\subseteq F_{s,\iota}^{n-1}}}
          \mathbf 1_{K^\iota}(x)>u_0
    \right\}.
\]
title: $F_{s,\iota}^n$

[Lemma 2 (Representation of the SN distribution through symmetrization) of arXiv:2606.28678, '2606.28678'] Let $M\in \mathcal{S}^d$ and $\Psi,\Sigma\in \mathcal{S}_{++}^d$ be such that $\Psi\Sigma = \Sigma\Psi$. Let $\mathfrak{G}$ be a $d\times d$ random matrix such that all its entries are independent standard normals. Then
\begin{equation}
\mathfrak{Z} = M + \frac{\Psi^{1/2}\mathfrak{G}\Sigma^{1/2} + \Sigma^{1/2}\mathfrak{G}^{\top}\Psi^{1/2}}{2} \sim \mathcal{SN}_{d\times d}(M,\Psi,\Sigma).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 15 (Change of variables) of arXiv:2604.21389, 'Existence and uniqueness for \\ singular stochastic differential equations \\ with piecewi'] Let Hypothesis~\hypref{hyp:nu} and assume that $b$ and $\sigma$ are measurable and locally bounded.

For every $(X,B)$, weak non-explosive solution to~\eqref{eqn:SDE_general}, let $I$ denote the smallest interval such that~$X_t\in I$ for all $t\geq 0$ $\mathbb{P}$-a.s.. Then $(\Phi_\nu(X),B)$ is a weak non-explosive solution to the classical SDE
\begin{equation}
Y_t=\Phi_\nu(x_0)+\int_0^t \widetilde b(Y_s)\,\vd s+\int_0^t \widetilde\sigma(Y_s)\,\vd B_s,
\qquad t\ge 0.
\end{equation}
Moreover $\Phi_\nu(X)\in J$ for all $t\geq 0$ $\mathbb{P}$-a.s..

Conversely, if $(Y,B)$ is a weak non-explosive solution to~\eqref{eq:SDE_no_nu} and $Y_t\in J$ for all $t\geq 0$ $\mathbb{P}$-a.s., then $(\Psi_\nu(Y),B)$ is a weak non-explosive solution to~\eqref{eqn:SDE_general} and $\Psi_\nu(Y_t)\in I$ for all $t\geq 0$ $\mathbb{P}$-a.s.. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Change of variables

body: [Theorem 20 of arXiv:2609.00209, 'Exit Times for Brownian Motion and Location Detection'] Assume $\mathcal R=(0,a)\times (0,b)$ is a rectangular domain with $a<b$. Let $u_k(x,y)=\mathbb{E}^{(x,y)}[\tau_{\mathcal R}^k]$ denote the exit time moments for $k\geq 1$. Given positive real numbers $c_1, c_2, ...$, the intersection of the level curves $u_k(x,y)=c_k$ is either empty, or consists of one, two, or four points.

body: Theorem (campaign status: audited-pass): For u in U let Z_u record whether the residual L_u = A + B_u is active. For every activation pattern z in {0,1}^U, the optimal selector certificate satisfies |(A_n)_z| <= 2^{n+1-d-|z|}, d = ceil(n/3). Proof: on the a=1 half, z records the intersection of an independent set of C_n with U; a length-two gap has 2,1,1 completions and a length-three gap 3,2,1, according to the sum s+t of its endpoint states, both bounded by 2^{g-1-(s+t)/2} (g = gap edge-length). Multiplying over gaps gives 2^{n-d-|z|} completions; antipodality supplies the factor two. Summing the cells: |A_n|/2^{n+1} <= (3/4)^d, i.e. d <= ell(A_n)/log2(4/3). Notes: Solves the cycle in the stronger CELLWISE form needed for recursive entropy charging, not merely a class-count quotient. Exponents 2^{n+1-d-|z|}, 2^{g-1-(s+t)/2}, (3/4)^d reconstructed from flattened extraction; arithmetic re-verified (sum of (g-1) over gaps = n-d, sum of endpoint states = 2|z|).

body: [Lemma 100 of arXiv:2609.03875, 'Measure theory without infinities'] Let $\mf A$ be a monoid and $g\colon K\to \mf A$ be a finite family. If $K = \varnothing$, then $\finsum g = 0$. If $k_0\in K$, then $\finsum g = g(k_0) + \finsum g|_{K\setminus\{k_0\}}$.

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2608.31070, 'Sub-Laplacians on Compact Lie Groups: Heat Kernels, Distance, and Zeta Determinants'] Assume that $(G,L)$ is a two-step pair and that $G$ is simply connected. Then, for every $0<\tau\le1$,
		\[
		\log\det\nolimits_\zeta'(-\Delta_{\pLie})
		=\gamma_{\mathrm E}+\log\tau
		-C_{G,L}\mathscr A_{Q/2,\tau}(\beta_{G,L})
		-\mathcal R_{\mathrm{lat}}(\tau)
		-\mathcal R_{\mathrm{spec}}(\tau).
		\]
		The local series $\mathscr A_{Q/2,\tau}$ depends only on $Q/2$, $\tau$, and $\beta_{G,L}$ and is given explicitly in \Cref{zeta:section}. The terms $\mathcal R_{\mathrm{lat}}$ and $\mathcal R_{\mathrm{spec}}$ are absolutely convergent sums over nonzero coroot lattice orbits and positive branching eigenvalues, respectively. The expression is independent of $\tau$ and satisfies the exponential truncation bounds in \eqref{zeta:lattice-tail} and \eqref{zeta:spectral-tail}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let (X_{n, k})_{1 \le k \le r_n, n \ge 1} be a triangular array of row-wise independent random variables with \mathbb{E}[X_{n, k}] = 0 and \sigma_{n, k}^2 = \mathbb{E}[X_{n, k}^2] < \infty. Set s_n^2 = \sum_{k=1}^{r_n} \sigma_{n, k}^2. The array satisfies the Lindeberg condition if for every \epsilon > 0, \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{s_n^2} \sum_{k=1}^{r_n} \mathbb{E}\left[ X_{n, k}^2 \mathbf{1}_{\{|X_{n, k}| > \epsilon s_n\}} \right] = 0.
X_{n, k} row-wise independent, mean zero, finite variance

[Definition def:uniformly_monotone of arXiv:2608.30491, 'The Daugavet property in symmetric operator spaces'] \upshape
	Let \((X,\leq, \left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert_X)\) be a partially ordered normed linear space.  
	$(X, \left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert_X)$  is   \emph{uniformly monotone} whenever for any \(\varepsilon>0\),  there exists \(\delta(\varepsilon)>0\) such that for all \(0\le x,y\in X\),  we have  
	\[
	\|x+y\|_X > 1+\delta(\varepsilon),
	\]
	whenever \(\|y\|_X\ge\varepsilon\) and \(\|x\|_X=1\).
title: Definition def:uniformly_monotone of arXiv:2608.30491

  following equality is defining a bounded operator,
  
   \be  {\rm Op}_h^{\nu}(F) =  (2 \pi h)^{-2n}  \int _{\R^{4n} }  \Pi _{X h} 
   (F \star \nu)^{\rm ext}(Y, X)  \Pi _{Y h} dX  dY,\ee 
   
   where $ \Pi _{X h} $ is the orthogonal projection on the space spanned by the coherent space $ \Psi _{X h}$.  Moreover, we have for all $X\in\R^{2n}$,
    
 $$ < {\rm Op}_h ^{\nu} (F) \Psi _{X h},  \Psi _{X h} > =
  (F \star \nu) (X).$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Fix an effective enumeration phi_0, phi_1, phi_2, ... of all partial computable functions, so phi_e is the function computed by program number e. Kleene's recursion theorem states that for every total computable function f there exists an index e, a fixed point, such that phi_e equals phi_{f(e)}: program e computes exactly the function computed by the program obtained by applying f to e. This yields self-referential programs that can effectively obtain and use their own index or source code during execution, and underlies proofs of Rice's theorem and other diagonalization arguments. Proved by Stephen Kleene in 1938.
title: Kleene's recursion theorem

[Theorem t:crossing of arXiv:2606.11503, 'Percolation on hierarchical lattices'] For any directed graph $G_{1}$ satisfying (e:hypothesis of the paper), we have
  \begin{enumerate}[\quad a)]
  \item ``Uniqueness of phase transition'':\\
    $f$ has exactly three fixed points, namely: $0, 1$ and $p_\star = p_\star(G_1) \in (0, 1)$.
  \item ``The critical point $p_\star$ is a hyperbolic repeller'':\\
    While $f'(0) = f'(1) = 0$,
    \begin{equation}
      
      \zeta := f'(p_\star) \geq \bigg( 1 - \frac{(1-p_\star)^{\deg(a_1) \vee \deg(b_1)}}{2} \bigg)^{-1} > 1.
    \end{equation}
  \item ``The critical point can be determined in terms of crossing probabilities'':\\
    \begin{equation}
      
      p_\star = \sup \{p \in [0, 1]: \lim_k f_k(p) = 0 \}.
    \end{equation}
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). Let mu be a probability measure on a finite distributive lattice satisfying the FKG lattice condition mu(x v y) mu(x ^ y) >= mu(x) mu(y) for all x, y, a condition automatically satisfied by any product measure on {0,1}^E, in which case the conclusion is called the Harris inequality. Then for any two increasing (or two decreasing) functions f, g in L^2(mu), E[fg] >= E[f]E[g]; equivalently, for increasing events A, B, mu(A ^ B) >= mu(A) mu(B), so increasing events are positively correlated. This is the basic monotone-coupling tool throughout percolation and interacting particle systems, lower-bounding joint probabilities of increasing events, such as several disjoint crossings occurring together, by the product of their individual probabilities, and it justifies a wide range of comparison and sprinkling arguments. It does not give any upper bound on the correlation, which requires separate and generally harder tools such as the van den Berg-Kesten inequality for disjoint occurrence; it does not apply to a mix of an increasing and a decreasing event without flipping a sign; and the strength of the positive correlation is not quantified beyond nonnegativity. Typical failure: Applying FKG to a pair of events where one is increasing and the other decreasing without flipping the sign, which reverses the direction of the inequality; or invoking FKG for a non-product Gibbs measure, such as a random-cluster model outside the ferromagnetic regime with cluster weight q<1, without checking the lattice condition, which is known to fail there. Canonical reference: Fortuin, Kasteleyn and Ginibre, 1971, Communications in Mathematical Physics; Harris, 1960, Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society.
mu satisfies the FKG lattice condition, automatic for independent product measures but requiring verification for dependent Gibbs measures
f, g, or the events A, B, are both increasing, or both decreasing, with respect to the same partial order
the state space is finite or otherwise compactified so that all expectations involved are well defined

body: [Definition 11 (Definition 3.5\cite{AbbeBoix2020}) of arXiv:2607.21392, 'Gaussian Convexity Principles for Sharp Moderate Deviations of Gaussian Maxima and Critica'] Let \(\mathcal{G}=(V,E)\) be a finite graph. For each edge \(e=\{i,j\}\in E\), let \(Q_e(\cdot\mid\cdot)\)   be a probability kernel from the binary input alphabet \(\{-1,+1\}\) to a measurable output space \((\mathsf Y_e,\mathcal A_e)\). We write $Q_{e,+}(\cdot)=Q_e(\cdot\mid +1),  Q_{e,-}(\cdot)=Q_e(\cdot\mid -1).$ The associated graphical channel is the channel from \(\{-1,+1\}^V\) to \(\prod_{e\in E}\mathsf Y_e\) defined as follows: given \(x=(x_v)_{v\in V}\in\{-1,+1\}^V\), the edge observations \((Y_e)_{e\in E}\) are conditionally independent, and for \(e=\{i,j\}\), $Y_e \sim Q_e(\cdot\mid x_i x_j).$ We say that the edge channel \(Q_e\) is symmetric if there exists a measurable involution $T_e:\mathsf Y_e\to \mathsf Y_e, T_e^{-1}=T_e,$ such that for every \(A\in\mathcal A_e\), \[ Q_e(A\mid +1)=Q_e(T_e(A)\mid -1). \] Equivalently, since \(T_e\) is an involution, \[ Q_e(T_e(A)\mid +1)=Q_e(A\mid -1), \qquad A\in\mathcal A_e. \] The graphical channel is called symmetric if \(Q_e\) is symmetric for every \(e\in E\).
title: Definition 3.5\cite{AbbeBoix2020}

[Theorem 6 (Hoeffding's inequality, two-sided) of arXiv:2604.21113, 'Tail Bounds via Southwest Boundary'] Let \(X_1, \dots, X_N\) be independent symmetric Bernoulli r.v.'s, and let \(a = (a_1, \dots, a_n) \in \mathbb{R}^N\). Then, for any \(t \ge 0\), we have
\[
P\left( \left| \sum_{i=1}^N a_i X_i \right| \ge t \right) \le 2 \exp\left( -\frac{t^2}{2 \|a\|_2^2} \right).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Hoeffding's inequality, two-sided

body:
Let Ω ⊂ R^n be open, 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ and k ≥ 1 an integer. W^{k,p}(Ω) is the set of u ∈ L^p(Ω) all of whose distributional derivatives D^α u with |α| ≤ k lie in L^p(Ω): for each α there is g_α ∈ L^p(Ω) with ∫_Ω u D^α φ dx = (−1)^{|α|} ∫_Ω g_α φ dx for every φ ∈ C_c^∞(Ω); one writes D^α u = g_α (the weak derivative, unique a.e.). The norm is ||u||_{W^{k,p}} = ( Σ_{|α| ≤ k} ||D^α u||_{L^p}^p )^{1/p} (maximum over α for p = ∞). W^{k,p}(Ω) is a Banach space, separable for p < ∞ and reflexive for 1 < p < ∞. H^k(Ω) := W^{k,2}(Ω) is a Hilbert space with ⟨u, v⟩ = Σ_{|α| ≤ k} ∫_Ω D^α u D^α v dx. W^{k,p}_0(Ω) is the closure of C_c^∞(Ω) in W^{k,p}(Ω) (functions 'vanishing on the boundary' together with derivatives of order < k); H^1_0(Ω) := W^{1,2}_0(Ω). The Sobolev conjugate of p < n is p* = np/(n − p), i.e. 1/p* = 1/p − 1/n.

Facts: C^∞(Ω) ∩ W^{k,p}(Ω) is dense in W^{k,p}(Ω) for p < ∞ and any open Ω (Meyers–Serrin); restrictions of C^∞(R^n) functions are dense when Ω is bounded with Lipschitz boundary; W^{k,p}_0(R^n) = W^{k,p}(R^n); for bounded Ω, W^{1,p}_0(Ω) is a proper closed subspace of W^{1,p}(Ω) (nonzero constants are excluded by the Poincaré inequality). On an interval, W^{1,p} functions have absolutely continuous representatives; in dimension n ≥ 2 a W^{1,p} function with p ≤ n can be unbounded and discontinuous. For a bounded Lipschitz domain, W^{1,∞}(Ω) is the space of Lipschitz functions on Ω̄.
Ω ⊂ R^n open; derivatives taken in the distributional sense
title: Sobolev spaces W^{k,p}(Ω), W^{k,p}_0(Ω), H^k(Ω)

[Proposition 10 (Properties of the Hermite Process) of arXiv:2607.23548, '\textbf{A CIR-Type Diffusion Driven by Hermite Processes:\\ Well-Posedness, Positivity and'] Let $q \geq 1$ and $H \in \bigl(\tfrac{1}{2}, 1\bigr)$.
The process $Z^{(q,H)}$ defined in~\eqref{eq:hermite_def}
satisfies the following:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
  \item \textbf{Covariance.} For all $s, t \geq 0$,
    \[
    \mathbb{E}\!\left[Z_s^{(q,H)} Z_t^{(q,H)}\right]
    = \frac{1}{2}\bigl(s^{2H} + t^{2H} - |t-s|^{2H}\bigr).
    \]
    This follows from the normalisation of $c(H,q)$, which ensures
    $\mathbb{E}[(Z_1^{(q,H)})^2] = 1$ for all $q \geq 1$
    (see~\cite[Definition~2.1]{nourdin2019statistical}).

  \item \textbf{$H$-self-similarity.} For every $c > 0$,
    $\{Z_{ct}^{(q,H)}\}_{t \geq 0}
    \overset{d}{=}
    \{c^H Z_t^{(q,H)}\}_{t \geq 0}$.

  \item \textbf{Stationary increments.}
    $\{Z_{t+h}^{(q,H)} - Z_h^{(q,H)}\}_{t \geq 0}
    \overset{d}{=}
    \{Z_t^{(q,H)}\}_{t \geq 0}$ for every $h > 0$.

  \item \textbf{Long-range dependence.}
    The covariance of increments satisfies, as $k \to \infty$,
    \[
    \mathbb{E}\!\left[\bigl(Z_{t+1}^{(q,H)} - Z_t^{(q,H)}\bigr)
    \bigl(Z_{t+k+1}^{(q,H)} - Z_{t+k}^{(q,H)}\bigr)\right]
    \sim c_H\, k^{2H-2},
    \]
    so the series of autocovariances diverges whenever $H > \tfrac{1}{2}$.

  \item \textbf{H\"{o}lder regularity.}
    The sample paths of $Z^{(q,H)}$ are $\alpha$-H\"{o}lder continuous
    for every $\alpha \in (0, H)$.
    In particular, they belong almost surely to
    $C^{H-\beta}([0,T])$ for every $\beta \in (0, H - \tfrac{1}{2})$.

  \item \textbf{Kernel regularity.} For all $s, t \geq 0$,
    \begin{equation}
    
    \bigl\|L_t^{H,q} - L_s^{H,q}\bigr\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^q)}
    = \sqrt{q!}\, |t-s|^{H}.
    \end{equation}
    (This is an exact identity, not merely a bound: it follows from
    $\langle L_t^{H,q}, L_s^{H,q}\rangle_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^q)}
    = \tfrac{q!}{2}\bigl(t^{2H}+s^{2H}-|t-s|^{2H}\bigr)$
    together with $\|L_t^{H,q}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^q)} = q!\,t^{2H}$;
    see~\cite[Proposition~2.1]{tudorbook}.)

  \item \textbf{Non-Gaussianity for $q \geq 2$.}
    The distribution of $Z_t^{(q,H)}$ is non-Gaussian for every $t > 0$
    when $q \geq 2$.
    Its excess kurtosis is strictly positive and increasing in $q$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Properties of the Hermite Process

body: In computational complexity theory, NP-complete problems are the hardest of the problems to which solutions can be verified quickly. Somewhat more precisely, a problem is NP-complete when:It is a decision problem, meaning that for any input to the problem, the output is either "yes" or "no". Each input to the problem is associated with a collection of short solutions, which might or might not validly solve the input. The output is "yes" when at least one of these solutions is valid, and "no" when none of them are. The validity of each solution can be verified quickly, and a brute-force search algorithm can find a valid solution by trying all possible solutions. The problem can be used to simulate every other problem for which we can verify quickly that a solution is valid. Hence, if we could find valid solutions of some NP-complete problem quickly, we could quickly find valid solutions for every other problem in which a given solution can be easily verified.
title: NP-completeness

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The number of fixed points of permutations,
$$\chi(\sigma)=\#\left\{i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\Big|\sigma(i)=i\right\}$$ 
when regarded as random variable $\chi:S_N\to\mathbb N$, satisfies the formula
$$\chi\sim p_1$$
that is, follows the Poisson law of parameter $1$, in the $N\to\infty$ limit.

[Definition ARTASS of arXiv:2603.12774, 'Synchronization by noise for stochastic differential equations driven by fractional Browni'] Let \((\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P}, \theta)\) be a measurable metric dynamical system, and let \(\mathcal{X}\) be a Polish space.
	\begin{itemize}
		\item A random variable \(Y : \Omega \rightarrow (0, \infty)\) is called \emph{tempered} if
		\begin{align*}
			\limsup_{|t| \to \infty,\, t \in \mathbb{T}} \frac{1}{|t|} \log^{+} Y(\theta_t \omega) = 0,
			\quad \text{for } \mathbb{P}\text{-almost every } \omega \in \Omega,
		\end{align*}
		where \(\log^{+} x := \max\{ \log x, 0 \}\).
		
		\item Let \(\mathcal{E}=\{\mathcal{E}(\omega)\}_{\omega \in \Omega}\) be a family of non-empty subsets of \(\mathcal{X}\) such that, for every \(x \in \mathcal{X}\), the function \(\omega \mapsto d(x, \mathcal{E}(\omega))\) is measurable, and with probability one each \(\mathcal{E}(\omega)\) is bounded in \(\mathcal{X}\). We call \(\mathcal{E}\) a {tempered set} if the random variable
		\[
		r(\mathcal{E}(\omega)) := \sup_{x \in \mathcal{E}(\omega)} d(x, x_0)
		\]
		is tempered for some fixed reference point \(x_0 \in \mathcal{X}\). The collection of tempered sets in $\mathcal{X}$ is denoted by $\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{X})$.
	\end{itemize}

[Lemma lem:tight2 of arXiv:2507.19554, 'Full extremal process in four-dimensional membrane model'] There are constants $c_3, c_4 \in (0, \infty)$ such that the following is true for all $\epsilon, \delta > 0$ that are sufficiently small: 
			Set $\sigma := -\frac{\log \delta}{\epsilon}$, given $\lambda > 0$ and $\ell \in \mbN$, and define
			\bequn
				\lambda' := \lambda + c_4(1 + \log \sigma +  \sqrt{\log(\ell/\delta)\log \sigma}).
			\eequn
			If for some $N' \geq 1$, 
			\bequn
				\mbP(S_{\ell, N'} < \ell(m_N- \lambda')) > \delta,
			\eequn
			then 
			\bequn
				\mbP(|A_{N, \lambda}| > \ell ) < \epsilon
			\eequn
			holds for all $N \in \mbN$ with $N \leq c_3 \sigma^{-1/2}N'.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:tight2 of arXiv:2507.19554

body:
Let G=(V,E) be an infinite connected locally finite graph, assign iid Uniform(0,1) labels U(e), and use these same labels for all objects below. Define G[p]={e:U(e)<p}. The free minimal spanning forest F_f deletes edges that are strictly largest on some finite cycle. The wired minimal spanning forest F_w also deletes edges that are strictly largest on some bi-infinite simple path. Fix epsilon in (0,1), and independently of all labels let omega be Bernoulli(epsilon) bond percolation on G. Then the spanning subgraph F_f union omega is almost surely connected. This conclusion holds for every infinite connected locally finite graph, without transitivity, bounded-degree or amenability assumptions. It concerns the minimal spanning forest, and does not assert that F_f alone is connected. Source: Minimal spanning forests, Theorem 3.22 and proof, pp.17-18; cut formula (3.1), p.8.
Infinite connected locally finite graph
0<epsilon<1
The added Bernoulli percolation is independent of the minimal forest

Let $A \ge 1$. Suppose that for each $N\ge1$ and each $AN$-separated subset $S$ of $\Z^d$, the family $\{Y_\mathcal{\mathbf{z}} = N\}_{\mathbf{z} \in S}$ is independent. Define $q_N := \sup_{\mathbf{z} \in \Z^d} \P(Y_\mathbf{z} = N)$. Suppose for some $B<\infty$ we have $\sum_{N=0}^\infty N^{d+2}q_N^{1/d} \le B$. Then there exists $C$ depending only on $d, A,$ and $B$ such that the following holds. For any random path $\Pi$ in $\Z^d$ starting from $0$
such that every vertex of the path has $l^\infty$-distance 1 from the preceding vertex, and any $L \in \mathbb{N}$ we have
\[
\E[\sum_{\mathbf{z} \in \Pi}Y_\mathbf{z}] \le CL + C\sum_{\ell \ge L} \ell \P(|\Pi| = \ell)^{1/2}
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 11 of arXiv:2607.25645, 'Estimates of the total variation distance between laws of Sobolev mappings on Gaussian spa'] Let $k\in\mathbb N$, let $p>6k$, let $\varkappa\in(0,1)$, and let $a,b>0$. Set
\[
\beta:=\frac{p\varkappa}{p+2k\varkappa}.
\]
Assume that $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)$ and $g=(g_1,\ldots,g_k)$
with $
f_j,g_j\in W^{2,p}(\gamma)$,
satisfy
\[
\max_{1\le j\le k}\|f_j\|_{\dot W^{2,p}(\gamma)}\le b,
\quad
\max_{1\le j\le k}\|g_j\|_{\dot W^{2,p}(\gamma)}\le b,
\]
and
\[
\gamma(\Delta_f\le s)\le as^\varkappa
\quad \forall\, s>0.
\]
Then
\[
d_{\rm TV}(f,g)
\le
176k^4(1-\varkappa)^{-1}
\bigl(a^{1/\varkappa}b^{2k-1}\max_{1\le j\le k}\|f_j-g_j\|_{W^{1,p}(\gamma)}\bigr)^\beta.
\]

[Lemma lem:dual_3moment of arXiv:2604.20094, 'Persistence and local extinction for superprocesses in random environments'] For any $T>0$, there exists $C(T) > 0$
independent of $n$ and $x$ such that
$$
\sup_{n\geqslant 1}\sup_{t\in[0,T]} {\mathbf E} \left[(Y_t^{(n)}(x))^3\right] \leqslant C(T) \phi^3_\rho(x) \quad \hbox{ for every }  x\in {\mathbb R}^d.
$$
Consequently,
$$
\sup_{n\geqslant 1}\sup_{t\in[0,T]} {\mathbf E} \left[ Y_t^{(n)}(x) Y_t^{(n)}(y) \right]\leqslant C(T) \phi_\rho(x) \phi_\rho(y)
\quad \hbox{ for every }  x,y\in {\mathbb R}^d.

SOURCE SCOPE, not a restatement of the quantitative rigidity theorem. Knowles and Yin, Anisotropic local laws for random matrices, arXiv:1410.3516v4, study covariance matrices Q=T X X* T* with deterministic T and independent centered entries X_i_mu of variance 1/N, together with the dimension, moment and population-spectrum conditions summarized in Assumption 2.1. Theorem 3.12 (PDF p16) is eigenvalue rigidity under that assumption and regularity of the specified edges and bulk components in Definition 2.7. Section 2.1 (PDF p8, before Eq (2.4)) explicitly requires entry independence, not merely independence of column vectors. The abstract separately states an additive Wigner result for W+A; it is not a statement for an arbitrary nonlinear sample covariance plus an additive matrix. Application to centered ReLU feature columns with dependent coordinates and an additive input Gram requires a separate representation or edge-level transfer argument and verification of the regularity hypotheses. Matching a feature covariance or proving a fixed-positive-ridge deterministic equivalent does not verify those source assumptions. No impossibility of another theorem or a separately justified transfer is asserted.
Scope of arXiv:1410.3516v4; Section 2.1, Assumption 2.1, Definition 2.7 and Theorem 3.12
No quantitative eigenvalue-rigidity theorem is restated or claimed for ReLU
Source applicability finding; independent review pending

[Thm 2 (Exponential decay of correlations) of arXiv:2605.21638, 'Markov renewal theory for transfer operators and point processes on the line'] Let $(Z_n)_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}$ be a stationary process sequence that satisfies Assumptions \ref{ass:markov}-\ref{MAssu:Inversion} and let  $(X_n)_{n\in \Z}$ be defined as in~\eqref{eq:defX}.  Then the point process $\Phi$ with Palm version $\Phi^0=\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} \delta_{X_n}$ satisfies the following:  there exists $\epsilon >0$ such that, for all bounded intervals $A,B \subset \R$,
    \begin{equation*}
		\E\bigl[ \Phi(A) \Phi(B+t)\bigr] - \E\bigl[ \Phi(A) \bigr]\E\bigl[ \Phi(B) \bigr] = \Or(\e^{-\epsilon t})  \quad \textrm{as } t\to\infty.
    \end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma lem:orderSclosed of arXiv:2603.16824, 'Age-dependent random connection models with arc reciprocity: clustering and connectivity'] Assume \(\gamma\in[1/2,1)\) and consider \(S^c(t_o)\) as defined in~(equation eq:defSclosed of the paper). 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
	\item 
		If \(\Gamma>0\), we have
		\begin{equation*}
			\int\limits_{1/(t\log t)}^1 S^c(t_o)\,\mathrm{d} t_o
			=
			\begin{cases}
				O(1), & \gamma<2/3,
				\\
				O(\log t), & \gamma=2/3,
				\\
				O((t\log t)^{3\gamma-2}), & 2/3<\gamma<1.
			\end{cases}
		\end{equation*}
	\item
		If \(\Gamma=0\), we have instead
		\[
			\int\limits_{1/(t\log t)}^1 S^c(t_o)\,\mathrm{d} t_o
			=
			\begin{cases}
				O(1), &  \gamma<2/3,
				\\
				O(\log t), & \gamma =2/3
				\\
				O((t\log t)^{3-2/\gamma}), & \gamma>2/3.
			\end{cases}
		\]
		In particular, for all \(\gamma>2/3\), we have \(\int_{1/(t\log t)}^1 S^c(t_o)\,\mathrm{d} t_o=o((t\log t)^{2\gamma-1})\).
\end{enumerate}
title: Lemma lem:orderSclosed of arXiv:2603.16824

[Theorem branched_covers_lift.thm of arXiv:2609.00163, 'Decompositions and diagrams of symplectic surfaces in Weinstein domains'] Let $(W,S)$ be a symplectic surface in the Weinstein domain $(W,\omega)$ equipped with a bridge-multisection-with-divides structure $(W,S)=(W_1,\mathcal{D}_1)\cup \ldots \cup (W_n,\mathcal{D}_n)$. Suppose that $S$ is the branching set of a smooth branched cover $f:(W',S')\rightarrow (W,S)$.  Then $(W',S')=(f^{-1}(W_1),f^{-1}(\mathcal{D}_1))\cup \ldots \cup (f^{-1}(W_n),f^{-1}(\mathcal{D}_n))$ is a bridge multisection of $S'=f^{-1}(S)$ in a Weinstein domain $(W',\omega')$, with fillings of each $(f^{-1}(W_i),\omega'|_{f^{-1}(W_i)}
)$ uniquely determined by $f$ and $(W_i,\omega|_{W_i})$. In particular, $f$ is a branched cover of Weinstein fillings.
title: Theorem branched_covers_lift.thm of arXiv:2609.00163

orders $m$ and $n$.
For every cross pairing $P$ and $1\le r<\infty$,
\begin{equation}

 \norm{\operatorname{Sym}_{q(P)}(L\circ_PK)}
       _{\mathfrak W_{q(P),r}}
 \le
 \norm L_{\mathfrak W_{n,r}}\norm K_{\mathfrak W_{m,r}},
\end{equation}
where $\operatorname{Sym}_0=\Id$.  Consequently,
\[
 (L,K)\longmapsto\operatorname{Sym}_{q(P)}(L\circ_PK)
\]
extends uniquely to a contractive bilinear map from
$\mathfrak W_{n,r}\times\mathfrak W_{m,r}$ to
$\mathfrak W_{q(P),r}$.  The extension is independent of the labelled
copies used to define the three same-field completions.

body:
[Proposition RS.thm of arXiv:2605.17725, 'Limit theorems for random walks with spatio-temporal drift'] Let $(X_n)_{n\ge0}, (Y_n)_{n\ge0},  (\alpha_n)_{n\ge0}, (\beta_n)_{n\ge0}$ be sequences of nonnegative random variables adapted to $(\mathcal{F}_n)$ such that
     $$\mathbb{E}[X_{n+1} \mid \mathcal{F}_n] \le (1 + \alpha_n) X_n + \beta_n - Y_n, \quad \text{a.s.}$$
Then,  on the event $\Big\{\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \alpha_n < \infty \quad \text{and} \quad \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \beta_n < \infty\Big\}$, we have:
 \begin{itemize}
     \item  $X_{n}$ converges a.s. to a finite random variable $X_{\infty}$;
     \item  $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} Y_n < \infty$ a.s.
 \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

and~\ref{ass:endpoint-posterior}, the signed quantity in
\eqref{eq:app-local-objective} admits the endpoint-conditioned form
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
    G_i(\omega_i\mid y;\vec\omega_i,\psi)
    =
    \int_{\R^d}
    \int_{\R^d}
    &
    \Bigl(
        u_{t_i}(x\mid x_1,y)
        -
        v_{t_i}^\theta(x\mid y;\omega_i)
    \Bigr)
    \cdot \grad\psi(x)

\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Consequently, \(\mathcal L_i\) can be evaluated from endpoint-conditioned
velocities and posterior endpoint weights, which proves
Theorem~\ref{thm:endpoint-conditioned-objective}.

[Theorem 3 (Asymptotic validity and power of the test) of arXiv:2608.29465, 'Deciding When to Decide:\\Testing Operational Suboptimality Under Distributional Shift'] Suppose the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:delta_hat_rate} and the local inverse-stability condition in Assumption~\ref{assm:error_bound_P0} hold, and suppose the conditional CLT in Assumption~\ref{ass:eval_clt} holds. Let
\[
a_n:=n^{-1/(2\kappa)}
\]
denote the preference-estimation error rate. If $\delta_{\rm inv}=0$ and $\sqrt{m''}\,a_n\to0$, then the Wald test in \eqref{eq:T_wald} has asymptotic level $\alpha$:
\[
\limsup_{n,m',m''\to\infty}
\Pr\{\mathrm{reject}\ H_0\}
\le \alpha
\qquad
\text{whenever } \Delta^\star\le \tau .
\]
Without this relative-rate condition, the same conclusion holds on any fixed-margin null $\Delta^\star\le\tau-\eta$, $\eta>0$. More generally, if $\delta_{\rm inv}>0$, the unadjusted test controls Type-I error on the separated null $\Delta^\star\le\tau-\delta_{\rm inv}-\eta$. Under the alternative, for any fixed $\eta>0$, if $\Delta^\star\ge \tau+\delta_{\rm inv}+\eta$, then

[Lemma 5 of arXiv:2605.16733, 'Concentration Inequalities for Sample Cross-Covariances'] Let \((X_i)_{i=1}^N\) be i.i.d. copies of a centered Gaussian random
vector \(X\in\mathbb R^{d_X}\) with covariance matrix \(\Sigma_X\), and let
\(L\) be a fixed matrix such that $        P:=L\Sigma_XL^\top $ is nonzero. Then
\[
\E \left\|
\bigg( \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N
X_iX_i^\top -\E XX^\top\bigg) L^\top
\right\|
\gtrsim
(\|\Sigma_X\|\|P\|)^{1/2}
\bigg(
\sqrt{\frac{r_X+r_P}{N}}
+
\frac{\sqrt{r_Xr_P}}{N}
\bigg),
\]
where
\[
r_X:=\frac{\tr(\Sigma_X)}{\|\Sigma_X\|},
\qquad
r_P:=\frac{\tr(P)}{\|P\|}.
\]

[Proposition 23 of arXiv:2609.03951, 'Generalized Semi-Riemannian Submersions and Foliations'] If $\pi: (M,g) \to (B,\mathcal{D},h)$ is a generalized semi-Riemannian submersion such that $\mathcal{D}$ is integrable, then there exists $V_0 \in \mathfrak{X}(\mathcal{R})$ such that   
\[
\nabla_{\tilde{X}} \tilde{Y} = \widetilde{\nabla^h_X Y} + \frac{1}{2} ([\tilde{X},\tilde{Y}] - \widetilde{[X,Y]}) + V_0
\]
for all $X,Y \in \mathfrak{X}(\mathcal{D})$, where $\tilde{X}, \tilde{Y}$, and $\widetilde{\nabla^h_X Y}$ are their respective horizontal lifts.

Result: The q = 2 proof uses (i) the parafermionic observable being discretely holomorphic (full Cauchy-Riemann), (ii) RSW-type crossing estimates for tightness, (iii) identification of the limit via the martingale observable. For q in (1,4) not 2: (ii) is available (Duminil-Copin-Sidoravicius-Tassion 2017 for q in [1,4]); (iii) would follow from (i); (i) fails: for general q the observable satisfies only the contour relations (half of the Cauchy-Riemann equations), the same obstruction as in C0017. So the conjecture is reduced, for q in [1,4], exactly to finding an additional discrete relation for the parafermionic observable; the count of unknowns versus equations (one complex relation per face versus two needed) is the precise deficit. For q < 1 even RSW is unavailable. No new relation found. Obstruction: Discrete holomorphicity is only half-satisfied for q not 2.

Let U subset R^n be open, and Lu = -sum_{i,j=1}^n partial_j(a^{ij}(x) partial_i u) a divergence-form second-order elliptic operator with a^{ij} in C^1(U), symmetric, and uniformly elliptic on U (there is theta>0 with sum_{i,j} a^{ij}(x)xi_i xi_j >= theta|xi|^2 for all x in U, xi in R^n). Suppose u in H^1(U) is a weak solution of Lu=f on U for some f in L^2(U): integral_U sum a^{ij} partial_i u partial_j v dx = integral_U f v dx for all v in C_c^infinity(U). Then u in H^2_loc(U): for every open V with compact closure in U, u in H^2(V), with ||u||_{H^2(V)} <= C(||f||_{L^2(U)} + ||u||_{L^2(U)}) for a constant C depending only on n, theta, V, U and the C^1 norms of the a^{ij}. (If a^{ij} in C^{k+1}(U) and f in H^k(U), then u in H^{k+2}_loc(U) with the analogous estimate; if the coefficients and f are C^infinity, u is C^infinity in the interior.)

[Lemma lem:se-sojourn of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix $\lambda \in (0,1/3)$. Let $\overline{p}$ be a send sequence with $p_0=1$ such that, for all positive integers~$x$, $W_x \le (6/\lambda)^x$. 
Let $i$ be a sufficiently large integer and suppose that bin~$i$ is a bottleneck. 
Let $U = (U^A,U^B,U^C)$ be the under-backoff process with birth rate~$3\lambda$ and send sequence~$\overline{p}$.
Then the expected sojourn time of $U$ from the empty state back to the empty state is at least $e^{{i}^{1/2}}$.

[Definition of arXiv:2509.02432, 'A threshold for online balancing of sparse i.i.d. vectors'] Let $(\ell,r,k,s)$ be integers satisfying $\ell\leq 0\leq r$,
$0\leq k\leq n$, and $s\geq 0$. Say that 
the pair $(A,\sigma)$ ``contains an $(\ell,r)$--spread
of size at least $s$ at time $k$'' if there exist collections of indices 
\[
    (i^{(\ell)}_j)_{j \in [s]} \quad \text{ and } \quad  (i^{(r)}_j)_{j \in [s]},
\]
such that: all $2s$ indices are distinct, and for every $1 \leq s' \le s$, it holds:
\[
    \langle {\rm row}_{i^{(\ell)}_{s'}}(A),\sigma\rangle_{[k]}=\ell; \quad \langle {\rm row}_{i^{(r)}_{s'}}(A),\sigma\rangle_{[k]}=r.
\]

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] For the segment graphs having $N$ vertices, the characteristic polynomials $P_N$ of the adjacency matrices are subject to the following recurrence, 
$$P_0=1\quad,\quad P_1=x\quad,\quad P_{N+1}=xP_N-P_{N-1}$$
and are the well-known Chebycheff polynomials, enjoying many interesting properties. The corresponding numbers of loops and measures can be deduced from this.

[Defn 74 (Parabolic H\"older spaces) of arXiv:2510.22155, 'Random walks in space-time random media in all spatial dimensions: the full subcritical fl'] We define $C_c^\infty(\Psi_T)$ to be the set of functions on $\Psi_T$ that are restrictions to $\Psi_T$ of some function in $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^{d+1})$, in particular we do not impose that elements of $C_c^\infty(\Psi_T)$ vanish at the boundaries of $\Psi_T.$ 
  
    For $\alpha\in(0,1)$ we define the space $C^{\alpha,\tau}_\mathfrak s(\Psi_T)$ to be the completion of $C_c^\infty(\Psi_T)$ with respect to the norm $$\|f\|_{C^{\alpha,\tau}_\mathfrak s(\Psi_T)}:= \sup_{(t,x)\in \Psi_T} \frac{|f(t,x)|}{w(x)} + \sup_{|s-t|^{1/2}+|x-y|\leq 1} \frac{|f(t,x)-f(s,y)|}{w(x)(|t-s|^{1/2}+|x-y|)^{\alpha}}.$$
		For $\alpha<0$ we let $r=-\lfloor \alpha\rfloor$ and we define $C^{\alpha,\tau}_\mathfrak s(\Psi_T)$ to be the completion of $C_c^\infty(\Psi_T)$ with respect to the norm $$\|f\|_{C^{\alpha,\tau}_\mathfrak s(\Psi_T)}:= \sup_{(t,x)\in\Psi_T} \sup_{\lambda\in (0,1]} \sup_{\varphi \in B_r} \frac{(f,S^\lambda_{(t,x)}\varphi)_{L^2(\Psi_T)}}{w(x)\lambda^\alpha}$$ where the scaling operators are defined by 
		\begin{align}
			
			S^\lambda_{(t,x)}\varphi (s,y) = \lambda^{-d-2}\varphi(\lambda^{-2}(t-s),\lambda^{-1}(x-y)),
		\end{align}
		and where $B_r$ is the set of all smooth functions of $C^r$ norm less than 1 with support contained in the unit ball of $\mathbb R^{d+1}$.
title: Parabolic H\"older spaces

body:
[Corollary C:containment-quadrangle of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Consider a weighted directed acyclic graph $G = (V, E, M)$, and we let $H = (W, E|_{W\times W}, M|_{W})$ be the subgraph of $G$ induced by a vertex set $W \subset V$. Consider vertices $x_1 \prec y_1$ and $x_2 \prec y_2 \in H$ and suppose that we have the following {\bf path-crossing} property:
\begin{itemize}
    \item Let $\tau$ be any path in $H$ from $x_1$ to $y_1$ and $\pi = (\pi_0, \dots, \pi_k)$ be any path in $G$ from $x_2$ to $y_2$. Then if $\pi_i \notin W$ for some $i \in \llbracket1,k-1 \rrbracket$, there are indices $i^- < i < i^+$ such that the vertices $\pi(i^-), \pi(i^+)$ are on the path $\tau$.
\end{itemize}
Then
$$
H(x_1; y_1) + G(x_2; y_2) \le G(x_1; y_1) + H(x_2 ; y_2).
$$

[Theorem thm:moments of arXiv:2602.14617, 'Stochastic Burgers equation driven by multiplicative Rosenblatt noise: local existence, un'] Let $u \in \mathcal{Y}_{T_0}$ be the unique local mild solution from Theorem (thm:existence of the paper) with deterministic initial condition $u_0 \in L^\infty(\mathbb{R})$. Then for every $p \ge 2$,
\[
\sup_{t \in [0,T_0]} \sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} \mathbb{E}[|u(t,x)|^p] < \infty.
\]
Consequently, $u \in \mathcal{X}_{T_0}^p$ for all $p \ge 2$.

[Lemma lemmabalanced of arXiv:2411.11085, 'Universal constant order fluctuations for the cokernels of block triangular matrices'] Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $\mathcal{P}$ be the set of prime divisors of $|G|$. There is a $c>0$ such that for all large enough $n$, if $\mathbf{M}$ is a $(\mathcal{P},\varepsilon)$-balanced $n\times n$ random matrix and $G_0$ is a subgroup of $G$, then
\[\exp(-\exp(-cn))\le \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{g}\in G_0^n\\\langle\mathbf{g}\rangle=G_0}} \min_{\mathbf{f}\in G_0^n} \mathbb{P}(\mathbf{M}\mathbf{g}=\mathbf{f})\le \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{g}\in G_0^n\\\langle\mathbf{g}\rangle=G_0}} \max_{\mathbf{f}\in G_0^n} \mathbb{P}(\mathbf{M}\mathbf{g}=\mathbf{f})\le \exp(\exp(-cn)).\]

${\mathcal V}_n\big(\Omega_1, {\bm W}_1\big)$ and ${\mathcal V}_n\big(\Omega_1, \rho^{d_1} {\bm W}_2\big)$ are eigenspaces of their
respective spectral operator for each $n$.

body:
[Lemma 10 (Decay of the first derivatives of the decoupled flow) of arXiv:2605.03057, 'Uniform-in-time quantitative fluctuations of large scale interacting particle systems'] Assume Assumption~\ref{ass:coeff-level-new}. Fix $ x \in \R^d $, $ \mu \in \Ptwo $, let
$ X_t^{x,\mu} $ be the decoupled flow, and $\omega$ be the constant
defined in \eqref{eq:def-omega-uniform-time}. Then, the following hold.

\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For every $ h \in \R^d $, the first spatial derivative
$ \partial_x X_t^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right] $ exists and solves
\begin{equation}

d\left( \partial_x X_t^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right] \right)
=
\partial_x b\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\partial_x X_t^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right] dt
+
\partial_x \sigma\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\partial_x X_t^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right] dB_t,
\end{equation}
with initial condition $\partial_x X_0^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right] =
h$. Moreover, for every $ p \in \mathcal P $ and all $t \ge 0$,
\begin{equation}

\E\left(
\abs{\partial_x X_t^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right]}^p
\right)
\le
e^{-\frac{p\kappa_p}{2} t} \abs{h}^p
\le
e^{-p\omega t} \abs{h}^p.
\end{equation}

\item[(ii)] For every $ v \in \R^d $, the Lions derivative
$ \partial_\mu X_t^{x,\mu}\left( v \right) $ exists and solves
\begin{align}

d\left( \partial_\mu X_t^{x,\mu}\left( v \right) \right)
&=
\Bigg(
\partial_x b\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\partial_\mu X_t^{x,\mu}\left( v \right)
+
\widetilde{\E}\left(
\partial_\mu b\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\left( \widetilde{X}_t^{v,\mu} \right)
\partial_x \widetilde{X}_t^{v,\mu}
\right)
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+
\widetilde{\E}\left(
\partial_\mu b\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)

Let P be a Markov kernel on a Polish space, reversible for probability measure mu. Let f be bounded measurable with integral f dmu=0. For every pair of starts x,y, couple two P-chains so that their time-k marginals are respectively P^k(x,.) and P^k(y,.). Assume a finite constant L uniformly bounds sum_(k>=0)|E[f(X_k)-f(Y_k)|X_0=x,Y_0=y]| for all x,y. Then F(x,y)=sum_(k>=0)E[f(X_k)-f(Y_k)|X_0=x,Y_0=y] is bounded and antisymmetric. If X has law mu and X_prime conditional on X has law P(X,.), then (X,X_prime) is exchangeable and E[F(X,X_prime)|X]=f(X). Equivalently, the summands are P^k f(x)-P^k f(y); uniform absolute summability of this series is the hypothesis of Lemma4.1. No pathwise ordering of the coupled chains is assumed.
Reversible kernel with stationary probability mu; bounded measurable centered f.
Both coupled time-k marginals are the required P^k laws for every initial pair.
Uniform finite bound on the sum of absolute conditional expected differences; measurability of the construction.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact tree identity, source-specific recurrence or explicit limiting obstruction Result: For any fixed clade shape chi of size m with positive model probability, its expected count is asymptotically n*p(chi)/m. The later fixed-clade variance bound is O(n), so Chebyshev gives probability O(1/n) that its count is zero. For any fixed finite list of distinct positive-probability shapes, all are therefore present with probability tending to1. It follows that the number of distinct shapes tends to infinity in probability, while it is always at most n-1 for internal clades. Check: For a count N with E N~c*n and Var N=O(n), P(N=0)<=Var N/(E N)^2=O(1/n). A finite union bound then proves the stated divergence without assuming independence between shapes. Obstruction: This supplies no growth rate: the constants and count estimates are not uniform over growing shapes. Largest repetitions and smallest missing shapes need joint tail information across an exponentially growing family.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0346-distinct-and-repeated-clade-shapes-in-critical-beta-splitting-trees

Assume that $\mathfrak{a}$ is a point separating a void from a band while $\mathfrak{b}$ is not (and is allowed to be $+\infty$). Then for any $\eps>0$, there exists $C>0$ depending only on $\eps$ and on the constants in the assumptions, such that
 \[
 \P\big[\exists i \in [N] \quad \big| \quad \ell_i \in [\N(\mathfrak{a}+\eps),\N\mathfrak{b}] \bigg] \leq C\exp\bigg(-\frac{\N}{C}\bigg).

\[
\P\big[\exists i \in [N] \quad \big| \quad \ell_i \in [\N\mathfrak{a},\N(\mathfrak{b}-\eps)]\big]\leq C\exp\bigg(-\frac{\N}{C}\bigg).

body:
[Prop Spc*-levelwise-tensor of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let ${\mathcal{C}}$ be any $S$-cocomplete $T$-$\infty$-category. Then the levelwise tensor product ${\Spc_*}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}$ is again $S$-cocomplete, the map ${\mathcal{C}}\to{\Spc_*}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}$ induced by $(-)_+\colon\Spc\to\Spc_*$ is $S$-cocontinuous, and it moreover admits the following universal property: for every pointed $S$-cocomplete $T$-$\infty$-category ${\mathcal{D}}$, restriction defines an equivalence
    \[
        \ul{\textup{Fun}}^\textup{$S$-cc}_T({\Spc_*}\otimes{\mathcal{C}},{\mathcal{D}})\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}\ul{\textup{Fun}}^\textup{$S$-cc}_T({\mathcal{C}},{\mathcal{D}}).
    \]
    \begin{proof}
        In light of Proposition~(prop:univ-prop-*-cc-param of the paper), it will be enough to construct an equivalence ${\Spc_*}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}{\mathcal{C}}_*$ under ${\mathcal{C}}$. For this, we consider the commutative diagram
        \[
            \begin{tikzcd}
                {\Spc}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}_{\hphantom{*}}\arrow[d]\arrow[r] & {\Spc_*}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}_{\hphantom{*}}\arrow[d]\\
                {\Spc}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}_*\arrow[r] & {\Spc_*}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}_*
            \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        with horizontal maps induced by $(-)_+\colon\Spc\to\Spc_*$ and vertical maps induced by $(-)_+\colon{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{C}}_*$. We claim that the right-hand vertical map and the bottom horizontal map are equivalences; this will then complete the proof of the corollary.

        To see that the bottom horizontal map is an equivalence, it suffices to show that ${\Spc}\otimes{\mathcal{D}}\to{\Spc_*}\otimes{\mathcal{D}}$ is invertible for every (non-parametrized) pointed cocomplete ${\mathcal{D}}$, or equivalently that the induced map between corepresented functors on $\CAT_\infty^\text{cc}$ is an equivalence. By the defining property of the tensor product, the latter amounts to saying that we have an equivalence
        \begin{equation}
            {-}\circ(-)_+\colon{\textup{Hom}}(\Spc_*,{\textup{Fun}}^\text{cc}({\mathcal{D}},{\mathcal{E}}))\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}{\textup{Hom}}(\Spc,{\textup{Fun}}^\text{cc}({\mathcal{D}},{\mathcal{E}}))
        \end{equation}
        for any cocomplete ${\mathcal{E}}$. By [CLL_Global]*{Corollary 4.1.10${}^{\textup{op}}$}, the full subcategory of ${\textup{Fun}}({\mathcal{D}},{\mathcal{E}})$ spanned by the functors preserving the initial object is pointed, whence so is the smaller subcategory ${\textup{Fun}}^\text{cc}({\mathcal{D}},{\mathcal{E}})$ as it still contains the initial object. Thus, applying the Proposition~(prop:univ-prop-*-cc-param of the paper) for $S=T=1$ shows that $((eq:univ-prop-pted of the paper))$ is an equivalence.

        For the vertical map, we similarly compare corepresented functors on fiberwise cocomplete $\infty$-categories. Arguing as above, this reduces us to invertibility of
        \[
            {\textup{Hom}}({\mathcal{C}}_*,{\textup{Fun}}^\text{cc}(\Spc_*,-)\circ{\mathcal{D}})\to
            {\textup{Hom}}({\mathcal{C}},{\textup{Fun}}^\text{cc}(\Spc_*,-)\circ{\mathcal{D}}),
        \]
        and applying the above levelwise shows that ${\textup{Fun}}^\text{cc}(\Spc_*,-)\circ{\mathcal{D}}$ is pointed. The claim therefore follows from the special case $S=\core T$ of the proposition.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop Spc*-levelwise-tensor of arXiv:2608.28504

[Proposition 39 of arXiv:2608.05931, 'Effective Lagrangian regularity and the uniqueness threshold for random H\"older velocity '] Let $\alpha \in (0,1)$ with $\alpha + \beta>1$ and $\alpha + \beta/2 <1$. Suppose for all $p \geq 1,$ there exists $K(p)>0$ such that for all $j \in \N$ and $n \in \{0,1,2\}$,
    \[\|\nabla^n u^j\|_{L^p_\omega \mathcal{C}^0_{t,x}} \leq K(p) 2^{(n-\alpha)j}.\]
    Then for all $\ep<C(\alpha,\beta)^{-1}$ and $p\geq 1$, there exists $C(K,\alpha,\beta,\ep,p)>0$ such that, letting
    \[\nu := 2\alpha + \beta -1 -\ep \quad \text{and} \quad \gamma := \frac{1 - \alpha + \ep}{\beta} - \ep,\]
    for all $y\in \T^d$ and $N \in \N$,
    \[\|\iop^{N} U^N\|_{ \mathcal{C}^0_y L^p_\omega \mathcal{C}^{\gamma }_t \mathcal{C}^\nu_x} \leq C.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:existence_of_v_seq of arXiv:2505.09604, 'Exceptional force, uncountably many solutions in the KPZ fixed point'] The following holds on a single event of full probability. Let $\xi \in \mathbb{R}$, and let $b$ be a $\xi$-eternal solution. Then, for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$ and compact interval $[x,y] \in \mathbb{R}$, there exists a sequence $\mathbf v_n = (x_n,t_n)$ with $t_n \to -\infty$ and $\frac{x_n}{|t_n|} \to \xi$ and $N \in \mathbb{N}$ so that
\[
b(w,t) - b(x,t) = \mathcal{L}(\mathbf v_n;w,t) - \mathcal{L}(\mathbf v_n;x,t),\quad\text{ for all }w\in [x,y] \text{ and } n \ge N. 
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma Upcrossing_lemma of arXiv:2608.08299, 'Non-linear optimal stopping with Bermudan strategies: the infinite horizon case'] Let $\rho$, depending on the first index only, satisfy properties (i),(iv),(v),(vii),(viii),(ix),(x), and the normalisation property $\rho_0[1]=1$. 
\\
   Let $X$ be a \textbf{non-negative} \emph{$(\Theta, \rho)$}-supermartingale.
    Let $0<a<b<+\infty$ ( $a,b \in \mathbb{Q}$).
    We define, by induction, the following stopping times: 
   $ T_0:=0 $
 and for all $k\in \mathbb{N}^*$, 
 \begin{align*}
S_k&:=\inf\{n \geq T_{k-1}:X_n \leq a\},  \\
T_k&:=\inf\{n \geq S_{k}:X_n \geq b\},
\end{align*}  
 with the convention that $inf \emptyset = + \infty$.
 \\ 
 Let $N_{\infty}([a,b])$ be the number of upcrossings of the interval $[a,b]$. 
  Let $N_{n}([a,b])$ be the number of upcrossings of the interval $[a,b]$ before time $n$.
  \\ Then, 
   \begin{compactenum}
   \item[(i)] $\rho_{S_k \wedge n}[\mathbb{I}_{\{T_k \leq n\}}]\leq (\frac{a}{b})\mathbb{I}_{\{S_k \leq n\}}$.
   \item[(ii)] $\rho_0[\mathbb{I}_{\{T_k<+\infty\}}]\leq (\frac{a}{b})^k$.
    \item[(iii)] 
  $P(N_{\infty}([a,b])< +\infty ) =1$.
   \end{compactenum}

Let D_n(c) be the counterclockwise trapezoidal edge-integral sum around cell c. If, for every axis-aligned rectangle R compactly contained in Omega and grid rectangle approximants R_n tending to R, the signed sum of D_n(c) over cells of R_n tends to zero, then f is holomorphic. [Lemma lem:one-hole of arXiv:2608.20480, 'When Clean Data Hurts: Learning with Monotone \\ Corruptions Beyond Binary Classification'] Let $F_i:O_i\hookrightarrow\Omega_r$, $i\in[d]$, where each $O_i$ is a union of complete petals, and put
\[
    Y
    =
    \{y\in\Omega_r:\bigcup_iF_i[y]\text{ is injective}\}.
\]
Exactly one of the following holds.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Roman*),leftmargin=2.5em]
    \item The raw union $\bigcup_iF_i$ is injective. Fix a bijection $u$ extending it. For $y\in Y$, if $u^{-1}(y)=\infty$, then every profile is internal; if $u^{-1}(y)=e_{B,a}$, then precisely the tables containing the $B$-petal use the common profile $(B,a)$, while all remaining tables are internal.

    \item The raw union is not injective. Either $|Y|\le1$, or $|Y|=q$ and there are one direction $B$, a bijection $\theta:Y\to\mathbb{F}_q$, and constants $\beta_i\in\mathbb{F}_q$ for the tables containing $E_B$ such that, for every $y\in Y$, tables hiding $B$ are internal and a table seeing $B$ uses profile $(B,\theta(y)-\beta_i)$, with exponent zero interpreted as internal.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: One-hole synchronization

[Lemma 39 of arXiv:2609.02785, 'Characterization of Stanley-Reisner varieties by their automorphism group'] Let $\Delta$ satisfy $\mathcal{R}(\Delta)\neq\emptyset$, and define the set of \emph{ray directions}
$$
\mathcal{D}(\Delta):=\bigl\{d\in\ZZ^n \text{ primitive}\;:\; \alpha+\ZZ_{\geq0}\,d\subseteq\mathcal{R}(\Delta) \text{ for some } \alpha\in\mathcal{R}(\Delta)\bigr\}.
$$
Then
$$
\mathcal{D}(\Delta)=\bigl\{d\in\ZZ^n_{\geq0}\text{ primitive}\;:\;\emptyset\neq\supp(d)\subseteq S \text{ for some } S\in\textstyle\bigcup_i\mathcal{A}_i(\Delta)\bigr\},
$$
and $\cone(\mathcal{D}(\Delta))=\RR_{\geq0}^{\Supp(\Delta)}:=\cone(\mathbf{e}_j : j\in\Supp(\Delta))$, a simplicial cone whose extreme rays are the $\RR_{\geq0}\mathbf{e}_j$ with $j\in\Supp(\Delta)$.

body:
Pointwise identity. Let Ω ⊂ R^n be open, x the position vector, and u ∈ C^2(Ω). Then, everywhere in Ω,
   div( (x·∇u) ∇u − (1/2)|∇u|^2 x ) = (x·∇u) Δu − ((n−2)/2) |∇u|^2.
The same holds almost everywhere for u ∈ H^2_loc(Ω) (all terms are then in L^1_loc). Replacing x by x − x_0 for any fixed x_0 gives the same identity (translation invariance).

Integrated form (Rellich). Let Ω be a bounded open set with Lipschitz boundary, ν the outward unit normal, dS surface measure, and u ∈ C^2(Ω̄), or u ∈ H^2(Ω) with the boundary integrals read through the L^2(∂Ω) traces of ∇u. Then
   ∫_Ω (x·∇u) Δu dx = ((n−2)/2) ∫_Ω |∇u|^2 dx + ∫_∂Ω [ (x·∇u)(∂_ν u) − (1/2)|∇u|^2 (x·ν) ] dS.

Dirichlet case. If in addition u = 0 on ∂Ω (trace sense), then the tangential gradient vanishes on ∂Ω, ∇u = (∂_ν u) ν there, and the boundary term collapses to (1/2) ∫_∂Ω (x·ν) (∂_ν u)^2 dS. If moreover −Δu = λu in Ω, then
   λ ∫_Ω u^2 dx = (1/2) ∫_∂Ω (x·ν) (∂_ν u)^2 dS,
the Rellich formula expressing a Dirichlet eigenvalue by a boundary integral; equivalently 2λ||u||^2_{L^2(Ω)} = ∫_∂Ω (x·ν)(∂_ν u)^2 dS. For a domain star-shaped with respect to the origin (x·ν ≥ 0 on ∂Ω) the right side is nonnegative term by term. The same computation with −Δu = f(u), u = 0 on ∂Ω, is the Pohozaev identity.

Where it fails / hypotheses that matter. The integrated form needs enough regularity to give ∇u a boundary trace: u ∈ H^2(Ω) (or C^2 up to the boundary). A Dirichlet eigenfunction on a Lipschitz domain that is not convex (a re-entrant corner) need not belong to H^2(Ω), and the identity is then not available in this form without a separate justification. Without u = 0 on ∂Ω the tangential gradient contributes and the simplified boundary term (1/2)∫(x·ν)(∂_ν u)^2 is wrong: the full bracket must be kept. The sign of x·ν is not fixed for a general domain, so conclusions that use x·ν ≥ 0 (star-shapedness, Pohozaev-type nonexistence) fail otherwise. In dimension n = 2 the interior term ((n−2)/2)∫|∇u|^2 vanishes. The identity is for the Laplacian; for a variable-coefficient operator div(A∇u) extra terms involving x·∇A appear.
pointwise form: u ∈ C^2(Ω) (or H^2_loc, a.e.)
integrated form: Ω bounded with Lipschitz boundary, u ∈ C^2 up to the boundary or u ∈ H^2(Ω)
eigenvalue formula: additionally u = 0 on ∂Ω and −Δu = λu in Ω

[Thm 8 (GOE and GUE with finite-rank critical deformation) of arXiv:2605.30779, '2605.30779'] Let \(H_N\) be the GOE (resp.\ GUE) matrix of dimension \(N\) specified by \eqref{eq:defn_GOE} (resp.~\eqref{eq:defn_GUE}). Fix \(r\ge1\), and let $d_1, \dotsc, d_r$ be specified in \eqref{eq:defn_d_i}, $\w_1, \dotsc, \w_r$ be deterministic orthonormal vectors, and the spiked model $H^{(D)}_N$ be the $N \times N$ random matrix defined in \eqref{eq:defn_H^D_N}.

Let
\[
\lambda_1^{(D)}\ge \lambda_2^{(D)}\ge \cdots \ge \lambda_N^{(D)}
\]
be the eigenvalues of \(H_N^{(D)}\), and let \(\x_k^{(D)}\) be a unit eigenvector associated with \(\lambda_k^{(D)}\). Fix \(i\in\{1,\dots,r\}\) and let \(k\ge1\) be independent of \(N\). Let $\beta = 1$ for the GOE case and $\beta = 2$ for the GUE case. Put
\begin{equation}
  \Theta^{(i)}
  =
  (\theta_1,\dots,\theta_{i-1},\theta_{i+1},\dots,\theta_r),
  \qquad
  \mathcal G^{(\beta)}_{(r-1),i^c}:=\mathcal G^{(\beta)}_{\Theta^{(i)}},
\end{equation}
where \(\mathcal G^{(\beta)}_{\Theta^{(i)}}\) is the Airy-Green function from Proposition~\ref{pro:multispike_airy_green}. Let \(s_{\beta, k}^{(i)}\) be the unique solution in
\[
\bigl(
a_{\beta,k}^{(\Theta^{(i)})},
a_{\beta,k-1}^{(\Theta^{(i)})}
\bigr), \qquad a_{\beta,0}^{(\Theta^{(i)})}:= +\infty,
\]
of
\begin{equation} 
  \mathcal G^{(\beta)}_{(r-1),i^c}(x)=\theta_i.
\end{equation}
Then, as \(N\rightarrow\infty\), we have the joint convergence in distribution
\begin{align}
 N^{2/3}\bigl(\lambda_k^{(D)}-2\bigr) \Longrightarrow {}& s_{\beta,k}^{(i)},  & N^{1/3}\bigl|\langle \w_i,\x_k^{(D)}\rangle\bigr|^2
\Longrightarrow {}&
-\frac{1}{(\mathcal G^{(\beta)}_{(r-1),i^c})'\!\bigl(s_{\beta, k}^{(i)}\bigr)}.
\end{align}
Moreover, for any finite $K$, \eqref{GOE_Airy Green fun} holds jointly for $k = 1, 2, \dotsc, K$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: GOE and GUE with finite-rank critical deformation

\[ \int_{|y| > Y} |F(\sigma + iy)| dy \le \frac{2Y \tau_n(Y/K)}{\sigma}. \]
Also, if $Y \le K/a_{N + 1}$ then we may replace $\tau_n$ by $\tau$.

body: [Proposition prop:radial-resampling of arXiv:2411.19810, 'Radial conformal welding in Liouville quantum gravity'] Fix $\alpha>-\chi$, $\beta\in\mathbb{R}$, and $\theta_1,\theta_2$ in the range (equation eq:flowline-angle of the paper). Let $\mu_{\alpha\beta}$ be the joint law of the curves $(\eta_1,\eta_2)$ in Proposition~(prop:radial-flowline of the paper). Also consider a Markov chain  $(X_n)_{n\ge0}$ on pair of non-crossing continuous curves $(\tilde\eta_1,\tilde\eta_2)$ from $-i$ to 0 in $\mathbb{D}$ such that in each step one uniformly randomly picks $j\in\{1,2\}$, then resamples $\tilde\eta_j$ according to the conditional law of $\eta_j$ given $\eta_{3-j}$ as described in Proposition~(prop:radial-flowline of the paper)(equation item-resample of the paper). Then any invariant $\sigma$-finite measure $\mu$ of $(X_n)_{n\ge0}$ can be written as $\mu = \int_\mathbb{R} \mu_{\alpha\beta}\nu(d\beta)$ where $\nu$ is a $\sigma$-finite measure on $\mathbb{R}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:radial-resampling of arXiv:2411.19810

Fix gamma in (0,2) and kappa=16/gamma^2. Let (C,h,0,infinity) be a gamma-quantum cone in its circle-average embedding. Independently sample a whole-plane space-filling SLE_kappa from infinity to infinity, then parametrize it by gamma-LQG area, with eta(0)=0 and mu_h(eta([s,t]))=t-s. Normalize L_0=R_0=0 and define L_t-L_s as the gamma-LQG length of the left boundary of eta([s,t]) adjacent to eta([t,infinity)) minus that adjacent to eta((−infinity,s]); define R analogously with the right boundary. Then Z=(L,R) is a two-sided correlated Brownian motion: for a deterministic a=a(gamma)>0, Var(L_t)=Var(R_t)=a*|t| and Cov(L_t,R_t)=-a*|t|*cos(pi*gamma^2/4). Almost surely Z determines (h,eta) modulo rotation about the origin. The relation kappa=16/gamma^2 is a hypothesis of this theorem, not a universal dictionary for every decorated LQG model. Source: Mating of trees for random planar maps and Liouville quantum gravity: a survey, Theorem 4.6, equation (4.4), p.36; setup in Section 4.2.1, p.35; proof outline Section 4.2.2.

[Corollary 19 (Replicated Jacobi transfer) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] Let \(\Sigma\in\operatorname{Sym}_r^{++}(\R)\) and
\(\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\ldots,t_r)\) with \(t_1\cdots t_r\neq0\).  For the
replicated phase
\[
 F_{\Sigma,\boldsymbol t}(\boldsymbol x)
 =
 -\frac12
 \sum_{a,b=1}^r
 (\Sigma^{-1})_{ab}\langle x_a,x_b\rangle
 +
 i\sum_{a=1}^rt_aP(x_a),
\]
the principal Koszul differential is
\[
 i\sum_{a=1}^rt_a\,\mathrm dP_m(x_a)\wedge.
\]
It is regular, and the twisted de Rham module has exact rank
\[
 \mu_r=(m-1)^{rd}.
\]
Every replicated polynomial insertion, in particular
\(\prod_{a=1}^rP(x_a)\), has exact Jacobi coordinates rational in
\(\Sigma,\boldsymbol t\), and the coefficients of \(P\).  After choosing
Jacobi, de Rham, and thimble frames as in
\cref{thm:thimble-factorisation}, now in \(rd\) variables, denote the
resulting rational frame change and thimble period matrix by
\(B_{\mathrm{Jac}}^{(r)}\) and
\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{th}}^{(r)}\).  The period matrix against the Jacobi
normal-form frame then factors as
\[
 \Pi_{\mathrm{Jac}}^{(r)}
 =
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{th}}^{(r)}
 B_{\mathrm{Jac}}^{(r)}.
\]
For chosen cycles it is left-multiplied by their Betti coordinate matrix,
as in \eqref{eq:correct-global-factorisation}.

[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2604.04823, '2604.04823'] For any~$a\geq 1$ and $\nu > 0$, there exist~$\hat\epsilon(a), \eta(\nu), \hat  \gamma (\nu)> 0$ such that
for any~$\epsilon, h, \gamma > 0$ such that
\begin{equation}
\epsilon \leq \hat\epsilon\,,\quad
h \le \eta\epsilon^2\,,
\quad\text{and}\quad
\gamma < \hat  \gamma\,,
\end{equation}
$\hat P, \hat U$,$W$, and~$\hat Q_{h, \epsilon}$ are well-defined as in ~\eqref{e:Ptilde-def}, \eqref{e:Utilde-def}, \eqref{e:Wdef}, and Lemma~\ref{l:lyapunov}, respectively, and
\begin{align}
\frac{\hat Q_{h,\epsilon}W}{W}(x) - 1 &\le I_1 + I_2,\quad \forall x \in  \Omega \setminus \Omega_h\,,\\

\frac{\hat Q_{h,\epsilon}W}{W}(x) - 1 &\le I_1 + I_3,\quad \forall x \in  \Omega_h
\end{align}
where
\begin{align}
I_1 &\defeq \E\!\left[(\exp(\gamma D)-1)\exp(-\beta D)\right]\,, \\
I_2 &\defeq \E\!\left[(\exp(\gamma D)-1)(1-\exp(-\beta D))\one_{\{D<0\}}\right]\,,\\
I_3 &\defeq \E\brak{\paren{\exp\paren{\gamma D} - 1} \paren{ \one_{E^c\cap\set{D \leq 0}}-\exp\paren{-\beta D}\one_{E \cup \set{D \leq 0} }}}\,.
\end{align}
Moreover, the terms $I_1, I_2$, and~$I_3$ satisfy
\begin{align}

I_1 &\le -\gamma \beta \tilde I_1 
      + \frac12 \gamma h^2 \sigma^2 \Delta \hat U(x) 
      + \nu \gamma h^2\,, \quad \forall x \in  \Omega \\

\tilde I_1 &= \E\brak*{D^2}  = h^2\sigma^2 \abs{D\hat U(x)}^2 + O(h^3) \,, \quad\forall x \in \Omega \\

I_2 &\le (1+\nu)\gamma\beta \E\!\left[D^2 \one_{\{D\leq 0\}}\right]\,,
\quad \forall x \in  \Omega\setminus \Omega_h
\\

I_3 &\leq (1+\nu)\gamma\beta \E\brak{D^2 \one_{\set{D\leq 0}  \cup \paren*{\set{D>0}\cap E} }} - \gamma\E\brak{D\one_{E}}\,,
\quad \forall x \in  \Omega_h\,.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 19 of arXiv:2604.04823

[Lem 2 of arXiv:2608.21312, 'Interface between competing random walks on a cycle'] Let $\eta$ and $\eta'$ be independent random variables, each with the same distribution as $\tau_1$ under $\pr_0$. Then there are constants $0<c<C<\infty$ such that, for every $t\ge1$,
\begin{enumerate}
\item 
\[
    c t^{-1/2}\le \pr(\eta>t)\le C t^{-1/2}.
\]
\item 
\[
  c t^{-1/2}\le\pr\left(\frac32 t<\eta\le 2 t\right)\le C t^{-1/2}.
\]
\item 
\[
  ct^{-1/2} \le \pr(\eta-\eta'>t)\le C t^{-1/2}.
\]
\item
\[
  \E\left((\eta-\eta')^2\ind_{\{|\eta-\eta'|\le t\}}\right)\le C t^{3/2}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

[Definition 8 (Top-AE and diff-AE manifolds) of arXiv:2608.29427, '\small Positive mass and rigidity \\ for asymptotically flat tangent bundles'] A manifold \(M^n\) is called \emph{topologically asymptotically Euclidean} (top-AE), respectively \emph{differentially asymptotically Euclidean} (diff-AE), if there exists a compact set \(K\Subset M\) such that
	\[
	M\setminus K=M_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup M_k,
	\]
	where each end \(M_a\) is homeomorphic, respectively diffeomorphic, to
	\[
	\mathbb R^n\setminus\overline{B_{R_a}}
	\]
	for some \(R_a>0\).
	\par Moreover, the corresponding homeomorphisms or diffeomorphisms are assumed to be restrictions of maps
	\[
	\varphi_a:M_a\longrightarrow\mathbb R^n
	\]
	whose expression in polar coordinates is
	\[
	\varphi_a(p)=(r,q),
	\]
	with \(r\) increasing monotonically toward infinity along the end. More precisely, if
	\[
	K_1\Subset U\subset K_2,
	\]
	where \(U\subset M_a\) is open, then every point of \(M_a\setminus K_2\) has strictly larger \(r\)-coordinate than every point of \(U\setminus K_1\). See \cite[Definition 1.1]{AsadiFathiLakzian2025}.

[Thm eq:variance-CR-introduction of arXiv:2608.10215, 'The variance of the Pitman--Yor process: a Cifarelli--Regazzini identity and inversion for'] Let $\alpha \in (0,1)$ and $\theta > 1/2$ be fixed constants. Let $\mathsf{G}$ be a probability measure on $[0, +\infty)$ such that $\int_0^{+\infty} x^{2\alpha} \mathsf{G}(\mathrm{d} x) < +\infty$. 
Then, for any $t \ge 0$, there holds
\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}_{(\alpha, \theta)}\left[ \left(\frac{1}{1 + t\mathfrak{V}}\right)^{\theta - 1/2} \right] &= \int_0^1 {\mathcal B eta}(\mathrm{d}\rho; 1/2, \theta - 1/2) \times \nonumber \\
& \times \frac 12 \left\{ \Psi_+(\sqrt{t \rho (1 - \rho)}, t(1 - \rho)) + \Psi_-(\sqrt{t \rho (1 -\rho)}, t(1 - \rho)) \right\} \mathrm{d} \rho 
\end{align}
with
\[
\Psi_{\pm}(u, v) := \left\{ \int_0^{+\infty} [1 \pm 2ux + vx^2]^{\alpha} \mathsf{G}(\mathrm{d} x) \right\}^{-\theta/\alpha} \ .
\]
Moreover, if $\theta > 3/2$, one has
\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}_{(\alpha, \theta)}\left[\frac{1}{z + \mathfrak{V}}\right] &= \int_0^{+\infty} \frac{f_{\mathfrak{V}}(x)}{z + x} \mathrm{d} x \nonumber \\
&= z^{\theta - 1} \int_{\Delta_2} {\mathcal D ir}(\mathrm{d}\xi \mathrm{d}\eta; 1/2, 1, \theta - 3/2) 
\left[\frac{\Psi_+(z; \xi, \eta) + \Phi_-(z; \xi, \eta) }{2} \right] 
\end{align}
with
\begin{displaymath}
\Phi_{\pm}(z; \xi, \eta) := \left\{\int_0^{+\infty}  [z \pm 2\sqrt{z \xi\eta} x + \eta x^2]^{\alpha} \mathsf{G}(\mathrm{d} x) \right\}^{-\theta/\alpha}\ . 
\end{displaymath} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm eq:variance-CR-introduction of arXiv:2608.10215

$V_{\theta,\boldsymbol\ell}(h)$ in (equation eq:amplifier-value of the paper) is realized as
$|hC|$ by a primitive $(d+1+t)$-set obtained from $B_\theta$ by $t$ cyclic suspensions,
and
\begin{equation}
 |\mathcal R(h,d+1+t)|
 \gg_{d,t,I_1,\ldots,I_t}
 \left(\frac h{\log h}\right)^t\frac{N_h^2}{E_h}.
\end{equation}
If, throughout the shift window,
\begin{equation}
 c_0 h^d\leq |(h-J)B_\theta|\leq C_0 h^d
\end{equation}
for fixed $0<c_0<C_0$, then every value used to prove
(equation eq:prime-suspension-quantitative of the paper) lies in a fixed interval
\begin{equation}
[c_{d,t,\mathbf I}h^{d+t},C_{d,t,\mathbf I}h^{d+t}],
\end{equation}
where these constants also depend on the fixed bounds $c_0,C_0$ in
(equation eq:amplifier-macroscopic-seed of the paper).

Every counted value admits a witness $C$ satisfying
\begin{align}
 \mathcal H_C(z)
 &=\mathcal H_{B_\theta}(z)\prod_{i=1}^t[\ell_i]_z,
 \\
 \mathcal K_C(z)
 &=\mathcal K_{B_\theta}(z)\prod_{i=1}^t(1-z^{\ell_i}),
 \\
 \mathcal B_C(\xi,z)
 &=\mathcal B_{B_\theta}(\xi,z)\prod_{i=1}^t(1+\xi z^{\ell_i}),
 \\
 r_q(C)&=r_q(B_\theta)+\#\{i:\ell_i\leq q\}
 \qquad(q\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}),
 \\
 \operatorname{ndiam}(C)&=\left(\prod_{i=1}^t\ell_i\right)\operatorname{ndiam}(B_\theta).
 
\end{align}
If the seed projective coordinate ring is Cohen--Macaulay, then projective
Cohen--Macaulayness and Cohen--Macaulay type are preserved.  Since every
$\ell_i<h$, maximal degree-$h$ active rank propagates from the seed to $C$.

DRAFT source-to-need comparison. Ahlberg-Hoffman arXiv:1609.02447, A1 and Theorem 2.1, apply to atomless iid weights with finite E[min(X1,X2,X3,X4)^2]; all deterministic diverging endpoint sequences have origin-hit probabilities tending to zero. Maximizing over each finite S_R pair set therefore yields q_R->0, but supplies no adaptive union decay rate. Dembin-Elboim-Peled arXiv:2204.02332v5 Theorem 1.2 instead needs absolute continuity, a finite exponential moment, and more than 40 limit-shape extreme points; its bound C log^2(D+2)/D^(1/16) is insufficient for summing 32R^2-4R pairs. Theorem 1.3 bounds the union over common-height pairs ((-n,s),(n,s)), s in Z, by C log^2(n)/n^(1/24), already handling that restricted selector family. An arbitrary bigeodesic through 0 is not proved to have witnesses in that family. Source checks and these failed substitutions do not prove P0117. A separate September 24, 2026 OpenAI preprint claims the full moment-class result; its mathematical validity is still under audit.
Each cited theorem retains its own distribution and geometry hypotheses
D is the smaller endpoint-to-vertex distance
