[Cor non-crossing-surfaces of arXiv:2609.01499, 'On the rigidity of sloped height functions in $d\ge 3$ \\ and non-crossing surfaces'] Fix $D\ge 2$. There exists $\beta_0(D)>0$ such that for all $p\ge 1$,  $\beta>\beta_0$, and $\theta \in (0,\infty)$, the following holds. There exists an infinite-volume Gibbs measure over an infinite family $(\psi^{(i)}_v)_{v\in \mathbb{Z}^D,i\in \mathbb Z}$ of zero-slope $|\nabla\phi|^p$ height functions conditioned on non-crossing ($\psi^{(i+1)}_v \ge \psi_{v}^{(i)}$) and expected spacing $\theta$ in the sense of $\mathbb{E}[\psi_v^{(i+1)}- \psi_v^{(i)}]=\theta$ for all $v,i$, such that: 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item It is unique (modulo global integer shifts) among the family of such measures with ergodic minimal gradient and expected spacing $\theta$.
        \item There exists a pair of random variables $h_0, \alpha$, where $\alpha \sim \text{Unif}[0,1]$ if $\theta \notin \mathbb Q$ and $\alpha \sim \text{Unif}\{0,...,\frac{n-1}{n}\}$ if $\theta\in \mathbb Q$ with denominator $n$, such that  in almost every extremal component, for all $k\in \mathbb{Z}$, the $k$'th surface has dominant height $h_0 + \lfloor \alpha + k \theta \rfloor$. 
        \item The family of surfaces has exponential decay of correlations in the $\mathbb Z^{D+1}$-distance within its extremal components in the sense of~(equation eq:exponential decay local functions of the paper).
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor non-crossing-surfaces of arXiv:2609.01499

body:
[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2609.00087, 'Translational tiles without spectra\\ in finite abelian $p$-groups'] Let $H$ and $L$ be finite abelian groups.  Let $A\subset H$, and for each
$y\in L$ let $C_y\subset H$ satisfy
\[
 A\oplus C_y=H.
\]
Put
\[
 R=\bigcup_{y\in L}(C_y\times\{y\})\subset H\times L,
 \qquad q=|C_y|=\frac{|H|}{|A|}.
\]
For a nontrivial $\chi\in\widehat H$, define
\[
 W(\chi)=\sum_{y\in L}\widehat{\1_{C_y}}(\chi),
 \qquad
 D=\{\chi\ne0:W(\chi)=0\}.
\]
Let $\mathcal G_D$ be the Cayley graph on $\widehat H$ in which distinct
$u,v$ are adjacent when $u-v\in D$.  If $\mathcal G_D$ has no clique of
size $q$, then $R$ tiles $H\times L$ but is not spectral.

[Dfn 119 (continuous-time smoothed coefficients) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Analogously to Definition~\ref{d:sp.smooth}, we define the spatially smoothed continuous-time coefficients
	\[\srrr(t,y)\equiv
	\frac{\overline{\varrho_{\rrr,t}*\sphi}(y)}
		{\overline{\varrho_t*\sphi}(y)}\,,\quad
	\swww(t,y)\equiv
	\frac{\varsigma_{\www,t}*\sphi(y)}
		{\varsigma_t*\sphi(y)}\,,\]
as well as
	\begin{align*}
	\sB(t,y)
	&\equiv
	\frac{\overline{\varrho_{D,t}*\sphi}(y)}
		{\overline{\varrho_t*\sphi}(y)}
	\equiv
	p'(t)^{1/2} \cdot \sbbb(t,y)\,,\\
	\sV(t,y)
	&\equiv
	\frac{\overline{\varrho_{V,t}*\sphi}(y)}
		{\overline{\varrho_t*\sphi}(y)}
	\equiv
	p(t) \cdot \svvv(t,y)\,,\\
	\sU(t,y)
	&\equiv
	\frac{\overline{\varrho_{U,t}*\sphi}(y)}
		{\overline{\varrho_t*\sphi}(y)}
	\equiv
	\Big[ p(t) \cdot t p'(t) \Big]^{1/2}
		\cdot \suuu(t,y)\,.
	\end{align*}
Analogously to Definition~\ref{d:t.smooth}, we define the 
temporally smoothed continuous-time coefficients
	\beq
	
	\tB(t,y)
	\equiv
	\int_{\R} \tphi(s) \sB(t-s,y)\,ds
	= \tE\Big[ \sB(t-\sss,y)\Big]
	\eeq
and similarly $\tV$, $\tU$, $\trrr$, $\twww$. We define also the scaled coefficients
	\begin{align*}
	\tbbb(t,y)
	&\equiv\frac{\tB(t,y)}
		{p'(t)^{1/2} }\,,\\
	\tvvv(t,y)
	&\equiv \frac{\tV(t,y)}{p(t) } 
	\,,\\
	\tuuu(t,y)
	&\equiv
	\frac{\tU(t,y)}{[ p(t)
		\cdot t p'(t)]^{1/2}} \,.
	\end{align*}
and abbreviate $\tGam\equiv(\tbbb,\tvvv,\tuuu)$. Likewise, analogously to Definition~\ref{d:t.smooth.variant}, we define $\TGam\equiv(\Tbbb,\Tvvv,\Tuuu)$ as well as $(\iB,\iV,\iU,\ir,\iw)$.
We then let
	\begin{align*}
	\sF(t,y)
	&\equiv\Big\{ \sV+2\sU+\srrr\Big\}(t,y)\,,\\
	\tF(t,y)
	&\equiv\Big\{ \tV+2\tU+\trrr\Big\}(t,y)\,,\\
	\iF(t,y)
	&\equiv\Big\{ \iV+2\iU+\ir\Big\}(t,y)\,,
	\end{align*}
analogously to \eqref{e:sp.smoothed.F.N}, \eqref{e:temp.smoothed.F.N}, and \eqref{e:ideal.smoothed.F.N}.
title: continuous-time smoothed coefficients

[Proposition prop:SCinf-characterizations of arXiv:2608.11931, '\texorpdfstring{Nonlinear parabolic characterizations of stochastic completeness at infini'] Let $G$ be a graph.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \(G\) satisfies \hyperref[def:SC-infinity]{\textup{{(SC\textsubscript{$\infty$})}}}{}.
\item For one (equivalently, all) \(\lambda>0\),
      \(S_\lambda=\operatorname{id}+\lambda\Delta\) is injective on \(\ell^\infty(X)\).
\item For one (equivalently, all) \(\beta>0\), every
      \(0\le h\in\ell^\infty(X)\) satisfying
      \((\Delta+\beta)h\le0\) vanishes.
\item Bounded solutions of the heat equation are uniquely determined
      by bounded initial data.
\item $G$ satisfies the weak Omori--Yau maximum principle.
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma 49 (Fixed-chaos lower-moment comparison) of arXiv:2606.29292, 'Intrinsic Gaussian Tensor Geometry and Random Operator Spectra'] Let $B$ be a Banach space and let $X\in L^2(\Omega;B)$ belong to the
closed $q$th homogeneous Gaussian chaos, where $q\ge1$.  Then, for every
$1\le s\le2$,
\begin{equation}

 \norm X_{L^2(\Omega;B)}
 \le c_q\norm X_{L^s(\Omega;B)},
 \qquad c_q:=4\sqrt2\,3^{2q}.
\end{equation}
In particular, moments with any two exponents in $[1,\infty)$ on a fixed
homogeneous chaos are comparable with a constant depending only on the
order and the two exponents.

the model is a continuum rotationally invariant Riemannian first passage percolation on the PLANE
the model lies in the class for which Basu-Sidoravicius-Sly (2023) established their fluctuation estimates for passage times and geodesics
rotational invariance is used; the lattice Z^2 has none, so the result does not transfer as stated
the value of epsilon is not stated in the abstract

MECHANISM, in the authors' words: the argument 'uses fluctuation estimates for passage times and geodesics derived in Basu, Sidoravicius and Sly (2023) together with a multi-scale argument to establish that the geodesic exhibits disorder chaos, i.e., upon resampling a small fraction of the underlying randomness, the updated geodesic has on average a small overlap with the original one; this, established at a large number of scales, leads to a polynomial improvement of the variance bound.'
SO THE CAMPAIGN'S TARGET SHAPE IS THE RIGHT SHAPE: geodesic disorder chaos telescoped over many scales is the only route that has ever produced a polynomial gain. What it has never produced is a LATTICE gain, and the reason is that rotational invariance is consumed.
118 pages, 23 figures. Vladas Sidoravicius died in 2019; the authorship is as listed on arXiv.
SOURCE: arXiv:2604.01214v1, official arXiv API record retrieved by lane P4 on 2026-08-22; no journal reference as of that date.
VERIFICATION STATUS: theorem-checked-against-source at the level of the authors' abstract, which states the model class, the conclusion, the dependency and the mechanism. The 118-page proof was NOT read, so nothing is asserted here about the internal hypotheses, the size of epsilon, or which steps consume rotational invariance.
title: Basu-Sidoravicius-Sly (arXiv:2604.01214, submitted 1 April 2026): for a class of ROTATIONALLY INVARIANT RIEMANNIAN first passage percolation ON THE PLANE, the variance of the passage time is O(n^{1-epsilon}) for some epsilon > 0. This is the first polynomial improvement over the n/log n barrier in any variant of first-passage percolation - and it is a continuum, rotationally invariant result, NOT a lattice result: on Z^d the best known upper bound is still n/log n.

[Definition 13 ($\vartheta$-self-concordant barrier) of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Fix $\vartheta\ge1$. Let $N\ge1$, and let
$\Omega\subset\R^N$ be convex and relatively open in its affine hull,
that is, in the smallest affine subspace containing $\Omega$. Set
	\[
	\mathsf V_\Omega
	:=\operatorname{span}\{z-z':z,z'\in\Omega\}.
	\]
	Let $\Psi:\Omega\to\R$ be convex and $C^3$ along line segments in
	$\Omega$. Define the local seminorm
	\[
		\|h\|_{\Psi,z}^2:=\mathrm D^2\Psi(z)[h,h],
		\qquad z\in\Omega,\quad h\in\mathsf V_\Omega.
	\]
	We call such a convex function $\Psi$ a \emph{$\vartheta$-self-concordant barrier} for
	$\Omega$ if $\Psi(z)\to\infty$ as $z$ approaches the relative boundary
	of $\Omega$ and, for every $z\in\Omega$ and $h\in\mathsf V_\Omega$,
	\begin{equation*}
		\tag{SC}
		\bigl|\mathrm D^3\Psi(z)[h,h,h]\bigr|
		\le 2\|h\|_{\Psi,z}^3.
	\end{equation*}
	It must also satisfy the barrier-parameter bound for all $h\in \mathsf V_\Omega$
	\begin{equation*}
		\tag{$\mathrm{BP}_\vartheta$}
		|\mathrm D\Psi(z)[h]|
		\le \sqrt{\vartheta}\,\|h\|_{\Psi,z}.
	\end{equation*}
title: $\vartheta$-self-concordant barrier

[Lemma 14 (Scalar octant lemma) of arXiv:2608.15805, 'Spectral duality structures and the Fisher--Rao geometry of reset distributions'] For $\alpha,\beta>0$,
\[
\bigl\{x\in\mathbb R^2_{\ge0}:\ \alpha x_1^2=\beta x_2^2\bigr\}
=\bigl\{x\in\mathbb R^2_{\ge0}:\

body: [Abstract of arXiv:2609.04138, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ I:\\ subsequential limits of the non-simple...'] We consider the conformal loop ensemble (CLE) with the parameter $\kappa=4$, the critical value at or below which the loops are simple and do not intersect each other or the domain boundary. We show that the loops of a $\CLE_4$ uniquely determine a conformally invariant, local, and geodesic metric so that the metric ball growth from the domain boundary coincides with the uniform exploration of Werner and Wu. This metric was previously constructed in unpublished work of Sheffield, Watson, and Wu. Our approach differs in that we show that the metric arises as the renormalized limit of the graph metric on $\CLE_\kappa$ loops as $\kappa \downarrow 4$. In this first paper in a series of three, we prove that the subsequential limits exist and define a non-trivial conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ which is local and such that the metric ball growth from the boundary is given by the uniform exploration of Werner and Wu. In subsequent work, we will show that the subsequential limit exists as a true limit.

[Lemma l:der-psi of arXiv:2411.16913, 'Entropies of the Poisson distribution as functions of intensity: ``normal'' and ``anomalou'] For all $\alpha>0$ and $\lambda>0$, the function $\psi(\alpha, \lambda)$ introduced by (equation psifunction of the paper) is well defined and continuously differentiable in two variables, moreover, the partial derivatives can be computed as follows:
    \begin{gather}
    
    \frac{\partial}{\partial \alpha} \psi(\alpha, \lambda) = 
    \sum_{i=0}^\infty (p_i(\lambda))^\alpha \log p_i(\lambda),
    \\
    
    \frac{\partial}{\partial \lambda} \psi(\alpha, \lambda) = \alpha e^{-\alpha \lambda} \sum_{i=0}^\infty (i-\lambda) \frac{\lambda^{\alpha i - 1}}{(i!)^\alpha},
    \end{gather}
    where $p_i(\lambda) = e^{-\lambda} \frac{\lambda^i}{i!}$.

[Lemma 23 of arXiv:2604.19738, 'Phase Transitions in the Fluctuations of Functionals of Random Neural Networks \\'] Let $\kappa$ satisfy~\Cref{ass:cri-pot} and set $\rho := (\gamma_1-1)^{-1}$.
There exist constants $\beta_0>0$ and $\beta_1$, depending only on $\kappa$,
such that the renormalized iterates
\begin{equation}
\beta_L(x)
:=
L^{\rho+1}
\Big(
\kappa_L(x)
-1
+\beta_0 L^{-\rho}
-\beta_1 L^{-(\rho+1)} \log L
\Big),
\qquad x\in[-1,1),
\end{equation}
converge pointwise as $L\to\infty$ to a limit function  $\beta:[-1,1)\to\mathbb R$.

Moreover, setting $\nu = 1- \gamma_1$, there exist $L_1>0$ and constants $0<\delta<1$ and $C>0$ such that for all
$L\ge L_1$ one has
\begin{align}

|\beta_L(x)|
&\lesssim
(1-x^2)^{-\nu},
&& x\in (-1,1),\\[6pt]

\beta_L(x)
&\gtrsim
(1-x)^{-\nu} [ 1 - C(1-x)^{-\nu}L^{-1}]
&& x\in(1-\delta,1),

\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 44 (De Sitter and  hyperbolic   parallels \cite{IT2007}) of arXiv:2608.26823, 'Evolutes, involutes and parallels of Legendre curves in hyperbolic and de Sitter 2-spaces '] \rm
Let $(\bgamma_d,\bgamma_d^h):I\rightarrow\overline{\Delta}_1$ be a spacelike Legendre curve  with curvature $(m_d,n_d)$ and $\theta\in\R$.  
The \textit{de Sitter parallel} $\overline{DP}_{\theta}(\bgamma_d,\bgamma_d^h):I\rightarrow S_1^2$      of $(\bgamma_d,\bgamma_d^h)$ is   defined as
$$
\overline{DP}_{\theta}(\bgamma_d,\bgamma_d^h)(t)=\sinh \theta\bgamma_d^h(t)+\cosh\theta\bgamma_d(t).$$
The \textit{hyperbolic parallel} $\overline{HP}_{\theta}(\bgamma_d,\bgamma_d^h):I\rightarrow H^2$   of $(\bgamma_d,\bgamma_d^h)$ is   defined as
$$
\overline{HP}_{\theta}(\bgamma_d,\bgamma_d^h)(t)=\cosh \theta\bgamma_d^h(t)+\sinh\theta\bgamma_d(t).$$
title: De Sitter and  hyperbolic   parallels \cite{IT2007}

body:
[Definition 3 (Free energy) of arXiv:2605.28473, 'The BKT transition and surface tension differentiability'] For fixed $\beta\in(0,\infty)$, the free energy is a function $f_\beta:\R\to\R$ defined by
    \begin{equation}
        
        f_\beta(s) := \lim_{n\to\infty}-\frac{1}{|\Lambda_n^*|}\log Z_{\Lambda_n^*,\beta}^s.
    \end{equation}
    With this normalisation, $f_\beta$ is symmetric and strictly
    convex~\cite{Sheffield_2005_RandomSurfaces}.
    We write $f'_\beta$ for its \emph{right} derivative at points where the distinction
    matters, and $f''_\beta$ for its second derivative when it exists.
    If $f'_\beta(0)>0$, then the free energy is not differentiable at $0$ and we say that
    the free energy has a \emph{corner} at $0$.
title: Free energy

[Theorem berry of arXiv:2411.06006, 'Mixing time of the torus shuffle'] Let $Y_1, \dots, Y_N$ be independent random vectors in ${\mathbf R}^2$ with mean zero,
  and let $S = Y_1 + \cdots + Y_N$. Suppose that the covariance matrix $\Sigma$, of $S$, is
  invertible. Let $Z$ be a centered normal random vector with variance matrix  $\Sigma$.
Then for any convex set $U \subset {\mathbf R}^2$, we have
\begin{align}
    \left \vert { \mathbb P}(S \in U) - { \mathbb P}(Z \in U) \right \vert \leq C(2)^{\frac{1}{4}}\gamma,
    
\end{align}
where $C$ is a universal constant and $\gamma = \sum_{q=1}^{N}{\mathbf E}\left[\abs{\Sigma^{-1/2}Y_q}_2^3\right]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a Hilbert space $H$, with scalar product $<x,y>$ and norm $||x||=\sqrt{<x,x>}$, the norms, or lengths, are subject to the parallelogram identity
$$||x+y||^2+||x-y||^2=2(||x||^2+||y||^2)$$
and the scalar products can be recovered from lengths via the polarization identity:
$$<x,y>
=\frac{||x+y||^2-||x-y||^2+i||x+iy||^2-i||x-iy||^2}{4}$$
Also, we can say that two vectors are orthogonal when their scalar product is zero.

[Theorem main-thm of arXiv:2608.23202, 'Locally finite Fixed points of Branching Brownian Motion'] Let $\lambda \geq \sqrt{2}$ and $\Pi$ be a point process. Then $\Pi$ is a fixed point of BBM with drift $\lambda$ in the sense of Definition (def-fixed-point of the paper) if and only if there exists a $[-\infty, \infty)$-valued random variable $S$ independent of $\widetilde{\mathcal E}_\infty^\lambda$ such that 
\[ \Pi \overset{d}{=} \widetilde{\mathcal E}_\infty^\lambda (\cdot - S). \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem main-thm of arXiv:2608.23202

[Theoaen of arXiv:2608.25865, 'Instability of Böhm's Einstein metrics'] If $(g_i)$ denotes a sequence of Böhm metrics on $S^{k+1}\times S^l$ or $S^{k+l+1}$, with $k,l\geqslant 2$, $k+l\leqslant 8$, and if $\nu_i$ denotes the number of negative eigenvalues of the Lichnerowicz Laplacian associated with $g_i$ (called the \textit{index}), then
$$\nu_i\underset{i\to+\infty}{\longrightarrow}{+\infty}.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered theoAen of arXiv:2608.25865, 'Instability of Böhm's Einstein metrics'

body: [Lemma 21 of arXiv:2506.15736, 'Coming down from infinity for coordinated particle systems'] Suppose a $\Lambda$-coalescent with death according to $D(dz)$ has an infinite number of particles enter before time $t_0$, i.e. particles enter at random times $(s_n)_{n \in \N}$ where $s_n \leq t_0$ for all $n \in \N$. Denote the block counting process of this coalescent by $(\mathring{N}(t))_{t \geq 0}$. Then there is a coupling such that $N(t_0) \leq \mathring{N}(t_0)$ where $(N(t))_{t\geq 0}$ is the block counting process of the $\Lambda$-coalescent with killing according to $D(dz)$ starting with infinitely many particles.
title: Lemma 21 of arXiv:2506.15736

Let X be a centered Gaussian measure on a real separable Hilbert space K with covariance operator Q_X, and let (P_u) be its Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroup, P_u h(x) = E[h(e^{-u} x + sqrt(1 - e^{-2u}) X)]. For a test function h in C_b^2(K), the infinite-dimensional Stein equation Tr(Q_X D^2 U(x)) - <x, DU(x)>_K = h(x) - E[h(X)] is solved, uniquely up to an additive constant, by U(x) = -int_0^infinity (P_u h(x) - E[h(X)]) du (Shih); substituting t = e^{-2u}, U(x) = -int_0^1 (1/(2t)) (E[h(sqrt(t) x + sqrt(1 - t) X)] - E[h(X)]) dt.
K is a real separable Hilbert space
Q_X is trace-class

[Lemma 23 (It\^o's formula) of arXiv:2606.08776, 'Approximation of certain stochastic integrals with anticipating integrands'] Assume $f: [0,1]\times\R\times\R^{K} \to  \R$ such that the partial derivatives $f_x, f_t, \nabla_y f, f_{xx}, \nabla_y f_x$ exist, are continuous,
and polynomially bounded in $(x,y)$ uniformly in $t$.  Assume that $L=(L_1,\dots,L_K)$ is a  random variable such that  $L_i \in \DD_{1,4}$.
Then for $0\le s < t \le 1$ one has, a.s.,
\begin{align*}
   f(t, X_t,L)
& = f(s, X_s,L) + \int_s^t f_u(u, X_u,L) du \\
&\quad  +\int_s^t f_x(u, X_u,L) \sigma(X_u) \delta W_u \\
&\quad  +\half \int_s^t f_{xx}(u, X_u,L) \sigma^2(X_u) du \\
&\quad  + \int_s^t\nabla_y f_x(u, X_u,L) \sigma(X_u) \cdot D_uL du.
\end{align*}
title: It\^o's formula

Let $f\in L^1(\mathbb T)$, $x\in\mathbb T$ and $s\in\mathbb C$. (Dini) If $\int_0^{1/2}\frac{|f(x+t)+f(x-t)-2s|}{t}\,dt<\infty$, then the symmetric partial sums converge: $S_Nf(x)\to s$. In particular, if $f$ is Holder continuous at $x$ of some order $\alpha>0$ (i.e. $|f(x+t)-f(x)|\le C|t|^\alpha$ for all small real $t$, of either sign), or differentiable at $x$, or more generally if the two-sided Dini integral $\int_{|t|\le1/2}\frac{|f(x+t)-f(x)|}{|t|}\,dt$ is finite, then $S_Nf(x)\to f(x)$ (the two-sided condition dominates the symmetric one with $s=f(x)$, by the triangle inequality). (Riemann localization) If $f,g\in L^1(\mathbb T)$ agree on an open interval containing $x$, then $S_Nf(x)-S_Ng(x)\to0$; so convergence or divergence of a Fourier series at $x$ depends only on the behaviour of $f$ near $x$, even though the coefficients depend on $f$ globally.
f integrable on the circle
Dini: the integral of |f(x+t)+f(x-t)-2s|/t over (0,1/2) is finite; mere continuity at x is NOT enough
the Holder / two-sided Dini conditions must control t of both signs
symmetric partial sums (the statement is about S_N, not about arbitrary summation orders)

body:
[Definition 1 of arXiv:2608.26565, 'A Horizon-Free Extrinsic Penrose Inequality'] The end $\mathcal E_+$ is \emph{asymptotically flat} if, after a rigid motion, there
are $R_0>0$, $\tau>1/2$, a compact set $K\subset S$, and a smooth function
$\psi:\mathbb R^2\setminus B_{R_0}\to\mathbb R$ such that
\[
 S_+=\{(y,\psi(y)):|y|>R_0\},
\]
where $S_+$ is the component of $S\setminus K$ representing
$\mathcal E_+$. Along this component, the chosen outward normal is
\[
 \nu_S(y,\psi(y))
 =\frac{(D\psi(y),-1)}{\sqrt{1+|D\psi(y)|^2}}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 |D\psi(y)|+|y||D^2\psi(y)|
 =O(|y|^{-\tau}).
\]
With this orientation, the \emph{extrinsic mass of the distinguished end} is
\begin{equation}
 m_+(S)=\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac1{2\pi r}
 \int_{|y|=r}y\cdot D\psi\,d\mathcal H^1.
 
\end{equation}
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2608.26565

[Corollary 19 (Spectral consequences) of arXiv:2608.04824, 'Strong Convergence for a General Class of Random Matrix Models'] On the probability-one event of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)] If \(Q=Q^*\) is a fixed self-adjoint \(*\)-polynomial, then
\[
 d_{\rm H}\bigl(\spn(Q(X_n,X_n^*)),
                    \spn(Q(c,c^*))\bigr)\longrightarrow0.
\]
\item[(2)] For every fixed \(*\)-polynomial \(Q\),
\[
 d_{\rm H}\bigl(\operatorname{sv}(Q(X_n,X_n^*)),
                    \operatorname{sv}(Q(c,c^*))\bigr)\longrightarrow0.
\]
\item[(3)] If \(Q(c,c^*)\) is invertible, then \(Q(X_n,X_n^*)\) is invertible
for all sufficiently large \(n\), and
\[
 \|Q(X_n,X_n^*)^{-1}\|\longrightarrow\|Q(c,c^*)^{-1}\|.
\]
\item[(4)] For every \(1\leq\kappa\leq d\),
\[
 \|X_{\kappa,n}\|\longrightarrow2\sigma_\kappa.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Assertions~(1)--(3) also hold when \(Q\) has coefficients in a fixed matrix
algebra. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Spectral consequences

[Prop prop-vmexist of arXiv:2411.14350, 'Randomized Geodesic Flow on Hyperbolic Groups'] [bh-book] Given $\delta \geq 0$, there exists $a > 1$ such that if
	$(X,d)$ is $\delta-$hyperbolic, then for any base-point $o$,
	a visual metric $d_v $
	with parameter $a>1$ exists on $\partial X$ with respect to the base-point $o$.
	Further, for any $o' \in X$, let $d_v'$ be a visual metric on $\partial X$
 with respect to the base-point $o'$ and
	with parameter $a>1$. Then $d_v'$
	is equivalent (as a metric) to $d_v$.
	
	There exists a natural topology on $\hat{X} = X \cup \partial X$ such that
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item $X$ is open and dense in $\hat X$,
		\item $\partial X$ and $\hat{X}$ are compact if $X$ is proper,
		\item the subspace topology on $\partial X$ agrees with that given by $d_v$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop prop-vmexist of arXiv:2411.14350

body:
[Lemma 30 of arXiv:2506.17045, '\LARGE{On bivariate Archimax copulas: Level sets, mass distributions and related results}'] Let $I_1,I_2,I_3$ be open sub-intervals of $\mathbb{R}$ and let $\iota \colon I_1 \rightarrow I_2$ be a function whose left-hand derivative $D^-\iota$ exists. Moreover, let $\eta \colon I_2 \rightarrow I_3$ be an arbitrary function. Then the following assertions hold:
      \begin{itemize}
          \item[$(i)$] If $\eta$ is strictly decreasing and convex, then
          $$
          D^-\eta^{-1}(z) = \frac{1}{D^+\eta(\eta^{-1}(z))}
          $$
          holds for every $z \in I_3$, whereby $\eta^{-1}$ denotes the inverse function of $\eta$.
          \item[$(ii)$] If $D^-\eta$ exists and $\iota$ is a non-decreasing function, then
          $$
          D^-(\eta\circ\iota)(t) = D^-\eta(\iota(t)) \cdot D^-\iota(t)
          $$
          holds for every $t \in I_1$.
        \item[$(iii)$] If $D^-\eta$ exists and $\iota$ is a non-increasing function, then
          $$
          D^-(\eta\circ\iota)(t) = D^+\eta(\iota(t)) \cdot D^-\iota(t)
          $$
          holds for every $t \in I_1$.
      \end{itemize}

[Theorem result2 of arXiv:2607.01463, 'Two Multi--Draw Coupon Collector models with different retention rules'] Consider the  $d$ coupon collector's problem (d--CCP), where in each run we keep \textbf{the least} collected coupon so far. Let $T_{N,1}$ be the number of trials until all $N$ different types of coupons, which are uniformly distributed, are collected (at least once). Then, as $N\rightarrow \infty$
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}[T_{N,1}]=
\frac{N}{d}\log N
+\left(\frac{\gamma}{d}+
C_d\right)N
-
\frac{d-1}{2d}\log N
+
D_d
+
\mathcal{O}\!\left(\frac{\log N}{N}\right),

\end{equation}
where,
\begin{equation}
C_d:
=
\int_0^1
\left(
\frac{1}{1-(1-x)^d}-\frac{1}{dx}
\right)\,dx,

\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
D_d:
=
\frac{2d^2-3d+3-2\gamma \left(d-1\right)}{4d}
-\frac{d-1}{2}C_d.

\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let {e_i : i in I} be an orthonormal basis of a Hilbert space H. Then for every x in H, x = sum over i of <x, e_i> e_i (with at most countably many nonzero terms, converging in norm), and ||x||^2 = sum over i of |<x, e_i>|^2. More generally <x, y> = sum over i of <x, e_i> times the conjugate of <y, e_i>. Conversely, an orthonormal family for which ||x||^2 = sum over i of |<x, e_i>|^2 holds for every x is an orthonormal basis.

[Theoremi thm_main_directed of arXiv:2604.04672, 'Connected components and topological ends of stationary planar forests'] Assume additionally that with probability one, $G$ is oriented with out-degree $1$, non-empty and all directed infinite path $(\pi_n)_{n\geq0}$ in $G$ satisfies $\lim_{n\to\infty}\pi_n\cdot e_2=+\infty$, where $e_2\coloneqq (0,1)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and $\cdot$ denotes the standard scalar product. Then, exactly one of the following holds almost surely:
        \begin{itemize}
            \item $G$ is a single one-ended tree, or
            \item $G$ consists of infinitely many disjoint two-ended trees.
        \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition prop:ito-centered-lyapunov-differential of arXiv:2605.20697, 'Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for \\ Second-Order Consensus-Based Optimization'] Let \(p\geqslant2\), and assume the conditions of (assump:centered-decay of the paper).
Let
\[
    L_p(t):=L_p(\mathcal X_t^J,\mathcal V_t^J)
\]
denote the pathwise centered Lyapunov functional defined in
(equation eq:random-Lp-def of the paper) for \(p>2\), and in (equation eq:random-L2-def of the paper) for \(p=2\).

Define the local martingale \(M_{p,t}:=J^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^J M_{p,t}^j\) by
\begin{equation}
    \mathrm d M_{p,t}^j
    :=
    \begin{cases}
        \displaystyle
        2\left\langle \hat Z_t^j,\mathrm d M_t^{j,\mathrm{center}}\right\rangle
        +
        \frac5\gamma
        \left\langle Y_t^j,\mathrm d M_t^{j,\mathrm{center}}\right\rangle,
        & p=2,\\[1.2em]
        \displaystyle
        p|\hat Z_t^j|^{p-2}
        \left\langle \hat Z_t^j,\mathrm d M_t^{j,\mathrm{center}}\right\rangle
        +
        \frac m\gamma |Y_t^j|^{p-2}
        \left\langle Y_t^j,\mathrm d M_t^{j,\mathrm{center}}\right\rangle,
        & p>2.
    \end{cases}
\end{equation}
Then there exists a local martingale \(M_{p,t}\) such that, in the sense of semimartingale differentials,
\begin{equation}
    \mathrm d L_p(t)
    \leqslant
    -\lambda_p L_p(t)\,\mathrm d t+\mathrm d M_{p,t},
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
    \lambda_p
    :=
    \begin{cases}
        \displaystyle
        \frac{\min\{v_1,v_3\}}{c_2^{(2)}},
        & p=2,\\[1.2em]
        \displaystyle
        \frac{p\mu_{\mathrm{gap},p}}{4\gamma},
        & p>2.
    \end{cases}
\end{equation}
Here, for \(p=2\),
\[
    v_1:=\frac1{m\gamma}+\frac3{\gamma^3}-K_\sigma,
    \qquad
    v_3:=\frac{2\gamma}{m}-\frac3\gamma,
\]
and \(c_2^{(2)}\) is the upper norm-equivalence constant associated with \(\psi_2\).

Moreover, when \(p>2\), the stronger componentwise estimate holds:
\begin{equation}
    \mathrm d L_p(t)
    \leqslant
    -\widehat\lambda_Y
    \left(\frac1J\sum_{j=1}^J |Y_t^j|^p\right)\mathrm d t
    -\widehat\lambda_Z
    \left(\frac1J\sum_{j=1}^J |\hat Z_t^j|^p\right)\mathrm d t
    +
    \mathrm d M_{p,t},
\end{equation}
where
\begin{align}
    \widehat\lambda_Y
    &:=
    \frac1\gamma
    \left[
        C_{\mathrm{pos}}
        -
        \gamma\left(\frac2m+\frac1{\gamma^2}\right)
        \left(\frac4\gamma\right)^{p-1}
        +
        \frac{m(p-1)}{\gamma^2}
    \right],
    \\
    \widehat\lambda_Z
    &:=
    p\left(\frac\gamma m+\frac1\gamma\right)
    -
    \left(
        \frac{p-1}{2m}\gamma+\frac{p-1}{4\gamma}
    \right)
    -
    \frac{2m(p-1)}{p\gamma}
    -
    \Lambda_p\sigma^{\frac{2p}{p-2}}\gamma^{\frac2{p-2}}\,,
    
\end{align}
where $C_{\mathrm{pos}} = 1-\frac{3\mu_{\mathrm{gap},p}}{16} - \frac{m(p-1)(p-2)}p$ as defined from (equation eq:Cpos-def of the paper). Under (assump:centered-decay of the paper), these coefficients satisfy
\begin{equation}
    \widehat\lambda_Y
    \geqslant
    \lambda_p
    \left(
        a_p+\frac{m(p-1)}{p\gamma}
    \right),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
    \widehat\lambda_Z
    \geqslant
    \lambda_p
    \left(
        1+\frac{m}{p\gamma}
    \right).
\end{equation}

body: [Corollary 3.12 of arXiv:2603.27659, 'Operator Norm Bounds for Multi-leg Matrix Tensors and Applications to Random Matrix Theory'] With $Y$ the partial-trace matrix of partial permutations $\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k}\in\mathcal{P}^{\prime}([m])$ applied to contractions $A_{1},\ldots,A_{m}\in M_{N}(\mathbb{C})^{\otimes k}$, $N^{M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})}\leq\max_{\|A_{1}\|,\ldots,\|A_{m}\|\leq 1}\|Y\|\leq N^{C(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})}.$ The lower bound is attained by the same permutation tensors as in Theorem 3.11. Here, for the graph $G_{\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k}}$ of the permutations, $M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})$ is the maximum over blue-edge configurations of the number of directed cycles, and $C(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})=\min_{G^{\prime}}R_{G^{\prime}}$, the minimum over full simple partial graphs $G^{\prime}$ (partial graphs keeping every rectangle and containing no directed cycle for any blue-edge configuration) of the number $R_{G^{\prime}}$ of colored edges removed to obtain $G^{\prime}$ (Definition 2.1).

[Proposition prop:sharp-lri-4d of arXiv:2608.23135, 'Graph distance and effective resistance of the random walk trace in four and five dimensio'] ([ShiraishiWatanabe2026])

Let $S^1$ and $S^2$ be independent simple random walks on $\mathbb Z^4$ started from
$0$.  For $k\ge1$, set
\begin{align*}
        f(n,k)=
        \mathbb P\bigl(S^1[0,n]\cap S^2[kn,(k+1)n]\ne\emptyset\bigr).
\end{align*}
Then, uniformly in the range of $k$ used in this paper,
\begin{equation}

        f(n,k)=
        \frac{1}{2\log n}
        \log\left(1+\frac{1}{k^2+2k}\right)
        \left\{1+O\left(\frac{1}{k(\log n)^{3/25}}\right)\right\}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.03497, 'Connective Constants on Nested Fractal Graphs'] The limits of the rooted and uniform self-avoiding walk counts exist and
are equal:
\[
  \mu
  :=
  \lim_{n\to\infty}c_n^{1/n}
  =
  \lim_{n\to\infty}u_n^{1/n}
  =
  \inf_{n\ge1}u_n^{1/n}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
  1\le\mu\le D-1<\infty.
\]
Thus \(\mu\) is the connective constant of \(F_\infty\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Proposition 42 (Conditional LAN for coarser windows) of arXiv:2604.10792, 'Variable-Length Markov Chains on Finite Quivers: Boundary-Window Identifiability, Exact De'] Fix $m<r$ and assume exact depth $r$ at $\theta_0$. Then $Z^{(m)}$ is a deterministic function of the hidden finite-state Markov chain $Z^{(r)}$. Suppose, in addition, that the projected family satisfies the hypotheses of a standard finite hidden-Markov-model LAN theorem appropriate to this deterministic-emission setting, including the required fixed hidden support, irreducibility/mixing, smooth dependence of the positive hidden transitions on $\theta$, and any domination or identifiability conditions used by the invoked theorem. Then the experiment generated by $Z^{(m)}$ is LAN at $\theta_0$ on every fixed tangent block $T\subset T_{\theta_0}\Theta$. This statement provides only bare LAN for the coarse observation scheme and does not by itself yield the factorized shift representation required in \cref{ass:lan}.

[Theorem 27 (Block contraction theorem) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Under the standing fixed-threshold application, fix \(\delta_0\geq c_0\).
There are constants
\[
        T_{\mathrm{blk}}<\infty,\qquad
        \eta_{\mathrm{blk}}>0,\qquad
        \theta_{\mathrm{blk}}>0,\qquad
        \Lambda_*<\infty
\]
with the following property.  The constants
\(\eta_{\mathrm{blk}},\theta_{\mathrm{blk}},\Lambda_*\) depend only on
\(K,\delta_0,N,\sigma\).  The start-time threshold \(T_{\mathrm{blk}}\) may
additionally depend on the fixed Bamler tail data \(T_B(c_0)\) and
\(\eps_B^{c_0}\) for the given flow.

Let \(p(\tau)\) be a parabolically rescaled \(\delta_0\)-large block starting
at \(S\geq T_{\mathrm{blk}}\), fix a torus fibration \(\pi:M\to S^1\), and put
\[
        q(1)=p(1),\qquad r(1)=\overline{q(1)}.
\]
Suppose that \(r(1)\) is Riemannian and, with
\[
 b=\|q(1)-r(1)\|_{C^{N,\sigma}(M,r(1))},
 \qquad d=d_{\TT^2}(r(1)),
\]
one has
\[
        b<\eta_{\mathrm{blk}},\qquad
        d<\theta_{\mathrm{blk}},\qquad
        \BG_N(r(1);\Lambda_*).
\]
Equivalently, \((q(1),r(1))\) is an admissible stage start in the sense of
Definition~\ref{def:admissible-stage-start}, with constants
\(\Lambda_*,\eta_{\mathrm{blk}},\theta_{\mathrm{blk}}\).
Then the invariant Ricci flow \(r\) and the Ricci--DeTurck flow \(q\) relative
to it exist on \([1,100]\).  At the rescaled endpoint, put
\[
        q^+(1)=100^{-1}q(100),\qquad
        \rho^+=100^{-1}r(100),\qquad
        r^+(1)=\overline{q^+(1)},
\]
and set
\[
        b^+=\|q^+(1)-r^+(1)\|_{C^{N,\sigma}(M,r^+(1))}.
\]
Then \(r^+(1)\) is Riemannian and
\begin{equation}
        b^+\leq\tfrac12 b,\qquad
        d_{\TT^2}(r^+(1))<\theta_{\mathrm{blk}},\qquad
        \BG_N(r^+(1);\Lambda_*).
\end{equation}
Thus the same admissible-start conditions hold at the restart.  The ordinary
Ricci flow corresponding to \(q\) is \(p\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Block contraction theorem

[Definition 12 of arXiv:2606.03534, 'Construction and simulation of a path-valued model of dendrite development'] The \textit{graph representation} of a measure $\mu \in \mathcal{N}_\mathcal{S}^{\#}$ is a graph $G=(V,E)$ describing the spatial embedding of $\mu$, defined as follows. Let 
    \begin{align*}
        V &= \Big\{ x \in X \, \Big| \, \exists \, (\omega,a) \in [\mu] \text{ s.t. } x = \omega(0) \text{ or } x=\hat{\omega}  \Big\} \,, \\
        E &= \Big\{ (x,y) \in V \times V \, \Big| \, \exists \, (\omega,a) \in [\mu] \text{ s.t. } \omega(0)=x \text{ and } \hat{\omega}= y  \Big\} \,.
    \end{align*}
    To an edge $(x,y) \in E$ we assign the corresponding path $\omega_{xy} \in \mathcal{W}$ to be the element $(\omega_{xy},a) \in [\mu]$ with $\omega_{xy}(0)=x$ and $\hat{\omega}_{xy} = y$. 
    This network is fully determined by $\mu$ and so defines a mapping $\mu \mapsto (V,E)$ from $\mathcal{N}_\mathcal{S}^\#$ into a space of networks. Denote this mapping by $G(\mu)$.

[Theorem 29 (Strict cycle characterization) of arXiv:2608.26516, '2608.26516'] Fix a finite hypothesis set $H$, a deterministic $H$-valued learner $A$, positive coefficients $\lambda(S)$, and a finite family of samples $\Scal$.  There exists a regularizer $\psi:H\to\R_{\ge0}$ for which $A(S)$ is the unique minimizer of
\[
    h\longmapsto\emp_S(h)+\lambda(S)\psi(h)
\]
for every $S\in\Scal$ if and only if every directed cycle in $G_{A,\lambda}(\Scal)$ has strictly positive total weight.

body:
[Theorem 41 of arXiv:2609.03070, 'Variants of order semicontinuity in Banach lattices'] Let $F$ be an AM-space. Then:
\item[(i)] $F$ is semicontinuous if and only if it isometrically embeds as a regular sublattice of $C\left(K\right)$, for some compact Hausdorff space $K$.
\item[(ii)] $F$ is demicontinuous if and only if it isomorphically embeds as a regular sublattice of $C\left(K\right)$, for some compact Hausdorff space $K$. In this case it is topologically semicontinuous.
\item[(iii)] $F$ is pointwise demicontinuous if and only if it injectively embeds as a regular sublattice of $C\left(K\right)$, for some compact Hausdorff space $K$.\medskip

    Moreover, ``regular'' can be replaced with ``order dense'', while $K$ can be assumed extremally disconnected.

body:
[Proposition pro:green of arXiv:2509.21253, '\bf Capacity in high dimensional percolation'] Let $\lambda>0$. For each $R>0$ let $\mathcal{G}_{\lambda,R}$ be the random set obtained by keeping each point of $\ball{0}{R}$ independently with probability $1-e^{-\lambda}$. We then have 
		\[
		\E{\pcap{\mathcal{G}_{\lambda,R}}} = \pcap{\ball{0}{R}} \cdot \left(1 - \lim_{\|z\|\to\infty}\econd{e^{-\lambda |\mathcal{C}(z)\cap \ball{0}{R}|}}{z\longleftrightarrow \ball{0}{R}}   \right).
		\]
title: Proposition pro:green of arXiv:2509.21253

body:
[Defn degree of arXiv:2608.29914, 'Fixed points in abstract provability structures'] The \emph{degree} $d(\triangle)$ of a one-variable meet APS term $\triangle v$ is recursively defined as follows: 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $d(v)=0$, 
    \item $d(\Box\triangle_0)=d(\triangle_0)$, 
    \item $d(\boxtimes\triangle_0)=d(\triangle_0)+1$, 
    \item $d(\triangle_0\land\triangle_1) = \max\{d(\triangle_0),d(\triangle_1)\}$. 
\end{enumerate}
title: degree

Let $E = \bigoplus_{i \in I} K(p_i, n_i)$ be an arbitrary coproduct of Morava $K$-theories. In the localized category $L_E \operatorname{Sp}$, every homological Bousfield class is uniquely of the form $\langle \bigoplus_{j \in J} K(p_j, n_j) \rangle$ for some subset $J \subseteq I$. Thus the lattice of homological Bousfield classes is isomorphic to the boolean power set algebra $\mathcal{P}(I)$.
E is a coproduct of distinct Morava K-theories
Localization is L_E Sp

[Definition def:speed of arXiv:2608.21125, 'Two problems for threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees: '] Let $\varphi_{d,d'}(\theta) := \mathbb{E}\bigl[e^{-\theta A_e} \,\big|\, d, d'\bigr]$ denote the activation Laplace transform (conditioned on the endpoint types), and set
\[
B(\theta)_{d,d'} := m_*\, q(d')\, p_{d,d'}\, \varphi_{d,d'}(\theta), \qquad (m \times m).
\]
Define
\[
c_* := \Bigl(\, \inf_{\theta > 0} \frac{\log \rho(B(\theta))}{\theta} \Bigr)^{-1} \qquad \text{when } \rho(M) > 1,
\]
the reciprocal of the standard BRW velocity variational formula; $\theta_*$ denotes the optimiser.
title: Activation Laplace transform and the speed

[Corollary 4 (Selected chart pullbacks) of arXiv:2608.06393, 'Intrinsic Tangential Hadamard Differentiability of Rough-BSDE Solution Maps'] Let $B$ be a Banach space and let
$J:B\to\mathbb T_{\mathbf x}^p$ be continuous and linear. Suppose a
set-theoretic representation $\mathfrak r(Ju)=(\mathbf Z_{Ju},a_{Ju})$ is
defined for $u\in B$, is bounded in the budget
\eqref{eq:representative-budget} on bounded subsets of $B$, and is
ray-homogeneous:
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf Z_{\lambda\tau}=D_{1,\lambda*}\mathbf Z_\tau,
 \qquad
 a_{\lambda\tau}=\lambda a_\tau,
 \qquad
 D_{1,\lambda}(v,w)=(v,\lambda w).
\end{equation}
Define $\chi(0)=\mathbf x$ and, near zero,
\begin{equation}
 \chi(u):=\mathbf x^{1;\mathbf Z_{Ju},a_{Ju}}.
\end{equation}
Then the pullback $\mathcal S\circ\chi:B\to\mathcal X$ is Fr\'{e}chet
differentiable at zero, with
\begin{equation}
 D(\mathcal S\circ\chi)(0)=A_{\mathbf x}\circ J.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Selected chart pullbacks

[Theorem eq:wiener_hopf_factors of arXiv:2604.08889, 'Matrix Representations for Scale Functions of Spectrally Negative Lévy Processes with Rati'] Let $\{W_t\}_{t\geq 0}$ be a Brownian motion with variance $\sigma^2>0$, drift $d\in \mathbb{R}$ and starting point $W_0=0$. 
Let $U$ be a stopping time, and for fixed $\lambda+q > 0$ let $E\sim {\rm Exp}(\lambda+q)$, independent of $\{W_t\}_{t\geq 0}$. 
Then, $W_U-\min_{t\in [0,E]}W_{U+t}$ and $W_{U+E}-\min_{t\in [0,E]}W_{U+t}$ are independent and exponentially distributed random variables with respective rates
\begin{equation}
\omega_{\lambda+q} = \frac{\sqrt{d^2 + 2\sigma^2 (\lambda+q)} + d}{\sigma^2}, \qquad \eta_{\lambda+q} = \frac{\sqrt{d^2 + 2\sigma^2 (\lambda+q)} - d}{\sigma^2}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Wiener-Hopf factorisation for Brownian motion

[Definition 2 (Complex array normal distribution) of arXiv:2608.21551, '\bf Sparse Separable Factor Analysis in the Complex Domain with an Application to Local Fi'] Let $\Mcal\in\CC^{c_1\times\cdots\times c_d}$, and let $\Vb_j\in\CC^{c_j\times c_j}$ be Hermitian positive definite for $j=1,\ldots,d$. A $d$-mode array $\Ycal$ follows a proper complex array normal distribution with mean $\Mcal$ and mode-specific covariance matrices $\Vb_1,\ldots,\Vb_d$ if
\begin{align}
  
  \operatorname{vec}(\Ycal)
  \sim
  \CC\Ncal_{\prod_{j=1}^d c_j}
  \left(
    \operatorname{vec}(\Mcal),
    \Vb_d\otimes\cdots\otimes\Vb_1
  \right),
\end{align}
where $\otimes$ denotes the Kronecker product. We write $\Ycal\sim \CC\Ncal_{c_1\times\cdots\times c_d} (\Mcal,\Vb_1,\ldots,\Vb_d)$.
title: Complex array normal distribution

body:
[Cor 17 (\cite{MR51275}; see also \cite{MR317760}) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Take $A,b,C,d$ as in Theorem~\ref{t:hoffman} with $(b,d)\in F(A,C)$.
Let $B(M_0)$ denote the ball of radius $M_0$ in $\R^n$, centered at the origin.
\begin{enumerate}[a.]
\item  Suppose $(b',d')\in F(A,C)$, and
suppose further that the (nonempty) sets
$S_{A,C}(b,d)$ and $S_{A,C}(b',d')$ are both contained in $B(M_0)$.
Then
	\[d_H\Big(S_{A,C}(b,d),S_{A,C}(b',d')\Big)
	\le c\left\| \begin{pmatrix}
	b-b'\\d-d'\end{pmatrix}\right\|_2
	\]
where $c$ is a finite constant depending only on $A,C,M_0$.
\item 
Now suppose we have $(A,b,C,d)'$ of the same dimensions,
with $(b',d')\in F(A',C')$. 
Suppose further that the (nonempty) sets
$S\equiv S_{A,C}(b,d)$ and $S'\equiv S_{A',C'}(b',d')$ are both contained in $B(M_0)$.
Then, for any $x'\in S'$ there exists $x\in S$ with
	\[\|x-x'\|_2
	\le c \left\| \begin{pmatrix} A-A'\\ C-C'\\
	b-b'\\d-d'\end{pmatrix}\right\|_2\,,
	\]
where $c$ is a finite constant depending only on $A,C,M_0$, and on the right-hand side we treat $A$ and $C$ as vectors of length $mn$ and $qn$ respectively.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{proof}
Suppose $x'\in S'$. Then
	\[
	Ax'-b
	=[A'+(A-A')] x'- [b' + (b-b')]
	\le (A-A')x'-(b-b')\,,
	\]
from which it follows that
	\[
	\|(Ax'-b)_+\|
	\le \| [(A-A')x'-(b-b')]_+\|
	\le \|A-A'\|_\textup{op} M_0 + \|b-b'\|\,.
	\]
Similarly, we can bound
	\[
	\|Cx'-d\|
	\le \|C-C'\|_\textup{op} M_0 + \|d-d'\|\,.
	\]
The operator norm is bounded by the Frobenius norm, so the conclusion of part~\eqref{i:hoffman.semicty} follows.
Part \eqref{i:hoffman.rhs} then follows from part~\eqref{i:hoffman.semicty}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \cite{MR51275}; see also \cite{MR317760}

\iota\left(e^{-\alpha t}\tilde{S}_{t}f\right)\,dt \\
&=\int_{0}^{\infty}
e^{-\alpha t}[\tilde{S}_{t}f]\,dt \\
&=\int_{0}^{\infty}
e^{-\alpha t}T_{t}[f]\,dt \\
&=G_{\alpha}[f].

[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2605.24445, 'Matrix concentration inequalities for time-inhomogeneous Markov chains'] \label[lemma]{lem:tropp_step}
Let $P$ be a Markov operator on a Polish metric space $(\Omega,d)$. Let $G\colon \Omega \to \Hm$ and $x \in \Omega$ such that $PG(x) = 0$. Let $A \in \Hm$ such that $G(y)^2 \preceq A^2$ for any $y \in \supp P(x,\cdot)$.
Then, for any deterministic $H \in \Hm$,
\[
P \tr\exp\left( H + G \right)(x) \le  \tr\exp\left( H +  2 A^2 \right).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 14 of arXiv:2605.24445

body:
Li-Nica-Roy Proposition A.6 conditional drift and diffusion moment checks, in a precise conditional-moment specialization. Fix d,p,delta,h_n and the Markov transition increment Delta_n(y)=h_n*B_n(y)+sqrt(h_n)*sigma_n(y)*xi_n+h_n*n^(-delta)*R_n(y). Assume the companion small-jump hypotheses with q=4, uniformly on each compact set. Conditional on each current state y assume E[B_n(y)|y]=b_n(y), E[xi_n|y]=0, and E[xi_n*xi_n^T|y]=I_d. Within-step B_n,xi_n,R_n may be correlated. Suppose the deterministic b_n and sigma_n converge uniformly on compact sets to b and sigma. Let Pi_n(y,dz) be the law of y+Delta_n(y). Define the truncated characteristics beta_n(y)=h_n^(-1)*integral_{||z-y||<=1}(z-y)Pi_n(y,dz) and alpha_n(y)=h_n^(-1)*integral_{||z-y||<=1}(z-y)(z-y)^T Pi_n(y,dz). Then beta_n converges uniformly on compact sets to b, alpha_n converges uniformly on compact sets to sigma*sigma^T, and h_n^(-1)*Pi_n(y,{z:||z-y||>epsilon}) converges uniformly on compact sets to zero for every epsilon>0. These are the transition-characteristic conditions used in source equationsA.6-A.7 and checked in A.12-A.14. Path convergence additionally needs the appropriate tightness/compact-containment and well-posed diffusion/martingale-problem hypotheses; the displayed moment conclusions alone do not assert stopped or unstopped path convergence.
Fixed dimension and p,delta>0; conditional one-step moments uniformly bounded on each compact set as stated.
Additional conditional mean/covariance and coefficient convergence assumptions appear explicitly in the characteristics lemma.

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited), independent mathematical, priority and scope audits pending. Let N>=3,K>=2,1<=r<K,F=K-r,gcd(r,F)=1. One unknown A/S context pair has an arbitrary r-truth support in A and all K truths in S; N-2 other contexts are known S. The source chooses a context uniformly then a true candidate uniformly. Observe n iid untagged facts and independent uniform ell-subsets of truths in BOTH variable contexts, including S, 0<=ell<=r. Every realized generator of a randomized learning policy must satisfy source Mis_infinity<=c in all data-compatible worlds, where 0<=c<1/(2NrK), and source coarsening is uniform in exact generator-score bins. For sample counts u,v and truth-union sizes a,b in actual A,S coordinates, set h=min(a,b), kappa=F/K, A_h=F/(2(K-h))*((2-h/r-h/K)/N-c), O_a=F/(K-a)*max((r-a)/(Nr)-c,0), L(u,j)=(K/r)^u*binom(K-j,r-j)/binom(K-ell,r-ell) if j<=r and zero otherwise. For b<=r let pi=max(L(u,a),L(v,b))/(L(u,a)+L(v,b)). Set f=O_a when b>r, f=A_h when b<=r,h>=1, and f=kappa/N-kappa*c*pi when b<=r,h=0. Define P_m(j|u)=binom(m-ell,j-ell)/m^u * sum_{i=0}^{j-ell}(-1)^i binom(j-ell,i)(j-i)^u, with 0^0=1. The exact global expected robust minimax false mass is Gamma=sum_{u+v+w=n} n!/(u!v!w!)*(N-2)^w/N^n *sum_{a=ell}^r sum_{b=ell}^K P_r(a|u)P_K(b|v)f. The same-data known-partition oracle replaces f by O_a; the difference is the exact experiment-specific learning penalty. For ell>=1 the posterior whole-context correction vanishes; for ell=r, Gamma=(kappa/(2N)-c/2)*(1-kappa/N)^n. The efficient causal policy pools uncertified residuals when h>=1, reduces the posterior-more-likely-A whole context when h=0, and uses the residual oracle when resolved. Policy symmetrization, not averaging output laws, supplies global matching. This does not establish an arbitrary-VC or classical labeled-sample ERM/PAC result.

General multi-pair/VC frontier remains open.

Model: N>=3 contexts, K>=2 atoms per context, 1<=r<K, F=K-r,
gcd(r,F)=1. One variable A/S pair; A has arbitrary r truths, S all K.
N-2 other contexts are known S. The source chooses a context uniformly,
then a true atom uniformly. Observe n iid facts without orientation tags,
plus independent uniform ell-subsets of truths from BOTH variable contexts,
including S, with 0<=ell<=r. Every realized generator of a randomized
learning policy must have source Mis_infinity<=c in every compatible world.
Let 0<=c<1/(2NrK). Gamma(c)=inf_policy sup_fixed_world E[false mass].

In actual A/S coordinates let u,v be sample counts, a,b known union sizes,
h=min(a,b), kappa=F/K. Define

 A_h(c)=F/(2(K-h))*((2-h/r-h/K)/N-c),
 O_a(c)=F/(K-a)*max((r-a)/(Nr)-c,0),
 L(u,j)=(K/r)^u*binom(K-j,r-j)/binom(K-ell,r-ell) for j<=r,
         zero for j>r.

For unresolved data b<=r set pi_max=max(L(u,a),L(v,b))/(L(u,a)+L(v,b)).
Define f=O_a if b>r; f=A_h if b<=r and h>=1;
f=kappa/N-kappa*c*pi_max if b<=r and h=0.

For m>=ell, let

 P_m(j|u)=binom(m-ell,j-ell)/m^u
             *sum_{i=0}^{j-ell}(-1)^i binom(j-ell,i)(j-i)^u.

Use 0^0=1. The proposed exact global frontier is

 Gamma(c)=sum_{u+v+w=n} n!/(u!v!w!)*(N-2)^w/N^n
                *sum_{a=ell}^r sum_{b=ell}^K
                    P_r(a|u)*P_K(b|v)*f(u,v,a,b;c).          (1)

The same-data known-partition oracle is the same sum replacing f by O_a.
Their difference is the exact learning penalty in this VC-one family.

## Hardest step: conditional BAYES all-generator lower bound

This is the decisive analytic step; finite exact checks support it below,
and independent review remains necessary. A conditional minimax bound cannot
simply be averaged into a global expected minimax bound.

Source bin masses are integer multiples of 1/(NrK). Robustness gives
pairwise coarsened-source TV<=2c<1/(NrK); thus all score-bin source masses
are invariant across compatible worlds. This is a BIN-MASS lattice,
not a coarsened-atom-probability lattice.

Support swaps force each unsaturated outside-known set into one bin.
If one context is saturated, coprimality forces its outside-known set
into one bin too: F divides r*v, hence F divides v, and 0<=v<=F.
This is C019's already saved structural step.

Unless both contexts are saturated, outside-known bins either differ or
agree. If they differ, each contains an ENTIRE context and none of its
sibling. If common, the bin contains K-k atoms from EACH sibling, with
the same k known truths omitted from each, 0<=k<=h, plus possible fixed-S
safe atoms. Every false atom belongs to this bin. Its source score is
at least b_k=[1/K+(r-k)/(r(K-k))]/(2N), since fixed-S atoms have density
lambda=1/(NK)>=b_k. With w safe atoms, its false fraction is at most
tau_k=F/(2(K-k)). Its actual false mass in either orientation is at least
F*b_k-tau_k*c. This decreases with k, hence is at least A_h(c).
Pooling after selecting h known truths in each sibling, then transferring
c residual mass to fixed S, attains A_h in every world.

In whole-context mode, baseline posterior false mass is kappa/N. Every
bin's posterior false fraction is <=kappa*pi_max, even with safe mixing.
TV c therefore permits reduction at most kappa*pi_max*c. Removing c mass
from the more-likely-A context and adding it to fixed S attains
B_pi(c)=kappa/N-kappa*c*pi_max.

If both unions have size r, an invariant bin satisfies
F*(u_L-u_R)=r*(v_L-v_R), with u known counts, v outside counts.
Coprimality implies either balanced counts u_L=u_R,v_L=v_R, or the bin
contains an entire context and none of its sibling. One whole-context
bin forces the rest of the sibling into its own whole-context bin.
Otherwise all bins are balanced. For balanced bins, posterior false
fraction is <=1/2 and independent of orientation. Artificial fair mean
density is lambda/2 on outside atoms, while all safe densities are
>=lambda. Coarsening cannot lower mass on the outside set; TV c implies
false mass >=F*lambda/2-c/2=A_r(c). Pooling attains this.
Thus conditional Bayes optimum is min(A_h,B_pi) in every unresolved case.

For h>=1, A_h always wins on this c interval. Indeed
D_h=kappa/N-F*b_h=h*F^2/(2NrK(K-h)) and
B_pi-A_h>=D_h-c*(kappa-tau_h).
If kappa-tau_h>0, positivity at c*=1/(2NrK) reduces to
2K*h*F>K-2h, true for h>=1,F>=1. For h=0, B_pi<=A_0 since pi_max>=1/2.

Resolved data b>r identify the A context. Swaps force its outside atoms
into one bin if a<r. Safe mixing raises baseline density, and the exact
known-partition value is O_a(c). If a=r, it is zero, not an oracle slope
inferred from a zero-mass group.

## Actual posterior and global matching

Use the uniform prior on orientations and A supports. The verifier-set
marginal is identical in A and S. Conditional A supports are uniform
r-subsets containing the certificate. Relative to S, the factual sample
sequence likelihood in a context is exactly L(u,j) above. Thus pi is
the TRUE posterior, not a surrogate fair bit. With ell=0, u repeated
copies of one fact have likelihood ratio (K/r)^(u-1), not (K/r)^u.

The finite group generated by sibling swaps and within-context atom
permutations is transitive on worlds and equivariant on the experiment.
Symmetrize LEARNING POLICIES, retaining each separately realized generator.
Never average generator laws: exact-score calibration is not convex in g.
The symmetrized policy remains feasible pathwise and has constant-world
risk equal to original uniform-prior risk. Worst risk is always at least
prior-average risk. Conditional Bayes minima above are attained, so global
minimax equals their uniform-prior average. This is standard finite-group
minimax methodology, not a new minimax theorem.

Condition on sample context counts u,v. Their multinomial distribution is
the coefficient in (1). Choose j-ell new truths and use inclusion-exclusion
to require each chosen new truth to appear: this gives P_m(j|u), with
samples allowed to hit the ell original verifier truths. The two context
occupancy experiments are independent given context counts and a fixed
world. The conditional Bayes value is symmetric, hence averaging in ANY
fixed world's actual A/S coordinates yields (1).

Equivalently let V_cond=O_a on resolved data, A_h otherwise. Then

 Gamma(c)=E[V_cond]-kappa*c*
      E[(pi_max-1/2)*1_{unresolved and h=0}].                (2)

The correction vanishes for ell>=1. It must not be applied on resolved
data. At ell=r, (1) reduces to
(kappa/(2N)-c/2)*(1-kappa/N)^n. At c=0, Gamma=E[V_cond] for ONE pair.
C020's zero-budget averaging failure uses TWO pairs and is consistent.

pp.8--9. Structural inputs: C017/C019, unaudited. Standard minimax card:
recall/walk005.txt. Independent mathematical, priority, scope audit pending.

## Efficient policy and target scope

The policy uses sample multiplicities and observed truth unions. If the
partition is identified, use the A residual group with its native density,
remove min(c,residual source mass), and transfer this mass to fixed S.
For unresolved h>=1, choose an h-subset of known truths uniformly in each
sibling, pool their 2(K-h) remaining atoms at the common source density,
and move c mass to fixed S. Other selected-known atoms have their common
paired source score. For h=0, choose the posterior-more-likely A context
(uniform tie break), lower its entire context mass by c, and add it to
fixed S. All these operations use observed quantities only. Selected known
subsets and ties randomize policies, never averages of output laws.

The output law and the required likelihood comparison have polynomial
arithmetic complexity in n and the explicit alphabet size NK. The finite
sum (1) is also polynomial-time evaluable in n,K by precomputing the
occupancy tables. This is an expected minimax result under a pathwise
compatible-world robustness requirement, not a high-probability PAC result.
The two orientation functions form a VC-one partition class. Factual
observations do not provide labeled partition examples; this does not prove
a classical labeled-sample ERM rate or the unrestricted arbitrary-VC target.
The exact difference of sums is an experiment-specific estimation penalty,
not an assertion that it equals ordinary classification error. A MAP
orientation can be used as a data-dependent tie break among feasible
partitions, but the optimal pooled output need not be an oracle plug-in
using that single orientation. These distinctions require scope review.

## Exact independent finite checks

logs/global_single_pair_check.json records 237 conditional Bayes games and
588969 exhaustive invariant score partitions, 621 actual all-world
generator calibration checks, 237 full-world likelihood-posterior checks,
330 direct sequence/occupancy comparisons, 720 global occupancy-sum checks,
252 full-verifier closed-form checks, 24 two-sample closed-form checks, and
seven genuine repeated-fact wrong-exponent controls. Exhaustive partition
checks have NK<=9; larger parameter checks concern occupancy and algebra.

Separately logs/global_single_pair_policy_check.json sums the explicit
causal policy under all six fixed N=3,K=3,r=2 worlds, ell=0..2, n=0..4,
at zero and positive budgets: 59400 actual data/verifier histograms and
180 exact fixed-world expectations and normalizations. These equal (1)
and are constant across fixed worlds, without substituting posterior risk
for an actual-world loss. Both scripts use only integers and Fraction.

[Proposition 7 (Paralinearization of the transformed fractional flux operator) of arXiv:2608.29726, '\LARGE A Priori Estimates for Singular Fractional Stochastic Burgers Equations'] Let \(1<\gamma<2\), \(0<\beta<1\), and let
\(\Psi\in C^{1+\beta}(\T)\) be an orientation-preserving bi-Lipschitz map
with Jacobian satisfying \eqref{eq:J-bounds}.
The operator \(\Dcal_{\Psi}^{\gamma}\) defined in
\eqref{eq:Dflux} admits the paralinearization
\begin{equation}
  \Dcal_{\Psi}^{\gamma}f
  =(J^\gamma)^\Phi\prec\Rcal_\gamma f
  +\mathcal S_\Psi f,
\end{equation}
where \(\prec\) is the spatial Bony paraproduct.  For every
\(f\in H^{\gamma/2}\) and every
\begin{equation}
 \sigma<\min\{\gamma/2,1-\gamma/2+\beta\},
\end{equation}
the remainder satisfies
\begin{equation}
  \norm{\mathcal S_\Psi f}_{H^\sigma}
  \lesssim\norm f_{H^{\gamma/2}}.
\end{equation}
Thus \(\mathcal S_\Psi\) has order at most
\(\max\{0,\gamma-1-\beta\}+\).  Consequently,
\begin{align}
  \norm{\Dcal_{\Psi}^{\gamma}f}_{H^{1-\gamma/2}}
  &\lesssim\norm f_{H^{\gamma/2}},
  \\
  \norm{\Acal_{\Psi}^{\gamma}f}_{H^{-\gamma/2}}
  &\lesssim\norm f_{H^{\gamma/2}}.
  
\end{align}
The map
\[
 \Psi\longmapsto\Acal_\Psi^\gamma
 \quad\text{with values in}\quad
 \mathcal L(H^{\gamma/2},H^{-\gamma/2})
\]
is continuous on bounded subsets of \(C^{1+\beta}\) with fixed
bi-Lipschitz constants.  After any loss from \(\beta\) to
\(\beta_0<\beta\), this dependence has a local H\"older modulus.  All
displayed bounds are locally uniform under these assumptions.

valid for any $x\in\mathbb R$.

[campaign result 2026-09-14; values computed exactly from the intersection-array identity tau_0 = k sum_{i=1}^d (k_i+...+k_d)/(k_i c_i). That identity was checked against a direct linear-algebra solve on twelve graphs, among them the cubic graphs K_{3,3}, Q_3, Petersen, Heawood, Pappus, Desargues and the dodecahedron, with the complete graph and the cycle as independent controls.] This is the cubic case of Open Problem 7.31 in David Aldous and James Allen Fill's Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, unfinished monograph (2002, recompiled 2014; official source https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/RWG/book.html). For a finite connected simple distance-regular graph G with n vertices, let tau_0 = max_{x,y} E_x[T_y] for simple random walk. By the known classification, there are exactly thirteen cubic (valency-three) distance-regular graphs. Their (n, tau_0) values are: K_4 (4, 3); K_{3,3} (6, 6); cube Q_3 (8, 10); Petersen (10, 12); Heawood (14, 19); Pappus (18, 27); Desargues (20, 65/2); dodecahedron (20, 35); Coxeter (28, 45); Tutte-Coxeter (30, 48); Foster (90, 675/4); Biggs-Smith (102, 195); Tutte 12-cage (126, 234). Hence, given the classification, the maximum of tau_0/(n-1) over all cubic distance-regular graphs is 195/101 (about 1.9307), attained uniquely by the Biggs-Smith graph. This reproduces exactly the value Aldous and Fill attribute to Biggs and settles, for valency three, Biggs's outlined claim that it is the largest. The general O(n) conjecture over non-cycle distance-regular graphs is not settled by this computation. This is an unrefereed campaign result.

body:
[Lemma 52 (Uniform convergence of a localized rescaled well kernel) of arXiv:2607.20882, 'An Eyring--Kramers Law for the Hypoelliptic Third-Order\\ Langevin Diffusion'] For $i\in\{m,s\}$, let $A_i$ be the linearized drift matrix at $x_i$ and let
$P_i^{\rm OU}(t,x,y)$ be the transition density of
\begin{equation}

dY_t=A_iY_t\,dt+\sqrt{2\gamma/L}\,(0,0,dB_t).
\end{equation}
Fix the common radius $r_0$ of
Lemma~\ref{lem:local-hypocoercive-lyapunov}.  Extend
only the rescaled force smoothly outside $B(0,r_0/\sqrt\eps)$, keeping its
positive-order derivatives uniformly bounded and leaving the linear chain
$W\to V\to Q$ unchanged.  Denote the density of this chain-compatible cutoff
process by
$\bar P_{i,\eps}(t,x,y)$.  The cutoff agrees with the true rescaled process
about $x_i$ up to
exit from $B(0,r_0/\sqrt\eps)$.
For every $0<t_-<t_+<\infty$ and compact $K_0,K_1\subset\R^{3d}$,
\[
\sup_{\substack{t\in[t_-,t_+]\\x\in K_0,\,y\in K_1}}
\left|
\bar P_{i,\eps}(t,x,y)
-P_i^{\rm OU}(t,x,y)
\right|\longrightarrow0
\qquad\text{as $\eps\downarrow0$}.
\]
The convergence holds for both $i=m,s$.

body:
[Lemma 27 of arXiv:2608.29157, 'Dilator-based analysis of $\KP$'] For each $n\in\bbN$, let $A$ be the leading formula of $[\ttX_n]\vdash \Gamma_n$. 
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item If $A \equiv B\land C$, then either $B$ or $C$ is in $\Gamma_{n+1}$.
            \item If $A \equiv B\lor C$, then both $B$ and $C$ are in $\Gamma_{n+1}$.
            \item If $A \equiv \forall^\tau x B(x)$ for $\tau\neq \ord$, then there is a free variable $x$ of type $\tau$ such that $B(x)$ is in $\Gamma_{n+1}$.
            \item If $A \equiv \exists^\tau x B(x)$ for $\tau\neq \ord$, then for every term $t$ of type $\tau$, there is $m>n$ such that $B(t)$ occurs in $\Gamma_m$.
            \item If $A\equiv \forall^\ord x B(x)$, then there is $v\in \ttX$ such that $B(v)$ is in $\Gamma_{n+1}$.
            \item If $A\equiv \exists^\ord x B(x)$, then for every $v\in \ttX$ there is $m>n$ such that $B(v)$ occurs in $\Gamma_m$.
        \end{enumerate}

[Proposition 47 (Smooth-transform criterion) of arXiv:2608.07820, 'Linear Spectral Statistics for Entrywise-Transformed Spiked Wigner Matrices under Shifted '] Assume \(f\in C^2(\mathbb R)\), \(\E_\nu f=0\),
\(\E_\nu f^2=1\),
\[
        \E\sup_{|u|\le\delta_0}|f(\zeta+u)|^4<\infty,
\]
and that the Taylor remainders of \(f\) and \(f^2\) satisfy
\[
        \E\sup_{|u|\le\delta_0}|f''(\zeta+u)|<\infty,
        \qquad
        \E\sup_{|u|\le\delta_0}\bigl(|f'(\zeta+u)|^2+|f(\zeta+u)f''(\zeta+u)|\bigr)<\infty.
\]
Then Condition~\ref{cond:profile-admissibility} holds with
\[
        a_1=\E f'(\zeta),
        \qquad
        b_1=2\E[f(\zeta)f'(\zeta)],
\]
\[
        b_2=\E\bigl[f'(\zeta)^2+f(\zeta)f''(\zeta)\bigr].
\]

body:
[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] We can talk about ellipses, in several possible ways, as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
\item As the curves appearing via $d(z,p)+d(z,q)=l$, with $p,q\in\mathbb R^2$, and $l>0$.

\item Up to a translation and rotation, as the curves given by $(x/a)^2+(y/b)^2=1$.

\item Or equivalently, in polar coordinates, given by $x=a\cos t$, $y=b\sin t$.

\item As the conics, that is, the plane curves of degree $2$, which are compact. 

\item As the compact curves obtained by cutting a 3D cone with a plane.

\item As the pictures of a circle, taken from various 3D perspectives.

\item As the trajectories of the planets around the Sun.
\end{enumerate}

  such that the tail distribution function $\widebar{F}_{j}$ of each marginal $X_{1, j}$ 
   belongs to $\SRV{\alpha}{\rho_{j}}$ with auxiliary function~$A_{j}$, for a common $\alpha > 0$
  and possibly different $\rho_{j} < 0$,
  $j=1,\ldots , d$. Then,
  for some $C > 0$ and every $n \geq 1$ we have 
\[
\prob\big(\exists j \in \lbra 1, d \rbra,\ \exists i' \neq i \in \lbra 1,n \rbra,\ X_{i, j} = X_{i', j}\quad \mathrm{and} \quad X_{i, j} \ge X_{1, j}, \dots, X_{n, j} \big) \leq C\Big(\frac{1}{n} + A_{j_{0}}(a_{n, j_{0}})\Big),
\]
where $a_{n, j} = F_{j}^{\leftarrow}(1 - n^{-1})$ and $j_{0}$ is such that $\rho_{j_{0}} \geq \rho_{j}$ for every $j \in \lbra 1, d \rbra$.

[Theorem fredi of arXiv:2412.09290, 'Asymptotics of Harish-Chandra transform and infinitesimal freeness'] Let $n$ be a fixed integer. Let $A$ be a random Hermitian matrix of size $N$ and assume
  that for every finite $r$ one has
  \begin{equation}
    \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} N^{n \varepsilon} \left( \frac{1}{N} \log
    \mathbb{E}[H \text{} C (x_1, \ldots, x_r, 0^{N - r} ; \lambda_1 (A),
    \ldots, \lambda_n (A))] - \sum_{j = 0}^{n - 1} \sum_{i = 0}^r
    \frac{1}{N^{j \varepsilon}} \Psi_j (x_i) \right) = \sum_{i = 1}^r \Psi_n
    (x_i), 
  \end{equation}
  where $\Psi_0, \ldots, \Psi_n$ are smooth functions in a complex neighborhood of
  $0$, the above convergence is uniform in a complex neighborhood of $0^r$ and $0 <
  \varepsilon < n^{- 1}$. Then the $1 / N^{n \varepsilon}$ correction of the
  average empirical distribution of $N^{- 1} A$ is given by
  \begin{equation}

body:
[Proposition 81 (Common bracket-variation and operator-envelope domains) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Let $G_Q$ be the domain constructed in the proof of
\Cref{cor:common-representative}; equivalently,
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 G_Q=\{x\in G_J:\;&Q_t(x)-Q_s(x)\in\mathcal S_1(H)_+,\\
 &\Tr(Q_t(x)-Q_s(x))\le\Lambda(t-s)
 \text{ for all rational }0\le s<t\le T\}.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
Fix a countable dense $\mathbb Q$-linear subspace $H_{\mathbb Q}\subset H$ and, for
$\Gamma\in\mathcal S_1(H)_+$, define
\begin{equation}
 G_Q^\Gamma
 :=\left\{x\in G_J:
 0\le\langle Q_{s,t}(x)h,h\rangle
 \le(t-s)\langle\Gamma h,h\rangle
 \text{ for all rational }s<t\text{ and }h\in H_{\mathbb Q}\right\}.
\end{equation}
Then $G_Q$ and $G_Q^\Gamma$ are Borel and
$c_{\Smax}(G_Q^c)=0$.  For every model subclass
$\mathcal P_\Gamma\subset\Smax$ satisfying
$0\preceq a_t^P\preceq\Gamma$ for $\dd t\otimes P$-almost every
$(t,\omega)$ and every $P\in\mathcal P_\Gamma$,
\[
 c_{\mathcal P_\Gamma}((G_Q^\Gamma)^c)=0.
\]
On $G_Q$, $Q$ is trace-norm Lipschitz and has bounded variation.  On
$G_Q^\Gamma$, for all $0\le s<t\le T$,
\begin{equation}
 0\preceq Q_{s,t}\preceq(t-s)\Gamma,
 \qquad
 \|Q_t-Q_s\|_1\le(t-s)\Tr\Gamma.
\end{equation}
Both domains are stable under stopping, every shift, and finite temporal
concatenation.

		\[

	\mathcal{L}\bigl(W_0^{s,p}(\Gamma)\bigr),
	\]
	where $s$ and $p$ are determined by $0<\alpha<d$.

[Lemma lem:dgt4-linearization-from-survival of arXiv:2609.02829, 'Quantitative explosion and percolation of the divisible sandpile'] Suppose that the scenery variables are independent and identically
	distributed, atomless, centered, and have finite positive variance.
	Fix $T>0$, let $n_R\coloneqq\lfloor R^2T\rfloor$, and let
	$q_{R,j}\in[0,1]$ be deterministic for $0\leq j<n_R$. Suppose that
	as $R\to\infty$,
	\[
		R^{-2}\sum_{j=0}^{n_R-1}
		\mathbf E_0\left|
		\mathbb{P}(S_{n_R,j}(X)=1\mid X)-q_{R,j}
		\right|
		\longrightarrow0,
	\]
	and that there is $C<\infty$ such that, for every $\delta\in(0,T)$, there are
	deterministic numbers $\varepsilon_R(\delta)\geq0$ with
	$\varepsilon_R(\delta)\to0$ as $R\to\infty$ and, uniformly over
	$0\leq i,j\leq n_R-\delta R^2$ and all deterministic nearest-neighbor paths
	$X=(X_0,\ldots,X_i)$ and $Y=(Y_0,\ldots,Y_j)$,
	\[
		\left|
		\Cov(S_{n_R,i}(X),S_{n_R,j}(Y)\mid X,Y)
		\right|
		\leq
		\frac{C}{\delta R^2}
		\sum_{r=0}^i\sum_{h=0}^j\mathbf{1}_{\{X_r=Y_h\}}
		+\varepsilon_R(\delta)\, .
	\]
	Then, for every
	$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$,
	\begin{equation}
		\mathbb{E}\Biggl[\Biggl(R^{(d-4)/2}\Biggl(
		u_{n_R}-\mathbb{E} u_{n_R}(0)
		-\sum_{j=0}^{n_R-1}q_{R,j}P^j\zeta
		\Biggr)^{(R)}(\varphi)\Biggr)^2\Biggr]
		\longrightarrow0\, .
	\end{equation}
	Consequently, for every $s>(d-4)/2$,
	\[
		R^{(d-4)/2}
		\left(u_{n_R}-\mathbb{E} u_{n_R}(0)
		-\sum_{j=0}^{n_R-1}q_{R,j}P^j\zeta\right)^{(R)}
		\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}0
		\quad\text{in }H^{-s}_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^d)\, .
	\]

[Proposition 1 (Full-space reduction and its interior equality case) of arXiv:2609.03466, 'Least-Favorable Location for Binomial Top-$t$ Selection'] For $p\in[0,1-\delta]$, let $P_{n,k,t,\delta}(p)$ be the PCS for $k-t$ probabilities equal to $p$ and $t$ probabilities equal to $p+\delta$. For each $\boldsymbol\theta\in\ThetaPZ$, define
\[
 p(\boldsymbol\theta)=\theta_{[k-t+1]}-\delta\in[0,1-\delta].
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \PCS_n(\boldsymbol\theta)
 \ge P_{n,k,t,\delta}\bigl(p(\boldsymbol\theta)\bigr).
 
\end{equation}
If $p(\boldsymbol\theta)\in(0,1-\delta)$, equality holds if and only if
\[
 \theta_{[1]}=\cdots=\theta_{[k-t]}=p(\boldsymbol\theta),
 \qquad
 \theta_{[k-t+1]}=\cdots=\theta_{[k]}
 =p(\boldsymbol\theta)+\delta.
\]
Consequently, for every $n,k,t$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$,
\begin{equation}
 \inf_{\boldsymbol\theta\in\ThetaPZ}\PCS_n(\boldsymbol\theta)
 =\min_{0\le p\le1-\delta}P_{n,k,t,\delta}(p).
 
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Full-space reduction and its interior equality case

[Corollary 5 (Regret under the logarithmic buffer) of arXiv:2608.22227, '\fontsize{18pt}{20pt}\selectfont \bf Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning with Smoothed Q'] For each $t$ choose \(\beta_t = \frac{\tau} {\log(\mathrm e + t)},\) and define \(K_\tau \coloneqq \left\lceil \exp\!\left(\frac{\tau}{\rho_\tau}\right)-\mathrm e \right\rceil\). Then, under the conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:UCB-BQRL-finite}, with probability at least \(1-2\delta\), $\Reg_\tau(T)\le\;2H K_\tau+ \allowbreak \frac{c\log(\mathrm e+T-1)}{\tau}\sqrt{SA TH^4\log\!\frac{2SATH}{\delta}} + \allowbreak\frac{c\log(\mathrm e+T-1)}{\tau}\sqrt{\frac{TH^4}{2}\log\!\frac{2SATH}{\delta}\log\!\frac{1}{\delta}} \allowbreak$. Consequently,
\(\Reg_\tau(T) = \widetilde{\mathcal O}\!\left(
\frac{1}{\tau}\sqrt{SATH^4}
\right) + O(K_\tau H)\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Regret under the logarithmic buffer

[Theor thm:c4-finite-subgraph of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] There exists a universal constant
$C_{\ifmmode\text{\tiny(thm:c4-finite-subgraph of the paper)}\else{\tiny(thm:c4-finite-subgraph of the paper)}\fi}\ge1$ such that the following holds.
Fix an integer $d\ge2$, a real $\rho\in(0,1]$, and positive integers $k,r,n$ with  
 $$2 \le \rho k \le r\le k\le n.$$

Let $G=(I,J,M)$ be $C_4$-free with $|I|=k$, $|J|=n$, and right degrees satisfying
\[
2\le |N_G(j)|\le d
\qquad\forall j\in J.
\]

Define
\[
K_\star:=
\max\left\{
K\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}:
K\log K\le \Lambda 
\right\}, \quad \mbox{ where } \Lambda :=\min\left(\frac r2,\frac nk\right). 
\]
and let $m_\star$ be a positive integer satisfying
\[
\left(\frac{C_{\ifmmode\text{\tiny(thm:c4-finite-subgraph of the paper)}\else{\tiny(thm:c4-finite-subgraph of the paper)}\fi}d^4m_\star}{\rho}\right)^{C_{\ifmmode\text{\tiny(thm:c4-finite-subgraph of the paper)}\else{\tiny(thm:c4-finite-subgraph of the paper)}\fi}d^3m_\star}
\le K_\star.
\]
Assume such an $m_\star$ exists.
If $\Omega\subseteq J$ is chosen uniformly from $\binom Jr$, then
\[
\mathbb P\bigl(\text{$G[\Omega]$ contains a \hyperref[def:weight-compatible-rooted-matching-tree]{\textcolor{PineGreen}{\emph{weight-compatible $m_\star$-matching rooted tree}}}}\bigr)
\ge
1-\exp(-\sqrt{K_\star})-\frac{32d}{\log K_\star}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Finite $C_4$-free sampling theorem

[Prop mom-dbm of arXiv:2411.10829, 'Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble and its Laplace transform'] For any $C_1>0$, there exists $C=C(C_1)>0$ such that the following holds.
For any $N\in\mathbb N$, $0\le \boldsymbol{\tau}_1<\boldsymbol{\tau}_2 \le C_1$, $C_1^{-1}N^{2/3}<k<C_1N^{2/3}$, we have
\[
\mathbb E \left[  \left( \sum_{i=1}^N \left(1+N^{-2/3}\mathbf Y_i^{(N)}(\boldsymbol{\tau}_1)/2 \right)^k - \sum_{i=1}^N \left( 1+N^{-2/3}\mathbf Y_i^{(N)}(\boldsymbol{\tau}_2)/2\right)^k\right)^4  \right] < C (\boldsymbol{\tau}_2-\boldsymbol{\tau}_1)^2.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop mom-dbm of arXiv:2411.10829

[Lemma lem:OnejVolumeAnalysis of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] There exists a real number $\lambda_0 \in (0,1/2)$ such that the following holds. Consider any $\lambda \in (0,\lambda_0)$ and a send sequence $\overline{p}$ such that $p_0=1$ and, for all $i \ge 1$, $W_i \le (4/\lambda)^i$. Suppose that $\overline{p}$ has finitely many bins which are strongly exposed. 
Let $j_0$ be a sufficiently large positive integer
where  all strongly-exposed bins are in $[j_0-1]$.
Let $\tau_0$ be a non-negative integer. Let $\Psi_0$ be the   initialising high-level state with  $\tau^{\Psi_0} = \tau_0$ and $j^{\Psi_0} = j_0$. 
Let $\mathrm{hls}$ be the $\Psi_0$-backoff bounding rule from Definition~(def:backoff-bounding-rule of the paper).  
Let $V$ be a volume process from $\Psi_0$ with transition rule $\mathrm{hls}$, 
 send sequence~$\overline{p}$, and birth rate~$\lambda$  (Definition~(def:volume-process of the paper)).
For any
$t \ge \tau_0$, 
let   $T(t) = \{\tau_0,\ldots,t\}$.
Then  the following statement holds  for
every $t > \tau_0$ and
every tuple
$ 
\overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)} = (\psi_{\tau_0},\dots,\psi_{t-1})$  of high-level states 
such that  
$\mathbb{P}( \overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)}) > 0$, 
$\psi_{t-1}$ is a $j$-filling state, 
$\tau^{\psi_{t-1}} = t-1$, and $z_j^{\psi_{t-1}} = 0$.
Conditioned on $\overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)} $,
with 
probability at least $1-
\exp(-\lambda j/1000) $,  
the following events occur, where  
\[
\tau_{j,\mathrm{full}} = \min\{t'  \geq t \colon \textup{type}^{\Psi(t')} = \textup{failure} \mbox{ or }j^{\Psi(t')} = j+1\}.\]
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $\Psi(\tau_{j,\mathrm{full}})$ is $(j+1)$-filling or $(j+1)$-advancing
and $z_{j+1}^{\Psi(\tau_{j,\mathrm{full}})}=0$.

\item $\tau_{j,\mathrm{full}} \leq t+
\lceil 4(4 j)^{\phi} W_j\rceil
$.
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma lem6.11 of arXiv:2508.12951, '\textbf{On the central limit question for strictly stationary, reversible Markov chains}'] Suppose $\phi: [1,\infty) \to (-\infty, 0]$ is a function
that satisfies the following conditions: \hfil\break
(a) $\phi$ is continuous, strictly decreasing, and convex 
on $[1, \infty)$; \hfil\break
(b) $\phi$ is continuously differentiable on the open 
half line $(1, \infty)$; and \hfil\break 
(c) one has that
\begin{equation}

\lim_{x \to \infty} \phi(x)\ =\ -\infty 
\indent {\rm and} \indent
\lim_{x \to \infty} \frac {\phi(x)} {x}\ =\ 0.
\end{equation}

   For each $y \in (1, \infty)$ (the open half line), let 
$L^{(y)}: \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$ denote the affine function whose graph is tangent to that 
of $\phi$ at the point $(y, \phi(y))$ --- that is, the affine function that satisfies
\begin{equation}

L^{(y)}(y)\ =\ \phi(y) \indent {\rm and} \indent 
L^{(y)}(x)\ \leq\ \phi(x)\ \ {\rm for\ all}\ x \in [1, \infty). 
\end{equation}
 
   Then the following statements (I), (II), and (III) hold:
\medskip

   (I) The following statements hold: \hfil\break
(i) For each $x \in (1, \infty)$,
$\phi(x) < \phi(1) \leq 0$ and $\phi'(x) < 0$.  \hfil\break  
(ii) The function $x \mapsto \phi'(x)$ for $x \in (1, \infty)$, 
is nondecreasing. \hfil\break  
(iii) One has that $\lim_{x \to \infty} \phi'(x) = 0$. \hfil\break
(iv) For each $y \in (1, \infty)$,  
$[{\rm slope\ of}\ L^{(y)}] = \phi'(y) < 0$. \hfil\break 
(v) For each $y \in (1, \infty)$, 
$L^{(y)}(0) = \phi(y) + y \cdot (-\phi'(y)) > \phi(y)$.
\medskip

   (II) For any negative number $D$ and any positive number 
$s$, there exists a number    
$T = T(\phi, D, s) > 1$ with the following property:

   For each $y \geq T$, the affine function 
$L^{(y)}$ in (the entire sentence of) eq.\ ((eq6.112 of the paper))
satisfies 
\begin{equation}

-s\ \leq\ [{\rm slope\ of}\ L^{(y)}]\ =\ \phi'(y)\ <\ 0 
\indent {\rm and} \indent
L^{(y)}(0)\ \leq\ D. 
\end{equation}
  
   (III) Suppose also that $\psi: [1, \infty) \to [0, \infty)$ is a  
function such that $\lim_{x \to \infty} \psi(x) = \infty$.
 
Then for any negative number $D$ and any positive numbers
$B$ and $s$, there there exists a real number 
$T^* := T^*(\phi, \psi, B, D, s) > 1$ with the following 
property:
\smallskip

For each $y \geq T^*$, the affine function 
$L^{(y)}$ in (the entire sentence of) eq.\ ((eq6.112 of the paper))
satisfies ((eq6.113 of the paper)) and also 
[strengthening part of ((eq6.113 of the paper))] satisfies  
\begin{equation}
  
L^{(y)}(0) + B\ \leq\ D \indent {\rm and} \indent
L^{(y)}(x) + B\ \leq\ \phi(x) + \psi(x)\ \ 
{\rm for\ all}\ x \geq 1.    
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem6.11 of arXiv:2508.12951

[Prop integrable of arXiv:2411.08725, 'Berry-Esseen bounds for large-time asymptotics of one-dimensional diffusion processes via '] {\rm ([BS02], [SY05])}
Let $a>0$ and let $f$ be a bounded Borel function on ${\mathbb R}$ such that $\int_0^{\infty}f(x)dx<\infty$, 
and let $M=\sup_{x\in {\mathbb R}}f(x)$. 
Then for any $c \in \left[ 0, \frac{a^2}{2M}\right)$, 
\[
E\left[\exp\left(c\int_0^{\infty}f(B_t^{x,a})dt\right)\right]<\infty, \quad x\in {\mathbb R}.
\]
In particular, for any $p\in [0,\infty )$
\[
E\left[ \left| \int_0^{\infty}f(B_t^{x,a})dt \right| ^p \right]<\infty, \quad x\in {\mathbb R}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop integrable of arXiv:2411.08725

[Proposition prop:moment_R_ex1 of arXiv:2510.21186, 'Weingarten Calculus with Virtual Isometries'] Let $m$, $l$, $q$ be nonnegative integers, and consider four sequences:
\[
\bm{i}=(i_1,\dots, i_m), \qquad \bm{j} =(j_1,\dots, j_m), \qquad
\bm{i}'=(i_1',\dots, i_l'), \qquad \bm{j}' =(j_1',\dots, j_l')
\]
 of positive integers in $\{1,2,\dots,n\}.$
Then, for each $1 \le s \le n$ the moment
\[
\mathbb{E} \bigl[p_{i_1 j_1} \cdots p_{i_m j_m} \overline{p_{i_1' j_1'} \cdots p_{i_l' j_l'}} r_{ss}^q\bigr]
\]
 vanishes unless $\bm{i} \sqcup \bm{j}'$ is a permutation of $\bm{j} \sqcup \bm{i}'$.
In this case, the moment is equal to
\[
\alpha_1 ! \cdots \alpha_{n-1}! \, \frac{n^{\uparrow \alpha_n}}{n^{\uparrow (m+q)} n^{\uparrow l}}
\times
\begin{cases}
(n+m-\alpha_s-1)^{\uparrow q} & \text{if $s<n$}, \\
(m-\alpha_n)^{\uparrow q} & \text{if $s=n$},
\end{cases}
\]
where $\alpha_k:=\mathsf{m}_{k}(\bm{i}\sqcup \bm{j}') = \mathsf{m}_{k}(\bm{j}\sqcup\bm{i}')$
for all $k=1,2,\dots, n$.
Note that the last factor may be zero.
title: Proposition prop:moment_R_ex1 of arXiv:2510.21186

[Lemma lem:rationalize-prefix-free-ball-code of arXiv:2608.29561, 'Ball codes: A coding characterization of Hausdorff and packing dimensions'] For every prefix-free ball code \(\varphi\), there is a prefix-free ball code
\(\varphi'\) whose values are rational closed balls such that
\[
K_{\varphi'}(x;r)
\le
K_\varphi(x;r+1)
\]
for all \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(r\in\omega\).  In particular, in the

[Prop 49 of arXiv:2603.05174, 'Regularization of the superposition principle: Potential theory meets Fokker-Planck equati'] Let $X=(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathcal{F}(t) , X(t), \theta(t) , \mathbb{P}_x), x\in E$ and $\tilde{X}=(\tilde{\Omega}, \tilde{\mathcal{F}}, \tilde{\mathcal{F}}(t), \tilde{X}(t), \tilde{\theta}(t), \tilde{\mathbb{P}}_x, x\in E)$ be two right processes on a Lusin measurable space $E$ sharing the same resolvent $\mathcal{U}$. 
Further, let $\tau$ be a natural (hence Lusin) topology on $E$ (with respect to $\mathcal{U}$), such that $X$ has continuous paths with respect to $\tau$ $\mathbb{P}_\mu$-a.s. for some $\mu\in \mathcal{P}$.
Then
\begin{equation}
    \mathbb{P}_\mu\circ \left(X\right)^{-1} = \tilde{\mathbb{P}}^\mu\circ \left(\tilde{X}\right)^{-1} \quad \mbox{as laws on the path-space }  C([0,\infty);E,\tau), 
\end{equation}
where $C([0,\infty);E,\tau)$ denotes the space of continuous functions defined on $[0,\infty)$ with values in $E$ endowed with the topology $\tau$.
