body:
[Lemma lem.regeneration-toolkit of arXiv:2605.26082, 'Quantitative Einstein relation for reversible diffusions in a random environment'] The coupled regeneration construction of [ballistic2003shen,ballistic2004shen] and [Einstein2012gantert], as recalled in Subsection~(ss.renewal-setup of the paper), has the following properties.
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item[\rm(a)] The regeneration times depend only on the path and Bernoulli marks. Under $\widehat{\mathbb P}_0^\lambda$ they are almost surely finite, take values in $\Delta\mathbb{N}$, satisfy $\tau_1\ge2\Delta$, and obey
			\[
				\tau_{k+1}=\tau_k+\tau_1\circ\theta_{\tau_k}\, .
			\]
			\item[\rm(b)] For every $n\ge2$, the first-regeneration slice has an event
			\[
				\Gamma_{1,n}\in\sigma(X^\lambda_s:0\le s\le n\Delta-\Delta)\vee\sigma(Y_0,\ldots,Y_{n-2})
			\]
			such that
			\[
				\{\tau_1=n\Delta\}
				=\Gamma_{1,n}\cap\{Y_{n-1}=1\}\cap\{D\circ\theta_{n\Delta}=\infty\}
			\]
				almost surely, and
				\[
					\Gamma_{1,n}\subseteq
					\left\{\sup_{0\le s\le n\Delta-\Delta}e_1\cdot X^\lambda(s)
					\le e_1\cdot X^\lambda(n\Delta-\Delta)+R\right\}.
				\]
					\item[\rm(c)] At the bridge step ending at $n\Delta$, given the path up to $n\Delta-\Delta$ and the marks through $Y_{n-2}$, the mark $\{Y_{n-1}=1\}$ contributes $p_*$, and the endpoint is averaged uniformly over $B^{X^\lambda(n\Delta-\Delta)}$. Given endpoint $y$, the shifted future path and marks have the coupled law $\widehat P_y^{\lambda,\omega}$.
				\item[\rm(d)] Before the terminal bridge the candidate has advanced at least $2R$ in the $e_1$ direction from the previous regeneration time. The successful bridge satisfies
				\begin{equation}
					X^\lambda(s)\in B_{6R}\bigl(X^\lambda(n\Delta-\Delta)+5Re_1\bigr),\qquad n\Delta-\Delta\le s\le n\Delta .
				\end{equation}
					\item[\rm(e)] The half-space measurability bounds are as follows. For the past factor, if $H_{\rm pre}$ is bounded and measurable in the path on $[0,n\Delta-\Delta]$ and the marks $Y_0,\ldots,Y_{n-2}$, then
					\[
						\omega\mapsto\widehat E_0^{\lambda,\omega}\!\left[
							H_{\rm pre}\,
						\mathbf 1_{\{\sup_{0\le s\le n\Delta-\Delta}e_1\cdot X^\lambda(s)\le y\cdot e_1-7R\}}
					\right]
				\]
				is $\mathcal H_{\mathsf L(y\cdot e_1-4R)}$-measurable. For the future factor, if $\Phi$ is a product of a bounded functional of the shifted future path and shifted marks with a bounded functional of the shifted environment restricted to $\mathsf R_+$, then
				\[
					\omega\mapsto \widehat E_y^{\lambda,\omega}[\Phi(\mathcal Y_0);D=\infty]
					\]
					is $\mathcal H_{\mathsf R(y\cdot e_1-2R)}$-measurable.
				\item[\rm(f)] The coupled kernel is spatially covariant:
				\[
					\widehat P^{\lambda,(\mathbf{a},e^{-2V})}_y
					=\bigl((X^\lambda,Y)\mapsto(y+X^\lambda,Y)\bigr)_{\#}
				\widehat P^{\lambda,T_y(\mathbf{a},e^{-2V})}_0\, .
			\]
		\end{enumerate}

body:
For a sequence of random vectors x_p in R^p and Gaussian comparison vectors g_p distributed as N(mu_p,Sigma_p), a sequence of symmetric convex sets S_p subset R^p is a domain of Gaussianity if, for every fixed bounded Lipschitz function phi:R->R, sup_{theta in S_p}|E phi(theta^T x_p)-E phi(theta^T g_p)| tends to zero as p tends to infinity. The supremum is over deterministic directions in the entire stated domain. This definition does not assert that projections at directions fitted using the same observations are Gaussian. Coordinate delocalization is an example of a domain condition for suitable independent-coordinate laws, not the definition for arbitrary dependent features.
Sequences indexed by p; symmetric convex comparison domains and a specified Gaussian law.
The limit holds for every fixed bounded Lipschitz scalar test function, uniformly over the domain.

body:
[Lemma Delta_t of arXiv:2608.29507, 'Denoising as Projection: Constrained Optimization with Gradient-Guided Diffusion'] Let $u_t, v_t$ be defined as in (equation eq:def-u-v of the paper) and let $\Delta_t := (\Phi_{t}(A^\top u_{t}) - \Phi_{t}(x_{t}^\star))$ and $\widetilde{\eta}$ defined as in (equation eq:subspace-dynamics of the paper), then under the conditions specified in Theorem (theorem: convergence-guided-diffusion of the paper), we have
    \begin{align*}
        \Delta_{t-1} \le (1-\widetilde{\eta} \mu c)\Delta_t + \frac{(\sigma_t^2 - \sigma_{t-1}^2)\eta^{-1}D^2}{2} +  \frac{\widetilde{\eta} L^2}{2}\|v_t\|^2
    \end{align*}
\begin{proof}
    We start with bounding
    \begin{align*}
        \mathrm{LHS}
        &:= \bigl(\Phi_t(A^\top u_{t-1})-\Phi_t(x_t^\star)\bigr)
        -\bigl(\Phi_t(A^\top u_t)-\Phi_t(x_t^\star)\bigr)\\
        &=\Phi_t(A^\top u_{t-1})-\Phi_t(A^\top u_t).
    \end{align*}
    From the $L$-smoothness of $f$, the definition of $\Phi_t$, and the fact that
    $AA^\top=I$, we have
    \begin{align*}
        \mathrm{LHS}
        &\le
        \left\langle
        \nabla\Phi_t(A^\top u_t),
        A^\top(u_{t-1}-u_t)
        \right\rangle\\
        &\quad
        +\frac{1}{2}
        \left\langle
        u_{t-1}-u_t,
        \left(
        LI+\frac{\sigma_t^2}{\eta}\Sigma^{-1}
        \right)
        (u_{t-1}-u_t)
        \right\rangle.
    \end{align*}
    By (equation eq:subspace-dynamics of the paper),
    \[
        u_{t-1}-u_t
        =
        -\widetilde{\eta} M_tA\nabla\Phi_t(x_t).
    \]
    Therefore,
    \begin{align*}
        \mathrm{LHS}
        &\le
        -\widetilde{\eta}
        \left\langle
        \nabla\Phi_t(A^\top u_t),
        A^\top M_tA\nabla\Phi_t(x_t)
        \right\rangle\\
        &\quad
        +\frac{\widetilde{\eta}^2}{2}
        \left\langle
        M_tA\nabla\Phi_t(x_t),
        \left(
        LI+\frac{\sigma_t^2}{\eta}\Sigma^{-1}
        \right)
        M_tA\nabla\Phi_t(x_t)
        \right\rangle.
    \end{align*}
    Note that, since $\widetilde{\eta}=\eta\epsilon$, $\widetilde{\eta} L\le 1$, and
    $\epsilon\le 1$,
    \begin{align*}
        \widetilde{\eta}
        \left(
        LI+\frac{\sigma_t^2}{\eta}\Sigma^{-1}
        \right)
        &=
        \widetilde{\eta} LI+\epsilon\sigma_t^2\Sigma^{-1}\\
        &\preceq
        I+\sigma_t^2\Sigma^{-1}
        =
        M_t^{-1}.
    \end{align*}
    Hence,
    \begin{align*}
        \widetilde{\eta} M_t
        \left(
        LI+\frac{\sigma_t^2}{\eta}\Sigma^{-1}
        \right)
        M_t
        \preceq M_t.
    \end{align*}
    It follows that
    \begin{align*}
        \mathrm{LHS}
        &\le
        -\widetilde{\eta}
        \left\langle
        \nabla\Phi_t(A^\top u_t),
        A^\top M_tA\nabla\Phi_t(x_t)
        \right\rangle\\
        &\quad
        +\frac{\widetilde{\eta}}{2}
        \left\langle
        \nabla\Phi_t(x_t),

[Proposition 9 of arXiv:2606.23896, 'The one-point Schreier Poisson boundary of Thompson's group \(F\)'] The no-holding trace \(Q\) is the reversible
nearest-neighbor random walk on the rooted binary tree \(B\) with conductances

\[
c(w,w0)=1,
\qquad
c(w,w1)=\frac12 .
\]

Equivalently, the edge resistances are

\[
r(w,w0)=1,
\qquad
r(w,w1)=2 .
\]

More explicitly, at the root,

\[
Q(\varnothing,0)=\frac23,
\qquad
Q(\varnothing,1)=\frac13 .
\]

If \(w\ne\varnothing\) ends in \(0\), then

\[
Q(w,w^-)=\frac25,
\qquad
Q(w,w0)=\frac25,
\qquad
Q(w,w1)=\frac15 .
\]

If \(w\ne\varnothing\) ends in \(1\), then

\[
Q(w,w^-)=\frac14,
\qquad
Q(w,w0)=\frac12,
\qquad
Q(w,w1)=\frac14 .
\]

The trace probabilities before deleting holds are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}
\text{state } \gamma
& \widehat P(\gamma,\gamma)
& \widehat P(\gamma,p(\gamma))
& \widehat P(\gamma,\gamma_0)
& \widehat P(\gamma,\gamma_1)
\\ \hline
\text{non-root }0\text{-child}
& 3/8 & 1/4 & 1/4 & 1/8
\\
\text{non-root }1\text{-child}
& 1/2 & 1/8 & 1/4 & 1/8
\\
o=\varnothing
& 5/8 & - & 1/4 & 1/8
\end{array}
\]

Here \(p(\gamma)\) denotes the parent of a non-root vertex, and
\(\gamma_i=f_i(\gamma)\). The no-holding kernel \(Q\) is obtained by
normalizing each row after removing the holding column.

[Theorem 8 (Existence and stationarity of max-id processes) of arXiv:2604.11434, 'Maxima of stationary systems of randomly time-changed L\'evy particles'] Let $\alpha$ be a mass function satisfying Assumption~\ref{asu:alpha}, let $(L_t)_{t\ge 0}$ be a L\'evy process satisfying Assumption~\ref{asu:levy}, and let $(X_t)_{t\ge 0}$
  be the time-changed process in the sense of Lemma~\ref{lem:existence_tcp},
  and consider the process $(Z_t)_{t\ge 0}$ defined by
\begin{align*}
  Z_t
  \ = \
  \max
  \mathfrak{P}_t((X_t)_{t\ge 0}, \alpha(x)\exp(-x)\mathrm{d}x)
  \,.
\end{align*}
  Then the process $(Z_t)_{t\ge 0}$ has paths in $\mathbb{D}([0,\infty))$ and is stationary.
If, furthermore, $(L_t)_{t\ge 0}$ has continuous paths, then $(Z_t)_{t\ge 0}$ has paths in $\mathbb{C}([0,\infty))$.
title: Existence and stationarity of max-id processes

body:
[Definition 4 (One-spike BBP distribution) of arXiv:2608.20552, 'One-point fluctuations for exponential last passage percolation under upper-tail condition'] For $\ww,\rr\in\R$, define the one-spike BBP distribution function by
\beq

	F_{\tn{BBP},\ww}(\rr)=1+\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(-1)^n}{(n!)^2(2\pi\ii)^{2n}}\int_{(\Sigma_{\rL})^n}\dd\bu\int_{(\Sigma_{\rR})^n}\dd\bv\,\K_n(\bu\mid\bv)^2\prod_{i=1}^n\frac{e^{-u_i^3/3+\rr u_i}(v_i-\ww)}{e^{-v_i^3/3+\rr v_i}(u_i-\ww)}.
\eeq
Here,
$\K_n(\bu\mid\bv)=\det\bigl[\frac{1}{u_i-v_j}\bigr]_{i,j=1}^n$
is the Cauchy determinant. The contours $\Sigma_{\rL}$ and $\Sigma_{\rR}$ are the usual left and right Airy contours, running from $\infty e^{-2\ii\pi/3}$ to $\infty e^{2\ii\pi/3}$ and from $\infty e^{-\ii\pi/3}$ to $\infty e^{\ii\pi/3}$, respectively.\footnote{Throughout the paper, all infinite contours are oriented from bottom to top, and all simple closed contours are oriented counterclockwise.} 
They are disjoint, $\Sigma_{\rR}$ lies to the right of $\Sigma_{\rL}$, and $\Sigma_{\rL}$ lies to the right of $\ww$.
title: One-spike BBP distribution

[Proposition G1pn of arXiv:2411.16647, 'The stochastic evolution of an infinite population with logistic-type interaction'] There exists a countable set $\mathcal{V}\subset C_{\rm b}^{+}(X)$, which contains constants and is closed under addition, such that the set $\widetilde{\mathcal{F}} =\{ \widetilde{F}_v: v\in \mathcal{V} \}$ has the following properties:  
\begin{itemize}
 \item[(i)] The space of $\mathcal{B}(\Gamma_*)$-measurable functions is the bounded point-wise closure of $\widetilde{\mathcal{F}}$, see [Dawson], and $\mathcal{B}(\Gamma_*)$ is generated by  $\widetilde{\mathcal{F}}$.
 \item[(ii)] $\widetilde{\mathcal{F}}$ is a strongly separating, and hence separating, subset of $C_{\rm b}(\Gamma_*)$. The former implies that this set is weak convergence determining. That is, for $\{\mu_n\}\subset \mathcal{P}(\Gamma_*)$ and $\mu \in\ \mathcal{P}(\Gamma_*)$, it follows that $\mu_n \Rightarrow \mu$ as $n\to \infty$ if and only if
 $\mu_n(\widetilde{F}_v) \to \mu(\widetilde{F}_v)$ for all $\widetilde{F}_v\in \widetilde{\mathcal{F}}$.  
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition G1pn of arXiv:2411.16647

body: The GAUSSIAN ORTHOGONAL ENSEMBLE GOE_n is the law of a real symmetric n by n matrix H whose entries are independent up to symmetry with H_{ii} distributed as N(0, 2/n) and H_{ij} distributed as N(0, 1/n) for i < j. Its density with respect to Lebesgue measure on the space of real symmetric matrices is proportional to exp( - (n/4) trace(H^2) ), and the law is invariant under H -> O H O^T for every orthogonal O. The GAUSSIAN UNITARY ENSEMBLE GUE_n is the law of a Hermitian H with H_{ii} distributed as N(0, 1/n) real and, for i < j, H_{ij} = x + i y with x and y independent N(0, 1/(2n)), so that E|H_{ij}|^2 = 1/n; its density is proportional to exp( - (n/2) trace(H^2) ) and it is invariant under H -> U H U^* for every unitary U. With THESE normalisations the empirical spectral distribution of either ensemble converges to the semicircle law on [-2, 2], the largest eigenvalue converges to 2, and the edge fluctuations are of order n^{-2/3} with Tracy-Widom limits (beta = 1 for GOE, beta = 2 for GUE). The DIAGONAL VARIANCE DIFFERS BETWEEN THE TWO ENSEMBLES - 2/n for GOE, 1/n for GUE - and that is what makes both densities come out as the invariant exponential of the trace; getting it wrong changes the density but not the limiting spectral law. Normalisation conventions vary widely across the literature: some authors use unnormalised entries of variance 1 and divide by sqrt(n) afterwards, some put the semicircle on [-1,1] or [-2 sqrt(2), 2 sqrt(2)], and some use exp(-trace(H^2)/2) with n absorbed elsewhere. Any imported constant must be checked against the convention it was derived under. [standard; e.g. Anderson, Guionnet and Zeitouni, An Introduction to Random Matrices, Sections 2.5 and 2.6]

$\widehat{G}$ denote its Pontryagin dual, with Fourier transform $f \mapsto
\widehat{f}$ mapping $L^2(G) \to L^2(\widehat{G})$. Let $F \subset
L^2(G)$ be bounded. The following assertions are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $ F$ is relatively compact in $L^2(G)$.
\item[(ii)] \text{Decay of $ F$ and of $\widehat{ F}$:} for
every $\varepsilon > 0$, there exist compact sets $K \subset G$ and $\widehat K
\subset \widehat G$ such that
$$
        \int_{G \setminus K} |f(x)|^2 \, dx < \varepsilon^2
        \quad\text{and}\quad
        \int_{\widehat{G} \setminus \widehat{K}} |\widehat{f}(\chi)|^2 \, d\chi < \varepsilon^2
        \qquad \text{for all } f \in F.
$$
\item[(iii)] \text{Equicontinuity of $ F$ and of $\widehat{
F}$:} for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is an open neighbourhood $V$ of $e\in G$
and an open neighbourhood $\widehat{V}$ of the trivial character in $\widehat{G}$
such that
$$
\|\tau_xf-f\|_{L^2(G)}<\varepsilon \ \text{ for all } x\in V,
\quad\text{and}\quad
\|\tau_\chi\widehat f-\widehat f\|_{L^2(\widehat G)}<\varepsilon \ \text{ for all
} \chi\in\widehat V,
$$
for all $f\in F$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

	\begin{equation}
		
		\Phi(a, b, z) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(a)_n}{(b)_n n!}z^n
	\end{equation}\\
	\noindent where $(a)_n = a(a+1)\cdots(a+n-1)$. It is well known \cite{Hazewinkel} that as either a function of $z$ with $a$ and $b$ fixed, or as a function of $a$ with $b$ and $z$ fixed, $\Phi(a,b,z)$ is an entire function. It is a meromorphic function of $b$ with $a$ and $z$ fixed with simple poles at $b = 0, -1, -2, \dots$.

[Theorem thm : big3 of arXiv:2609.00105, 'Weighted composition operators and classification of weighted Hardy spaces'] Let $\mathcal{H}_1$ and $\mathcal{H}_2$ be weighted Hardy spaces in $d$ variables. 
    Assume that $G_1(t)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_nt^n$ is the generating function of $\mathcal{H}_1$ and $G_2(t)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty b_nt^n$ is the generating function of $\mathcal{H}_2$. 
    If there exist $C,c,\gamma\in (0,\infty)$ such that $c\le \frac{b_n}{a_n}\gamma^n\le C$ for all $n$, then $\mathcal{H}_1$ and $\mathcal{H}_2$ are isomorphic via an RKHS isomorphism.

body:
[Defn 1 of arXiv:2608.13208, 'Universality in dimension $1$ of kinetically constrained lattice gases'] A kinetically constrained lattice gas is a Markov
process on $\Omega=\{0,1\}^{\Z}$ with generator 
\begin{equation}
\cL f(\eta)=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{x,y\in\Z}c(x,y,\eta)(f(\eta^{xy})-f(\eta)),
\end{equation}
where $\eta^{xy}$ is the configuration after exchanging $x$ and
$y$. The rates are given by the \emph{constraint function} $c:\Z\times\Z\times\Omega\to[0,\infty]$
satisfying:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Nearest-neighbor jumps: $c(x,y,\eta)=0$ if $\left|x-y\right|\neq1$.
By convention $c(x,y,\eta)=c(y,x,\eta)$.
\item Translation invariance: $c(x,y,\eta)=c(x+z,y+z,\tau_{z}\eta)$ for
all $x,y,z$, where $\tau_{z}$ is the translation by $z$.
\item $c(x,y,\eta)$ does not depend on the occupation at $x$ and $y$,
i.e., $c(x,y,\eta)=c(x,y,\eta^{xy})$.
\item Finite range: there exists $r>0$ such that $c(x,y,\eta)$ depends
only on the configuration in $x+[-r,r]$.
\item Monotonicity: if $\eta(x)\le\omega(x)$ for all $x$, then $c(x,y,\eta)\ge c(x,y,\omega)$.
That is, adding vacancies speeds up transitions.
\end{enumerate}
We can also define the process on a finite segment $[a,b]$ of $\Z$
by fixing boundary conditions; in this article we always consider
filled boundary, i.e., for $x,y\in[a,b]$ the constraint in the segment
is given by $c_{[a,b]}(x,y,\eta)=c(x,y,\tilde{\eta})$ where $\tilde{\eta}$
agrees with $\eta$ on $[a,b]$ and equals $1$ outside.

body:
Let X be a nonempty COMPACT metrizable space and let T : X -> X be continuous. Then T admits at least one invariant Borel probability measure: there exists a Borel probability mu on X with mu(T inverse of A) = mu(A) for every Borel A. The set of such measures is nonempty, convex and weak-* compact, and its extreme points are exactly the ERGODIC invariant measures; by the Krein-Milman theorem an ergodic measure therefore exists as well.
COMPACTNESS of X and CONTINUITY of T are both essential - a continuous map of a non-compact space may have no invariant probability measure (translation on R is the standard example), and a merely measurable map of a compact space may have none either.
No hypothesis of minimality, transitivity or the existence of a reference measure is needed.

For every $r<\infty$, there are an integer $R_r$, an admissible base weight
\begin{align}
 V_r(w)=
 (1+\|w\|_{H^b}^2)^{R_r}
 \exp(\eta_0\|w\|_2^2),
 
\end{align}
where one sufficiently small $\eta_0>0$ is fixed for the whole hierarchy,
and $C_r<\infty$ such that, uniformly over unit $\mathsf p\in H$,
\begin{align}
 \mathbf E_{w,\mathsf p}\|\mathsf p_{t_*}\|_{H^1}^{2r}

 \\
 \mathbf E_w\|w_{t_*}\|_{C^\beta}^r

\end{align}
The same estimates hold after every almost surely finite stopping time $S$:
\begin{align}
 \mathbf E\left[
  \|\mathsf p_{S+t_*}\|_{H^1}^{2r}\mid\mathcal F_S\right]
 &\le C_rV_r(w_S),
 \\
 \mathbf E\left[
  \|w_{S+t_*}\|_{C^\beta}^{r}\mid\mathcal F_S\right]
 &\le C_rV_r(w_S).
 
\end{align}
The constants do not depend on $S$ or on the value of $\mathsf p_S$.

For every fixed $T\ge t_*$, every $r<\infty$, and every unit
$\mathsf p\in H^1$,
\begin{align}
 \mathbf E_{w,\mathsf p}
 \left(\int_0^T\|\mathsf p_s\|_{H^1}^2\,\dd s\right)^r
 \le C_{r,T}\bigl(V_r(w)+1+\|\mathsf p\|_{H^1}^{R_r}\bigr),
 
\end{align}
where the polynomial orders are independent of $T$.  Finally, all weights
may be chosen from one nested hierarchy.  Given any finite list of moment
orders and polynomial powers, one member $V_*$ dominates every corresponding
right hand side and satisfies
\begin{align}
 P_T^{\rm base}V_*
 \le C_{0,*}e^{-\gamma_*T}V_*+B_*,
 \qquad T\ge0.
 
\end{align}

[Lem 39 of arXiv:2608.28355, 'About the contractibility of the walking coinductive equivalence'] Let $\ell\geq 0$ and $0\leq p\leq s\leq  \ell +2$.
Fix a strict $\omega$-category $\cP$,
an injective map
\[\overline{\rho}\colon \Delta[s-p]\to \Delta[\ell+2-p],\]
and a map of marked simplicial sets.
\[\widetilde{\gamma}\colon\Sigma^p\Delta[\ell+2-p]\to N^{RS}\cP.\]
Assume that the $(s-p)$-simplex
\[\Delta[s-p]\xrightarrow{\overline{\rho}} \Delta[\ell+2-p]\xrightarrow{\widetilde{\beta}} N^{\mathrm{RS}}(\cP^{(p)}(\glboundary{\widetilde{\gamma}}))\]
is marked,
where $\widetilde{\beta}$ is the transpose of $\widetilde{\gamma}$
under the adjunction \cref{IteratedSuspensionAdjunctionMarked}
(using the identification of \cref{NvsIteratedHom} and the notation from \cref{GlobularBoundary}).
Then the composite 
\[
\Delta[s]\twoheadrightarrow\Sigma^p\Delta[s-p]\xrightarrow{\Sigma^p\overline\rho}\Sigma^p\Delta[\ell+2-p]\xrightarrow{\widetilde\gamma}N^{\mathrm{RS}}\cP
\]
is a marked $s$-simplex of $N^{\mathrm{RS}}\cP$.

[Lemma 6 (Morse--Mostow lemma) of arXiv:2607.08632, 'Uncountably many extremal Series--Sinai states for the Ising model on Lobachevsky lattices'] Let us assume that \(X\) is \emph{\(\delta\)-hyperbolic}.
    Then, there exists a constant \(C > 0\) such that for all \(k\ge 1\) and \(c\ge 0\) and all \((k, c)\)-quasigeodesic segment \(f:[0, t]\to \Hyp{2}\), we have
    \begin{equation}
        \hausdorffDistance{f([0, t])}{[f(0), f(t)]} \le C k^2 (c + \delta).
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Morse--Mostow lemma

body: The expectation of a random variable X is E[X] = integral X dP (sum x P(X=x) in the discrete case, integral x f(x) dx with a density). It is linear (E[aX + bY] = aE[X] + bE[Y]) even without independence, monotone, and satisfies the law of the unconscious statistician E[g(X)] = integral g dP_X. For independent X, Y, E[XY] = E[X]E[Y]. Expectation exists when E|X| < infinity.
title: Expectation (Expected Value)

body:
[Definition def:block of arXiv:2608.28007, 'Exact Risk Ratios for Weighted Data Selection in Linear Regression'] A whitened system $\{(\xi_i,\eta_i)\}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ has \emph{orthogonal
circuit-block structure} with dimension vector $r=(r_1,\dots,r_s)$,
$\sum_jr_j=d$, if
$\mathbb{R}^d=E_1\oplus^{\perp}\dots\oplus^{\perp}E_s$ with $\dim E_j=r_j$, every
nonzero feature lies in some $E_j$, and every $E_j$ contains a positive
circuit of $r_j+1$ gradients spanning $E_j$. Here a positive circuit of
gradients means a set of indices whose gradients $g_i=\eta_i\xi_i$ carry a
strictly positive zero-sum relation, minimal with respect to support. Write
$I_j=\{i:\xi_i\in E_j\setminus\{0\}\}$ and
$R_j=\frac1N\sum_{i\in I_j}\eta_i^2$, so $\sum_jR_j\le1$; points with
$\xi_i=0$ belong to no block. The \emph{model class} $\mathcal D_r$ consists
of the datasets $D$ with full feature rank and $L_D^{\star}>0$ whose whitened system
under Lemma~(lem:whiten of the paper) has orthogonal circuit-block structure with
dimension vector $r$.
title: Definition def:block of arXiv:2608.28007

Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, full calibration, paired). Given that the long-only gain is the estimation variance the constraint removes at the rows the stack is scored on, the amount of constraint was chosen with the evaluation inputs: a blend w(t) between the simplex and least-squares stacks with t minimising the cross-validated calibration error plus the excess bootstrap variance of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows, and a per-row version t_i = 1/(1 + kappa v_i/median v) that leans to the simplex where least squares is uncertain. P24 (a) HELD: on EMIT the per-cell blend reads +0.08 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 39 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 t* is at or above 0.5 on 30 of 30 cells and the blend reads +0.66 vs least squares; (c) REFUTED: the per-row blend vs the per-cell blend is +0.70 on Y2 and -0.14 on EMIT overall; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Fresh-split replication (P25, split C, SPLIT_SEED 11, the criterion uses no evaluation targets): P25 (a) HELD: on split C the EMIT blend reads +0.63 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 35 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend reads +0.84 vs the simplex (wins 30 of 30) and +0.65 vs least squares; (c) HELD: t* averages 0.34 on EMIT and 0.67 on OCO-2; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Bootstrap-size stability (P28, B = 16 against B = 8 on split B): P28 (a) HELD: t*(16) equals t*(8) on 86 pct of the 70 cells and is within 0.2 on 100 pct; (b) HELD: the blend's mean gain against the simplex moves from +0.08 to +0.06 on EMIT and from +0.83 to +0.83 on OCO-2, and the both-endpoints win count on OCO-2 is 30 of 30 at B = 16; falsifier (agreement below 50 pct or a gain moving by more than 0.5) not triggered. Break test: a fixed midpoint t = 0.5 matches the criterion on OCO-2 (+0.96 / +1.01 against +0.83 / +0.84 on the two splits) but loses 1.6 and 4.4 pct on EMIT where the criterion stays at +0.08 and +0.63 - the criterion's value is knowing, without labels, when not to leave the simplex; the EMIT shortfall against the hindsight-best t is the bias-shift term of the risk identity. Scarce calibration (P30, 240 of the calibration rows per cell, split B): P30 (a) HELD: at n = 240 the simplex beats least squares by +14.10 on EMIT (full calibration +8.83); (b) REFUTED: t* averages 0.22 on EMIT and the blend reads -2.61 vs the simplex; (c) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend beats both endpoints on 30 of 30 cells and the simplex reads +2.27 vs least squares (full calibration -0.18); falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT) TRIGGERED. The observable part of the bias shift (P31): adding t^2 (D_ev - D_cal), the shift in the two bases' mean squared disagreement between the evaluation and calibration rows, to the criterion - P31 (a) REFUTED: the R'-blend reads -0.71 vs the simplex on EMIT split B (R-blend +0.08) and +0.71 on split C (R-blend +0.63); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the R'-blend is -0.11 vs the R-blend on split B and -0.12 on split C; (c) REFUTED: mean t** 0.39 against t* 0.33 on EMIT, share of the hindsight optimum 0.07 -> -0.62; falsifier (R'-blend worse than the R-blend by more than 0.3 on any corpus or split) TRIGGERED. Per-output mixing weights (P34, the criterion decoupled across outputs): P34 (a) REFUTED: the per-output blend reads -0.41 vs the per-cell blend on EMIT split B and -0.53 on split C; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 -0.02 and -0.08 on split C; (c) REFUTED: on Y2 the share of outputs at t_d = 0 is 0.20 and at t_d >= 0.5 is 0.34; falsifier (per-output worse than per-cell by more than 0.3 anywhere) TRIGGERED. A nearest-neighbour proxy for the bias shift (P35, the simplex's out-of-fold residuals at the nearest calibration rows standing in for its bias at the scored rows): P35 (a) REFUTED: the full-shift blend reads -0.69 vs the R-blend on EMIT split B and -0.12 on split C; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 -0.08 and -0.14 on split C; (c) REFUTED: cross-only vs full on EMIT -0.05 vs -0.62 (split B); falsifier (either variant worse than the R-blend by more than 0.3 anywhere) TRIGGERED. Scarce calibration, the ratio-metric criterion (P41, 240 calibration rows, split B, three-vertex form, registered and R_1 choices side by side): P41 (a) HELD: at n_cal = 240 the R_1 blend reads +1.17 vs the simplex on EMIT (within 1.0; the registered three-vertex blend reads -1.83); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the R_1 blend beats both endpoints on 30 of 30 cells (at least 25); (c) HELD: R_1 vs the registered blend on EMIT +1.38 (at least +1.0); falsifier (R_1 worse than the simplex by more than 2.0 on EMIT) not triggered. So the P30 caveat is confined to the squared-loss criterion; the criterion in the score's own metric keeps the simplex where it should at scarce calibration. P44: the shipped tool against the driver (P44): P44 (a) REFUTED: the tool's mixing weight is within 0.2 of the driver's on 14 (squared) and 11 (ratio) of 14 cells; (b) HELD: the tool's blend scores within 1 pct of the driver's on 12 / 12 of 14; (c) HELD by the clause's wording (worse than both endpoints by more than 1 pct while the driver beats one: none); under the stricter test the analyzer was first written with (worse than the better endpoint by more than 1 pct): one cell, emit s102 Y3 (ratio); falsifier not triggered by the clause's wording, TRIGGERED under the stricter test. P55: the seed-102 diagnostic (P55): P55 (a) REFUTED: with the target norms at the scored rows the tool's ratio choice is within 0.2 of the driver's on 0 of 3 cells; (b) REFUTED: with the shipped convention at B = 32 on 2 of 3 (at most one); (c) REFUTED: on Y3 arm A stays at the least-squares endpoint; falsifier TRIGGERED (the draw decides - raise B before the ratio metric is the default). P49: scarce calibration on the held-out split (P49): P49 (a) HELD: on split D at 240 rows the R_1 blend reads +0.56 vs the simplex on EMIT (within 1.0; the registered blend -0.52); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 it beats both endpoints on 30 of 30 cells; (c) HELD: R_1 vs the registered blend on EMIT +1.00 (at least +1.0); falsifier (R_1 worse than the simplex by more than 2.0 on EMIT) not triggered. P50: the shipped tool on the held-out split (P50): P50 (a) HELD: the tool's mixing weight is within 0.2 of the driver's on 14 (squared) and 14 (ratio) of 14 cells; (b) HELD: the tool's blend scores within 1 pct of the driver's on 13 / 13 of 14; (c) HELD by the clause's wording (worse than both endpoints by more than 1 pct while the driver beats one: none); under the stricter test the analyzer was first written with (worse than the better endpoint by more than 1 pct): one cell, emit s102 Y2 (squared); falsifier not triggered by the clause's wording, TRIGGERED under the stricter test. P58: the P24 shift retired on the held-out splits (P58): P58 (a) HELD: on split D EMIT the delta = 0 ratio blend vs the full R_1 blend reads +0.47 (vs the simplex: R_1 +1.27, delta = 0 +1.73; at least +0.3); (b) HELD: on split D OCO-2 +0.00 (within 0.2); (c) HELD: on split C EMIT +0.52 (R_1 +2.24, delta = 0 +2.77 vs the simplex) and OCO-2 -0.00; (d) HELD: R_3 vs the delta = 0 arm = D -0.08 / -0.00, C +0.01 / +0.00 (each within 0.2); the registered criterion for the record, split D EMIT +0.13 full / +0.03 delta = 0, split C +0.70 / +0.57; falsifier (delta = 0 worse than R_1 by more than 0.3 on EMIT on either split) not triggered.

body:
Let V be a finite honeycomb vertex set, E the edges with both endpoints in V, H the boundary mid-edges with exactly one endpoint in V, and c the number of components of (V,E). Prescribe complex g on H and b_v=sum_{h in H incident to v}(h-v)g(h). Arbitrary complex interior midpoint values F satisfying sum_{p adjacent to v}(p-v)F(p)=0 exist iff sum_{v in C}b_v=0 on every component C. If solvable, their complex affine dimension is |E|-|V|+c. For a connected plane graph this equals the number of bounded faces. This is an author-proved auxiliary result, pending full independent review.
Finite honeycomb graph; arbitrary complex midpoint fields

body: Two hubs whose remainder crosses a split (bounded-density quadratic-form conjecture). Let X_H in R^2 and X' be independent with independent coordinates of densities <= 1, L = M X' in R^2, R(X') = X'^T A_R X' + b^T X' + c any real quadratic. Split the light coordinates into I, J; let M_J (columns in J) have singular values s_1' >= s_2' > 0, Pi the projection onto the row space of M_J, and C = (A_R)_{I,J} (Id - Pi) with rows c_i. If F = ||C||_F > 0 and |c_i|^2 <= F^2/2, then for every symmetric 2 x 2 B and beta, Q = X_H^T B X_H + 2 <X_H, L + beta> + R satisfies |phi_Q(eta)| <= pi^{3/2} 2^{5/4} (s_1' s_2' F)^{-1/2} |eta|^{-3/2} and ||p_Q||_inf <= 5.35 (s_1' s_2' F)^{-1/3}. Proof: Plancherel in the partner, then |E_{X_I} E_{X_J}|^2 <= E_{X_I} |E_{X_J}|^2 with a copy of X_J: every term inside a half cancels or becomes a phase, the crossing terms give prod_{i in I} psi_i(2 eta <a_i, D_J>), and Hoelder with weights |c_i|^2/F^2 finishes. Twists inside either half are free. The same decoupling with one hub gives |phi_Q| <= 2 pi (|w_J| F)^{-1/2} |eta|^{-1} and P(|Q - s| <= delta) <= C delta log(1/delta) for every remainder (Proposition 6.6), and |eta|^{-3/2} when the projected crossing block has rank two (Proposition 6.8).

Let $X_1,\dots,X_m$ be iid random rows in $\mathbb{R}^m$ and let $S, T$ be two distinct $(m-1)$-subsets of row indices. Put $A = S \cap T$, $B = S \setminus T$, $C = T \setminus S$ and $D = m - |A|$, so that $|B| = |C| = D - 1$. Condition on the rows indexed by $A$, let $E_A = \operatorname{span}(A)^{\perp}$, which has dimension $D$ almost surely, and let $Q_A : \mathbb{R}^D \to E_A \subset \mathbb{R}^m$ be any isometry (an $m \times D$ matrix with orthonormal columns). Then the unit null normals $u_S, u_T$ of the two $(m-1) \times m$ row submatrices satisfy $u_S = Q_A v$ and $u_T = Q_A w$, where $v, w \in S^{D-1}$ are the null directions of the residual matrices $U = B Q_A$ and $V = C Q_A$. Conditionally on $A$ the matrices $U$ and $V$ are independent, each with iid rows of law $Q_A^{\top} X$, and the pair correlation is preserved exactly: $\rho_{ST}^2 = \langle u_S, u_T \rangle^2 = \langle v, w \rangle^2$. Writing $M_A = \mathbb{E}[v v^{\top} \mid A]$ for the conditional second-moment matrix of the residual null line, $\mathbb{E}[\langle v,w\rangle^2 \mid A] = \operatorname{tr}(M_A^2)$. The content of the lemma is that a pair correlated only through a shared part becomes, after conditioning on that part, two independent objects in the lower dimension $D$ that measures exactly how much the two index sets fail to overlap.

Load-bearing hypotheses: the periodization $Pf(x)=\sum_nf(x+n)$ must be continuous at the point where the identity is evaluated, and its Fourier series must converge there (absolute summability of $(\hat f(k))_k$ is the usual sufficient condition). For a general $f\in L^1(\mathbb R)$ all that is true is $\widehat{Pf}(k)=\hat f(k)$, i.e. Poisson summation as an identity of Fourier series of an $L^1(\mathbb T)$ function - which says nothing pointwise. Concrete failure: $f=\mathbf 1_{[0,1]}$ (with $f(0)=f(1)=1$). Then $\sum_nf(n)=f(0)+f(1)=2$, while $\hat f(0)=1$ and $\hat f(k)=\int_0^1e^{-2\pi ikx}dx=0$ for $k\ne0$, so $\sum_k\hat f(k)=1\ne2$. The periodization equals $1$ off $\mathbb Z$ and $2$ on $\mathbb Z$: it is discontinuous exactly where the identity is being evaluated, and the Fourier series converges to the midpoint $1$. Redefining $f(0)=f(1)=1/2$ restores the identity. Second trap: pure decay of $f$ is not enough - one needs decay (or summability) on the transform side as well, since the right-hand series must converge; $f$ continuous and integrable with $\hat f$ merely tending to zero gives no pointwise statement. When quoting a rate, the clean hypothesis is $|f(x)|\le C(1+|x|)^{-1-\delta}$ and $|\hat f(\xi)|\le C(1+|\xi|)^{-1-\delta}$ with $f$ continuous, or simply $f\in\mathcal S$.

[Definition 6 of arXiv:2608.25785, 'Proper Actions on Homogeneous Spaces of the Upper Triangular Matrix Group via Coarse Geome'] Let $L$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group, $S$ a locally compact Hausdorff space, $\rho :L\times S\rightarrow S$ a continuous action. 
    The action $\rho$ is said to be \emph{proper} if the map
    \[
    \Psi : L \times S \to S \times S, \quad (g, x) \mapsto (x, gx)
    \]
    is topologically proper.

[Lemma kemma2.2spectralradius of arXiv:2412.06246, 'The smallest singular value for rectangular random matrices with Lévy entries'] [[seginer2000expected], Corollary 2.2] 
    Consider $Y=(y_{ij})$ some $m_1\times m_2$ random matrix with i.i.d. zero mean entries. If we use $Y_{i\cdot}$ and $Y_{\cdot j}$ to denote the $i$-th row (and resp. the $j$-th column) of $X$, then we can find $C>0$ so that for any $q\leq 2\log\max(m_1,m_2)$, we have
    $$
\mathbb{E}\|Y\|^q\leq C^q\left(\mathbb{E}\max_{1\leq i\leq m_1}\|Y_{i\cdot}\|_2^q+\mathbb{E}\max_{1\leq j\leq m_2}\|Y_{\cdot j}\|_2^q
\right).
    $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2609.03974, '2609.03974'] There is an exact solution to the equation
    \begin{equation}
       u_t(t,x)=u_{xx}(t,x)-\sum_{j=2}^{n}p_ju^j(t,x)+u(t,x) 
    \end{equation}
    in the form
    $$u(x\mp ct)=\frac{1}{\left(1+p\exp\left({\pm k\left(x\mp ct\right)}\right)\right)^{\frac{2}{n-1}}}, \quad p>0,$$
    with
    \[
     c=\frac{n+2p_n+1}{\sqrt{p_n\left(2n+2\right)}}, \qquad k=\frac{\sqrt{p_n}\left(n-1\right)}{\sqrt{2n+2}},
    \]
    where $p_n=1$ and $p_j=0,$ $j=2,...,n-1$ in the case of even $n$ and $p_n>0,$ $p_n+p_{\frac{n+1}{2}}=1,$ $p_j=0, j=2,...,n-1; j\ne\frac{n+1}{2}$ in the case of odd $n.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT, unaudited; novelty is unestablished. Gaussian extensive-rank product reference has a C1 MI limit and pointwise MMSE limit for all positive finite aspect ratios, proof unaudited. For B=UV^T/sqrt(N), independent real standard Gaussian factors, P/N->alpha>0, M/N->beta>0, normalized MI converges to a C1 function on s>0 and normalized MMSE converges to twice its derivative. In canonical n<=p, p/n->kappa>1, gamma=1/kappa, rho_t is the symmetric positive-singular law of UV^T/n+sqrt(t/n)G; i(s)=E_gamma(rho_(1/s))+(log s)/2-E_gamma(noise), and m(s)=1/s-Phi_gamma(1/s)/s^2. Real Wishart output laws, gap/density regularity025, entropy chain rule026 and calibration027 separately pay the premises. Near-square sequences use022; transpose and SNR rescaling handle alpha<1. Together with006/023, every fixed centered iid finite-second-moment unit-variance factor pair has limsup per-entry MI and MMSE excess over Gaussian <=0 at every fixed s>=0. Noncentered and dimension-dependent priors are not asserted. Novelty unestablished.
Independent real Gaussian reference factors and standard Gaussian channel noise.
Positive finite limiting P/N and M/N.
For the extremality consequence, fixed centered iid unit-variance factor laws with finite second moments and independent factor arrays.

metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:ff69908262824ba48716cbe4d812386b2868967019e642923e44a45d36eb896a","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/ff/ff69908262824ba48716cbe4d812386b2868967019e642923e44a45d36eb896a.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:9548f3adc68903b67cd441efcd18bebcb2f7ac02a496d314a765992a9a4498a7","bundle_entry_key":"gaussian-product-all-aspects-mi-c1-mmse-w718","bundle_id":"population.t287-rectangular-reference-c1-and-noncentered-comparison-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian channels and extensive-rank matrix inference","draft":"w718/bundle_009.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.gaussian_channels:gaussian-product-all-aspects-mi-c1-mmse-w718","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Gaussian extensive-rank reference: all positive finite aspect ratios

Claim draft w718-T287-028, version 1. Kind: moved; target: 2. Status: proof (unaudited). Every earlier dependency is also unaudited. Novelty is unestablished. This completes the rectangular-reference route conditional on the supporting proofs, and gives a centered finite-variance partial answer to the dossier wording. Noncentered priors are not included here because centering is not explicit in that wording. Target1 remains open.

## Statement

Let independent standard real Gaussian U,V have sizes N by M and P by M, with P/N->alpha>0 and M/N->beta>0 finite. Set B=UV^T/sqrt(N), with independent standard Gaussian channel noise G. Then

i_N(s)=I(B;sqrt(s)B+G)/(NP)

has a pointwise limit i(s), continuously differentiable for every s>0. The normalized Gaussian-reference product risk m_N(s)=E||B-E[B|sqrt(s)B+G]||F^2/(NP) converges to 2i'(s) at every such s. At zero it tends to beta.

Consequently for independent iid factor arrays with fixed centered unit-variance real laws and finite second moments, at the same dimensions and noise level,

limsup_N [m_iid,N(s)-m_N(s)]<=0 for every fixed s>=0,      (1)

and likewise limsup_N[i_iid,N(s)-i_N(s)]<=0. Gaussian factors thus maximize both limiting comparisons in this centered fixed-law class; no finite-dimensional extremality is claimed. The conclusion allows a risk limsup without assuming existence of the iid-prior risk limit. The scaling is UV^T/sqrt(N); raw UV^T loss must be divided by N.

The hardest new step is the real rectangular reference C1 limit. Its most delicate dependencies are the physical boundary-branch continuation in claim025 and the logarithmic chain rule in claim026. The present proof separates those steps from MI calibration and from derivative convergence.

## 1. Canonical strictly rectangular dimensions

First take n<=p, p/n->kappa>1, M/n->b>0. Let S=UV^T/n, Z entries iid N(0,1/n). Signal B_c=sqrt(n)S is the canonical entry-scaled product. For t>0 let rho_t be the symmetrized limiting law of the n singular values of S+sqrt(t)Z. Supporting claims024-025 show compact support, a uniform gap at zero on compact positive heat intervals, bounded density, and the boundary/transport regularity needed by claim026. The source is the real conditional population-Wishart representation; no complex-to-real freeness theorem is used.

Put gamma=1/kappa and let rho_noise be the symmetric singular law of Z. Write

E_gamma(rho)=gamma Sigma(rho)+(1-gamma)integral log|x|rho(dx).

For s>0 the limiting observation law of sqrt(s)S+Z is the dilation D_sqrt(s) rho_(1/s). We claim its normalized MI limit is

i_c(s)=E_gamma(rho_(1/s))+(log s)/2-E_gamma(rho_noise).   (2)

The next two steps pay the expected-W2 and unbounded-input premises of calibration027, so (2) is not an assumed information formula.

## 2. Expected spectral W2 convergence

Conditional on U, sqrt(s)S+Z has the law T_n^(1/2)H/sqrt(n), where T_n=I+s C_n, C_n=UU^T/n, and H is independent standard Gaussian n by p. The checked Silverstein theorem gives a deterministic weak limiting squared-singular law. Gaussian sphere-net tails for U/sqrt(n), V/sqrt(n), H/sqrt(n) imply bounded moments of every fixed order of their operator norms and almost-sure eventual norm bounds, since the aspect ratios are bounded. The same holds for S and the observation.

For A_n=||T_n^(1/2)H/sqrt(n)||F^2/n, exact Gaussian conditional moments give

E[A_n|U]=(p/n) tr(T_n)/n,
Var(A_n|U)=2p tr(T_n^2)/n^4.

The expected conditional variance is O(n^-2). Also Var(tr C_n/n)=2(M/n)/n^2, so the total variance is O(n^-2), while E A_n=(p/n)(1+s M/n). Thus A_n tends almost surely to kappa(1+s b) by Chebyshev and Borel-Cantelli. Weak convergence plus convergence of these second singular moments gives singular-law W2 convergence. Its square is uniformly integrable, since it is bounded by twice the empirical second moment plus a constant and operator fourth moments are uniformly bounded. Therefore the squared W2 distance converges in expectation too.

The same argument applies at s=0 and to heat time t. Distributional conditional-Wishart representations may be coupled on a common probability space for this argument; the expected-W2 conclusion depends only on their marginals.

## 3. Norm-event conditioning and calibration

Choose a fixed C sufficiently large that E_n={||S||op<=C} has complement of exponentially small probability, by the two Gaussian-factor norm bounds. Let S^E have the conditional law of S given E_n; this law remains biorthogonally invariant. Couple S^E=S on E_n and draw an independent sample from that conditional law on its complement. This has the required marginal. With a_n=||S||F^2/p, define

d_n^2=E||S-S^E||F^2/p
 <=2E[a_n 1_(E_n^c)]+2P(E_n^c)E[a_n|E_n]->0.           (3)

Uniform operator fourth moments and the bounded aspect ratios give uniform second moments of a_n and pay the first term by Cauchy-Schwarz; E a_n=M/n and P(E_n)->1 pay the second. In particular E||S^E||F^2/p->b.

Share the noise between the two observations. Their expected squared singular-law W2 distance is at most s(p/n)d_n^2 by Hoffman-Wielandt, so the conditioned observation has exactly the same deterministic output limit in expected W2. That limit has bounded density and a positive lower edge by claims024-025. Claim027 applies to the bounded conditional prior and yields its MI limit as the difference of E_gamma at the output and pure-noise laws.

Claim006's dimension-uniform Gaussian entropy/W2 estimate transfers back:

|I(S;sqrt(s)S+Z)/(np)-I(S^E;sqrt(s)S^E+Z)/(np)|
 <=sqrt(s)d_n ->0.                                    (4)

To verify the normalization in (4), multiply both S and Z by sqrt(n). The standard-noise signal coupling error per entry is n E||S-S^E||F^2/(np)=d_n^2. MI is invariant under the common invertible rescaling. Calibration027 and the dilation identity E_gamma(D_c rho)=E_gamma(rho)+log c now prove (2).

## 4. C1 and reference MMSE

Claim026 gives E_gamma(rho_t) continuously differentiable for t>0, with derivative Phi_gamma(t)/2, where

Phi_gamma(t)=4gamma integral [H_t(x)+(kappa-1)/(2x)]^2rho_t(dx).

Consequently (2) is C1 and

2i_c'(s)=1/s-Phi_gamma(1/s)/s^2.                        (5)

For every finite n the normalized information is concave and differentiable and I-MMSE gives i_c,n'(s)=m_c,n(s)/2, with m_c,n=E||S-E[S|sqrt(s)S+Z]||F^2/p. This equals the per-entry risk for B_c=sqrt(n)S. For h>0 with s-h>0, concavity gives

[i_c,n(s+h)-i_c,n(s)]/h <=i_c,n'(s)
 <=[i_c,n(s)-i_c,n(s-h)]/h.

Take dimension limits and then h down to zero. C1 of (2) proves convergence to (5) at every fixed s>0. At s=0 both reference and centered unit-variance iid-prior risks are M/n exactly. No derivative of a merely convergent MI sequence was taken without the secant argument.

## 5. Arbitrary original aspect ratios

If alpha>1, eventually take n=N,p=P above. If alpha<1, transpose and take n=P,p=N; then B_original^T=sqrt(P/N) B_c, the canonical hidden ratio tends to beta/alpha, and

i_original,N(s)=i_c,n(s P/N).

The canonical information functions are Lipschitz in SNR with derivative at most (M/n)/2, so pointwise convergence at the limiting argument implies i_original,N(s)->i_c(alpha s). This limit is C1. Apply the same original-variable concave secants to conclude m_original,N(s)->2alpha i_c'(alpha s). This avoids assuming uniform convergence of canonical derivatives at moving arguments.

If alpha=1, claim022 already treats every sequence P/N->1, including sequences switching sides of the square. Thus all positive finite original aspect ratios are covered. At s=0 the normalized Gaussian-reference risk is M/N->beta in every case.

## 6. Fixed centered finite-variance priors

Claim023 gives expected ordered singular-profile coupling of an iid product X=UV^T/sqrt(N) to an independent Gaussian-factor reference B at all positive finite aspects, assuming fixed centered unit-variance laws and finite second moments only. Claim006 Haarizes X and proves that both its MI and its Bayes risk can only increase under the unknown orthogonal rotations. Its dimension-uniform entropy coupling estimate identifies the Haarized MI limit with the Gaussian reference. The C1 limit just proved then gives convergence of the Haarized risks by concave secants. The finite-dimensional risk inequality m_X<=m_HaarX proves (1). The corresponding MI inequality and the same value convergence give the asserted MI comparison. At s=0 both centered risks are exactly M/N. Non-unit centered variances follow by replacing SNR by their variance product and scaling the risk.

## Audit boundary

Dependencies006,017,022-027 remain proof drafts without independent PASS. In particular the weak population-Wishart law alone does not prove (2), and MI convergence alone does not prove (5); the separate calibration and C1 lemmas are essential. The conclusion is a fixed-SNR asymptotic comparison, not a finite-size inequality and not a uniform statement on dimension-dependent shrinking SNR intervals. Noncentered or dimension-dependent factor laws are not claimed here. Target1's first unsuppressed prior-dependent coefficient and uniform remainder are still open.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:965a7f6569046bdab574a5d8dade402280c470a6610623c9409c56ed763549bc","revision_digest":"sha256:3b800e4799833aee34c41412251a2c93b12d80120081dfe802ca5e2421ba863c","source_id":"owner:w718:T287:gaussian-product-all-aspects-mi-c1-mmse-w718","source_revision":"2026-10-21 w718-T287-028 version1, proof unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Definition 96 (Geometric forms and related integrals) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] \hfill
	\begin{itemize}
		\item Recall that $\gnulltori$ is the first fundamental form of the torus $\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}$.
		We define the canonical area form of $\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}$ 
		induced by $\gnulltori$
		in the double-null coordinates $(\ubar,u,x^2,x^3)$ by:
		\begin{align} 
			\voldoublenulltori 
			& = \voldoublenulltori(\ubar',u',x^2,x^3) 
			\eqdef 
			\sqrt{\det \gnulltori (\ubar',u',x^2,x^3)} \, \mathrm{d} x^2 \mathrm{d} x^3,
		\end{align}
		where $\det \gnulltori(\ubar',u',x^2,x^3)$ is the determinant of the $2 \times 2$ matrix
		$\left(\gnulltori(\ubar',u',x^2,x^3) \left(\nullgeop{x^A},\nullgeop{x^B}\right) \right)_{A,B=2,3}$
		(see RHS\,\eqref{E:DOUBLENULLTORIFIRSTFUNDRESTRICTEDTODOUBLENULLTORI}).
		\item We define the (non-canonical) area form $\volingoingnullhypersurface$ of $\ingoingcharacteristicsurfacetwoarg{\ubar}{J}$ 
		in the double-null coordinates $(\ubar,u,x^2,x^3)$ by: 
		\begin{align} 
			\volingoingnullhypersurface 
			& = \volingoingnullhypersurface(\ubar,u',x^2,x^3) 
			= \voldoublenulltori(\ubar,u',x^2,x^3) \, \mathrm{d} u'.
		\end{align}
		\item We define the (non-canonical) area form $\voloutgoingnullhypersurface$ on $\outgoingcharacteristicsurfacetwoarg{u}{I}$ 
		in the double-null coordinates $(\ubar,u,x^2,x^3)$ by:  
		\begin{align} 
			\voloutgoingnullhypersurface 
			= 
			\voloutgoingnullhypersurface(\ubar',u,x^2,x^3) 
			& \eqdef \voldoublenulltori(\ubar',u,x^2,x^3) \, \mathrm{d} \ubar'.
		\end{align} 
		\item We define the (non-canonical) volume form $\voldiamond$ of $\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{I}{J}$ 
		in the double-null  coordinates $(\ubar,u,x^2,x^3)$ by:
		\begin{align} 
			\voldiamond 
			= \voldiamond(\ubar',u',x^2,x^3) 
			& 
			\eqdef 
			\voldoublenulltori(\ubar',u',x^2,x^3) \, \mathrm{d} u' \, \mathrm{d} \ubar'.
		\end{align}
	\end{itemize}
	
	Unless we explicitly indicate otherwise, 
	all integrals along 
	$\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}, \, \outgoingcharacteristicsurfacetwoarg{u}{I}, \, \ingoingcharacteristicsurfacetwoarg{\ubar}{J}$, and $\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{I}{J}$
	are defined with respect to the above forms. 
	Moreover, we will often suppress the variables with respect to which we integrate, 
	e.g., we write:
	\begin{subequations} 
		\begin{align}
			\int_{\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}} 
			f 
			\, \voldoublenulltori 
			& 
			\eqdef 
			\int_{(x^2,x^3) \in \T^2}  
			f(\ubar,u,x^2,x^3) 
			\, \voldoublenulltori(\ubar,u,x^2,x^3),   
			 \\
			\int_{\outgoingcharacteristicsurfacetwoarg{u}{I}} 
			f \, 
			\voloutgoingnullhypersurface 
			& 
			\eqdef \int_{\ubar' \in I}  
			\int_{(x^2,x^3) \in \T^2} 
			f(\ubar',u,x^2,x^3) \, \voldoublenulltori(\ubar',u,x^2,x^3)
			\, \mathrm{d} \ubar', 
			 \\
			\int_{\ingoingcharacteristicsurfacetwoarg{\ubar}{J}} 
			f 
			\, \volingoingnullhypersurface 
			& \eqdef 
			\int_{u' \in J} \int_{(x^2,x^3) \in \T^2} 
			f(\ubar,u',x^2,x^3) 
			\, \voldoublenulltori(\ubar,u',x^2,x^3) \, \mathrm{d} u', 
			 \\
			\int_{\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{I}{J}} 
			f 
			\, \voldiamond 
			& 
			\eqdef 
			\int_{\ubar' \in I} 
			\int_{u' \in J} 
			\int_{(x^2,x^3) \in \T^2} 
			f(\ubar',u',x^2,x^3) 
			\, \voldoublenulltori(\ubar',u',x^2,x^3)
			\, 
			\mathrm{d} u' \, \mathrm{d}\ubar'.
			
		\end{align}
	\end{subequations}

[Definition of arXiv:2603.12774, 'Synchronization by noise for stochastic differential equations driven by fractional Browni'] Let $\Phi$ be an RDS and \( \mathcal{A}=\{\mathcal{A}(\omega)\}_{\omega \in \Omega} \) be a family of non-empty subsets of  $\mathcal{X}$. 
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item  [1)] The family \( \mathcal{A} \) is called a random closed set (random compact set) if, with probability one, each \( \mathcal{A}(\omega) \) is closed (compact), and for every \( x \in \mathcal{X} \), the function \( \omega \mapsto d(x, \mathcal{A}(\omega)) \) 
		is \( \mathcal{F} \)-measurable.
		\item [2)] We say that $\mathcal{A}$ is invariant under \( \Phi \) if for all \( t \geq 0 \),
		\[
		\Phi^{t}_{\omega}(\mathcal{A}(\omega)) = \mathcal{A}(\theta_t\omega) 
		\]
		holds for \( \mathbb{P} \)-almost every \( \omega \in \Omega \).
		\item [3)] The set $\mathcal{A}$ is called {random absorbing} if, 
		for every $\mathcal{E} \in \mathcal{D}(\mathcal{X})$, there exists a (random) time 
		$T = T(\mathcal{E}, \omega)$ such that
		\[
		\varphi(t, \theta_{-t}\omega, \mathcal{E}(\theta_{-t}\omega)) \subset \mathcal{A}(\omega),
		\quad \forall\, t \ge T(\mathcal{E}, \omega),
		\]
		for $\mathbb{P}$-almost every $\omega \in \Omega$.
		
	\end{enumerate}

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact identities, finite controls and structural obstruction Result: A sufficient criterion is summability over all pairs of the probabilities of an inversion relative to the reference level order. Borel-Cantelli then gives only finitely many inversions, so an existing ranking permutation differs from the identity on finitely many labels. Merely making high-level inversion probabilities tend to zero is insufficient. Independently swap the two labels in block {2j-1,2j} with probability1/j for j>=2. This defines a permutation with displacement at most1 and marginal displacement probability tending to zero, yet it has infinitely many swaps almost surely. Check: The independent second Borel-Cantelli lemma applies because sum1/j diverges. Each realized transposition is confined to a disjoint two-label block, so the example is a valid permutation rather than an ordering of an unbounded collection without a first element. Obstruction: The toy permutation is not a KPZ counterexample. The missing source-specific estimate is a summable bound on deep-level inversions, together with existence of the infinite ranking. Bounded displacement alone cannot answer the finitary part, as the explicit example shows.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0285-finitary-ordering-permutation-of-a-kpz-line-ensemble-vertical-slice
No independent review

[Prop uniconv of arXiv:2510.23430, 'On the Martin boundary for discrete TASEP'] Let $n\geq 0$, $r\in (0,1)$. Then the series
$$
\sum_{\lambda\in\mathbb{G}^p_k}c_\lambda \frac{G_\lambda^{(0,-p)}(z_1, \dots, z_n)}{G_\lambda^{(0,-p)}(1^n)}
$$
converges uniformly as a function of complex variables $\{c_\lambda\}_{\lambda}$, $z_1,\dots, z_n$ satisfying $|c_\lambda|\leq 1$, $|z_i|\leq r$ for all $\lambda, i$. In particular, the series is analytic in $z_1,\dots, z_k$ on the open unit disk for fixed $\{c_\lambda\}_\lambda$ satisfying $|c_\lambda|\leq 1$ for all $\lambda$.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:b2c90ee64b816e452de510ff36819edf601e14cdd0f48148155bb800aace4196","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/b2/b2c90ee64b816e452de510ff36819edf601e14cdd0f48148155bb800aace4196.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:f5b457bacd54fce17fd19ddf9b71b96d23b44bcdc8102cf320baf07a411545cd","bundle_entry_key":"t250_w712_c023","bundle_id":"population.w712-t250-c023-squared-activation-prior-clt","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"probability and neural networks","draft":"w712/bundle_017.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.neural_networks:squared-activation-fixed-depth-wasserstein-two-literature-corollary","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C023 v1: Target 3 is covered by a prior covariance-moment theorem

Kind: literature. Target: 3. Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty is claimed.

## Precise model and conclusion
Fix a positive hidden depth L, input dimension d, output dimension k, and nonzero deterministic x in R^d. All L hidden widths equal n. Use independent centered Gaussian weights of variance 1/(input width) in each affine layer, zero biases, and activation sigma(t)=t^2. The output is the final preactivation vector in R^k, not its coordinatewise square. All of L,d,k,x are fixed as n varies.

Let K_1=||x||^2/d and K_(ell+1)=3 K_ell^2 for ell=1,...,L. Let K=K_(L+1)>0. There exists a finite constant C depending on the fixed model parameters such that, for every n>=1,

W_2(Law(z^(L+1)(x)), N(0,K I_k)) <= sqrt(k*(C+C^2)/K) n^(-1/2).

This is a corollary of existing literature. It establishes the named one-activation, fixed-depth version of Target 3. It does not establish the general Tensor Program theorem, length-polynomial constants, or a claim of new research. For sigma(t)=t^2 the kernel grows rapidly with L, so this model does not address Target 1 stability.

## Primary source and hypothesis matching
Favaro, Hanin, Marinucci, Nourdin, Peccati, Quantitative CLTs in Deep Neural Networks, arXiv:2307.06092v5 (17 June 2024). Primary PDF papers/favaro_2307.06092v5.pdf; DOI of later journal version 10.1007/s00440-025-01360-1. The argument below uses the arXiv v5 statements, not an assumed identity with the journal text.

Definition 2.1: take r=1 and sigma(t)=t^2, which is smooth with polynomially bounded derivative. Remark 2.2 ensures the mixed conditional-covariance derivatives required there are well defined for a smooth activation. Assumption 3.1 (PDF p.10): C_b=0, C_W=1, c_1=c_2=1. The input is nonzero and fixed. Take one input and no derivative operators (all multi-indices have order zero).

Theorem 5.1, PDF pp.23-24, equation (5.1), is explicitly attributed there to Theorem 3.1, Corollary 3.4 and equation (11.31) of reference [41]. It supplies for the last conditional variance Sigma=Sigma^(L)_(alpha,alpha):

Var(Sigma)<=C/n and |E Sigma-K|<=C/n.

Enlarge C to cover the two constants if necessary. The smooth-activation alternative in Theorem 5.1 suffices; no derivative covariance nondegeneracy is asserted or required in this use. The population scalar kernel is positive at every layer by the displayed recursion.

Lemma 2.5, PDF p.9, equation (2.8): conditional on the previous layers the k output coordinates are independent centered Gaussians with common variance Sigma. In particular Sigma>=0. These two cited facts are the entire nontrivial stochastic input. We do not reprove the source's covariance moment theorem.

## Explicit corollary calculation
On an auxiliary probability space take Z~N(0,I_k) independent of Sigma. Then sqrt(Sigma) Z has exactly the network output law by Lemma 2.5. Couple it with sqrt(K) Z, whose law is the claimed infinite-width Gaussian. The squared coupling cost is

k E(sqrt(Sigma)-sqrt(K))^2
= k E[(Sigma-K)^2/(sqrt(Sigma)+sqrt(K))^2]
<= (k/K) E(Sigma-K)^2
= (k/K) [Var(Sigma)+(E Sigma-K)^2]
<= (k/K) [C/n+C^2/n^2]
<= k(C+C^2)/(K n).

Take a square root and the infimum over all couplings. This argument never transports through the non-Lipschitz map and never factors dependent layer errors.

## Related source bounds and metric distinction
Theorem 3.3, PDF p.11, gives O(n^(-1)) for W_1 and total variation of a scalar output with order-zero nondegeneracy; Definition 2.4 reduces that condition on a singleton to positivity of every scalar K_ell. This also applies to the squared model. It is not an O(n^(-1)) W_2 statement. Theorem 3.6's n^(-1/2) multivariate convex-distance bound is also not a W_2 statement. The W_2 conclusion above instead uses Theorem 5.1 and Lemma 2.5 directly.

## Review focus
Check the absolute bias term in equation (5.1), the smooth-activation alternative, and the k-coordinate conditional Gaussian representation. This is an author source check and corollary, not an independent audit. [Proposition prop:HigherOrderSphereIntr of arXiv:2507.08692, 'Some notes on higher order concentration of measure'] Let $f \colon {\mathbb S}^{n-1} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a $\mathcal{C}^2$-smooth function with ${\mathbb E} f =0$.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item Assuming $\lVert \nabla_S f \rVert_{\mathrm{HS},2} \le 1/\sqrt{n-1}$ and $\lVert f''_S \rVert_{\mathrm{op},\infty} \le 1$, we have
		\[
		\int_{{\mathbb S}^{n-1}} \exp\Big(\frac{n-1}{32e} |f|\Big) d\nu_n \le 2.
		\]
		\item For $C = 16e^2/\log(2)$ and any $t \ge 0$,
		\[
		\nu_n(|f-\nu_n(f)| \ge t) \le 2 \exp\Big(-\frac{n-1}{C}\min\Big(\frac{t^2}{\lVert \nabla_S f \rVert_{\mathrm{HS},2}^2}, \frac{t}{\lVert f_S'' \rVert_{\mathrm{op},\infty}}\Big)\Big).
		\]
		\item If ${\mathbb E} \nabla_S f = 0$, the bounds in (1) and (2) continue to hold with $\lVert \nabla_S f \rVert_{\mathrm{HS},2}^2$ replaced by $\lVert f_S'' \rVert_{\mathrm{HS},2}^2/(n+2)$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:HigherOrderSphereIntr of arXiv:2507.08692

 	\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\mathbf{E}\Big[\big|X(t)\big|^{p}\Big]<\infty

 	\int_0^T ds \int_0^\infty \big|f(s)\big|^{2p}ds <\infty.

 	Then there exists a constant $C>0$ depending only on $p$ such that
 	\begin{eqnarray} 
 	\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\mathbf{E}\Big[ \big| \widetilde{N}_1(f,t) \big|^{2p}  \Big] 
 	
 	\!\!\!&\leq\!\!\!& C  \cdot \sup_{t\in[0,T]}\mathbf{E} \Big[\big|X(t)\big|^p \Big] \cdot \Bigg| \int_0^T  \int_0^\infty\big|f(s,y)\big|^{2} \nu_1(dy)  ds\Bigg|^{p} \cr

body:
[Lemma lem:definetti-identities of arXiv:2606.25976, 'Gaussian rigidity for infinite exchangeable sequences'] Let \((X_i)_{i\ge1}\) be an exchangeable sequence of \(\mathbb{R}^d\)-valued random vectors with de Finetti directing measure \(\eta\).  For every Borel function \(\phi:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb C\) such that \(\mathbb{E}|\phi(X_1)|<\infty\),
\[
        \mathbb{E}[\phi(X_1)\mid\eta]
        =\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\phi(x)\eta(\,\mathrm{d} x)
        \qquad\text{a.s.}
\]
In particular,
\[
        \mathbb{E}\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\phi(x)\eta(\,\mathrm{d} x)=\mathbb{E}\phi(X_1)
\]
Moreover, for Borel functions \(\phi,\psi:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb C\) such that \(\mathbb{E}|\phi(X_1)\psi(X_2)|<\infty\),
\[
        \mathbb{E}\bigl[\phi(X_1)\psi(X_2)\mid\eta\bigr]
        =\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\phi(x)\eta(\,\mathrm{d} x)\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\psi(y)\eta(\,\mathrm{d} y)
        \qquad\text{a.s.}
\]

body:
[Defi 9 of arXiv:2511.10535, 'Eigenvalues of Brownian Motions on $\mathrm{GL}(N,\mathbb{C})$'] Let $\bs{a} = (a_1,\ldots ,a_d)$ be a $d$-tuple of non-commutative random variables in some $W^\ast$-probability space $(\A,\tau)$. The {\bf $\ast$-distribution} of $\bs{a}$ is the linear functional $\mu_{\bs{a}}\colon\PP_{2d}\to\C$ given by $P \mapsto \tau\left[ P(\bs{a}, \bs{a}^\ast) \right]$.

If $(\A_N,\tau_N)$ is a sequence of $W^\ast$-probability spaces for $N\ge 1$, and $\bs{a}_N \in\A_N$ are $d$-tuples, we say $\bs{a}_N$ {\bf converges in $\ast$-distribution to $\bs{a}$} if the $\ast$-distributions $\mu_{\bs{a}_N}$ converges pointwise to $\mu_{\bs{a}}$; i.e.\ if, for all $P\in\PP_{2d}$
\[ \lim_{N\to\infty} \tau_N[P(\bs{a}_N,\bs{a}_N^\ast)] = \tau[P(\bs{a},\bs{a}^\ast)]. \]
We say that $\bs{a}_N$ {\bf converges strongly to $\bs{a}$} if, in addition to converging in $\ast$-distribution, also
\[ \lim_{N\to\infty} \|P(\bs{a}_N,\bs{a}_N^\ast)\| = \|P(\bs{a},\bs{a}^\ast)\|. \]
title: Definition 9 of arXiv:2511.10535

[Defi 20 of arXiv:2608.06576, 'The Resultant Distribution Method: Universality for $p$-adic Random Matrices and Polynomia'] We denote by
$$
\Y
=
\left\{
\lambda=(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\ldots):
\lambda_1\geq\lambda_2\geq\cdots\geq 0,\ 
\lambda_i\in\Z,\ 
\lambda_i=0\text{ for all but finitely many }i
\right\}
$$
the set of integer partitions. The positive integers $\lambda_i$ are called
the \emph{parts} of $\lambda$. For $\lambda\in\Y$, we write
$$
|\lambda|
:=
\sum_{j\geq 1}\lambda_j,
\qquad
\ell(\lambda)
:=
\#\{j:\lambda_j>0\}.
$$
We refer to $\lambda_1$ as the \emph{largest part} of $\lambda$, with the
convention that $\lambda_1=0$ for the zero partition.

body: [Proposition 2.5 ([BT17], Lemma 2.3) of arXiv:2512.05720, 'First-passage percolation, non-positive curvature, and radial maps'] Let X be a connected graph, and let γ be a self avoiding path. Assume 0 < b = Eωe < ∞. Then for a.e. ω, there exists r0 = r0(ω) such that for all i ≤0 ≤j, |γ([i, j])|ω ≤2b(j −i) + r0.

body:
[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2609.03750, '\bf Pullback Measure Attractors, Zero-Noise Limits, and Moderate Deviations for 2D Stochas'] Suppose Hypotheses \ref{PEeqAssum-2.2} and \ref{PEeqAssum-2.3} hold. Let $\zeta$ be an $\mathscr F_\tau$-measurable, $\mathcal H$-valued random variable such that
$\mathbb E\left[|\zeta|^4+|\partial_z\zeta|^4\right]<\infty$, and assume that
$g,\partial_zg\in L^4([\tau,\tau+T];H)$.
Then problem \eqref{PEeq-2.15} admits a unique global solution $v$ in the sense of Definition  \ref{PEeqDef-2.4}.
 Furthermore,  
 there exist $\epsilon_0\in (0,1)$ and a positive constant $C:=C(T,\|g\|_{L^4([\tau,{\tau+T}];H)},\|\partial_{z}g\|_{L^4([\tau,{\tau+T}];H)})$ such that for every $\epsilon\in (0,\epsilon_0)$,
\begin{align}
	\mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{\tau\leq t\leq \tau+T}|v(t)|^{2p}+\left(\int^{\tau+T}_{\tau}\|v(t)\|^{2}dt\right)^{p}\right]\leq C\left(1+\mathbb{E}\left[|\zeta|^{2p}\right]\right),
\end{align}
and
\begin{eqnarray}
	\mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{\tau\leq t\leq \tau+T}|\partial_zv(t)|^{2p}+\left(\int^{\tau+T}_{\tau}\|\partial_zv(t)\|^{2}dt\right)^{p}\right]\leq C\left(1+\mathbb{E}\left[|\partial_z\zeta|^{2p}\right]\right),
\end{eqnarray}	
where $p\in \{1,2\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 6 of arXiv:2609.03750

body:
[Defn 7 of arXiv:2606.29132, '\bf Local Well-posedness of General Mean Field Game Master Equations'] Given $\cL_{\xi_1} = \mu_1\in \cP_2(\dbR^{d_1})$ and $x_0\in \dbR^{d_0}$, we say $(\a^*, \bm^*)\in \cA\times \cM$ is a mean field equilibrium (MFE) of MFGM \reff{MFGM-X}-\reff{MFGM-J}-\reff{MFGM-Xxi} at $(0,x_0, \mu_1)$ if

(i) Given $\bm^*$, $\a^{0*}$ is optimal for the major player:
\bea

J_0(\bm^*;  x_0, \a^{0*}) = \inf_{\a^0\in \cA_0} J_0(\bm^*;  x_0, \a^{0}).
\eea

(ii) Given $(\bm^*,\a^{0*})$, $\a^{1*}$ is optimal for the representative minor player:
\bea

J_1(\bm^*;  x_0, x_1, \a^{0*}, \a^{1*}) = \inf_{\a^1\in \cA_1} J_1(\bm^*;  x_0, x_1, \a^{0*}, \a^1),\q \mbox{for $\mu_1$-a.e. $x_1\in \dbR^{d_1}$}.
\eea

(iii) Given $\a^*$, $\bm^*$ is the conditional law of the minor's population:
\bea

\cL_{X^{\bm^*,1, x_0, \xi_1, \a^*}_t|\cF^{X^{\bm^*,0, x_0, \a^{0*}}_t}} = \bm^*_t(X^{\bm^*, 0, x_0, \a^{0*}}),~ 0\le t\le T,~\mbox{ a.s.}
\eea
title: Definition 7 of arXiv:2606.29132

body: [Defn 34 of arXiv:2608.26068, 'All once-extended 3D TQFTs are Reshetikhin--Turaev theories'] Let $\Gamma = (V,E,L)$ be a ribbon graph, and $T = (V_T,E_T,\emptyset)$ be a ribbon subgraph whose underlying graph is a tree. The \emph{contraction} $\Gamma/T = (V/V_T,E\setminus E_T,L)$ is the ribbon graph with the cyclic order at the vertex $V_T/V_T$ induced by the cyclic order of the edges incident at the disc $|T|$.
title: Definition 34 of arXiv:2608.26068

[Theorem thm: skewBM meeting of arXiv:2411.04773, 'Meeting of squared Bessel flow lines and application to the skew Brownian motion'] Set $\delta= \frac{1-|\beta|}{|\beta|}$ and $\widehat{\delta}=\frac{1-\beta_0}{\beta_0}$.
    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item   Suppose that  $\beta\in (0,1)$ and $\widehat{\delta}<\delta+2$.  The process $(\widehat L_{T(r)} ,\, r\ge 0)$ is distributed as the process $(U(r),\, r\ge 0)$ of Theorem (thm: main left of the paper). 
\item Suppose that $\beta\in (0,1)$ and $\delta<\widehat{\delta}+2$. The process $(\widehat L_{T(-r)}, r\ge 0)$ is distributed as the process $(U(-r),\, r\ge 0)$ of Theorem (thm: main right of the paper) with $\delta'=2+\delta$ there. 
\item Suppose that $\beta\in (-1,0)$. The  process $(\widehat L_{T(r)},\,r\ge 0)$ is distributed as the process $(-V(-r),\, r\ge 0)$ of Theorem (thm: main dual of the paper) with   $2+\delta$ in place of $\delta$ there. 
 \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lem 22 of arXiv:2605.07050, 'Universality of the fluctuations of the free energy in generalized Sherrington--Kirkpatric'] Assume that $\caX$ is not a Rademacher prior. Fix an ($N$-independent) constant $s$. Then, for any multicycle $\gamma$ with $n^\gamma<s$,
\begin{itemize}
	\item if all nodes of $\gamma$ are with degree $2$, then $Y(\gamma) \leq 1$ and $1- Y(\gamma) = o(1)$, and
	\item if at least one node of $\gamma$ is with degree $4$ or higher, then $Y(\gamma) > 1$ for any sufficiently large $N$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
STATUS: proof (unaudited). For a width-n Gaussian-row ReLU correlation transition with delta=1-rho in (0,delta0], a relative-Gram good-event self-loop regularization admits delta_star=d+e-d*w-e*w+d*w^2-(1-d)*H^2/2+R with ||R||_p<=C_p*delta*n^(-3/2) for every fixed p>=2. Thus a sufficient defect exponent is a=1. Here S=avg(x^2+y^2)=1+w, D=avg((x-y)^2)=d+e, H=avg(x^2-y^2), d=1-kappa(rho). The regularization fails with probability O(exp(-cn)) uniformly in delta. Exact row moment coefficients give mean(delta_star-d)=beta/n+O(delta*n^-3/2), second moment=sigma2/n+O(delta^2*n^-3/2), with beta=2delta+O(delta^3/2), sigma2=8delta^2+O(delta^5/2). Full row definitions: x=a_+, y=(rho*a+sqrt(1-rho^2)*g)_+ for independent standard Gaussians. kappa=(sin(theta)+(pi-theta)*cos(theta))/pi with rho=cos(theta). beta=-Cov(r,s)+d Var(s)-(1-d)E h^2/2 and sigma2=E(r-d*s)^2, r=(x-y)^2,s=x^2+y^2,h=x^2-y^2. Fixed sufficiently small delta0>0 and eta>0. Preactivation rows iid jointly standard Gaussian with correlation rho. Regularizer uses E_n={|w|<=eta,|e|<=eta*d,|H|<=eta*sqrt(d)}, otherwise self-loop. Constants independent of delta,n at fixed p,delta0,eta. No raw inverse-angle moments or Gaussian independence of Gram entries. Sufficient exponent a=1, not claimed optimal. A regularized-kernel statement, not finite raw inverse-angle integrability.

Constants independent of delta,n at fixed p,delta0,eta. No raw inverse-angle moments or Gaussian independence of Gram entries.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:b7d57f736a6f68e8d6fbeaa86cf45fdcebb3d98dd5f2bc62512820f84551e546","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/b7/b7d57f736a6f68e8d6fbeaa86cf45fdcebb3d98dd5f2bc62512820f84551e546.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:8274a16de42033e0f2011357542e34317ff1a1faf1e4dda639cad33f019bd3be","bundle_entry_key":"relu-defect-weighted-gram-remainder","bundle_id":"population.t244-defect-weighted-gram-remainder-008","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; random neural networks; sample correlation","draft":"w691/bundle_008.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.randomnetworks:gaussian-relu-correlation-defect-weighted-gram-taylor-remainder","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C020: a defect-weighted correlation remainder, exponent a=1

Version 1. Target 1, proof (unaudited). This is a different derivation of the missing network estimate, using a scale-normalized Gaussian-row Gram expansion. It does not use the printed paper's absolute remainder. The outputs are not an untruncated Wishart matrix after ReLU: only the preactivation rows are Gaussian. The coordinate moment bounds below account for the ReLU explicitly.

Fix 0<delta=1-rho<=delta0<1, rho=cos(theta). Let a_i,g_i be iid independent standard normals, b_i=rho*a_i+sqrt(1-rho^2)*g_i, x_i=(a_i)_+, y_i=(b_i)_+. Define single-row variables

    s_i=x_i^2+y_i^2, h_i=x_i^2-y_i^2, r_i=(x_i-y_i)^2.

Let S=average(s_i)=1+w, H=average(h_i), D=average(r_i)=d+e, where

    kappa=(sin(theta)+(pi-theta)*cos(theta))/pi,
    d=1-kappa=E r_i, E s_i=1, E h_i=0.

For fixed sufficiently small eta>0 define

    E_n={|w|<=eta, |e|<=eta*d, |H|<=eta*sqrt(d)}.

Use the exact correlation transition on E_n and self-loop in delta off E_n. Write its defect as delta_star. This regularization is essential for later reciprocal moments; no such moments are asserted for the exact kernel.

For every fixed p>=2 there are finite constants C_p,c>0, independent of n and delta in the stated interval, such that

    P(E_n^c)<=C exp(-cn),
    delta_star = d+e-d*w-e*w+d*w^2-(1-d)*H^2/2 + R,
    ||R||_p <= C_p delta*n^-3/2.                     (1)

The exponent in the requested correlation-dependent stochastic remainder is therefore a=1. This is a second-order polynomial expansion in the actual correlated Gram fluctuations, not a claim that those fluctuations are exactly Gaussian or independent.

## Uniform row moments and the good event

Put z_i=(a_i-b_i)/sqrt(2delta), which is standard normal, possibly correlated with a_i,b_i. The pointwise Lipschitz inequality for ReLU yields

    0<=r_i/delta<=2 z_i^2,
    |h_i|/sqrt(delta)<=sqrt(2)|z_i|(|a_i|+|b_i|).

The Gaussian square and product bounds give exponential moments near zero uniformly in rho for r_i/delta, h_i/sqrt(delta), and s_i. No independence within a row is used: for example Cauchy-Schwarz/Young bounds products by Gaussian squares. Rows are independent. Also d/delta is bounded above and below by positive constants on (0,delta0]. The iid centered-sum moment inequality consequently gives, for every fixed p,

    ||w||_p<=C_p n^-1/2,
    ||e||_p<=C_p delta*n^-1/2,
    ||H||_p<=C_p sqrt(delta)*n^-1/2.                (2)

For completeness, for even integer p=2m one can expand the centered sum: only index patterns in which every index appears at least twice survive, so there are at most m distinct indices, giving n^-m after normalization. General fixed p follows by increasing to an even integer. A Chernoff bound for the same uniformly exponentially integrable normalized rows gives the displayed exponential failure probability for E_n. This does not treat the row products as independent coordinates.

## Algebra of the defect and the Taylor remainder

The two squared norms are S+H and S-H, while the cross Gram entry (in the same normalization) is S-D. Thus on E_n

    delta_next=1-(S-D)/sqrt(S^2-H^2)
      =D/S+(D/S-1)*[(1-H^2/S^2)^(-1/2)-1].        (3)

Choose eta and delta0 sufficiently small that |H|/S<=1/2. Taylor expansion of the two scalar denominators gives the polynomial in (1). Its omitted terms on E_n are bounded by a constant times

    d|w|^3 + |e||w|^2 + H^2|w| + |e|H^2 + H^4.

Holder and (2), with sufficiently high moments, bound their Lp norms by C_p delta*n^-3/2. The H^4 term is O(delta^2/n^2) and is smaller. Off E_n, define R to make (1) an identity with delta_star=delta. Every polynomial term has fixed high-moment norm O(delta), so Holder and P(E_n^c)<=C exp(-cn) bound this contribution by C_p delta exp(-c_p n), absorbed in (1). This explains why an exponential deletion does not lose the defect factor.

The same small eta ensures c*d<=delta_next<=C*d on E_n. Indeed D is within a small relative error of d, and the subtraction in (3) is O(H^2)<=C eta^2 d. Thus delta_star/delta stays between two fixed positive constants. Extinction and zero angle are excluded on E_n, so this regularized chain couples to the exact killed chain up to O(nT exp(-cn)) before any additional stopping.

## Drift and noise coefficients

Define the exact row coefficients

    beta(delta)=-Cov(r_i,s_i)+d*Var(s_i)-(1-d)*E h_i^2/2,
    sigma2(delta)=E(r_i-d*s_i)^2.

Writing Delta=delta_star-d, (1)-(2) imply

    E Delta=beta(delta)/n+O(delta*n^-3/2),
    E Delta^2=sigma2(delta)/n+O(delta^2*n^-3/2),
    E|Delta|^3<=C delta^3*n^-3/2.                 (4)

The leading centered fluctuation is e-dw=average(r_i-d*s_i); its row mean is zero. The quadratic terms have Lp norm O(delta/n). Holder controls their covariance with the linear term; no independence of these terms is asserted.

These coefficients have the small-defect expansions

    d=delta-(2sqrt(2)/(3pi))*delta^(3/2)+O(delta^(5/2)),
    beta(delta)=2delta+O(delta^(3/2)),
    sigma2(delta)=8delta^2+O(delta^(5/2)).          (5)

Here is a checkable moment derivation. Set m31=E x^3*y and m22=E x^2*y^2. Gaussian polar integration gives

    m31=[(2+rho^2)sin(theta)+3rho(pi-theta)]/(2pi),
    m22=[(1+2rho^2)(pi-theta)+3rho sin(theta)]/(2pi).

For instance integrate the radial fourth moment E radius^4=8 and angular products cos(phi)^3 cos(phi-theta), respectively cos(phi)^2 cos(phi-theta)^2, over their common-positive interval phi in [theta-pi/2,pi/2], with angle density1/(2pi). These are elementary trigonometric integrals. In particular

    m31=3/2-(3/2)delta+O(delta^(5/2)),
    m22=3/2-2delta+delta^2+O(delta^(5/2)).

Since E x^4=E y^4=3/2,

    beta=4m31-kappa*(9/2+m22),
    sigma2=(3-8m31+6m22)
             -2d*(3-4m31+2m22)+d^2*(3+2m22).

Substitution proves (5). In particular beta/(2d)->1 and sigma2/(8d^2)->1, each with O(sqrt(delta)) error. This is the cancellation needed when transforming to the angle, and fixes the +2delta/n finite-width drift without assuming a sign from the source paper.

Scaling consequence: on any positive-time compact where q=l^2 delta stays bounded and l is proportional to n, the stochastic remainder l^2 R is O_Lp(q n^-3/2). Its accumulated first absolute moment over O(n) steps is O(n^-1/2). That closes the absolute-remainder rescaling obstruction on these stopped compacts. It does not alone establish the initial entrance or compact containment; those are addressed separately in C021.

Hardest remaining verification: the uniform weighted Taylor estimates and their reciprocal transformation must pass independent review. No numerical evidence is used in (1)-(5).","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:1c39785266e925042f74ca3720fade4db9078f54af6fc2eb4915b9fdf5181407","revision_digest":"sha256:3bc1691470641a8051ef822764149851721a49e8e743f513cd4426f2efb12ccd","source_id":"own-work:T244-w691-C020:v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20-v1","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Theorem thm:rad-non-convex of arXiv:2606.14687, 'Lehner's operator norm formulas, semidefinite programming, and spiked matrix models'] There exist $\bm A_0, \bm A_1, \dots, \bm A_n \in \mathbb{C}^{d \times d}_{\mathsf{herm}}$ such that the function $F: \{\bm Z \in \mathbb{C}^{d \times d}_{\mathsf{herm}}: \bm Z \succ \bm 0\} \to \mathbb{R}$ defined by
    \[ F(\bm Z) \colonequals \lambda_{\max}\left(\bm Z + \bm A_0 + \sum_{i = 1}^n \frac{1}{2}\bm Z^{1/2}((\bm I_d + 4(\bm Z^{-1/2}\bm A_i \bm Z^{-1/2})^2)^{1/2} - \bm I_d)\bm Z^{1/2}\right), \]
    the objective function of the optimization (equation eq:lehner-rad of the paper), is not convex.
    These may further be chosen to satisfy $\bm A_i \succ \bm 0$ for all $i = 0, 1, \dots, n$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Non-convexity of Lehner's Rademacher objective

[Definition eq:localized-defect-count of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[definition]{def:localization-defect}
Set
\begin{align}
 \mathscr L_{N,L}^J(V)
 &:=
 \mathbb E\sum_{\substack{x:\nabla_SH_N^J(\sqrt N x)=0\\x\notin D_{N,L}}}
 e^{-NV(h_N^J(x))},\\
 \overline\Lambda_L^J(V)
 &:=
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathscr L_{N,L}^J(V),\qquad
 \underline\Lambda_L^J(V)
 :=
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathscr L_{N,L}^J(V).
 
\end{align}
We use \(\log0=-\infty\) and allow extended-real exponents.

[Definition 4 of arXiv:2605.30616, 'Brownian motion: the hyperbolic number setting'] Let $\mu=\mu_{1}+k\mu_{2}$ be a $\mathbb{H}$-valued measure on a
measurable space $\left(X,\sigma\left(X\right)\right)$. This $\mathbb{H}$-valued
measure $\mu$ is said to be a $\mathbb{H}$-valued probability, if

(i) $\mu_{1}+\mu_{2}$ and $\mu_{1}-\mu_{2}$ are non-negative measures
on $\left(X,\sigma\left(X\right)\right)$, and

(ii) $\mu\left(X\right)\in\left\{ 1,e_{+},e_{-}\right\} $, i.e.,
$\mu\left(X\right)=1$, or $\mu\left(X\right)=e_{+}$, or $\mu\left(X\right)=e_{-}$.

[Lemma 17 of arXiv:2604.13454, 'Invariant and periodic measures in classical spin systems on infinite lattices with highly'] Let $P$ and $Q$ be two probability measures on $\Omega_{Spin}$ and let $\mathcal{C}$ be the class of the finite-dimensional closed sets, that is to say, the sets of the form
		$$
		C=\left\{z\in C([0, \infty), \ell_\rho^{2}(\mathbb{Z}^+)); (z(t_1),\cdots,z(t_l))\in(q_m^{-1}\Gamma_1,\cdots,q_m^{-1}\Gamma_l) \right\}
		$$ 
		with  $l,m\geq 1$, $T>0$, $t_i\in[0,T]\bigcap \mathbb{Q}$, closed sets $\Gamma_j\subset \mathbb{R}^m$, for $j=1,\cdots,l$ and continuous linear functional $ q_m(x)=\left(x_1,x_2,\cdots,x_m,0_{i\in\mathbb{Z}^+\backslash \Lambda_m}\right)$ $:\ell_\rho^{2}(\mathbb{Z}^+)\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^m$. If $P(C)=Q(C)$ for every $C\in \mathcal{C}$, then $P=Q$.
