[Corfr cor:abstractdiffalgcriterianonhomog of arXiv:2606.06187, 'How to Study Reflected Brownian Motion in a Quadrant via Kernel Functional Equations?\\ \m'] Let $K=\mathbb{C}(z)$ with the usual derivation and the field automorphism~$\sigma$ defined by $\sigma (f) (z)=f(z+1)$.
Then the fixed field of $\sigma$ is $K^\sigma=\mathbb{C}$ and one can take $L$ to be the set of meromorphic functions on $\mathbb{C}$.
 Let $f\in L$ be a non-zero meromorphic function satisfying 
 $$f(z+1)= a(z)f(z) $$ 
 for some $a \in \mathbb{C}(z)$. 
 If $f$ is differentially algebraic over $\mathbb{C}(z)$, then there exist $N \in \mathbb{N}_0$,
 constants $c_0,\dots,c_N \in \mathbb{C}$, not all zero, and $h \in \mathbb{C}(z)$ such that
 \begin{equation}
   c_0 \frac{\partial a }{a}(z) +c_1 \partial \left(\frac{\partial a }{a}\right) (z) +\dots +c_N \partial^N\left( \frac{\partial a}{a}\right)(z)= h(z+1)-h(z).
 \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary cor:barycentric.interpolation.geodesic of arXiv:2604.22453, 'Adapted Wasserstein Barycenters of Gaussian Processes'] Let \(Q\in\mathscr Q(L_0,L_1)\), and define \(\hat{\mathbb{X}}_u=\mathbb{G}^{\hat a_u,\hat L_u}\) by (equation eq:two.point.interpolation of the paper).  Then, in the quotient \(\mathrm{FG}\),
\[
\mathcal{AW}_2(\mathbb{X}_0,\hat{\mathbb{X}}_u)=u\mathcal{AW}_2(\mathbb{X}_0,\mathbb{X}_1),
\qquad
\mathcal{AW}_2(\hat{\mathbb{X}}_u,\mathbb{X}_1)=(1-u)\mathcal{AW}_2(\mathbb{X}_0,\mathbb{X}_1).
\]
Consequently, \(u\mapsto[\hat{\mathbb{X}}_u]\) is a constant-speed minimizing geodesic from \([\mathbb{X}_0]\) to \([\mathbb{X}_1]\).

[Definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The partial transpose of a complex Wishart matrix $W$ of parameters $(dn,dm)$ is the matrix
$$\widetilde{W}=(id\otimes t)W$$
where $id$ is the identity of $M_d(\mathbb C)$, and $t$ is the transposition of $M_n(\mathbb C)$.

body: [Lemma 12 (Sub-Gaussian max, the $\sqrt{\log G}$ law) of arXiv:2608.25188, 'Transforms for LLM Quantization:\\ The Great Inversion and Format Co-Design'] Let $z_1,\dots,z_G$ be mean-zero sub-Gaussian with proxy variance $\tau^2$. Then $\E\max_k|z_k|\le \tau\sqrt{2\log(2G)}$, and $\Pr[\max_k|z_k|\ge t]\le 2G\exp(-t^2/2\tau^2)$. Consequently, if in addition the group's realized RMS satisfies $\sigma\ge c\,\tau$ for a constant $c>0$, then $\E[\mathrm{CF}]\le c^{-1}\sqrt{2\log(2G)}$, and $\mathrm{CF}\le c^{-1}\sqrt{2\log(2G/\delta)}$ with probability at least $1-\delta$; in either form $\mathrm{CF}=O(\sqrt{\log G})$, the logarithm natural.

[Definition 58 of arXiv:2607.18104, '2607.18104'] Let $(\eta_t)_{t \geq 0}$ be an ASEP on $\Z$ and $(\bar{\eta}^{\per}_t)_{t \geq 0}$ be an unwrapped periodic ASEP evolving  according to the $(\rho,\theta,1,N)$-reference frame basic coupling for some $\rho \in (0,1)$, $\theta \in \R$ and $N\in \N$. We set
\begin{equation}
\xi_t(x) := \begin{cases}
\one & \text{ if } \eta_t(x)=1 \text{ and } \bar{\eta}^{\per}_t(x)=1, \\
\zero & \text{ if } \eta_t(x)=0 \text{ and }\bar{\eta}^{\per}_t(x)=0, \\
\Aup & \text{ if } \eta_t(x)=1 \text{ and } \bar{\eta}^{\per}_t(x)=0, \\
\Bup & \text{ if } \eta_t(x)=0 \text{ and } \bar{\eta}^{\per}_t(x)=1, \\
\end{cases}
\end{equation} for all $x\in \Z$ and $t \geq 0$.
 We refer to $(\xi_t)_{t \geq 0}$ on the state space $\{\one,\zero,\Aup,\Bup\}^{\Z}$ as the \textbf{extended colored ASEP with reference frame $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{I}_{N}^{\rho}(\theta,\theta+1)}$}. 
 
 Note that in the same way, replacing the process $(\bar{\eta}^{\per}_t)_{t \geq 0}$ by a full-space ASEP $(\eta'_t)_{t \geq 0}$, we can couple two full space ASEPs under the $(\rho,\theta,1,N)$-reference frame basic coupling, i.e., we use the same Poisson clocks for all $(x,t) \in \mathcal{I}^{\rho}_N(\theta,\theta+1)$ in the two ASEPs, and independent Poisson clocks for all for all $(x,t) \notin \mathcal{I}^{\rho}_N(\theta,\theta+1)$. We refer to the resulting process as \textbf{full space extended colored ASEP under the $(\rho,\theta,1,N)$-reference frame basic coupling}.

The Green function is G(x)=sum_{n>=0} P_0(X_n=x) for full-space discrete-time uniform nearest-neighbor SRW, and the vacant-set law is P(K subset V^u)=exp(-u cap(K)) with escape-probability capacity. No comparison theorem to parking holes is asserted. Novelty: KNOWN capacity identities; UNCHECKED prior appearance of this exact asymptotic. Status: independently checked proof.

whether this precise mean-spacing asymptotic has previously been stated.
This is a comparison model, not a result about the parking process.

Let V^u be the vacant set of simple-random-walk random interlacements on
Z^4. The walk makes one uniform nearest-neighbor step at each integer time.
There is no killing or boundary. Write G(x)=sum_{n>=0} P_0(X_n=x),
g=G(0), h=exp(-u/g), and use graph distance |x|_1 for balls. For every
fixed a>0, as u tends to infinity,

    sum_{0<|x|_1<=floor(a h^(-1/4))}
      P(x in V^u | 0 in V^u)  --> (2/3) a^4.

In particular the Palm number of other vacant sites in this mean-spacing
ball stays bounded. This holds despite the divergence of G*G in dimension
four. No coupling or comparison to surviving parking holes is asserted.

## Primary normalization and identities

Sznitman defines this full-space discrete-time Green function in (1.5),
equilibrium mass by the probability of never returning in (1.6), and
capacity as its total mass in (1.7). Proposition 1.5 gives

    P(K subset V^u) = exp(-u cap(K)),
    cap({0})=1/g,   cap({0,x})=2/(g+G(x)).

The last formula also follows by solving the two equations for equilibrium
weights: symmetry makes both equal 1/(g+G(x)). Hence for x!=0,

    P(0,x in V^u)=h^2 exp(2 L G(x)/(g+G(x))),  L=log(1/h).

The full-space Green bound G(x)<=C/(1+|x|_1)^2 follows from
Lawler--Limic, Theorem 4.3.1, with norm equivalence. Also G(x)<g for
x!=0: G(x)/g is the probability of hitting 0 from x, and transience and
the maximum principle give a strict bound below one at every such x.

## Summation with uniform errors

Put f(x)=G(x)/(g+G(x)). For each fixed x!=0, 2f(x)<1. Choose a fixed
integer M large enough that 2f(x)<=1/4 for |x|_1>=M. For the finite set
0<|x|_1<M, the conditional probabilities are h^(1-2f(x)), and their sum
tends to zero.

In the region M<=|x|_1<L, each conditional probability is at most h^(3/4).
There are O(L^4) such sites, so this region contributes O(L^4 h^(3/4)),
which tends to zero. Floors and the finitely many small values of L do
not affect the limit.

For |x|_1>=L, the exponent obeys

    0<=2 L f(x)<=C/L.

Thus uniformly in this entire remaining region the conditional probability
is h(1+O(1/L)). Let R=floor(a h^(-1/4)). Since R/L tends to infinity,
the sum over L<=|x|_1<=R is

    h (|B_R|-O(L^4))(1+O(1/L)).

The graph-ball counting polynomial has leading coefficient 2^4/4!=2/3:
|B_R|=(2/3)R^4+O(R^3). Therefore h|B_R| tends to (2/3)a^4,
hL^4 tends to zero, and the claimed limit follows.

## Remaining transfer gap

C9 requires a bounded Palm cluster count for the actual surviving holes of
one fixed parking law. The interlacement calculation supplies a benchmark
only. Parking walks stop at holes, their trajectories depend on the
environment, and the surviving-hole field is not an interlacement vacant
set. Neither the capacity identity nor this asymptotic transfers without
a separate comparison theorem. That is the hardest missing step of this

[Theorem thm:exact-spectrum-flat-core of arXiv:2609.00399, 'Shannon's problem on the monotonicity of entropy and a Conjecture of Tao'] Fix $n\geq1$, $0\leq L<\infty$, $d\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}$,
$0<\kappa<\infty$, and $0\leq\delta<1$.  For each $j$, let $G_j$ be a
torsion-free abelian group, let $p_j$ be a finitely supported probability
mass function on $G_j$, and set
\begin{equation}
 q_j=p_j^{*n},
 \qquad f_j=p_j^{*(n+1)}.
\end{equation}
Assume the following.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There is a proper affine GAP datum $A_j$ in $G_j$ of rank
$d_{A,j}\geq1$, represented with positive integer half-sides by
\begin{align*}
 \mathcal A_j:=\operatorname{Im}(A_j)
 &=z^A_j+\left\{\sum_{s=1}^{d_{A,j}}t_sv^A_{s,j}:
 t_s\in\mathbb Z,\ |t_s|\leq N_{s,j}\right\},\\
 N_{1,j}&=\max_sN_{s,j}\longrightarrow\infty.
\end{align*}
There is also a jointly distributed pair $(U_j,Z_j)$ of $G_j$-valued random
variables.  The variable $U_j$ belongs to $\mathcal A_j$ almost surely, the
law of $U_j+Z_j$ has probability mass function $q_j$, and
\begin{equation}
 D\!\left(\mathcal L(U_j,Z_j)\middle\Vert
 u_{A_j}\otimes\mathcal L(Z_j)\right)\leq L.
\end{equation}
\item There is a proper affine GAP datum $B_j$ in $G_j$, of rank at most
$d$, and a probability mass function $h_j$ supported on
$\operatorname{Im}(B_j)$ such that
\begin{equation}
 d_{\mathrm{TV}}(h_j,q_j)\leq\delta,
 \qquad
 \|h_j\|_\infty\leq\frac{\kappa}{|B_j|}.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
Then there exist an index $j_\star$ and nonzero shifts $r_j\in G_j$, defined
for all $j\geq j_\star$, such that
\begin{equation}
 \limsup_{j\to\infty}d_{\mathrm{TV}}(f_j,\tau_{r_j}f_j)\leq3\delta.
\end{equation}
The modulus $3\delta$ is independent of $L,d,\kappa$.  No uniform bound in
these parameters is asserted for the starting index, the shifts, or the
convergence rate.  The parameter $d$ bounds only the ranks of $B_j$; no
uniform rank bound on the reference progressions $A_j$ is assumed. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:transport-cover-intro of arXiv:2609.00399, 'Shannon's problem on the monotonicity of entropy and a Conjecture of Tao'] For every $0<a<1$ and $0\leq L<\infty$, there is an integer $M=M(a,L)$
with the following property.  Let $G$ be a discrete abelian group.  Let $A$
be a proper affine generalized arithmetic progression datum of rank
$d\geq1$, with positive integer half-sides, whose image is
\[
 \mathcal A:=\operatorname{Im}(A)
 =z+\left\{\sum_{s=1}^dt_sv_s:
 t_s\in\mathbb Z,\ |t_s|\leq N_s\right\}\subseteq G,
 \qquad N_1=\max_sN_s.
\]
Let $V$ be uniform on $\mathcal A$.  Suppose that $(U,Z)$ is an arbitrary
jointly distributed pair of $G$-valued random variables with
$U\in\mathcal A$ almost surely.  Let $q$ be the finitely supported
probability mass function of $U+Z$, and assume
\begin{equation}
 D\!\left(\mathcal L(U,Z)\middle\Vert\mathcal L(V)\otimes\mathcal L(Z)\right)\leq L.
\end{equation}
Then the set
\[
 \Lambda_a(q):=\{\chi\in\widehat G:|\widehat q(\chi)|\geq a\}
\]
has characters $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_m\in\Lambda_a(q)$, with
$1\leq m\leq M$, such that every $\chi\in\Lambda_a(q)$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \left\|\arg_{\mathbb T}\chi(v_1)
 -\arg_{\mathbb T}\chi_j(v_1)\right\|_{\mathbb T}
 <\frac1{2N_1+1}
\end{equation}
for some $j$.  The number $M(a,L)$ is independent of the rank and side
lengths of the datum $A$, the support of $Z$, and the ambient group. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma prop:dyadic-stitching of arXiv:2608.25551, 'Beyond Optimal Rates in Stochastic Optimization: Trajectory-Adaptive Stopping Rules'] Let $\{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t \ge t_0-1}$ be a filtration. Let $\{X_t\}_{t \ge t_0}$ be adapted, and let $\{v_t\}_{t \ge t_0}$ be nonnegative and predictable. Define
\[
    \bar X_{t_0-1} \coloneqq 0,
    \qquad
    \bar X_t \coloneqq \sum_{s = t_0}^t X_s,
    \qquad
    V_{t_0-1} \coloneqq 0,
    \qquad
    V_t \coloneqq \sum_{s = t_0}^t v_s .
\]
Fix $\gamma \in \mathbb{R}$. Suppose that, for every $\lambda>0$ and every $t \ge t_0$,
\[
    \mathbb{E}\left[
        \exp\left(
            \lambda X_t - 2^\gamma \lambda^2 v_t
        \right)
        \,\middle|\,
        \mathcal{F}_{t-1}
    \right]
    \le 1 .
\]
For $t \ge t_0-1$, let
\[
    V_{t,\mathrm{eff}}\coloneqq\max\{V_t, 1\},
    \qquad
    m_t \coloneqq \left\lceil \log_2 V_{t,\mathrm{eff}}\right\rceil .
\]
Then, for every $\alpha \in (0,1)$,
\[
    \mathbb{P}\left(
        \forall t \ge t_0:\
        \bar X_t
        \le
        2^{(\gamma+3)/2}
        \sqrt{
            V_{t,\mathrm{eff}}
            \left(
                \log\frac{1}{\alpha}
                +
                \log\bigl((m_t+1)(m_t+2)\bigr)
            \right)
        }\,
    \right)
    \ge
    1-\alpha .
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Anytime-valid stitched sub-Gaussian bound

body:
This is a source-status clarification, not a proved meander scaling theorem. In the survey's Problem 6.3 the earlier conjecture asks for a correlated two-dimensional Brownian limit for a uniform-meander encoding walk, with correlation -cos(pi*gamma^2/4) and gamma satisfying central charge -4=25-6*(gamma/2+2/gamma)^2. An Update immediately after the problem instead says that the expected limit is central-charge -4 LQG decorated by two independent SLE_8 curves. For this gamma, 8 is not 16/gamma^2, so the standard Duplantier-Miller-Sheffield mating-of-trees theorem does not apply directly to justify the earlier correlation. The update cites Borga-Gwynne-Sun [BGS22]. Neither the old Brownian-limit conjecture nor the updated expected meander limit is asserted here as a theorem. Source: Mating of trees for random planar maps and Liouville quantum gravity: a survey, Problem 6.3 and Update, pp.55-56.

body:
[Definition def1 of arXiv:2605.01958, 'High-dimensional limits for reflected Brownian motion in the orthant'] Given $n\in{\mathbb N}$, $b\in{\mathbb R}$, $\sigma>0$, an $n\times n$ matrix $R$ and a probability measure $\nu$ on $(S^{(n)},{\mathcal S}^{(n)})$, an SRBM associated with the data $(n,b,\sigma,R,\nu)$ is an $\{{\mathcal F}_t\}$-adapted, $n$-dimensional process $X$ defined on some filtered probability space $(\mathnormal{\Omega},{\mathcal F},\{{\mathcal F}_t\},{\mathbb P})$ such that ${\mathbb P}$-a.s.,
\[
\text{$t\mapsto X(t)$ lies in $C({\mathbb R}_+,S^{(n)})$ and }
X=X_0+W+RL,
\]
and under ${\mathbb P}$,
\begin{itemize}
\item
$X_0$ has distribution $\nu$,
\item
$W$ is an $(n,b,\sigma)$-BM and, for each $i\in[n]$, $\{W_i(t)-bt,t\ge0\}$ is an $\{{\mathcal F}_t\}$-martingale,
\item
$L$ is an $n$-dimensional $\{{\mathcal F}_t\}$-adapted process such that ${\mathbb P}$-a.s.,
\begin{equation}
\text{$t\mapsto L_i(t)$ lies in $C_+({\mathbb R}_+,{\mathbb R}_+)$ and } \int_0^\infty X_i^n(t)dL_i^n(t)=0, \qquad i\in[n].
\end{equation}
\end{itemize}

body:
[Lemma LS of arXiv:2609.00324, 'Quantitative Stability for Fractional Yamabe minimizers'] Let $(M^n,[\hat h])$ be the conformal infinity of an asymptotically
hyperbolic manifold $(X^{n+1},g^+)$, and fix
$u_*\in\mathcal M_1$. Then there exist an open neighborhood $\mathcal U\subset K$ of $0$
and a smooth map
\begin{align*}
    F:\mathcal U\longrightarrow K^\perp
\end{align*}
such that $F(0)=0$ and $\nabla F(0)=0$, and the following properties hold.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item
    Let $q:\mathcal{U} \to \mathbb{R}$ be the function defined by $q(\phi) := I_\gamma [u_* + \phi + F(\phi)]$. Then, we have
    \begin{align*}
        \mathcal S
        :=
        \left\{ u_* + \phi + F(\phi): \phi \in \mathcal{U}
        \right\} \subset\mathcal{B},
    \end{align*}
    and
    \begin{align*}
    \nabla_{\mathcal B} I_\gamma
        [u_* + \phi + F(\phi)]
        &=
        \pi_K \nabla_{\mathcal B} I_\gamma
        [u_* + \phi + F(\phi)]\\
        &=
        \nabla q(\phi).
    \end{align*}
    Moreover, $q$ is real analytic.
    \item
    There exists $\delta>0$, depending on $u_*$, such that for every
    $u\in  \mathcal{B} (u_*,\delta)$, we have $\pi_K (u-u_*) \in \mathcal{U}$. Moreover, if $u\in \mathcal{B} (u_*,\delta)$ is a critical point of
    $I_\gamma$, then
    \begin{align*}
        u = u_* + \pi_K (u-u_*) + F(\pi_K (u-u_*)).
    \end{align*}
    \item
    Fix $\alpha\in(0,1)$ such that $2\gamma+\alpha\notin\mathbb N$, then there exists $C>0$ such that, for every
    $\phi\in\mathcal U$ and every $\psi\in K$,
    \begin{align*}
        \|\nabla F(\phi)[\psi]\|_{C^{2\gamma+\alpha}(M)}
        \leq
        C\|\psi\|_{C^\alpha(M)}.
    \end{align*}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

This draft is not a new frontier-rate advance. Owner campaign proof (unaudited), independent review pending. Let N_1,...,N_T be orthogonal task projections, P_i=I-N_i, Q=T^-1 sum_i N_i and Phi(Y)=T^-1 sum_i P_i Y P_i. Draw iid uniform labels i_1,...,i_k and set e_j=P_(i_j)e_(j-1). Assume Phi^l(Q)<=C Q for every l>=0, with C>=1. Then E[e_k^T Q e_k]<=C||e_0||^2/(k+1). The occurrence-weighted historical mean k^-1 sum_(j=1)^k E[e_k^T N_(i_j)e_k] is at most 2(C+1)||e_0||^2/k. The expected mean of e_k^T N_i e_k over distinct observed labels is at most [8(C+1)+1]||e_0||^2/k. All historical losses here omit the conventional factor 1/2. The quasi-domination premise remains open for general projector families.

[Proposition lem:differenceQuotientEOT of arXiv:2609.03094, 'Discrete Gromov--Wasserstein Duality: Algorithms and Isomorphism Testing'] Let $(\nu_0,\nu_1)\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X_0)\times \mathcal P(\mathcal X_1)$ be arbitrary and let $\mu_{i,t}\coloneqq \mu_i+t(\nu_i-\mu_i)$ for $t\in(0,1)$ with $i=0,1$. Then,  
  \[
 \begin{aligned}
    \lim_{t\downarrow 0}t^{-1}\left(\mathsf{EGW}_p^{\varepsilon}(\mu_{0,t},\mu_{1,t})-\mathsf{EGW}_p^{\varepsilon}(\mu_{0},\mu_{1})\right)& 
    \\
    &\hspace{-5em}= \inf_{\pi^{\star}\in \Pi^{\star}(\mu_0,\mu_1)}\left\{ \int \varphi_0^{\pi^{\star}}d(\nu_0-\mu_0)+\int \varphi_1^{\pi^{\star}}d(\nu_1-\mu_1)\right\}
    \\
    &\hspace{-5em}= \inf_{\pi^{\star}\in \Pi^{\star}(\mu_0,\mu_1)}\left\{  v_{\varphi_0^{\pi^{\star}}}^{\intercal}\left(w_{\nu_0}-w_{\mu_0}\right)+v_{\varphi_1^{\pi^{\star}}}^{\intercal}\left(w_{\nu_1}-w_{\mu_1}\right)\right\}
\end{aligned}
\]   
where $\Pi^{\star}(\mu_0,\mu_1)$ is the set of all optimal couplings for $\mathsf{EGW}_p^{\varepsilon}(\mu_{0},\mu_{1})$ and $(\varphi_0^{\pi^{\star}},\varphi_1^{\pi^{\star}})$ is the unique  (up to additive constants) pair of  EOT potentials for the EOT problem $\mathsf{EOT}^{\varepsilon}_{c_{\pi^{\star}}}(\mu_0,\mu_1)$ with cost function 
$
c_{\pi^{\star}}(x,y)=2\int \left|\kappa_0(x,x')-\kappa_1(y,y')\right|^pd\pi^{\star}(x',y').
$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let P be a finite poset and a,b distinct elements. Write D(x)={z:z<x} and U(x)={z:x<z}. The pair (a,b) is good if either in P or in its dual the following hold together: D(a) is a subset of D(b), U(b) minus U(a) is a chain (possibly empty), and the uniform linear-extension probability that a precedes b is at most 1/2. The probability condition is evaluated in the same chosen order, P or its dual. A good pair is necessarily incomparable, but that particular pair need not be 1/3-balanced.
P finite
a and b distinct

\]

We compute
\begin{align*}
\frac{d}{dt}\exp\left(-\sqrt{-1}tF_0+F_z\right)&=\underbrace{\exp\left(-\sqrt{-1}tF_0+F_z\right)}_{\eqqcolon E}(-\sqrt{-1}F_0) \\

&= -\frac{\sqrt{-1}}{2}[E(A-A^*),A-A^*]_s

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Try a fractional-moment (Aizenman-Molchanov) argument adapted to band matrices at fixed W in d = 2. Result: The fractional-moment method proves localisation when the expected s-th moment of the Green function E|G_{xy}(E + i eta)|^s decays exponentially in |x - y|; for band matrices at fixed W in d = 2 the required a priori bound is a decoupling of the moment across a band-width-sized block, which for the Anderson model comes from the rank-one structure of the diagonal disorder. Band matrices have no rank-one structure: the randomness at a site is a W^2-dimensional block, and the decoupling lemma degrades by a factor that grows with W^2, so the method proves localisation only for W <= W_0 small (large disorder regime), not for every fixed W. The conjectured localisation length exp(W^2) matches the expected scaling of the failure of the fractional-moment bound: the moment decays only after distances of order exp(cW^2), consistent with the conjecture but not proving it. A rigorous partial statement I can defend: for every fixed W there is a positive density of localised states at the spectral edges (Lifshitz-tail regime), by the standard edge-localisation argument, which does not touch the bulk. No bulk result. Obstruction: Fractional-moment decoupling loses a factor growing with W^2; no method reaches exp(W^2) localisation lengths.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0054-localisation-of-all-bulk-states-for-two-dimensional-random-band-matric
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

[Cor 3 of arXiv:2603.28702, 'Distribution of the magnetization of the critical Ising model on sparse random graphs'] For the continuous time Glauber dynamics where each vertex is updated at rate 1:
\begin{enumerate}
\item 
On the random $d$-regular graph graph with $\beta=\beta_c$, there exists some constant $c_0>0$ such that with probability $1-o(1)$, the mixing time of the Glauber dynamics satisfies $t_{mix}\ge c_0\sqrt{n}$.
\item 
On the random Erd\"os-R\'enyi random graph $G(n,d/n)$, at $\beta=\beta_c$, for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that $\mathbb{P}[t_{mix}\geq \delta\sqrt{n}]\geq 1-\varepsilon$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: In spectral graph theory, the Alon–Boppana bound provides a lower bound on the second-largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of a $d$ -regular graph, meaning a graph in which every vertex has degree $d$. The reason for the interest in the second-largest eigenvalue is that the largest eigenvalue is guaranteed to be $d$ due to $d$ -regularity, with the all-ones vector being the associated eigenvector. The graphs that come close to meeting this bound are Ramanujan graphs, which are examples of the best possible expander graphs.

[Lemma lem:dc of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] Suppose that $f \in \mathcal{C}\{M_k\}([0,b])$, and let $B,K \ge 0$ be the corresponding values such that
\[ \sup_{x\in[0,b]}\bigl|f^{(k)}(x)\bigr|\le B K^{k}\,M_k
\quad\forall\,k\ge0. \]
Let $m \ge 1$ be such that 
\[ f^{(k)}(0) = 0 \]
for all $1 \le k \le m$. Then for any $x \le (a_1 + \cdots + a_m)/8K$, 
the following inequality holds:
\[ |f(x)| \le [8B K/(a_1 + \cdots + a_m)] |x|. \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 41 of arXiv:2606.16164, 'A Low-Regularity Semigroup Sewing Lemma via Quotient Structures'] Let $S_t=e^{-t(1-\Delta)}$ on $H^\alpha(\T^d)$, and let $H\in Z\hC^{\gamma}(\Delta_T^3;B_\alpha)$ satisfy the parabolic residual tail condition of
Definition~\ref{def:parabolic-tail-condition}.  Assume also that the residual continuity criterion \eqref{eq:residual-continuity-criterion} holds for the heat spectral rule.  Then the heat spectral splitting produces a semigroup Sewing representative
\[
\hat\Lambda^{\mathsf{heat}}_{S,\gamma,\alpha}H:=R^{\mathsf s,\mathrm{heat}}(H).
\]
If $0<\gamma<1$, then on sufficiently short time intervals one has
\[
\hat\Lambda^{\mathsf{heat}}_{S,\gamma,\alpha}H\in C^{\gamma}(\Delta_T^2;B_\alpha), \quad\hdd\hat\Lambda^{\mathsf{heat}}_{S,\gamma,\alpha}H=H,
\]
and 
\[
\norm{\hat\Lambda^{\mathsf{heat}}_{S,\gamma,\alpha}H}_{\gamma,\alpha}\le C_T\bigl(\norm{H}_{\gamma,\alpha}+K\bigr).
\]
At the endpoint $\gamma=1$,
\[
\hat\Lambda^{\mathsf{heat}}_{S,1,\alpha}H\in C_{\log}^{1}(\Delta_T^2;B_\alpha), \quad\hdd\hat\Lambda^{\mathsf{heat}}_{S,1,\alpha}H=H,
\]
and
\[
\norm{\hat\Lambda^{\mathsf{heat}}_{S,1,\alpha}H}_{1,\log;\alpha}\le C_T\bigl(\norm{H}_{1,\alpha}+K\bigr).
\]
On any linear class where $K\le C\norm{H}_{\gamma,\alpha}$ and the residual continuity criterion holds uniformly, this construction defines a continuous linear Sewing map.

[Corollary 27 (Sharp pure-chaos constant) of arXiv:2608.12492, 'Weak Limits of Wiener Chaos: Primitive--Fock Classification and Hilbert--Stein Extraction'] Let $q\ge2$, $f=(f_a)_{a\le d}\subset H^{\odot q}$, and define
\[
 T_s(f)h=(f_a\otimes_sh)_{a\le d},
 \qquad
 \rho(f)=\max_{1\le s<q}\norm{T_s(f)}_{\op},
 \qquad
 E(f)=\sum_a\norm{f_a}^2.
\]
Then
\begin{align}
 &\sum_{a,b}
 \norm{\Gamma(I_q(f_a),I_q(f_b))-q!\ip{f_a}{f_b}}_2^2
 \le (q!)^2a_qE(f)\rho(f)^2.
 
\end{align}
The constant $(q!)^2a_q$ is optimal.

[Definition Type $\operatorname{I}$ and $\operatorname{II}$ curves of arXiv:2607.24640, 'The Yang-Mills measure on surfaces via Morse theory'] Let $\gamma$ be a $V$-oriented and primitive elementary curve. We say that $\gamma$ is of type $\operatorname{I}$ if $N(\gamma)=0$, i.e. $\gamma([0,1])\cap\cup_{ \mathrm{ind} (a)=1}W^u(a)=\emptyset$. Otherwise, we say that $\gamma$ is of type $\operatorname{II}$. 

For a curve $\gamma$ of type $\operatorname{II}$, we denote by $a(\gamma)$ the only saddle point of $f$ such that $\gamma(\{0,1\})\cap W^u(a(\gamma))\neq\emptyset$ and we say that it is of type $\operatorname{II}_\pm$ if there exists a sequence $(t_n)_{n\geq 1}$ in $(0,1)$ such that $\gamma(t_n)\in  W^u(a(\gamma))$ and such that, for $n$ large enough, the orbit of $\varphi_f^{-t}(\gamma(t_n))$ enters the region $\pm x_2\geq 0$ (in the Morse chart near $a(\gamma)$) for $t\geq 0$.
title: Type $\operatorname{I}$ and $\operatorname{II}$ curves

body: [Proposition 25 (Reverse water-filling \citep{cover2006elements}; high-rate allocation form as in \citet{goyal2001transform}) of arXiv:2608.25188, 'Transforms for LLM Quantization:\\ The Great Inversion and Format Co-Design'] Given transformed variances $\sigma_1^2,\dots,\sigma_d^2$, not all zero, and total rate $R>0$, the real rates $R_k\ge0$ minimizing $\sum_k\sigma_k^2 2^{-2R_k}$ subject to $\sum_k R_k=R$ are $R_k=\max\!\big(0,\tfrac12\log_2(\sigma_k^2/\theta)\big)$, where $\theta>0$ is the unique level solving $\sum_k\max\!\big(0,\tfrac12\log_2(\sigma_k^2/\theta)\big)=R$; coordinates with $\sigma_k^2\le\theta$ receive zero bits.

body:
[Theorem thm:projection-before-mgle-barycenter-final of arXiv:2604.22453, 'Adapted Wasserstein Barycenters of Gaussian Processes'] Let \(\mathbb{X}^k:=\mathbb{G}^{L^k}\in\mathcal{FG}(T,d)\)for each \(k\in[K]\), and set
\(
(\mathbb{X}^k)^{\mathrm{mgle}}:=\mathbb{G}^{(L^k)^{\mathrm{mgle}}}.
\)
Then
\begin{align}

&\inf_{\mathbb{Y}\in\mathcal{FG}_{\mathrm{mgle}}(T,d)}
\sum_{k=1}^K\lambda_k\mathcal{AW}_2^2(\mathbb{X}^k,\mathbb{Y})\notag\\
&\quad=
\sum_{k=1}^K\lambda_k\|L^k-(L^k)^{\mathrm{mgle}}\|_F^2
+
\inf_{\mathbb{Y}\in\mathcal{FG}_{\mathrm{mgle}}(T,d)}
\sum_{k=1}^K\lambda_k\mathcal{AW}_2^2((\mathbb{X}^k)^{\mathrm{mgle}},\mathbb{Y}).
\end{align}
Moreover, the two infima over \(\mathcal{FG}_{\mathrm{mgle}}(T,d)\) have exactly the same minimizers.
Applying Theorem~(thm:unrestricted-FG-mgle-barycenter-final of the paper) to the
projected martingale inputs, this becomes
\begin{align}

&\inf_{\mathbb{Y}\in\mathcal{FG}_{\mathrm{mgle}}(T,d)}
\sum_{k=1}^K\lambda_k\mathcal{AW}_2^2(\mathbb{X}^k,\mathbb{Y})\notag\\
&
\quad=
\sum_{k=1}^K\lambda_k\|L^k-(L^k)^{\mathrm{mgle}}\|_F^2
+
\inf_{\mathbb{Z}\in\mathrm{FP}_2}
\sum_{k=1}^K\lambda_k\mathcal{AW}_2^2((\mathbb{X}^k)^{\mathrm{mgle}},\mathbb{Z}).
\end{align}
Consequently, a martingale representative \(\mathbb{Y}\in\mathcal{FG}_{\mathrm{mgle}}(T,d)\) solves
(equation eq:constrained-mgle-barycenter-problem-final of the paper) if and only if \(\mathbb{Y}\) is an
unrestricted adapted barycenter representative of
\((\mathbb{X}^1)^{\mathrm{mgle}},\ldots,(\mathbb{X}^K)^{\mathrm{mgle}}\).

[Lemma l:xi-infty-BL of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Let  $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$  be a marked point process on $\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{K}$ with non-null, finite intensity $\rho$.  Let $\xi : \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K} \times \hat\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K}} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a marking function. 

\begin{enumerate}[wide,label=(\roman*),labelindent=0pt]
\item 
If $\xi$ is stabilizing (resp. fast stabilizing) on finite windows as in  Definition~(def.stabilizing_marking of the paper)(i.stabilizing-windows of the paper) (resp. ~(i.stabilizing-fast of the paper)) then $\xi$ is \textnormal{BL}-localizing (resp. fast \textnormal{BL}-localizing) on finite windows as in ~Definition~(def.Lp-stabilizing_marking of the paper)(i.BL-localizing-windows of the paper) (resp.~(i.BL-localizing-fast of the paper)). The same implications hold if $\xi$ is defined on the whole space $\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K} \times \mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K}}$, involving the stopping set Definition~(def.stabilizing_marking of the paper)(i.stabilizing of the paper) and the \textnormal{BL} \,stabilizing Definition~(def.Lp-stabilizing_marking of the paper) (i.BL-localizing of the paper).

\item 
If  $\xi$ is stabilizing (resp. fast stabilizing) on finite windows and if moreover 
$$
\tilde{\xi}_{\infty}(\tilde{x}_i,\tilde{\mathcal{P}}) := \lim_{n \to \infty} \xi(\tilde{x}_i,\tilde{\mathcal{P}}_n)
$$
exists,  $\mathbb{P}_{x_1,\ldots,x_p}$-a.s. for all $p \in \mathbb{N}$ and all $x_1,\ldots,x_p \in \mathbb{R}^d$ then $\tilde{\xi}_{\infty}$ is \textnormal{BL}-localizing  (resp. fast \textnormal{BL}-localizing) as in (equation Lp-stab-infinite of the paper).  
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 20 of arXiv:2609.04033, 'From configuration spaces to graph complexes via $\mathbf{FA}$-modules'] Let $\op{M}$ be a modular operad for which $\mathsf{Com}\subset \op{M}$.  For each $g$, the symmetric sequence $\op{M}(g,-)$ inherits the structure of an $\mathbf{FS}^{op}$-module; applying the cobar construction gives a sequence of subcomplexes
$$	
\mathsf{B}_{\mathbf{FS}}(\op{M}(g,-))\subset \mathsf{cFT}(\op{M})(g,-).
$$
Dually, $\op{M}(g,-)^\ast$ inherits the structure of an $\mathbf{FS}$-module; applying the cobar construction gives a sequence of quotient complexes
$$	
\mathsf{FT}(\op{M})(g,-) \twoheadrightarrow \Omega_{\mathbf{FS}}(\op{M}(g,-)^\ast).
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 20 of arXiv:2605.05864, 'Classification and Metrization of Classes of Smooth measures'] Assume that the Dirichlet form $(\form, \dom)$ is transient and $\mu\in {\cal S}$ and its potential $R\mu$ belongs to $L^\infty(E;m)$. 
Let $\{F_\ell\}$ be a (compact) nest attached to $\mu$, that is, $1_{F_\ell}\mu \in {\cal S}^{(0)}_0$ holds for each $\ell \in{\mathbb N}$.
Then for all compact sets $K\subset E$ and $\ell \in{\mathbb N}$, the following inequalities hold$:$
$$
\mu(K\cap F_\ell)  \le  \sqrt{{\rm Cap}_{(0)}(K)} \sqrt{\form(U(1_{K\cap F_\ell}\mu),U(1_{K\cap F_\ell}\mu))} 
$$
and
$$
\form(U(1_{K\cap F_\ell}\mu),U(1_{K\cap F_\ell}\mu)) \le \|R\mu\|_\infty \mu(K \cap F_\ell).
$$
In particular, we have$:$
$$
\mu(K) \le {\rm Cap}_{(0)}(K) \|R\mu\|_{\infty}<\infty.
$$
This implies that $\mu$ is a Radon measure. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 20 of arXiv:2605.05864

[Prop 11 of arXiv:2605.07050, 'Universality of the fluctuations of the free energy in generalized Sherrington--Kirkpatric'] Suppose that the random variables $\{ P^{(n)}_{ij} \}_{i<j}$ ($n=1, 2, 3, 4$) satisfy the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item For any $n$, $P^{(n)}_{ij}$ are i.i.d., and for any integer $s>2$, there exists a constant $C^P_s$ such that $\E[|P^{(n)}_{ij}|^s] \leq C^P_s$.
\item For any $n$, $\E[P^{(n)}_{ij}] = 0$ and $\E[(P^{(n)}_{ij})^2] = \cn_n$ for some ($N$-independent) constants $\cn_n$.
\item $\E[P^{(1)}_{ij} P^{(2)}_{ij}] = \E[P^{(2)}_{ij} P^{(3)}_{ij}] = \E[P^{(3)}_{ij} P^{(4)}_{ij}] = \E[P^{(1)}_{ij} P^{(4)}_{ij}] = 0$ and $\E[P^{(1)}_{ij} (P^{(2)}_{ij})^2] = 0$.
\end{itemize}
Similarly, we suppose that the random variables $\{ P^{(n)}_{d,kk} \}_{1\le k \le N}$ ($n=1, 2$) satisfy the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item For any $n$, $P^{(n)}_{d, kk}$ are i.i.d., and for any integer $s>2$, there exists a constant $C^P_{d, s}$ such that $\E[|P^{(n)}_{d, kk}|^s] \leq C^P_{d, s}$.
\item For any $n$, $\E[P^{(n)}_{d,kk}] = 0$ and $\E[(P^{(n)}_{d,kk})^2] = \cn'_n$ for some ($N$-independent) constants $\cn'_n$.
\item $\E[P^{(1)}_{d,kk} P^{(2)}_{d,kk}] = 0$.
\end{itemize}
In addition, we also assume that for any $n=1, 2, 3, 4$, $m=1, 2$, $i<j$ and $k$, $P^{(n)}_{ij}$ and $P^{(m)}_{d,kk}$ are independent.
Fix $\epsilon \in (0, 1/60)$ and let
\[
	\Omega_\caX^\epsilon := \{ \max_{1 \leq k \leq N} |x_k| \leq N^{-1/2 +\epsilon} \} \cap \{ | \| \bsx \| - 1 | \leq N^{-1/5} \}.
\]
Suppose that Assumption \ref{assump:second_moment} holds with $\SNR_c$. If $\F < \SNR_c$,
\beq \begin{split} 
	&\log \E_\caX \left[ \indi(\Omega_\caX^\epsilon) \prod_{i<j} \left( 1 + P^{(1)}_{ij} \sqrt{N} x_i x_j + P^{(2)}_{ij} N x_i^2 x_j^2 + P^{(3)}_{ij} N^{3/2} x_i^3 x_j^3 + P^{(4)}_{ij} N^2 x_i^4 x_j^4 \right) \right. \\
	&\qquad \qquad \left. \times \prod_{k=1}^N \left( 1 + P^{(1)}_{d,kk} \sqrt{N} x_k^2 + P^{(2)}_{d,kk} N x_k^4 \right) \right] \Rightarrow \caN(-\rho, 2\rho)
\end{split} \eeq
as $N \to \infty$, where
\[
	\rho:= -\frac{1}{4} \left( \log (1-\F) + (\F - 2 \F') + \frac{\F^2}{2} \right) + \frac{\G}{4}.
\]
Similarly, under the same assumption
\beq \begin{split} 
	&\log \E_\caX \left[ \indi(\Omega_\caX^\epsilon) \prod_{i<j} \left( 1 + P^{(1)}_{ij} \frac{\sqrt{N} x_i x_j}{\| \bsx \|^2} + P^{(2)}_{ij} \frac{N x_i^2 x_j^2}{\| \bsx \|^4} + P^{(3)}_{ij} \frac{N^{3/2} x_i^3 x_j^3}{\| \bsx \|^6} + P^{(4)}_{ij} \frac{N^2 x_i^4 x_j^4}{\| \bsx \|^8} \right) \right. \\

\end{split} \eeq
as $N \to \infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition 53 (Uniform selection pair) of arXiv:2511.09517, 'From Cannings model to Brownian motion conditioned on local time profile'] Fix a base height $h^*$. For $0\le h\le h^*$, $1\le p\le q_n(h^*)$ and $1\le k\le q_n(h)$, let $(A,\mathcal{V})$ be a pair consisting of
\begin{itemize}
    \item an event $A$ measurable with respect to $\mathcal{G}_{h}^{(p)}\vee \sigma(\Lambda_h)$, and
    \item a random vector $\mathcal{V}$ of $k$ vertices taking values in $\{x^{h}_1,\ldots, x^{h}_{q_n(h)}\}$.
\end{itemize}
We say that $(A,\mathcal{V})$ is a $(p,h,k)$-uniform selection pair if, under $\mathbb{P}_n$,
\[
(\mathcal{V}\mid A)\,\overset{d}{=}\,\{u^{h}_1,\ldots,u^{h}_k\},
\]
that is, conditionally on $A$, the vector $\mathcal{V}$ has the same distribution as a uniformly chosen $k$-tuple of distinct vertices at height $h$. When \(p=q_n(h^*)\), we abbreviate this as an \((h,k)\)-uniform selection pair.
title: Uniform selection pair

Start W_0=0 in Z^3. On the first departure from each vertex, change only the third coordinate by +1 or -1 with equal probabilities. On every subsequent departure from that vertex, change the first two coordinates by a uniformly chosen two-dimensional nearest-neighbor simple-random-walk step. Use fresh independent random choices at successive departures. Then ||W_n|| tends to infinity almost surely. After permuting coordinates, this is the M(1,2) nonoverlapping balanced excited random walk; it does not settle M(2,1) or recurrence of M(1,1). Source: Martingale defocusing and transience of a self-interacting random walk, Theorem 1.1, p.2; proof Section 3, especially eq.(3.2), pp.8-9.

[Theorem 66 of arXiv:2609.03070, 'Variants of order semicontinuity in Banach lattices'] Let $F$ be an AM-space. Then:
\item[(i)] $F$ is $\sigma$-semicontinuous if and only if it isometrically embeds as a $\sigma$-regular sublattice of $C\left(K\right)$, for some compact Hausdorff space $K$.
\item[(ii)] $F$ is $\sigma$-demicontinuous if and only if it isomorphically embeds as a $\sigma$-regular sublattice of $C\left(K\right)$, for some compact Hausdorff space $K$. In this case it is topologically $\sigma$-semicontinuous.

Let (X, B, mu) be a probability space and T : X -> X measure-preserving (invertibility is not assumed). Let P_1 <= P_2 <= ... be an increasing sequence of countable measurable partitions (each P_{k+1} refines P_k) with H_mu(P_k) < infinity for every k, and assume the sequence GENERATES: the sigma-algebra generated by the union of the P_k equals B up to mu-null sets. Then h_mu(T) = lim_k h_mu(T, P_k) = sup_k h_mu(T, P_k), where h_mu(T) is the supremum of h_mu(T,Q) over all finite-entropy partitions Q. The classical generator form is the special case: for an invertible T and a partition P with H_mu(P) < infinity whose two-sided join over all integer translates generates B, take P_k = the join of T^{-n}P over |n| <= k and conclude h_mu(T) = h_mu(T,P); for non-invertible T take the one-sided join over 0 <= n <= k. WHERE IT FAILS: (i) generation is the entire content. If the union of the P_k generates only a proper sub-sigma-algebra, the limit computes the entropy of the corresponding sub-process and can be strictly smaller than h_mu(T); with every P_k trivial the limit is 0 for a system of arbitrarily large entropy. In particular a partition that separates points topologically but only generates a smaller sigma-algebra modulo mu is not enough. (ii) Monotonicity of the sequence (or at least H_mu(Q | P_k) -> 0 for every finite-entropy Q) is used; an arbitrary sequence of partitions that 'converges' in some other sense need not have monotone entropies and the comparison step breaks. (iii) H_mu(P_k) < infinity is needed for the comparison inequality. (iv) Generation is modulo mu-null sets only, and the conclusion says nothing pointwise. (v) For non-invertible T the one-sided generator computes h_mu(T); using the two-sided join for a non-invertible map is meaningless.
(X,B,mu) is a probability space and T preserves mu
the partitions P_k are countable, measurable, and increasing: P_{k+1} refines P_k
H_mu(P_k) < infinity for each k
the union of the P_k generates B modulo mu-null sets
h_mu(T) is defined as the supremum of h_mu(T,Q) over countable partitions Q of finite entropy

[Theorem Prop_pre_post_inf_dist of arXiv:2606.27573, 'Conditional Path Decomposition at the Infimum and Maximum Drawdowns for Spectrally Negativ'] Conditionally on $I_{T}=a$, the pre-$H_{I}$ and post-$H_{I}$ processes are independent. 
     
i. The law of the pre-$H_I$ process is an $h$-transform of the law of the spectrally negative L\'{e}vy process killed at  $\tau_a\wedge T $ with 
\[
h(x) = \frac{\gamma}{\Phi(\gamma)} W^{(\gamma)\prime}(x-a) -\gamma W^{(\gamma)}(x-a)
\] 
for $x\ge a$. Moreover, the distribution of the supremum and the maximum drawdown of the pre-infimum process, $S_{H_{I}}$, $M_{0, H_{I}}^{-},$ respectively, when $I_{T}=a$ are given by
	\begin{eqnarray*}
		
        &&\mathbb{P}_0\left\{S_{H_{I}} < b \mid I_{T}=a\right\}=1-\frac{ \frac{\gamma}{\Phi(\gamma)} W^{(\gamma)\prime}(b-a) -\gamma W^{(\gamma)}(b-a) }{\frac{\gamma}{\Phi(\gamma)} W^{(\gamma)\prime}(-a) -\gamma W^{(\gamma)}(-a)}\left[\frac{W^{(\gamma)}(-a)}{W^{(\gamma)}(b-a)}\right]
	\end{eqnarray*}
	for  $b\ge 0$, and
    \begin{eqnarray*}
\mathbb{P}\left\{M_{0, H_{I}}^{-}< d \mid I_{T}=a \right\} =1-\frac{ \frac{\gamma}{\Phi(\gamma)} W^{(\gamma)\prime}(d) -\gamma W^{(\gamma)}(d) }{\frac{\gamma}{\Phi(\gamma)} W^{(\gamma)\prime}(-a) -\gamma W^{(\gamma)}(-a)}\left[\frac{W^{(\gamma)}(-a)}{W^{(\gamma)}(d)}\right]
\end{eqnarray*}
for $d\ge -a.$

ii. The law of the post-$H_{I}$ process is the $h$-transform of the law of the spectrally negative L\'{e}vy process killed at $T \wedge \tau_{a}^{-}$with	
	$$
	h(x)=1-Z^{(\gamma)}(x-a)+\frac{\gamma}{\Phi(\gamma)} W^{(\gamma)}(x-a).
	$$	
	Moreover, the distribution of the supremum of the post-infimum process, $S_{H_{I}, T}$, when $I_{T}=a$ is given by

	

\[
\mathbb{P}_{a}\left\{S_{H_{I}, T} \le b \mid I_{T}=a\right\}  = \frac{\Phi(\gamma)({Z^{(\gamma)}}(b-a)-1)}{\gamma W^{(\gamma)}(b-a)} 
\]
	for $b>a$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem Prop_pre_post_inf_dist of arXiv:2606.27573

Fix z₀ ∈ ℂ and let γ₀, γ₁: [0,1] → ℂ \ {z₀} be continuous closed curves. (a) Free homotopy: γ₀ and γ₁ are homotopic through closed curves in ℂ \ {z₀} (a continuous H: [0,1]×[0,1] → ℂ \ {z₀} with H(0,·) = γ₀, H(1,·) = γ₁ and H(s,0) = H(s,1) for every s) if and only if n(γ₀, z₀) = n(γ₁, z₀). (b) Based version: if γ₀(0) = γ₁(0) = p, they are homotopic through loops based at p in ℂ \ {z₀} if and only if their winding numbers about z₀ agree. (c) Consequently the map π₁(ℂ \ {z₀}, p) → ℤ, [γ] ↦ n(γ, z₀), is a well-defined group isomorphism; every integer k is realized by the circle t ↦ z₀ + r e^{2πikt} (moved to the base point along a path), and a loop in ℂ \ {z₀} is null-homotopic exactly when its winding number about z₀ is zero. The same statements hold with ℂ \ {z₀} replaced by any annulus {r < |z − z₀| < R} (0 ≤ r < R ≤ ∞) or by the circle S¹ (degree of a map S¹ → S¹). Sharp edges. (1) Two or more punctures: in ℂ \ {a, b} (a ≠ b) the fundamental group is free on two generators, hence non-abelian, and the pair of winding numbers does NOT classify loops: the commutator loop α β α⁻¹ β⁻¹ of small circles α about a and β about b has winding number 0 about both a and b (and about every point outside the domain) yet is not null-homotopic. In a general open Ω ⊂ ℂ, having equal winding numbers about every point of ℂ \ Ω is the condition for two loops to be HOMOLOGOUS in Ω (Ahlfors' definition, the one used in the general Cauchy theorem); it is strictly weaker than being homotopic. (2) No puncture: in ℂ itself every loop is null-homotopic, so the winding number about a point of the domain is not a homotopy invariant there; the invariance in (a) uses that the homotopy avoids z₀.
exactly one point z₀ is removed from ℂ (or the domain is an annulus around z₀)
the curves and homotopies stay in ℂ \ {z₀}

[Proposition 244 (ALE coordinates are identical to acoustical geometric coordinates) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Let $\eta, n, \tau$ be as in \eqref{E:DEFINITIONOFSTEVEFLOWMAP}--\eqref{E:DEFINITIONOFTANGENTVECTORSFORSTEVEOUTGOINGCHAR}, where we recall that equation \eqref{E:DEFINITIONOFSTEVEFLOWMAP} is solved in conjunction with the compressible Euler equations. Let $\mathbf{n}= (n_0,n_1,n_2)$ be the $\mathbf{g}$-null one-form from 
	\eqref{E:OUTGOINGCOCHARCHOICE}, let $\Lunit^{ALE}$ be as in \eqref{E:ALELUNIT}, 
	and let $\Lambda_{ALE}$ be the flow-map of $\Lunit^{ALE}$ as in \eqref{E:FLOWMAPOFALELUNIT}. 
	Then for $C^1$ solutions to the compressible Euler equations, the following hold:
			\begin{enumerate}
				\item \underline{\textbf{The flow of $\Lunit^{ALE}$}}. The flow map $\Lambda_{ALE}$ satisfies $\Lambda_{ALE}^0 = t$ and $\Lambda_{ALE}^i = \eta^i$ for $i = 1,2$.
				\item \underline{\textbf{$\Gamma_{x^1}(T)$ are characteristics in the sense of Def.\,\ref{D:CHARACTERISTICSURFACESCANONICAL}}}. 
				Recall that $\Gamma_{x^1}(T)$ is the surface defined in \eqref{E:CHARACTERISTICS}.
				For any $\Gamma_{x^1}(T)$-tangent vectorfield $W$, we have $\mathbf{n}_\alpha W^\alpha = 0$. Hence, $\Gamma_{x^1}(T)$ is a characteristic surface as in Def.\,\ref{D:CHARACTERISTICSURFACESCANONICAL}.
				\item \underline{\textbf{$\Gamma_{x^1}(T)$ are $\gfour$-null hypersurfaces}}. There exists a $\Gamma_{x^1}(T)$-tangent vectorfield $V$ 
					that is $\gfour$-orthogonal to the tangent space of $\Gamma_{x^1}(T)$. In particular, $\gfour(V,V) = 0$.
				\item \underline{\textbf{The geometric coordinates are identical to ALE coordinates}}. Suppose that $u$ is the solution to the eikonal equation $(\gfour^{-1})^{\alpha\beta}\p_\alpha u \p_\beta u = 0$ with $u \restriction_{t=0} = x^1$ and\footnote{For the proposition to be correct, $\partial_t u < 0$ is the right sign; $\partial_t u > 0$ would correspond to constructing the ingoing characteristics. We point out that  we have $\partial_t u > 0$ in \eqref{E:EIKONALBRANCHINTRO}. The reason is that in the bulk of the paper, we chose the initial data \eqref{E:EIKONALDATAINTRO} to have the opposite sign compared to this proposition.} 
				$\partial_t u \restriction_{t=0} < 0$. 
				Then $x^1_{ALE} = u$. In addition, the vectorfield $\Lunit$ defined by \eqref{E:LUNIT} satisfies $\Lunit = \Lunit^{ALE}$.				
				\item \underline{\textbf{$\Lunit^{ALE}$ is a non-affinely  parametrized geodesic vectorfield}}. There is a non-vanishing function $\smoothfunction$ such that $\Dfour_{\Lunit^{ALE}}\Lunit^{ALE} = \smoothfunction \Lunit^{ALE}$, where $\Dfour$ is the Levi-Civita covariant derivative defined by $\gfour$. In particular, the evolution equation \eqref{E:DEFINITIONOFSTEVEFLOWMAP} satisfied by $\eta$ is a rewriting of $\frac{1}{\smoothfunction} \Dfour_{\Lunit^{ALE}}(\Lunit^{ALE})^i = (\Lunit^{ALE})^i$. 
			\end{enumerate}

[Proposition prop:convViaInclusion of arXiv:2608.13452, 'Wasserstein stability of the zero cell of a Poisson hyperplane tessellation under directio'] Let \((\Theta_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\) and \(\Theta\) be locally finite measures on the space of hyperplanes \(\mathcal{H}\) that satisfy \(\Theta([0]_{\mathcal{H}})=0\) and \(\Theta_n([0]_{\mathcal{H}})=0\) for all \(n\).
    Let \(Z_0^n\) and \(Z_0\) be the zero cells of the Poisson hyperplane processes \(\Psi_n\) and \(\Psi\) whose intensity measures are \(\Theta_n\) and \(\Theta\) respectively.
    Assume that \(Z_0^n\) and \(Z_0\) have non-empty interior and are compact almost surely. 
    If \(\Theta_n\) converges vaguely to \(\Theta\), then \(Z_0^n\) converges to \(Z_0\) in distribution. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Theorem 1 of arXiv:1809.05092, 'Polynomial mixing time of edge flips on quadrangulations'] Let νn be the spectral gap of the edge flip Markov chain Fn on the set Qn of rooted quadrangulations with n faces. There are positive constants C1, C2 independent of n such that C1n−11 2 ≤νn ≤C2n−5 4 . Consequently, the mixing time for Fn is O(n13/2).
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:1809.05092: Polynomial mixing time of edge flips on quadrangulations

body: [Theorem thm:transient-nonstab of arXiv:2604.13968, 'Divisible sandpiles via random walks in random scenery'] For every $p\in(0,3)$, there exists a transient bounded-degree graph~$G$ such that for every $\mu<1$, there is an i.i.d.\ law bounded from below with $\mathbb{E}[\sigma]=\mu$ and $\mathbb{E}[|\sigma-\mu|^p]<\infty$ for which $u_\infty(o)=\infty$ almost surely. In particular, the divisible sandpile does not stabilize. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Defn 9 (Unified recursive tree) of arXiv:2606.22960, '2606.22960'] A {\it unified recursive tree} is a random recursive sequence of trees \((T_n)_{n\geq 1}\), where \(T_n\) has vertex set \([n]:=\{1,\dots,n\}\), $1$ denotes the root, and the probability that the vertex $n+1$ will be attached to a vertex $v$ is given by
	\[
	\mathbb P(n+1\sim v\mid T_n)=\frac{\alpha \deg_n^+(v)+\beta\,\mathbf 1_{\{v\neq 1\}}+1}{(\alpha+\beta)(n-1)+n},
	\qquad v\in[n],
	\]
	where \(\deg_n^+(v)\) denotes the out-degree of \(v\) in \(T_n\).
title: Unified recursive tree

body: [Theorem 8 of arXiv:2609.00209, 'Exit Times for Brownian Motion and Location Detection'] Let $\mathcal P$ be our parabolic domain and let $u_1(x,y)=\mathbb{E}^{(x,y)}[\tau_{\mathcal P}]$ and $u_2(x,y)=\mathbb{E}^{(x,y)}[\tau_{\mathcal P}^2]$  be the first two moments of the exit time from $\mathcal P$. Given positive real numbers $c_1$ and $c_2$, if the level curves $u_1(x,y)=c_1$ and $u_2(x,y)=c_2$ intersect, then their intersection is either two points or a single point determined by $c_1$ and $c_2$.
title: Theorem 8 of arXiv:2609.00209

		$\psi_{f} = \sqrt{\mathfrak{f}} \in C^{2}(0,1)$ is strictly positive
		and
		\begin{equation}
			U_{f} = -\,\frac{2\,\psi_{f}''}{\psi_{f}},
			\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
			\psi_{f}'' + \tfrac12\,U_{f}\,\psi_{f} = 0:
			
		\end{equation}
		the rank amplitude is a positive solution of the Hill equation of
		$U_{f}$. Moreover $Q_{f}' = \psi_{f}^{-2}$, so that, with
		$\widetilde\psi := \psi_{f}\int_{z_{0}}^{\cdot}\psi_{f}^{-2}$, the
		quantile function is the solution ratio
		$Q_{f} = \widetilde\psi/\psi_{f} + \mathrm{const}$ and the pair
		$(\widetilde\psi, \psi_{f})$ has Wronskian
		$\widetilde\psi'\psi_{f} - \widetilde\psi\psi_{f}' = 1$.

[Prop 19 ({\cite[Theorem~4.1) of arXiv:2609.02561, 'NON-NEF LOCI IN MIXED CHARACTERISTIC'] {Mus} and \cite[Proposition~4.1]{Sato}}]
With notation as above, let $A$ be a globally generated ample line bundle, $M$ be a line bundle on $X$, and $n$ be a positive integer such that $n>\max_{s\in S}\dim X_{s}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item
If $M-(K_X +\Delta)$ is ample,
then $\tau(X,\Delta)\otimes\sO_{X}(nA+M)$ is globally generated.
\item
If $M-(K_X +\Delta)-D$ is ample, then $\tau(X,\Delta,\|D\|)\otimes\sO_{X}(nA+M)$ is globally generated.
\end{enumerate}

[Corollary 93 (Convergence of the localized cutoff data) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] For every deterministic $T_0\le1$, there exist a tuple $\Xi$ satisfying
Definition~\ref{def:Xi-assumptions} and a distribution $\Theta$ such that
\begin{equation}
 d_{T_0}^{\Theta}
 \bigl((\Theta_\Lambda,\Xi_\Lambda),(\Theta,\Xi)\bigr)
 \longrightarrow0
 \qquad\text{in probability}.
\end{equation}
The convergence holds in every finite probability moment for the distributional
components and in the stated operator modes for $T^{a;b,c}$.  A
fixed-profile dyadic family converges simultaneously almost surely on a common
event; a general admissible family converges in probability.  The localized
limit is independent of the admissible spectral profile.

[Corollary cor:finite-rank-chaos-recurrence of arXiv:2606.21006, 'Law of the Iterated Logarithm for Weighted Sums of Functionals of Long-Memory Gaussian Seq'] Let \(T<\infty\). Let
\(E\subset D_{\mathbb R}\) be finite-dimensional, and let
\(Q_t\in E^{\odot m}\), \(0\le t\le T\), be a continuous
finite-rank kernel family. Fix \(\xi\in E\) with
\(\|\xi\|_{\mathfrak H_{\mathbb R}}<1\). Then there exists a sparse deterministic sequence
\(n_k=\lfloor\exp(k^\gamma)\rfloor\) and, with probability one, a subsequence
\(k_\ell\to\infty\) such that
\[
    \frac{I_m(Q_t;W_{n_{k_\ell}})}
    {(2\log\log n_{k_\ell})^{m/2}}
    \longrightarrow
    \langle Q_t,\xi^{\otimes m}\rangle_{\mathfrak H_{\mathbb R}^{\otimes m}}
\]
uniformly for \(t\in[0,T]\).

body:
Let n ≥ 2. A pair (q,r) is wave-admissible (in the sense of Keel–Tao) if 2 ≤ q ≤ ∞, 2 ≤ r ≤ ∞, 1/q + (n−1)/(2r) ≤ (n−1)/4, and (q,r,n) ≠ (2,∞,3). It is sharp wave-admissible when equality holds, 1/q + (n−1)/(2r) = (n−1)/4. The exponent (n−1)/2 is the dispersive decay rate of frequency-localized waves; the associated regularity s is fixed separately by the scaling relation 1/q + n/r = n/2 − s. Examples in n = 3: (4,4) with s = 1/2, (5,10) and (4,12) with s = 1, and (∞,2) with s = 0, which is the bound ‖u‖_{L^∞_t L²_x} ≲ ‖u0‖_{L²} + ‖u1‖_{Ḣ^{−1}}. Note that the energy bound ‖u‖_{L^∞_t Ḣ¹} + ‖∂_t u‖_{L^∞_t L²} ≲ ‖u0‖_{Ḣ¹} + ‖u1‖_{L²} is not a different admissible pair: it is the pair (∞,2) applied at regularity s = 1, i.e. to |∇|u. The scaling relation always ties s to (q,r), so s = 0 is the only value that goes with (q,r) = (∞,2) in the Lebesgue-norm form of the estimate. Also note that r = ∞ is allowed in this definition but not in the Lebesgue-space wave Strichartz theorem, which requires r < ∞.

[Lemma lem:chi2 of arXiv:2606.27073, 'Retention Profiles and KL Contraction Bounds in Finite Markov Chains'] For each $x\in S$,
\[
  \chi^2(P(x,\cdot)\|\pi)
  :=\sum_{y\in S}\frac{(P(x,y)-\pi(y))^2}{\pi(y)}
  =\sum_{i=2}^n\lambda_i^2\,\phi_i(x)^2.
\]
Consequently,
$\sum_{x\in S}\pi(x)\,\chi^2(P(x,\cdot)\|\pi)=\sum_{i=2}^n\lambda_i^2$.
title: $\chi^2$--spectral identity

[Theorem theoremonline89 of arXiv:2606.01664, 'Brown measure convergence for the spectrum of polynomials in Ginibre matrices'] Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $\mathfrak{p}\in\mathbb{C}\langle x_1,\cdots,x_n\rangle$ be a non-commutative polynomial of any degree. Then for any $z\neq\mathfrak{p}(0)$ there are constants $c_0(\mathfrak{p}),c(\mathfrak{p}),c_1(\mathfrak{p})$ depending only on $\mathfrak{p}$, and a constant $\widehat{C}(\mathfrak{p},z)>0$ depending on both $\mathfrak{p}$ and $z$, so that we have the following estimate. Let $X_1^N,\cdots,X_n^N$ be independent $N\times N$ complex Ginibre matrices and denote by $P^N=\mathfrak{p}(X_1^N,\cdots,X_n^N)$. Then for this $z\neq \mathfrak{p}(0)$, we can find some fixed $N_0=N_0(\mathfrak{p},z)$ such that whenever $N\geq N_0$, we have for any $\epsilon>0,$
    $$
\mathbb{P}\{\sigma_{min}(P^N-z)\leq\epsilon
\}\leq \widehat{C}(N^{c_0}\epsilon^c+\exp(-c_1N)).
    $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem theoremonline89 of arXiv:2606.01664

[Definition def.hepp_3 of arXiv:2607.10105, 'The four-dimensional Anderson model: a case study for critical SPDEs'] Let $\mathcal T$ be a Hepp tree with marking $(N_\mathfrak n)$. A mapping $(z_\mathfrak l):\mathcal L\to\mathbb Z_M^4$ is called \emph{admissible}, if it is injective (i.e. $z_\mathfrak l$ are different for different $\mathfrak l$), and satisfies that
\begin{enumerate}[{(a)}]
\item $|z_\mathfrak l-z_{\mathfrak l'}|\geq \frac{1}{2}N_{\mathfrak l\vee\mathfrak l'}$ for $\mathfrak l,\mathfrak l'\in\mathcal L$ with $\mathfrak l\neq\mathfrak l'$;
\item For any $\mathfrak n\in\mathcal B$, all its children $\mathfrak n_1,\cdots,\mathfrak n_s$ can be connected by some links between them, such that for each link $(j,k)$, there exists $\mathfrak l\in \mathcal L_{\mathfrak n_j}$ and $\mathfrak l'\in \mathcal L_{\mathfrak n_k}$ such that $|z_\mathfrak l-z_{\mathfrak l'}|\leq N_{\mathfrak n}$.
\end{enumerate} 
Let $Z$ be a (non-repeating) subset of $\mathbb Z_M^4$ with $|Z|=r$ (the number of leaves of $\mathcal T$), we define $Z\leftrightarrow (\mathcal T,N_\mathfrak n)$, if there exists a bijective mapping $(z_\mathfrak l):\mathcal L\to Z$ that is admissible.

Now, suppose we are also given the multiplicities $m_\mathfrak l$, and let $m=\sum_{\mathfrak l\in\mathcal L} m_\mathfrak l$. For any $(y_1,\cdots,y_{m})\in(\mathbb Z_M^4)^{m}$, we define $(y_1,\cdots,y_{m})\leftrightarrow (\mathcal T,N_\mathfrak n,m_\mathfrak l)$, if there exists an admissible $(z_\mathfrak l)$ such that the \emph{multiset} $\{y_1,\cdots,y_{m}\}=\cup_{\mathfrak l\in\mathcal L}\{\textrm{$m_\mathfrak l$ copies of $z_\mathfrak l$}\}$. We also write $(y_1,\cdots,y_{m})\leftrightarrow(\mathcal T,N_\mathfrak n)$ (resp. $(y_1,\cdots,y_{m})\leftrightarrow\mathcal T$), if there exists some choice of $(m_\mathfrak l)$ (resp. some choice of $(N_\mathfrak n,m_\mathfrak l)$) such that $(y_1,\cdots,y_{m})\leftrightarrow (\mathcal T,N_\mathfrak n,m_\mathfrak l)$.
title: Definition def.hepp_3 of arXiv:2607.10105

[Defn def:black-noise of arXiv:2607.18194, 'Temperature chaos in directed polymers'] Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\{\mathcal{F}_R\}_{R\in\mathcal{R}}, \mathbb{P},\{\theta_h\}_{h\in\mathbb{R}^d})$ be a $d$-dimensional noise.
    A random variable $X\in L^2(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$ is called \emph{linear} if 
    for all $R_1,R_2,R_3\in\mathcal{R}$ with $R_1\cap R_2=\varnothing$ and $\overline{R_1\cup R_2}=\overline{R_3}$, we have
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbb{E}[X|\mathcal{F}_{R_3}] = \mathbb{E}[X|\mathcal{F}_{R_1}]+\mathbb{E}[X|\mathcal{F}_{R_2}].
    \end{align*}
    The noise is \emph{black} if the only linear random variable is zero.
    Note that a noise being black depends on the $\sigma$-algebras $\{\mathcal{F}_R\}_{R\in\mathcal{R}}$ only up to $\mathbb{P}$-null sets.
title: Black noise

let $\eta_R$ and $\Cap_R=\eta_R(\partial A)$ be the bounded-domain weak
equilibrium measure and weak capacity in $\calD_R$ for the pair $(A,B)$.
Set
\[
    h_\infty^*(z)=\Pbb_z^*(\tau_A<\tau_B),
    \qquad z\in\R^{3d}.
\]
As before, $h_\infty^*$ is extended by the boundary values $1$ on
$\overline A$ and $0$ on $\overline B$.
Then there exists a unique finite positive Borel measure $\eta_\infty$ on
$\partial A$ such that, for every $\varphi\in C^2(\partial A)$ and every
$\Phi\in C_c^2(\R^{3d})$ satisfying $\Phi|_{\partial A}=\varphi$ and
$\Phi=0$ in a neighborhood of $\overline B$,
\begin{equation}
    \int_{\partial A}\varphi d\eta_\infty
    =
    \int_{\R^{3d}}h_\infty^*(-\calL_\eps\Phi) d\pi^\eps .
\end{equation}
Moreover, as $R\to\infty$, $\eta_R\Rightarrow\eta_\infty$ weakly on
$\partial A$ and
$\Cap_R\to\Cap_\infty:=\eta_\infty(\partial A)$.
In addition,
\begin{equation}
    \int_{\partial A}\E_z[\tau_B] \eta_\infty(dz)
    =
    \int_{\R^{3d}}h_\infty^* d\pi^\eps .
\end{equation}
Consequently $\Cap_\infty>0$, and the corresponding normalized whole-space
hitting identity follows by dividing \eqref{eq:exhaustion-hitting} by
$\Cap_\infty$.

body:
[Theorem thm:mtd2_converges of arXiv:2609.02832, 'Copula Transformations for Data-Consistent Inversion'] Let $\mathbb{P}_{1} \supset \mathbb{P}_{2} \supset \dots$, where each $\mathbb{P}_k$ is a nonempty convex set that is closed in the total variation topology and for which the corresponding I-projection of $P^0$ exists with finite KL divergence.
Let $\mathbb{P}= \bigcap_{j=1}^{\infty}\mathbb{P}_j$ and suppose that the I-projection of $P^0$ onto $\mathbb{P}$ exists with finite KL divergence and that
the sequence $\{\argmin_{P \in \mathbb{P}_{k}}D_{\rm KL}(P \| P^{0})\}$ is relatively compact.
Then,
$
\argmin_{P \in \mathbb{P}_{k}}D_{\rm KL}(P \| P^{0})
\xrightarrow{\mathrm{TV}}
\argmin_{P \in \mathbb{P}}D_{\rm KL}(P \| P^{0})
$.
title: Theorem thm:mtd2_converges of arXiv:2609.02832

body:
[Lem characterization-of-interpolation-spaces of arXiv:2601.19145, 'Stochastic Persistence in Infinite Dimensions'] Let $a = 1$ if the boundary conditions in (sass-A of the paper) are Neumann, and $a = 0$ otherwise. Then for $1 < p < \infty$:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item For $1/(2p) + a/2 < \vartheta < 1$, $\mathcal{B}_{\vartheta,p} = \{u \in W^{2\vartheta,p} \mid Bu \equiv 0 \text{ on } \partial D\}$ (where $B = \partial_\nu$ for Neumann and $B = 0$ for periodic).
    \item For $0 < \vartheta < 1/(2p) + a/2$, $\mathcal{B}_{\vartheta,p} = W^{2\vartheta,p}$.
    \item For $-1 < \vartheta < 0$, $\mathcal{B}_{\vartheta,p} = (\mathcal{B}_{-\vartheta,p^*})^*$, where $1/p + 1/p^* = 1$. In particular, for periodic boundary conditions $\mathcal{B}_{\vartheta,p} = W^{2\vartheta,p}$ for all $-1 \leq \vartheta \leq 1$.
    
    
    
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem characterization-of-interpolation-spaces of arXiv:2601.19145

body:
[Corollary 46 (Separation mixing time) of arXiv:2604.09933, 'Explicit cutoff profiles for colored top-\texorpdfstring{$m$}{m}-to-random shuffles'] Fix \(p\ge1\) and \(m\ge1\), independent of \(n\). Let
\[
t_{\sep}^{(m)}(\varepsilon)
:=\min\left\{k\ge0:\sep\bigl((Q^{(m)})^{*k},U\bigr)\le\varepsilon\right\},
\qquad 0<\varepsilon<1.
\]
Let \(c_{\varepsilon,p}\) be the unique real number satisfying
\[
s_p(c_{\varepsilon,p})=\varepsilon.
\]
Then
\[
t_{\sep}^{(m)}(\varepsilon)
=
\frac{n}{m}\bigl(\log n+c_{\varepsilon,p}\bigr)+o(n).
\]
For \(p\ge2\),
\[
c_{\varepsilon,p}=-\log\bigl(-\log(1-\varepsilon)\bigr).
\]

$$\int\int f(x,\xi) \xi(dx)\mathsf{P}(d\xi) = \int\int f(x,\theta_{-x}\xi) \mathsf{P}^0(d\xi)dx$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 23 of arXiv:2606.11994, 'Sample Path Properties of the\\ Fractional Wiener--Weierstrass Bridge II'] Assume $H>1/2$ and put $p=1/H$.  For fixed $s,t\in[0,1]$, define
\[
\begin{aligned}   h_{s,t}(x):=\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}\alpha^m   \left(   J(\fp{b^m s},\fp{b^m t})(x)   -\kappa(\fp{b^m t})+\kappa(\fp{b^m s})   \right).
\end{aligned}
\]
Then the series defining $h_{s,t}$ converges absolutely in $L^p[0,1]$, and
\[   Y(t)-Y(s)=\int_0^1 h_{s,t}\dd W_H   \quad\text{in }L^2(\Omega).
\]
Consequently $Y(t)-Y(s)$ is a centered Gaussian random variable and
\[   \operatorname{Var}(Y(t)-Y(s))=\|h_{s,t}\|_{\calH}^2.
\]
title: Lemma 23 of arXiv:2606.11994

body:
[Lemma 22 (Finite-time reduction for first-hit decisions) of arXiv:2607.19752, 'Weak Equilibrium Measures and Capacity--Hitting Identities\\ for the Hypoelliptic Third-Or'] Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:U} and~\ref{ass:controlled-coefficients} hold,
and adopt the \hyperref[setup:domains]{bounded-domain setup}.
Let $K\subset\Omega$ be compact.  Then
\[
    \lim_{M\to\infty}
    \limsup_{\delta\downarrow0}
    \sup_{z\in K}
    \Pbb_z^\delta\left(
        \tau_A^\delta\wedge\tau_\calC^\delta>M
    \right)=0 .
\]
Moreover,
\[
    \lim_{M\to\infty}
    \sup_{z\in K}
    \Pbb_z\left(
        \tau_A\wedge\tau_\calC>M
    \right)=0 .
\]
The same statements hold for the adjoint family.

Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, paired; one n = 60 draw per cell). The long-only stack ($\|w\|_1 = 1$) against the same estimator under a gross-exposure constraint $\|w\|_1 \le c$ for $c \in \{1.5, 2\}$ and the unconstrained sum-to-one form, all on the raw relative-metric error covariance (the cleaner is irrelevant inside the constraint). At full calibration the best finite $c$ gains $+1.00$ percent on EMIT and $+0.12$ on OCO-2 over $c = 1$ ($c = 2$: $-1.45$ / $-0.11$; $c = 1$ within one percent of the best on 29 of 40 and 30 of 30 cells). At $n = 60$ calibration rows $c = 1.5$ reads $-7.07$ / $-4.22$, $c = 2$ $-10.16$ / $-6.39$ and the unconstrained form $-63.8$ / $-18886.9$ against $c = 1$ - the $c^2$ growth of the excess-risk bound seen directly, with the unconstrained plug-in's collapse at the end of the ladder. Reading: a modest relaxation buys a little at full calibration and costs at small n, so long-only is the right default and the exposure cap is a tuning knob with a cross-validated price

body:
[Lemma of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] The restriction of the cocone $\tilde\sigma$ to $\ul\textup{VRep}_{[d]}$ factors (necessarily uniquely) through $\smash{\textbf{\textup{BOP}}^{[d]}\hookrightarrow\textbf{\textup{BOP}}}$.
    \begin{proof}
        For any map of $G$-orthogonal spaces $f\colon X\to\textbf{\textup{BOP}}$, $X$ splits up to isomorphism as $\coprod_{d\in{\mathbb{Z}}} f^{-1}(\textbf{\textup{BOP}}^{[d]})$. If the underlying space of $X$ is path-connected (e.g.\ when $X$ is weakly contractible), exactly one of these summands is non-empty, and we define $d(f)$ to be the corresponding index; equivalently, this is the unique $d$ such that $f$ factors through $\textbf{\textup{BOP}}^{[d]}$ (on the pointset level). It is clear that if $f\to g$ is any map over $\textbf{\textup{BOP}}$ and $g$ factors through $\textbf{\textup{BOP}}^{[d]}$, then so does $f$; in particular, if $f$ and $g$ are moreover in ${{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\text{$G$-gl}^\circ[\textbf{\textup{BOP}}]$, then $d(f)=d(g)$.
        
        With this established, it is easy to check that $f\mapsto d(f)$  defines a symmetric monoidal global functor $\smash{\ul{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{gl}^\circ[\textbf{\textup{BOP}}]^\otimes\to\textup{const}({\mathbb{Z}},+)}$. Moreover, its restriction along ${{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{gl}[i]^\otimes\circ y_{\textup{top}}^\otimes$ agrees with $\dim\colon\ul\textup{Rep}^\oplus\to\textup{const}({\mathbb{Z}},+)$ by direct inspection, so $d\circ\bar y_{\textup{top}}=\dim$ by the universal property of group completion. Thus, $\bar y_{\textup{top}}$ maps $\smash{\ul\textup{VRep}_{[d]}}$ into the subcategory of $\ul{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{gl}[\textbf{\textup{BOP}}]$ of maps factoring through ${\textbf{\textup{BOP}}^{[d]}}$, which is in turn equivalent to $\tilde\sigma$ factoring accordingly.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered lemma of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'

[Theorem nongaussiantheorem of arXiv:2606.01664, 'Brown measure convergence for the spectrum of polynomials in Ginibre matrices'] Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\mathfrak{p}\in\mathbb{C}\langle x_1,\cdots,x_n\rangle$.
    Let $\xi$ be a complex-valued random variable with 
    $$
\mathbb{E}[\xi]=0,\quad\mathbb{E}[|\xi|^2]=1,
    $$and assume that $\xi$ has a density $f$ on $\mathbb{C}$ satisfying, for some fixed $K>0$,
    \begin{equation}
\|f\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{C})}\leq K<\infty.
    \end{equation}Further assume that $\xi$ has finite moments of all orders: for any $Q\in\mathbb{N}_+$ there exists $M_Q<\infty$ such that
    \begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}[|\xi|^Q]\leq M_Q<\infty.
    \end{equation}
    Consider a random matrix $X^N=(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}x_{ij})_{1\leq i,j\leq N}$ where the $x_{ij}$ are i.i.d. random variables with law $\xi$. Let $X_1^N,\cdots,X_n^N$ be i.i.d. copies of $X^N$. We similarly denote by $P^N=\mathfrak{p}(X_1^N,\cdots,X_n^N)$. Then the same Brown measure convergence in Theorem (mainconvergencetheorem of the paper) also holds for this matrix $P^N$ with non-Gaussian law. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem nongaussiantheorem of arXiv:2606.01664

[Theorem 6 (Stable-rank small-ball estimate for Rademacher images) of arXiv:2608.30722, 'Intermediate Singular Values of Random Matrices\\ under Second-Moment and Anti-Concentrati'] There exist absolute constants $\eta_{\mathrm{rad}}, c_{\mathrm{rad}} > 0$
such that the following holds. Let
$\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_N)$ be a vector of independent
Rademacher random variables, and let $D$ be a deterministic real matrix. Then
\[
  \sup_{u}

    \|D\varepsilon-u\|_2
    \le
    \eta_{\mathrm{rad}}\|D\|_{HS}
  \right)
  \le
  2\exp\!\left(-c_{\mathrm{rad}} \sr(D)\right).
\]

[Lemma lemmaLocalizedSDEAwayOrigin of arXiv:2608.11178, 'A submartingale for the probability of avoiding the origin in one-point interaction ground'] Fix \(d\in\{2,3\}\), \(T,\gamma>0\), and
\(x\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\). There exists a \(d\)-dimensional
standard Brownian motion
\(\{W_t^{T,\gamma}\}_{t\in[0,T]}\) on the probability space
\((\Omega,\mathcal B_x^T,\mathbb P_x^{T,\gamma})\), with respect to the
filtration \(\{\mathcal F_t^{T,x}\}_{t\in[0,T]}\), such that the coordinate
process \(X=\{X_t\}_{t\in[0,T]}\) satisfies
\begin{align}
dX_t
=
dW_t^{T,\gamma}
+
b^\gamma(X_t)\,dt,
\qquad
X_0=x,
\end{align}
in the following sense:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item If \(d=2\), then~(equation CanonicalGSDSDE of the paper) holds on \([0,T]\),
\(\mathbb P_x^{T,\gamma}\)-almost surely~[Chen3].

\item If \(d=3\), then~(equation CanonicalGSDSDE of the paper) holds locally on every
time interval on which \(X\) remains away from
the origin.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 22 (Smooth duality) of arXiv:2506.09637, 'Nonlinear Stochastic Filtering with Volterra Gaussian Noises'] Assume the Conditions of Theorem \ref{lem:backward_dual_equation} hold. Let \(\hat{J}^\epsilon\) be a sequence in as in Definition \ref{approximation_class_rpde}, and let
\(\varkappa^\epsilon\) be a finite measure-valued solution of the smooth weak
Zakai equation
\[
\begin{aligned}
    \varkappa_t^\epsilon(\phi)
    &=
    \varkappa_0^\epsilon(\phi)
    +
    \int_0^t
        \varkappa_s^\epsilon
        \bigl(A_{Y_s^\epsilon}\phi\bigr)\,dc^\epsilon_s        \\
    &\quad
    +
    \int_0^t
        \varkappa_s^\epsilon
        \bigl(f(\cdot,Y_s^\epsilon)\phi\bigr)\,dW_s^\epsilon
    -
    \frac12
    \int_0^t
        \varkappa_s^\epsilon
        \bigl(f(\cdot,Y_s^\epsilon)^2\phi\bigr)\,ds .
\end{aligned}
\]
Let \(\varphi^{\epsilon,t,\psi}\) be the smooth backward solution with
terminal condition
\(
    \varphi_t^{\epsilon,t,\psi}=\psi.
\)
Then
\(
    \varkappa_t^\epsilon(\psi)
    =
    \varkappa_0^\epsilon(\varphi_0^{\epsilon,t,\psi}).
\)

In the stated Gaussian network, fix an output coordinate k and let delta_(k,l)=grad_(u_l) f_k. Define qhat_l=||h_l||^2/M_l and qtilde_l=||delta_(k,l)||^2; the latter is a sum, not a width-normalized average. Assumption1 permits evaluating backward order parameters with a separate parameter set from the one used in the forward chain, thereby decoupling dependencies that exist with tied forward/backward weights. Under this backward-weight decoupling closure, the authors use qhat_0=1, v_l=sigma_w^2*qhat_(l-1)+sigma_b^2 and qhat_l=E[phi(sqrt(v_l)*Z)^2] for hidden l=1,...,L-1, Z~N(0,1). Backward values obey qtilde_L=1 and qtilde_l=sigma_w^2*qtilde_(l+1)*E[phi_prime(sqrt(v_l)*Z)^2] for l=L-1,...,1. These scalar recurrences describe the source mean-field closure; stating them does not prove the decoupling substitution for an actual tied-weight gradient.
Fixed L>=2 and fixed positive integers C,T. Widths M_l/M->alpha_l>0 for l=0,...,L-1; M_L=C. Hidden layers h_l=phi(u_l), u_l=W_l*h_(l-1)+b_l; output f=u_L is linear.
Independent Gaussian initialization W_l[i,j]~N(0,sigma_w^2/M_(l-1)) and b_l[i]~N(0,sigma_b^2), sigma_w>0 and sigma_b>0. Inputs are iid standard Gaussian. Parameters theta include all weights and biases.
phi and phi_prime have finite squared Gaussian integrals at each recursively occurring preactivation variance. The empirical FIM normalization is F=(1/T)*sum_(t=1)^T sum_(k=1)^C grad_theta f_k(x_t)*grad_theta f_k(x_t)^T.

body:
Fix a finite Netsor program. Its inputs are fixed real vectors of fixed dimensions and independent matrix variables W of shape n by m with independent N(0,1/m) entries. Its only instructions are MatMul g=W h and coordinatewise NonLin h=phi(h_1,...,h_k), with matching dimensions; a matrix variable may be reused, but transposition is not an instruction. Let n_hidden be the program collection of dimensions internal to chains of matrix contractions, and n_output the output dimensions; input dimensions remain fixed. Write h^ell in R^(n_ell) for the finite-width variable on line ell and bar_h^ell for the infinite-width execution. In the latter, every MatMul variable bar_g is centered Gaussian, all MatMul variables are jointly Gaussian, different matrix variables have zero cross-covariance, and two products using the same W, with parent variables bar_h,bar_h_prime in R^m, have cross-covariance [E(bar_h^T bar_h_prime)/m] I_n. NonLin instructions apply the same functions coordinatewise to this Gaussian execution. Assume every NonLin map is globally Lipschitz. For any two vector variables h,h_prime in R^n and every p>=1, ||h^T h_prime/n-E(bar_h^T bar_h_prime)/n||_(L^p) <= c sum_(m in n_hidden union n_output) m^(-1/2), where c depends only on p and the structural constants of the fixed program. The additional output-width summands are needed when the empirical kernel is computed at output dimensions. This is an L^p error bound for the random empirical kernel, not merely convergence of its expectation.

Own-work draft, proof (unaudited), T326-w697-C08 v1; independent reviewer PASS pending. For one arbitrary nonzero deterministic training task in any dimension d, the source augmented linear-attention model with separately trained K,Q and scalar v22, v21 held zero and m21 trained, converges to zero loss from Q0=K0=alpha I_(d+1), v22,0=alpha sqrt(d), 0<alpha^3/sqrt(d)<1. In the exact two-coordinate task-space reduction, positive coordinate dynamics give exponential residual decay; C07 supplies global boundedness and hence convergence of the factors. The selected map equals TPR+alpha v_infinity A_infinity(I-P)R. For fixed epsilon in (0,1), alpha=epsilon/sqrt(d), fixed rho>=0 and one iid standard Gaussian training task, its conditional fresh-task excess risk converges in probability to 2, worse than the zero predictor risk 1. This removes C07's convergence hypothesis for M=1; M>=2 remains open. After rotating the single task to the first coordinate, x_s=(||w||/d,||w||^2/d+rho), a0=(alpha,0), h0=alpha x_s, and v0=alpha sqrt(d). The exact equations are a'=v r h^T, h'=v r||x_s||^2 a^T and v'=r a h, with r=||w||-v a h. Then r'=-K r, K=(a h)^2+v^2||h||^2+v^2||x_s||^2||a||^2. The positive orthant makes all active coordinates nondecreasing, so K>=v0^2 alpha^2||x_s||^2>0. C07 supplies global boundedness, and integrable residuals give convergence of the factors. The method is elementary single-example deep-linear dynamics; no general novelty claim is made. The additional unit of fresh risk is caused by the retained scalar-feature column, absent in the square Kwon reduction. The risk limit is in probability, not expectation over the training task.

body:
[Theorem 1 (Unique finite-time limit) of arXiv:2609.00501, 'Uniqueness of Finite-Time Varifold Limits for the M\"obius-Invariant Willmore Flow'] Let $F\colon[0,T)\times\Sigma\to\Sph^3$ be a smooth MIWF of a compact
torus, where $T<\infty$, and write $F_t:=F(t,\cdot)$.  Let $A_t^0$
denote the trace-free second fundamental form of $F_t$.  Put
\[
 W(t):=\Will(F_t),\qquad W_0:=W(0),\qquad
 \mu_t:=\mu_{F_t^*g_{\Sph^3}}.
\]
Assume that
for some $c_0>0$,
\[
 \inf_{0<t<T}\min_{x\in\Sigma}|A_t^0(x)|^2\geq c_0.
\]
Let $\Var_t$ denote the multiplicity-counting integral two-varifold in
$\R^4$ induced by $F_t$, and set
$\lambda_t:=\lVert\Var_t\rVert=(F_t)_\#\mu_t$.
Then there exists a unique integral two-varifold
$\Var_T$ in $\R^4$, possibly the zero varifold, such that, with
$\rightharpoonup$ denoting weak varifold convergence,
\begin{equation}
 
 \Var_t\rightharpoonup\Var_T
 \qquad\text{as }t\nearrow T.
\end{equation}
No reparametrizations of $\Sigma$ and no M\"obius transformations of
$\Sph^3$ are required.

More precisely, there are finite nonnegative Radon measures $\mu_T$ on
$\Sigma$ and $\lambda_T=\lVert\Var_T\rVert$ on $\Sph^3$ such that
$\mu_t\to\mu_T$ in total variation and
$\lambda_t\to\lambda_T$ in the bounded-Lipschitz distance
$d_{\BL}$ defined in \eqref{eq:bl-distance}.  Setting
\[
 W_T:=\lim_{t\nearrow T}W(t),
\]
there holds, for every $0<s<T$,
\begin{align}
 
 \lVert\mu_T-\mu_s\rVert_{\TV}
 &\leq \frac{2\sqrt{W_0}}{c_0}
 \sqrt{(T-s)\bigl(W(s)-W_T\bigr)},\\
 
 d_{\BL}(\lambda_T,\lambda_s)
 &\leq \frac{2\sqrt{W_0}}{c_0}
 \sqrt{(T-s)\bigl(W(s)-W_T\bigr)}.
\end{align}
Moreover, $\Var_T$ has generalized Euclidean mean-curvature vector
$H_{\Var_T}^{\R^4}\in L^2(\lVert\Var_T\rVert;\R^4)$ and
\begin{equation}
 
 \frac14\int_{\R^4}|H_{\Var_T}^{\R^4}|^2
 \dd\lVert\Var_T\rVert\leq W_T.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unique finite-time limit

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Sprinkling plus the Z^d theta-asymptotics. Result: The natural argument: at p = p_c(1+eps) the density of vertices in clusters of size at least K (K large but fixed relative to eps) on the torus is close to theta_{Z^d}(p) ~ c eps by local comparison with Z^d (finite clusters of bounded size are local), and sprinkling a further eps' << eps of open edges merges the large clusters into one giant of size about theta(p) V, provided large clusters are spread out enough that sprinkled edges connect them (the standard ADS/ Borgs et al. argument). The merging step needs that clusters of size >= K have a total number of boundary edges of order their size, which holds, and that any two such large clusters are within reach of a sprinkled edge, which needs the clusters to be 'well spread' in the torus (their vertices not confined to a small region); in d > 6 the large clusters at p above p_c have diameter of order eps^{-1/2}?? the correlation length scaling xi ~ eps^{-1/2} in mean field... but the clusters relevant have size eps V >> xi^d ... hmm: this is the crux: the merging argument works above the window because the giant's linear scale (V^{1/d}) exceeds the correlation length eps^{-1/2} only when eps >> V^{-2/d}, and V^{-2/d} << V^{-1/3} iff d > 6, so in d > 6 the whole regime eps >> V^{-1/3} lies above the correlation-length crossover: the giant is spread over the torus and sprinkling merges it. The remaining gap is quantitative: the second largest cluster o(eps V) needs a bound on the number of clusters of size between eps V delta and eps V, which requires the cluster-size tail P(|C| >= k) for the torus at eps above p_c, available only up to constants. The constant c: it is the right derivative of theta at p_c since the density of large clusters is theta(p_c(1+eps)) ~ c eps; identification of the constant is fine given the local comparison. Key identity: d > 6 <=> V^{-2/d} << V^{-1/3}: the whole supercritical regime above the window is above the correlation-length crossover, so sprinkling should merge large clusters. Obstruction: Uniform cluster-size tail bounds on the torus in the slightly supercritical regime are missing.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0068-concentration-and-uniqueness-of-the-giant-component-above-the-scaling
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

body:
For the ordinary nearest-neighbor hard-core model on Z^2 at uniform activity 0<lambda<=2.48, strong spatial mixing holds, hence the infinite-volume Gibbs measure is unique. Vera, Vigoda and Yang prove this using multi-type branching bounds and piecewise linear message functions certified by linear programming. They also prove a limitation of a specified Weitz-tree method: for every assignment sigma of a FIXED neighbor ordering to each graph vertex, the loop-boundary-pruned self-avoiding-walk tree T_saw^sigma(Z^2) does not have strong spatial mixing when lambda>3.4. If the ordering is homogeneous (the same ordering at every vertex), strong spatial mixing already fails for lambda>3. These are failures of strong spatial mixing on the computational trees; they do not prove phase coexistence on Z^2 at those activities. The fixed-vertex ordering hypothesis must be retained: this theorem is not automatically an obstruction for a path-dependent relative ordering based on the incoming edge, nor a ceiling for every conceivable SAW-tree contraction method.
Ordinary nearest-neighbor hard-core model on Z^2 with uniform activity
Positive SSM result: 0<lambda<=2.48
3.4 limitation: each graph vertex has a fixed neighbor ordering sigma_v; lambda>3.4
3 limitation: the fixed orderings are homogeneous; lambda>3
Loop-closing leaf pins are retained in the Weitz tree

[Defn def:VSSM at a distance of arXiv:2603.17858, 'Decay of correlations and zeros for the hard-core model'] Let $\varphi \colon \mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}^{+}$ be a function with positive
    values. 
    The hard-core model on a family $\mathcal{G}$ of bounded degree graphs satisfies
    \emph{very strong spatial mixing from distance $\varphi$ ($\varphi$-VSSM)} at a parameter $\lambda>0$ if there
    exist constants $\alpha\in[0,1),C>0$ such that for all $G=(V,E)\in\mathcal{G}$ and any induced subgraph $H$ of $G$ and $v\in V(H)$, and for all boundary conditions $\sigma,\tau:S_{T_{\mathrm{SAW}(H,v)}}(v,\ell)\to\{0,1\}$ we have
    \begin{equation}
        \abs{R_{(T_{\mathrm{SAW}(H,v)},\sigma),v}(\lambda)-R_{(T_{\mathrm{SAW}(H,v)},\tau),v}(\lambda)}\le C\cdot \alpha^{\ell}\quad \text{for all }\ell\geq \varphi(|V|).
        
    \end{equation}

Then, $(\mathcal{D}_{\max} (\mathcal{L}),
  \mathcal{L})$ generates a strongly continuous contraction semigroup on $L^2
  (\mu)$. Moreover, $(1 - \mathcal{L})^{- 1} \in L (L^2 (\mu))$ (uniquely)
  extends to an element $(1 - \mathcal{L})^{- 1} \in L (\mathcal{H}^1_0,
  \mathcal{H}^{- 1}_0)$ and it holds that $(1 - \mathcal{L}) \mathcal{C}
  \subset \mathcal{H}^{- 1}_0$ is dense.
