body:
[Proposition prop:reversal of arXiv:2608.05089, 'Correlation decay in area-tilted line ensembles'] There is some $\lambda_0 > 1$ and $C, c > 0$ such that for all $\lambda \geqslant \lambda_0$,
all $\varepsilon > 0$, all $k \in \mathbb{N}$, and all $t > 0$, there is a coupling (depending on $\varepsilon$, $k$, and $t$)
between $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ such that
\begin{equation}
    \mathbb{P} \mleft[
        X^i(0) - Y^i(0) \leqslant \varepsilon \text{ and }
        X^i(t) - Y^i(t) \leqslant \varepsilon
        \text{ for all } i \leqslant k
    \mright] \geqslant 1 - C e^{-c t}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Reversal coupling

[Theorem 52 (Nies--Paolini \cite{NP}) of arXiv:2608.26628, 'Open Problems in Mathematical Logic'] \begin{enumerate}[(1)]
        \item Let $G$ be a non-archimedean Roelcke precompact group. Then the group $\text{Aut}(G)$ of continuous automorphisms of $G$ carries a natural Polish topology and $\text{Inn}(G)$ is closed in it.
        \item Suppose in addition that $G$ is oligomorphic, then $\text{Out}(G) = \text{Aut}(G)/\text{Inn}(G)$ with the quotient topology is totally disconnected, locally compact (t.d.l.c.).
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own work draft; proof (unaudited), no novelty established. Let d>=2, E^T E=I_2, A_*=diag(1,3), and let the teacher be (1/3)sum_j N(a E A_*u_j,I_d), with unit equilateral vertices u_j. Use the canonical equal-weight identity-covariance mixture score and physical Euclidean unit-step population DDPM GD on all unrestricted mean parameters, initialized iid N(0,3a^2/(2d)). For 0<rho<=1/100, set sigma_0=1/(80 sqrt(d)), S=10 log(100/(sigma_0 rho)), a^2=c rho exp(-84(S+1)), gamma=2a^2/3 and N=ceil(S/gamma), with a sufficiently small absolute c. With probability at least 79/200, at time N the decomposition M_N=a b_N 1^T+a sqrt(3/2) Z_N V^T, V=sqrt(2/3)U^T, satisfies ||b_N||<=C a^4 and min_{O in O(2)}||Z_N-E A_*O||_F<rho. Throughout entry ||b_k||<=11, ||Z_k||_F<=5. The factor Z_N is within rho/8 of the anisotropic covariance surrogate at N gamma; its surrogate polar phase is uniform conditional on the right-invariant good initial event in either determinant branch, but the actual DDPM angle is only coupled to it. For fixed rho, N=O(C_rho d^420 log d). This is unrestricted population covariance entry, not a post-entry component-learning theorem, empirical sample guarantee, finite-precision guarantee, or full-DDPM bad-basin probability.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:484d17c19e8ad8dea511bb4df58d3080457473c0a2ac9732d95163ec7209f023","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/48/484d17c19e8ad8dea511bb4df58d3080457473c0a2ac9732d95163ec7209f023.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:ff2cc182d0748273dfe914f9bfb36ab5f57f3d4ab1489dc7dbca688581c0e2a0","bundle_entry_key":"t309-c17","bundle_id":"population.t309-unrestricted-anisotropic-ddpm-entry-draft","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian mixture learning and diffusion objectives","draft":"w721/bundle_010.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.learning:gaussian-mixture-ddpm-unrestricted-anisotropic-random-covariance-entry","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"Own work draft; T309-w721-C17 v1; proof (unaudited); Target 2 route 12 entry lemma.

# Unrestricted population DDPM GD reaches the anisotropic covariance orbit from iid means

This extends C10's finite-step comparison to C16's anisotropic surrogate. It supplies random covariance entry for actual population mean GD with a free centroid and arbitrary ambient directions. It does not supply the post-entry unrestricted angular trapping estimate, a component-learning guarantee, or a full-DDPM bad-basin probability. All dependencies remain unaudited; no novelty finding is claimed.

## Statement

Let d>=2, E^T E=I_2, A_*=diag(1,3), D=E A_*^2 E^T, and let the teacher be the equal-weight mixture of N(a E A_* u_j,I_d), with unit equilateral vertices u_j. Use the canonical equal-weight identity-covariance mixture score in the population single-time DDPM objective. Initialize all entries of the unrestricted d-by-3 mean matrix M_0 independently as N(0,3a^2/(2d)), and apply physical Euclidean unit-step GD.

For 0<rho<=1/100 put sigma_0=1/(80 sqrt(d)), S=10 log(100/(sigma_0 rho)). There is a sufficiently small absolute c>0 such that choosing

    a^2=c rho exp(-84(S+1)),
    gamma=2a^2/3, N=ceil(S/gamma)                       (1)

gives, with probability at least 79/200, a decomposition

    M_N=a b_N 1^T+a sqrt(3/2) Z_N V^T,
    ||b_N||<=C a^4,
    min_{O in O(2)}||Z_N-E A_* O||_F<rho.              (2)

Here V=sqrt(2/3)U^T, U=(u_1,u_2,u_3). Through the entry interval ||b_k||<=11 and ||Z_k||_F<=5. For fixed rho the step count is polynomial in d; this is a real-arithmetic population-gradient statement, not finite precision or finite samples.

The comparison also couples Z_N to the C16 surrogate at the fixed time N gamma within rho/8. Conditional on the stated good initialization event and either determinant branch, the SURROGATE polar angle is uniform. The actual angle is close to it but is not asserted to be uniform.

## 1. Free-mean coordinates and differentiated expansion

Every mean matrix has the unique orthogonal decomposition

    M=a b 1^T+a c_0 Z V^T, c_0=sqrt(3/2),
    b=M1/(3a), Z=MV/(a c_0).

Its metric is 3a^2||db||^2+c_0^2 a^2||dZ||_F^2. C06's free-centroid expansion, applied to this fixed bounded teacher geometry, gives

    F_a(b,Z)=a^2||b||^2
       +a^4[||ZZ^T-D||_F^2/4-b^T ZZ^T b]+a^6 H_a(b,Z). (3)

On ||b||<=11, ||Z||<=5, H_a and its first parameter derivatives have an absolute bound independent of d. This follows by the same finite-span dominated Gaussian/softmax Taylor estimate as C06/C10: the student locations, teacher plane and the finitely many differentiation directions span a bounded number of dimensions; the teacher unit locations have norm at most three. The change from an equilateral teacher to A_*u_j changes the constants and D, not the order or the metric. In particular no ambient ||Gaussian|| bound is used to claim dimension independence.

Physical unit-step GD is therefore exactly

    b_+=(I/3+(2a^2/3)ZZ^T)b-(a^4/3)partial_b H_a,
    Z_+=Z+gamma[f_D(Z)+2bb^T Z-a^2 grad_Z H_a],
    f_D(Z)=(D-ZZ^T)Z.                                (4)

For sufficiently small absolute a, these imply

    ||b_+||<=||b||/2+C a^4,
    ||b_k||<=2^(-k)||b_0||+2C a^4,                   (5)

as long as the shape stays in its stopped ball. Starting with ||b_0||<=10, this keeps ||b_k||<11.

## 2. The anisotropic comparison constants

On the Frobenius ball ||Z||<=5, the derivative of ZZ^T Z has operator norm at most 3||Z||^2. Since ||D||=9,

    Lip(f_D)<=9+3*25=84,
    ||f_D||<= (9+25)*5=170.                          (6)

Let z(s) solve z_dot=f_D(z), z(0)=Z_0. C16 bounds its norm by four on the Gaussian good event. Its one-step Euler defect is at most C gamma^2, using (6) along the bounded flow and the mean value theorem. Stop the exact GD comparison at the first possible exit from ||Z||<=5 or ||b||<=11. If e_k=||Z_k-z(k gamma)||, (4),(6) give

    e_{k+1}<=(1+84gamma)e_k
                    +Cgamma a^2+Cgamma||b_k||^2+Cgamma^2. (7)

From (5), ||b_k||^2<=2*4^(-k)||b_0||^2+C a^8. Its decaying part contributes a total unweighted impulse at most (8/3)gamma||b_0||^2. Applying the geometric series in (7), including the constant floor and Euler defect, gives

    e_k<=C a^2(1+||b_0||^2)exp(84k gamma).            (8)

For example the constant-forcing sum is bounded by its forcing divided by 84gamma times exp(84k gamma); no factor proportional to a^(-2) is left after this division. The centroid transient is bounded directly by its summable impulse times the maximal growth factor. These two different estimates avoid treating the order-one initial centroid as a persistent forcing.

For k<=N, k gamma<=S+gamma<=S+1. With ||b_0||<=10, choose c in (1) so (8)<=rho/8. Then ||Z_k||<=4+rho/8<5, while (5) keeps the centroid below 11. The stopped induction closes for the whole interval. This is a logarithmic-rescaled-time comparison, not a Gronwall argument over the slower component-identifying time.

## 3. Entry at the discrete terminal time

Since N gamma>=S, C16's factor-orbit bound still applies at time N gamma. Its two controlling bounds e^(-2s)(17+32s) and e^(-2s) decrease for all s>=S; the derivative of the former is e^(-2s)(-2-64s)<0. Thus

    min_O ||z(N gamma)-E A_*O||<rho/2.

Combining this with (8) gives the stronger factor bound 5rho/8<rho in (2). Formula (5) gives ||b_N||<=10*2^(-N)+C a^4=O(a^4). The last comparison uses N>=3/(2a^2), S>=1, and the elementary fact that exp(-c'/a^2)<=a^4 for all sufficiently small a. A sufficiently small absolute choice of c in (1) enforces this range uniformly in d and rho.

The actual and surrogate planar whitened factors are nonsingular at entry. They are within O(rho) of O(2), and the polar map is smooth with bounded derivative on a fixed neighborhood of that compact group. Thus their polar angles differ by O(rho), interpreted on the same determinant branch. Smoothness follows directly by differentiating C -> (CC^T)^(-1/2) C on a compact positive-definite spectral interval. This is a coupling statement, not rotational invariance of the exact DDPM field.

## 4. Probability and polynomial work

Orthogonal Gaussian projection gives Z_0 with iid N(0,1/d) entries and b_0~N(0,I_d/(2d)), independently. C16's right-invariant event E_good has probability at least 2/5. Since E||b_0||^2=1/2, Markov gives P(||b_0||>10)<=1/200. A union bound gives

    P(E_good and ||b_0||<=10)>=79/200.

The joint law and event are invariant under right rotations of Z_0 with b_0 unchanged, by the independence of those two Gaussian projections. C16 therefore supplies a uniform surrogate polar angle conditional on this joint event in either determinant branch. No product of dependent event probabilities is used.

For fixed rho, S=5 log d+C_rho. Consequently (1) chooses a^2=C'_rho d^(-420), and N=O(C''_rho d^420 log d); the dimension exponent is fixed, though enormous. We count exact population gradient access here. This estimate is not an empirical sample bound or a practical runtime claim. If rho varies, (1) is also a fixed polynomial in its inverse, up to the displayed logarithm.

## Scope and checks

C17 supplies unrestricted anisotropic covariance entry in arbitrary ambient dimension, paying the exact finite-step comparison left by C16. It does not make C15's centered planar trapping proof apply to the resulting configuration: the free centroid is small rather than identically zero, and perpendicular directions are small rather than absent. Their post-entry contraction and angular disturbances remain the hardest unpaid transfer. Nor does covariance matching identify all mixture components. General Target 2 remains open.

Exact finite checks in scripts/check_unrestricted_anisotropic_entry.py cover the physical metric and expansion gradient, the constants 84 and 170, probability arithmetic, transient-series coefficient and dimension exponent. They do not certify dominated Taylor differentiation, the stopped comparison, polar-map regularity or full-GD post-entry dynamics. [Prop 20 of arXiv:2607.04943, '\textbf{Approximation of Random Differential Equations Driven by Physical Brownian Motion '] (i) Let
	$$Y^\ep_3(t):=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\ep}}\int_t^\infty \E(\Phi(\xe_t,\bbxe_t,\ee_s)|\F^{t/\ep})ds,$$
	and
	$$\ze_3(t):=\lim_{h\to 0}\frac{1}{h}\E(\ye_3(t+h)-\ye_3(t)|\F^{t/\ep})\enspace \text{in probability},$$ then
	$$\ze_3(t)=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{\ep}}\Phi(\xe_t,\bbxe_t,\ee_t)+\sum_{i,j}\Theta^{ij}(\xe_t,\bbxe_t)W^{\ep,i}_tD^{\ep,j}_t\enspace\text{a.s.},$$ where $D^{\ep,j}_t:=\frac{1}{\ep}\int_t^\infty\E(\eta^{\ep,j}_s|\F^{t/\ep})ds.$
	
	(ii)
	Set $Q^{\ep,ij}_s:=W^{\ep,i}_sW^{\ep,j}_s+W^{\ep,i}_sD^{\ep,j}_s-\E(W^{\ep,i}_sW^{\ep,j}_s+W^{\ep,i}_sD^{\ep,j}_s)$. Let
	$$Y^\ep_4(t):=\int_t^\infty\E(\sum_{i,j}\Theta^{ij}(\xe_t,\bbxe_t)Q^{\ep,ij}_s|\F^{t/\ep})ds,$$ and$$\ze_4(t):=\lim_{h\to 0}\frac{1}{h}\E(\ye_4(t+h)-\ye_4(t)|\F^{t/\ep})\enspace \text{in probability},$$
	then $$\ze_4(t)=\mathcal{E}^\ep_t-\sum_{i,j}\Theta^{ij}(\xe_t,\bbxe_t)Q^{\ep,ij}_t,$$ where
	$$\mathcal{E}^\ep_t=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\ep}}\sum_{i,j}\Xi^{ij}(\xe_t,\bbxe_t,\we_t)\int_t^\infty\E(Q^{\ep,ij}_s|\F^{t/\ep})ds.$$
	
	(iii) The family of random variables $$\{h^{-1}\E[\ye_k(t+h)-\ye_k(t)|\F^{t/\ep}]:0<h<T, 0<t<T-h\}$$ is uniformly integrable for each $\ep\in (0,1],$ $k=3,4.$
	
	(iv) For each $p\geq 1$ and $t\in [0,T]$,
	$$\lim_{\ep\to 0}\|\ye_3(t)\|_p\vee\|\ye_4(t)\|_p\vee\Big\|\intot\mathcal{E}^\ep_rdr\Big\|_p=0.$$

[Lemma Lem.FinEnsSatGB of arXiv:2410.23899, 'Tightness for interlacing geometric random walk bridges'] Let $\vec{x}, \vec{y} \in \mathfrak{W}_k$, $T_0, T_1 \in \mathbb{Z}$ with $T_0 < T_1$, and $g: \llbracket T_0, T_1 \rrbracket \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}$ be an increasing path. Suppose that $\Omega_{\mathsf{Inter}}(T_0, T_1, \vec{x}, \vec{y}, \infty,g) \neq \emptyset$ and $\mathfrak{Q}$ has law $\mathbb{P}_{\mathsf{Inter}, \operatorname{Geom}}^{T_0,T_1, \vec{x}, \vec{y}, \infty, g}$ as in Definition (DefSGP of the paper). Define the $\llbracket 1, k+1 \rrbracket$-indexed geometric line ensemble $\mathfrak{L}: \llbracket 1, k+1 \rrbracket \times \llbracket T_0, T_1 \rrbracket \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}$ through
$$\mathfrak{L}(i,j) = \mathfrak{Q}(i,j) \mbox{ for } i \in \llbracket 1, k \rrbracket, j \in \llbracket T_0, T_1 \rrbracket, \mbox{ and } \mathfrak{L}(k+1,j) = g(j) \mbox{ for } j \in \llbracket T_0, T_1 \rrbracket.$$
Then, $\mathfrak{L}$ satisfies the interlacing Gibbs property from Definition (DefSGP of the paper) with $N = k+1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: In mathematics, the Cheeger constant of a graph is a numerical measure of whether or not a graph has a "bottleneck". The Cheeger constant as a measure of "bottleneckedness" is of great interest in many areas: for example, constructing well-connected networks of computers, card shuffling. The graph theoretical notion originated after the Cheeger isoperimetric constant of a compact Riemannian manifold.

general i.i.d. edge-weight distributions on Z^d - the point of the paper is removing the special-distribution restriction under which such statements were previously proved
the conclusion is anti-concentration (an interval-avoidance statement), NOT a variance lower bound
the log||x|| variance lower bound it cites is available only in two dimensions

WHY THE DISTINCTION IS NOT PEDANTRY: an anti-concentration statement bounds how much mass the law of T(0,x) can put in a short interval. It does not by itself lower-bound the variance, and a variance lower bound does not by itself give anti-concentration. Chaining them silently is a category error.
METHOD: inducing a fluctuation in the number of edges in a box whose weights are of 'hi-mode' (large).
THE LITERATURE STATEMENT IS THE SECOND REASON THIS NODE EXISTS: it is a dated, first-hand confirmation from four people working directly on the problem that Newman-Piza's logarithmic bound had not been improved.
SOURCE: arXiv:1810.08270v2, 'Lower bounds for fluctuations in first-passage percolation for general distributions'. Official arXiv API record retrieved by lane P4 on 2026-08-22.
VERIFICATION STATUS: theorem-checked-against-source at abstract level for both the conclusion shape and the literature statement; the proof was not read and the precise 'general distributions' hypothesis is not stated in the abstract.
title: Damron-Hanson-Houdre-Xu (2019) prove ANTI-CONCENTRATION rather than a variance lower bound: for GENERAL edge-weight distributions on Z^d they show T(0,x) is with high probability not contained in an interval of size o(log||x||)^{1/2}, with similar statements for first-passage percolation in thin cylinders. In the same abstract they record that the log||x|| variance lower bound was found in the 1990s and 'there has not been any improvement since'.

body:
[Lemma 23 (Nesterov look-ahead risk control) of arXiv:2609.02728, 'Momentum in large-batch training: Polyak enlarges the critical batch size, Nesterov improv'] Assume the stable small-step condition \(\eta\lambda_1\le c_{\rm st}\), where \(c_{\rm st}>0\) is sufficiently small.  Then the look-ahead risk admits the coordinate expansion
\[
    \mathcal L_m
    =
    \frac12\sum_{j\ge1}\lambda_j
    \left((1+\rho)e_m(j)-\rho e_{m-1}(j)\right)^2.
\]
Moreover, the deterministic look-ahead risk is comparable to the next deterministic Nesterov risk:
\[
    \frac12\sum_{j\ge1}\lambda_j
    \left((1+\rho)e_m^{\mathrm{det}}(j)-\rho e_{m-1}^{\mathrm{det}}(j)\right)^2
    \eqsim
    \cS_{\nesterov}(m+1).
\]
For the stochastic iterates, the corresponding expectation-level control is
\[
    c\,\mathbb{E}\mathcal E_{m+1}-C\frac{\eta^2\sigma^2}{B}
    \le
    \mathbb{E}\mathcal L_m
    \le
    C\,\mathbb{E}\mathcal E_{m+1},
\]
where the constants are independent of \(m,\eta,\rho,B\).

[Corollary 13 (Finite jets and naturality) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] For every \(M\geq0\), the associative realization induces an injection
\[
 L/\gamma_{M+1}(D)\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow T(V)/J^{M+1}.
\]
Its successive normal quotients are \(L/D\) in order zero and
\(\gamma_r(D)/\gamma_{r+1}(D)\) in orders \(1\leq r\leq M\).
Every linear map \(A:V\to W\) induces compatible maps
\begin{equation}
 Q(A):Q(V)\longrightarrow Q(W),
 \qquad
 Q(A)(\rho_vq)=\rho_{Av}Q(A)(q),
 
\end{equation}
and hence a graded Hopf homomorphism
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak N(A):
 T(Q(V))\#_\rho S(V)\longrightarrow T(Q(W))\#_\rho S(W).
 
\end{equation}
Under \eqref{cc:eq-normal-cone}, this is the normal-cone map induced
by \(T(A)\).  Hence \(G^{\mathrm{full}}_{n,r}\) is a homogeneous
degree-\(n\) polynomial functor, and \(E^{\mathrm{full}}_{n,r}\) is its
contravariant algebraic dual.  These assertions remain algebraically
valid for infinite-dimensional \(V\).

[Theorem thm:main-thm-limit-shape of arXiv:2606.06612, 'The limit shape and emergence of the \\ Discrete Gaussian level lines'] Fix $\beta>0$ large enough and consider $\phi\sim \pi^0_\Lambda$, the $(2+1)$\textsc{d}  \ensuremath{\mathbb Z\textsc{gff}}\xspace on $\Lambda=\llbracket 1,L\rrbracket^2$ with a floor and zero boundary conditions. Set $H(L)$ and $N_n$ per (eq:H-def,eq:Nn-def of the paper). Fix $m\geq 1$, and let ${\ensuremath{\mathscr L}}_n$ ($n=0,\ldots,m$) be obtained by placing the 4 quadrants of the Wulff shape $\ensuremath{\mathcal W}$ defined above, rescaled by $N_n$, in the 4 corners of $\Lambda$, and joining them via straight lines along  $\partial \Lambda$. Let $\mathfrak{L}_n$ be the \texttt{large} $(H+1-n)$ level line loop(s) of $\phi$.
Then, with probability $1-O(L^{-10})$:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item{} For each $1\leq n\leq m$, $\mathfrak{L}_n$ is a single loop that satisfies $d_\ensuremath{\mathcal H}(\mathfrak{L}_n,{\ensuremath{\mathscr L}}_n)< N_n e^{-\sqrt{\log L}}$.

\item{} For $n=0$, either $\mathfrak{L}_0$ is empty (no \texttt{large} $(H+1$) level-line loops), or it is a single loop that satisfies $d_\ensuremath{\mathcal H}(\mathfrak{L}_0, {\ensuremath{\mathscr L}}_0) < N_0 e^{-\sqrt{\log L}}$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:coarse-graining of arXiv:2608.30829, 'Free energy and phase transition for\\ 2D directed polymers with critical spatial correlat'] There exists a (small) constant \(\eta = \eta(d)\) such that, if there exists \(L \in \mathbb{N}\) and \(\beta>0\) such that 
  \begin{equation}
    
    \sup_{ f \in \mathcal{M}_1(\sqrt{L})} \mathbb{E}\Big[ W_L^{\beta}(f)^{1/2} \Big] \leq \eta_d \,,
  \end{equation}
  then for all \(N\in \mathbb{N}\), we have
  \[
  \sup_{ f \in \mathcal{M}_1(\sqrt{L})} \mathbb{E}\Big[ W_N^{\beta}(f)^{1/2} \Big] \leq 3 \, \mathrm{e}^{-N/L} \,.
  \]

body:
[Definition Recursive Terminal Attachment of arXiv:2608.12415, 'Sharp Phase Transition for Ellipsoid Fitting'] Let \(s\) be a square vertex. A recursive terminal attachment at \(s\) is
generated by the following rules.

\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Base case: \(h_2\)-attachment.}
    The attachment may be a single \(h_2\)-edge from \(s\) to a circle vertex
    \(a\):
    \[
        s \xrightarrow{h_2} a .
    \]

    \item \textbf{Concatenated-path attachment.}
    For any \(t \ge 1\), let \(\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_t\) be backbone-dangling
    shapes with compatible circle boundaries, and let
    \[
        \mathcal{R}=\tau_t \circ \tau_{t-1}\circ \cdots \circ \tau_1
    \]
    denote their proper concatenation. If \(U_\mathcal{R}\) and \(V_calR\) are the left
    and right circle boundary vertices of \(\mathcal{R}\), then \(\mathcal{R}\) may be attached
    to \(s\) by adding two \(h_1\)-edges connecting \(s\) to \(U_\mathcal{R}\) and
    \(V_\mathcal{R}\). That is, we add
    \[
        U_\mathcal{R} \xrightarrow{h_1} s \xrightarrow{h_1} V_\mathcal{R} .
    \]
    When \(U_\mathcal{R}=V_\mathcal{R}\), we use the diagonal convention and attach \(s\) to
    this single circle vertex by two parallel \(h_1\)-edges. \anote{I don't think we want to allow this as if $U_\mathcal{R}=V_\mathcal{R}$ then we either don't have a proper concatenation or $t = 0$.}
\end{enumerate}

Own-work proof draft (unaudited), no novelty priority claimed. Fix a finite oracle table and all other interfaces independently of a random erased row set H. Each row is included with marginal probability at most delta; different row indicators need not be independent. A nonnegative weight algorithm is monotone under complete-row erasure and has at most t positive-query rows on each reference run. Its reference normalizer is positive. Then its expected relative mass loss after erasing H is at most t*delta. For epsilon,alpha in (0,1), except with probability at most t*delta/epsilon, every partial erasure A contained in H simultaneously has KL(P_A || (1-alpha)P_H+alpha*Uniform) <= log(1/(1-alpha)) + epsilon/(1-epsilon)*(log|X|+log(1/alpha)). The comparison law is independent of the protected-bit assignment A. This is an auxiliary lemma, not an oracle existence proof; monotonicity and independence are essential.
A fixed reference oracle and fixed other interfaces independent of the random erased set, or the stated conditional marginal bound.
Nonnegative weights monotonically decrease under whole-row erasure; reference total weight positive.
At most t positive-query rows per output; each row erased with marginal probability at most delta.
0<epsilon<1 and 0<alpha<1.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:a779800c4944e3afadf84bffdd212c01f0512971f1df7e414f8bd4104138bb7e","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/a7/a779800c4944e3afadf84bffdd212c01f0512971f1df7e414f8bd4104138bb7e.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:e9089ff16a3df49fc1d91f4ede3602b031163aba909e7ad3b360042dd0d5187d","bundle_entry_key":"random-row-erasure-normalized-weight-stability","bundle_id":"population.t410-padded-nested-mask-oracle-separation-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"oracle complexity; average-case complexity; autoregressive models; forward KL; random masks","draft":"w739/bundle_008.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:complexity.cryptography:random-row-erasure-normalized-weight-stability","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Random row erasure: uniform robustness over all remaining protected bits

T410-w739-C014 v1. Kind: bound. Target: 2.
Status: proof (unaudited). An auxiliary construction lemma; no full oracle
construction, target closure, or novelty priority is claimed.

## Exact setup

Fix a finite binary oracle table T, partitioned into rows, and fix all other
oracle interfaces. For a row subset A let T_A replace every bit in the rows
of A by zero, retaining all other answers. A fixed deterministic weight
algorithm on the finite output space X computes nonnegative weights v_A(x)
using T_A and those fixed interfaces. Its reference run on T queries at most
t distinct rows containing a queried positive bit, for each x. Repeated
queries to a row count once; an ordinary t-query bound suffices.

The essential restriction is ROW-ERASURE MONOTONICITY:

    A subset B implies 0 <= v_B(x) <= v_A(x), for every x.

This concerns erasure of complete rows, not arbitrary changes of individual
bits. Let u=v_empty, Z=sum_x u(x)>0. Choose a random row set H, independently
of the fixed reference table, weight algorithm and other interfaces, with
Pr[y in H] <= delta for each row y. Independence of different row indicators
is NOT required. More generally all statements hold conditionally on data
fixing the reference system, if these marginal bounds hold conditionally.

Write Z_A=sum_x v_A(x), r(H)=(Z-Z_H)/Z. For 0<epsilon<1 and 0<alpha<1:

1. E r(H) <= t delta and Pr[r(H)>epsilon] <= t delta/epsilon.
2. On r(H)<=epsilon, Z_A>0 for EVERY A subset H, simultaneously.
   Put P_A=v_A/Z_A, Q_H=v_H/Z_H, U=uniform(X), and
   Q_alpha=(1-alpha)Q_H+alpha U. Then, simultaneously for every A subset H,

   KL(P_A || Q_alpha) <= log(1/(1-alpha))
       + [epsilon/(1-epsilon)] [log |X| + log(1/alpha)].

The simultaneity is pointwise over all A subset H; no union bound over the
exponentially many possible protected-bit assignments is taken.

## Proof of the random loss bound

For each x with u(x)>0, let R_x be the positive-query rows on its reference
run. If H misses R_x, the run on T_H has exactly the same transcript: at
each step a reference zero answer stays zero, and a reference one answer
lies outside H. Induction over the deterministic computation gives
v_H(x)=u(x). Always 0<=u(x)-v_H(x)<=u(x), by row-erasure monotonicity.
For u(x)=0 monotonicity also forces v_H(x)=0. Therefore

 E[u(x)-v_H(x)] <= u(x) Pr[H intersects R_x] <= u(x) t delta.

Sum over the finite set X and divide by Z. Markov's inequality gives (1).
Both steps use only marginal row bounds and a finite union bound.

## Proof uniform over all protected-bit assignments

Fix H with r=r(H)<=epsilon<1. For any A subset H, monotonicity gives
v_H<=v_A<=u pointwise, so Z_A>=Z_H=(1-r)Z>0. Define

 gamma_A=(Z_A-Z_H)/Z_A <= r/(1-r) <= epsilon/(1-epsilon).

If gamma_A>0 let R_A=(v_A-v_H)/(Z_A-Z_H), a probability law. Then exactly

 P_A=(1-gamma_A) Q_H + gamma_A R_A.

If gamma_A=0, P_A=Q_H and choose R_A arbitrarily. This identity holds for
every A, regardless of how A is selected after seeing H or the reference
table. In particular it remains valid if those choices encode all the
protected NP truth bits.

Introduce a binary component label for the two mixtures. The relative
entropy between their joint laws, followed by discarding that label, gives

 KL(P_A || Q_alpha) <= d(gamma_A || alpha) + gamma_A KL(R_A || U).

For completeness the discarding inequality is the finite log-sum inequality:
if a_i,b_i>=0, b_i>0 whenever a_i>0, then
sum a_i log(a_i/b_i) >= (sum a_i) log(sum a_i/sum b_i).
Normalize the a_i; it follows from Jensen for the convex function -log.
Apply it separately at every x to the two labeled masses. Zero labeled
masses are interpreted by continuity, or omitted. U has full support.

Since KL(R_A||U)=log|X|-entropy(R_A)<=log|X| and binary entropy is
nonnegative,

 d(gamma||alpha) <= log(1/(1-alpha)) + gamma log(1/alpha).

Substitution proves (2). Every probability space here is finite.

## Length-indexed consequence and efficient smoothing

For |X_n|=2^{L_n}, t_n polynomial in n and L_n polynomial in n, take
delta_n=2^{-floor(sqrt(n))}, epsilon_n=n^{-k}, alpha_n=epsilon_n, n>=2.
The failure bound t_n delta_n/epsilon_n is summable for each fixed k.
The first Borel-Cantelli lemma (proved directly by the union bound on the
tail of this convergent series) implies the displayed KL bound eventually
almost surely. No independence between lengths is needed. Taking k larger
than the polynomial degree of L_n plus any desired error exponent makes
the KL error smaller than that inverse polynomial, eventually. A countable
intersection permits every fixed uniform family satisfying the hypotheses
and every fixed desired exponent, if the conditional marginal hypotheses
hold for each family. This does not provide those hypotheses for a live
oracle construction.

If Q_H already has a polynomial-size AR representation with polynomial-bit
rational next-bit probabilities, the mixture also has one: compute its
prefix probabilities Q_H(h) by multiplying at most L such probabilities,
and use

 [(1-alpha)Q_H(hb)+alpha 2^{-(|h|+1)}]
 / [(1-alpha)Q_H(h)+alpha 2^{-|h|}].

For dyadic polynomial-bit alpha this uses polynomial time and bit length.
No exact evaluation of a general rational-weight partition function is
claimed. The efficient representation of Q_H remains an extra obligation.

## Exact limits of this construction step

The result resolves one potential stability step under explicit hypotheses:
all protected-bit choices inside H can be installed after obtaining the
loss bound. It does not require an additional probability union bound over
those choices. It cannot be applied when future helper answers depend on H
in a way invalidating the reference marginal calculation.

Row-erasure monotonicity includes weights that require a positive witness
for every row whose answers affect them: erasing any queried row kills its
positive certificate. It can include residual witness filters of the form
O(y,w) times [1-O(y,R(y))] when R and other interfaces are fixed and erasing
the row kills the first factor. It does not include arbitrary oracle
weights, nor filters whose helper algorithm changes after erasure.

Here is an exact negative control for dropping monotonicity. Take N rows
with one known reference bit 1 in each; delete one uniformly random row,
so delta=1/N. Give a dummy output weight 1 and output y weight
M*[1-O(y)]. Under the reference table only the dummy has positive weight.
After erasure the erased-row output has probability M/(1+M). Its TV
distance from the reference law is M/(1+M), not O(t delta), although each
output uses one query. New support is created, rather than removed.
The negative control does not refute constructions hiding the old positive
witnesses; it identifies the extra fact such a construction must prove.

The remaining Target 2 bottlenecks are (i) a corresponding stability theorem
for arbitrary efficient weights with hidden witnesses and existing helpers,
(ii) mutually consistent polynomial-size AR helpers, and (iii) NP circuit
hardness after adding every helper. Pinto's Remark 3.7 in Quantitative limit theorems for generalized Polya urns with applications to random tree models, arXiv:2607.07309. Take five colours, with the colours in the displayed order, and replacement matrix R=[[0,0,4,0,2],[2,4,0,0,0],[0,0,3,3,0],[2,0,0,4,0],[0,6,0,0,0]]. All row sums are lambda=6. All entries are nonnegative, so the urn is tenable from any initial composition. Its positive off-diagonal directed graph is strongly connected, so it is irreducible. Let J_4=diag(1,1,1,1,0), let C_4=[I_4|-1_4], where 1_4 is the all-ones column, and let symm(A)=(A+A^T)/2. The matrix G=symm(C_4 J_4(R^T-6I_5)C_4^T)=[[-6,-2,2,1],[-2,-8,-3,-3],[2,-3,-3,3/2],[1,-3,3/2,-2]] satisfies z^T G z=6 for z=(-1,1,-1,-1)^T. Hence lambda_max(G)>0, so no A>0 exists, and the strict negative contractivity condition of Remark 3.7 with p=d-1 fails for this tenable irreducible urn under this ordering of colours. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
The matrix, ordering of colours, and p=4 truncation are exactly those displayed.

body:
[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2511.04938, 'Uniform dimension theorems for parabolic SPDEs'] Consider an $\R^p$-valued random field $\{ Z(s) \}_{s\in I}$
	where $I\subset\R^N$ is a non-random, compact, upright
	rectangle. Choose and fix $\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_N \in (0\,,1]$, and 
	metrize $I$ using
	$\mathsf{d}(s\,,s') = \sum_{j=1}^N |s_j-s'_j|^{\alpha_j}$
	for all $s,s'\in I.$
	For every $n \in \N$, $\delta \in (0\,,1)$, $\nu \in \R^p$, 
	and $r > 0$, define
	\begin{align}\begin{split}
		&\mathcal{N}_n^\delta(\nu\,, r) = \# \{ s \in F_n^\delta : Z(s) \in B(\nu\,, r) \}, \text{ where}\\
		&F_n^\delta = I \cap \bigcup_{j_1,\ldots,j_N\in\Z}
		\left\{ (j_1 2^{-(1+\delta)n/\alpha_1}, 
		\dots, j_N 2^{-(1+\delta)n/\alpha_N} )\right\},
	\end{split}\end{align}
	and suppose that the following two conditions hold:
	\begin{compactenum}[(i)]
	\item For every $\varepsilon\in(0\,,1)$,
		$\sup_{s,s'\in I:s\neq s'}\| Z(s)-Z(s')\|/\mathsf{d}(s\,,s')^{1-\varepsilon}<\infty;$
	\item For every  $R>0$, $\lim_{\delta\to0+}\limsup_{n\to\infty} n^{-1} \sup_{\nu \in B(0, R)}
		\log \mathcal{N}_n^\delta(\nu\,, 2^{-n}) =0$ a.s.\
	\end{compactenum}
	Then, there exists a $\P$-null set off which
	$\dimh  Z(G) = \dim_{_{\rm H}}^\rho G$,
	uniformly for all compact sets $G \subset I$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 21 of arXiv:2511.04938

[Proposition propositionnoinvariance of arXiv:2606.01664, 'Brown measure convergence for the spectrum of polynomials in Ginibre matrices'] Assume that $Z$ is irreducible for the coefficient family, which means 
$$
\text{there does not exist any }0\neq W\subsetneq Z\text{ such that }R_\ell W\subset W\quad \forall \ell.
$$ Then except in the following degenerate case where $$\Sigma_R=0,\quad \mathcal{D}_R=\operatorname{End}(Z),\quad Y(E)=0,$$ the following holds:
$$
0\neq E\subset \mathcal{D}_R\Rightarrow Y(E)\nsubseteq E.
$$ Moreover, $E$ cannot be a left ideal of $\operatorname{End}(Z)$ and we also have
$$
\dim Y(E)-\dim (E\cap Y(E))\geq1.
$$

[Theorem thm:intGeo of arXiv:2505.09604, 'Exceptional force, uncountably many solutions in the KPZ fixed point'] On an event of probability one, the following holds for every $\xi\in\Xi$. Let $b$ be a $\xi$-eternal solution, and let $\tau^-$ and $\tau^+$ be the associated elements of $\overline \mathcal{T}^-$ and $\overline \mathcal{T}^+$ from the bijection in Theorem (thm:mr of the paper). 
    \begin{enumerate} [label=(\roman*), font=\normalfont]
        \item If $p$ lies strictly to the left of $\tau^-$, then the set of $b$-geodesics equals the set of all $\xi-$ geodesics starting from $p$, and all $b$-geodesics from $p$ lie strictly to the left of $\tau^-$.
        \item If $p$ lies strictly to the right of $\tau^+$, then the set of $b$-geodesics started from $p$ equals the set of all $\xi+$ geodesics starting from $p$, and all $b$-geodesics from $p$ lie strictly to the right of $\tau^+$.
        \item If $p$ lies  between $\tau^-$ and $\tau^+$ (possibly on one of the interfaces), then the set of $b$-geodesics  started from $p$ equals the union of the set of all $\xi-$ geodesics and the set of all $\xi+$  geodesics starting from $p$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:intGeo of arXiv:2505.09604

[Lemma 9 (localised scalar oscillator) of arXiv:2609.01093, 'Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold'] Let $\breg\in(\frac12,1)$, $0<T\le1$, $a_0,a_1\in\mathbb C$, and
$g\in L^2(\Real)$.  With
\[
 C_\lambda(t):=\cos(t|\lambda|),\qquad
 S_\lambda(t):=\frac{\sin(t|\lambda|)}{|\lambda|},\quad S_0(t):=t,
\]
put
\[
 u_\lambda(t):=\chi(t)C_\lambda(t)a_0+\chi(t)S_\lambda(t)a_1
 +\chi(t/T)\int_0^tS_\lambda(t-t')g(t') dt'.
\]
Then, uniformly in $\lambda$ and $T$,
\begin{equation}
 \big\|\Omega_\lambda\widetilde u_\lambda\big\|_{L^2_\tau}
 \le C(\chi,\breg)\Big(
 \langle\lambda\rangle|a_0|+|a_1|
 +T^{1-\breg}\|g\|_{L^2_t}\Big).
\end{equation}

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Regular-tree equality and a local-entropy countercheck Result: On a deterministic b-ary tree, symmetry makes harmonic measure uniform on children for every transient bias lambda<b, so its dimension is log b, independent of lambda. Thus strict monotonicity must exclude deterministic offspring. A local root-entropy proof also fails: attach regular trees of branching 2 and 4 as two root subtrees. Their escape probabilities are 1-lambda/2 and 1-lambda/4 for lambda<2; last-exit child probabilities are proportional to these values and become more unequal as lambda increases toward 2, so their entropy decreases. Check: The two-child example is not an iid Galton-Watson tree. Its role is to disprove a pointwise local entropy monotonicity claim, not the global dimension conjecture. Obstruction: Global dimension averages local entropy under a bias-dependent law of the environment seen along the ray. Controlling that changing law remains necessary.

[Prop branchingMPhi of arXiv:2510.23430, 'On the Martin boundary for discrete TASEP'] Let $\Phi_1,\Phi_2\in\mathcal{F}$. Then for any $n\geq 0$ and $\lambda,\nu\in \mathbb{G}^p_n$ we have
$$
M_n^{\Phi_1\Phi_2}(\lambda/\nu)=\sum_{\mu\in \mathbb{G}_n^p}M_n^{\Phi_1}(\lambda/\mu)M_n^{\Phi_2}(\mu/\nu).
$$

[Lemma Le:exp of arXiv:2411.04116, 'Poisson genericity in numeration systems with exponentially mixing probabilities'] Let $\mu$ be an invariant  and exponentially $\psi$-mixing measure on $\Omega^{\mathbb N}$ with contraction ratio  $\rho$.
Let $S\subset \mathbb R^+$ be  a finite union of bounded intervals.
  For each $k\in \mathbb N$,  for each fixed $w \in \Omega^k$,  the following hold

\begin{enumerate}
\item 
$ {\mathds{E}}_\mu\left[ M_k^w(S) \right]=

|S|+O(\rho^k),
 $
 \item ${\mathds{E}}_\mu\left[ \left( M_k^w(S) \right)^2 \right] 
 
 =\left| S \right| + \left| S \right|^2  + O\left( k \rho^k \right)  + O\pare{\sum_{\ell \in \pi_w} \rho^\ell}, $
 
 \item 
 $     \mathbb V_{\mu}(M_k^w(S)) = \left| S \right| + O(k \rho^k) 
    + O\pare{\sum_{\ell \in \pi_w} \rho^\ell},
$

where $\pi_w$ are the periods of the word $w\in \Omega^k$ and the hidden constant in the $O$-term only depends on~$S$.
\end{enumerate}

[Definition of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions on co-evolutionary networks'] The space of node-edge probability-graphons with node features in \(\mathcal{X}\) and edge weights in
	\(\mathcal{Y}\) is defined as
	\[
		\mathcal{N}(\mathcal{X})\mathcal{E}(\mathcal{Y}) := \mathcal{P}_{\nu}(\mathcal{X}\times[0,1]) \times \mathcal{P}_{\nu\otimes\nu}(\mathcal{Y}\times[0,1]^2).
	\]
	We also define the corresponding subset with node features in a fibered Wasserstein space of order \(p,q\in [1,\infty)\): 
	\[
		\mathcal{N}_{p,q}(\mathcal{X})\mathcal{E}(\mathcal{Y}) := \mathcal{P}_{p,q,\nu}(\mathcal{X}\times[0,1]) \times \mathcal{P}_{\nu\otimes\nu}(\mathcal{Y}\times[0,1]^2).
	\] 
	For any pair \((\mu,q),(\bar{\mu},\bar{q})\in \mathcal{N}(\mathcal{X})\mathcal{E}(\mathcal{Y})\), we define the coupled labeled and unlabeled distances as follows: 
	\[
		\begin{aligned}
			d_{(\text{BL},1),(\text{BL},\square)}((\mu,q),(\bar{\mu},\bar{q})) &= d_{\text{BL},1}(\mu,\bar{\mu}) + d_{\text{BL},\square}(q,\bar{q}), \\ 
			\delta_{(\text{BL},1),(\text{BL},\square)}((\mu,q),(\bar{\mu},\bar{q})) &= \inf_{\varphi \in S_{[0,1]}} d_{(\text{BL},1),(\text{BL},\square)}((\mu,q),(\bar{\mu},\bar{q})^{\varphi}),
		\end{aligned}
	\]
	where \((\bar{\mu},\bar{q})^{\varphi}\) denotes the joint rearrangement of the node-edge probability-graphon
	by \(\varphi\), {\it i.e.}, \((\bar{\mu},\bar{q})^{\varphi} = (\bar{\mu}^{\varphi},\bar{q}^{\varphi})\). 
	
	Similarly, for any pair \((\mu,q),(\bar{\mu},\bar{q})\in \mathcal{N}_{p,q}(\mathcal{X})\mathcal{E}(\mathcal{Y})\),
	we define the corresponding distances:
	\[
		\begin{aligned}
		d_{(W_p,q),(\text{BL},\square)}((\mu,q),(\bar{\mu},\bar{q})) &= d_{W_p,q}(\mu,\bar{\mu}) + d_{\text{BL},\square}(q,\bar{q}), \\ 
		\delta_{(W_p,q),(\text{BL},\square)}((\mu,q),(\bar{\mu},\bar{q})) &= \inf_{\varphi \in S_{[0,1]}} d_{(W_p,q),(\text{BL},\square)}((\mu,q),(\bar{\mu},\bar{q})^{\varphi}).
		\end{aligned}
	\]
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions '

[Corollary 37 (Propagation of $T_2$ for the nonlinear law) of arXiv:2608.28827, 'Quantitative Target Convergence and Uniform-in-Time\\ Propagation of Chaos for Langevin-Re'] Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:core-target}, \ref{ass:W2}, and
\ref{ass:initial-T2}, the nonlinear law satisfies
\begin{equation}
    \mu_t\in T_2(C_t),
    \qquad C_t\le C(1+C_0)e^{\ell t},

[Proposition 12 of arXiv:2604.13819, 'Convolution, cumulants and infinitesimal generators in the formal power series ring'] Consider $j \ge i \ge 1$ with $j-i \in 2\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$. Let $\bm{a}=(a_1,\dots, a_i) \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}^i$ and $\bm{b}=(b_1,\dots, b_j) \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}^j$ be tuples such that $a_r-b_r>0$ for all $1\le r \le i$. Then we obtain
$$
\mathcal{H}^{(-1)} \begin{bmatrix}
\bm{b}\\
\bm{a}
\end{bmatrix} (z) = M_X(z)
$$
where $X$ is a random variable distributed as 
$$
\text{\rm Beta}(b_1, a_1-b_1) \circledast \cdots \circledast \text{\rm Beta}(b_i, a_i-b_i) \circledast \text{\rm Ga}(b_{i+1})\circledast \dots \circledast \text{\rm Ga}(b_j),
$$
where $\mu \circledast \nu$ denotes the classical multiplicative convolution, that is, the distribution of the product $XY$ of two independent positive random variables $X \sim \mu$ and $Y \sim \nu$.

body: The conditional probability of A given B (with P(B) > 0) is P(A | B) = P(A intersect B) / P(B). Events A, B are independent iff P(A intersect B) = P(A)P(B), equivalently P(A|B) = P(A). The multiplication rule P(A intersect B) = P(A|B)P(B) and the law of total probability P(A) = sum_i P(A | B_i) P(B_i) over a partition {B_i} follow directly.

body: In graph theory, the Robertson–Seymour theorem states that the undirected graphs, partially ordered by the graph minor relationship, form a well-quasi-ordering. Equivalently, every family of graphs that is closed under taking minors can be defined by a finite set of forbidden minors, in the same way that Wagner's theorem characterizes the planar graphs as being the graphs that do not have the complete graph or the complete bipartite graph as minors.

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For statistical mechanics models on a torus whose Hamiltonian and lattice satisfy reflection positivity across midplanes between sites, the Gaussian domination (infrared) bound gives an upper bound on the Fourier transform of the two-point function: hat{G}(k) <= C / (beta E(k)), where E(k) is the quadratic energy form of the interaction (e.g. E(k)=sum_i (1-cos k_i) for nearest-neighbor coupling) and C is an explicit constant (often 1/2; exact value depends on normalization and is not always recalled precisely across variants). Combined with a spin-wave/Gaussian domination inequality this yields, for models such as the classical Heisenberg or XY model in dimension d>=3, or the Ising model in sufficiently high dimension, existence of long-range order at low temperature via a second-moment argument applied to the infrared-bounded Fourier integral. It does not give critical exponent values, does not apply in dimension d<=2 where the infrared integral diverges (consistent with the Mermin-Wagner theorem ruling out continuous-symmetry breaking there), and requires the specific reflection-positive algebraic structure; it gives no control for models lacking this symmetry, such as many disordered, frustrated, or non-bipartite systems. Typical failure: Assuming reflection positivity survives a seemingly minor modification of the Hamiltonian, such as adding next-nearest-neighbor terms, a random field, or working on a non-bipartite lattice, without re-checking the checkerboard decomposition; reflection positivity is a delicate algebraic property that most natural perturbations destroy, so the infrared bound and everything built on it, including the Frohlich-Simon-Spencer long-range order conclusion, silently stops applying. Canonical reference: Frohlich, Simon and Spencer, 1976, Communications in Mathematical Physics; Frohlich, Israel, Lieb and Simon, 1978, Communications in Mathematical Physics.

translation invariance, typically verified on a torus with periodic boundary conditions
finite-range or sufficiently decaying interaction with a well-defined quadratic energy function E(k)
dimension d>=3 so the infrared integral of 1/E(k) is finite

[Definition 9 of arXiv:2608.30859, 'Conservation Laws with Discontinuous Flux:\\ A First Application to Traffic Flow'] A vector field $H : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ is said to have 
    \emph{locally bounded directional variation} if, for every 
    $(t_0,x_0) \in \mathbb{R}^2$, there exist $\delta>0$ and a constant $C>0$
    such that
    \[
    \sum_{i=1}^N 
    \bigl| H(t_i,x_i) - H(t_{i-1},x_{i-1}) \bigr|
    \;\le\; C
    \]
    for every finite sequence $(t_i,x_i)$, $i=0,\ldots,N$, satisfying
    \[
    (t_0,x_0) \prec (t_1,x_1) \prec \cdots \prec (t_N,x_N),
    \qquad t_N < t_0 + \delta .
    \]
    Here $\prec$ denotes the partial order on $\mathbb{R}^2$ induced by the cone
    \begin{equation}
        \Gamma_M := \{ (t,x) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : |x| \le M t\}, 
    \end{equation}
    namely
    \begin{align}
    (t,x) \prec (t',x')
    \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad
    |x - x'| \le M (t - t') .
    \end{align}
title: Definition 9 of arXiv:2608.30859

body: Let (Omega, F, P) be a probability space with a filtration (F_n)_{n >= 0}, an increasing family of sub-sigma-algebras of F. A sequence (X_n)_{n >= 0} of random variables is a MARTINGALE with respect to (F_n) if (i) X_n is F_n-measurable for every n (adapted), (ii) E|X_n| < infinity for every n (integrable), and (iii) E[X_{n+1} | F_n] = X_n almost surely for every n. It is a SUBMARTINGALE if (iii) is weakened to E[X_{n+1} | F_n] >= X_n almost surely, and a SUPERMARTINGALE if E[X_{n+1} | F_n] <= X_n almost surely. Mnemonic: a supermartingale decreases in expectation, so it is what a gambler faces in an unfair game. All three notions are relative to a specified filtration; a process can be a martingale for its own natural filtration and fail to be one for a larger filtration. Integrability in (ii) is part of the definition, not a consequence: without it the conditional expectation in (iii) need not exist. If (X_n) is a martingale and phi is convex with phi(X_n) integrable for every n, then (phi(X_n)) is a submartingale by conditional Jensen; in particular |X_n| and X_n^2 are submartingales when integrable. [standard; e.g. Williams, Probability with Martingales, Chapter 10]

[Lemma l5.4 of arXiv:2411.19255, 'Moderate, large and super large deviations principles for Poisson process with uniform cat'] Let $\nu$ be random variable with Poisson distribution
	with $\mathbf{E}\nu=\beta$.
Then for any $u\in[0,1)$, $z>0$ the following inequality holds
\begin{equation} 
\mathbf{P}(\nu\leq z)\leq \exp\bigg\{-\beta(1-u)
 -z\ln u \bigg\}.
\end{equation}

[Lemma of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] \label[lemma]{lem:support_size_one_or_two}
All $f \in \Sym$ satisfy $|\supp(f)| \ge 2$, 
and if $|\supp(f)| = 2$ then $f = f_{-X}$.  

\begin{proof}
Taking $Y \sim f$, the first assertion is clear: $Y$ a constant would force $Y = 0$ (as the support of $X+Y$ must be symmetric), 

contradicting asymmetry of $X$. 

Now consider $\supp(f) = \{y_1, y_2\}$ with $y_1 < y_2$.
By symmetry of $X+Y$, $(1-p)f(y_1) = pf(y_2)
= p(1-f(y_1))$; hence $f(y_1)=p$. 

\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: In mathematics, Tychonoff's theorem states that the product of any collection of compact topological spaces is compact with respect to the product topology. The theorem is named after Andrey Nikolayevich Tikhonov, who proved it first in 1930 for powers of the closed unit interval and in 1935 stated the full theorem along with the remark that its proof was the same as for the special case. The earliest known published proof is contained in a 1935 article by Tychonoff, "Über einen Funktionenraum".
title: Tychonoff's theorem

[Theorem 10 of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] Fix $m\in\N$, $Q\in\conbodo[m]$. Let $f\in \mathcal{F}_n$. Then, for every measurable $g:M_{n,m}(\R)\to\R_+$ and measurable, non-increasing function $\Omega:\R_{+}\to\R_{+}$ such that
    $$f(v) g(A)\leq \Omega^{m+1}\left(h_Q(A^tv)\right) \quad \text{for all } (A,v)\in M_{n,m}(\R)\times \R^n,$$ 
    it holds
    \[
    \left(\int_{M_{n,m}(\R)}g(A)dA\right)\Bigg(\int_{\R^n} f(v)^\frac{1}{m}dv\Bigg)^m
    \!\!\!\!\leq\! \left(\int_{M_{n,m}(\R)}\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\Omega(\|A\|_{(B_2^n)^{\star,Q}}^{m+1})dA\right)\!\left(\int_{\R^n}\Omega\left(|v|^\frac{m+1}{m}\right)dv\right)^{m}.
\]
    There is equality when $\Omega$ is log-concave and $f = \frac{1}{C} \cdot \Omega\left( |\cdot|^{\frac{m+1}{m}}\right)^m$ and $g = C\cdot \Omega\left( \|\,\cdot\,\|_{(\B)^{\star, Q}}^{m+1}\right)$ for some constant $C>0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop soldt of arXiv:2506.08202, 'Stochastic dissipative systems in Banach spaces driven by L\'evy noise'] Assume that Hypotheses (EU2 of the paper) hold true. For every small $\theta,\delta\geq 0$ and\\ $x\in E$, the PDE (equation eqdt of the paper) has a unique mild solution $y_{\delta,\theta}(\cdot,x)\in C([0,T],E)$ and it is \\left-differentiable. Moreover for every small enough $\tau,\delta, \theta>0$, for every $x,z\in E$ and \\$t\in [0,T]$ we have
\begin{align}
&|y_{\delta,\theta}(t,x)|_{H}\leq e^{\zeta t}|x|_{H}+(1+\delta\max\{0,\zeta_F\})\int_0^te^{\zeta (t-s)}\left({\left|F(f(s))\right|}_{H}+2\max\{0,\zeta_F\}{\left|f(s)\right|}_{H}\right)ds,\\
&\norm{y_{\delta,\theta}(t,x)}_E\leq e^{\zeta t}{\left\|x\right\|}_E+(1+\delta\max\{0,\zeta_F\})\int_0^te^{\zeta (t-s)}\left({\left\|F(f(s))\right\|}_E+2\max\{0,\zeta_F\}{\left\|f(s)\right\|}_E\right)ds,	\\
&\abs{y_{\delta,\theta}(t,x)-y_{\delta,\theta}(t,z)}_{H}\leq  e^{\zeta t}{\left|x-z\right|}_{H}\\
&\norm{y_{\delta,\theta}(t,x)-y_{\delta,\theta}(t,z)}_E\leq  e^{\zeta t}{\left\|x-z\right\|}_E,\\
&\abs{y_{\delta,\theta}(t,x)-y_{\tau,\theta}(t,x)}_{H}^2\leq C(\delta+\tau)
\end{align}
where $\zeta$ is the constant defined in (equation zeta of the paper) and $C:=C(A,\zeta,x,F,T)$ is a positive constant.

[Proposition p:perfect of arXiv:2411.04773, 'Meeting of squared Bessel flow lines and application to the skew Brownian motion'] ([aïdékon2023stochastic])
Let $\mathcal S$ be a general ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow. Then almost surely:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]

 \item ((Almost) perfect flow property) For every $r\le x\le y$ and $a\ge 0$ with $\mathcal S_{r,x}(a)>0$, $\mathcal S_{r,y}(a)=\mathcal S_{x,y}\circ \mathcal S_{r,x}(a)$. 

 \item (Coalescence) If $r,r'< x$, $0\le a,a'$ and $\mathcal S_{r,x}(a)=\mathcal S_{r',x}(a')$, then $\mathcal S_{r,y}(a)=\mathcal S_{r',y}(a')$ for all $y\ge x$. If $\mathcal S$ is a ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow, it also holds  when $\max(r,r')=x$.

\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2608.29148, '2608.29148'] Let $(M, H, J)$ be a $3$-dimensional strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold and $(\mathcal{C}, [g^{\mathrm{F}}_\th])$ the Fefferman space over $M$. Then, there exists an $S^1$-invariant straight pre-ambient metric $\wt g$ on $\wt{\mathcal{G}}=\mathcal{G}\times(-\e_0, \e_0)_\rho$ which satisfies 
\[
 \wt g(\wt K, \wt K)=\frac{\wt \rho}{4}
\]
and
\[
\wt E_{AB}=O(\rho^\infty), \quad \wt L^-_{ABCD}=O(\rho^\infty), \quad (\wt F')^-_{AB}=O(\rho^\infty).
\]
The metric $\wt g$ is unique modulo $O(\rho^\infty)$ up to pull-back by $\mathbb{C}^*$-equivariant diffeomorphisms of $\wt{\mathcal{G}}$ fixing points on $\mathcal{G}\times\{0\}$. Moreover, the expansion of each component in the normal form of $\wt g$ with respect to a representative $g^{\mathrm{F}}_\th$ can be expressed by a universal formula in terms of the curvature and torsion of the Tanaka-Webster connection. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:largeoutdegree of arXiv:2607.22291, 'Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declum'] Assume that $\mu$ is critical and belongs to the domain of
    attraction of an $\alpha$-stable law for some $\alpha\in(1,2]$. Let $(d_n)$ be a sequence of positive integers such that
$d_n\to\infty$, and $\mu_{d_n}>0$ for all sufficiently large
$n$. Assume that there exists a cutoff sequence $(M_n)$ such that
$d_n=o(a_{M_n})$.
Set $
D_n
=
\#\{u\in\mathcal T^n:k_u(\mathcal T^n)=d_n\}$.
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] If $(n\mu_{d_n})$ is bounded, then
$$
d_{\mathrm{TV}}\left(D_n,\mathrm{Poisson}(n\mu_{d_n})\right)
\longrightarrow0.
$$
In particular, if $n\mu_{d_n}\to\lambda\in[0,\infty)$, then
$D_n$ converges in distribution to $\mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda)$.

\item[(ii)] If $n\mu_{d_n}\to\infty$, then
$$
\frac{D_n}{n\mu_{d_n}}
\quad\mathop{\longrightarrow}^{(\P)}_{n\to\infty}\quad
1.
$$
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2609.02464, 'When does propagation of chaos in the critical Curie-Weiss model stop?'] Assume $h=0$ and $\beta=1$, and let $k=k(N)\leq N$ with $k(N)\to\infty$.
Then the following statements hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $k(N)/N^{1/2}\to0$, then
$d_{\mathrm{TV}}\left(\mu_N\circ\mathcal P_{k(N)}^{-1},
\bin \left(k(N),\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)\to 0$.
\item If $k(N)/N^{1/2}\to\alpha\in(0,\infty)$, then
\begin{equation*}
u(\alpha) = \lim\limits_{N\to\infty}d_{\mathrm{TV}}\big(\mu_N\circ\mathcal P_{k(N)}^{-1},\bin \big(k(N),\frac{1}{2}\big)\big) \text{ exists and } 0 < u(\alpha) < 1.
\end{equation*}
An explicit formula for $u(\alpha)$ is given in \eqref{formula-distance}.
\item If $k(N)/N^{1/2}\to\infty$, then
$
d_{\mathrm{TV}}\left(\mu_N\circ\mathcal P_{k(N)}^{-1},
\bin \left(k(N),\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)\to1.
$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Corollary 11 (Exact matrix isospectrality) of arXiv:2607.26377, '\textbf{Entire Logarithmic Signatures\\ of Bounded-Variation Paths in Finite Dimensions}'] Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real normed space, let $\gamma:[0,T]\to V$ be continuous and of bounded variation, put $g=S(\gamma)$, let $l=\log g=\sum_{n\geq 1}l_n$, and put $v=l_1$.
Assume $R(l)=\infty$.
For every $q\geq1$ and every complex-linear map $\Phi:V_{\C}\to M_q(\C)$, write $I=I_q$ and define
\[
A_{\Phi}(z)=\sum_{n\geq 1}z^n\Phi^{(n)}(l_n).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
\det(\zeta I-A_{\Phi}(z))
 =\det(\zeta I-z\Phi(v))
\end{equation}
for all $z,\zeta\in\C$.
Thus $A_{\Phi}(z)$ and $z\Phi(v)$ have the same eigenvalue multiset, counted with algebraic multiplicity, and
\[
\tr\bigl(A_{\Phi}(z)^p\bigr)
 =z^p\tr\bigl(\Phi(v)^p\bigr)
\qquad (p\geq1).
\]
title: Exact matrix isospectrality

[Definition 9 of arXiv:2608.29713, '\textbf{A Cartan geometry from a correspondence space in Riemannian geometry}'] Let $(p:\mathcal P\to N,\omega)$ be a Cartan geometry of type $(G,H)$, and let $K^\omega=d\omega+\frac12[\omega,\omega]$ be its curvature form.  The torsion of $\omega$ is the $\mathfrak m$-part of its curvature function
$\kappa^\omega$, that is, the map
\[
T^\omega:=\operatorname{pr}_{\mathfrak m}\circ\,\kappa^\omega\colon
\mathcal P\longrightarrow\Lambda^2\mathfrak m^*\otimes\mathfrak m,
\qquad
T^\omega(u)(X,Y)=\operatorname{pr}_{\mathfrak m}\left[K^\omega(u)\big(\omega^{-1}(X)(u),\omega^{-1}(Y)(u)\big)\right].
\]
We say that $\omega$ is normal if $\partial^*T^\omega=0$.
title: Definition 9 of arXiv:2608.29713

[Lemma 20 of arXiv:2608.30743, 'Perspectives on the Bott spectral sequence for Lie groupoids'] Consider a regular Lie groupoid $G$ with a multiplicative Ehresmann connection $E$. Assume that the connection $\mathcal{D}$ chosen in the construction of the coadjoint action satisfies that $\mathcal{D} \subset E$ as distributions on $G_1$. Then the splitting
    \[
        A = A_{\iso} \oplus (A \cap E).
    \]
    will identify $\Ad$ with the direct sum of the canonical adjoint representation on $A_{\iso}[2]$ and the representation up to homotopy on
    \[
        \mathcal{F}[2] \rightarrow T G_0[1].
    \]
    defined by the inclusion as the differential, the map $R_1^{-1}$ of Definition \ref{DefiAdjointRuth} and its restriction to $\mathcal{F}$ as $R_1^{-2}$ as well as the map $R_2^{-1}$ given by
    \begin{align*}
        G_2 \times TG_0 & \rightarrow \mathcal{F} \\
        (x,y, Y) & \mapsto R^{-1}_2(x)(Y) := Tt(V)-Tt(Z) \in T_{t(x)} G_0,
    \end{align*}
    where for $W \in \mathcal{D}_y$ the unique element satisfying $Ts(W)=Y$ we denote by $V \in \mathcal{D}_x$ the unique element satisfying $Ts(V)=Tt(W)$, and by $Z \in \mathcal{D}_{\mu(x,y)}$ we denote the unique element satisfying $Ts(Z)=Y$.

body: In mathematical analysis, Cesàro summation assigns values to some infinite sums that are not necessarily convergent in the usual sense. The Cesàro sum, also known as the Cesàro mean or Cesàro limit, is defined as the limit, as n tends to infinity, of the sequence of arithmetic means of the first n partial sums of the series.

[Thm 2. thm: precompactness in sP of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{Precompactness in $\mathscr{P}(S)$}] 
  A non-empty subset $\{\pi_{j}\}_{j \in J}$ of $\mathscr{P}(S)$ is precompact in $\mathscr{P}(S)$ 
  if and only if the following conditions are satisfied.
  \begin{enumerate} [label = (\roman*)]
    \item 
      The subset $\{\pi_{j}\}_{j \in J}$ is precompact in the vague topology.
    \item 
      For each $r>0$, 
      $\displaystyle \sup_{j \in J} W^{(r)}(\pi_{j}) < \infty$ 
      and $\displaystyle \lim_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0} \sup_{j \in J} M_{\varepsilon}^{(r)}(\pi_{j}) = 0$.
  \end{enumerate}

[Theorem Foster's theorem of arXiv:2605.24671, 'Immigration Processes with Binomial Catastrophes and Random Survival Parameters'] Let $\{W_n\}_{n\geq 0}$ be an irreducible and aperiodic Markov chain on a countable state space $\mathcal{S}=\{\alpha_i,\ i\geq0\}$. Then $\{W_n\}_{n\geq 0}$ is ergodic if and only if there exist a positive function $g:\mathcal{S}\to(0,\infty)$, a constant $\varepsilon>0$, and a finite set $A\subset\mathcal{S}$ such that
\[
\mathbb{E}\big[g(W_{n+1})-g(W_n)\mid W_n=\alpha_j\big]\le -\varepsilon,
\qquad \alpha_j\notin A,
\]
and
\[
\mathbb{E}\big[g(W_{n+1})\mid W_n=\alpha_i\big]<\infty,
\qquad \alpha_i\in A.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Foster's theorem

[Thm 11 of arXiv:2607.03360, 'Smoluchowski-Kramers Approximation Meets Khasminskii Averaging Principles in Nonequilibriu'] Let the function $u$ and $f$ be continuous on the interval $[0,1]$ and let the function $\CK$ be continuous and non-negative on the triangle $0\leq s \leq t \leq 1$. If 
\beq{eq-uf}
u(t)\leq f(t)+ \int_0^t \CK(t,s) u(s)ds, \quad 0\leq t\leq 1,
\eeq
then 
\beq{gron-uf}
u(t) \leq f(t)+ \int_0^t \CH(t,s)f(s)ds, \quad 0\leq t \leq 1,
\eeq
where 
$\CH(t,s)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty \CK^{*,n}(t,s), 0\leq s \leq t \leq 1$, is the resolvent kernel, and the $\CK_n\,(n=1,2,\dots)$ are the iterated kernels of $\CK$.

[Lem lemma:g:taylor of arXiv:2607.09841, 'Mixing and cutoff for the systematic scan dynamics of the mean-field ferromagnetic Potts m'] For any $\ell \in Q$ and $s,\tilde s \in \mathcal S_q$,
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item  there exists an $R : \mathcal{S}_q \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $g_\beta^\ell(s) = \frac{1}{q} + \frac{\beta}{q} \Big(s_\ell - \frac{1}{q}\Big) + R(s)$  and $\lvert R(s) \rvert \leq 3q\beta^2 \lVert s-\hat e\rVert_2^2$ ;
    \item  $\big\lVert g_\beta(s) - g_\beta(\tilde{s}) \big\lVert_1
    = \frac{\beta}{q} \big\lVert s - \tilde{s} \big \rVert_1 +  \lVert s - \tilde{s} \rVert_1 \Big\{ O\big(\lVert s - \hat{e} \rVert_1 + \lVert \tilde{s} - \hat{e} \rVert_1\big) \Big\}$;

body:
Let c>=20 be fixed, G be the finite simple binomial graph G(n,c/n), and colour G by Anastos strong-4-core peeling: initially all vertices are black; repeatedly make a black or blue vertex with fewer than four black neighbours red and its black neighbours blue. For each component T induced by final red and blue vertices let phi(T) be the minimum number of red vertices uncovered by a family of vertex-disjoint paths in G[T] with blue endpoints, allowing one-vertex paths at blue vertices. With probability 1-O(n^-2), the circumference equals n minus the sum of phi(T) over all such components.
c>=20 fixed
n tends to infinity
Final colouring is the strong-4-core colouring
Paths have blue endpoints; isolated blue vertices are allowed

[Lemma lem:mds-tildeMi-proof of arXiv:2601.08184, 'Wasserstein-p Central Limit Theorem Rates: From Local Dependence to Markov Chains'] Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\) be a probability space, and let
\((\mathcal F_t)_{t\ge 0}\) be a filtration. Suppose that
\((M_t)_{t\ge 0}\) is an \(\mathbb{R}^d\)-valued martingale with respect to
\((\mathcal F_t)\), with \(M_0=0\). Let \((T_i)_{i\ge 0}\) be an increasing
sequence of stopping times such that
\[
0=T_0<T_1<T_2<\cdots
\qquad \text{a.s.},
\]
and define $\mathcal G_i:=\mathcal F_{T_i}$ for any $i\ge 0.$ For each \(i\ge 1\), let $\widetilde M_i:=M_{T_i}-M_{T_{i-1}}.$ Assume that there exists \(q>1\) such that
\begin{equation}
\sup_{t\ge 0}\mathbb{E}\|M_{t\wedge T_i}\|^q<\infty,
\qquad \text{for every fixed } i\ge 1.
\end{equation}
Then \((\widetilde M_i,\mathcal G_i)_{i\ge 1}\) is a martingale difference
sequence, i.e.,
\[
\mathbb{E}[\widetilde M_i\mid \mathcal G_{i-1}]=0,
\qquad i\ge 1,
\]
and, in particular,
\[
\mathbb{E}[\widetilde M_i]=0,
\qquad i\ge 1.
\]

Fix d>=2. Let P_l be the degree-l polynomials orthogonal for weight (1-t^2)^((d-3)/2) on [-1,1], normalized by P_l(1)=1. A polynomial is called positive definite in the Cohn-Kumar coefficient sense when all its P_l coefficients are nonnegative. It is strictly positive definite when every coefficient from degree0 through its degree is strictly positive. For any nonconstant real polynomial g all of whose roots lie in [-1,1), let H(a,g) be the unique polynomial of degree<deg(g) matching a and its derivatives at those roots to their multiplicities. The polynomial g is conductive if H(a,g) is positive definite for every smooth a on [-1,1) such that a and all its derivatives are nonnegative there. It is strictly conductive if it is conductive and, for every such a whose derivatives of all orders are strictly positive in (-1,1), H(a,g) is strictly positive definite of degree deg(g)-1. Endpoint derivatives at -1 are one-sided. Multiplying g by a nonzero scalar does not change H(a,g). This is Definition5.2; strict positivity refers to polynomial coefficients, not to nonsingularity of every finite kernel matrix.

For ReLU activation, there is a sequence of probability laws mu_d, supported in the unit Euclidean ball of R^(4d), and functions f_d with an absolute Lipschitz constant, such that the following hold for every shallow coefficient cap C>0 and sufficiently large d. Any depth-2 ReLU network N whose affine coefficients (including biases) all have magnitude at most C and which satisfies E_mu_d[(N-f_d)^2] <= 1/400 has width at least Omega(exp(Omega(d))/poly(C)), with asymptotic constants depending only on the activation. For every epsilon>0, there exists a depth-3 ReLU network with width O(d^2/epsilon) and affine coefficients of magnitude O(d/epsilon^2), whose error from f_d is at most epsilon uniformly on supp(mu_d). Depth means hidden-layer count plus one affine output. The constructed law is uniform on a special union of translated small boxes, not on the whole unit ball. The uniform deep-network approximation is only on this support; a Lipschitz extension to the entire ball exists, but efficient uniform approximation of that extension is not asserted. The lower bound is a width/weight tradeoff and does not apply to unrestricted coefficients. An unspecified arbitrary exponential cap is insufficient to conclude exponential width, because the polynomial-in-C denominator matters.

[Proposition eq:strict-tilted-product of arXiv:2607.14087, 'Stochastic Domination of Gaussian Maxima: A Resolution of the Weak Simplex Conjecture'] \label[proposition]{prop:strict-tilted-product}
Let $R$ be an $m\times m$ correlation matrix with $R\neq I_m$, and let
$X\sim\mathcal N(0,R)$.  For each $i$, let
\[
  f_i(z)=e^{a_i z}\mathbf 1_{(-\infty,b_i]}(z),
  \qquad a_i>0,\quad b_i>0,
\]
and suppose that $\int zf_i(z)\,d\gamma_1(z)=0$.  Then
\begin{equation}
  \mathbb E\prod_{i=1}^m f_i(X_i)
  >\prod_{i=1}^m\int f_i\,d\gamma_1.
\end{equation}
The matrix $R$ may be singular.

[Proposition 20 (Reference measure and asymptotics) of arXiv:2608.30551, 'Critical Discrete Hardy Inequalities in $L^p$'] Let \(p\in(1,\infty)\), \(\sigma\in(0,1/2)\), and
\(\alpha\in(\sigma,1/2)\). Let \(\mu_{p,\sigma,\alpha}\) and
\(w_{p,\sigma,\alpha}\) be defined as in
Proposition~\ref{prop: fractional Hardy weights}. Define \(\gamma_p\) by
\[
    1-2\gamma_p=a_p(1-2\alpha).
\]
Then
\[
    \mu_{p,\sigma,\alpha}(x)\asymp (1+|x|)^{-2\sigma},
    \qquad x\in\Z.
\]
Moreover, as \(|x|\to\infty\),
\[
    w_{p,\sigma,\alpha}(x)
    =
    \frac{\Psi(p,\sigma,\alpha)}{|x|^{2\sigma}}
    +
    O\left(
        \frac{1}
        {|x|^{2\sigma+1-\max\{2\sigma,1-2\alpha\}}}
    \right),
\]
where
\[
    \Psi(p,\sigma,\alpha)
    =
    \frac{1}{a_p+1}
    \frac{\mathcal A_{\gamma_p-\sigma}}{\mathcal A_{\gamma_p}}
    +
    \frac{a_p}{a_p+1}
    \frac{\mathcal A_{\alpha-\sigma}}{\mathcal A_{\alpha}}.
\]
title: Reference measure and asymptotics

Own-work draft; status: independently checked proof. For a finite-alphabet exterior process indexed by Z minus {0}, assume every finite exterior cylinder has positive probability and the central variable is binary. Write f_m(eta)=P(Y_0=+1|eta on O_m). Define D_n=sup_{m>=n} sup_{eta,zeta equal on O_n}|f_m(eta)-f_m(zeta)|. Every infinite exterior configuration is good in the finite-cylinder tail-tampering definition if and only if D_n tends to zero. The forward implication uses compactness: each good exterior has a central cylinder on which all deeper finite kernels have small diameter; a finite cylinder subcover gives a uniform radius. The reverse implication is immediate. Finite-depth numerical diameters are only lower bounds on D_n and cannot alone establish the limiting criterion.

[Corollary cor:discrete-height-phase-results of arXiv:2608.18320, 'Asymptotics for Beta-Splitting Trees via Homogeneous Fragmentations and Meromorphic Potent'] For every $\beta>-2$, as $n\to\infty$,
    \begin{equation}
            \mathsf E L_n
            \sim
            \begin{cases}
            \displaystyle
            \frac{\phi_\beta(\infty)}{\mu_\beta}\log n,
            &\beta>-1,\\[1em]
            \displaystyle
            \frac1{2\mu_{-1}}(\log n)^2,
            &\beta=-1,\\[1em]
            \displaystyle
            \frac{\Gamma(\beta+2)}{(-\beta-1)\phi_\beta(-\beta-1)}
            n^{-\beta-1},
            &-2<\beta<-1,
            \end{cases}
    \end{equation}
    where
    \[
            \phi_\beta(\infty)
            :=
            \lim_{a\to\infty}\phi_\beta(a)
            =
            B(\beta+2,\beta+1),
            \qquad\text{for }\beta>-1.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let B be a bounded Jordan measurable set in R^2 of positive area. Let P_i be countably many disjoint open Jordan measurable patches covering B up to a null set. For every i fix a finite-period Z^2 pattern h_i and let f_i(j) be its fraction of height j in one period. Suppose a discrete configuration s_N on B intersect N^(-1)Z^2 differs from h_i(Nx) at o(N^2) sites in each fixed P_i intersect B. Then for every integer j its height-j frequency in B converges to (1/area(B)) sum_i area(B intersect P_i) f_i(j). This is a sufficient condition; the required patchwise agreement for the actual sandpile, and the sandpile identity-element limit, are not proved here.

[Prop 21 of arXiv:2511.20322, 'Dissertation'] Let $\cR : \R^d \to \R \in \dC 2$ be $\la$-strongly convex and $L$-smooth with $\nabla \cR(0) = 0$ and $\nabla^2 \cR$ Hölder continuous.
Let $X$ be locally Hölder continuous and assume that $X$ does not vanish on any closed interval of positive measure.
Let $Y_0 = Z_0 \in \R^d$, and $Y, Z$ be the solutions to the Young differential equations
\begin{align*}
dY_t = &-u_t \nabla \cR(Y_t)\,dt + u_t\,dX_t,\\
dZ_t = &- u_t \nabla^2 \cR(0) Z_t\,dt + u_t\,dX_t, \quad t\geq 0.
\end{align*}
Let $f$ be regularly varying with negative index and assume $|Z_t| \leq f(t), t\to \infty$.
Then also
\[|Y_t| \leq f(t) + o(f(t)), \quad t\to \infty.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 21 of arXiv:2511.20322

body:
[Definition Langevin diffusion on $\ScS_N$ of arXiv:2411.09075, 'Weak Poincar{\'e} Inequalities, Simulated Annealing, and Sampling from Spherical Spin Glas'] Let $\pi$ be a distribution on $\ScS_N$ with $\dif \pi(x) \propto e^{-V(x)} \dif \rho(x)$, where $V: \ScS_N \to \R$. The Langevin diffusion process with stationary distribution $\pi$ is the solution to the stochastic differential equation
    \[ \dif Z_t = - \grad_{\sp} V(Z_t) \dif t + \sqrt{2} \dif B_t, \]
    where $(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ is a standard spherical Brownian motion.
    (For a textbook introduction to spherical Brownian motion, see [Hsu02].)
title: Langevin diffusion on $\ScS_N$

[Theorem thm : graet of arXiv:2609.00105, 'Weighted composition operators and classification of weighted Hardy spaces'] Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a weighted Hardy space in $d$ variables. 
    The following are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\operatorname{Mult}(\mathcal{H})$ contains the coordinate functions.
        \item $\operatorname{Mult}(\mathcal{H})$ forms a dense subset of $\mathcal{H}$.
        \item There exists $c\in\mathcal{H}$ such that $\overline{\operatorname{Mult}(\mathcal{H})c}=\mathcal{H}$.
        \item $\mathcal{H}$ is algebraically consistent on its natural maximal domain.
    \end{enumerate}

X = \mathrm{sign}(\theta_0+\Theta)\left(V(\Theta)/W\right)^{(1-\alpha)/\alpha}

$$
X = \frac{2}{\pi}\left[ \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\Theta \right)\tan(\Theta)+ \log\left(\frac{\pi W\cos(\Theta)}{\pi-2\Theta}\right)\right].
$$

[Proposition 25 of arXiv:2609.03831, 'On flows generated by square-integrable vector fields'] Let $\v \in \boldsymbol{L}^2(\R^d)$ be a compactly supported divergence-free
	vector field.
	Let $I \subset \R$ be a nonempty bounded open interval and suppose that
	for any $s\in I$ and any $\rho_0 \in L^2(\R^d)$ the continuity
	equation has at most one weak solution $\rho \in L^\infty(I; L^2(\R^d))$
	such that $\rho|_s = \rho_0$.
	Then the operator $A_0 \colon L^2(\R^d) \to L^2(\R^d)$ given by $A_0 = \v \cdot
	\nabla$ with the domain $D(A_0) = C_c^\infty(\R^d)$ is essentially skew-adjoint.

body: [Proposition 10 (The two regimes are opposed) of arXiv:2608.25188, 'Transforms for LLM Quantization:\\ The Great Inversion and Format Co-Design'] Fix the total energy $\sum_k v_k$ over the transformed per-coordinate energy vector $v=(v_k)\ge0$. (i)~The variable-rate distortion is governed by the geometric mean $\mathrm{GM}(v)=(\prod_k v_k)^{1/d}$: exactly proportional to it when every coordinate draws positive rate and the per-coordinate quantizers share one shape constant (as under the Gaussian source of \Cref{thm:klt}), and bounded below by the water-filling floor of \Cref{prop:waterfill} when the allocation is not interior; $\mathrm{GM}$ is symmetric and Schur-concave, hence minimized at the most concentrated (majorizing) $v$; equivalently the coding gain \eqref{eq:codinggain}$\,=\mathrm{AM}(v)/\mathrm{GM}(v)$ is Schur-convex. (ii)~The uniform-grid fixed-rate distortion is a sum of per-group maxima, $D_{\mathrm{fr}}=\sum_g\max_{k\in g}v_k$, which by the max-vs-mean bound satisfies $D_{\mathrm{fr}}\ge\frac1G\sum_k v_k$ with equality iff every group is internally \emph{uniform}; it is therefore minimized by within-group flattening and driven to its maximum by concentration. As functionals on the energy vector $v$, then, the two surrogate objectives are extremized at opposite ends of the \emph{within-group} majorization order, at fixed, strictly positive group sums. Because $D_{\mathrm{fr}}$ depends on the grouping it is not permutation-symmetric, hence not a functional of the global order at all, and the across-group placement of energy is a separate lever, the one the permutation family of \Cref{sec:tax-permutation} exploits; which energy vectors a given transform can actually realize, and hence whether these extrema are attainable, is the separate question taken up in \Cref{sec:inversion}.

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2606.24167, '\bf On the stability of rarefaction for stochastic viscous conservation law'] Assume {\rm{(H1)-(H3)}} hold. Let  $u(0,\cdot)-\bar u(0,\cdot)\in H^1(\R)$ and set
$$
	\mathfrak M\coloneqq\|u(0,\cdot)-\bar u(0,\cdot)\|_{L^\infty(\R)}+u_+-u_-.
$$
	 Then there exists a constant $C^*(\mathfrak M,\mu, b',\sigma'')>0,$ such that, if
	\baee
	\left\|u(0,\cdot)-\bar u(0,\cdot)\right\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})} \leq C^*(\mathfrak M,\mu, b',\sigma''),
	\eaee
	then for any $T>0,$ there exists a $u-\bar u\in L^2\big((0,T)\times \Omega,H^2(\mathbb R)\big)$ solves the equation \eqref{perturbation} with the following decay estimates
	\baee
 \mathbb E \| u(t,\cdot)-u^r(t,\cdot) \|_{ L^\infty (\mathbb R)}  &\leq C(1+t)^{-\frac{1}{4}}\ln^\frac{1}{2}(2+t),\\
	\E \|u_x(t,\cdot)- u^r_x(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2(\R)}&\leq C (1+t)^{-\frac12} \ln^\frac12(2+t).
	\eaee (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem Le:Cs of arXiv:2411.09949, '$W_{\bf d}$-convergence rate of EM schemes for invariant measures of supercritical stable '] Let $\rho$ be an admissible weight, and let $\beta' \geqslant \beta > 0$ be non-integers and ${\mathbb N}\ni m > \beta$.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item Let $\delta^m_v f := \delta_v(\delta^{m-1}_v f)$ be the $m$-order difference operator. Then we have
\begin{align*}
\|f\|_{{\mathbf C}^\beta_\rho} \asymp_C \|f\|_{L^\infty_\rho} + \sup_{|v| \leqslant 1}  \|\delta^m_v f\|_{L^\infty_\rho}/|v|^\beta.
\end{align*}
\item Let $\theta \in (0,1)$ be such that $\theta \beta$ is not an integer. Then we have
\begin{align*}
\|f\|_{{\mathbf C}^{\theta \beta}_\rho} \lesssim_C \|f\|_{L^\infty_\rho}^{1 - \theta} \|f\|_{{\mathbf C}^{\beta}_{\rho}}^{\theta}.
\end{align*}
\item

Let $\ell$ be the parameter associated with $\rho$ as in Definition (Def31 of the paper)
and let $k > \beta' - \beta\geqslant 0$. Then we have
$$
\|\delta^k_v f\|_{{\mathbf C}^\beta_\rho} \lesssim_C |v|^{\beta' - \beta} (1 + |v|^\ell) \|f\|_{{\mathbf C}^{\beta'}_\rho}, \quad \forall v \in \mathbb{R}^d.
$$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 1 of arXiv:2605.26669, '2605.26669'] Let $Y^1_0$ and $Y^2_0$ be non-negative integers such that $T_0:=Y^1_0+Y^2_0>0$. For any positive integers $a,b,c$ and any $p\in (0,1)$,
we can establish the following properties for the total number of balls $T_n$ after $n$ draws,  along with the function $f(x)$ and the increment $\Delta M_{n+1}$ as defined in  (\ref{f}) and (\ref{M}):
\begin{enumerate}[$(i)$]
 \item For any $n\ge 1$, we have
  \beq
\frac{1}{T_0+n\max\{a+b,c\}}\le\frac{1}{T_n}\le \frac{1}{n\min\{a+b,c\}}.
\deq

\item For any $x\in [0,1]$, we have
\beq
\left|f(x)\right|\le b.
\deq

\item
For any $n\ge 0$, we have
\beq
|\Delta M_{n+1}|\le 2a+3b+2c.
\deq

 \item
 For any $n\ge 1$, we have
\beq
\left|\ee\left[\frac{\Delta M_{n+1}}{T_{n+1}}\Big|\FF_n\right]\right|\le \frac{K}{n^2}.
\deq
\end{enumerate}
Here, $K$  is a positive constant. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Prop 14 of arXiv:2608.06576, 'The Resultant Distribution Method: Universality for $p$-adic Random Matrices and Polynomia'] Let $d,k\geq 0$ be nonnegative integers, and let $P^S\in\mathscr{P}_{\leq d}^S$ be fixed. Then there exist finitely many polynomials
$Z_1,\ldots,Z_r\in\mathscr{P}^S$ such that the following holds. For every
$Q^S_1\in\mathscr{P}_{\leq d}^S$ satisfying
$$
Q^S_1\equiv P^S\pmod{p^k}
$$
and every $Q^S_2\in\mathscr{P}_{\leq d}^S$ satisfying
$$
Q^S_2\not\equiv P^S\pmod{p^k},
$$
we have
$$
\left(\val\bigl(\Res(Q^S_1,Z_1)\bigr),
\ldots,\val\bigl(\Res(Q^S_1,Z_r)\bigr)
\right)\neq\left(
\val\bigl(\Res(Q^S_2,Z_1)\bigr),
\ldots,
\val\bigl(\Res(Q^S_2,Z_r)\bigr)
\right).
$$

body:
[Theorem 31 of arXiv:2609.03831, 'On flows generated by square-integrable vector fields'] Let $I\subset \R$ be an open interval.
	Let $\v \in \boldsymbol{L}^2(\R^d)$ be a compactly supported divergence-free
	vector field.
	Suppose that for any $s\in I$ and any $\rho_0 \in L^2(\R^d)$ the continuity
	equation has at most one weak solution $\rho \in L^\infty(I; L^2(\R^d))$
	such that $\rho|_s = \rho_0$.
	Then for any $\rho_0 \in L^2(\R^d)$ the continuity equation has a unique solution $\widetilde{\rho} \in L^\infty(\R; L^2(\R^d)) \cap C_w(\R; L^2(\R^d))$ such that $\widetilde{\rho}|_0 = \rho_0$. Furthermore,
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item[($\ast$)] the function $t\mapsto \widetilde{\rho}(t,\cdot)$ is strongly continuous in $L^2(\R^d)$;
		\item[($\ast\ast$)] the function $t\mapsto \|\widetilde{\rho}(t,\cdot)\|$ is constant.
	\end{enumerate}

For a unit-rate directed six-cycle Q with stationary pi uniform, choose D=diag(1/3,2/5,2/3,1,2/3,2/5). The time-stationary mean f(x)=pi(D-xQ)^(-1)1 is not convex for x>0: f double-prime at0 equals-1. Exact positive arguments1/1000,2/1000,3/1000 give f(1/1000)+f(3/1000)-2*f(2/1000)<0. Since event-stationary SCV=2*lambda*f(x)-1 with fixed lambda=pi D1, that SCV is also not convex in x. This refutes the convexity part of He2021 section4.3; it does not refute the separate monotonicity question or the reversible-chain theorem. Novelty is unverified.
Q is the specified directed six-cycle generator
All six diagonal entries of D are strictly positive
x scales only Q, not D or its stationary phase law

[Theorem 18 of arXiv:2609.02850, 'Canonical-row Chern flow on Bott--Samelson towers:\\ realizable-volume models for Schubert'] Let $X$ be an integral projective variety of dimension $d$ over the field $\kk$, and let $E_1,\ldots,E_n$ be globally generated vector bundles on $X$, of ranks $r_1,\ldots,r_n$.  Define
\[
 T_{X,E_\bullet}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)
 =\sum_{\substack{\alpha\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^n\\|\alpha|=d}}
 \deg\!\left(\prod_{i=1}^n c_{\alpha_i}(E_i)\cap[X]\right)x^\alpha.
\]
If this polynomial is nonzero, then its factorial normalization
\[
 \Nrm(T_{X,E_\bullet})
 =\sum_{|\alpha|=d}
 \deg\!\left(\prod_i c_{\alpha_i}(E_i)\cap[X]\right)
 \frac{x^\alpha}{\alpha!}
\]
is a realizable-volume polynomial over $\kk$.  If $\operatorname{char}(\kk)=0$, it has a realization on a smooth integral projective variety by semiample Cartier divisor classes.
