[Theorem 7 (Two-layer mean-field verification) of arXiv:2608.30261, 'Estimating Population-Risk Curves Along Nonconvex Gradient Flows from the Training Sample'] For $m\geq1$, $n\geq2$, and a realized sample
$S=((x_j,y_j))_{j=1}^n\in\mathsf Z^n$,
\cref{eq:mean-field-network} defines the model and Hilbert geometry.  Fix
$T\in[0,\infty)$ and let
$\cH\subset[0,T]\times\Lambda$.  Suppose
$\sigma\in C^3(\R)$, $\varphi(\cdot,y)\in C^3(\R)$ for every
$y\in\mathcal Y$.  Let
$X,Q_0,(\mathsf S_j)_{j=0}^3$, and $(\mathsf L_j)_{j=1}^3$ be finite nonnegative
deterministic constants.  Suppose
$\max_{1\leq j\leq n}\|x_j\|\leq X$, and
$\max_{1\leq r\leq m}\|q_{r,0}\|\leq Q_0$.  Suppose also that
\begin{equation}
 \|\sigma^{(j)}\|_\infty\leq \mathsf S_j\quad(0\leq j\leq3),
 \qquad
 \sup_{\substack{u\in\R\\y\in\mathcal Y}}|\partial_u^j\varphi(u,y)|\leq \mathsf L_j
 \quad(1\leq j\leq3).
\end{equation}
Then, for $1\leq i\leq n$ and $\lambda\in\Lambda$, the paths
$\theta_\cdot^\lambda$,
$\theta_{-i,\cdot}^\lambda$, and the deletion response
$d_{i,\cdot}^\lambda$ in \cref{eq:flow-alo-response} exist uniquely on
$[0,T]$.  Moreover, there are
finite deterministic constants
$K_{{\rm ker},T},C_{{\rm ker},T}\in[0,\infty)$, depending only on
$T,\lambda_{\max},X,Q_0,(\mathsf S_j)_{j=0}^3$, and
$(\mathsf L_j)_{j=1}^3$, such that, uniformly for $\lambda\in\Lambda$:
\begin{align}
 \max_{\star\in\{{\rm ch},{\rm res}\}}
 \|\mathcal K_m^{\star,\lambda}\|_{\infty,\op;\{x\in\mathcal X:\|x\|\leq X\},\mathbf h}
 &\leq K_{{\rm ker},T},
 \\
 \|\mathcal K_m^{\rm ch,\lambda}-\mathcal K_m^{\rm res,\lambda}\|
       _{\infty,\op;\{x\in\mathcal X:\|x\|\leq X\},\mathbf h}
 &\leq\frac{C_{{\rm ker},T}}{n-1}.
 
\end{align}
Consequently,
\begin{align}
 \sup_{\substack{1\leq i\leq n,\ (t,\lambda)\in\cH\\
                  x\in\mathcal X,\ \|x\|\leq X}}
 \|f_{m,\theta_{-i,t}^\lambda}(x)
     -f_{m,\theta_t^\lambda+d_{i,t}^\lambda}(x)\|
 &\leq\frac{2T\mathsf L_1C_{{\rm ker},T}}{n(n-1)},
 \\
 \sup_{(t,\lambda)\in\cH}
 |\Score_n^{\LOO}(t,\lambda)-\widetilde\Score_n(t,\lambda)|
 &\leq\frac{2T\mathsf L_1^2C_{{\rm ker},T}}{n(n-1)}.
 
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Two-layer mean-field verification

body: [Lemma lem:range of arXiv:2606.12143, 'Continuous stochastic flows driven by white noise and their duals'] For any $T \ge r$, there exists a random compact set $K \subset {\mathbb R}$ such that, almost surely, the ranges of $(X^n)_{n\ge1}$ and $X$ on $[r,T]$ are contained in $K$, and ${\mathbb E} \bigl[\sup_{z\in K}|z|^4\bigr]<\infty$.

body:
Let X, Y be Banach spaces. A linear operator K : X → Y is compact if it maps the closed unit ball of X onto a relatively compact subset of Y; equivalently, for every bounded sequence (x_n) in X the sequence (Kx_n) has a norm-convergent subsequence. Compact operators are bounded. They form a norm-closed two-sided ideal in the bounded operators: norm limits of compact operators are compact, and BK and KB are compact whenever K is compact and B is bounded. Every bounded finite-rank operator is compact; in a Hilbert space (and in every Banach space with the approximation property) every compact operator is a norm limit of finite-rank operators. K is compact iff its adjoint K* is compact (Schauder). The identity of an infinite-dimensional space is not compact (Riesz), so on an infinite-dimensional space a compact operator never has a bounded inverse. A compact operator maps weakly convergent sequences to norm-convergent sequences; the converse (complete continuity implies compactness) holds when X is reflexive, e.g. a Hilbert space, but fails in ℓ^1 (Schur property).

Examples: diag(λ_n) on ℓ^2 is compact iff λ_n → 0; integral operators with L^2 kernels (Hilbert–Schmidt operators) are compact; the embedding H^1_0(Ω) → L^2(Ω) for bounded open Ω is compact (Rellich), so the inverse of the Dirichlet Laplacian is a compact self-adjoint operator on L^2(Ω). Non-examples: the shift operators on ℓ^2; multiplication by a function f on L^2[0,1] is compact only when f = 0 a.e.
X, Y Banach spaces

Let (a_n)_{n >= 0} be a nonincreasing sequence of nonnegative reals with a_n -> 0. Then the alternating series S = sum_{n >= 0} (-1)^n a_n converges, and for every N the remainder satisfies |S - S_N| <= a_{N+1}, where S_N = sum_{n=0}^{N} (-1)^n a_n; moreover S lies between any two consecutive partial sums, and S - S_N has the sign of the first omitted term (-1)^{N+1} a_{N+1}. The monotonicity hypothesis cannot be dropped: with a_{2k-1} = 1/k and a_{2k} = 1/k^2 one has a_n -> 0 but sum (-1)^n a_n diverges, since pairing consecutive terms gives sum_k (-1/k + 1/k^2), whose harmonic part diverges. The series need not converge absolutely (a_n = 1/(n+1) gives the conditionally convergent series log 2 = 1 - 1/2 + 1/3 - ...).

Let H be a Hilbert space (real or complex) and let f be a bounded linear functional on H. Then there exists a unique vector y in H such that f(x) = <x, y> for every x in H, and moreover ||f|| = ||y||. The map sending y to the functional x -> <x, y> is thus an isometric bijection from H onto its continuous dual H* (linear in the real case, conjugate-linear in the complex case).

[Proposition 46 of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] Let \(k\) be a perfect field of characteristic \(p>0\), and let
\[
\pi\colon Y \to  X
\]
be a smooth projective morphism between smooth projective \(k\)-schemes.
Let \(D\) be a simple normal crossings divisor on \(X\), and let \(E\)
be a relative simple normal crossings divisor on \(Y\) over \(X\).
Set $B \defeq E+\pi^*D$ and
\[
d \defeq \dim X,\qquad
n \defeq \dim(Y/X),\qquad
N \defeq \dim Y=d+n.
\]
Suppose that the following conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the pair \((Y,B)\) is \(W_2(k)\)-liftable;
\item \(d\leq p\);
\item for every \(0\leq b\leq n\), one has
\[
R^q\pi_*
\left(
\Omega^b_{Y/X}(\log E)\otimes\omega_{Y/X}
\right)=0
\qquad(q<n).
\]
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Corollary cor:TT-log of arXiv:2608.30166, 'Square Functions and Rectifiability\\ under Monotone Transformations of the Density'] Let $\mu$ be a Radon measure in $\mathbb{R}^d$ such that
$0<\Theta^n_*(x,\mu)\le\Theta^{n,*}(x,\mu)<\infty$ for $\mu$-a.e.\ $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$. The
following are equivalent:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] $\mu$ is $n$-rectifiable.
\item[(b)] $\displaystyle\int_0^1\Bigl|\log\frac{\mu(B(x,r))}{\mu(B(x,2r))}+n\log2\Bigr|^2
\,\frac{dr}{r}<\infty$ for $\mu$-a.e.\ $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$.
\item[(c)] $\displaystyle\lim_{r\to0}\frac{\mu(B(x,r))}{\mu(B(x,2r))}=2^{-n}$ for
$\mu$-a.e.\ $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$.
\end{itemize}
The same holds for a Borel set $E\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ with $\mathcal H^n(E)<\infty$ and
$\Theta^n_*(x,\mathcal H^n|_E)>0$ for $\mathcal H^n$-a.e.\ $x\in E$, with
$\mu=\mathcal H^n|_E$ and ``$E$ is $n$-rectifiable'' in place of (a).

[Lem commutatortrick of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Let $N$ be an even positive integer. Let 
    $$\Homeo_{N\mathbb{Z}}^+(\mathbb{R}) \coloneqq \big\{f\in \Homeo_+(\mathbb{R}) \mid \forall x \in \mathbb{R}, \ f(x+N) = f(x) + N \big\}.$$
    Let $0 < \varepsilon < 1/100$, and suppose $f$, $g$, $\overline{f}$, and $\overline{g}$ are four elements of $\Homeo^+_{N\mathbb{Z}}(\mathbb{R})$ satisfying the following properties:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)] $f$ has $N$ fixed points $x_1,\dots x_N$ (and possibly other fixed points as well) and $g$ has $N$ fixed points $y_1,\dots y_N$,
        \item[(b)] $x_i \in (i-\varepsilon, i+\varepsilon)$,
        \item[(c)] $y_i \in (i+0.5-\varepsilon,i+0.5+\varepsilon)$,
        \item[(d)] On the interval $[x_i,x_{i+1}]$, if $i$ is odd then $f$ is $\varepsilon$-strongly increasing. For $i$ even, $\overline{f}$ is $\varepsilon$-strongly increasing,
        \item[(e)] On the interval $[y_i,y_{i+1}]$, if $i$ is odd then $g$ is $\varepsilon$-strongly increasing. For $i$ even, $\overline{g}$ is $\varepsilon$-strongly increasing.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then $\overline{g}\overline{f}gf$ has positive translation number (in fact, a translation number $\geq 2$).
title: Commutator trick

body: [Abstract of arXiv:2609.03589, 'Correlated initialization of deep residual networks'] We study the large-depth behavior of residual networks whose weights are correlated across layers at initialization. Our results confirm and extend a conjecture of \citet{marionScalingResNetsLargedepth2025}, according to which correlated initializations should interpolate continuously between the Brownian stochastic differential equation arising from independent initialization and the ordinary differential equation arising from perfectly correlated initialization. When the initialization is obtained from the application of a feature function to a stationary Gaussian sequence with regularly varying correlation, we prove that there exists a unique critical scaling such that the infinite-depth limit is the solution of a Young differential equation driven by a Hermite process. Hermite processes reduce to the fractional Brownian motion if the feature function generating the initialization has Hermite rank one, which is the case for the identity function, for example. We show that the critical scaling and asymptotic limit are uniquely determined by the decay of correlations together with the Hermite rank of the feature function. Consequently, the correlation structure and Hermite rank of the initialization represent meaningful hyperparameters in the asymptotic regime. By contrast, under finite-variance iid initialization, the asymptotic driver is universally Brownian up to normalization regardless of the choice of distribution. Our proofs rely on a collection of novel results establishing a robust stability theory for Young differential equations in Banach spaces. \smallskip \noindent{\bf Keywords:} Residual networks, correlated initialization, large-depth limit, Young differential equations, Hermite processes, fractional Brownian motion, long-range dependence, functional limit theorems \noindent{\bf AMS Classification:} 60G18, 60G22, 60H10, 60L20, 60L90, 60F17, 68T07.
title: Abstract of arXiv:2609.03589: Correlated initialization of deep residual networks

body:
[Prop 2.2 of arXiv:2412.00708, 'Stochastic PDE approach to fluctuating interfaces'] Consider the SPDE (equation eq:2.3-1 of the paper) with $n=1$ and independent space-time
Gaussian white noises $\dot{{\mathbb W}}$ and $\dot{W}$.
Then, $\widetilde{\Psi} = \widetilde{\Psi}^{N,K}$ 
defined by (equation eq:2.stretch of the paper)
satisfies the following SPDE in law
\begin{align}  
\partial_t \widetilde{\Psi}(t,z,\underline{x}) =(- & K \mathcal{A}^K_z + \Delta_{\underline{x}})
\widetilde{\Psi}(t,z,\underline{x})  
 \\
&+ K^{3/4}\partial_z \big(g_1(\bar v^K(z))\dot{W}^1(t,z,\underline{x})\big) + K^{1/4}
g_1(\bar v^K(z)) \nabla_{\underline{x}} \cdot \dot{{\mathbb W}}^2(t,z,\underline{x})  \notag \\
& + K^{3/4} g_2(\bar v^K(z)) \dot{W}(t,z,\underline{x}),  
\notag
\end{align}
for $(z,\underline{x}) \in \sqrt{K}{\mathbb{T}} \times {\mathbb{T}}^{d-1}$, where
\begin{align} 
&\mathcal{A}^K \equiv \mathcal{A}_z^K
= - \partial_z^2 -f'(\bar v^K(z)), \quad z\in \sqrt{K}{\mathbb{T}} = [-\sqrt{K}/2,\sqrt{K}/2),
\intertext{and}  
& \Delta_{\underline{x}} = \sum_{i=2}^d \partial_{x_i}^2, \quad \underline{x}=(x_2,\ldots,x_d) \in {\mathbb{T}}^{d-1},
\end{align}
and $\dot{W}^1(t,z,\underline{x})$, 
$\dot{{\mathbb W}}^2(t,z,\underline{x}) := \{\dot{W}^i(t,z,\underline{x})\}_{i=2}^d$ and
$\dot{W}(t,z,\underline{x})$ are $d+1$ independent space-time
Gaussian white noises on $[0,\infty)\times \sqrt{K}{\mathbb{T}}\times{\mathbb{T}}^{d-1}$.

In view of the SPDE (equation eq:2.2-2 of the paper), we introduce a further scaling
\begin{align}  
\Psi(t,z,\underline{x}) \equiv \Psi^{N,K}(t,z,\underline{x}) 
:= K^{-3/4} \widetilde{\Psi}^{N,K}(t,z,\underline{x}).
\end{align}
Then, $\Psi$ satisfies the SPDE 
\begin{align}  
\partial_t \Psi = & (- K \mathcal{A}_z^K + \Delta_{\underline{x}})\Psi 
\\
& +  \partial_z \big( g_1(\bar v^K(z))\dot{W}^1(t,z,\underline{x})) + K^{-1/2}
g_1(\bar v^K(z))\nabla_{\underline{x}} \cdot \dot{{\mathbb W}}^2(t,z,\underline{x})  \notag  \\
&  + g_2(\bar v^K(z)) \dot{W}(t,z,\underline{x}),  \notag
\end{align}
for $(z,\underline{x})\in \sqrt{K}{\mathbb{T}}\times{\mathbb{T}}^{d-1}$.
Note that the noise terms for $\Psi$ behave as $O(1)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 20 (Upcrossings Counting Function) of arXiv:2606.17452, 'Optional Stopping for Superhedging Supermartingales'] For $0 \leq n < T+1$ and $S \in \mathcal{S}$, denote by $U^{[a,b]}_n(S)=U_n(S)$ the number of upcrossings of the sequence $\{f_i(S)\}_{i=0}^n$ through the interval $[a,b]$ and so given by:
\[U_n(S) =\max\{k\in \mathbb{N}: \tau_{k}(S)\le n\}.\]
The total number of upcrossings for $\{f_i(S)\}_{0 \leq i < T+1}$ is defined by
\[U^{[a,b]}(S)=U(S)= \sup\{U_n(S): 0 \leq n < T+1\}.\]

			{\bf1}_{(\delta\varepsilon^{-3/4},
				\,2\delta\varepsilon^{-3/4})}.
		\end{equation}
		After assigning the last term to \(E_{02}\), one has
		\begin{equation}
			\int_1^{2\delta\varepsilon^{-3/4}}
			r|E_{01}(r)|\,dr
			\le
			C\delta^4+o_\varepsilon(1).
		\end{equation}

Consider a finite-state finite-action discounted MDP, bounded rewards with conditional mean r(s,a), discount 0<gamma<1, fixed target policy pi, and a fixed behavior policy mu whose state-action chain is ergodic with stationary vector d_mu>0. Let X have row x(s,a)^T and full column rank, D=diag(d_mu), and let P_pi be the row-stochastic target transition matrix on state-action pairs. Use Euclidean vector and operator norms, and define ||P_pi||_D=||D^(1/2)P_pi D^(-1/2)||_2. Fix ridge eta>0 and xi in (0,1). Set C0=2(1-xi)sqrt(eta)/(gamma||P_pi||_D) and C1=||r||/(2 xi sqrt(eta))+1. Assume ||X||<C0 and choose radii C1<R1 and R1-xi<R2<R1. For the concentric balls B1,B2 and projections Gamma1,Gamma2, take theta_0 in B1 and finite w_0. Let alpha_t,beta_t be deterministic positive nonincreasing sequences with sum alpha_t=sum beta_t=infinity, sum alpha_t^2+sum beta_t^2<infinity, and for some p>0, sum_t (beta_t/alpha_t)^p<infinity. Generate the behavior trajectory with A_t sampled from mu(.|S_t). Put x_t=x(S_t,A_t), xbar_(t+1)=sum_a pi(a|S_(t+1))x(S_(t+1),a), delta_t=R_(t+1)+gamma xbar_(t+1)^T theta_t-x_t^T w_t, and update w_(t+1)=w_t+alpha_t(delta_t x_t-eta w_t), theta_(t+1)=Gamma1(theta_t+beta_t[Gamma2(w_t)-theta_t]). Then w_t converges almost surely to the unique solution w_eta of (A+eta I)w=b, where A=X^T D(I-gamma P_pi)X and b=X^T D r. The target iterate also converges to this same fixed point by the general target-network theorem. This states the convergence clause of source Theorem2, with bounded rewards explicitly imposed; it concerns decreasing two-timescale steps, fixed linear features, both projections, and ridge regularization.
Finite state/action MDP; bounded rewards with the stated conditional mean
Fixed target and behavior policies; ergodic behavior state-action chain with positive stationary law
0<gamma<1; eta>0; xi in (0,1)
Feature matrix full column rank with ||X||<C0
Both projections with C1<R1 and R1-xi<R2<R1
Positive deterministic nonincreasing nonsummable square-summable main and target step sequences
Some p>0 with sum(beta_t/alpha_t)^p finite
theta_0 in B1; finite main-network initial vector

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2512.02322, 'Ursell functions in lattice gauge theory'] Consider the term $c_{I,\mathfrak{P}}$ from \eqref{eq:defCIp}, where $I \subset [n]$ and $\mathfrak{P} \in \mathfrak{F}_n$.
Then the following holds. \newline 
(a) For any $\mathfrak{P} \in \mathfrak{F}_n$, we have $c_{\emptyset,\mathfrak{P}}=0$. \newline 
(b) If $\mathfrak{P}=\{[n]\}$ and $I \subset [n]$, we have $
c_{I,\mathfrak{P}} = \mathbbm{1}\{|I| ~ \text{odd}\}$. \newline 
(c) For any $\mathfrak{P} \in \mathfrak{F}_n$ and any $i \in [n]$, we have $c_{\{i\},\mathfrak{P}}=1$.
\newline 
(d) For any $\mathfrak{P} \in \mathfrak{F}_n$ and any $I \subset [n]$, we have $
c_{I,\mathfrak{P}} \in \{0,...,n\}$. \newline 
(e) For any $I=\{i,j\} \subset [n], i \neq j$, then we have 
    \begin{equation*}      
        c_{I, \mathfrak{P}} = 2 \cdot \mathbbm{1}\{i,j ~ \text{are in different partitions elements of } \mathfrak{P}\}.
    \end{equation*}
    In particular if $|I|=2$, then $c_{I,\mathfrak{P}} \neq 0$ if and only if $c_{I,\mathfrak{P}} = 2$. \newline 
(f) Let $\mathfrak{P} \in \mathfrak{F}_n \setminus \{[n]\}$. Then there exists $i \in [n-1]$, such that for $I=\{i,i+1\}$ we have $c_{I,\mathfrak{P}} \neq 0$.

[Lemma of arXiv:2606.11043, 'Thick points under Gaussian free field dynamics'] The measure $\mathbb{Q}_{\varepsilon}^{\gamma,N}$ converges 
    in the weak topology to a measure $\mathbb{Q}^{\gamma,N}$ that fulfils 
    \begin{equation*}
        \mathbb E_{\mathbb{Q}^{\gamma,N}}[F(\Psi,(\vec{x},t))] 
        =
        \mathbb E_{\mathbb{P}\times \mathbb{U}}\left[
        F\left(\Psi +
        \gamma\sum_{i=1}^{N} \mathrm{cov}(\cdot, (x_i,t)), (\vec{x},t)
        \right)
        \right],
    \end{equation*}
    where $\mathrm{cov}(\cdot, (x_i,t))$ is the limit in the Schwartz sense of $\mathrm{cov}(\cdot, \Psi_{\varepsilon}(x_i,t))$.

[Thm phase_transition_231 of arXiv:2604.23751, 'Large deviation principles for pattern-avoiding permutations, and limit shapes for constra'] For $\beta >0,$ we let
\[
    f^{231}_\beta(x) := 1 - \frac{1}{\beta} \log\left( 1 + \textup{e}^\beta - \textup{e}^{\beta x} \right) \,.
\]
Then, the random permutations $\tau^{\beta,231}_{n}$ converge almost surely in the sense of permutons to the deterministic permuton
\[
    \mu^{231}_\beta :=  \big(X,f^{231}_\beta(X)\big)_\# \min\left(1,(f^{231}_\beta)'(x) \right) \textup{d} x
    + \big( X,1-X \big)_\# \max\left(0, 1- (f^{231}_\beta)'(x) \right) \textup{d} x 
\]
if $\beta>0$,
and to the diagonal permuton if $\beta\le 0.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm phase_transition_231 of arXiv:2604.23751

[Theorem 12 of arXiv:2609.03195, 'Lecture hall polytopes and\\Lakshmibai-Seshadri paths'] The algebra $A(b)$ is Gorenstein if and only if
\[
\displaystyle(\frac{1}{N_1},\ldots,\frac{1}{N_{n+1}})
\]
is an L-S path, i.e. if and only if
\[
b_j\cdot\left(\frac{1}{N_1} + \cdots + \frac{1}{N_j}\right) \in \NN, \quad \textrm{for each } j = 1, \ldots, n + 1.
\]

[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2604.06645, '2604.06645'] Let $p$ be large enough such that $\frac{d+2}{p} + \frac{d}{p-2} < 1-\eta$, where $\eta$ is given in Assumption \ref{assump: convolution singularity}, and let $a$ be given by \eqref{eq: alpha}. Fix $n \in \mathbb N$,
$i \in \{1,\dots,m\}$, and let $0 \le s < t \le T$. Set $h=t-s$ and for $\tau \in [0,h]$
define the shifted process
\[
u_n^{(s)}(\tau,x):=u_n(s+\tau,x).
\]
Also define the shifted stochastic convolutions
\[
Z_{i,n}^{(s),k}(\tau,x)
:=
\int_s^{s+\tau}\int_D
G_i(s+\tau-r,x,y)\sigma_{ik,n}(u_n(r,y))\,W_k(dy\,dr),
\qquad k=1,\dots,r,
\]
and
\[
Z_{i,n}^{(s)}(\tau,x):=\sum_{k=1}^r Z_{i,n}^{(s),k}(\tau,x).
\]
Then, there exists a constant $C_{p,T}>0$, independent of $n$, $s$, $t$, and $h$, such that
for every $i \in \{1,\dots,m\}$,
\[
\mathbb E \|Z_{i,n}^{(s)}\|_{L^p(Q_h)}^p
\le
C_{p,T} h^{a+1}
\left(
h+\mathbb E\sum_{j=1}^m \|u_{j,n}^{(s)}\|_{L^p(Q_h)}^p
\right).
\]

[Theoremen 5 (A refined time-uniform clipped-mean bound) of arXiv:2608.18999, '2608.18999'] Let \(H\) be a separable real Hilbert space, let \(1<p\le2\), let
\((\mathcal F_i)_{i\ge0}\) be a filtration, and let \((X_i)_{i\ge1}\) be
adapted to it.  Suppose that, for some deterministic \(\mu\in H\) and
\(v\in[0,\infty)\), almost surely,
\[
\E[X_i\mid\mathcal F_{i-1}]=\mu,
\qquad
\E[\norm{X_i-\mu}^p\mid\mathcal F_{i-1}]\le v
\quad (i\ge1).
\]
Fix \(k\ge1\), \(\lambda,\rho>0\), and
\(\delta_1,\delta_2\in(0,1)\) with \(\delta_1+\delta_2<1\).  Suppose that
the \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable pilot estimator \(\widehat Z_k\) satisfies
\[
\mathbb P\!\left(
  \norm{\widehat Z_k-\mu}\ge r(\delta_2,k)
\right)\le\delta_2
\]
for a deterministic radius \(r(\delta_2,k)\).  For \(n>k\), define
\[
\widehat\mu_n
=\widehat Z_k+
\frac1{n-k}\sum_{i=k+1}^n
C_{1/\lambda}(X_i-\widehat Z_k).
\]
Then, on an event of probability at least
\(1-\delta_1-\delta_2\), simultaneously for every \(n>k\),
\begin{equation}
\norm{\widehat\mu_n-\mu}
\le
2^{p-1}\kappa_p\!\bigl(\rho h(\rho)\bigr)
\lambda^{p-1}
\bigl(v+r(\delta_2,k)^p\bigr)
+\frac{\log(2/\delta_1)}{\rho\lambda(n-k)}.
\end{equation}

[Lemma 25 of arXiv:2607.19176, 'Exponential Convergence of the Sinkhorn Algorithm for the Schrödinger Bridge with Regime S'] Let $0<\tau<T$, $R>0$, and $\alpha\in(0,1)$. Then there exists a constant
$C=C(\tau,T,R,\alpha)>0$, independent of $\varepsilon$, such that for every
$k\in\mathcal I$,
\[
\|p^{\varepsilon,k}\|_{C^{1+\alpha/2,\,2+\alpha}([\tau,T]\times B_R)}
\le C .
\]
Consequently, for every sequence $\varepsilon_n\downarrow0$, there exist a
subsequence, still denoted by $\varepsilon_n$, and functions
$(p^k)_{k\in\mathcal I}$ such that, for every $k\in\mathcal I$,
\[
p^{\varepsilon_n,k}\longrightarrow p^k
\quad\text{in } C^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}\bigl((0,T]\times\mathbb R^d\bigr).
\]
In particular,
\[
p^k\in C^{1,2}\bigl((0,T]\times\mathbb R^d\bigr),
\qquad k\in\mathcal I .
\]

body:
[Lemma l:prior.W.logconcave of arXiv:2607.02013, 'Resolution of the Detection Threshold Conjecture for Random Geometric Graphs in the $d>n$ '] For $d \ge (1+\epsilon)n$, the prior distribution $W\sim\mathbb{P}_{0}$ conditioned on ${\mathcal{H}}$ in \prettyref{eq:calH}
is $(c_0 d)$-strongly log-concave, where $c_0$ is a positive constant depending on $\epsilon$.

\begin{proof}
Under the prior distribution $\mathbb{P}_{0}$, 
the density of $W$ is given by (see e.g.\ [anderson2003introduction])
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{P}_0(W) 
&\propto e^{-V(W
)} \mathbf{1}\{ I+W \succ 0\}\,, \\
V(W) &= - \frac{d-n-1}{2}\log \det(I+W)\,.
\end{align*}
Abbreviate ${\widetilde{W}}=I+W$, and denote by 
$\nabla^2$  the Hessian with respect to the lower triangular elements of $W$. Let $H$ be an $n\times n$ symmetric matrix with zero diagonal. Then
    \begin{align*}
    \log\det({\widetilde{W}}+\epsilon H)
    &=\log\det({\widetilde{W}})
    +\log\det(I+\epsilon B)\,,\\
    B &= {\widetilde{W}}^{-1/2}H{\widetilde{W}}^{-1/2}\,.
    \end{align*}
$B$ is a symmetric matrix. Denoting its eigenvalues by $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n$, we have
    \begin{align*}
    \log\det({\widetilde{W}}+\epsilon H)
    &= \log\det({\widetilde{W}})
    +\sum_{i=1}^n\log(1+\epsilon\lambda_i) 
    = \log\det({\widetilde{W}})
    +\epsilon \sum_{i=1}^n \lambda_i
    -\frac{\epsilon^2}{2}
    \sum_{i=1}^n (\lambda_i)^2\\
    &= \log\det({\widetilde{W}})
    +\epsilon \mathop{\rm tr}(B)
    -\frac{\epsilon^2}{2}
    \mathop{\rm tr}(B^2)\,.
    \end{align*}
It follows that
\begin{equation}
-H^\top\nabla^2 \big[\log\det \widetilde{W} \big] H =\mathop{\rm tr}(\widetilde{W}^{-1}H\widetilde{W}^{-1}H)=\|\widetilde{W}^{-1/2}H\widetilde{W}^{-1/2}\|_{\operatorname{F}}^2\ge \frac{\|H\|_{\operatorname{F}}^2}{\|\widetilde{W}\|_{\operatorname{op}}^2}\,,

\end{equation}
that is to say, the log-determinant function is strongly log-concave.\footnote{From  \prettyref{eq:hess-prior} we see that 
as long as $d\geq n+1$,
the prior distribution $\mathbb{P}_{0}$ is always strongly log-concave with constant $\Theta(\frac{d-n-1}{n^2}$); this is tight when all $x_i$'s are aligned. Lemma~(l:prior.W.logconcave of the paper) improves the curvature to $\Theta(d)$ by truncating on the typical behavior of $W$.} Next recall from \prettyref{eq:calH} that 
${\mathcal{H}}=\{\|\widetilde{W}\|_{\operatorname{op}} \leq 4\}$, which is a convex set in $W$. 
For each $W \in {\mathcal{H}}$, the right-hand side of \prettyref{eq:hess-prior} is further lower bounded by $\|H\|^2/16$, and hence
\[
\nabla^2 V(W)\succeq \frac{d-n-1}{16}I_{n(n-1)/2}\succeq c_0 d I_{n(n-1)/2}\,,
\]
for a constant $c_0>0$ depending on $\epsilon$. This proves the claim.
\end{proof}
title: Lemma l:prior.W.logconcave of arXiv:2607.02013

[Lemma lem:gaussian-polynomial-estimates of arXiv:2608.23938, 'Generalization, memorization, and overfitting \\for diffusion models trained in the lazy h'] Fix \(d\geq1\) and \(s>0\). Suppose that
\[
    P({\boldsymbol x})=\sum_{k=0}^{N}\<{\boldsymbol A}_k,{\boldsymbol x}^{\otimes k}\>_\mathrm{F},\qquad {\boldsymbol A}_k\in\mathrm{Sym}^k(\mathbb{R}^d).
\]
Then there are unique tensors \({\boldsymbol B}_k\in\mathrm{Sym}^k(\mathbb{R}^d)\) such that
\[
    P({\boldsymbol x})=\sum_{k=0}^{N}\<{\boldsymbol B}_k,{\rm He}_k({\boldsymbol x}/s)\>_\mathrm{F}.
\]
Moreover, there exists \(C=C(d,s)<\infty\) such that
\[
    e^{-CN\log(N+2)}\sum_{k=0}^{N}\|{\boldsymbol A}_k\|_\mathrm{F}^2\leq\sum_{k=0}^{N}\|{\boldsymbol B}_k\|_\mathrm{F}^2 =  \|P\|_{L^2(\gamma_s)}^2\leq e^{CN\log(N+2)}\sum_{k=0}^{N}\|{\boldsymbol A}_k\|_\mathrm{F}^2.
\]
title: Gaussian polynomial estimates

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2608.01516, 'Nondegeneracy and regularity of polynomial pushforwards'] Let $0<a\le b<\infty$, $\eta>0$, $k,d\in\mathbb N$, and $d\ge2$. There exists
a constant $C:=C(a,b,\eta,k,d)>0$ such that, for every $n\in\mathbb N$, every
log-concave measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^n$, and every
$
f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)\in\mathcal P_d(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb R^k)
$
satisfying
\[
a\le \operatorname{Var}_{\mu}(f_j)\le b
\quad
\forall j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}
\quad
\text{and}
\quad
\det \Sigma_\mu^d(f)\ge \eta,
\]
one has
\[
\sigma(\mu\circ f^{-1},t)
\le
C t^{\frac{1}{k(d-1)+1}}
\quad
\forall t>0.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 3 of arXiv:2608.01516

[Theorem 15 of arXiv:2608.08242, 'Bang--bang representation of $3\times 3$ embeddable stochastic matrices'] Let $P$ be a row-stochastic matrix. Suppose  that
	$P\in R_n\setminus\bigl(R_{n-1}\cup\V\bigr)$ and   $n\geq 6$.

	\[
	P=(K_1K_2K_3K_4K_5)(K_6\cdots K_n),
	\]

	\[
	P'=K_1K_2K_3K_4K_5\in\V
	\]
	satisfies exactly one vestibule equality. Moreover, in any such
	representation, if the unique vestibule equality is $V_{ji}(P')=0$ and $k$ is the remaining state, then the move types of the e.r.s. matrices 
	$K_1,\ldots,K_n$ are, successively,
	\[
	(k,i),\ (j,k),\ (i,j),\ (k,i),\ (j,k),\ (i,j),\ldots .

[Definition Def:labeled process of arXiv:2512.12902, 'Non-equilibrium fluctuations for the \\stirring process with births and deaths'] [The labeled process]

Given $\omega\in \Omega$, we can follow unambiguously the motion of each
individual particle so that we can give them   labels at time 0
which then remain attached to the particles during their motion. We
shall denote by $\underline x=(x_{i_1},\dots,x_{i_n})$ a labeled
configuration of $n$ particles, ($i_1,\dots,i_n$ the labels,
$x_{i_j}$ the positions); configurations obtained under permutations
of the labels are now considered  distinct. We write $\underline x(t)$ for
the labeled process induced by the active/passive marks and denote
by $X(t)$ the unlabeled configuration obtained from $\underline x(t)$,
(i.e.\ only the positions in $\underline x(t)$ are recorded by $X(t)$). By
an abuse of notation we shall write $\mathbf{P}_\epsilon$ and $\mathbf{E}_\epsilon$ both

body:
[Thm 5 (Kronecker theorem ++) of arXiv:2609.00974, 'On Algebraic Integrability\\ of Vector Fields \\ with Rational Function Coefficients\\ tha'] Let $P\in \mathbb{Q}(t_1,\ldots,t_r)[X]$ be an irreducible polynomial. 
    If modulo all maximal primes $q$ from an open dense subset of an integral model of $\mathbb{Q}(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$ it has a root in $\mathbb{F}_p$, where $p>0$ is the characteristic of $\kappa(q)$, then $P$ is linear, and its root is a rational number.

    Consequently, if $K$ is a field of characteristic zero, $f\in K$, and $f$ modulo $q$ for all maximal ideal $q$, in an open dense subset of a suitable integral finite-type model of a subfield $f\in K'\subset K$, satisfies $X^p=X$, where $p>0$ is the characteristic of $\kappa(q)$, then $f\in \mathbb{Q}$.
title: Kronecker theorem ++

[Corollary 8 (Score-based generative models) of arXiv:2607.25685, 'Mimicking diffusion processes with differential equations'] Consider the variance-preserving SDE  
\begin{equation}
f(x,s)=-\beta(s)x,\quad  \sigma=\sqrt{2\beta},\qquad 0<\beta_{\min}\le\beta(s)\le\beta_{\max}<\infty\qquad\text{for a.e.\ }s\in[0,T],
\end{equation}
or the variance-exploding SDE ($f\equiv0$) with $\sigma$ satisfying \textup{(E1)}. Let
$p_0\in L^1\cap L^\infty(\R^d)$ satisfy (I2) i.e. have finite entropy and finite second moment. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(i)}] \textup{(E1)}, \textup{(D$_{\mathrm L}$)} and \textup{(I)} hold. For the
variance-preserving model \eqref{eq:vpbeta} is exactly what \textup{(E1)} requires, since
$\sigma^2=2\beta$; the upper bound alone does not suffice.
\item[\textup{(ii)}] If, in addition, $p_0$ satisfies the two-sided log-Hessian condition
\eqref{eq:p0hess} of Proposition~\ref{prop:linear}, namely
$-\beta_0I\preceq\nabla^2\log p_0\preceq-\alpha_0I$ with $0<\alpha_0\le\beta_0<\infty$, then
Proposition~\ref{prop:linear} supplies \textup{(S)} on $[0,T]$ and
Theorem~\ref{thm:lagrangian} gives a unique RLF for
$\dot Z_s=-\beta(s)Z_s-\tfrac12\sigma(s)^2\nabla\log p_s(Z_s)$ transporting $p_0$ onto $p_s$.
\item[\textup{(iii)}] Condition \eqref{eq:p0hess} may \emph{not} be omitted: it is not
implied by the hypotheses of \textup{(i)}, and without it \textup{(S)} can fail ; see
Remark~\ref{rem:corfix}. But if $\supp p_0\subset B_R$ then for every $\delta\in(0,T)$, \textup{(S)}
holds on $[\delta,T]$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:earlystop} 
and Theorem~\ref{thm:lagrangian} applies there. The constant in $(S3)$ is
$O(R^2\varsigma_{\min}^{-4})$, the constant in $(S4)$ is
$O(\varsigma_{\min}^{-2})$, and the log-Hessian bound governing
$(S2)$ is
$O(\varsigma_{\min}^{-2}+R^2\varsigma_{\min}^{-4})$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Score-based generative models

If two dilation weights coincide, then there exists a connected real-analytic embedded nonflat minimal hypersurface patch whose image under every $D_t$ is again minimal. [Lemma 23 (\cite{Minh2024:FisherRaoGaussian}, Lemma 23) of arXiv:2506.10494, 'Geometric Jensen-Shannon Divergence Between Gaussian Measures On Hilbert Space'] Let $A \in \SymHS(\Hcal)_{< I}$ with eigenvalues $\{\lambda_k\}_{k=1}^{\infty}$. Then
	\begin{align}
		\log\dettwo[(I-A)^{-1}] &= -\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\left[\frac{\alpha_k}{1-\alpha_k} + \log(1-\alpha_k)\right]
		\\
		&= - [\log\dettwo(I-A) + \trace(A^2(I-A)^{-1})].
	\end{align}
	In particular, for $A \in \SymTr(\Hcal)_{< I}$, $\log\dettwo[(I-A)^{-1}] = -\log\det(I-A) - \trace[A(I-A)^{-1}]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm-invariant of arXiv:2605.15395, 'Equivalence and Separation for Multivariate Matrix-Exponential and Phase-Type Distribution'] Let $\bm{Y}\in\if\relax\detokenize{n}\relax\mathrm{MPH}^{*}\else{}_{n}\mkern1.5mu\mathrm{MPH}^{*}\fi$ with joint Laplace transform $L_{\bm{Y}}(\mathbf{s})=P(\mathbf{s})/Q(\mathbf{s})$ in minimal form. After multiplying numerator and denominator by a non-zero scalar if necessary, the leading homogeneous part $Q_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathbf{s})$ of $Q$ factors as a product of real linear functions with non-negative coefficients,

\]
for some $c_{0}>0$ (with $\nu=0$ and the empty product allowed when the minimal denominator is constant).

body:
Let n,m,N be positive integers with m>=2 and N>=(n+1)*m. For any family F_s:{0,1}^n->{0,1}, sample a seed S and a coordinate permutation Pi independently of a uniform N-bit pad Z. The seed and permutation may have any joint law. Fix y in{0,1}^N independently of(S,Pi,Z). Parse the first(n+1)*m bits of(Pi^(-1) applied to y) xor Z into m disjoint pairs(X_j,W_j) in{0,1}^n times{0,1}. Put A=sum_j indicator{W_j=F_S(X_j)}. Conditional on each(S,Pi), A has the Binomial(m,1/2) law. Consequently for every t>=0, P(A>m/2+t)<=exp(-2*t^2/m); in particular the Algorithm1 acceptance threshold m/2+ln(m)*sqrt(m) has false-acceptance probability at most exp(-2*ln(m)^2). If the parameter-dependent m is polynomially bounded above and m>=lambda^c for some fixed c>0 eventually, this probability is negligible in lambda. Neither pseudorandomness nor locality of F_s is needed for this soundness statement. The fixed-word independence is essential; this is not adaptive chosen-word soundness against an adversary that knows the pad.
Positive integer n,m,N,m>=2,N>=(n+1)*m; m disjoint parsed pairs.
The N-bit pad is uniform and independent of the seed, permutation, and tested fixed word.
For the negligible-security-error corollary only: m>=lambda^c eventually for a fixed c>0.

body:
[Lemma 2 of arXiv:2606.22533, '{Symmetries of Random Partitions}'] For $A\subset[n]$ and $B\subset[n]$, let $\rho: A\to B$ be a bijection. Suppose the random partition $\Pi_n$ has the property that $\Pi|_B$ follows the same distribution as the partition obtained by transporting $\Pi|_A$ to $B$ via $\rho$. Then 
$$(\xi_i, i\in A) \stackrel{d}{=} (\xi_{\rho(i)}, i\in A).$$

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Largest coefficient dimension compatible with strong convergence structural calculation Result: Expected outlier counts can fail as a method even when the extreme eigenvalue converges in probability. Let E_N have probability p_N tending to0, and take X_N=1_(E_N)*I_(D_N). Then its norm tends to0 in probability, but the expected number of eigenvalues above1/2 equals D_N*p_N. With D_N=exp(N) and p_N=exp(-N/2), that count diverges. Check: The event norm(X_N)>1/2 is exactly E_N, whereas the count on that event is exactly D_N. This isolates multiplicity rather than a failure of norm convergence. Obstruction: The example does not refute strong convergence in the requested models. It explains why a trace-statistic proof needs a different mechanism once coefficient dimension creates large multiplicities.

body:
Setting: online SGD for a soft committee machine with K students w_1..w_K in R^N and M = K orthonormal teachers v_1..v_K, activation g(x) = erf(x/sqrt 2), output sum_i g(w_i . x), Gaussian inputs, no noise, step eta/N. As N -> infinity the overlaps Q_ij = w_i . w_j and R_in = w_i . v_n follow a deterministic ODE in time t = steps/N (the Saad-Solla equations, including the eta^2 term). For K = M, the symmetric fixed point of the eta -> 0 flow has every student equal to r(v_1 + ... + v_K) with r^2 = 1/(K(2K-1)), so Q_ii = Q_ij = 1/(2K-1) and R_in = r. The unstable rate lambda(eta) of the plateau satisfies lim_{eta -> 0} lambda(eta)/eta = 2K / (pi sqrt(2K-1) (2K+1)^(3/2)), which is 4 sqrt(15)/(75 pi) = 0.0657498 at K = 2, about 0.0461179 at K = 3 and asymptotically 1/(2 pi K).
K = M
noiseless teacher

DRAFT author-derived material; independent review pending; no novelty or parent-solved claim. Fix 0<beta<beta_c in the translation-invariant symmetric free Ising state on Z^3. Let G>=0, chi=sum G<infinity, xi the positive finite exponential correlation length, and K=-U4>=0 be summable over its last three indices. Define g_+=sum K(0,x2,x3,x4)/(chi^2 xi^3). Let ell be the smallest positive integer with sum_{|z|_infinity<=ell}G(z)>=chi/2; put R=max(1,ceil(xi),ell), Lambda={|x|_infinity<=2R}, N=(4R+1)^3, S=sum_{x in Lambda}sigma_x, V=E S^2, r=sqrt(V)*y_1, and B=-kappa4(S)/V^2. Here y_1 is the first zero of the infinite-volume Gibbs-marginal block-field MGF, not an isolated free-boundary partition function. Positivity gives -kappa4(S)<=N*g_+*chi^2*xi^3, while V>=N*chi/16 and N>=64*xi^3. Consequently g_+>=B/4>=3/r^4. Bounded r along beta_n increasing to beta_c is a sufficient condition for nonvanishing g_+. An eventual bound r<=C implies liminf g_+>=3/C^4. This does not prove such a bound or the converse implication from r escaping to g_+ vanishing.
0<beta<beta_c, nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Ising free state on Z^3
Translation invariance and spin-flip symmetry
G nonnegative and chi finite
xi positive and finite with the source's exponential definition
-U4 nonnegative for all indices and summable
Correct Gibbs-marginal Lee–Yang application

[Lemma LSI-strongly-log-concave of arXiv:2606.19763, 'Optimal Sparsification of Gaussian Processes'] Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\R^n$ with density proportional to $e^{-V}$, where $V\in C^2(\R^n)$ satisfies $\nabla^2 V \succeq I$.
	Then there is a universal constant $C>0$ such that for every $u\in\R^n$
	and every $p\geq2$,
	\[
		\left\|
			x\cdot u-\Ex_{\bx\sim\mu}\sbra{\bx\cdot u}
		\right\|_{L^p(\mu)}
		\leq
		C\sqrt p\,\|u\|_2\,.
	\]

[Proposition \cite{bridgeland07} of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] Let $\sigma=(Z,(\cC_{\phi})_\phi)$ be a stability condition, then
    \begin{enumerate}[(1)]
        \item $\cA\coloneqq \cC_{(0,1]}$ is the heart of a bounded t-structure on $\cC$, in particular an abelian category. It follows that $K_0(\cA)\cong K_0(\cC)$.
        \item $Z\colon \Gamma\to\mathbb C$ is a central charge on $\cA$ satisfying the HN property (see Definition~(def:slopestability of the paper), Definition~(def:HNabelian of the paper)) and the support property.
        Moreover, an object $E\in\cA$ is $Z$-semistable iff $E\in\cC_{\phi(E)}$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Conversely, given $\cA\subset\cC$ and $Z$ satisfying the above conditions, there is a unique corresponding stability condition where for $\phi\in(0,1]$, $\cC_{\phi}$ is given by slope-semistable objects $E\in\cA$ of phase $\phi(E)=\phi$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:type FL and duality topologically for G f.p. of arXiv:2609.00233, 'A survey on mapping class groups of 3-manifolds'] \leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
        \item A group $G$ is geometrically finite if and only if it is finitely presented and of type \emph{FL}.
        \item Suppose $G$ is finitely presented. Let $X$ be a compact $m$-manifold with nonempty boundary which is a $K(G, 1)$, and let $\widetilde{X}$ be its universal cover. Then $G$ is a duality group if and only if for some $q$ we have (reduced) homology $H_i(\partial \widetilde{X}) = 0$ for all $i \neq q$ and $H_q(\partial \widetilde{X})$ is torsion-free. In this case, the dimension of $G$ is $m-q-1$.
    \end{enumerate}

		with sparsity parameter $d \in (0,N/2)$ if the following holds. 
		\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
			\item $(X_{xy})_{x, y \in [N]}$ is a family of independent, centred random variables, in particular, $\mathbb{E}[X_{xy}]= 0$ for all $x$, $y \in [N]$,

			\item

		\end{enumerate}

[Lem 81 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For sufficiently small $\epsilon$, we have $|\lambda(I)| \ge |I| \ge 1 - q_0 - \epsilon^{1/10}$.

\begin{proof}
Define the ``bad'' intervals
    \begin{align*}
    I_1 &\equiv |\{t \in [q_0,\gamma(1)] : \lambda'(t) > 1 + \epsilon^{1/4}\}|\,,\\
    I_2&\equiv   |\{t \in [q_0,\gamma(1)] : \bbE[w_{\lambda(t)}] > \bbE[\tilde w_t] + \epsilon^{1/8} \}|\,.
    \end{align*}
By Markov's inequality combined with Proposition~\ref{p:gamma-1},
    \[
    |I_1|
    \le \int_{q_0}^{\gamma(1)}
    \frac{\lambda'(s)-1}{\epsilon^{1/4}}\,ds
    =\frac{1-\gamma(1)}{\epsilon^{1/4}}
    \le \frac{4\epsilon^{1/2}}{\epsilon^{1/4}}
    = 4\epsilon^{1/4}\,.
    \]
Similarly, by Markov's inequality combined with Proposition~\ref{p:budget-loss-small},
    \[
    |I_2|
    \le
     \int_{q_0}^{\gamma(1)} \frac{\big(\E[w_{\lambda(s)}] - \E[w_s]\big)_+
     }
        {\epsilon^{1/8}}\,ds
    \le \frac{2\epsilon^{1/4}}{\epsilon^{1/8}}
    \le 2\epsilon^{1/8}\,.
    \]
Combining with Proposition~\ref{p:gamma-1} shows
    \begin{align*}
        |I| &\ge \gamma(1) - q_0 - (4\epsilon^{1/4} + 2\epsilon^{1/8}) \\
        &\ge 1 - q_0 - (4\epsilon^{1/2} + 4\epsilon^{1/4} + 2\epsilon^{1/8})
        \ge 1 - q_0 - \epsilon^{1/10}\,,
    \end{align*}
    where the last inequality holds
    for sufficiently small $\epsilon$.
    Finally, since $\lambda' \ge 1$, we have $|\lambda(I)| \ge |I|$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 81 of arXiv:2608.29416
Existence of the exponent

For equal-weight unit equilateral triples sharing a plane and noise-scaled radius a, their exact population excess score loss as a function of relative angle is a^6(1-cos(3theta))/4+O_C2(a^8), uniformly in d. For sufficiently small positive a it has exactly three global minima and three maxima per full circle. Scope limits: Independent review pending. Versions 1 and 2 superseded by exact tensor-norm correction; see CORRECTIONS.md. The fixed-radius circle alone does not imply full GD.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:12a2f982345d5409a65dec9989ac472ec9b0659824a22175fae0dc84fcdac626","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/12/12a2f982345d5409a65dec9989ac472ec9b0659824a22175fae0dc84fcdac626.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:e46b93d5bf149b2fff836bcc7c52bd70b1d1130f4c72842e2b881bd3fbe0cbc1","bundle_entry_key":"t309-c01","bundle_id":"population.t309-equilateral-ddpm-symmetry-breaking-drafts","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability, score matching, Gaussian mixture learning","draft":"w721/bundle_001.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.learning:equilateral-three-gaussian-high-noise-angular-loss","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T309: the first angular signal for three equilateral components

Claim T309-w721-C01, version 3. Status: proof (unaudited), restricted population model. This is not a solution of Target 2 and makes no novelty claim.

The hardest open piece remains the transfer from a data-independent random initialization to a neighborhood in which covariance, mean, and plane errors are smaller than the angular signal. The theorem below describes the exact population loss on the covariance-matched angular circle. It does not assert that this circle is invariant under ordinary GD.

## Statement

Let d >= 2 and let u_j=(cos(2 pi j/3),sin(2 pi j/3)), j=0,1,2, embedded in a fixed two-dimensional plane in R^d. Let R_theta rotate this plane. For a>0 define

    q_{a,theta}(x) = (1/3) sum_j phi_d(x-a R_theta u_j),
    s_{a,theta} = grad_x log q_{a,theta},
    F_a(theta) = E_{X~q_{a,0}} ||s_{a,theta}(X)-s_{a,0}(X)||^2.

There exist absolute a_0>0 and C<infinity, independent of d, such that, for 0<a<=a_0,

    ||F_a(theta) - (a^6/4)(1-cos(3 theta))||_{C^2(R/2pi Z)} <= C a^8.       (1)

For all sufficiently small such a the only critical points are theta = n pi/3. The even n are strict global minima with F_a=0, and the odd n are strict local maxima. In particular, every solution of the scalar gradient flow theta'=-F_a'(theta) starting away from the maxima converges to a correct permutation of the three centers.

There are also absolute constants c,C_1 such that F_a'(theta)/sin(3theta) lies between c a^6 and C_1 a^6 away from the zeros, with continuous extension at each zero. For scalar GD with a step size at most 1/(C_1' a^6), an initialization at angular distance at least delta>0 from every maximum reaches angular distance at most eta from a minimum in O((h a^6)^(-1) [1+log(1/delta)+log(1/eta)]) steps. The implied constants are absolute; take 0<delta,eta<=1/10 and h>0. This is a one-variable constrained optimization guarantee, not a guarantee for updates of the full d-by-3 parameter matrix.

## 1. Reduction to two dimensions and relation to DDPM

All mixtures factor as their planar density times a standard Gaussian in the perpendicular coordinates. The perpendicular scores agree exactly. Integration over those coordinates is 1. Consequently F_a is precisely the same function for every d>=2; none of the estimates below use a d-dimensional Gaussian norm.

For a fixed OU noise level t>0, the population DDPM objective in Shah--Chen--Klivans, Eq. (5), differs from E||s(X_t)-grad log q_t(X_t)||^2 by a constant independent of s. Indeed, conditioning its denoising label Y=-Z/sqrt(1-exp(-2t)) on X_t gives E[Y|X_t]=grad log q_t(X_t); the conditional cross term vanishes. Thus F_a is the exact excess objective for their Eq. (9) student restricted to these means. An original radius r becomes a=r exp(-t), since each component's covariance stays I under OU smoothing (their Lemma 3). Large original separation sqrt(3)r is compatible with arbitrarily small a. The theorem remains a restricted optimization result even in that regime.

## 2. The score expansion and its justification

Write y for the two planar coordinates, v_j=R_theta u_j, and

    Z(a,theta,y)=(1/3) sum_j exp(a v_j dot y),
    b(a,theta,y)=a (sum_j v_j exp(a v_j dot y))/(sum_j exp(a v_j dot y)).

The common factor exp(-a^2/2) cancels in the score, giving s=-x+b. The triples obey E_j v_j=0 and E_j v_j v_j^T=I_2/2. Taylor expansion at a=0 yields

    b(a,theta,y)=a^2 y/2 + (a^3/2) T_theta[y,y] + O(a^4),                (2)

where T_theta=(1/3)sum_j v_j tensor v_j tensor v_j and T[y,y] has coordinates sum_{k,l} T_{i,k,l} y_k y_l. Its trace vanishes: sum_k T_{i,k,k}=E_j v_{j,i}||v_j||^2=0. Thus T_theta[y,y]=T_theta:(yy^T-I_2), the quadratic Hermite term.

The remainders in this argument are valid after expectation and after any fixed finite number of a and theta derivatives. Here is an explicit domination argument, needed to avoid treating a pointwise expansion as an integrated one. For |a|<=1 every softmax weight is between 0 and 1. Every fixed mixed derivative of b is a finite sum of products of weights, bounded components of v_j and their theta derivatives, powers of a, and monomials in y. It is therefore bounded in absolute value by a polynomial in 1+||y||, uniformly in a and theta. This follows inductively from differentiating weights: a derivative is a weight multiplied by a derivative of its logit minus the weighted average of that derivative. No inverse softmax weight is introduced.

The teacher density divided by phi_2 is exp(-a^2/2) Z(a,0,y). Its fixed finite derivatives in a are bounded by a polynomial in 1+||y|| times exp(||y||). The latter times phi_2 is integrable, with every polynomial factor. Products required for derivatives of ||b_theta-b_0||^2 have the same domination. In particular F_a is C^8 in a with all theta derivatives through order 2 continuous and uniformly bounded for |a|<=1. This justifies differentiation under the integral and Taylor's theorem uniformly in theta. Higher orders used to obtain C^8 in a and C^2 in theta are also covered by the same fixed-order argument.

The common a^2 term in (2) cancels. The teacher density tends to phi_2, so

    F_a(theta) = (a^6/4) E_{G~N(0,I_2)} ||(T_theta-T_0)[G,G]||^2 + O_C2(a^7).

For a trace-free symmetric order-three tensor D, Wick's formula gives

    E ||D[G,G]||^2 = 2 ||D||_F^2.                                    (3)

In detail, E[G_j G_k G_l G_m] is delta_jk delta_lm + delta_jl delta_km + delta_jm delta_kl. The first contraction is the squared trace vector, which is zero, and the remaining two are each ||D||_F^2. This is a Gaussian moment computation, with no independence assertion about successive GD iterates.

Finally F_{-a}(theta)=F_a(theta): change variables y to -y in its integral and use b(-a,theta,-y)=-b(a,theta,y). The odd Taylor coefficients vanish identically as functions of theta. Applying the uniform order-eight Taylor remainder improves O_C2(a^7) to O_C2(a^8).

## 3. Exact tensor coefficient

Writing c=cos(3theta), s=sin(3theta), the independent tensor entries are

    T_xxx=c/4,  T_xxy=s/4,  T_xyy=-c/4,  T_yyy=-s/4.

The multiplicities of these entries in the Frobenius norm are 1,3,3,1. Hence ||T_theta||_F^2=1/4, <T_theta,T_0>=cos(3theta)/4, and

    ||T_theta-T_0||_F^2 = (1-cos(3theta))/2.

Together with (3), this proves (1). In particular the first orientation-identifying score term is quadratic in y and order a^3. A cubic-only score truncation that drops this term misses the leading angular signal for this family.

## 4. Exact critical points, not just limiting critical points

The loss has period 2pi/3 because rotating the student by that angle permutes its components. It is even in theta, since reflection in the x-axis preserves the teacher and takes the student angle theta to -theta. These two symmetries force F_a'(n pi/3)=0 exactly for every integer n.

Let E_a(theta)=F_a(theta)-(a^6/4)(1-cos(3theta)). It has the same symmetries, so E_a'(n pi/3)=0 and ||E_a''||_infinity<=C a^8. If rho is the distance from theta to the nearest n pi/3, then 0<=rho<=pi/6. The mean value theorem gives |E_a'(theta)|<=C a^8 rho. On this interval |sin(3theta)|=sin(3rho)>=(6/pi)rho. Therefore

    |E_a'(theta)| <= (pi C/6) a^8 |sin(3theta)|.

Choose a_0 small enough that (pi C/6) a_0^2 <= 3/8. Then F_a'(theta) has exactly the sign of sin(3theta), and its quotient by that sine lies in [3a^6/8,9a^6/8]. At the zeros, (1) gives F_a''(n pi/3)=(9a^6/4)(-1)^n+O(a^8), which has the asserted strict sign after decreasing a_0 if needed. These are all critical points. At even n the student equals the teacher as a distribution, so F_a=0.

## 5. Scalar GD rate and its interpretation

Each open basin between consecutive maxima has one minimum. Let x in (0,pi/3) be angular distance to that minimum on one side. Then F_a'(x)=k_a(x) sin(3x), with c a^6<=k_a(x)<=C_1 a^6. Also |F_a''|<=L a^6 for an absolute L by (1). For h<=1/(L a^6), the update map x -> x-h F_a'(x) is nondecreasing. It fixes the endpoints 0 and pi/3, hence never overshoots either. The loss derivative has the right sign throughout the interval, so the iterates decrease to 0.

If x>=pi/6, write z=pi/3-x, the distance to the adjacent maximum. Then sin(3x)=sin(3z)>=(6/pi)z. While this phase persists, z_next>=z(1+(6c/pi)h a^6), so it lasts O((h a^6)^(-1)[1+log(1/delta)]) steps if z_0>=delta. Once x<=pi/6, the same sine lower bound gives x_next<=x(1-(6c/pi)h a^6). This phase needs O((h a^6)^(-1)[1+log(1/eta)]) steps to reach eta. Other sides of other basins follow by the exact symmetries. A uniform random initial angle lies within delta of some maximum with probability 3delta/pi for delta<=pi/3; this is the union of three intervals of length 2delta on a circle of circumference 2pi.

If the actual means are constrained to the angular circle and updated by its induced Euclidean gradient flow, the circle metric is sum_j ||d(a R_theta u_j)/dtheta||^2=3a^2. Thus theta'=-F_a'(theta)/(3a^2); its natural time scale is a^(-4), whereas the coordinate gradient theta'=-F_a'(theta) has scale a^(-6). This metric distinction matters when comparing this calculation with the original algorithm.

## What this does not establish

The covariance-matched angular circle need not be invariant under the full gradient. A student may have the correct covariance and still have nonzero derivatives in radius, centroid, or anisotropic shape. Consequently the scalar theorem does not imply the target's random-initialization GD theorem. A valid transfer needs a quantitative normal-attraction/tracking estimate and an anti-concentration argument for the resulting angular coordinate, followed by finite-sample and discrete-step control. None is claimed here.

Source: Shah, Chen, Klivans, arXiv:2307.01178v1 (4 July 2023), Eqs. (5), (8), (9), pp. 7--8, and Theorem 16 with Assumptions 14--15, p. 12. [Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.30132, 'R-equivalence of quandle colorings and \\ inner automorphisms'] Let $X$ be a connected quandle and $f$ a quandle $3$-cocycle of $X$.
 Suppose that $X$-colorings $\mathscr{C}$ and $\mathscr{C}^{\prime}$ of an oriented knot diagram $D$ are R-equivalent to each other.
 Then, for any region colorings $\mathscr{R}$ and $\mathscr{R}^{\prime}$ of $D$ with respect to $\mathscr{C}$ and $\mathscr{C}^{\prime}$, respectively, $W_{f}(D, \mathscr{C}, \mathscr{R}) = W_{f}(D, \mathscr{C}^{\prime}, \mathscr{R}^{\prime})$.

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2608.26038, 'Rotated semicircle laws for permanental roots of Gaussian random matrices'] Let \(\beta\in\{1,2\}\), let \(H_N\sim\Pp_{\beta,N}\), and define the
monic polynomial
\[
  R_N(z):=\ii^{-N}P_N(\ii z),
  \qquad z\in\C.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
  \E\|R_N\|_N^2
  =
  \sqrt{2\pi}\,
  \frac{(1+2/\beta)_N}{N^{N+1/2}}
  =
  \kappa_{\beta,N}h_N,
\end{equation}
where
\[
  h_N:=\sqrt{2\pi}\frac{N!}{N^{N+1/2}},
  \qquad
  \kappa_{\beta,N}:=\frac{(1+2/\beta)_N}{N!}.
\]

body: In mathematics, Hensel's lemma, also known as Hensel's lifting lemma, named after Kurt Hensel, is a result in modular arithmetic, stating that if a univariate polynomial has a simple root modulo a prime number p, then this root can be lifted to a unique root modulo any higher power of p. More generally, if a polynomial factors modulo p into two coprime polynomials, this factorization can be lifted to a factorization modulo any higher power of p.

body: [Defn Covering numbers of arXiv:2411.10633, 'A Geometric Perspective on the Injective Norm of Sums of Random Tensors'] Let $(T,\mathbf{d})$ be a semi-metric space (i.e., a metric space without the assumption that $\mathbf{d}(x,y) = 0$ implies $x=y$). For any $\varepsilon > 0$, we define $\mathcal{N}(T, \mathbf{d}, \varepsilon)$ to be the minimum cardinality of a subset $N \subseteq T$, such that for any $t \in T$ there exists a $t' \in N$ with $\mathbf{d}(t,t') \leq \varepsilon$. We refer to such a set $N$ as an $\varepsilon$-\emph{covering}, and $\mathcal{N}(T, \mathbf{d}, \varepsilon)$ the \emph{covering numbers} of the space $(T, \mathbf{d})$.
title: Covering numbers

Suppose $\mathcal{B}=\{B_v\}_{v\in T}$ is a rooted block cover of $T$ that has 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item cover radius $R^*$,
    \item non-reconstruction with block decay $\rho\in (0,\tfrac{1}{20})$, and
    \item local mixing with factor $C^*$ uniformly over all boundary conditions.
\end{enumerate}
Then, if $10\rho R^* < 1$, the spectral gap of the Glauber dynamics  $P_\nu$ on $T$ is at least $(8R^* C^*|V|)^{-1}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT, unaudited; novelty is unestablished. Let B=U_G V_G^T/sqrt(N) for independent standard real Gaussian factors of sizes N by M and P by M, where M>=N+P+1. Let X be any random N by P matrix with finite second moment. For any coupling of their decreasing singular-value profiles a,b, put delta^2=E sum_(j=1)^min(N,P) (a_j-b_j)^2/(NP). Define m_Q(s)=E||Q-E[Q|sqrt(s)Q+W]||_F^2/(NP), with independent standard Gaussian W, s>=0. Then m_X(s)<=(sqrt(m_B(s))+2delta)^2 and m_X(s)-m_B(s)<=4sqrt(M/N)delta+4delta^2, uniformly in s>=0. The Gaussian product log-concavity gives a globally 1/sqrt(s)-Lipschitz, biorthogonally equivariant Bayes denoiser for s>0; shared Haar singular vectors and Gaussian noise give the direct risk comparison. Consequently, for independent fixed centered iid unit-variance finite-fourth-moment real factor laws, positive finite limits alpha=P/N,beta=M/N, and M>=N+P+1 eventually, the expected spectral W2 coupling of unaudited claim 008 gives limsup_N sup_(s>=0)[m_X_N(s)-m_B_N(s)]<=0; beta>1+alpha suffices. The asymptotic part depends on that unaudited spectral-coupling proof. These are channel-scaled product losses: for raw R=UV^T, L_R=N*m_X, so the raw comparison divides the loss gap by N. Other aspect regimes, including N=P=M, remain open; novelty and independent audit are pending.
Real matrices; standard independent Gaussian observation noise, per-entry squared error.
Finite-dimensional comparison: any X with finite second moment, Gaussian reference B, and M>=N+P+1.
Asymptotic consequence: independent arrays of fixed centered iid real unit-variance entry laws with finite fourth moments, and positive finite aspect limits.
The asymptotic conclusion depends on the expected spectral W2 coupling in unaudited claim 008; no MMSE limit existence is assumed.
metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:ac8e009ef6b13b4daaaab39f320e0cd617128a098fff917c77ed919b6a9a891a","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/ac/ac8e009ef6b13b4daaaab39f320e0cd617128a098fff917c77ed919b6a9a891a.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:235e82196ece14cc4302c0cd85fe5c21acc54bb11c4aacd75c90153e26068f72","bundle_entry_key":"gaussian-product-mmse-logconcave-wedge-w718","bundle_id":"population.t287-gaussian-product-logconcavity-mmse-and-normalization-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian channels and extensive-rank matrix inference","draft":"w718/bundle_004.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.gaussian_channels:gaussian-product-mmse-logconcave-wedge-w718","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Gaussian-reference MMSE extremality in the log-concavity wedge

**Proof draft, unaudited.** Primary source hypotheses have been checked.
Independent review and novelty assessment remain open. The asymptotic
corollary uses the unaudited spectral-coupling result in claim 008.

All matrices are real. Squared errors use the Frobenius norm and are divided
by d=NP. Information and mutual-information derivatives are not used here.


## Product-loss convention

Here the signal is the channel-scaled product X=UV^T/sqrt(N). For the raw
product R=UV^T in the same observation, its NP-normalized Bayes loss L_R
is exactly N*m_X. Thus the uniform asymptotic comparison below is
limsup_N sup_s (L_R-L_R^G)/N<=0. It does not assert an unscaled raw-loss
gap tending to zero. The literal raw loss diverges even for Gaussian
factors at fixed positive noise; proofs/product_loss_normalization.md
gives the exact identity and a finite-dimensional lower bound.

## 1. Statement of the finite-dimensional comparison

Fix positive integers N,P,M with M>=N+P+1. Let

    B=U_G V_G^T/sqrt(N),

where U_G is N by M, V_G is P by M, and both have independent standard
Gaussian entries. Let X be any random N by P matrix with finite second
moment. Put r=min(N,P). Choose any coupling of the decreasing singular-value
vectors a of X and b of B, and set

    delta^2=E sum_(j=1)^r (a_j-b_j)^2/(NP).

For Q=X or B, define

    m_Q(s)=E||Q-E[Q|sqrt(s)Q+W]||_F^2/(NP),

with W independent standard Gaussian noise. For every s>0,

    m_X(s) <= (sqrt(m_B(s))+2 delta)^2.                 (1)

In particular, since E||B||_F^2/(NP)=M/N,

    m_X(s)-m_B(s) <= 4 sqrt(M/N) delta+4 delta^2.        (2)

The same bound applies at s=0, by the zero estimator and the L2 triangle
inequality; for the centered equal-variance products considered below their
two zero-SNR MMSEs are both M/N. The constants in (1)-(2) do not depend on s.

## 2. The Gaussian product has a log-concave density

Put h=N+P and stack the factors into the h by M Gaussian matrix
T=[U_G; V_G]. Its Wishart Gram matrix S=T T^T has density proportional to

    det(S)^k exp[-tr(S)/2], S>0,
    k=(M-h-1)/2 >= 0.                                 (3)

The density is with respect to the h(h+1)/2 independent symmetric matrix
coordinates; only a positive normalization constant is omitted. Its domain
is the convex positive definite cone. Log det is concave there, as follows
from the second directional derivative

    -tr(S^(-1)H S^(-1)H)<=0, H symmetric.

Thus (3), extended by zero outside S>0, is log-concave. Its upper-right
block is exactly U_G V_G^T. Write the block coordinates as

    S = [ A, sqrt(N) B; sqrt(N) B^T, C ].              (4)

This is an invertible linear change between symmetric S and the independent
coordinates A in Sym_N, C in Sym_P, B in R^(N by P), with a constant
positive Jacobian. Prékopa's marginalization theorem, integrating A,C,
therefore makes the B density log-concave.

The marginal is positive for every B: the fiber contains the positive
definite block matrix with A=t I_N,C=t I_P whenever
t>sqrt(N)||B||_op, together with an open neighborhood in the fiber. It is
finite for every B as well. On the positive cone, A,C are positive
definite and det(S)^k is at most ((tr(A)+tr(C))/h)^(h*k). Hence its fiber
integral is bounded by a polynomial times exp[-(tr(A)+tr(C))/2] integrated
over the two positive definite cones. This is finite, since their traces
dominate their Frobenius norms. No regularity or integrability assertion
about the marginal is being inferred from a value on a null set.

The exact marginal theorem is recorded in Saumard-Wellner, arXiv:1404.5886,
Theorem 3.3, with two proofs following it; the result is due to Prékopa.
The existing brain card is the Prékopa-Leindler inequality, full id
claim_1d4b5a350b6c1f8b10c1e28f6294d7585ab806703fc9ee66340f1431f547361d.

## 3. The reference Bayes denoiser is globally Lipschitz

Fix s>0 and let p_s(y) be the density of sqrt(s)B+W. The joint density
p_B(b) phi(y-sqrt(s)b) is log-concave in b,y, so Prékopa's theorem makes p_s
log-concave. Gaussian convolution makes it smooth and strictly positive.
Its moments and likelihood derivatives can be differentiated under the
integral: on each compact y set, a polynomial times the Gaussian likelihood
is bounded as a function of b, and p_B is a probability density.

Define the everywhere-defined posterior mean

    F_s(y)= integral b p_B(b) phi(y-sqrt(s)b) db / p_s(y).

In vectorized coordinates, direct differentiation of this ratio gives

    D F_s(y)=sqrt(s) Cov(B|sqrt(s)B+W=y),
    Hess log p_s(y)=s Cov(B|sqrt(s)B+W=y)-I_d.          (5)

Since p_s is log-concave, its log Hessian is negative semidefinite. Equation
(5) therefore gives, for every y,

    0 <= Cov(B|Y=y) <= I_d/s,
    ||D F_s(y)||_op <= 1/sqrt(s).                     (6)

Integration along line segments proves the global 1/sqrt(s)-Lipschitz bound
for F_s in Frobenius norm. No smoothness of the prior log density is needed.

The Gaussian factors make B biorthogonally invariant. Changing variables
in the posterior integral proves, for all orthogonal L,R and all y,

    F_s(L y R^T)=L F_s(y) R^T.                        (7)

## 4. Coupling, equivariance and the risk comparison

Take coupled profiles a,b as in Section 1 and independent Haar orthogonal
matrices L of size N and R of size P. Form rectangular diagonal matrices
D(a),D(b) with those profiles, and define

    X_tilde=L D(a) R^T,  B_tilde=L D(b) R^T.

Biorthogonal invariance implies B_tilde has the law of B: averaging any test
function over the left/right group depends only on singular values. X_tilde
has the law of an independent Haar rotation of X. By construction,

    E||X_tilde-B_tilde||_F^2/(NP)=delta^2.             (8)

Use the same independent Gaussian W for both channels. From (6), pointwise,

    ||F_s(sqrt(s)X_tilde+W)-X_tilde
        -F_s(sqrt(s)B_tilde+W)+B_tilde||_F
      <= ||F_s(sqrt(s)X_tilde+W)-F_s(sqrt(s)B_tilde+W)||_F
           +||X_tilde-B_tilde||_F
      <= 2||X_tilde-B_tilde||_F.                     (9)

The L2 triangle inequality, (8), and Bayes optimality of F_s for B give

    sqrt(E||F_s(sqrt(s)X_tilde+W)-X_tilde||_F^2/(NP))
      <= sqrt(m_B(s))+2 delta.                       (10)

The risk of F_s is unchanged by independent Haar rotations of X: condition
on fixed L,R, use (7), and rotate the isotropic Gaussian noise. Thus the left
side is the square root of the risk of F_s on the original X. Bayes
optimality for X bounds m_X by that risk. This proves (1). Expanding the
square and using m_B(s)<=M/N proves (2).

At s=0, m_X(0)<=E||X||_F^2/(NP), and the profile coupling gives
sqrt(E||X||_F^2/(NP))<=sqrt(M/N)+delta. This is sufficient for (2) there
as well. In the stated application both means vanish and both variances
are exactly M/N, so the gap at zero is zero.

## 5. Extensive-rank consequence and remaining gap

Let X_N=U_N V_N^T/sqrt(N), with independent centered iid real unit-variance
factor laws, fixed with N and having finite fourth moments. Assume P/N and
M/N converge to positive finite limits alpha,beta. The spectral-coupling
result in claim 008 gives couplings of the Gaussian and non-Gaussian
profiles for which delta_N->0. Equivalently, if mu_X and mu_B are the r-point
empirical singular-value laws of X_N/sqrt(N), B_N/sqrt(N), then

    delta_N^2=(r/P) E W_2(mu_X,mu_B)^2 -> 0.

If M>=N+P+1 eventually, (2) holds with the same delta_N for every s>=0,
and hence

    limsup_N sup_(s>=0) [m_X_N(s)-m_B_N(s)] <= 0.      (11)

In particular beta>1+alpha guarantees this conclusion. No existence of an
individual thermodynamic MMSE limit is assumed. Fixed positive factor
variances reduce to the unit-variance statement by rescaling the signal
and SNR.

This is a partial Target 2 result. The proof does not cover the general
remaining aspect region, including N=P=M. It also does not pay the uniform
Taylor-remainder obligation in Target 1. The central remaining MMSE issue
is risk transfer for a Gaussian reference outside this log-concavity regime.

## Checked sources and dependency

The Gaussian Wishart density is printed as f_(n,d)(A) in the proof of
Theorem 7, page 17, of Bubeck-Ding-Eldan-Rácz, *Testing for high-dimensional

Own-work draft; status: independently checked proof; F0124_C14 version 1. For theta=(1-p)/p>0 let h_{L+1}(theta) be the unrestricted constant-word WHOLE no-cut coefficient, summing theta^B2^(L+1-R) over all L-step nearest-neighbor paths without an upward cut. Then limsup over even L of h_{L+1}^(1/L)>=4sqrt(theta). Confined loops starting and ending at zero have no upward cut; on [-K,K] their count is >=[2cos(pi/(2K+2))]^L/(K+1) for even L. Their contribution gives h_{L+1}>=2^(-2K)[4sqrt(theta)cos(pi/(2K+2))]^L/(K+1). Hence raw geometric activity decay with any finite prefactor is impossible for p<=16/17, and raw activities grow exponentially for p<16/17. This limits a raw-activity proof of the conjectured good interval 4/5<p<=16/17, not the RWRS model itself. No summability claim is made at exactly p=16/17; normalization by competing blocks can matter.

body:
Let D be a nonempty bounded open subset of C with finitely many connected components and with boundary having finitely many connected components, each of positive Euclidean diameter. Let D_N be finite subsets of Z^2 such that D_N is contained in {x:dist_infinity(x/N,D^c)>1/N}, and for each epsilon>0 contains {x:dist_infinity(x/N,D^c)>epsilon} for all sufficiently large N. Let h^{D_N} be the centered zero-boundary discrete Gaussian free field with covariance equal to the Green function of nearest-neighbor simple random walk killed on leaving D_N. Put g=2/pi and alpha=2/sqrt(g). Fix 0<lambda<1 and any real sequence a_N with a_N/log N tending to 2 sqrt(g) lambda. Set K_N=N^2 (log N)^(-1/2) exp[-a_N^2/(2g log N)]. There exists a random finite Borel measure Z_lambda^D, independent in law of the approximation and threshold sequences, such that K_N^(-1) sum_{x in D_N} delta_(x/N) tensor delta_(h^{D_N}(x)-a_N) converges in law to Z_lambda^D(dx) tensor exp(-alpha lambda h) dh, in the vague topology on D times R. Its total mass has finite positive expectation and is strictly positive almost surely; every nonempty open subset of D has positive mass almost surely. Moreover K_N^(-1) #{x in D_N:h^{D_N}(x)>=a_N} converges in law to (alpha lambda)^(-1) Z_lambda^D(D). These normalized counts are uniformly integrable, so their expectations converge to the expectation of this limit as well. Source: On intermediate level sets of two-dimensional discrete Gaussian Free Field, two-coordinate projection of Theorem 2.1, Corollary 2.2, pp.3-4, and Theorem 2.3(7), pp.4-5; proof strategy Section 2.5, pp.9-10; Sections 3-4.
The stated admissible continuum domains and lattice approximations
Zero-boundary DGFF normalized by the killed simple-random-walk Green function
0<lambda<1; deterministic threshold sequence with the displayed leading asymptotic
The size convergence includes uniform integrability, not an almost-sure coupling

body: In the mathematical discipline of group theory, Cayley's theorem, named in honour of Arthur Cayley, states that every group G is isomorphic to a subgroup of a symmetric group. More specifically, G is isomorphic to a subgroup of the symmetric group Sym(G) whose elements are the permutations of the underlying set of G. Explicitly, for each g in G, the left-multiplication-by-g map L_g : G -> G sending each element x to gx is a permutation of G, and the map L : G -> Sym(G) sending each element g to L_g is an injective homomorphism, so it defines an isomorphism from G onto a subgroup of Sym(G).

Prover-written mathematical claim; independent review pending. Let H,W be finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces, 1<=p<=q, and T in H^(tensor(p+q)) tensor W. Assume T is symmetric in its first p positions and separately its next q positions. If P_q averages permutations of the first q positions, leaving all others fixed, then ||T||<=binom(q,p)||P_qT|| in the Hilbert tensor norm. The factor is optimal when dim H>=2 and W is nonzero. The case p=d,q=2d has factor binom(2d,d); BKL Lemma 2.2 already obtains this factor in its proof before stating the coarser 4^d bound. Complete incidence-identity and explicit sharpness proofs are in w348/ATTEMPT.md L1; this is not a full KLS proof.

Ordered Hilbert tensor norm
Optimality requires dim H>=2 and W nonzero

body:
[Lemma lem: Diagram of arXiv:2604.08462, 'Convergence of $k$-point functions in\\ high dimensional percolation'] Let $v$ be a vertex of the connectivity tree $T(\omega)$. Suppose $v$ has $m$ children, $w_1,\ldots, w_m$ in $T$, that is, $p(w_i)=v$ for $1\le i\le m$.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The configuration $\omega$ contains an open tree spanning the subset of $x_i$ corresponding to the subset of $\{x_0,\ldots,x_k\}$ in $T_{\prec v}$, the part of $T$ below $v$: $T_{\prec v}:=\{w\in V(T): w\prec v\}$.
    \item For any $1\le i\neq j\le m$, the configuration $\omega$ contains two edge-disjoint paths $\pi_1$, resp. $\pi_2$, between $w_i$ and $v$, respectively $w_j$ and $v$.
    
    \item If $m \ge 3$,  then choosing $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$ corresponding to $w_1$ and $w_2$ respectively, in $\omega$ additionally:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item  for each $j$, there are vertices $a,b,c\in \mathbb{Z}^d$ such that $a\in \pi_1$, $b\in \pi_2$, such that 
        \[\omega\in \{v\leftrightarrow a\}\circ \{a\leftrightarrow c\}\circ \{w_j\leftrightarrow c\}\circ \{c \leftrightarrow b\}\circ \{b\leftrightarrow v\},\]
        so that in particular $\gamma: v\rightarrow a\rightarrow b\rightarrow c\rightarrow v$ forms an open cycle,
        \item each $w_j$, $1\le j \le m$ lies in a open rooted tree, whose leaf set lies in $\{x_i\}_{0\le i\le k}$, as is attached to $\gamma$ at a single vertex, but is edge disjoint from it. For $j \geq 3$, choosing $a, b, c$ as above, we have that $w_1$ lies in the tree attached at $a$, $w_2$ in the tree attached at $b$, and $w_j$ in the tree attached at $c$.
    \end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
\begin{proof}
Let $v\in T$ and $e(v)$ be the unique pivotal edge emanating from $v$. Closing $e(v)$ disconnects some subset $C=\{y_1,\ldots,y_\ell\}\subset \{x_1,\ldots,x_k\}$ from $x_0$. Choose $x\in C$. There exists an open path $t_1$ in $\omega$ from $y_1$ to $v$. We then construct a spanning tree $t_n$ iteratively by attaching the remaining $y_n$ to the tree by the portion of the path $y_n\rightarrow v$ until the first point it hits $t_{n-1}$, until $C$ is exhausted.

If $w_i$, $w_j$ are direct descendants of $v$, then $v$ coincides with $m_{ij}$. The existence of $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$ follows directly from this. 

For the third item, for $j \geq 3$ we select a path $\pi_j: w_j\rightarrow v$ disjoint from $\pi_1$ and a path $\pi_j':w_j\rightarrow v$ disjoint from $\pi_2$. This is possible by the same argument guaranteeing the existence of $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$. We then  let $a$ be the first intersection of $\pi_j'$ with $\pi_1$, and let $b$ be the first intersection of $\pi_j$ with $\pi_2$ and $c$ be the last common vertex between $\pi_j$ and $\pi_j'$ appearing before  $a$ and $b$ on either path. (Note that some of these points may coincide.)
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Corollary 3.8 of arXiv:2603.27659, 'Operator Norm Bounds for Multi-leg Matrix Tensors and Applications to Random Matrix Theory'] Let $m,N,k\in\mathbb{N}$, $a_{1},\ldots,a_{k}\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k}\in\mathcal{P}([m])$ be any permutations. With $M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k};a_{1},\ldots,a_{k})$ and $C(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k};a_{1},\ldots,a_{k})$ as defined above, we have $\displaystyle N^{M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k};a_{1},\ldots,a_{k})}\leq\max_{\|A_{1}\|,\ldots,\|A_{m}\|\leq 1}\left|\left(\mathrm{Tr}_{\sigma_{1}}\otimes\ldots\otimes\mathrm{Tr}_{\sigma_{k}}\right)\left(A_{1},\ldots,A_{m}\right)\right|\leq N^{C(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k};a_{1},\ldots,a_{k})}.$ Here, for the graph $G_{\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k}}$ of the permutations, $M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})$ is the maximum over blue-edge configurations of the number of directed cycles, and $C(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})=\min_{G^{\prime}}R_{G^{\prime}}$, the minimum over full simple partial graphs $G^{\prime}$ (partial graphs keeping every rectangle and containing no directed cycle for any blue-edge configuration) of the number $R_{G^{\prime}}$ of colored edges removed to obtain $G^{\prime}$ (Definition 2.1).

body: Proposition 2.3.5. Let r and s be two positive integers. Let G be a simple graph with |V(G)| >= binom(r + s - 2, r - 1). Then, at least one of the following two statements holds: Statement 1: There exist r distinct vertices of G that are mutually adjacent (i.e., each two distinct ones among these r vertices are adjacent). Statement 2: There exist s distinct vertices of G that are mutually non-adjacent (i.e., no two distinct ones among these s vertices are adjacent).

[Lemma lem:packetless-ricci-shell of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Form $\mathcal C_{k,{\rm R}}$ by the exact split
(eq:3.5.1 of the paper), retaining the complete Christoffel--Darboux
derivative-position sum, reflection orbit, weak chronological sum, and
orthogonal-Weingarten sum.  After equal-time fusion, fix a complete
$(p,q,r)$ atom only to classify its coefficient components.  For its
selected aggregate-Ricci root $R$, let $\mathcal P_R$ be the set of
external multibox $q$-components assigned wholly to the fresh root color;
immediately adjacent current-plane strings remain part of the root and are
not in $\mathcal P_R$.  Let $\mathcal C_{k,{\rm R}}^{(0)}$ be the sum of
all terms for which $\mathcal P_R=\varnothing$, with the full sums just
listed restored before taking the $L^2$ norm.  Remove the completely
root-only recurrence-dimer subfamily of
(lem:ricci-scalar-dimer of the paper), and write
\[
 \mathcal C_{k,{\rm R}}^{(0,+)}
 :=\mathcal C_{k,{\rm R}}^{(0)}-
   \mathcal C_{k,{\rm R}}^{\rm dim}.
\]
Thus every term retained in $\mathcal C_{k,{\rm R}}^{(0,+)}$ contains
at least one nonroot monomer.  Let
$\mathcal C_{k,{\rm R}}^{(0,{\rm hard})}$ be its subfamily in which the
Ricci residual component contains an ordinary hard resource in the sense
of (lem:ricci-internal-hard of the paper), and put
\[
 \mathcal C_{k,{\rm R}}^{(0,{\rm soft})}
 :=\mathcal C_{k,{\rm R}}^{(0,+)}-
   \mathcal C_{k,{\rm R}}^{(0,{\rm hard})}.
\]
Resolve the internal full-centered hard blocks of this last family as in
(lem:ricci-soft-threshold of the paper).  Route every all-Weyl child and,
by (lem:ricci-mixed-closed-hard of the paper), every nonzero mixed child
back into $\mathcal C_{k,{\rm R}}^{(0,{\rm hard})}$; one-box mixed
children vanish.  Thus the residual soft family has $u=0$.  Let
$\mathcal C_{k,{\rm R}}^{(0,{\rm low})}$ be the restored sum of exactly
those resolved children for which
\[
 \Delta_0=o+\frac v2<f_R.
\]
Denote the restored sum of the complementary soft children with
$\Delta_0\ge f_R$ by
$\mathcal C_{k,{\rm R}}^{(0,{\rm soft},\ge)}$; it is covered by
(lem:ricci-soft-threshold of the paper) and is not part of the low family.
Resources in different Haar-separated components do not enter this
classification.

For every fixed $L$ there are $A_L,C_L<\infty$ and a numerical $B$ such
that, for $m\le cN$, $c\ge1$, and $k\le L\log n$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\mathcal C_{k,{\rm R}}^{(0,{\rm low})}\|_2^2
 \le C_L n c^{k+1}(k+1)^B A_L^{2k}.}
\tag{3.3.1w$_{12k}$}
\]
The assertion is only about this intact physical low-debit sum: the complete term
has at least one nonroot monomer, while its Ricci component has no internal
ordinary hard resource.  The Ricci component may itself be all-dimer when
the monomer lies behind a Haar separator; that exterior resource remains
owned by its own component.  It makes no
termwise estimate after fixing a ribbon, status, Green coefficient, or
Weingarten pairing.

[Lemma lem:analytic-moments of arXiv:2608.23742, 'Second-order fusion asymptotics for $\Sine_\beta$ correlation functions'] Let $\beta,\delta>0$, let $0<s<2\delta$, let $R>0$, and let $k\ge0$ be an integer. Then
\begin{equation}
\sup_{N\ge1}\mathbb E\sup_{|z|\le R}|f_N^{(k)}(z)|^s<\infty,
\qquad
\mathbb E\sup_{|z|\le R}|\xi^{\beta,\delta\,(k)}(z)|^s<\infty.
\end{equation}
Consequently, for $s>1$ the families $\{f_N^{(k)}(0)\}_N$ are uniformly integrable.

[Theorem thm:mtp-lindeberg-clt of arXiv:2512.21026, 'Minimax Duality in Game-Theoretic Probability\thanks{Work in progress: mistakes are likely'] Let $\{X_n, \mathcal{F}_n\}_{n \geq 0}$ be a square-integrable martingale with $X_0 = 0$, and let $\{Y_n = X_n - X_{n-1}, \mathcal{F}_n\}_{n \geq 1}$ be the martingale differences. Let the cumulative variance be given by
  \(
  V_n = \sum_{i=1}^n \mathbb{E}[Y_i^2 | \mathcal{F}_{i-1}]~.
  \)
  Suppose $V_n \to \infty$ a.s., and
  for all $\delta > 0$,
  \begin{equation}
    
    \frac{1}{V_n} \sum_{i=1}^n \mathbb{E}\left[Y_i^2 \mathds{1}\{|Y_i| > \delta \sqrt{V_n}\} \, \middle| \, \mathcal{F}_{i-1}\right] \xrightarrow{P} 0 \quad \text{as} \ n \to \infty~.    
  \end{equation}
  Then
  \(
  \dfrac{X_n}{\sqrt{V_n}} \xrightarrow{D} N(0, 1)
  \). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lindeberg martingale CLT

[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2607.16017, 'On large networks of integrate-and-fire neurons with short-term synaptic plasticity'] For any $g \in Lip_1 $ such that $ \|g \|_\infty \le 1, $ the function $ x \mapsto \E \left[ g  (V_{s, t}^{ a, \delta_{(0, x)} } , X_{s, t }^{a, \delta_{(0, x)} } )\right] =: R_{s, t}^{a, g } ( x) $ is Lipschitz continuous with Lipschitz constant 
$$ \sup_{ x \neq x' }\frac{| R_{s, t}^{a, g } ( x) - R_{s, t}^{a, g } ( x')| }{|x-x'|} \le e^{ \|f\|_\infty (t-s) }. $$
If moreover $g \in C^1 ( \R \times [0, 1 ]; \R),$ then $x \mapsto R_{s, t}^{a, g } ( x)$ is also differentiable.
title: Lemma 14 of arXiv:2607.16017

body: Lemma (campaign status: audited-pass): Let N_0 be the outside coordinates that are never conditionally free. For every realized core pattern each X_j, j in N_0, has at most one possible sign, so the WHOLE VECTOR X_{N_0} (not merely each coordinate separately) is a deterministic function of X_C: H(X_C, X_{N_0}) = H(X_C) (tag 21). For uniform X on S, r - ell = H(X) <= H(X_C) + r - |C| - |N_0| (tag 22), hence |N_0| <= ell - (|C| - H(X_C)) <= ell (tag 23). Notes: S6 flags this explicitly: 'This is the point at which a naive conditioning argument can go wrong. Equation (21) is valid precisely because never free is required for EVERY realized core pattern.' A per-coordinate version of the argument is false.
