STATUS: proof (unaudited). For the exact iid Gaussian zero-bias width-n ReLU angle chain started at any theta0 in (0,pi], killed at zero norm or angle and embedded as angle0 after killing, each fixed positive integer p and T<infinity admit constants C_(p,T),c,n0, uniform in theta0, with E[theta_k^p;alive]<=C_(p,T)/(k+1)^p for0<=k<=Tn and n>=n0. For0<eta<=pi and0<=m<=N<=Tn, P(max_(m<=k<=N)theta_k>=eta)<=C_(p,T)/(eta^p(m+1)^p)+C_T n exp(-cn). A specified hybrid normalized/ordinary Gram self-loop kernel satisfies both estimates without the exponential maximal-error term. Assumptions: Independent Gaussian rows across coordinates and layers; zero-bias ReLU and width n sufficiently large; constants depend on fixed p,T and good-box choices. Inverse-U moments are interpreted only on alive states, U=1/(n theta). The hybrid kernel uses normalized difference coordinates below a fixed small angle threshold and ordinary Gram coordinates above it, with fixed concentration boxes and self-loop off the selected box. The angle transition uses n independent row pairs x=max(g,0), y=max(cos(theta)g+sin(theta)h,0), g,h iid standard Gaussians, independent across layers, and the angle between the resulting vectors. Kill at zero norm or zero angle. For the hybrid kernel use a fixed small concentration box for (mean(x^2+y^2),mean((x-y)^2)/theta^2,mean(x^2-y^2)/theta) at small theta, and ordinary Gram averages at larger theta, each centered at its expectation; self-loop on failure. Limit: New global localization proof awaits reviewer audit. This is moment decay and rare-return control, not the sharp asymptotic E theta_k~3pi/k or a finite-width weak-rate theorem. Literature novelty not asserted.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:d217043545da2a40987c42088792bfbac5c0890229369c9694436297afecd9b8","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/d2/d217043545da2a40987c42088792bfbac5c0890229369c9694436297afecd9b8.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:98724c8e7c4c4475db5c666bd81d25ff0417c42dc077cf1ae14f24f3ad7d26fa","bundle_entry_key":"relu-global-angle-moments","bundle_id":"population.t244-logarithmic-bounded-weak-rate-015","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; random neural networks","draft":"w691/bundle_015.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.randomnetworks:t244-relu-global-angle-moments","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C039: global angle moment decay and rare late returns

Version 1, 20 October 2026. Target 1, kind moved, proof (unaudited).
This removes the small-angle stopping restriction from C037 by specifying
a global hybrid regularization. No novelty relative to the literature is
asserted. Its purpose is quantitative entrance localization for the rate.

## Statement

Let the width-n Gaussian, zero-bias ReLU angle chain start at any
theta0 in (0,pi]. Set the angle to zero and absorb when either layer vector
vanishes or its angle is exactly zero. For every fixed positive integer p
and finite T there are C_(p,T),c>0 and n0 such that for n>=n0,

    E[theta_k^p; alive at k] <= C_(p,T)/(k+1)^p,
                              0<=k<=floor(Tn).                (1)

For 0<eta<=pi and integers 0<=m<=N<=floor(Tn),

    P(max_(m<=k<=N) theta_k >= eta)
       <= C_(p,T)/(eta^p (m+1)^p)+C_T n exp(-cn).              (2)

The same estimates hold for the hybrid regularized chain below; its
exponential error term in (2) is unnecessary. These constants are uniform
in the initial angle. The alive indicator excludes any cemetery inverse
moments; on alive states U_k=1/(n theta_k) and (1) gives
E[U_k^(-p);alive]<=C_(p,T)n^p/(k+1)^p.

In particular, for any delta>0, r>0, fixed eta>0, and p with delta*p>r,
the probability of any return to theta>=eta between ceil(n^delta) and Tn
is o(n^(-r)). Here delta<1 ensures a nonempty interval eventually.

## 1. Hybrid concentration event, uniform over all angles

For independent standard Gaussians g_i,h_i write

    x_i=(g_i)_+, y_i=(cos(theta)g_i+sin(theta)h_i)_+.

Fix a sufficiently small angle threshold theta_*>0. When theta<=theta_*,
use C032's fixed small concentration box for the averages of

    (x^2+y^2, (x-y)^2/theta^2, (x^2-y^2)/theta)

about their population mean. On it the output angle divided by theta
is bounded above and below by positive constants; it is a smooth function
of those averages with uniformly bounded first and second derivatives.
These facts follow directly from C032's positive Gram determinant and
uniform normalized angle formula, not from a reciprocal raw moment.

When theta>theta_*, use the ordinary Gram averages

    (A,B,C)=(mean x^2, mean y^2, mean xy).

Their mean is (1/2,1/2,kappa(theta)/2), where

    kappa(theta)=[sin(theta)+(pi-theta)cos(theta)]/pi.

Since kappa(theta)<=kappa(theta_*)<1, a fixed sufficiently small box
about these means ensures A,B bounded away from zero and
C/sqrt(AB) in a compact subinterval of (-1,1), uniformly in this angle
range. This is valid also at theta=pi, where the population cross term
is zero. On the box

    alpha=arccos(C/sqrt(AB))

and (alpha/theta)^p have uniformly bounded first and second coordinate
derivatives, and alpha/theta is bounded above and below by positive
constants. The artificial part of the box with C<0 only supplies a smooth
extension; every realized ReLU cross term is nonnegative.

Both sets of row coordinates have uniformly bounded moments and a common
positive neighborhood of exponential integrability. For the normalized
rows this is the Gaussian quadratic-form domination in C032; for the
ordinary rows it follows from |xy|<=(x^2+y^2)/2 and Gaussian squares.
Chernoff bounds give a uniform good-event failure probability C exp(-cn).
Uniform row second moments also imply E|Zbar-EZ|^2<=C/n.

Define the global regularized transition to use the actual angle on its
appropriate good event and self-loop off it. Its angle stays in (0,pi]
and its angle ratio is bounded above and below uniformly. Piecewise choice
at theta_* is measurable; no differentiability of this kernel in theta is
used.

## 2. A global one-step nonlinear drift

Let F(theta)=arccos(kappa(theta)). The second-order sample-average Taylor
argument used in C037, now applied to each of the two boxes, gives

    E[(theta_next/theta)^p]
        <= [F(theta)/theta]^p+C_p/n,
                          uniformly for 0<theta<=pi.          (3)

For small theta use the normalized angular ratio test; for larger theta
divide the ordinary angle test by theta^p, whose denominator is bounded
below by theta_*^p. Centered linear terms have zero mean before truncation
and exponentially small deleted expectation. Quadratic remainders are
O(1/n). Off-box self-loops and bounded deterministic test values add only
exponentially small errors. Thus (3) does not divide an absolute angular
error by an arbitrarily small theta.

For theta>0, kappa(theta)-cos(theta)=(sin(theta)-theta cos(theta))/pi>0:
the numerator has derivative theta sin(theta)>0 on (0,pi) and starts at0.
Hence 0<F(theta)<theta. At zero F(theta)/theta=1-a theta+O(theta^2),
a=1/(3pi). The continuous function

    [1-(F(theta)/theta)^p]/theta

is therefore strictly positive on the compact interval [0,pi], with
limiting value p*a at zero. Choose c_p>0 below its minimum and small enough
that c_p*pi<=1/2. Equation (3) then implies

    E[theta_next^p | theta]
           <= (1+C_p/n)theta^p-c_p theta^(p+1).                (4)

## 3. Moment decay and the maximal bound

With m_k=E theta_k^p, Jensen transforms (4) into

    m_(k+1)<=rho m_k-c_p m_k^(1+1/p), rho=1+C_p/n.

The discrete nonlinear comparison in C037 applies on [0,pi] too: put
v_k=rho^(-k)m_k, decrease c_p if necessary so (c_p/rho)v_k^(1/p)<=1/2,
and use (1-z)^(-1/p)>=1+z/p. It gives v_k<=C_p/(k+1)^p, uniformly in
m0<=pi^p. Multiplication by rho^k<=exp(C_p T) proves (1) for the
regularized chain.

By (4) without its negative term, rho^(-k)theta_k^p is a nonnegative
supermartingale. Apply its conditional maximal inequality starting at m:

    P(max_(m<=k<=N)theta_k>=eta)
       <=rho^(N-m) E theta_m^p/eta^p
       <=C_(p,T)/(eta^p(m+1)^p).

This proves (2) for the regularized chain.

## 4. Transfer to the exact chain

Use identical Gaussian rows until the first hybrid good-event failure.
Its probability by time N is at most C N exp(-cn), uniformly over the
entire state range, by conditioning on the past at each layer. Until then
both chains are nondegenerate and have identical angles. Killed exact
angles lie in [0,pi]. Their pth moments thus differ at time k by at most
C pi^p k exp(-cn); their late-return event probabilities differ by at most
C N exp(-cn). For k<=Tn the moment error can be absorbed in C_(p,T)/(k+1)^p,
since (Tn+1)^(p+1) exp(-cn) is uniformly bounded. This proves (1)-(2).

## Remaining matching problem

These estimates allow a polynomial burn-in followed by small-angle
localization with an arbitrarily high fixed polynomial confidence level.
They do not determine the coefficient of the singular occupation sum.
In particular, an upper bound E theta_k<=C/(k+1) is not the asymptotic
E theta_k~3pi/k needed to identify the logarithmic bias coefficient.
That sharp mesoscopic statement and the associated weak-error matching
remain separate steps.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:48d5412d05f2566420246d906fe5e2cb5ea63da0a7aee9e2d7460ec5d88ae3f3","revision_digest":"sha256:3fa83ce44fb574362f46b2a57b62c0857f8fe7e4bc8ae34f8b6d54ca52943321","source_id":"own-work:T244-w691-C039:v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20-v1","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Proposition prop:limit_of_difference_operator_intro of arXiv:2507.22011, 'Random Lozenge Waterfall:\\Dimensional Collapse of Gibbs Measures'] \begin{enumerate}[$\bullet$]
		\item
			If $(\mathsf{t},\mathsf{x})$ is above or below $\mathcal{W}$, we have $d(\Delta x)=0$ and $a(\Delta x)=-1$, that is, the
			limiting difference operator is the negative identity $(-Id)$;
		\item If $(\mathsf{t},\mathsf{x})$ lies on the upper boundary of $\mathcal{W}$,
			then
			\begin{equation*}
				d(\Delta x)=-\kappa^{2} q^{2\Delta x+1/2},
				\qquad
				a(\Delta x)=-1-\kappa^{2}(1+q)q^{2\Delta x+1}.
			\end{equation*}
			On the lower boundary of $\mathcal{W}$, 
			one has to 
			replace the powers of $(q,\kappa)$ with those of
			$(q^{-1},\kappa^{-1})$, while the factor $1+q$ is kept
			the same.
		\item 
			Inside $\mathcal{W}$ but away
			from its center line $\lfloor
			L\hspace{1pt}\mathsf{x}\rfloor=\tfrac12(S+t)$, the
			coefficients in the upper half are
			\begin{equation*}
				d(\Delta x)=-\kappa^{2} q^{2\Delta x+1/2},
				\qquad 
				a(\Delta x)=-\kappa^{2}(1+q)q^{2\Delta x+1}.
			\end{equation*}
			The formulas for the lower part are obtained from these by the same symmetry as in the preceding item.
		\item
			On the center line, we get
			\begin{equation}
				
				d(\Delta x)=\dfrac{-\kappa^2(1 - \kappa^2 q^{2\Delta x})^{-1} q^{2\Delta x+1/2}}{
				\sqrt{(1 - \kappa^2 q^{2\Delta x-1}) (1 - \kappa^2 q^{2\Delta x+1})}}
				,\qquad
				a(\Delta x)=
				\dfrac{-\kappa^2 (1+q) \hspace{1pt} q^{2\Delta x+1}}{(1-\kappa^2 q^{2 \Delta x})(1-\kappa^2 q^{2\Delta x+2})}.
			\end{equation}
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm Sprobab of arXiv:2608.13084, '\bf Branching random walk in random environment'] The following holds for any dimension and for any $p\in(0,1)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textbf{(1)}] If $\max\{m_\circ, m_\bullet\}\le 1$ and $\min\{\mu_\circ(1), \mu_\bullet(1) \}<1$, then for ${\bf P}_p$-a.s. environment $\omega$,
\[
{\mathbb P}^\omega(\mathcal{S}) =0.
\]
\item[\textbf{(2)}] If $\max\{m_\circ, m_\bullet\}> 1$ and $\max\{\mu_\circ(0), \mu_\bullet(0) \}<1$, then for ${\bf P}_p$-a.s. environment $\omega$,
\[
{\mathbb P}^\omega(\mathcal{S}) >0.
\]
\item[\textbf{(3)}] If $\max\{m_\circ, m_\bullet\}> 1$ and $\max\{\mu_\circ(0), \mu_\bullet(0) \}=1$, then 
\[
{\mathbb P}(\mathcal{S})>0,
\]
and 
\[
{\bf P}_p\left( \omega : {\mathbb P}^\omega(\mathcal{S}) = 0 \right) >0. 
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\[\widetilde{\Sigma} = k + \frac{(\mu-k)^3}{k^2}.\]
Furthermore, when $k = \frac{\mu}{2}$, these simplify into $\Sigma = \frac{\mu}{2-2p}$ and $\widetilde{\Sigma} = \mu. $ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Fix an irrational theta and reduced rationals p_j/q_j tending to theta with q_j tending to infinity. The clock/shift pairs U_j,V_j from the nilpotent construction, with omega_j=exp(2*pi*i*p_j/q_j) and c_j=exp(pi*i/q_j), converge in all star-moments and in the norms of every fixed matrix-valued star-polynomial to the canonical irrational rotation pair u,v. This uses simplicity and the faithful canonical trace of the irrational rotation C*-algebra. The cached Fang--Jiang--Lin--Xu paper, arXiv:1210.4771v1, Theorem 12.2, identifies the Brown measure of u+v in this canonical tracial representation as Haar measure on the unit circle. Every finite sum U_j+V_j has empirical eigenvalue measure delta_0. This gives a candidate counterexample to the implication from arbitrary strong convergence to Brown-measure convergence, pending independent review and with no novelty claim. It does not address independent Ginibre ensembles or a free limiting family.

PRIVATE EXHAUSTIVE COMPUTATION, author-checked. For each n <= 40, among all p(n) partitions of n (p(40) = 37338) the maximum of the dimension n!/prod(hooks) is attained either by a single self-conjugate partition (n in {1,3,5,6,8,10,12,15,17,21,23,27,30,34,36,38}) or by exactly one pair of mutually conjugate partitions; no tie between non-conjugate shapes occurs. Since conjugation preserves the hook multiset, dim(lambda) = dim(lambda'), so Romik's question (The surprising mathematics of longest increasing subsequences, Section 1.18) whether the maximal-dimension shape is unique must be read up to conjugation; with that reading it holds for all n <= 40 and is open beyond.

body:
[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2604.07478, 'Mixing Times and Cutoff for the Rook's Walk'] For any $n\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 3}$ and $d\in \mathbb{Z}_{ \geq 2}$, let   $\Omega,\Omega_*$, $P,P_*$ and $\pi,\pi_*$ be the state space, transition matrix and stationary distribution of the standard Rook's walk and the RWBD chains resp. each with parameters $n$ and $d$. Also, let $x\in \Omega_*$. Then,
  \[\Vert P_*^t(x,\cdot) - \pi_*(\cdot) \Vert_\text{TV} = \Vert (P^t \mu_x)(\cdot) - \pi(\cdot) \Vert_\text{TV}\]
  where $\mu_x$ is a distribution of $\Omega$ with probabilities uniformly distributed over $H_x$. That is,
   \[\mu_x(h) = \begin{cases}
      \frac{1}{\varphi(x)}, \quad &h\in H_x\\
      0, \quad &h\not\in H_x
   \end{cases}\]
   for all $h\in \Omega$, where $\varphi(x) = {d \choose i}(n-1)^i$ as in Definition \ref{defphi}.
   \begin{proof}
      \begin{align*}
         \Vert P_*^t(x,\cdot) - \pi_*(\cdot) \Vert_\text{TV} &= \frac{1}{2}\sum_{y\in \Omega_*}|P^t_*(x,y) -\pi_*(y)|\\
         &= \frac{1}{2}\sum_{y\in \Omega_*}|(P^t \mu_x)(H_y) -\pi(H_y)| \tag{By Def. \ref{BDRW}}\\
         &= \frac{1}{2}\sum_{y\in \Omega_*}\sum_{h_y\in H_y}|(P^t \mu_x)(h_y) -\pi(h_y)|\\
         &= \frac{1}{2}\sum_{z\in \Omega}|(P^t \mu_x)(z) -\pi(z)|\\
         &= \Vert (P^t \mu_x)(\cdot) - \pi(\cdot) \Vert_\text{TV}
      \end{align*}
   \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 8 of arXiv:2604.07478

[Theorem ww1 of arXiv:2512.17727, 'Stochastic transport equation with L\'evy noise'] {Under the assumptions of Theorem (d32 of the paper),}
there exists a $\mathbb{P}$-full event $\Omega^{\prime\prime}$ such that,
for all  $\omega \in \Omega^{\prime\prime}$ and $T>0$,  $0\le s \le  t \le T$,
the mapping: \[\mathbb R^d \ni x \mapsto \phi_{s,t}(x) \in \mathbb R^d\] is  a surjective diffeomorphism of $C^1$-class and,
for any $\delta \in (0,\frac{\alpha}2+\beta-1)$,
the function
\[
\mathbb{R}^d \ni x \mapsto D \phi_{s,t}(x)   \in \mathscr{L}(\mathbb R^d,\mathbb R^d) \]
is locally $\delta$-H\"older continuous  uniformly in $(s,t) \in [0,T] \times [0,T]$.

Moreover,  for every  $\omega \in \Omega^{\prime\prime}$ and  for any $\delta \in (0,\frac{\alpha}2+\beta-1)$,
the  function
\[ \mathbb{R}^d \ni x \mapsto  D (\phi_{s,t}^{-1} )(x) \in \mathscr{L}(\mathbb R^d,\mathbb R^d) \]
  is     locally $\delta$-H\"older continuous  uniformly in $(s,t) \in [0,T] \times [0,T]$.

  Finally, for every  $\omega \in \Omega^{\prime\prime}$  and for every $x \in \mathbb R^d, $  the functions
  \begin{align}
  & [0,T]\times [0,T] \ni (s,t) \mapsto D \phi_{s,t}(x)
   \\&
    [0,T]\times [0,T] \ni (s,t) \mapsto  D (\phi_{s,t}^{-1} )(x)
  \end{align}
 are separately c\`adl\`ag, i.e., for each $s \in [0,T]$,
  \[ [0,T] \ni t \mapsto  D \phi_{s,t}(x) \in \mathbb R^d \mbox{ is c\`adl\`ag}\] and  for each $t \in [0,T]$, the map
  \[ [0,T] \ni s \mapsto  D \phi_{s,t}(x)\in \mathbb R^d  \mbox{ is c\`adl\`ag}.\]
  The same holds for $ D (\phi_{s,t}^{-1} )(x)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Prop S-T-slice-univ-prop of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $S\subset T$ be a cleft, and let $X\in\Spc_T$. The Yoneda embedding $y\colon{\mathpalette\ulhelper{X}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}\to\ul\Spc_{T/X}$ factors uniquely through $\ul\Spc_{S\triangleright T/X}\coloneqq\smash{\ul\Spc_{T/X}\times_{\ul\Spc_T}\ul\Spc_{S\triangleright T}}$, exhibiting the latter as $S$-cocompletion. Moreover, given any commutative monoid structure $X^\otimes$ on $X$, $\ul\Spc_{S\triangleright T/X}$ is a symmetric monoidal subcategory with respect to the slice symmetric monoidal structure on $\smash{\ul\Spc_{T/X}}$, and $\smash{y^\otimes\colon{\mathpalette\ulhelper{X}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}^\otimes\to\ul\Spc_{S\triangleright T/X}^\otimes}$ is a symmetric monoidal $S$-cocompletion.
    \begin{proof}
        Proposition~(prop:spc-T-cart-pres-sym-mon of the paper) shows that $\smash{\ul\Spc_{S\triangleright T/X}^\otimes}$ is a symmetric monoidal subcategory for any commutative monoid $X^\otimes$. In light of the previous proposition, it will therefore once more suffice to prove the non-monoidal universal property. By [martiniwolf2021limits]*{Theorem 7.1.13} this reduces to showing that $\smash{\ul\Spc_{S\triangleright T/X}}\subset\ul\Spc_{T/X}$ is the smallest subcategory containing the Yoneda image and closed under $S$-colimits.

        By design, $\ul\Spc_{S\triangleright T}\subset\ul\Spc_T$ contains the terminal object, and so the description of the Yoneda image from Remark~(rk:slice-vs-shift of the paper) shows that the Yoneda embedding factors through $\ul\Spc_{S\triangleright T/X}$. Moreover, as $\ul\Spc_{S\triangleright T}\subset\ul\Spc_T$ is closed under $S$-colimits, so is $\ul\Spc_{S\triangleright T/X}\subset\ul\Spc_T$. Conversely, let $A\in T$ be arbitrary, let $a\colon A\to 1$ be the unique map in $\PSh(T)$, and let $Y\to a^*X$ define an element of $\ul\Spc_{S\triangleright T/X}(A)\subset(\PSh(T)_{/A})_{/X\times A}$; we want to show that $Y$ is an $S$-colimit of objects in the Yoneda image, which translates to saying that every $(f,g)\colon Z\to X\times A$ with $Z\in\Spc_S\subset\Spc_T$ is an $S$-colimit in $\ul\Spc_{T}(X\times{-})$ of objects in the Yoneda image. But it follows straight from the definitions that $(f,g)$ is the image under $f_!$ of $(\textup{id},g)\colon X\to X\times A$, and the latter belongs to the Yoneda image by Remark~(rk:Yoneda-image of the paper).
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop S-T-slice-univ-prop of arXiv:2608.28504

[Lemma lem:spread of arXiv:2608.24830, 'Motion helps the contact process: survival below\\ the percolation threshold on Poisson Br'] Fix the ratio $\mathfrak{b}=\beta/L^2$. There is $c_p=c_p(\mathfrak{o},\mathfrak{b},d)>0$ such that the following holds
for all large $L$. Let $\mathcal F$ be generated by the auxiliary objects of the cell together
with the marked configuration on $[\tau\beta,\tau\beta+T_L]$, so that each $\Upsilon_z$ is
$\mathcal F$-measurable and its particles lie in the reduced super-cube $Q^{*}_-(i)$ at time
$\tau\beta+T_L$. Then,
conditionally on $\mathcal F$, the events
\begin{align*}
  \mathcal S_v&=\big\{v\text{ carries no recovery mark in }(\tau\beta+T_L,(\tau+1)\beta]\big\},\\
  \mathcal T_v^{i'}&=\big\{v\text{ stays in }Q^{*}(i)\text{ on }[\tau\beta+T_L,(\tau+1)\beta]
  \text{ and }v\in C_{i'}\text{ at time }(\tau+1)\beta\big\}
\end{align*}
are independent over $v\in\Upsilon_z$, and $\mathbb{P}[\mathcal S_v\cap\mathcal T_v^{i'}\mid\mathcal F]
\ge c_p\,e^{-\mu\beta}$ for every $v\in\Upsilon_z$ and every $i'$ with
$\|i'-i\|_\infty\le\mathfrak{o}-1$. Consequently, if $|\Upsilon_z|\ge n$ then for every $\nu$ with $1\le\nu\le n+1$
\[
  \mathbb{P}\big[\text{fewer than }\nu\text{ particles }v\in\Upsilon_z\text{ satisfy }
  \mathcal S_v\cap\mathcal T_v^{i'}\ \big|\ \mathcal F\big]
  \ \le\ \binom{n}{\nu-1}\big(1-c_pe^{-\mu\beta}\big)^{n-\nu+1} .
\]

[Corollary 20 (No atoms under partial coordinate shifts) of arXiv:2607.16502, 'Asymptotic Behavior of Path Functionals for Vector-Valued Gaussian Processes at High Level'] Let \(L>0\), let \(G:\R^d\to\R_+\) be continuous and coordinatewise
non-decreasing, and let
\(\mu\) be a regular finite capacity satisfying the support-intersection
property on \(E\), with \(\mu(E)>0\).  Let
\(D\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) be non-empty, let
\(\bm c\in\R^{D^c}\), and put
\[
  G_{D,\bm c}(\bm y_D)=G(\bm y_D,\bm c_{D^c}).
\]
Let \(\bm U\) be a continuous \(\R^{|D|}\)-valued stochastic process on
\(E\), and suppose that \(G_{D,\bm c}\) and \(\mu\) satisfy either
condition~\ref{sojorn F2 condition a} or
condition~\ref{sojorn F2 condition b} of
Lemma~\ref{sojorn_F2_cap}.  Then
\[
  \pk{
    \int_E G_{D,\bm c}(\bm U(t)-\bm x_D)\,d\mu(t)=L
  }=0
\]
for Lebesgue-a.e. \(\bm x_D\in\R^{|D|}\).  If this expression is embedded in a
full shift vector \(\bm x\in\R^d\) but is independent of
\(\bm x_{D^c}\), the same no-atom statement holds for Lebesgue-a.e.
\(\bm x\in\R^d\).

[Defn def:3.2 of arXiv:2606.16237, 'The Backward Stochastic Partial Differential Integral Equations: Solvability and Compariso'] A triple of processes \((u, q, r) \in \mathbb{S}^2(H^1) \cap \mathbb{H}^2 \times \mathbb{H}^1 \times \mathbb{H}^{\nu,1}\) is called a strong solution to BSPDIE (equation eq:3.2 of the paper) if, for any \(t \in [0,T]\) and a.e. \(x \in \mathbb{R}^d\),
\begin{eqnarray*}
u(t,x) &=& \varphi(x) + \int_t^T \Bigg(
a^{ij}(s,x) D_{ij} u(s,x) + b^i(s,x) D_{i} u(s,x) + c(s,x) u(s,x) \nonumber\\
&&+ \int_Z \Big[ u(s, x + k(s,e,x)) - u(s,x) - k^i(s,e,x) D_{i} u(s,x) \Big] \nu(de) \nonumber\\
&&+ \sigma^i(s,x) D_{i} q(s,x) + v(s,x) q(s,x) + f_0(s,x) \nonumber\\
&&+ \int_Z \Big[ r(s,e, x + k(s,e,x)) - r(s,e,x) \Big] \nu(de)
\Bigg) ds \nonumber\\
&&- \int_t^T q(s,x)dW_s - \int_t^T \int_Z r(s,e,x)\tilde{\mu}(de,ds).
\end{eqnarray*}
title: Defn def:3.2 of arXiv:2606.16237

[Conjecture Typical AHMS dimension of arXiv:2609.02155, 'Exact Limits of Random Projections for Preserving Geometry:\\ Distance Recovery, Nearest-N'] \label[conjecture]{conj:ordinal-gaussian}
For Gaussian point clouds whose ambient dimension is at least proportional to
$n$, the AHMS dimension of the induced strict distance ordering is
$\Omega(n)$ with high probability. Thus Gaussian orderings would have the same
linear-dimensional order as the worst case. More quantitatively, the minimum
Kendall distance to $\mathcal O_{n,m}$ should interpolate between the classical counting
obstruction and the pairwise $\sqrt{m/d}$ law. The counting ratio cannot
prove this distribution-specific statement because Gaussian distance
orderings are not uniform. (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Typical AHMS dimension

[Lemma 9 (Parity-weighted inner comparison) of arXiv:2609.02788, '\textbf{Quantized Einstein Metrics on \(S^7\) with \(SU(3)\)-Symmetry}'] At the overlap $t=\delta_b=b^{1/2}$,
\begin{equation}
 |V_{\PE}(s_b)-V_{\RF}(s_b)|
 \le C\delta_b^2\,|V_{\RF}(s_b)|,
\end{equation}
uniformly for $|\mu|\le\mu_0$.  Equivalently, the
positive-Einstein perturbation changes the rotating odd amplitude only by the
relative factor $1+O(\delta_b^2)$.
title: Parity-weighted inner comparison

[Lemma 13 of arXiv:2605.12475, 'Central limit theorem for the homozygosity of the hierarchical Pitman-Yor process'] The stable contribution satisfies
\bal
X_{m,L}(\alpha, \theta_0, \beta, \theta) \xrightarrow{D} N(0, \sigma_{X,m,L}^2),
\eal
as $\theta_0, \theta \to \infty$ such that $\frac{\theta_0}{\theta} \to c$, where 
\bal
\sigma_{X,m,L}^2 &= \frac{\sum_{j=1}^{2m} \tilde{A}_j(\beta, m, L) \frac{(1 - \alpha)_{(j-1)}}{\beta^j c^{j-1}} -  \sum_{1 \leq i,j \leq m} A_i(\beta, m, L) A_j(\beta, m, L)  \frac{(1 - \alpha)_{(i+j-1)}}{\beta^{i+j} c^{i+j-1}}  }{\left( \sum_{j=1}^m A_j(\beta, m, L) \frac{(1 - \alpha)_{(j-1)}}{\beta^j c^{j-1}} \right)^2}
\eal
and the coefficients $\{\tilde{A}_j(\beta, m, L)\}_{1 \leq j \leq 2m}$ are defined by
\bal
\tilde{A}_j(\beta, m, L) = \sum_{\bm{m}_1 \in M_{m,L}} \sum_{\bm{m}_2 \in M_{m,L}} \sum_{\bm{j} \in M_{j,L}} \prod_{k=1}^L \Cs(m_{1k} + m_{2k}, j_k, \beta).
\eal

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2609.03112, '2609.03112'] The function in \eqref{eq:rational-theta-component} is a finite linear
combination of theta components on finite-volume arithmetic quotients of
$G^2$.  Along the associated affine horocycle, each component lies on one of
finitely many rational translates of $Y$, with irrational translation
coordinate $q\alpha+r$, where $q\in\Q^\times$ and $r\in\Q$.  Hence, if
$\alpha$ is Diophantine of finite type,
\cref{lem:marklof-nonescape,lem:theta-domination} apply componentwise.

body: [Lemma cob-decomp of arXiv:2608.27904, 'Instantons, indefinite 4-manifolds, and Dehn surgery'] Suppose $W: Y \to Y'$ is a cobordism between rational homology spheres with $b^+(W) = k > 0$ and $b_1(W) = 0$. [Theorem 24 (see \cite{FrGue}) of arXiv:2608.01516, 'Nondegeneracy and regularity of polynomial pushforwards'] Let $K$ be a compact convex set in $\mathbb R^n$, let
$p\in\mathbb N$, and let
\[
u_j\colon K\to\mathbb R,
\quad j=1,\ldots,p,
\]
be continuous functions. Let $P_{u_1,\ldots,u_p}(K)\ne\emptyset$ be the set of all
log-concave measures $\nu$ supported in $K$ such that
\[
\int_K u_j\,d\nu\ge0,
\quad j=1,\ldots,p.
\]
Let
\[
\Phi\colon P(K)\to\mathbb R
\]
be a convex continuous functional, where $P(K)$ is the space of all Borel
probability measures on $K$, equipped with the weak topology. Then
\[
\sup_{\nu\in P_{u_1,\ldots,u_p}(K)} \Phi(\nu)
\]
is attained at a log-concave measure $\nu\in P_{u_1,\ldots,u_p}(K)$ such that
the affine span $S(\nu)$ of $\operatorname{supp}(\nu)$ satisfies
\[
\dim S(\nu)\le p.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\sup_{\mu\in P_{u_1,\ldots,u_p}(K)} \Phi(\nu)
=
\sup_{\substack{\nu\in P_{u_1,\ldots,u_p}(K)\\ \dim S(\nu)\le p}}
\Phi(\nu).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:sc-dual-Darboux of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] Let $K$ be dual dressing compatible with $(\Psi, \Phi)$, with
resolvent $R(u) = (I - zK(u))^{-1}$.  Define the dressed
observable and dressed waves by
\[
\mathcal{M}(u) \vcentcolon= I + z\Phi(u)R(u)\Psi(u),
\]
\[
\widehat\Psi(u) \vcentcolon= R(u)\Psi(u), \qquad
\widehat\Phi(u) \vcentcolon= \Phi(u)R(T^{-1}u).
\]
Then $\mathcal{M}(u)$ is invertible for every
$u \in \mathcal{V}$.  The dressed waves
$\widehat\Psi, \widehat\Phi$ satisfy the dual
linear problem
(equation eq:sc-dual-linear-1 of the paper)--(equation eq:sc-dual-linear-j of the paper) and
dual adjoint problem
(equation eq:sc-dual-adjoint-1 of the paper)--(equation eq:sc-dual-adjoint-j of the paper)
respectively, with data $(\mathcal{M}_k, \Lambda_k)$: for each $j \geq 2$,
\begin{align*}
\partial_1\widehat\Psi(Tu)
  &= \widehat\Psi(Tu)\mathcal{M}_1(u)
     - \widehat\Psi(u)\Lambda_1(u), \\
\widehat\Psi(S_j u)
  &= \widehat\Psi(Tu)\mathcal{M}_j(u)
     - \widehat\Psi(u)\Lambda_j(u),
\shortintertext{and}
\partial_1\widehat\Phi(Tu)
  &= \Lambda_1(Tu)\widehat\Phi(T^2u)
     - \mathcal{M}_1(u)\widehat\Phi(Tu), \\
\widehat\Phi(Tu)
  &= \mathcal{M}_j(u)\widehat\Phi(S_j u)
     - \Lambda_j(Tu)\widehat\Phi(TS_j u),
\end{align*}
where the dressed edge weights are given by
\begin{align}
\mathcal{M}_1(u)
  &\vcentcolon= \mathcal{M}(Tu)^{-1}C_1(u)\mathcal{M}(Tu)
  + \mathcal{M}(Tu)^{-1}\partial_1\mathcal{M}(Tu),
   \\
\mathcal{M}_j(u)
  &\vcentcolon= \mathcal{M}(Tu)^{-1}C_j(u)\mathcal{M}(S_j u),
  
\end{align}
and $\widehat K(u) \vcentcolon= K(u)R(u)$ is dual dressing compatible
with $(\widehat\Psi, \widehat\Phi)$.
Moreover, $(\mathcal{M}_k, \Lambda_k)$ satisfies the dual
diamond equations of
Corollary~(cor:sc-dual-diamonds of the paper).

[Cor sparsestack-no-osi of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] For every integer $\zeta\ge2$ and every choice of
$\varepsilon,\alpha>0$ there are constants $B_0,C>0$
depending only on $\zeta, \varepsilon,\alpha$
with the following property.
Let $b\geq B_0$, let $k=\zeta b$ and $n\geq C\,k$,
and assume that the $n\times k$ matrix $S$
is SparseStack with row
sparsity $\zeta$ and with block size $b$.
Let $\Omega$ be any non-random subset of $[n]$ of size at least $\varepsilon\,k$.
Then with probability at least $0.99$,
\[
s_{\min}\left((S^\top)_{\Omega}\right)< \alpha,
\]
where $s_{\min}\left((S^\top)_{\Omega}\right)$ is the 
smallest singular value of the $k\times |\Omega|$ submatrix $(S^\top)_\Omega$.
In particular, $S$ is not $(\varepsilon\,k,\alpha)$--OSI. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: No OSI for constant-sparsity SparseStack model

$$
where $\text{Sub}(G)$ denotes the set of all subgroups of $G$.

body:
[Defn d:noise of arXiv:2607.18194, 'Temperature chaos in directed polymers'] For $d\in\mathbb{N}$, a \emph{$d$-dimensional noise} consists of a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$, a collection of sub-$\sigma$-algebras $\{\mathcal{F}_R\}_{R\in\mathcal{R}}$ where $\mathcal{R}$ is the set of open $d$-dimensional rectangles in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and a measurable $\mathbb{R}^d$-action $\{\theta_h\}_{h\in\mathbb{R}^d}$ on $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$,
    such that the following properties hold.
    \begin{enumerate}[label={\rm(N\arabic*)},ref={\rm N\arabic*}]
        \item
        \textup{(Exhaustive filtration).} $\mathcal{F} = \bigvee_{R\in\mathcal{R}} \mathcal{F}_R$.
        \item 
        \textup{(Translation covariance).}
        For all $h\in\mathbb{R}^d$, we have $\theta_h(\mathcal{F}_R) = \mathcal{F}_{R+h}$.
        \item 
        \textup{(Independence).}
        For all $R_1,R_2\in\mathcal{R}$ with $R_1\cap R_2=\varnothing$, the $\sigma$-algebras $\mathcal{F}_{R_1}$ and $\mathcal{F}_{R_2}$ are independent.
        \item
        \textup{(Join).}
        For all $R_1,R_2,R_3\in\mathcal{R}$ with $R_1\cap R_2=\varnothing$ and $\overline{R_1\cup R_2}=\overline{R_3}$, we have $\mathcal{F}_{R_1}\vee \mathcal{F}_{R_2} = \mathcal{F}_{R_3}$ up to null sets.
    \end{enumerate}
title: Noise

body:
Let $T: X \to X$ be a continuous map of a compact metric space $(X, d)$. For $n \ge 1$ define the dynamical metric $d_n(x, y) = \max_{0 \le k < n} d(T^k x, T^k y)$. A set $E \subset X$ is $(n, \varepsilon)$-separated if $d_n(x, y) > \varepsilon$ for all distinct $x, y \in E$; let $s(n, \varepsilon)$ be the maximal cardinality of such a set (finite by compactness). A set $F$ is $(n, \varepsilon)$-spanning if every $x \in X$ has $d_n(x, y) \le \varepsilon$ for some $y \in F$; let $r(n, \varepsilon)$ be the minimal cardinality. The topological entropy is
$$h_{top}(T) = \lim_{\varepsilon \to 0} \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n} \log s(n, \varepsilon) = \lim_{\varepsilon \to 0} \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n} \log r(n, \varepsilon) \in [0, \infty],$$
using $r(n,\varepsilon) \le s(n,\varepsilon) \le r(n, \varepsilon/2)$; the limit in $\varepsilon$ exists by monotonicity, and replacing the $\limsup$ in $n$ by a $\liminf$ gives the same value. The value is independent of the compatible metric (this uses compactness) and coincides with the open-cover definition $h_{top}(T) = \sup_{\mathcal{U}} \lim_n \frac1n \log N(\mathcal{U}^n_0)$ where $N$ counts the minimal subcover of the join $\mathcal{U}^n_0 = \bigvee_{k<n} T^{-k}\mathcal{U}$. Basic properties: $h_{top}(T^m) = m\, h_{top}(T)$ for $m \ge 1$; $h_{top}(T^{-1}) = h_{top}(T)$ for homeomorphisms; $h_{top}$ is an invariant of topological conjugacy; a Lipschitz map of a compact metric space of finite box dimension has finite entropy, but a continuous map of a compact metric space can have $h_{top} = \infty$. On a NON-compact space the separated-set quantity depends on the metric, not merely on the topology, and the equalities above can fail.

body:
[Lemma 42 (Difference equation for two Ricci--DeTurck solutions) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Let \(s(t)\) be a Ricci-flow background and let \(v_0(t)\) and \(v_1(t)\)
be two positive definite solutions of the Ricci--DeTurck equation relative to
\(s(t)\) on the same time interval.  Put
\[
        U=v_1-v_0,
        \qquad v_\vartheta=v_0+\vartheta(v_1-v_0),
        \quad 0\leq\vartheta\leq1,
\]
and assume that every \(v_\vartheta\) is positive definite.  With \(\nabla\)
the connection of \(s(t)\), the difference satisfies a homogeneous linear
system
\begin{equation}
        \partial_tU-P^{pq}\nabla_p\nabla_qU
        =B^p\nabla_pU+CU,
\end{equation}
where the second-order part is diagonal in the tensor components: in a fixed
frame, every component \(U^A\) is acted on by the same operator
\(P^{pq}\nabla_p\nabla_q\), and no second derivative of a different component
occurs.  More precisely, for
\[
        \mathcal Q_s(v)=-2\Ric(v)+\Lie_{W(v,s)}v,
\]
one has the structural formula
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
        \mathcal Q_s(v)
        ={}&v^{pq}\nabla_p\nabla_qv
        +v^{-1}*v^{-1}*\nabla v*\nabla v \\
        &\quad+\mathcal R(\Rm(s),v,v^{-1}),
\end{split}
\end{equation}
and the mean-value identity
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
        \partial_tU
        &=\mathcal Q_s(v_1)-\mathcal Q_s(v_0)\\
        &=\int_0^1D\mathcal Q_s|_{v_\vartheta}[U] \,d\vartheta.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Differentiating \eqref{eq:rdt-structural-form} gives
\begin{equation}
        D\mathcal Q_s|_{v_\vartheta}[Z]
        =v_\vartheta^{pq}\nabla_p\nabla_qZ
          +\mathcal B_\vartheta^p\nabla_pZ+\mathcal C_\vartheta Z,
\end{equation}
with
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
        \mathcal B_\vartheta
        &=v_\vartheta^{-1}*v_\vartheta^{-1}*\nabla v_\vartheta,\\
        \mathcal C_\vartheta
        &=v_\vartheta^{-1}*v_\vartheta^{-1}*\nabla^2v_\vartheta
          +v_\vartheta^{-1}*v_\vartheta^{-1}*v_\vartheta^{-1}
             *\nabla v_\vartheta*\nabla v_\vartheta\\
        &\qquad+\mathcal R_1(\Rm(s),v_\vartheta,v_\vartheta^{-1}).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Here \(*\) denotes universal tensor contractions, and \(\mathcal R\) and
\(\mathcal R_1\) are algebraic in the displayed arguments; in particular,
\(\mathcal R_1\) contains no derivatives of \(v_\vartheta\).  The
coefficients in \eqref{eq:rdt-difference-system} are
\[
 P^{pq}=\int_0^1v_\vartheta^{pq}\,d\vartheta,
 \qquad B^p=\int_0^1\mathcal B_\vartheta^p\,d\vartheta,
 \qquad C=\int_0^1\mathcal C_\vartheta\,d\vartheta.
\]
Consequently, uniform metric equivalence and finite-order bounds for
\(v_0,v_1\), and \(s\) give the corresponding ellipticity and H\"older bounds
for \(P,B,C\).

[Theorem thm-existence of arXiv:2507.09922, 'A scaling limit for Vlasov equations with electrostatic fluctuations'] Assume that the initial condition $f_0\in (L^1\cap L^3)(\mathbb{T}^3\times \mathbb{R}^3,\mathbb{R}_+)$ has finite kinetic energy
  $$\mathcal K(f_0):= \int |v|^2 f_0(x,v)\, dx dv<+\infty.$$
Then the stochastic Vlasov equation (equation stoch-Vlasov-Ito of the paper) admits a weak solution $f\in L^\infty\big(0,T; (L^1\cap L^3)(\mathbb{T}^3\times \mathbb{R}^3,\mathbb{R}_+) \big)$ such that
\begin{itemize}
\item[\rm(a)] for any $p\in [1,3]$, $\mathbb{P}$-a.s. $\|f_t \|_{L^p_{x,v}} \le \|f_0 \|_{L^p_{x,v}}$ for all $t\in [0,T]$;
\item[\rm(b)] for all $q\ge 1$, it holds $\mathbb{E} \mathcal K(f_t)^{2q} \le C_{q,T}<\infty$  for all $t\in [0,T]$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 61 (Poisson-regime limit for likelihood-ratio functionals) of arXiv:2604.09933, 'Explicit cutoff profiles for colored top-\texorpdfstring{$m$}{m}-to-random shuffles'] Assume \eqref{eq:mu-Poisson-assump}. Let \(\Phi:[0,\infty)\to\R\) be continuous and satisfy
\begin{equation}
|\Phi(t)|\le C_\Phi(1+t^d)
\qquad(t\ge0)
\end{equation}
for some \(C_\Phi>0\) and \(d\ge0\). Assume in addition that there exists \(B\ge1\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\) and all \(u\ge0\),
\[
0\le \mu_n(n-u)\,u!\,p^u\le B^u.
\]
Then
\[
\sum_{x\in G_{n,p}}U(x)\,\Phi\!\left(\frac{M_n(x)}{U(x)}\right)
\longrightarrow
\sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty}
\left(\frac{1}{\ell!\,p^\ell}-\frac{1}{(\ell+1)!\,p^{\ell+1}}\right)\Phi\!\bigl(s(\ell)\bigr).
\]

[Definition def:mesh-rewrite of arXiv:2608.15923, 'Universality of two-dimensional Markovian holonomy fields'] Let ${\mathbb{G}}=(V,E,F)$ be a topological map embedded in $\Sigma$. We write
\[
 {\mathrm{mesh}}({\mathbb{G}})
 =
 \max\left\{
 \max_{e\in E}\ell(e),
 \max_{f\in F}\operatorname{diam}(\overline f)
 \right\}.
\]
A sequence $({\mathbb{G}}_n)_{n\geq1}$ has mesh tending to zero if ${\mathrm{mesh}}({\mathbb{G}}_n)\to0$. We always require $o\in V({\mathbb{G}}_n)$.
title: Definition def:mesh-rewrite of arXiv:2608.15923

[Corollary cor:conjugate-constant-poc of arXiv:2607.00149, '\bf Uniform-in-time Propagation-of-Chaos for\\ Stein Variational Gradient Descent'] Let $X_i^N(0)$ be i.i.d. with law $\mu_0$, and set $Y_i^N(0):=A(X_i^N(0))$.  If
\[
        \mathbb E\left\|A(X(0))\right\|^2<\infty,
\]
then the matrix-SVGD flow for $(\pi_A,K_A^{(1)})$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
        \mathbb E\left[\sup_{t\ge0}\, d_{A,1}^2(\mu_t^N,\mu_t)\right]
        \le
        \frac{\operatorname{Tr}\operatorname{Cov}(A(X(0)))}{N}.
\end{equation}
The same estimate holds with $\mu_t^N,\mu_t$ replaced by their time averages.

[Lemma 22 (Hermitian Hoeffding's lemma) of arXiv:2605.24445, 'Matrix concentration inequalities for time-inhomogeneous Markov chains'] \label[lemma]{lem:matrix_hoeffding}
Let \(Y\) be a random matrix in \(\Hm\) such that \(\E Y=0\) and assume there exists $R > 0$ such that \(-R\Id\preceq Y\preceq R\Id\) almost surely.
Then, for all \(s\in\R\),
\[
\E\big[\exp(sY)\big]\ \preceq\ \cosh(sR)\,\Id\ \preceq\ \exp\!\Big(\frac{s^2R^2}{2}\Big)\Id.
\]
In particular, \(\|\E[\exp(sY)]\|_{\op}\le \exp(s^2R^2/2)\) and
\(\E[\tr \exp(sY)]\le m\,\exp(s^2R^2/2)\).

body: Consider a parametric model with parameter theta in an open subset of R^d, satisfying standard regularity (identifiability, smoothness, nonsingular Fisher information, true parameter interior to the space), and a null hypothesis restricting theta to a smooth submodel of codimension k. Let Lambda_n be the likelihood ratio: the supremum of the likelihood over the full model divided by its supremum over the null submodel, from n iid observations. Wilks' theorem states that under the null hypothesis, as n -> infinity, 2 log Lambda_n converges in distribution to a chi-squared distribution with k degrees of freedom, justifying the asymptotic chi-squared likelihood-ratio test. Due to Samuel S. Wilks.
title: Wilks' theorem

[Thm 6 (CLT for the normalized traces) of arXiv:2604.26499, 'Spectrum of Random Matrices with Exploding Moments'] Let $M$ be the matrix same as in Condition \ref{cond:matrixcond_1_NonHer} with $\alpha=1$. For any partition $\pi\in\bigcup_{k}\mathcal{P}(k)$, let $Z_N(T_\pi)$ be defined similar as in \eqref{eq:centered and normalized random variables Z_N} for matrix $M$.
Then the family
$
\big(Z_N(T_\pi)\big)_{\pi\in\bigcup_{k}\mathcal{P}(k)}
$
converges, as $N\to\infty$, to a centered Gaussian process
$\big(z(T_\pi)\big)_{\pi\in\bigcup_{k}\mathcal{P}(k)}$.

$$
\mathrm{Cov}\left(z(T_{\pi_1}),z(T_{\pi_2})\right)
=
\sum_{T\in\mathcal P^{\#}(T_{\pi_1},T_{\pi_2})}
\tau^{nh}[T],
$$
where $\mathcal{P}^{\#}(T_{\pi_1},T_{\pi_2})$ denotes the collection of graphs obtained by disjoint copies of the graphs $T_{\pi_1}$ and $T_{\pi_2}$ and gluing them with at least one common edge, and where $\tau^{nh}[T]$ is same as defined in the Theorem \ref{thm:Convergence of normalized trace for non-Hermitian matrices with independent exploding entries}.

[Prop smash-well-based of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $G$ be a compact Lie group and let ${\mathcal{F}}_1,{\mathcal{F}}_2$ be two families of closed subgroups of $G$. If $X$ is ${\mathcal{F}}_1$-cofibrant, then $X\smashp-$ sends $({\mathcal{F}}_1\cap{\mathcal{F}}_2)$-weak equivalences between well-based $G$-spaces to ${\mathcal{F}}_2$-weak equivalences.
    \begin{proof}
       Let $f\colon Y\to Y'$ be an $({\mathcal{F}}_1\cap{\mathcal{F}}_2)$-weak equivalence of well-based $G$-spaces. We note that $(X\smashp f)^H$ agrees up to homeomorphism with $X^H\smashp f^H$ for any $H\subset G$. If $H\in{\mathcal{F}}_2\smallsetminus{\mathcal{F}}_1$, then $X^H=0$, so that $(X\smashp f)^H$ is a homeomorphism; on the other hand, if $H\in{\mathcal{F}}_1\cap{\mathcal{F}}_2$, then $X^H\smashp f^H$ is a weak equivalence as $f^H$ is a weak equivalence of well-based spaces and $X^H$ is well-based.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop smash-well-based of arXiv:2608.28504

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] For a variable $f:X\to\mathbb R$ which follows the uniform law of $[a,b]$,
$$F_f(x)=\frac{e^{ibx}-e^{iax}}{i(b-a)x}$$
is its Fourier transform, $F_f(x)=E(e^{ifx})$.

[Theorem loiexpo of arXiv:2607.00753, 'Threatening excursions in large population\\ quasi-stationary birth and death systems.\\ O'] Let $A$ be an open subset of $\mathds R_{+}^{d}$ satisfying Assumption ${\bf (HS)}$.
For any $t\ge0$
$$
\lim_{K\to\infty}{{\mathds P}}^{({\scriptscriptstyle K})}_{\nu_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}}\big(T^{({\scriptscriptstyle K})}_{A}>t\, M_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}(A)\, \eta_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}(A)\big)=e^{-t}\;.
$$
In other words, the sequence  $\Big(\frac{T^{({\scriptscriptstyle K})}_{A}}{ M_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}(A)\, \eta_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}(A)}\Big)$ issued from $\nu_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}$ converges in law to the exponential law of parameter $1$, as $K$ tends to infinity.
title: Theorem loiexpo of arXiv:2607.00753

[Proposition prop:concentreGp* of arXiv:2603.00773, 'Long-time $L^p$ Wasserstein contraction for diffusion processes without global dissipativi'] Under Assumptions~(Assum:basic of the paper) and~(Assum:PointwiseContractInfty of the paper), assume moreover that $\eta$ is Lipschitz continuous with constant $L_\eta$ and that the contraction~(equation eq:contraction_def of the paper) holds with $p=1$ for some $C_1,\lambda_1>0$. Denote by $\mu_\infty$ the invariant measure of the diffusion process~(equation eq:EDS_X of the paper). Then, for all $p\geqslant 1$ and $t\geqslant 0$,
\[G_p^*(t) \leqslant A e^{- \min(\rho,\rho') t }\]
 with
 \begin{equation}
 
 A= \exp\left(     \frac{p L_\eta C_1}{\lambda_1} \left( R+\int_{\mathbb R^d}|y|\mu_\infty(\text{d} y)\right)  \right)\,, \qquad		\rho' =  - p \mu_\infty(\eta) -  \frac{  |\sigma|^2 C_1^2 p^2 L_\eta^2 }{\lambda_1^2} \,.
 \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:concentreGp* of arXiv:2603.00773

[Lemma l.list of arXiv:2411.12003, 'Central Limit Theorem for non-stationary random products of $\SL(2, \R)$ matrices'] Let the sequence $(\rho_n,\delta_n)_{n\ge n_0}$, \emr{where $n_0$ is given by Lemma~(l:var-lower of the paper)},
    be chosen in such a way that the following conditions hold:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item As $n\to\infty$, one has
        $  \rho_n\to \infty$ and  $\delta_n\to 0$.
        \item For some $n_1\ge 2n_0$, we have
        \[
        \rho_n=\rho'_0, \quad \delta_n= 3 \overline{C}^{\textcolor{black}{2+{\varepsilon}}} \quad \text{for all}\quad n=n_0,\dots,n_1,
        \]
        where $\overline{C}$ is given by Corollary~(c.3 of the paper),
        \[
            \rho'_0=\min \left(\rho_0, \frac{1}{20\overline{C}} \right)
        \]
        and $\rho_0$ is given by Lemma~(lm:Start of the paper).
        \item For every $m>2n_0$, taking $n=\lfloor\frac{m}{2}\rfloor$ and $n'=m-n$,
        one has
        
            \begin{gather}
                
                
                 \rho_{m} \le L \min(\rho_n, \rho_{n'}),
                \\
                
                \rho_m^{\textcolor{black}{2+{\varepsilon}}} \delta_m \le \frac{1}{100},
                
                \\
                 \left( \lambda \max(\delta_{n}, \delta_{n'}) + 2 \,\frac{K e^{\frac{\rho_{m}^2}{2}}}{m^{\textcolor{black}{{\varepsilon}/2}}} \right) \le \delta_{m},
            \end{gather}
            where constants $L$ and $\lambda$ are defined by the conclusion of Lemma~(lm:Contr of the paper) for $C=2\left(\frac{C_{\sigma}}{C_1}\right)^2$, where $C_1$ is given by Lemma~(l:var-lower of the paper), and $C_{\sigma}$ is given by~(equation eq:C-2 of the paper).
            
    \end{itemize}
    Then the conclusion of Proposition~(p.boot of the paper) holds for this sequence.

body:
[Proposition 8 of arXiv:2603.28226, '2603.28226'] Let \(f\ge0\) belong to \(L^1(\mathcal F_\infty)\), let \(\lambda>0\), and let
\(\theta\ge0\). Retain the notation of Section~\ref{sec:proof} and
\eqref{eq:s-theta}; thus
\[
r:=\inf\{n\ge1:\ f_n>\lambda\},
\qquad
\varepsilon_n:=d f_n\,\mathbf1_{\{r=n\}},
\qquad
\gamma_n:=d f_n\,\mathbf1_{\{r>n\}},
\]
\[
\Lambda_0:=0,
\qquad
\Lambda_m:=\sum_{k=1}^{m}\mathbb E_k[\varepsilon_{k+1}],
\qquad
s_\theta:=\inf\{m\ge1:\ \Lambda_m>\theta\lambda\},
\qquad
t_\theta:=r\wedge s_\theta.
\]
Also set
\[
r^-:=r-1 \ \text{on }\{r<\infty\},
\qquad
r^-:=\infty \ \text{on }\{r=\infty\}.
\]

Define
\[
g_\theta:=f-f_{t_\theta},
\]
\[
h_{\theta,n}:=
\sum_{j=1}^{n}
\bigl(\varepsilon_j-\mathbb E_{j-1}[\varepsilon_j]\bigr)\mathbf1_{\{s_\theta\ge j\}},
\qquad n\ge1,
\]
\[
k_{\theta,n}^{\mathrm{st}}
:=
\sum_{j=1}^{n}\gamma_j\,\mathbf1_{\{s_\theta\ge j\}},
\qquad
k_{\theta,n}^{\mathrm{pr}}
:=
\sum_{j=1}^{n}\mathbb E_{j-1}[\varepsilon_j]\mathbf1_{\{s_\theta\ge j\}},
\qquad n\ge1.
\]
Then \(h_{\theta,n}\) converges almost surely and in \(L^1\) to a limit
\(h_\theta\in L^1(\mathcal F_\infty)\), and the sequences
\[
k_{\theta,n}^{\mathrm{st}},
\qquad
k_{\theta,n}^{\mathrm{pr}}
\]
converge almost surely and in \(L^1\) to limits
\[
k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}},
\qquad
k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}
\in L^1(\mathcal F_\infty).
\]
Moreover,
\[
f=g_\theta+h_\theta+k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}}+k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}.
\]

\medskip
\noindent\textup{(a)}
\[
\mathbb P\Bigl(\sup_{n\ge1}|\mathbb E_n[g_\theta]|>0\Bigr)
\le \frac{\|f\|_1}{\lambda},
\qquad
\|g_\theta\|_1\le 2\|f\|_1.
\]

\noindent\textup{(b)}
\[
\Bigl\|\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}
\bigl|\mathbb E_n[h_\theta]-\mathbb E_{n-1}[h_\theta]\bigr|
\Bigr\|_1
\le 2\|f\|_1.
\]
In particular,
\[
\|h_\theta\|_1\le 2\|f\|_1.
\]

\noindent\textup{(c)}
\[
k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}}=f_{s_\theta\wedge r^-},
\qquad
0\le k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}}\le \lambda
\quad\text{a.s.}
\]

\noindent\textup{(d)}
\[
k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}
=
\Lambda_{s_\theta-1}\,\mathbf1_{\{s_\theta<\infty\}}
+
\Bigl(\sup_{m\ge1}\Lambda_m\Bigr)\mathbf1_{\{s_\theta=\infty\}},
\qquad
0\le k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}\le \theta\lambda
\quad\text{a.s.}
\]

\noindent\textup{(e)}
\[
\mathbb E[h_\theta]=\mathbb E[\varepsilon_1],
\]
\[
\|k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}}\|_1+\|k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}\|_1
=
\|f\|_1-\mathbb E[\varepsilon_1]
\le \|f\|_1,
\]
\[
\|k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}}\|_2^2
\le \lambda\|k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}}\|_1,
\qquad
\|k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}\|_2^2
\le \theta\lambda\|k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}\|_1,
\]
and
\[
\|k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}}+k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}\|_2^2
\le (1+\theta)\lambda\|f\|_1.

body: Load-bearing hypothesis: finite speed of propagation and the domain-of-dependence cone are properties of the wave equation (and of symmetric hyperbolic systems), proved by a local energy identity on the cone. The Schrödinger equation has no such identity and propagates instantaneously. Concrete counterexample: let f ∈ L¹(R^n) be nonzero and compactly supported and let t ≠ 0. By the kernel formula, e^{itΔ}f(x) = (4πit)^{−n/2} e^{i|x|²/(4t)} · G(x/(2t)) where G is the Fourier transform of the compactly supported integrable function y ↦ e^{i|y|²/(4t)}f(y). By the Paley–Wiener theorem G extends to an entire function on C^n, and it is not identically zero, so its zero set contains no nonempty open set. Hence e^{itΔ}f is nonzero almost everywhere on every open subset of R^n at every t ≠ 0: compactly supported data instantly become globally supported. The same phenomenon rules out any cone-shaped domain of dependence, and the heat equation behaves the same way. What survives for Schrödinger are local smoothing, dispersive decay and (pseudo)locality statements about wave packets moving at velocity ≈ 2ξ, not a finite propagation speed; the wave equation's finite-speed argument must never be transplanted to a dispersive or parabolic equation.
title: Pitfall: Finite Speed of Propagation Is Hyperbolic, Not Dispersive — It Fails for Schrödinger

body: [Lemma 2.8 (Borel–Cantelli) of arXiv:2512.05720, 'First-passage percolation, non-positive curvature, and radial maps'] Let $(A_{n})_{n\geq 1}$ be a sequence of events in a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$. [Proposition BTP of arXiv:2608.30747, 'Compact homogeneous complex manifolds'] If a Hermitian C-space is BTP, then the following conditions hold for any $\alpha,\beta,\alpha+\beta\in\Delta_\qg^+$:
\begin{enumerate}[{\rm (i)}] 
\item $x_{\alpha+\beta}=x_\alpha$ or $\tfrac{1}{x_\beta}A_\beta = \tfrac{1}{x_{\alpha+\beta}}A_{\alpha+\beta}$.  

\item $x_{\alpha+\beta}=x_\alpha+x_\beta$ or 
$
\tfrac{1}{x_\alpha}A_\alpha+ \tfrac{1}{x_\beta}A_\beta=\tfrac{1}{x_{\alpha+\beta}} A_{\alpha+\beta}.
$   
\item If $\alpha-\beta\notin\Delta_\qg^-$, then either $x_{\alpha+\beta}=x_\alpha+x_\beta$ or $x_{\alpha+\beta}=x_\alpha$. 

\item If $\alpha-\beta\notin\Delta_\qg^+$, then either $x_{\alpha+\beta}=x_\alpha+x_\beta$ or $x_{\alpha+\beta}=x_\beta$. 

\item If $\gamma, \alpha+\beta+\gamma \in \Delta_\qg^+$ and $\alpha+\gamma, \beta+\gamma \notin \Delta_\qg$, then $x_{\alpha+\beta} =x_{\alpha} + x_\beta$ or $x_{\alpha+\beta+\gamma}=x_\gamma$.  

\item If $\gamma, \beta+\gamma, \alpha+\beta+\gamma \in \Delta_\qg^+$ and $\alpha+\gamma \notin \Delta_\qg$, then 
\begin{align*}
\tfrac{1}{x_{\beta+\gamma}} & N_{\beta,\gamma} N_{\alpha, \beta+\gamma} (x_{\beta+\gamma} -x_\beta - x_\gamma)(x_{\alpha+\beta+\gamma} - x_{\alpha})\\
=& \tfrac{1}{x_{\alpha+\beta}} N_{\alpha, \beta} N_{\alpha+\beta, \gamma}(x_{\alpha+\beta}- x_\alpha)(x_{\alpha+\beta+\gamma} - x_{\alpha+\beta} - x_\gamma).  
\end{align*}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:subcritical of arXiv:2609.02820, 'Sharpness and critical scaling of parking'] Under the assumptions and notation above, let
	\[
		a\coloneqq\frac13\int_0^{\lambda_1}\delta(\lambda)\,d\lambda\,.
	\]
	Then $a>0$ and, for every $t\geq0$ and every $k\geq1$ in the support of
	$\eta(0)$,
	\begin{equation}
		\mathbb{P}\bigl(\tau_1>t\mid\eta(0)=k,\ X_0,\ldots,X_t\bigr)
		\leq\exp\Bigl\{\tfrac13\int_0^{\lambda_1}\mathbb{E}_\lambda|\eta(0)|
		\,d\lambda\Bigr\}\,e^{\lambda_1(k-1)/3-a|R_t|}\,.
	\end{equation}
	Consequently $S_t\leq C\mathbb{E}_0e^{-a|R_t|}$.

[Proposition 9 (Weak stability of positive \(L^2\) Stein kernels) of arXiv:2608.27657, '\bfseries Stein Kernels and Normal Approximation\\ for Log-Concave Bilinear Forms'] Let \(\mu_k\Rightarrow\mu\) weakly on \(\R^n\), where each \(\mu_k\)
is centered and has finite second moments.  Let \(Y_k\sim\mu_k\), and
suppose that \(\mu_k\) admits a symmetric positive-semidefinite Stein
kernel \(\tau_k\) such that
\begin{equation}
  L:=\sup_k\E\|\tau_k(Y_k)\|_{\HS}^2<\infty.
  \tag{4.2}
\end{equation}
Then \(\mu\) is centered, \(\mu_k\to\mu\) in \(W_2\), and \(\mu\)
admits a symmetric positive-semidefinite Stein kernel \(\tau\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
  \E\tau(Y)=\Cov(Y),
  \qquad
  \E\|\tau(Y)\|_{\HS}^2
  \leq
  \liminf_{k\to\infty}\E\|\tau_k(Y_k)\|_{\HS}^2,
  \tag{4.3}
\end{equation}
where \(Y\sim\mu\).  The same kernel may be chosen with the following
additional permanence properties.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item
If \(F:\mathsf S_n\to[0,\infty]\) is convex and lower semicontinuous and
\(\sup_k\E F(\tau_k(Y_k))\leq C_F\), then
\[
  \E F(\tau(Y))\leq C_F.
\]

\item
If, for every \(A\in\mathsf S_n\),
\[
  \Var\!\left(\Tr(A\tau_k(Y_k))\right)
  \leq C_{\rm tr}\Tr(A^2),
\]
then
\begin{equation}
  \Var\!\left(\Tr(A\tau(Y))\right)
  \leq C_{\rm tr}\Tr(A^2)
  \qquad(A\in\mathsf S_n).
  \tag{4.4}
\end{equation}

\item
If, for every \(A\in\mathsf S_n\),
\[
  \E\Tr(A\tau_k(Y_k)A\tau_k(Y_k))
  \leq C_{\rm en}\Tr(A^2),
\]
then
\begin{equation}
  \E\Tr(A\tau(Y)A\tau(Y))
  \leq C_{\rm en}\Tr(A^2)
  \qquad(A\in\mathsf S_n).
  \tag{4.5}
\end{equation}

\item
If a constant \(C_{\rm wp}\) satisfies
\[
  \Var_{\mu_k}g
  \leq
  C_{\rm wp}\,
  \E\langle
    \tau_k(Y_k)\nabla g(Y_k),\nabla g(Y_k)
  \rangle
\]
for every \(k\) and every \(g\in C_c^\infty(\R^n)\), then
\begin{equation}
  \Var_\mu g
  \leq
  C_{\rm wp}\,
  \E\langle
    \tau(Y)\nabla g(Y),\nabla g(Y)
  \rangle
  \qquad(g\in C_c^\infty(\R^n)).
  \tag{4.6}
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
title: Weak stability of positive \(L^2\) Stein kernels

[Lemma long-range-percolation-coupling of arXiv:2608.00399, 'The Heavy-tailed Frog Model'] Let $d\ge1$, $\alpha \in (0, d)$, and $Q \in \mathcal{H}_{\alpha, K}$. 
    Fix $r \in \mathbb N^+$ and $\lambda > 0$. 
    Then, $\{ Y_{(u, v)}^{[L]} \}_{u \neq v}$ are mutually independent for each $L \ge r$.
    Moreover, there exist $\beta_1$ with $\beta_1 \to \infty$ as $r \to \infty$,
    such that, for any $L \ge r$ and any distinct $u, v \in \mathbb{T}^{[L]}$, we have
    \begin{align} 
        \mathbb P_{L}\left(Y_{(u, v)}^{[L]} = 1\right) \ge 1 - \exp\left(- \beta_1 |u - v|^{-s}\right),
    \end{align}
    where $|u - v|$ denotes the $\ell_\infty$-distance between $u$ and $v$ on $\mathbb{T}^{[L]}$ and $s := \alpha + d$.
title: Lemma long-range-percolation-coupling of arXiv:2608.00399

body:
Let T be a MINIMAL homeomorphism of a compact metric space X and let f be a continuous real function on X. Then the following are equivalent: (i) the Birkhoff sums S_n f(x) = sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f(T^k x) are uniformly bounded in n for SOME point x; (ii) the Birkhoff sums are uniformly bounded in n and in x; (iii) f is a continuous coboundary, that is f = g composed with T minus g for some continuous g on X. In particular a cohomological equation with continuous data is solvable continuously precisely when its Birkhoff sums stay bounded at a single point - a striking upgrade from one orbit to the whole space, which is where minimality is used.
MINIMALITY of T and CONTINUITY of f.
Without minimality the equivalence fails;
with merely measurable data the corresponding statement is the Gottschalk-Hedlund analogue for measurable coboundaries and is different.

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2607.25645, 'Estimates of the total variation distance between laws of Sobolev mappings on Gaussian spa'] Let $k\in\mathbb N$, let $p>2k-1$, and set
\[
q:=\frac{p}{p-2k+1}.
\]
Let $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)$ with $f_j\in W^{2,p}(\gamma)$ and
\[
\max_{1\le j\le k}\|f_j\|_{\dot{W}^{2,p}(\gamma)}\le b.
\]
Let $g\in W^{1,q}(\gamma)\cap L^\infty(\gamma)$, and let
$\theta=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_k)\in\mathbb R^k$ satisfy $|\theta|=1$.
Then for every $\varepsilon>0$,
\[
\biggl|
\int_E \sum_{i,j=1}^k \theta_i (A_f)_{i,j}
\langle \nabla f_j,\nabla g\rangle_{H(\gamma)}
\Delta_f^{-1}\Phi_\varepsilon(\Delta_f)\,d\gamma
\biggr|
\le
32\bigl(\|\Phi'\|_\infty+2\bigr)k\|g\|_\infty b^{2k-1}
\bigl(h_{\gamma,q}(\Delta_f,\varepsilon)\bigr)^{1/q}.
\]

For m>=5 and q>=2, the arc-transitive graph C_m[empty_q] has mq vertices and degree 2q. Its mean hitting time from a target twin is mq, and from fiber j!=0 is j(m-j)+m(q-1). Its maximal commute time is 2 floor(m^2/4)+2m(q-1), its stationary mean hitting time is (m^2-1)/6+m(q-1), and its rate-one continuous-time relaxation time is 1/(1-cos(2*pi/m)). For fixed q their maximal-commute to twice stationary-hitting ratio tends to 3/2.
All hypotheses and scope restrictions in the statement apply.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:56fbe937b985212af54cac95ba016b633852bb232153be8e6b5b88a4ddec8c1f","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/56/56fbe937b985212af54cac95ba016b633852bb232153be8e6b5b88a4ddec8c1f.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:b6fe48a3609acff7cac38e87905ed070074475fda2593538887a0990dfc80d57","bundle_entry_key":"q-fold-cycle-hitting-times-and-relaxation","bundle_id":"population.w336-p0208-checked-attempt-20261010","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"w336/bundle_001.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.markov-chains:q-fold-cycle-hitting-times-and-relaxation","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# P0208: exact q-fold cycle calculation

Status: proof written by w336, independent KEEP pending. This extends the recorded q=2 campaign counterexample; it is not a new literature priority claim. The source's tau_star is a maximal commute time, not a maximal one-way hitting time. Relaxation here uses the rate-one continuous-time generator P-I.

Let m>=5, q>=2 and G=C_m[empty_q]. Its vertices are (i,a), with i modulo m and 1<=a<=q; two vertices are adjacent precisely when their first coordinates differ by one modulo m. G is simple, connected, 2q-regular, has n=mq vertices, and is not a cycle. Rotations, reflection of C_m and independent permutations inside each fiber act transitively on directed edges, so G is arc-transitive.

Fix target (0,1). Let a be the mean hitting time from a different vertex in fiber 0. Every visit to fiber 0 from elsewhere chooses a uniformly distributed vertex. If h_j is the mean from fiber j!=0, the quotient cycle's hitting-time equation gives

    h_j = j(m-j) + ((q-1)/q)a.

The identity j(m-j)=1+[(j-1)(m-j+1)+(j+1)(m-j-1)]/2 verifies that equation away from 0. From a twin of the target, a=1+h_1=m+((q-1)/q)a, so a=mq and h_j=j(m-j)+m(q-1). These values solve all first-step equations. A finite connected chain hits the target with finite mean, so uniqueness of the killed-chain linear system identifies them with the actual hitting times.

The graph automorphisms exchange any two vertices of a specified fiber separation, so hitting times are symmetric. For m>=5, floor(m^2/4)>m, hence the largest one-way hitting time is floor(m^2/4)+m(q-1), larger than the twin value mq. Consequently

    tau_star = 2 floor(m^2/4) + 2m(q-1),
    tau_0 = (m^2-1)/6 + m(q-1).

The second formula is the stationary mean hitting time of the fixed target, including its zero self-hitting time: sum_{j=1}^{m-1}j(m-j)=m(m^2-1)/6, and the remaining constant terms sum to m(q-1). A neighbor has mean hitting time m-1+m(q-1)=n-1.

P equals (A(C_m)/2) tensor (J_q/q). The fiber-constant subspace has eigenvalues cos(2*pi*k/m), 0<=k<m; its orthogonal complement has m(q-1) zero eigenvalues. Since cos(2*pi/m)>0 for m>=5, tau_2=1/(1-cos(2*pi/m)). This is the continuous-time relaxation time; for even m the non-lazy discrete-time absolute spectral gap vanishes, which is a different parameter.

For each fixed q>=2 and m tending to infinity,

    tau_star/n^2 -> 1/(2q^2),
    tau_2/n^2 -> 1/(2*pi^2*q^2),
    tau_star/(2*tau_0) -> 3/2.

Thus the same family refutes the three bounds recorded for Aldous-Fill Problem 7.27: O(n log n), O(n), and ratio 1+o(1). This statement relies on the cached problem's parameter definitions and does not establish whether the refutation was previously published.

Checks: scripts/check_p0208.py solves the full hitting-time systems, compares the full transition spectrum, checks the directed-edge orbit, and tests the stationary sum and neighbor identity. The proof covers all m>=5 and q>=2; finite checks supply validation, not the universal argument.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:6611f602491569522b255cbc2e27d93831a536afc7f6c21d6d129583b5b3eb06","revision_digest":"sha256:405c3edbd080e4ab09c7c9d7631f325297537e779f9158172ed4d856392c4891","source_id":"owner:campaign:w336:P0208:q-fold-cycle-hitting-times-and-relaxation","source_revision":"author-proof-2026-10-10; independent audit w346 pending","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Maximal stationary antivoter variance structural calculation Result: On the complete graph all distinct-pair correlations equal c. At stationarity, the generator applied to eta_i*eta_j gives c=-(1+(n-2)c)/(n-1), hence c=-1/(2n-3). Therefore Var(S)=n+n(n-1)c=n(n-2)/(2n-3). The general source inequality Var(S)<n/2 has the same leading term but leaves the exact gap n/[2(2n-3)]. Check: The correlation equation can also be obtained by conditioning on which member of the pair updates and whether it samples its partner. Each route gives the same c. In particular merely proving Var(S)<=n/2 cannot resolve the proposed finite-n optimizer. Obstruction: A sharp bound on the return-parity expression for the meeting chain, or on averaged spin correlations, is missing. Pairwise correlations need not all be bounded by the complete-graph value.

[Lemma 32 of arXiv:2608.12804, 'Scaling Limits for Ising Models on Inhomogeneous Random Graphs and Applications'] Let
\(
    K,K':[0,1]^2\rightarrow\mathbb R
\)
be symmetric, Riemann-integrable kernels, and suppose that
$\{\sigma_i\}_{i\geq1}$ and $\{\tau_i\}_{i\geq1}$ are two independent
sequences of i.i.d. Rademacher random variables. Let
$\{\lambda_r(K)\}_{r\geq1}$ and
$\{\lambda_r(K')\}_{r\geq1}$ denote the nonzero eigenvalues of
$T_K$ and $T_{K'}$, respectively, repeated according to
multiplicity. Then, we have:
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
\displaystyle
\frac{1}{2N}
\sum_{1\leq i\neq j\leq N}
K\left(\frac{i}{N},\frac{j}{N}\right)
\bigl(\sigma_i\sigma_j+\tau_i\tau_j\bigr)
\\[4mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{1}{2N}
\sum_{1\leq i\neq j\leq N}
K'\left(\frac{i}{N},\frac{j}{N}\right)
\sigma_i\tau_i\sigma_j\tau_j
\end{pmatrix}
\xrightarrow{d}
\begin{pmatrix}
\displaystyle
\frac12\sum_{r=1}^{\infty}
\lambda_r(K)(X_r^2-1)
+
\frac12\sum_{r=1}^{\infty}
\lambda_r(K)(Y_r^2-1)
\\[4mm]
\displaystyle
\frac12\sum_{r=1}^{\infty}
\lambda_r(K')(Z_r^2-1)
\end{pmatrix},
\]
where
$\{X_r\}_{r\geq1}$,
$\{Y_r\}_{r\geq1}$, and
$\{Z_r\}_{r\geq1}$ are mutually independent sequences of
i.i.d. standard Gaussian random variables.
All three infinite series appearing in the distributional limit converge in $L^2$ and almost surely.

[Lem 20 (Subadditivity of entropy) of arXiv:2608.18276, 'The branching random walk in a uniform magnetic field : magnetization concentration and ov'] For every ${\bf q} \in \mathcal{P}$,
\[
S({\bf q}) \;\le\; s(m_1({\bf q})) + s(m_2({\bf q})),
\]
with equality if and only if ${\bf q}$ is of product form, i.e.
\[
q_{ab} = \left(\frac{1 + a\, m_1({\bf q})}{2}\right)\left(\frac{1 + b\, m_2({\bf q})}{2}\right),
\qquad \forall\, a, b \in \{-1,1\}.
\]
Equivalently, equality holds if and only if the two coordinates are
independent under ${\bf q}$, in which case $\rho({\bf q}) = m_1({\bf q})\, m_2({\bf q})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Subadditivity of entropy

body:
[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2609.03669, 'Volterra Integral Reduction \\ for Boundary Diffusion Problems'] Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:smooth}--\ref{ass:func} and~\ref{ass:potential}, 
for each fixed $y$, the function $t \mapsto \partial_x f(t,y^+)$ 
is the unique solution in $C[0,T]$ of the following Volterra integral 
equation of the second kind with a continuous kernel
\begin{equation}
\alpha(t,y)\,\partial_x f(t,y^+)
=
G(t,y)
+
\int_0^t
\gamma_1(t-s,y)\,k(t,s)\,
\partial_x f(s,y^+)\,ds.
\end{equation}
Here,
\begin{equation}
G(t,y)
=
\partial_x g(t,y)
+
\frac{\beta(\psi(y))}{\sigma(y)}
\big(g(t,y)-f(t,y)\big),
\qquad
\gamma_1(\tau,y)
=
r_0(\tau,y,y)
+
\frac{\beta(\psi(y))}{\sigma(y)}
r_1(\tau,y,y),
\end{equation}
where $r_1(\tau,y,y)$ and $r_0(\tau,y,y)$ are continuous functions exhibiting $O_K(\tau^{1/2})$ behavior uniformly for $y$ in compact sets.

$h\geq 1$. Then there exist a set $S_0\subseteq[n]$ and a subspace

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2605.29030, 'Preferential relocations enhance survival \\ for Markov chains with killing'] Consider an arbitrary $\a\in \calCp(\S)$ such that
$\Kk\a(\s)>0$ for all $\s\in\S$.
Introduce the conservative biased kernel $\g$ given for any $t\in S$ and $\s\in \S$ by 
\begin{equation} 
\g(t\s) = \frac{ \kk(t\s) \a(t\s)}{\Kk \a(\s)}.
\end{equation}
Suppose that $\g$ is uniquely ergodic and write  $ \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\a}$ for its  Doeblin measure. Then for 
any
probability measure $\boldsymbol{\nu}$ on $\S$,

body:
[Definition def-adm of arXiv:2603.17861, 'Gaussian concentration, integral probability metrics, and coupling functionals\\ for infin'] A probability measure $\mu$ on $(\Omega,\mathfrak{F})$ is said to be asymptotically
decoupled if there exist $g:\mathds N\to\mathds N$ and $c:\mathds N\to [0,\infty)$ such that
$\lim_{n\to\infty}g(n)/n=0$, $\lim_{n\to\infty} c(n)/|\ensuremath{\Lambda}_n|=0$, and
\[
\forall j\in\mathds Z^d,\ \forall n\in\mathds N,\ \forall A\in\mathfrak{F}_{\ensuremath{\Lambda}_n+j},\ 
\forall B\in \mathfrak{F}_{(\ensuremath{\Lambda}_n+g(n)+j)^{\mathrm{c}}},
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
\e^{-c(n)}\mu(A) \mu(B)\leq \mu(A\cap B)\leq \e^{c(n)}\mu(A) \mu(B).
\end{equation}
If only the upper bound holds, one says that $\mu$ is asymptotically
decoupled from above.
title: Asymptotically decoupled measure

body:
[Thm equiv-flatness of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] If $X$ is a flat orthogonal $G$-spectrum, then the functor $X\smashp{-}\colon\cat{$\bm{G}$-OrthSp}\to\cat{$\bm{G}$-OrthSp}$ preserves $G$-equivariant weak equivalences. Moreover, for \emph{any} orthogonal $G$-spectrum $Y$ the functor ${-}\smashp Y$ preserves $G$-equivariant weak equivalences between flat orthogonal $G$-spectra.
    \begin{proof}
        For a published account of the first statement see [schwede2018global]*{Theorem 3.5.10}. For the second statement, we let $X_1\to X_2$ be any $G$-equivariant weak equivalence between flat orthogonal $G$-spectra and we pick a cofibrant replacement $Y'\to Y$. Then all maps in the induced square 
        \[
            \begin{tikzcd}
                X_1\smashp Y'\arrow[r]\arrow[d] & X_2\smashp Y'\arrow[d]\\
                X_1\smashp Y\arrow[r] & X_2\smashp Y
            \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        except possibly the bottom one are $G$-equivariant weak equivalences by the first part; thus, also the bottom map is a $G$-equivariant weak equivalence by 2-out-of-3.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Stolz

body:
[Theorem 8 (Error bound for the realised volatility classifier) of arXiv:2609.00402, '2609.00402'] Suppose Assumption~\ref{ass:volatility} holds. Fix \(\alpha_V\in(0,1)\), define \(a_{V,\alpha_V}=U^2\sqrt{n\log(1/\alpha_V)/2}\), and set \(\lambda_{V,\alpha_V}=n\nu_0+a_{V,\alpha_V}\). Then the exact classifier \(h_{V,\lambda_{V,\alpha_V}}(\bm X)=\mathbb I\{V(\bm X)>\lambda_{V,\alpha_V}\}\) satisfies \(\mathbb P\{h_{V,\lambda_{V,\alpha_V}}(\bm X)=1\mid Y=0\}\leq\alpha_V\) and
\[
\mathbb P\{h_{V,\lambda_{V,\alpha_V}}(\bm X)=0\mid Y=1\}
\leq
\exp\left\{-\frac{2(n\kappa_V-a_{V,\alpha_V})_+^2}{nU^4}\right\}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\operatorname{err}(h_{V,\lambda_{V,\alpha_V}})
\leq\pi_0\alpha_V+
\pi_1\exp\left\{-\frac{2(n\kappa_V-a_{V,\alpha_V})_+^2}{nU^4}\right\}.
\]

Now fix \(M>0\) and \(\epsilon_V>0\), and suppose that \(\sup_{\bm x\in\mathcal X_M}\lvert f_{\epsilon_V,M}^{RV}(\bm x)-V(\bm x)\rvert\leq\epsilon_V\). Define the clipped neural classifier $\overline h_V(\bm X)=\mathbb I\left\{f_{\epsilon_V,M}^{RV}(\operatorname{clip}_M(\bm X))>\lambda_{V,\alpha_V}+\epsilon_V\right\}.$ Then
\[
\operatorname{err}(\overline h_V)
\leq\pi_0\{\alpha_V+\tau_0(M)\}
+\pi_1\left[\exp\left\{-\frac{2(n\kappa_V-a_{V,\alpha_V}-2\epsilon_V)_+^2}{nU^4}\right\}+\tau_1(M)\right]
=:\mathfrak B_V(\alpha_V,\epsilon_V,M).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Error bound for the realised volatility classifier

body:
[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] There is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large
$h$,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\left\{|hA|:A\subset\mathbb Z,\ |A|=4,
 \ \operatorname{ndiam} A<\frac{13}{20}h^2\right\}\right|\geq ch^3.
\end{equation}
More locally,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\mathcal R(h,4)\cap
 \left[\binom{h+3}{3}-\frac{h^3}{250},
       \binom{h+3}{3}-\frac{h^3}{400}\right]\right|\geq ch^3,
\end{equation}
where the endpoints may be rounded to integers.  Consequently
\[
 \boxed{|\mathcal R(h,4)|=\Theta(h^3)},
 \qquad
 \liminf_{h\to\infty}
 \frac{|\mathcal R(h,4)|}{|[3h+1,\binom{h+3}{3}]\cap\mathbb Z|}>0.
\]
The values counted in (equation eq:localmain of the paper) may be chosen with primitive
representatives having two independent homogeneous relations of degree at
most $h$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Positive-density four-point spectrum

[Lemma 20 of arXiv:2608.01516, 'Nondegeneracy and regularity of polynomial pushforwards'] Let $n,d,k\in\mathbb N$, $n\ge k$, and let $\mu$ be an isotropic
log-concave measure on $\mathbb R^n$. Let
$f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)\in \mathcal P_d(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb R^k)$
and assume that
\[
\operatorname{Var}_\mu(f_j)>0,
\quad \forall j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}.
\]
Then
\[
\int_{\mathbb R^n}\Delta_{\hat f}\,d\mu=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\det \Sigma_\mu^d(f)=0.
\]

[Proposition prop:rectobs of arXiv:2608.28007, 'Exact Risk Ratios for Weighted Data Selection in Linear Regression'] In $\mathbb{R}^4$ let
\[
\begin{aligned}
&a_1=e_1,\quad a_2=e_2,\quad a_3=-e_1-e_2,\qquad
b_1=e_3,\quad b_2=e_4,\quad b_3=-e_3-e_4,\\
&h_1=-e_1-e_3,\qquad h_2=-e_2-e_4,
\end{aligned}
\]
and $G=\{a_1,a_2,a_3,b_1,b_2,b_3,h_1,h_2\}$. Then $G$ positively spans
$\mathbb{R}^4$; no subset of at most five vectors positively spans; the positive
circuits of $G$ are exactly
$\{a_1,a_2,a_3\}$, $\{b_1,b_2,b_3\}$, $\{a_1,b_1,h_1\}$,
$\{a_2,b_2,h_2\}$; and any cover of $G$ by circuit flats needs four planes,
of total dimension $8$.

[Definition 20 of arXiv:2608.05931, 'Effective Lagrangian regularity and the uniqueness threshold for random H\"older velocity '] For a function $g : X \to Y$, where $X = \T^d$ or $\R^d$ and $Y$ is a Banach space, we define for $s \geq 0$ the (semi)norm space $\mathcal{C}^s$ as follows. For $s=0$, we let
    \[\|g\|_{\mathcal{C}^0(X) Y} := \sup_{x \in X} \|g(x)\|_Y.\]
    For $s \in (0,\infty)$---letting $s = n + r$ where $r \in (0,1]$ and $n \in \N$---we define $\mathcal{C}^s(X)$ as a seminorm on a subspace of $C^n(X)$ by
    \[\|g\|_{\mathcal{C}^s(X) Y} := \sup_{x,x' \in X, x \ne x'} \frac{\|\nabla^n g(x) - \nabla^ng(x')\|_Y}{|x-x'|^r}.\]
    We note in particular that $\mathcal{C}^1$ is the Lipschitz seminorm and that $\mathcal{C}^0$ is the natural norm on the space of bounded functions---rather than $C^1$ and $C^0$ which have additional qualitative regularity hypotheses that we do not want to require, as we will frequently be working with Lipschitz functions that are not $C^1$.

    We also consider for $p \in [1,\infty), s\geq 0$ the fractional Sobolev (semi)norm spaces $W^{s,p}$. For $s \in \N$, we just let $\|g\|_{W^{s,p}(X)Y} := \|\nabla^s g\|_{L^p(X)Y}$, and for $s>0$ and $s \not \in \N$, we again write $s = n+r$ where $r \in (0,1)$ and $n \in \N$ and define
    \[\|g\|_{W^{s,p}(X) Y} := \Big(\int_X \int_X \frac{\|\nabla^n g(x) - \nabla^n g(x')\|^p_Y}{|x-x'|^{d + rp}}\,dx\,dx'\Big)^{1/p}.\]
title: Definition 20 of arXiv:2608.05931

[Lemma DFY of arXiv:2412.09850, 'Averaging principles for time-inhomogeneous multi-scale SDEs via nonautonomous Poisson equ'] Suppose that Assumption {\rm(A1 of the paper)} holds. Let $Y^{s,x,y}:=\{Y_t^{s,x,y}\}_{t\ge s}$ be the unique strong solution to the  SDE (equation FrozenE of the paper). Then, for any $t\ge s$, $Y^{s,x,y}_t$ is twice differentiable in the mean square sense with respect to $x$ and $y$, respectively; moreover, for $t\ge s$,
\begin{equation}\begin{split}
&\mathbb{E} \|\partial _yY_{t}^{s,x,y}\|^{4}\leqslant e^{-4\int^t_s\alpha(u)\,du},
\quad \mathbb{E} \|\partial^2_yY_{t}^{s,x,y}\|^{2}\leqslant e^{-2\gamma\int^t_s\alpha(u)\,du},\\
&\sup_{t\geqslant s}\mathbb{E} \|\partial_x Y^{s,x,y}_t\|^{4}\leqslant C,
\quad\sup_{t\geqslant s}\mathbb{E} \|\partial^2_x Y^{s,x,y}_t\|^{2}\leqslant C,
\end{split}\end{equation}
where $\gamma\in(0,1)$ is the constant in (equation A12 of the paper).
title: Lemma DFY of arXiv:2412.09850

body:
[Lemma 10 (Coarea formula) of arXiv:2608.09840, 'Langevin dynamics along the zero set of real-analytic potentials'] Let $N$ be an $n$-dimensional $C^1$ submanifold of some ambient Euclidean space, let $\sigma \colon N \to \R^d$ be a $C^1$ map whose derivative has constant rank $r$, and let $u \colon N \to \R$ be nonnegative and Borel measurable. Then
\[
\int_N u \, J_\sigma \, d\Hcal^n = \int_{\sigma(N)} \left( \int_{\sigma^{-1}(x)} u \, d\Hcal^{n-r} \right) d\Hcal^r(x),
\]
where $J_\sigma(p)$ denotes the $r$-dimensional Jacobian of the derivative $D\sigma(p)$, i.e., the product of its $r$ nonzero singular values, and the inner integral on the right-hand side is
$\Hcal^r$-measurable. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Coarea formula

\(

body: The halting problem is undecidable: there is no Turing machine H that, given as input an encoding of an arbitrary Turing machine M together with an input string w, always halts and correctly reports whether M halts on w. The halting set {(M, w) : M halts on w} is, however, computably enumerable (recognizable): a universal machine can simulate M on w and accept if the simulation halts.

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.27398, 'Strict Stability and Strict Minimality of Regular Area-Minimizing Hypercones: A Quantitati'] For $\nu\geq0$, let $J_\nu$ be the Bessel function of the first kind of
order $\nu$, and let $j_{\nu,1}$ denote its first positive zero.  Then, for
every $R>0$,
\begin{equation}
    \lambda_\C^D(R)
    =\frac{\lambda_\C^D(1)}{R^2}
    =\frac{j_{b_1,1}^2}{R^2}
    \geq\frac{4}{R^2}>0.
\end{equation}
Equivalently, $\frac{j_{b_1,1}^2}{R^2}$ is the optimal coefficient in
the quadratic inequality
\[
    Q_\C(\varphi)
    \geq\frac{j_{b_1,1}^2}{R^2}
      \int_\C\varphi^2\,d\cH^n,
    \qquad
    \varphi\in C^1(\C),\quad
    \spt\varphi\Subset B_R.
\]
Moreover, the sharp $|x|^{-2}$-weighted Jacobi inequality is
\[
    Q_\C(\varphi)
    \geq b_1^2
      \int_\C\frac{\varphi^2}{|x|^2}\,d\cH^n,
    \qquad
    \varphi\in C_c^1(\C\setminus\{0\}).
\]
In particular, $\C$ is strictly stable in the sense of
\cite{caffarelli1984minimal} if and only if $b_1>0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.27398

[Definition def: ample_Ban of arXiv:2412.07690, 'A law of large numbers concerning the distribution of critical points of random Fourier se'] An \emph{ample Banach space of sections} of $E$  is  a Banach space   ${\boldsymbol{U}}\subset   C^0(E)$   continuously embedded in $C^0(E)$  such that  \index{Banach space! ample}
\[
\forall t \in {\boldsymbol{T}},\;\;\spa\big\{\,u(t),\;\;u\in {\boldsymbol{U}}\,\big\}= E_t.
\]
Let $k\in {{\mathbb N}}$. We say that the Banach space ${\boldsymbol{U}}$ is \emph{$k$-ample} \index{Banach space! $k$-ample}  if for any \emph{distinct } points $t_1,\dotsc, t_k\in {\boldsymbol{T}}$ the map
\[
{\boldsymbol{U}}\ni u\mapsto  u(t_1)\oplus \cdots \oplus u(t_k)\in E_{t_1}\oplus \cdots \oplus E_{t_k}
\]
is onto.  \nobreak\hfill\penalty250 \hbox{}\nobreak\hfill$\rlap{$\sqcap$}\sqcup$\vskip\aline
title: Definition def: ample_Ban of arXiv:2412.07690

[Defi def_selfSimilarRiemann of arXiv:2608.17463, 'Persistence probabilities of fractional L\'evy fields indexed by hyperbolic space and othe'] Let $(X(\eta))_{\eta\in\mathcal{M}}$ be a weak stationary centred Gaussian field indexed by the Riemannian manifold $(M,\left\langle .,. \right\rangle_\mathcal{M})$ with Riemannian metric $\left\langle .,. \right\rangle_\mathcal{M}$ so that there is a function $g:\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ which determines the structure function of the process, i.e.\ $\mathbb{E}\left[(X(\eta)-X(\zeta))^2\right]=g(d_\mathcal{M}(\eta,\zeta))$ for all $\eta,\zeta\in\mathcal{M}$.
    
    The process is called self-similar (of order $H$), if for any $a>0$ and $\ol{\mathcal{M}} := (M, a^2 \left\langle .,. \right\rangle_\mathcal{M})$ the centred Gaussian field $(a^{-H} \mkern 1.5mu\overline{\mkern-1.5muX\mkern-1.5mu}\mkern 1.5mu(\eta))_{\eta\in\ol{\mathcal{M}}}$ determined by $\expec{(\mkern 1.5mu\overline{\mkern-1.5muX\mkern-1.5mu}\mkern 1.5mu(\eta) - \mkern 1.5mu\overline{\mkern-1.5muX\mkern-1.5mu}\mkern 1.5mu(\zeta))^2} = g(d_{\ol{\mathcal{M}}}(\eta,\zeta)) \\ = g(a ~d_\mathcal{M}(\eta,\zeta))$ exists and has the same finite dimensional distributions as $(X(\eta))_{\eta\in\mathcal{M}}$.
title: Defi def_selfSimilarRiemann of arXiv:2608.17463

[Deff r-functions of arXiv:2601.19145, 'Stochastic Persistence in Infinite Dimensions'] If $h: \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}^m$ is a continuous function  which is continuously differentiable in $x_u$ and satisfies $\pi_u \circ h \circ \pi_z = 0$, then $\tilde h: [0,\infty) \times \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}^m$ is defined as 
     $$\tilde h(r,x) \coloneqq \begin{cases}
        r^{-1}\pi_u(h(rx_u,x_z)) + \pi_z(h(rx_u,x_z))  & r > 0 \\
            \pi_u\big(\sum_{i \leq d}\frac{\partial h}{\partial x_i}(0,x_z)x_i\big) + h(0,x_z) & r = 0 \,.
        \end{cases}$$
    In other words, $\tilde h$ is the unique continuous function such that
    \begin{equation}
        (r\pi_u + \pi_z)(\tilde h(r,x)) = h(rx_u,x_z) \,.
    \end{equation}
    
    

    For the functions $F$ and $G$ from (SPDE-F of the paper) and 
    (SPDE-G-sass of the paper) we also denote
    $$\tilde F(r,x,\theta)(\cdot) \coloneqq \tilde f(\cdot, r,x(\cdot),\theta) \,, \quad \tilde G(r,x,\theta) \coloneqq \tilde \sigma(\cdot, r,x(\cdot),\theta) \cdot H \,.$$

       \mathrm e^{-zA_t}f(W_t)
    \right]
  
\end{equation}
for almost every $x$.  The right-hand side defines a canonical pointwise
version whenever it is finite.  In particular, if $z=\beta-iu$, then
\begin{equation}
  |\mathrm e^{-tH_{\beta-iu}}f|(x)
  \leq (\mathrm e^{-tH_\beta}|f|)(x)
  \leq (P_t|f|)(x),
  
\end{equation}
where $P_t=\mathrm e^{t\Delta/2}$ is the free Brownian semigroup.

[Lemma Polynomial basis identity of arXiv:2602.07920, 'On the position matrix of single-shelf shuffle and card guessing'] Let $N, m$ be a fixed positive integer. Then, 
    \[(N-x)^{\underline{m}} = \sum_{k=0}^{m}c_{N}(k, m) x^{\underline{k}},\]
    where \[c_N(k, m) = (-1)^{k}(N-k)^{\underline{m-k}}\binom{m}{k} = (-1)^{k}\frac{(N-k)!}{(N-m)!}\binom{m}{k},\qquad 0\leq k\leq m\;.\]
    In particular, $c_{N}(m, m)=(-1)^{m}$ and $ c_N(0, m)=N^{\underline{m}}$ for all $m$. Furthermore, $c_N(k, m)=0$ for $k>m$.
title: Lemma Polynomial basis identity of arXiv:2602.07920
