body:
[Definition def:rw_reset of arXiv:2603.24803, 'Critical Spectral Invariants in Random Walks with Geometric Resetting'] Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$ be a probability space. 
Fix $a \in \mathbb{N}$ and $z \in \{1,\dots,a-1\}$. 
Let $\{X_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ be a discrete-time stochastic process on 
$\{0,1,\dots,a\}$ with initial condition $X_0=z$.

Let $\{\xi_n\}_{n\ge1}$ be i.i.d.\ random variables, independent of 
everything else, with
\[
\mathbb{P}(\xi_n=+1)=p, 
\qquad 
\mathbb{P}(\xi_n=-1)=q=1-p.
\]

Let $\{\sigma_i\}_{i\ge1}$ be i.i.d.\ geometric random variables with 
parameter $\gamma\in(0,1)$, supported on $\{1,2,\dots\}$:
\[
\mathbb{P}(\sigma_i=k)=\gamma(1-\gamma)^{k-1}, 
\qquad k\ge1,
\]
independent of $\{\xi_n\}$. Define reset times recursively by
\[
\mathbf{t}_0:=0,
\qquad
\mathbf{t}_i := \sum_{j=1}^{i} \sigma_j,
\quad i\ge1.
\]

Then the process evolves according to
\[
X_n =
\begin{cases}
z, & \text{if } n \in \{\mathbf{t}_i\}_{i\ge1}, \\[6pt]
X_{n-1}+\xi_n, & \text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\qquad n\ge1,
\]
and is absorbed upon first hitting $0$ or $a$. Equivalently, at each 
step the walker resets to $z$ with probability $\gamma$ or performs a 
standard biased step with probability $1-\gamma$, independently of its 
current position.
title: Random walk with geometric resetting

 Then  for $j\in [2]$, the following hold in $(0,1)^2$:

Then sum_t c_t*E[f_t(x_t)-f_t(x_star)] <= (v_0^2/2)*||x_1-x_star||^2+(1/2)*sum_t eta_t^2*v_t^2*E||grad f_t(x_t)||^2 -(1/(2*beta))*sum_t eta_t*v_t*[sum_(s=1)^t (v_s-v_(s-1))*E||grad f_t(x_t)-grad f_t(x_s)||^2+v_0*E||grad f_t(x_t)-grad f_t(x_star)||^2]. The coefficients c_t need not be positive. Interpolation and independence of the whole sample sequence are not assumed.
Each f(.;z):R^d->R is convex and beta-smooth, beta>0; Euclidean norms.
For every s<=t, conditional on z_1,...,z_(s-1), z_s and z_t have the same distribution. This is conditional equality of marginal laws, not conditional independence.
Fixed comparator x_star and initialization x_1 in R^d; deterministic positive step sizes eta_1,...,eta_T. All displayed expectations are finite.
Positive nondecreasing deterministic weights v_0,...,v_T.

[Proposition 14 of arXiv:2605.31471, 'Convergence Rates of Continuous-Time Random Walks to Time-Fractional Diffusions with Unbou'] Consider the SDE \eqref{eq:SDE-flow} under Assumption \ref{asm:classical}.
    Fix $m \in \mathbb N$ and $p \ge 2$. Then there exist functions
    $A_m(\cdot,p) : [0,\infty) \to [0,\infty)$ such that, for all
    $v_1,\dots,v_m \in \cX$,
    \begin{equation}
        \E \bigl\| \DD^m X_t(x)[v_1,\dots,v_m] \bigr\|^p
        \;\le\; A_m(t,p) \prod_{j=1}^m \|v_j\|^p,
        \qquad t \ge 0.
    \end{equation}
    Moreover, there exist constants $\mu_{m,p}>0$ and $\lambda_{m,p}>0$
    depending only on $K,d,m,p$ such that
    \begin{align}
        A_1(t,p) &\le e^{\mu_{1,p} t}, \\
        A_m(t,p) &\le \lambda_{m,p} \bigl( e^{\mu_{m,p} t } - 1 \bigr),
        \qquad m \ge 2.
    \end{align}

body:
[Proposition p:exp.mu.n of arXiv:2601.12677, 'Stable and Fréchet limit theorem for subgraph functionals in the hyperbolic random geometr'] Let $\gamma\in \big(\frac{1}{2\alpha},1\big)$. \\
$(i)$ We have, uniformly for $u \in (0,{\gamma R_n})$, 
$$
\mu_{k,n}(u) \le \big( 1+o_n(1) \big) B_{k,\alpha} \bigg( 1+ \sum_{\ell=0}^{k-2}\binom{k-1}{\ell} (e^{\frac{1}{2} (d-1)(1-2\alpha)u} +s_n)^{k-1-\ell} \bigg) e^{\frac{1}{2}(d-1)(k-1)u}, 
$$
where $s_n:= B_\alpha^{-1} n^{-(2\alpha-1)(1-\gamma)} e^{\alpha(d-1)\omega_n}$. \\
$(ii)$ We have, uniformly for $u \in (0,{\gamma R_n})$, 
$$
\mu_{k,n}(u) \ge \big( 1+o_n(1) \big) B_{k,\alpha} \big( 1- e^{\frac{1}{2} (d-1)(1-2\alpha)u} \big)^{k-1} e^{\frac{1}{2}(d-1)(k-1)u}. 
$$
$(iii)$ There exists $C\in (0,\infty)$, independent of $n$ and $u$, such that for all $n\ge1$ and $u\in (0,R_n)$,  
$$
\mu_{k,n} (u) \le C e^{\alpha(d-1)(k-1)\omega_n}\cdot e^{\frac{1}{2}(d-1)(k-1)u}, 
$$ 
where $\omega_n :=\log \log R_n$.

Author-derived scoped result; review/provenance gates tracked separately. For a fixed elliptic nearest-neighbor environment and a fixed nonzero direction, q(x)=P_x^omega(A_l) is either identically 0, identically 1, or strictly between 0 and 1 everywhere with inf_x q=0 and sup_x q=1. Uniform ellipticity only supplies the distance-dependent bound q(x)>=kappa^{|x-y|_1}q(y). Under a stationary ergodic law with 0<E[q(0)]<1 the third alternative holds almost surely.

Assume the fixed nearest-neighbor environment is elliptic, so its walk is irreducible. For any finite path x=x_0,...,x_r=y with path probability p>0, the Markov property gives q(x)>=p q(y). Apply the same argument to the complementary tail event to obtain 1-q(x)>=p(1-q(y)). Thus positivity of q, and positivity of 1-q, propagate to every starting site. Under uniform ellipticity kappa, a shortest path gives q(x)>=kappa^{|x-y|_1}q(y); the bound depends on distance.

Consequently exactly one of the following holds: q is identically zero; q is identically one; or 0<q(x)<1 at every site and inf_x q(x)=0, sup_x q(x)=1. In the third case L1 rules out a positive infimum; L1 applied to the complementary event rules out a supremum below one.

For a stationary ergodic environment law, {q(0)>0} is invariant under every spatial shift: q_{theta_z omega}(0)=q_omega(z), and the preceding positivity propagation holds pathwise. If the annealed probability alpha=E[q(0)] is positive, this event therefore has probability one. If 0<alpha<1, apply the same argument to 1-q; almost every environment is in the third alternative. Stationarity and ergodicity alone do not exclude that alternative. [Prop 8 of arXiv:2608.21787, 'Stability of extremal hyperplane projections of balls in $\ell_p^n(\R)$'] There exists a positive constant $c_{\infty}'$ such that for every $n \ge 1$ and every vector $a = (a_1, \ldots, a_n) \in \R^n$ with $\sum_{i=1}^na_i^2 = 1$ and $a_1 \ge a_2 \ge \ldots \ge a_n \ge 0$ we have
        \begin{align*}
            \frac{\vol_{n-1}\left(\Proj_{a^{\perp}}B_{\infty}^n\right)}{\vol_{n-1}\left(\Proj_{a_{(n)}^{\perp}}B_{\infty}^n\right)} \le 1 - \frac{c'_{\infty}}{a_1^3\sqrt{n}}\sum_{i=1}^n\left(a_i^2 - \frac 1 n\right)^2.
        \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 8 of arXiv:2608.21787

Suppose that after the $i$th step of the REA the tree part $T$

none of which are the final target edge of $W$.

Consider the $j$th step, for some $j>i$,

body:
[Theorem 152 (Restart composition from sequential responses) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] For every restart-congruent sequential presentation,
\[
 \mathfrak C_{\mathbf O}:=\mathsf W(\Sigma)/\!\sim_{\mathbf O}
\]
carries the unique marked partial semigroupoid product
\begin{equation}
 [w]\diamond_{\mathbf O}[v]:=[wv].
\end{equation}
The realized joint response image $\mathbf O(\mathsf W(\Sigma))$ carries the
transported product
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf O(w)\star_{\mathbf O}\mathbf O(v):=\mathbf O(wv).
\end{equation}
Moreover $\mathfrak C_{\mathbf O}$ is the least algebraic restart realization:
any restart realization through which all sequential responses factor admits a
unique surjective restart homomorphism onto $\mathfrak C_{\mathbf O}$ after
restriction to the generated sub-semigroupoid.

[Theorem t:main square-integrable of arXiv:2605.22803, 'Persistence of asymptotic variance under transport:\\ from hyperfluctuation to stealthy hy'] Suppose that $\Phi$ is a locally absolutely square-integrable invariant random complex measure, and that $K$ is an invariant transport kernel. Further, assume that either Condition~(c:condition square-integrable general of the paper) or Condition~(c:condition square-integrable Markov of the paper) holds.
Then $K\Phi$ is locally absolutely square-integrable.
\begin{proof}
If Condition~(c:condition square-integrable general of the paper) holds, the assertion follows from Lemma~(l:remainder2case1 of the paper). If Condition~(c:condition square-integrable Markov of the paper) holds, the assertion follows from Lemma~(l:remainder2case2 of the paper). In both cases, we apply the lemmas with $p=0$. The lemmas each actually include a stronger statement, which we do not need here but in the following subsection. Also, while Lemmas~(l:remainder2case1 of the paper) and~(l:remainder2case2 of the paper) make the same statements under different conditions, the proofs differ completely. The proof of Lemma~(l:remainder2case2 of the paper) follows a technique that is adapted from a proof in~[Dereudre_Flimmel_Huesmann_Leblé_2024].
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem t:main square-integrable of arXiv:2605.22803

[Theorem 5 (Metastability) of arXiv:2608.15914, 'Absorption cutoff and stationary singularities for rounded Gaussian random dynamical syste'] Assume $A>A_{\mathrm{ex}}(\varrho)$, and let $(h_-,h_+)$ be the
  rightmost positive-drift component of $\mathcal O_{A,\varrho}$. Fix a
  compact set $B\subset(h_-,h_+]$ and deterministic initial states
  $Y_0^{(N)}$ satisfying $\mathscr H_0^{(N)}\in B$ for every $N\geq1$.
  Then there are
  $T\in\N_0$ and $c>0$ such that
  \begin{equation*}
    \Pp\left(
      \tau_\varrho^{(N)}
      >
      T+\lfloor\exp(cN)\rfloor
    \right)
    \to1 .
  \end{equation*}
  For each fixed $N$, however, absorption still occurs almost surely for every
  deterministic choice of $Y_0^{(N)}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2604.20617, 'Structured random perturbations of \\ tridiagonal twisted Toeplitz matrices'] Consider the symbol defined on $[0,1] \times \T$
\[
a(x,z) = d(x) z^{-1} + b(x) + c(x) z,
\]
where $b,c,d$ are continuous complex-valued functions on $[0,1]$. Let $\mu_n$ be the sequence of eigenvalue-counting measures
\[
\mu_n = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{\lambda \in \mathrm{sp}(\mathcal{T}_n(a))} \delta_{\lambda}.
\]
Then $\mu_n$ converges weakly to the measure $\mu$ defined by
\[
\mu=\int_0^1 \alpha_x~dx,
\]
where $\alpha_x$ denotes the arcsine measure on the complex interval
\[
\bigl[b(x)-2\sqrt{d(x)c(x)},\, b(x)+2\sqrt{d(x)c(x)}\bigr].
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2604.20617

title: Current best upper bound on the NON-RANDOM fluctuation in first-passage percolation: if F(0) < p_c and E[Y^2] < infinity, where Y is the minimum of d i.i.d. copies of tau_e, then there is C = C(F,d) with mu(x) <= E T(0,x) <= mu(x) + C (|x| log |x|)^{1/2} for every x in Z^d with |x| > 1. Obtained by Damron-Kubota with Alexander's method plus a lower-tail concentration inequality; it improves Kesten's n^{5/6} log n.

body:
[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2608.31164, 'The anisotropic Michael-Simon inequality'] Let $\mu_j, \mu \in \cM( \Omega; \bR^d)$ be vector-valued measures on an open set $\Omega \subset \bR^n$ that converge strictly, $\mu_j \to \mu$, meaning that $\mu_j \xrightharpoonup{*} \mu$ and $|\mu_j|(\Omega) \to |\mu|(\Omega)$.
    Let $F: \Omega \times \bR^d \to \bR$ be a continuous, positively $1$-homogeneous function in the second variable satisfying a uniform linear bound,
    \[
    F(x,tz) = t \, F(x,z) \quad \text{for every } \; t \geq 0, \qquad |F(x,z)| \leq C |z| \quad \text{for every } \; (x,z) \in \Omega \times \bR^d.
    \]
    Then, it holds that
    \[
    \int_{\Omega} F \Bigl( \frac{d \mu_j}{d |\mu_j|} \Bigr) \, d |\mu_j| \to \int_{\Omega} F \Bigl( \frac{d \mu}{d |\mu|} \Bigr) \, d |\mu|.
    \]
    The same statement holds on the flat torus $\bT^n$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 12 of arXiv:2608.31164

body:
[Thm 2 of arXiv:2604.11489, '2604.11489'] Assume that the function $g:[0,1] \to \rr$ is differentiable and its derivative $g'$ is $\beta$-H\"{o}lder
continuous for some $\beta \in (0,1]$. Let
\beq
\sigma^2_n=\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}p_{n,i}\left(g'\left( p_{n,i}\right)\right)^2-\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}p_{n,i}g'\left( p_{n,i}\right)\right)^2
\deq
and
\beq
\gamma=
\begin{cases}
\beta/2 \ \ &\text{if}\ \ \beta\in (0,0.5]\\
\beta-0.5 \ \ &\text{if}\ \ \beta\in (0.5,1]
\end{cases}.
\deq
If
\begin{enumerate}[$(1)$]
\item $\beta\in (0.5,1]$ or
\item $\beta\in (0,0.5]$ and
\beq
\sup_{n}\sum_{i=1}^\infty p_{n,i}^{(\beta+1)/2}<\infty,
\deq
\end{enumerate}
then we have
\beq
\sup_x\left|\pp\left(\frac{\sqrt{n}}{\sigma_n}(\hat \theta_n-\theta_n)\le x\right)-\Phi(x)\right|\le\frac{C}{n^{\gamma/2} \sigma_n^{1/2}},
\deq
where $\Phi$ denotes the standard normal distribution function. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 2 of arXiv:2604.11489

body:
[Theorem 17 of arXiv:2605.24445, 'Matrix concentration inequalities for time-inhomogeneous Markov chains'] Let $F_t:\Omega\to\Hm$ be $L$-Lipschitz for all $t \ge 1$.
\par\noindent
Let \(\sigma_{\infty} \coloneqq \sup_{t \ge 1, x \in \Omega} \diam \supp P_t(x,\cdot)\).
Then, for any $\varepsilon > 0$,
\[
\Pbb_{X_0}\!\left(\left\|\frac{1}{T}  \sum_{k=1}^T F_k(X_k) - \E_{X_0}\!\left[\frac{1}{T}  \sum_{k=1}^T F_k(X_k)\right]\right\|_{\op} >  \varepsilon\right)
\le 2m \exp\left(-\frac{\tilde\kappa^2 T \varepsilon^2 }{8L^2\sigma_\infty^2}\right).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 17 of arXiv:2605.24445

body:
[Theorem 65 (four-factor Cartan-list consequence) of arXiv:2609.03593, '\textbf{New Homogeneous Einstein Metrics from Detection}'] Assume that $H/K$ is an effective irreducible compact symmetric pair and
that both $H$ and $K$ are simple.  Then the normalized
$\Gamma_{4,3}$-fixed $3+1$ family on $H^4/\Delta K$ contains exactly two
positive asymmetric Einstein metrics precisely for
\[
 \frac{\SU(n)^4}{\Delta\SO(n)},
 \qquad n=3\ \text{or}\ n\ge5,
\]
\[
 \frac{\SU(2n)^4}{\Delta\Sp(n)},
 \qquad n\ge9,
\]
and
\[
 \frac{E_6^4}{\Delta\Sp(4)},\qquad
 \frac{E_7^4}{\Delta\SU(8)},\qquad
 \frac{E_8^4}{\Delta\SO(16)}.
\]
For $2\le n\le8$ in type $AII$, for $E_6/F_4$ and
$F_4/\mathrm{Spin}(9)$, and for the sphere-type pairs
$\SO(m+1)/\SO(m)$ with $m\ge5$, this $3+1$ family contains no positive
asymmetric Einstein metric.

In addition, at the first $AII$ Cartasn value below the four-factor response
wall, $n=9$, the balanced $\Gamma_{4,2}$-fixed family contains exactly one
positive asymmetric Einstein metric up to block interchange and homothety.
It lies on the analytic branch issuing from the response wall, is Riemannian
irreducible, and is not naturally reductive.

[Proposition 1 of arXiv:2608.22595, 'Sparse Additive Off-Policy Evaluation for Reinforcement Learning with Potentially Limited '] Assumption~\ref{sparseQ} holds if there exists an index set
$\mathcal K\subseteq[d]$ with $|\mathcal K|\ll d$ such that either of the
following conditions is satisfied:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{(Sufficient Condition 1)}
    The reward function and the full transition kernel depend on the current
    state only through $x_{\mathcal K}$:
    $r(x,a)=r(x_{\mathcal K},a)$ and
    $
    p(x'\mid x,a)=p(x'\mid x_{\mathcal K},a)$.

   \item \textbf{(Sufficient Condition 2)}
     {The reward function and the target policy depend only on
    $x_{\mathcal K}$:
    $
    r(x,a)=r(x_{\mathcal K},a)$,
    $
    \pi(a\mid x)=\pi(a\mid x_{\mathcal K})$,
    and the transition of the active state satisfies
    $p(x'_{\mathcal K}\mid x,a)
    =
    p(x'_{\mathcal K}\mid x_{\mathcal K},a)$.}
\end{itemize}
Under either condition,
$
Q^\pi(x,a)=Q^\pi(x_{\mathcal K},a)$,
so that $\mathcal K$ can serve as an active feature set in
Assumption~\ref{sparseQ}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 1 of arXiv:2608.22595

[Defi 3 of arXiv:2609.02261, 'Quantization and process'] For each $h>0$,  the space 
  $D_h ( \R^{2 n })$  stands for the set of   functions $F$ on $\R^{2 n }$ such that there exists an analytic  function $ (X,Y)\rightarrow F^{\rm ext} (X , Y)$ on   $\C^{2n }$ 
  having the following properties.
  
  i)  $F^{\rm ext}$ satisfies for any $(X,Y)\in\R^{4n}$,

    \be   (\partial _{x_j } + i \partial _{\xi_j }) 
   F^{\rm ext} (X , Y) = 0 ,\quad
     (\partial _{y_j } - i \partial _{\eta_j })
      F^{\rm ext}    (X , Y) = 0,\ee 
      
  ii) We have $$F^{\rm ext}(X , X) = F(X).$$ 
  
 iii) There is 
a function $\psi_F \in L^1(\R^{2n}) \cap L^{\infty}(\R^{2n})$ verifying the estimate for all $(X,Y)\in\R^{4n}$,
       
       $$ | F^{\rm ext}(X , Y)| \leq e^{ \frac { 1 }  { 4h } |X-Y|^2  } 
       \psi_F (X - Y) .$$
       
When the conditions i) ii) and iii) are fulfilled, we set,

$$ \Vert F \Vert _{D_h( \R^{2n})}  =  \Vert \Psi_F  \Vert _{L^1 (\R^{2n})} + 
 \Vert \Psi_F \Vert _{L^{\infty } (\R^{2n})}.  $$
title: Definition 3 of arXiv:2609.02261

[Lem AnaLem of arXiv:2506.18207, 'Cartan's Path Development, the Logarithmic Signature and a Conjecture of Lyons-Sidorova'] Let $N\geqslant2$ be a given fixed integer. Suppose
that $S_{n}(a_{1},\cdots,a_{n})=0$ for all $n\leqslant N-1$ and
all non-degenerate sequences $(a_{1},\cdots,a_{n})$ with $a_{j}\in2\pi i\mathbb{Z}$.
Let $(b_{1}^{*},\cdots,b_{N}^{*})$ be a fixed non-degenerate sequence
with $b_{j}\in2\pi i\mathbb{Z}$. Given $w\in\mathbb{C}$, we define
the path development $F_{w}:\mathbb{C}^{2}\rightarrow\mathfrak{sl}_{N+1}(\mathbb{C})$
by 
\begin{equation}
F_{w}({\rm e}_{1})\triangleq A_{w},\ F_{w}({\rm e}_{2})\triangleq E_{12}+\cdots+E_{N,N+1},
\end{equation}
where $A_{w}\in\mathfrak{h}$ is chosen to satisfy 
\begin{equation}
[A_{w},E_{k,k+1}]=(b_{k}^{*}+w)E_{k,k+1}\ \ \ (k=1,\cdots,N).
\end{equation}
Then for any vector $K=(k_{1},\cdots,k_{n})$ satisfying $|K|=N,n\geqslant2$ or $|K|\leqslant N-1,n\geqslant1$ and any $j=1,\cdots,N,$ there exists a meromorphic function $\Psi_{K,j}:\mathbb{C}^{|K|}\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$
(i.e. the quotient of two holomorphic functions) in $|K|$ complex variables,
such that 
\[
\hat{F}_{w}(H_{K})=\sum_{j}\Psi_{K,j}(b_{j}^{*}+w,\cdots,b_{j+|K|-1}^{*}+w)E_{j,j+|K|}
\]
and the function $w\mapsto\Psi_{K,j}(b_{j}^{*}+w,\cdots,b_{j+|K|-1}^{*}+w)$
is analytic in a neighbourhood of $w=0$ for all $(K,j)$. Here $\hat{F}_{w}$
is the induced Lie homomorphism on ${\cal L}((\mathbb{C}^{2}))$ (cf.
((eq:HatF of the paper))). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem AnaLem of arXiv:2506.18207

body:
[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2608.14802, 'Dynamical Gibbs-non-Gibbs transitions for finite-alphabet models on trees'] Let $(U,d)$ be a metric space, $(G_a)_{a\in A}$ a family of $s$-tree contractions with corresponding contraction constants $\lambda_a$ satisfying
\begin{equation*}
  \lambda:=\sup_{a\in A}\lambda_a<1.
\end{equation*}
Furthermore, let $U_0\subset U$ satisfy $D:=\mathrm{diam}(U_0)=\sup_{x,y\in U_0}d(x,y)<\infty$
and $G_a\big((U_0)^s\big)\subset U_0$ for every $a\in A$.
Then, large distance behavior of any tree-indexed sequence of initial boundary data $U_0$ under any tree-indexed composition of maps $(G_a)_{a\in A}$ becomes asymptotically independent of the intial boundary data $U_0$. 

More precisely, let $(G^{(i)})_{i\in\N_0}$
be a tree-indexed sequence of maps from the family $(G_a)_{a\in A}$, where $G^{(i)}_j$
is attached to the $j$-th vertex in the $i$-th annulus and $G_j^{(i)}=G_{a(i,j)}$ for arbitrary $a(i,j)\in A$. Let
\begin{equation*}
    u^{(n)}=\left(u^{(n)}_1,\dots,u^{(n)}_{s^n}\right),~~\text{and}~~v^{(n)}=\left(v^{(n)}_1,\dots,v^{(n)}_{s^n}\right)
\end{equation*}
be arbitrary boundary data in $U_0^{s^n}$ for each $n\in\N$.
Let $x_n$ and $y_n$ denote the output of the same depth-$n$ tree composition with boundary data
$u^{(n)}$ and $v^{(n)}$, respectively.
Then
\begin{equation*}
     d(x_n,y_n)\leq \lambda^n D
\end{equation*}
for all $n\in \N$.
title: Lemma 19 of arXiv:2608.14802

body:
[Theo 25 of arXiv:2609.01932, 'Essential dimension and faithful rank of finite $p$-gerbes'] Let $F$ be a field of characteristic different from $p$, and let $\cX/F$
be a gerbe banded by $\fC=(\mu_p)^c$.  If
\[
\beta:\fC^*\ra\Br(F)[p]
\]
is its character-obstruction map, then
\begin{equation}
\ed_F(\cX;p)=\ed_F(\cX)=
\min_{\mathcal B\text{ basis of }\fC^*}
\sum_{\chi\in\mathcal B}\ind\beta(\chi).
\end{equation}

[Proposition prop:variance of arXiv:2601.09976, 'Stochastic Calculus as Operator Factorization:\\ An Operator--Covariant Derivative and Uni'] Under the hypotheses of Theorem~(thm:CO of the paper), for $\mathcal{F}_T^X$-measurable $F \in L^2(\Omega)$:
\[
\mathrm{Var}(F) = \|\Pi_X D_X F\|_{\mathcal{H}_X}^2.
\]
For continuous martingales with quadratic variation, this becomes
\[
\mathrm{Var}(F) = \mathbb{E}\!\bigl[\textstyle\int_0^T |(\Pi_X D_X F)_t|^2\, d\langle X \rangle_t\bigr].
\]

[Lemma 23 (Uniform moment bounds for the shifted process) of arXiv:2605.24937, '2605.24937'] Let $p\ge 1$ and define the shifted process $\widetilde Y_n := (1-\eta_n)Y_n' + \eta_n \widehat X_n$ for $n\ge0$. Under the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:P-moment-drift} (with constants $q, C > 0$), and assuming $\widehat M_p := \sup_{n\ge 0} \E\|\widehat X_n\|^p < \infty$, we have
\[
  \E\|\widetilde Y_n\|^p \le e^{-q\lambda n}\E\|\widetilde Y_0\|^p + \frac{C\lambda+\widehat M_p}{1-e^{-q\lambda}},
\]
yielding the uniform bound $\sup_{n\ge 0} \E\|\widetilde Y_n\|^p \le \E\|\widetilde Y_0\|^p + \frac{C\lambda+\widehat M_p}{1-e^{-q\lambda}} < \infty$.

[Definition 13 of arXiv:2609.02755, 'The Sharp Rate of Probabilistically Strong Convergence to the KPZ Equation'] Given a rooted tree $\tau$, we say that $C \subset E_+(\tau)$ is a cut of $\tau$ if any path in $E(\tau)$ with the root of $\tau$ as an endpoint contains at most one edge in $C$. We denote by $\mathbb{C}[\tau]$ the set of all cuts of $\tau$.
	We recall that for a rooted tree $\tau$, there is a natural partial ordering on $E(\tau)$ in which $e \ge e^\prime$ iff $e^\prime$ lies on the unique path from $e$ to the root.
	
	 We write $\tau_{\ng C}$ for the subgraph consisting of those edges $e \in E(\tau)$ such that there does not exist $\tilde{e} \in C$ with $e \ge \tilde{e}$.

[Lemma lem:critical-density of arXiv:2609.02820, 'Sharpness and critical scaling of parking'] Let $\eta=(\eta(x))_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}$ be independent copies of a nonconstant integer-valued
	$\eta(0)$ with mean zero. There is a universal $c>0$ such that
	$\liminf_{t\to\infty}tS_t\geq c$, and there is
	$C<\infty$ such that, for every $n\geq2$,
	\begin{equation}
		\mathbb{E} U_n(0)\geq c\log n-C\,.
	\end{equation}

body: [Lemma lem:cox_J of arXiv:2412.04589, 'Inverting the Markovian projection for pure jump processes'] Let $\lambda$, $\Lambda$, $E$ and $\tau$ be given by Lemma~(lem:cox of the paper). Furthermore, suppose that $\Omega$ supports a non-vanishing integrable random variable $J$ which is independent of $\mathcal{F}_\infty \lor \sigma(E)$. Define the filtration $\widetilde{\mathbb{A}} = (\widetilde{\mathcal{A}}_t)_{t \geq 0}$ by $\widetilde{\mathcal{A}}_t \coloneqq \sigma(J\bm{1}_{\{\tau \leq s\}}; s \leq t)$. Let $\widetilde{\mathbb{G}} \coloneqq \mathbb{F} \newtriangledown \widetilde{\mathbb{A}}$. Then, the process $(J\bm{1}_{\{\tau \leq t\}} - \mathbb{E}[J]\Lambda_{\tau \land t})_{t \geq 0}$ is a $\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}$-martingale, and we have $\mathbb{F} \hookrightarrow \widetilde{\mathbb{G}}$.

body:
[Proposition 21 (Strong local error) of arXiv:2605.24937, '2605.24937'] Let Assumptions~\hyperref[ass:PJG]{\textup{(A1)}}--\hyperref[ass:D]{\textup{(A4)}} hold.
Let \(X_t\) denote the solution of \eqref{eq:LSDE} started from \(X_0=x\), and
\(\widehat X_t\) the one-step interpolation associated with \eqref{eq:kTULA} started from \(\widehat X_0=x\).
Set \(M := \max\{3(\ell+1),\,2\ell'+4\ell\}\).
Then there exists a constant \(C>0\), independent of \(x\in\R^d\), \(d\), and \(\lambda\in(0,1]\), such that for every \(x\in\R^d\),
\[
  \|\widehat X_\lambda - X_\lambda\|_{L^2}
  \;\le\;
  C\bigl(1+d^{M/2}+\|x\|^{M}\bigr)\,\lambda^{3/2}.
\]
In particular,
\[
  E_{\mathrm{strong}}(x)
  :=
  C\bigl(1+d^{M/2}+\|x\|^{M}\bigr)\,\lambda^{3/2}.
\]

body: [Definition of arXiv:2607.02410, 'Polynomial mixing for polygonal side matchings'] The length of a chord connecting sides $A$ and $B$ is $1$ plus the number of sides between $A$ and $B$ (the smallest of the two possibilities). A \emph{canonical} chord diagram is one where each chord is either of length $1$, or is of length $2$ and intersects another chord of length $2$.

\end{equation}

[Theorem thm:max_lh of arXiv:2607.22291, 'Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declum'] Assume that $\mu$ is critical and belongs to the domain of attraction of a stable law.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)]  Assume that $\mu_{1}>0$. There exists a constant $C_{\mu}>0$ such that the following holds. Set
$$k^*_{n} =  \frac{1}{\log(1/\mu_{1})}\log n +  \frac{1}{\log(1/\mu_{1})} \log\bigl((1-\mu_1)C_{\mu}\bigr).$$
Then for every $t \in \mathbb{R}$ we have
\[
\P\bigl(\lambda(\mathcal{T}^n) \leq \lfloor k^*_{n} + t\rfloor\bigr) - \exp\bigl(-\mu_1^{t+1 - \{k^*_{n} + t\}}\bigr) \to 0.
\]
\item[(ii)] Assume that $\mu_{1}=0$. Set $\kappa = \min\{i \geq 2 : \mu_i > 0\}$. There exists a constant $D_{\mu} \in (0,1)$ such that the following holds. Set
$$
k_{n}^{**} \coloneqq  \log_\kappa \log n - \log_\kappa \log(1/D_{\mu}).
$$
 Write $m_n=\lfloor k_n^{**}\rfloor$ and
$\theta_n=\{k_n^{**}\}$, and define
$$
  J_n=
  \begin{cases}
    \{m_n-1,m_n\},&\theta_n\le\tfrac12,\\
    \{m_n,m_n+1\},&\theta_n>\tfrac12.
  \end{cases}
$$
Then $\P(\lambda(\mathcal T^n)\in J_n)\longrightarrow1$. In addition, if $\liminf_n\min(\theta_n,1-\theta_n)>0$, then
$\P(\lambda(\mathcal T^n)=m_n)\to1$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 19 of arXiv:2609.02105, 'Contact fundamental forms and \\ adjoint varieties'] For $h \in \sH$, the vector space $U_k(\fn_h)^*$ is a subspace of $J^k_h$ by the exact sequence in Definition \ref{d.contact} (iii). By Theorem \ref{t.Taylor}, it can be identified with the vector space of polynomials of the form   $$ \sum_{|I|= k} c_I \ h^*(xyt)^I $$ with coefficients $c_I \in \C$.  
  For each $1 \leq a \leq m$, define the  homomorphism  $\delta_{\sX_a,h}$ (resp. $\delta_{\sY_a,h}$)  from $U_k(\fn_h)^*$ to $U_{k-1}(\fn_h)^*$
 as follows. 
\begin{eqnarray*} 
\delta_{\sX_a,h} \big( \sum_{|I|= k} c_I \ h^*(xyt)^I \big) & := & (\frac{\p}{\p x_a} + \frac{y_a}{2} \frac{\p}{\p t}) \big( \sum_{|I|= k} c_I \ h^*(xyt)^I \big)
 \\
\delta_{\sY_a,h} \big( \sum_{|I|= k} c_I \ h^*(xyt)^I \big) & := & (\frac{\p}{\p y_a} - \frac{x_a}{2} \frac{\p}{\p t}) \big( \sum_{|I|= k} c_I \ h^*(xyt)^I \big),
\end{eqnarray*}
where on the righthand side, the vector fields act on the polynomial functions on $\sH$ as derivative. 
Also define the homomorphism $\delta_{T,h}: U_k(\fn_h)^* \to U_{k-2}(\fn_h)^*$ by
\begin{eqnarray*} 
\delta_{T,h} \big( \sum_{|I|= k} c_I \ h^*(xyt)^I \big) & := &  \frac{\p}{\p t} \big( \sum_{|I|= k} c_I \ h^*(xyt)^I \big).
\end{eqnarray*}
They define vector bundle homomorphisms $$\delta_{\sX_a}, \delta_{\sY_a}: U_k(\fn)^* \to U_{k-1}(\fn)^*, \ \delta_T: U_k(\fn)^* \to U_{k-2}(\fn)^*$$ and corresponding sheaf homomorphisms, which we denote by the same symbols,
$$\delta_{\sX_a}, \delta_{\sY_a}: \sO(U_k(\fn)^*) \to \sO(U_{k-1}(\fn)^*), \ \delta_T: \sO(U_k(\fn)^*) \to \sO(U_{k-2}(\fn)^*).$$

[Proposition prop:endpoint-deconvolution of arXiv:2607.18070, 'The Brownian loop-catcher'] Fix \(E\subset V\) and nonempty \(S\subset E\), and put
\(B=E\setminus S\).  There are numbers
\(\boldsymbol{\nu}_S(C)\ge0\), \(\varnothing\ne C\subset B\), such that, for every
\(W\subset B\),
\begin{equation}
        \mathbf H_S(W)d_W=
        \sum_{\varnothing\ne C\subset W}\boldsymbol{\nu}_S(C)d_{W\setminus C} .
\end{equation}
Consequently
\begin{equation}
        \boldsymbol{\rho}_S^1(C)=\frac{d_{B\setminus C}}{d_B}\boldsymbol{\nu}_S(C)\ge0,
        \qquad C\ne\varnothing .
\end{equation}
Moreover \(\boldsymbol{\nu}_S(C)\), and hence \(\boldsymbol{\rho}_S^1(C)\), vanishes unless \(C\) is
\(S\)-attached.

body: A graph G = (V, E) is a finite set V of vertices together with a set E of edges, each an unordered pair of vertices; G is simple if it has no loops or repeated edges. A subgraph uses a subset of the vertices and edges. The degree of a vertex is the number of incident edges, and the handshake lemma gives sum of degrees = 2|E|. A walk is a vertex-edge alternation; a path has distinct vertices, a cycle is a closed path, and G is connected if every two vertices are joined by a path. Standard families: the complete graph K_n (all pairs adjacent), a tree (connected and acyclic, with |V|-1 edges), and a bipartite graph (vertices two-colorable so every edge crosses, equivalently no odd cycle). The vertex connectivity kappa(G) and edge connectivity lambda(G) are the least numbers of vertices, respectively edges, whose deletion disconnects G (or reduces it to a single vertex), and kappa(G) <= lambda(G) <= min-degree.
title: Graph, Subgraph, and Basic Invariants

[Defin definition:parisi functional of arXiv:2605.05631, 'Wandering Exponents and the Free Energy of the High-Dimensional Elastic Polymer'] For $q\in (0,\infty)$ and $\zeta\in P([0,q))$ let $\delta$ denote the function defined in ((eqn:def:delta-P of the paper)). We define the functional
		\[\mathcal{P}_{\beta}(q,\zeta)=\frac{1}{2}\left(\int_{0}^{q_*} \frac{du}{\beta t\delta(u)^2}-\frac{1}{\beta t(q-q_*)}-2\beta^2\int_0^q\zeta([0,u])B'(2(q-u)) du-\beta\mu q+\frac{2\sqrt{\mu}}{\sqrt{t}}\right),\]
		where here $q_*\in [0,q]$ is any point such that $\zeta([0,q_*])=1$. It is easily verified that $\mathcal{P}_{\beta}(q,\zeta)$ is independent of the choice of $q_*$.
title: The Parisi Functional

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Assuming that $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is $n$ times differentiable, we have
$$f(x+t)\simeq\sum_{k=0}^n\frac{f^{(k)}(x)}{k!}\,t^k$$
where $f^{(k)}(x)$ are the higher derivatives of $f$ at the point $x$.
title: Unnumbered theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'

[Mainthm 3 of arXiv:2507.08909, 'Annealed almost periodic entropy'] Let $\phi:\G\to \rmM_k$ be positive definite. If $\phi$ is tempered, then for every neighbourhood $O$ of $\phi$ we have
	\[\bbP(\X(\pi_n,O) \ne \emptyset) \to 1.\]
	On the other hand, if $\phi$ is not tempered, then there are a neighbourhood $O$ of $\phi$ and a positive value $c$ such that
	\[\bbP(\X(\pi_n,O) \ne \emptyset) \le e^{-cn + o(n)}.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Mainthm 3 of arXiv:2507.08909

body:
Let X, Y be Banach spaces and T: D(T) ⊂ X → Y a linear operator defined on a linear subspace D(T). Its graph is G(T) = {(x, Tx) : x ∈ D(T)} ⊂ X × Y. T is closed if G(T) is closed in X × Y; equivalently, whenever x_n ∈ D(T), x_n → x in X and Tx_n → y in Y, then x ∈ D(T) and Tx = y. Equivalently, D(T) is complete under the graph norm ‖x‖_T = ‖x‖ + ‖Tx‖. S is an extension of T (written T ⊂ S) if D(T) ⊂ D(S) and Sx = Tx for x ∈ D(T). T is closable if it has a closed extension; equivalently, x_n ∈ D(T), x_n → 0 and Tx_n → y imply y = 0; equivalently, the closure of G(T) is the graph of an operator, called the closure T̄ (the smallest closed extension). If T is closed, a subspace D_0 ⊂ D(T) is a core for T if D_0 is dense in D(T) for the graph norm, i.e. the closure of T restricted to D_0 equals T. A closed operator need not be bounded, and being closed says nothing about D(T) being dense; by the closed graph theorem a closed operator with D(T) = X is bounded.
X and Y are Banach spaces
T is linear on a linear subspace D(T) of X
title: Closed Operator, Closable Operator, and Core

[Proposition 2 of arXiv:2609.02426, 'Deformations of the $\osp(n|2)$-action on the superspace\\ of symbols of differential oper'] For any fixed $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)\in\{0,1\}^{n-1}\times\frac 12\mathbb{N}$, with $|\alpha|=k$, the submodule of  $\Dc^{n,k}_{\lambda,\mu}/\Dc^{n,k-\frac{1}{2}}_{\lambda,\mu}$ spanned, as a $C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^{1|n})$-module, by the class of $D^\alpha$ is isomorphic to $\Fc_{\mu-\lambda-k}^n$. The isomorphism is induced from the following map:
$$
a(x,\theta)D^\alpha\mapsto a(x,\theta)\omega_n^{\mu-\lambda-k}.
$$

body:
[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2606.03122, 'Propagation of support for super-Brownian motion with general branching mechanism'] Given a super-Brownian motion $X$ with a branching mechanism $\Psi$ satisfying Condition \ref{con_localize}, for any $\mu\in M_c$, $0<R_1<R$ and $0<t<\dfrac{R_1^2}{d}$, we have
$$
\begin{aligned}
&\mathbb{P}_\mu\left\{X_u\left((S(\mu)^R)^c\right) > 0 \text{ for some } u \leq t\right\} \\
&\quad \leq \mu(1) \cdot u_{R,\Phi_{\rho(\mu)+R}}(R_1) \cdot C(d) \left(\frac{R_1}{\sqrt{t}}\right)^{d-2} \exp\left(-\frac{R_1^2}{2t}\right) \\
&\quad \leq \mu(1) \cdot G_{\Phi_{\rho(\mu)+R}}^{-1}(R-R_1) \cdot C(d) \left(\frac{R_1}{\sqrt{t}}\right)^{d-2} \exp\left(-\frac{R_1^2}{2t}\right),
\end{aligned}
$$
where $C(d)$ is a constant depending only on dimension $d$, and $u_{R,\Phi_{\rho(\mu)+R}}$ denotes the unique radial classical solution of singular boundary value problem \eqref{SBVP} in $B(0,R)$ with $\Phi$ replaced by $\Phi_{\rho(\mu)+R}$. If $\Psi$ satisfies Condition \ref{con_general} with lower bound $\Phi$, then this estimate reduces to the same bound with $u_{R,\Phi_{\rho(\mu)+R}}$ and $G_{\Phi_{\rho(\mu)+R}}^{-1}$ replaced by $u_{R,\Phi}$ and $G_\Phi^{-1}$, respectively. In particular, the spatially constant case is obtained by taking $\Psi(x,u)=\Phi(u)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2606.03122

[Proposition 33 (Log-convexity of the partition function for integer loop weights) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Assume \(\theta\in\mathbb N\) and \(\theta>1\). Then, for every finite graph
\(G=(V,E)\) and every \(u\in[0,1]\), the map
\[
t\longmapsto Z_G(\theta,t,u)
\]
is log-convex on \([0,\infty)\), that is,
\[
\frac{\dd^2}{\dd t^2}\log Z_G(\theta,t,u)\ge 0
\qquad\text{for all } t\ge 0.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Log-convexity of the partition function for integer loop weights

body: For a convex problem (convex objective and inequality constraints, affine equalities), Slater's condition - the existence of a strictly feasible point where every inequality holds strictly - implies strong duality: the primal and dual optimal values coincide and the dual optimum is attained. Without convexity or a constraint qualification, a duality gap can exist.
title: Slater's Condition and Strong Duality

[Prop boundconditionalmoment of arXiv:2602.08739, '\large \bf MOMENTS OF C$\beta$E FIELD PARTITION FUNCTION, $\mathsf{Sine}_{\beta}$ CORRELAT'] For $p \geq 2$, let $(\theta_m)_{1 \leq m \leq p}\in \mathbb{R}^p$, $(s_m)_{1 \leq m \leq p}\in\mathbb{R}_+^p$, 
and $j,\ell \in \mathbb{N}\cup \{0\}$ so that $j \geq \ell$.  
Then, 
\begin{align*}
& \mathbb{E} \left[ \prod_{m=1}^p \left|\Phi^*_{j+\ell} (\mathrm{e}^{\textnormal{i} \theta_m})
\right|^{2s_m} \;  \bigg| \mathcal{F}_j \right]
\\ & \leq \prod_{m=1}^p \left|\Phi^*_{j} (\mathrm{e}^{\textnormal{i} \theta_m})
\right|^{2s_m} \, \exp \left[ 
\frac{2 \ell}{\beta (j+1)}  
 \sum_{m=1}^{p} s_m^2 
+ \frac{K}{j+1} \min \left( \ell, \left(\min_{1 \leq m_1 \neq m_2 \leq p} 
||\theta_{m_1} - \theta_{m_2}|| \right)^{-1} \right)  \dots \right.
\\ & \left.  \dots
+ K \left(\frac{\ell}{j+1} \right)^{3/2}    \left(1 + \sqrt{\log \left(\frac{1+j}{1 + \ell} \right) } \right)   
\right],
\end{align*}
where $K > 0$ depends only on $\beta, p$
and on the sequence $(s_m)_{1 \leq m \leq p}$, and $||a||$ denotes the distance between $a$ and the set $2 \pi \mathbb{Z}$.

[Theorem th:nsenoftraveltimes of arXiv:2601.05361, 'Noise sensitivity in last-passage percolation'] For $n\ge1$, let $T_n = T_n(\omega)$ denote the last-passage time from $(0, 0)$ to $(n, n)$ with respect to the weight configuration $\omega$. 
Planar last-passage percolation with geometric weights is noise sensitive in the sense that, for every $p\in(0,1)$ and $t>0$,

\[
\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \Corr \big(T_n(\omega), T_n(\omega^t) \big) = 0 .
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem th:nsenoftraveltimes of arXiv:2601.05361

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, Free multiplicative convolution and log-unimodality: three questions of Hasebe, Ueda and Wang (2026) answers Problems 4.3, 4.7 and 4.11 of T. Hasebe, Y. Ueda and J.-C. Wang, Log-unimodality for free positive multiplicative Brownian motion (Colloq. Math. 169, 2022, 209-226; arXiv:2009.13848), sigma_t denoting that Brownian motion. Theorem A: the free multiplicative convolution of two multiplicatively symmetric log-unimodal laws need not be log-unimodal; for L >= 6 the log-uniform law on [e^-L, e^L] convolved with itself has a log-density with a strict local minimum at 0. Theorem B: for nu = (delta_{1/10} + delta_{10})/2, sigma_t ⊠ nu is not log-unimodal for any t > 0. Proposition D: if nu is log-unimodal and supported in [alpha, beta], then sigma_t ⊠ nu is log-unimodal for all t >= (pi/2)(beta/alpha + alpha/beta). Theorem C: sigma_t is not ⊠-strongly log-unimodal for any t > 0. Paper and a Lean 4 check of the inequalities: https://github.com/yspennstate/free-multiplicative-log-unimodality (commit 8f7665f177d6). Not refereed.
title: Hasebe-Ueda-Wang Problems 4.3, 4.7 and 4.11 answered: free multiplicative convolution and log-unimodality of free positive multiplicative Brownian motion (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/free-multiplicative-log-unimodality)

[Proposition 42 (Coxeter orbit of the monomial physical contour) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] In the adjacent basis of
\cref{cor:monomial-Gaussian-Betti-row}, let \(M_m\) be the positive
Coxeter monodromy of the \(A_{m-1}\) sector fan, fixed by
\[
 M_m\Gamma_0=-\sum_{j=0}^{m-2}\Gamma_j,
 \qquad
 M_m\Gamma_j=\Gamma_{j-1}
 \quad(1\leq j\leq m-2).
\]
Then
\[
 \chi_{M_m}(\lambda)=\frac{\lambda^m-1}{\lambda-1}.
\]
For the physical class
\[
 r_m=[\R]=-\sum_{j=0}^{\ell-1}\Gamma_j,
 \qquad \ell=\lfloor m/2\rfloor,
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
 \dim_\C\Span\{M_m^kr_m:k\in\mathbb Z\}
 =
 \begin{cases}
  m-1,&m\ \mathrm{odd},\\[1mm]
  m/2,&m\ \mathrm{even}.
 \end{cases}
 
\end{equation}
For even \(m\), the missing dimension equals the dimension of the
parity-odd Jacobi sector.  Thus the Betti orbit rank agrees numerically
with \eqref{eq:monomial-observable-rank}; this rank count alone does not
assert a canonical identification of the two sectors.  The rank in
\eqref{eq:monomial-Betti-orbit-rank} is the rank of the monodromy orbit
ledger; the single physical row \(C_\R\) itself, of course, has matrix
rank one.

Let M_n be an n by n matrix whose n^2 entries are independent and uniform on {-1,+1}. Then E[(det M_n)^2]=n!. Consequently, for every function omega(n)>0 tending to infinity, P(|det M_n|<=omega(n)*sqrt(n!))->1 as n tends to infinity. Independence of all entries is required; the same moment identity is not asserted for a symmetric sign matrix. Source: Recent progress in combinatorial random matrix theory, Section 6, equation (3), p.9.
n is a positive integer
all n^2 entries are independent fair signs

[Theorem thm:int-3_one-dim_version of arXiv:2510.06891, 'Multivariate CLT for L\'evy processes: convergence rates without moment assumptions'] Let $Y=(Y_t)_{t\geqslant0}$ be a real-valued symmetric L\'evy process, and let $Z$ be a standard Gaussian random variable. Assume there exists a measurable function $B:[1,\infty) \to \mathbb{R}$ such that
\[
t \mapsto t^{-1}d_{\mathscr{K}}(B(t)^{-1}Y_t,  Z )\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(+\infty),
\]
where $B(t)$ is non-zero for all sufficiently large $t$ and $ B(t) \to \infty$ and $B(t)^{-1} B(f(t))\to 1$ as $t \to \infty$ for any non-decreasing $f$ with $f(t)/t\to 1$. Then $\mathds{E}[Y_1^2]<\infty$ and $d_{\mathscr{K}}( B(t)^{-1}Y_t,  Z )\to 0$ as $t\to\infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 7 (Error bound for the slope change classifier) of arXiv:2609.00402, '2609.00402'] Suppose Assumption~\ref{ass:slope} holds. Let \(T\geq5\), \(\mathcal I=\{3,\ldots,T-2\}\), and \(m_T=\lvert\mathcal I\rvert=T-4\). For \(\tau\in\mathcal I\), define \(v_\tau=1/D_L(\tau)+1/D_R(\tau)\), \(v_T^{\max}=\max_{\tau\in\mathcal I}v_\tau\), and, for \(\alpha_S\in(0,1)\), \(\lambda_{S,\alpha_S}=\sigma_S\sqrt{2v_T^{\max}\log(2m_T/\alpha_S)}\). Then \(h_{S,\lambda_{S,\alpha_S}}(\bm X)=\mathbb I\{S(\bm X)>\lambda_{S,\alpha_S}\}\) satisfies \(\mathbb P\{h_{S,\lambda_{S,\alpha_S}}(\bm X)=1\mid Y=0\}\leq\alpha_S\) and
\[
\mathbb P\{h_{S,\lambda_{S,\alpha_S}}(\bm X)=0\mid Y=1\}
\leq
\exp\left\{-\frac{(\kappa_S-\lambda_{S,\alpha_S})_+^2}{2\sigma_S^2v_T^{\max}}\right\},
\]
where \(x_+=\max\{x,0\}\). Consequently,
\[
\operatorname{err}(h_{S,\lambda_{S,\alpha_S}})
\leq\pi_0\alpha_S+
\pi_1\exp\left\{-\frac{(\kappa_S-\lambda_{S,\alpha_S})_+^2}{2\sigma_S^2v_T^{\max}}\right\}
=:\mathfrak B_S(\alpha_S).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Error bound for the slope change classifier

body:
[Prop nonzero-imag-bispectrum of arXiv:2605.13004, 'Orientation in Poisson Cluster Processes via Imaginary Bispectra'] Let $0<m<1$, let $h$ be a probability density supported on $(0,\infty)$, and consider the stationary one-sided linear Hawkes, equivalently Poisson branching-cluster, process with immigrant rate $\nu$ and offspring density $mh$. Let $B$ denote its reduced third factorial-cumulant bispectrum. Suppose either
\begin{enumerate}
\item
\[
\int_x^\infty h(u)\,du\sim x^{-\alpha}L(x),\qquad x\to\infty,
\]
for some $0<\alpha\le2$ and slowly varying $L$; or
\item $h$ is nonincreasing on $(0,\infty)$, $\int_0^\infty u^2h(u)\,du<\infty$, and $h$ is not of the form $a^{-1}\1_{(0,a)}$ for some $a>0$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists $t_0>0$ such that
\[
\mathrm{Im} B(t_0,t_0)\neq0.
\]
Consequently, this one-sided process is separated at third order from every reversible process whose reduced third factorial cumulant has an $L^1$ density. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Non-vacuity of the imaginary bispectrum

[Lem 8 of arXiv:2609.02686, 'The Bonnet-Myers theorem on Finsler manifolds with integral weighted Ricci curvature bound'] {\rm (\cite{ChF1}, Theorem 1.1)} Let $(M, F, m)$ be an $n$-dimensional forward complete Finsler measure space. Assume that ${\rm Ric}_{\infty}\geq -K$  for some $K\geq 0$.  Then, for any $0< r_{1} < r_{2}$, we have
\be
\frac{m(B_{r_{2}}(x_0))}{m(B_{r_{1}}(x_0))}\leq \left(\frac{r_{2}}{r_{1}}\right)^{n+1}e^{\frac{K+ \vartheta_{0}^{2}}{6}r_{2}^2}, 
\ee
where  $x_{0}\in M$ is an arbitrary fixed point and $\vartheta_{0}$ is defined by (\ref{supS}). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Method: Existence of finite FPP geodesics without distributional assumptions structural argument Result: If all edge times are at least a>0, a fixed connecting path of cost M bounds any competing path length by M/a; only finitely many simple paths of that length start at a fixed vertex, so a minimum exists. Without a positive lower bound, a deterministic ladder can fail: give each vertical edge from height j-1 to j on both rails weight2^(-j), and the rung at height k weight3*2^(-k). A route across at height k costs2+2^(-k), with infimum2 unattained. Check: For a finite ladder route attaining maximum height k, vertical cost is at least2(1-2^(-k)) and at least one rung has cost at least3*2^(-k); this gives the same strict lower bound. Embed the ladder into Z^d with all other edges cost100 to preserve failure. Obstruction: The ladder environment is deterministic and spatially inhomogeneous, so it is only a counterexample to a general compactness inference. The iid critical case requires additional probabilistic structure.

[Theorem theo_graph_sec_graph of arXiv:2503.24372, 'A criterion on the free energy for log-Sobolev inequalities in mean-field particle systems'] Let $G_N$ satisfy Assumption~(ass_graph of the paper) and $V$ satisfy Assumption~(ass_doublewell of the paper). 
Let $T>T_c$, 
the critical temperature (equation eq_def_beta_c of the paper) in the mean-field case. 
Then, for $N$ large enough depending only on $T,\gamma_V$, the measure $m^{G_N}_T$ satisfies a log-Sobolev inequality with constant:

\begin{equation}
\frac{1}{\gamma^{G_N}_{\rm LS}(T)}
\leq 
\frac{1}{(T-T_c)\gamma_V^2} + \frac{1}{\gamma_V} + O(\epsilon_N)
,

\end{equation}
where the constant $\gamma_V$ depends only on the confinement potential $V$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem theo_graph_sec_graph of arXiv:2503.24372

body: [Lemma lem-swallowed-delta-qle of arXiv:2605.03385, 'Quantum Loewner evolution in quantum natural time: phases and Markov properties'] In the setting of Definition~(def-delta-QLE-finite of the paper) and Lemma~(lem-duration-indep of the paper)  with $\gamma \in (2\sqrt3 - 2, 2)$ and $\eta = \frac{3\gamma^2}{16} - \frac12$, the jumps of $(L^\delta_\cdot)_{[0,\mathcal{S}^\delta)}$ are in bijection with the quantum surfaces swallowed by $(\phi^\delta, (K^\delta_\cdot)_{[0,\mathcal{S}^\delta]})$, wherein at each jump time the process swallows a quantum surface whose $\gamma$-LQG boundary length is the jump size. Moreover, conditioned on $(L^\delta_{\cdot})_{[0,\mathcal{S}^\delta)}$, the swallowed quantum surfaces are conditionally independent, and the conditional law of the quantum surface corresponding to a jump of size $\ell$ is $\mathrm{QD}(\ell)^\#$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem-swallowed-delta-qle of arXiv:2605.03385

[Lem 5 of arXiv:2607.03360, 'Smoluchowski-Kramers Approximation Meets Khasminskii Averaging Principles in Nonequilibriu'] Suppose that \assmref{ass:mom-bdd} and \assmref{ass:gd-lip} hold. For each $t\in [0,T]$, the quantity $\sqrt{m} |v_t^m|$ is bounded in $L^2(\Omega)$. More precisely, there exists a constant $C_{T,\la_0,|v_0|}>0$, independent of $m$, such that 
\beq{bdd-mvs}
\EE\Big[m|v_t^m|^2\Big] \leq C_{T,\la_0,|v_0|}.
\eeq
Consequently,
\beq{0-mvs}
\EE\Big[|mv_t^m|^2\Big] \leq C_{T,\la_0,|v_0|}m.
\eeq
and hence $m|v_t^m| \to 0$ in $L^2(\Omega)$, thus in probability. Moreover, we also have
\beq{4-mv}
\EE|mv_t^m|^4 \leq C_{T,\la_0,|v_0|}.
\eeq

[Lem 171 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let indices $a(q_d),a^\frozen(q_d)$
be sampled as in Definition~\ref{d:rerand}, and let
indices $i(q_d),i^\frozen(q_d)$
be sampled as in Definition~\ref{d:rerand.Ising}. 
For $N$ large enough, we have
	\[\max_{\sigma\in\{\RomII,\RomIII\}}
	\E\bigg[
	\max_{r\in[s,t]} 
	\bigg|
	\sum_{\ell=s}^{r-1}
	\Delta X^\sigma(q_\ell,a(q_{\ell+1}))
	\bigg|^8
	\bigg]
	\le L^{O(1)} (q_t-q_s)^4
	\]
for all $0\le s\le t\le \dmax$.
The same bound holds
	with $\Delta X^{\trunc,\sigma}(q_d,a(q_{d+1}))$
	or $\Delta X^{\frozen,\sigma}(q_d,a^\frozen(q_{d+1}))$
	in place of $\Delta X^\sigma(q_d,a(q_{d+1}))$.
We also have
	\[
	\E \left[
	\max_{r\in[s,t]}
	\left|
	\sum_{\ell=s}^{r-1}
	\Delta X^{\Ising}(q_\ell,i(q_{\ell+1}))
	\right|^8
	\right]
	\le L^{O(1)}(q_t-q_s)^4\,,
	\]
and likewise with $\Delta X^{\trunc,\Ising}(q_\ell,i(q_{\ell+1}))$ or $\Delta X^{\Isplus}(q_\ell,i^\frozen(q_{\ell+1}))$ in place of $\Delta X^{\Ising}(q_\ell,i(q_{\ell+1}))$.

\begin{proof}
This follows by a very similar argument as for Lemma~\ref{l:martingale.sup.bound.X.II.III.Ising}. We will describe the proof for $X^\RomII$. A key difference is that in Lemma~\ref{l:martingale.sup.bound.X.II.III.Ising} we considered $X^\RomII(q_d,a)$ as a process indexed by time $q_d$ for a fixed index $a\in[M]$, with respect to the filtration $\cG(t)$. Here, we instead consider the process $X^\RomII(q_d,a(q_d))$, with respect to the filtration $\cFt(t)$ defined by \eqref{e:gaus.filt.plus}. With this change, repeating the argument of
Lemma~\ref{l:martingale.sup.bound.X.II.III.Ising} gives the conclusion for $X^\RomII$ (cf.\ \eqref{e:martingale.X.holder.estimate}). The conclusions for $X^\RomIII$ and $X^\Ising$ follow similarly. It is straightforward to verify that the same bounds hold for the modified processes 
$X^{\trunc,\sigma}$ and $X^{\frozen,\sigma}$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 9 of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] Given a $C^0$ hive $h \in H(\la, \mu; \nu)$, let $L_n(h)$ denote the point  in $H_n(\la_n, \mu_n; \nu_n)$ whose $ij^{th}$ coordinate is given by $$(L_n(h))_{ij} := n^2 h\left(\frac{i}{n}, \frac{j}{n}\right),$$ for all $i, j \in [n+1]$ such that $i \leq j$.
   Let $U_n$ denote the set of lattice points $(x, y) \in \Z^2$ belonging to the triangle in a $[n+1]\times [n+1]$ index set of an augmented hive, such that $0 < y < x \leq n+1$. 
   
   Let $U$ denote the set of points $(x, y) \in [0, 1]^2$ such that $0 < y < x \leq 1.$

body:
[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2607.23640, '{\sl Non-equilibrium fluctuations of a two-species exclusion process with slow boundary }'] There exist constants \(C>0\) and \(\kappa>0\) such that, for every
		\(\bm f\in \mathcal L^2((0,1);\mathbb R^2)\),
		\[
		\|T_t\bm f\|_{\mathcal L^2}
		\le
		Ce^{-\kappa t}\|\bm f\|_{\mathcal L^2},
		\qquad t\ge0.
		\]
		Consequently, the adjoint semigroup also satisfies
		\[
		\|S_t\bm f\|_{\mathcal  L^2}
		\le
		Ce^{-\kappa t}\|\bm f\|_{\mathcal L^2},
		\qquad t\ge0.
		\]
		In particular,
		\[
		\lim_{t\to\infty}T_t\bm f=0,
		\qquad
		\lim_{t\to\infty}S_t\bm f=0
		\]
		in \(\mathcal  L^2((0,1);\mathbb R^2)\).

[Cor derivative bound F of arXiv:2603.17858, 'Decay of correlations and zeros for the hard-core model'] Let $\Delta\in\mathbb{N}$ and let
    $\lambda>0$. Let $K\subset B_{\lambda/2}(\lambda/2)$ be a compact
    set containing a neighbourhood of $[\ell_{\Delta}(\lambda),r_{\Delta}(\lambda)]$.
    There exists a constant $C>0$ such that for any sequence $(\lambda_{n})$
    in $[\ell_{\Delta}(\lambda),\lambda]$, for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$
    and the maps $F_{n}=f_{\lambda_{n}}\circ\cdots\circ f_{\lambda_{1}}$,
    we have 
    \begin{equation}
    \norm{F_{n}'}_{K}\leq C|F_{n}(0)-F_{n}(\lambda)|.
    \end{equation}

body:
[Thm conv-DL-zero of arXiv:2411.16376, 'Higher order approximations in arcsine laws for subordinators'] Under the assumption of Theorem $(Thm:potential-zero of the paper)$ with $\beta_0=\beta\in(0,1]$,  let us define a function $\varepsilon_2:(0,+\infty)\to\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$ by 
\begin{align}
    \Pi((x,+\infty))=
    \frac{c_0 x^{-\beta}}{\Gamma(1-\beta)}+\varepsilon_2(x),
    \quad
   0<x<+\infty.	
\end{align}
Set 
\begin{align}
 \varepsilon_3(s,x)
   =
   s\Pi((s-sx,+\infty))\varepsilon_1(sx),
   \quad 0<s, x<+\infty.	
\end{align}
Then, for $s\in(0,+\infty)$, the finite measure 
\begin{align}
\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}\bigg(\frac{X_{T(s)-}}{s}\in dx,\; 0<\frac{X_{T(s)-}}{s}<1\bigg),
\quad 0<x<1,
\end{align}
 admits a density expressed in the form
\begin{align}
   s\Pi((s-sx,&+\infty))u(sx)
   \\
   =\,&
   \frac{\sin(\pi\beta)}{\pi}x^{-1+\beta}(1-x)^{-\beta}
   +
   \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{c_0 s^{\beta_k-\beta}}{c_k\Gamma(\beta_k)\Gamma(1-\beta)}
   x^{-1+\beta_k}(1-x)^{-\beta}
   \\
   &+
   \sum_{k=0}^n \frac{s^{\beta_k}}{c_k\Gamma(\beta_k)}
   x^{-1+\beta_k}\varepsilon_2(s-sx)
   +
   O(\varepsilon_3(s,x)),
   \quad
   \text{as $s\to0+$,}	
\end{align}
uniformly in $x\in I$ for any closed interval $I\subset (0,1)$. 
Therefore, for any closed interval $I\subset (0,1)$,
\begin{align}
	&\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}\bigg(\frac{X_{T(s)-}}{s}\in I\bigg)
	\\
	=\,&
	 \frac{\sin(\pi\beta)}{\pi}
	 \int_I x^{-1+\beta}(1-x)^{-\beta}\,dx
	 +
	 \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{c_0 s^{\beta_k-\beta}}{c_k\Gamma(\beta_k)\Gamma(1-\beta)}
   \int_I x^{-1+\beta_k}(1-x)^{-\beta}\,dx 
   \\	
   &+
   \sum_{k=0}^n \frac{s^{\beta_k}}{c_k\Gamma(\beta_k)}
   \int_I
   x^{-1+\beta_k}\varepsilon_2(s-sx)\,dx
   + 
   O\bigg(\sup_{x\in I}\varepsilon_3(s,x)\bigg),
   \quad
   \text{as $s\to0+$}.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: higher order approximation in short-range Dynkin--Lamperti theorem

body:
[Thm unstable-equiv-main of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] The global $\infty$-category $\ul{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}$ is equivariantly presentable, and the unique equivariantly cocontinuous functor $\ul\Spc_{{\vphantom{\textup{t}}\smash{\textup{Orb}}}\triangleright\textup{Glo}}\to\ul{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}$ preserving the terminal object is an equivalence.
    \begin{proof}
        The topological functor $\ensuremath{c}$ induces a global functor $\smash{{N_\textup{top}}(\textbf{\textup{Top}}^\flat)}\to\smash{{N_\textup{top}}(\cat{$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}^\flat)}$, which by Proposition~(prop:triv-ff of the paper) descends to a fully faithful and levelwise left adjoint functor $\ensuremath{c}\colon\ul{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}\to\ul{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{gl}$. To complete the proof, it will now suffice to show that the essential image of the composite
        \[
            \Psi\colon\ul{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}\xrightarrow{\;\ensuremath{c}\;}\ul{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{gl}\xrightarrow[\smash{\raise3.5pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\sim$}}]{\;\,\Phi\,\;}\ul\Spc_{\textup{Glo}}
        \]
        agrees with $\ul\Spc_{{\vphantom{\textup{t}}\smash{\textup{Orb}}}\triangleright\textup{Glo}}\subset\ul\Spc_{\textup{Glo}}$, where $\Phi$ denotes the unique equivalence.

        To see that $\Psi$ factors through $\ul\Spc_{{\vphantom{\textup{t}}\smash{\textup{Orb}}}\triangleright\textup{Glo}}$, it suffices by Elmendorf's Theorem to show that the left adjoint $\Psi_G\colon{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_G\to\ul\Spc_{\textup{Glo}}(G)$ maps $G/H$ into $\ul\Spc_{{\vphantom{\textup{t}}\smash{\textup{Orb}}}}(G)$ for any compact Lie group $G$ and any closed subgroup $H\subset G$. To this end, let us write $i\colon H\hookrightarrow G$ for the inclusion, so that $\ensuremath{c}(G/H)\simeq\textbf{\textup{L}}i_!\ensuremath{c}(1_H)$ by Proposition~(prop:quotient-we-global of the paper) and hence $\Psi_G(G/H)=\Phi_G\textbf{\textup{L}}i_!\ensuremath{c}(1_H)=i_!\Phi_H\ensuremath{c}(1)=i_!1\in\ul\Spc_{{\vphantom{\textup{t}}\smash{\textup{Orb}}}\triangleright\textup{Glo}}(G)$.

        For the converse, note that $\ul\Spc_{{\vphantom{\textup{t}}\smash{\textup{Orb}}}}(\mathbb B{G})\simeq\PSh({\vphantom{\textup{t}}\smash{\textup{Orb}}}_{/\mathbb B{G}})$ is generated under ordinary colimits by the objects $(i\colon H\hookrightarrow G)=i_!1_H$ for closed subgroups $H\subset G$, so that also $\ul\Spc_{{\vphantom{\textup{t}}\smash{\textup{Orb}}}\triangleright\textup{Glo}}(\mathbb B{G})$ is generated by the objects $i_!1_H$. We have just seen that $\Psi_G(G/H)\simeq i_!1_H$; thus, the essential image of the fully faithful left adjoint $\Psi_G$ contains a set of generators of $\ul\Spc_{{\vphantom{\textup{t}}\smash{\textup{Orb}}}\triangleright\textup{Glo}}(\mathbb B{G})$, so it already has to be all of $\ul\Spc_{{\vphantom{\textup{t}}\smash{\textup{Orb}}}\triangleright\textup{Glo}}(\mathbb B{G})$.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm unstable-equiv-main of arXiv:2608.28504

[Lem denominatorsofwg of arXiv:2412.00593, 'A new approach to strong convergence II.\\The classical ensembles'] For every $\alpha\in \mathrm{S}_L$, there exists
$a_\alpha\in\mathcal{P}$ so that
$$
	\mathrm{Wg}_L(\alpha, N)=\frac{a_\alpha(N)}{N^L
	\prod_{k=1}^L (N^2-k^2)^{\lfloor\frac{L}{k}\rfloor}}
	\quad\text{for all }N>L.
$$

[Definition 10 (The configuration process) of arXiv:2605.02499, '2605.02499'] Let $\gs_0\subseteq[N]$ and fix a root-type configuration $S\in\varSigma_{\gs_0}^R$. The \emph{configuration process}, denoted by
$(\Theta_t(S))_{t\geq 0}$, is constructed on the basis of the transitions of $(\As_{[0,t]}(\gs_0))_{t\geq 0}$ as follows.
The process starts at
$\Theta_0(S)= S$. Suppose that at some time the state of the process is the finite collection of cylinders
$\{C^{(i)}\}_{i=1}^r$ for some $r>0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item At the times of a coalescence or a relocation event $\coal{\alpha}{\beta}$, every cylinder $C^{(i)}$, $i \in [r]$, performs the transition $$C^{(i)}\mapsto\ocoal{\alpha}{\beta}(C^{(i)}),$$
and the new state of the process is the collection $\{\ocoal{\alpha}{\beta}(C^{(i)})\}_{i=1}^r$.
\item At the times of a deleterious mutation $\timesa$, every cylinder $C^{(i)}$, $i \in [r]$, performs the transition $$C^{(i)}\mapsto\omutr{\alpha}(C^{(i)}),$$
and the new state of the process is the collection$\{ \omutr{\alpha}(C^{(i)})\}_{i=1}^r$. 
\item At the times of a beneficial mutation $\circa$, every cylinder $C^{(i)}$, $i \in [r]$, performs the transition $$C^{(i)}\mapsto \omutb{\alpha}(C^{(i)}),$$
and the new state of the process is the collection $\{\omutb{\alpha}(C^{(i)})\}_{i=1}^r$. 
\item At the times of an FTW event $\ftw{\alpha}{\Bs}$, every cylinder $C^{(i)}$, $i \in [r]$, performs the transition $$C^{(i)}\mapsto\oftw{\alpha}{\Bs}(C^{(i)}),$$
and the new state of the process is the collection $ \bigcup_{i=1 }^r \oftw{\alpha}{\Bs}(C^{(i)})$.
\item At the times of an interactive neutral event $\ine{\alpha}{\beta}{\gamma}$, every cylinder $C^{(i)}$, $i \in [r]$, performs the transition
$$C^{(i)}\mapsto\onint{\alpha}{\beta}{\gamma}(C^{(i)}),$$
and the new state of the process is the collection $\bigcup_{i=1 }^r  \onint{\alpha}{\beta}{\gamma}(C^{(i)})$.
\end{enumerate}
By construction, we have
\begin{equation}
\Ss\big(\As_{[0,t]}(\gs_0), S\big)=\bigcup_{C\in\Theta_t(S)} C.    
\end{equation}
title: The configuration process

[Thm 2 of arXiv:2608.27880, 'Precise universal edge asymptotics for planar $\beta=2$ Coulomb gases with radial external'] Under the same assumptions as Theorem \ref{main}, we have the following asymptotic equivalences, classified according to the deviation scale.

(1) Large deviations (fixed displacement). For any fixed $t>t_0$,
\[
\mathbb{P}\bigl( \max_{1\le i\le n}\Re \sigma_i \ge t \bigr)
\sim
\frac{\sqrt{\alpha }\, t^2\, t_0 \exp(-nV(t)+nV(t_0))}{2\pi n(t^2-t_0^2) (tV'(t)-2)^{3/2}}
(\frac{t}{t_0})^{2n}.
\]

(2) Critical Gumbel scale and its refined correction.

(a) Pure Gumbel scale (fixed $t>1$):
\[
\mathbb{P}\bigl( \max_{1\le i\le n}\Re \sigma_i \ge t_0+\frac{t\sqrt{\gamma_n}}{\sqrt{\alpha n}} \bigr)
\sim
t^{-5/2}(\frac{8\pi^4 (\log n)^5}{\alpha n t_0^2 })^{\frac{t^2-1}{4}}.
\]

(b) Fine correction beyond the Gumbel scale ($1\ll v_n\ll \log n$):
\[
\mathbb{P}\bigl( \max_{1\le i\le n}\Re \sigma_i \ge t_0+\frac{\sqrt{\gamma_n}}{\sqrt{\alpha n}}+\frac{v_n}{\sqrt{\alpha n \gamma_n}} \bigr)
\sim
\exp\bigl(-v_n-\frac{v_n^2}{2\gamma_n}\bigr).
\]

(3) Moderate deviations on scale $d_n$. Given $d_n>0$:

\[\aligned
&\quad\mathbb{P}\bigl(\max_{1\le i\le n}\Re\sigma_i \ge t_0 + d_n \bigr)\\
&
\sim
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{t_0}}{4\pi \alpha n d_n^{5/2}}
\exp(-\frac{\alpha  n d_n^2}{2}), & \frac{\sqrt{\log n}}{\sqrt{n}} \ll d_n \ll n^{-\frac13},\\[1.2em]
\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{t_0} \exp(-nV(t_0+d_n)+nV(t_0))}{4\pi \alpha n d_n^{5/2}}
(\frac{t_0+ d_n}{t_0})^{2n}, & n^{-\frac13}\lesssim d_n\ll 1.
\end{cases}
\endaligned\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 2 of arXiv:2608.27880

[Thm 3 (Deya, Norredine, Nourdin, \cite{MR3089666}) of arXiv:2511.20875, 'Double $q$-Wigner Chaos and the Fourth Moment'] Let $f_k$ be a sequence of {\bf fully} symmetric functions in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^n_+)$ with $\|f_k\|_2\to 1$ as $k\to\infty$.  Then the following three conditions are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $\displaystyle{\lim_{k\to\infty}\tau_q[I_q(f_k)^4] = 2+q^{n^2}}$.
    \item $\displaystyle{\lim_{k\to\infty} f_k \overset{p}{\frown} f_k = 0}$ in $L^2(\mathbb{R}_+^{2(n-p)})$ for $p=1,\ldots,n-1$.
    \item The sequence $(I_q(f_k))_{k\in\N}$ converges in $\ast$-distribution to a $q^{n^2}$-Gaussian random variable.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theo 14 of arXiv:2609.02261, 'Quantization and process'] Let  $\Phi$ be a function on $\R^{4n}$ 
  written as  $\Phi = \Phi _1  +  \Phi _2 $.  
 Suppose that  the function $\Phi_1 $ is the symbol of a bounded operator in  $L^{\infty } (\R^{4n} )$  commuting with  translations. 
Assume that the function $\Phi_2 \in C^{\infty } (\R^{4n} )$ and that, for any $\alpha\in \N^{4n}$,
   there exists a real number $A_{\alpha }$ such that, for every  $u\in\R^{4n}$,
  
   \be | \partial ^{\alpha }\Phi_2 (u) | \leq A_{\alpha } (|u|^2 +1).
  \ee
  
Also suppose that there exists $m  \in \R$  such that,  for any $u\in\R^{4n}$ large enough,
  
      \be  {\rm Re} \,\Phi_2 (u) \leq  m |u|^2 .\ee
   
  
   
Set  $\lambda >0 $ and  $\mu >0$ satisfying,
   
   \be   m < \lambda,\quad 
   0 < \mu <  4 ( \lambda -m) . \ee 
   
Then, there exists an operator  $T$ bounded from $ D_{\lambda h}(\R^{4n})$ 
  into $ D_{\mu h}(\R^{4n})$ which is commuting with  translations and with  symbol equals to
  $e^{h \Phi (u) }$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 5 (True risk) of arXiv:2608.30246, '2608.30246'] Let $X$ be a Polish space, let $\cC$ be a Borel concept
  class on $X$, and let $L=(L_n)_{n\geq1}$ be a learning rule for $\cC$.
  The \emph{true risk} of $L$ with respect to $C\in\cC$, a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $X$, and $n\geq1$ is the function $r_{C,\mu,n}:X^n\to[0,1]$ defined by
  \[
    r_{C,\mu,n}(s)
      =\mu\bigl(L_n(S_C(s))\mathbin\triangle C\bigr),
  \]
  where $s\in X^n$ and $\mathbin\triangle$ denotes the symmetric difference
  of sets.
  For each $\varepsilon>0$, $n\geq1$, $C\in\cC$, and Borel
  probability measure $\mu$ on $X$, the \emph{bad-sample event} at accuracy
  $\varepsilon$ is
  \[
    B_{C,\mu,n}(\varepsilon)
    =\{s\in X^n:r_{C,\mu,n}(s)>\varepsilon\}.
  \]
title: True risk

body: [Prop hpc13 of arXiv:2412.09535, 'Local limit theorem for joint subgraph counts'] A positive integer $n \geq 5$ is $(\frac{1}{3}, +)$-HPC if and only if it is $(\frac{2}{3}, -)$-HPC, which occurs if and only if $3^9 \mid n$ or $3^{10} \mid n-2$. A positive integer $n \geq 5$ is $(\frac{1}{3}, -)$-HPC if and only if it is $(\frac{2}{3}, +)$-HPC, which occurs if and only if $3^{10} \mid n-1$ or $3^{10} \mid n-2$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 9 (Poisson-type concentration of roots) of arXiv:2607.13210, 'Punctured Wilson--Evolving Sets and Root Identities for Massive Kirchhoff Forests'] For $U\subset V$, let $\mu_q(U):=\sum_{x\in U}\beta_q(x).$\\
For every family $(s_x)_{x\in U}$ of non-negative numbers, we have:
\begin{equation*}
  \Ee\left[
    \prod_{x\in U}\left(1+s_x\1_{\{x\in\Root\}}\right)
  \right]
  \leq
  \prod_{x\in U}(1+s_x\beta_q(x)).
\end{equation*}
Consequently, for every $\theta\geq0$, it results:
\begin{equation}
  \Ee[e^{\theta N_q(U)}]
  \leq
  \prod_{x\in U}\left(1+\beta_q(x)(e^\theta-1)\right)
  \leq
  \exp\left(\mu_q(U)(e^\theta-1)\right).
\end{equation}
For every $\delta>0$, one finds:
\begin{equation}
  \Pp\left(N_q(U)\geq(1+\delta)\mu_q(U)\right)
  \leq
  \exp\left[-\mu_q(U)
  \bigl((1+\delta)\log(1+\delta)-\delta\bigr)\right].
\end{equation}
Moreover, one gets:
\begin{equation*}
  \Ee[(N_q(U))_k]
  \leq
  k!\,e_k\bigl((\beta_q(x))_{x\in U}\bigr)
  \leq\mu_q(U)^k.
\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Poisson-type concentration of roots

[Lemma 22 of arXiv:2608.21995, '2608.21995'] Consider an \textsc{VarDE--MCTS} process. Fix a depth $t\in\{1,\dots,H\}$ and a node $s_t\in\mathcal{S}$.
If for every successor state $s_{t+1} \in \cup_{a\in\mathcal{A}(s_t)} \mathcal{S}(s_t,a)$ and every fixed $\varepsilon_{s_{t+1}}>0$, there exist constants $C_{s_{t+1}}>0$ and $k_{s_{t+1}}(\varepsilon_{s_{t+1}})>0$ such that
\[
\Pr\!\Big(\big|\hat V(s_{t+1})-V^*(s_{t+1})\big|>\varepsilon_{s_{t+1}}\Big)
\;\le\;
C_{s_{t+1}}\exp\!\Big(-k_{s_{t+1}}(\varepsilon_{s_{t+1}})\,\varepsilon_{s_{t+1}}^{2}\,N(s_{t+1})\Big),
\]
then, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, there exist constants $C>0$ and $k_\varepsilon>0$ such that
\[
\Pr\!\Big(\big|\hat V(s_t)-V^*(s_t)\big|>\varepsilon\Big)
\;\le\;
C\exp\!\Big(-k_\varepsilon\,\varepsilon^{2}\,N(s_t)\Big).
\]

[Theorem thm:reverse of arXiv:2510.22778, 'Free denoising diffusion models'] Let $(X_{t})_{t\in[0,T]}$ solve (equation eq:forward of the paper) and let $\varepsilon\in(0,T)$. On
$[0,T-\varepsilon]$ set $Y_{s}:=X_{T-s}$. Then there exists a free Brownian motion
$(\bar S_{s})$, adapted to the filtration generated by $(Y_{r})_{r\le s}$, such that
\begin{equation}
  \mathrm{d} Y_{s}=\Big(\tfrac12\beta(T-s)\,Y_{s}-\beta(T-s)\,\xi_{\mu_{T-s}}(Y_{s})\Big)\mathrm{d} s
  +\sqrt{\beta(T-s)}\;\mathrm{d}\bar S_{s},
\end{equation}
where $\xi_{\mu_{t}}=2H\mu_{t}$ is well defined in $L^{2}$ for $t\ge\varepsilon$ by
Lemma~(lem:regularise of the paper). The spectral law of $Y_{s}$ is $\mu_{T-s}$; in particular
$\mu_{Y_{T-\varepsilon}}=\mu_{\varepsilon}\to\mu_{0}$ weakly as
$\varepsilon\downarrow0$.

[Theorem th:ERA of arXiv:2510.10299, '\Large Sparse graphs and their Benjamini-Schramm limits: a spectral tour'] Let $d > 0$, $G$ be an Erd\H{o}s–Rényi graph on $n$ vertices and edge probability $\min(1,d/n)$. Let $\mu_1 \geq  \mu_2  \ldots   \geq \mu_n$ be the eigenvalues of its adjacency operator $A$. Then, for any $\epsilon \in (0,1)$, with probability tending to one as $n \to \infty$, for all $1 \leq k \leq n^{1-\epsilon}$, we have
$$
 \ABS{ \mu_k - \sqrt{d_k} } \leq  \epsilon \sqrt{d_1} \quad \hbox{ and } \quad   \ABS{ \mu_{n+1-k} + \sqrt{d_k} }  \leq \epsilon \sqrt{d_1},
$$ 
where $d_1 \geq d_2 \geq \cdots$ is the ordered degree sequence of $G$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem th:ERA of arXiv:2510.10299

Let X be a normed vector space over R or C. The closed unit ball B of the dual space X^* is COMPACT in the weak-* topology, that is the topology of pointwise convergence on X. Two refinements matter. (a) If X is SEPARABLE then the weak-* topology restricted to B is metrizable and B is weak-* SEQUENTIALLY compact, so bounded sequences of functionals have weak-* convergent subsequences; without separability compactness need not give sequential compactness. (b) The general theorem uses Tychonoff's theorem for a product of compact scalar discs and therefore, in ZF, is not provable without some choice; the separable case needs only a diagonal argument. The theorem does NOT say the ball is norm-compact: by Riesz's lemma the closed unit ball of a normed space is norm-compact if and only if the space is finite-dimensional. Nor does it say the ball of X itself is weakly compact - that characterises reflexivity (Kakutani). [standard; e.g. Rudin, Functional Analysis, 2nd ed., Theorem 3.15]

For every neighborhood U of 0 in X, its polar U^circ = {phi in X^*: |phi(u)| <= 1 for every u in U} is weak-* compact. Here X^* is the continuous dual and the weak-* topology is pointwise convergence on X; neither completeness nor separability of X is needed.
X a normed space; no completeness of X is needed
for metrizability and sequential compactness of the ball: X separable
Tychonoff (hence a form of the axiom of choice) in the general case

body: Every n by n complex matrix A can be written as A = U P, where U is unitary and P is positive semidefinite Hermitian, specifically P = (A* A)^{1/2}. If A is invertible, this decomposition is unique and P is positive definite. The analogous statement holds for real matrices with U orthogonal and P symmetric positive semidefinite. [standard, e.g. Horn and Johnson, Matrix Analysis]

[Lemma 20 of arXiv:2512.19517, 'Spiking and Resetting'] Suppose $(h^\varepsilon)_{\varepsilon>0}$ and $h$ are non-negative continuous non-increasing functions from $[0,\infty)$ into $\mathbb R$ uniformly bounded by a constant $M>0$. If
\[
\forall \sigma>0, \quad \lim_{\varepsilon \to 0} \int_0^\infty e^{-\sigma s} h^\varepsilon (s) \, ds = \int_0^\infty e^{-\sigma s} h (s) \, ds \ ,
\]
then $(h^\varepsilon)_{\varepsilon> 0}$ converges to $h$ uniformly on compact subsets of $[0,\infty)$.

body: Events A_1, ..., A_n are independent if for every subset S of indices, P(intersection of A_i for i in S) = product of P(A_i) over i in S. Random variables are independent if the sigma-algebras they generate are independent, equivalently their joint distribution is the product of the marginals. An infinite family is independent if every finite subfamily is.

body:
[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2603.25400, 'One-arm probabilities for the two-dimensional metric-graph and discrete Gaussian free fiel'] Let $h>0$. There is a coupling such that the clusters of loops and excursions (in the union of $\wt\Lc^{1/2}_N$ and $\Xi^h_N$) correspond to the sign clusters of $\mphi_{N}+h$ in the following way. 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item The zero set of $\mphi_{N}+h$ is exactly the set of vertices not visited by any loop or excursion. 
        \item $\wt\A^{-h}_N$ is the set of vertices that can be connected to $\partial\wt B_{N+1}$ via a continuous path in $\wt E^{\ge-h}_N$.
        \item For those clusters that contain no excursion, each has equal probability to be a cluster in $\wt E_N^{>-h}$ or $\wt E_N^{<-h}$, which does not intersect $\partial\wt B_{N+1}$.
    \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 11 of arXiv:2603.25400

body:
[Lemma mainlemma of arXiv:2508.02416, 'On the surjectivity of the conditional expectation\\ given a real random variable'] Let \( A  \in \mathcal{B}([0,1]) \). There exists a Borel set \(\widehat{A} \subset A\), a non-negative measurable function \(g_{\widehat{A}} \), and \(m\ge 3\) such that
\begin{itemize}\small
    \item[(i)] \(\lambda(\widehat{A}) \ge \frac{1}{80}\,\lambda(A),\)
    \item[(ii)] \(\mu(dx)\text{-a.e.,}\quad \int_{y \in \mathbb{R}} g_{\widehat{A}} (y)\,\pi_{X=x}(dy) = \mathbf{1}_{\widehat{A}}(x),\)
    \item[(iii)] \(\{y \in \mathbb{R} : g_{\widehat{A}} (y) > 0\} \subset \left[2^{-m} - 4^{-(m+1)},\, 2^{-m} - 4^{-(2m+1)}\right].\)
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma mainlemma of arXiv:2508.02416

body: Let N = 2n with n >= 4 and 1 = lambda_1 = lambda_2 < lambda_3 = lambda_4 < ... < lambda_{N-1} = lambda_N, write |x|^2 = sum_l x_l^2, |x|_{-1}^2 = sum_l x_l^2/lambda_l, mu_i = lambda_{2i} (1 <= i <= n) and C = {(u,v): 0 <= v <= u <= lambda_N v}. The functions q_l on C, regular versions of the conditional expectations under the Gaussian measure mu of x_l^2 given |x|^2 = u and |x|_{-1}^2 = v, satisfy u = sum_l q_l(u,v) and v = sum_l q_l(u,v)/lambda_l on C, and q_{2i} = q_{2i-1}; write qhat_i = q_{2i} + q_{2i-1}. body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, Entropy and singularity of spectral and pivotal sets in planar percolation (arXiv:2609.15388, September 2026) proves that for crossings of critical bond percolation on the square lattice, and of site percolation on the triangular lattice with critical or inhomogeneous near-critical parameters, the Shannon entropies of the spectral sample and of the pivotal set are both comparable to the total influence, of order R^2 alpha_4(R). This answers Question 1 in Section 11 of C. Garban, G. Pete and O. Schramm, The Fourier spectrum of critical percolation (Acta Math. 205, 2010, 19-104), and proves both bounds of Conjecture 8 in G. Kalai, Three puzzles on mathematics, computation, and games (Proc. ICM 2018), for these crossings; the spectral bound is the percolation case of the Friedgut-Kalai Fourier entropy-influence conjecture. For critical triangular-site square crossings the two laws are asymptotically mutually singular. Paper: https://github.com/yspennstate/percolation-crossing-entropy (commit 29a39246dc9c); ResearchGate record 414266816. Not refereed.
title: Garban-Pete-Schramm Section 11 Question 1 answered and Kalai's Conjecture 8 (ICM 2018) proved for planar percolation crossings: entropy of the spectral sample and the pivotal set (Shmalo 2026, arXiv:2609.15388, repository yspennstate/percolation-crossing-entropy)

body:
[Lemma eq:dpi_InfEps of arXiv:2512.20338, 'Up-down chains and scaling limits: \\ application to permuton- and graphon-valued diffusio'] For any permuton $\mu$, pattern $\pi$ of size $k \ge 1$, and $ \varepsilon $ in $[0,1]$, we have
  \begin{multline}
  \mathbb E\Big[ d _\pi^o \big( \textrm{Inf}^{\,  \varepsilon }(\mu) \big) \Big]
  = (1- \varepsilon )^{k}  d _\pi^o(\mu)
  + p \sum_{m \ge 1} \binom{k}{m} \frac{(1- \varepsilon )^{k-m}  \varepsilon ^m}{k-m+1} \left( \sum_{(\tau,i) \in \mathcal I_m(\pi)}  d _\tau^o(\mu)  \right)\\
  + (1-p) \sum_{m \ge 1} \binom{k}{m} \frac{(1- \varepsilon )^{k-m}  \varepsilon ^m}{k-m+1} \left( \sum_{(\tau,i) \in {\mathcal D}_m(\pi)}  d _\tau^o(\mu)  \right).
\end{multline}

[Thm t:harveylawson of arXiv:2607.24640, 'The Yang-Mills measure on surfaces via Morse theory'] Let $f:\Sigma\rightarrow \mathbb{R} $ be a $\mathcal{C}^\infty$ perfect Morse function and let $h_f$ be a $\mathcal{C}^\infty$ locally flat metric. Suppose that $(f,h_f)$ has the Morse-Smale property. Then, there exists $N_0\geq 1$ such that, for every $0\leq k\leq 2$, for every $0<\beta<1$ and for every $\psi\in\Omega^k(\Sigma)$, 
 $$
 \forall t\geq 0,\quad \varphi^{-t*}_f(\psi)=\sum_{a:\operatorname{ind}(a)=k}\left(\int_{W^s(a)}\psi\right)[W^u(a)]+\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{D}^\prime}(e^{-t\beta}),
 $$
 where the constant in the remainder depends only on $\beta$ and $\|\psi\|_{\mathcal{C}^{N_0}}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Harvey-Lawson, Dang-Rivi\`ere

body:
[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2608.31070, 'Sub-Laplacians on Compact Lie Groups: Heat Kernels, Distance, and Zeta Determinants'] For every compact connected two-step pair there are $c>0$ and $N\ge0$ such that, as $t\downarrow0$,
		\[
		p_t(e)=C_{G,L}t^{-Q/2}e^{\beta_{G,L}t}
		+O(t^{-N}e^{-c/t}).
		\]
		Moreover, with the orthonormal bases $Y_a$ of $\lLie$ and $X_i$ of $\pLie$ fixed in \Cref{sec:preliminaries}, and with all norms induced by the fixed invariant inner product,
		\[
		\beta_{G,L}
		=\frac{\operatorname{Scal}_G-\operatorname{Scal}_L}{6}
		=\frac1{12}\sum_{a,i}|[Y_a,X_i]|^2
		+\frac1{24}\sum_{i,j}|[X_i,X_j]|^2,
		\]
		and $C_{G,L}$ admits the root-theoretic integral and the absolutely convergent positive multiple Dirichlet series of \Cref{zeta:complete-local-constants}. Consequently the formulas determine every local heat coefficient, every zeta residue, and every nonpositive zeta value. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition 4 (Upper and lower Minkowski content) of arXiv:2605.18198, 'Large deviations of crowding in finite $\beta$-ensembles'] Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ and let $0\le d\le n$ be an integer. Denote
	\(
	A_r:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\operatorname{dist}(x,A)<r\}
	\), the $r$-neighbourhood of $A$.
	The $d$--dimensional upper Minkowski content of $A$ is defined as
	\[
	\mathcal M^{*d}(A)
	=
	\limsup_{r\downarrow 0}
	\frac{m(A_r)}{\alpha(n-d)\,r^{\,n-d}},
	\]
	and the $d$--dimensional lower Minkowski content is defined as
	\[
	\mathcal M_{*}^{d}(A)
	=
	\liminf_{r\downarrow 0}
	\frac{m(A_r)}{\alpha(n-d)\,r^{\,n-d}},
	\]
	where $\alpha(k)$ denotes the Lebesgue measure of the unit ball in
	$\mathbb{R}^k$. If $	\mathcal M^{*d}(A)=\mathcal M_{*}^{d}(A)$, then the common value is called
	the $d$--dimensional Minkowski content of $A$ and is denoted by
	$\mathcal M^{d}(A)$.
title: Upper and lower Minkowski content

body:
[Prop CG1P3.1 of arXiv:2606.11043, 'Thick points under Gaussian free field dynamics'] Consider $u_{\varepsilon, y}(x,t)=\mathbb E[\Psi_{\varepsilon}(y)\Psi_{\varepsilon}(x,t)]$. Then, there are $c<C\in \mathbb R$, such that
    \begin{equation*}
        c+ \ln\left (\frac{1}{|x-y|\lor \sqrt{|t|}\lor \varepsilon}\right ) 
        \leq 
        u_{\varepsilon, y}(x,t)
        \leq 
        C+ \ln\left(\frac{1}{|x-y|\lor \sqrt{|t|}\lor \varepsilon}\right).
    \end{equation*}
    The upper bound is uniformly on $\varepsilon,t,x,y $, meanwhile the lower bound depends on the distance of the boundary of $x$ and $y$.

[Lemma 15 of arXiv:2604.20631, 'The Ising Model on a Two-Community Stochastic Block Model'] For $np \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$, the two following statements hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] For all $\sigma \in \mathcal{X}_n$,
$$ 
\E[T(\sigma)] = 
e^{- \frac{\beta^2}{8} (1+\alpha_n^2)-\frac{\beta}{2} + \left(\frac{\beta}{2}n+O\left(\frac{1}{np^2}\right)\right) E_{\alpha_n}(\bm^{(n)}(\s)) +O \left ( \frac{1}{n}\right )},
$$
where $E_{\alpha_n}(\bm)$ is defined in \eqref{def:hamiltonian_CW_magnet}.
\item[(ii)] For all $\sigma, \tau \in \mathcal{X}_n$,
\[
\begin{split}
\E[T(\sigma)T(\tau)] 
= &\, e^{- \frac{\beta^2}{4} (1+\alpha_n^2) -\beta
 + \left(\frac{\beta}{2}n+O\left(\frac{1}{np^2}\right)\right)
\Big( E_{\alpha_n} (\bm^{(n)}(\sigma)) +E_{\alpha_n}(\bm^{(n)}(\tau)) \Big)}\\
& \cdot e^{ O\left(\frac{1}{p}\right) E_{\alpha_n} (\bm^{(n)}(\sigma\tau))+ O \left ( \frac{1}{n}\right)}\,,
\end{split}
\]
where $\sigma \tau$ is the configuration obtained by multiplying the spins of $\sigma$ and $\tau$ component-wise, that is for each 
$i \in V$ we have $(\sigma \tau)_i=\sigma_i \tau_i$.
\end{itemize}
