[Proposition 52 of arXiv:2608.26823, 'Evolutes, involutes and parallels of Legendre curves in hyperbolic and de Sitter 2-spaces '] Suppose that
there exists  $\widetilde{\varphi}:I\rightarrow\R$ such that $m_T(t)\cos\widetilde{\varphi}(t)+ n_T(t)\sin\widetilde{\varphi}(t)=0$ for all $t\in I$.  Let $\widetilde{\bmu}_{DE}(\bgamma_T,\bgamma_T^d)= \widetilde{DE}(\bgamma_T,\bgamma_T^d)\wedge \widetilde{\bnu}_{DE}(\bgamma_T,\bgamma_T^d)$ and denote the moving frame of $\widetilde{DE}(\bgamma_T,\bgamma_T^d)$ by $ ( \widetilde{DE}, \widetilde{\bmu}_{DE},\widetilde{\bnu}_{DE}   ) (\bgamma_T,\bgamma_T^d)$.  Then  
$$( \widetilde{DE}, \widetilde{\bmu}_{DE},\widetilde{\bnu}_{DE} )^T(\bgamma_T,\bgamma_T^d) =\overline{R}(-\widetilde{\varphi} ) ( \bgamma_T,   \bgamma_T^d ,\bgamma_T^h  )^T .$$
That is,  $(\widetilde{DE}(\bgamma_T,\bgamma_T^d)(t), \widetilde{\bmu}_{DE}(\bgamma_T,\bgamma_T^d)(t),\widetilde{\bnu}_{DE}(\bgamma_T,\bgamma_T^d)(t))$ is obtained by applying a  rotation with angle $-\widetilde{\varphi}(t)$   to  $ (\bgamma_T(t),   \bgamma_T^d (t),\bgamma_T^h(t) )$ for all $t\in I$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm: rescale fdd of arXiv:2505.05921, 'Limit Theorems for step reinforced random walks\\ with regularly varying memory'] Let $\{S_n\}_{n\geq 0}$ be the SRRW-RVM with zero mean, unit variance innovation sequence $\{\xi_n\}$, the memory sequence $\mu_n = n^\gamma (\log n)^{-(\gamma+1)}$ and the recollection probability $p=p_c$. Then, we have
    \[
    \left(\frac{S_{\floor{n^{t}}}}{\sqrt{n^{t}\log n\log\log n}} : t> 0 \right) \to_{\rm{fdd}} \left( (2\gamma+1) \sqrt{t} Z: t> 0 \right), \quad \text{and} \]
    \[
    \left(\frac{S_{\lfloor \exp\left( (\log n)^t\right)\rfloor}}{\sqrt{\exp\left( (\log n)^t \right) (\log n)^t \log \log n}}  : t> 0 \right) \to_{\rm{fdd}} \left( (2\gamma+1) B(t): t> 0 \right).
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary cor:cauchy of arXiv:2605.26688, 'Absolute moment inequalities under quadratic-form positivity'] Let \((X,Y)\) have either the joint probability mass function (equation eq:cauchy-discrete of the paper) or the joint density function (equation eq:cauchy-density of the paper). Assume that \(0<r<2\) and \(\mathbb{E}\left\lvert X\right\rvert^{r}<\infty\). Then
\[
   \mathbb{E}\left\lvert X+Y\right\rvert^{r}\ge \mathbb{E}\left\lvert X-Y\right\rvert^{r}.
\]
Consequently, the open question posed by [ZhuangHu2026] is proved.

body:
Let $A$ be measurable and uniformly parabolic with constants $\lambda,\Lambda$ and let $u\ge0$ be a local weak solution of $\partial_tu=\mathrm{div}(A\nabla u)$ in $B_{2r}(x_0)\times(t_0-4r^2,t_0)$. Set $Q^-=B_r(x_0)\times(t_0-3r^2,t_0-2r^2)$ and $Q^+=B_r(x_0)\times(t_0-r^2,t_0)$. Then $\sup_{Q^-}u\ \le\ C\,\inf_{Q^+}u$ with $C=C(n,\lambda,\Lambda)$. The time lag is essential and so is the direction: the past cylinder's supremum is controlled by the future cylinder's infimum, never the reverse, and no inequality of this form holds on a single time slice. Nonnegativity on the whole cylinder $B_{2r}\times(t_0-4r^2,t_0)$ is required. Consequences: interior Holder continuity of solutions, the near-diagonal lower bound for the fundamental solution, and (through chaining) Aronson's Gaussian lower bound; the inequality is equivalent to the conjunction of the volume doubling property and a Poincare inequality in the Grigor'yan-Saloff-Coste characterization on manifolds and graphs.
A measurable, uniformly parabolic with constants lambda, Lambda; divergence form
u >= 0 and a local weak solution on the whole cylinder B_{2r} x (t_0 - 4r^2, t_0)
the two cylinders are separated in time, with Q^- earlier than Q^+

[Definition 1 of arXiv:2603.13798, 'Iterated Graph Systems (I): random walks and diffusion limits'] See Figure~\ref{fig:canonical_xi} and Figure~\ref{fig:two_colour} for examples.

An \emph{Edge Iterated Graph System} is a triple
\[
   \mathscr I=(\Xi^{0},\mathcal R,\mathcal S)
\]
specified as follows.
Let $K\in\mathbb N$ be the number of edge colours.
For every graph $G$ that appears in the construction, let
$
   \mathscr{C} : E(G) \longrightarrow[K]
$
be a colour map.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Initial graph.}
      $\Xi^{0}$ is an edge-coloured finite directed graph.
      If $\Xi^{0}$ is just an edge, we denote its two vertices by $\mathfrak v_+$ and $\mathfrak v_-$.
      In particular, $\Xi_{\iota}^0$ denotes the special case that the initial graph is just one $\iota$-coloured directed edge.
      In this paper, $\iota$ always represents the colour of the initial graph if it only contains one edge or one vertex.

\item \textbf{Rule graphs.}
      $\mathcal{R} = \{ R_i \}_{i=1}^{K}$ is a family of finite directed graphs.
      Each $R_i$ contains two \emph{planting vertices}
      \[
         \beta_i^{+},\beta_i^{-} \in  V(R_i)
         \quad\&\quad
         \beta_i^{+}\neq\beta_i^{-}.
      \]
      Every edge of $R_i$ is coloured by the same map $\mathscr{C}$.

\item \textbf{Substitution operator.}
      For an edge $e=(a,b)\in E(G)$, the operator
      $
         \mathcal S\colon e\longmapsto R_{\mathscr{C}(e)}  \ \big|\
         a\equiv\beta_i^{+},\ b\equiv\beta_i^{-}
      $
      replaces $e$ by a \emph{fresh copy} of the rule graph $R_i$ where \(i=\mathscr C(e)\), identifying
      $
         a\equiv\beta_i^{+}
      $ and
      $
         b\equiv\beta_i^{-}.
      $
      All arcs are substituted \emph{simultaneously in parallel} at each step.
      Vertices are identified only at the planting vertices of their respective copies, and no further identifications are made.

\item \textbf{Iteration.}
      Set $\Xi^{n+1}:=\mathcal S(\Xi^{n})$ for $n\ge 0$; explicitly
      \[
         \Xi^{n+1}
         =
         \bigcup_{e\in E(\Xi^{n})}\mathcal S(e),
      \]
      where the union is taken with the vertex identifications described above.
      The sequence $(\Xi^{n})_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is called the \emph{EIGS substitution networks}.
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2603.13798

[Corr FRSB of arXiv:2605.05631, 'Wandering Exponents and the Free Energy of the High-Dimensional Elastic Polymer'] Consider the model $B(x)=(1+x)^{-\gamma}$ for $\gamma<1$ at some fixed $(\beta,t)$. The Larkin mass $\mu_{Lar}(\beta;t)$ exists and is given by the unique $\mu$ which solves the equation
		\[2\gamma(\gamma+1)\left(1+\frac{2}{\beta \sqrt{\mu t}}\right)^{-\gamma-2}=\sqrt{\mu^3t}.\] 
		For all $\mu\ge \mu_{Lar}(\beta;t)$ the model is RS, and for all $\mu<\mu_{Lar}(\beta;t)$ the model is FRSB.\\
		
		\noindent Moreover, in the FRSB case, the Parisi pair, $(q_c,\zeta_c)$, in Theorem (theorem:intro:1-d continuum T>0:FRSB of the paper) may be found explicitly. The value for the unique triple $(q_0,q_*,q_c)$ immediately follows from the equations
		\[q_c-q_0=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{c_0}{\mu^{\frac{3}{2(2+\gamma)}}}-1\right),\;\;\; q_0=c_1\mu^{\frac{3(\gamma+1)}{2(2+\gamma)}+3},\;\;\; q_c-q_*=\frac{1}{\beta\sqrt{\mu_{Lar}(\beta;t)t}}, \]
		with constants given by $c_0=(\frac{2\gamma(\gamma+1)}{\sqrt{t}})^{1/(\gamma+2)}$ and $c_1=\frac{\gamma t}{c_0^{1+\gamma}}$. The measure $\zeta$ can then be found from its CDF, which is given for $s\in [q_0,q_*)$ by 
		\[\zeta_c([0,s])=\frac{\gamma+2}{3\beta}\left(\frac{4}{t\gamma(\gamma+1)}\right)^{1/3}(1+2q_c-2s)^{\frac{\gamma-1}{3}}, \]
		and otherwise by $\zeta_c([0,s])=0$ if $s\in [0,q_0)$ and $\zeta_c([0,s])=1$ if $s\in [q_*,q_c]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The orthogonal polynomials for $L^2(\mathbb R)$, with scalar product
$$<f,g>=\int_0^\infty f(x)g(x)e^{-x^2}\,dx$$
are the Hermite polynomials $\{P_k\}$, satisfying the following differential equation,
$$P_k''(x)-2xP_k'(x)+P_k(x)=0$$
as well as the following order $2$ recurrence relation,
$$P_{k+1}(x)=2xP_k(x)-2kP_{k-1}(x)$$
and which are given by the following formula,
$$P_k(x)=(-1)^k e^{x^2}\cdot\frac{d^k}{dx^k}\big(e^{-x^2}\big)$$
called Rodrigues formula for the Hermite polynomials.
title: Unnumbered theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'

[Proposition prop:CSPI of arXiv:2509.04155, 'An Approach to Sub-Gaussian Heat Kernel Estimates via Analysis on Metric Spaces'] Let $p^* \in (p,\infty]$ be given by
    \[
    p^* := 
    \begin{cases}
        pQ_U/(Q_U - \beta_L) & \text{ if } \beta_L < Q_U\\
        \infty & \text{ if } \beta_L \geq Q_U.

Let \(\{X_t\}_{t\in\mathbb Z}\) be a stationary Markov chain. Let \(2\le m\le k\) and let $h\in \mathcal I_m$.
Define
\[
\widehat{h}_{m,k}(x_1,\ldots,x_k)
=
\sum_{i=1}^{k-m+1}
h(x_i,\ldots,x_{i+m-1}).
\]
For this function the Green--Kubo series is finite, and
\[
B_k \widehat{h}_{m,k}=(k-m+1) \widehat{h}_{m,k}.

body: [Lemma compatible sequence of arXiv:2605.03151, 'Giants through Higher-Order paths in Random Simplicial Complexes'] Let $\left( (X_r, \sigma_r) \right)_{r \geq 0}$ be a sequence of $(k+1)$-connected $k$-rooted simplicial complexes locally finite above dimension $k$. Moreover, $(X, \sigma)$ is unique up to isomorphisms.

[Lemma lemm_gaussian of arXiv:2503.24372, 'A criterion on the free energy for log-Sobolev inequalities in mean-field particle systems'] For any $G:(\R^{d})^N\to\R_+$ and $\Phi:\bbH\to\R_+$,

\begin{equation}
\E_{\nu^r_T}\Big[ \Phi(\psi)\E_{\mu^{N,\psi}_T}[G(x)]\Big]
=
\E_{m^{N}_T}\Big[G(x)\,  \E_{\gamma^{\bbH,x}_{T/N}}[\Phi(\psi)]\Big]
,
\end{equation}

where $\gamma^{\bbH,x}_{T/N}$ is the Gaussian measure on $\bbH$ with variance $T/N$ (as in (equation eq: Gaussian H of the paper)) and mean 
$\big( \frac{1}{N}\sum_i n_k(x_i) \big)_{k \geq -d}$.

body: Let 1 <= p < infinity and let Omega be a bounded connected open subset of R^n with Lipschitz boundary. Poincare-Wirtinger form: there is a constant C depending only on p and Omega such that ||u - u_Omega||_{L^p(Omega)} <= C ||grad u||_{L^p(Omega)} for every u in W^{1,p}(Omega), where u_Omega denotes the average of u over Omega. Zero-boundary form: for u in W_0^{1,p}(Omega), with Omega merely bounded in one direction, ||u||_{L^p(Omega)} <= C ||grad u||_{L^p(Omega)}, so the gradient term alone is an equivalent norm on W_0^{1,p}(Omega). The inequality says a Sobolev function is controlled by its gradient once its mean (or boundary value) is pinned; it is the engine behind coercivity of variational problems, spectral gaps for the Laplacian, and compactness arguments.
title: Poincare inequality

[Lemma 5 of arXiv:2609.01166, 'Nonparametric inference for density-dependent McKean--Vlasov diffusions'] For every candidate $\xi$, and \(M>v_\star\),
\begin{eqnarray}
 \KL(\pi_0\Vert\pi_\xi)
 &=& (1-\tau_0(M))\KL(\pi_0^M\Vert\pi_\xi^M) + (1-\tau_0(M))\log\frac{1-\tau_0(M)}{1-\tau_\xi(M)} + R_\xi(M)\\
 &\leq& \KL(\pi_0^M\Vert\pi_\xi^M)+d_m(M)+\bar R_m(M),
\end{eqnarray}
where $R_\xi(M):=\int_{A_M^c}\pi_0(x) \log(\pi_0(x)/\pi_\xi(x))\,\dd x$. Moreover, 
\begin{equation}
\KL(\pi_0^M\Vert\pi_\xi^M)
\leq \frac{1}{c_M}\left(
\KL(\pi_0\Vert\pi_\xi)+d_m(M)+\bar R_m(M)
\right)
\end{equation}
with \(c_M:=\int_{A_M} e^{-K(V(x)-v_\star)}\,dx\left(\int_{\R^d} e^{-\kappa(V(x)-v_\star)}\,dx\right)^{-1}\in(0,1)\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:multil of arXiv:2411.10829, 'Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble and its Laplace transform'] Choose $m\in \mathbb N$, $\vec \mathbf k \in \mathbb R^m_+ $, and $\vec \boldsymbol{\tau}\in \mathbb R_{\ge 0}^m$ such that $\boldsymbol{\tau}_1\le \cdots \le \boldsymbol{\tau}_m$, any real $C_1>0$, and a large enough $N\in \mathbb N$. We take the rank $N$ G$\beta$E corners process $\{y^n_i\}_{1\leq i\leq n\leq N}$, with variance $\tau=2N/\beta$; and $\vec k \in \mathbb Z^m$, and integers $N\ge N_1\ge \cdots \ge N_m$,  such that
\begin{equation} 
|k_\ell-\mathbf k_\ell N^{2/3}|<C_1, \qquad  |N - \boldsymbol{\tau}_\ell N^{2/3}-N_\ell|<C_1, \qquad \text{for each }\ell\in\llbracket 1,m\rrbracket.
\end{equation}
Then as $N\to\infty$, uniformly over the ($N$--dependent) choices of $\vec k$ and $\vec N$ satisfying (equation eq_x1 of the paper):
\[
 \mathbb E \left[ \prod_{\ell=1}^m \left(\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^{N_\ell} \left(\frac{y^{N_\ell}_i}{2\sqrt{N_\ell N}}\right)^{k_\ell}+\left(\frac{y^{N_\ell}_i}{2\sqrt{N_\ell N}}\right)^{k_\ell+1}\right) \right]\to \mathbf L_\beta(\vec \mathbf k, \vec\boldsymbol{\tau}).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Hanin-Nica, Finite Depth and Width Corrections to the Neural Tangent Kernel, arXiv1909.05989v1, Section2 and Theorem1 (PDFp4), is a source for initialization moments of the diagonal NTK of a fully connected ReLU network. Its setting uses a scalar output, zero-initialized but trainable biases, independent identically distributed raw weights with a Lebesgue density, symmetry about zero, variance one and finite fourth moment. Its Theorem1 gives an exact first-moment formula and a two-sided comparison for the second moment, including an exponential factor in a sum of inverse widths and a multiplicative error involving a sum of inverse squared widths. A comparison E[K^2] comparable to (E[K])^2 exp(5 beta) does not by itself establish Var(K)=O(1/n), even if beta tends to zero: the unspecified comparison constants prevent subtracting (E[K])^2 to obtain that rate. This comparison is also not a quantitative theorem for arbitrary smooth activations or transposed/reused-matrix Tensor Programs. Before using the exact formulas, resolve these printed-v1 conventions: Section2 prose says the output is linear but Eq2 applies ReLU for i=1,...,d; Eq3 prints reciprocal square-root normalization factors; beta is defined by a sum through d while n_d=1 is specified, whereas the equal-hidden-width consequence writes beta=d/n. These are unresolved source-interpretation questions, not a refutation of the authors intended theorem. This card records source scope and the limitation of a second-moment comparison; it does not assert a corrected NTK theorem or an NTK nonconcentration inference from moments alone.
Source-v1 scope note; intended endpoint and normalization conventions remain for independent source review.

body: Lemma (campaign status: proved): For twelve nonzero coefficients, an affine atom which is not the central atom of twelve equal magnitudes has size at most $792$. Unequal-magnitude case: reorient positively and condition on an unequal pair; its four signed sums are distinct, and the ten-coordinate subsets hitting one of the four required targets form a four-Sperner family, so their total is at most $\binom{10}{5}+2\binom{10}{4}+\binom{10}{3}=252+210+210+120=792$. Equal magnitudes with noncentral target: largest noncentral layer is $\binom{12}{5}=792$. A three-sign affine atom has size three only for three equal magnitudes at a one-minority target; otherwise at most two. Notes: VERIFIED: $252+420+120=792$. Consequence: more than $2592$ joint states forces both own-layer rows to be equimodular, since otherwise the joint count is at most $3\cdot792=2376$ or $2\cdot924=1848$. The four-Sperner step is the reusable device.

body:
[Proposition 46 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] Assume $q\in C([-L,L])$, $q\ge q_0>0$, $a\in C([-L,L])$, $m\ge0$ and $J(0)>0$. Put
\[
T_q=\int_{-L}^{L}\frac{dx}{q(x)},\qquad
A_q=\int_{-L}^{L}\frac{a(x)}{q(x)}\,dx,
\]
and
\[
C_m:=\mathbf 1_{\{m=0\}}
+\frac1{T_q}\left[
2\log\frac{m+1}{T_q}-\log\big(J(0)q(-L)\big)-A_q
\right].
\]
Then
\[
\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,m,L})
=\frac{m+1}{T_q}\log\sigma
+\frac{2}{T_q}\log\log\sigma
+C_m+o(1)
\qquad(\sigma\to+\infty).
\]
In particular, $\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,m,L})\to+\infty$.

	\Phi_{\boldsymbol{w}}(\tfrac{1}{N}).
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition conv of arXiv:2412.06701, 'Matsumoto-Yor processes on Jordan algebras'] Let $T\ge 0$. If $\widetilde{G}_k^n=P(w_1^n)\dots P(w_k^n)$, for $k\ge 0$, then 
 
the sequence of processes 
$$ \widetilde{g}^{(n)} = \left(\widetilde{g}^{(n)}_t := \widetilde{G}_{\lfloor nt\rfloor}^n \ ; \ t\in [0,T] \right), \, n\ge 1, $$ 
converges in law in $\mathcal D([0,T],G)$ equipped with the Skorokhod topology towards the diffusion $(\widetilde{g}_t \ ; \ t \in [0,T])$. Moreover, the sequence of processes $$\left(\Lambda_{\lfloor nt\rfloor}^n,L_{\lfloor nt\rfloor}^n,I_{\lfloor nt\rfloor}^n \ ; \ t\in [0,T]\right), \, n\ge 1,$$ converges in law in $\mathcal D([0,T],E^{\times 3})$ towards $\left(\widetilde\lambda_t,\widetilde\ell_t,\widetilde\iota_t \ ; \ t\in [0,T]\right)$.

body:
If a probability distribution F on R has a symmetric unimodal density, then F is n-completely mixable for every integer n>=2. Thus for each such n there exist X_1,...,X_n with the same marginal law F and with a constant sum almost surely. If the density is symmetric about m, the coupling can be centered at m, so that the sum is n*m. Finite first moments are not required by the statement. Source: Ruodu Wang, Current Open Questions in Complete Mixability, Section 2.2(a), p.9; attribution [40], and discussion immediately following (f).
F has a symmetric unimodal density on R
n is an integer with n>=2

body:
[Corollary Ball-like certificates of arXiv:2606.23025, 'Spectral-Capacitary Bounds for Homological Recovery from Reflected Brownian Trajectories'] There exist
constants \(C > 0\) and \(\varepsilon_{0} > 0\), depending
only on the geometric and analytic data of \(M\), such that the
following holds. Let \(0 < \varepsilon < \varepsilon_{0}\) and
let
\(\mathcal{A = \{}B_{M}\left( y_{1},\varepsilon \right),\ldots,B_{M}\left( y_{m},\varepsilon \right)\}\)
be a degree-\(q\), radius-\(r\) homological
certificate for \(M\). Then, for every \(z \in M\) and
\(\delta \in (0,1)\),

\begin{multline*}
\mathbb{P}_{z}\left( H_{q}\left( \Gamma_{T}^{r} \right) \cong H_{q}(M) \right) \geq 1 - \delta\\
\text{whenever}\quad T \geq C\left( s_{0} + \kappa_{d}(\varepsilon)^{- 1}\left( \log m + \log\tfrac{1}{\delta} \right) \right).
\end{multline*}

If \(\mathcal{A}\) is a full certificate, the same
condition gives simultaneous recovery of all homology groups.

body:
[Theorem thm:marstrand of arXiv:2608.26904, 'Hyperarithmetic directions can all be exceptional for Marstrand's projection theorem'] Suppose $B \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ is an analytic set. Let $\alpha = \={dim}_H(B)$ be the Hausdorff dimension of $B$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item For almost every line through the origin, the Hausdorff dimension of the projection of $B$ onto that line has Hausdorff dimension  $\min\{1, \alpha\}$; and
\item If $\alpha > 1$, then for almost every line through the origin, the projection of $B$ onto that line has positive measure in the line.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Marstrand's Projection Theorem~\cite{Marstrand:projection}

   \rho=\frac{1-b}{2}.
\]
Then there exist \(p\in[\rho,1-\rho]\), measurable functions
\(f,\delta:(0,1)\to\R\) with \(\delta(t)\neq0\) for all \(t\in(0,1)\), and
independent random variables \(T\sim{\rm Unif}(0,1)\) and
\(\varepsilon\sim{\rm Bernoulli}(p)\) such that
\[
   \xi\stackrel d=f(T)+\delta(T)\varepsilon.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\[
\mathbb P\bigl\{ |\eta_x|\le A_H(x;\delta)\text{ for all }x\in H\bigr\}\ge 1-\delta

\forall x\in H:\qquad

\le L_{\tau(t)}(x)
\le t+\sqrt{2t}\,A_H(x;\delta/2)+\frac12A_H(x;\delta/2)^2.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let n ≥ 1 and F ∈ C^{⌊n/2⌋+1}([0,∞)×R^n). For each s ≥ 0 let v(·,·;s) be the solution of ∂_t²v − Δv = 0 on {t > s} with v(s,·;s) = 0 and ∂_t v(s,·;s) = F(s,·). Then u(t,x) := ∫_0^t v(t,x;s) ds is C² on [0,∞)×R^n and solves ∂_t²u − Δu = F, u(0,·) = 0, ∂_t u(0,·) = 0. In semigroup notation u(t) = ∫_0^t ( sin((t−s)|∇|)/|∇| ) F(s) ds. For n = 3 this is the retarded potential u(t,x) = (1/4π) ∫_{B(x,t)} F(t − |y−x|, y) |y−x|^{−1} dy. Adding the solution of the homogeneous problem with data (u0,u1) solves the general Cauchy problem.

body:
[Definition 21 of arXiv:2606.02036, 'Self-intersection local times for Volterra Gaussian processes in stochastic flows with int'] A family of random maps $\{\phi_{s,t}:\mbR^d\times\Omega\to\mbR^d,\ 0\leqslant s\leqslant t<\infty\}$ is called a stochastic flow of homeomorphisms if for $\prob$-almost all $\omega\in\Omega:$  
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
 \item $\phi_{s,t}(\omega)=\phi_{r,t}(\omega)\circ\phi_{s,r,}(\omega)\ \text{holds for all}\ s\leqslant r\leqslant t.$ 
 \item $\phi_{s,s}(\omega)$ is the identity map for all $s\geqslant 0.$
 \item $\phi_{s,t}(\omega):\mbR^d\to\mbR^d$ is a homeomorphism for all $s\leqslant t.$ 
 \end{enumerate}
 If additionally, the mapping  $\phi_{s,t}(\omega):\mbR^d\to\mbR^d$ is $k$-times continuously differentiable for all $s\leqslant t,$ then $\phi$ is a stochastic flow of $C^k$-diffeomorphisms.

[Definition def_martingale of arXiv:2505.24043, 'Weak solutions of Navier-Stokes Equation with purely discontinuous L\'evy Noise'] A process  $\mathrm{M}\colon  \Omega  \times [0,\infty) \to \mathbb{R}$ is a martingale with respect to a filtration $\mathbb{H}=(\mathscr{H}_t)_{t\geq 0}$ if and only if it satisfies the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For every   $t \geq 0$ the function $M_t\coloneqq M(\cdot,t)$ is $\mathscr{H}_t$-measurable,
\item[(ii)] For every   $t \geq 0$ the function $M_t$ is integrable,
\item[(iii)] For all pairs $(s,t) \in [0,\infty)^{2}_{+}$,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}\left[ M_t|\mathscr{H}_s \right] = M_s,
\end{equation}
i.e.\ for every $A\in \mathscr{H}_s$
\[
\int_A{M_t}\, \mathrm{d} \mathbb{P}=\int_A{M_s}\, \mathrm{d} \mathbb{P}.
\]
or
\[
\mathbb{E} \bigl[ \1_A(M_t-M_s) \bigr]=0.
\]

\end{enumerate}
title: Definition def_martingale of arXiv:2505.24043

[Proposition 19 (Posterior Gaussian-mixture geometry) of arXiv:2608.21709, 'Posterior Information Dynamics of Diffusion Models for Linear Inverse Problems'] For \(c\in\{\pm1\}\),
\begin{equation}

X_0\mid r,C=c\sim\calN(Kr+c\delta,S),
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}

S=\Sigma-\Sigma A^\top Q^{-1}A\Sigma,
\qquad
\delta=(\Id_d-KA)m.
\end{equation}
The posterior class weights are
\begin{equation}

P(C=\pm1\mid r)
=
\alpha_\pm(r)
=
\frac{e^{\pm \eta(r)}}{2\cosh \eta(r)},
\qquad
\eta(r)=(Am)^\top Q^{-1}r.
\end{equation}
With \(\Lambda_t=a_t^2S+\Delta_t\Id_d\) and \(Z_t=X_t-a_tKr\), write
\(\widetilde p_t(z\mid r)=p_t(z+a_tKr\mid r)\) for the noised posterior density
in the shifted coordinate.  Then
\begin{equation}

\widetilde p_t(z\mid r)
=
\alpha_+\calN(z;a_t\delta,\Lambda_t)
+
\alpha_-\calN(z;-a_t\delta,\Lambda_t),
\end{equation}
or equivalently
\begin{equation}

\widetilde p_t(z\mid r)
\propto
\exp\{-z^\top \Lambda_t^{-1}z/2\}
\cosh\{\eta(r)+a_t\delta^\top \Lambda_t^{-1}z\}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Defi defn:higher-order-path of arXiv:2605.03151, 'Giants through Higher-Order paths in Random Simplicial Complexes'] For any pair of $(d-1)$-dimensional simplices $\sigma, \sigma' \in S_{d-1}(X)$, we say that they are \textit{adjacent} if there exists a $d$-dimensional simplex $\tau \in S_d(X)$ such that $\sigma \subseteq \tau$ and $\sigma' \subseteq \tau$.  
For any pair of $(d-1)$-dimensional simplices $\sigma_1, \sigma_2 \in S_{d-1}(X)$, we say that they are \textit{adjacent} if there exists a $d$-dimensional simplex $\tau \in S_d(X)$ such that $\sigma_1 \subseteq \tau$ and $\sigma_2 \subseteq \tau$. Also, we say that $\sigma$ and $\sigma'$ are connected through a \textit{$d$-dimensional path}, denoted by $\sigma \overset{\scriptscriptstyle d}{\longleftrightarrow} \sigma'$ if there exist distinct elements $(\sigma_i)_{i=0}^m\subseteq S_{d-1}(X)$ with $\sigma_0 = \sigma$ and $\sigma_m = \sigma'$ such that $\sigma_{i-1}$ and $\sigma_{i}$ are adjacent for all $i = 1, \dots, m$.

The smallest simplicial complex containing all $d$-dimensional simplices $\{\tau_i\}_{i=1}^m$ each of which defines the adjacency $\sigma_{i-1} \sim \sigma_i$ is called a $d$-dimensional path of length $m$ connecting $\sigma = \sigma_0$ and $\sigma' = \sigma_m$. The length of the shortest path between $\sigma,\sigma' \in S_{d-1}(X)$ is the minimum value of $m$ such that there exists a $d$-dimensional path between $\sigma,\sigma'$ of length $m$.
title: $d$-dimensional paths

body: In information theory, the entropy of a random variable quantifies the average level of uncertainty or information associated with the variable's potential states or possible outcomes. This measures the expected amount of information needed to describe the state of the variable, considering the distribution of probabilities across all potential states. Given a discrete random variable $X$, which may be any member $x$ within the set ${\mathcal {X}}$ and is distributed according to $p\colon {\mathcal {X}}\to [0,1]$, the entropy is $\mathrm {H} (X):=-\sum _{x\in {\mathcal {X}}}p(x)\log p(x),$ where $\Sigma$ denotes the sum over the variable's possible values. The choice of base for $\log$, the logarithm, varies for different applications. Base 2 gives the unit of bits (or "shannons"), while base e gives "natural units" nat, and base 10 gives units of "dits", "bans", or "hartleys". An equivalent definition of entropy is the expected value of the self-information of a variable.

[Definition def:H of arXiv:2509.06273, 'Normalized Matching Property for Competing Urn Models'] Let \. $X\subseteq [m]$ \. be an  odd set, and set \. $k:=\tfrac{|X|-1}{2}$.
Define the bipartite graph \. $H_X:=(W_1,W_2,F):=(W_1(X), W_2(X), F(X))$ \.  by
\begin{align*}
	& W_{1} \ := \ \binom{X}{k}, \quad W_{2} \ := \  \binom{X}{k+1}, \\
	& F \ := \ \{ \. (S,T) \in W_{1} \times W_{2}  \. \mid \. S \subset T \. \}.
\end{align*}
Let 
$\nu$ be a probability measure on $[m]$ (corresponding to the random balls ending in the
$n$-th urn).
We define a weight function  \. $g_{\nu}:=g_{\nu,X}$ \. on the vertices of  $H_X$  by
\[  g_{\nu}(S) \ := \ \nu(S) \. \nu(X\setminus S).  \]
By construction, $g_{\nu,X}$ is a balanced weight function.
title: Urn incidence graph

body: [Definition def:marked_GUE of arXiv:2603.27906, 'Marked GUE-corners process in doubly periodic dimer models'] Let~$\mathbb{P}_{\operatorname{GUE}}$ be the GUE-corners process defined on~$\Lambda=\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\times \mathbb{R}$. For a measurable function~$\theta:\Lambda\to [0,1]$, the \emph{marked GUE-corners process}~$\mathbb{P}_{\operatorname{GUE}}^\theta$ is the point process on~$\Lambda_{\{0,1\}}=\Lambda \times \{0,1\}$ obtained by assigning to each point in a given realization from~$\mathbb{P}_{\operatorname{GUE}}$ an independent mark~$m\sim \operatorname{Bernoulli}(\theta(t,\mu))$, where~$(t,\mu)\in \Lambda$ is the location of the point. We denote its corresponding point configurations ~$(\xi_{s,j}^t)_{1\leq s\leq t}$.
title: Definition def:marked_GUE of arXiv:2603.27906

body:
[Proposition of arXiv:2507.19554, 'Full extremal process in four-dimensional membrane model'] There exist absolute constants $C, c > 0$ such that for all $N \in \mbZ_+$ and $\lambda, r \geq C$
	\bequn	
		\mbP\lp \exists A \subset \Xi_{N, r}, \lv A \rv \geq \log r: \forall \lp u, v \rp \in A: h_{u}^{N} + h_{v}^{N} \geq 2m_N- 2\lambda \log \log r \rp \geq 1 - Ce^{-\sqrt{\lambda} \log\log r}.
	\eequn

body:
[Theorem equiv of arXiv:2412.02087, 'The spectral distribution of random graphs with given degree sequences'] Consider the degree sequence $\{ d_1^{(n)}, d_2^{(n)}, \cdots, d_n^{(n)} \}$ with total degree $D^{(n)}=d_1^{(n)}+d_2^{(n)}+\cdots+d_n^{(n)}$ for each $n\geq 1$, and recall the normalized Laplacian matrix $M^{(n)}$ as defined in (sec:preliminaries of the paper). Suppose the following condition holds: for arbitrarily large $C > 0$ and arbitrarily small $\varepsilon > 0$, the degree sequence satisfies that $\sum_{i = 1}^n \mathbbm{1}\{ d_i^{(n)} < C \sqrt{D^{(n)}/n} \} \leq \varepsilon n$ for all large $n > N(C, \varepsilon)$. Then the empirical eigenvalue distribution $\mu_n$ of $M^{(n)}$ weakly converges to the semicircle distribution $\rho_{\rm sc}$ in probability: 
    $$\mu_n \xrightarrow{D} \rho_{\rm sc} \quad \text{in probability.}$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem equiv of arXiv:2412.02087

[Proposition prop: domain markov of arXiv:2506.21466, 'The Markov property for $\varphi^4_3$ on the cylinder'] Let $\varphi_-,\varphi_+ \in S'(\mathbb T^2)$. Let $F^+,F^-:S'(M)\rightarrow \mathbb R$ be bounded functions such that $F^\pm$ is ${\rm Int}(M^\pm)$-measurable, and let $F=F^+ F^-$ be their pointwise product. Then
 \begin{equation}
  \mathbb E_{\mu_{\varphi_-,\varphi_+}}[ F]
  =
\mathbb E_{\tilde\mu^0}\left[  \mathbb E_{\mu^-}[F^-(\varphi^- + H^-(\varphi_-,\varphi^0)) ]\mathbb E_{\mu^+}[F^+(\varphi^+ + H^+(\varphi_+,\varphi^0)) ] \right], 
  \end{equation}
  where $\varphi^{\sigma} \sim \mu^\sigma$ is the Dirichlet GFF on $M^\sigma$ and $\varphi^0 \sim \tilde\mu^0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop: domain markov of arXiv:2506.21466

[Lemma of arXiv:2609.01439, 'Box-Delaunay graphs of large chromatic number'] Let $I\subset [n]$. The probability that $I$ is an independent set in $G$ is at most 
$$2^{-|I|k}\left(\frac{|I|m}{n}+1\right)^{kn/m}.$$

body:
[Corollary cor:backoff-finite-SE-bins of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] There exists a real number $\lambda_0\in (0,1)$ such that the following holds. 
Consider any $\lambda \in (0,\lambda_0)$. Consider any send sequence~$\overline{p}$ such that $p_0=1$ and, for all $i\geq 1$, $W_i \leq (2/\lambda)^i$. Suppose that $\overline{p}$ has infinitely many bins which are strongly exposed. Then
the backoff process with birth rate~$\lambda$ and send sequence~$\overline{p}$ is not positive recurrent.

body:
[Theorem bt2 of arXiv:2603.05467, 'Thresholds for colouring the random Borsuk graph'] We have

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{P}(\chi(G({n},\alpha)) > 1)
=\begin{cases}
    1 & \text{if }n^2\alpha^d\to \infty,\\
    1-e^{- c \cdot \nu} & \text{if }n^2\alpha^d\to \nu \in (0,\infty), \\
    0 & \text{if } n^2\alpha^d\to 0,
\end{cases}
$$

\noindent
where $c := \Gamma((d+3)/2) / \left( 2 \cdot (d+1)\cdot \sqrt{\pi} \cdot \Gamma((d+2)/2) \right)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem bt2 of arXiv:2603.05467

\[
 E_2(x,u)=0,
 \qquad
 R_n(x,u)=0.
\]
Then there exists $z>1/3$ such that
\[
 E_1(x,z,u)=E_3(x,z,u)=0.
\]

[Lemma 2 of arXiv:2609.01166, 'Nonparametric inference for density-dependent McKean--Vlasov diffusions'] Assume \(\Xi_0\in\mathcal H^\beta([0,U],H)\) satisfies \eqref{eq:truth-interior-envelope}, and Assumption~\ref{ass:log} holds. 
Consider the graded mesh with 
\(
\vartheta>
(2\beta+2)/(2\beta+1)
\).
There exist fixed architecture constants 
\(L, C_p, C_s, C_B\)
and 
\(m_0, H_1<\infty\) 
such that, for every \(m\geq m_0\), there exists a candidate \(\xi_m \in \cX_m\) 
satisfying the exact moment cancellations on every cell, namely,
\begin{equation}
 \int_{J_{j,m}}\left( 
 \xi_m(u)-\Xi_0(u)
 \right) 
 \frac{\dd u}{u\Xi_0(u)^2}=0.
\end{equation}
This candidate achieves
\begin{equation}
\|\xi_m-\Xi_0\|_{\infty,[0,U]}
\leq C_{\mathrm{app}}m^{-\beta}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\|\mathcal A(\xi_m-\Xi_0)\|_{L^2(\nu_0)}
\leq C_{\mathrm{fwd}}m^{-(\beta+1)}
\end{equation}
with
\(
C_{\mathrm{app}}
=C_{\mathrm{app}}(\beta,H,U,\kappa,K,\vartheta),
\)
and
\(
C_{\mathrm{fwd}}
=C_{\mathrm{fwd}}
(\beta,H,U,\kappa,K,\vartheta,r_0,\alpha,C_\nu)
\).
Moreover, for \(\varepsilon\in(0,1]\), 
the sieve entropy satisfies 
\[
\log N(\varepsilon,\mathfrak X_m,\|\cdot\|_\infty)
\leq
C_{\mathrm{ent}}m
\log\left(C_{\mathrm{ent}}m/\varepsilon\right),
\]
where \(C_{\mathrm{ent}}\) depends only on the fixed sieve-architecture constants, 
\(U\), \(\kappa\), \(K\) and
\(L_\tau\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 2 of arXiv:2609.01166

[Thm 2boxtimesfp of arXiv:2608.29914, 'Fixed points in abstract provability structures'] Let $S$ be an APS and let $\triangle v$ be a one-variable APS term of degree two. 
Then $\mathsf{E}_S(\triangle)$ holds. 
More precisely, the following statements hold.  
Let $k, m, n$ be natural numbers. 
 \begin{enumerate}
        \item If $m \geq n$, then $\boxtimes \Box^m \boxtimes \Box^n v$ has a fixed point $\boxtimes \top$.
        
        \item If $m < n$, then $\boxtimes \Box^m \boxtimes \Box^n v$ has a fixed point $\boxtimes \Box^m \boxtimes \top$.
        
        \item If $m \geq n + k$, then $\Box^k \boxtimes \Box^m \boxtimes \Box^n v$ has a fixed point $\Box^k \boxtimes \top$.
        
        \item If $m < n + k$, then $\Box^k \boxtimes \Box^m \boxtimes \Box^n v$ has a fixed point $ \Box^k \boxtimes\Box^m \boxtimes \top$. 
    \end{enumerate}

[Definition def:spectral_duality of arXiv:2605.00657, 'Spectral Duality and Reset-Neutral Distributions\\ in Random Walks with Multi-Site Geometr'] Let $\{z_1,\dots,z_m\}$ be a set of sites. A
\emph{spectral duality} on this set is an involution
$sigma:\{z_1,\dots,z_m\}\to\{z_1,\dots,z_m\}$
(i.e., $sigma^2=\mathrm{id}$) together with positive
coefficients $kappa(z)>0$, independent of $nu$, such that
\begin{equation}
B_nu(z) = kappa(z)\,A_nu(sigma(z))
\qquad \forall\,nu=1,\dots,N,\quad \forall\,z\in\{z_1,\dots,z_m\}.

\end{equation}
A site $z_0$ with $sigma(z_0)=z_0$ is called a
\emph{spectrally neutral site}. A pair $(z,sigma(z))$ with
$sigma(z)\neq z$ is called a \emph{spectral pair}.
title: Spectral duality with $\nu$-independent weights

[Thm 1 of arXiv:2609.02686, 'The Bonnet-Myers theorem on Finsler manifolds with integral weighted Ricci curvature bound'] {\rm(\cite{ChF}, Theorem 3.1)}
Let $(M, F, m)$ be an $n$-dimensional Finsler metric measure manifold. Assume that $\mathbf{S}\geq -\vartheta$ for some $\vartheta \geq 0$.
Then, for $p>\frac{n}{2}$, $K \in \mathbb{R}$ and $r>0$ $(r \leq \frac{\pi}{2 \sqrt{K}}$ when $K>0)$, we have
$$
\int_0^r \varphi^{2 p}(t, \theta) \mathrm{e}^{-\vartheta t} \sigma(t, \theta) d t \leq \left(\frac{(n-1)(2 p-1)}{2 p-n}\right)^p \int_0^r\left(\operatorname{Ric}_{\infty}^{K}\right)^{p} \mathrm{e}^{-\vartheta t} \sigma(t, \theta) d t
$$
and
\be
\varphi(r, \theta)^{2 p-1} \mathrm{e}^{-\vartheta r} \sigma(r, \theta) \leq (2 p-1)^p\left(\frac{n-1}{2 p-n}\right)^{p-1} \int_0^r\left(\operatorname{Ric}_{\infty}^K\right)^p \mathrm{e}^{-\vartheta t} \sigma(t, \theta) d t, 
\ee
where $(t, \theta)$ denotes the geodesic polar coordinates centered at $x \in M$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 1 of arXiv:2609.02686

[Coro of arXiv:2411.02033, 'Two stochastic versions of the Arps curve decline'] The mean hitting time for $(Q_t)$ to reach the level $x<q_0$ is bounded as follows:
$$
\mathbb{E}[T_{Q,x}] \geqslant \phi^{(1)}(0,x) - \phi^{(1)}(0,q_0),
$$
where:
$$
\phi^{(1)}(0,z) = \frac{1}{d_0} \left( \frac{z\sqrt{d_0 \pi}}{\sigma} F\left( \frac{1}{2},\frac{3}{2},\frac{d_0z^2}{\sigma^2} \right) + \sum_{m=0}^{\infty} \frac{2^m}{(m+1)(m+2)!!} \left( \frac{z\sqrt{d_0}}{\sigma} \right)^{2m+2} \right). 
$$
in which $F$ denotes the Kummer function (or confluent hypergeometric function). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered coro of arXiv:2411.02033, 'Two stochastic versions of the Arps curve decline'

body:
[Prop exm of arXiv:2411.14236, 'Size of chaos for Gibbs measures\\of mean field interacting diffusions'] Suppose that one of the following assumptions holds true.
\begin{itemize}
\item (Flat semi-convexity \dots)
The interaction kernel writes $W = W_+ - W_-$
with both $W_+$, $W_-$ being continuous and of positive type.
The probability measures $\Pi[m]$ satisfy a $\rho_0$-log-Sobolev
inequality uniformly in $m \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)$ for some $\rho_0 > 0$.
Moreover, one of the followings holds.
\begin{itemize}
\item (\,\dots\ with bounded force)
The kernels $W$, $W_-$ satisfy
$\lVert \nabla_1W\rVert_{L^\infty} \leqslant M_W < \infty$
and $\lVert \nabla_1W_-\rVert_{L^\infty} \leqslant M_W^-
< \sqrt{\rho_0}/2$.
In this case, we set
\[
\rho = \rho_0\biggl(1 - \frac{2M^-_W}{\sqrt{\rho_0}}\biggr),\qquad
\gamma = 2M_W,\qquad
M = 4M_W^2.
\]
\item (\,\dots\ with Lipschitz force)
The state space $\mathcal X$ is $\mathds R^d$.
The kernels $W_+$, $W_-$ are $\mathcal C^2$ and satisfy
$\lVert \nabla_{1,2}^2W_+\rVert_{L^\infty} \leqslant L_W^+ < \infty$
and $\lVert \nabla_{1,2}^2W_-\rVert_{L^\infty} \leqslant L_W^- < \rho_0/2$.
In this case, we set
\begin{align*}
\rho &= \rho_0\biggl( 1 - \frac{2L^-_W}{\rho_0}\biggr),\\
\gamma &= \frac{64(1+\delta_N)^2(L^+_W+L^-_W)^2}{\lambda_N},\\
M &= 4(L^+_W+L^-_W)^2
\biggl( \frac{\delta_N}{\lambda_NN} + \frac{d}{\rho_0}\biggr),
\end{align*}
where $\lambda_N$, $\delta_N$ are given by
(equation eq:def-lambda-N of the paper), (equation eq:def-delta-N of the paper)
respectively with $\varepsilon$ replaced by $1/2$
and $\Var m_*$ by $d / \rho_0$.
\end{itemize}

\item (Displacement convexity)
The state space $\mathcal X$ is $\mathds R^d$.
The confinement $V$ is $\mathcal C^2$ and satisfies
$\nabla^2V \succcurlyeq \kappa_V$ for $\kappa_V > 0$
and the interaction $W$ is given by
$W(x,y) = W'(x - y)$ for some $\mathcal C^2$ and even $W' \colon \mathds R^d \to \mathds R$
satisfying $\nabla^2W' \succcurlyeq 0$
and $\lVert \nabla^2W'\rVert_{L^\infty} \leqslant L_W$.
In this case, we set
\[
\rho = \frac{\kappa_V}{2(1 + L_W^2/\kappa_V^2)},\qquad
\gamma = \frac{2L_W^2}{\kappa_V},\qquad
M = 4L_W^2 \biggl(1 + \frac{L_W^2}{\kappa_V^2N}\biggr)\frac{d}{\kappa_V}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then Theorem~(thm:sharp of the paper) applies with the constants
$\rho$, $\gamma$, $M$ whenever
$N$ is large enough such that $\gamma \geqslant 0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop exm of arXiv:2411.14236

[Theorem th-hr of arXiv:2605.01958, 'High-dimensional limits for reflected Brownian motion in the orthant'] For $n\in{\mathbb N}$, there exists a map $\Gamma^{(n)}:C_{S_n}({\mathbb R}_+,{\mathbb R}^n)\times{\mathcal R}^{(n)}\to C^{(2n)}$ such that whenever
$(\hat\Xi,\hat{\mathcal A},\hat Q)$ is a probability space supporting $X_0\sim\nu^{(n)}$, $W$ an $(n,b,\sigma)$-BM independent of $X_0$, and $\{\hat{\mathcal A}_t\}$ is the filtration generated by $X_0+W(t)$, $t\in{\mathbb R}_+$, then, upon setting $(X,L)=\Gamma^{(n)}(X_0+W;R)$, the tuple $(X_0,W,X,L)$ satisfies all requirements in Definition (def1 of the paper), but with the filtered probability space being $(\hat\Xi,\hat{\mathcal A},\{\hat{\mathcal A}_t\},\hat Q)$. Moreover, $\Gamma^{(n)}$ is jointly measurable in both arguments. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2609.01268, 'Resultant multiplicity via projective degrees\\ and applications to tensor eigenvalues'] For a general $\hh$ as above, the intersection \[
    \Gamma_{\ff}\cap \Gamma_{\hh}
    \] is contained in $G_{\ff}$, is transverse, and is therefore zero-dimensional and reduced.
    It is isomorphic to $\mathcal{C}(\ff,\hh)$ by projection onto the first coordinate.
    Moreover, \[
    C(\ff,\hh) = \sum_{\ell=0}^{n-1} d^{n-\ell-1} y_\ell.
    \]

[Theo steeptheo1 of arXiv:2510.23430, 'On the Martin boundary for discrete TASEP'] With the notation above:

(1) The limit
$$
\lim_{N\to \infty}G^{(0,-p)}_{\lambda(N)}(\mathbf z, 1^{N-n})\ N^{\frac{d}{2}}\prod_{i=1}^k\left(\frac{1-\tilde \chi_i-p}{1-p}\right)^{N} (\tilde\chi_i+p)^{\lambda(N)_i}
$$
does not depend on $\lambda(N)_i$ for $i$ such that $\alpha_i<\frac{p}{1-p}$. When $\alpha_i<\frac{p}{1-p}$ for all $i$ the limit above is equal to $1$.

(2) When $\alpha_1,\dots, \alpha_k>\frac{p}{1-p}$:
\begin{multline}
G^{(0,-p)}_\lambda(\mathbf z, 1^{N-n})\ N^{\frac{d}{2}}\prod_{i=1}^k\left(\frac{1-\tilde \chi_i-p}{1-p}\right)^{N}(\tilde \chi_i+p)^{\lambda(N)_i}\\
\to Z (2\pi)^{-\frac{k}{2}}\prod_{i=1}^{k}\frac{e^{-\frac{x_i^2}{2}}}{\sqrt{\alpha_i(1+\alpha_i)}}\prod_{\substack{i<j\\\alpha_i=\alpha_j}}\frac{x_i-x_j}{\sqrt{\alpha_i(1+\alpha_i)}}\prod_{i=1}^n\Phi^{\mathcal A,\varnothing}(z_i),
\end{multline}
where
$$
 Z=\frac{\prod_{\chi>0} (\chi+p)^{\binom{m(\chi)+1}{2}}\prod_{\substack {i<j:\\ \chi_i>\chi_j}}(\chi_i-\chi_j) }{\prod_{i=1}^k\chi_i^{k-i+1}},\qquad \Phi^{\mathcal A,\varnothing}(z)=\prod_{i=1}^k\frac{1-\frac{p}{1-p}(z-1)}{1-\alpha_i(z-1)}.
$$
Moreover, this convergence is uniform over choices of $\lambda(N)$ such that $\mathbf x$ vary over the compact subset $C\subset\mathbb R^k$ and $\{\lambda(N)_i-N\alpha_i-\sqrt{N\alpha_i(1+\alpha_i)}x_i\}_{i,N}$ are uniformly bounded. In other words, for a compact subset $C\subset \mathbb R^k$ and a constant $M$ there exists a positive real sequence $(\Lambda_n)$ such that $\lim_{n\to\infty}\Lambda_n = 0$ and
\begin{multline*}
\Big|G^{(0,-p)}_\lambda(\mathbf z, 1^{N-n})\ N^{\frac{d}{2}}\prod_{i=1}^k\left(\frac{1-\tilde \chi_i-p}{1-p}\right)^{N}(\tilde \chi_i+p)^{\lambda(N)_i}\\
- Z (2\pi)^{-\frac{k}{2}}\prod_{i=1}^{k}\frac{e^{-\frac{x_i^2}{2}}}{\sqrt{\alpha_i(1+\alpha_i)}}\prod_{\substack{i<j\\\alpha_i=\alpha_j}}\frac{x_i-x_j}{\sqrt{\alpha_i(1+\alpha_i)}}\prod_{i=1}^n\Phi^{\mathcal A,\varnothing}(z_i)\Big|<\Lambda_n
\end{multline*}
for every sequence $\lambda(N)$ such that $|\lambda(N)_i-N\alpha_i-\sqrt{N\alpha_i(1+\alpha_i)}x_i|< M$ for some vector $\mathbf x\in C$ and all $i, N$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop pr:moment_decay_1 of arXiv:2411.03482, 'Ergodicity of 2D singular stochastic Navier--Stokes equations'] Fix $t_0$ such that $\mathbb{P}(T < t_0) < \frac{1}{10}$\,. Let $N\in \mathbf{N}^*$ and $V^{(N)}_{\alpha_0}(u[0]) < \infty $\,. 
	If $\alpha_0$ is sufficiently small (independent of $N$), then we have
	\begin{equs}
	
		\mathbb{E} \left(V^{(N)}_{\alpha_0}(u[T\wedge t_0])\right)^N &\leq \rho \big(V^{(N)}_{2\alpha_0}(u[0])\big)^{N} + (CN)^{2N}\;, \\
	
		\sup_{a\leq t_0} \mathbb{E} \bigl(V_{2\alpha_0}^{(N)}(u[T\wedge a])\bigr)^N &\leq 6^N \big(V^{(N)}_{\alpha_0}(u[0])\big)^{N} +(CN)^{2N} \;,
	\end{equs}
	where $0 < \rho < 1$ and $C>0$ are some constants independent of $N$.
title: Prop pr:moment_decay_1 of arXiv:2411.03482

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Second Ray-Knight isomorphism to transfer the DGFF level-set result to local times. Result: By the second Ray-Knight theorem the local time at level theta of the walk is, in law, (1/2)(h + sqrt(2 theta ...))^2 for an independent DGFF-type field h; level sets of the local time at height eta times the cover-time scale correspond to DGFF level sets at height lambda log N with lambda determined by eta and theta, giving eta < 1 + (1/2) sqrt(theta)... in the notation of the notes exactly the range where the corresponding DGFF lambda is below 1. The transfer is rigorous for the part of the level set where the sign of h + constant is positive; the difficulty is the negative branch, where the square masks the sign and the point measures of the two branches are dependent. For eta near the upper endpoint the negative branch contributes a lower-order but not negligible set; separating it needs a joint limit of the two branches, which is again Problem 16.1 in disguise. Obstruction: Sign ambiguity in the isomorphism couples two DGFF level sets; no joint limit is available.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0011-scaling-limit-of-local-time-level-sets-of-planar-random-walk-in-the-fu

[Lemma lem:Eprocess of arXiv:2607.05671, 'Bi-infinite systems of singularly interacting Brownian particles and the KPZ equation'] Fix $(t,x) \in [0,\infty)\times \mathbb{R}$ and $\delta, \varepsilon>0$.
\begin{enumerate}[label = (\roman*)]

\item The sum (equation eq:Edef of the paper) defining $\{\mathcal{E}^{t,x,\delta, \varepsilon}(s), s \in [0,t+\delta)\}$ converges uniformly on compacts subsets of $[0,t+\delta)$, in $L^r(\mathbb{P})$, for all $r \in [1,\infty)$. In particular, $\sup_{0 \leq s \leq T'}  \mathcal{E}^{t,x,\delta,\varepsilon}(s) \in L^r(\mathbb{P})$
for all $r \in [1,\infty)$ and $T' \in [0,t+\delta)$. 

\item For all $s \in [0,t+\delta)$, the following equality holds:
\begin{equation} 
\mathcal{E}^{t,x,\delta,\varepsilon}(s) - \mathcal{E}^{t,x,\delta,\varepsilon}(0) = -\sum_{i \in \mathbb{Z}} e^{\sigma\varepsilon^{1/4}i} \int_0^s p_{t-u+\delta}(X_i^\varepsilon(u) - x) dB_i^\varepsilon(u),
\end{equation}
where the sum on the right-hand side converges uniformly on compact subsets of $[0,t + \delta)$, in $L^r(\mathbb{P})$, for all $r \in [1,\infty)$. In particular, $\{\mathcal{E}^{t,x,\delta,\varepsilon}(s), s \in [0, t + \delta)\}$ is a continuous square-integrable martingale.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:Eprocess of arXiv:2607.05671

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Infinitely many planar FPP geodesic rays for continuous laws structural argument Result: Finite geodesic existence and finite lattice degree yield at least one ray: among geodesics to points tending to infinity, choose an infinite subsequence with a common first edge, then a common second edge, and continue. Every finite segment of the diagonal limit is minimizing. Check: At each stage finitely many choices ensure an infinite subsequence. Path lengths tend to infinity, and any shortcut of a limiting finite segment would contradict minimization in all sufficiently long selected paths. Obstruction: This compactness proof gives one ray, not many eventually disjoint rays. Endpoint sequences in different directions could still share the same limiting tail without additional shape information.

body: [Proposition prp:variational problem for v of arXiv:2411.10311, 'Planar Novikov-Shubin invariant for adjacency matrices of structured directed dense random'] Up to rescaling, the solution, $v$, to the Dyson equation (equation Dyson equation of the paper) is the unique minimizer for $J$, i.e., $v$ lies in the domain of $J$ and for $ J_\ast:=\inf_{x} J(x)$ we have $J(v) = J_\ast$. Furthermore, any minimizing sequence $x^{(n)}$ with $\lim_{n \to \infty}J(x^{(n)}) = J_\ast$ and $\avg{x^{(n)}}=\langle v \rangle$ satisfies $x^{(n)} \to v$.

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2606.29131, '2606.29131'] Let $g\in \M_{\beta}$ for some $\beta>0$, and let $u_g\in C_b^\infty(\R^d)$ be the solution to following equation:
$$
\lambda u_g(x)-\bar \sL_2 u_g(x)=g(x),\quad x\in \R^d,
$$ where $\sL_2$ is given by \eqref{e2-1a-}.
Then, $u_g\in \M_{\beta}$, and there exists a constant $C_1:=C_1(\beta)>0$ $($which is independent of $g$$)$ such that for all $k\ge0$,
$$
\|u_g\|_{\M_{\beta},k}\le C_1\|g\|_{\M_{\beta},k} .
$$

STATUS: proof (unaudited). For fixed Q>0, positive integer p, Y_q(Z)=tanh(sqrt(q)Z)^2/q, and S_(n,q) the average of n iid copies, sup_(0<q<=Q,n>=4p) E S_(n,q)^(-p)<infinity. Its deviations outside any fixed sufficiently small interval about E Y_q have probability <=C exp(-cn), uniformly in q; E[S^(-p);bad]<=C exp(-cn/2) for n>=8p. These exact negative moments justify deletion of inverse tails for critical tanh. Assumptions: Standard Gaussian iid rows, fixed finite Q>0 and moment order p. Constants may depend on Q,p and concentration-box radius; all sample averages are positive almost surely. Model: K_(j+1)=n^-1 sum_(i=1)^n tanh(sqrt(K_j)Z_(j,i))^2, with independent standard Gaussian rows and layers, K0>0 fixed, no bias, Gaussian weight variance exactly1/n, and no width-dependent normalizer. Write Y_q=tanh(sqrt(q)Z)^2/q, S_(n,q)=n^-1 sum_i Y_q(Z_i), q=K_j, v=1/(nq), V_next=1/(nK_(j+1)). Limit: Unaudited analytic proof; no novelty claim. Provides inverse-tail control, not a cumulant expansion.

Write Y_q=tanh(sqrt(q)Z)^2/q for q>0 and Z standard Gaussian, and
S_(n,q)=n^(-1)sum_(i=1)^n Y_q(Z_i), with iid rows.

## C044: uniform inverse sample moments and deleted tails

For every fixed Q<infinity and positive integer p, there is a finite
C_(Q,p) such that

    sup_(0<q<=Q, n>=4p) E[S_(n,q)^(-p)] <= C_(Q,p).            (1)

For any fixed sufficiently small eta>0, with m(q)=E Y_q and
G_(n,q)={|S_(n,q)-m(q)|<=eta},

    P(G_(n,q)^c)<=C_Q exp(-c_Q n),
    E[S_(n,q)^(-p);G_(n,q)^c]<=C_(Q,p)exp(-c_Q n/2), n>=8p.   (2)

Constants can be made explicit from the Gaussian expectations in the
proof. The sample mean is strictly positive almost surely. These are
exact-chain inverse moment estimates, in contrast with the ReLU atom and
near-collinearity obstruction.

Proof. tanh(x)/x decreases for x>0: tanh(x)-x sech(x)^2 has derivative
2x sech(x)^2 tanh(x)>0 and value0 at zero. Therefore Y_q>=Y_Q for q<=Q,
and Y_q<=Z^2. Let H=Y_Q>0 and phi(s)=E exp(-sH). For small y>0,

    P(H<=y)=P(|Z|<=arctanh(sqrt(Qy))/sqrt(Q))<=C sqrt(y),

using arctanh(w)<=2w for w<=1/2 and the bounded Gaussian density.
Increasing C_Q extends P(H<=y)<=C_Q sqrt(y) to every y>0.
Integration by parts gives phi(s)<=C'_Q s^(-1/2). Also for0<=s<=1,

    phi(s)<=1-c_Q s<=exp(-c_Q s), c_Q=E[H exp(-H)]>0,

and rho_Q=phi(1)<1. The Gamma identity and independence yield

    E[(n^(-1)sum_i H_i)^(-p)]
       =n^p/Gamma(p) integral_0^infinity s^(p-1)phi(s)^n ds.    (3)

Choose s0>=max(1,(2C'_Q)^2). On [0,1], (3) is bounded by c_Q^(-p).
On [1,s0], use rho_Q^n, giving at most
n^p s0^p rho_Q^n/(p Gamma(p)), uniformly bounded in n. On [s0,infinity),
for n>=4p,

    integral_(s0)^infinity s^(p-1)(C'_Q/sqrt(s))^n ds
      <= s0^p 2^(-n)/(n/2-p).

After multiplication by n^p/Gamma(p), this is uniformly bounded too.
This proves (1), since S_(n,q)>=n^(-1)sum H_i under the common-row coupling.

Uniform exponential integrability follows from0<=Y_q<=Z^2; m(q)>=E H>0.
Centered exponential-moment bounds and Chernoff give the first part of(2),
uniformly in q. Choose eta< E H/2 so G also stays uniformly away from zero.
Cauchy-Schwarz, (1) at order2p and the first bound in(2) prove its second
bound. All integrations use nonnegative integrands, so Tonelli applies.

## C045: full next drift of the exact reciprocal

Consider the exact scalar critical chain K_next=q S_(n,q) and
v=1/(nq), V_next=1/(n K_next). There are epsilon>0,C,c,n0 such that for
0<q<=epsilon and n>=n0,

    E(V_next-v)
      =(2v+2)/n + [4v-4-5/(3v)]/n^2+r_n(v),
    |r_n(v)|<=C[v/n^(5/2)+(1+1/v+1/v^2)/n^3+v exp(-cn)].     (4)

The exact inverse moments in C044 justify this unbounded observable.
In particular the singular next correction is negative. On any fixed
0<q<=Q, the following coarser estimates hold uniformly for sufficiently
large n (depending on Q and the indicated moment orders):

    E[(V_next/v)^j]<=1+C_(Q,j)(q+1/n), j=1,2,
    E[(V_next-v)^2]<=C_Q(v^2/n+1/n^2),                        (5)
    |E(V_next-v)-(2v+2)/n|
                         <=C_Q[q/n+1/n^2+v/n^(3/2)].         (6)

Proof of(4). Global Taylor inequalities for tanh, using boundedness on
|x|<=1 and polynomial domination on |x|>=1, imply

    m(q)=1-2q+(17/3)q^2+O(q^3),
    Var(Y_q)=2-16q+O(q^2),
    kappa_3(Y_q)=8+O(q).

For example tanh(x)^2=x^2-(2/3)x^4+(17/45)x^6+O(x^8), with a global
remainder bound C|x|^8. Similarly E Y_q^2=3-20q+O(q^2). Every fixed
positive row moment is bounded; its first variation is O(q) since
|Y_q-Z^2|<=Cq Z^4.

Taylor expand 1/S about m(q) through order four on G. The fifth absolute
sample-average moment is O(n^(-5/2)); it follows, for instance, from the
sixth moment bound for centered iid sample sums and Holder. The exact
sample-mean third moment is kappa_3(Y_q)/n^2, and its fourth moment is
3 Var(Y_q)^2/n^2+O(n^-3). Deleted inverse tails are exponentially small
by C044. Therefore uniformly on0<q<=epsilon,

    E S^(-1)=m^(-1)+Var(Y_q)/(n m^3)
              +[-kappa_3(Y_q)/m^4+3 Var(Y_q)^2/m^5]/n^2
              +O(n^(-5/2))+O(exp(-cn))
      =1+2q-(5/3)q^2+(2-4q)/n+4/n^2
              +O(q^3+q^2/n+q/n^2+n^(-5/2)+exp(-cn)).         (7)

Multiply by v, subtract v, and use vq=1/n. This gives(4).

For(5), the same good-event Taylor expansion through order two applied

E S^(-1)=1+2q+2/n+O(q^2+q/n+n^(-3/2)) for small q, which gives(6).
On epsilon<=q<=Q, v<=1/(n epsilon); the error is O_Q(1/n), absorbable

[Lemma 11 (Finite, possibly inflated, offspring variance) of arXiv:2608.15987, 'Threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees: a conditional bra'] In the saturated regime, $N\,|\,(\text{types})\sim\mathrm{Bin}(\text{children},p_{d,d'})$ and
\[
\sigma^2_{\mathrm{off}}=\underbrace{\E[(\deg-1)]\,\bar p(1-\bar p)}_{\text{Bernoulli}}+\underbrace{\Var(\deg-1)\,\bar p^{\,2}}_{\text{degree fluctuation}}<\infty,
\]
where $\bar p$ is the $\pi$-averaged transmission probability and $\deg-1$ the offspring count. In the sensitive regime an additional Cox term $\E[(\deg-1)(\deg-2)]\Var_A(p(A))$ appears; it is also finite since $p(\cdot)\in[0,1]$. Both expressions are finite under the standing assumption $\E[\deg^2]<\infty$ ($\Leftrightarrow g''(1)<\infty$).

body:
[Theorem thm:2DNSE of arXiv:2412.01381, 'Ergodicity and mixing for locally monotone stochastic evolution equations'] Assume that $B\in L_2(U,W^{1,2}_{0,\,\operatorname{sol}}({\mathcal O}))$. Assume that for some $\lambda\in (0,1)$,
\[\|B\|^2_{L_2(U,H)}\le\frac{1}{4}\lambda\nu^3 c_0^2,\]
and
\[\|B\|^2_{L_2(U,H)}\le(1-\lambda)\nu c_0^2.\]
Then the Markovian Feller semigroup $(P_t)_{t\ge 0}$ of the stochastic incompressible 2D Navier-Stokes equations~(equation eq:2DNSE of the paper) with degenerate additive Wiener noise possesses a unique invariant measure $\mu_\ast$ with second moments in $V$.

Furthermore, if there exists $\gamma\in (0,\nu c_0^2]$ and $\lambda\in (0,1)$ such that
\[\|B\|^2_{L_2(U,H)}\le\frac{1}{4}\lambda(\nu^3 c_0^2-\nu^2\gamma),\]
and
\[\|B\|^2_{L_2(U,H)}\le(1-\lambda)\nu c_0^2,\]
then $(P_t)_{t\ge 0}$ is exponentially mixing and exponentially ergodic, and we have the following upper bound for the $\varepsilon$-mixing time
\[\tau^x_{\textup{\textsf{mix}}}(\varepsilon)\leq 
\frac{2}{\gamma}\left[\frac{1}{\lambda \nu^2 }\|x\|^{2}_H+\log\left(\|x\|_H+\frac{\|B\|_{L_2(U,H)}}{\sqrt{2\lambda \nu}c_0}\right)+\log\left(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\right)\right].\]

[Prop max_concave of arXiv:2604.23751, 'Large deviation principles for pattern-avoiding permutations, and limit shapes for constra'] Let $E$ be a topological vector space and $K \subset E$ compact and convex, and let $f:K \to \mathbb{R}$ be lower semicontinuous and strictly convex.
    Then $f$ has a minimum which is attained at exactly one point $x_0 \in K$.
    Moreover, if $x \in K$ is such that for any $y \in V_x(K)$, we have
    \[ \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\Big|_{t=0^+} f(x+ty)=0 ,\]
    then $x=x_0$.

[Proposition 6 of arXiv:2609.01866, 'The Multiorbital Bivariate Chromatic Polynomial'] Let $\Gamma$ be a finite graph and let $G\leq\Aut(\Gamma)$. Then
$c_G$ is constant on the conjugacy classes of $G$. Moreover, if
$g,h\in G$ are conjugate, then
\[
\Gamma/g\cong\Gamma/h
\]
and consequently
\[
P_{\Gamma/g}(x,y)
=
P_{\Gamma/h}(x,y).
\]

[Lem 13 of arXiv:2605.30779, '2605.30779'] Let \(U\subset\mathbb C\) be an open set, let \(x_0\in U\cap\mathbb R\), and assume that \(\{f_N\}_{N=1}^\infty\xrightarrow{\mathrm{mer}} f\) on \(U\). Suppose that \(x_0\) is not a pole of \(f\), and
  \begin{align*}
    f(x_0)= {}& 0, & f'(x_0) \neq {}& 0 .
  \end{align*}
  Then there exists \(\delta>0\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(N\), \(f_N\) has exactly one zero \(z_N\) in the disc \(\{z:|z-x_0|<\delta\}\), and \(z_N\to x_0\). Moreover,
  \[
    f_N'(z_N)\to f'(x_0).
  \]
  If, in addition, \(f_N(\overline z)=\overline{f_N(z)}\) on this disc, then \(z_N\in\mathbb R\).

[Definition Configuration of arXiv:2411.10586, 'A convergence framework for Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble\\ via pole evolution'] A \emph{configuration} on ${\mathbb R}$ is a Radon measure of the form
\[
\mu = \sum_{x\in P} \delta_{x},
\]
where $P$ is a finite or countable multiset consisting of elements in ${\mathbb R}$, and
\[
\mu(K) < \infty \quad \text{for every compact set } K \subset {\mathbb R}.
\]
That is, $\mu$ is a purely atomic Radon measure consisting of unit
masses at its atoms, with only finitely many atoms in each bounded region.
title: Configuration

Let d>=2 and let phi_d:[-1,1]->R be 1-Lipschitz with |phi_d(t)|<=1. For ReLU activation, or another activation satisfying Assumption 1 of Venturi-Jelassi-Ozuch-Bruna, the radial function f_d(x)=phi_d(||x||_2) on the Euclidean unit ball admits, for every 0<epsilon<1, uniform approximation by a one-hidden-layer neural network with N <= exp(O(epsilon^(-5) log(d/epsilon))) neurons. The maximum parameter magnitude can also be bounded at this exponential scale in the normalized setting. The constants are independent of d and epsilon and may depend on the fixed activation. This is depth 2 when the affine output is counted as a layer. For a general 1-Lipschitz radial profile on [0,1], subtract its value at zero, extend evenly, apply the normalized width result, and restore the value as an affine output constant; the bound on the restored bias must then include that offset. Corollary 13 already improves the earlier Safran-Eldan-Shamir exponent 9 to 5; neither optimality of 5 nor a joint polynomial-in-(d,1/epsilon) bound is asserted. The later paper's quantitative activation hypothesis must not be replaced by the earlier paper's weaker activation hypothesis.
d>=2; 0<epsilon<1
Normalized 1-Lipschitz radial profile with uniform absolute value <=1
Fixed ReLU activation, or the source's Assumption 1
Uniform approximation on the Euclidean unit ball; one hidden layer and affine output

i.i.d. non-negative edge weights tau_e on the nearest-neighbour lattice Z^d
E[tau_e^2] < infinity
P(tau_e = 0) < p_c(d), the critical probability for undirected nearest-neighbour bond percolation on Z^d
the law of tau_e is not concentrated at one point (non-degeneracy)
x a nonzero lattice point; no direction or curvature hypothesis is used

CONSTANT DEPENDENCE: C_1 and C_2 depend on the weight law F and on d only. They do not depend on x, on ||x||, or on the direction of x. The bound is direction-uniform.
METHOD: Kesten introduced the method of bounded differences to FPP; the survey sketches the argument through the Efron-Stein inequality, consuming E #Geo(0,x) <= C||x||_1 and the one-edge resampling bound T_i(0,x) - T(0,x) <= tau'_{e_i}.
EARLIER, WEAKER BOUND, same author: Kesten, 'Aspects of first passage percolation' (Saint-Flour XIV, Lecture Notes in Math. 1180, 1986), Theorem 5.16, gave Var T(0,ne_1) <= C(n / log^{1/p} n)^2 with p = 9d + 3 - only a logarithmic improvement on the trivial n^2 for bounded weights. Do not cite that for the linear bound.
NOTE ON C_1: the lower half of the sandwich is a CONSTANT, not a growing bound. The growing lower bound is Newman-Piza's B log n and it holds only in d = 2 and only under an extra atom condition - see the Newman-Piza node.
SOURCE: Kesten, 'On the speed of convergence in first-passage percolation', Ann. Appl. Probab. 3 (1993), 296-338. Statement read in Auffinger-Damron-Hanson, '50 years of first passage percolation', arXiv:1511.03262v2 (AMS University Lecture Series 68, 2017), theorem 'thm: kesten_variance', tex lines 1072-1082. Independently corroborated by the authors of arXiv:2604.01214, whose abstract attributes the O(n) variance upper bound to 'Kesten's O(n) upper bound (Ann. Appl. Probab., 1993)'.
VERIFICATION STATUS: survey-claim. Lane P4 did not read Kesten (1993) itself.
title: Kesten (1993): for i.i.d. first-passage percolation on Z^d, if E[tau_e^2] < infinity, P(tau_e = 0) < p_c(d), and the weight law is not concentrated at a single point, then there exist constants C_1, C_2 > 0 with C_1 <= Var T(0,x) <= C_2 ||x||_1 for every nonzero x in Z^d. The linear upper bound is what gives the fluctuation-exponent bound 0 <= chi(d) <= 1/2 in every dimension, and that upper bound on chi is still the best known unconditionally.

[Prop PropGLfiniteCharPolyEq of arXiv:2605.06429, '\large \bf $\mathsf{GL}_N(\mathbb{C})$ BROWNIAN MOTION AND STOCHASTIC PDE ON ENTIRE FUNCTI'] For any $N\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\theta\in\mathbb{R}$,
    $\mathfrak{gl}_{t;N}(z)$ satisfies the following equation
\begin{align}
    \mathrm{d}\mathfrak{gl}_{t;N}(z)
    =
\mathrm{d}\mathsf{M}^N_t(z;\mathfrak{gl})
       +\left[\frac{\theta}{2}z\partial_z\mathfrak{gl}_{t;N}(z)\mathrm{d}t
    -
    \frac{z^2}{2}\partial_{z}^2\mathfrak{gl}_{t;N}(z)\right]\mathrm{d}t,
\end{align}
where $\mathsf{M}^N\in \mathrm{C}(\mathbb{R}_+;\mathsf{H}(\mathbb{C}))$ and for all $z\in \mathbb{C}$, $t\mapsto \mathsf{M}_t^N(z;\mathfrak{gl})$ are continuous local martingales with covariation, for $z,w \in \mathbb{C}$,
\begin{equation}
\langle \mathsf{M}_t^N(z;\mathfrak{gl}),\mathsf{M}_t^N(w;\mathfrak{gl})\rangle=\frac{zw}{z-w}\int_0^t\left(\mathfrak{gl}_{s;N}(z)\partial_w\mathfrak{gl}_{s;N}(w)-\mathfrak{gl}_{s;N}(w)\partial_z\mathfrak{gl}_{s;N}(z)\right)\mathrm{d}s.
\end{equation}

body:
[Definition 1 (Total variation cutoff) of arXiv:2608.15914, 'Absorption cutoff and stationary singularities for rounded Gaussian random dynamical syste'] Let $\mathcal I\subset\R$, and let $r_\ast\in[-\infty,\infty]$ belong to the
  closure of $\mathcal I$ in the extended real line. For each $r\in\mathcal I$, let $P_r$ be a
  Markov kernel on a measurable space $E_r$, let $\pi_r$ be an invariant
  probability measure, and let $x_r\in E_r$. Set
  \begin{equation}
    d_r(t)
    :=
    \norm{P_r^t(x_r,\cdot)-\pi_r}_{\TV},
    \qquad
    t\in\N_0 .
  \end{equation}
  For $u\in\R$, write
  $\lfloor u\rfloor_+:=\max\{0,\lfloor u\rfloor\}$.
  Let $t_r\to\infty$ and $a_r=o(t_r)$ with $a_r>0$. We say that
  $(P_r,x_r,\pi_r)_{r\in\mathcal I}$ has total variation cutoff at time $t_r$
  with window $a_r$ if
  \begin{equation}
    \lim_{c\to\infty}\liminf_{r\to r_\ast}
    d_r\left(\lfloor t_r-ca_r\rfloor_+\right)
    =
    1,
    \qquad
    \lim_{c\to\infty}\limsup_{r\to r_\ast}
    d_r\left(\lfloor t_r+ca_r\rfloor_+\right)
    =
    0.
  \end{equation}
  A function $F:\R\to[0,1]$ is a cutoff profile on the scale $a_r$ if, for
  every $c\in\R$,
  \begin{equation}
    d_r\left(\lfloor t_r+ca_r\rfloor_+\right)
    \to
    F(c),
    \qquad
    r\to r_\ast,
  \end{equation}
  where $F(c)\to1$ as $c\to-\infty$ and $F(c)\to0$ as $c\to\infty$.

  When no window is specified, cutoff at time $t_r$ means that, for every
  fixed $\delta\in(0,1)$,
  \begin{equation}
    d_r\left(\lfloor(1-\delta)t_r\rfloor_+\right)\to1,
    \qquad
    d_r\left(\lfloor(1+\delta)t_r\rfloor_+\right)\to0,
    \qquad
    r\to r_\ast.
  \end{equation}
  Equivalently, there exists $b_r=o(t_r)$ with $b_r>0$ such that the family
  has cutoff at time $t_r$ with window $b_r$.
title: Total variation cutoff

body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Try to derive transience from the quenched invariance principle route used for balanced walks, in the general case. Result: For balanced environments Lawler's argument uses the invariant measure of the environment process (from the maximum principle) to get a quenched CLT and then transience via the Green function decay; for general elliptic i.i.d. environments no invariant measure absolutely continuous with respect to P is known to exist (its existence is Open question 2.19's territory), so the route fails at the first step. An alternative is the Lyapunov-exponent route: transience follows if the quenched Green function G_omega(0,0) is finite a.s., which for a random walk with bounded-range transitions in d >= 3 follows from a lower bound on the spectral gap of the walk killed outside large boxes; in a random environment the killed walk's Perron eigenvalue could be arbitrarily close to 1 if the environment contains near-recurrent regions, and under (E) alone such regions exist at all scales with small probability. A quantitative bound needs the density of such traps to decay fast enough with their size, which is a large-deviation statement about the i.i.d. environment that I could not verify without (UE). Under (UE) the trap analysis of Bolthausen-Sznitman-Zeitouni suggests transience should hold but no proof exists. No result. Obstruction: No invariant measure for the environment process; trap density under mere ellipticity uncontrolled.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0043-transience-of-i-i-d-elliptic-rwre-in-dimensions-d-3

body:
[Definition def:backoff-cohorts of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and 
a distribution $\mathcal{D}$ on non-negative integers. 
Let $X$ be the {backoff process}  
with send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and birth distribution~$\mathcal{D}$.
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a finite set of cohorts. The $\mathcal{C}$-cohorts of~$X$  are defined as follows.
For every $t\geq 1$, partition the set  $\mathbf{n}^{X}(t)$ of balls born at time $t$ 
by choosing a cohort~$D\in \mathcal{C}$ uniformly at random for each ball,
and letting $\mathbf{n}^{X^D}(t)$ be the balls in~$\mathbf{n}^X(t)$ that choose cohort~$D$.
 The cohorts have no effect on the evolution of the backoff process -- they will be  useful only for accounting in proofs.
For each $t\geq 1$, each $j\geq 0$, and each $D\in \mathcal{C}$, define
\begin{align*}
\newsym{b-j-X-D}{balls in bin~$j$ after step~$t$ in cohort~$D$, Def~(def:backoff-cohorts of the paper)}{\mathbf{b}_j^{X^D}(t)} &= \mathbf{b}_j^{X}(t) \cap \cup_{t'=1}^{t} \mathbf{n}^{X^D}(t'),\\
\newsym{B-j-X-D}{balls in bin~$j$ before sends at~$t$ in cohort~$D$, Def~(def:backoff-cohorts of the paper)}{\mathbf{B}_j^{X^D}(t)} &= \mathbf{B}_j^{X}(t) \cap \cup_{t'=1}^{t} \mathbf{n}^{X^D}(t'),\\
\newsym{s-j-X-D}{sends from bin~$j$ at step~$t$ in cohort~$D$, Def~(def:backoff-cohorts of the paper)}{\mathbf{s}_j^{X^D}(t)} &= \mathbf{s}_j^{X}(t) \cap \cup_{t'=1}^{t} \mathbf{n}^{X^D}(t'),\\
\newsym{e-j-X-D}{escapes from bin~$j$ at step~$t$ in cohort~$D$, Def~(def:backoff-cohorts of the paper)}{\mathbf{e}_j^{X^D}(t)} &= \mathbf{e}_j^{X}(t) \cap \cup_{t'=1}^{t} \mathbf{n}^{X^D}(t').
\end{align*}
The respective sizes of these are $b_j^{X^D}(t)$, $B_j^{X^D}(t)$, 
$s_j^{X^D}(t)$, and $e_j^{X^D}(t)$.
title: Definition def:backoff-cohorts of arXiv:2602.21315

[Lemma 121 (Properties of $\CHOVgeotodoublenull$ on the closure of $\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] }$ and quasi-convexity] 

		The following results hold.
		
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item $\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot]}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}$ 
				is precompact in the topology of the geometric coordinates $(t,u,x^2,x^3)$.
			\item The change of variables map $\CHOVgeotodoublenull(t,u,x^2,x^3) = (\ubar,u,x^2,x^3)$
				extends to a $C^{1,1}$ diffeomorphism on the closure of
				$\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}$,
				which we denote by $\mbox{\upshape cl} \left(\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]} \right)$.
				Moreover,
				 $\mbox{\upshape cl} \left(\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]} \right)
				= \characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot]}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}$,
				and
				$\CHOVgeotodoublenull\left(\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot]}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}\right) 
			= [\leftubar,\ubarboot] \times [\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2] \times \mathbb{T}^2$.
		\item The following estimates hold for the extended maps:
		\begin{align}
				\frac{1}{2} \blowupdeltadoublenull	
				&
				\leq
				\geop{t} \ubar
				\leq 
				\frac{3}{2} \blowupdeltadoublenull,
				&&
				\mbox{on } \characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot]}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}.   \\
				\frac{3}{4} \blowupdeltadoublenull	
				&
				\leq
				\Lunit \ubar

				\frac{5}{4} \blowupdeltadoublenull,
				&&
				\mbox{on } \characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot]}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}.   	
		\end{align}
		\item 	\begin{align} 
				\nullgeop{\ubar} t 
				& =
				\mydet \left(d_{\textnormal{null}} \CHOVgeotodoublenull \right)
				\approx 1,
				&&
				\mbox{on } [\leftubar,\ubarboot] \times [\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2] \times \mathbb{T}^2,
		\end{align}
		\item \begin{align}
							\left\| 
								\CHOVgeotodoublenull
							\right\|_{C_{\textnormal{geo}}^{1,1}(\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot]}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]})}
							& \leq C,
								 
									\\
							\left\| 
								\CHOVgeotodoublenull^{-1}
							\right\|_{C_{\textnormal{null}}^{1,1}([\leftubar,\ubarboot] \times [\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2] \times \mathbb{T}^2)}
							& \leq C,
							
								\\

							\right\|_{C_{\textnormal{geo}}^{0,1}\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot]}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]})}
							& \leq C \auxbootsmall. 
							
						\end{align}
				\item (\textbf{Quasi-convexity of} 
				$\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot]}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}$). 
					For every pair of points 
					$q_1,q_2 \in [\leftubar,\ubarboot] \times [\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2] \times \mathbb{T}^2$,
					we have:
					\begin{align} 
						\textnormal{dist}_{\textnormal{flat}}
						\left(\CHOVgeotodoublenull^{-1}(q_1),\CHOVgeotodoublenull^{-1}(q_2) \right)

					standard Euclidean distance between $q_1$ and $q_2$ in the flat space

					Moreover, $\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot]}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}$ is quasi-convex.\footnote{Here,

[Lem lem-unstable-ssl of arXiv:2411.06301, 'Inverting the operation of conditioning a branching process on extinction'] Fix $m\in\mathbbm N$. 
\begin{enumerate}[$(i)$]
\item Let $\lambda \in [0,\infty)^d \setminus \{0\}$ and assume that $\limsup_{r \to\infty} | g^{(r m )}(\lambda)| < \infty$. 
If $\eta \in [0,\infty)^d$ such that $\eta < \lambda$, then $\lim_{r \to\infty} |g^{(r m)}(\eta)| = 0$.  
\item Let $\lambda \in [0,\infty)^d \setminus \{0\}$ and assume that $\limsup_{r \to\infty} | g^{(r m)}(\lambda)| > 0 $. 
If $\eta \in [0,\infty)^d$ such that $\eta > \lambda$, then $\limsup_{r \to\infty} |g^{(r m)}(\eta)| = \infty$.  
\end{enumerate}

[Defn 6 of arXiv:2606.21778, 'Pontryagin Maximum Principle in Free Probability Theory'] A function 
	$f:\mathcal{A} \rightarrow \mathcal{A}$ is called  locally operator Lipschitz in $L_p(\varphi),~1\leq p \leq \infty$, if there is a constant $L_f(K), K>0$ such that
	$$
	\|f(X_1)-f(X_2)\|_p\leq L_f(K)\|X_1-X_2\|_p,
	$$
	for all $\|X_i\|_p \leq K, i=1,2$.
	$f$ is called globally operator Lipschitz in $L_p(\varphi)$, if $L_f$ does not depend on $K$.

body:
Bounded-spectrum specialization of Pourkamali-Macris Theorem4. Let N,M tend to infinity with N<=M, N/M->alpha in(0,1], and M/N bounded. Let S_N=U_N*Sigma_N*V_N^T be a real N by M biorthogonally invariant signal, where U_N,V_N are independent Haar orthogonal matrices independent of the singular values in Sigma_N. Assume a deterministic K<infinity bounds ||S_N||_op almost surely for every N. Suppose the empirical singular-value probability laws converge almost surely weakly to a deterministic probability density mu on[0,K]. Let bar_mu be its symmetrization to R. Require integral integral log|x-y| dbar_mu(x)dbar_mu(y)>-infinity and integral log|x| dbar_mu(x)>-infinity; the second moment is finite. For fixed lambda>0 observe Y_N=sqrt(lambda)*S_N+Z_N, where the entries of Z_N are iid N(0,1/N), independently of S_N. Define I_{N,M}(A,B)=E_{U,V} exp(N*Tr(A^T*U*B*V^T)) with independent normalized Haar U,V. Let J_lambda be the deterministic limiting value of log I_{N,M}(sqrt(lambda)*S_N,Y_N)/(N*M), supplied by the rectangular spherical-integral asymptotics for these limiting spectral laws. Then lim I(S_N;Y_N)/(N*M)=lambda*alpha*integral x^2 mu(x)dx-J_lambda, with mutual information in nats. The uniform operator-norm cap is an explicit additional restriction of this card, implying source Assumption3 and making the spectral approximation uniformly integrable. Source Assumption2, including density and logarithmic integrability, is retained. This card does not supply an extension to limiting spectral atoms or general non-rotationally-invariant factor priors.
Proportional dimensions with N/M->alpha in(0,1].
Biorthogonally invariant signal independent of iid Gaussian noise of variance1/N.
Deterministic uniform operator-norm bound: an explicit restriction of this source specialization.
Deterministic limiting singular-value density with compact support, finite logarithmic energy and finite log moment.
Fixed lambda>0; natural logarithms and N*M information normalization.

[Lemma lem:aligned-perfect of arXiv:2601.07045, 'From Continuous to Discrete: \\ a No-U-Turn Sampler for Permutations'] Fix $1\le i<j\le n$ and let $\eta\in\Omega_{ij}$ with $\ord(\eta)=2m$, so that
$\eta^{m}=\tau_{ij}$. For $\sigma\in S_n$ set $\sigma' := \sigma \circ \tau_{ij}$ and
recall the orbit notation
\[
  X_t := \sigma\eta^{t},\qquad
  Y_t := \sigma'\eta^{t},\qquad t\in\mathbb{Z}.
\]
Then for all $t\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
  Y_t = X_{t+m},
\]
so the two length-$2m$ orbits $\{X_t\}_{t=0}^{2m-1}$ and
$\{Y_t\}_{t=0}^{2m-1}$ coincide up to the fixed index shift $m$. In
particular, for any window $W\subset\{0,\dots,2m-1\}$ the categorical laws
of $X_T$ and $Y_{T'}$ with weights proportional to $w(X_t)$ and $w(Y_t)$
can be coupled with total variation distance~$0$ by taking $T$ and
$T' = T+m \pmod{2m}$.
title: Perfect coupling in the aligned case

body:
[Theorem main_thm_2 of arXiv:2605.10491, 'Zero-couplings of infinite measures with cyclically monotone support and multivariate regu'] Let $P$ and $Q$ in $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ be regularly varying probability measures with auxiliary functions $b_1$ and $b_2$, indices $\alpha_1 > 0$ and $\alpha_2 > 0$, and limit measures $\mu$ and $\nu$ in $\mathrm{M}_{0}(\mathbb{R}^d)$, respectively. 
    Let $\pi \in \Pi_{\mathrm{cm}}(P,Q)$ with $\operatorname{spt} \pi \subset \partial \psi$ for some closed convex function $\psi : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R} \cup \left\{\infty\right\}$. 
    
    
    If we further assume that
    
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item $\mu$ vanishes on sets of Hausdorff dimension not larger than $d-1$,
        \item         $
        \forall y \in \operatorname{spt}\nu\setminus \left\{0\right\}:
        \exists x \in \operatorname{spt}\mu:
         \langle{x,y}\rangle>0
        $,
    \end{enumerate}
    then we have the following properties:
    
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item
    $\Gamma_{0,\mathrm{cm}}(\mu,\nu)$ is a singleton with single element $\gamma= ( \operatorname{Id} \times \nabla\bar{\psi})_{\#}\mu$ for some closed convex function $\bar{\psi}$ satisfying $\operatorname{spt} \gamma \subset \partial \bar{\psi}$ and $\bar{\psi}(0) = \inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d} \bar{\psi}(x) < \infty$.
    Moreover, $\gamma$ is proper, so that $\gamma = \operatorname{res} \rbr{(\operatorname{Id} \times \nabla\bar{\psi})_{\#}\mu}$ and $\nu = \operatorname{res} \rbr{(\nabla\bar{\psi})_{\#}\mu}$.

    \item
    Writing $V = \operatorname{int} \left(\operatorname{spt} \mu\right)$ and $B(t) = \operatorname{diag}(b_1(t) 1_d, b_2(t) 1_d)$ for $t > 0$, we have, as $t \to \infty$,
    \begin{align}
    
        t \, \operatorname{res}\pi(B(t) \,\cdot\,) &\raisebox{-0.5pt}{\,\scriptsize$\stackrel{\raisebox{-0.5pt}{\mbox{\tiny $0$}}}{\longrightarrow}$}\, \gamma 
        &&\text{in $\mathrm{M}_{0}(\reals^d\times\reals^d)$}, \\
    
        (B(t)^{-1} \partial \psi) \llcorner V
        
        &\raisebox{-0.5pt}{\,\scriptsize$\stackrel{\raisebox{-0.5pt}{\mbox{\tiny $\mathcal{F}$}}}{\longrightarrow}$}\, \left( \partial\bar{\psi} \right) \llcorner V  
        && \text{in $\mathcal{F}(V\times\mathbb{R}^d)$}.
    \end{align}

    \item
    The measure $\gamma$ is homogeneous in the sense that, writing $E = \operatorname{diag}(\alpha_{1}^{-1} 1_d, \alpha_{2}^{-1} 1_d)$, for all $\lambda > 0$, we have
    \begin{align}
        
        \gamma(\lambda^{-E}\,\cdot\,) &= \lambda \gamma,
        \\
        
        \lambda^E \operatorname{spt} \gamma &= \operatorname{spt} \gamma.
    \end{align}
    

    \item
    The gradient $\nabla\bar{\psi}$ is defined and determined uniquely $\mu$-almost everywhere. We have
	\begin{equation}
		
    	\nabla\bar{\psi}(\lambda x) = \lambda^{\alpha_1/\alpha_2} \,\nabla\bar{\psi}(x), 
        \qquad \lambda > 0,
    \end{equation}
	for $\mu$-almost every $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$. Moreover, the function $\bar{\psi}$ may be modified such that $\bar{\psi}(0)= 0$; then it is determined uniquely $\mu$--almost everywhere and satisfies
	\begin{equation}
         
    	\bar{\psi}(\lambda x) = \lambda^{\alpha_1/\alpha_2+1} \, \bar{\psi}(x),
    	\qquad \lambda \geqslant 0,
    \end{equation}
	for $\mu$-almost every $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$.
    
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Regular variation and monotone transport

body:
[Theorem thm:main-mixing of arXiv:2601.07045, 'From Continuous to Discrete: \\ a No-U-Turn Sampler for Permutations'] Let $K$ be the shiftable kernel from Definition~(def:shiftable-kernel of the paper), 
with stationary distribution $P_\beta$, and let $(I,J)$ be chosen uniformly from $\{(i,j):1\le i<j\le n\}$ at each step. Assume that the energy $E$ is Lipschitz with respect to the Cayley distance, i.e.
\begin{equation}

  |E(\pi)-E(\rho)|
  \;\le\;
  L_E\, d_{\mathrm{Cay}}(\pi,\rho)
  \qquad\text{for all }\pi,\rho\in S_n.
\end{equation}
In particular, whenever $\pi$ and $\rho$ differ by one transposition
($d_{\mathrm{Cay}}(\pi,\rho)=1$) we have $|E(\pi)-E(\rho)|\le L_E$.
Then for every adjacent pair $(\sigma,\sigma \circ \tau_{ij})$ there exists a one-step coupling $(U,V)$ of $K(\sigma,\cdot)$ and $K(\sigma \circ \tau_{ij},\cdot)$ such that
\[
  \mathbb{E}\bigl[d_{\mathrm{Cay}}(U,V)\bigr]
  \;\le\;
  \delta(\beta)
  \;:=\;
  \Bigl(1-\frac{2}{n(n-1)}\Bigr)
  \Bigl[\,1 + (D_{\mathrm{cross}}-1)\,\tanh(\beta L_E)\Bigr].
\]
When $\delta(\beta)<1$, the path–coupling condition (equation eq:edge-contraction of the paper) holds with $\rho=d_{\mathrm{Cay}}$ and $e^{-\alpha}=\delta(\beta)$. Consequently, for all $t\ge 0$,
\[
  \max_{\sigma\in S_n}
  \bigl\|K^t(\sigma,\cdot)-P_\beta\bigr\|_{\TV}
  \;\le\;
  D_{\max}\,\delta(\beta)^{\,t},
\]
and for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ the $\varepsilon$–mixing time satisfies
\[
  t_{\mathrm{mix}}(\varepsilon)
  \;\le\;
  \frac{\log D_{\max} + \log(1/\varepsilon)}{-\log\delta(\beta)}.
\]

body:
[Lemma eq:positive-time-local-density-equivalence of arXiv:2608.16119, 'Fully nonlinear parabolic equations under a fixed reference diffusion: weighted \texorpdfs'] Under Assumption~(ass:reference-diffusion of the paper), there is a function
$\varrho\in C((0,T]\times\mathbb R^d)$, locally H\"older continuous on $Q$, such
that
\begin{equation*}
 \mu_t(\,\mathrm d x)=\varrho(t,x)\,\mathrm d x,
 \qquad \varrho(t,x)>0,
 \qquad (t,x)\in(0,T]\times\mathbb R^d.
\end{equation*}
For every $0<\varepsilon<T$ and $K\Subset\mathbb R^d$,
\begin{equation}
 0<\inf_{(t,x)\in[\varepsilon,T]\times K}\varrho(t,x)
 \leq\sup_{(t,x)\in[\varepsilon,T]\times K}\varrho(t,x)<\infty.
 
\end{equation}
Consequently, Lebesgue measure and the occupation measure $\mathfrak m$ are
locally equivalent on every positive-time cylinder.
