ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Controlled generators, exact finite-state diagnostic, coupling, renewal reward or capacity comparison Result: For exponential sizes with a common rate mu, every nonidling policy has the same queue-count death rate mu*min(m,k), so scheduling is immaterial for that special law. With nonexponential sizes the departure intensity becomes sum_i h(a_i) over served jobs, and the age vector has policy-dependent drift. Thus queue count ceases to close: two states with equal m but different service ages can have different next-departure laws. A proposed extension of the exponential argument must retain this age information and its effect on future capacity. Check: Independent exponential residuals survive conditioning unchanged, deriving the special-case death rate. For a deterministic size, an age just below completion and age zero have distinct completion times despite the same queue count, checking failure of closure. Obstruction: No optimal age-vector control is constructed. The reduction supplies a known special case and an obstruction to extending its proof.

[Definition defa of arXiv:2604.11412, 'Stability of invariant measures of the stochastic Landau-Lifshitz-Bloch equation with vani'] Given 
  $ \mathbf{u}_0 \in H^1({\mathbb R}^2)$,
  $\varepsilon\in [0,1]$, $\delta\in(0,1]$ and 
  $T>0$,
   a  
 continuous     $H^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$-valued  $\mathcal{F}_t$-adapted
 process $\mathbf{u}^{\varepsilon,\delta}$
   is called a solution of (equation 1.3* of the paper) if 
$$
 \mathbf{u}^{\varepsilon, \delta}\in 
L^2(\Omega; L^\infty(0,T; H^1(\mathbb{R}^2)))
\cap
L^2(\Omega; L^2(0,T; H^3(\mathbb{R}^2)))
 $$ 
such that for all $t\in [0,T]$,   $\mathrm{P}$-almost 
surely,
\begin{align*}
&\mathbf{u}^{\varepsilon, \delta}(t)=\mathbf{u}_0+\int_{0}^{t}\Delta \mathbf{u}^{\varepsilon, \delta}(s)ds-\int_{0}^{t}\delta\Delta^2 \mathbf{u}^{\varepsilon,\delta}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\mathbf{u}^{\varepsilon,\delta}(s)\times \Delta \mathbf{u}^{\varepsilon,\delta}(s)ds\nonumber\\
&\quad-\int_{0}^{t}(1+|\mathbf{u}^{\varepsilon,\delta}(s)|^{2})\mathbf{u}^{\varepsilon,\delta}(s)ds
+\frac{\varepsilon^2}{2}\sum_{k= 1}^\infty
\int_{0}^{t}(\mathbf{u}^{\varepsilon,\delta}(s)\times \mathbf{f}_k)\times \mathbf{f}_kds
+\varepsilon\sum_ {k= 1}^\infty\int_{0}^{t}(\mathbf{u}^{\varepsilon,\delta}(s)\times \mathbf{f}_k+\mathbf{f}_k)d W_k 
\end{align*}
in   
$H^{-1}(\mathbb{R}^2 )$.
title: Definition defa of arXiv:2604.11412

body:
[Definition def:double-overlap-partner of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] Column $j'$ of a matrix $M$ 
is a \textcolor{PineGreen}{\emph{double-overlap partner}} of $j$ if
\begin{equation}

\bigl|\operatorname{supp}M_{\cdot j}
\cap
\operatorname{supp}M_{\cdot j'}\bigr|\ge2.
\end{equation}

For a deterministic sequence of matrices  
\(
M^{(k)} \in \mathbb{R}^{k \times n_k}
\)
for $k \in \mathbb{N}$, 
we say that it satisfies
the \textcolor{PineGreen}{\emph{local sparse double-overlap condition}} if
there are sets
\[
\mathcal G_k\subseteq[n_k]
\quad \mbox{ and } \quad \varepsilon_k \searrow 0
\]
such that
\[
|\mathcal G_k|=(1-o(1))n_k
\]
and, for every $j\in\mathcal G_k$,
\[
\left|
\left\{
j'\in[n_k]\setminus\{j\}:
\bigl|\operatorname{supp}M^{(k)}_{\cdot j}
\cap
\operatorname{supp}M^{(k)}_{\cdot j'}\bigr|\ge2
\right\}
\right|
\le
\varepsilon_k\,\frac{n_k}k.
\]
title: Double-overlap

[Lemma lem:witness-density of arXiv:2605.21744, 'Return Probability for the Switch--Walk--Switch Lamplighter Walk on a Regular Tree'] Let \(P_\omega\) be a bounded self-adjoint equivariant random operator on
\(\ell^2(T_d)\). Let \(W_\omega\subseteq V\) be an equivariant random set,
and let \(Q_\omega\) be multiplication by \(\mathbf 1_{W_\omega}\). Fix
\(E\in\mathbb R\). Suppose that
\[
        \mathbf 1_{[E,\infty)}
        \bigl((1-Q_\omega)P_\omega(1-Q_\omega)\bigr)
        =
        0
        \qquad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Then
\[
        \tau\bigl(\mathbf 1_{[E,\infty)}(P_\omega)\bigr)
        \le
        \tau(Q_\omega)
        =
        \mathbb P(o\in W_\omega).
\]
If the same hypothesis holds with \(P_\omega\) replaced by \(-P_\omega\),
then
\[
        \tau\bigl(\mathbf 1_{(-\infty,-E]\cup [E,\infty)}(P_\omega)\bigr)
        \le
        2\mathbb P(o\in W_\omega).
\]

    \item  Let $\mathcal{T}_s$ (\textit{the truncation event}) be the event that for any $1\leq s<i\leq n$ we have
    \[|\boldsymbol{v}_i(s)|\leq 10\sqrt{\frac{\log d}{d}}.\]
    \item  Let $\Pi_s$ (\textit{the projection event}) be the event that
    \[ \Big| \|\pi_s(\boldsymbol{v}_i)\|_2^2-\frac{s}{d}\Big|\leq 10\frac{\sqrt{n\log d}}{d}\text{ for all $s<i\leq n,$ and }  \big|\langle \pi_s(\boldsymbol{v}_i),\pi_s(\boldsymbol{v}_j)\rangle\big|\leq 10\frac{\sqrt{n\log d}}{d}\text{ for all $s<i<j\leq n$}.\]
\end{enumerate}
Finally, set $\mathcal{F}=\bigwedge_{s=1}^n(\mathcal{T}_s\wedge \Pi_s)$.
title: Vector event $\cF$.

Let N be a discrete phase-type absorption count supported on positive integers, with transient substochastic matrix P and initial probability row eta. If X is the continuous phase-type time with subgenerator P-I and the same initial law, then E[X]=E[N], E[X^2]=E[N^2]+E[N], and SCV(N)=SCV(X)-1/E[N]. Thus equality of the discrete and continuous second moments is false. For P=[[0,1/2],[1/2,0]] and eta=(1/2,1/2), N is geometric with mean2, second moment6 and SCV1/2; X has mean2, second moment8 and SCV1. The claim in He2021 section4.2 that the same SCV>=1 bound transfers is therefore false under its stated PH construction. This is a convention check, not an originality claim.

body:
Let (Z_n) be a Galton-Watson branching process with Z_0 = 1 and offspring distribution (p_k)_{k >= 0} having generating function f(s) = sum_k p_k s^k and mean m = sum_k k p_k, assumed finite. Let q = P( Z_n = 0 for some n ) be the extinction probability. Then q is the SMALLEST root in [0,1] of the equation f(s) = s, and: if m < 1 (subcritical) then q = 1; if m = 1 (critical) then q = 1 UNLESS p_1 = 1, in which case the process is deterministic and never dies; if m > 1 (supercritical) then q < 1. The critical case is the one that gets misquoted: a critical branching process dies out almost surely even though E[Z_n] = 1 for every n, so the population is not uniformly integrable and the mean survives while the process does not. Excluding the degenerate p_1 = 1 is necessary. A second standard trap: q < 1 does not mean the process survives with probability 1 - it survives with probability exactly 1 - q, and conditioned on survival Z_n grows geometrically at rate m. [standard; e.g. Athreya and Ney, Branching Processes, Chapter I, or Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, 5th ed., Section 4.3.3]
offspring distribution with finite mean m
Z_0 = 1 (otherwise q is raised to the power of the initial population)
the critical conclusion excludes the degenerate case p_1 = 1

To see it is the SMALLEST fixed point, let r be any fixed point and show by induction that P(Z_n = 0) <= r. For n = 1, P(Z_1 = 0) = p_0 = f(0) <= f(r) = r since f is nondecreasing on [0,1]. If P(Z_n = 0) <= r then P(Z_{n+1} = 0) = f(P(Z_n = 0)) <= f(r) = r. Since P(Z_n = 0) increases to q, we get q <= r. Now the shape of f: on [0,1], f is nondecreasing and convex, with f(1) = 1 and f'(1^-) = m. Excluding the degenerate cases p_0 = 0, where q = 0 trivially, and p_1 = 1, where f(s) = s identically, f is STRICTLY convex, so f(s) = s has at most two roots in [0,1], one of which is 1. If m <= 1 then f(s) > s for every s in [0,1), because f(1) = 1 and the strictly convex f lies strictly above its chord to the point (1,1) with slope f'(1^-) = m <= 1; hence the only fixed point is 1 and q = 1. body:
In a Hilbert space H a sequence (x_n) converges weakly to x, written x_n ⇀ x, if ⟨x_n, y⟩ → ⟨x, y⟩ for every y ∈ H; by the Riesz representation theorem this is convergence against every bounded linear functional. The weak topology on H is the coarsest topology making every functional x ↦ ⟨x, y⟩ continuous. Norm convergence implies weak convergence; the converse fails in infinite dimensions (an orthonormal sequence e_n converges weakly to 0 while ||e_n|| = 1). Weak limits are unique; weakly convergent sequences are norm-bounded (Banach–Steinhaus); the norm is weakly lower semicontinuous (||x|| ≤ liminf ||x_n|| when x_n ⇀ x); norm-closed convex sets are weakly closed (Mazur), and in infinite dimensions the weak closure of the unit sphere is the closed unit ball. If x_n ⇀ x and ||x_n|| → ||x|| then x_n → x in norm (Radon–Riesz property of Hilbert spaces). Bounded operators preserve weak convergence; compact operators turn weak convergence into norm convergence.

In a general normed space X the weak topology is the coarsest topology making every f ∈ X* continuous, and the weak-* topology on X* is the coarsest making every evaluation f ↦ f(x), x ∈ X, continuous. The weak-* topology on X* is in general coarser than the weak topology of X* (which is induced by X**); the two coincide when X is reflexive. In a Hilbert space, after identifying H* with H, weak and weak-* convergence are the same notion.
H a real or complex Hilbert space; X a normed space for the general remarks
title: Weak convergence and the weak / weak-* topologies

[Prop 11 (Independent Poisson comparison) of arXiv:2606.20816, 'Spectral Properties of Dense Barab\'asi--Albert Graphs'] For $k > t_0$ and $j < k$, define
\[
\bar \lambda_{k j}
\ := \
\E\left[\widetilde M_{k j}\right]
\ = \
\E\left[M_{k j}\right].
\]
Let $P_{k j}$ be independent random variables with
\[
P_{k j}
\ \sim \
\mathrm{Poisson}\left(\bar \lambda_{k j}\right),
\qquad
k > t_0,\ j < k.
\]
Define the symmetric random matrix $H$ as
\[
H_{k j}
\ := \
\frac{P_{k j}-\bar \lambda_{k j}}{\sqrt m},
\qquad
H_{j k}
\ := \
H_{k j},
\qquad
k > t_0,\ j < k,
\]
and set $H_{k j}=0$ for entries in the initial clique, i.e. when $k \le t_0$ and $j \le t_0$. Then, for every fixed $z \in \mathbb{H}$,
\[
\abs{s_{\widetilde Y}\left(z\right)-s_H\left(z\right)}
\ \to \
0
\]
in probability. Consequently, $\widetilde Y$ and $H$ have the same limiting spectral measure.

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2604.24664, 'Absolute continuity of Rosenblatt measures'] Let $(B_t)_{t \in [0, T]}$ be an $\FctT$-Wiener process. Let $\phi: [0, T] \times \Omega \to \Rbb$ be an $\FctT$-progressively measurable process such that $\phi \in L^2([0, T])$ almost surely and assume that the process $(Z_t)_{t\in [0,T]}$ defined by
	\begin{equation}
		
		Z_t = \exp\left( - \int_0^t \phi_s \d{B_s} - \frac12 \int_0^t \phi^2_s \d{s} \right), \quad t \in [0, T],
	\end{equation}
	is an $\FctT$-martingale. Let $\tilde{\Pbb}$ be the probability measure on $(\Omega, \Fcal)$ defined by $\d{\tilde{\Pbb}} = Z_T \d{\Pbb}$. Then the process $(\tilde{B}_t)_{t \in [0, T]}$ defined by
	\[
		\tilde{B}_t = B_t + \int_0^t \phi_s \d{s}, \quad t \in [0, T],
	\]
	is an $\FctT$-Wiener process with respect to $\tilde{\Pbb}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2604.24664

Own work draft; proof (unaudited), no novelty established. For sufficiently small positive noisy radius a, full population DDPM GD initialized at a randomly rotated equilateral triple with the correct radius and plane converges almost surely to the teacher up to permutation. Away from the three unstable angles by delta, matched mean error O(a eta) is reached in O((h a^4)^-1(1+log(1/delta)+log(1/eta))) steps for 0<h<=h0/a^2, uniformly in d. Scope limits: Independent review pending. Uses corrected angular coefficient from C01 v3; no generic random initialization or finite-sample theorem in this claim.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:e767be6490ac7e0dd22a85699dc9939b70e59a554202d4911951f5a4708c9abc","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/e7/e767be6490ac7e0dd22a85699dc9939b70e59a554202d4911951f5a4708c9abc.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:e46b93d5bf149b2fff836bcc7c52bd70b1d1130f4c72842e2b881bd3fbe0cbc1","bundle_entry_key":"t309-c03","bundle_id":"population.t309-equilateral-ddpm-symmetry-breaking-drafts","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability, score matching, Gaussian mixture learning","draft":"w721/bundle_001.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.learning:equilateral-gaussian-population-ddpm-random-angle","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T309: a population GD symmetry-breaking step for equilateral triples

T309-w721-C02 v1 (invariance) and C03 v2 (population convergence).
Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty claim. The general empirical Target 2 remains open.

The next unpaid step is to reach this invariant family from a generic random triple in an unknown plane, or to replace exact population equivariance with an empirical argument. The initialization here is random in angle, has known radius and plane, and is exactly equilateral. These are substantive extra assumptions. It can be outside every componentwise warm-start basin.

## The population statement

Let the target be an equal-weight mixture N(a u_j,I_d), j=0,1,2, where u_j are the unit equilateral vectors in a known plane, centered at zero. Its orientation in that plane need not be known. Assume 0<a<=a_0 for a sufficiently small absolute constant. Parameterize the student by three unrestricted mean vectors m_j in R^d, using exactly Eq. (9) of Shah--Chen--Klivans. Train on the population DDPM objective at this fixed noise level, with all three means updated by ordinary Euclidean GD with the same step h.

Initialize m_j=a R_Theta u_j, where Theta is uniform on the circle, independently of the target orientation. There are absolute h_0,c,C>0 such that for 0<h<=h_0/a^2 the following hold:

1. Every iterate has m_j=a r_n R_{theta_n}u_j, with 1/2<r_n<2.
2. Except at the three exact unstable initial angles (a probability-zero event), the iterates converge to the true mean triple up to permutation.
3. If the initial angle is at distance at least delta from every unstable angle, then for 0<delta,eta<=1/10, after at most

       C/(h a^4) [1+log(1/delta)+log(1/eta)]

   iterations, the matched mean error is at most C a eta. Consequently the probability statement can be made 1-p by taking delta=pi p/3, or a smaller delta<=1/10. The dependence on d is absent at population level. This does not yet establish polynomial sample complexity or arbitrary random initialization.

The same statement applies to the high-noise training stage of a well-separated original mixture with center radius R: choose t so that R exp(-t)=a. Rescaling the recovered means multiplies the error by R/a. Learning to an arbitrary original mean error therefore requires eta of the corresponding order. This observation does not remove the known-plane and known-radius initialization assumptions.

## 1. The invariant family under unrestricted mean updates

Let Q be rotation by 2pi/3 in the target plane and identity on its orthogonal complement. The target law and population DDPM loss are invariant under Q. The objective is also invariant under permutations of the three student labels. Combining the rotation with the inverse cyclic label permutation gives an orthogonal linear action on the whole parameter space which fixes every configuration satisfying m_{j+1}=Q m_j (indices modulo 3).

For a differentiable function L invariant under an orthogonal map A, differentiating L(Ax)=L(x) gives grad L(Ax)=A grad L(x). If Ax=x, then A grad L(x)=grad L(x). Both a GD step and the gradient flow therefore preserve its fixed-point subspace.

There is another exact symmetry: reflection S which is identity on the target plane and minus identity on its orthogonal complement. At a planar configuration, every parameter is fixed by S, so the gradient is planar. Intersecting the two fixed-point subspaces leaves precisely

    m_j=Q^j z,    z in the target plane.

For z nonzero write z=a r R_theta u_0. This is the full radius-angle equilateral family. Its invariance is exact, holds for every a, and concerns the unrestricted population objective. In particular its proof does not assume that two spaces of the same dimension coincide: it explicitly solves the fixed-point equations. For d=2 the perpendicular reflection is unnecessary.

The radius-one angular circle alone is generally not invariant. Section 2 below gives F_r(1,theta)=(3a^6/4)(1-cos(3theta))+O(a^8), which is nonzero away from the aligned angles for sufficiently small a.

## 2. Uniform expansion with a variable radius

Let F_a(r,theta) denote the population excess score loss between this student and the target. Uniformly for r in [1/4,3], and with every fixed finite number of r,theta derivatives needed below,

    F_a(r,theta)=a^4 A4(r)+a^6 A6(r,theta)+O(a^8),                    (1)
    A4(r)=(r^2-1)^2/2,
    A6(r,theta)=(r^6+1-2r^3 cos(3theta))/8
                 -(r^2-1)(r^4-1)/2+(r^2-1)^2/4.                   (2)

The proof uses the same dominated Taylor argument as angular_landscape.md. In that argument the logit has magnitude at most 3|a| ||y|| instead of |a| ||y||. This still has Gaussian-integrable domination. It supplies any fixed derivative order, not merely a pointwise remainder.

For completeness, the score expansions through order four are

    b_student = a^2 r^2 y/2 + a^3 r^3 T_theta[y,y]/2
                  -a^4 r^4 y||y||^2/16 + O(a^5),
    b_target  = a^2 y/2 + a^3 T_0[y,y]/2
                  -a^4 y||y||^2/16 + O(a^5).

The teacher density relative to phi_2 is 1+a^2(||y||^2/4-1/2)+O(a^3). Squaring the score difference and integrating gives (1)--(2): the order-six contributions are the squared order-three term, the cross term between orders two and four, and the order-two teacher-density correction multiplying the squared order-two term. Their expectations respectively are

    (r^6+1-2r^3 cos(3theta))/8,
    -(r^2-1)(r^4-1)/2,
    (r^2-1)^2/4.

Odd powers again vanish by the exact a -> -a, y -> -y symmetry. The script scripts/check_angular.py verifies these Gaussian polynomial identities with exact symbolic arithmetic. It is not used to prove the domination.

Periodicity and reflection give, by the zero-preserving remainder argument in angular_landscape.md, uniformly on 1/2<=r<=2,

    F_theta(r,theta)=a^6 k_a(r,theta) sin(3theta),
    c <= k_a(r,theta) <= C.                                       (3)

Here the leading coefficient is 3r^3/4, bounded above and below on this annulus. Bounds on the remainder after two theta derivatives force its first derivative to vanish linearly at each n pi/3. This justifies the uniform division by the sine, including near its zeros.

Near r=1, the expansion and the exact identity F_r(1,0)=0 give

    F_r(r,0)=a^4 g_a(r)(r-1),       c<=g_a(r)<=C,                   (4)
    |F_r(r,theta)-F_r(r,0)|<=C a^6 theta^2                        (5)

for |r-1|<=1/10 and |theta|<=pi/3, interpreting theta relative to the nearest minimum. To check (4), F_rr(r,0)=2a^4(3r^2-1)+O(a^6) is positive throughout this radial neighborhood; apply the mean value theorem. For (5), the a^4 term is independent of theta, the mixed derivative F_{r theta theta} is O(a^6), and F_{r theta}(r,0)=0 by exact evenness; integrate twice in theta. All constants are absolute.

## 3. The exact discrete update

At an equilateral configuration, the symmetry from Section 1 implies that every gradient is the same linear combination of its own radial and tangential unit vectors v_j=R_theta u_j and Jv_j. Differentiating with respect to r and theta fixes the coefficients:

    grad_{m_j} L = F_r v_j/(3a) + F_theta Jv_j/(3ar).

Set

    A = r-h F_r/(3a^2),     B=-h F_theta/(3a^2 r).

Then ordinary GD on the three means gives the exact update

    r_next=sqrt(A^2+B^2),    theta_next=theta+atan2(B,A).             (6)

The Euclidean gradient is not the coordinate gradient of F in (r,theta). Formula (6) accounts for the induced metric and for the discrete tangential step's second-order radial effect.

## 4. Radial confinement and descent

On r in [1/4,3], the gradient in the z-coordinate of the invariant linear subspace is O(a^3), and its Hessian is O(a^2), by (1) and the chain rule away from z=0. The three-mean Euclidean metric on this subspace is 3 times the metric of z, which only changes absolute constants. Choose h_0 sufficiently small to satisfy the descent bound h<=1/(L a^2) and to make the largest possible one-step radial displacement from r in [0.9,1.1] less than 0.1. Both choices use uniform bounds on the larger annulus.

Initially r=1 and F_a=O(a^6). Suppose an iterate lies in [0.9,1.1] and has F_a<=C_0 a^6, where C_0 is an absolute bound for all initial angles. The step segment stays in [1/2,2] by the displacement bound, so the descent lemma applies along that segment. It gives F_next<=F_current. Equation (1) then implies

    (r_next^2-1)^2 <= C a^2,

because A6 and the remainder are uniformly bounded on the annulus. Thus |r_next-1|<=C' a. Decrease a_0 until C' a_0<0.1. This proves the induction and confinement. It also proves monotone descent. No assumption about a sublevel barrier preventing a discrete jump is needed; the step-segment bound was established first.

## 5. Angular convergence and rate

Confinement implies A is bounded above and below by positive absolute constants after further decreasing h_0 if needed. By (3) and (6), the angular displacement has the opposite sign to sin(3theta), and its absolute value lies between

    c h a^4 |sin(3theta)|    and    C h a^4 |sin(3theta)|.           (7)

Indeed |B/A|<=C h a^4<=C h_0 a^2, so arctan(|B/A|) is between |B/A|/2 and |B/A|. Make a_0 small enough that 3C h a^4<1/2. Since |sin(3theta)| is at most three times the distance to either neighboring zero of the sine, no step can cross a minimum or maximum. Every open angular basin is invariant.

The same geometric-growth and geometric-decay argument as in angular_landscape.md, now using h a^4 rather than h a^6, proves that the angle reaches distance eta from its basin's minimum in at most

    C/(h a^4) [1+log(1/delta)+log(1/eta)]

steps. It remains there and continues toward zero. An exact maximum is stationary in angle; it is excluded. There are exactly three such initial angles modulo 2pi, and their delta-neighborhood has probability 3delta/pi under a uniform angle.

## 6. Radius follows the angular convergence

Write e=r-1, and let theta be measured relative to the basin's minimum. From (4)--(5),

    F_r=a^4 g_a(r)e+f,       |f|<=C a^6 theta^2.

The relation sqrt(A^2+B^2)-A=B^2/(sqrt(A^2+B^2)+A) and A>=c>0 bound the radial correction by C h^2 a^8 theta^2. Since h a^2<=h_0, it is bounded by C h a^4 theta^2 (after adjusting an absolute constant). Shrinking h_0 so the radial linear factor is nonnegative, (6) gives

    |e_next| <= (1-c h a^2)|e| + C h a^4 theta^2.                  (8)

After the angular stage makes |theta|<=eta, iteration of (8) yields

    |e_{n+k}| <= (1-c h a^2)^k |e_n| + C' a^2 eta^2.

An additional C/(h a^2)[1+log(1/eta)] steps therefore makes |e|<=C'' eta. This is bounded by the iteration order asserted in the theorem since a<=a_0<1. The matched mean error is at most a(|e|+r |theta|)<=C a eta. Letting eta tend to zero proves convergence, and using the rate at a fixed eta proves the finite-time claim.

## Checks and scope

The proof uses equal weights, exact equilateral geometry, known centering and plane, and a population objective. Removing any of them breaks the fixed-point argument or the single-angle landscape reduction. At a=0 every student center in this initialization is zero and there is no angular signal, so the strict requirement a>0 is necessary. At an exact antipodal angle the gradient cannot choose a component labeling; this is why a measure-zero exception and a distance-from-saddles parameter appear. The dimension-independent reduction does not apply to an arbitrary initial triple with perpendicular components.

For an empirical objective, an individual sample set usually lacks the target's rotational invariance. Orbit augmentation by the known 120-degree rotation could preserve the invariant family, but the needed uniform gradient estimates and the resulting finite-sample convergence theorem are not supplied here. For an unknown plane, estimating and entering the plane is also unpaid. These are limitations of the result, not details covered by the population theorem.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:dd2cd7dabd7ec9f2c960407731e32a2f94dbb925d22de6cdbb0cfb15c3f46028","revision_digest":"sha256:460bfdb8aa909dad0a4cbe9a0d4ce027699c0cfb3f295b9b658f6abfc1d76314","source_id":"own-work:T309-w721-C03-v2","source_revision":"C03 version 2; saved 2026-10-20","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Theorem thm:learning_rate of arXiv:2608.24195, '\textbf{A Heterogeneous Mixture of Experts Framework for Interpretable Machine Learning}'] Under the multinomial softmax gating parametrization,
\[
  \frac{2A_t}{|C_t|} \geq 2.
\]
Consequently, every learning-rate sequence satisfying $0 < \gamma_t < 2$ guarantees
monotone ascent of the gating auxiliary function:
\[
  Q_{\mathrm{gate}}(\boldsymbol{\Theta}^{(t+1)})
  \geq Q_{\mathrm{gate}}(\boldsymbol{\Theta}^{(t)})
\]
for all~$t$. Hence, the resulting optimization procedure defines a valid generalized EM
algorithm [wu1983].

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2607.17662, 'On the Strong Law of Large Numbers under Sublinear Expectations'] \textnormal{(Chebyshev's inequality)}
		Let $f(x) > 0$ be a non-decreasing function on $\mathbb{R}$. Then for any $x$,

		V(X \geq x) \leq \frac{\mathbb{E}[f(X)]}{f(x)}, \qquad v(X \geq x) \leq \frac{\mathcal{E}[f(X)]}{f(x)}.
		\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Cor 32 of arXiv:2609.02879, 'On the cut locus of Hamilton--Jacobi equations I: structure and propagation via the touchi'] Let $H$ be a Tonelli Hamiltonian on $\T^n$ and let $\phi$ be a viscosity solution of \eqref{eq:HJs}.
	Then the following statements are true:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item If $\gamma: \mathbb{S}^1 \to \T^n$ is a periodic $(\phi,H)$-calibrated curve and $\gamma(t_0) \in \operatorname{Alex}(\phi)$ for some $t_0 \in \mathbb{S}^1$, then $\gamma(t) \in \operatorname{Alex}(\phi)$ for all $t \in \mathbb{S}^1$, and $Q(t)=D^2\phi(\gamma(t))$, $t \in \mathbb{S}^1$ is of class $C^1$ and satisfies the matrix Riccati equation \eqref{eq:Ricc}.
		\item  Suppose  $\cut(\phi)$ is closed. If $\gamma: (-\infty,0] \to \T^n$ is a $(\phi,H)$-calibrated curve and $\gamma(t_0) \in \operatorname{Alex}(\phi)$ for some $t_0\in(-\infty,0)$, then $\gamma(t) \in \operatorname{Alex}(\phi)$ for all $t \in (-\infty,0)$, and $Q(t)=D^2\phi(\gamma(t))$, $t \in (-\infty,0)$ is of class $C^1$ and satisfies the matrix Riccati equation \eqref{eq:Ricc}.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor 32 of arXiv:2609.02879

body:
[Proposition 52 (Sum/intersection duality) of arXiv:2606.29292, 'Intrinsic Gaussian Tensor Geometry and Random Operator Spectra'] Let $m\ge1$ and $1\le r\le2$.
The space $\mathfrak T_{m,r}^{\Sigma}$ is Banach, stochastic-leg
permutations act isometrically on it, and symmetrization is a contraction.
Common factorwise finite-rank projections act contractively and converge to
the identity in $\mathfrak T_{m,r}^{\Sigma}$; in particular, algebraic
kernels are dense.  The completion of $\mathcal K_{\mathrm{alg}}$ in
\eqref{eq:algebraic-low-cut-norm} is canonically and isometrically
$\mathfrak T_{m,r}^{\Sigma}$, and the analogous symmetric completion is
$\mathfrak W_{m,r}^{\Sigma}$.
Moreover,
\begin{equation}

 \mathfrak T_{m,2}^{\Sigma}=\mathfrak T_{m,2},
 \qquad
 \mathfrak W_{m,2}^{\Sigma}=\mathfrak W_{m,2}
\end{equation}
isometrically.  For $1<r<2$ and $r'=r/(r-1)$, the coefficient pairing
induces the conjugate-linear isometric isomorphism
\begin{equation}

 \mathfrak T_{m,r'}\longrightarrow
 (\mathfrak T_{m,r}^{\Sigma})^*,
 \qquad
 L\longmapsto\bigl[K\longmapsto\ip{K}{L}\bigr],
 \qquad
 \norm{K\mapsto\ip{K}{L}}_{(\mathfrak T_{m,r}^{\Sigma})^*}
 =\max_{S\subset[m]}\norm{\Flat_S(L)}_{\Sch_{r'}}.
\end{equation}
Finally, for $1\le r\le2$ the identity on algebraic kernels extends to
contractive inclusions
\begin{equation}

 \mathfrak T_{m,r}^{\cap}\longrightarrow\mathfrak T_{m,r}^{\Sigma},
 \qquad
 \mathfrak W_{m,r}^{\cap}\longrightarrow\mathfrak W_{m,r}^{\Sigma},
\end{equation}
with norm at most one.

[Theorem 10 (Gauge-invariant convergence statement) of arXiv:2608.30374, 'Compact and Infinite-Order Error Analysis\\ for Null-Space SVD Estimation'] Assume the boundary collisions are generic.  The spectral projector onto the
retained branch set \(\cI_q\) is analytic for \(|s|<\rho_q\), and its Taylor
series about zero converges to the exact SVD projector in that disk.  A
compatible analytic frame, including the recursions above, has truncation
error \(O(|s|^{K+1})\).  At \(|s|>\rho_q\), increasing \(K\) cannot make the
Taylor series converge to the SVD projector. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Gauge-invariant convergence statement

[Theorem descents technical of arXiv:2603.09008, 'On the statistics of random-to-top shuffles'] Let $K_n$ be a sequence of random variables satisfying the following assumptions.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $K_n/n\to a\in (0,1)$ in probability.
        \item $n^{-1/2}(K_n-\mathbb{E} K_n)\Rightarrow_d\mathcal{N}(0,\tau^2)$ for some fixed $\tau\in[0,\infty)$.
        \item $\operatorname{Var} K_n=O(n)$ and $\mathbb{E}[K_n]=an+o(\sqrt{n})$.
    \end{enumerate} 
    Let $U_i$ be iid continuous uniform on $(0,1)$. Set $T_n=\sum_{i=1}^{\lfloor K_n\rfloor -1}\, \1(U_i>U_{i+1})$. We have
    \[\frac{T_n-\mathbb{E} [T_n]}{\sqrt{n}}\Rightarrow_d\,\mathcal{N}\left(0,\frac{a}{12}+\frac{\tau^2}{4}\right).\]
title: Theorem descents technical of arXiv:2603.09008
Fair STIT

Independently checked proof (PASS w667 and w668): C004 v1. Partition compactly supported F into finite measurable cells, with exact masses b_j and enclosing coordinate boxes of maximum width h. Enumerate n-label multisets whose box-sum intervals contain n*mean(F), and form occupancy columns A_(j,a)=count of j divided by n. If F is n-CM then A lambda=b has a nonnegative solution. Conversely, feasible solutions along h tending to zero give couplings with exact marginals F and sum error at most n*h in each coordinate; compactness yields an exact n-mix. An exact dual vector with y^T A>=0 and y^T b<0 disproves continuous n-CM. Floating solver failures and inner point-grid infeasibility are not certificates. Finite outer-LP successes are numerical evidence only.
F Borel probability with compact support
Correct partition masses
Boxes enclose all cells
Mesh tends to zero for sufficiency
Exact dual verification required for refutation

[Theorem thm:downward of arXiv:2604.10214, 'Large deviations for maximum local time of simple random walk in dimensions \texorpdfstrin'] For any $\beta \in (0,1]$ and $u \in \mathbb{R}$, as $t \to \infty$ or $n \to \infty$, we have
\begin{align}
\mathbb{P}\bigl(\ell^*(t) \le \beta \cdot \gamma^{-1}\log t + u\bigr)
&= \exp\bigl\{-(1+o(1)) \gamma e^{-\gamma u} t^{1-\beta}\bigr\}, \\
\mathbb{P}\bigl(\xi^*(n) \le \beta \cdot \alpha \log n + u\bigr)
&\le \exp\bigl\{-(1+o(1)) c_{\beta,n,u}\gamma (1-\gamma)^u n^{1-\beta}\bigr\}. 
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Downward deviations

[Theorem thm:Main2 of arXiv:2606.19313, 'Stability of Khintchine-type inequalities via log-monotonicity'] Let $X$ be a symmetric random variable and $r_k=r_k(X)$. 

\begin{enumerate}
\item If $(r_k)$ is log-concave, then $X$ has the Schur-concave property for any even $p\geq 2$.\\

\item If $(r_k)$ is log-convex, then $X$ has the Schur-convex property for any even $p\geq 2$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2608.05931, 'Effective Lagrangian regularity and the uniqueness threshold for random H\"older velocity '] Let $\beta >0$ and $\alpha \in (0,1)$ such that
    \[\alpha + \beta >1 \quad \text{and} \quad \alpha + \beta/2 <1.\]
    Suppose $U:[0,1]\times\T^d\rightarrow \R^d$ is a $C^0([0,1],C^{\alpha-}(\T^d))$ multiscale finite range random velocity field; that is, $U$ satisfies Assumption~\ref{asmp:main for refreshing}, and~\eqref{eq:refreshing theorem hypothesis} holds for all $p \geq 1$.
    
    Then for all $\ep>0$ and $y \in \T^d$ there exists a random constant $M(y)$ such that $M(y) \in L^p_\omega$ for all $p \geq1$ and if $X^1, X^2$ are any solutions to~\eqref{eq:main refreshing ODE s} with $s=0$, then we have the (quasi)-stability estimate for all $t \in [0,1]$,
    \[d_{\T^d}(X^1_t, X^2_t) \leq M(y)t^{\frac{1-\alpha}{\beta(2 - 2\alpha - \beta)}-\ep}.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem: estimate of Kostka of arXiv:2604.23890, 'The Cutoff Profile for Random Transpositions on Repeated Cards in the Full Range of Parame'] Let $\lambda\vdash n$, and $r:=n-\lambda_1,r':=n-\lambda_1'$. Then, we have
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\lambda_1'>m$, then $K_{\lambda,(l^m)}=0$.
\item $K_{\lambda,(l^m)}\le m^r$. 
\item $K_{\lambda,(l^m)}\le\binom{n}{r}K_{\lambda^*,(\lfloor r/m\rfloor+1,\ldots,\lfloor r/m\rfloor+1,\lfloor r/m\rfloor,\ldots,\lfloor r/m\rfloor)}$. Here and from now on, for the partition $(\lfloor r/m\rfloor+1,\ldots,\lfloor r/m\rfloor+1,\lfloor r/m\rfloor,\ldots,\lfloor r/m\rfloor)$, there are $r-m\lfloor r/m\rfloor$ parts of size $\lfloor r/m\rfloor+1$, and $m\lfloor r/m\rfloor+m-r$ parts of size $\lfloor r/m\rfloor$.
\item $K_{\lambda,(l^m)}\le\binom{n}{r'}K_{\lambda^\bullet,(\lfloor r'/m\rfloor+1,\ldots,\lfloor r'/m\rfloor+1,\lfloor r'/m\rfloor,\ldots,\lfloor r'/m\rfloor)}$. Here and from now on, for the partition $(\lfloor r'/m\rfloor+1,\ldots,\lfloor r'/m\rfloor+1,\lfloor r'/m\rfloor,\ldots,\lfloor r'/m\rfloor)$, there are $r'-m\lfloor r'/m\rfloor$ parts of size $\lfloor r'/m\rfloor+1$, and $m\lfloor r'/m\rfloor+m-r'$ parts of size $\lfloor r'/m\rfloor$.
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2604.01257, '2604.01257'] Let Basic Axioms hold with $\gamma<0$ and let $\mu:=2\delta-\nu>0$. If ${C_{\textsf{L}}}=|\gamma|$
    in {(\ref{IIB4.3})}, then
\begin{equation}                
    {{e}^{\mathcal{T}(t)}}\mathcal{P}(t;s)=\mathcal{U}(s)\cdot\left(1+\zeta(t;s)\right),
\end{equation}
    where the limiting GF $\mathcal{U}(s)$ has the form
\begin{equation}                
    \mathcal{U}(s)=\exp\left\{\frac{1}{{(1-s)}^{|\gamma|}}+
    \int_{{1}/{(1-s)}}^{\infty}{\frac{|\gamma|-\textsf{L}(u)}{{u^{1-|\gamma|}}}du}\right\}
\end{equation}
    and
\[
    \zeta(t;s)=\frac{|\gamma|}{\delta\mu}\frac{{{\mathcal{N}}^{\mu}}(t)}{{(\nu{t})}^{{\mu}/{\nu}}}\left(1+\sigma(t;s)\right),
\]
    where $\mathcal{N}(\cdot)\in{{\mathcal{SV}}_{\infty}}$ is defined with the property {\eqref{IIB3.2}}
    and $\sigma(t;s)=\mathcal{O}\left({\ln{t}}/{t}\right)$ as $t\to\infty$ uniformly in $s\in[0,d],\;d<1$.

[Proposition prop:scott-surfaces of arXiv:2609.00233, 'A survey on mapping class groups of 3-manifolds'] Let $M$ be irreducible and boundary irreducible. Let $f \colon M \to M$, with $f^{-1}(\partial M) = \partial M$, be a homotopy equivalence. Let $F \subseteq M$ be incompressible and suppose that  either $F$ is non-separating, or, if  $M \setminus \nu F$ has two components, suppose that neither of these components  has fundamental group $\pi_1(F)$. Then $f \simeq g$ such that either
    \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
        \item $g| \colon g^{-1}(F) \to F$ is a homeomorphism; or
        \item $g(M) \subseteq \partial M$, and $M$ is an interval bundle over $F$, i.e.~$M \cong F \times I$ or $M \cong F \widetilde{\times} I$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:scott-surfaces of arXiv:2609.00233

[Deff 1 of arXiv:2606.08115, '2606.08115'] A stochastic process
$$\left\{\bol{Z_n} = \left(Z_n^{(1)}, \ldots, Z_n^{(N)} \right), \, n \in \mathbb{N}_0 \right\}, \quad Z_0^{(j)} = 1, \; j = 1, \ldots, N$$
is said to be the group of $N$ branching processes in a joint random environment $\bol{f}$ if for every natural number $n$ the following equalities hold:
$$\left. \exf \left( \prod\limits_{j = 1}^{N} t_j^{Z_n^{(j)}}\right|\bol{Z_{n-1}}\right) :=\left. \ex \left( \prod\limits_{j = 1}^{N} t_j^{Z_n^{(j)}}\right|\bol{f}, \bol{Z_{n-1}}\right) = \prod \limits_{j = 1}^N \left(f_n^{(j)} \right)^{Z_{n-1}^{(j)}} \left( t_j\right).$$

H_0 := 1 + \frac{H-1}{q} \in \Bigl(1 - \frac{1}{2q},\, 1\Bigr),
\qquad
c(H,q) := \sqrt{\frac{H(2H-1)}{q!\,\beta^q\!\left(H_0 - \tfrac{1}{2},\,
2 - 2H_0\right)}},
\]
where $\beta$ denotes the Beta function.
The \emph{Hermite process of order $q$ and self-similarity parameter $H$}
is the stochastic process $Z^{(q,H)} = \{Z_t^{(q,H)}\}_{t \geq 0}$
defined by
\begin{equation}

Z_t^{(q,H)} = I_q\!\left(L_t^{H,q}\right),
\qquad
L_t^{H,q}(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_q)
:= c(H,q) \int_0^t \prod_{j=1}^q
\bigl(s - \xi_j\bigr)_+^{H_0 - 3/2}\, ds,
\end{equation}
with the convention $\theta_+^\alpha := \theta^\alpha \mathbf{1}_{\theta > 0}$.
title: Hermite Process

Let x be uniform on {-1,1}^n, A an n x n symmetric matrix of complex numbers and L an arbitrary linear form. (Thm 6) If every row of A has at least r nonzero entries, r >= exp((ln n)^{1/4}), then for every fixed delta > 0: sup_c P(x^T A x = L(x) + c) = O_delta(r^{-1/2+delta}). (Cor 1) The same with r replaced by m if A has at least mn nonzero entries and m >= 3 exp((ln n)^{1/4}); the exponent 1/2 is sharp, see (x_1+...+x_n)(x_1+...+x_m). (Thm 4) If at least r rows of an m x n array A each have at least r nonzero entries and x, y are independent uniform sign vectors, sup_c P(x^T A y = c) = O(r^{-1/2}). (Thm 5) If every row has >= r nonzero entries, r and m are large and P(x^T A y = f(y)) >= r^{-1+eps}, then A has a rank-one submatrix of size at least (m - O_eps(r/log^6 r)) x (n - O_eps(r/log^6 r)).

Assumes: x uniform on {-1,1}^n (Thm 5 also allows lazy {0,+-1} entries in y); many nonzero coefficients per row (Thm 6) or in total (Cor 1)

Method: Exact integral manipulation, Palm calculus, mass transport, limiting obstruction or conditional construction Result: Uniform probability measures on finite approximating cells do not automatically pass to invariant probability kernels on the limiting classes. The elementary sequence uniform[-n,n] on Z has mass 1/(2n+1) at each included point; every coordinate tends to zero, so its pointwise limit is the zero measure, not a probability measure. Check: Sum each finite kernel to obtain one, but sum its pointwise limit to obtain zero. This directly demonstrates failure of the needed exchange of infinite summation and limit. Obstruction: No Voronoi-specific uniform amenability estimate is proved. Conversely, the known arbitrary finite-relation counterexamples need not arise from low-density Voronoi cells.

[Definition 4 of arXiv:2604.03213, 'Asymptotic expansion for transport maps \\ between laws of multimatrix models'] ~
	
	\begin{enumerate}[font=\normalfont,label=(\roman*)]
		\item A $\mathrm{W}^*$-probability space $(\cA,\tau) $ is a unital von Neumann algebra $\cA$ (with operator norm $\norm{\cdot}$) endowed with a faithful, normal, tracial state $\tau \colon \cA \to \C$, i.e., a $\sigma$-WOT--continuous linear map $\tau \colon \cA \to \C$ satisfying $\tau(1_{\cA})=1$, $\tau(ab) = \tau(ba)$ for all $a,b \in \cA$, and $\tau(a^*a)\geq 0$ for all $a\in \cA$, with equality if and only if $a=0$.
        An element of $\cA$ is called a (noncommutative) random variable.
		\item Unital $\ast$-subalgebras $\cA_1,\dots,\cA_n$ of $\cA$ are said to be freely independent, or free for short, if for all $k \in \N$ and all $a_1\in\cA_{j_1},\ldots,a_k \in \cA_{j_k}$ such that $j_1\neq j_2, j_2\neq j_3,\ldots,j_{k-1}\neq j_k$,
		\begin{equation}
			
			\tau\Big( (a_1-\tau(a_1))(a_2-\tau(a_2))\dots (a_k-\tau(a_k)) \Big) = 0.
		\end{equation}
		Families of noncommutative random variables are said to be free if the $\ast$-subalgebras they generate are free. Note, in particular, that if $X$ and $Y$ are free, then
		\begin{equation}
			
			\tau(XY)=\tau(X)\tau(Y).
		\end{equation}

        \item Write $\C \la \cB \ra$ for the free unital $\C$-algebra on the set $\cB$, i.e., the set of noncommutative (complex) polynomials in the indeterminates $X = (X_e)_{e \in \cB}$.
        Two families $x=(x_e)_{e \in \cB} \in \cA^{\cB}$ and $y=(y_e)_{e \in \cB} \in \cA^{\cB}$ of noncommutative random variables are said to have the same noncommutative law or distribution if for all $P \in \C\la \cB \ra$,
        $$ \tau(P(x)) = \tau(P(y)).$$
		
		\item A family $x = (x_e)_{e \in \cB}$ of noncommutative random variables is called 
		a free semicircular system when the noncommutative random variables are free, 
		$x_e$ is self-adjoint (i.e., $x_e=x_e^*$) for all $e \in \cB$, and for all $k \in \N$ and all $e \in \cB$,
        $$
		\tau( x_e^k) = \begin{cases}
		    c_{\frac{k}{2}} & \mbox{if } k \text{ is even}, \\
			0 & \text{otherwise,}
		\end{cases}
		$$
		where $c_n$ is the $n^{\text{th}}$ Catalan number for all $n \in \N$.
        See \cite[Proposition 7.15]{nica_speicher} for a construction of such a system.
	\end{enumerate}

body:
[Proposition 9 of arXiv:2607.21374, 'Local structure at the maximum and sharp persistence asymptotics of rough fractional Brown'] For the grids of Proposition~\ref{prop:dyadic-grid-diagonal}, define
\begin{equation}
  \Lambda_{n,k}:=\{h_n(j-k):0\leq j\leq M_n\},
  \qquad 0\leq k\leq M_n,
  
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
  Q_{n,k}:=\mathcal L\left(
    B\,\middle|\, B_t\leq0\text{ for every }t\in\Lambda_{n,k}
  \right),
  \qquad
  p_{n,k}:=\PP(B_t\leq0:t\in\Lambda_{n,k}).
  
\end{equation}
Then
\(p_{n,k}=\PP(K_n=k)>0\),
\(\sum_{k=0}^{M_n}p_{n,k}=1\), and
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal L(\Xi_n^{\mathrm{grid}})
  =\sum_{k=0}^{M_n}p_{n,k}Q_{n,k}.
  
\end{equation}
Write
\begin{equation}
  L_{n,k}^-=h_nk,
  \qquad L_{n,k}^+=h_n(M_n-k).
  
\end{equation}
For \(0<k<M_n\), the component \(Q_{n,k}\) is
\(Q_{h_n,L_{n,k}^-,L_{n,k}^+}\) from \eqref{eq:pure-wall-law}.  The endpoint
components \(k=0,M_n\) retain their direct conditional definitions in
\eqref{eq:mixture-components}; they are full-path laws constrained on only
one side of the pin and are not covered by the positive-two-horizon
definition \eqref{eq:pure-wall-law}.

Method: Transform asymptotics, exact special case, coupling reduction or identifiability check Result: Take two servers and two simultaneously present jobs with identical replica durations a<=b across servers. Replicating the shorter job on both servers first gives completion times a and a+b, with mean a+b/2. Assigning one job to each server immediately gives completion times a and b, with mean (a+b)/2. The second policy improves the mean by a/2. Therefore a proof based on always assigning every free server to the currently shortest job cannot be valid across the correlated-copy model class. Check: List the two completion epochs directly; at a=b=1 the means are 3/2 versus 1. This is a two-job scheduling example, not a stationary optimality theorem. Obstruction: Need a dynamic rule and a stochastic comparison or control proof for the full arriving system. Finite-workload preference need not identify a steady-state optimizer.

[Lem oracle_access__approximation of arXiv:2609.03129, 'A Closed-Form Formula for Consistent Lipschitz Regression on Metric Spaces with Sparse Neu'] Let $(X,\rho)$ be a totally bounded metric space with
$
    \operatorname{diam}(X)\le 1
$
and doubling dimension at most $d\in\mathbb N_+$.  Let
$
    \{x_n\}_{n=1}^N
$
be an $\tfrac{1}{N^{1/d}}$-net of minimal cardinality in $(X,\rho)$.  For any
$1$-Lipschitz map $f:X\to[-1,1]$, define
\[
    \theta_f
    \ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}
    \big((f(x_n),x_n,1)\big)_{n=1}^N .
\]
Then the reconstruction formula $\hat{f}_{\theta_f}$ from~(equation eq:formula of the paper)
satisfies
\[
    \sup_{x\in X}
        |f(x)-\hat{f}_{\theta_f}(x)|
    \lesssim
        N^{-1/d}.
\]

body: [Definition def:endogenous_uncertainty_set of arXiv:2507.22577, 'A Mean-Field Theory of $\Theta$-Expectations'] Let $\Theta$ be a compact metric space representing the possible regimes of systemic ambiguity. Let $g: \mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}) \to \Theta$ be a continuous map. For each $\theta \in \Theta$, let $\mathcal{U}_\theta$ be a non-empty, compact subset of the control space $E_A$. We refer to the law-dependent set $\mathcal{U}_{g(\mu)} \subset E_A$ as the \textbf{endogenous uncertainty set}. The map $g$ translates the state of the system (the law of the value process $\mu$) into a specific ambiguity regime $\theta$, which in turn selects the set of available models $\mathcal{U}_\theta$.

[Definition def:halfannulus of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] Let \(N\) be a sutured manifold and admit a compatible semiflow \(\phi\).
A \emph{half annulus} in \(N\) is an immersed, \(\phi\)-saturated annulus \(H\), so that
\begin{enumerate}
\item the interior of \(H\) is embedded,
\item one component  of \(\partial H\) covers a closed \(\phi\)-orbit \(\gamma\); the other component is a closed curve on \(\partial N\),
\item either each point in \(H\) converges to \(\gamma\) in forward time, or each point converges to \(\gamma\) in backward time.
\end{enumerate}
In other words, \(H\) is orbit equivalent to the half of a blown-up annulus (cutting along a transverse core circle).
We denote by \(\mathcal{H}(N)\) the union of half annuli in \(N\).

We say \((N_{1},\phi_{1})\) and \((N_{2},\phi_{2})\) are \emph{orbit equivalent outside half annuli} if there is a homeomorphism from \(N_{1}\setminus \mathcal{H}(N_{1})\) to \(N_{2}\setminus \mathcal{H}(N_{2})\), which maps \(\phi_{1}\)-orbits to \(\phi_{2}\)-orbits.
title: Half annulus

body:
[Theorem 12 of arXiv:2608.19576, 'Convex order preservation for graphon mean-field systems'] Assume that Assumptions \ref{A:assump:1} and \ref{A:assump:2} are in force. For every $u \in I$, let $X^u := \{X^u_t\}_{t \geq 0}$, $Y^u := \{Y^u_t\}_{t \geq 0}$ denote the unique solutions of systems \eqref{A:eqn:1} and \eqref{A:eqn:2}, and for every $t \geq 0$, let $\mu^u_t$, $\nu^u_t$ denote the probability distributions of $X^u_t$ and $Y^u_t$. Then, we have
    
    \textup{(a)} \textup{Marginal convex order:} $\mu^u_t \preceq_{cv} \nu^u_t$, $\forall t \geq 0, \; \forall u \in I$.

    \vspace{1mm}
    
    \textup{(b)} \textup{Functional convex order:} for any convex function $F: (\mathcal{C}^d_\infty, \|\cdot\|_K) \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ with quadratic growth, one has 
    $$
    \mathbb{E} \Big[F\big(X^u\big)\Big] \leq \mathbb{E} \Big[F\big(Y^u\big)\Big], \quad \forall u \in I.
    $$
title: Theorem 12 of arXiv:2608.19576

[Lemma 45 (Local one-derivative gain for Ricci--DeTurck systems) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Fix an integer \(k\geq2\) and \(\sigma\in(0,1)\).  Let \(Q\) and \(Q'\) be
concentric coordinate cylinders in a fixed spatial chart, with \(Q'\) having
smaller spatial radius and a positive time gap from the lower time face of
\(Q\); the two cylinders may share their upper time face.  Let \(r(t)\) be a
smooth reference metric on \(Q\), and let \(q(t)\) be a smooth positive
definite solution of the Ricci--DeTurck equation relative to \(r(t)\).  In a
fixed tensor frame this equation has the scalar-principal form
\begin{equation}
 \partial_tq^A-q^{ij}\partial_i\partial_jq^A
 =\mathcal F^A\bigl(x,t,q,q^{-1},\partial q;
                 r,\partial r,\partial^2r\bigr),
\end{equation}
where \(\mathcal F\) is a universal smooth expression and contains no second
spatial derivatives of \(q\).  Suppose, in the fixed coordinates, that
\[
 \lambda I\leq(q_{ij})\leq\Lambda I,
 \qquad
 \|q\|_{C^{k+\sigma,(k+\sigma)/2}(Q)}
 +\|r\|_{C^{k+1+\sigma,(k+1+\sigma)/2}(Q)}\leq A.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \|q\|_{C^{k+1+\sigma,(k+1+\sigma)/2}(Q')}
 \leq C,
\end{equation}
where \(C\) depends only on the displayed bounds, the rank and dimension, and
the fixed spatial and lower-time separations between \(Q'\) and \(Q\).
Consequently, the estimate is uniform in any bounded-geometry atlas with fixed
nested-cylinder ratios.

body:
[Lemma 26 of arXiv:2607.14948, 'Graph alignment in sparse inhomogeneous models via self-overlap'] Let $\eta, \eps > 0$. Let $X \subseteq [n]$ with $|X| \geq \eps n$, and let $X_2, \ldots, X_L, X_{>L}, X_c$ form a partition of $X$. Denote $\kappa = \frac{|X|}{n}$. Let $\rho_2, \ldots, \rho_L, \rho_{>L}, \rho_{c}, \rho_s \geq 0$ be such that $\sum_{i} \rho_i \geq (\frac{1}{2 \alpha -1} + \eta) \kappa$. Then, there exists $\delta = \delta(\eta, \eps) > 0$ such that, for large enough $n$,

    \begin{equation}
        \Proba\left(\exists \sigma \in \Sym_n: X \subseteq \Der \sigma,\begin{cases}
            \mc{C}_2(\sigma, X) = X_2 \\
            \mc{C}_3(\sigma, X) = X_3 \\
            \hspace{29pt}\vdots \\
            \mc{C}_c(\sigma, X) = X_c
        \end{cases}, \begin{cases}
            e_2(\sigma, X) \geq \rho_2 n \\
            e_3(\sigma, X) \geq \rho_3 n \\
            \hspace{29pt}\vdots \\
            e_c(\sigma, X) \geq \rho_c n \\
            e_s(\sigma, X) \geq \rho_s n
        \end{cases} \right) \leq e^{-\delta n \log n}.
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 26 of arXiv:2607.14948

[Theorem 36 of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] Let $(X,d,\mu)$ be a Polish probability space with enlargement functions
$(R_s)_{s\geq 0}$ and associated function $\Theta$. Suppose that $\Theta$ is continuous and decays to zero at infinity. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The space $(X,\mu)$ satisfies the metric-Santal\'o inequality induced by $2\cdot\Theta$ on the domain $(\mathcal{B}(X),\mathcal{B}(X))$.

    \item Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal D\subset \mathcal{B}(X)$ be sub-collections
    satisfying $\mu(A\cap D)=0$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$ and $D\in\mathcal D$. Then $(X,\mu)$ satisfies

[Definition 7 of arXiv:2608.18688, 'Regularity Preservation for Jump-Type Stochastic Transport Equations with Singular Drift'] We call $\tau(x)=\tau(x,\omega)$ an accessible lower-semicontinuous stopping time if the following conditions hold:

(i) For each $x$, $\tau(x)$ is a stopping time.

(ii) For almost all $\omega$, $\tau(\cdot,\omega)$ is a positive lower semicontinuous function on $\mR^d$.

(iii) There is an increasing sequence of random fields $\tau_n(x,\omega)$ with  properties (i) and (ii) above such that $\tau_n(x)<\tau(x)$ and $\tau_n(x)$ converges $\tau(x)$ for any $x$ a.s..

body: In mathematics, the Poincaré inequality is a result in the theory of Sobolev spaces, named after the French mathematician Henri Poincaré. The inequality allows one to obtain bounds on a function using bounds on its derivatives and the geometry of its domain of definition. Such bounds are of great importance in the modern, direct methods of the calculus of variations. A very closely related result is Friedrichs' inequality.

[Corollary 119 (Restart covariance of the common density) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Let $x,y\in G_*^\Gamma$ and let $s\in[0,T]$.  Up to equality for Lebesgue
almost every time,
\begin{align}
 \mathfrak a_t(r_sx)
 &=\one_{\{t<s\}}\mathfrak a_t(x),
 \\
 \mathfrak a_v(\theta_sx)
 &=\one_{\{v<T-s\}}\mathfrak a_{s+v}(x),
 \\
 \mathfrak a_t(x\otimes_sy)
 &=\one_{\{t<s\}}\mathfrak a_t(x)
   +\one_{\{t>s\}}\mathfrak a_{t-s}(y).
 
\end{align}
If $\tau$ is a bounded raw stopping time and $x\in G_*^\Gamma$, then
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak a_t(r_\tau x)
 =\one_{\{t<\tau(x)\}}\mathfrak a_t(x)
 \qquad\text{for a.e. }t.
\end{equation}
Thus deterministic restart and random stopping transport the covariance-energy
fibres by the corresponding restriction and time-shift rules, with the same
common density representative.

Let G be a finite undirected loopless multigraph on n vertices with positive edge weights w_e, L its weighted Laplacian, and t > 0. A spanning rooted forest is a spanning forest with one chosen root in each tree; its weight is t^|E(F)| prod_{e in F} w_e (so an unrooted forest with trees T_1, ..., T_k counts prod |T_i| times). Z(t) is the total weight of spanning rooted forests, and Q_t = (I + tL)^-1. For all vertices i and j, (Q_t)_ij = f_ij(t) / Z(t), where f_ij(t) is the total weight of spanning rooted forests in which i belongs to the tree rooted at j. In particular Q_t is symmetric, entrywise nonnegative and doubly stochastic.

Let N be a positive integer and mu_D the Moebius function of D(N) ordered by divisibility. For d | e | N, mu_D(d, e) = mu(e/d), where mu is the arithmetic Moebius function: mu(1) = 1, mu(m) = 0 if p^2 divides m for some prime p, and mu(m) = (-1)^omega(m) for squarefree m, omega(m) the number of distinct prime divisors. In particular the value does not depend on N.
N is a positive integer
d and e divide N and d divides e
mu_D is the Moebius function of D(N) under divisibility

   \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]

   \end{enumerate}

body: [Lem 94 of arXiv:2510.22155, 'Random walks in space-time random media in all spatial dimensions: the full subcritical fl'] Consider a martingale $M$ defined on any filtered probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal F, P),$ and suppose that the increments of $M$ satisfy a uniform $q^{th}$ moment bound under the probability measure $P$: $$\mathcal S_q(M;P):=\sup_{n\ge 1}  E [|X_{n+1} -X_n|^q]<\infty,$$ where $q\ge 2$. Then $E [ |M_r-M_s|^q ] \leq C_q (r-s)^{\frac{q}2} \mathcal S_q(M;P),$ for some absolute constant $C_q$ that is uniform over all martingales $M$ and probability spaces $(\Omega, \mathcal F,P).$
title: Lem 94 of arXiv:2510.22155

[Proposition of arXiv:2609.00105, 'Weighted composition operators and classification of weighted Hardy spaces'] Assume that $X$ is a maximal domain for $\mathcal{B}$. 
    For $S\subset X$, define $$\mathcal{B}_S=\set{f|_S: f\in \mathcal{B}}.$$
    The following are equivalent 
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item $\widehat{S}=\widehat{X}$ and $\widehat{\mathcal{B}_S}=\widehat{\mathcal{B}}$.
            \item The map $f\mapsto f|_S$ is isometric isomorphism and $f|_Sg|_S=h|_S$ if and only if $h=fg$.
        \end{enumerate}

body:
[Theorem 17 of arXiv:2607.10102, 'Dynamical mean-field limit and replica-symmetric free energy for the orthogonally-invarian'] Suppose there exists a (deterministic or random) initial state $\btheta^0$ for
which Assumptions \ref{assump:X} and \ref{assump:dynamics} hold with $f=-U'$.
Suppose that the bound $\alpha>0$ in
\eqref{eq:Uconvexity} satisfies
\begin{equation}
\alpha>\Lambda_{\max},
\qquad \alpha>\sum_{p \geq 1}|\kappa_{p+1}|
\left(\frac{1}{n}\langle \|\btheta\|_2^2 \rangle
-\frac{1}{n}\langle \btheta^\top \btheta' \rangle+\eps\right)^p
\end{equation}
almost surely for all large $n$ and some constant $\eps>0$.
Suppose that Assumption \ref{assump:convergence} holds for this initial state
$\btheta^0$.

For any $v \geq q \geq 0$ such that the R-transform series
\begin{equation}
\cR_\Lambda(x)=\sum_{p \geq 1} \kappa_{p+1}x^p
\end{equation}
is absolutely convergent in a neighborhood of $v-q$ and $q\cR_\Lambda'(v-q) \geq 0$, define
the probability density on $\R$
\begin{equation}
\mu(\theta \mid v,q,\xi)
\propto
\exp\left(-U(\theta)+\frac{1}{2}\cR_\Lambda(v-q)\theta^2+\sqrt{q\cR_\Lambda'(v-q)}\,\xi\theta\right).
\end{equation}
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item There exist deterministic almost-sure limits
\begin{equation}
v_*=\lim_{n \to \infty}\frac{1}{n}\langle \|\btheta\|_2^2 \rangle,
\qquad q_*=\lim_{n \to \infty}\frac{1}{n}\langle \btheta^\top \btheta' \rangle
\end{equation}
satisfying the above conditions.
These solve the fixed-point equations
\begin{equation}
v_*=\E_{\xi \sim \cN(0,1)}
\langle \theta^2 \rangle_{v_*,q_*,\xi},
\qquad q_*=\E_{\xi \sim \cN(0,1)} \langle \theta \rangle_{v_*,q_*,\xi}^2
\end{equation}
where $\langle \cdot \rangle_{v,q,\xi}$ denotes the expectation under
$\mu(\cdot \mid v,q,\xi)$. Furthermore, almost surely
\begin{equation}
\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n}\langle \btheta^\top \X\btheta\rangle
=v_*\cR_\Lambda(v_*-q_*)+q_*(v_*-q_*)\cR_\Lambda'(v_*-q_*).
\end{equation}
For any function $f:\R \to \R$ satisfying
$|f(x)-f(y)| \leq C(1+|x|+|y|)|x-y|$ for some $C>0$, almost surely
\begin{equation}
\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \langle f(\theta_i) \rangle
=\E_{\xi \sim \cN(0,1)} \langle f(\theta) \rangle_{v_*,q_*,\xi}.
\end{equation}
\item Suppose, in addition, that almost surely over $(\X,\btheta^0)$ for all
large $n$, for every $\beta \in [0,1]$,
the condition \eqref{eq:alphacondition} and Assumption
\ref{assump:convergence} hold for the Gibbs measure, dynamics, and free
cumulants associated to $\beta \X$, with some constants $C,c,\eps>0$
that are uniform over $\beta \in [0,1]$.

Let $\cZ$ be
the partition function \eqref{eq:partition} (for $\beta=1$). Then almost surely
\begin{align}
\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n}\log \cZ
&=\E_{\xi \sim \cN(0,1)} \log \int \exp\Big({-}U(\theta)
+\frac{1}{2}\cR_\Lambda(v_*-q_*)\theta^2+\sqrt{q_*\cR_\Lambda'(v_*-q_*)}\,\xi\theta\Big)\notag\\
&\hspace{0.2in}+\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{v_*-q_*} \cR_\Lambda(s)\d s
-\frac{1}{2}(v_*-q_*)\cR_\Lambda(v_*-q_*)-\frac{1}{2}q_*(v_*-q_*)\cR_\Lambda'(v_*-q_*).
\end{align}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 17 of arXiv:2607.10102

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2511.07350, 'Decoupling of clusters in independent sets in a percolated hypercube'] For $p > 0.391$, we have
\begin{equation}
    \sum_{\substack{S_2 \in \Sep_2 \\ S_2 \sse \Cpt_2(S_1)}} \prod_{\fd \in S_2} \phi_\fd
    \psim \Exp{\sum_{\fd \not \sim S_1} \phi_\fd} = \Exp{\Delta - \Adj(S_1)},
\end{equation}
where the approximation is uniform among all $S_1 \sse \cH$ (recall what this means from above the statement of
Theorem \ref{thm:main}).
The same statement also holds with $\phi_\fd$ replaced by $\fphi_\fd$, $\Delta$ replaced by $\tilde{\Delta}$,
and $\Adj$ replaced by $\tAdj$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 4 of arXiv:2511.07350

body: [Corollary 66 of arXiv:2604.01685, 'Probability with Measure\footnote{Lecture notes. University of Ljubljana.}'] Let $(X,\AA,\mu)$ be a measure space, $\{f,g\}\subset \AA/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$. Suppose $\int_A f\dd\mu= \int_Ag\dd\mu$ for every $A\in \AA$, all the integrals being well-defined. If  $f$ or $g$ is $\mu$-integrable (in which case both are) or if $\mu$ is $\sigma$-finite, then $f=g$ a.e.-$\mu$. Furthermore, in case $f$ and $g$ are $\mu$-integrable, then actually, ceteris paribus, it is enough to ask for  $\int_A f\dd\mu= \int_Ag\dd\mu$ to hold true merely for every  $A\in \BB\cup \{X\}$, where $\BB\subset \AA$ is a $\pi$-system that generates $\AA$ on $X$, and still  the same conclusion prevails.

[Definition def:admissible_classes of arXiv:2607.04514, 'Boundary-layer asymptotics for Gaussian-smoothed singular measures'] Let \(\ell\in\mathbb N\) and \(\omega>0\). Fix \(A,\sigma_0>0\) and \(R\in(0,\infty]\).

  \begin{enumerate}
    \item A function \(B:\overline{\mathbb B}_A\times \mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}}\times (0,\sigma_0]\to\mathbb
    R\) belongs to \(\mathfrak B_\ell\) if its pullback \( B(a,\varphi (\theta),\sigma)\) is
    \(C^\ell\) in \((a,\theta, \sigma)\) and, for every \(\gamma\) with \(|\gamma| \leqslant \ell\),
    \begin{equation*}
      \sup_{{\mathcal D}_{A,\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}},\sigma_0}} \bigl| \partial_{a,\theta,\sigma}^{\gamma}
      B(a,\varphi(\theta),\sigma) \bigr|<\infty.
    \end{equation*}

    \item A function \(E:\overline{\mathbb B}_A \times\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}}\times (0,\sigma_0]\to\mathbb
    R\) belongs to \(\mathfrak E_\ell^\omega\) if its pullback \( E(a, \varphi (\theta),\sigma)\) is
    \(C^\ell\) in \((a, \theta, \sigma)\), and there exists \(c>0\) such that, for every \(\gamma\)
    with \(|\gamma|\leqslant\ell\), there is a constant \(C_\gamma>0\) satisfying
    \begin{equation*}
      \bigl|\partial_{a,\theta,\sigma}^{ \gamma} E(a,\varphi(\theta),\sigma) \bigr|
      \leqslant C_\gamma e^{-c/\sigma^{\omega}},\quad
      \forall (a,\varphi(\theta),\sigma)\in {\mathcal D}_{A,\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}}, \sigma_0}.
    \end{equation*}

    \item A function \(P: \mathcal D_{R, A, \mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}}, \sigma_0} \to\mathbb R\) belongs to
    \(\mathfrak P_\ell \) if it is measurable in \(\zeta\) and its pullback
    \(P(\zeta;a,\varphi(\theta),\sigma)\) is \(C^\ell\) in the
    parameter variables \((a,\theta, \sigma)\), for every fixed \(\zeta\), and there exists
    \(n\geqslant 0\) such that
    \begin{equation*}
      \bigl| \partial_{a,\theta,\sigma}^{\gamma} P(\zeta; a,\varphi(\theta),\sigma) \bigr|
      \leqslant C_\gamma \bigl(1 + \|\zeta\|^n\bigr)
    \end{equation*}
    for every \(\gamma\) with \(|\gamma|\leqslant\ell\), uniformly on \(\mathcal D_{R, A,
    \mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}}, \sigma_0} \).

    \item A function \(G: \mathcal D_{R, A,\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}}, \sigma_0} \to\mathbb R\) belongs to
    \(\mathfrak G_\ell\) if it is measurable in \(\zeta\) and its pullback
    \(G(\zeta;a,\varphi(\theta),\sigma)\) is \(C^\ell\) in the
    parameter variables \((a,\theta,\sigma) \), for every fixed \(\zeta\), and there exist \(c_0>0,
    n\geqslant 0\) such that
    \begin{equation*}
      \bigl| \partial_{a,\theta,\sigma}^{\gamma} G(\zeta;a,\varphi(\theta),\sigma) \bigr|
      \leqslant C_\gamma\bigl(1+\|\zeta\|^n\bigr)\Gamma_{c_0}(\zeta;a)
    \end{equation*}
    for every \(\gamma\) with \(|\gamma|\leqslant\ell\), uniformly on \({\mathcal
    D}_{R,A,\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}},\sigma_0}\).
  \end{enumerate}
title: Admissible classes

[Lemma 11 (Asymptotics via Trapezoid Rule) of arXiv:2608.14143, 'Mod-$\phi$ convergence for random variables with cyclotomic generating functions'] Assume $a_{N,j}/s_N = f(j/N)$ for some function $f \in C^2[0, 1]$ with $f(t) \ge 0$.
Let
$$
\mathscr{D} = \Big\{z \in \mathbb{C} \mid \frac{1-e^{zf(t)}}{-zf(t)} \notin (-\infty, 0] \text{ for all } t \in [0, 1] \text{ such that } f(t) > 0\Big\}.
$$
Then, for $z \in \mathscr{D}$, the sum $S_N^a(z) = \sum_{j=1}^N h(a_{N,j}/s_N, z)$ admits the asymptotic expansion
\[
S_N^a(z) = N \int_0^1 h(f(t), z) dt + \frac{h(f(1), z) - h(f(0), z)}{2} + O(1/N),
\]
which holds locally uniformly for $z \in \mathscr{D}$.

Let X be a random variable with characteristic function \phi(t). If \phi \in L^1(\mathbb{R}) (i.e., \int_{-\infty}^\infty |\phi(t)| dt < \infty), then the distribution of X is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure, and its probability density function f(x) is continuous, bounded, and given by f(x) = \frac{1}{2\pi} \int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{-itx} \phi(t) dt.
\phi \in L^1(\mathbb{R})

[Lemma 30 (Consequences of the dominant energy condition) of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] Given a Navier--Stokes potential~$\chi$ as in \autoref{def-pot-hyperbolic}, one has the following inequalities between components in the orthonormal coframe $e^m$: for $m,n=0,1,2,3$,
\bel{Tchi-DEC}
|T_\chi^{mn}| \leq T_\chi^{00} , \qquad
-4 T_\chi^{00} \leq \eta_{mn} T_\chi^{mn} \leq 2 T_\chi^{00} .
\ee
The Euler stress-tensor with pressure law satisfying~\eqref{hyperbolic-eos-zero} admits the stronger trace bound
\bel{TrTE-lower}
- T_{\rm E}^{00} \leq \eta_{mn} T_{\rm E}^{mn} \leq 2 T_{\rm E}^{00} .
\ee

[Proposition prop:spectralgap of arXiv:2606.01937, 'Stationary fluctuations for an exclusion process with mass and energy conservation'] There exists a universal constant $C_5=C_5(\kappa )>0$ such that for any local function $f$ supported in $\{0,\hdots ,\ell -1\}$ for some $\ell\ge 1$, with $\psi_f(\rho ,\mathcal{E})=0$ for any $\rho \in [0,1]$ and $\mathcal{E}\in [\rho ,\kappa\rho]$, we have 
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{Var}_{\rho ,\mathcal{E}}(f) \le C_5\ell^2 \sum_{\substack {x,y\in\{0,\hdots ,\ell -1\}\\ |x-y|=1}} \Big( \mathfrak{D}_{x\to y}^p (f;\mu_{\rho ,\mathcal{E}}) + \mathfrak{D}_{x\to y}^e(f;\mu_{\rho ,\mathcal{E}})\Big).
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

When the degree exponent $\tau$ of the original pmf $\mathbf{p}$ satisfies $\tau>3$, for any $\epsilon>0$ we have

[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2607.17255, 'Large deviations for long-time occupation measures of stochastic evolution equations with '] There exist $M \in (0,\infty)$, depending only on $\|F\|_\infty$ and $\delta$,
and a family $(\varphi^\eps )_{\eps \in (0,1)} \subset \mathcal{A}_{b,M}$, such
that, for every $\eps \in (0,1)$,
\begin{equation}
  -\eps\, s^2(\eps) \log \mathbb{E} \exp\!\Big( -\frac{1}{\epsilon s^2(\epsilon)}F(\nu^\epsilon) \Big)
   \ge  \mathbb{E}\!\left(
    \frac{1}{2} \int_0^1 \bigl| \varphi^\eps(s) \bigr|_H^2 \, ds
     +  F\bigl(\bar\nu^\eps\bigr)
  \right)  -  2 \delta,
\end{equation}
where $\bar\nu^\eps = \int_0^1 \delta_{\bar v^\eps(t)}\,dt$ and $\bar v^\eps$ is
the solution of the controlled equation~\eqref{veps-controlled} corresponding
to $\varphi = \varphi^\eps$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Thmc2 55 (contraction at the bolt-type stratum; Theorem \ref{thm:contracting_Ql}) of arXiv:2609.03332, 'Singularity Models of Finite-Time K\"ahler-Ricci Flows'] Let $\widehat{M}$ be as in Theorem C1, and again the total volume stays positive at the first singular time $T < \infty$. Now assume the singularity occurs at a bolt $Q_\ell := N$. Let $\mathcal{I}_\infty$ be the subset of $\{1, 2, \cdots, r\}$ such that $i_\infty \in \mathcal{I}_\infty$ if and only if the $N_{i_\infty}$-factor of $Q_\ell$ contracts to a point at the singular time $T$ of the K\"ahler-Ricci flow. Then, the blow-up limit splits as $( \operatorname{Tot} ( \mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{I}_\infty} ), g_{\mathrm{sol}} ( t ) ) \times \mathbb{C}^k$, where $k = \sum_{i_\infty \not\in \mathcal{I}_\infty,\, i_\infty \not= 1} \dim_{\mathbb{C}} N_{i_\infty}$, $\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{I}_\infty} \to \prod_{i_\infty \in \mathcal{I}_\infty} N_{i_\infty}$ is the \emph{line} bundle obtained from restricting the normal bundle of $Q_\ell \subset \widehat{M}$ to $\prod_{i_\infty \in \mathcal{I}_\infty} N_{i_\infty}$, with $c_1 ( \mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{I}_\infty} ) = \sum_{i_\infty\in \mathcal{I}_\infty} q_{i_\infty} [\omega_{i_\infty}]$, and $g_{\mathrm{sol}}$ is a complete gradient shrinking K\"ahler--Ricci soliton of ansatz form on the line bundle total space $\operatorname{Tot} ( \mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{I}_\infty} )$ --- the Feldman--Ilmanen--Knopf shrinker in \cite{FIK}, or its multi-base generalization by Dancer--Wang in \cite{DW2011}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem thm:global-drift of arXiv:2602.19192, 'Bakry--\'Emery Curvature of the Fractional Laplacian\\ via Fractional Brownian Covariance'] At $\gamma = 1$, the Hermitianized drift correction satisfies
the scalar identity
\begin{equation}
  \Gamma_{L,2}(f,f)(x) - \Gamma_{1,2}(f,f)(x)
  = \frac{\omega^2}{2}\cos(x)\;\Gamma(f,f)(x)
\end{equation}
for all $f \in \mathcal{T}_N^+$ and all $x \in \mathbb{T}$.
Consequently, the eigenvalues of the curvature operator
$\Gamma^{-1}\Gamma_{L,2}$ on $\mathcal{T}_N^+$ are
\begin{equation}
  \kappa_k(x) = (2k-1) + \frac{\omega^2}{2}\cos x,
  \qquad k = 1,\ldots,N,
\end{equation}
and the global Bakry--\'Emery curvature is
\begin{equation}
  \kappa(1,\omega^2) = 1 - \frac{\omega^2}{2},
\end{equation}
independent of $N$, achieved at $x = \pi$.
Combined with the cross-sign vanishing
(Corollary~(cor:block-diag of the paper)), this extends to all real
trigonometric polynomials.

In particular, $\mathrm{CD}(1-\omega^2/2,\,\infty)$ holds for
$\omega^2 < 2$, with consequences:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item Poincar\'e inequality:
  $\mathrm{Var}_\mu(f) \leq \frac{1}{1-\omega^2/2}\,\mathcal{E}_L(f,f)$.
\item Gradient estimate:
  $\Gamma(P_t^L f, P_t^L f)
  \leq e^{-2(1-\omega^2/2)t}\,P_t^L[\Gamma(f,f)]$.
\end{enumerate}

body: [Abstract of arXiv:2609.02331, 'Metastability of Interacting Stochastic Systems with Countably Many Metastable States...'] Metastability is typically formulated for systems with finitely many metastable states, most often in positively recurrent settings. In this article, we extend the resolvent framework for metastability to Markov processes with countably many metastable states, thereby encompassing null-recurrent and transient dynamics. For a family of processes on locally compact Polish spaces, we prove, under a mild boundary regularity assumption, that the asymptotic flatness of microscopic resolvent solutions, supplemented by two compactness conditions, is equivalent to convergence in law of the projected trace processes to a limiting Markov chain and to the negligibility of the time spent outside the metastable sets. We apply this framework to two non-compact stochastic systems. First, we study a condensing inclusion process on a countably infinite, uniformly locally finite graph, in a setting where the process may be null recurrent or transient. We prove that the condensate location converges to a weighted random walk on the underlying graph, while the time spent away from the fully condensed configurations is negligible. Second, we study a small-noise one-dimensional Langevin diffusion with countably many stable equilibria, without assuming ergodicity. In the Eyring--Kramers time scale associated with the minimal energy barrier, we establish local equilibration inside each well, convergence of the well-index process to an explicit nearest-neighbor Markov chain on $\mathbb{Z}$, and negligibility of inter-well excursions. Together, these results broaden the scope of resolvent-based metastability theory beyond finite metastable state spaces and positive recurrence.
title: Abstract of arXiv:2609.02331: Metastability of Interacting Stochastic Systems with Countably Many Metastable States...

Own-work draft, C009 version 1, proof (unaudited); dependencies C004 v2 and C006 v2 also await independent review, and priority is not established. Fix any L>=3 and T<infinity, set H=L-1, and use equal hidden widths m with h1_i=sigma(w_i dot x), hl_j=sigma(m^(-1)sum_i B^l_ji h(l-1)_i) for 2<=l<=H, and f=m^(-1)sum_j a_j hH_j. Assume a globally C2 activation with absolute values of sigma and its first two derivatives at most one, data ||X||<=1 and |Y|<=1, and population half-squared risk. Two runs are independently initialized from the same laws: w_i iid with Euclidean norm <=1, a_i iid with |a_i|<=1, and iid entries in [-1,1] in each middle matrix; all named arrays are mutually independent. Layer entry laws can differ and need not be centered. Train all parameters simultaneously by fresh-iid SGD or finite minibatch averages, with multipliers m on w,a and m^2 on every middle matrix, using common deterministic nonnegative steps of total at most T. The runs may see independent data. Put S2=sum eta_k^2, A=2exp(T), M_l=1+2A^2 T product_{s=l+1}^H M_s backwards from l=H to 2, W=1+2A^2 T product_{s=2}^H M_s, R=max(1,A,W,M_2,...,M_H), and kappa=64L^2 R^(2L). For r_cov(m)=inf_{k,q positive integers}[4/q+2/sqrt(k+1)+2sqrt(2)sqrt(q^(k+1)/m)], an initialization-selected compatible tuple of hidden permutations gives expected population loss-chord barrier <=8R^L exp(kappa T)[r_cov(m)+6(L-2)/sqrt(m)+4LR^L sqrt(S2)]. Thus eta_max<=1/log(m) yields O_{L,T}(sqrt(log(log(m)+e)/log(m))) uniformly in input dimension, including dimensions growing arbitrarily with width, provided the stated Euclidean bounds hold uniformly. The proof matches initial boundary pairs using |delta a|+||Sigma^(1/2)delta w|| for Sigma=E[XX^T], propagates the cut-norm estimates in L2 of the input distribution for population gradients only, and compares SGD to population Euler in the full normalized Hilbert norm. Singular Sigma is allowed; no inverse covariance or teacher model is assumed. This does not assert samplewise covariance stability, a ReLU result, unbounded initialization, a fixed independent-data step result, low-risk endpoints, uniform growing-depth control, an independent audit, or novelty.

[Theorem 77 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{Assumptions_Theta}, \ref{Assumptions_basic} and \ref{Assumptions_offcrit} hold. Take $h \in [H]$ and a saturated interval $(\mathfrak{a},\mathfrak{b}) \subseteq [\hat{a}_h,\hat{b}_h]$ of the equilibrium measure $\boldsymbol{\mu}$. Assume that $\mathfrak{a}$ is a
point separating a saturation from a band, but $\mathfrak{b}$ is not.\footnote{As the equilibrium measure has finite mass, this situation requires $\mathfrak{b}$ to be finite.} Then for each $\eps>0$ there exists $C>0$ depending only on $\eps$ and the constants in the assumptions, such that
\[
\P\big[\textnormal{There are no holes in}\, [\mathfrak{a}+\eps,\mathfrak{b}]\big]\geq 1- C\exp\bigg(-\frac{\N}{C}\bigg).
\]
Similarly, if $\mathfrak{b}$ is a point separating a saturation from a band, but $\mathfrak{a}$
is not, then
\[
\P\big[\textnormal{There are no holes in}\, [\mathfrak{a},\mathfrak{b}-\eps]\big] \geq 1- C\exp\bigg(-\frac{\N}{C}\bigg).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 77 of arXiv:2601.16377

body:
[Theorem 18 (Theorem~IV.10  of \cite{FS09}) of arXiv:2606.27520, 'Critical curve of loop percolation on the $d$-regular tree'] Let $G(z)$ be a function meromorphic at all points of the closed disc $|z| \le R$, with poles at points $z_1, \ldots, z_m$, and Taylor expansion
\[
G(z) = \sum_{n\geq 0} g_n z^n
\]
around the origin.
Assume that $G(z)$ is analytic at all points of $|z| = R$ and at $z = 0$.
Then there exist $m$ polynomials $\{\Pi_j(x)\}_{j=1}^m$ such that
\[
g_n = \sum_{j=1}^{m} \Pi_j(n)z_j^{-n} + O(R^{-n}).
\]
Furthermore, the degree of $\Pi_j$ is equal to the order of the pole of $G(z)$ at $z_j$ minus one.

For any Boolean sign function under uniform measure, let alpha=I_i(f) and Delta_i=H(f)-(H(f_+)+H(f_-))/2 with base-2 spectral entropy. The accompanying derivation gives 0<=Delta_i<=h_2(alpha)+(2/ln 2)min(alpha,1-alpha), and hence Delta_i<=alpha log_2(1/alpha)+(3/ln 2)alpha, with the zero-alpha convention. For a real scalar Z define ||Z||_psi2=sup_{p>=1} p^(-1/2)*(E|Z|^p)^(1/p); for a real vector a define ||a||_psi2=sup_{||x||_2=1} ||<a,x>||_psi2. All matrix norms below are Euclidean operator norms. Let N,n>=1 be integers and let A be a real N-by-n random matrix with independent rows a_i^T. Assume all rows have the same uncentered second-moment matrix Sigma=E[a_i a_i^T] and max_i ||a_i||_psi2<=K for a fixed K>0. Then there are C_K,c_K>0, depending only on K, such that for every t>=0, with probability at least 1-2 exp(-c_K*t^2), ||A^T A/N-Sigma||_op<=max(delta,delta^2), where delta=C_K*sqrt(n/N)+t/sqrt(N). Sigma may be singular. Neither zero row means, identical row laws, nor independence of coordinates within each row is required. This is the additive, unwhitened bound in Remark 5.40(1), Eq. (5.25). Consequently, if n/N<=rho and ||Sigma||_op<=S for deterministic constants rho,S, setting t=sqrt(N) gives P(||A^T A/N||_op>S+max(D,D^2))<=2 exp(-c_K*N), where D=C_K*sqrt(rho)+1. Uniform K,rho,S give a constant threshold and a probability smaller than N^(-d) for every fixed d>0 for all sufficiently large N. This consequence uses the unwhitened row bound, not a bound for Sigma^(-1/2)a_i.
Finite real dimensions N,n>=1; independent rows with common uncentered second moment Sigma.
Uniform directional sub-Gaussian row norm at most K>0, with the moment-norm convention in the statement.
Only the final constant-threshold consequence additionally assumes n/N<=rho and ||Sigma||_op<=S, uniformly in N.

body:
[Definition 25 of arXiv:2506.10511, '2506.10511'] For $s>0$, ${\bm z}\in\mathds{R}^d$, $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and  $b>0$, we say that a cube $V_{3s}({\bm z})$ is $(3s,\alpha, b)$-good if the following condition holds.
For any two different edges $\langle {\bm u}_i,{\bm v}_i\rangle\in\mathcal{E}$, $i=1,2$, with ${\bm u}_1\in V_s({\bm z})^c$, ${\bm v}_1\in V_s({\bm z})$, ${\bm u}_2\in V_{3s}({\bm z})$ and ${\bm v}_2\in V_{3s}({\bm z})^c$, we have $|{\bm v}_1-{\bm u}_2|\geq \alpha s$ and
$$
D({\bm v}_1,{\bm u}_2;V_{3s}({\bm z}))\geq (b\alpha s)^\theta.
$$
Additionally, we say that the tuple $({\bm u}_1,{\bm v}_1, {\bm u}_2,{\bm v}_2)$ forms a $V_{3s}({\bm z})$-special pair of edges if $\langle {\bm u}_i,{\bm v}_i\rangle\in\mathcal{E}$, $i=1,2$, with ${\bm u}_1\in V_s({\bm z})^c$, ${\bm v}_1\in V_s({\bm z})$, ${\bm u}_2\in V_{3s}({\bm z})$ and ${\bm v}_2\in V_{3s}({\bm z})^c$.
title: Definition 25 of arXiv:2506.10511

body:
[Definition def:local-collision-pieces of arXiv:2608.12415, 'Sharp Phase Transition for Ellipsoid Fitting'] Fix a gadget record
\[
    \tau_t\cdot\tau_{t-1}\cdot\dots\cdot\tau_1,
    \qquad
    \tau_i\in\{\alpha,\beta, \frac{1}{d} I_m, M_D\}.
\]
A consecutive sub-record
\(
    R
    =
    \tau_b\cdot\tau_{b-1}\cdot\dots\cdot\tau_a
\)
is called a \emph{local-collision piece}, abbreviated \emph{LCP}, if it
satisfies the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Each constituent gadget is a gadget in $A$, i.e., from $\{\alpha,\beta, \frac{1}{d} I_m, M_D\}$.

    \item The concatenation preceding the terminal gadget is locally
    proper; namely,
    \(
        \tau_{b-1}\circ\tau_{b-2}\circ\cdots\circ\tau_a
    \)
    has no vertex intersections beyond the prescribed concatenation
    boundaries.

    \item The terminal gadget is either $\frac{1}{d}I_m $ or $M_D$, or a gadget \(\tau_b\) that has a nontrivial vertex
    intersection with a gadget that appeared earlier in the global record.
    This earlier gadget may lie inside the same block or inside a preceding
    block of the global decomposition.

    \item If the terminal interaction is an isolated well-behaved
    backtracking pair
    \(\tau_b\cdot\tau_{b-1}\), then its leading reduced contribution is
    canceled by the MP recurrence and is not regarded as an error term.
    Only a backtracking-residual term in the sense of
    (def:backtracking-residuals of the paper) is retained, supported on the same
    two-gadget record
    \(\tau_b\cdot\tau_{b-1}\).
\end{enumerate}
The length of an LCP is the number of underlying gadgets in its record.
We call \(\tau_a\) its start and \(\tau_b\) its terminal gadget.
title: Local-Collision Pieces for MP Polynomials

body: In mathematical logic, the lambda calculus is a formal system for expressing computation based on function abstraction and application using variable binding and substitution. Untyped lambda calculus, the topic of this article, is a universal machine, i.e. a model of computation that can be used to simulate any Turing machine. It was introduced by the mathematician Alonzo Church in the 1930s as part of his research into the foundations of mathematics. In 1936, Church found a formulation which was logically consistent, and documented it in 1940.
title: Lambda calculus

[Lemma lem:purntbd of arXiv:2606.02472, 'Correlated uniform attachment trees'] [Lemma~3 of [Pekoz2017]]
Let $R_m$ be the number of red balls in a standard P\'olya urn  started with $r\in\mathbb{N}$ red balls and $b\in \mathbb{N}$ blue balls after $m$ draws and replacements. Then there is a coupling of $R_m$ and  $B_{r,b}\sim\mathrm{Beta}(r,b)$ such that
\[
|R_m - m B_{r,b}| \leq 2(b\wedge r) (r+b), 
\]
and consequently

\begin{align*}
	\mathbb{P}(R_m \geq t) &\geq  \mathbb{P}(m B_{r,b} \geq t + 2(b\wedge r) (r+b)).
\end{align*}
