[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2506.10817, 'On the Weak Error for Local Stochastic Volatility Models'] Let $(\eta_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a bounded adapted process that is also bounded from below by a positive constant. Let $X_t=x_0+\int_0^t \eta_s\,dW_s$. Then there
        exists a weak (Markov) solution of 
\begin{align*}
dY_t&=\widehat{\eta}\bigl(t, Y_t\bigr) \, dW_t,
\\
Y_0&=x_0,
\end{align*}
where the function $\widehat{\eta}$ is given by
$
\widehat{\eta}^2\bigl(t, X_t \bigr)=\E\bigl[ \eta_t^2 \big| X_t\bigr],
$
and it holds that
$Y_t \stackrel{d}{=} X_t$ for all $t \ge 0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Defstar of arXiv:2605.06488, 'Continuous-state branching processes with L\'evy-Khintchine drift-interaction: Laplace dua'] The boundary point $\Delta$ is classified as follows:
	\begin{itemize}
		\item \textbf{Entrance} if, when $X$ is started from $\Delta$, it leaves $\Delta$ and never returns almost surely. 
		Equivalently, $\Delta$ is non-absorbing and inaccessible from the interior.
		
		\item \textbf{Exit} if $X$ hits $\Delta$ with positive probability and, once there, remains at $\Delta$ forever. 
		That is, $\Delta$ is accessible and absorbing.
		
		\item \textbf{Regular} if $X$ hits $\Delta$ with positive probability and can subsequently leave it with positive probability; in other words, $\Delta$ is accessible and non-absorbing. Precisely, for any $x\in (0,\infty)$,
		\[
		\mathbb{P}_x\!\left(\exists\, 0 < s < t < \infty : X_s=\Delta \text{ and } X_t \neq \Delta \right) > 0.
		\]
		
		\item \textbf{Natural} if $\Delta$ is inaccessible and absorbing.
	\end{itemize}

[Definition def:standard-couple of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and two distributions $\mathcal{D}$ and~$\mathcal{D}'$ on non-negative integers such that~$\mathcal{D} \gtrsim \mathcal{D}'$.
Let $X$ be the backoff process with 
send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and
birth distribution~$\mathcal{D}$ 
and let $X'$ be the backoff process with send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and birth distribution~$\mathcal{D}'$.
The \emph{\newsym{standard coupling}{standard coupling of two backoff processes}{\textrm{standard coupling}}} of~$X'$ and~$X$ has the following invariants for every $i\geq 0$ and $t\geq 0$.
\begin{description}  
\item  [Inv-$b_i(t)$:] $\mathbf{b}_i^{X'}(t) \subseteq \mathbf{b}_i^{X}(t)$.
\item  [Inv-$B_i(t)$:] $\mathbf{B}_i^{X'}(t) \subseteq \mathbf{B}_i^{X}(t)$.
\item [Inv-$s_i(t)$:] $\mathbf{s}_i^{X'}(t) \subseteq \mathbf{s}_i^{X}(t)$.
\end{description}
The coupling is defined as follows.
For each $i\geq 0$, $\mathbf{b}_i^{X'}(0) = \mathbf{b}_i^{X}(0) = \emptyset$, establishing Inv-$b_i(0)$.
 
For each positive integer~$t$, 
the coupling evolves as follows.
First,
the pair $(n^X(t),n^{X'}(t))$ is chosen from the joint distribution~$C$ from Definition~(def:phi of the paper), so that $n^X(t) \sim \mathcal{D}$, $n^{X'}(t) \sim \mathcal{D}'$ and $n^X(t) \geq n^{X'}(t)$.
Then for each $Z\in\{X',X\}$, the set $\mathbf{n}^Z(t)$
is defined according  to Definition~(def:backoffasgen of the paper). In particular, if
 $n^{Z}(t) = 0$ then $\mathbf{n}^{Z}(t) = \emptyset$. Otherwise, ${\mathbf{n}^Z(t)} = \{\mathcal{B}(t,0,1),\ldots,\mathcal{B}(t,0,n^Z(t))\}$.
For all $i\geq 0$, the sets
$\mathbf{B}^{X'}_i(t)$, $\mathbf{s}^{X'}_i(t)$,  
$\mathbf{e}^{X'}_i(t)$, $\mathbf{b}^{X'}_i(t)$, and $B^X_i(t)$ are chosen according to Definition~(def:backoffasgen of the paper).

Using Inv-$b_0(t-1)$, we get
$\mathbf{B}_0^{X'}(t) = \mathbf{n}^{X'}(t) \cup \mathbf{b}_0^{X'}(t-1) \subseteq
\mathbf{n}^{X}(t) \cup \mathbf{b}_0^{X}(t-1) = \mathbf{B}_0^{X}(t)$, 
establishing Inv-$B_0(t)$.
Also, 
for $i\geq 1$ 
using Inv-$b_i(t-1)$, we get $\mathbf{B}_i^{X'}(t) = \mathbf{b}_i^{X'}(t-1) \subseteq \mathbf{b}_i^{X}(t-1) = \mathbf{B}_i^{X}(t)$, establishing Inv-$B_i(t)$

For every   $i\geq 0$, $\mathbf{S}^{X}_i(t)$ is formed by including each ball in 
$\mathbf{B}_i^{X}(t) \setminus \mathbf{B}_i^{X'}(t)$ 
independently with probability~$p_i$.
Then $\mathbf{s}^{X}_i(t) = \mathbf{S}^{X}_i(t) \cup \mathbf{s}^{X'}_i(t)$, establishing Inv-$s_i(t)$.

Finally, for every $i\geq 0$, $\mathbf{e}_i^{X}(t)$ and $\mathbf{b}_i^{X}(t)$ are chosen according to Definition~(def:backoffasgen of the paper).
The invariant Inv-$b_i(t)$ is established for all $i\geq 0$ as follows.  Fix $i$ and consider   a ball $\beta \in \mathbf{b}_i^{X'}(t)$. We wish to show $\beta \in \mathbf{b}_i^{X}(t)$.
There are two possibilities.
\begin{itemize}
\item   $\beta \in \mathbf{B}_i^{X'}(t) \setminus \mathbf{s}_i^{X'}(t)$:  
In this case, by Inv-$B_i(t)$, $\beta \in \mathbf{B}_i^{X}(t)$. By construction,   $\beta\notin \mathbf{s}_i^{X}(t)$ so $\beta \in \mathbf{b}_i^{X}(t)$.
\item (for $i\geq 1$) $\beta \in \mathbf{s}^{X'}_{i-1}(t) \setminus \mathbf{e}^{X'}_{i-1}(t)$:
From Definition~(def:backoffasgen of the paper), $s^{X'}(t) \geq 2$, By
Inv-$s_{i-1}(t)$, $\beta \in \mathbf{s}^{X}_{i-1}(t)$. By all of the constraints Inv-$s_k(t)$, $s^{X}(t) \geq s^{X'}(t) \geq 2$ so $e^{X}_{i-1}(t) = \emptyset$ and
$\beta \in \mathbf{s}^{X}_{i-1}(t) \setminus \mathbf{e}^{X}_{i-1}(t)$ which implies
$\beta \in \mathbf{b}_i^{X}(t)$.
\end{itemize}
title: Definition def:standard-couple of arXiv:2602.21315

[Theorem prop:Tweedie3.10 of arXiv:2603.20078, '\bf \Large Gated Infinite Server Queues in Light Traffic'] Let $P$ be the transition law of a $\psi$-irreducible, aperiodic Markov chain on ${\sf X}$.
The chain is positive recurrent with an invariant probability measure $\pi$ satisfying
$\int_{\sf X} h(x)\pi(dx)< \infty$ for a non-negative function $h$ if and only if there is
a non-negative function $V(x)$, finite $\pi$-almost everywhere, and a small set $C$ such
that 
\begin{equation}  
\int_{\sf X} P(x,dy) V(y) \leq V(x) - h(x) + b {\bf 1}_C(x),\hspace{0.3in} x\in {\sf X}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own work draft, proof (unaudited), conditional on the unaudited fixed-slab limit C003. In the noiseless Gaussian teacher-student max-margin model with an independently specified perfect probe, fix original-pool ratio beta=N/(d-1)>0 and any finite slab threshold b>0 before taking dimension to infinity. The draft proves that the limiting test error satisfies e_beta(b)>=atan(1/max(1,6 beta))/pi. Thus inf over all finite b>0 is at least 1/(12 pi beta) for beta>=1/6; no threshold b=b(beta), fixed within each dimension limit, yields an exponential original-pool-budget envelope. The proof converts angle stationarity into a mean identity for a monotone tilt of the probability density J'(x)/J(c), where J(x)=E[(x-H)_+^2]. For rho>=1 it forces c<2 and hence rho<6 beta; rho<1 is a separate branch. The argument does not concern the paper's kept-data envelope, dimensions with b_d->0, the exact unpruned endpoint, imperfect probes, or the optimal fraction. Independent mathematical and novelty review are pending; this is not a settled brain theorem.

body:
[Defn of arXiv:2411.10318, 'Polynomial Mixing of the critical Glauber Dynamics for the Ising Model'] \begin{itemize}
\item 
Let $G$ be a graph on a vertex set $V$. The Ising model on this graph with inverse temperature $\beta$ and external field $h:V\to[-\infty,\infty]$ is the probability measure $\mu$ on $\{-1,1\}^V$ satisfying
$$\mu_{\beta,h}(\sigma)=\dfrac{1}{Z_{G,h}}\exp\left(\beta\sum\limits_{u\sim v}\sigma_u\sigma_v+\sum\limits_{v\in V}h(v)\sigma_v\right).$$
By $\mu_\beta$ we will just denote the Ising model with $h=0$.
\item
For a configuration $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^V$ and for some $i\in[n]$, let $\sigma^i$ be the configuration $\sigma$ in which we have flipped coordinate $i$. For two configurations $\sigma,\tau\in\{-1,1\}^V$, we write $\sigma\sim\tau$ if $\tau=\sigma^i$ for some $i\in[n]$. The Glauber Dynamics on $G$ is a Markov chain with transition probabilities, for $\sigma\neq\tau$, equal to
$$P_\beta(\sigma,\tau)=\begin{cases}
\dfrac{\mu_\beta(\tau)}{\mu_\beta(\sigma)+\mu_\beta(\tau)},\ \ \text{if}\ \ \sigma \sim \tau
\\ \\
0,\ \ \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}$$
\item
On the set of probability measures on $\{-1,1\}^n$, we define the \textbf{Total Variation Distance} between $\mu,\nu$ to be
$$\text{d}_{\text{TV}}(\mu,\nu):=\sup\limits_{A}|\mu(A)-\nu(A)|=\dfrac{1}{2}\sum\limits_{\sigma}|\mu(\sigma)-\nu(\sigma)|.$$
\item 
The mixing time of this Markov Chain is defined to be
$$t_{\beta,\text{mix}}(\varepsilon)=\inf\{t\ge0:\text{d}_{\text{TV}}(P_\beta^t\delta_{\sigma_0},\mu_\beta)\le\varepsilon,\ \forall\sigma_0\in\{-1,1\}^V\},$$
where $\delta_{\sigma_0}$ is the probability measure that gives mass 1 to $\sigma_0$. We set
$t_{\beta,\text{mix}}:=t_{\beta,\text{mix}}\left(1/4\right).$
\end{itemize}
title: Unnumbered defn of arXiv:2411.10318, 'Polynomial Mixing of the critical Glauber Dynamics for the I'

[Thm t:Dtmoment of arXiv:2411.10586, 'A convergence framework for Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble\\ via pole evolution'] {[bourgade2022optimal]}
We consider $\beta$-ensemble $x_1\ge \cdots \ge x_n$ whose distribution density is given by (equation e:beta of the paper), with potential $V(x)$ satisfying (a:Vasump of the paper). Denote
\[
    s_n(z)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{1}{x_i-z}, \quad m_V(z)=\int\frac{{\rm d} \mu_V(x)}{x-z}.
\]
There exist $\eta>0$, and $C>0$ such that for any $q\geq 1$ and $n\geq 1$, the following holds
\begin{enumerate}
\item For any $0\leq u\leq n^{2/3}$, it holds that
\[
    \mathbb{P}(\exists k\in \llbracket 1,n\rrbracket,  x_k\not\in [A-u n^{-2/3}, B+u n^{-2/3}])\leq Ce^{-u^{3/4}/C}.
\]
\item For any $z\in \mathbb{H}$, with $A-\eta\leq {\rm Re}[z]\leq B+\eta$ and $0<{\rm Im}[z]\leq \eta$,
\[
    \mathbb{E}[|s_n(z)-m_V(z)|^q]\leq \frac{(Cq)^{2q}}{(n{\rm Im}[z])^q}. 
\]
For  $z\in \mathbb{H}$ with $\kappa=|{\rm Re}[z]-A|\wedge |{\rm Re}[z]-B|$, $0<{\rm Im}[z]\leq \eta$, and $Cq^{1/2}/(n\sqrt{\kappa}) \le {\rm Im}[z] \le \kappa$, 
\[
    \mathbb{E}[|s_n(z)-m_V(z)|^{2q}]\leq \frac{(Cq)^{2q}}{(n{\rm Im}[z])^{4q}\kappa^{q}} + \frac{(Cq)^q}{n^{2q}(\kappa {\rm Im}[z])^q } +\frac{(Cq)^{2q}}{ n^{2q}\kappa^q}
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm t:Dtmoment of arXiv:2411.10586

[Definition D_WG of arXiv:2510.26724, 'Sharp Fuss-Catalan thresholds in graph bootstrap percolation'] Recall that $E_t$ denotes the set of edges added to a graph 
$G$ in the $t$th round of the $H$-dynamics. 
For each $e\in E(\langle W^{(e)} \rangle_H)=\bigcup_{t\geqslant0}E_t$, 
we define $W^{(e)}$ as follows. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $e\in E_0$, we simply put $W^{(e)}=e$. 
\item Otherwise, if $e\in E_t$, for some $t\geqslant1$, 
we select a copy $H^{(e)}$ of $H$, for which 
$E(H^{(e)}\setminus e)\subset \bigcup_{s<t}E_s$, 
and put 
\begin{equation}
W^{(e)}=\bigcup_{f\in E(H^{(e)}\setminus e)} W^{(f)}. 
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

[Prop 22 of arXiv:2608.25829, 'Topology of low-dimensional generalized Ricci solitons and string backgrounds'] Let $M^6$ be a compact simply connected manifold with a locally
free $T^2$-action with orbit space $B$.  Assume:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $B$ is cyclic,
    \item The orbifold locus of $B$ consists of a finite union of points and a union of closed oriented surfaces 
    \[
        D=\bigcup_{i=1}^r D_i
    \]
    meeting transversely,
    \item for every intersection point $p\in D_i\cap D_j$, the natural map
    \[
\Gamma_i\oplus\Gamma_j\longrightarrow\Gamma_p
    \]
    is injective, where $\Gamma_i\cong\mathbb Z/m_i$ is the generic
    stabilizer along $D_i$.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\[
    \Tor H_2(M)
    \cong
    \bigoplus_{i=1}^r H_1(D_i;\mathbb Z/m_i)
    \cong
    \bigoplus_{i=1}^r (\mathbb Z/m_i)^{2g(D_i)}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 21 (Tightness criterion) of arXiv:2604.26549, 'Existence and uniqueness results of a stochastic nonlinear heat equation with a constraint'] Let $\{X_m \}_{m \in \N }$ be a sequence of continuous $\Fb-$adapted $L^2(\bO) -$valued processes. Then
		\begin{itemize}
			\item[(a)] there exists a positive constant ${C}_{1}$ such that
			$$
			\sup_{m\in \N} \E \Big[ \sup_{t \in [0,T]} \big( \| X_m (t) \|_{H^1_0(\bO)}^{2} + \|X_m(t)\|_{L^p(\bO)}^p\big) \Big]  \le {C}_{1} ,
			$$
			\item[(b)] there exists a positive constant ${C}_{2}$ such that
			\begin{equation*}
				 \sup_{m \in \N} \E \left[  \int_{0}^{T} \|AX_m (t)\|_{L^2(\bO)}^2  dt \right] \le {C}_{2} ,
			\end{equation*}
			\item[(c)]  $\{X_m \}_{m \in \N }$ satisfies the Aldous condition $[\mathbf{A}]$ in $L^2(\bO)$.
		\end{itemize}
		Let $\Pr_{m}$ be the law of $X_m $ on $\mathcal{Z}_T$, for all $m\in\N$.
		Then, for every $\varepsilon >0 ,$ there exists a compact subset ${K}_{\varepsilon }$ of $\mathcal{Z}_T $ such that 
		$$
		\sup_{m\in \N} \Pr_m ({K}_{\varepsilon })\ge 1-\varepsilon .
		$$
title: Tightness criterion

[Proposition pro:equivalence of arXiv:2411.14921, 'A boundary Harnack principle and its application to analyticity of 3D Brownian intersectio'] Let $\widehat A $ be a closed set in $\mathbb R^3$ such that $\widehat A ^\circ=\varnothing$ and $U\setminus\widehat A $ is connected for any domain $U\subset\mathbb{R}^{3}$. Then, the following two statements are equivalent:

    \textnormal{(i)} For any rational point $x\in\mathbb R^3$ and any rational $r>0$, there exist positive constants $\delta_1$ and $\delta_2$ that only depend on $\widehat A , x$ and $r$ such that for all $A\subseteq\widehat A $ and $y\inB(x,r/2)\setminus A$,
    \begin{equation}
        \mathbf{P}_y\Big(W(\tau_{\partialB(x,r)})\notin\sausage{\widehat A}{\delta_1} \,\Big |\,  W[0,\tau_{\partialB(x,r)}]\cap A=\varnothing\Big)>\delta_2.
    \end{equation}

    \textnormal{(ii)} For each domain $U$ and compact set $K\subseteq U$, there exists a constant $C(U,K,\widehat A )$, such that for any closed subset $A$ of $\widehat A $, and any two bounded positive harmonic functions $u,v$ on $U\setminus A$ that vanish continuously on regular points of $A\cap U$, we have
    \[
    u(x_1)\,v(x_2)<C\,u(x_2)\,v(x_1),\quad \text{ for all } x_1,x_2\in K\setminus A.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 2 (Reachability and mutual reachability) of arXiv:2608.28991, 'Jigsaw-CRL: Recovering Global Latent Causal Order from Fragmented Multi-Client Interventio'] For two nodes $i,j \in \cV_k$, we say that $i$ is \emph{reachable} to $j$, written $i \rightsquigarrow_k j$, if there exists a sequence of nodes
$i = v_0, v_1, \dots, v_m = j$, 
such that for every $\ell = 0,\dots,m-1$, either $v_\ell \prec_k v_{\ell+1}$ or $v_\ell \leftrightarrow v_{\ell+1} \in \cD_k$.
Two nodes $i,j \in \cV_k$ are said to be \emph{mutually reachable} if $i \rightsquigarrow_k j$ and $j \rightsquigarrow_k i$.
title: Reachability and mutual reachability

	\]

Then the finite free infinitesimal generator of $\mathfrak{q}$ satisfies
\begin{align*}
\iota_d\bigl(\mathcal{L}[\mathfrak{q}] f\bigr)
= \mathcal{L}^{(d)}\bigl[\iota_d(\mathfrak{q})\bigr]\bigl(\iota_d(f)\bigr) 
\qquad f \in \mathbb{R}[x]_d,
\end{align*}
where $\iota_d(\mathfrak{q}) \coloneqq \{\iota_d(q_s)\}_{s\ge0} \subset \operatorname{Im}\iota_{d}$ is a $\boxplus^d$-semigroup.

body: [Theorem mainv2 of arXiv:2609.04023, 'Characterizing Contractions and Weighted Blowdowns'] Suppose $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Z}$ are smooth separated Deligne--Mumford surfaces, and there is a contraction $f : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Z}$ whose exceptional $\mathcal{C}$ is a smooth stacky curve (not necessarily irreducible). Moreover, suppose that there is a closed reduced substack $\mathcal{Y}\subseteq \mathcal{Z}$ of dimension 0 such that $f(\mathcal{C})=\mathcal{Y}$ set theoretically and $f : \mathcal{X} \setminus \mathcal{C} \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathcal{Z} \setminus \mathcal{Y}$ is an isomorphism. Then $f$ is a regular weighted blowup with reduced center $\mathcal{Y}$, in particular $f|_\mathcal{C} : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{Y}$ is a weighted projective bundle, and $\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{X}}(\mathcal{C})|_{\mathcal{C}} \simeq \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}}(-1) \otimes f^*\mathcal{L}$ for some line bundle $\mathcal{L}$ on $\mathcal{Y}$. }

body:
[Definition 12 (Block stratification) of arXiv:2606.16005, '\bfseries An Algebraic Matrix Spencer Theorem'] Let
\[
H=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\mathcal B}H_\alpha
\]
be a fixed common block decomposition, and write $b_\alpha:=\dim H_\alpha .$ A \emph{block stratification} is a partition
\[
\mathcal B=\mathcal P_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup \mathcal P_J
\]
of the block index set into nonempty groups, called strata. For a stratum $\mathcal P_j$, define
\[
\cH_{\mathcal P_j}:=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\mathcal P_j}\cH_\alpha,
\qquad
h_j:=\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal P_j} b_\alpha,
\qquad
m_j:=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal P_j} b_\alpha,
\]
and $q_j:=h_jm_j$. The total stratified block complexity is $Q(\mathcal P):=\sum_{j=1}^J q_j= \sum_{j=1}^J h_jm_j$.

We also write
\[
\cH_{\max}:=\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal B}b_\alpha,
\qquad
M:=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal B}b_\alpha,
\]
for the largest block size and total ambient dimension of the compressed block system.
title: Block stratification

body:
For data uniform on the sphere (dimension d >= 3) or Gaussian, labels with independent noise, and ANY width-m two-layer network with a continuous piecewise-linear activation (ReLU included), arbitrary unbounded weights, bias, and skip connection: fitting eps below the noise floor forces Lip(f) at least of order eps sqrt(n / (m log(C m n d / eps))) with high probability. This proves the Bubeck-Li-Nagaraj conjectured lower bound up to one logarithmic factor for the piecewise-linear class, removing the boundedness assumption; depth two is the critical case since the law fails at depth three with unbounded weights. The fully log-free, every-activation conjecture remains open.

[Proposition of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] For any $\textsf{N}_\Diamond$-corr singular model $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \set{ w_\bot }, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$,
  there is an infallible model $\mathfrak{M'}$ that validates the same set of formulas.
  \begin{proof}
    We let $\mathfrak{M'} = (W', \emptyset, \leq', \sqsubset', V')$, where $W' = W \setminus \set{ w_\bot }$,
    ${\leq'} = {\leq \upharpoonright_{W'}}$,
    ${\sqsubset'} = (\sqsubset \upharpoonright_{W'}) \cup \set{ (x, y') \in W' \times W'; x \sqsubset w_\bot \mathrel{\text{\&}} \exists x' \in W'\,(x \leq x' \sqsubset y') }$,
    and $V'(p) = V(p) \cap W'$ for any $p \in \mathord{\mathrm{PropVar}}$.
    Here, $\mathfrak{M'}$ is clearly infallible.
    Since every formula is true at $w_\bot$ by Proposition (prop:all-is-fair of the paper),
    it suffices to show that $w \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M'} \varphi \mathrel{\Leftrightarrow} w \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \varphi$ for any $w \in W'$ and $\varphi \in \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$.
    We use an induction on the construction of $\varphi$. We shall only prove the modal cases.

    ($\Box\Rightarrow$) Suppose $w \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M'} \Box \psi$ and take any $w', x' \in W$ such that $w \leq w' \sqsubset x'$.
    If $x' = w_\bot$, then $w_\bot \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi$.
    Otherwise, $x' \ne w_\bot$, so $w' \ne w_\bot$ by $\set{ w_\bot }$ being upward closed with respect to $\sqsubset$.
    Here, $w \leq w' \sqsubset x'$ and $w, w', x' \in W'$ imply $w \leq' w' \sqsubset' x'$ by definition,
    then $w' \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M'} \psi$ by the assumption, so $w' \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by the induction hypothesis.
    Therefore, $w \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$.

    ($\Box\Leftarrow$) Suppose $w \not \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M'} \Box \psi$, then there are $w', x'' \in W'$ such that $w \leq' w' \sqsubset' x'' \not \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M'} \psi$.
    Here, $x'' \not \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by the induction hypothesis.
    Also, $w' \sqsubset' x''$ implies either $(w \leq)\, w' \sqsubset x'' \,(\not \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi)$,
    or there is $w'' \in W'$ such that $(w \leq)\, w' \leq w'' \sqsubset x'' \,(\not \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi)$.
    Therefore, $w \not \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$.

    ($\Diamond\Rightarrow$) Suppose $w \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M'} \Diamond \psi$ and take any $w' \in W$ such that $w \leq w'$.
    If $w' = w_\bot$, then $w' \sqsubset w_\bot \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi$. 
    Otherwise, $w' \ne w_\bot$ implies $w' \in W'$, then $w \leq' w'$ by definition,
    so by assumption, there is $x' \in W'$ such that $w' \sqsubset' x' \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M'} \psi$, then $x' \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by the induction hypothesis.
    Here, $w' \sqsubset' x'$ implies either $w' \sqsubset x' \,(\Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi)$
    or $w' \sqsubset w_\bot \,(\Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi)$.
    Therefore, $w \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$.

    ($\Diamond\Leftarrow$) Suppose $w \not \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M'} \Diamond \psi$, then there is $w' \in W'$ such that $w \leq' w'$ and $\forall x' \in W'\, (w' \sqsubset' x' \mathrel{\Rightarrow} x' \not \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M'} \psi)$.
    Here, $w \leq w'$ by definition.
    We distinguish the following cases:
    \begin{itemize}
      \item Suppose $w' \not \sqsubset w_\bot$.
            Take any $x' \in W$ such that $w' \sqsubset x'$, then $x' \ne w_\bot$, then $w' \sqsubset' x'$ by definition,
            then $x' \not \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M'} \psi$ by the assumption,
            so $x' \not \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by the induction hypothesis.
            Therefore, $w \not \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$.
      \item Now suppose $w' \sqsubset w_\bot$.

body:
[Lemma lem:flow-wellposed of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] For every $f_{0} \in \mathcal{D}$ the evolution
			equation~(equation eq:flow of the paper) has a unique global mild solution in
			$L^{1}(\mathbb{R})$, which remains in $\mathcal{D}$ and preserves
			$\mathcal{D}_{+}$, symmetry, and the median. If moreover
			$f_{0} \in \mathcal{D}_{+}$ and the rank profile
			$\mathfrak{f}_{0} = f_{0}\circ Q_{0}$ satisfies
			\begin{equation}
				\int_{0}^{1}\big|\log \mathfrak{f}_{0}(z)\big|\,dz < \infty,
				\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
				\mathbb{E}_{f_{0}}\big|\log f_{0}(X)\big| < \infty,
				
			\end{equation}
			then the entropy law~(equation eq:entropy-law of the paper) holds:
			$H(f_{t}) = -t + \log(4/f_{0}(m)) + o(1)$; the discrete analogue
			holds in the sharper form
			$H(f_{n}) = -n\log 2 + H(\mathcal{K}) - \log f_{0}(m) + o(1)$, with
			$\mathcal{K}$ the Koenigs law of Theorem~(thm:limit-law of the paper), so in
			particular $H(f_{n+1}) - H(f_{n}) \to -\log 2$.

[Definition maindefi-n of arXiv:2412.06701, 'Matsumoto-Yor processes on Jordan algebras'] Let $n$ be a positive integer and $\left(w_k^{n} \ ; \ k \ge 1\right)$ be a sequence of i.i.d. random variables on $E_+$ distributed according to $\mathrm{GIG}_{E_+}\left( p ; ne, ne \right)$. The Markov chain $\left( L^{n}_k \ ; \ k \ge 0\right)$ and the random processes 
$\left( \Lambda^{n}_k \ ; \ k \ge 0\right)$,
$\left( I_k^n \ ; \ k\ge 0\right)$ defined by
\begin{align*}
L^{n}_{k+1}       := & \ \mathrm P(w^{n}_{k+1})(L^{n}_k)+\frac{1}{n}w^{n}_{k+1} \ , \\
\Lambda^{n}_{k+1} := & \ \mathrm P\left( w^{n}_{k+1}+\frac{1}{n}(L^{n}_k)^{-1} \right)(\Lambda^{n}_{k}) \ , \\
I_k^{n}           := & \ 
   \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\mathrm P((w^{n}_1)^{-1})\dots \mathrm P((w_i^n)^{-1})(w_{i+1}^n)^{-1} \ ,
\end{align*}
with starting points $L^{n}_0=\ell_0$, $\Lambda^{n}_0=\lambda_0$.
title: Definition maindefi-n of arXiv:2412.06701

[Prop annulus-crossing of arXiv:2604.14122, 'The scaling limit of random walk and\\ the intrinsic metric on planar critical percolation'] Let $f\in\mathbf N$ and consider the annulus $A(0;2n^{-1}R^{\kappa-f},4n^{-1}R^{\kappa-f})$. Let $s<1$ and define $G=G(s,f)$ to be the event that for each pair of open annulus crossings that are that are connected inside $B(0,2n^{-1}R^{\kappa-f})$, the geodesic resp.\ resistance distance between them within $B(0,4n^{-1}R^{\kappa-f})$ is at most $s\mathbf{q}_n$. Then for every $\zeta,p'>0$, there exists $C=C(\zeta,p')>0$ independent of $f,s$ and some event $F$ depending only on the sites in $A(0;n^{-1}R^{\kappa-f},n^{-1}R^{\kappa-f+1})$ such that $\mathbf{P}(F)>1-p'$ uniformly in $n,f$ and for all $R$ sufficiently large depending on $\zeta$, and $p$ small enough depending on $R$,
\begin{equation}
    \mathbf{P}(G^{c}\mid F)\leq Cs^{-(\frac{3}{4}+\zeta)\alpha}R^{-\alpha f}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: OPEN PROBLEM (optimal quadratic Littlewood-Offord bound). For Q = sum c_ij xi_i xi_j with all coefficients nonzero and xi_i i.i.d. Bernoulli, is sup_z P(Q = z) = O(n^{-1/2})? More generally, the optimal anti-concentration exponent for polynomials of degree d. Source: Tao and Vu, From the Littlewood-Offord problem to the circular law, Section 6. Known: Costello (2013) proved n^{-1/2+o(1)} for quadratic forms. Meka, Nguyen and Vu (2016) proved, for a multilinear polynomial of degree d and rank r with Rademacher inputs and every interval I of length 1, P(P(xi) in I) <= min{B d^{4/3} (log r)^{1/2} r^{-1/(4d+1)}, exp(B d^2 (log log r)^2) r^{-1/2}}. For d = 2 the second bound is r^{-1/2} times exp(4B (log log r)^2), a factor that grows faster than every power of log r, so the loss is superpolylogarithmic, not logarithmic; the exact O(n^{-1/2}) remains open.

body:
[Definition def:nprefix of arXiv:2604.20660, 'The Legendre structure of the TAP complexity\\ for the Ising spin glass'] Fix $n\geq 1$ and set $q_0=0$. Given a strictly increasing sequence
		$(q_i)_{1\leq i\leq n}$ in $(0,1)$ and a strictly increasing sequence of
		weights $(u_i)_{1\leq i\leq n}$ in $(0,1)$, we write
		$\mathrm{Prefix}_{n+1}\!\bigl((u_i)_{1\leq i\leq n},(q_i)_{1\leq i\leq n}\bigr)$
		for the collection of probability measures $\zeta$ on $[0,1]$ satisfying
		\begin{equation*}
			\mathrm{supp}(\zeta)\cap[0,q_n]=\{q_0,q_1,\ldots,q_n\}
			\qquad\text{and}\qquad
			\zeta([0,q_{i-1}])=u_i \;\text{ for all }\; i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}.
		\end{equation*}
		We say that such $\zeta$ has an \emph{$(n+1)$-atom prefix} $\{0,q_1,\ldots,q_n\}$.
title: Probability measures with an $(n+1)$-atom prefix

body:
[Theorem thm: convergence introduction of arXiv:2602.04429, 'Disordered systems and (subcritical) polynomial chaos\\ with heavy-tail disorder'] Assume that the noise \(\omega\) is centered and has a tail distribution given by~(equation def: omega tail of the paper) with \(\gamma \in (1,2)\). 
	Assume also that there exists some \(q\in (\gamma,2]\) such that the correlation functions \((\psi_{\delta}^{(k)})_{k\geq 1}\) satisfy the following:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item For every \(k\in \mathbb{N}\) there exists some continuous \(k\)-point correlation function \(\boldsymbol\psi^{(k)}\) such that 
		\[
		\lim_{\delta\downarrow 0} \big\| \overline{\psi}_{\delta}^{(k)} - \boldsymbol\psi^{(k)} \big\|_q=0 \,;
		\]

		\item The following uniform integrability condition is verified: for every \(C>0\),
		\[
		\limsup_{\delta \downarrow 0} \sum_{k \, \geqslant\, 0} C^k \| \overline{\psi}_{\delta}^{(k)} \|_{q} < +\infty
		\quad \text{ and } \quad
		\lim\limits_{M \to +\infty} \displaystyle\displaystyle\limsup_{\delta \downarrow 0} \sum\limits_{k > M} C^k \| \overline{\psi}_{\delta}^{(k)} \|_{q} = 0.
		\]
	\end{enumerate}
	Then, under the \emph{subcritical} condition \(\lambda < \frac{d_{\mathrm{eff}}}{\gamma}\), in the intermediate disorder regime of~(equation eq: intermediate disorder window of the paper), \textit{i.e.}\ if \(\lim_{\delta\downarrow 0}   \beta_{\delta} \delta^{d_{\mathrm{eff}}/\gamma - \lambda} = \hat{\beta} \in [0,\infty)\), we have the following convergence in distribution:
	\[
	Z_{\Omega_{\delta}}^{\omega,\beta_{\delta}} \xrightarrow{\ (d)\ }  {\ensuremath{\mathcal Z}}_{\Omega}^{\boldsymbol\zeta,\hat{\beta}} \,,
	\]
	where \({\ensuremath{\mathcal Z}}_{\Omega}^{\boldsymbol\zeta,\hat{\beta}}\) is defined in~(equation eq: limiting chaos expansion of the paper), with \(\boldsymbol\zeta = \lim_{\delta \downarrow0} \zeta_{\delta}\) a \(\gamma\)-stable Lévy white noise. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\[
 \E f_{n-1}(P_N)
 \geq n^{n/2}e^{-C_{\mu,\alpha}n}

\]

body:
[Theorem thm:carpet of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] For almost every $\tau$, the following holds for every
		$f \in \mathcal{D}_{+}$ that is continuously differentiable and
		positive on the interior of its support, every compact
		nondegenerate interval $J$ in that interior, and every phase
		$\theta$:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\normalfont(\roman*), leftmargin=*]
			\item the transported amplitude in every quadrature,
			$\Psi_{\theta,\tau} :=
			\mathrm{Re}\big[e^{i\theta}\,u_{\tau}(F)\big]\sqrt f$, has graph of
			upper box dimension exactly $\tfrac32$ on $J$;
			\item the density $f_{\tau}$ itself has graph of upper box
			dimension exactly $\tfrac32$ on $J$;
			\item at every rational $s$, by contrast, all these graphs are
			piecewise continuously differentiable, of dimension one.
		\end{enumerate}
		The value $\tfrac32$ is independent of the law, the interval, and
		the quadrature: the fractal is woven entirely in rank space and
		printed on every law through its quantile chart. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: The universal quantum carpet

body:
[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2608.23742, 'Second-order fusion asymptotics for $\Sine_\beta$ correlation functions'] Let $\beta>0$, $m\ge2$, and suppose $m\beta>1$. For pairwise distinct $a_1,\ldots,a_m\in\mathbb R$, as $\varepsilon\to0$,
\begin{align}
\rho^{(m)}_\beta(\varepsilon a_1,\ldots,\varepsilon a_m)
&=C^{(m)}_\beta|\varepsilon|^{\beta\binom m2}\prod_{i<j}|a_i-a_j|^\beta\notag\\
&\quad\times\left[1-\frac{\beta^2}{8(m\beta-1)(2m+1)}V(a)\varepsilon^2+o(\varepsilon^2)\right].
\end{align}
The remainder is locally uniform when $a$ ranges over compact subsets of the set of pairwise distinct configurations. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Second-order fusion asymptotics

body:
[Prop 53 (Strict convexity of the rate functional) of arXiv:2604.00635, 'Large deviations of the periodic Toda chain'] For any pair of probability measures $\mu_0, \mu_1 \in \mathcal{M}_1(\mathbb{R})$ (possibly equal), and any $\alpha \in \intff{0}{1}$, we have
$$I[(1-\alpha) \mu_0 + \alpha \mu_1 ] \leq (1-\alpha) I[\mu_0] + \alpha I[\mu_1] \, .$$
If $I[\mu_0], I[\mu_1] < +\infty$ and $ \mu_0 \neq \mu_1$, then for all $\alpha \in ]0;1[$ we have the strict inequality
$$I[(1-\alpha) \mu_0 + \alpha \mu_1 ] < (1-\alpha) I[\mu_0] + \alpha I[\mu_1] \, .$$
title: Strict convexity of the rate functional

body:
[Lem Lemma: Intertwining cocycle of arXiv:2605.16921, '${\ASL_n}(\mathbb Z)$ invariant random subsets of $\mathbb Z^n$'] Let $(X, \mu)$ be an ergodic $\ASL_d(\mathbb{Z})$-system and $\pi: X \to Y$ a nilfactor over $Z^0(X)$ commensurated by $\SL_d(\mathbb{Z})$. Identify $Y$ via Lemma (Lemma: Def common nilpotent group of the paper) with
    $$ Y = \bigsqcup_{n \geq 0} \Omega_n \rtimes_{\rho_n} N / \Gamma_n,$$
    where $N$ is in the standing class and the lattices $\Gamma_n$ are pairwise commensurable. Let $\mathrm{Comm}_{\Aut(N)}(\Gamma_0)$ denote the subgroup of automorphisms of $N$ preserving the commensurability class of $\Gamma_0$.

    Then there exists a map
    $$ \alpha: \ASL_d(\mathbb{Z}) \times Z^0(X) \to \mathrm{Comm}_{\Aut(N)}(\Gamma_0)$$
    with the following property: for every $\gamma \in \SL_d(\mathbb{Z})$ and $\nu$-a.e.\ $\omega \in Z^0(X)$, the canonical isomorphism $Y_\omega \to Y_{\gamma \cdot \omega}^\gamma$ induced by $\gamma$ acts on the fibre $N/\Gamma_n$ at $\omega$ by the affine map $\overline{x} \mapsto \overline{b(\gamma, \omega) \cdot \alpha(\gamma, \omega)(x)}$ for some Borel cochain $b: \ASL_d(\mathbb{Z}) \times Z^0(X) \to N$.

    Moreover, $\alpha$ satisfies the following weak cocycle identity: for $\gamma \in \SL_d(\mathbb{Z})$ and almost all $\omega \in Z^0(X)$ we have 
    $$ \alpha(\gamma_1\gamma_2, \omega) = \alpha(\gamma_1, \gamma_2\cdot \omega) \circ \alpha(\gamma_2,\omega)   \mod{ \mathrm{inn(H_\omega)}}$$
    where $H_\omega$ denotes the intersection of all lattices appearing above $\omega$ in the bundle decomposition of systems commensurable with $Y$ and $\mathrm{inn}$ denotes the set of inner automorphisms.

[Definition eq:FundAugmentedCyl of arXiv:2411.14936, 'Massive Particle Systems,\\Wasserstein Brownian Motions,\\ and the Dean--Kawasaki Equation'] For each~$\varphi\in\mcB_b(\mbbI)$ and~$f\in\mcB_b(\tau)$, we define a functional on~$\msP$ by
\begin{align}
(\varphi\otimes f)^\star(\mu)\eqdef \int \varphi(\mu_x)\, f(x) \,\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\mu(x) \,\mathrm{,}\;\,
\end{align}
and ---for notational simplicity, with slight abuse of notation--- we let
\[
\boldsymbol\varphi\otimes \mbff\eqdef \left(\varphi_1\otimes f_1,\dotsc, \varphi_k\otimes f_k\right)\,\mathrm{,}\;\, \qquad k\in {\mathbb N}_1\,\mathrm{,}\;\, \varphi\in\mcB_b(\mbbI)\,\mathrm{,}\;\, f_i\in \mcB_b(\tau)\,\mathrm{,}\;\,
\]
and we denote by
\[
(\boldsymbol\varphi\otimes \mbff)^\star \eqdef {\big((\varphi_1\otimes f_1)^\star,\dotsc, (\varphi_k\otimes f_k)^\star\big)}\colon \msP\longrightarrow{\mathbb R}^k
\]
the functional obtained by taking~$\square^\star$ componentwise.

Finally, we simply write
\begin{equation}
f^\star \eqdef\ (\car\otimes f)^\star \colon \mu\longmapsto \int f \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\mu \,\mathrm{,}\;\, \qquad f\in \mcB_b(\tau)\,\mathrm{.}
\end{equation}

body:
[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2506.10256, 'Clustering of large deviations events in heavy-tailed moving average processes: the catast'] Suppose that the sets $\Gamma$ and
$\Psi$ both satisfy Assumption \ref{ass:failure.set}.  For each \(n\), define  
\[
J_n^{\Psi,+} =  \inf \{ j \geq 0 : S_j^n \in n\Psi^c \}, \ \ J_n^{\Psi,-} =  \sup \{ j <0 : S_j^n \in n\Psi^c \}.
\]  
Then, as \(n \to \infty\), the conditional distribution of
\((J_n^{\Psi,+}/n,\, -J_n^{\Psi,-}/n)\) given \(B_0(n, \Gamma)\)
converges weakly to  the law of a random vector equal to 
\[
  \left\{ \begin{array}{ll}
            (U,1-U) & \ \text{with probability} \ \mu(\Psi), \\
            (0,0) & \ \text{with probability} \ 1-\mu(\Psi),
\end{array} \right. 
\]  
where  $U$ is a standard uniform random variable and 
\[
\mu(\Psi) = \frac{\nu(\mathcal{A}^{-1} (\Psi \cap \Gamma))}{\nu(\mathcal{A}^{-1} \Gamma)}.
\]
In particular, the conditional distribution of
\((J_n^{\Gamma, +}/n,\, -J_n^{\Gamma, -}/n)\) given \(B_0(n, \Gamma)\)
converges weakly to  the law of a random vector $(U,1-U)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2506.10256

[Prop OP_Wrap0 of arXiv:2609.01751, 'Orthogonal polynomials which are eigenfunctions of a partial differential operator'] Let polynomials ${\mathsf Q}_{{\bm j}, {\bm k}, m}^n$ of $d_1+d_2$ variables be defined by
\begin{equation*}
   {\mathsf Q}_{{\bm j}, \ell, m}^n({\bm x}, {\bm y}) = {\bm R}_{{\bm j},n-m}^{(m)}({\bm y}) [\rho({\bm y})]^m {\mathsf Y}_{\ell}^m \left(\frac{{\bm x}}{\rho({\bm y})}\right),  \quad
   ({\bm x},{\bm y}) \in \big[\Omega_1^{d_1}\big]_0 \rtimes \Omega_2^{d_2},
\end{equation*}
where $0 \le m \le n$, $|{\bm j}| = n-m$ with ${\bm j} \in {\mathbb N}_0^{d_2}$, $1\le \ell \le \dim {\mathcal H}_m^{d_1}$, and $({\bm x},{\bm y})\in
\big[\Omega_1^{d_1}\big]_0 \rtimes \Omega_2^{d_2}$. 
Then the set $\left\{{\mathsf Q}_{{\bm j}, \ell, m}^n: 1 \le \ell \le \dim {\mathcal H}_m^{d_1} \,  |{\bm j}| = n-m, \, {\bm j} \in {\mathbb N}_0^{d_2}, 0 \le m \le n\right\}$ 
is an orthogonal basis of ${\mathcal V}_n\big([\Omega^{d_1}]_0 \! \rtimes \Omega^{d_2},{\mathsf W}^{[\Omega_1]_0 \rtimes \Omega_2}\big)$.

Moreover, the norm square defined by 
${\mathsf h}_{{\bm j}, \ell, m}^{n, [\Omega_1]_0 \rtimes \Omega_2} 
= {\langle}  {\mathsf Q}_{{\bm j}, \ell, m}^n, {\mathsf Q}_{{\bm j}, \ell, m}^n{\rangle}_{\mathsf W}$, is equal to 
$$
{\mathsf h}_{{\bm j},\ell, m}^{n, [\Omega_1]_0 \rtimes \Omega_2} = {\bm h}_{n-m}\big(\rho^{2m+d_1}{\mathsf W}\big) {\mathsf h}_{\ell, m}({\mathsf W}_1).
$$

[Proposition prop:Ritz-ladder of arXiv:2608.30831, 'Sharp discrete Hardy constants in dimensions three and four\\ and strict upper bounds from'] For $N\ge3$ and $1\le k\le N$,
\begin{equation}
 C(N)\le \Lambda_k(N).

   -2k^2(k-1)(N-k+1)P_{k-2}(\lambda;N)
 
\end{align}
for $2\le k\le N$.

[Proposition pr:reduction of arXiv:2604.21142, 'Gaussian fluctuations for Internal DLA on cylinders'] Fix $\n > 0$ and $m \geq 1$, with $T^\sharp$ as in the statement of Theorem~(th:max_fluct of the paper). For every integer $T$ with $T^\sharp \leq T \leq N^m$ and every $N$ large enough, there exist an integer $T'$ with $1 \leq T' \leq T^\sharp$ and a non-negative integer $k$ with $T' + N k = T$, together with a coupling of $A(T)$ and an IDLA process $(A_*(t))_{t \geq 0}$ on ${\ensuremath{\mathbb G}} _N$ starting from $A_*(0) = R_0$, such that

where $A_*(T') + R_k \coloneqq \{(x, y+k) : (x, y) \in A_*(T')\}$.

[Definition 3 (Capacity terminology) of arXiv:2607.16502, 'Asymptotic Behavior of Path Functionals for Vector-Valued Gaussian Processes at High Level'] Let \(E\subset\R\) be non-empty and compact.  A \emph{finite capacity} on
\(E\) (not necessarily normalized) is a set function \(\mu:\mathcal B(E)\to[0,\infty)\) such that
\(\mu(\emptyset)=0\) and \(\mu(A)\le\mu(B)\) whenever \(A\subset B\).  It is
\emph{regular} if, for every Borel set \(A\subset E\),
\[
  \mu(A)
  =\sup\{\mu(K):K\subset A,\ K\text{ compact}\}
  =\inf\{\mu(U):A\subset U,\ U\text{ relatively open in }E\}.
\]
It is \emph{convex} (equivalently, supermodular) if
\[
  \mu(A\cup B)+\mu(A\cap B)\ge\mu(A)+\mu(B),
  \qquad A,B\in\mathcal B(E).
\]
Its support is the closed set
\[
  \supp\mu
  =\{t\in E:\mu(U)>0\text{ for every relatively open neighbourhood }U\ni t\}.
\]
We say that \(\mu\) has the \emph{support-intersection property} if
\[
  \mu(U)>0
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  U\cap\supp\mu\ne\emptyset
\]
for every relatively open \(U\subset E\).  This property implies
\(\mu(E\setminus\supp\mu)=0\), but for a non-additive capacity it need not imply
\(\mu(\supp\mu)=\mu(E)\); the latter equality will be called the property that
the support \emph{carries full capacity}.  We say that the capacity has
\emph{full support} if \(\supp\mu=E\).

A capacity \(\nu\) on the Borel subsets of \(\R\), possibly taking the value
\(+\infty\), is \emph{locally finite} if \(\nu(K)<\infty\) for every compact
\(K\subset\R\).  For compact \(E\), its restriction \(\nu|_E\) is the capacity
on \(E\) given by \((\nu|_E)(A)=\nu(A)\), \(A\in\mathcal B(E)\).
title: Capacity terminology

[Definition def:planar of arXiv:2607.18635, 'Remainders of generalised Taylor expansions and a priori bounds for rough differential equ'] A \emph{planar binary} rooted tree $(V,E,\mathfrak{v})$ is a rooted tree such that
	every vertex has either two or zero children and endowed with
	\begin{itemize}
	\item a left-to-right total order between children of every vertex
	\item a decoration $\mathfrak{v}:L\to\mathbb{N}$, where $L\subset V$ are the leaves of the tree.
	\end{itemize}
	We denote by ${\mathcal T}_{b}$ the set of \emph{planar binary} rooted trees. 
		If $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and $I\in(\mathbb{N}\setminus\{0\})^k$ is a string of $k$ positive integers, then we denote by ${\mathcal T}_b^{I}$ the set of $\rho\in{\mathcal T}_{b}$ with 
		$k+1$ leaves and such that 
		\begin{itemize}
		\item the rightmost leaf has $\mathfrak{v}$-decoration $0$,
		\item the $i$-th leaf from the {\it right} receives as $\mathfrak{v}$-decoration the $i$-th element of $I$.
\end{itemize}		
 When $I=\emptyset$, ${\mathcal T}_b^I=\{\bullet_0\}$.		We also adopt the notation
		\[
		I_k:=(1,\ldots,k)\in\mathbb{N}^k
		\]
		and, for $\Sigma_k$ the set of permutations of $\{1,\ldots,k\}$ and for $p\in\Sigma_k$, $p(I_k):=(p(1),\ldots,p(k))$. 
		
		Finally, in analogy with the grafting of rooted trees on a new common root,  we denote by $[\cdot,\cdot]:{\mathcal T}_b\times{\mathcal T}_b\to{\mathcal T}_b$ the operation of grafting an ordered pair of planary binary trees on a new root, with the first tree on the
	left and the second on the right.
title: Planar binary trees

\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 49 of arXiv:2607.18104, '2607.18104'] Suppose that  $(\eta_t)_{t \geq 0}$ and $(\eta^{\prime}_t)_{t \geq 0}$ are defined on the same underlying graph $G=(V,E)$ (either the integer lattice or the torus of length $N$), but are allowed to have different initial data. 
We define the \textbf{basic coupling} $\mathbf{P}$ between the ASEPs $(\eta_t)_{t \geq 0}$ and $(\eta^{\prime}_t)_{t \geq 0}$ as follows.
For all edges in $E$, we place independent rate $(1+q)$ Poisson clocks. Whenever the clock of an edge $e=\{ x,x+1\}$ rings, and the exclusion processes are in states $\eta$ and $\eta^{\prime}$, respectively, we sample an independent Bernoulli-$(1+q)^{-1}$-distributed random variable $B$. If
\begin{itemize}
\item $B=1$: Then, if $\eta(x)=1-\eta(x+1)=1$ holds, we move the particle at site $x$ to site $x+1$ in configuration $\eta$. Similarly, if $\eta^{\prime}(x)=1-\eta^{\prime}(x+1)=1$ holds, we move the particle at site $x$ to site $x+1$ in configuration $\eta^{\prime}$. 
\item $B=0$. Then, if $\eta(x)=1-\eta(x+1)=0$ holds, we move the particle at site $x+1$ to site $x$ in configuration $\eta$. Similarly, if $\eta^{\prime}(x)=1-\eta^{\prime}(x+1)=0$ holds, we move the particle at site $x+1$ to site $x$ in configuration $\eta^{\prime}$. 

\end{itemize}
In all other cases, the configuration does not change.

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2609.03098, 'Standing waves for Schr\"odinger equations with Kato class potentials and $L^\infty$-bound'] Let $f$ satisfy the conditions $(f1)$\,--\,$(f3)$ and \eqref{bound-f} with $f(x,0)=0$ for a.e.\ $x\in\R^N$, and suppose there exists $\alpha \in L^\infty(\R^N)$ satisfying $(L_0)$. Assume that $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue
of $-\Delta+V$ such that
$$\hat \varrho (|\alpha|) < \inf \sigma_{ess} (-\Delta+V) - \lambda$$ and that one of the following conditions is satisfied: \\[3pt]
\noindent\makebox[7mm][r]{$(i)$} \parbox[t][][t]{155mm}{$(LL)_+$ holds and $d^-(V,\lambda) +\dim \ker (-\Delta+V-\lambda) \neq d^{-} (V-\alpha,\lambda)$,}\\[3pt]
\noindent\makebox[7mm][r]{$(ii)$} \parbox[t][][t]{155mm}{$(LL)_-$ holds and $d^-(V,\lambda) \neq d^{-} (V-\alpha,\lambda)$.}\\[3pt]
Then there exist a nonzero solution $\bar u\in H^2(\R^N)$ of $(E)_\lambda$ and a bounded solution $u:\R\to H^1(\R^N)$ of $(P)_\lambda$ such that either $\bar u$ belongs to the $\alpha$-limit set of $u$ and $u(t)\to 0$ in $H^1(\R^N)$ as $t\to -\infty$, or $\bar u$ belongs to the $\omega$-limit set of $u$ and $u(t)\to 0$ in $H^1(\R^N)$ as $t\to +\infty$. On P_2(R^d), let F=G+tau H be convex under linear mixing, where tau>0 and H(mu)=integral log(dmu/dx) dmu for absolutely continuous mu, and +infinity otherwise. For every mu, G admits a first variation G_prime[mu] in C^1(R^d) of the form G_prime[mu](x)=a|x|^2/2+V[mu](x), with a,L>0 independent of mu and |grad V[mu](x)|<=L for every mu,x. A Wasserstein gradient flow here means a P_2-continuous distributional solution partial_t mu_t=div(mu_t grad G_prime[mu_t])+tau Delta mu_t, positive for t>0, which satisfies F(mu_t2)-F(mu_t1)=-integral_t1^t2 integral |grad G_prime[mu_s]+tau grad log(mu_s)|^2 dmu_s ds. Define tau_c=inf{s>=0:G+s H is convex}. Let mu_0 satisfy integral exp(|x|^2/M_0^2) dmu_0<=2 for some M_0>0. Enlarge M_0 if necessary so that M_0>=sqrt(8 tau/a), which preserves this moment assumption. (1) If tau>=tau_c>0, set t_0=a^(-1)[5+log(M_0^2 a/tau)]. There is C>0 depending only on d,a,tau,L,M_0 such that for t>=t_0, F(mu_t)-inf F <= [(F(mu_t0)-inf F)^(-1)+C(t-t_0)]^(-1). (2) If tau>tau_c>=0, then for every kappa>1, set t_0=a^(-1)[5+log(M_0^2 a kappa/tau)]. There is C>0 depending only on d,kappa,a,tau,L,M_0 such that for t>=t_0, F(mu_t)-inf F <= [(F(mu_t0)-inf F)^(-1/kappa)+C(tau-tau_c)^(1+1/kappa)(t-t_0)]^(-kappa). A zero gap at t_0 remains zero. Constants are computable from the proofs; the theorem does not assert polynomial dependence on d or 1/tau.

A function $F : D \to \mathbb{C}$ is \emph{holomorphic} (or \emph{complex analytic})
if for every $z_0 \in D$ there exists $r>0$ and a sequence of complex coefficients $(a_n)_{n\ge 0}$
such that

F(z) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n (z-z_0)^n
\qquad \text{for all } |z-z_0| < r.

Let X^(B) be obtained by replacing X_B by an independent draw from ⊗_{i∈B} μ_i, independent of X, while retaining X_{B^c}. Then E Var(f(X) | X_{B^c}) = (1/2) E[(f(X)-f(X^(B)))^2].

B is a nonempty subset of [n]
the replacement block X'_B is independent of X and has the same product marginal ⊗_{i∈B} μ_i

body:
[Lemma lem:ht.coupling of arXiv:2607.12459, 'Renormalisation of Inhomogeneous Random Graphs'] For $\ell\in\mathbb{N}$, let $F_\ell$ be the distribution function of $\hat X_I^{(\ell)}$, and let $F$ be the distribution function of $\sigma_\gamma Y$. Then the following hold:
 \begin{enumerate} 
\item[(i)] 
$F_\ell$ and $F$ are continuous distribution functions. 
\item[(ii)] 
If $U_I$, $I\in[N_{L-\ell}]$, are i.i.d.\ $\mathrm{UNIF}[0,1]$, then 
\[ 
\hat X_I^{(\ell)}=F_\ell^{\leftarrow}(U_I), \qquad \hat Y_I=\sigma_\gamma^{-1}F^{\leftarrow}(U_I), \qquad I\in[N_{L-\ell}], 
\] 
define two coupled families such that $\{\hat X_I^{(\ell)}\}_I$ is i.i.d.\ with the block-sum law above, while $\{\hat Y_I\}_I$ is i.i.d.\ with the standard positive $\gamma$-stable law. Here, 
\[ 
G^{\leftarrow}(u)=\inf\{x\geq0\colon G(x)\geq u\} 
\] 
denotes the generalised inverse, or quantile function, of a distribution function $G$. 
\item[(iii)] For Lebesgue-a.e.\ $u\in(0,1)$, 
\[ 
F_\ell^{\leftarrow}(u)\longrightarrow F^{\leftarrow}(u). 
\] 
Consequently, for every fixed $I$, 
\[ 
\hat X_I^{(\ell)}-\sigma_\gamma\hat Y_I \longrightarrow 0 \qquad\text{a.s.} 
\] 
\end{enumerate}
title: Lemma lem:ht.coupling of arXiv:2607.12459

[Lemma 33 (Lexicographic difference decomposition) of arXiv:2608.22342, 'Completely Positive Entropy and Fourier Central Limit Theorems for Stationary Random Measu'] Let $(\mathscr H_k)_{k\in\bZ^d}$ be an increasing family of closed subspaces of
a Hilbert space, indexed by the lexicographic order, and put
\[
    \mathscr H_-:=\bigcap_{k\in\bZ^d}\mathscr H_k,
    \qquad
    \mathscr H_+:=\overline{\bigcup_{k\in\bZ^d}\mathscr H_k}.
\]
Suppose that for every nonprincipal cut $\bZ^d=L\sqcup R$,
\[
    \overline{\bigcup_{k\in L}\mathscr H_k}
    =\bigcap_{k\in R}\mathscr H_k.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}

    \mathscr H_+\ominus\mathscr H_-
    =\bigoplus_{k\in\bZ^d}
      \bigl(\mathscr H_k\ominus\mathscr H_{k-e_d}\bigr).
\end{equation}

[Definition def:external-K-sparse-event of arXiv:2605.06511, 'Logarithmic Mixing of Random Walks on Dynamical Random Cluster Models'] Given $v \in V$, let $E_v \coloneqq E\left(B_R (v)\right)$ and consider the discrete-time random cluster Glauber dynamics $\left(\eta_{\langle t \rangle}^{E_v}\right)_{t \in \mathbb{N}}$ with parameters $(p, q)$, that is, the dynamics where all edges in $E_v$ are wired open. 
		
		For all $F \subseteq \partial B_R (v)$, we define $S^F_{\langle t \rangle} \left(B_R(v)\right)$ as the event that, in the graph $\left(V,\eta_{\langle t \rangle}^{E_v}  \setminus E_v\right)$, the vertices in $\partial B_R (v)$ which are in non-trivial components are exactly $F$. 
		
		We define $S_{\langle t \rangle} \left(B_R(v), K\right)$ as the event that $S^F_{\langle t \rangle} \left(B_R(v)\right)$ holds for some $F \subseteq \partial B_R (u)$ such that $|F| \leq K$. Furthermore, we define $S_{\langle t \rangle} (R, K) \coloneqq \cap_{v \in V} S_{\langle t \rangle} (B_R(v), K)$. For $t'' > t' > 0$, by $S_{\langle[t', t'']\rangle} (R, K)$ we denote the event that $S_{\langle t \rangle} (R, K)$ holds for all $t \in [t', t'']$.
		
		By  $S^F_t \left(B_R (v)\right)$, $S_t \left(B_R (v), K\right)$, $S_t (R, K)$ and $S_{[t', t'']} (R, K)$ we will denote the continuous-time analogues of each event, respectively.

   \begin{enumerate}

[Definition Local scales \cite{helfter2025scales} of arXiv:2512.06984, 'Infinite Dimensional Multifractal Analysis of the Wiener measure'] Given a scaling $ \mathsf{scl} $, the upper and lower local scales of a Borel measure $ \mu$ on a metric space $ (X,d) $ are given at a point $x \in X$ by: 
\[ \underline{\mathsf{scl}}_{ \mathrm{loc}} \mu (x )  = \sup \left\{ \alpha > 0 :   \frac{\mu ( B(x, \varepsilon)) }{\mathit{scl}_\alpha( \varepsilon) }  \xrightarrow[\varepsilon \to 0]{}  0  \right\} \]
and \[ \overline{\mathsf{scl}}_{ \mathrm{loc}} \mu (x )  = \inf \left\{ \alpha > 0 :   \frac{\mu ( B(x, \varepsilon)) }{\mathit{scl}_\alpha( \varepsilon) }  \xrightarrow[\varepsilon \to 0]{}  + \infty   \right\}  \; . \] 
Moreover when they coincide, we denote $ \mathsf{scl}_{\mathrm{loc}}  ( x) :=  \underline{\mathsf{scl}}_{ \mathrm{loc}} \mu (x ) = \overline{\mathsf{scl}}_{ \mathrm{loc}} \mu (x ) $ their common value.
title: Local scales \cite{helfter2025scales}

body:
[Cor lyapunov-explosive of arXiv:2511.10223, 'Stochastic Reaction Networks Within Interacting Compartments with Content-Dependent Fragme'] Let $X$ be a continuous-time Markov chain on a countable state space $\mathbb S$ with generator $\mathcal L$. Suppose there exists a finite set $K\subset\mathbb S$ and a positive function $V$ on $\mathbb S$ such that
\[
    \mathcal LV(x)\le-1
\]
for all $x\in\mathbb S\setminus K$. Suppose further that $V$ is bounded from above. If there exists $z\in K$ such that $z$ is in a closed, irreducible component of $\mathbb S$, and there exists a $y\in\mathbb S$ reachable from $z$ such that $V(y)<\inf_{x\in K} V(x)$, then $X$ is explosive.
\begin{proof}
    On the one hand, if $X$ was not explosive, every state in a closed, irreducible component of $\mathbb S$ would be positive recurrent by Theorem (thm:lyapunov-stuff of the paper). In particular, the point $z\in K$ given by the statement of the corollary would be positive recurrent for $X$.

    On the other hand, if $X$ was not explosive, then applying Theorem (thm:lyapunov-transience of the paper) to $X$ with function $-V$ would yield that $\mathbb P_{x_0}(\tau_K<\infty)<1$ for any $x_0$ such that $\sup_{x\in K} -V(x)<-V(x_0)$. In particular, taking $x_0$ to be the $y$ given to us by the statement of the corollary, we would have $\mathbb P_y(\tau_K<\infty)<1$. But then when the chain was started from $z$, it would reach $y$ with positive probability by assumption, and then fail to return to $z$ with positive probability.

    Thus Theorems (thm:lyapunov-stuff of the paper) and (thm:lyapunov-transience of the paper), taken together, show that if $X$ were not explosive then the point $z$ given in the statement of this corollary would be both positive recurrent and transient. This is absurd, so $X$ is explosive.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor lyapunov-explosive of arXiv:2511.10223

[Proposition 26 (Two-sided finite-matrix criticality certificates) of arXiv:2608.15987, 'Threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees: a conditional bra'] For $k\in\mathbb N$ partition $[0,a_*]$ into cells $I_1,\dots,I_k$ of mesh $a_*/k$, giving the finite partition $\{X_j\}$ of $X$ into $mk$ cells. Define the $mk\times mk$ nonnegative matrices
\[
\big(M^{(k)}_-\big)_{ij}=\inf_{x\in X_i,\ y\in X_j}\kappa(x,y)\,\nu(X_j),\qquad \big(M^{(k)}_+\big)_{ij}=\sup_{x\in X_i,\ y\in X_j}\kappa(x,y)\,\nu(X_j).
\]
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Sandwich.) $\rho\big(M^{(k)}_-\big)\le\rho(K)\le\rho\big(M^{(k)}_+\big)$ for every $k$.
\item (Convergence.) $\rho\big(M^{(k)}_\pm\big)\to\rho(K)$ as $k\to\infty$.
\item (Certificates.) $\rho(M^{(k)}_-)>1$ for some $k$ certifies supercriticality of the sensitive-regime cascade skeleton; $\rho(M^{(k)}_+)<1$ certifies subcriticality. Both certificates are verifiable in finite linear algebra, and one of the two obtains for every non-critical parameter point.
\end{enumerate}

[Proposition 34 of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] Let \(a>1\), define
\[
\Sigma_a
:=
\left\{
\theta\in\mathbb{C}:
1+(e^{\theta}-1)r\in(-\infty,0]
\text{ for some } r\in[0,\rho_a]
\right\}.
\]
Then \(\Lambda_a\) extends holomorphically to \(\mathbb{C}\setminus\Sigma_a\). For every integer \(n\geq1\),
\[
\Lambda_a^{(n)}(0)
=
\frac{1}{4\pi(a-1)}
\sum_{m=1}^{n}
(-1)^{m+1}(m-1)!S(n,m)
B\left(\frac{m}{a-1},m+1\right),
\]
where \(S(n,m)\) is the Stirling number of the second kind. The Taylor radius \(R_a\) of \(\Lambda_a\) at \(0\) is
\[
R_a
=
\operatorname{dist}(0,\Sigma_a)
=
\sqrt{
\pi^2+
\left(
\max\left\{
\log\frac{1-\rho_a}{\rho_a},
0
\right\}
\right)^2
}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
R_a
=
\begin{cases}
\pi,
&
a\geq a_c,\\[2mm]
\sqrt{\pi^2+\log^2\left(\frac{1-\rho_a}{\rho_a}\right)},
&
1<a<a_c,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(a_c>1\) is the unique solution of \((a_c-1)a_c^{-a_c/(a_c-1)}=1/2\).

body:
[Lem 48 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Suppose $J_+ \neq \emptyset$, and define
    \begin{align}
        
        \Delta_+(\vartheta) 
        &\equiv \vartheta + \gamma_+(z_\star) - \gamma_+(\beta_\star(\gamma_\star + \vartheta))
        \,,\\
        
        \Delta_-(\vartheta) 
        &\equiv \vartheta + \gamma_+(\beta_\star(\gamma_\star - \vartheta)) - \gamma_+(z_\star)\,.
    \end{align}
These functions are continuous and strictly increasing on the intervals $[0,+\infty)$ and $[0,\vartheta_{-,\max})$ respectively, where in the latter case we define
    \[
        \vartheta_{-,\max} \equiv \sup\lt\{
            \vartheta \ge 0 : \beta_\star(\gamma_\star - \vartheta) > z_0
        \rt\}\,.
    \]
    Furthermore, $\Delta_+(0) = \Delta_-(0) = 0$ and 
    \beq
        
        \lim_{\vartheta \uparrow +\infty} \Delta_+(\vartheta)
        = \lim_{\vartheta \uparrow \vartheta_{-,\max}} \Delta_-(\vartheta)
        = +\infty\,.
    \eeq
    In particular, for any $\delta > 0$, there exist (unique) solutions $\vartheta_+ \in (0,+\infty)$, $\vartheta_- \in (0,\vartheta_{-,\max})$ to the equations
    \beq
        
        \Delta_+(\vartheta_+) = \Delta_-(\vartheta_-) = \delta\,.
    \eeq
\begin{proof}
    Since $J_+ \neq \emptyset$, we have $\hv_1 > 0$ and $z_0 = m^{-1}(\alpha / \hv_1)$, and thus case \eqref{i:fp-case2} or \eqref{i:fp-case3} of Remark~\ref{r:fp.cases} holds. In either case, we have $z_\star > z_0$. Note that $\gamma_+$ is strictly decreasing for $z > z_0$. Since $\beta_\star(\gamma_\star) = z_\star$, we have $\Delta_+(0) = \Delta_-(0) = 0$.
Recall that $\beta_\star$ is nondecreasing by Lemma~\ref{l:fp-g2}\eqref{i:fp-beta-incr}; it follows that $\beta_\star(\gamma_\star - \vartheta) > z_0$ for all $\vartheta \in [0,\vartheta_{-,\max})$. Moreover, $\beta_\star$ is continuous, so $\Delta_+$ and $\Delta_-$ are continuous and strictly increasing on their respective domains. It remains to verify \eqref{e:fp-vartheta-limit}.
Since $\Delta_+(\vartheta)\ge\vartheta$, it is clear the limit involving $\Delta_+$ is $+\infty$.
Similarly, since $\Delta_-(\vartheta)\ge\vartheta$, 
 the limit involving $\Delta_-$ is also clearly $+\infty$ in the case $\vartheta_{-,\max} = +\infty$.
    Otherwise, we must have $\beta_\star(\gamma_\star - \vartheta) \downarrow z_0$ as $\vartheta \uparrow \vartheta_{-,\max}$, so $\gamma_+(\beta_\star(\gamma_\star - \vartheta)) \uparrow +\infty$.
    This proves \eqref{e:fp-vartheta-limit}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 48 of arXiv:2608.29416

[Definition 8 ($\pi$-Convergence in $\mathcal{B}_m(H)$) of arXiv:2607.03318, 'Continuous Differentiability of the Value Function for Infinite-Dimensional Finite-Horizon'] A sequence $\{\varphi_n\}_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \subset \mathcal{B}_m(H)$ is said to $\pi$-converge to a mapping $\varphi \in \mathcal{B}_m(H)$, denoted as $\pi\text{-}\lim_{n \to \infty} \varphi_n = \varphi$, if:
\begin{enumerate}[label={(\textit{\roman*})}, leftmargin=*]

\end{enumerate}

[Proposition proposition of arXiv:2411.05541, 'Gaskets of $O(2)$ loop-decorated random planar maps'] Let $(g_j)_{j\ge 1}$ be a sequence of non-negative real numbers such that $\sum_{j\ge 1} jg_j \le 1$. Let $\nu$ be defined by (equation eq nu 2 of the paper). Assume that $\nu(0)<1$ and that for all $k\in \mathbb{Z}$, we have $\nu(k)\ge 0$. Then $\nu$ is a probability distribution and $h^\downarrow$ is $\nu$-harmonic on $\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}$. Moreover, for all $k\ge 1$,
	$$
	\nu(k-1) - \nu(-k-1)= g_k\ge 0.
	$$
	In particular, the sequence ${\bf q}= (q_k)_{k\ge 1}$ defined by setting for all $k\ge 1$,
	$$
	q_k = \nu(k-1) (\nu(-1)/2)^{k-1}
	$$
	is the weight sequence of the gasket of a critical $O(2)$ loop-decorated map. The associated triple $(\widetilde{\bf q}, 1/c_{\bf q}, 2)$ is given by $c_{\bf q} = 2/\nu(-1)$ and for all $k\ge 1$,
	$$
	\tilde{q}_k = g_k (\nu(-1)/2)^{k-1}.

[Lemma le:BF of arXiv:2411.09949, '$W_{\bf d}$-convergence rate of EM schemes for invariant measures of supercritical stable '] Let $\alpha\in(\frac{1}{2},2)$ and $X,\xi$ be two independent random variables with
 $$\mathbb{E}(|X|^{\varsigma}+|\xi|^\varsigma)<\infty,\quad \forall \varsigma\in(0,\alpha).$$
Then for any $\ell\in(0,1)$, there is $C=C(\varsigma,\Theta)>0$ such that

(1) if $\alpha\in(\frac{1}{2},1)$, then for any $\vartheta\in(1-\alpha,\alpha)$ and $\varsigma\in(0,\alpha)$ with $\varsigma+(\gamma\alpha)\wedge \vartheta>1$,
\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}[\left|b(X)\cdot(\nabla f(X+\ell\xi)-\nabla f(X))\right|]\leqslant C\left(\ell^{\gamma\wedge\vartheta}+\ell^{\varsigma\gamma-\frac{\varsigma\gamma\alpha}{\varsigma+(\gamma\alpha)\wedge\vartheta}}\right).

(2) if $\alpha\in[1,2)$, then for any $\vartheta\in(0,1)$ and $\varsigma,\varsigma_1\in(0,1)$ with

\varsigma_1(1+\vartheta)<\alpha$,

\mathbb{E}[\left|b(X)\cdot(\nabla f(X+\ell\xi)-\nabla f(X))\right|]\leqslant C\left(\ell^{\gamma\wedge\vartheta}+\ell^{\varsigma\gamma-\frac{\varsigma\gamma\alpha}{\varsigma+(\gamma\varsigma_1)\wedge\vartheta}}\right).
\end{align}

On the configuration model with asymptotic degree distribution having mean degree d_bar, there exists a critical contagion threshold c_* > 0 such that: for c < c_*, default cascades triggered by a vanishing fraction of initial defaults affect only an asymptotically vanishing fraction of nodes (resilient regime); whereas for c > c_*, the cascade percolates through the giant component, causing a macroscopic fraction of the network to default (fragile regime).

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Identify what makes q = 1 and q = 2 expandable and whether a q-analogue of the random-current switching lemma exists. Result: q = 1 is Bernoulli percolation (independence gives the pivotal decomposition); q = 2 is expandable through the random-current representation and the switching lemma (Sakai's lace expansion for the Ising model). For integer q >= 3 the Potts model has a random-current-like representation (the 'random-current representation for Potts' via the Edwards-Sokal coupling with q colours) but the switching lemma fails because currents are Z_q-valued and the pairing structure that gives the switching identity is specific to Z_2. A lace expansion needs a 'pivotal' notion for which the model factorises across the pivotal: in FK with general q the cluster weight q^{k(omega)} couples the two sides of a pivotal edge only through the count of clusters, which changes by one when the pivotal is closed; this suggests an expansion in which each pivotal carries a factor q or 1 depending on whether closing it splits a cluster, i.e. a lace expansion for the two-point function with the cluster count as an extra variable, which is exactly the generating function in the number of clusters, i.e. the Tutte polynomial. So the expansion would be an expansion of the Tutte polynomial's two-point version, which is #P-hard to evaluate in general, suggesting no simple diagrammatic expansion exists for generic q; for the infrared bound one might instead use reflection positivity (available for integer q and for the FK model on Z^d with q >= 1 via the Potts representation), which gives the infrared bound for the Potts spin-spin covariance directly for integer q >= 1 (Frohlich-Simon-Spencer), without a lace expansion. Recorded: for integer q the infrared bound is available by reflection positivity (this is classical), so the source's 'and use it to derive an infrared bound' is partly moot for integer q; the genuinely open content is the expansion itself and the non-integer q infrared bound. Key identity: Reflection positivity gives the infrared bound for integer-q Potts covariances without any expansion; the open part is non-integer q and the expansion. Obstruction: No switching lemma for Z_q currents; the natural expansion variable is a Tutte-polynomial quantity.

[Proposition prop:inv of arXiv:2505.14012, 'Ergodicity for stochastic neural field equations'] Suppose that
Assumptions (assu:space of the paper), (assu:noise of the paper), (assu:hat of the paper), and (assu:inv of the paper) hold.
Set
\[\beta:=\sqrt{2}(1+C_{\check{K}})\|(\pm\hat{K})^{-\frac{1}{2}}\|_{L(H)}^2 \left(\operatorname{Lip}(f) + |f(0)|\|\rho\|_{L^1(U)}^{1/2}\right)+\tilde{C}_B.\]
and assume that for some $\delta\in (0,1)$,
\[\gamma(\delta):=2\alpha-\beta-\frac{9}{\delta}\tilde{\tilde{C}}_B>0.\]
Then, for
\[\eta:=\sqrt{2}|f(0)|\|\rho\|_{L^1(U)}^{1/2}+\left(1+\frac{9}{\delta}\right)\tilde{\tilde{C}}_B,\]
and for any $u_0\in H_1$, and any $t\in [0,T]$, it holds that,
\begin{align*}
(1-\delta)\mathbb{E}\left(\sup_{0\leq s\leq t}\|u(s)\|^2_1\right)+\gamma(\delta)\mathbb{E}\int_0^t\|u(s)\|_1^2\,ds \leq \|u_0\|^2_1 + \eta t,
\end{align*}
where $\gamma(\delta)>0$ is as in Assumption (assu:inv of the paper).
In particular, for $u_0\in H_1$, $u\in L^2(\Omega;L^{\infty}([0,T];H_1))\cap L^2([0,T]\times\Omega;H_1)$.

Hence this is the Fourier expansion. There is no constant coefficient. [Theorem thm:explicit_current_2 of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Let $(X_t)_{t\geq 0}$ be an ergodic diffusion with invariant measure $\mu$ whose
symmetric part $\mathcal{L}_S$ satisfies the Poincar\'e inequality~(equation eq:poincare of the paper)
with spectral gap $\lambda_\mathrm{gap}>0$ (Assumptions~(ass:dynamics of the paper)). 
Let $\overline{J}_t(U)$ denote the empirical current according to Definition~(def:empirical_current of the paper)
with ergodic mean $\E^\mu[\overline{J}_t(U)]=\E^\mu[v_{\textrm{s}}\cdot U]= \E^\mu[W]$,
and let $\nu\ll\mu$ with $\mathrm{d}\nu/\mathrm{d}\mu\in L^2(\mu)$.
Then for all $t > 0$ and $a > 0$,
\begin{align}
\mathbb{P}^\nu\left(\overline{J}_t(U) - \E^\mu[\overline{J}_t] \geq a\right)
\leq
\left\|\frac{\mathrm{d}\nu}{\mathrm{d}\mu}\right\|_{L^2(\mu)}
\exp\left[-t \frac{\tilde\sigma_{J,2}^2}{c_{J,2}^2}
  h\left(\frac{c_{J,2} a}{\tilde\sigma_{J,2}^2}\right)\right],

\end{align}
where $h(u) = 1 + u - \sqrt{1+2u}$ and the parameters 
$\tilde\sigma_{J,2}^2$ and $c_{J,2}$ as in
Lemma~(lem:bernstein_current of the paper).

\mathscr{F}\1_{B_R}(\xi)=\int_{B_R}e^{-{\mathbf{i}\mkern1mu} x\cdot \xi }\mathrm{d} x=(2\pi R)^{d/2} \|\xi\|^{-d/2}J_{d/2}(R\|\xi\|), \quad  \text{for }  \xi\in\mathbb R^d,\]

[Proposition prop:clock of arXiv:2608.01253, 'The pseudo-quantum representation of \\finite reversible Markov chains'] For the symmetric chain, $\cos\theta(t)=e^{-2t}$ is the relaxation factor of the
slowest non-constant mode, whose generator eigenvalue is $-2$ by
(cor:ehr-spec of the paper). Moreover $\theta(t)/2$ is a statistical angle. If

Bhattacharyya coefficient $\mathrm{BC}(p,q)=\sum_i\sqrt{p_iq_i}$ and the statistical
angle $\arccos\mathrm{BC}$ ((sec:primer-info of the paper)),

\[
\mathrm{BC}(\delta_a,q_t)=\sqrt{p(t)},\qquad
\arccos\mathrm{BC}(\delta_a,q_t)=\arccos\sqrt{p(t)}=\frac{\theta(t)}2 .
\]

[Lemma lem:oddevenAT of arXiv:2604.15146, 'Renormalised two-point functions of CLE$_4$ gaskets'] Let $g\in \left((2-1/\sqrt{2})^2,(1+ 1/\sqrt{2})^2\right)\cup [4,+\infty)$,

$\mathbb{P}(\widetilde F^{\rm{two}}_{\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2}) \leq C\min(\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2)^{1/4+\beta_g}$.

[Lemma 42 (Central needles and exact norm detection) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Fix $I=[s,s+r]\subset[0,T]$, $r>0$, and let
\[
 \chi_I(u)=
 \begin{cases}
 0,&u\le s,\\
 (u-s)/r,&s<u<s+r,\\
 1,&u\ge s+r.
 \end{cases}
\]
For finite-rank $B^*=-B\in E_A$ and $C^*=C\in E_Q$, define
\[
 \iota_I(B,C):=(0,A^{r;B},q^{r;C}),\qquad
 A_u^{r;B}=r^{2\eta}\chi_I(u)B,\qquad
 q_u^{r;C}=r^{2\eta}\chi_I(u)C.
\]
Then $\iota_I(B,C)\in\mathsf Z_{\eta;\mathfrak I,1}(H)$ and
\begin{align}
 d_{\eta;\mathfrak I,1}(\iota_I(B,C),0)
 &=\|B\|_{\mathfrak I}+\|C\|_{\mathcal S_1},
 \\
 d_{{\rm op},L}(\iota_I(B,C),0)
 &=\|B\|_{L_A}+\|C\|_{L_Q}.
 
\end{align}
Thus finite-rank central directions embed the two ideal norms and the two
probe seminorms into the state and response geometries with no loss of
constants.

body:
[Theorem 6 (Global exponential convergence for $\beta_1=0$) of arXiv:2608.20638, 'Provable Edge-of-Stability for Adam on a One-Dimensional Quadratic'] Assume
\[
    \beta_1=0,
    \qquad
    w_{\max}=\frac{\eta}{\varepsilon}<2.
\]
Then every trajectory of Adam converges to the origin.  More precisely, for
every initial state $(x_0,m_0,v_0)\in\R^2\times[0,\infty)$, there exist
constants $C>0$ and $\gamma\in(0,1)$, depending on the initial state and
the parameters, such that
\[
    \abs{x_t}+\abs{m_t}+v_t
    \le C\gamma^t,
    \qquad t\in\Nzero.
\]
In particular, $(x_t,m_t,v_t)\to(0,0,0)$.

[Proposition instantaneous_coalescing of arXiv:2411.04773, 'Meeting of squared Bessel flow lines and application to the skew Brownian motion'] Let $\mathcal S$ be a general $\rm BESQ^\delta$ flow for $\delta\in {\mathbb R}$. Then with probability 1, for every $(a,r)\in {\mathbb R}_+\times{\mathbb R}$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there exist some  $(a_n,r_n)\in \mathcal{D}$ arbitrarily close to $(a,r)$ 
such that $\mathcal S_{r,x}(a)=\mathcal S_{r_n,x}(a_n)$ for all $x\geq r+\varepsilon$.

[Proposition stat_ergodic of arXiv:2504.04860, 'Stochastic differential equations driven by fractional Brownian motion: dependence on the '] Assume that $\mu  \in C^1(\mathbb{R}^d;\mathbb{R}^d)$ satisfies (equation lip of the paper) and (equation dissip of the paper). Then, there exists a stochastic process $\overline{X}_t^H, t \geq 0$, such that 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[(a)] we have  ${\overline{X}_t^H} \stackrel{\mathcal{L}}{=} {\overline{X}_0^H}$ for all $t \geq 0$ and  $\mathbf{E}\big[\| \overline{X}_0^H\|^p \big]<\infty$ for all $p \geq 1$,
		\item[(b)] we have   $$\lim_{t \rightarrow \infty}    \|{X}_t^H- \overline{X}_t^H\|\, \stackrel{a.s.}{=} \, 0,$$ 
		\item[(c)]  we have  $$\lim_{T \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{T} \int_0^T \varphi(X^H_t) \,\mathrm{d} t  \, \stackrel{a.s.}{=} \, \mathbf{E} \big[ \varphi( \overline{X}^H_0) \big] $$  for all $\varphi \in C^{1}_{pol}(\mathbb{R}^d; \mathbb{R})$.
	\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 87 (Dyadic convergence of alternating It\^o iterates) of arXiv:2606.29292, 'Intrinsic Gaussian Tensor Geometry and Random Operator Spectra'] Let $\pi_m$ be the uniform dyadic subdivision of $[s,t]$, and let
$\underline v_m$ be the left endpoint of the cell containing $v$.  Define
\[
 \Xi_0^{(m),s,u}:=1,
 \qquad
 \Xi_k^{(m),s,u}
 :=\int_s^u\Xi_{k-1}^{(m),s,\underline v_m}\wedge dM_v.
\]
Then, for every fixed $k$,
\begin{equation}

 \mathbb E\sup_{u\in[s,t]}
 \|\Xi_k^{(m),s,u}-\Xi_k^{s,u}\|_{\wedge^kE}^2
 \longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
At $u=t$, the approximant is the alternating sum over ordered $k$-tuples of
increments of $M$ along $\pi_m$.
title: Dyadic convergence of alternating It\^o iterates

[Theorem of arXiv:2606.01664, 'Brown measure convergence for the spectrum of polynomials in Ginibre matrices'] Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\mathfrak{p}\in\mathbb{C}\langle x_1,\cdots,x_n\rangle$. Let $\xi$ have the distribution stated in Theorem (nongaussiantheorem of the paper). Then there are constants $c_0(\mathfrak{p},\xi)$ and $c(\mathfrak{p},\xi)$ depending on $\mathfrak{p}$ and $\xi$; a constant $\widehat{C}(\mathfrak{p},\xi,z)>0$ depending on $\mathfrak{p}$, $\xi$ and $z$; as well as for any $q\in\mathbb{N}_+$ a constant $C_q=C_{\mathfrak{p},q,\xi}>0$ depending on $\mathfrak{p},q,\xi$, so that we have the following estimate. Let $X_1^N,\cdots,X_n^N$ be independent $N\times N$ complex matrices with i.i.d. entries of law $\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\xi$; and denote by $P^N=\mathfrak{p}(X_1^N,\cdots,X_n^N)$. Then for any $z\in\mathbb{C},z\neq \mathfrak{p}(0)$ we can find some fixed $N_0=N_0(z,\mathfrak{p},\xi)$ such that whenever $N\geq N_0$, we have for any $\epsilon>0$,
    $$
\mathbb{P}\{\sigma_{min}(P^N-z)\leq\epsilon
\}\leq \widehat{C}(N^{c_0}\epsilon^c)+C_qN^{-q}.
    $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 26 of arXiv:2608.26698, 'Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion '] For $g \geq 1$ the mapping torus construction $\rho : \mathcal{I}(M_g) \rightarrow {\Omega}^{\mathrm{Spin}}_6((\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^g)$ is an isomorphism, thus $\mathcal{I}(M_g)$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}^{2g + 2{\binom{g}{2}} + {\binom{g}{3}}}$. Moreover:
      	\begin{itemize}
      		\item[(1)] A basis of $\mathcal{I}(M_g)$ is given by the following Dehn twists:
      		\begin{align*}
      			& \mathbf{t}_{S_k, \alpha}, & 1 \leq k \leq g; \\
      			& \mathbf{t}_{S_k \# S_k, \alpha}, & 1 \leq k \leq g; \\
      			& \mathbf{t}_{S_k \# S_l, \alpha}, & 1 \leq k < l \leq g; \\
      			& \mathbf{t}_{S_k \# S_k \# S_l, \alpha}, & 1 \leq k < l \leq g; \\
      			& \mathbf{t}_{S_k \# S_l \# S_h, \alpha}, & 1 \leq k < l < h \leq g.
      		\end{align*}
      		
      		\item[(2)] A ``standard" basis of $\mathcal{I}(M_g)$, mapping to the standard basis of $\mathbb{Z}^{2g + 2{\binom{g}{2}} + {\binom{g}{3}}}$ via the composition of $\rho$ and the bordism invariants described below Lemma \ref{lem:homologyeffect}, is given by the following diffeomorphisms:
      		\begin{align*}
      			& \mathbf{t}_{S_k \# S_k, \alpha} - 8\mathbf{t}_{S_k, \alpha}, & 1 \leq k \leq g; \\
      			& \mathbf{t}_{S_k, \alpha}, & 1 \leq k \leq g; \\
      			& \mathbf{t}_{S_k \# S_l, \alpha} - (\mathbf{t}_{S_k, \alpha} + \mathbf{t}_{S_l, \alpha}), & 1 \leq k < l \leq g; \\
      			& \mathbf{t}_{S_k \# S_k \# S_l, \alpha} + 2\mathbf{t}_{S_k, \alpha} + \mathbf{t}_{S_l, \alpha} - (\mathbf{t}_{S_k \# S_k, \alpha} + 2\mathbf{t}_{S_k \# S_l, \alpha}), & 1 \leq k < l \leq g; \\
      			& \mathbf{t}_{S_k \# S_l \# S_h, \alpha} + \mathbf{t}_{S_k, \alpha} + \mathbf{t}_{S_l, \alpha} + \mathbf{t}_{S_h, \alpha} - (\mathbf{t}_{S_k \# S_l, \alpha} + \mathbf{t}_{S_k \# S_h, \alpha} + \mathbf{t}_{S_l \# S_h, \alpha}), & 1 \leq k < l < h \leq g.
      		\end{align*}
      	\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

W^{-k,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)
:=\Big\{\,f\in\mathcal S' : f=\sum_{|\alpha|\le k}\partial^\alpha f_\alpha,\ f_\alpha\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)\,\Big\},
\]
with norm $\ \|f\|_{W^{-k,1}}:=\inf\big\{\sum_{|\alpha|\le k}\|f_\alpha\|_{L^1}\big\}$ over such representations.
Equivalently,
\[
W^{-k,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)\ \cong\ \big(W^{k,\infty}_0(\mathbb{R}^d)\big)'\!,
\]
via $\langle \varphi, f\rangle_{W^{k,\infty}_0-W^{-k,1}}=\sum_{|\alpha|\le k}(-1)^{|\alpha|}\!\int f_\alpha\,\partial^\alpha\varphi$.
title: Negative Sobolev space

\begin{enumerate}
\item If $R$ is FID and $P$ a permutation matrix, then $RP$ and $PR$ are FID.
\item 
A  matrix $R$ with non-negative entries is FID if and only if there exist a permutation matrix $ {P}$ 
such that $ {R}{P} $ is irreducible and has positive main diagonal. 
\item 
 If $ {R} $ is FID, then there is an integer $k \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $R^k$ has strictly positive entries,  i.e. $R$ is primitive. 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Lemma lem:independence-across-bands-boundary-lengths of arXiv:2606.10973, 'Quasisymmetric rigidity of the Brownian sphere'] For each $\zeta > 0$ and $b \in (0, 1)$, there exists $\lambda_\ast = \lambda_\ast(\zeta, b) \in (0, 1)$ such that for each $\lambda \in (0, \lambda_\ast]$, the following is true: Let $(\BC, \Phi; 0, \infty)$ be a $\sqrt{8/3}$-LQG cone. Let $(M,g)$ be a complete Riemannian manifold of dimension $n$ with nonnegative Ricci curvature and without boundary (for instance $M=\mathbb R^n$), and let $u>0$ be a smooth solution of $u_t=\Delta u$ on $M\times(0,\infty)$. Then the differential Harnack (Li-Yau) inequality holds pointwise: $\frac{|\nabla u|^2}{u^2}-\frac{u_t}{u}\le\frac{n}{2t}$, equivalently $-\Delta\log u\le\frac n{2t}$. Integrating along geodesics gives the classical Harnack form: for $x_1,x_2\in M$ and $0<t_1<t_2$, $u(x_1,t_1)\le u(x_2,t_2)\Big(\frac{t_2}{t_1}\Big)^{n/2}\exp\Big(\frac{d(x_1,x_2)^2}{4(t_2-t_1)}\Big).$ Both are sharp: equality in the differential form holds for the Gaussian $u=\Phi(x,t)$ on $\mathbb R^n$. Positivity of $u$ on the whole of $M\times(0,\infty)$ and $\mathrm{Ric}\ge0$ are both needed; if $\mathrm{Ric}\ge-K$ with $K>0$ the estimate degrades to $\alpha\frac{|\nabla u|^2}{u^2}-\frac{u_t}{u}\le\frac{n\alpha^2}{2t}+\frac{n\alpha^2K}{2(\alpha-1)}$ for any $\alpha>1$.

body: [Defn def:almost_constant of arXiv:2604.10446, 'Least singular values of shifted sparse random combinatorial matrices'] Let $\delta, \rho \in (0,1)$. We define the set of  almost-constant  $\mbox{Cons}(\delta, \rho)\subset \mathbb{C}^{n}$  as the set of vectors $v\in \mathbb{C}^{n}$ for which there exists a complex number $\lambda$ such that the number of coordinates $i\in [n]$ satisfying $|v_i-\lambda|\le\rho\|v\|_2/\sqrt{n}$ is strictly larger than $(1-\delta)n$. The vectors in the remaining set $\lr{\mbox{Cons}(\delta, \rho)}^c=\mathbb{C}^n\setminus \mbox{Cons}(\delta, \rho)$ are called non-almost-constant.

[Theorem thm:backward-stein-nonconvex of arXiv:2608.29507, 'Denoising as Projection: Constrained Optimization with Gradient-Guided Diffusion'] Let Assumption (assump:data-convex of the paper) and the conditions of Lemma~(lem:one-step-descent-convex-nonconvex of the paper) hold. Consider the backward update as in (equation eq:projected-gradient-guidance-relaxed of the paper).
Then, with $\alpha_{\eta,\epsilon}$, $\Gamma_1$, $\Gamma_2$, $G$, and $L$ defined as in Lemma~(lem:one-step-descent-convex-nonconvex of the paper), define
\begin{align*}
\Delta_T
:=
\max_{x\in\mathcal{X}}f(x)-\min_{x\in\mathcal{X}}f(x)
+
\frac{\Gamma_1\|n_T\|}{\epsilon}
+
\frac{\Gamma_2\|n_T\|^2}{\epsilon}
+
GC_{\mathcal{X}}\sigma_T
+
\epsilon LC_{\mathcal{X}}^2\sigma_T^2,
\end{align*}
where $C_{\mathcal{X}}$ is the constant from Lemma~(lem:stein-convex-projection of the paper). Then
\begin{align*}
\textstyle \alpha_{\eta,\epsilon}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|\mathcal G_\eta(p_t)\|^2
\le
\Delta_T, \quad \Longrightarrow \quad
\min_{1\le t\le T}\|\mathcal G_\eta(p_t)\|^2
\le
\frac{\Delta_T}{\alpha_{\eta,\epsilon}T}.
\end{align*}
Moreover, the normal component satisfies
$\|n_0\|\le (1-\epsilon)^T\|n_T\|.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

more than half of the vertices. In this case, $G$ contains a spanning $\{1,2\}$-factor, by Fact~\ref{fact:12-factor}, and $G$ is totally Hall-universal, by Theorem~\ref{thm:hedet}. Now suppose $2M>n$. Then there is a unique largest part, say $A_0$, so that $|A_0|=M$. Let $H$ be a graph on $V$ such that $(H,G)$ satisfies Hall's condition. By

[Thm 1 of arXiv:2506.12443, 'Error Rates for Large Deviations in the domain of an $\alpha=1$ stable law'] Assume~\eqref{q:Psi'Est} and~\eqref{q:tail1} (so $\alpha = 1$).
    Fix a large finite number $a > 2$.
    Put $N=N(n)\defeq x(n)+b_n$ and assume that $x(n)$ is such that $n (\log N)^2 = o(N)$ as $n\to\infty$.

        \P(S_n>N)=n\P(X_1>N)+O\left(\frac{n^2(\log N)^2}{N^{2}}\right)+O\left(\frac{n}{N^{2-2/a}}\right)\qquad \text{ as }n\to\infty,

[Theorem 29 (EFIID implies analyticity \cite{Ott_Analyticity_Ising,Ott_Analyticity_RCM}) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Let $\mu$ be a stationary random field on $S^{\Z^d}$.
 Write $\sigma\sim\mu$ for the random element.
 Consider a finite set $A\subset\Z^d$
 and a bounded observable $F_A$ that is $\sigma|_A$-measurable.

[Theorem thm:stable-threshold of arXiv:2606.28869, '\bfseries A General Theory of Paths:\\ \large Signatures, Jump Lifts, and Expected Signatu'] Let $X$ be a one-dimensional symmetric $\gamma$-stable Levy process with $\gamma\in(0,2)$ and let $\mathrm{Sig}^M(X)$ be its geometric Marcus lift. For every integer $k\ge1$,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}\left[\left|\inner{\mathrm{Sig}^M(X)_{0,T}}{1^k}\right|\right]<\infty
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
k<\gamma.
\end{equation}
Consequently the full expected signature is not finite beyond the levels allowed by the stable moment threshold, and expected-signature characterization is unavailable at every level $k\ge\lceil\gamma\rceil$.
title: stable-law moment threshold for the expected signature

\]
If the nonzero transition coefficients are retained, we define the edge weight

\]
