body:
[Theorem th:GW of arXiv:2510.10299, '\Large Sparse graphs and their Benjamini-Schramm limits: a spectral tour'] Let $d >0$, $T$ be a Galton-Watson tree with $\mathrm {Poi}(d)$ distribution  whose root is denoted by $o$, $A$ its adjacency operator and $m_d = \mathbb {E} m_A^{\delta_o}$ its average spectral measure. There exist $1 \leq  d_1 \leq d_2$ such that 
\begin{enumerate}[label = (\roman*)]
\item (Average spectral measure: atoms) 
$m_d(\{\lambda \}) > 0$ if and only of $\lambda$ is a totally-real algebraic integer.  
\item (Dimension of kernel)  $
m_d (\{0 \}) = q + e^{-dq} + d q e^{-dq} -1
$, where $q \in (0,1)$ is the smallest root to $q = e^{-d e^{-dq}}$.

\item (Average spectral measure: continuous part) 
$m_d$ has a non-trivial continuous part if and only if $d >1$.

\item (Average spectral measure: ac part) 
$m_d$ has a non-trivial ac part for all $d > d_1$ and its total mass goes to $1$ as $d \to \infty$. Moreover, the limit
$
\lim_{t \to 0} m_d([-t,t]\backslash \{0\})/ t 
$
exists and is positive if and only if $d > e$.

\item (Spectral decomposition: atoms)   For all $d> 1$, conditioned on $T$ being infinite, with probability one, there is an $\ell^2$-eigenvector with eigenvalue $\lambda$ for all totally-real algebraic integers.

\item (Spectral decomposition: ac) 
For all $d > d_2$, conditioned on $T$ being infinite, with probability one,  $A$ has non-trivial ac spectrum. Moreover the total mass of the ac part of  $m_A^{\delta_o}$ goes to $1$ in probability as $d \to \infty$.

\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem th:GW of arXiv:2510.10299

body:
[Lem TechnicalLem of arXiv:2410.23859, 'Subcritical regimes in the Poisson Boolean percolation on Ahlfors regular spaces'] Let $c > 1$. Let $f,g \colon [1, \infty) \to [0,\infty)$ be bounded measurable functions satisfying the following properties:
       \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
        \item $f|_{[1, 10c]} \leq \frac{1}{2}$ and $g \leq \frac{1}{4}$,
        \item for all $r \geq 10c$, $f(r) \leq f(\frac{r}{10c})^2 + g(r)$.
       \end{enumerate}
       Then $\lim_{r \to \infty}g(r) = 0$ implies $\lim_{r \to \infty} f(r) = 0$. Moreover, if there exists $\theta > 0$ such that the integral $\int_1^\infty r^{\theta-1}g(r) dr$ is finite, then the integral $\int_1^\infty r^{\theta-1}f(r) dr$ is also finite. body:
[Definition DEAFRS of arXiv:2603.12774, 'Synchronization by noise for stochastic differential equations driven by fractional Browni'] Let $\varphi$ be a continuous SDS. For $t \geq 0$ and $\Gamma \in \sigma(\mathcal{X}) \otimes \sigma(\mathcal{B})$, define
	\begin{align}
		\mathcal{Q}_{t}\left((x,\omega^-); \Gamma\right) 
		:= \int_{\mathcal{B}} 
		\chi_{\Gamma}\!\left( 
		\varphi^{t}_{P_{t}(\omega^-, \omega^+)}(x), 
		P_{t}(\omega^-, \omega^+) 
		\right) 
		\mathbf{P}(\mathrm{d}\omega^+).
	\end{align}
	The family $\{\mathcal{Q}_t\}_{t \geq 0}$ forms a Feller transition semigroup on $\mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{B}$.  
	
	A probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{B}$ is called an \emph{invariant measure} for $\varphi$ if it satisfies:
	\begin{itemize}
		\item The marginal of $\mu$ on $\mathcal{B}$ coincides with $\mathbf{P}$, i.e.
		\begin{align}
			(\Pi_\mathcal{B})_{\star}\mu = \mathbf{P}.
		\end{align}
		
		\item The measure $\mu$ is invariant under the semigroup $\{\mathcal{Q}_t\}_{t \geq 0}$, meaning that for all $t \geq 0$ and $\Gamma \in \sigma(\mathcal{X}) \otimes \sigma(\mathcal{B})$,
		\[
		(\mathcal{Q}_t)_{\star}\mu(\Gamma)
		:= \int_{\mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{B}}
		\mathcal{Q}_t\big((x,\omega); \Gamma\big)\,
		\mu(\mathrm{d}(x,\omega))
		= \mu(\Gamma).
		\]
	\end{itemize}
	We also call $\mu$ \emph{ergodic} if it is ergodic with respect to the shift map on 
	$C(\mathbb{R}^+, \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{B})$; see \emph{[DPZ96]} for further details.
title: Definition DEAFRS of arXiv:2603.12774

[Lemma 21 (Doeblin minorization) of arXiv:2512.02661, 'Worst-case mixing estimates for Brownian motion with semipermeable barriers'] Suppose that one is given some $C,T>0$ such that for every $x_0\in D$ and measurable $E\subseteq D$,
	\begin{align}
		\bbP(X_T \in E \mid X_0 = x_0) \geq C  \Area(E).
	\end{align}
	Then,
	$
		\pi_{\min} \geq C
	$ and the mixing time satisfies
	$
		\tmix \leq T \lceil \ln(1/4)/\ln(1 - C\Area(D))\rceil.
	$

body: In infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, Gaussian measures with different covariance operators are mutually singular by the Cameron-Martin / Feldman-Hajek theorem, making the total variation distance $d_{\mathrm{TV}}$ degenerate ($= 1$). The $d_2$ probability metric, requiring two continuous bounded Fréchet derivatives on test functions, provides the natural topology for quantitative functional CLTs in infinite-dimensional path spaces.

[Corollary of arXiv:2609.00105, 'Weighted composition operators and classification of weighted Hardy spaces'] Assume that $\mathcal{H}_1$ and $\mathcal{H}_2$ are $2$-interpolating and $T:\mathcal{H}_2\to\mathcal{H}_1$ is a bounded linear operator.
    Suppose also that $X_2$ is a maximal domain for $\mathcal{H}_2$ and $T^{\ast}(k^1_x)\neq 0$ for all $x\in X_1$. 
    The following are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $T$ is a composition operator.
        \item $T(fg)=T(f)T(g)$ whenever $f,g\in\mathcal{H}_2$ such that $fg\in\mathcal{H}_2$.
    \end{enumerate}

body: Theorem 1.12 (0/1-Polytopes with Poor Vertex Expansion). Let pi be the uniform distribution. For any k > 2 and any n > 2k sufficiently large, there is a 0/1-polytope Q = Q_{n,k} in {0, 1}^n with O(n^k) vertices and psi(Q) <~ (4k)^k / n^{k-2}. Here psi(Q) is the weighted vertex expansion (Definition 1.2) of the graph of Q: for S in V with vertex boundary dS := {v not in S | uv in E for some u in S}, psi(S) := pi(dS)/pi(S), and psi(G) := min{1, min over S in V with 0 < pi(S) <= 1/2 of psi(S)}; with pi uniform, psi(S) = |dS|/|S|.

body:
[Lemma lem:variables of arXiv:2510.09818, 'On the Fourier dimension of fractional Brownian graphs'] [LL25]
	For $q \ge 1$, let $\varepsilon \in \{-1,1\}^{2q}$ and $\sigma \in \Sigma(q)$ as defined in (equation b4 of the paper).
	With the notation introduced above, we set
	\begin{gather}\begin{gathered}
		\{j_1<\cdots<j_I\} = \{ j : [\sigma_{k_m}\cdots\sigma_{k_1} (\varepsilon)]_j \not\in \{0, \ast\} \}\quad \text{and}\quad\\
		(a_1,\dots, a_I) = ([\sigma_{k_m}\cdots\sigma_{k_1} (\varepsilon)]_{j_1}, \dots, [\sigma_{k_m}\cdots\sigma_{k_1} (\varepsilon)]_{j_I}).
	\end{gathered}\end{gather}
	Then we have
	\begin{align}
	\sigma_{2q-1} \cdots \sigma_3 \sigma_1 G_\varepsilon(u) = \partial_{u_{k_1'}}\cdots \partial_{u_{k_\ell'}}G_{\sigma_{k_m} \cdots \sigma_{k_1} (\varepsilon)}(u),
\end{align}
	which is a function depending on the variables $u_{j_1},\dots, u_{j_I}$ and independent of all other variables $u_j$ with $j \not\in\{j_1, \dots, j_I\}$.
	If we label the non-trivial variables $u_{j_1},\dots,u_{j_I}$ as $s_1,\dots,s_I$,
	then all differentiation variables $u_{k_1'},\dots,u_{k_\ell'}$ are non-trivial variables and can be labelled as $s_{p_1},\dots,s_{p_\ell}$ for a subset of indices $p_1<\cdots<p_\ell$.
	Hence, one can recast (equation E:sigmaG of the paper) as
	\begin{align}
		\sigma_{2q-1}\cdots\sigma_3\sigma_1 G_\varepsilon(u) = \partial_{s_{p_1}}\cdots\partial_{s_{p_\ell}} G_{\sigma_{k_m} \cdots \sigma_{k_1} (\varepsilon)}(s).
	\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:variables of arXiv:2510.09818

[Lemma 43 of arXiv:2607.29495, 'Fast Mixing for Low-Temperature Potts Models via Poisson Trees'] For any non-leaf vertex \(v\in V(T)\), we have that
    \[
    \frac{Z^{\mi}_v}{Z^{\pl}_v} = \prod_{u:\, u\prec v} f\Big(\frac{Z^{\mi}_u}{Z^{\pl}_u}\Big) \mbox{ where } f(z) \coloneqq \frac{(q-2+\emm^\beta)z + 1}{(q-1)z+\emm^\beta},
    \]
    and \(u\prec v\) denotes that \(u\) is a child of \(v\).

[Lemma cap.translation of arXiv:2411.19145, 'On the intersection of critical percolation clusters and other tree-like random graphs'] For any finite sets $A,B \subset V$, one has the subadditivity property, 
$${\rm Cap}_\beta(A\cup B) \le {\rm Cap}_\beta(A) + {\rm Cap}_\beta(B). $$ 
Furthermore ${\rm Cap}_\beta$ is monotone for the inclusion of sets.

On G = {0,1}^2 put F(0,0) = 1/10, F(1,0) = F(0,1) = 3/5 and F(1,1) = 1. F is order-preserving and F(1,1) = 1, but its mixed difference at (1,1) is 1 - 3/5 - 3/5 + 1/10 = -1/10 < 0, so F is the CDF of no random vector on G: a negative full mixed difference, not a failure of monotonicity, is what rules it out.
G = {0,1}^2 has the coordinatewise order
order-preserving means x <= y implies F(x) <= F(y)

body: In mathematics, a simple group is a nontrivial group whose only normal subgroups are the trivial group and the group itself. A group that is not simple can be broken into two smaller groups, namely a nontrivial normal subgroup and the corresponding quotient group. This process can be repeated, and for finite groups one eventually arrives at uniquely determined simple groups, by the Jordan–Hölder theorem.
title: Simple group

[Corollary Wulff corollary of arXiv:2608.27248, 'Optimal Transport and the ABP Method in Higher Codimension'] Let $n\geq2$ and $1\leq m\leq4$.  Let
$X:\Sigma\to\mathbb{R}^{n+m}$ be a compact minimal immersion with smooth boundary,
and let $\mathcal E\subset\mathbb{R}^{n+m}$ be a centered ellipsoid.  Then
$\partial\Sigma\ne\varnothing$ and
\[
 \int_{\partial\Sigma}h_{\mathcal E}(\eta)\,\mathrm d\sigma
 \geq nV_*(\mathcal E)^{1/n}|\Sigma|^{\frac{n-1}{n}}.
\]
Equality holds if and only if, for an $n$-plane $P$ realizing
$V_*(\mathcal E)$, $X$ is an embedding onto
$x_0+r\,\overline{\operatorname{proj}_P\mathcal E}$ for some
$x_0\in\mathbb{R}^{n+m}$ and $r>0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Sharp ellipsoidal Wulff inequality

body: Invariance of domain: Let n >= 1, let U be an open subset of R^n, and let f : U -> R^n be an injective continuous map. Then f(U) is open in R^n, and f is a homeomorphism from U onto f(U). The equality of dimensions is essential: the conclusion fails for injective continuous maps of an open subset of R^n into R^m with m > n (for example, the inclusion of R^1 as a line in R^2 has image with empty interior).
title: Invariance of domain

Then we have the following decomposition of $\mu_A$ into ``product measures'' restricted to $\Omega$, where $\lambda_{H}$ denotes Lebesgue measure on the hyperplane $H$:
    \begin{align*}
\mu_{A,h}|_{\Omega}(\sigma) 
&=\int_{\im(A)} p(u) 
\mu_{X^{\mathsf{T}} u + h}|_{\Omega}(\sigma) 
d\lambda_{\im(A)}(u) \\
\text{where }p(u) &\propto \exp\pa{-\fc 12 \left\Vert {u}\right\Vert^2}
\sum_{\sigma\in \Omega} \exp\left( {\left\langle
Xu+h, \sigma\right\rangle
} \right).
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Definition def:le of arXiv:2605.22787, 'Invariant measures for half-space geometric LPP: classification and the one force--one sol'] For each $n \in \mathbb{N}$, consider $(\lambda^0(n),\ldots,\lambda^n(n))$ distributed according to (equation Eq.SchurProcess of the paper) with $m=n$. For $i\in \mathbb{N}$ and $j\in \llbracket 0,n \rrbracket$ set  $L_i^n(j)=\lambda_i^j(n)$.   We extend these functions to $[0,\infty)$ by linear interpolation on $[0,n]$ and by setting them equal to $L_i^n(n)$ on $[n,\infty)$. The random functions $(L_i^n)_{i\in \mathbb{N}}$ are called the \textit{half-space geometric line ensemble} [dy25,ddy26], where $L_i^n$ denotes the $i$-th line.

[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2609.00448, 'Equivariant formality and representation theory'] \textnormal{(cf. \cite[Theorem 6.2]{CFok}).}
	We have the ring isomorphism
	\[K^*(G/K; \mathbb{Q})\cong (R(K; \mathbb{Q})/i^*I(G; \mathbb{Q})\oplus\mathfrak{a})\otimes\bigwedge\nolimits^*P.\]
	Here $R(K; \mathbb{Q})/i^*(G; \mathbb{Q})$ is the image of the map $\alpha: R(K; \mathbb{Q})\to K^0(G/K; \mathbb{Q})$ defined by the associated vector bundle $\alpha(\rho):=[G\times_K V]$, $\mathfrak{a}$ is an ideal of the first tensor factor on the RHS. We also have that $j^*$ maps $P$ isomorphically onto $Q$. Moreover, $\text{dim }P=\text{dim }Q\leq \text{rank }G-\text{rank }K$, and equality holds if and only if $G/K$ is formal, if and only if $\mathfrak{a}=0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition lck-prop2 of arXiv:2608.30747, 'Compact homogeneous complex manifolds'] Let $(M=G_f/K\times S^1,J,g)$ be an LCK Hermitian C-space defined as in (equation LCK-M of the paper)-(equation LCK-g of the paper) by $F=G_f/H_f$, a regular $W\in\zg(\hg_f)$ and $a,b,c,t\in\RR$.  Then the  following holds: 
\begin{enumerate}[{\rm (i)}]
\item $(J,g)$ is never balanced and it is LCB if and only if $a=0$.   
 
\item $(J,g)$ is always BTP and it is BAS if and only if $M=\SU(2)\times S^1$, the Hopf surface.  
  
\item If $c_1(M,J)=0$, then the metric $g$ is CYT if and only if  
$$
\tfrac{t}{c} = (a^2+1)|\Delta_\qg^+| |Z_{J_\qg}|,
$$  
where $|\Delta_\qg^+|$ denotes the number of positive complementary roots of the flag $F=G_f/H_f$.  In particular, $(M=G_f/K\times S^1,J)$ is always a CYT manifold.     
\end{enumerate}

[Definition 2 (Exact depth at $\theta_0$) of arXiv:2604.10792, 'Variable-Length Markov Chains on Finite Quivers: Boundary-Window Identifiability, Exact De'] Fix $r\ge1$.
The model has \emph{exact depth $r$ at $\theta_0$} if there exists a neighborhood $U\ni\theta_0$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item for every $\theta\in U$, every admissible context $\xi$ of length at least $r$, and every admissible appended edge $a$, the quantity $\mu_\theta(a\mid\xi)$ depends only on the suffix $R_r(\xi)$,
\item for every integer $k$ with $1\le k<r$ there exist admissible contexts $\xi,\xi'$ of length at least $k$ and an appended edge $a$ which is admissible from both $\xi$ and $\xi'$ such that $R_k(\xi)=R_k(\xi')$ and the maps $\theta\mapsto\mu_\theta(a\mid\xi)$ and $\theta\mapsto\mu_\theta(a\mid\xi')$ are not identical on any neighborhood of $\theta_0$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Exact depth at $\theta_0$

[Proposition prop:normal of arXiv:2411.16913, 'Entropies of the Poisson distribution as functions of intensity: ``normal'' and ``anomalou'] For the Poisson distribution with parameter $\lambda>0$: 
    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item {\normalfont\textrm{[braiman2024]}} The Shannon entropy $\mathbf H_{SH}(\lambda)$ is strictly increasing and concave as a function of $\lambda\in(0,\infty)$. 
\item {\normalfont\textrm{[braiman2024]}}
    For any $\alpha \in (0,1) \cup (1,\infty)$, the R\'enyi entropy $\mathbf H_R(\alpha,\lambda)$ strictly increases as a function of $\lambda\in(0,\infty)$.
    \item 
    For any $\alpha \in (0,1) \cup (1,\infty)$, the Tsallis entropy $\mathbf H_{T}(\alpha, \lambda)$ strictly increases as a function of~$\lambda\in(0,\infty)$.
    \item 
    For any $\alpha,\beta \in (0,1) \cup (1,\infty)$, the  Sharma--Mittal entropy $\mathbf H_{SM}(\alpha, \beta, \lambda)$ strictly increases as a function of $\lambda\in(0,\infty)$.
    \end{enumerate}

[Theorem 28 (Local well-posedness) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Let $\parvec$ satisfy \eqref{eq:parameter-vector}, let
Assumption~\ref{ass:exponents} hold, let the Cauchy data satisfy
\eqref{eq:data-space}, and let $\xi_{\W},\xi_{\K}$ be the independent white-in-time, spatially stationary Gaussian forcings generated by admissible Fourier symbols in Definition~\ref{def:gaussian-forcing-profile}.  There is a compatible family of local solutions in the sense of
Definition~\ref{def:compatible-local-solutions}, based on the exhaustion
$K_n=\overline{B(0,n)}$, whose lifetimes are almost surely positive.  For every
compact $K\Subset\R^3$, it induces a measurable lifetime $\tau_K$ and a local
paracontrolled solution $(u,v,\mathcal N)$ on $[0,\tau_K)\times K$ in the
sense of Definitions~\ref{def:local-solution}
and~\ref{def:random-interval-solution}.  The lifetimes may be chosen so that
\[
 K_1\subset K_2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \tau_{K_1}\ge\tau_{K_2}.
\]
On every common existence interval, the local solution is independent of the
adapted localization pair.  For fixed $(\Theta,\Xi)$, it is unique in the
class of Definition~\ref{def:local-solution}.  The stability assertion is
understood on a common deterministic interval and in a common contraction
ball: for every compact $K$, every $T\in(0,1]$, and every realization in
$\{T<\tau_K\}$, there exist $R_{K,T}<\infty$, $\delta_{K,T}>0$, and
$C_{K,T}<\infty$ such that the reference map is a strict contraction of
the closed radius-$R_{K,T}$ ball of $\mathcal Z_T$.  If
\[
 d_T\bigl((\Xi,y),(\widetilde\Xi,\widetilde y)\bigr)<\delta_{K,T},
\]
then the perturbed map for the same localization pair is also a strict
contraction of that ball, has a unique fixed point on $[0,T]$, and
\[
 \|Z-\widetilde Z\|_{\mathcal Z_T}
 \le C_{K,T}
 d_T\bigl((\Xi,y),(\widetilde\Xi,\widetilde y)\bigr),
\]
where $d_T$ is defined in \eqref{eq:Xi-distance}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Local well-posedness

body:
[Lemma Morse Lemma of arXiv:2607.24640, 'The Yang-Mills measure on surfaces via Morse theory'] Let $f:\Sigma\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be a $\mathcal{C}^\infty$ Morse function. Then, for any $a$ in $\operatorname{Crit}(f)$, there exists a smooth chart centered at $a$ such that, in these local coordinates, the function $f$ reads
$$
f(x) = f(a)+\frac {1}{2}\left(\varepsilon_1x_1^2+\varepsilon_2 x_2^2\right),
$$
with $\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2\in\{-1,1\}$. If $\varepsilon_1=\varepsilon_2=1$, we say that $a$ has index $0$ (local minimum). If $\varepsilon_1=1,\varepsilon_2=-1$, we say that $a$ has index $1$ (saddle point). If $\varepsilon_1=\varepsilon_2=-1$, we say that $a$ has index $2$ (local maximum). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Morse Lemma

body:
Let A and B be sub-sigma-fields of a probability space. Define alpha(A,B)=sup_{E in A,F in B}|P(E intersection F)-P(E)P(F)| and rho(A,B)=sup |Corr(f,g)| over real square-integrable A-measurable f and B-measurable g with strictly positive variances; put rho=0 if either sigma-field supports no such variable. Then 4 alpha(A,B)<=rho(A,B). For a stationary sequence, take A=sigma(X_j:j<=0), B=sigma(X_j:j>=n) to obtain 4 alpha(n)<=rho(n). In particular rho-mixing implies alpha-mixing; the converse is not asserted.

Square-integrable real functions of positive variance in rho definition

[Proposition 3 of arXiv:2607.27082, '2607.27082'] Assume that the one-step increment $\xi_1$ is symmetric and satisfies \eqref{eq:cond_nalpha} with $\alpha=1$ and $L_\xi$ slowly varying. Suppose that
\(
0<\E[\eta_0]<\infty\) and \(
0<\E[\frac{\pi}{1-\pi}]<\infty.
\)
Then the following items hold:
\begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] If
    \[
    \liminf_{n\to\infty}L_\xi(n)>
    \frac{4}{\E\!\left[\frac{\pi\eta_0}{1-\pi}\right]},
    \]
    then the interval-activation frog model survives with positive probability.

    \item[(ii)] Assume additionally that
    \(\E[(1-\pi)^{-2}]<\infty.
    \)
    If
    \[
    0<\liminf_{n\to\infty}L_\xi(n)
    \le
    \limsup_{n\to\infty}L_\xi(n)
    <
    \frac{1}{2\E\!\left[\frac{\pi\eta_0}{1-\pi}\right]},
    \]
    then the interval-activation frog model dies out almost surely.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 25 of arXiv:2608.03497, 'Connective Constants on Nested Fractal Graphs'] Fix \(r\ge1\).  For each \(\sigma\in\cS_r\), fix a forest
\(\Gamma_\sigma\in\cC_r(\sigma)\).  For a walk \(w\) and an \(r\)-cell
\(\Delta\) that contains neither endpoint of \(w\) and satisfies
\(\Gamma_\Delta(w)\ne\varnothing\), put
\[
  \sigma_\Delta(w)
  =\operatorname{tr}_r\bigl(S_\Delta^{-1}\Gamma_\Delta(w)\bigr).
\]
We call \(\Delta\) \emph{canonical for \(w\)} if
\[
  S_\Delta^{-1}\Gamma_\Delta(w)=\Gamma_{\sigma_\Delta(w)}.
\]
Let \(\mathsf m_r(w)\) be the number of canonical \(r\)-cells of \(w\).
There is a constant \(a>0\) such that
\begin{equation}
  \limsup_{n\to\infty}
  \#\{w\in\cW_{O,n}:\mathsf m_r(w)\le\lfloor an\rfloor\}^{1/n}
  <\mu.
  
\end{equation}

[Theorem thm:spectral-lower of arXiv:2606.27073, 'Retention Profiles and KL Contraction Bounds in Finite Markov Chains'] For a reversible chain with stationary distribution $\pi$, define
\[
  g(x,y) := \frac{P(x,y)}{\pi(y)} - 1,
  \qquad
  T_3(x) := \sum_{y\in S}\pi(y)\,|g(x,y)|^3.
\]
Then
\[
  I(X_0;X_1)
  \;\ge\;
  \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=2}^n\lambda_i^2
  \;-\;
  \frac{1}{6}\sum_{x\in S}\pi(x)\,T_3(x).
\]
If $\pi$ is uniform, then
\[
  \bar r_\pi
  \;\ge\;
  \frac{1}{2\log n}\sum_{i=2}^n\lambda_i^2
  \;-\;
  \frac{1}{6\log n}\sum_{x\in S}\pi(x)\,T_3(x).
\]

[Theorem 37 of arXiv:2609.01190, 'Rough differential equations on manifolds via natural bundles'] Let $n\in\Nsf$, let $M'$ be a manifold and let $f: M'\to R_n^2M'$ be a rough velocity field. Let also $M$ be a properly embedded submanifold of $M'$ with $\phi: M\to M'$ being the embedding. Then the following statements are equivalent:
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)]
	\itemsep0em
	\item It holds that $(f\circ\phi) (M)\subseteq \mathrm{Im}( R_n^2\phi )$.
	\item For every interval $[S,T]\subseteq\Rsf$, every $n$-dimensional branched rough path $X$ on interval $[S,T]$ with regularity $p\in [1,3)$ and control function $\omega$, and every integral curve $Y:[S,T]\to M'$ of $f$ driven by $X$ such that $Y(S)\in \phi(M)$, we have that $Y(t)\in \phi(M) $ for every $t\in [S,T]$.
	\end{enumerate}

[Lemma L:massOutofCompact of arXiv:2606.03079, 'Mean Field Limits for Stochastic, Underdamped Reactive Langevin Dynamics Models'] There exists a sequence of $C_{b}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d)$ functions $\{f_{m}(x,v)\}_{m \geq 0}$ with $f_{0} \equiv 1$ such that
$$
\begin{aligned}
f_{m}(x,v) &=0 \text { when }\|x\| + \|v\| \leq m-1 \\
f_{m}(x,v) &=1 \text { when }\|x\|+ \|v\|>m \\
0 \leq f_{m}(x,v) & \leq 1 \text { when } m-1<\|x\| + \|v\|\leq m .
\end{aligned}
$$
Additionally, $\displaystyle\sup _{m \geq 0}\|f_{m}(x,v)\|_{C_{b}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d)}:=\sup _{m \geq 0} \mkern22mu \smashoperator{\sup_{\substack{ x \in \mathbb{R}^{d},v \in \mathbb{R}^{d},\\ |\alpha| \leq 2\strut}}}|D_{\alpha} f_{m}(x,v)|<\infty$. For such a sequence of functions $\{f_{m}(x,v)\}_{m \geq 0}$, we have
$$
\lim _{m \rightarrow \infty} \limsup _{\zeta \rightarrow 0} \mathbb{E}\left[\sup _{t \in[0, T]}\langle f_{m}, \mu_{t}^{\zeta, j}\rangle \right]=0
$$
for all $j=1,2, \cdots, J$.

[Lemma lemER of arXiv:2607.12459, 'Renormalisation of Inhomogeneous Random Graphs'] {\bf [Invariance property for deterministic weights]}

For every $\delta\in(0,\infty)$, $\eta\in[0,\infty)$ and $w\in(0,\infty)$, the deterministic weight law concentrated at $w$ is invariant under averaging of weights: if $W_1,\ldots,W_m$ are deterministic random variables equal to $w$, then 
\[
m^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^m W_i \stackrel{d}{=}W_1,
\]
where in this case equivalence in distribution coincides with equality in value. Combined with the invariant connection functions $g^{\neq}_\delta(x,y) = \delta xy$ and $g^{=}_\eta(x,x) = \eta x$ identified in Lemma~(leminv of the paper), this gives a two-parameter homogeneous Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph with edge and self-loop  connection probability equal to
\[
p^{\neq} = 1-\mathrm{e}^{-\delta w^2}, \qquad p^{=} = 1-\mathrm{e}^{-\frac12(\delta w^2+\eta w)}.
\]
The above random graph is invariant in distribution under the renormalisation transformation, provided the aggregated weights are rescaled by $m^{-1}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lemER of arXiv:2607.12459

$$\begin{aligned}
    &\mathbb{P}_X\left(Q_*(A_n,X,\lambda_i)\leq 2Ct_i\delta_i,\quad \frac{\|(A_n-\lambda_i I_n)^{-1}X\|_2}{\|(A_n-\lambda_i I_n)^{-1}\|_*}\geq t_i,\quad \forall i=1,2 
    \right)\\& \leq 4\sum_{k_1,k_2=1}^n\mathbb{P}_X(Q_*(A_n,X,\lambda_i)\leq 2Ct_i\delta_i,\langle X,v_{k_i}(\lambda_i)\rangle\geq t_i\log(1+k_i),\forall i=1,2),
\end{aligned}$$ where $v_k(\lambda_i)$ is the eigenvector associated with the $k$-th largest singular value  of $(A_n-\lambda_i I_n)^{-1}$ ((i.e., $\mu_k(\lambda_i)$), for each $i=1,2$ and $k\in[n]$. The set of eigenvectors $v_k(\lambda_i),k\in[n]$ form an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb{R}^n$.

\ee

[Definition 11 of arXiv:2608.26084, 'Localic Esakia Duality\\via Conic Frames'] A \emph{monotone map} $f\colon (X,R)\to (Y,Q)$ between locales equipped with localic relations consists of a locale map~${f\colon X\to Y}$ satisfying:
	\[
	
	\begin{tikzcd}[cramped]
		R & Q \\
		{X\times X} & {Y\times Y.}
		\arrow["{\exists \bar f}"', dashed, from=1-1, to=1-2]
		\arrow[tail, from=1-1, to=2-1]
		\arrow[tail, from=1-2, to=2-2]
		\arrow["{f\times f}"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	The map $\bar f$ is unique if it exists. The commutativity of the square above is equivalent to saying that the \emph{source} and \emph{target squares} commute:
	\[\begin{tikzcd}[cramped]
		R & Q \\
		X & Y
		\arrow["{\bar f}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
		\arrow["{s_R}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
		\arrow["{s_Q}", from=1-2, to=2-2]
		\arrow["f", from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\end{tikzcd}
	\qquad\text{and}\qquad
	\begin{tikzcd}[cramped]
		R & Q \\
		X & {Y.}
		\arrow["{\bar f}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
		\arrow["{t_R}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
		\arrow["{t_Q}", from=1-2, to=2-2]
		\arrow["f", from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\end{tikzcd}\]
title: Definition 11 of arXiv:2608.26084

[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2606.06757, 'Path-Dependent Ergodic Optimal Control \\ and Backward Stochastic Differential Equations'] Let $(b,H), (\tilde b,\tilde H)$ be coefficients satisfying  Assumptions~\ref{dissipativity_assumption},~\ref{hamiltonian_assumption}, together with \eqref{eq:delta_bH} for some measurable maps $\delta b,\delta H:\R_+\rightarrow\R_+$. Then,
there exists a constant $C>0$, depending only on $\eta_1$, $\eta_2$, $\theta_0$, $\theta$, and $L_H$, such that for all $K\in\K$:
\begin{equation*}
|\lambda_*(K)-\tilde{\lambda}_*(K)|+|\lambda^*(K)-\tilde{\lambda}^*(K)|\leq \, \limsup_{\rho\downarrow 0}\Big\{ C \,  \Big(\int_0^\infty K_{\rho}(t)(\delta b(t))^2dt\Big)^{\frac{1}{2}} + \int_0^\infty K_{\rho}(t) \delta H(t)dt \Big \} \, .    
\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 7 of arXiv:2606.06757

[Proposition 16 of arXiv:2608.15914, 'Absorption cutoff and stationary singularities for rounded Gaussian random dynamical syste'] Let $\varepsilon_\varrho\downarrow0$ satisfy
  \begin{equation*}
    L_{\varepsilon_\varrho}
    =L_\varrho+o(\sqrt{L_\varrho}).
  \end{equation*}
  Then, for every fixed $a\in\R$,
  \begin{equation}
    \Pp\left(
      \theta_{\varepsilon_\varrho}^{\mathrm{rad}}>t_\varrho(a)
    \right)
    \to
    \Phi_{\mathrm G}(-a),
    \qquad
    \varrho\downarrow0.
  \end{equation}
  The same limit holds if $t_\varrho(a)$ is replaced by
  $\max\{0,\lfloor t_\varrho(a)+u_\varrho\rfloor\}$ for any deterministic
  $u_\varrho=o(\sqrt{L_\varrho})$.
title: Proposition 16 of arXiv:2608.15914

[Defi 39 of arXiv:2608.09700, 'A general paracontrolled ansatz for singular SPDEs'] One says that $u$ develops in the  paracontrolled system associated with \eqref{eq_gPAM} to order $\gamma$, if for any $\tau\in\mcT$ with $|\mcI(\tau)|<\gamma$ we have 
		$$
		u_\tau = \sum_{\substack{\sigma\succ\tau \\ |\mcI(\sigma)|<\gamma}} \P(u_\sigma,Z_{\sigma/\tau} ) + u_\tau^\#.
		$$
		with $u_\tau^\# \in C^{\gamma-|\mcI(\tau)|}$.
			We write $\mcD^\gamma_\P(\mcZ)$ for the vector space of such paracontrolled systems, we endow it with the norm
		$$
		\norme{u}_{\mcD^\gamma_\P(\mcZ)} = \sum_{\substack{|\mcI(\tau)|<\gamma} } \lVert u_\tau^\#\lVert_{C^{\gamma-|\mcI(\tau)|}}.
		$$
title: Definition 39 of arXiv:2608.09700

proved in Propositions~(prop:add of the paper) and~(prop:flip of the paper)

[Theorem thm:upper_bd_local_time_bdry_PushTASEP of arXiv:2509.20779, 'Diffusive Scaling limit of stochastic Box-Ball systems and P\MakeLowercase{ush}TASEP'] Let $\partial \mathbb{S}^{d}:=\{ x\in \mathbb{Z}^{d}\,:\, \text{$x_{1} < \cdots < x_{d}$ and $x_{i+1}-x_{i}=1$ for some $i=1,\dots,d-1$}\}$. 
	
	Consider a configuration with $d$ balls and run the PushTASEP dynamics $\xi$ for time $T$. Let $N_T^{(d)}$ be the length of time up to time $T$ that $\xi$ spends in the set $\partial \mathbb{S}^{d}$. Then $\mathbb{E}[N_T^{(d)}] = \Theta(\sqrt{T})$. Furthermore, the location $\xi_t(i)$ of the $i$th particle at time $t$ in PushTASEP satisfies 
	\begin{align}
		\mathbb{E}[\xi^{(i)}_{T}]  
		&= T+O(\sqrt{T}).
	\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:upper_bd_local_time_bdry_PushTASEP of arXiv:2509.20779

[Definition Almost Sure Logistic Stability of arXiv:2411.05369, 'Stochastic games of parental vaccination decision making and bounded rationality'] We say that a process $Y(t)\in [0,1]$ has an almost sure logistically stable equilibrium at $y=0$ and $1$ if for some $c>0$,
    $$\lim_{t\to \infty} \frac{1}{t} \log \frac{Y(t)}{1-Y(t)} = (-1)^{y+1} c$$ almost surely.

      \leq
      \tilde{c}_2(K,t) 2^{-\ell \varepsilon}.
    \end{equation}

[Definition Complex Radon Measure of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] A \emph{complex Radon measure} \(\mu\) on \(\mathbb{R}^d\) is a countably additive function
\[
  \mu: \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^d) \;\longrightarrow\; \mathbb{C}
\]
such that both the real part \(\mathrm{Re}(\mu)\) and the imaginary part \(\mathrm{Im}(\mu)\) are (real) Radon measures. Equivalently, if one writes
\[
  \mu \;=\; \mu_{1} \;+\; i\,\mu_{2}, 
  \quad 
  \mu_{1},\,\mu_{2}\colon \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^d)\to\mathbb{R},
\]
then \(\mu_{1}\) and \(\mu_{2}\) are each (real) Radon measures in the sense of the previous definition.
title: Complex Radon Measure

body:
[Prop 1 (Anchor-averaged regularity bound) of arXiv:2608.21652, 'GeoQ: Geometry-Aware Conditional Quantile Error Estimation for Scientific Surrogate Models'] Let $(\mathcal X,d_{\mathcal X})$ be a metric input space and
$(\mathscr Y,d_{\mathscr Y})$ be a metric output space. Let
$F,\widehat F:\mathcal R\subseteq\mathcal X\to\mathscr Y$ satisfy, for all
$x,x_0\in\mathcal R$,
\[
d_{\mathscr Y}(F(x),F(x_0))\le L_F d_{\mathcal X}(x,x_0),
\qquad
d_{\mathscr Y}(\widehat F(x),\widehat F(x_0))
\le L_{\widehat F}d_{\mathcal X}(x,x_0),
\]
where $L_F,L_{\widehat F}\ge 0$. Define the scalar surrogate error
\[
E(x)=d_{\mathscr Y}(F(x),\widehat F(x)).
\]
Then, for any $x,x_0\in\mathcal R$,
\begin{equation}
E(x)\le E(x_0)+(L_F+L_{\widehat F})d_{\mathcal X}(x,x_0).

\end{equation}
Moreover, for any finite anchor set
$\mathcal A(x)\subseteq\mathcal R$,
\begin{equation}
E(x)
\le
\frac{1}{|\mathcal A(x)|}
\sum_{x_a\in\mathcal A(x)} E(x_a)
+
\frac{L_F+L_{\widehat F}}{|\mathcal A(x)|}
\sum_{x_a\in\mathcal A(x)}
d_{\mathcal X}(x,x_a).

\end{equation}

DRAFT proof (unaudited), T318-C6 v2. Let s>0 and, conditionally on a random training environment, let V_p(g)>=0 and f_p(g) be test functions with E_g V_p -> c>0, Var_g V_p ->0, E_g f_p^2 ->R>0 in probability and E_g f_p^4=O_P(1). Then all measurable exact or o_P(1)-approximate global minimizers over T>=0 of L_p(T)=0.5 E_g[log((s+T V_p)/s)+(s+f_p^2)/(s+T V_p)-1] converge in probability to R/c. No independence of V_p and f_p is assumed. Compact uniform convergence follows from a uniform derivative bound; the event V_p>=c/2 has test probability tending to one and gives a logarithmic tail lower bound excluding all diverging T uniformly. Applied to the unaudited C4 shared-feature Gaussian teacher model with fixed nonconstant globally Lipschitz activation, independent spherical hidden directions, Gaussian inputs, positive finite aspect ratios, prior variance s_p^2>0, teacher variance s_*^2>=0, and correct positive test/training noise sigma^2, this proves whole-posterior finite-model temperature minimizers converge to 1+(r-1)lambda m_2(lambda)/m(lambda). Here lambda=sigma^2/s_p^2, r=s_*^2/s_p^2, m(a) is the positive centered-covariance weighted resolvent from C4 and m_2=-mprime. This includes raw ReLU. Likelihood tempering is excluded; no independent audit or priority claim.

[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2608.05842, 'Asymptotic Expansion of the Kallianpur–Striebel Formula under Perturbations of Linear Mode'] We have the expression
  \begin{align*}
      &E_Q[z_t(y)]\\
    =&\sqrt{\det(I_{d_1}-\Sigma^\frac{1}{2}\phi(0;t)\Sigma^\frac{1}{2})}\exp\left( \frac{1}{2}\int_0^t b(s)^\top \phi(s;t)b(s)ds \right)\\
  &\times \exp\biggl(\frac{1}{2}\beta(t;y)^\top \Sigma^\frac{1}{2}(I_{d_1}-\Sigma^\frac{1}{2}\phi(0;t)\Sigma^\frac{1}{2})^{-1}\Sigma^\frac{1}{2}\beta(t;y) \biggr)\\
  &\times \exp\biggl(\mu^\top \alpha(0,t;t)^\top y(t)\\
  &- \int_0^ty(s)^\top \left\{ a(s)+b(s)b(s)^\top \phi(s;t) \right\}\alpha(0,s;t)ds \mu+\frac{1}{2}\mu^\top \phi(0;t) \mu\biggr)\\
  &\times \exp\biggl( \frac{1}{2}y(t)^\top \gamma(t)y(t)
  +\frac{1}{2}\int_0^t y(s)^\top b(s)b(s)^\top y(s)ds\\
  &-\int_0^t y(s) b(s)b(s)^\top y(t) ds  \biggr),
  \end{align*}
  where
  \begin{align*}
    &\mu=E[X_0],~~\Sigma=\mathrm{Cov}(X_0,X_0),\\
    &\alpha(u,s;t)=\exp\left( \int_u^s \{a(r)+b(r)b(r)^\top \phi(r;t)\}dr \right),\\
    &\beta(t;y)= \alpha(0,t;t)^\top y(t)- \int_0^t \alpha(0,s;t)^\top \left\{ a(s)+b(s)b(s)^\top \phi(s;t) \right\}^\top y(s) ds\\
    &\qquad \qquad+ \phi(0;t)\mu,\\
    &\gamma(t)=\int_0^t \alpha(s,t;t)b(s)b(s)^\top \alpha(s,t;t)^\top ds.
  \end{align*}

body:
[Prop 7 of arXiv:2603.25536, 'The $H^{2|2}$ monotonicity theorem revisited'] Partition the vertex set $V$ into two subsets: the bulk $V_1 = \{1, \dots, N-1\}$ and the boundary $V_2 = \{N,\delta\}$.\footnote{The boundary was $\{1,\delta\}$ in Section~\ref{subse:boundary_variations}; we choose $\{N,\delta\}$ here to cleanly perform the block decomposition.} This partition induces a block decomposition of the symmetric matrices $H_\beta$ and $G$:
\begin{equation*}
    H_\beta = \begin{pmatrix} H_\beta^{V_1, V_1} & H_\beta^{V_1, V_2} \\ H_\beta^{V_2, V_1} & H_\beta^{V_2, V_2} \end{pmatrix}, \quad G = \begin{pmatrix} G^{V_1, V_1} & G^{V_1, V_2} \\  G^{V_2, V_1} & G^{V_2, V_2} \end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation*}
Then conditionally on \((\beta_{i})_{i\in V_{1}}\), \((G^{V_2,V_2})^{-1}\) is distributed according to \(q_{\{N,\delta\}}^{\widetilde{W}_{N\delta},1}\), where
\[\widetilde{W}_{N\delta} = W_{N\delta} + \left[H_{\beta}^{V_{2},V_{1}} (H_\beta^{V_1, V_1})^{-1} H_{\beta}^{V_{1},V_{2}}\right]_{N\delta}.\]
In particular, \(\frac{d \widetilde{W}_{N\delta}}{dW_{N\delta}} =1\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition prop:SDPI:synchronous of arXiv:2605.16904, 'Positive-rate PCA and IPS with stationary Bernoulli measures are rapidly forgetful \footno'] Let $\Sigma$ be a finite set.
	Let $\theta\colon\Sigma\times\Sigma\to(0,1)$ be a strictly positive stochastic matrix with stationary distribution~$q\colon\Sigma\to(0,1)$.  Let $\kappa>0$ be such that $\theta(a,b)\geq\kappa q(b)$ for each $a,b\in\Sigma$.
	Let $n$ be a positive integer.
	Then,
	\begin{equation}
		D\left(\underline{p}\theta_n \relto[\big] \otimes_{i=1}^n q\right) \leq (1-\kappa) D\big(\underline{p} \relto[\big] \otimes_{i=1}^n q\big)
	\end{equation}
	for every probability distribution $\underline{p}\colon\Sigma^n\to[0,1]$.
title: Strong data processing inequality for synchronous updating

body: Theorem (campaign status: audited-pass): In the component encoding, sequences with k = O(n/log n) and ell -> infinity are controlled whenever 4^ell = o(ell*log n); the residual error from 9*4^ell + ell is then negligible against the leading saving -(n-r)*ell. Equivalently the uniformly controlled range includes ell ≤ (1/2)*log2 log n + (1/2)*log2 log log n - omega(1). Quantifier (audit-corrected): if a sequence merely fails the little-o condition, the corresponding lower bound on ell is valid only along a subsequence where 4^ell/(ell*log n) stays bounded below - not an every-index conclusion for an oscillating sequence. Fixed-defect cases are handled separately by finite-core enumeration. Notes: 'Controlled' is relative to the moment-argument encoding; this does NOT decide the conjecture, and a substantial regime remains where 4^ell is too large to pay directly. Threshold re-checked: at the stated ell bound, 4^ell = (log n)(log log n)*2^(-omega(1)) = o(ell*log n). Superscripts flattened in extraction.

[Lemma lem: distribution of X of arXiv:2604.23890, 'The Cutoff Profile for Random Transpositions on Repeated Cards in the Full Range of Parame'] Let $n=ml$, such that $m,l\ge 2$. Suppose the entries of $A=(a_{ij})\in\Mat_m(\mathbb{Z})$ are nonnegative, and all the rows and columns have sum $l$. Let $\tau$ be distributed with respect to $U_{\mathfrak{S}_n}$. Then, we have
$$\mathbf{P}(X(\tau)=A)=\frac{(l!)^{2m}}{n!\cdot\prod_{1\le i,j\le m}a_{ij}!}.$$
Moreover, suppose 
$t=\frac n2\left(\log n-\frac 12\log l+c\right)$,  where $c\in \mathbb{R}$ is an absolute constant. Let $\sigma$ be distributed with respect to $\mu_n^t$. Then, for all $k\ge 0$, we have
$$\mathbf{P}(X(\sigma)=A\mid |S_t|=k)=\sum_{r_1+\cdots+r_m=k}\frac{k!(l!)^m\prod_{i=1}^m(l-r_i)!}{n!\prod_{i\ne j}a_{ij}!}\prod_{i=1}^m\binom{a_{ii}}{r_i}.$$

\[ \big| p^{a'}(e_o) -  p^{a''}(e_o) \big|  \le  D\big( 1  - (2D)^{-D} \big)^{r-3}. \]
Moreover, the same bound continues to hold if we take $a'' \equiv +\infty.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:asymptotic-direction of arXiv:2607.24018, 'Jeu de taquin forests \\ and the inverse infinite RSK correspondence'] Let $A \subset \mathbb{N}_0^2$ be an infinite set of boxes in the positive
	quarter-plane.
	We say that $A$ has an \emph{asymptotic direction} if the limit
	\[
		\alpha_\textnormal{asym}(A) := \lim_{n\to\infty} \alpha(x_n, y_n)
	\]
	exists for any enumeration $((x_n,y_n))_{n=1}^\infty$ of
	the elements of $A$ for which $x_n+y_n
	\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{} \infty$. The limit value
	$\alpha_\textnormal{asym}(A) \in [0,1]$ is called the \emph{asymptotic
		RSK-angle of~$A$}, or, in a slight abuse of language, the
	asymptotic direction of~$A$.

[Definition def-kulkarni of arXiv:2605.15395, 'Equivalence and Separation for Multivariate Matrix-Exponential and Phase-Type Distribution'] An \(m\)-state Markovian reward-based representation is specified by a triplet \((\boldsymbol{\upalpha},\mathbf{T},\mathbf{K})\), where \(\boldsymbol{\upalpha}\) is the initial row vector, \(\mathbf{T}\) is the transient subgenerator, and \(\mathbf{K}\) is the reward matrix. In this Markovian case, \(\mathbf{t}\) and \(p_0\) are determined by \(\mathbf{t}=-\mathbf{T}\mathbf{1}\) and \(p_0=1-\boldsymbol{\upalpha}\mathbf{1}\). A random vector $\bm{X}\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{n}$ belongs to $\if\relax\detokenize{n}\relax\mathrm{MPH}^{*}\else{}_{n}\mkern1.5mu\mathrm{MPH}^{*}\fi$ if there exist $m\ge 1$, a sub-probability row vector $\boldsymbol{\upalpha}\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{1\times m}$, a transient subgenerator $\mathbf{T}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}$, and a non-negative reward matrix $\mathbf{K}\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{m\times n}$ such that
\begin{equation}
  L_{\bm{X}}(\mathbf{s})=\mathbb{E}\bigl[e^{-\langle \mathbf{s},\bm{X}\rangle}\bigr] =p_{0}+\boldsymbol{\upalpha}\bigl(-\mathbf{T}+\Delta(\mathbf{K}\mathbf{s})\bigr)^{-1}\mathbf{t},
\end{equation}
where $\mathbf{t}=-\mathbf{T}\mathbf{1}$ and $p_{0}=1-\boldsymbol{\upalpha}\mathbf{1}\ge 0$. In probabilistic terms, the underlying continuous-time Markov chain starts according to $\boldsymbol{\upalpha}$ unless it is absorbed at time zero with probability $p_0$. If \(J_t\) denotes the transient state occupied at time \(t\), then the \(j\)-th coordinate is the accumulated reward
\[ 
  X_j=\int_0^\tau \mathbf{K}_{J_t j}\,\mathrm{d}t,
\]
where \(\tau\) is the absorption time. Thus, while the chain is in transient state \(i\), coordinate \(j\) accumulates reward continuously at rate \(\mathbf{K}_{ij}\ge0\). The vector $\bm{X}$ belongs to $\if\relax\detokenize{n}\relax\mathrm{MME}^{*}\else{}_{n}\mkern1.5mu\mathrm{MME}^{*}\fi$ if its transform admits a representation of the form~(equation eq-kulkarni of the paper) with \(\mathbf{T}\) Hurwitz-stable, but without the Markovian and sign constraints on \(\boldsymbol{\upalpha}\), \(\mathbf{T}\), \(\mathbf{K}\), or \(\mathbf{t}\), and subject only to \(L_{\bm X}\) being the Laplace transform of a genuine probability measure on \(\mathbb{R}_+^n\).
title: $\MPH{n}$ and $\MME{n}$

[Lemma 15 of arXiv:2609.00516, 'Exceptional points on Atkin--Lehner quotients'] Let $N$ be squarefree and suppose $\psi:X_0^*(N) \to E$ admits a degree 3 morphism over $\Q$ with $E$ an elliptic curve.  
Then for every prime $p \nmid N$, we have
\[ \frac{\Psi(N)}{2^{\omega(N)}} = \prod_{q\mid N}\frac{q+1}{2} \leq 12\cdot \frac{3(p+1)^2 - 1}{p - 1}\]
where $\Psi$ is the Dedekind psi function $\Psi(N) = \prod_{q\mid N}(q+1)$ for squarefree $N$.

[Proposition 26 (Light-tail quotient norm lower bound) of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\R^d$ be i.i.d. random vectors with
		independent coordinates satisfying
		\eqref{eq:independent:coordinate:distribution:assumption} with $K_x>0$.
		Suppose $n/d^2\to \alpha\in (0,1/2)$ as $n\to\infty$. There exist $K>0$ and $\gamma>0$, depending only on

		probability $1-o(1)$, the following holds.  For every
		$\mathcal I\subset[n]$ with $|\mathcal I|\le C_0d\log d$ and every $K$-light $t$

		\[
		\inf_{\substack{\supp h\subset \mathcal I\\ \|h\|_1\le d^{2/3}\|t\|_2}}
		\|\mathcal{L}_X^*(h+t)\|_*

		\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:uniform flows of arXiv:2506.10765, 'A General Coupling for Ising Models and Beyond'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite graph, $q\geq 2$ be an integer, $x_e\in (0,1)$ for each $e\in E,$ $\Omega=\{0,1\}^E,$ $\Sigma=\ker(\partial)$ and $f:\Omega\to 2^{\Sigma}$ be defined by $f(\omega)=\ker(\partial^\omega)$ and 
$$
\rho[\omega]\propto \mathbb{P}_x[\omega],\quad\forall \omega\in \Omega,\qquad \gamma[\eta]\propto 1,\quad\forall \eta\in \Sigma.
$$
	Then, under the coupling measure $\mathscr{P}$ defined in Theorem (thm:generalcoupling of the paper), 
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item[(a)] The marginal of $\mathscr{P}$ on $\Sigma$ is $\ell^q_{G,x}$.
        For each $\omega\in\Omega$, the conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\;\cdot \mid \omega]$ on $\Sigma$ is the uniform  measure on $\ker(\partial^\omega)$, i.e. a uniform divergence free $q$-coloring of $\omega$.
		\item[(b)] The marginal of $\mathscr{P}$ on $\Omega$ is the random-cluster model with cluster-weight $q$ and edge-weights $(p_e)_{e\in E}$  satisfying $\frac{x_e}{1-x_e}=\frac{p_e}{q(1-p_e)},$ 
        \[
        \phi^q_{G,p}[\omega]\propto \left(\prod_{e\in \omega} \frac{p_e}{1-p_e}\right)q^{\kappa(\omega)}.
        \]
        For each $\eta\in\Sigma$, the 
        conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\;\cdot \mid \eta] = \mathbb{P}_{x} \cup \delta_{\eta}$ on $\Omega$ is Bernoulli percolation on $E$ with parameter $(x_e)_{e\in E}$ conditioned on all edges in $\eta$ being open.
	\end{enumerate}

body:
[Theorem CCLT of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given variables $x_1,x_2,x_3,\ldots$ which are i.i.d./f.i.d., centered, with variance $t>0$, we have, with $n\to\infty$, in moments,
$$\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sum_{i=1}^nx_i\sim G_t/\Gamma_t$$
where $G_t/\Gamma_t$ are the complex normal and Voiculescu circular law of parameter $t$, given by:
$$G_t=law\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(a+ib)\right)\quad,\quad 
\Gamma_t=law\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(\alpha+i\beta)\right)$$
where $a,b/\alpha,\beta$ are independent/free, each following the law $g_t/\gamma_t$.

[Lemma ergodicity of arXiv:2607.07616, '\vspace{-5cm}The End of the Double Random Current'] Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a vertex-transitive, amenable, infinite graph. Then, the double random current  triplet
$\ell^0_{\mathbb{G}}\otimes \ell^0_{\mathbb{G}}\otimes \mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{G}}$ is tail-trivial and ergodic.
Moreover, $\ell^0_{\mathbb{G}}\cup \ell^0_{\mathbb{G}}\cup \mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{G}}$ has at most one infinite cluster almost surely.

[Theorem Theorem 3_2 of arXiv:2607.19651, 'Metastability and phase transition in a social network model with multiple opinions'] For any $0<\alpha<\frac{1}{M-1}$, there exists $\beta_0, C_1>0$ and  $C_2>0$, depending only on $\alpha$, $M$ and $N$, such that for any $\beta\geq \beta_0$, for any $o\in\mathcal{O}$ and for any  $u\in \mathcal{C}^o_\alpha$,
$$
\sup_{t\geq 0}\left|{\mathbb P}\left(\frac{R^{\alpha,\beta,u}(\mathcal{C}^{-o}_{\alpha})}{\mathbb{E}(R^{\alpha,\beta,u}(\mathcal{C}^{-o}_{\alpha}))}>t\right)-e^{-t}\right| \leq C_1\beta^3e^{-C_2 \beta}.
$$
Moreover, for any $u,v \in \mathcal{C}^o_{\alpha}$,
$$
\left|\frac{\mathbb{E}(R^{\alpha,\beta,u}(\mathcal{C}^{-o}_{\alpha}))}{\mathbb{E}(R^{\alpha,\beta,v}(\mathcal{C}^{-o}_{\alpha}))}-1\right| \leq C_1\beta^3e^{-C_2 \beta}.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem Theorem 3_2 of arXiv:2607.19651

[Thm 3 of arXiv:2506.19008, 'Sprinkled Decoupling for Hammersley's Process'] Assume that $p_\circ<p_\bullet$. For any $\rho<\rho_{c-}$ we have that $v_-(\rho)>\rho$ and there exist $\tilde{c}_1\in(0,\infty)$ and $\tilde{v}>\rho$ such that 
$$\tilde{p}_H(\tilde{v},\rho)\leq \tilde{c}_1\exp\left(-2\log^{3/2} H \right)\,,\,\forall\,H\geq 1\,.$$
For any $\rho>\rho_{c+}$ we have that $v_+(\rho)<\rho$ and there exist $c_1\in(0,\infty)$ and $v<\rho$ such that 
$$p_H(v,\rho)\leq c_1\exp\left(-2\log^{3/2} H \right)\,,\,\forall\,H\geq 1\,.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 3 of arXiv:2506.19008

PRIVATE HEURISTIC, author-recorded. In scale-free percolation with weight tail exponent tau and long-range parameter alpha (connection probability 1 - exp(-lambda W_x W_y |x-y|^{-alpha d})), the annealed two-point connection decays like |x-y|^{-alpha d (tau-1)}, i.e. like long-range percolation with P(x <-> y) ~ |x-y|^{-d-s} for s = d(alpha(tau-1) - 1). Long-range percolation is mean-field for d > 3 min(s, 2) (Heydenreich-van der Hofstad-Sakai), which predicts mean-field critical behaviour for scale-free percolation iff alpha(tau - 1) < 4/3 or d > 6, with tau > 3 (for tau in (2,3) the model percolates instantly). This is a prediction for Heydenreich-van der Hofstad Open Problem 16.8, not a theorem: the quenched weights induce correlations that the annealed long-range comparison ignores.
Scale-free percolation on Z^d with parameters alpha, tau, lambda
Long-range percolation upper critical dimension 3 min(s,2)
title: Scale-free percolation: an effective long-range exponent and the predicted mean-field region

body:
[Theorem thm:deformed-moment-convergence of arXiv:2609.03532, 'Airy limit for the Jack process and topological expansion'] For every $\theta>0$, $\boldsymbol k\in\mathbb R_{>0}^m$, and
$\tau_1\geq\cdots\geq\tau_m$, the series
$\mathbf L_b[\boldsymbol k;\boldsymbol\tau]$ is absolutely convergent.  Moreover, for
every $\boldsymbol\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^m$,
\begin{equation}
  \lim_{N\to\infty}
  \mathcal A_N(\boldsymbol\varepsilon;\boldsymbol k
    ,\boldsymbol\tau)
  =\mathbf L_b[\boldsymbol k;\boldsymbol\tau],
  \qquad b=\theta^{-1}-1.
  
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
  \lim_{N\to\infty}\mathcal M_N(\boldsymbol k
    ;\boldsymbol\tau)
  =(1+\mu_+)^m\mathbf L_b[\boldsymbol k
    ;\boldsymbol\tau].
  
\end{equation}
Both convergence statements are locally uniform in the
ordered vector $\boldsymbol\tau$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Convergence of the deformed moments

[Definition of arXiv:2411.16103, 'Non-commutative Stein's Method: Applications to Free Probability and Sums of Non-commutati'] Suppose $([n],E)$ is a graph over $[n]$. For $i,j\in[n]$, we write $i\sim j$ if $\{i,j\}\in E$. For $i\in[n]$, we let $N_i$ denote the adjacency neighbourhood of $i$, defined as the set 
$$N_i:=\{i\}\cup\{j\in[n]; j\sim i\}.$$ 
We say that the graph $([n],E)$ is a dependency graph for a collection of random variables $\{\xi_i\ ;\ i\in[n]\}$ if for any two disjoint subsets $I_1, I_2$ of $[n]$ such that there are no edges connecting $I_1$ to $I_2$, the collection of random variables $\{\xi_i\ ;\  i \in I_1 \}$ is free from $\{\xi_i\ ;\  i \in I_2 \}$.

[Defn of arXiv:2608.29914, 'Fixed points in abstract provability structures'] Let $S = \langle L, \leq, \top, \bot, \Box, \boxtimes\rangle$ be an APS and $\triangle v$ be a one-variable APS term.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item An element $p \in L$ is called a \emph{fixed point} of $\triangle v$ in $S$ if $\triangle p = p$. 

    \item The statement ``$\triangle v$ has a fixed point in $S$'' is denoted by $\mathsf{E}_S(\triangle)$.
    Here $\mathsf{E}$ stands for `existence'. 

    \item The statement ``$\triangle v$ has at most one fixed point in $S$'' is denoted by $\mathsf{U}_S(\triangle)$.
    Here $\mathsf{U}$ stands for `uniqueness'. 
\end{enumerate}
title: Unnumbered defn of arXiv:2608.29914, 'Fixed points in abstract provability structures'

[Proposition p:taub of arXiv:2605.20587, 'Persistence and entropic repulsion of stationary Gaussian fields with spectral singularity'] Let $\alpha \in [0,d)$, let $w$ be slowly varying at infinity, and let $f$ be an SGF on $\mathbb{R}^d$ or $\mathbb{Z}^d$ satisfying one of the following:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item As $x \to \infty$,
\[ K(x) \sim  B_{\alpha,d} |x|^{-\alpha} w(|x|) . \] 
\item $\alpha>0$, and $\mu$ has density $\rho$ in a neighbourhood of the origin such that, as $\lambda \to 0$,
\[ \rho(\lambda) \sim A_{\alpha,d} |\lambda|^{\alpha-d} w(1/|\lambda|). \]
\end{enumerate}
Then, as $T \to \infty$,
\[\mu[B(1/T)] \sim T^{-\alpha} w(T) \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition p:taub of arXiv:2605.20587

[Lemma lem:hypergeom of arXiv:2608.04900, 'A Sharper Hoeffding Bound for Weighted Sums of Exchangeable Random Variables'] Let $H\sim\mathrm{Hypergeometric}(N,K,m)$ with $0\le K\le N$ and $1\le m\le N-1$, and let $\mu=K/N$. Set $s=m\wedge(N-m)$. Then for every $t\in\mathbb{R}$,
\begin{align*}
\log \mathbb{E} \big[e^{t(H-m\mu)}\big]
\le
\frac{t^2}{8}B_{N,m},
\qquad
B_{N,m}=(N-s)^2\sum_{\ell=N-s}^{N-1}\frac{1}{\ell^2}.
\end{align*}
title: Lemma lem:hypergeom of arXiv:2608.04900

body: [Abstract of arXiv:2609.03607, 'Scaling limit for the pinning model in correlated Gaussian environment beyond the...'] In this paper, we study the scaling limit of the pinning model in correlated Gaussian environment. The tail probability of the underlying renewal process of the model has a polynomial decay with exponent $\alpha>0$. The covariance of the Gaussian environment $\{\omega_n\}_{n\in\bbN}$ is given by $\cov_{\bbP}(\omega_n,\omega_m)\sim |n-m|^{2H-2}$ with $H\in(0,1)$. Assuming $\alpha\in(0,\frac12]$, $H\in(\frac12,1)$ and $\alpha+2H>2$, we show that the partition function of the disordered pinning model, under the appropriate scaling, converges in distribution to the $L^1$-solution of the fractional stochastic heat equation driven by Gaussian noise correlated in time and localized at the origin. In particular, it is known that the solution is not $L^2$-integrable when $\alpha<\frac12$. \vspace{0.2cm}

[Defn 7 (Colored fat tree) of arXiv:2604.26499, 'Spectrum of Random Matrices with Exploding Moments'] A connected directed graph $T=(V, E)$, whose each edge is colored by red or blue, is called colored fat tree if it satisfies the following properties.
Any directed edge $u\to v$ is accompanied by at least one more edge of any color in the same direction, and there is no edge in the reverse direction. It does not contain any vertex with a loop. Additionally, the underlying simple graph $\mathcal{T}=(V, \mathcal{E}),$ obtained by ignoring orientation and multiplicity satisfies $|V|=|\mathcal{E}|+1$.

body: [Abstract of arXiv:2609.02320, 'Analysis of Triggered Packet Streams: A Matrix-Analytic Method for Exponential Triggering...'] In many communication networks, the transmission of a packet may automatically trigger the transmission of a subsequent packet from the same source after a (possibly random) delay, without requiring acknowledgment or feedback. Such behavior arises in multi-stage status updating, proactive protocols, and other applications where users generate causally dependent packet streams. In this paper, in order to analyze these systems, we introduce the $\mathrm{M^T/G/1}$ queue. In this model, primary customers arrive according to a Poisson process, and each primary customer triggers a secondary customer to join the queue after an independent delay. This arrival mechanism falls outside the scope of classical queueing models with renewal arrival processes. When the triggering delays follow an exponential distribution, we exploit the memoryless property to set up a tractable Markov description. By truncating the number of pending secondary customers, we derive a finite system of linear algebraic equations in the Laplace--Stieltjes transform domain and solve them using matrix-analytic methods. Based on the resulting workload distribution, we compute class-specific performance metrics using PASTA for primary customers and Palm conditioning for secondary customers. Finally, we validate the accuracy of this truncation through numerical experiments.
title: Abstract of arXiv:2609.02320: Analysis of Triggered Packet Streams: A Matrix-Analytic Method for Exponential Triggering...

[Conj periodicAttractivePhaseDiagram of arXiv:2609.02743, 'Sharp mean-field estimates for diffusive log/Riesz gases in the Hilbert--Schmidt regime'] \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item If $1\le\mathsf{d}\le10$, then $\beta_{\mathrm{gm}}(\mathsf{d})=2\mathsf{d}$ and
\begin{align}
{\mathsf{K}}_{N,\beta}(\mu_{\mathrm{unif}})
\longrightarrow
\mathrm{det}_2(\mathrm{Id}-\beta T_\mathsf{d})^{-1/2},
\qquad 0\le\beta<2\mathsf{d}.
\end{align}
\item In dimension $\mathsf{d}=11$, the determinant limit holds for
$0\le\beta<\beta_{\mathrm{gm}}(11)$, while
\begin{align}
\frac1N\log{\mathsf{K}}_{N,\beta}(\mu_{\mathrm{unif}})
\longrightarrow
-\inf_{\mu\ll\mu_{\mathrm{unif}}}\mathcal J_{\beta,11}(\mu)>0,
\qquad
\beta_{\mathrm{gm}}(11)<\beta<22.
\end{align}
No assertion is made here at the coexistence point
$\beta=\beta_{\mathrm{gm}}(11)$.
\item If $\mathsf{d}\ge12$, then
$\beta_{\mathrm{gm}}(\mathsf{d})=\beta_{\mathrm{s}}(\mathsf{d})$ and the transition at
$\beta_{\mathrm{s}}(\mathsf{d})$ is continuous.  The leading quartic term of $\mathcal J_{\beta_{\mathrm{s}}(\mathsf{d}),\mathsf{d}}^{\mathrm{red}}$ is strictly positive away from the origin in $E_1$.  Moreover,
\begin{align}
{\mathsf{K}}_{N,\beta}(\mu_{\mathrm{unif}})
&\longrightarrow
\mathrm{det}_2(\mathrm{Id}-\beta T_\mathsf{d})^{-1/2},
&&0\le\beta<\beta_{\mathrm{s}}(\mathsf{d}),\\
{\mathsf{K}}_{N,\beta_{\mathrm{s}}(\mathsf{d})}(\mu_{\mathrm{unif}})
&\sim C_\mathsf{d} N^{\mathsf{d}/2},
&&C_\mathsf{d}\in(0,\infty),\\
\frac1N\log{\mathsf{K}}_{N,\beta}(\mu_{\mathrm{unif}})
&\longrightarrow
-\inf_{\mu\ll\mu_{\mathrm{unif}}}\mathcal J_{\beta,\mathsf{d}}(\mu)>0,
&&\beta_{\mathrm{s}}(\mathsf{d})<\beta<2\mathsf{d}.
\end{align}
\end{enumerate} (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)

[Theorem 4 (Sharp one-arm asymptotics) of arXiv:2607.24561, 'Range convergence and sharp one-arm asymptotics\\for the critical percolation cluster in h'] Consider critical nearest-neighbour bond percolation on $\Z^d$ with $d\geq 11$. Then
\[
\lim_{r\to\infty}\ r^2\,\bP\bigl(0\leftrightarrow\partial B_r\bigr)
\;=\;\theta_1\;\in(0,\infty),
\]
where, with $\mathfrak a,\lambda$ as in \eqref{eq:guiding-kp}
\[
\theta_1\;=\;\mathbb{N}_{0,\lambda/\mathfrak a}\bigl(\Ran\not\subset\overline B_1\bigr)\;=\;\frac{\mathfrak a}{\lambda}\,\mathbb{N}_{0,1}\bigl(\Ran\not\subset\overline B_1\bigr),
\]
and $\mathbb{N}_{0,1}$ is the standard canonical measure of super-Brownian motion (i.e.\ the $(\tfrac12\Delta,1)$-super-Brownian motion); thus $\theta_1$ equals $\mathfrak a/\lambda$ times the probability that the range of standard super-Brownian motion is not contained in the unit ball. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Sharp one-arm asymptotics

[Theorem positionmatrix of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'] Suppose a deck of $n$ cards is shuffled once in a shelf-shuffler with one shelf. Let $p_{i,j}$ be the probability that card $i$ lands in position $j$. Then, we have 
    \[p_{i,j}=\frac{\binom{i-1}{j-1}+\binom{i-1}{n-j}}{2^i},\;\;\;1\leq i\leq n,\;\;\;1\leq j\leq n\]
with the convention that $\binom{0}{0}=1$ and $\binom{0}{k}=0$ for all positive integers $k$. In particular, $p_{i,j}=0$ if and only if $i+1\leq j\leq n-i$, and $p_{i,n-j+1}=p_{i,j}$ for all $i,j$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem positionmatrix of arXiv:2507.10294

[Lemma lem:discToCont of arXiv:2607.05671, 'Bi-infinite systems of singularly interacting Brownian particles and the KPZ equation'] Assume $\{X_i(0)\}_{i \in \mathbb{Z}} \sim \gamma_1$. Fix
$\theta\in(0,1)$, $T<\infty$, and $\varphi\in\mathcal{D}(\mathbb{R})$. Then
\begin{equation*}
\mathbb{E}\Bigg[
\int_0^T
\Bigg|
(1 - e^{-\sigma\varepsilon^{1/4}})^2
\sum_{i \in \mathbb{Z}}
\mathcal{G}^\varepsilon(s,Y_i^\varepsilon(s))^2
(p_{\varepsilon^{1/2\theta}} * \varphi)(Y_i^\varepsilon(s))^2
-
\sigma^2\int_{\mathbb{R}}
\tilde{\mathcal{E}}_\theta^\varepsilon(s,z)^2\varphi(z)^2\,dz
\Bigg|\,ds
\Bigg]\to 0
\end{equation*}
as $\varepsilon\to0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 15 (Strong convergence) of arXiv:2608.04824, 'Strong Convergence for a General Class of Random Matrix Models'] A random matrix tuple \(Y_n\) converges almost surely strongly to a tuple
\(y\) if, on one probability-one event, for
every noncommutative \(*\)-polynomial \(Q\),
\[
 \trn_n Q(Y_n,Y_n^*)\longrightarrow\tau(Q(y,y^*)),
 \qquad
 \|Q(Y_n,Y_n^*)\|\longrightarrow\|Q(y,y^*)\|.
\]

Let n>=1 and y_i in {-1,+1}, and let f(w;x_i) be continuously differentiable in w in R^D. Assume global constants rho>0 and beta>0 satisfy ||grad f(w;x_i)||_2<=rho and ||grad f(w;x_i)-grad f(v;x_i)||_2<=beta||w-v||_2 for every w,v and every training index i. Define L(w)=(1/n)sum_i log(1+exp(-y_i f(w;x_i))) and w_{k+1}=w_k-eta grad L(w_k), where eta>0 denotes the source paper's eta_tilde. If an integer r>=0 satisfies L(w_r)<=1/[eta(2rho^2+beta)], then L(w_t) is non-increasing for t>=r. Suppose additionally a global constant kappa>0 satisfies |f(w;x_i)-<grad f(w;x_i),w>|<=kappa for every w,i, and an integer s>=0 satisfies L(w_s)<=min{1/[2n exp(kappa+2)],1/[eta(4rho^2+2beta)]}. Then as t->infinity, L(w_t)=Theta(1/t), ||w_{t+1}||>=||w_t|| for t>=s, and ||w_t||=Theta(log t). For the normalized margin gamma_bar(w)=min_i y_i f(w;x_i)/||w||, there exists a modified margin gamma_c, non-decreasing and bounded along t>=s, and a constant c>0 with gamma_c(w_t)<=gamma_bar(w_t)<=[1+c/log(1/L(w_t))]gamma_c(w_t). Constants may depend on the fixed problem and initial stable-phase state; no dimension- or width-uniform constants are claimed. This theorem is conditional on reaching the displayed risk levels. The fixed-output-sign, trainable-first-layer network example in the source is one application; this statement does not establish a burn-in theorem when both layers are trained.

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2603.00353, 'Aldous-type Spectral Gaps in Unitary Groups'] Let $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}$ and denote $\rho_k=\rho_{(k,0,\ldots,0,-k)}$. Let $\rho\in\irr(\U(n))$ and let $\alpha$ be any eigenvalue of $\L(\Gamma,\rho)$ which is \textbf{not} associated with $\L_\torinv(\Gamma,\rho)$.
Then $\lambda_{\min}(\Gamma,\rho_k)\le\alpha$.

In particular, if $\rho$ is unbalanced, then for all $k$, $\rho_k$ ``spectrally dominates $\rho$":
\[
    \lambda_{\min}(\Gamma,\rho_k)\le\lambda_{\min}(\Gamma,\rho).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let (X, Y) be a jointly Gaussian random vector in R^a x R^b with means mu_X, mu_Y and covariance blocks A = Cov(X), B = Cov(X, Y), C = Cov(Y), so its covariance matrix is M = [[A, B], [B^T, C]], possibly singular; A^+ is the Moore-Penrose inverse, and a value x is compatible when x - mu_X lies in the range of A (the support of X). body: A map f from a topological space X to a topological space Y is continuous if for every open set V of Y the preimage f^(-1)(V) = {x in X : f(x) in V} is open in X. Equivalently: the preimage of every closed set is closed; equivalently, for every x in X and every open neighborhood V of f(x) there is an open neighborhood U of x with f(U) contained in V (continuity at every point). For maps between metric spaces this agrees with the epsilon-delta definition. Compositions of continuous maps are continuous.
title: Continuous map between topological spaces

[Proposition 87 of arXiv:2604.01685, 'Probability with Measure\footnote{Lecture notes. University of Ljubljana.}'] Let $((\Omega_\lambda,\FF_\lambda))_{\lambda\in \Lambda}$ be a family of measurable spaces. 
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
		\item $\otimes_{\lambda\in \Lambda}\FF_\lambda$ is the smallest $\sigma$-field $\GG$ on $\prod_{\lambda\in \Lambda}\Omega_\lambda$ for which  $\pr_\lambda\in \GG/\FF_\lambda$ for all $\lambda\in \Lambda$ (i.e. such as makes all the canonical projections   measurable). 
		\item For a measurable space $(\Omega,\FF)$ and a family of functions $f_\lambda:\Omega\to \Omega_\lambda$, as $\lambda$ ranges over $\Lambda$, we have that $f_\lambda\in \FF/\FF_\lambda$ for all $\lambda\in\Lambda$ iff $(f_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\in \FF/\otimes_{\lambda\in \Lambda}\FF_\lambda$. 
		\item Let there be given a probability $\mu_\lambda$  on $\FF_\lambda$ for each $\lambda\in \Lambda$. There exists a unique probability measure $\mu$ on $\otimes_{\lambda\in \Lambda}\FF_\lambda$ such that $\mu\circ\pr_\lambda^{-1}=\mu_\lambda$ for all $\lambda\in \Lambda$ and rendering $(\pr_\lambda)_{\lambda\in \Lambda}$ an independency under $\mu$. 
		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 87 of arXiv:2604.01685

denote the Gibbs average along the cavity interpolation Hamiltonian defined in~\pref{sec:cavity-interpolation}. Set
\[
m_i(s):=\langle\sigma_i\rangle_s,\qquad D_{ii}(s):=\frac{1}{1-m_i(s)^2} = \cosh^2(\operatorname{arctanh}(m_i(s)))\,.
\]
Then, for every $p\in \mathbb Z_+$, there exists a constant $C_{p,\beta,t}$ such that
\begin{equation}
    \sup_{s\in[0,1]}\ \sup_{i\in[n]}\ \mathop{{}\mathbb{E}}\big[D_{ii}(s)^p\big]\ \leqslant\ C_{p,\beta,t}.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\[
\sup_{s\in[0,1]}\ \mathop{{}\mathbb{E}}\Big[\mathsf{Tr}\big(D(m(s))^p\big)\Big]
=
\sup_{s\in[0,1]}\ \sum_{i=1}^n \mathop{{}\mathbb{E}}\big[D_{ii}(s)^p\big]
\leqslant C_{p,\beta,t}\,n.
\]

[Lemma lem:G-cert of arXiv:2608.19050, 'Online Permutation Embedding: \\ Optimal Stopping and Scaling Laws'] The functions \(\mathsf B_q\), \(\mathsf P_{p,q}\), and \(\mathsf I_{p,q}\)
are elementary on their stated domains. Moreover, for \(p,q\ge0\), we have the following (elementary) interval certificates on $G$:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item If \(p=q=0\), then \(G(p,q)\in[1,1]\).
    \item If \(p=0<q\), and if \(0\le \underline{u}\le \overline{u}\) satisfy
    \[
        \mathsf B_q(\underline{u})\le0\le\mathsf B_q(\overline{u}),
    \]
    then
    \[
        G(0,q)\in\br{q+\sqrt q\,\underline{u},\ q+\sqrt q\,\overline{u}}.
    \]
    The case \(q=0<p\) is symmetric.
    \item If \(p,q>0\), and if \(0<\underline{u}\le \overline{u}\) satisfy
    \[
        \mathsf I_{p,q}(\underline{u})\le0\le\mathsf I_{p,q}(\overline{u}),
    \]
    then
    \[
        G(p,q)
        \in
        \br{
        p+q+2\sqrt{pq}\cosh \underline{u},
        p+q+2\sqrt{pq}\cosh \overline{u}}.
    \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Lem isotopy_extension of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a $\Phi$-horizontal foliation on $M$. Let $(h_t)_{t\in [0,1]}$ be a $C^0$-isotopy of $\partial \mathcal{F}$ through $\Phi$-horizontal foliations on $\partial M$ which is smooth in the $t$ and leafwise directions. Then $h_t$ extends to a $C^0$ isotopy $\overline h_t$ of $\mathcal{F}$ through $\Phi$-horizontal foliations on $M$. Moreover, if $h_t$ is $\varepsilon$-small, then $\overline h_t$ is $O(\varepsilon)$-small, where the implicit constants may depend on $\Phi$ and $\mathcal{F}$ only.

body:
[Lemma 24 (Propagation and monotonicity of the two singular masses) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] Assume \hyp{A}{A}, let $\alpha, \sigma : \XXA \to [0,\infty)$ be finite measures and
let $\mu, \nu \in \Prob$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},nosep,topsep=3pt,leftmargin=2.4em,itemsep=3pt]
  \item \emph{Absolute continuity propagates forwards:} if $\nu \ll \pi$ then
        $T\circ\nu \ll \pi$.
  \item \emph{So does domination of the target:} if $\pi \ll \nu$ then
        $\pi \ll T\circ\nu$. Hence $T\circ\nu \sim \pi$ whenever $\nu \sim \pi$, and,
        for every $x \in \XX$ and every $m \in \N$, each of the relations
        $T^{m}_{x} \ll \pi$, $\pi \ll T^{m}_{x}$ and $T^{m}_{x} \sim \pi$, once it
        holds, holds at every later time $n \ge m$.
  \item \emph{The singular mass is monotone in the measure:} if $\sigma \le \alpha$
        then $\sing(\sigma\mid\pi) \le \sing(\alpha\mid\pi)$.
  \item \emph{It does not increase along the dynamics:}
        $\sing(T\circ\alpha\mid\pi) \le \sing(\alpha\mid\pi)$. Consequently the map
        $\Nz \to [0,1]$, $n \mapsto \sing(T^{n}\circ\mu\mid\pi)$, is non-increasing.
  \item \emph{Nor does the reversed singular mass:}
        $\sing(\pi \mid T\circ\nu) \le \sing(\pi\mid\nu)$. Consequently the map
        $\Nz \to [0,1]$, $n \mapsto \sing(\pi\mid T^{n}_{x})$, is non-increasing, for
        every $x \in \XX$.
\end{enumerate}
Part (i), and the first assertion of (ii), are the vanishing cases of (iv) and (v), by
the last sentence of Proposition \ref{prop:singforms}; they are proved first because
(iv) uses (i).

[Lemma 20 (Control of the good event) of arXiv:2604.25470, 'A mathematical analysis of hierarchical Hopfield models'] Fix $\delta\in(0,1)$ and $\rho\in\mathbb N_0$. For $\ell\in\mathbb N$ let
	$
	m_\ell:=\lfloor \delta \ell\rfloor+1
	$
	and define the envelope probabilities
	\begin{equation}
		
		q_-(\ell)
		:=
		\max_{\mu\in S_\alpha}
		\mathbb P(x_\mu=0\mid \eta^{(\alpha)},L_\alpha=\ell),
		\quad\text{and}\quad
		q_+(\ell)
		:=
		\max_{\mu\notin S_\alpha}
		\mathbb P(x_\mu=1\mid \eta^{(\alpha)},L_\alpha=\ell).
	\end{equation}
	
	Then for every $\ell$,
	\[
	\mathbb P\bigl(\mathcal G_\alpha(\delta,\rho)^c \mid L_\alpha=\ell\bigr)
	\le
	\binom{\ell}{m_\ell}\,q_-(\ell)^{m_\ell}
	+
	\frac{\bigl((M-\ell)q_+(\ell)\bigr)^{\rho+1}}{(\rho+1)!}.
	\]
	Consequently, if for some window $[\ell_M,u_M]$,
	\begin{equation}
		\max_{\ell\in[\ell_M,u_M]}
		\binom{\ell}{m_\ell}\,q_-(\ell)^{m_\ell}\to0,
	\end{equation}
	and
	\begin{equation}
		\max_{\ell\in[\ell_M,u_M]}
		(M-\ell)q_+(\ell)\to0,
	\end{equation}
	then
	\[
	\max_{\ell\in[\ell_M,u_M]}
	\mathbb P\bigl(\mathcal G_\alpha(\delta,\rho)^c \mid L_\alpha=\ell\bigr)\to0.
	\]
	Moreover,
	\[
	\mathbb P\bigl(\mathcal G_\alpha(\delta,\rho)^c\bigr)
	\le
	\mathbb P(L_\alpha\notin[\ell_M,u_M])
	+
	\max_{\ell\in[\ell_M,u_M]}
	\mathbb P\bigl(\mathcal G_\alpha(\delta,\rho)^c \mid L_\alpha=\ell\bigr).
	\]
	Therefore, $\mathbb P\bigl(\mathcal G_\alpha(\delta,\rho)^c\bigr)\to 0$ whenever \eqref{eq:sup1}, \eqref{eq:sup2} and
	\[
	\mathbb P(L_\alpha\notin[\ell_M,u_M])\to 0
	\]
	all hold.

Let n>=1 data (x_i,y_i) in R^d times {-1,+1} satisfy ||x_i||_2<=1. Assume a unit vector w_star and a fixed gamma>0 satisfy y_i <x_i,w_star> >= gamma for every i. Define ell(q)=log(1+exp(-q)), L(w)=(1/n)sum_i ell(y_i<x_i,w>), and full-batch GD w_{k+1}=w_k-eta grad L(w_k) with constant eta>0. Assume w_0=0. For every integer t>=1, (1/t)sum_{k=0}^{t-1}L(w_k)<=[1+log(gamma^2 eta t)^2+eta^2/4]/(gamma^2 eta t). Define F(w)=(1/n)sum_i exp(-y_i<x_i,w>). If L(w_s)<=1/eta at some nonnegative integer s, then risk is non-increasing from s onward, and every integer t>s satisfies L(w_t)<=[2F(w_s)+log(gamma^2 eta(t-s))^2]/[gamma^2 eta(t-s)]. There is such an s<=tau with F(w_s)<=1, where tau=(60/gamma^2)max{eta,n,exp(1),((eta+n)/eta)log((eta+n)/eta)}. The step eta can be any fixed positive real number. The all-time first estimate concerns the average loss; the second is a last-iterate estimate after the displayed stable-phase condition.

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2412.04328, 'The critical Karp--Sipser core of Erdős--Rényi random graphs'] For $i \geqslant 2$, let $D_i(n)$ be the number of vertices of degree $i$ in the Karp--Sipser core of $ \mathrm{G}[n, \mathrm{e}/n]$. Then we have the joint convergence in distribution
	\begin{equation}
	\left(\begin{array}{c}n^{-3/5} \cdot D_{2}(n) \\  n^{-2/5} \cdot D_{3}(n) \\ n^{-1/5} \cdot D_4(n) \\ D_5(n) \end{array}\right)  \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{(d)} \left( \begin{array}{c} \frac{2^{9/5}3^{4/5}}{\mathrm{e}^{3/5}} \vartheta^{-2} \\  
	\frac{2^{16/5}3^{1/5}}{\mathrm{e}^{2/5}} \vartheta^{-3} \\ \frac{2^{13/5}3^{3/5}}{\mathrm{e}^{1/5}} \vartheta^{-4} \\ \mathrm{Poi} \left( \frac{48}{5} \vartheta^{-5} \right) \end{array}\right),
	\end{equation}
	where $\vartheta=\inf\{t \geqslant 0 : W_t=t^{-2}\}$ for a standard Brownian motion $W$ started from $0$, and $\mathrm{Poi}(\lambda)$ stands for a Poisson variable with parameter $\lambda$. Moreover, with high probability, we have $D_i(n)=0$ for all $i \geqslant 6$. Finally, conditionally on $\left( D_i(n) \right)_{i \geqslant 2}$, the Karp--Sipser core is a configuration model\footnote{We refer to Section~(sec:model of the paper) for a precise definition of the configuration model.} conditioned to be simple.
	Moreover, the same result is true if we replace $\mathrm{G}[n, \mathrm{e}/n]$ by $ \mathrm{G}(n,m_n)$ where $(m_n)_{ n \geqslant 1}$ is a sequence satisfying $m_n=\frac{\mathrm{e}}{2} n +O \left( \sqrt{n}\right)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let P be a probability measure on a measurable space X, and W:X x X->[0,cmax] a measurable symmetric kernel, where 0<cmin<=d_P(x)=integral W(x,y)dP(y) and cmax>=cmin. Define L_P g(x)=integral W(x,y)g(y)/sqrt(d_P(x)d_P(y)) dP(y). For vector functions g=(g_i), write ||g||_2=(sum_i ||g_i||_(L2(P))^2)^(1/2) and ||g||_infty=(sum_i ||g_i||_sup^2)^(1/2), where sup is over X. Let f^(0)=f have finite indicated norm. For layers s=0,...,M-1 define f_j^(s+1)=sigma(sum_i h_ij^(s)(L_P) f_i^(s)+b_j^(s)), where b^(s) is a constant finite-dimensional vector, h_ij^(s)(z)=sum_{k>=0} beta_ijk^(s) z^k and |sigma(u)|<=|u|, |sigma(u)-sigma(v)|<=|u-v|. Set B_k^(s)=(beta_ijk^(s))_(j,i), H_2^(s)=sum_k ||B_k^(s)|| and H_infty^(s)=sum_k ||(|beta_ijk^(s)|)_(j,i)|| (2cmax/cmin)^k. Assume the H_* sums used are finite; polynomial filters are allowed. Then for every ell<=M and either *=2 or *=infty, ||f^(ell)||_* <= ||f||_* product_{s=0}^{ell-1} H_*^(s) + sum_{s=0}^{ell-1} ||b^(s)||_2 product_{p=s+1}^{ell-1} H_*^(p), with empty product equal to one. In the infinity norm the order of channel summation and supremum is part of the definition; it is not replaced by sup_x ||g(x)||_2. No Lipschitz partition assumption on W is needed for this norm estimate.

[Definition 5 ($d$-dimensional Hausdorff measure) of arXiv:2605.18198, 'Large deviations of crowding in finite $\beta$-ensembles'] Let $E \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ and let $d \ge 0$. For $\delta > 0$ define
		\[
		\mathcal{H}^d_\delta(E)
		=
		\inf \left\{
		\sum_{i=1}^{\infty} (\operatorname{diam} U_i)^d
		:\;
		E \subset \bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty} U_i, \;
		\operatorname{diam}(U_i) < \delta
		\right\},
		\]
		where $\operatorname{diam}(U) := \sup\{\|x-y\| : x,y \in U\}$.	The \emph{$d$-dimensional Hausdorff measure} of $E$ is defined by
		\[
		\mathcal{H}^d(E)
		=
		\lim_{\delta \to 0} \mathcal{H}^d_\delta(E)
		=
		\sup_{\delta>0} \mathcal{H}^d_\delta(E).
		\]
title: $d$-dimensional Hausdorff measure

body:
[Lem F_l of arXiv:2411.11408, 'Multidimensional specific relative entropy between continuous martingales'] \begin{enumerate}
    \item  Let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}_+$. then $F_l(\alpha \mathcal{I})=l F_1(\alpha)$.
    \item  Let $D=diag(\sigma_i^2)$ be a diagonal matrix with $\sigma_i^2 \in \mathbb{R}_+$ ($i=1, \dots, l$) on the diagonal. Then $F_l(D)=\sum _{i=1}^lF_1(\sigma_i^2)$.
    \item  Let $\Sigma \in \mathbb{R}^{l \times l}$ symmetric and positive definite, and let $D=A^{-1}\Sigma A=diag(eigenvalues\, of \, \Sigma)$. Then $F_l(\Sigma)=F_l(D)=\sum_{\sigma^2\in eigenvalues\, of \, \Sigma} F_1(\sigma^2)$. 
    \item 
    The function $X\mapsto F_l(X):= \frac{1}{2}(tr(X)-l-\log(\det X))$, from the set of $l\times l$ symmetric positive semidefinite matrices into the reals, is convex, non-negative, and it vanishes exclusively at $X=\mathcal I$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem F_l of arXiv:2411.11408

    {\mathbf{D}}_{{\mathbf{R}}^\pm}^\pm + {\mathfrak a} \mskip0.5mu\colon\thinspace \mathbf{E}_{{\mathbf{R}}^\pm}^\pm \to f^*\mathbf{F}^\mp

On the event $E_t(A)$, set $i=N_t(A)$ and $A'=A\cup\{i\}$.
Then $X_{t+1}[A']\sim \pi_{|A'|}$ and $X_{t+1}[A']$ is independent of $(S_{t+1},U_{t+1},S_{t+2},U_{t+2},\dots)$.

body:
Let L be a finite lattice with Moebius function mu. If a > 0, then for every b in L, sum over x with x v a = b of mu(0, x) = 0. Dually, if a < 1, then for every b, sum over x with x ^ a = b of mu(x, 1) = 0. In the Boolean lattice this is the vanishing of the alternating sum over the subsets X of B with X union A = B (A nonempty).
L a finite lattice

body:
[Lemma 30 of arXiv:2508.04938, 'Perfect t-embeddings of doubly periodic Aztec diamonds'] Let~$w_0$,~$w_{\ell N-1}$,~$b_0$ and~$b_{\ell N-1}$ be the boundary vertices of the reduced Aztec diamond, and let~$w=w_{\ell x'+i,y'}$ and~$b=b_{\ell x+i,y}$ be vertices in the interior of the reduced Aztec diamond, that is, with~$0<\ell x'+i'<\ell N-1$,~$0\leq y'\leq \ell N-2$,~$1\leq \ell x+i\leq \ell N-1$ and~$0<y<\ell N-1$. Then
\begin{align}
 &K_{\operatorname{reduced}}^{-1}(w_0,b)=\frac{1}{\gamma_1}\prod_{m=1}^\ell\left(-\frac{\alpha_1}{\gamma_1}-\beta_m\right)^{-N}\\
  &\times\frac{1}{2\pi\i}\int_{\Gamma}
  \prod_{m=1}^\ell (\gamma_mz_2+\alpha_m)^N\prod_{m=1}^{i}\frac{\gamma_m+\alpha_m z_2^{-1}}{1-\beta_m z_2^{-1}}\frac{w_2^{x-N}}{z_2^y}\frac{\d z_2}{z_2\left(z_2+\frac{\alpha_1}{\gamma_1}\right)}, \\
& K_{\operatorname{reduced}}^{-1}(w_{\ell N-1},b)=
\prod_{m=1}^\ell(\beta_\ell\gamma_m+\alpha_m)^{-N} \\
  &\times \frac{1}{2\pi\i}\int_{\Gamma} \prod_{m=1}^\ell (\gamma_mz_2+\alpha_m)^N\prod_{m=1}^{i}\frac{\gamma_m+\alpha_m z_2^{-1}}{1-\beta_m z_2^{-1}}\frac{w_2^{x-N}}{z_2^y}\frac{\d z_2}{z_2(z_2-\beta_\ell)}, \\
&  K_{\operatorname{reduced}}^{-1}(w,b_0)
  = -\prod_{m=1}^\ell (-\beta_m)^N \\
  &\times\frac{1}{2\pi\i}\int_{\Gamma}\left(\frac{\prod_{m=1}^{i'+1}(\gamma_m+\alpha_m z_1^{-1})}{\prod_{m=1}^{i'}(1-\beta_m z_1^{-1})}\right)^{-1}\prod_{m=1}^\ell(z_1-\beta_m)^{-N}\frac{z_1^{y'}}{w_1^{x'}}\frac{\d z_1}{z_1},  \\
&  K_{\operatorname{reduced}}^{-1}(w,b_{\ell N-1})
  =\frac{1}{2\pi\i}\int_{\Gamma}\left(\frac{\prod_{m=1}^{i'+1}(\gamma_m+\alpha_m z_1^{-1})}{\prod_{m=1}^{i'}(1-\beta_m z_1^{-1})}\right)^{-1}\prod_{m=1}^\ell(z_1-\beta_m)^{-N}\frac{z_1^{y'}}{w_1^{x'}}\d z_1, 
\end{align}
where~$w_1=w(z_1)$,~$w_2=w(z_2)$ and
\begin{equation}
w=w(z)=\prod_{m=1}^\ell\frac{\gamma_m+\alpha_m z^{-1}}{1-\beta_m z^{-1}},
\end{equation}
and~$\Gamma$ is a simple closed curve with~$z=0$ and~$w=\infty$ in its interior and~$z=\infty$ and~$w=0$ in its exterior. Moreover,
\begin{align*}
 &K_{\operatorname{reduced}}^{-1}(w_0,b_{\ell N-1})
 =\frac{1}{\gamma_1}\prod_{m=1}^\ell\left(-\frac{\alpha_1}{\gamma_1}-\beta_m\right)^{-N},\\
 &K_{\operatorname{reduced}}^{-1}(w_{\ell N-1},b_{\ell N-1})
 =\prod_{m=1}^\ell(\beta_\ell\gamma_m+\alpha_m)^{-N}, \\
 &K_{\operatorname{reduced}}^{-1}(w_0,b_0)
 =\frac{1}{\alpha_1}\prod_{m=1}^{\ell}(-\beta_m)^N\prod_{m=1}^\ell\left(-\frac{\alpha_1}{\gamma_1}-\beta_m\right)^{-N}, \\
 &K_{\operatorname{reduced}}^{-1}(w_{\ell N-1},b_0)
 =-\frac{1}{\beta_\ell}\prod_{m=1}^{\ell}(-\beta_m)^N\prod_{m=1}^\ell(\beta_\ell\gamma_m+\alpha_m)^{-N}.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 30 of arXiv:2508.04938

[Corollary 27 (uniform Lipschitz bound; the circle is enslaved) of arXiv:2609.03332, 'Singularity Models of Finite-Time K\"ahler-Ricci Flows'] With $C_0$ as in \eqref{eq:li-yau}:
	
	\emph{(i)} $| \nabla f_i | \leq \tfrac{1}{2} \sqrt{C_0}$ on $\widehat{M} \times [0, T)$: the fiber sizes are uniformly Lipschitz, since $| \nabla f_i |^2 = | \nabla f_i^2 |^2 / ( 4 f_i^2 )$.
	
	\emph{(ii)} By \eqref{eq:kahler-condition} and \eqref{eq:radial-gradient}, $| \nabla f_i^2 | = | q_i |\, h$, so
	
	\begin{equation}
		h \;\leq\; \frac{\sqrt{C_0}}{| q_i |}\; f_i \qquad \text{on } \widehat{M} \times [0, T) \quad \text{for every } i \,:
	\end{equation}
	
	the circle fiber is pointwise dominated by each of the collapsing fibers.
	
	\emph{(iii)} Combining \eqref{eq:li-yau} with Proposition \ref{prop:two-bolt-time}, for every $i$,
	
	\[
	\frac{q_i^2\, h^2}{f_i^4} \;=\; \frac{| \nabla f_i^2 |^2}{f_i^4} \;\leq\; \frac{C_0}{f_i^2} \;\leq\; \frac{C}{T - t} \,.
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:Idot_well_def_and_rep of arXiv:2605.15401, 'Noise Tradeoffs, Stationary Information Flow, and Structural Balance in Unit-Birth Network'] Fix $i \in \{1,\dots, N\}$.
For the unit-birth model with generator (equation eq:generator of the paper), suppose
Assumption~(ass:standing of the paper) holds. Then the series defining
$(\dot I)_{X_i}$ in (equation eq:Idot_clean_def of the paper) is absolutely convergent.

More precisely, writing
\[
(\dot I)_{X_i}
=
\sum_{n\ge0}\sum_v
\left(
\pi(n,v)f_i(v)-\pi(n+1,v)\frac{n+1}{\tau_i}
\right)
\big(h_i(n,v)-h_i(n+1,v)\big),
\]
each of the four nonnegative sums
\begin{align}

\sum_{n,v}\pi(n,v)f_i(v)\,h_i(n+1,v),
\qquad
\sum_{n,v}\pi(n,v)f_i(v)\,h_i(n,v),\\
\notag
\sum_{n,v}\pi(n+1,v)\frac{n+1}{\tau_i}\,h_i(n+1,v),
\qquad
\sum_{n,v}\pi(n+1,v)\frac{n+1}{\tau_i}\,h_i(n,v)
\end{align}
is finite. Consequently, $L_i h_i\in L^1(\pi)$ and
\begin{equation}
(\dot I)_{X_i}
=
-\mathbb{E}_\pi\big[(L_i h_i)(X)\big].
\end{equation}

        Let $\pm A$ be an element of $\psl\setminus \{\pm \mathrm I\}$,
