body: [Conjecture conjCL of arXiv:2607.06952, 'Universality for cokernels of partially random integral matrices'] Let $S_X^+$ (resp. $S_X^-$) denote the set of positive (resp. negative) fundamental discriminants $D$ with $|D| < X$. Let $p$ be an odd prime and $B$ a finite abelian $p$-group. Then \[\lim_{X \to \infty} \frac{\#\{D \in S_X^{\pm}: \Cl(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{D}))_p \simeq B\}}{|S_X^\pm|} = \frac{\prod_{k=1}^\infty (1-p^{-k-u})}{|B|^{u}|{\mathrm{Aut}}(B)|},\] where $u = 0$ if we consider $S_X^-$ and $u =1$ if we consider $S_X^+$. (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)

body:
[Theorem 21 of arXiv:2603.13798, 'Iterated Graph Systems (I): random walks and diffusion limits'] Fix $n\in\mathbb N$ and a vertex $v\in V_k(\Xi^n)$.
Fix an integer $m$ with $c_0+1\le m\le n-k-c_0$.
Assume that the radius $r>0$ satisfies
$
c_{\dist}\rho_{\min}(\mathcal D)^m
\le
r
\le
C_{\dist}\rho_{\min}(\mathcal D)^m.
$
Then there exist constants $c_{\mathrm{exit}},C_{\mathrm{exit}}>0$, depending only on the EIGS, such that
\[
c_{\mathrm{exit}}\rho(\mathbf M)^m\rho(\Psi)^m
\le
\mathbb E^v\big[\tau_{B_{\Xi^n}(v,r)^{\mathrm c}}^{\Xi^n}\big]
\le
C_{\mathrm{exit}}\rho(\mathbf M)^m\rho(\Psi)^m.
\]

body:
[Theorem thm:variable-range-eb of arXiv:2608.25551, 'Beyond Optimal Rates in Stochastic Optimization: Trajectory-Adaptive Stopping Rules'] Fix a deterministic integer $t_0 \ge 1$. Let $\{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t \ge t_0-1}$ be a filtration. Let $\{H_t\}_{t \ge t_0}$ be a real-valued integrable adapted process, and let $\{c_t\}_{t \ge t_0}$ be an almost surely finite,\footnote{No uniform upper bound on the process $\{c_t\}_{t \ge t_0}$ is assumed.} nonnegative predictable process such that
\[
    |H_t|
    \le
    c_t
    \qquad
    \text{almost surely for every } t \ge t_0.
\]
Define
\[
    \overline H_{t_0-1}
    \coloneqq
    0,
    \qquad
    \overline H_t
    \coloneqq
    \sum_{s = t_0}^t
    \left(
        H_s - \mathbb{E}[H_s \mid \mathcal{F}_{s-1}]
    \right),
\]
and
\[
    W_{t_0-1}
    \coloneqq
    0,
    \qquad
    W_t
    \coloneqq
    \sum_{s = t_0}^t H_s^2,
    \qquad
    C_t
    \coloneqq
    \max_{t_0 \le s \le t} c_s,
    \qquad
    t \ge t_0.
\]
Then, for every $\alpha \in (0,1)$,
\begin{equation}

    \mathbb{P}\left(
        \forall t \ge t_0:\
        \overline H_t
        \le
        \mathfrak B_\alpha(W_t, C_t)
    \right)
    \ge
    1-\alpha.
\end{equation}
Moreover, the map $(v, b) \mapsto \mathfrak B_\alpha(v, b)$ is nondecreasing in each argument. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Empirical Bernstein bound with a growing predictable range

body:
[Coro 20 of arXiv:2608.16144, 'Central limit theorem in R\'enyi divergence for lattice random variables'] Let $\alpha>1$ and $\beta=\alpha/(\alpha-1)$. Suppose $D_{\alpha}(S_{n_{0}}||Z_{n_0})<\infty$ for some $n_0$. Then the function $\psi(t) =\mathbb{E}e^{tX}e^{-\beta t^{2}/2}$ is integrable with power $\ell n_{0}$ for any integer $\ell\geq \alpha$, and moreover 
$$
\int_{\mathbb R}\psi(t)^{\ell n_{0}} ~\text{d}t \leq \sqrt{\frac{2\pi}{\beta \ell n_{0}}}\left[\frac{h+\sqrt{2\beta}}{Q_{n_0}}\cdot e^{D_\alpha(S_{n_0}\|Z_{n_0})}\right]^{\ell/\beta},
$$
where $Q_{n_0}=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}q_{n_0, k}$.

body:
[Lemma l.law_dalpha of arXiv:2411.14105, 'Simultaneous replica-symmetry breaking \\ for vector spin glasses'] The law of $\alpha^{-1}(U)$ is $\mathrm{d}\alpha$, where $U$ is a uniform random variable over $[0,1]$. Consequently, for every bounded measurable $h:[0,T]\to \mathbb{R}$, we have that $\int_0^1 h\circ\alpha^{-1}(s)\mathrm{d} s = \int_0^T h(t)\mathrm{d}\alpha(t)$. Moreover, $\supp \mathrm{d}\alpha = \overline{\alpha^{-1}((0,1])}$ and
\begin{align}
    \alpha^{-1}\circ\alpha(t+) = t,\quad \forall t \in \{0\}\cup \supp\mathrm{d} \alpha.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma l.law_dalpha of arXiv:2411.14105

body:
[Proposition 6 (Compatibility with separable tensor products) of arXiv:2608.30589, 'Vector-Valued Wavelet Bases as Hilbert $\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$-Module Bases: A Construc'] Let $d_1,d_2\ge 1$ and $m\ge 1$.
Let $f,r\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_1},\mathbb{R}^m)$ and $g,u\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_2},\mathbb{R}^m)$.
Define $h,k\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_1+d_2},\mathbb{R}^m)$ by
\[
h(x,y):= f(x)\odot g(y),\qquad
k(x,y):= r(x)\odot u(y),
\]
where $\odot$ denotes the componentwise product: $(a\odot b)_i:=a_i b_i$.
This compatibility will be used later in our separable construction of multivariate vector-valued wavelets.
Then

\[
\langle h,k\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}
=
\langle f,r\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}\ \odot\ \langle g,u\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})},
\]
where on the right-hand side $\odot$ denotes the Hadamard (entrywise) product of matrices:
$(A\odot B)_{ij}:=A_{ij}B_{ij}$.
title: Compatibility with separable tensor products

body:
[Definition 1 of arXiv:2512.04807, 'Existence and uniqueness of the canonical Brownian motion in non-simple conformal loop ens'] Suppose that we have the setup described just above. We say that a resistance form $(\rform{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}, \rfdomain{\Gamma})$ on $\Upsilon_\Gamma$ is a \clekp{} resistance form if the following holds. For each $V \in \metregions$, there exists a resistance form $(\rformres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}, \rfdomainres{V}{\Gamma})$ on $\ol{V} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma$  such that the following properties are satisfied.
\begin{enumerate}[I.]
\item $(\rform{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}, \rfdomain{\Gamma})$ is a local, regular resistance form, and its associated resistance metric $\rmet{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}$ is topologically equivalent to $\dpathY$.
\item Let $V_1,\ldots,V_n \in \metregions$, $n \in \N$, such that $V_i \cap V_j = \emptyset$ for $i \neq j$ and $\bigcup_i \ol{V_i} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma = \Upsilon_\Gamma$. Then
 \begin{align*}
  \rfdomain{\Gamma} &= \{ f : f|_{\ol{V_i} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma} \in \rfdomainres{V_i}{\Gamma} \text{ for each } i \} ,\\
  \text{and}\quad
  \rform{f}{f}{\Gamma} &= \sum_i \rformres{V_i}{f|_{\ol{V_i} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma}}{f|_{\ol{V_i} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma}}{\Gamma} .
 \end{align*}
 See Figure~\ref{fi:cle_rf_locality}.
\item If $V,V' \in \metregions$, $V \subseteq V'$, and $f\colon \ol{V'} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma \to \R$ is a continuous function that is constant on each $\dpathY$-connected component of $\ol{V'} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma \setminus \ol{V}$, then
\begin{align*}
 & f \in \rfdomainres{V'}{\Gamma} \text{ if and only if } f|_{\ol{V} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma} \in \rfdomainres{V}{\Gamma} \\
 \text{and}\quad & \rformres{V'}{f}{f}{\Gamma} = \rformres{V}{f}{f}{\Gamma} .
\end{align*}
\item For each open, simply connected $U \subseteq \C$, the collection $(\rformres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma})_{V \in \metregions[U]}$ is a.s.\ determined by $(\Gamma_{U^*}, \dpathY[U])$.
\item Let $U \subseteq \C$ be open, simply connected, and $z \in \C$. Then
\[ (\rformres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma_{U^*}})_{V \in \metregions[U]} = (\rformres{V+z}{T_{z}\cdot}{T_{z}\cdot}{\Gamma_{U^*}+z})_{V \in \metregions[U]} \quad\text{a.s.,} \]
where $T_{z} f = f(\cdot -z)$ denotes translation by $z$.
\item There exists a constant $\resexp > 0$ so that the following holds. Let $U \subseteq \C$ be open, simply connected, and $\lambda > 0$. Then
\[ (\rformres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma_{U^*}})_{V \in \metregions[U]} = (\lambda^{\resexp}\rformres{\lambda V}{S_{\lambda}\cdot}{S_{\lambda}\cdot}{\lambda\Gamma_{U^*}})_{V \in \metregions[U]} \quad\text{a.s.,} \]
where $S_{\lambda} f = f(\lambda^{-1}\cdot)$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2512.04807

body:
[Proposition 6 (Time-dependent family of maps $G_t$: tree contraction on small balls at large times) of arXiv:2608.14802, 'Dynamical Gibbs-non-Gibbs transitions for finite-alphabet models on trees'] Let $\lambda$ denote the spectral radius of $Df(l)$ and fix $\lambda_G\in (\lambda,1)$. For each $r>0$, set $U_r=U_r(l):=\{x\in\Delta^{q-1}:\|x-l\|_l<r\}$. Then there exists a radius $r_0=r_0(\lambda_G)>0$ such that, for every $r\in (0,r_0)$, there exists a time threshold $t_R=t_R(r,\lambda_G)\geq 0$ with the following properties: for every $t\geq t_R$ and every $k\in S$, the map $G_t^{[k]}$ is a $d$-tree contraction on $U_r$ with contraction constant $\lambda_G$, where $U_r$ is equipped with the metric induced by $\|\cdot\|_l$.
    Moreover, the set $U_r$ is invariant under each map $G_t^{[k]}$ in the sense that $G_t^{[k]}\left((U_r)^d\right)\subset U_r$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Time-dependent family of maps $G_t$: tree contraction on small balls at large times

body:
[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked, no independent read] This is the finite-moment part of Svante Janson's Conjecture 20.1 in Simply generated trees, conditioned Galton-Watson trees, random allocations and condensation, Probability Surveys 9 (2012), arXiv:1112.0510. Let pi = (pi_j)_{j>=0} be a nondegenerate offspring law on the nonnegative integers with pi_0 > 0, sum j pi_j = 1, and variance sigma^2 in (0,infinity). Let xi have law pi, let T be the ordered Galton-Watson tree in which all vertices independently have pi-distributed numbers of children, and let T_n have the law of T conditional on its total number of vertices being n, along admissible n for which that event has positive probability. For a rooted tree A define ell_k(A) as its number of vertices at graph distance k from the root. Define the Kesten tree T_hat by an infinite distinguished spine: a spine vertex has j children with probability j pi_j, one uniformly selected child continues the spine, and every other child starts an independent ordinary pi Galton-Watson tree. Fix an integer k >= 1. If r >= 1 is real and E[xi^(r+1)] < infinity, then the family {ell_k(T_n)^r}_n is uniformly integrable and E[ell_k(T_n)^r] -> E[ell_k(T_hat)^r] < infinity. Here uniform integrability means lim_{K->infinity} sup_n E[ell_k(T_n)^r; ell_k(T_n)^r > K] = 0. For 0 < r < 1 the same conclusion follows under the displayed finite-variance assumption. k is fixed and positive; conditioning sizes are admissible.

*The weight of a truncated tree.* Let $t$ be a finite plane tree whose vertices of depth less than $k$ have prescribed outdegrees and whose vertices at depth $k$ are leaves of $t$ with unspecified subtrees; call the former the interior $I(t)$, put $N = |I(t)| = 1 + \ell_1(t) + \dots + \ell_{k-1}(t)$ and $\ell = \ell_k(t)$. $$\mathbb{P}\big(T_n^{(k)} = t\big) = \ell\,\frac{n}{n - N}\,\mathbb{P}(Y_i = d_i,\ i \le N),$$
where $(Y_1, \dots, Y_n)$ is the allocation $B_{n-1,n}$, i.e. $n$ i.i.d. copies of $\xi$ conditioned on $S_n = n - 1$; so
$$\mathbb{P}\big(T_n^{(k)} = t\big) = \mathbb{P}_{\mathrm{GW}}\big(T^{(k)} = t\big)\;W_n(t), \qquad W_n(t) := \frac{n\,\ell\;\mathbb{P}(S_{n-N} = n - N - \ell)}{(n - N)\;\mathbb{P}(S_n = n - 1)}, \tag{2}$$
with $\mathbb{P}_{\mathrm{GW}}(T^{(k)} = t) = \prod_{v \in I(t)}\pi_{d(v)}$ the probability that the first $k$ generations of the unconditioned Galton–Watson tree $T$ are $t$. Two bounds follow from (1) and (2). First,
$$W_n(t) \le \frac{n\,\ell\,C (n-N)^{-1/2}}{(n-N)\,c\,n^{-1/2}} = C'\,\ell\Big(\frac{n}{n-N}\Big)^{3/2}, \qquad C' = C/c. \tag{3}$$

body:
[Theorem 3 (Main result; see \Cref{thm:main}) of arXiv:2604.06532, 'Random permutations from $q$-Demazure products'] Fix $q \in (0,1)$ and $p \in (0,1)$.
Let $\sigma_n \in S_n$ be the random permutation obtained by the $q$-Demazure product
with deletion probability $1-p$ applied to the standard reduced decomposition of~$w_0$.
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[\upshape(i)]
  \item The sequence of permutons $\mu_{\sigma_n}$ converges weakly, in probability,
  to a deterministic permuton $\mu_{p,q}$.
  \item $\mu_{p,q}$ coincides with the limiting permuton $\mu_{p'}$ from
  \cite{GrothendieckShenanigans2024} for the Demazure product ($q=0$) with adjusted parameter
  \[
    p' \;=\; \frac{p(1-q)}{1-qp}.
  \]
  \item The explicit height function of $\mu_{p,q}$ is given in \cref{eq:h_refl,eq:height_rescaling}.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

form a Morita equivalence between $A/J$ and $B/I$, with pairings induced from the original pairings.

[Theorem thm:oco-lower-dim of arXiv:2608.24731, 'Optimal Alternating Regret for Online Learning and Games\thanks{Authors are alphabetically'] For every $d\ge2$, every horizon $T\ge16$, and every possibly randomized online
algorithm $\mathcal A$, there is a sequence of continuous convex losses
$f_1,\ldots,f_T:\+X\to[0,1]$ such that
\[
  \mathbb E_{\mathcal A}\left[\operatorname{Reg}_{\mathrm{Alt}}^T\right]\ \ge\ \frac{mK}{125}
  \quad\text{where}\quad
  m:=\min\left\{\left\lfloor\frac d2\right\rfloor,\left\lfloor\frac T{16}\right\rfloor\right\},
  \quad
  K:=\left\lfloor\log_{16}\left\lfloor\frac Tm\right\rfloor\right\rfloor .
\]
In particular $\mathbb E_{\mathcal A}[\operatorname{Reg}_{\mathrm{Alt}}^T]=\Omega\!\left(d\log(1+T/d)\right)$.

Let T>=2 unit normals in R^T have common pairwise inner product c in [-1/(T-1),1]. For iid uniform projections onto their jointly realizable hyperplanes and initial error e_0, define Q=T^-1 sum_i n_i n_i^T and Phi(Y)=T^-1 sum_i (I-n_i n_i^T)Y(I-n_i n_i^T). Constants are uniform in T, c and horizon. Losses are squared residuals without factor 1/2. This is a family result, not a solution for arbitrary rank-one tasks.

body:
[Corollary 19 (Gaussian Brunn--Minkowski inequality with sine coefficients) of arXiv:2607.10769, '\fontsize{14}{17}\selectfont\bfseries Sharp Poincar\'e interpolation along Wasserstein geo'] Under the assumptions of
	Corollary~\ref{cor:barycenter-BM}, fix $t\in(0,1)$ and denote
	\[
	\omega=\sqrt{2/n}
	\left(
	W_2^2(\gamma_{K_0},\gamma_{K_1})
	-|b_{K_1}-b_{K_0}|^2
	\right)^{1/2},
	\]
	and 
	\[
	\alpha=\frac{\sin((1-t)\omega)}{\sin\omega},
	\qquad
	\beta=\frac{\sin(t\omega)}{\sin\omega},
	\]
	with $\alpha=1-t$ and $\beta=t$ when $\omega=0$. Then
	\begin{equation}
		e^{|b_t|^2/(2n)}\gamma(K_t)^{1/n}
		\geq
		\alpha e^{|b_{K_0}|^2/(2n)}\gamma(K_0)^{1/n}
		+\beta e^{|b_{K_1}|^2/(2n)}\gamma(K_1)^{1/n}.
	\end{equation} 
	Moreover, equality in \eqref{eq:distortion-BM} at some
	$t\in(0,1)$ holds if and only if
			$\bar K_0=\bar K_1$. In this case, equality holds for every
	$t\in[0,1]$.
title: Gaussian Brunn--Minkowski inequality with sine coefficients

[Theorem 1tm of arXiv:2411.16647, 'The stochastic evolution of an infinite population with logistic-type interaction'] Let the parameters of the Kolmogorov operator $L$ introduced in
  ((L of the paper)) satisfy Assumption (1ass of the paper) and $\mathcal{F}$ be as
  in ((X18 of the paper)). Then, for each $\mu_0\in \mathcal{P}_{\rm exp}$, the Fokker-Planck
  equation for $(L, \mathcal{F} , \mu_0)$ has a unique solution
  such that $\mu_t \in \mathcal{P}_{\rm exp}$ for all $t\geq0$. This
  solution has the following properties:
 \begin{itemize}
  \item[(a)] For each $\theta \in C_{\rm cs}^{+}(X)$, 
  \begin{equation}
  
\mu_t (F^\theta ) \leq \pi_{\varrho_t}  (F^\theta ) \mu_0^{q_t}
(F^\theta ), \qquad t >0,
\end{equation}
$\varrho_t$ and
$q_t$ are as in ((Y of the paper)) and $\mu_0^{q_t}$ is the
$q_t$-thinning of $\mu_0$, see Definition (Thdf of the paper).
  \item[(b)] For each compact $\Lambda\subset X$ and $n\in \mathds{N}$, there
exists $C_{n,\Lambda}>0$ such that
\begin{equation}
  
 \forall t > 0 \qquad  \mu_t (N^n_\Lambda) \leq C_{n,\Lambda},
\end{equation}
i.e., the moments of the observable ((NG of the paper)) are globally bounded
in time.
\item[(c)] The sets defined in (equation X18 of the paper) and (equation NGa of the paper) satisfy $\mathcal{F}\subset \mathcal{F}_{\rm max}$, and $\mu_t$ solves the Fokker-Planck equation (equation FPE of the paper) with each $F   \in  \mathcal{F}_{\rm max}$.
 \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:fb7b9dd12f1402292e1cc556bc918d784e6f840ed881500381c6ebcf71c1951d","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/fb/fb7b9dd12f1402292e1cc556bc918d784e6f840ed881500381c6ebcf71c1951d.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:dd45cc5a37eb2bdf6ee694037d47cb625d9da2c201909daabff05ac8adbb64c5","bundle_entry_key":"draft-clipped-score-tv-stability","bundle_id":"population.w740-t411-polynomial-lsi-hardness-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"posterior sampling and functional inequalities","draft":"w740/bundle_002.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.sampling:draft-clipped-score-tv-stability","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Gaussian-smoothed score approximation is stable in total variation after clipping

Status: proof draft, unaudited. Exact algebraic checks are pending. Input lemma for T411 Target 2.

Let P,Q be Borel probability laws on R^D with TV(P,Q)<=a. For u>0 write P_u=P*N(0,u^2 I), Q_u=Q*N(0,u^2 I), and let s_P,s_Q denote their scores. Suppose E_{P_u}||f-s_P||^2<=e^2. For L>0 let h be f clipped coordinatewise to [-L/u,L/u]. Then

E_{Q_u}||h-s_Q||^2 <=2 e^2 + [12 D exp(-L^2/2)+8 a D(L^2+1)]/u^2.

No moment or smoothness assumption on P,Q is needed. Gaussian convolution gives positive smooth densities, including when the unsmoothed prior has lattice coordinates.

## Proof

For X~P and independent N~N(0,I_D), set Y=X+uN. Differentiating the Gaussian convolution gives s_P(Y)=-E[N|Y]/u. Each fixed Gaussian-kernel derivative is bounded as a function of X, which justifies differentiation against any probability law. Conditional Jensen gives E exp(t u s_{P,j}(Y))<=E exp(-t N_j)=exp(t^2/2). The same holds for Q.

Write Pi for clipping to the box. The two-sided sub-Gaussian tail and Tonelli's theorem give

E_{P_u}||s_P-Pi s_P||^2
 <=(D/u^2) integral_0^infinity 4t exp(-(L+t)^2/2)dt
 <=4D exp(-L^2/2)/u^2=:b.

Here L>=0 and integral_0^infinity t exp(-t^2/2)dt=1. The same bound holds for Q.

Define R_P(g)=E||g(X+uN)+N/u||^2. Conditional expectation is the L2 projection, so R_P(g)=m_P+E_{P_u}||g-s_P||^2, with finite minimum m_P. The minimum restricted to box-valued fields is m_P+b_P, where b_P=E||s_P-Pi s_P||^2<=b. The analogous assertions hold for Q.

Use the common-part coupling X~P,X'~Q with Pr(X!=X')<=a, and take the same fresh N independent of the pair. For any box-valued g the two losses agree on X=X'. Otherwise their absolute difference is at most 4D L^2/u^2+4||N||^2/u^2. The mismatch event is independent of N, so

|R_P(g)-R_Q(g)|<=4aD(L^2+1)/u^2=:k.

The bound is uniform over the restricted class and hence over its two minimum risks. Thus m_P-m_Q<=k+b. Since clipping is a contraction,

E_{P_u}||h-s_P||^2<=2E||Pi f-Pi s_P||^2+2b_P<=2e^2+2b.

Consequently E_{Q_u}||h-s_Q||^2=R_Q(h)-m_Q<=2e^2+3b+2k, proving the bound. Every conditional expectation lies in L2. Independence is used before conditioning, never asserted after observing Y.

Coordinate clipping is a ReLU construction: clip(t,-M,M)=-M+ReLU(t+M)-ReLU(t-M). Polynomial L and polynomial ranges of u preserve polynomial network size and weight bounds. This does not construct exact-score oracles.

Clipping is essential: if P is a point mass at zero and Q=(1-a)P+a delta_M, the unbounded exact P_u score -y/u^2 can have Q_u error of order a M^2/u^4. A small prior TV distance alone gives no bound for that unbounded field.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:7ab9e28c856e2293467a5e36ef14790c8a81e7db0b438eb38951cbab6bdbf181","revision_digest":"sha256:4bb49c4ed56cb42686de979be69dabb934ea4d4c36e6dd11a085171ea1843c0d","source_id":"owner:T411:w740:C005-v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20-v1-unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

Own-work proof (unaudited), C004 v1, route-failure for T368 Target 2; no novelty or GD nonconvergence claim. Let p>q>=1, tau=(p-q)/(p+q), and a,b>0 satisfy a^2+b^2<=1 and a^2<tau*b^2. Take p signed samples z_i=y_i*x_i=(a,b) and q signed samples (a,-b), with arbitrary labels +/-1 and x_i=y_i*z_i. These data are separated by (1,0) with margin a. Their signed mean mu=(a,tau*b) has negative inner product with the minority samples. Put e=mu/||mu|| and kappa=(tau*b^2-a^2)/||mu||>0. For f(theta,x)=m^-1 sum_j a_j phi(w_j dot x), width m>=1, centered C1 activation phi(0)=0, c=phi'(0)>0 and beta-Lipschitz derivative beta>=0, let P be the orthogonal projection onto the per-neuron spans of (1,e), and Q=I-P. This is the positive expanding eigenspace of simultaneous both-layer logistic-GD linearization at zero for any positive step. Write U=||Ptheta||>0, V=||Qtheta||, R=||theta||. If V<=epsilon*U, epsilon>0, epsilon+epsilon^2/2<=kappa/4, and beta*R*(1+epsilon^2)<=c*kappa/4, then every minority sample has y_i*f(theta,x_i)<=-c*kappa*U^2/(8m)<0. For beta=0 the radius condition is automatic. The cone is nonempty at arbitrarily small radii. The strict data inequalities persist under perturbations when a^2+b^2<1, giving an open family. For general data with nonzero signed mean, that mean separates all samples exactly when all signed Gram row sums sum_l z_i dot z_l are positive; existence of some separator does not imply this. Thus local saddle escape or arbitrarily close expanding alignment alone cannot establish positive margins. This does not control nonlinear trajectories after escape or refute eventual Gaussian burn-in. The exact rational example p=3,q=1,a=3/10,b=4/5 has e=(3/5,4/5), kappa=23/50. The written analytic proof, not its 1722 finite rational assertions, supplies the universal proposition.
Both layers trained, centered C1 activation with positive derivative at zero and Lipschitz derivative.
Explicit separable signed-data family and small-radius cone conditions in statement.
Proof (unaudited), T368-w734-C004 version 1; no novelty claim and no nonlinear-trajectory conclusion.
title: T368 signed-mean expanding cone can misclassify separable data (unaudited)

[Definition 16 of arXiv:2608.18557, 'Randomly Permuted Orthogonal Products and Fast Dimension Reduction'] Let \( \lambda \ge1\). We say that \(\mathcal C\) is
	\emph{\(\lambda\)-secant-generating} if, for every
	\(x,y\in S_{\mathcal C}\), there exist \(s\in\mathbb N\) and
	\(h_1,\ldots,h_s\in\mathcal C\) such that
	\[
	x-y
	=
	\sum_{j=1}^s h_j
	\qquad\text{and}\qquad
	\sum_{j=1}^s\norm{h_j}_2
	\le
	 \lambda \norm{x-y}_2.
	\]
	Equivalently,
	\[
	\seca (S_{\mathcal C})
	\subseteq 
	\lambda \operatorname{co}(S_{\mathcal C}).
	\]

body: [Lemma le:variation_one_scale of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] For any $p > d_{\rm SLE}$ there exists $c>0$ such that the following is true. Then $\mathbf{P}[E^c] = o^\infty(ru)$ as $ru \searrow 0$.

Let (X, B, mu, T) be a measure-preserving system on a Lebesgue space and let P be a countable measurable partition of finite entropy. If P is a GENERATOR - that is, the smallest T-invariant sigma-algebra containing P is B modulo null sets (for invertible T one uses the two-sided join over all integers, for non-invertible T the one-sided join over nonnegative integers) - then the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy of the system equals the entropy of that one partition: h(T) = h(T, P). There is also an increasing-partitions form: if P_1 is contained in P_2 is contained in ... is an increasing sequence of finite-entropy partitions whose union generates B modulo null sets, then h(T, P_n) increases to h(T).
Finite entropy of the generating partition, and generation modulo null sets.
For an INVERTIBLE T the generator must be two-sided;
using the one-sided join for an invertible map computes a different (in general larger) quantity and is the standard slip.
The Lebesgue-space assumption is the usual standing hypothesis.

[Prop 1 (Weak existence and uniqueness in law by piecing-out) of arXiv:2604.21389, 'Existence and uniqueness for \\ singular stochastic differential equations \\ with piecewi'] Assume Hypothesis~\hypref{hyp:weak_pasting} and Hypothesis~\hypref{hyp:pasting} and let $I$ given by~\eqref{eq:state_space}. 
Then for every $x\in \text{Interior}(I)$ there exists a unique weak solution $(X,B)$ to~\eqref{eqn:SDE_general}
with $X_0=x$ and $(\nu,b,\sigma)$ defined as in~\eqref{eq:coeffs}.
Moreover, this solution is non-explosive and $I$ is its state space, i.e. 
$
    \PP\big(X_t\in I \ \forall t\ge 0\big)=1.
$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Weak existence and uniqueness in law by piecing-out

body: [Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.09700, 'A general paracontrolled ansatz for singular SPDEs'] We suppose that the noises $ \xi_\ell $, for $ \ell \in \{1,...,\ell_0\} $ belongs to $ C^{-\frac{|\mathfrak{s}|}{2} - s_\ell} $ with $ s_{\ell} \geq - \frac{|\mathfrak{s}|}{2} $ and $\s$ the scaling given in \eqref{scaling}. The noises are also centered, space invariant and that they satisfy the spectral gap Assumption \ref{assumption_spectral gap}. Then, for any mollifier $\varrho$ and the BPHZ preparation map $R^m$, the stochastic data $ (\widehat{Z}_{\tau}^m)_{\tau} $ converges in $L^q$ for any $ 1 \leq q < + \infty $. The limit is independent of the mollifier $\varrho$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem_real_proj of arXiv:2609.01250, 'Global regularity for 2D gravity water waves with two retreating point vortices'] Let f be a real-valued function. Suppose that $(I-\mathfrak{H})f=g$ or $(I-\mathfrak{H})f\bar\zeta_\alpha=g$, then
    for $0\leq k\leq s$,
    $$
        \left\lVertf\right\rVert_{H^k}\lesssim\left\lVertg\right\rVert_{H^k}.

    Furthermore, for $0\leq l\leq s-2$,
    $$
    \left\lVertf\right\rVert_{W^{l,\infty}}\lesssim\left\lVertg\right\rVert_{W^{l,\infty}}.
    $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2609.03961, 'On the exponential sum over squarefree integers'] Let $p\ne p'$ be odd primes, let $m=pp'$, and for $t\in\Z$ put
\[
  G_m(t):=\sum_{u\bmod m}\chi_{pp'}(u)\e\left(\frac{tu}m\right).
\]
Then $|G_m(t)|\le\sqrt m$ for every $t$, and $G_m(t)=0$ if $(t,m)>1$.

body:
[Theo 24 of arXiv:2602.14618, 'Finitary coding and Gaussian concentration\\ for random fields'] Let $d\ge2$ and $q\ge2$.

If $\beta<\beta_c(q)$, then the (unique) Gibbs measure
$\nu_{\beta,q}$ satisfies Gaussian concentration.

If $\beta>\beta_c(q)$, then none of the extremal
shift-invariant Gibbs measures
$\nu_{\beta,q}^1,\dots,\nu_{\beta,q}^q$
satisfies Gaussian concentration.

[Lemma lem:kaczmarz of arXiv:2412.07643, 'Ballistic Convergence in Hit-and-Run Monte Carlo and a Coordinate-free Randomized Kaczmarz'] Let $x^\ast\in\mathbb R^m$ be the solution to (equation eq:linsystem of the paper).
Starting from any initial state $x_0\in\mathbb R^m$, the iterates $(x_k)_{k\geq0}$ of the generalized randomized Kaczmarz algorithm converge to $x^\ast$ in the sense that
\begin{equation}  
\sqrt{\mathbb E|x_k-x^\ast|^2}\ \leq\ (1-\rho)^k|x_0-x^\ast| \quad \text{with rate} \quad 
    \rho\ =\ \frac12\inf_{|\zeta|=1}\mathbb E_{v\sim\tau}\Bigr(\zeta\cdot\frac{A^Tv}{|A^Tv|}\Bigr)^2\;.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:kaczmarz of arXiv:2412.07643

body:
[Corollary 4 of arXiv:2604.10310, 'Weak convergence from projections along a positive-measure set of directions'] Let \((P_n)_{n\ge1}\) and \(P\) be Borel probability measures on
		\(\mathbb R^d\), with \(d\ge2\), and let \(A\subset\mathbb S^{d-1}\) be
		a Borel set with \(\sigma(A)>0\). If \(\pi_u(P_n)\weakto\pi_u(P)\) for
		every \(u\in A\), and each projected law \(\pi_u(P)\), \(u\in A\), has
		finite moments of all orders and is moment-determinate, then
		\(P_n\weakto P\).
title: Corollary 4 of arXiv:2604.10310

[Lemma 13 of arXiv:2607.13379, 'Quantitative Propagation of Chaos and Fluctuations for Kinetic McKean--Vlasov SDEs with Si'] Let $\xi_1,\dots,\xi_m$ be $\mH$-valued random variables.
Assume that, conditionally on $\cG$, they are independent and satisfy
for some deterministic constants $a>0$ and $\Lambda\in(1,\infty)$,
\[
\E[\xi_i\mid \cG]=0,
\qquad
\E\bigl[\exp(a\norm{\xi_i}_{\mH}^{2})\mid \cG\bigr]\le \Lambda,
\qquad i=1,\dots,m.
\]
Then, for every $D>\beta:=8\log \Lambda+2$ and every $m\ge1$,
\begin{equation}
\E\left[
\exp\left(
\frac{a}{Dm}
\left\|
\sum_{i=1}^{m}\xi_i
\right\|_{\mH}^{2}
\right)
\Bigm|\cG
\right]
\le
\exp\left[
\frac{\log \Lambda}{\beta}
\log\frac{D}{D-\beta}
\right]
\qquad\text{a.s.}
\end{equation}

[Theorem 17 of arXiv:2609.03418, 'Sampling and Density Theorems for the Fractional Opdam--Cherednik Transform'] Let $S=[-\Omega,\Omega]$, $\alpha\ge\beta\ge-\frac12$, $\alpha>-\frac12$, and $0<\theta<\pi$. Suppose that
$$ \operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\mathbf{L}_{I,S}^{\theta}-(\mathbf{L}_{I,S}^{\theta})^2\bigr)=o(R), \quad I=[-R,R]. $$

If $\Lambda$ is a separated sampling set for $PW_{\alpha,\beta}^{\theta}(S)$, then
$$ \liminf_{R\to\infty}\frac{n([-R,R])}{R} \ge \frac{2^{1-2\rho}}{\pi}\Omega\csc\theta. $$

If $\Lambda$ is a separated interpolation set, then
$$ \limsup_{R\to\infty}\frac{n([-R,R])}{R} \le \frac{2^{1-2\rho}}{\pi}\Omega\csc\theta. $$

[Proposition 41 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] Assume $q\equiv c>0$ and $a\in C([-L,L])$. For compactly supported $J$, the functions $M$ and $\cH$ are analytic near the origin and $\cH(v)=\sum_{k\ge1}h_{2k}v^{2k}$,
where, writing $D_j=D_j(J)=\int_{\mathbb R}z^jJ(z)\,dz$,
\[
h_2=\frac1{2D_2},\qquad
h_4=-\frac{D_4}{24D_2^4},\qquad
h_6=\frac{D_4^2}{72D_2^7}-\frac{D_6}{720D_2^6}.
\]
For every integer $K\ge1$ and every fixed $1<m<2$,
\[
\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,m,L})
=\sum_{k=1}^{K}h_{2k}c^{2k}\sigma^{(2k-1)m-2k}
-\max a
+O\!\left(\sigma^{(2K+1)m-(2K+2)}\right)+o(1).
\]
More intrinsically, define $N(m)=\max\{k\ge1:(2k-1)m-2k\le0\}$.
Then the expansion through every nonvanishing order is
\[
\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,m,L})
=\sum_{k=1}^{N(m)}h_{2k}c^{2k}\sigma^{(2k-1)m-2k}
-\max a+o(1).
\]
The $k$th correction becomes order one at $m=2k/(2k-1)$; the successive thresholds are $4/3,6/5,8/7,\ldots$.

Let gamma be the standard Gaussian measure on R^n. For every locally Lipschitz f with f and grad f in L^2(gamma), Ent_gamma(f^2) <= 2 E_gamma[ |grad f|^2 ], where Ent(g) = E[g log g] - E[g] log E[g] for g >= 0. The constant 2 is sharp, with near-equality for exponentials f = e^{a . x / 2}. As with the Poincare inequality the constant is DIMENSION-FREE, obtained from the one-dimensional case by tensorization of entropy. Gross's theorem states that this inequality is EQUIVALENT to Nelson's hypercontractivity for the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroup, and it implies the Gaussian Poincare inequality by linearisation. Combined with the Herbst argument it yields Gaussian concentration for Lipschitz functions with the sharp sub-Gaussian variance proxy equal to the square of the Lipschitz constant. Care with normalisation: the inequality is often written as Ent(f) <= 2 E[ |grad sqrt(f)|^2 ] for f >= 0, which is the same statement after substituting f -> f^2, and some sources carry a factor 1/2 from using a different generator normalisation; the version stated here is the one matching the standard Gaussian and the generator L = Laplacian minus x . gradient. [Gross (1975); see Bakry, Gentil and Ledoux, Analysis and Geometry of Markov Diffusion Operators, Chapter 5]
gamma the standard Gaussian measure on R^n
f locally Lipschitz with f and grad f in L^2(gamma)
the generator normalisation L = Laplacian minus x . gradient, which fixes the constant 2

Theorem 3.18: let W be a mean zero, variance one random variable and let W^z be defined on the same space as W and have the zero-bias distribution with respect to W; if Z ~ N(0,1), then d_W(W, Z) ≤ 2E|W^z − W|.

[Lemma 35 ({\bf Obus--Pries}) of arXiv:2609.03191, 'On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes '] Suppose that $\underline{z}=(z_0,\ldots,z_{s-1})\in W_s(k((x)))$ is in standard form in the sense of \cite{OP}, Sect.\ 3.2, i.e.,
each non-zero $z_i$ is a polynomial in $x^{-1}$ whose monomial exponents are not
divisible by $p$. For $i\in\llbracket1,s\rrbracket$, let $d_i$ be the pole order of $z_{i-1}$ at $x=0$, with
$d_i:=-\infty$ if $z_{i-1}=0$. If $\wp(\underline{y})=\underline{z}$ defines a cyclic extension of $k((x))$ of degree
$p^s$, then its $i$-th upper jump is
\[
u_i:=\max(p^{i-j}d_j\mid j\in\llbracket1,i\rrbracket).
\]
In particular, $u_1=d_1$ and $u_i=\max(p u_{i-1},d_i)$ for $i\in\llbracket2,s\rrbracket$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: {\bf Obus--Pries}

body: [Defi 23 of arXiv:2608.28148, 'Flows and homotopies of Banach Lie algebroids'] A mapping $f \colon U \times V \rightarrow F$ on a cartesian product of locally convex subsets of Banach spaces with dense interior is called $C^{r,s}$-map (with $r,s \in \N_0\cup\{\infty\})$ if it is continuous and for each fixed $y \in V$ the map $f(\cdot , y)$ is Bastiani $C^r$ and each of its iterated directional derivatives is Bastiani $C^s$ with respect to the parameter $y \in V$.

body:
[Theorem a10 of arXiv:2411.19926, 'Sparse Pseudospectral Shattering'] Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C$ be a set such that
\[\inf_{\deg(p)\le k}\sup_{z\in\Omega}\mleft|1-zp(z)\mright|\le C\alpha^k.\]
Let $\varepsilon, \delta \in (0,1)$ and let
$M$ be a matrix such that $\left\|M\right\|\le\poly(n)$ and
$\Lambda_\delta(M)\subset\Omega$. \textnormal{\texttt{shatteredGMRES}} is an algorithm which, in \[k=O\pare{\dfrac{\log(n/\delta)\log(n)+\log(1/\varepsilon)}{\log(1/\alpha)}}\] iterations, outputs $x$ such that
\[(M+\Delta_M)x=(b+\delta_b), \quad \left\|\Delta_M\right\|\le\delta,\quad\left\|\delta_b\right\|\le\varepsilon\]
and uses
\(O\mleft( k\nnz(M)+kn\log^6(n)+k^2n \mright)\)
arithmetic operations.
title: Theorem a10 of arXiv:2411.19926

[Theorem thm:local_analyticity of arXiv:2604.18558, 'Uniform analyticity of local observables in FK-percolation and analyticity of the Ising sp'] Assume that $(d,p,q) \in \mathcal G_{\mathsf{FK}}$. Then, there exists $\delta > 0$ such that:

\begin{enumerate}
\item For any \emph{local} function $F$, for any $z \in \mathbb C$ satisfying $|z|<\delta$, the following limit exists:
\[
\phi_{p + z, q}[F(\omega)] \coloneqq \lim_{N\rightarrow \infty} \phi_{\mathbb T_N, p + z, q}[F(\omega)] \in \mathbb C.
\]
Furthermore, the function 
\[ z \in \mathbb D_\delta(0) \mapsto \phi_{p + z, q}[F(\omega)]\in \mathbb C \]
 is complex analytic.
\item 

There exists a sequence $c_\epsilon$, going to 0 when $\epsilon$ goes to 0, such that for any $|z| < \epsilon < \delta$ and any non-negative \emph{local} function $F$ which is not identically 0, 
\begin{equation}\tag{$\star$}
\left| \frac{\phi_{p + z, q}[F(\omega)]}{\phi_{p, q}[F(\omega)]} \right| \leq 2\exp(c_\epsilon |\mathsf{Supp}_F|),
\end{equation}
where $\mathsf{Supp}_F$ is the support of $F$.

 \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2607.09246, 'Scaling limit of 1+1 dimensional directed polymer with power-law tail and spatial correlat'] Assume that conditions \textbf{(A)} and \textbf{(B)} hold. Let the tail exponent satisfy $\alpha > \frac{6}{3-2r}$. For a sequence of inverse temperatures $\beta_N$,  the log-partition function $\ln Z_N(\beta_N; \omega)$ exhibits the following two limit behaviors:

\noindent
\textbf{(a)} 
If $\beta_N N^{H/2} \to \beta \in (0, \infty)$ as $N \to \infty$, then the log-partition function centered by its multi-order polynomial drift converges in distribution to the logarithm of the continuous Wiener chaos:
$$
    \ln Z_N(\beta_N; \omega) - N \sum_{j=2}^{\lfloor 2/H \rfloor} \frac{\beta_N^j}{j!} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}}[\bar{\xi}^j] \sum_{y=-\infty}^{\infty} \psi_y^j \stackrel{D}{\Longrightarrow} \ln Z_{\sqrt{2}\beta}(1, \cdot),
$$
where $Z_{\sqrt{2}\beta}(t, \cdot)$ is the unique solution to the following stochastic heat equation (SHE)
$$
    \partial_t u = \frac{1}{2} \Delta u + \sqrt{2}\beta u \dot{W}, \quad u(0,x) = \delta_0(x),
$$
driven by a centered Gaussian space-time noise $\dot{W}$ with covariance structure
$$
    \mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}}[\dot{W}(t,x) \dot{W}(s,y)] = H(2H-1)\delta(t-s) |x-y|^{2H-2}.
$$

\noindent
\textbf{(b)} 
Let $\beta_N N^{H/2} \to 0$ as $N \to \infty$, and there exists a constant $a$ with $0 < a < A_{*}(\alpha, H)$, which is defined in \eqref{A_alpha_H}, such that 
\[
\beta_N N^{H/2} \gg N^{-a}.
\]
Then the normalized fluctuation converges to a Gaussian distribution:
$$
    \frac{1}{\beta_N N^{H/2}} \left( \ln Z_N(\beta_N; \omega) - N \sum_{j=2}^{p'} \frac{\beta_N^j}{j!} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}}[\bar{\xi}^j] \sum_{y=-\infty}^{\infty} \psi_y^j \right) \stackrel{D}{\longrightarrow} \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_H^2),
$$
where $p'=\left\lfloor\frac2H\right\rfloor$. \(\text{More generally, \(p'\) can be replaced by any integer }
p\le \lfloor2/H\rfloor
\text{ such that }
\frac{N\beta_N^{p+1}}{\beta_NN^{H/2}}\to0.\) The variance is given by
$$
    \sigma_H^2 = 2H(2H-1) \int_0^1 \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} \rho(t,x)\rho(t,y)|x-y|^{2H-2} \,dx \,dy \,dt,
$$
with $\rho(t,x)$ being the standard heat kernel. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2607.09246

body: [Definition 2 (Limit cycle and basin of attraction) of arXiv:2605.24611, 'Beyond Fixed Points: Superpolynomial Capacity of Asymmetric Hopfield Networks'] A limit cycle of period P ≥1 is a set of distinct states C = {x(0), x(1), . . . , x(P −1)} such that, for the synchronous update map F : {−1, 1}n → {−1, 1}n, we have F(x(i)) = x(i+1) for i = 0, . . . , P −2 and F(x(P −1)) = x(0). The special case P = 1 is a fixed point. The basin of attraction of C is B(C) = {y ∈{−1, +1}n : ∃T ≥ 0 such that F T (y) ∈C}. Clearly, C ⊆B(C); we call C a limit-cycle attractor if C ⊊B(C).

body: In graph theory, the Robertson–Seymour theorem (also called the graph minors theorem) states that the undirected graphs, partially ordered by the graph minor relationship, form a well-quasi-ordering. Equivalently, every family of graphs that is closed under taking minors can be defined by a finite set of forbidden minors, in the same way that Wagner's theorem characterizes the planar graphs as being the graphs that do not have the complete graph $K_{5}$ or the complete bipartite graph $K_{3,3}$ as minors.

Let (T(t))_{t ≥ 0} be a C_0-semigroup on a Banach space X with generator A, and let M ≥ 1, ω ∈ ℝ satisfy ‖T(t)‖ ≤ M e^{ωt}. Then: (a) A is densely defined and closed, and A determines T uniquely (two C_0-semigroups with the same generator are equal). (b) For x ∈ D(A) and t ≥ 0, T(t)x ∈ D(A) and d/dt T(t)x = A T(t)x = T(t) A x, the derivative being two-sided for t > 0. (c) For every x ∈ X, ∫_0^t T(s)x ds ∈ D(A) and A ∫_0^t T(s)x ds = T(t)x − x; for x ∈ D(A), T(t)x − x = ∫_0^t T(s)Ax ds. (d) Every λ ∈ ℂ with Re λ > ω belongs to the resolvent set ρ(A), and R(λ, A)x = (λ − A)^{-1}x = ∫_0^∞ e^{-λt}T(t)x dt (an absolutely convergent improper Riemann integral), with ‖R(λ, A)^n‖ ≤ M/(Re λ − ω)^n for all n ≥ 1. (e) The abstract Cauchy problem u'(t) = Au(t), u(0) = x has, for x ∈ D(A), the unique classical solution u(t) = T(t)x. (f) A subspace D ⊂ D(A) which is dense in X and invariant under every T(t) is a core for A.

\]

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Examine whether the moment condition controls the back-and-forth trap time and hence the regeneration-time tail. Result: The quantity 1/(1 - omega(0,e) omega(e,-e)) is the expected number of visits to 0, the first included, during the two-site back-and-forth excursion between 0 and e (a round trip steps from 0 to e and back from e to 0, with probability omega(0,e) omega(e,-e)), so the moment condition bounds the expected holding time in two-site traps but not in larger traps (a trap of k sites in a line has holding time controlled by products of k such ratios, whose expectation is not bounded by the first-moment condition). Proposition 2.21 of the source shows the condition is necessary; sufficiency would need a bound on the expected time spent in traps of every size, i.e. on E[tau_1 | D = infinity]. A natural sufficient strengthening is a moment condition on the exit time from every finite box, which is implied by the two-site condition only under an additional assumption on the transition probabilities to move away. I therefore see the question as open in the sense that the two-site condition is strictly weaker than what the regeneration argument needs, and the Dirichlet case works because of the specific reversal identity of Dirichlet environments (Sabot's exit-time integrability). No new result. Obstruction: Two-site moment condition does not control larger traps; the Dirichlet argument uses a special reversal identity.

[Theorem thm:vectorfield of arXiv:2411.06827, 'The Exponential Lie Series and a Chen--Strichartz Formula for L{\'e}vy Processes'] For any letter $i^{(m)}\in {\mathbb A}$, $m\ge 1$, the renormalised differential operator 
$$
	V_{i^{(m)}}:=\bar{\mu}((\overline i^{(m)})^0)
$$ 
is a vector field. More precisely, $V_{i^{(m)}}$ is given by the $m$-th component of the pre-Lie Magnus expansion of the vector field $V_{i^{(1)}}=V_i \cdot \partial$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: The Galton–Watson process, also called the Bienaymé-Galton–Watson process or the Galton-Watson branching process, is a branching stochastic process arising from Francis Galton's statistical investigation of the extinction of family names. The process models family names as patrilineal, while offspring are randomly either male or female, and names become extinct if the family name line dies out.
title: Galton–Watson process

[Proposition 39 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Fix \(t<0\).  There are adapted centres \(p_i\), converging in a fixed
regular chart, such that
\[
 \int_Xd_{g_{i,t}}(p_i,y)^2\,d\nu_t^i(y)\le C_t(-t).
\]
Put \(b_i=\pi(p_i)\), and let \(w=(w^1,\ldots,w^m)\) be holomorphic
coordinates near \(q\).  After passing to a subsequence, the maps
\[
 W_i\circ\pi,\qquad
 W_i(y)=(1-t_i)^{-1/2}\bigl(w(y)-w(b_i)\bigr),
\]
converge smoothly on compact subsets of \(\mathcal R_t\) to a
holomorphic map
\[
 \Pi_t:\mathcal R_t\longrightarrow\C^m.
\]
Thus \(\Pi_t\) is the pointed limit of
\[
 \pi:(X,g_{i,t},p_i)\longrightarrow
 \bigl(Y,(1-t_i)^{-1}g_Y,b_i\bigr).
\]

[Lemma lem:countable-KL of arXiv:2609.00399, 'Shannon's problem on the monotonicity of entropy and a Conjecture of Tao'] For $s,t\in[0,1]$, define
\[
 \Phi_{\rm rel}(s,t)=
 \begin{cases}
 s\log(s/t)-s+t,&s>0,\ t>0,\\
 t,&s=0,\\
 +\infty,&s>0,\ t=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
If $p,q$ are probability mass functions on a countable set $E$, then
\begin{equation}
 D(p\|q)=\sum_{x\in E}\Phi_{\rm rel}(p(x),q(x)).
\end{equation}
Consequently, if $\{p_c:c\in C\}$ and $\{q_c:c\in C\}$ are probability
kernels on $E$, where $C$ is a measurable space and every coordinate map
$c\mapsto p_c(x),q_c(x)$ is measurable, then
$c\mapsto D(p_c\|q_c)$ is measurable as an extended-real-valued function.

[Theorem 5 (Sparse Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graphs: averaged version) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Fix \(\lambda>0\), \(u\in[0,1]\), and \(\theta>0\), and let \(G_n\sim G(n,\lambda/n)\). Assume
\begin{equation}
\lambda>2c_{\theta,u}
=
2\bigl(1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}\bigr).

\end{equation}
Then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
\[
\Pbb\!\left(
\frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
\right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Consider the Gaussian network and empirical FIM F_M specified in assumptions,with fixed depth L,sample count T>=1 and output dimension C>=1. Write g_(k,t)=grad_theta f_k(x_t),P=dim(theta),and F_M=(1/T)*sum_(k,t) g_(k,t)g_(k,t)^T. Let alpha>0 satisfy P/M^2->alpha,and assume explicitly that <g_(k,s),g_(kprime,t)>/M->delta_(k,kprime)*alpha*K_st,where K has diagonal kappa1 and off-diagonal kappa2,with kappa1>=kappa2>=0. All these finitely many limits hold jointly almost surely,or jointly in probability. Then Tr(F_M^2)/P -> C*alpha*((T-1)*kappa2^2/T+kappa1^2/T),in the same convergence mode. In the source closure,kappa1=(1/alpha)*sum_(l=1)^L alpha_(l-1)*qtilde_l*qhat_(l-1),and kappa2=(1/alpha)*sum_(l=1)^L alpha_(l-1)*qtilde_pair_l*qhat_pair_(l-1). Here qhat is the width-normalized inner product of forward activations and qtilde the unnormalized inner product of backward signals,with diagonal or distinct-sample limits respectively. The backward-weight decoupling is Assumption1 of the source;the explicit gradient Gram convergence is an additional hypothesis here. This is a conditional formulation of the leading second-moment formula,not a proof of those convergence premises for tied-weight backpropagation or a proportional-T regime. Draft,independent review pending.
Fixed L>=2 and fixed positive integers C,T. Widths M_l/M->alpha_l>0 for l=0,...,L-1; M_L=C. Hidden layers h_l=phi(u_l), u_l=W_l*h_(l-1)+b_l; output f=u_L is linear.
Independent Gaussian initialization W_l[i,j]~N(0,sigma_w^2/M_(l-1)) and b_l[i]~N(0,sigma_b^2), sigma_w>0 and sigma_b>0. Inputs are iid standard Gaussian. Parameters theta include all weights and biases.
phi and phi_prime have finite squared Gaussian integrals at each recursively occurring preactivation variance. The empirical FIM normalization is F=(1/T)*sum_(t=1)^T sum_(k=1)^C grad_theta f_k(x_t)*grad_theta f_k(x_t)^T.
C,T,L are fixed as M tends to infinity. P is the total number of weights and biases,alpha=sum_(l=1)^(L-1) alpha_l*alpha_(l-1),and P/M^2->alpha>0.
Explicit additional hypothesis: for every fixed k,kprime in1..C and s,t in1..T,the inner product of parameter gradients divided by M converges to delta_(k,kprime)*alpha*(kappa1 if s=t else kappa2). Convergence is either almost surely throughout,or in probability throughout.
The finite constants satisfy kappa1>=kappa2>=0. Forward and backward same-sample and distinct-sample order parameters entering the source formulas have finite deterministic limits common to each sample or sample pair. These convergence and output-decoupling statements are premises,not consequences proved here from Assumption1.

[Lemma 32 of arXiv:2605.27222, '2605.27222'] For every $q\ge0$, the operator
\[
f\mapsto (\eta-\chi)G_f
\]
sends $L^2(I)$ continuously into $H^q(\mathbb R)$. Moreover, for every
$q\ge0$ there exists $C_q>0$ such that
\begin{equation}
\|(\eta-\chi)G_{e_k}\|_{H^q(\mathbb R)}
\le C_q(1+\mu_k)^{-1/2},
\qquad k\ge1.
\end{equation}

[Lemma 10 (Mixtures of discrete uniform laws) of arXiv:2608.10992, '2608.10992'] Let \((p_k)_{k\geq1}\) be a non-increasing probability mass function and
set \(a_n:=n(p_n-p_{n+1})\). Then \((a_n)_{n\geq1}\) is a probability mass
function and
\begin{equation}

        p_k=\sum_{n\geq k}\frac{a_n}{n}.
\end{equation}
Equivalently, if \(\mathbb{P}(N=n)=a_n\), then a random variable which,
conditionally on \(N=n\), is uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), has law
\((p_k)\).

[Theorem theorem1.111 of arXiv:2412.06246, 'The smallest singular value for rectangular random matrices with Lévy entries'] [[MR1235416]] 
    Let $X=(x_{ij})\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times n}$ with independent, identically distributed (i.i.d.) entries $x_{ij}$ satisfying $\mathbb{E}[x_{ij}]=0$, $\mathbb{E}[|x_{ij}|^2]=1$, $\mathbb{E}[|x_{ij}|^4]<\infty$. Assume that the aspect ratio satisfies $N/n\to \mathbf{a}$ as $n\to\infty$ for some $\mathbf{a}>1$. Then almost surely 
    $$n^{-1/2} \sigma_{min}(X)\to \sqrt{\mathbf{a}}-1,\quad\text{ as } n\to\infty,
    $$ where $\sigma_{min}(X)$ denotes the smallest singular value of $X$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let R > 0, let f be holomorphic on an open set containing the closed disk |z| ≤ R, with f(0) ≠ 0 and f having no zeros on the circle |z| = R. Let a_1, ..., a_N be the zeros of f in the open disk |z| < R, listed with multiplicity. Then log|f(0)| = Σ_{k=1}^{N} log(|a_k|/R) + (1/2π) ∫_0^{2π} log|f(R e^{iθ})| dθ. Equivalently, (1/2π)∫_0^{2π} log|f(Re^{iθ})| dθ - log|f(0)| = Σ_k log(R/|a_k|) = ∫_0^R n(t) dt/t, where n(t) is the number of zeros of f in |z| ≤ t counted with multiplicity. The formula remains valid if f has zeros on the circle |z| = R, the boundary integral still converging absolutely; if f(0) = 0 of order m one applies the formula to f(z)/z^m and adds m log R. The immediate consequence used constantly: for an entire function of finite order ρ the zero counting function satisfies n(r) = O(r^{ρ+ε}).
f is holomorphic on a neighborhood of the closed disk |z| ≤ R
f(0) ≠ 0 (otherwise divide by z^m)
zeros in the open disk are listed with multiplicity
no zeros on |z| = R in the stated form (the formula extends to that case)

body: In the mathematical field of set theory, a large cardinal property is a certain kind of property of transfinite cardinal numbers. Cardinals with such properties are, as the name suggests, generally very large, such that the cardinal is inaccesible through standard set theory functions, power sets or successors of smaller cardinals.. The proposition that such cardinals exist cannot be proved in the most common axiomatization of set theory, namely ZFC, and such propositions can be viewed as ways of measuring how "much", beyond ZFC, one needs to assume to be able to prove certain desired results. In other words, they can be seen, in Dana Scott's phrase, as quantifying the fact "that if you want more you have to assume more".

[Definition 4 of arXiv:2608.10876, 'Exponential Contraction for Underdamped Langevin Diffusions with Superlinear Forces'] Let \((x,v)\in E\) and \((x',v')\in E\). A probability measure \(\mathbf{Q}\in\mathcal{P}(\Xi_1\times\Xi_1)\)
is called a weak coupling of two solutions to
\eqref{eq4.1} starting from \((x, v)\) and \((x', v')\), respectively, if \(\mathbf{Q}(\pi_1^{-1}(A))=\mathbf{P}^{(x, v)}(A)\) and \(\mathbf{Q}(\pi_2^{-1}(A))=\mathbf{P}^{(x', v')}(A)\), \(A\in\mathcal B(\Xi_1)\),
where \(\pi_1(\omega,\omega'):=\omega\) and \(\pi_2(\omega,\omega'):=\omega'\)
are the two coordinate projections. On the canonical probability space \((\Xi_1\times\Xi_1,
\mathcal{B}(\Xi_1)\otimes\mathcal{B}(\Xi_1),
\mathbf{Q})\), define the two canonical coordinate processes by
\[(X_t,V_t)(\omega,\omega'):=\omega(t),\qquad (X'_t,V'_t)(\omega,\omega'):=\omega'(t),\qquad t\geq 0.\]
The marginal conditions imply that \(\operatorname{Law}_{\mathbf{Q}}\bigl((X_t,V_t)_{t\geq 0}\bigr)=\mathbf{P}^{(x, v)}\)
and \(\operatorname{Law}_{\mathbf{Q}}\bigl((X'_t,V'_t)_{t\geq 0}\bigr)=\mathbf{P}^{(x', v')}\).
In particular, \((X_0,V_0)=(x, v)\), \((X'_0,V'_0)=(x', v')\), \(\mathbf{Q}\text{-a.s.}\),
and each coordinate process, when considered with respect to its own natural filtration, is a weak solution to \eqref{eq4.1} with the corresponding initial condition.
title: Definition 4 of arXiv:2608.10876

\[
  H_m(z)=
  \sum_{\substack{w\text{ is a self-avoiding walk in }F_m\\w(0)=O}}
  z^{L(w)}.
\]
The number of \(n\)-step self-avoiding walks in \(F_m\) starting at
\(O\) is \([z^n]H_m(z)\).  Let \(P_m(z)\) be the sum of \(z^{L(w)}\)
over all self-avoiding paths joining a fixed pair of
diagonally opposite boundary vertices, and define
\(Q_m(z)\) in the same way for a fixed adjacent pair.  Dihedral symmetry
makes these polynomials independent of the
chosen pair.  They satisfy
\begin{equation}
  \begin{aligned}
  P_{m+1}&=P_m^3,\\
  Q_{m+1}&=P_m^2Q_m,\\
  H_{m+1}&=H_m+P_m(1+2Q_m+P_m)(H_m-1),
  \end{aligned}
  
\end{equation}
with
\[
  H_0=1+2z+2z^2+2z^3,\qquad
  P_0=2z^2,\qquad Q_0=z+z^3.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 22 of arXiv:2609.02850, 'Canonical-row Chern flow on Bott--Samelson towers:\\ realizable-volume models for Schubert'] For a word $\mathbf i=(i_1,\ldots,i_\ell)$ and
$j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, declare
\[
 (j,s)\sim(j,t)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 i_q\ne j\text{ for every }
 \min\{s,t\}<q\le\max\{s,t\}.
\]
Write $\sigma_j(t)=[j,t]$ for the equivalence class.  Its unique
creation-time representative is
\[
 \bigl(j,\tau_j(t)\bigr),\qquad
 \tau_j(t)=\max\bigl(\{0\}\cup\{q\le t:i_q=j\}\bigr).
\]
On the quotient-flag tower constructed in \cref{sec:canonical}, if
$s\le t$ and $(j,s)\sim(j,t)$, then
$F_j^{(t)}$ is canonically the pullback of $F_j^{(s)}$.  Hence the pullback
to the final tower of the bundle represented by $\sigma_j(t)$ is
independent of the representative.

[Defn of arXiv:2411.10633, 'A Geometric Perspective on the Injective Norm of Sums of Random Tensors'] Given symmetric tensors $T_1, \ldots, T_n \in (\mathbb R^d)^{\otimes r}$, we define the \emph{natural distance} $\mathbf{d}$ on $\mathbb R^d$ as follows:

[Corollary cor:modal-cubes-fifteen of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] For $L \in \set{ \textbf{C}, \textbf{W}, \textbf{I} }$, there are exactly 15 different logics in the form $L\textbf{K}X$, where $X \subseteq \set{ \textsf{D}, \textsf{T}, \textsf{B}, \textsf{4}, \textsf{5} }$.
  \begin{proof}
    It is well known that there are exactly 15 different classical modal logics in the form $\textbf{K}X$ (cf.~[CZ97]).
    So, by $\textbf{CK} \subseteq \textbf{K}$, there are at least 15 different logics in the form $\textbf{CK}X$.
    On the other hand, by Proposition (prop:ck-cube of the paper), there are at most 15 such logics.
    The rest follows from $\textbf{CK} \subseteq \textbf{WK} \subseteq \textbf{IK} \subseteq \textbf{K}$.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Definition d:A-order of arXiv:2609.03731, 'Weightings and Lie groupoids'] Let $A_\bullet$ be a filtration of $A$. If $X \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{A}}_k$ then we say that $X$ (or $X^L$ or $X^R$) has $A_\bullet$-\emph{order at most} $k$. For a monomial $P=X_1\cdots X_l$ in the universal enveloping algebra, we say that $P$ (or $P^L$ or $P^R$) has $A_\bullet$-\emph{order at most} $k$ if $X_1\in \ensuremath{\mathcal{A}}_{k_1},...,X_l\in \ensuremath{\mathcal{A}}_{k_l}$ and $k_1+\cdots+k_l\le k$. The definition is extended to arbitrary elements of $\ensuremath{\mathcal{U}}\ensuremath{\mathcal{A}}$ by declaring that the $A_\bullet$-order of a sum of monomials is at most the maximum of upper bounds for the $A_\bullet$-orders of the summands.

[Proposition prop:parametric-lower of arXiv:2605.11108, 'Empirical Convergence of Even-Order Gromov--Wasserstein Functionals'] Fix \(r,k\ge 1\), \(d_x,d_y\ge 1\), and \(R>0\). There exists a constant \(c>0\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\sup_{\substack{
\operatorname{diam}(\operatorname{supp}\mu)\le R\\
\operatorname{diam}(\operatorname{supp}\nu)\le R
}}
\mathbb E\left|
\mathcal D_{r,k}(\widehat\mu_n,\widehat\nu_n)
-
\mathcal D_{r,k}(\mu,\nu)
\right|
\ge
cR^{4kr}n^{-1/2}.
\]
Consequently, when \(d_x\wedge d_y<4\), the rate in Theorem~(thm:main of the paper) is sharp.

body: [Definition 3 (Colored top-$m$-to-random) of arXiv:2606.29530, 'Cutoff profiles for colored top-\texorpdfstring{$m$}{m}-to-random shuffles with growing bl'] For $1\le m\le n$, one step of $p$-colored top-$m$-to-random is the following shuffle. Remove the top $m$ cards, recolor those $m$ cards by independent uniform elements of $C_p$, apply a uniform random permutation to the removed block, choose an $m$-element set of final positions uniformly among all $\binom nm$ possibilities, and insert the removed cards into those positions. The remaining $n-m$ cards preserve their relative order and color.  Let $Q_{n,p}^{(m)}$ denote the one-step law on $G_{n,p}$.

body:
[Proposition prop:three-causes of arXiv:2607.04620, 'The Exact Ville Identity\\ \large From the Absorbing Case to the General Law\\ with an App'] For a nonnegative supermartingale $(M_n)$ with $M_0=1$ crossing the level $b>1$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item The martingale-versus-supermartingale gap governs $D_b$. If $(M_n)$ is a martingale then $\delta_n\equiv0$ and $D_b=0$; the loss term is nonzero precisely to the extent that the process is a strict supermartingale, that is, sheds predictable mass before crossing.
\item Bounded overshoot governs $O_b$. If the conditional landing value satisfies $\mathbb{E}[M_{T_b}\mid \mathcal{F}_{T_b-1},T_b=n]\le b+\omega$ a.s. for a constant $\omega$, then $O_b\le\omega$ ((sec:overshoot of the paper)); on a lattice that includes $b$, $O_b=0$. The overshoot is nonzero precisely to the extent that the increments can carry the process strictly past the boundary.
\item Wobbling governs $R_b$. If, in the martingale case, conditions (i)--(ii) of (thm:wobbling of the paper) hold (sufficient wobbling and bounded overshoot), then $\mathbb{P}(T_b<\infty)=1$, so the survival event is null and $R_b=0$. The residual is nonzero precisely to the extent that wobbling fails -- that is, to the extent that paths can settle and survive forever without crossing.
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma lem:Laplace.derivative.Wishart of arXiv:2606.04859, 'Stein's method for the Wishart distribution'] Let $\alpha > 3d-3$ be given, and let $\mathrm{adj}(\cdot)$ denote the adjugate matrix operator. \[
\left(\prod_{\ell=1}^k \nabla_{\Theta, i_{\ell} j_{\ell}}\right) f_{\alpha, I_d, \Theta}^{\mathcal{W}}(X)

\]
where $\nabla_{\Theta}$ acts on the noncentrality parameter $\Theta$ and $\nabla_{\!X}$ acts on the state variable $X$.

[Lemma of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] \label[lemma]{lem:Rd_projection_works}
Let $Y = (Y_1, \dots, Y_d)$ be an independent symmetrizer for $X = (X_1, \dots, X_d)$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$. 
Then, for any nonempty $E \subseteq [d]$, $Y[E]$ is an independent symmetrizer for $X[E]$. 
In particular, for all $i \in [d]$, $Y_i$ is an independent symmetrizer for $X_i$. 
\begin{proof}
Fix $E = \{ i_1, \dots, i_k \} \subsetneq [d]$. 

Clearly, for any $z \in \mathbb{R}^d$
\begin{align*}
f_{X + Y}(z)
&= f_{(X + Y)[E]}(z[E]) f_{(X + Y)[E^c] \mid (X + Y)[E]}(z[E^c] \mid z[E]) .
\intertext{Since $Y$ is an independent symmetrizer of $X$, we have 
$f_{X + Y}(z) = f_{X + Y}(-z)$ and}
f_{(X + Y)[E]}(z[E]) &f_{(X + Y)[E^c] \mid (X + Y)[E]}(u \mid z[E]) \\
&= f_{(X + Y)[E]}(-z[E]) f_{(X + Y)[E^c] \mid (X + Y)[E]}(u \mid -z[E]) .
\intertext{where we have written $u = z[E^c]$. 
Now, write $S = \supp((X + Y)[E^c])$ and sum over $u \in S$:}

 f_{(X + Y)[E]}(z[E]) &\sum_{u \in S} f_{(X + Y)[E^c] \mid (X + Y)[E]}(u \mid z[E]) \\
&= f_{(X + Y)[E]}(-z[E]) \sum_{u \in S} f_{(X + Y)[E^c] \mid (X + Y)[E]}(u \mid -z[E]) .
\end{align*}

Thus
$ f_{(X + Y)[E]}(z[E]) = f_{(X + Y)[E]}(-z[E]) . $
Independence of $X[E]$ and $Y[E]$ is inherited from independence of $X$ and $Y$. 

\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Integrator-authored exact special-case argument and failure analysis after checking the incoming source Result: Let f(theta)=g(k*theta). Its Fourier coefficients vanish at lags not divisible by k, so the determinantal kernel is block diagonal on the k residue classes. Determinant factorization proves that these restrictions are independent copies of P_g. If P_g can be represented as F(U_j,...,U_(j+r)) with iid U, define Y_i=F(U_i,U_(i+k),...,U_(i+r*k)). This is a shift-equivariant function of the window U_i,...,U_(i+r*k), so is an (r*k+1)-block factor. The residue-class families use disjoint iid coordinates and have the correct laws. In particular any single-harmonic symbol a+b*cos(k*theta)+c*sin(k*theta) with range in [0,1] inherits the known degree-one construction and is a (k+1)-block factor. Check: For cylinder events on distinct residue classes, all mixed kernel entries vanish and every required inclusion determinant factors. Inclusion-exclusion upgrades those identities to independence of the complete finite-dimensional distributions. The proposed coding depends only on positions at distances k, making its full window length exactly r*k+1. Obstruction: General mixed-harmonic symbols remain untreated. Finite dependence by itself does not imply a block-factor representation.

body:
[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2608.03497, 'Connective Constants on Nested Fractal Graphs'] \phantomsection

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If the nested fractal graph is \(h\)-flexible,
then
\begin{equation}
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{c_{n+h}}{c_n}=\mu^h.
  
\end{equation}
In particular, \(1\)-flexibility implies
\[
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{c_{n+1}}{c_n}=\mu.
\]
\item For the regular polygonal \(N\)-gasket with \(N\ge3\) and
\(4\nmid N\), write
\[
  N=4k_N+\ell_N,\qquad
  \ell_N\in\{1,2,3\},\qquad
  s_N=k_N+1,
\]
and put
\[
  h_N
  =
  \gcd\bigl(N-2s_N,\,2s_N-(N-2s_N)\bigr).
\]
Then \(h_N\) is the smallest flexibility step.  In fact, the graph is
\(h_N\)-flexible at scale \(2\), and
\[
  h_N=
  \begin{cases}
    2,&N\equiv2\pmod4,\\
    3,&N\equiv9\pmod{12},\\
    1,&\text{otherwise}.
  \end{cases}
\]
Consequently,
\[
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{c_{n+h_N}}{c_n}=\mu_N^{h_N}.
\]
\item The standard Vicsek graph is not \(h\)-flexible for any
\(h\ge1\).  Its connective constant is
\(\mu=\sqrt2\), but, for every \(k\ge2\),
\begin{equation}
  \begin{aligned}
  c_{3^k-2}&=2^{(3^k+1)/2},\\
  c_{3^k-1}&=3\cdot2^{(3^k-3)/2},\\
  c_{3^k}&=3\cdot2^{(3^k-1)/2}.
  \end{aligned}
  
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\[
  \frac{c_{3^k-1}}{c_{3^k-2}}=\frac34,
  \qquad
  \frac{c_{3^k}}{c_{3^k-1}}=2,
\]
and the successive ratios do not converge.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition Function $K_2^{\mathrm{ad}}$ of arXiv:2607.24528, 'On Feige's conjecture'] For \(x,y\geq 0\), let \(a=\min(x,y)\) and \(b=\max(x,y)\). When \(0\leq a<1<b\), let \(\tau(a,b)\) be the larger root of
\[
t^2-b(1+a)t+ab=0.
\]
Define \(K_2^{\mathrm{ad}}\colon[0,\infty)^2\to[0,1]\) by
\[
K_2^{\mathrm{ad}}(a,b)
=
\begin{cases}
1,
& b\leq 1,\\
\frac{2}{\tau(a,b)}-\frac{1}{\tau(a,b)^2},
& 0\leq a<1<b,\\
\frac{1}{ab},
& 1\leq a.
\end{cases}
\]
title: Function $K_2^{\mathrm{ad}}$

[Proposition prop:all-is-fair of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] Let $\mathfrak{M} = (W, W_\bot, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$ be a CK-model. Then $x \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \varphi$ for every $x \in W_\bot$ and $\varphi \in \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$.
  \begin{proof}
    We use an induction on the construction of $\varphi$.

    It is trivial when $\varphi = \bot$ or $\varphi = p$ for some $p \in \mathord{\mathrm{PropVar}}$.

    Suppose $\varphi = \psi_1 \circledcirc \psi_2$, for $\circledcirc \in \set{\land, \lor}$, then it is easily proven with the induction hypothesis.

    Suppose $\varphi = \psi_1 \to \psi_2$. Take any $x'$ such that $x \leq x' \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi_1$, then $x' \in W_\bot$ by $W_\bot$ being upward closed with respect to $\leq$,
    then $x' \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi_2$ by the induction hypothesis. Therefore, $x \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi_1 \to \psi_2$ holds.

    Suppose $\varphi = \Box \psi$. Take any $x', y'$ such that $x \leq x' \sqsubset y'$, then $x', y' \in W_\bot$ by $W_\bot$ being upward closed with respect to $\leq$ and $\sqsubset$,
    then $y' \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by the induction hypothesis. Therefore, $x \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$.

    Suppose $\varphi = \Diamond \psi$. Take any $x'$ such that $x \leq x'$, then $x' \in W_\bot$ by $W_\bot$ being upward closed with respect to $\leq$.
    By $W_\bot$ being $\sqsubset$-serial, there is $y'$ such that $x' \sqsubset y'$,
    then $y' \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by the induction hypothesis. Therefore, $x \Vdash^{\text{c}}_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: All is fair in a fallible world

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:3b9357a8b1b9e4566308a015c1ffd2ba58780c5fbcfcb2d1a51b65fb57fad37b","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/3b/3b9357a8b1b9e4566308a015c1ffd2ba58780c5fbcfcb2d1a51b65fb57fad37b.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:7429cd0460d732743a1028161c6daade984e4e6863e0d6b6dc26b8fe6ec7bb81","bundle_entry_key":"t326-c12","bundle_id":"population.t326-balanced-curves-open-pool-basins","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"in-context learning; linear matrix factorization; gradient flow","draft":"w697/bundle_007_r1.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.incontext:t326-balanced-invariant-level-descent-curve","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Negative curvature survives the three conserved constraints

Target 2(b). Status: proof (unaudited), diagnostic. This is not saddle avoidance from the exact isotropic initialization.

Let C be positive semidefinite, P its range projector, N=I-P, T=d[I,0], E=vAB-T, and L=tr(ECE^T)/2. Suppose (A,B,v) is a positive-loss critical point of the C07 flow with v>0 and

BB^T-A^TA=alpha^2 ee^T, v^2=||A||_F^2, BN=alpha N.

Then there is a smooth two-sided curve through the point preserving all three identities exactly, with zero first derivative of loss and strictly negative second derivative.

Proof. Criticality gives A^T EC=0 and EC B^T=0. Choose a unit right singular vector b of EC for a positive singular value sigma, with associated left singular vector l. Let a=-l, so a^T EC b=-sigma. The two criticality identities imply A^T a=0 and Bb=0. Also b lies in range C, so b^T N=0. The proof of C11 gives a unit u in ker A intersect e-perp, and hence B^T u=0.

Define

A(t)=A+t a u^T, B(t)=B+t u b^T, v(t)=sqrt(v^2+t^2).

All square roots are taken positive. Since a,b,u are unit, the quadratic terms in B(t)B(t)^T-A(t)^TA(t) cancel. Its linear terms vanish because Bb=0 and A^Ta=0. Further ||A(t)||^2=||A||^2+t^2, and B(t)N=BN, proving exact preservation. Because Au=0 and u^TB=0,

A(t)B(t)=AB+t^2 a b^T.

At t=0 the first derivative of v(t)AB(t) is zero. Its second derivative is AB/v+2v a b^T. Scalar criticality gives <AB,EC>=0, so

L''(0)=<AB/v+2v a b^T,EC>=-2v sigma<0.

This proves the curve claim without treating the invariant level set as a smooth manifold at a rank-deficient point.

## Why it still does not prove avoidance

Even a descending curve inside an invariant level set does not imply that every trajectory on that set avoids the critical point. A concrete scalar example is f(a,b)=(ab-1)^2/2, with invariant b^2-a^2=0. The curve a=b=t descends from the critical origin. Nevertheless the other branch a=-b has gradient-flow solutions a'=-a(1+a^2) converging to the origin from every nonzero point on that branch. The origin is an ambient strict saddle and a saddle on the invariant set. These starts have loss above the zero predictor, so this example refutes the implication from invariant-set descent alone; it does not satisfy or refute C07's strict initial-loss gap. C11 separately supplies a positive-loss point below that gap but does not prove reachability.

Known background: Bah et al., 1910.05505v5, Theorem 28 printed p.14 gives ambient almost-everywhere avoidance, not avoidance at a specified initialization or on every invariant branch. No new general landscape theorem is claimed.

body:
[Definition 20 of arXiv:2608.25785, 'Proper Actions on Homogeneous Spaces of the Upper Triangular Matrix Group via Coarse Geome'] Let $(S,\mathcal{E})$ and $(T,\mathcal{F})$ be coarse spaces.
A map $f : S \rightarrow T$ is called: 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \emph{controlled} (cf.~\cite{BunkeEngel2020}) if, for each $E\in \mathcal{E}$, 
    \[
    \Ad_f(E) = \{ (f(x_1),f(x_2)) \mid (x_1,x_2) \in E \} \subset T \times T
    \]
    is an entourage on $T$, 
    \item  \emph{coarsely proper} (cf.~\cite{LeitnerVigolo2023}) if the set $f^\dagger[D]=f^{-1}(D)$ is bounded in $S$ for any bounded subset $D$ of $T$,  
    \item \emph{coarse} (cf.~\cite{Roe2003LectureCoarse}) if it is controlled and coarsely proper,
    \item  \emph{effectively proper} (cf.~\cite{DikranjanZavaCatCoarseGp2020}) if, for any $F\in \mathcal{F}$, the relation 
    \[
    \Ad_{f^\dagger}F = \{ (p,q) \mid (f(p),f(q)) \in F \} \subset S \times S
    \]
    is also an entourage on $S$,
    \item   \emph{a coarse embedding} (cf.~\cite{DikranjanZavaCatCoarseGp2020}) if $f$ is controlled and effectively proper,
    \item  \emph{coarsely surjective} (cf.~\cite{LeitnerVigolo2023}) if there exists $F\in \mathcal{F}$ such that $F[f(S)] = T$,
    \item  \emph{a coarse equivalence} (cf.~\cite{DikranjanZava2017}) if $f$ is controlled and there exists a controlled map $h: T\to S$ such that $h\circ f\sim \id_S$ and $f\circ h\sim \id_T$.
\end{enumerate}

[Prop Lem2 of arXiv:2608.29390, 'The Test and Find Model'] Fix $i\in\{1,2,\dots,n\}$, $s\in \Sigma$, and let $x=M(s)$. If $s_i=0$, then $x\in\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ and
$$
\alpha_i(s) =b \frac{(n-k)}{x}\frac{g_{n-1,k}(x-1)}{g_{n,k}(x)}=:\alpha^-(x,k).
$$
If $s_i=1$, then $x\in\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$ and
$$
\alpha_i(s) = (1-b)\frac{(n-k)}{n-x}\frac{g_{n-1,k}(x)}{g_{n,k}(x)}=: \alpha^+(x,k).
$$
Moreover, we have
$$
x  \alpha^-(x,k) + (n-x) \alpha^+(x,k) = n-k.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:56672755211c4fbbd2ae9814363ba78634eb2be478e4e4e12742caac9ee2502e","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/56/56672755211c4fbbd2ae9814363ba78634eb2be478e4e4e12742caac9ee2502e.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:01206d6ebf0d8659f42bf613a2f917d326ca1cbcacd37d248ec55d046cb75c7a","bundle_entry_key":"i0005-c1","bundle_id":"population.i0005-four-dimensional-parking-partials-002","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"interacting particle systems and random-walk potential theory","draft":"w661/bundle_002.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.particle-hole:i0005-c1-draft","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# I0005-C1 v1: the four-dimensional cutoff convolution

Novelty: KNOWN. This is a standard local-central-limit consequence, rederived here to fix the coefficient and the obstruction in Bou-Rabee–Panagiotis (2026), equation (46). Primary reference: Lawler–Limic, *Random Walk: A Modern Introduction*, Chapter 2 (local CLT). No novelty claim is made. Audit status: unaudited.

Let X be discrete-time nearest-neighbor simple random walk on Z^4, with each of the eight steps equally likely. Put p_n(x)=P_0(X_n=x), and

K_N(x)=sum_{n=0}^N (n+1)p_n(x).

There is an absolute constant C such that, for every integer N≥1 and every x in Z^4,

|K_N(x) − (4/π²) log_+(N/(1+|x|_2²))| ≤ C.

In particular, for fixed x, K_N(x)=(4/π²)log N+O_x(1), and the infinite Green convolution is infinite at every separation. The covariance normalization is Cov(X_1)=I/4; replacing it or making the walk lazy changes the coefficient.

## 1. Uniform periodic local CLT, including its error

The characteristic function is φ(θ)=(1/4)sum_{j=1}^4 cos θ_j on the torus [-π,π]^4. Fourier inversion gives

p_n(x)=(2π)^−4 integral e^{−iθ·x} φ(θ)^n dθ.

The only torus points where |φ|=1 are 0 and a=(π,π,π,π), identified periodically at the corners. Choose disjoint small torus neighborhoods of these points. On their complement |φ|≤ρ<1 by compactness. Near zero,

φ(θ)=1−|θ|²/8+O(|θ|⁴),
log φ(θ)=−|θ|²/8+O(|θ|⁴).

The neighborhoods can be chosen so the real quadratic decay dominates the remainder. The inequality |e^u−e^v|≤|u−v|exp(max(u,v)) for real u,v then gives

|φ(θ)^n−exp(−n|θ|²/8)|≤Cn|θ|⁴ exp(−cn|θ|²).

Its integral is at most Cn·n^−4=Cn^−3 (dimension four). Extending the Gaussian integral from the neighborhood to R^4 adds an exponentially small error. The factor e^{−iθ·x} has modulus one, so all errors are uniform in x. The Gaussian Fourier integral is

(2π)^−4 integral_{R^4} e^{−iθ·x}e^{−n|θ|²/8}dθ
= (4/(π² n²))exp(−2|x|²/n).

Under the torus shift θ↦θ+a, φ changes sign and the Fourier phase gains (−1)^{sum_j x_j}. Thus the second neighborhood contributes (−1)^{n+sum_j x_j} times the first. Consequently, for n≥1,

p_n(x)=1_{n≡sum_j x_j mod 2} (8/(π²n²))exp(−2|x|²/n)+O(n^−3),

uniformly in x. The forbidden parity is actually zero, since every step changes the parity of the coordinate sum. Finitely many small n are absorbed into the uniform constant.

## 2. Summation and parity

Writing r²=|x|², the accumulated error from (n+1)O(n^−3) is bounded by an absolute constant. Replacing (n+1)/n² by 1/n costs at most Csum n^−2, also bounded. The n=0 term is at most one. Hence

K_N(x)=(8/π²)sum_{1≤n≤N, n≡sum x_j mod 2} e^{−2r²/n}/n + O(1).

For f(s)=e^{−2r²/s}/s, the difference between either parity sum and half the full sum is uniformly bounded. Indeed, it is half an alternating sum. For r=0, f decreases and the alternating sum is bounded by f(1)=1. For r>0, f increases up to s=2r² and decreases thereafter, with sup f≤1, so its total variation on [1,N] is at most two. Summation by parts with bounded partial sums of (−1)^n bounds the alternating sum by sup f plus total variation. Therefore

K_N(x)=(4/π²)sum_{n=1}^N e^{−2r²/n}/n+O(1).

If r=0, this is the harmonic sum log N+O(1). If r²≥1 and N≥r², the sum below r² is bounded uniformly: sum–integral comparison for a unimodal function reduces it to integral_1^{r²}e^{−2r²/s}ds/s, which is bounded after u=r²/s. Above r², replacing the exponential by one costs at most 2r² sum_{n≥r²}n^−2=O(1). The remaining harmonic sum is log(N/r²)+O(1). Replacing r² by 1+r² changes this by at most log 2. If N<r², the same integral bound and bounded unimodal sum–integral error show the whole sum is O(1), while log_+(N/(1+r²))=0. This proves the asserted uniform formula.

## 3. Relation to equation (46)

Let G(y)=sum_{j≥0}p_j(y), finite in dimension four. By symmetry, Chapman–Kolmogorov and Tonelli,

sum_y G(y)G(y−x)
=sum_{j,k≥0}sum_y p_j(y)p_k(y−x)
=sum_{j,k≥0}p_{j+k}(x)
=sum_{n≥0}(n+1)p_n(x)=∞.

Every interchange is valid for nonnegative terms; the last equality is an equality in [0,∞]. Thus even widely separated targets do not admit the finite infinite-time kernel used in the source's bounded-differences and two-hole proofs. The cutoff formula is a diagnostic, not an extension of that proof: a finite-time or killed-walk replacement would have to be justified separately.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:a717cab0408ba62fa14a8ae11b44e2c6621727ffa391b3ed98fd0857f08973f1","revision_digest":"sha256:4c75fbde3dec791808b1267fc45c59dfdea234297cafb825c4589175a4768e92","source_id":"own-work:w661:I0005-C1:v1","source_revision":"v1; 2026-10-14T05:23:59.4615090+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

The residually finite construction supplies labels from actual finite quotients; it does not show that arbitrary unlabelled approximating graphs admit globally compatible generator labels on almost every root. [Proposition first card of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'] Let $n\geq 3$. Then, $I_1^*=I_n^*=\{1\}$, i.e. the player should guess card $1$ in positions $1$ and $n$.
    \begin{proof}
        Note that for a two-card deck, $p_{i,j}=1/2$ for all $i,j$, so any strategy is best. If $n\geq 3$, we notice that $p_{1,1}=p_{1,n}=1/2$ by direct computation or because card $1$ is drawn last, so it must go to the top or the bottom of the shuffled deck. Using Proposition $(doubly stochastic of the paper)$, we have that the column sums of $M$ are $1$. Furthermore, one can verify that there exists an $i\neq 1$ such that $p_{i,1}>0$. Therefore $p_{i,n}>0$ for that same $i$ by Proposition $(guessing strategy symmetry of the paper)$. The pigeonhole principle then implies the result.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let U ⊂ C be a nonempty, open, simply connected set with U ≠ C (equivalently: U is open and connected, its complement in the Riemann sphere is connected, and U is not all of C). Then there exists a biholomorphic map F from U onto the open unit disk D (holomorphic, bijective, with holomorphic inverse). Given any point z0 in U, there is exactly one such F with F(z0) = 0 and F'(z0) > 0. Consequently any two simply connected proper open subsets of C are conformally equivalent. The theorem says nothing about boundary behaviour: for that one needs Carathéodory's theorem (if U is bounded by a Jordan curve, F extends to a homeomorphism of the closures).

Unreviewed finite counterexample, awaiting w542. For 0<h<1, let U,V in {-1,1} have joint law P(U=u,V=v)=(1+h u v)/4. Set A0=B0=U, Ar=V and Br=(V-hU)/(1+h). All are centered and bounded by one. Then E[A0 Ar]=h, E[B0 Br]=0, ||B0-A0||2=0 and ||Br-Ar||2^2=2h^2/(1+h). Thus an unspecified L2 error O(h) does not preserve a positive lower correlation bound of order h. For centered reference observables of L2 norm at most M and both observable errors at most delta, expansion and Cauchy-Schwarz give a correlation error at most 2M delta+delta^2. A sufficiently small explicit relative constant or o(h) can preserve the leading correlation; the example does not challenge such hypotheses. This is a finite transfer obstruction, not a constructed Riesz Gibbs state.

[Proposition 19 of arXiv:2609.01574, 'A linear bound for Fujita's freeness conjecture'] Let $c$ be a positive integer and let $a\geq0$. Let $h_0,h_1,\ldots$ be a finitely supported sequence of nonnegative real numbers such that
$h_k\leq\binom{c+k-1}{k}$, $k\geq0$, and $\sum_{k\geq1}kh_k
 \leq a\sum_{k\geq0}h_k$. Then
$$ \sum_{k\geq0}h_k
 \leq\frac{(a+c)^{a+c}}{a^ac^c}.$$

[Lemma lem:c4-sparse-overlap of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] Let $G=(I,J,M)$ be $C_4$-free with $|I|=k$, $|J|=n\ge2$, and every right degree between $2$ and $d$. Then
\[
\eta(G)\le 2d\,\frac{k}{n}.
\]

Consequently, if $d$ is fixed and $G^{(k)}$ is a sequence of such graphs with $n_k/k\to\infty$, then $\eta(G^{(k)})=o(1)$.

where $\alpha(p)\in(1/2,1)$ and the law of $X(p)$ are as in~\cref{thm:main_permutations}. Moreover, $X(p)$ and $X(1-p)$ are deterministic measurable functions of the Brownian cographon $\bm{W}_p$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Corollary cor:disc_strongerror of arXiv:2412.05239, 'Conditions for uniform in time convergence: applications to averaging, numerical discretis'] Assume that there exists $\lambda>0$ and $C<\infty$ such that for all initial conditions $x,x'\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and $t\ge 0$ it holds
    $\mathbb{E}_{(x,x')}[|X_t-X_t'|^2]^{1/2}\le Ce^{-\lambda t} |x-x'|$.
    Assume that there exists a constant $\alpha>0$ and a function $\mathbf{M}:\mathbb{R}^d\to[0,\infty)$ such that for all $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and  $l\in \mathbb{N}$ with $l \delta \le 1$ the local strong error satisfies $\mathbb{E}_x[|X_{l\delta}-\mathbf{X}_l^{\delta}|^2]^{1/2}\le\delta^{\alpha} \mathbf{M}(x)$. Further suppose that for all $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$ there exists a constant $\mathbf{C}(x)$ such that for the process $\mathbf{X}_l^{\delta}$ starting in $x$ it holds $\sup_{l\in\mathbb{N}}\mathbb{E}_x[\mathbf{M}(\mathbf{X}_l^{\delta})]\le \mathbf{C}(x)$. 
    Then, for all $x\in \mathbb{R}^d$ there exists a constant $\tilde{\mathbf{C}}<\infty$ such that
    \begin{align*}
        \sup_{k\in \mathbb{N}} \mathbb{E}_{x}[|X_{k\delta}-\mathbf{X}_k^{\delta}|^2]^{1/2}\le \tilde{\mathbf{C}}\delta^{\alpha}\, .
    \end{align*}
