[Lemma lem:iterated-log of arXiv:2411.03609, 'Asymptotically optimal Wasserstein couplings for the small-time stable domain of attractio'] Define iteratively the functions $\ell_1(t)=\log(e+t)$ and $\ell_{n+1}(t)=\log(e+\ell_n(t))$ for $t\geqslant 0$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Then, the following statements hold.\\
{\normalfont(a)} For any $x>0$ and $c\geqslant 0$, we have $(c+\ell_n(xt))/(c+\ell_n(t)) \leqslant 1+\1_{\{x>1\}}\log x$.\\
{\normalfont(b)} We have $(e+t)\ell_n'(t)=\prod_{i=1}^{n-1}(e+\ell_k(t))^{-1}$.\\
{\normalfont(c)} Suppose $\ell(t)=\ell_n(t)^{q_n}\cdots\ell_m(t)^{q_m}$ for some $1\leqslant n\leqslant m$ in $\mathbb{N}$ and either $q_n,\ldots,q_m\geqslant 0$ with $q_n,q_m>0$ or $q_n,\ldots,q_m\leqslant 0$ with $q_n,q_m<0$. Set $\wt\ell(t)\coloneqq (e+t)\ell'(t)$, then we have
\[
\Sigma(x)
\coloneqq
\sup_{t>0,\,y\in [x\wedge 1,x\vee1]}\frac{\wt\ell(yt)}{\wt\ell(t)}
\leqslant\begin{cases}
(1+\log x)^{\sum_{j=n}^m q_j^+},
& x\geqslant 1,\\
(1+|\log x|)^{m+\sum_{j=n}^mq_j^-},
& x<1.
\end{cases}
\]

[Definition of arXiv:2411.00663, 'Ergodicity and Mixing of invariant capacities and applications'] Given a capacity space $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mu)$, a stochastic process $\left\{Y_{n}\right\}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ is called to be stationary if  for each $n \in \mathbb{N}, k \in \mathbb{Z}_{+}$ and Borel subset $A$ of $\mathbb{R}^{k+1}$,
	$$
	\mu\left(\left\{\omega\in\Omega:\left(Y_{n}(\omega), \ldots, Y_{n+k}(\omega)\right) \in A\right\}\right)=\mu\left(\left\{\omega\in\Omega:\left(Y_{n+1}(\omega), \ldots, Y_{n+1+k}(\omega)\right) \in A\right\}\right) .
	$$

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, A Brownian piece in front of a process absolutely continuous with respect to Brownian motion (2026). Burdzy and Scheutzow (Forward Brownian motion, Probab. Theory Related Fields 160 (2014), Problem 7.5) asked whether, for every process X whose law is equivalent to Wiener measure, a random piece of path can be put in front of X so that the new process is a Brownian motion. The paper proves that absolute continuity with respect to Wiener measure is enough: on an extension of the probability space there are a standard Brownian motion B and an almost surely finite random integer N >= 0 with X_t = B_{N+t} - B_N for all t >= 0; N cannot in general be a stopping time for B. More generally, for an invertible measure-preserving map theta of (E, P) and a target law fP, a forward shift theta^N with N built from a P-distributed point and independent uniforms carries P to fP if and only if E[f | I] = 1, I the invariant sigma-field; without the auxiliary uniforms only integer-valued densities can be reached. The construction is Rost's filling scheme (Chacon-Ornstein, Rost 1971) for the unit shift of two-sided Brownian motion. Paper and code: https://github.com/yspennstate/brownian-prefix-filling (commit eb410953a445). Not refereed.
title: A Brownian piece in front of a process absolutely continuous with respect to Brownian motion, answering Burdzy-Scheutzow Problem 7.5 via Rost's filling scheme (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/brownian-prefix-filling)

Independently checked by w389; draft concept only. For U uniform[0,1), the n^2 events A_(n,j)={floor(n^2 U)=j}, 0<=j<n^2, each have probability1/n^2 while their union has probability1 for every n; union events can thus be decreasing without their probabilities vanishing. This is a logical counterexample, not an iid FPP example. S_n has8n vertices and 32n^2-4n unordered endpoint pairs, so a union-bound route to root-crossing decay needs cardinality times the prescribed-pair bound to vanish. A uniform o(n^-2) pair bound suffices; merely tending to0 does not.

[Proposition 17 (Phases of the burglars) of arXiv:2609.03968, 'A one-parameter family of local-time conditioned processes : the generalized Brownian burg'] The burglar $X$ behaves in the following way depending on the parameter $\nu$ :

- For $\nu \geq 1 $, $X$ does not hit full local time anywhere else than its target, i.e.\ $L_X(T(X),x)<\lambda_0(x)$ for all $x\in I\setminus\{x_0\}$ almost surely.

- For $\nu \in (0,1)$, for any deterministic $x\in I\setminus\{x_0\}$, $L_X(T(X),x)<\lambda_0(x)$ almost surely, but there almost surely exists exceptional $x\in I\setminus\{x_0\}$ such that $L_X(T(X),x)=\lambda_0(x)$. 

- For $\nu \leq  0$, $X$ is ``local-time-filling", i.e.\ for all $x\in I$, $L_X(T(X),x)=\lambda_0(x)$ almost surely.
title: Phases of the burglars

[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2609.03726, 'Inverse Scattering for Single Photons in Quantum Optics'] Let $\alpha\in\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$, $\chi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n)$, $f=e^{ik\alpha\cdot(\cdot)}\chi$, and $x\in \mathbb{R}^n$. Then, there exists $k_{\rho}>0$ such that for $k>k_{\rho}$, the outgoing solution
    $\psi^{f}$ satisfies
    \begin{equation}
        \psi^{f}(x)
        =  \psi_0(x) - e^{ik\alpha\cdot x}\,
        \frac{g^2}{k - \Omega}\, T_\alpha(\rho\, b_0)(x)
        + O_{\rho,\chi,x}(k^{-2}),
    \end{equation}
    where $\psi_0 = R_k^0 f$ and
    $b_0$ is defined by \eqref{eq:b0_def}.
title: Lemma 12 of arXiv:2609.03726

body: The Nyquist–Shannon sampling theorem is a theorem in the field of signal processing which serves as a fundamental bridge between continuous-time signals and discrete-time signals. In the case of uniformly spaced (periodic) sampling, it establishes a sufficient condition on the sample rate that permits a discrete sequence of samples to capture all the information from a continuous-time signal of finite bandwidth, such that the original signal can be reconstructed exactly from those samples.
title: Nyquist–Shannon sampling theorem

[Corollary 52 (Parallel tempering converges) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] Let $\mathcal{Y},\lambda_{0},K,p_{k},\pi_{k}$ and $\XX,\XXA,\lambda,\pi$ be as above,
let $R_{1},\dots,R_{K}$ satisfy the hypotheses stated there including
\eqref{eq:temperingtheta}, let $\mathcal{S} \ne \emptyset$ and
$\omega \in [0,1)$, and let $T$ be the parallel tempering kernel. Then $\pi$ is the
unique invariant probability measure of $T$ and
\[
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\ \sup_{A \in \XXA}\bigl| (T^{n}\circ\mu)(A) - \pi(A) \bigr| = 0
  \qquad\text{for every } \mu \in \Prob .
\]
More precisely, with $c := (1-\omega)(\theta^{-})^{K} \in (0,1]$,
\[
  \sing\bigl( T^{n}\circ\mu \bigm| \pi\bigr) \;\le\; (1-c)^{n}
  \qquad (\mu \in \Prob,\ n \in \Nz) .

[Theorem 1 (Intersection of Moment Level Curves) of arXiv:2609.00209, 'Exit Times for Brownian Motion and Location Detection'] Let $D$ denote any of the non-rectangular domains from Table \ref{tab:domains} and suppose the level curves for the first two exit time moments $\mathbb{E}^{(x,y)}[\tau_D]=c_1$ and $\mathbb{E}^{(x,y)}[\tau_D^2]=c_2$ intersect for some positive constants $c_1$ and $c_2$.
\begin{itemize}
\item[1.] If $D=\mathcal E$, then the level curves intersect at either four points, two points, or one point determined by $c_1$ and $c_2$.
\item[2.] If $D=\mathcal P, \mathcal H, \mathcal W$, then the level curves intersect at either two points or a single point determined by $c_1$ and $c_2$.
\item[3.] If $D=\mathcal T$, then the level curves intersect at either six points, three points, or a single point determined by $c_1$ and $c_2$.
\end{itemize}

If $D=\mathcal R$ is a rectangular domain as in Table \ref{tab:domains} and $c_k$ for $k\geq 1$ are positive numbers such that the level curves $\mathbb{E}^{(x,y)}[\tau_{\mathcal R}^k]=c_k$ intersect, then their intersection is either one, two, or four points determined by the values $c_k$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Intersection of Moment Level Curves

For a uniform-root three-state calibrated observation law invariant under all coordinate permutations, barycentrically split each posterior onto a simplex grid of denominator N divisible by3. Round each whole orbit mass down to a multiple of1/S, S=2^b, and replace removed mass by uniform root revelation. The resulting experiment Blackwell-dominates the original. Applying a physical ferromagnetic edge once, then independently fusing fresh child experiments and upgrading after each binary combination, gives a finite-depth upper experiment on a regular d-child broadcast tree. Its expected squared posterior distance from uniform bounds the canonical signal. Zero-likelihood pairs are excluded before normalization; reused laws denote fresh conditional-root observations.

[Defi Def:W-homotopy-Equiv of arXiv:2608.29013, 'Weighted Homology and Cohomology of Weighted Polyhedra'] Let $(X,\lambda)$ and $(X',\lambda')$ be 
    weighted polyhedra of the same type and
       $f, g: (X,\lambda)\rightarrow (X',\lambda')$ be two  
     W-continuous maps. A \emph{W-homotopy} from $f$ to $g$ relative
to $A\subseteq X$ is a W-continuous map
$$H : (X \times [0, 1],\lambda\times \mathbf{1}) \rightarrow (X',\lambda')$$ which satisfies:
 \begin{itemize}
   \item $H(x, 0) =f(x)$ and $H(x,1)=g(x)$ for all $x\in X$;\vskip 0.1cm
   \item $H(a,t)=f(a)=g(a)$ for all $a\in A$ and 
   $t\in [0,1]$.\vskip 0.1cm
   \end{itemize}
   
   Here $([0,1],\mathbf{1})$ is considered as a weighted polyhedron, and $(X\times [0,1],\lambda\times \mathbf{1})$ is the product $(X,\lambda)$ with
   $([0,1],\mathbf{1})$.
   \vskip 0.1cm
   If there exists a W-homotopy from $f$ to $g$,
   we say that $f$ is \emph{W-homotopic to} $g$.
   If moreover $H$ is weight-preserving, we say
   that $f$ is \emph{strongly W-homotopic to} $g$ (a priori $f$ and $g$ must be both weight-preserving).

body:
[Lemma lem:bound_asymptotics of arXiv:2604.09509, 'An Improved Bipartition Cover Bound for the Multispecies Coalescent Model'] Let $\kappa_{q,k} := \log((k-3)/(1-q))$ and $u(T) := \frac{2-\exp(-T/2)}{1-\exp(-T/2)}$. Then
    
    \[M_o(k,T)  \sim \begin{cases}
    \frac{\kappa_{q,k}}{T}, & T \uparrow \infty, \\
    \frac{2^{k-3}\kappa_{q,k}}{(k-2)! T^{k-3}}, & T = o(k^{-2}), \\
    \frac{\kappa_{q,k}}{-\log(1-s(T))}, & T \text{ fixed}, k \to \infty
\end{cases}\]

    \[M_b(k,T) \lesssim 
        \frac{\kappa_{q,k}}{-\log(1-g_{u(T), 1}(T))}, \qquad T \text{ fixed}, k \to \infty\]

    \noindent Moreover, in the fixed $T$ regime, the improvement factor satisfies
    
    \[
    \liminf_{k\to\infty}\frac{M_o(k,T)}{M_b(k,T)}
    \geqslant \beta_T
    :=\frac{\log(1-g_{u(T),1}(T))}{\log(1-s(T))},
    \qquad
    \beta_T\sim \frac{\pi^2}{2T}
    \quad\text{as }T\downarrow0.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Bound Asymptotics

body:
[Definition 12 of arXiv:2606.31455, 'Discrete time-multidimensional renewal theory and applications'] Let $U\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}$ be a nonempty index set with $|U|=m$ and let
$\pi_U:\mathbb{N}^d\to\mathbb{N}^m$ be the coordinate projection.
Define the projected increments $X_n^{[U]}:=\pi_U(X_n)$.
Then $(X_n^{[U]})_{n\ge 1}$ is an i.i.d.\ sequence on $\mathbb{N}^m$ with pmf

\begin{equation}
f^{[U]}(k_U):=\mathbb{P}(X_1^{[U]}=k_U),
\qquad k_U\in\mathbb{N}^m.
\end{equation}

Assume $f^{[U]}(0_m)<1$ (non-degeneracy in the projected coordinates), and define the
projected renewal chain and counting process by

\begin{equation}
S_0^{[U]}=0_m,
\qquad
S_n^{[U]}=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i^{[U]},
\qquad n\ge 1,
\end{equation}

and

\begin{equation}
N^{[U]}(k_U):=\sup\{n\in\mathbb{N}: S_n^{[U]}\le_m k_U\},
\qquad k_U\in\mathbb{N}^m,
\end{equation}

where $\le_m$ denotes componentwise order in $\mathbb{N}^m$.
Its renewal function is

\begin{equation*}
M^{[U]}(k_U):=\mathbb{E}[N^{[U]}(k_U)].
\end{equation*}

\smallskip
\noindent
In particular, for $U=\{u\}$ one recovers the univariate marginal renewal process
$S_n^{[u]}=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i^{[u]}$ and the marginal counting process

$N^{[u]}(k_u)=\sup\{n:S_n^{[u]}\le k_u\}$.
title: Definition 12 of arXiv:2606.31455

body:
[Cor blowup of arXiv:2608.30847, 'An Almgren-type formula for planar $p$-harmonic functions'] Let $u$, $x_0$, and $\lambda=N_*(x_0,0+)$ be as in Theorem (thm:main of the paper).  If $u$ is not locally constant near $x_0$, then there exists a nonzero homogeneous $p$-harmonic function $P$ of degree $\lambda$ such that
$$
  \frac{u(x_0+r\,\cdot)-u(x_0)}{r^\lambda}
  \longrightarrow P
$$
locally uniformly and in $C^1$ on compact subsets of $\mathbb R^2\setminus\{0\}$ as $r\to0$.

[Lemma lem:volterra of arXiv:2607.20956, 'Sharp moduli of continuity for Gaussian fields and stochastic PDEs via correlation bounds'] Under Assumption (a:kappa of the paper), we have:
\begin{enumerate}[$(i)$]
    \item $\phi(|t-s|) \le \|X(t)-X(s)\|_2 \le \sqrt{2}\, \phi(|t-s|)$ uniformly for all $t,s \in [0\,,T]$; and\smallskip
    \item One-sided SLND:
    \[
        \Var(X(t)|X(t_1),\dots, X(t_n)) \ge \phi^2(t-t_n) \ge \tfrac12 \Var(X(t)-X(t_n))
    \]
    uniformly for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $0 \le t_1 < \cdots < t_n \le t \le T$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Lemma lem:volterra of arXiv:2607.20956

[Prop 5 of arXiv:2506.13661, 'Box-Covariances of Hyperuniform Point Processes'] Let $\eta$ be a stationary point process on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a truncated pair correlation measure $\beta$ s.t.\ $|\beta|(\mathbb{R}^d)<\infty$. The following are equivalent:
	\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
		\item The point process $\eta$ is hyperuniform, i.e.~\eqref{eq:HU} holds for boxes, balls or arbitrary convex sets. 
		\item It holds that $1+\beta(\mathbb{R}^d)=0$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 5 of arXiv:2506.13661

body: [Proposition 3.9 of arXiv:2304.14793, 'Learning Graph Neural Networks using Exact Compression'] There is a single 𝑑-reduct of a graph 𝐺up to isomorphism if and only if 𝑑is greater than or equal to the stable coloring number of 𝐺. A direct consequence of having different non-isomorphic reducts when𝑑is less than the coloring number is that some of these reducts may be smaller than others. In Example 3.7, 𝐺/𝜌1 has 3 nodes and 4 edges while 𝐺/𝜌2 has 3 nodes and only 3 edges.
title: Proposition 3.9 of arXiv:2304.14793: Learning Graph Neural Networks using Exact Compression

[Theorem 25 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Let \(\xi=(\mu_t)_{t<T}\) be a fixed limiting point of a compact
finite-time K\"ahler--Ricci flow of complex dimension \(n\ge2\), and
let \((Z,d,\cR,g,J,f,\mathfrak m)\) be the time-\((-1)\) model of a
tangent space at \(\xi\).  Thus \(Z\) has
the finite-time tangent-space package of
\cref{sp:prop:limiting-package}: it is the intrinsic completion
of its K\"ahler regular locus, is normal and klt, carries the normalized
shrinker measure and complete soliton flow, and has smooth
metric--complex--density convergence and the local ambient metric lower
bound.  Let \(A\) be the nonnegative
self-adjoint operator associated with the closure of
\[
 \cE_0(\phi,\psi)=
 \int_{\cR}\langle\nabla\phi,\nabla\overline\psi\rangle\,d\mathfrak m,
 \qquad \phi,\psi\in C_c^\infty(\cR).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
                     \sigma(A)\subset\{0\}\cup[1/2,\infty),
                     \qquad\ker A=\C1.
\end{equation}
If \(u:Z\to\C\) is holomorphic and globally \(d\)-Lipschitz, then
\(u\in L^2(Z,\mathfrak m)\), and
\begin{equation}
 A\left(u-\int_Zu\,d\mathfrak m\right)
 =\frac12\left(u-\int_Zu\,d\mathfrak m\right),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
          \nabla^2\Re u=\nabla^2\Im u=0\qquad\text{on }\cR.
\end{equation}
Here \(A\) is the canonical Friedrichs form generator; no
essential-self-adjointness assertion is made for the minimal operator on
the incomplete regular locus. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 25 of arXiv:2609.02878

[Lemma 159 (The key top-order integration by parts in $\Lunit$ identity tied to the acoustic geometry) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Let $N = \Ntop$, $(\ubar,u) \in [\leftubar,\ubarboot)\times[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]$,
	and let $\varphi$ and $\upeta$ be scalar functions on $\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubar)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,u]}$. Let $ \tander^N \in \mathfrak{P}^{(N)}$, where $\mathfrak{P}^{(N)}$ denotes the set of top-order commutator operators from Def.\,\ref{D:STRINGSOFCOMMUTATIONVECTORFIELDS}.
	Then the following integration by parts identity holds:
	\begin{align}
		\begin{split} 
			&
			\int_{\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubar)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,u]}}
			 (\muX \varphi) 
			(\Lunit  \tander^N \varphi) 
			\Yvf{A} \upeta \, \weight^{\blowupratetoporderwave} \ReciprocalLunitAppliedtoTimeFunction
			\, \voldiamond 
			\\
			& 
			= 
			\int_{\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubar)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,u]}}  
			(\muX \varphi) 
			(\Yvf{A} \tander^N \varphi) 
			\Lunit \upeta \, \weight^{\blowupratetoporderwave} \ReciprocalLunitAppliedtoTimeFunction
			\, \voldiamond \\
			& \ \
			- \int_{\ingoingcharacteristicsurfacetwoarg{\ubar}{[\moreinterestingu_1,u]}} 
			( \muX \varphi) \left\{ \frac{1}{\Speed^2} (\gtorus^{-1})^{AB} \gtorusdoublenullCOV_B^C \nullgeop{x^C}\tander^N \varphi \right\} \upeta \, \weight^{\blowupratetoporderwave}
			\, \volingoingnullhypersurface 
			\\
			&  \ \ 
			+ 
			\int_{\ingoingcharacteristicsurfacetwoarg{\leftubar}{[\moreinterestingu_1,u]}} 
			(\muX \varphi) \left\{ \frac{1}{\Speed^2} (\gtorus^{-1})^{AB} \gtorusdoublenullCOV_B^C \nullgeop{x^C} \tander^N  \varphi \right\} \upeta \, \weight^{\blowupratetoporderwave}
			\, \volingoingnullhypersurface 
			\\
			& \ \ 
			+ 
			\int_{\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubar)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,u]}}
			\left\{ \ErrorIBP_1^{AG;L}[\tander^N \varphi;\upeta;\Yvf{A}]+ \ErrorIBP_2^{AG;L}[\tander^N \varphi;\upeta;\Yvf{A}]  \right\}\ReciprocalLunitAppliedtoTimeFunction
			\, \voldiamond,
		\end{split}
	\end{align} 
	where:  
	\begin{align} 
		\begin{split} 
			\ErrorIBP_1^{AG;L}[\tander^N \varphi;\upeta;\Yvf{A}]
			&  
			\eqdef  \weight^{\blowupratetoporderwave} \Big\{
			(\muX \varphi) 
			([\Lunit, \Yvf{A}] \tander^N \varphi) 
			\upeta  
			\\
			& \ \
			+ 
			(\Lunit \muX \varphi) 
			(\Yvf{A} \tander^N \varphi)
			\upeta 
			- 
			(\Yvf{A} \muX \varphi) 
			(\Lunit \tander^N \varphi)
			\upeta  \\
			& \ \ 
			\left. - \frac{1}{2} (\muX \varphi) (\Lunit \tander^N \varphi)\upeta \mytr_{\gtorus} \, \angdeform{\Yvf{A}} +  (\muX \varphi) (\Yvf{A} \tander^N \varphi )\upeta \mytr_{\gtorus} \upchi \right\} ,
		\end{split} \\
		\begin{split}
			\ErrorIBP_2^{AG;L}[\tander^N \varphi;\upeta;\Yvf{A}] & \eqdef - \blowupratetoporderwave \, \weight^{\blowupratetoporderwave - 1} (\Yvf{A} \weight)(\muX \varphi) (\Lunit \tander^N \varphi) \upeta  \\
			& \ \  +  \blowupratetoporderwave \, \weight^{\blowupratetoporderwave - 1} (\newL  \weight) (\muX \varphi) (\Yvf{A} \tander^N \varphi) \upeta 
		\end{split}
	\end{align}

body:
[Question of arXiv:2605.02226, 'Finitely Dependent Processes on Subshifts'] \begin{enumerate}
\item A $d-$dimensional domino is a $ d$-dimensional box whose one side has length $2$ and all other sides have length 1 with its vertices in $\mathbb{Z}^d$. Does there exist a strongly irreducible subshift contained in the space of domino tilings of $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $d\geq 3$?
    \item In general, is there a natural characterization of the set of boxes $\mathcal{R}$ for which the space of tilings of $\mathbb{R}^d$ by the boxes in $\mathcal{R}$ contains a strongly irreducible subshift?
    
    We know that if the collection $ \mathcal{R}$ satisfies the condition of (thm:eventuallyuniversaltiles of the paper), then there exists a shift-invariant finitely dependent process on the tiling space $X(\mathcal{R})$. However, if $ p_1, p_2, \cdots, p_d$ are prime numbers and $ \mathcal{R} = \{ R_1, R_2, \cdots, R_d\}$ is a collection of bars where $ R_i$ is a bar whose sidelength in $ e_i$ direction is $ p_i$, then does $ X(\mathcal{R})$ contain a strongly irreducible subshift?
    \end{enumerate} (Stated as a question by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Unnumbered question of arXiv:2605.02226, 'Finitely Dependent Processes on Subshifts'

body: [Cor symmetric-branching-real of arXiv:2605.13004, 'Orientation in Poisson Cluster Processes via Imaginary Bispectra'] In the setting of Theorem~(thm:branching-bispectrum of the paper), let $C$ denote the rooted branching cluster. Suppose $h(x)=h(-x)$ a.e. Then the branching-cluster law satisfies $C\stackrel d=-C$, the stationary process is reversible, and both the complete and factorial third-order Fourier--Stieltjes transforms are real-valued. The relevant finite moments hold because the subcritical Poisson Galton--Watson cluster has finite third moment. Indeed, when the offspring distribution is Poisson with mean \(m<1\), the total progeny has the Borel distribution, which has finite exponential moments in a neighbourhood of the origin; see Dwass~[dwass1969total]. If the reduced third factorial cumulant has an $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ density, then the factorial bispectral density is real. The complete third cumulant still contains the usual diagonal singular components; by Lemma~(lem:ordinary-factorial-bispectrum of the paper), their Fourier--Stieltjes contribution is real. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Centrally symmetric branching kernels have real third-order spectra

[Theorem 11 of arXiv:2609.03803, 'List-distance consistent vertices in trees are confined to a path'] Let $G=SP(w;\ell_1,\dots,\ell_k)$ with $k\ge3$ and $\ell_1\ge2$. Then
\[
  \ldc(G)=
  \begin{cases}
    \bigl\lfloor \ell_3/2\bigr\rfloor+2, & \text{if } k=3,\\[2pt]
    \bigl\lceil \ell_k/2\bigr\rceil+1, & \text{if } k\ge4 .
  \end{cases}
\]

body:
[Thm DRC of arXiv:2602.06011, 'Excursion decomposition of the XOR-Ising model'] Let $D$ be a Jordan domain and $D_\delta$ be as above. For the (critical) coupling $\mathbb P_\delta$, 
    \begin{equation}
        (h_\delta, \hat\mathbf{n}_\delta, \hat\mathbf{n}_\delta^\dagger, c_\delta, c_\delta^\dagger, \xi_\delta, \xi^\dagger_\delta) \overset{(d)}{\longrightarrow} (\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}\lambda}\ h, \hat\mathbf{n}, \hat\mathbf{n}^\dagger, c, c^\dagger, \xi, \xi^\dagger),
    \end{equation}
    where
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item h is a GFF with zero boundary conditions in $D$, 
        \item The inner boundaries of the boundary cluster of $\hat\mathbf{n}_\delta$ converge to $\mathcal L_{-\sqrt{2}\lambda, \sqrt{2}\lambda}$. The label $c(\ell)$ of an inner boundary $\ell$ is such that the boundary values of $h$ in $\mathcal O(\ell)$ are $c(\ell)\sqrt{2}\lambda$.
        \item The outer boundaries of the outermost clusters of $\hat\mathbf{n}^\dagger_\delta$ converge to $\mathcal L_{-2\lambda, 2\lambda}$. The sign $\xi^\dagger(\gamma)$ of an outer boundary $\gamma$ is such that the boundary values of $h$ in $\mathcal O(\gamma)$ are $\xi^\dagger(\gamma)2\lambda$. Moreover, the inner boundaries of the cluster corresponding to $\gamma$ converge to
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item [(iii.a)] $\mathcal L_{-2\lambda, (2\sqrt{2}-2)\lambda}$ if $\xi^\dagger(\gamma)=+1$,
            \item [(iii.b)] $\mathcal L_{-(2\sqrt{2}-2)\lambda, 2\lambda}$ if $\xi^\dagger(\gamma)=-1$,
            \item [(iii.c)] where the label $c^\dagger(\ell)$ of an inner boundary $\ell$ is such that the boundary values of $h$ in $\mathcal O(\ell)$ are $\xi(\gamma)(c(\ell)+1)\sqrt{2}\lambda$. 
        \end{enumerate}
        \item The structure repeats iteratively by applying the Markov property (MP-free of the paper) of Theorem (thm:master of the paper), which gives the nesting of two-valued sets described in Section (sec:decomp of the paper).
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm DRC of arXiv:2602.06011

body:
[Theorem 6 (the inverse problem) of arXiv:2608.30138, 'High-frequency wave propagation for the viscoelastic wave equation with singular memory'] Let $0<p<1$. 
For every $\omega\in \S^{n-1}$, let $\chi\in C_0^\infty(\Omega)$ satisfy $\supp\chi\cap\overline{B(0,R)}=\emptyset$. Let $T>0$ be such that every point of $\overline{B(0,R)}$ lies on a ray $z+t\omega$, with $z\in\{\chi\ne0\}$ and $0<t<T$, and every such ray has exited $\overline{B(0,R)}$ by time $T$. Assume that $\Omega$ contains all the relevant incoming and outgoing ray segments up to time $T$. Then the family of corresponding solutions $u$ of \r{1b}, \r{IC1}, restricted to $[0,T]\times(\Omega\setminus B(0,R))$, for a fixed $\lambda$ in \r{lambda} and all $0<h\ll1$, uniquely determines $\sigma_{\mathfrak{m}}$ and the full jet $\{m_k(x)\}_{k\ge0}$ of $m(s,x)$ at $s=0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: the inverse problem

body: Publication record. Open Problem 7.27 of D. Aldous and J. A. Fill, Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, is answered by Y. Shmalo, Arc-transitive graphs that mimic the cycle (September 2026): over arc-transitive graphs other than the cycles, the maximal mean commute time need not be O(n log n), the relaxation time need not be O(n), and the ratio of the maximal mean commute time to twice the average hitting time need not tend to one. The paper gives the hitting times, the average hitting time and the relaxation time of the blow-up H[K_r-bar] of any regular graph H (each vertex replaced by r independent copies) in terms of those of H, and shows that every arc-transitive graph is such a blow-up of a twin-free arc-transitive graph, so the question reduces to twin-free graphs. Paper: https://github.com/yspennstate/arc-transitive-graphs-that-mimic-the-cycle (commit 9e30e48c8cf7); ResearchGate record 414324957. Not refereed.
title: Aldous-Fill Open Problem 7.27 answered negatively: arc-transitive graphs need not behave like the cycle in commute, relaxation and hitting times (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/arc-transitive-graphs-that-mimic-the-cycle)

[Lemma 60 (\cite{Lerner2010Metrics}*{Theorem 2.3.18}) of arXiv:2609.04153, '\vspace*{-3cm}Smooth autonomous fast dynamo action on the three-torus'] Let $a_\eps \in S_\eps(m_\eps;\ell_\eps)$. Then, 
$$
(\Op_x(a_\eps))^\star-\Op_x(a_\eps^\star) \in \Psi_\eps(m_\eps \ell_\eps^{-1};\ell_\eps),
$$
Furthermore, letting $\tilde a_\eps$ be the symbol of $(\Op_x(a_\eps))^\star-\Op_x(a_\eps^\star)$, there holds the explicit error estimate, for an explicit constant $C>0$ independent of $a, \eps, \lambda$, and an integer $L$ depending only on $m_\eps, K, d$ (notably, $L$ is independent of $\eps$), so that
$$
|\tilde a_\eps|_{m_\eps \ell_\eps^{-1},\ell_\eps,K} \leq C|a_\eps|_{m_\eps, \ell_\eps, K+L}.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Externaltheorem 11 (Junge--Mei group-semigroup theorem) of arXiv:2609.03993, 'The Endpoint Fractional Riesz Estimate on the Hamming Cube'] Let $G$ be a discrete group and let $\phi:G\to\mathbb R$ be symmetric,
		conditionally negative, and satisfy $\phi(e)=0$.  Define
		\[
		A\lambda(g)=\phi(g)\lambda(g),
		\qquad
		T_t\lambda(g)=e^{-t\phi(g)}\lambda(g).
		\]
		Then $(T_t)$ extends to a standard semigroup on $\VN(G)$ and satisfies
		$\Gamma_2\ge0$ in the sense of \eqref{eq:gamma2}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition prop:variance_explicit of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Consider the empirical density $\overline{\rho}_t(V)$ (Definition~(def:empirical_density of the paper))
and empirical current $\overline J_t(U)$ (Definition~(def:empirical_current of the paper))
and let Assumptions~(ass:dynamics of the paper) hold.
Then for all $t>0$,
\begin{align}
  \mathrm{Var}_\mu(\overline\rho_t)
    &\leq \frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(V)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}t},
  \\
  \mathrm{Var}_\mu(\overline J_t)
    &\leq \frac{1}{t}\left(2\E^\mu[Q]
      +\frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(W)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}}\right)
      \leq \frac{1}{t}\left(2\|Q\|_{L^\infty(\mu)}
      +\frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(W)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}}\right),
  
\end{align}
where $\lambda_\mathrm{gap}$ denotes the spectral gap~(equation eq:gap_variational of the paper) of $\mathcal{L}_S$
and $W=v_{\textrm{s}}\cdot U$ and $Q=U\cdot DU$ as before.
The corresponding asymptotic variances, 
defined by $\sigma_{A,\infty}^2\equiv\lim_{t\to\infty}t\mathrm{Var}_\mu(\overline A_t)$,
are bounded by the same constants, i.e., 
\begin{align}
  \sigma_{\rho,\infty}^2\leq\frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(V)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}},
	\quad\quad
  \sigma_{J,\infty}^2\leq 2\E^\mu[Q]+\frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(W)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}}
  \leq 2\|Q\|_{L^\infty(\mu)}+\frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(W)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}}.
  
\end{align}
title: Finite-time variance upper bounds

[Proposition prop:conformal_rectangles_tight of arXiv:2609.04138, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ I:\\ subsequential limits of the non-simple C'] We have the following convergences:
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
		\item The number $N^\kappa$ of crossings of $A$ by loops in $\Gamma^\kappa_A$ converges in law to the number $N^4$ of crossings of $A$ by loops in $\Gamma^4_A$ as $\kappa \uparrow 4$. More precisely, for all $\kappa_n \uparrow 4$ there exists an ordering of the crossings $\eta_1^n, \ldots, \eta^n_{N^{\kappa_n}}$ of $\Gamma^{\kappa_n}_A$ for which the random vectors $(N^{\kappa_n}, \eta^n_1, \ldots, \eta^n_{N^{\kappa_n}})$ converge in law to $(N^4, \eta_1, \ldots, \eta_{N^4})$, where $\eta_1, \ldots, \eta_{N^4}$ are the crossings of $A$ by loops in $\Gamma^4_A$, for the topology of Hausdorff convergence.
		\item Jointly with the above convergence, the compact sets $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{\kappa_n, \mathrm{out}}_A} \mathrm{int}(\SCL)}$ and $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{\kappa_n, \mathrm{in}}_A} \mathrm{int}(\SCL)}$ converge in distribution for the Hausdorff distance to $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{4, \mathrm{out}}_A} \mathrm{int}(\SCL)}$ and $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{4, \mathrm{in}}_A} \mathrm{int}(\SCL)}$.
		\item In particular, the conformal rectangles whose left and right sides are given by the crossings of $A$ by loops in $\Gamma^{\kappa_n}_A$ and whose top and bottom sides are respectively included in $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{\kappa_n, \mathrm{out}}_A} \SCL}$ and $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{\kappa_n, \mathrm{in}}_A} \SCL}$ converge in distribution as $n \to \infty$ in the Carath\'eodory sense (jointly with their corners) to the conformal rectangles whose left and right sides are given by the crossings of $A$ by loops in $\Gamma^{4}_A$ and whose top and bottom sides are respectively included in $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{4, \mathrm{out}}_A} \SCL}$ and $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{4, \mathrm{in}}_A} \SCL}$, and their moduli are tight in $(0,\infty)$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:conformal_rectangles_tight of arXiv:2609.04138

body:
[Proposition prop:la of arXiv:2607.07309, 'Quantitative limit theorems for generalized P\'olya urns with applications to random tree '] Suppose $p \in \{d,d-1\}$. Then
    \[
\langle w, w(R - \lambda I)\rangle_p \leq -A|w\|_p^2 
\quad \text{for all } w \in \mathbb{R}^{d} \text{ with } 
\sum_{i=0}^{d-1} w_i = 0.
\]
for 
\[
A:= -\lambda_{\max}(\operatorname{symm}(C_p J_p
(R^\top - \lambda I)C_p^\top)).
\]
Where $C_p$ is a $p \times d$ matrix, defined via
\begin{equation*}
    C_{p} := \begin{cases}
        I & \text{if }\ p =d\\[0.5cm]
	(I_{d-1},\ (-1,\ldots,-1)^\top) & \text{if }\ p=d-1    
\end{cases}
\end{equation*}
and $I_{d-1}$ denotes the $(d-1) \times (d-1)$ identity matrix.

[Lemma Local model convergence of arXiv:2606.23025, 'Spectral-Capacitary Bounds for Homological Recovery from Reflected Brownian Trajectories'] Assume
\(\partial M\) uniformly of class \(C^{1,1}\), and let
\(x_{\varepsilon} \in M\) satisfy
\(\operatorname{dist}\left( x_{\varepsilon},\partial M \right)/\varepsilon \rightarrow a \in \lbrack 0,\infty\rbrack\).
For fixed \(R > 1\) let \(D_{\varepsilon}(R)\) be the
Dirichlet energy of the capacitary potential of
\(B_{M}\left( x_{\varepsilon},\varepsilon \right)\) in
\(B_{M}\left( x_{\varepsilon},R\varepsilon \right)\backslash\overline{B_{M}\left( x_{\varepsilon},\varepsilon \right)}\)
with the Neumann condition on \(\partial M\), and
\(E_{a}(\varepsilon;R)\) the energy of the corresponding model
condenser at radii \((\varepsilon,R\varepsilon)\) --- the free
Euclidean condenser when \(a = \infty\), the reflected half-space
condenser at height \(a\) when \(a < \infty\). Then
\(D_{\varepsilon}(R) = E_{a}(\varepsilon;R)\left( 1 + o(1) \right)\)
as \(\varepsilon \rightarrow 0\) with \(R\) fixed,
uniformly along the sequence.

[Thm 30 of arXiv:2608.13976, 'Boundary Harnack principle for diffusion with jumps on metric measure spaces'] For each ball $B,$ there exists a transient Hunt process $\wh X^{b, B} $ in $B$ such
that $\wh X^{b, B} $ is a strong dual\vadjust{\goodbreak} of $X^{b, B}$ with respect to
the measure $\xi_B$; that is, the density of the semigroup $\{ \wh
P^{b, B}_t\}_{t\geq0}$ of $\wh X^{b, B}$ with respect to $\xi_B(dy)$ is given by
$\wh p^{b, B}(t, x, y):=\overline{p}^{b, B}(t,y,x)$ and thus

\[
\int_B f(x) P^{b, B}_t g(x) \xi_B(dx)=\int_B g(x) \wh P^{b, B}_t f(x) \xi_B(dx)
\qquad\mbox{for all } f, g\in L^2(B, \xi_B).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

$$
\mathbb{E}_{x_2} [\iprod{x_1}{x_2}^{2\ell}] = \frac{(2\ell-1)!!}{d(d+2)\cdots(d+2\ell-2)} .
$$

 \end{cases}	
 $$	
Then

body:
[Defn Radial Loewner chain of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherland system'] Let $g_t$ satisfies the radial Loewner equation

\begin{equation}
\partial_t g_t(z)=g_t(z) \frac{\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} \theta_t}+g_t(z)}{\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} \theta_t}-g_t(z)}, \quad g_0(z)=z,
\end{equation}

where $t \mapsto \theta_t$ is real continuous and called the driving function. 
Let $K_t$ be the set of points $z$ in $\mathbb{D}$ such that the solution $g_s(z)$ blows up before or at time $t$.  $K_t$ is called the radial SLE hull driven by $\theta_t$.

Radial Loewner chain in arbitrary simply connected domain $\Omega \subsetneq \mathbb{C}$ with a marked interior point $u \in D$, is defined via a conformal map from $\mathbb{D}$ onto $\Omega$ sending 0 to $u$.
title: Radial Loewner chain

Under the hypotheses of the cross-cut theorem, let C have m elements. If R is uniform over the 2^m subsets of C, then mu(0, 1) = 2^m E[(-1)^|R| 1{R is spanning}]. If 0 < p < 1 and R_p contains each element of C independently with probability p, then mu(0, 1) = (1 - p)^(-m) E[(-(1 - p)/p)^|R_p| 1{R_p is spanning}]; p = 1/2 gives the uniform form. These are unbiased Monte Carlo estimators of the Moebius number.
L a finite lattice
C a cross-cut
0 < p < 1

$p_b,p_\sigma,p_h,p_f$ satisfy the corresponding origin-integrability and diagonal
Lipschitz conditions of Assumptions~(ass:integ of the paper)--(ass:lip of the paper), and, for some
$c_{\mathrm{pert}}\ge0$, for a.e.\ $t\in[0,T]$ and all
$(\Theta,\mu),(\Theta',\mu')\in\mathcal D_t$,
\begin{multline}
\mathbb{E}\!\Big[\inner{\delta p_b}{G^{\!\top}\delta Y}+\inner{\delta p_\sigma}{G^{\!\top}\delta Z}_F
+\inner{-\delta p_f}{G\delta X}+\!\int_E\!\inner{\delta p_h(e)}{G^{\!\top}\delta U(e)}\nu(\mathrm{d} e)\Big]\\
\le c_{\mathrm{pert}}\,\mathbb{E}\big[|\delta X|^2+|\delta Y|^2+|\delta Z|_F^2+\lVert \delta U\rVert_{L^2(\nu)}^2\big]

\[

$$
\mathbb{Y}^{(\ell)} \otimes \mathbb{V'}^{(\ell)}\in (\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d)^{|\beta^{(\ell)}|},
$$
where we write
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{Y}^{(\ell)} \otimes \mathbb{V}'^{(\ell)} & \supseteq (\bm{y},\bm{v'}) =\bigl((y_{1}^{(1)},{v'}_{1}^{(1)}), \cdots, (y_{\beta_{\ell 1}}^{(1)},{v'}_{\beta_{\ell 1}}^{(1)}), \cdots, (y_{1}^{(J)},{v'}_{1}^{(J)}), \cdots, (y_{\beta_{\ell J}}^{(J)},{v'}_{\beta_{\ell J}}^{(J)})\bigr).
\end{align*}

 For $(\bm{y},\bm{v'}) \in \mathbb{Y}^{(\ell)} \otimes \mathbb{V'}^{(\ell)}$ a sampled product position and velocity configuration for one individual $\mathcal{R}_{\ell}$ reaction, $y_{r}^{(j)}$ then labels the sampled position for the $r$th product particle of species $j$ involved in the reaction, and ${v'}_{r}^{(j)}$ labels the sampled velocity for the same product particle. Let $d \bm{y} d\bm{v'}=\bigl(\bigwedge_{j=1}^{J}(\bigwedge_{r=1}^{\beta_{\ell_{j}}} d y_{r}^{(j)}d {v'}_{r}^{(j)})\bigr)$ be the corresponding volume form on $\mathbb{Y}^{(\ell)} \otimes \mathbb{V}'^{(\ell)}$, which also naturally defines an associated Lebesgue measure.

body:
[Lemma one-step-descent-convex of arXiv:2608.29507, 'Denoising as Projection: Constrained Optimization with Gradient-Guided Diffusion'] Let $\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be nonempty, closed, convex, and bounded, and let
   $ D_{\mathcal X}:=\sup_{u,v\in\mathcal X}\|u-v\|<\infty .$
Suppose that $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ is $\mu$-strongly convex and $L$-smooth on a convex neighborhood containing the iterates and $\mathcal X$. Let
    $x^\star:=\arg\min_{x\in\mathcal X} f(x),~~
    G_\star:=\|\nabla f(x^\star)\|.$
Consider the update in (equation eq:projected-gradient-guidance-relaxed of the paper)
with $\epsilon(1+L\eta)\le 2, \eta\mu<1.$
Assume that, for every $z$, $\widehat\pi_t(z)\in\mathcal X, \|\widehat\pi_t(z)-\pi_{\mathcal X}(z)\|\le E_t.$

Let ~~$ p_t:=\pi_{\mathcal X}(x_t),~n_t:=x_t-p_t,
    ~
    \mathcal V_t:=f(p_t)-f(x^\star)+\frac{1}{2\eta}\|p_t-x^\star\|^2.$
Define
\begin{align*}
    \rho:=1-\epsilon\eta\mu,&
    \quad
    A_{\eta,\epsilon}:=1+\epsilon\eta L,\quad 
    M_\eta:=G_\star+\left(L+\frac{1}{\eta}\right)D_{\mathcal X},
    \quad
    C_\eta:=\frac{L}{2}+\frac{1}{2\eta},\\
   & B_1:=M_\eta A_{\eta,\epsilon},
    \quad
    B_2:=2C_\eta A_{\eta,\epsilon}^2.
\end{align*}
Then
\vspace{-10pt}
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal V_{t-1}
    \le
    \rho\mathcal V_t
    +
    B_1\|n_t\|
    +
    B_2\|n_t\|^2
    +
    \epsilon M_\eta E_t
    +
    2\epsilon^2C_\eta E_t^2.
\end{align*}
Moreover, the normal component satisfies
   $ \|n_{t-1}\|
    \le
    (1-\epsilon)\|n_t\|.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 37 of arXiv:2604.22159, 'Adapted optimal transport between filtered Gaussian processes'] Let $\bX=\bX^{0,L}$ and $\bY=\bX^{0,M}$ be elements of $\cFG$. The minimal transport cost over all Gaussian adapted Brenier couplings is given explicitly (in terms of $L$ and $M$) by

\begin{align*}
\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{AB}}^2(L,M)&:=\;\|L\|_F^2+\|M\|_F^2-2\sum_{t=1}^N \bigg(
\tr\Big( (L^{\intercal} M)_{t,t} |L_{t,t}^\intercal M_{t,t}|^+ (L_{t,t}^{\intercal} M_{t,t})^{\intercal} \Big) \\
&+ \Big\| \big(I - (L_{t,t}^{\intercal} M_{t,t}) (L_{t,t}^{\intercal} M_{t,t})^+\big) (L^{\intercal} M)_{t,t} \big(I - (L_{t,t}^{\intercal} M_{t,t})^+ (L_{t,t}^{\intercal} M_{t,t})\big) \Big\|_*
\bigg),
\end{align*}

[Lem 86 (Controlling the difference between the discrete and continuum heat operators) of arXiv:2510.22155, 'Random walks in space-time random media in all spatial dimensions: the full subcritical fl'] Fix $\alpha<0, \tau>1$. Let $K_N$ be as in Definition \ref{dnlnkn}, and let $K : C^{\alpha,\tau}_\mathfrak s(\Psi_T) \to C^{\alpha+2,\tau}_\mathfrak s(\Psi_T)$ by \begin{align}
   
 			Kf(t,x):= \int_{\Psi_T} G_{t-s}(x-y)f(s,y)dsdy,
 		\end{align} where $G_t$ as usual is the deterministic keat kernel on $\mathbb R^d$. Then we have the operator norm bound $$\|K_N-K\|_{C^{\alpha,\tau}_\mathfrak s(\Psi_T) \to C^{\alpha-1,\tau}_\mathfrak s(\Psi_T)} \leq CN^{-1/4}.$$
		
		
  Here, $C$ is independent of $N$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem 52 of arXiv:2605.23308, 'Convergence rate estimates for semigroups and heat kernels associated with resistance form'] For any $x,y\in F,\;x_n,y_n\in F_n,\;f\in \BL^{\kappa}(M)$ and $i\in\N$, we have that
\begin{align*}
  |G^{\circ i}_xf(y)-(G^n_{x_n})^{\circ i}f(y_n)|
  \leq &\g{c}{itkill}\left( 1+D_n^i +D_n^{i-1}\sum_{j=0}^{i-2}D_n^j\right)\\
  &\qquad\qquad\qquad\times \Bigl\{\|f\|_{K_n}(d(x,x_n)+d(y,y_n))+\|f\|_{\BL^{\kappa}(K_n)}d_{\BL^{\kappa}}(\mu,\mu_n)\Bigr\}, 
\end{align*}
where $\g{c}{itkill}=\diam K_n\mu_n(F_n)^2+(1+\diam K_n)^2\mu_n(F_n)+\diam F+1$.
title: Lem 52 of arXiv:2605.23308

[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2609.02017, 'Optimal girth-dependent bounds for the Bethe approximation of the permanent'] Let $g\geq4$ be even, and let $G=(L\sqcup R,E)$ be a bipartite
graph of girth at least $g$, with $|L|=|R|=n\geq1$. Let $\mu$ be a
probability distribution on the perfect matchings of $G$, and define
$\bs{p}$, $\bs{p}^{X_u}$, and $\on{gap}(u)$ as in
\cref{eq:p-defns,eq:p-defns-cond,eq:gap-def}. Then
\[
  \sum_{u\in L}\on{gap}(u)\geq0.
\]
In particular, there exists a good vertex $u\in L$.

i.e., $\phi(\eta,\eta')=-\phi(\eta',\eta)$ for all $\eta,\eta'\in\Omega$.
We say that a flow is \emph{admissible} if $\phi(\eta,\eta')=0$ unless
$\eta'=\eta^{x,y}$ for a pair $x,y\in\Z^{d}$ such that $c(x,y;\eta)\neq0$.

We say that $\psi_{|\bar{\mathcal{D}} \cap U}$  is a $\Gamma$-convex function if, for any geodesic curve $\gamma$ on $\bar{\mathcal{D}} \cap U$, the function $\psi\circ\gamma:\,[0,1]\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ is convex.

Let G be a finite group and p a prime dividing the order |G|. Then G contains an element of order exactly p, hence a subgroup of order p. More precisely (McKay), the number of solutions to x^p = e in G is a multiple of p, and since x = e is one of them, there are at least p - 1 elements of order p; in fact the number of elements of order p is congruent to -1 modulo p. Cauchy's theorem is the p^1 case of Sylow's first theorem (a subgroup of order p^a exists whenever p^a divides |G|) and is the converse of Lagrange's theorem for prime orders; the converse of Lagrange fails in general (A_4 has order 12 and no subgroup of order 6).

body:
[Theorem thm:vector-valued of arXiv:2608.01279, 'Stochastic heat equation with nondegenerate Hölder diffusion coefficient: uniqueness below'] Let \(d\geq1\), \(\beta\in(2/3,1)\), and let
\[
    G:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{d\times d}
\]
be a measurable mapping that satisfies the following two conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item For some constant \(c_G>0\),
\[
    G(z)G(z)^{*}\geq c_G^2 I_d,
    \qquad z\in\mathbb R^d,
\]
\item    For some constant \([G]_{C^\beta}<\infty\),
\begin{equation}
    \|G(z)-G(z')\|_{\mathrm{HS}}
       \leq [G]_{C^\beta}\|z-z'\|^\beta,
    \qquad \forall z,z'\in\mathbb R^d.
    
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

Consider the following vector-valued stochastic heat equation
$$
    \partial_t U
      =\Delta U+G(U)\dot W,
      \qquad
      U(0)=u_0\in L^2(\mathbb T;\mathbb R^d),
$$
where \(W=(W^1,\ldots,W^d)\) is a \(d\)-dimensional
space--time white noise.

Then weak uniqueness holds for the above equation in
$
    C\bigl([0,T];L^2(\mathbb T;\mathbb R^d)\bigr)
$
for every \(T>0\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Finite-dimensional vector-field SHEs

body: [Lemma 16 of arXiv:2512.04807, 'Existence and uniqueness of the canonical Brownian motion in non-simple conformal loop ens'] Let $\vertexset$ be a finite set and $w_n\colon \vertexset\times\vertexset \to [0,\infty)$ be a sequence of edge conductances such that each $(\vertexset,w_n)$ is connected. Let $R_n\colon \vertexset\times\vertexset \to [0,\infty)$ be the associated effective resistance metrics. Suppose that $R_n \to R$ for some $R\colon \vertexset\times\vertexset \to [0,\infty)$ with $R(x,y) > 0$ for each $x \neq y$. Then there exists $w\colon \vertexset\times\vertexset \to [0,\infty)$ such that $w_n \to w$ and $R$ is the effective resistance associated with $w$.

[Lemma 128 (Fixed local functional-calculus construction) of arXiv:2606.29292, 'Intrinsic Gaussian Tensor Geometry and Random Operator Spectra'] Let $I\Subset(0,\infty)$ be compact and let $A\ge1$.  Fix the atlas,
cutoffs, and left semiclassical quantization described above.  For each chart
$\nu$ there are linear maps
\[
  \vartheta\longmapsto a_{\nu,\ell}[\vartheta],
  \qquad 0\le\ell<A,
\]
from $\mathscr X_I$ to $C_c^\infty(U_\nu\times\R^d)$ and, for
$0<h\le1$, a linear remainder map
$\vartheta\mapsto\mathcal R_{\nu,A,h}[\vartheta]$ such that
\begin{equation}

  (\chi_\nu\vartheta(P_h)u)\circ\varkappa_\nu
  =\sum_{\ell=0}^{A-1}h^\ell
       a_{\nu,\ell}[\vartheta](z,hD_z)
       ((\widetilde\chi_\nu u)\circ\varkappa_\nu)
    +\mathcal R_{\nu,A,h}[\vartheta]u
\end{equation}
for $u\in C^\infty(M)$.  The coefficient symbols satisfy
\begin{equation}

  \operatorname{supp}a_{\nu,\ell}[\vartheta]
  \subset
  \bigl\{(z,\xi):
     \varkappa_\nu(z)\in\operatorname{supp}\chi_\nu,
     \ p_\nu(z,\xi)\in\operatorname{supp}\vartheta\bigr\},
\end{equation}
and have the finite form
\begin{equation}

  a_{\nu,\ell}[\vartheta](z,\xi)
  =\sum_{j=0}^{J_{\nu,\ell}}
      c_{\nu,\ell,j}(z,\xi)
      \vartheta^{(j)}(p_\nu(z,\xi)),
\end{equation}
where the smooth coefficients $c_{\nu,\ell,j}$ depend only on the fixed
local construction.  If $s_-,s_+\ge0$ and $A\ge s_-+s_+$, then, for every
fixed $\vartheta\in\mathscr X_I$,
\begin{equation}

  \sup_{0<h\le1}
  h^{-(A-s_--s_+)}
  \|\mathcal R_{\nu,A,h}[\vartheta]\|_{
       H^{-s_-}(M)\to H^{s_+}(\R^d)}<\infty.
\end{equation}

body: [Corollary 3.4 (Estimation of wavelet coefficients / $S$) in the first version of arXiv:2512.18592, 'Wavelet Latent Position Exponential Random Graphs'] Assume the conditions of Theorem 3.3. Let $f(x,y):=\log\!\Big(\frac{W(x,y)}{1-W(x,y)}\Big)$ denote the logit of $W$. Under Definition 3.1 we have $\|f\|_{\infty}\leq B$ for a fixed constant $B<\infty$, hence $W$ is uniformly bounded away from $0$ and $1$. Fix a clipping level $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)$ and let $\widehat{W}_{n}^{\mathrm{clip}}$ be the clipped estimator from Theorem 3.3. Define $\widehat{f}_{n}(x,y):=\log\!\Big(\frac{\widehat{W}_{n}^{\mathrm{clip}}(x,y)}{1-\widehat{W}_{n}^{\mathrm{clip}}(x,y)}\Big).$ Let $\{\Psi_{\lambda}\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ be the tensor-product orthonormal wavelet basis used above and define the coefficient arrays $\beta:=\big(\langle f,\Psi_{\lambda}\rangle\big)_{\lambda\in\Lambda},\qquad\widehat{\beta}_{n}:=\big(\langle\widehat{f}_{n},\Psi_{\lambda}\rangle\big)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}.$ Equip coefficient arrays with the $\ell^{2}(\Lambda)$ (Hilbert–Schmidt) norm $\|T\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^{2}:=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}T_{\lambda}^{2}$. Then there exists a constant $C_{1}^{\prime}>0$ (depending only on $s,p,q,M,B$ and $\varepsilon$) such that, with the same exponent $C_{2}$ as in Theorem 3.3, $\sup_{W\in\mathcal{F}^{s}_{p,q}(M)}\mathbb{E}\,\|\widehat{\beta}_{n}-\beta\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^{2}\leq C_{1}^{\prime}\,N_{n}^{-\frac{2s}{2s+2}}(\log N_{n})^{C_{2}}.$

body:
[Corollary 11 (Consistency of FP selection) of arXiv:2608.20998, 'Free-Probability Kernels for Zero-Rollout Hyperparameter Selection in Reservoir Computing'] Assume that the deterministic kernel and the finite reservoir use the
same feature map. Fix finite candidate and ridge grids, with all ridge
parameters strictly positive. For any fixed maximum retained lag $L$,
if the deterministic validation score has a unique minimizer, then
finite-width reservoir selection returns the same minimizer with
probability tending to one as $n\to\infty$.

In the stable regime, a unique complete-history optimum is preserved
by all sufficiently large finite contexts, and selection based on the
complete finite-reservoir trajectory converges to this optimum as
$n\to\infty$.

body:
[Lemma lem:singleton-renewal of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] For a Kac plane $i$, let
\[
 W_i^\circ=\Pi_{\mathcal W}(\mathsf P_i-N^{-1}I_W)
\]
be its pure-Weyl coefficient.  On the common star space, with an arbitrary
passive ancillary Hilbert space $E$, put
\[
 (\mathsf M h)(i,\theta)=(W_i^\circ\otimes I_E)h(i,\theta),
 \qquad \mathsf J=\mathscr E^*\mathscr E,
 \qquad \mathsf Q=I-\mathsf J.
\]
Relative to $\operatorname{ran}\mathsf J\oplus
\operatorname{ran}\mathsf Q$, write
\[
 \mathsf M=
 \begin{pmatrix}0&\mathsf S^-\\ \mathsf S^+&\mathsf V\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{3.2.10n}
\]
We call $0,\mathsf S^-,\mathsf S^+,\mathsf V$ the four
\emph{star statuses} of a passive singleton; a status record chooses one
of these four blocks for every singleton after equal-time fusion.  These
statuses are distinct from the derivative-placement coefficients
$(\alpha,\beta)$ used in the Ricci root calculus.
Then
\[
 \|\mathsf S^-\|=\|\mathsf S^+\|
 \le\sqrt{\frac{n-3}{N(n-1)}}\le N^{-1/2},
 \qquad \|\mathsf V\|\le2,
\tag{3.2.10o}
\]
and the one-sided utilized-step maps factor through the innovation:
\[
 \mathscr E\mathsf M\mathscr T=\mathscr E\mathsf M\mathscr G,
 \qquad
 \mathscr T^*\mathsf M\mathscr E^*
 =\mathscr G^*\mathsf M\mathscr E^*.
\tag{3.2.10p}
\]
Consequently a passive singleton isolated between invariant separators is
zero.  A run of $s\ge2$ passive singletons with $s-1$ prescribed finite
Green gates has norm at most
\[
 \frac{2^{2s-3}}N.
\tag{3.2.10q}
\]
Thus its two endpoints create one $N^{-1}$ resource and every interior
singleton transports that same resource; no additional token is created.
The same conclusion holds when an endpoint is a $\mathscr D$- or
$\mathscr L$-incidence, with the corresponding mixed bound of
(lem:riesz of the paper) and with the already existing root or packet token
transported.

[Proposition 11 of arXiv:2609.02779, '2609.02779'] Let $\omega:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ be nondecreasing, with $\omega(0)=0$ and
$\omega(r)\to0$ as $r\downarrow0$.  There exists $V\in C^\infty(\T)$ such that
\[
  V\le0,\qquad V^{-1}(0)=\{0\},\qquad

\]
and, for $H(x,p)=\frac12p^2+V(x)$, the corresponding discounted solutions satisfy
\begin{equation}
  \|u_\lambda-u_0\|_\infty\ge\omega(\lambda)
\end{equation}
for every sufficiently small $\lambda>0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 43 (Finite-order Cauchy--Dirichlet estimate for scalar-principal systems) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Fix \(m\geq2\) and \(\sigma\in(0,1)\).  Let
\(Q_i^+=\Omega_i\times[a,a+\theta]\), where
\(\Omega_1\Subset\Omega_2\) are smooth Euclidean domains.  Suppose that a
smooth finite-dimensional vector-valued function \(Z\) satisfies on
\(Q_2^+\)
\[
 \partial_tZ-a^{ij}\partial_i\partial_jZ
 =\mathsf B^i\partial_iZ+\mathsf CZ+G,
\]
where \(a^{ij}=a^{ji}\) is uniformly parabolic and
\(\partial_t-a^{ij}\partial_i\partial_j\) acts componentwise with the same
coefficient matrix on every component; only \(\mathsf B^i\) and
\(\mathsf C\) may couple components.  The coefficients
\(a^{ij},\mathsf B^i,\mathsf C\) have uniformly bounded
\(C^{m-2+\sigma,(m-2+\sigma)/2}\)-norms.  Assume that \(Z=0\) on the initial
face, and that \(Z\) and \(G\) vanish in a fixed spatial collar of
\(\partial\Omega_2\times[a,a+\theta]\).  Then
\[
 \|Z\|_{C^{m+\sigma,(m+\sigma)/2}(Q_1^+)}
 \leq C\left(
   \|G\|_{C^{m-2+\sigma,(m-2+\sigma)/2}(Q_2^+)}
   +\|Z\|_{C^0(Q_2^+)}\right),
\]
where \(C\) depends only on the displayed coefficient and parabolicity bounds,
\(m,\sigma,\theta\), the rank, and the fixed domains \(\Omega_1\Subset
\Omega_2\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Finite-order Cauchy--Dirichlet estimate for scalar-principal systems

$\sreg\ge0$, $\preg\in\Real$ and $0<T\le1$. For every
$f_0\in Y^{\sreg,\preg}$,

$G\in L^{2}_tY^{\sreg,\preg-1}(\Rst)$ there is
$u$ on $\Rst$ with
\[
 \Box u=G\quad\text{on }[0,T],\qquad
 (u,\partial_tu)|_{t=0}=(f_0,f_1),
\]
satisfying
\begin{equation}
\big\|u\big\|_{H^{\sreg,\preg}_{\breg}}

 +T^{\varepsilon}\big\|G\big\|_{L^{2}_tY^{\sreg,\preg-1}}\Big),
\end{equation}
where $C_{\rm lin}=C(\chi,\breg)$ is independent of $T\le1$, of the
field, of the data and of the indices $\sreg,\preg$. Moreover,
\[
 u\in C([0,T],Y^{\sreg,\preg})
 \cap C^1([0,T],Y^{\sreg,\preg-1}).

body: [Lemma prop:crossing_distances_of_small_annuli_are_small of arXiv:2609.04140, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ III:\\ uniqueness'] Suppose that we have the same setup as in (lem:crossing_distances_of_small_annuli_are_uniformly_small of the paper). Let $\epsilon>0$.	 Then,  there exist constants $c_1,R_0>1$ (depending only on $x,y$,  $\epsilon$,  and $F$) and $c_2>0$ (depending only on $x,y$,  and $F$) such that the following is true for all $R \geq R_0$ and all $z \in F$. The probability that both $P$ and $\widetilde{P}$ intersect $\overline{B_{2^{-R}}(z)}$ before intersecting each other is at most $c_1 2^{-(2-\epsilon)R}$.  Moreover,  for all $c>0$ and conditioned on the event that both $P$ and $\widetilde{P}$ intersect $\overline{B_{2^{-R}}(z)}$ before intersecting each other,  the following holds off an event with conditional probability at most $c_1 e^{-c_2 c}$.  Let $t$ (resp.\ $\widetilde{t}$) be the first time that $P$ (resp.\ $\widetilde{P}$) intersects $\overline{B_{2^{-R}}(z)}$.  Then,  the distance between $P|_{[0,t]}$ and $\widetilde{P}|_{[0,\widetilde{t}]}$ with respect to $D_\Gamma$ (equivalently,  since $P$ is a $D_\Gamma$-geodesic,  the quantity $\len(P|_{[t , 1-\widetilde{t}]} ; D_\Gamma)$) is strictly less than $c / R$.

body: [Definition 8 of arXiv:2609.03875, 'Measure theory without infinities'] Let $\mf A$ be an HTM. A map $\mu$ is said to be an $\mf A$-valued $\sigma$-additive function if $\im\mu\subset \mf A$ and $\mu(A) = \sum \mu\circ\mb A$ for every $A\in D_\mu$ and every countable partition $\mb A$ of $A$ into elements of $D_\mu$. A map $\mu$ is called an $\mf A$-valued $\sigma$-content (premeasure)  if $\mu$ is an $\mf A$-valued $\sigma$-additive function and $D_\mu$ is a ring (resp., a $\delta$-ring).

body:
[Corollary 43 of arXiv:2607.21374, 'Local structure at the maximum and sharp persistence asymptotics of rough fractional Brown'] Let
\begin{equation*}
  h_n=2^{-r_n}\downarrow0,
  \qquad
  u_n,L_n\in h_n\mathbb Z_{\geq0},
  \qquad
  u_n\to0,
  \qquad
  L_n\to\infty.
\end{equation*}
Put
\begin{equation*}
  P_{h,u,L}:=(\mathscr M_{u,L})_*Q_{h,u,L},
  \qquad
  P_u:=(\mathscr A_u)_*Q^u\quad(u>0),
\end{equation*}
and let \(P_0\) be the law on \(\mathcal Y\) with zero lifetime, height, and
left arm, and right arm \((G_s)_{s\geq0}\) under \(Q^0\).  Thus
\(K_0=P_0\).  Then
\begin{equation}
\begin{gathered}
  \mathcal L_{Q_{h_n,u_n,L_n}}
    \bigl(W|_{[0,\infty)}\bigr)
  \Longrightarrow Q^0
  \quad\text{in }C_{\mathrm{loc}}([0,\infty)),\\
  P_{h_n,u_n,L_n}\Longrightarrow P_0,
  \qquad
  K_{h_n,u_n,L_n}\Longrightarrow K_0
  \quad\text{in }\mathcal Y.
\end{gathered}
  
\end{equation}
Consequently, the arm-valued map \(u\mapsto P_u\) and the endpoint-tilted map
\(u\mapsto K_u\) are weakly continuous on \([0,\infty)\).

[Definition def: distance and ball of arXiv:2606.13147, 'Scaling limits of the single-curve interface and outermost loops in the planar random fiel'] For any $I\subset \Lambda_M$ and any $x\in I$, recalling that
$\bar{\partial}\Lambda_M=
\partial\Lambda_M
\cup \partial\Lambda_{M/2}(u_i)
\cup \partial\Lambda_{M/4}(u_i),$
define
\[
d_x
=
\min\Big\{
{\operatorname{dist}}(x,\bar{\partial}\Lambda_M),
\min_{y\in I\setminus\{x\}}{\operatorname{dist}}(x,y)
\Big\}.
\]
 When $I=\{x\}$, we use the convention that $\min_{y\in I\setminus\{x\}}{\operatorname{dist}}(x,y)=\infty$.
	In addition, we write
	$$
	\mathrm{Ball}(I):=\bigcup_{x\in I}\Lambda_{d_x/10}(x).
	$$
    Here and throughout, whenever the subscript of $\Lambda$ is not an integer, it is understood to be rounded down to the nearest integer. In particular, $\Lambda_{d_x/10}$ stands for $\Lambda_{\lfloor d_x/10\rfloor}$, and the same convention applies to quantities such as $\Lambda_{d_x/9}$.  Moreover, we adopt the convention that  $\Lambda_{d_x/10}(x)=\{x\}$ whenever $d_x/10<1$.

[Theorem thm:taylor-eta2345 of arXiv:2607.02013, 'Resolution of the Detection Threshold Conjecture for Random Geometric Graphs in the $d>n$ '] There exist numerical constants $c,C>0$ such that the following holds. For $2\le k\le 5$, define the functions
\begin{align*}
E_2(x_1,x_2) 
&\triangleq \zeta^2\mathsf{S}_{2,1}\,,\\
E_3(x_1,x_2,x_3)
&\triangleq (1-1/d) a\zeta^3 \mathsf{S}_{3,2}\,,\\
E_4(x_1,\ldots,x_4)
&\triangleq \zeta^4 \mathsf{S}_{4,2}\,,\\
E_5(x_1,\ldots,x_5)
&\triangleq (1-1/d)a\zeta^5 \mathsf{S}_{5,3}\,,
\end{align*}
where $\mathsf{S}_{v,e}$ is the weighted sum over all graphs on vertex set $[v]$ with $e$ edges, such that each vertex is covered by at least one edge:
\begin{align*}
\mathsf{S}_{2,1} &= W_{12}\,,\\
\mathsf{S}_{3,2} &= W_{12} W_{13}
    +W_{12} W_{23}+W_{13} W_{23}\,,\\
\mathsf{S}_{4,2} &= W_{12} W_{34}
+
W_{13} W_{24}
+
W_{14} W_{23}\,,\\
\mathsf{S}_{5,3} &= \sum_{h=1}^5
\sum_{\{i,j\}\subset [5]\setminus\{h\}}
W_{hi}W_{hj}W_{uv},
\qquad
\{u,v\}=[5]\setminus\{h,i,j\}\,.
\end{align*}
Define the residuals $R_k\equiv \eta_k-E_k$. On the event $a^2\delta_k \le c$, 
    \[|R_k| \le C \left( \frac{p}{1-p}\right)^{k/2} (a^2\delta_k)^{\lceil k/2\rceil +1}\]
for all $2\le k\le 5$.

Additionally, we have
$$
|\eta_5(x_1,\ldots,x_5)|
\le C \left(\frac{p}{1-p}\right)^{5/2}(a^2\delta_5)^3
$$ as an overall bound for $k=5$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:taylor-eta2345 of arXiv:2607.02013

[Proposition 6 (All-partition normalization) of arXiv:2608.29585, '2608.29585'] Let $K$ be an oriented zero-framed knot.  For every $N\ge2$ and every
partition $\lambda$ with at most $N$ parts,
\begin{equation}
 \HH_\lambda(K;q^N,q)=J_K(V(\lambda);q^2).
\end{equation}
Here the right side is computed with the Hopf and ribbon convention
\eqref{eq:Hopf}--\eqref{eq:HL-R-convention}.  Thus the scalar family used
below in the algebraic dual interpolation formula is the standard reduced
colored HOMFLY--PT family.

[Lem 16 of arXiv:2605.15501, 'Well-posedness of the obstacle problem for generalized Dean--Kawasaki equation\thanks{ The'] (A priori estimates
for the kinetic measure) Let Assumption \ref{assu:assu for existence} and Assumption \ref{assu:assum for F} hold.

For any $n\in\mathbb{N}$
and $\alpha,\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, let $u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}$
be a solution to \eqref{eq:appro penalized eq}, then for all $N_{1},N_{2}\in(0,\infty)$
such that $N_{1}<N_{2}$, there exists a constant $C$ independent
of $n$, $\alpha$, $\varepsilon$, $N_{1}$ and $N_{2}$ such that
\begin{align}
 & \mathbb{E}\int_{x,t}\mathbf{1}_{\{u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}\in(N_{1},N_{2})\}}\Phi^{\prime}(u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon})|\nabla_{x}u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}|^2+\alpha\mathbb{E}\int_{x,t}\mathbf{1}_{\{u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}\in(N_{1},N_{2})\}}|\nabla_{x}u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}|^2\\
 & +\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\mathbb{E}\int_{x,t}\int_\theta|(u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}-\psi)^+|^2 \mathbf{1}_{\{u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}\in(\theta^{-1}(N_{1}-\psi)+\psi,\theta^{-1}(N_{2}-\psi)+\psi)\}}\nonumber\\
 & \leq C(N_2-N_1)\mathbb{E}\int_x (u_{\mathrm{init}}-N_1)^{+}
+C\mathbb{E}\int_{x,t}\mathbf{1}_{\{u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}\geq N_{1}\}}|\sigma_{n}(u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}\land N_{2})|^{2}.\nonumber
\end{align}
In particular, we have
\begin{align}
 & \lim_{N\rightarrow \infty}\Big[\mathbb{E}\int_{x,t}\mathbf{1}_{\{u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}\in(N,N+1)\}}\Phi^{\prime}(u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon})|\nabla_{x}u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}|^2 +\alpha\mathbb{E}\int_{x,t}\mathbf{1}_{\{u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}\in(N,N+1)\}}|\nabla_{x}u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}|^2\nonumber\\
 & +\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\mathbb{E}\int_{x,t}\int_\theta|(u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}-\psi)^+|^2 \mathbf{1}_{\{u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}\in(\theta^{-1}(N-\psi)+\psi,\theta^{-1}(N+1-\psi)+\psi)\}}\Big]=0.
 \end{align}
title: Lem 16 of arXiv:2605.15501

body:
[Theorem 32 (Regular Bartlett spectrum without a Fourier CLT) of arXiv:2608.22342, 'Completely Positive Entropy and Fourier Central Limit Theorems for Stationary Random Measu'] The stationary ergodic random measure $\eta$ defined by
\eqref{eq:rs-random-measure} has zero entropy and Bartlett density
\eqref{eq:rs-bartlett-density}. For every $\xi$ with $s_\eta(\xi)>0$, the sequence $W_N(\xi)$ does not
converge to any centered complex Gaussian law. In particular,
\begin{equation}

    W_N(\xi)\not\dto\mathcal{CN}(0,s_\eta(\xi)),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}

    |W_N(\xi)|^2
    \not\dto s_\eta(\xi)\operatorname{Exp}(1).
\end{equation}
Moreover, for every such $\xi$ there is $h\in C_c^\infty(\bR;\bC)$ for
which $R^{-1/2}M(h(\cdot/R)\chi_\xi)$ does not converge, as $R\to\infty$,
to $\mathcal{CN}(0,s_\eta(\xi)\lVert h\rVert_2^2)$. In particular, a bounded
continuous Bartlett density, positive $\lambda_1$-almost everywhere, does not
imply an almost-everywhere-frequency empirical Fourier CLT.

body:
[Proposition prop:it-results of arXiv:2608.23554, 'Provably adaptive sampling with uniform and remasking \\ discrete diffusion models'] Let $(X_t)_{t\in[0,T]}$ be a CTMC with rate matrices $(Q_t)_{t\in[0,T]}$ as in~(def:ctmc of the paper). Then,
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item 
    \[ \mathrm{DTC}(X_t) + \mathrm{TC}(X_t) = \sum_{i \in [d]} \mathrm{I}(X_t^i\ ;\, X_t^{-i}); \]

    \item for $i \in [d]$, it satisfies 
    \[ \frac{\partial}{\partial v}\mathrm{I}(X_t^i\ ;\,X_v^{-i}) = \bE_{x_t^i, x_v^{-i}} \left[\left(Q^{-i}_v \log \Pr(X_t^i = x_t^i \mid \cdot\ )\right)(x_v^{-i})\right]; \]

    \item for $i \in [d]$, we have
    \[ \frac{\partial}{\partial t}\mathrm{I}(X_t^i\ ;\,X_v^{-i}) = \frac{\partial}{\partial t} \mathcal{H}(X_t^i) + \bE_{x_t^i, x_v^{-i}} \left[\left(Q^{i}_t \log \Pr(\,\cdot \mid X_v^{-i} = x_v^{-i}\,)\right)(x_t^i)\right]; \]

    \item 
    \begin{align*}
        \sum_{i \in [d]} \frac{\partial}{\partial v} \mathrm{I}(X_t^i\ ;\, X_v^{-i}) \bigg\rvert_{t = v} &= \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} v} \mathrm{DTC}(X_v), \qquad \text{and} \qquad
        \sum_{i \in [d]} \frac{\partial}{\partial t} \mathrm{I}(X_t^i\ ;\, X_v^{-i}) \bigg\rvert_{v = t} = \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} t} \mathrm{TC}(X_t);
    \end{align*}

    \item for fixed $x_v^{-i}$, $j$, and $b$, let us define  
    \[ r(a) = \frac{\Pr(X_t^i = a \mid X_v^{-i} = x_v^{-i})}{\Pr(X_t^i = a \mid X_v^{-i} = x_v^{-i} \odot_j b)}.\]
    It then obeys
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{\partial^2}{\partial t \partial v} \mathrm{I}(X_t^i\ ;\, X_v^{-i}) 
        &= \bE_{x_v^{-i}} \sum_{j \neq i} \sum_{a, b, c}\cQ_v(x_v^j, b) \cQ_t(a, c)\Pr(X_t^i = a \mid x_v^{-i} \odot_j b) \times \left[r(a) \log \frac{r(a)}{r(c)} + r(c) - r(a) \right].
    \end{align*}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:it-results of arXiv:2608.23554

[Lemma lem:submartingale-occupation of arXiv:2509.08430, 'One-dimensional particle clouds with elastic collisions'] Let $X = (X_n)_{n \in {\mathbb Z}_+}$ be an ${\mathbb R}_+$-valued process, adapted to
    a filtration $({\mathcal F}_n)_{n \in {\mathbb Z}_+}$. Suppose that there exist $B \in {\mathbb R}_+$ and $v \in (0,\infty)$
    such that, for all $n \in {\mathbb Z}_+$,
    \begin{align}
    
    \Pr [ X_{n+1} - X_n  \leq B ] & = 1; \\
        
        \Exp [ X_{n+1} - X_n \mid {\mathcal F}_n ] & \geq 0, \ \text{a.s.}; \\
        
        \Exp [ (X_{n+1} - X_n)^2 \mid {\mathcal F}_n ] & \geq v, \ \text{a.s.}
    \end{align}
Then, for any $\gamma \in (0,1/2)$ and any $\varepsilon \in (0, \frac{1-2\gamma}{4})$, for all $n$ sufficiently large, 
\[ \Pr \Bigl[ {\mathcal L}^X_n (n^{\gamma}) \geq n^{\frac{1}{2} + \gamma + 4\varepsilon} \Bigr] \leq {\mathrm{e}}^{-n^\varepsilon} ,
\text{ and } \Exp {\mathcal L}^X_n (n^{\gamma}) \leq n^{\frac{1}{2} + \gamma + 4\varepsilon} . \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:submartingale-occupation of arXiv:2509.08430

[Cor cor312 of arXiv:2609.02795, 'Global smooth behavior in Kuznetsov and Westervelt type\\ viscous wave equations:\\ A unif'] Let $p\ge 2$ and $r\ge p$ be such that $r<\frac{np}{(n-2)_+}$.

	+ \Gamma_1(\varepsilon,p,r) \cdot \bigg\{ \int_\Omega \varphi^2 \bigg\}^\frac{p}{2}.
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 36 of arXiv:2604.25877, 'Asymptotic height of Plancherel random trees'] Recall that
$
\kappa(t)=\log \Gamma(t)+\log \Gamma(\theta+1)-\log \Gamma(\theta+t)$ and $
v_\star=\sup_{t>1}(-\frac{\kappa(t)}{t})$.
There exists $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that for every
\[
a\in (v_\star,\,v_\star+\varepsilon_0),
\]
there exists a unique $t\in(1,\infty)$ satisfying
$a=-\kappa'(t)$.

body:
[Definition of arXiv:2411.17104, 'Two-barriers-reflected BSDE with Rank-based Data'] Funcition $v(\cdot,\cdot)\in C([0,T]\times \Gamma^{n})$ is called a viscosity subsolution (respectively, supersolution) of ($(4 of the paper)$) on condition that  it satisfies for any $ x\in \Gamma^{n}$
\[
g(x)\geq v(T,x)\;(respectively,\;g(x) \leq v(T,x) ),
\]
and for any $(P,q,M)\in \bar{\mathcal K}_{v}^{2,+}(t,x)$, we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
	\left\{\begin{array}{l}
		\min\Big\{v(t,x)-L(t,x),\max\Big\{ v(t,x)-U(t,x),\\
\qquad\qquad \qquad \qquad\qquad \qquad-P-\delta\cdot q-\frac{1}{2}tr(\sigma^{2}M)-G(t,x,v(t,x),\sigma q)  \Big\}\Big\} \leq 0,\;x \in \Pi^{n}, \\
		\min\Big\{q_{k+1}-q_{k},\min\Big\{ v(t,x)-L(t,x),\max\Big\{v(t,x)-U(t,x), \\
\qquad\qquad \qquad \qquad\qquad \qquad-P-\delta\cdot q-\frac{1}{2}tr(\sigma^{2}M)-G(t,x,v(t,x),\sigma q) \Big\}\Big\}\Big\} \leq 0,\;x \in F_{k},\;k=1,\cdots,n.\\
	\end{array}\right.
\end{eqnarray*}
(respectively, for any $(P,q,M)\in \bar{\mathcal K}_{v}^{2,-}(t,x)$, we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
	\left\{\begin{array}{l}
		\min\Big\{v(t,x)-L(t,x),\max\Big\{ v(t,x)-U(t,x),\\
\qquad\qquad \qquad \qquad\qquad \qquad-P-\delta\cdot q-\frac{1}{2}tr(\sigma^{2}M)-G(t,x,v(t,x),\sigma q)  \Big\}\Big\} \geq 0,\;x \in\Pi^{n}, \\
		\max\Big\{q_{k+1}-q_{k}, \min\Big\{v(t,x)-L(t,x),\max\Big\{ v(t,x)-U(t,x),\\
\qquad\qquad \qquad \qquad\qquad \qquad-P-\delta\cdot q-\frac{1}{2}tr(\sigma^{2}M)-G(t,x,v(t,x),\sigma q)  \Big\}\Big\}\Big\}\geq 0,\;x \in F_{k},\;k=1,\cdots,n.)\\
	\end{array}\right.
\end{eqnarray*}

In all, if a function $v(\cdot,\cdot)\in C([0,T]\times \Gamma^{n})$ is both a viscosity subsolution and a supersolution, it is called a viscosity solution to ($(4 of the paper)$).

body: [Definition Cone-points of arXiv:2509.04333, 'The limiting law of the Discrete Gaussian level lines'] The $\delta$-forward cone from ${\ensuremath{\mathsf u}}$ is the set $\ensuremath{\mathcal Y}^\blacktriangleleft_\delta({\ensuremath{\mathsf u}}) := {\ensuremath{\mathsf u}} + \{(x, y) \in \mathbb Z^2: |y| \leq \delta x\}$. Similarly, the backward cone from ${\ensuremath{\mathsf u}}$ is the set $\ensuremath{\mathcal Y}^\blacktriangleright_\delta({\ensuremath{\mathsf u}}) = {\ensuremath{\mathsf u}} - \{(x, y) \in \mathbb Z^2: |y| \leq \delta x\}$. When $\delta$ is omitted from the notation, we assume $\delta = 1$. When ${\ensuremath{\mathsf u}}$ is omitted from the notation, we assume ${\ensuremath{\mathsf u}} = (0, 0)$. For a disagreement polymer $\gamma$, ${\ensuremath{\mathsf u}}$ is a cone-point of $\gamma$ if $\gamma \subset \ensuremath{\mathcal Y}^\blacktriangleright({\ensuremath{\mathsf u}}) \cap \ensuremath{\mathcal Y}^\blacktriangleleft({\ensuremath{\mathsf u}})$. Similarly, for an animal $\Gamma = [\gamma, \underline{\ensuremath{\mathsf W}}]$, ${\ensuremath{\mathsf u}}$ is a cone-point for $\Gamma$ if $\Gamma \subset \ensuremath{\mathcal Y}^\blacktriangleright({\ensuremath{\mathsf u}}) \cap \ensuremath{\mathcal Y}^\blacktriangleleft({\ensuremath{\mathsf u}})$.

Let T be a bounded subset of R^n, let eps_1, ..., eps_n be independent Rademacher signs, and let phi_i : R -> R be 1-Lipschitz with phi_i(0) = 0 for every i. Then E sup_{t in T} sum_{i=1}^n eps_i phi_i(t_i) <= E sup_{t in T} sum_{i=1}^n eps_i t_i. With ABSOLUTE VALUES inside the supremum the same statement holds with a factor 2: E sup_{t in T} | sum_i eps_i phi_i(t_i) | <= 2 E sup_{t in T} | sum_i eps_i t_i |. The distinction between the constants 1 and 2 is a standard source of misquotation; the constant 1 belongs to the version WITHOUT absolute values. The hypothesis phi_i(0) = 0 is needed for the version without absolute values and can be arranged by subtracting a constant, which is harmless for a symmetric process. In statistical learning the principle is what lets one strip a Lipschitz loss off a function class without changing the Rademacher complexity by more than a constant. [Ledoux and Talagrand, Probability in Banach Spaces, Theorem 4.12]
phi_i 1-Lipschitz with phi_i(0) = 0
eps_i independent Rademacher signs
T bounded so the suprema are finite; constant 1 WITHOUT absolute values, 2 WITH them

[Corollary 145 (Exterior lossless representation) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Equip the restarted exterior response image with the topology and
truncations transported from the corresponding $(x,A,q)$ increment-field
space through its degree-one and degree-two coordinates.
On the principal Hilbert operational state space, the restarted response
\[
 z\longmapsto\bigl((\mathscr E(x_{s,t},A_{s,t}))_{s,t},q\bigr)
\]
is stable-causal and lossless.  Hence it represents the same causal state as
the restarted It\^o signature.  Its scalar even--odd energy response is a
canonical nonlinear spectral scalarization: it is not lossless, but it
recovers exactly the unitary-invariant data described in
\Cref{thm:even-odd-spectral-decoding}.

[Lemma norm of arXiv:2412.00865, 'On the spectral problem and fractional diffusion limit for Fokker-Planck with(-out) drift '] $[LebPu,NaPu]$
For initial datum $f_0 \in Y^p_F(\mathbb{R}^{2d})$ where $p \geqslant 2$ and a positive time $T$.  \smallskip

\noindent 1.  The solution $f^\varepsilon$ of (equation fp-theta of the paper) is bounded in $L^\infty\big([0,T];Y^p_F(\mathbb{R}^{2d})\big)$ uniformly with respect to $\vare$ since it satisfies 
\begin{equation}\|f^\varepsilon(T)\|^p_{Y^p_F(\mathbb{R}^{2d})}+\frac{p(p-1)}{\theta(\varepsilon)}\int_0^T\int_{\mathbb{R}^{2d}}\bigg|\nabla_v\bigg(\frac{f^\varepsilon}{F}\bigg)\bigg|^2 \bigg|\frac{f^\varepsilon}{F}\bigg|^{p-2}\ F\ \mathrm{d}v \mathrm{d}x \mathrm{d}t \leqslant \|f_0\|^p_{Y^p_F(\mathbb{R}^{2d})}.
\end{equation}
2.  The density $\rho^\varepsilon(t,x)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}f^\varepsilon \ \mathrm{d}v$ is such that
\begin{equation} 
\|\rho^\varepsilon(t)\|^p_{L^p(\mathbb{R}^d)} \leqslant \|F\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)}^{p-1} \|f_0\|^p_{Y^p_F(\mathbb{R}^{2d})}\quad \mbox{ for all } \quad t\in [0,T].
\end{equation}
3.  Up to a subsequence, the density $\rho^\varepsilon$ converges weakly star in $L^\infty \big([0,T]; L^p(\mathbb{R}^d)\big)$ to $\rho$.  \smallskip

\noindent 4.  Up to a subsequence, the sequence $f^\varepsilon$ converges weakly star in $L^\infty \big([0,T]; Y^p_F(\mathbb{R}^{2d})\big)$ to the function $f=\rho(t,x)F(v)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma pathlength of arXiv:2606.27844, 'Critical percolation on preferential attachment graphs with infinite variance'] Let
$\mathcal{N}_k(\mathcal G_{n,\mu}^{_{(2)}})$ the set of vertices $x\in\{m+1,\ldots,n\}$, which are connected to $\mathcal G_{n,\mu}^{_{(2)}}$ by a shortest path of length at least $k$.  Then for any $k\ge\big\lfloor\tfrac{1-\gamma}{2\gamma-1}\big\rfloor +1  $ we have 
$$\frac{\#\mathcal{N}_{2k+1}(\mathcal G_{n,\mu}^{(2)})}{n\beta(n)^{\alpha/2}}\overset{\mathbb P}{\longrightarrow }0\qquad \text{ in probability.}$$
Also, all vertices at even distances are negligible, that is
$$\frac{1}{n\beta(n)^{\alpha/2}}\sum_{k=1}^\infty \#\big(\mathcal{N}_{2k}(\mathcal G_{n,\mu}^{(2)})\setminus \mathcal{N}_{2k+1}(\mathcal G_{n,\mu}^{(2)})\big)
\longrightarrow 0\qquad \text{ in probability.}$$
In particular if $\gamma>\tfrac23$, then
$$\frac{\#\mathcal{N}_2(\mathcal G_{n,\mu}^{(2)})}{n\beta(n)^{\alpha/2}}\longrightarrow 0\qquad \text{ in probability.}$$

[Corollary prop:conditioned_Bernoulli1 of arXiv:2506.10765, 'A General Coupling for Ising Models and Beyond'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite graph, $x_e\in (0,1)$ for each $e\in E$. Let $\Omega = \{0,1\}^E$, $\Sigma \subset \Omega$ , $f:\Omega\to 2^{\Sigma}$ be defined by $f(\omega)= \Sigma^{\downarrow}(\omega):=\{\eta \in \Sigma: \eta \subset \omega\}$ as well as
	$$\rho[\omega] \propto \mathbb{P}_{x}[\omega], ~\forall \omega\in \Omega, ~\gamma[\eta]\propto 1, ~\forall \eta\in \Sigma. $$
    	Then, under the coupling measure $\mathscr{P}$ defined in Theorem (thm:generalcoupling of the paper), 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)] The marginal of $\mathscr{P}$ on $\Sigma$ is $\mathscr{P}_{\Sigma}[\eta]=\mathbb{P}_{\frac{x}{1+x}}[\eta \mid \Sigma] \propto \prod_{e\in \eta} x_e$. 
        For each $\omega\in\Omega$ with $\mathscr{P}_\Omega[\omega] \neq 0$, the  conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\;\cdot \mid \omega]
        = \mathtt{UG}[\;\cdot \mid \Sigma^{\downarrow}(\omega)]$- the uniform subgraph of $\omega$ which belongs to $\Sigma$.
        \item[(b)]The marginal of $\mathscr{P}$ on $\Omega$ is $\mathscr{P}_\Omega= \mathscr{P}_{\Sigma} \cup \mathbb{P}_x$.
        For each $\eta\in\Sigma$ with $\mathscr{P}_{\Sigma}[\eta]\neq 0$, the conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\;\cdot \mid \eta] = \mathbb{P}_x \cup \delta_{\eta}$. 
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 35 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] Let $\Psi\in C^1([-L,L])$ and put $\phi=e^{-\Psi}u$. Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\cA_{\sigma,m,L}\phi(x)
&=e^{-\Psi(x)}\bigg[
\frac1{\sigma^m}\left\{\int_{-L}^{L}J_\sigma(x-y)e^{\Psi(x)-\Psi(y)}u(y)\,dy-u(x)\right\}\\
&\hspace{32mm}+q(x)u'(x)+(a(x)-q(x)\Psi'(x))u(x)\bigg].
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, multiplication by $e^{-\Psi}$ preserves the generalized principal value after conjugation.

body: [Definition Nash equilibrium and coarse correlated equilibrium of arXiv:2608.24731, 'Optimal Alternating Regret for Online Learning and Games\thanks{Authors are alphabetically'] A joint strategy profile $(\boldsymbol{x}, \boldsymbol{y})$ is an \emph{$\epsilon$-Nash equilibrium ($\epsilon$-NE)} if $u_1(\boldsymbol{x}, \boldsymbol{y}) \le \min_{\boldsymbol{x}' \in \+X} u_1(\boldsymbol{x}', \boldsymbol{y}) + \epsilon$ and $u_2(\boldsymbol{x}, \boldsymbol{y}) \le \min_{\boldsymbol{y}' \in \+X} u_2(\boldsymbol{x}, \boldsymbol{y}') + \epsilon$. A distribution $\sigma$ over joint strategy profiles $\+X \times \+Y$ is an \emph{$\epsilon$-coarse correlated equilibrium ($\epsilon$-CCE)} if $\-E_{(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y})\sim \sigma}[u_1(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y})] \le \min_{\boldsymbol{x}' \in \+X}\-E_{(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y})\sim \sigma}[u_1(\boldsymbol{x}',\boldsymbol{y})] + \epsilon$ and $\-E_{(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y})\sim \sigma}[u_2(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y})] \le \min_{\boldsymbol{y}' \in \+Y}\-E_{(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y})\sim \sigma}[u_2(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y}')] + \epsilon$.
title: Nash equilibrium and coarse correlated equilibrium

body:
Load-bearing hypotheses: (1) the growth bound $|F(z)|\le Ce^{A|z|}$ must hold for all complex $z$, not merely on $\mathbb R$; (2) $F$ must be square integrable on $\mathbb R$ (for the $L^2$ version) or have controlled polynomial growth (for the distributional version). Failure of (1): $F(z)=e^{-z^2}$ is entire and its restriction to $\mathbb R$ is in $L^2$, yet $|F(iy)|=e^{y^2}$, so $F$ is of order 2, not of exponential type; its Fourier transform is a Gaussian, supported everywhere - no band limitation. Failure of (2): $F(z)=\cos(Az)$ is entire of exponential type exactly $A$ and bounded on $\mathbb R$, but not in $L^2(\mathbb R)$; it is not $\int_{-A}^A\varphi(t)e^{itz}dt$ for any $\varphi\in L^2$, only for the measure $\frac12(\delta_A+\delta_{-A})$ - the correct statement in that regime is the Paley-Wiener-Schwartz theorem for compactly supported distributions, with a polynomial factor $(1+|\zeta|)^N$ allowed. Similarly $F(z)=e^{Az}$ has type $A$ but grows on the real axis. Two further traps: the exponential factor in Paley-Wiener-Schwartz measures the support of the transform only through the supporting function of its convex hull, so the theorem detects $\operatorname{ch}(\operatorname{supp}u)$, not the support itself; and no such function can have both itself and its transform compactly supported, since a nonzero entire function cannot vanish on an open set (see Benedicks' theorem for the measure-theoretic strengthening).
F entire on C (or C^d)
claims of band limitation require the growth bound off the real axis
L^2 version needs square integrability on R; distributions need the polynomial-growth version
title: Pitfall: Paley-Wiener Needs Exponential Type in Every Direction Plus Integrability on the Line

[Definition d:fun of arXiv:2508.21658, 'Infinite-dimensional stochastic differential equations for Coulomb random point fields'] \thetag{i} 
For $ \sss \in \sSS $, a coordinate of $\sss $ on $ \SR $ is a tuple 
$\mathbf{x}_{\rR }(\sss ) = (x_{\rR }^i(\sss ))_{i} 
\in \sqcup_{m=1}^{\infty} \SRm $ such that $ 
\piR (\sss ) = \sum_{i} \delta_{x_{\rR }^i(\sss )}$. 

\noindent \thetag{ii} The restriction $ \mathbf{x}_{\rR }^m (\sss ) $ of $ \mathbf{x}_{\rR }(\sss ) $ on $ \SRm $ is called the $ \SRm $-coordinate. 

\noindent \thetag{iii}
Let $ f:\sSS \to \mathbb{R} $ and $ \rR,m \in \mathbb{N} $. 
We say that $ f_{\Rs }^m $ is the $ \SRm $-representation of $ f $ if 
$ f_{\Rs }^m(\mathbf{x}) $ is a function on $ \SRm $ such that
\begin{align}\notag 
f_{\rR,\cdot}^m : \sSS \times \SRm \to \mathbb{R}, 
\qquad (\sss,\mathbf{x}) \mapsto f_{\Rs }^m(\mathbf{x}),
\end{align}
and the following conditions hold:
\begin{align}

\notag & f_{\Rs }^m(\mathbf{x}) \ \text{is symmetric in $\mathbf{x}$ for each $ \sss \in \SSRm $}
,\\

\notag 
& f_{\rR,\sss(1)}^m(\mathbf{x}) = f_{\rR,\sss(2)}^m(\mathbf{x}) 
\ \text{if } \piRc (\sss(1)) = \piRc (\sss(2))
,\\

\notag 
& f_{\Rs }^m(\mathbf{x}_{\rR } (\sss )) = f(\sss ) 
\ \text{for } \sss \in \SSRm,\\

\notag & f_{\Rs }^m(\mathbf{x}) = 0 
\ \text{for } \sss \notin \SSRm.
\end{align}
We define $ f _{\Rs }$ on $ \sqcup_{m\in\N } \SRm $ by $ f _{\Rs } (\mathbf{x}) = f_{\Rs }^m(\mathbf{x}) $ for $ \mathbf{x} \in \SRm $.
title: Definition d:fun of arXiv:2508.21658

Conjectured bond analogue (do not treat as an established theorem without reviewing a current proof): Let G be an infinite connected locally finite graph with finitely many vertex orbits under its automorphism group. In independent Bernoulli bond percolation with p_c(G)<1, the configuration at p_c(G) almost surely has no infinite open edge cluster. Benjamini and Schramm expressly said their nonplanar questions extend to bond percolation; Hutchcroft's 2016 theorem proves the exponential-growth subcase. A September/October 2026 release claims the full bond statement, but that claim is not certified by this draft.

[Lem density bound of arXiv:2602.22342, 'Sum of Gaussian vectors and large sets'] For some universal $\kappa\in (0,1)$, if $S$ is a real-valued $\kappa$-subgaussian variable, then there is a standard Gaussian random variable $G$ such that $S+G$ has distribution $f(x)dx$ where  $f:\R\to \R$ is a piecewise continuous function that satisfies
$$C^{-1} \varphi(x-y_0)\leq f(x) \leq C\varphi(x-y_0)$$
for some $y_0\in [-1,1]$ depending on $S$ and for some  universal constant $C\geq 1$.
