body:
Assuming NP is not contained in P/poly, there exists an efficiently computable normalizable weighted language p_tilde for which no ELNCP weighted language q_tilde has support(q_tilde)=support(p_tilde). The p_tilde constructed in the companion Theorem1 card has this property, so its support is even a polynomial-time decidable language. This is exact support separation for locally normalized models with compact nonuniform parameters, not a distribution-approximation or finite-precision lower bound.
Complexity assumption NP is not a subset of P/poly; the assumption is stronger than merely P!=NP.
Finite binary alphabet and finite strings of unbounded length; exact rational output for the constructed weights.
ELNCP is efficient local normalization with compact parameters: a fixed polynomial-time scheme with polynomial-size nonuniform advice for each prefix-length bound returns the actual next-symbol and termination conditional probabilities at positive-mass prefixes up to that bound.
Exact representability and conditional evaluation are the subject; no assertion about approximation in TV or KL follows from this theorem alone.

[Lemma 14 ({\cite{borel}}) of arXiv:2609.01128, 'Nonabelian Chabauty for the Thrice-punctured Line over Cyclotomic Fields'] $K_{2n-1}(\cO_{K,S})\otimes \bQ$ has the $\bQ$-dimension
$$d_n=\begin{cases}
r_1+r_2+\#S-1, & n=1,\\
r_1+r_2, & n\geq 3\quad \mathrm{odd},\\
r_2, & n\geq 2\quad \mathrm{even},
\end{cases}$$
where $r_1,r_2$ denote the number of real embeddings and pairs of complex embeddings of $K$.
For $n=1$, there is a canonical isomorphism $K_1(\cO_{K,S}) \otimes \bQ \cong \cO_{K,S}^\times\otimes\bQ$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 6 (Characterization by Bernoulli variables) of arXiv:2607.12365, 'Bernoulli--Doob representation, asymptotic limits and boundary behavior of bounded homogen'] Let $(\Omega,\cF,\FF,\Pr)$ satisfy the usual conditions with
$\cF=\cF_\infty$. Define $Z_t=\E[B\mid\cF_t]$ where
$B\sim\mathrm{Ber}(z)$. Then $Z$ is an $\FF$-martingale bounded
in $[0,1]$ with $Z_0=z$.

Moreover, suppose $\FF$ is a Brownian filtration and $Z$ is a
continuous time-homogeneous Markov process. Then $Z$
can be written as a homogeneous diffusion
\[
dZ_t = \sigma(Z_t)\,dW_t\quad\text{where}\quad Z_0=z
\]
for some $\sigma:[0,1]\to[0,\infty)$ and an $\FF$-Brownian motion
$W$. Furthermore, $\sigma(b)=0$ at any boundary $b\in\{0,1\}$
reachable in finite time.

body:
Own-work draft: proof (unaudited); C011 v2 has no independent PASS. For fixed n>=2, x0*y0!=0, zero-sum fixed b_i of variance s>0, common-Hessian f_i=x^2/2+kappa*y^2/2+b_i*x and kappa log(T)/T -> c in (0,infinity) excluding 4/3: if c<4/3 then T eta_opt/log T ->3/2 and min P~(27 n(n+1)s/384)log^3(T)/T^3; if c>4/3 then min P~(x0^2/2)exp(-4T/kappa), T(eta_opt-2/kappa)->0, and kappa eta_opt->2, for every global minimizer over eta>=0. Here T=nK with K epochs, each using a fresh independent uniform permutation of the n components; s=(sum_i b_i^2)/n>0. The initial point (x0,y0) and component linear terms remain fixed as T grows. P_T(eta) is the expected excess of the average objective F(x,y)=x^2/2+kappa_T*y^2/2 at the final iterate after T component-gradient steps, using constant eta throughout. Curvature is normalized to mu=1 and kappa_T>=1. No assertion is made at c=4/3, for growing n, or for general noncommuting finite sums.
T=nK, fresh independent uniform permutation each epoch
Fixed n, b_i, nonzero initial x0,y0; s>0; no stiff-coordinate linear terms
kappa>=1 and kappa log(T)/T ->c>0, c!=4/3

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:ab4ff9ca0abf3dfb7e5ca7cd659cdf5ae4a3c592a8a1c14e52748fc874240805","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/ab/ab4ff9ca0abf3dfb7e5ca7cd659cdf5ae4a3c592a8a1c14e52748fc874240805.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:3f4826bdfdc0beb3a53785e6f6e9de113e274a65dbc724e785f67bb3ec4ff22c","bundle_entry_key":"zero-stiff-noise-critical-ratio","bundle_id":"population.t362-zero-stiff-noise-010","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Finite-sum strongly convex quadratic optimization; common diagonal Hessian; fixed n","draft":"w732/bundle_010.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.randomreshuffling:common-hessian-random-reshuffling-zero-stiff-noise-critical-threshold","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C011 v2: zero stiff noise in the critical condition-number regime

Status: proof (unaudited). Independent review required. No priority claim.
Target 1 only; this uses the approved C001 recursion and C003 flat-variance expansion, not different component Hessians.

Fix n>=2, T=nK tending to infinity, fixed x0!=0, y0!=0, and fixed zero-sum b_i with s=mean b_i^2>0. Set
f_i(x,y)=x^2/2+kappa_T*y^2/2+b_i*x, kappa_T>=1.
Each epoch uses a fresh independent uniform permutation. Let P_T(eta) be expected final objective error and minimize over every eta>=0. Assume kappa_T log(T)/T -> c in (0,infinity), excluding c=4/3. Define A=x0^2/2, Y=y0^2/2 and D=n(n+1)s/48, all strictly positive. Then every global minimizer satisfies:

(a) If 0<c<4/3:
    T eta_T/log(T) -> 3/2,
    min P_T ~ (27D/8) log(T)^3/T^3.
(b) If c>4/3:
    min P_T ~ A exp(-4T/kappa_T),
    T(eta_T-2/kappa_T) -> 0, and kappa_T eta_T -> 2.

The actual kappa_T, not merely its first-order equivalent, is retained in (b).

## 1. Exact decomposition and facts already proved
By C001 write, with a=1-eta,
P_T(eta)=A a^(2T)+R_T(eta)+kappa Y(1-kappa eta)^(2T).
R_T is the flat-coordinate noise contribution; it is nonnegative for every eta. For eta->0 and T eta->infinity, the C003 fixed-n flat-variance sandwich gives
    R_T(eta)=D eta^3(1+o(1)).
For eta->0 without this divergence it still gives R_T(eta)=O(eta^3) on eta>0, because the finite-horizon factor is at most one. The last epoch and pair (0,1) give, for every eta>=0,
    R_T(eta)>=s eta^4/[2(n-1)].
These are invoked as settled dependencies, not new results. The exact P_T is a continuous coercive polynomial; for example its stiff deterministic term has positive leading coefficient kappa^(2T+1)Y. Thus global minimizers exist.

## 2. Subcritical candidate, 0<c<4/3
Let ell=log(T) and eta_c=3ell/(2T). Then q_c=kappa eta_c ->3c/2 in (0,2), so eventually |1-q_c|<=rho for a fixed rho<1. The stiff initial term is O(kappa rho^(2T))=o(ell^3/T^3). Here kappa=O(T/ell), and exponential decay dominates any fixed polynomial. The slow initial term equals A T^-3(1+o(1)), because T eta_c^2=O(ell^2/T)->0. The flat variance is asymptotic to D eta_c^3. Hence
    min P_T <= (27D/8+o(1))ell^3/T^3.                 (2)

## 3. All subcritical global optimizers
The quartic bound and (2) imply eta_T->0. If t_T=T eta_T were bounded on a subsequence, A(1-eta_T)^(2T) would remain bounded away from zero, contradicting (2). Thus t_T->infinity, and R_T(eta_T)=D eta_T^3(1+o(1)). This and (2) imply t_T=O(ell), hence T eta_T^2->0. Comparing the slow initial term with (2) gives
    2t_T >=3ell-3log(ell)-O(1).
Therefore liminf t_T/ell>=3/2. Comparing the variance with (2) gives limsup t_T/ell<=3/2. Consequently t_T/ell->3/2 and the variance lower bound matches (2), proving (a). This applies to every choice of a global minimizer; a failure of uniform localization would produce a contrary sequence.

## 4. Supercritical candidate, c>4/3
Put r=T/kappa, ell=log(T), delta=3ell/T, q_c=2-delta and eta_c=q_c/kappa. Eventually 0<delta<1 and 0<eta_c<1. Since r~ell/c and T/kappa^2=O(ell^2/T),
    A(1-eta_c)^(2T)=A exp(-4r)(1+o(1)).
Indeed 2T eta_c=4r-2r delta and r delta=O(ell^2/T)->0; the quadratic logarithmic remainder is also O(ell^2/T). The stiff term obeys
    kappa Y(1-delta)^(2T)<=kappa Y exp(-2T delta)
                                   =kappa Y T^-6=O(T^-5/ell).
The flat variance is O(eta_c^3)=O(ell^3/T^3).
Since exp(-4r)=T^(-4/c+o(1)) and 4/c<3, both error terms are o(exp(-4r)). For a formal comparison, choose epsilon>0 with 4/c+epsilon<3; eventually exp(4r)<=T^(4/c+epsilon). Thus
    min P_T <= A exp(-4r)(1+o(1)) ->0.              (4)

## 5. Supercritical global lower bound and steps
If q_T=kappa eta_T>=2, then |1-q_T|>=1 and P_T(eta_T)>=kappa Y, contradicting (4). Thus eventually 0<=eta_T<2/kappa<1. On this interval the slow deterministic contribution gives
    P_T(eta_T)>=A(1-eta_T)^(2T)
              >=A(1-2/kappa)^(2T)
               =A exp(-4r)(1+o(1)).
The final expansion is valid because T/kappa^2->0. Combine with (4) to prove the error equivalent. Uniformly over eta in [0,2/kappa], the logarithmic remainder O(T eta^2) is o(1), so
    A(1-eta_T)^(2T)/(A exp(-4r))
      =exp(2T(2/kappa-eta_T)+o(1)) <=1+o(1).
The difference 2/kappa-eta_T is nonnegative. Taking logarithms forces T(2/kappa-eta_T)->0. Multiplication by kappa/T~c/ell->0 gives q_T->2. This proves (b).

## Scope and failure cases
The critical value c=4/3 is unpaid; subleading deviations of kappa can affect the relative slow bias and flat variance there. No conclusion is made for growing n or changing b_i/initialization. y0!=0 is essential to step 5: if y0=0, the stiff coordinate stays exactly zero and the objective and its optimized value are independent of kappa. x0!=0 and s>0 are essential to the balancing argument. The results concern this common-Hessian finite sum only and do not solve general last-iterate RR.

Prior work: C001/C003 and the 18 Oct common-Hessian work credited in PRIOR_WORK_ATTRIBUTION.md. The 2303.07160/2609.04578 primary-source context is already recorded in SOURCES.jsonl. New OpenAlex search is metadata-only; no priority or literature-exhaustiveness conclusion follows. Least-trusted review steps: all-optimizer localization in step 3 and uniform logarithmic comparison in step 5.

## Verification record and practical limitation

The saved script scripts/check_zero_stiff.py performed 20 exact rational checks of the stiff-instability boundary and 48 Decimal diagnostic optimizations (65-digit arithmetic, two fixed n values, six c values, four horizons). These do not certify global numerical minima or asymptotic limits. At n=3, c=1.4, T=3,000,000,000 the diagnostic value is approximately 596.73 times the supercritical leading term: crossover near 4/3 is extremely slow. No finite-horizon accuracy claim is made. The Lean attempt for q>=2 implying (1-q)^2>=1 timed out after 60 seconds without a certificate; the formal target remains UNVERIFIED. [Definition def:swap of arXiv:2607.14266, 'The Swapping Mechanism for Interacting Diffusions: Framework, Comparison with Switching, a'] Let $\beta_i:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$, $\alpha_i:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$, and
		$\chi_i:\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ be measurable functions, and let
		$\gamma:\mathbb{R}^{2d}\to\mathbb{R}_+$ be measurable. A \emph{swapping process} with
		coefficients $(\beta_i,\alpha_i,\chi_i,\gamma)_{i=1,2}$ is an
		$(\mathcal{F}_t)$-adapted c\`adl\`ag process $Z=(X,Y):\mathbb{R}_+\times\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^{2d}$
		satisfying, for every $t\ge 0$,
		\begin{align}
			X_t &= X_0
			+\int_0^t\beta_1(X_{s-})\mathrm{d} s
			+\int_0^t\alpha_1(X_{s-})\mathrm{d} W^1_s
			+\int_0^t\!\!\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\chi_1(X_{s-},u)\widetilde N^1(\mathrm{d} s,\mathrm{d} u)
			\notag\\
			&\quad+\int_0^t\!\!\int_0^\infty(Y_{s-}-X_{s-})\,
			\mathbf{1}_{\{u\le\gamma(X_{s-},Y_{s-})\}}M(\mathrm{d} s,\mathrm{d} u),
			\\[4pt]
			Y_t &= Y_0
			+\int_0^t\beta_2(Y_{s-})\mathrm{d} s
			+\int_0^t\alpha_2(Y_{s-})\mathrm{d} W^2_s
			+\int_0^t\!\!\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\chi_2(Y_{s-},u)\widetilde N^2(\mathrm{d} s,\mathrm{d} u)
			\notag\\
			&\quad+\int_0^t\!\!\int_0^\infty(X_{s-}-Y_{s-})\,
			\mathbf{1}_{\{u\le\gamma(X_{s-},Y_{s-})\}}M(\mathrm{d} s,\mathrm{d} u).
			
		\end{align}
		At each atom $(t,u)$ of $M$ with $u\le\gamma(X_{t-},Y_{t-})$, the pair
		$(X,Y)$ performs the instantaneous exchange
		$(X_{t-},Y_{t-})\mapsto(Y_{t-},X_{t-})$.
title: Swapping process

body: Witness: endpoints (0,0) and (L,0) on Z^2; one n x W block carrying weight a on every edge, weight b outside. The straight horizontal path is the geodesic, uses exactly n edges of the block, and resampling the block to all-b moves the passage time by exactly (b-a)n. Hence any pointwise a.s. bound B on (X^Lambda - X)^+ over configurations satisfies B >= (b-a)n = Theta(n); for non-atomic laws the same holds up to o(1) by a positive-probability Lipschitz perturbation. Consequence: pointwise-increment routes to fourth-moment control in the resampling engine are pinned at B ~ n on the lattice; only truncation-plus-tail (moment) formulations can charge the increment at a smaller scale. Refereed 2026-08-09 (referee's own witness, D1). Provenance: campaign CRUX section 6d.

[Definition 10 of arXiv:2608.26953, '2608.26953'] Let \(A\) be a \(\Bbbk\)‑algebra. A \emph{differential graded algebra} (DGA) \((\Omega^\bullet,d,\wedge)\) on \(A=\Omega^0\) consists of a graded \(\Bbbk\)-vector space \( \Omega^\bullet =\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\Omega^n,\) with a unital associative, graded product \( \wedge \colon \Omega^p \otimes_\Bbbk \Omega^q \rightarrow \Omega^{p+q},\)
together with a \(\Bbbk\)‑linear differential \(d\colon \Omega^\bullet \rightarrow \Omega^{\bullet+1}\) satisfying \(d^2 = 0\) and the \emph{graded Leibniz rule} \[ d(\alpha \wedge\beta)
= (d\alpha)\wedge\beta + (-1)^{\lvert\alpha\lvert}\alpha\wedge(d\beta) ,
\quad \text{for all homogeneous } \alpha,\beta \in \Omega^\bullet . \] A \emph{morphism} of DGAs 
\(\varphi\colon(\Omega_A^\bullet,d_A,\wedge_A)\rightarrow(\Omega_B^\bullet,d_B,\wedge_B)\)
is a unital degree‑preserving algebra morphism that commutes with the differential. 
The category of all DGAs and their morphisms is denoted \(\mathsf{DG}\). For \(n\geq 0\), \( \mathsf{DG}_n \subseteq\mathsf{DG}\) denotes the full subcategory of DGAs of degrees at most \(n\).

body:
[Theorem thm:hypercube_variance of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] Let $Y = (Y_1, \dots, Y_d)$ and $X = (X_1, \dots, X_d)$ be as in (thm:hypercube_entropy of the paper). 
Then, $\@ifstar{\oldnorm}{\oldnorm*}{\Cov(Y)}_{1,1} \ge \frac{1}{d} \@ifstar{\oldnorm}{\oldnorm*}{\Cov(X)}_{1,1}$

with equality if and only if the following conditions are all satisfied:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item[(i)] The $Y_i$ are uncorrelated.
\item[(ii)] For all $i \in [d]$, $f_{Y_i} = f_{-X_i}$. 
\item[(iii)] $\Cov(X) = \Var(X_i)J_d$, for all $i \in [d]$, where $J_d$ is a p.s.d. matrix with all entries in $\{\pm1\}$. 
\end{enumerate}
\begin{proof}
We compute
\begin{align}
\@ifstar{\oldnorm}{\oldnorm*}{\Cov(Y)}_{1,1} 
&\ge {\rm tr}(\Cov(Y)) \label[ineq]{ineq:hypercube_covariance_1}\\

&\ge 

{\rm tr}(\Cov(X)) \label[ineq]{ineq:hypercube_covariance_2}\\
&\ge \frac{1}{d} \@ifstar{\oldnorm}{\oldnorm*}{\Cov(X)}_{1,1}. \label[ineq]{ineq:hypercube_covariance_3}
\end{align}
(ineq:hypercube_covariance_1 of the paper) 
attains equality exactly when the off-diagonal entries in $\Cov(Y)$ are all zero, i.e., the $Y_i$ are uncorrelated. 
(ineq:hypercube_covariance_2 of the paper) follows from $d$ applications of (thm:VarY_exceeds_VarX of the paper) and the fact that ${\rm tr}(\Cov(Y)) = \sum_i \Var(Y_i)$ (and similar for $X$); 
thus equality is attained in (equation ineq:hypercube_covariance_2 of the paper) exactly when 

$f_{Y_i} = f_{-X_i}$ for all $i \in [d]$. 
Finally, (equation ineq:hypercube_covariance_3 of the paper) follows from (lem:d_tr_dominates_oneone_norm of the paper). 
It is possible for equality to be attained in (equation ineq:hypercube_covariance_3 of the paper); one example is $X_1 = \dots = X_d$. 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:hypercube_variance of arXiv:2607.29020

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2607.29534, 'Expected signatures via partial integration, coordinate change and symmetrization'] Let $A$ be a deterministic path satisfying
    Assumption~\ref{ass:mambo}; in particular, this holds whenever $A$
    contains a time component. Fix
    $x_0\in\mathbb{R}^{|\mathcal{A}^{\prime\prime}|}$, and let
    $\mathbb{P}$ and $\mathbb{Q}$ be probability measures on
    $C([0,T];\mathbb{R}^d)$ such that
    $(\pi_{\mathcal{A}^{\prime}})_{\#}\mathbb{P}
    =
    (\pi_{\mathcal{A}^{\prime}})_{\#}\mathbb{Q}
    =
    \delta_A$, where $\pi_{\mathcal{A}^{\prime}}$ denotes the restriction
    to the $\mathcal{A}^{\prime}$-components, and which are concentrated on
    paths whose $\mathcal{A}^{\prime\prime}$-components start at $x_0$.
    Suppose that the partially symmetrized expected signatures
    $\widehat{\bmu}^{\mathbb{P}}$ and $\widehat{\bmu}^{\mathbb{Q}}$ are well
    defined and that, for every $t\in[0,T]$ and
    $\orange{i}\in\mathcal{A}^{\prime\prime}$, the one-dimensional
    marginals of $X_t^{\orange{i}}$ under $\mathbb{P}$ and $\mathbb{Q}$ are
    moment-determinate. Then
    \[
        \widehat{\bmu}^{\mathbb{P}}
        =
        \widehat{\bmu}^{\mathbb{Q}}
        \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
        \mathbb{P}
        =
        \mathbb{Q}.
    \]

    In particular, the linear functionals
    $X\mapsto\langle\ell,\Sigsym{A,X}_{0,T}\rangle$ form a universal class
    for the approximation of continuous functionals on compact subsets of
    $C([0,T];\mathbb{R}^{|\mathcal{A}^\prime|})$ restricted to paths starting at
    $x_0$, and the map $X\mapsto\Sigsym{A,X}_{0,T}$ is injective on this
    space. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: In complex analysis, the Riemann mapping theorem states that if $U$ is a non-empty simply connected open subset of the complex number plane $\mathbb {C}$ which is not all of $\mathbb {C}$, then there exists a biholomorphic mapping $f$ (i.e. a bijective holomorphic mapping whose inverse is also holomorphic) from $U$ onto the open unit disk $$D=\{z\in \mathbb {C} :|z|<1\}.$$

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2605.12475, 'Central limit theorem for the homozygosity of the hierarchical Pitman-Yor process'] For all $m \geq 1$ and $k \geq 1$, 
\bal
\E[W_k^m(\alpha, \theta_0, \beta, \theta) \mid \bm{V}, \gamma_{1/\beta}] &= \sum_{j=1}^m \Cs(m,j,\beta) \gamma_{1/\beta}^j V_k^j, \\
\E[W_k^m(\alpha, \theta_0, \beta, \theta) \mid \bm{V}] &= \sum_{j=1}^m \frac{\Cs(m,j,\beta) \prod_{s=0}^{j-1} (\theta + s\beta)}{\beta^j} V_k^j,
\eal
where $\Cs(m,j,\beta)$ is the generalized factorial coefficient.

body:
[Lemma lem:limit-kernel-L2 of arXiv:2606.21006, 'Law of the Iterated Logarithm for Weighted Sums of Functionals of Long-Memory Gaussian Seq'] Let \(T<\infty\), and define
\[
Q_t(x)
=
C_{m,\alpha,d}
\left(
    \int_0^t y^{-d}e^{iy(x_1+\cdots+x_m)}\,dy
\right)
\prod_{j=1}^m |x_j|^{(\alpha-1)/2},
\qquad 0\le t\le T.
\]
Assume
\(
    0<\alpha<1,\qquad \alpha m<1,\qquad 2d+\alpha m<2 .
\)
Then:

\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] \(Q_t\in L^2(\mathbb R^m)\) for every \(t\in[0,T]\);
\item[(b)] the map \(t\mapsto Q_t\) is continuous from \([0,T]\) into
\(L^2(\mathbb R^m)\);
\item[(c)]
\(
    \lim_{R\to\infty}
    \sup_{0\le t\le T}
    \int_{([-R,R]^m)^c}|Q_t(x)|^2\,dx
    =0 .
\)
Moreover, for \(0\le s\le t\le T\),
\[
    \|Q_t-Q_s\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^m)}^2
    =
    \widetilde C_{m,\alpha,d}
    \int_s^t\int_s^t
    y^{-d}z^{-d}|y-z|^{-\alpha m}\,dy\,dz ,
\]
where \(0<\widetilde C_{m,\alpha,d}<\infty\).

Here
\(
\widetilde C_{m,\alpha,d}
:=
C_{m,\alpha,d}^2 c_\alpha^m,
\quad
c_\alpha=2\Gamma(\alpha)\cos\left(\frac{\pi\alpha}{2}\right).
\)
In particular, \(\widetilde C_{m,\alpha,d}>0\), although
\(C_{m,\alpha,d}\) itself is signed when \(J_m<0\).

\item[(d)] There exist $C_T<\infty$ and
$\beta:=\min\{2H,\,2-\alpha m\}>0$ such that
\[
    \|Q_t-Q_s\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^m)}^2 \le C_T\,|t-s|^{\beta},
    \qquad 0\le s\le t\le T .
\]
Under the stronger condition $2d+\alpha m<1$, one has $\beta>1$.
\end{itemize}

With the normalization chosen above,
\(
\widetilde C_{m,\alpha,d}
=
\frac{1}{m! I_{m,\alpha,d}},
\)
where
\[
I_{m,\alpha,d}
=
\int_0^1\int_0^1
y^{-d}z^{-d}|y-z|^{-\alpha m}\,dy\,dz .
\]

[Theorem Wanted inequality of arXiv:2607.18531, 'Doubly reflected BSDEs driven by Inhomogeneous simple Lévy processes: Applications to gene'] Let $\big(Y_t,Z_t,V_t,K^{+}_t,K^{-}_t\big)_{t \leq T}$ be the unique solution of the DRBSDE ((basic equation Finance of the paper)). For any $\theta \in \mathcal{T}_{0}^T$, the $\mathcal{E}^f$-value of our game option at any time $\theta$ is given by:
	\begin{equation*}
		\essinf_{\eta_2 \in \mathcal{T}_{\theta}^T} \esssup_{\eta_1 \in \mathcal{T}_{\theta}^T} \mathcal{E}^f_{\theta,\eta_1 \wedge \eta_2}(\mathcal{P}(\eta_1,\eta_2))=Y_{\theta}=\esssup_{\eta_1 \in \mathcal{T}_{\theta}^T} \essinf_{\eta_2 \in \mathcal{T}_{\theta}^T} \mathcal{E}^f_{\theta,\eta_1 \wedge \eta_2}(\mathcal{P}(\eta_1,\eta_2)).
		
	\end{equation*}
	In particular $\mathbf{V}=Y_0$, i.e. the initial value $Y_0$ represents the $\mathcal{E}^f$-value of the game option.
	
	Assume moreover, that $L(S_{\cdot})$ and $-U(S_{\cdot})$ are l.u.s.c.  along stopping times, then the pair $(	\eta^{\theta,\star}_1,	\eta^{\theta,\star}_2)$ given by
	$$
	\eta^{\theta,\star}_1=\inf\{t \geq \theta:Y_t=L(S_t)\} \text{ and } \eta^{\theta,\star}_2=\inf\{t \geq \theta:Y_t=U(S_t)\},
	$$
	defines a $\theta$-saddle point for the game option.

[Prop mixing2 of arXiv:2411.13926, 'Random walks on random walks:\\ non-perturbative results in high dimensions'] Consider the RWRW model on $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^d$ with $d\geq 1$ and  $\lambda >0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[i)]  If for some $\alpha \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^d \setminus \{o\}$ the variance of $\alpha \cdot X_t$ diverges,  then $(\alpha \cdot X_t)$ satisfies the waFCLT of Theorem (thm:main2 of the paper)a) whenever $\lim_{t \rightarrow \infty} \phi(t) = 0$. Moreover, the statement holds with $h(n)=\sigma$ for some $\sigma \in (0,\infty)$ whenever $\sum_{t \geq 1} \sqrt{\phi(2^t)}<\infty$.
\item[ii)] If $\sum_{t \geq 1} \sqrt{\phi(2^t)}<\infty$, $(X_t)$ is truly d-dimensional and $d\geq 3$, then $(X_t)$  satisfies the aFCLT of Theorem (thm:main2 of the paper)b).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let X_1, ..., X_n be independent random variables and let Z = f(X_1, ..., X_n) be a nonnegative random variable with E[Z log Z] finite. Write Ent(Z) = E[Z log Z] - E[Z] log E[Z] and let Ent^{(i)}(Z) denote the same functional computed with respect to X_i alone, with the other coordinates held fixed. Then Ent(Z) <= sum_{i=1}^n E[ Ent^{(i)}(Z) ]. The same statement with variance in place of entropy is the Efron-Stein inequality, and the two are the p = 2 and p = 1 members of a family of phi-entropies that all tensorize. Tensorization is what converts a ONE-DIMENSIONAL functional inequality into an n-dimensional one with no loss of constant: if each coordinate's law satisfies a logarithmic Sobolev inequality with constant C, then the product law satisfies it with the SAME constant C, independent of n. That dimension-free feature is the whole reason the entropy method produces concentration bounds that do not degrade as n grows. Independence of the coordinates is essential. [standard; e.g. Boucheron, Lugosi and Massart, Concentration Inequalities, Theorem 4.10 and Section 4.1]
X_1, ..., X_n independent
Z = f(X) nonnegative with E[Z log Z] finite

Fix any U with E[e^U] <= 1 and let E_i denote conditional expectation given X_1, ..., X_i, with E_0 = E and E_n e^U = e^U. Telescope the exponential rather than U itself: e^U = E[e^U] * prod_{i=1}^n ( E_i e^U / E_{i-1} e^U ), so with U_i = log E_i e^U - log E_{i-1} e^U one has U = log E[e^U] + sum_i U_i <= sum_i U_i, because log E[e^U] <= 0. Hence E[Z U] <= sum_i E[Z U_i]. Now condition on X^{(i)} = (X_j)_{j != i}. By independence, E_{i-1} e^U is a function of X_1, ..., X_{i-1} alone, hence fixed given X^{(i)}, and averaging E_i e^U over X_i with the other coordinates fixed returns E_{i-1} e^U, so E[ e^{U_i} | X^{(i)} ] = 1. The one-variable duality formula, applied in the variable X_i with the others held fixed, then gives E[ Z U_i | X^{(i)} ] <= Ent^{(i)}(Z). Taking expectations and summing over i, E[Z U] <= sum_i E[ Ent^{(i)}(Z) ]; the supremum over admissible U is Ent(Z), which proves the inequality. (The earlier draft telescoped U linearly as E_i U - E_{i-1} U and claimed the conditional normalisation E[e^{U_i} | others] <= 1 by Jensen; that step does not hold, and the log-telescoping above is the standard repair - Boucheron, Lugosi and Massart, proof of Theorem 4.10.)","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:65bc8bd338d9119f2b8ee6c53a7945a71c4d874c489921ae4c702fb50c6fd474","revision_digest":"sha256:4dc336ffe1859932768872cd898d8a70b2b6935d4bd7b90c575ded181869d08f","source_id":"rederived:urn:mb-agent:dc73dee333054e1d-M9","source_revision":"re-derived-2026-08-22 at sketch level; statement and the variational-plus-telescoping proof structure written by the author; textbook cross-reference in the statement, source not fetched this session","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma terms_in_signature_first of arXiv:2411.13707, 'High-degree cubature on Wiener space \\ through unshuffle expansions'] \[
\sum_{1\leq i\leq d}(\epsilon_0,\epsilon_i^2)=\sum_{1\leq i\leq d}\Big (\xi_{0ii}+(\xi_0,\xi_i,\xi_i)\Big ) .
\]
\begin{proof}
Representation (equation eq:expansion of the paper) combined with (cor:parity of the paper) gives,
\[
\begin{aligned}
2\sum_{1\leq i\leq d}(\epsilon_0,\epsilon_i^2)&=\mathrm{e}^{\star 1}\Big (2\sum_{1\leq i\leq d}(\epsilon_0,\epsilon_i^2)\Big )+\mathrm{e}^{\star 3}\Big (2\sum_{1\leq i\leq d}(\epsilon_0,\epsilon_i^2)\Big )\\
&=\mathrm{e}^{\star 1}\Big (\sum_{1\leq i\leq d}(\epsilon_0\epsilon_i^2+\epsilon_i^2\epsilon_0)\Big )+\mathrm{e}^{\star 3}\Big (\sum_{1\leq i\leq d}(\epsilon_0\epsilon_i^2+\epsilon_i^2\epsilon_0)\Big )\\
&=\sum_{1\leq i\leq d}\Big (\xi_{0ii}+\xi_{ii0}\Big )+\sum_{1\leq i\leq d}2(\xi_0,\xi_i,\xi_i)\\
&=\sum_{1\leq i\leq d}\Big (2\xi_{0ii}+2(\xi_0,\xi_i,\xi_i)\Big ),
\end{aligned}
\]
as required, where we use \(\xi_{0ii}=\xi_{ii0}\) (reversal property) to obtain the final equivalence.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 99 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Let $p \in \amsmathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. Consider a variational datum satisfying Assumptions~\ref{Assumption_A}, \ref{Assumption_B} and \ref{Assumption_C}, with segment filling fractions $\hat{\boldsymbol{n}}^0$, and such that for each $h \in [H]$ the segment $[\hat{a}^{\prime\, 0}_h,\hat{b}^{\prime\,0}_h]$ contains a single band of the equilibrium measure. There exists a constant $\delta > 0$ depending only on the constants in the assumptions, with the following properties.

Consider any family of variational data parameterized by $\boldsymbol{t} = (\hat{\boldsymbol{a}}',\hat{\boldsymbol{b}}',\hat{\boldsymbol{n}},u)$ varying in the $\delta$-neighborhood of $\boldsymbol{t}^0 = (\hat{\boldsymbol{a}}^{\prime\,0},\hat{\boldsymbol{b}}^{\prime\,0},\hat{\boldsymbol{n}}^{0},0)$ in $\amsmathbb{R}^{3H + 1}$, such that the first three entries of $\boldsymbol{t}$ represent the segment endpoints and filling fractions and the variational datum for $\boldsymbol{t} = \boldsymbol{t}^0$ coincides with the original one. Suppose that these variational data satisfy Assumption~\ref{Assumption_B} for a $\boldsymbol{t}$-independent tuple of integers $\boldsymbol{\iota}^{\pm}$ and $\boldsymbol{t}$-independent complex domains $(\amsmathbb{M}_h)_{h = 1}^{H}$, and that for any $h \in [H]$ the regular part of the potential $U_h^{\boldsymbol{t}}(z)$ is a $p$-times continuously differentiable function of $\boldsymbol{t}$ --- with any partial derivative up to order $p$ being a holomorphic function of $z \in \amsmathbb{M}_h$.

Then, denoting $\boldsymbol{\mu}^{\boldsymbol{t}}$ the equilibrium measure corresponding to the $\boldsymbol{t}$-dependent variational datum, for any $h \in [H]$ the function
\[
\boldsymbol{t} \longmapsto \Gm_{\mu^{\boldsymbol{t}}_h}(z)
\]
is $p$ times continuously differentiable, with any partial derivative up to order $p$ being a holomorphic function of $z \in \amsmathbb{C} \setminus [\hat{a}_h^{\prime\,\boldsymbol{t}},\hat{b}_h^{\prime\,\boldsymbol{t}}]$. Simultaneously, for any $\boldsymbol{t}$ as above there remains exactly one band per segment and the endpoints of the bands are $p$ times continuously differentiable functions of $\boldsymbol{t}$. All the derivatives depend on the matrix of interactions $\boldsymbol{\Theta}$ in a continuous way.

body:
[Theorem 14 of arXiv:2506.13913, '2506.13913'] {Existence and uniqueness theorem for SDEs}{existence-uniqueness}
Let \((\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t \geq 0}, \mathbb{P})\) be a filtered probability space, and let \(\{W_t\}_{t \geq 0}\) be a standard \(m\)-dimensional Brownian motion adapted to the filtration \(\{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t \geq 0}\). Consider the SDE in \(\mathbb{R}^d\)
\[
\mathrm{d}X_t = \mu(t, X_t) \, \mathrm{d}t + \sigma(t, X_t) \, \mathrm{d}W_t, \quad X_0=Z,
\]
where \(Z\) is a random variable, \(\mathcal{F}_0\)-measurable, with \(\mathbb{E}[\|X_0\|^2] < \infty\). Furthermore, assume the following conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
    \item {Lipschitz continuity:} There exist constants \(L_{\mu}, L_\sigma > 0\) such that for all \(t \in [0, T]\) and \(x, y \in \mathbb{R}^d\)
    \[
    \|\mu(t, x) - \mu(t, y)\| \leq L_{\mu} \|x - y\|, \quad
    \|\sigma(t, x) - \sigma(t, y)\|_F \leq L_\sigma \|x - y\|,
    \]
    where \(\|\cdot\|_F\) denotes the Frobenius norm.
    
    \item {Linear growth:} There exist constants \(K_{\mu}, K_\sigma > 0\) such that for all \(t \in [0, T]\) and \(x \in \mathbb{R}^d\)
    \[
    \|\mu(t, x)\| \leq K_{\mu}(1 + \|x\|), \quad \|\sigma(t, x)\|_F \leq K_\sigma(1 + \|x\|).
    \]
\end{itemize}

Then, there exists a unique stochastic process \(\{X_t\}_{t \geq 0}\) satisfying the SDE such that:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Existence:} The solution \(X_t\) exists, is adapted to \(\{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t \geq 0}\), and satisfies
    \[
    \mathbb{E} \left[ \sup_{t \in [0, T]} \|X_t\|^2 \right] < \infty.
    \]
    \item \textbf{Uniqueness:} If \(\{X_t\}\) and \(\{Y_t\}\) are two solutions with the same initial condition \(Z\), then
    \[
    \mathbb{P} \left( X_t = Y_t, \, \forall t \in [0, T] \right) = 1.
    \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2604.22461, 'Large deviation principles for stationary solutions and invariant measures of a class of S'] [Theorem \ref{thm: stationary solution}] 
 Assume that the conditions {\rm [A1-A5]} hold. If $  \tilde{\gamma}_0<\gamma_0$, then for any $0 \leq \epsilon< \tilde{\epsilon}$, there is a pathwise unique stationary solution $\cY^{\epsilon} \in  L^{\infty}(\R; L^{2}(\Omega; H))$ for cocycle $(U^{\epsilon},\theta)$.
For any $-\infty<t_0<t<+\infty$, the stationary solution $\cY^{\epsilon} \in L^{2}(\Omega;\sC_{-\infty})$ $\P$-a.s. satisfies
\begin{equation}
    \scalV{\cY^{\epsilon}(t),v} = \scalV{\cY^{\epsilon}(t_0),v} + \int_{t_0}^{t} \scalV{A^{\epsilon}(\cY^{\epsilon}(s)),v} \d s + \sqrt{\epsilon} \int_{t_0}^{t} \scalH{B (\cY^{\epsilon}(s)) \, \d W_s,v},
\end{equation}
for any $v \in V$. Conversely, if a $\cF_{t}$-adapted process $\cY^{\epsilon}$ satisfies Eq. \eqref{eq: stationary solution} and $\sup_{t \in \R} \E \|\cY^{\epsilon}(t) \|_{H}^2< +\infty$, then it is indeed the stationary solution for cocycle $(U^{\epsilon},\theta)$. There exists a Borel measurable map $\mathcal{G}^{\epsilon}_{-\infty}: \W \rightarrow \sC_{-\infty}$ such that $\mathcal{G}^{\epsilon}_{-\infty}(W)(\cdot)$ is an $\mathcal{F}_{t}$-adapted solution to Eq. \eqref{eq: stationary solution} and $\sup_{t \in \R} \E \|\mathcal{G}^{\epsilon}_{-\infty}(W)(t) \|_{H}^2< +\infty$, called the strong stationary solution for cocycle $(U^{\epsilon},\theta)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2604.22461

[Def PCPS of arXiv:2607.19511, 'A Conditional Probability Hierarchy for Stochastic Choice\footnote{We thank Samson Abramsk'] Fix a CPS $p : {\cal G} \rightarrow \Delta(\Omega)$. Suppose there is a selection $s$ such that, for each $G \in \cal G$ and $F \in \cal F$:
\begin{equation}~
p_G(F) = \mathbf{1}_F(s(G)).
\end{equation}
That is, each $p_G(\cdot)$ is the Dirac measure concentrated on $s(G)$. We call such a CPS a \textbf{point CPS} (\textbf{PCPS}).

[Definition 49 of arXiv:2603.24616, 'Pinning in non-critical half-space geometric last passage percolation'] Assume the same parameters as in Definition \ref{Def.ParametersEdge} and fix $\kappa \in [0, \bar{\kappa})$. Suppose $x \in [\zc(\kappa), c]$, $\theta \in (0, \pi)$, $R > q^{-1}$ and $r \in [0, q^{-1} - c]$. With this data we define the contour $C(x, \theta, R,r)$ as follows. Let $z^{\pm}$ be the points where the rays $\{x + te^{\pm \im \theta}: t \geq 0\}$ intersect the $x$-centered circle of radius $r$, and let $\zeta^{\pm}$ be the points where they intersect the $0$-centered circle of radius $R$. The contour $C(x, \theta, R,r)$ consists of three oriented segments that connect $\zeta^-$ to $z^-$, $z^-$ to $z^+$, and $z^+$ to $\zeta^+$, as well as the counterclockwise oriented circular arc of the $0$-centered circle that connects $\zeta^+$ to $\zeta^-$. See the left side of Figure \ref{Fig.ContoursEdge}. We also recall that $C_r$ is the positively oriented zero-centered circle of radius $r > 0$. 

For a fixed $a \in \mathbb{C}$ and $\varphi \in (0, \pi)$, we recall from Definition \ref{Def.S1Contours} that $\mathcal{C}_{a}^{\varphi}=\{a+|s|e^{\mathrm{sgn}(s)\im\varphi}, s\in \mathbb{R}\}$ is the infinite contour oriented from $a+\infty e^{-\im\varphi}$ to $a+\infty e^{\im\varphi}$.  For $r > 0$ we define the contour $\mathcal{C}_{a}^{\varphi}[r]$, so that outside of the disc $\{z: |z-a| \leq r\}$ it agrees with $\mathcal{C}_{a}^{\varphi}$ and inside the disc it is a vertical segment that connects $a + re^{-\im \varphi}$ and $a + re^{\im \varphi}$. See the right side of Figure \ref{Fig.ContoursEdge}.

body:
Every real α has a regular continued fraction expansion α = a_0 + 1/(a_1 + 1/(a_2 + ...)) = [a_0; a_1, a_2, ...], produced by the Gauss algorithm: a_0 = floor(α), α_1 = 1/(α − a_0), a_k = floor(α_k), α_{k+1} = 1/(α_k − a_k). Here a_0 is an integer, every a_k (k ≥ 1) is an integer ≥ 1 (the partial quotients), and the α_k are the complete quotients, so a_k < α_k < a_k + 1 whenever the expansion continues. The expansion is finite iff α is rational (then it is unique once the last partial quotient is required to be ≥ 2); for irrational α it is infinite and unique.

The convergents p_n/q_n = [a_0; a_1, ..., a_n] are computed by p_{-1} = 1, q_{-1} = 0, p_0 = a_0, q_0 = 1 and p_{n+1} = a_{n+1} p_n + p_{n-1}, q_{n+1} = a_{n+1} q_n + q_{n-1} for n ≥ 0.

Basic identities: p_n q_{n-1} − p_{n-1} q_n = (−1)^{n-1} for n ≥ 0, so gcd(p_n, q_n) = 1; α = (p_n α_{n+1} + p_{n-1})/(q_n α_{n+1} + q_{n-1}); the even convergents increase strictly to α and the odd convergents decrease strictly to α (for irrational α); |α − p_n/q_n| < 1/(q_n q_{n+1}) < 1/q_n^2. The denominators satisfy 1 = q_0 ≤ q_1 < q_2 < q_3 < ..., with q_0 = q_1 exactly when a_1 = 1. The Gauss map x ↦ {1/x} on (0,1) preserves the Gauss measure dx/((1 + x) log 2), the ergodic-theoretic setting for the statistics of partial quotients.
α real; for the infinite-expansion statements α irrational
title: Regular continued fraction, complete quotients and convergents

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2609.04155, 'The subconvexity problem for symmetric square\\ $L$-functions in Level aspect'] Let $\pi\simeq\bigotimes_\nu^\prime\pi_\nu$ be a cuspidal automorphic representation for $\GL_2(\Q)$ of arithmetic conductor $q(\pi)=p^2$, with the central character $\omega_\pi$, the adelic lift of a primitive non-quadratic Dirichlet character $\chi_\pi$ modulo $p$. If $\pi_\nu$ is tempered for all $\nu<\infty$, $\pi_p\in\mathcal S$, and the spectral parameters of $\pi_\infty$ be bounded, then we have the following subconvex bound, 
         \[
         L\left(\frac{1}{2},\, \sym^2\pi\right)\ll_{\eps, \pi_\infty}q(\sym^2\pi)^{\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{168}+\eps},
         \]
         where the implied constants depends on $\eps$, and polynomially on spectral parameters of $\pi_\infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2609.04155

[Lemma 32 of arXiv:2609.00254, 'On the geometry and cohomology of almost abelian solvmanifolds'] Let $\mu = (\mu_1 \ge \dots \ge \mu_s)$ be the Jordan type of $N$ on $V_\mathbb{C}$. For any $N$-invariant subspace $W \subset V_\mathbb{C}$,
\[
c(W) \leq \sum_{j=1}^{\lfloor s/2 \rfloor} \mu_{2j}.
\]

\]
and the same holds with $f,\ f^-,\ a_n$ replaced by $\widehat f,\ \widehat f^-,\ \widehat a_n$.

[Lemma 36 (No thin visited regions) of arXiv:2607.24561, 'Range convergence and sharp one-arm asymptotics\\for the critical percolation cluster in h'] We invoke Theorem~\ref{thm:ulmb}; we also use the one-arm bound
(Proposition~\ref{prop:KN}).
Fix $K<\infty$, $\kappa\in(0,K)$ and
$\delta\in(0,\kappa/(5\sqrt d)]$. Then for every
$\eta\in(0,1]$,
\begin{multline*}
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\;
n^2\,\bP\Bigl(\exists\,x\in \mathcal C:\ \kappa n\le|x|\le Kn,\
\bigl|\mathcal C\cap \overline B(x,3\sqrt d\,\delta n)\bigr|\le\eta(\delta n)^4\Bigr)
\\
\le\;C(d)\,C_3\,K_2\Bigl(\frac{K}{\delta}\Bigr)^{d}\kappa^{-2}\,\eta^{1/4},
\end{multline*}
where $C_3=C_3(\Lambda)$ with $\Lambda:=(K+\delta)/\delta$ is the
constant of Theorem~\ref{thm:ulmb} and $K_2$ is the constant of the one-arm
bound (Proposition~\ref{prop:KN}). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem infiniteL1subseteqE of arXiv:2608.30491, 'The Daugavet property in symmetric operator spaces'] Let $({\mathcal M}, \tau)$ be a   non-$\sigma$-finite, semi-finite  atomless von Neumann algebra.   
		If a      symmetric  operator  space  $E(\mathcal{M}, \tau)$  
		has the Daugavet property and the associated      symmetric  function  space  $E$ on $(0, \tau({\bf 1}))$ satisfies one of the following  conditions: 
		\begin{enumerate}[\rm(a)]
			\item  $E$  is a KB-space and $E\cap L_{\infty} \neq  L_1 \cap  L_{\infty}$,  
			\item $E$ is uniformly monotone,   
		\end{enumerate}
		then  $L_1  \subseteq  E$ with continuous embedding.

[Prop 13 of arXiv:2609.03185, 'Uniqueness of tangent flows in free boundary flow'] There are $C, L, \epsilon > 0$ and $\gamma \in (0,1)$ with the following property. Suppose that 
$$\tau_0^{-1}, \sup\limits_{s\in [0,1]} d_V(\mu_{\mathscr{C}_+}, \mu_{M_{\tau_0-s}}), \mathcal A^\gamma (M_{\tau_0 - 1}) - \lim\limits_{\tau \to \infty} \mathcal A^\gamma(M_\tau) \leq \epsilon.$$
Then one of the following holds:
\begin{enumerate} [label=\normalfont(\roman*) ]
\item $\mathcal{D}(M_{\tau_0 + L}, M_{\tau_0 + 2L}) \leq Ce^{-\frac{\tau_0}{8}}.$
\item $\mathcal{D}(M_{\tau_0 + L}, M_{\tau_0 + 2L}) \leq \frac{1}{2} \mathcal{D}(M_{\tau_0}, M_{\tau_0 + L}).$
\item $\mathcal{D}(M_{\tau_0 + L}, M_{\tau_0 + 2L}) \leq C \Big(\mathcal A^\gamma(M_{\tau_0 + L}) -\mathcal A^\gamma(M_{\tau_0 + 2L}) \Big).$
\end{enumerate}
title: Prop 13 of arXiv:2609.03185

[Definition 17 of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] A \textbf{particle-production Einstein--Navier--Stokes areal flow} consists of $(\Phi,\Psi,\zeta)$ with $\Phi=(\Jperp,\Jpar,\Pbb,\Qbb)$ and $\Psi=(\ell,\log\Omega,\Kpar)$, satisfying the constraints~\eqref{eqchi-constr}, the evolution equations~\eqref{eqchi-evol}, and the energy conservation equation
\bel{prod-energy-conservation}
\opJ^0_\chi = 0 ,
\ee
together with the same algebraic inequalities~\eqref{eq:causal} on $\amdeux,\Omega,\Jbb$ and periodicity conditions~\eqref{equa-pericons} on $P_1,Q_1$ as in \autoref{def-quadr}.

A \textbf{dissipated-energy Einstein--Navier--Stokes areal flow} consists of $(\Phi,\Psi,\zeta)$ satisfying the inequalities~\eqref{eq:causal}, periodicity~\eqref{equa-pericons}, constraints~\eqref{eqchi-constr}, evolution equations~\eqref{eqchi-evol}, and the dissipated-energy equation
\bel{energy-dissip-Sigma}
\opJ^0_\chi = - \Sigma , \qquad
\Sigma \coloneqq
\frac{\Omega(-\Jbb\cdot\Jbb)}{\Numb^0} \, \mathfrak d_{\mathscr B} ,
\ee
where $\mathfrak d_{\mathscr B} = \zeta_{\alpha\beta} \mathscr B^{\alpha\beta} \geq 0$ is the production term defined in \autoref{def-pot-source}.

[Lemma lem:LG-seed-linear of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] The seed functions $\Psi$ (equation eq:LG-Psi-def of the paper) and $\Phi$
(equation eq:LG-Phi-def of the paper) satisfy the semi-discrete linear
problem (equation eq:sc-linear-1 of the paper)--(equation eq:sc-linear-j of the paper) and
adjoint problem
(equation eq:sc-adjoint-1 of the paper)--(equation eq:sc-adjoint-j of the paper) with edge
weights $(C_k, \Lambda_k)$.  Explicitly:
\[
s\partial_s\Psi(u)
=\Psi(Tu)C_1-\Psi(u)\Lambda_1,
\qquad
\Psi(S_ju)
=\Psi(Tu)C_j-\Psi(u)\Lambda_j,
\]
and
\[
s\partial_s\Phi(Tu)
=\Lambda_1\Phi(Tu)-C_1\Phi(u),
\qquad
\Phi(Tu)
=C_j\Phi(S_ju)-\Lambda_j\Phi(TS_ju).
\]

body:
[Prop ProdContSing of arXiv:2609.01501, 'Singularities of star cluster algebras'] Let $ \mathfrak{X} := V(h) \subseteq \ensuremath{\mathbb{A}}_\kappa^{\ell_1+\cdots + \ell_m} $,
	where
	\[
		h := \prod_{\alpha=1}^m P_{\ell_\alpha} (z_1^{(\alpha)}, \ldots, z_{\ell_\alpha}^{(\alpha)}) + \delta 
		\in \kappa [ z_1^{(\alpha)}, \ldots, z_{\ell_\alpha}^{(\alpha)} \mid \alpha \in \{ 1, \ldots, m \}]
	\]
	with 
	$ \delta \in \kappa $. 
	If $ \delta $ is invertible, 
	then $ \mathfrak{X} $ is singular if and only if the following two conditions hold:
	\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
		\item[(a)] 
		$ \ell_\alpha = 2 k_\alpha $ is even, 
		with $  k_\alpha \geq 1 $,
		for all $ \alpha \in \{ 1, \ldots, m \} $, and 
		
		\item[(b)] 
		$ (-1)^{k_1 + \cdots + k_m} + \delta  = 0 $.
	\end{enumerate}
	In the singular case, $ \Sing (\mathfrak{X}) $ is the origin and the hypersurface $ \mathfrak{X} $ has an isolated singularity of type $ A_1 $ at the origin. 
	\\
	On the other hand, if $ \delta = 0 $, then 
	$ \mathfrak{X} $ is a simple normal crossing divisor with $ m $ disjoint irreducible components, 
	i.e., after a suitable choice of coordinates $ h $ is of the form $ x_1 \cdots x_m $ with $ (x_1, \ldots, x_m) $ part of the chosen coordinates.

[Lem lem111 of arXiv:2609.02795, 'Global smooth behavior in Kuznetsov and Westervelt type\\ viscous wave equations:\\ A unif'] Assume ((h of the paper)), and let $p\ge 2$.
  Then there exist $\Gamma_6=\Gamma_6(p,a,h)>0$ and $\Gamma_7=\Gamma_7(p,a,h)>0$ such that if ((init of the paper)) holds and
  $t\in (0,T_{max}]$ is such that ((uut of the paper)) is satisfied with $\delta_1=\delta_1(h)$ as in Lemma (lem11 of the paper), then for any choice of $r>2$

  \begin{eqnarray}\label{111.1}

	\frac{d}{dt} \int_\Omega |\nabla v|^p

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.26996, 'A note on shifting distributions via Poisson races'] Let $P,Q$ be two distributions over the same finite set.
If $D(Q||P) < \infty$ then
there is a $P$ to $Q$ simulator $I$ such that
\begin{align*}
\E [\log I] 
\leq D(Q||P) + 1.45 \|Q-P\|_1.
\end{align*}
On the other hand, for every $P$ to $Q$ simulator $I$,
\[\E[\log I] \geq \frac{1}{2} \max \{ D(Q||P),  \|Q-P\|_1 \}.\]
In particular, if $D(Q||P)=\infty$ then there is no $P$ to $Q$ simulator. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.26996

body:
[Lemma small-class-of-colimits-cc of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $\textbf{\textup{U}}\subset\ul\Cat_T$ be small. Then the $\infty$-category $\Cat_T^\textup{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cc}$ of $\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cocomplete small $T$-$\infty$-categories and $\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cocontinuous functors has small colimits, and for any small diagram ${\mathcal{C}}_\bullet\colon I\to\Cat_T^\textup{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cc}$ and any ${\mathcal{D}}\in\Cat_T^\textup{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cc}$ the induced map
    \begin{equation}
        \ul{\textup{Fun}}_T^\textup{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cc}(\mathop{\textup{colim}}\nolimits_I {\mathcal{C}}_\bullet,{\mathcal{D}})\to\lim\nolimits_{I^{\textup{op}}}\ul{\textup{Fun}}_T^\textup{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cc}({\mathcal{C}}_\bullet,{\mathcal{D}})
    \end{equation}
    is invertible.
    \begin{proof}
        Fix any small diagram ${\mathcal{C}}_\bullet\colon I\to\Cat_T^\textup{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cc}$ and an extension to a colimit diagram $I^\triangleright\to\Cat_T$. Writing $\infty$ for the terminal object of $I^\triangleright$, it follows that for any $\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cocomplete ${\mathcal{D}}$, the induced equivalence
        \[
            {\textup{Hom}}_{\Cat_T}({\mathcal{C}}_\infty,{\mathcal{D}})\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}\lim\nolimits_{I^{\textup{op}}}{\textup{Hom}}_{\Cat_T}({\mathcal{C}}_\bullet,{\mathcal{D}})
        \]
        then restricts to an equivalence between the union of those path components of the left-hand side given by functors $F\colon{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{D}}$ such that each ${\mathcal{C}}_i\to{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{D}}$ is $\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cocontinuous and $\lim_{I^{\textup{op}}}{\textup{Hom}}_{\Cat_T^\textup{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cc}}({\mathcal{C}}_\bullet,{\mathcal{D}})$. On the other hand, [martiniwolf2022presentable]*{Proposition~A.4.2 and Remark~A.4.3} yield a map ${\mathcal{C}}_\infty\to{\mathcal{C}}_\infty'$ to a small $\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cocomplete $T$-$\infty$-category such that ${\textup{Hom}}_{\Cat_T^\textup{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cc}}({\mathcal{C}}_\infty',{\mathcal{D}})\to{\textup{Hom}}_{\Cat_T}({\mathcal{C}}_\infty,{\mathcal{D}})$ defines an equivalence of the union of the same set of path components. This provides the desired colimit.
        
        To see that $((eq:internal-colimit of the paper))$ is an equivalence, it suffices by the (non-parametrized) Yoneda lemma, that the induced map on ${\textup{Hom}}({\mathcal{K}},-)$ is an equivalence for every ${\mathcal{K}}\in\Cat_T$. However, this induced map may be identified with the equivalence
        \[
            {\textup{Hom}}_{\Cat_T^\text{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cc}}(\mathop{\textup{colim}}\nolimits_I{\mathcal{C}}_\bullet,{\textup{Fun}}({\mathcal{K}},{\mathcal{D}}))\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}
            \lim\nolimits_{I^{\textup{op}}}{\textup{Hom}}_{\Cat_T^\text{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cc}}({\mathcal{C}}_\bullet,{\textup{Fun}}({\mathcal{K}},{\mathcal{D}})).
            \qedhere
        \]        
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma small-class-of-colimits-cc of arXiv:2608.28504

[Definition 5 of arXiv:2607.02777, 'Hypocoercivity for Hamiltonian Diffusions \\ with Singular Drift'] A probability measure $\P$ on $\sZ$ is said to be a solution to the martingale problem associated with $(\sL, \core)$ if for every $f\in \core=C^2_c(\Omega_1\times \Omega_2)$
        \[
            M^f_t:= f(X_t , Y_t ) - f(X_0, Y_0) - \int_0^t \sL f (X_s, Y_s) \,\textup{d}s , \quad t\geq 0, 
        \]
       where $f(\partial)\defeq 0$ and $(\sL f)(\partial)\defeq  0$, is a continuous martingale under $\P$ with respect to the filtration $(\sF_{t+})_{t\geq 0}$.
title: Definition 5 of arXiv:2607.02777

[Def D2.1 of arXiv:2609.03848, 'The mean-field limit of the Schr\"{o}dinger-Lohe model\\ and emergent dynamics'] \emph{[C-C-H]}
Let $\Psi := \{ \psi_k \}$ be a global smooth solution to (equation SL of the paper). 
\begin{enumerate}
\item
The ensemble $\Psi$ exhibits {\em complete synchronization}, if the following estimate holds:
\[ 
\lim_{t \to \infty} \max_{1\le k,l\le N} \| \psi_l(t) - \psi_k(t) \|_{\mathfrak{H}} = 0. 
\]
\item
The ensemble $\Psi$ exhibits {\em practical synchronization},  if the following estimate holds:
\[ 
\lim_{\kappa \to \infty} \limsup_{t \to \infty} \max_{1\le k,l\le N} \| \psi_l(t) - \psi_k(t) \|_{\mathfrak{H}} = 0. 
\]
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem 31 (Law of large numbers) of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{Assumptions_Theta} and \ref{Assumptions_basic} hold.
Fix $h \in [H]$ and let $f$ be a bounded continuous function
defined on $\amsmathbb{A}_h^{\mathfrak{m}}$ for $\N$ large enough. Then
\[
 \lim_{\N\rightarrow\infty} \Bigg| \frac{1}{\N} \sum_{i=1}^{N_h} f\bigg(\frac{\ell_i^h}{\N}\bigg) -\int_{\hat
{a}'_h}^{\hat{b}_h'} f(x) \dd\mu_h(x)\Bigg|=0\qquad \text{in probability.}
\]
 In terms of the Stieltjes transform (Definition~\ref{def_empirical_mes}) for each $\N$-independent  $\varepsilon > 0$ and compact set $\amsmathbb{K}_h$ containing $[\hat{a}_h,\hat{b}_h]$  in its interior for $\N$ large enough, we have
\[
\lim_{\N\rightarrow\infty} \sup_{z\in \amsmathbb{C} \setminus \amsmathbb{K}_h}\,\P\Bigg[\bigg| \frac{G_h(z)}{\N} - \Gm_{\mu_h}(z)\bigg|>\eps\Bigg] =0.
\]
Both limits are uniform over the ensembles satisfying Assumptions~\ref{Assumptions_Theta} and \ref{Assumptions_basic} with fixed constant $C$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Law of large numbers

[Lemma failstep of arXiv:2412.04284, 'Approximately jumping towards the Origin'] Let $k \equiv -1$ modulo 4. Suppose that $z_k$ exists and that $|z_k|=r>1$. If $z_{k}=z_{k+2}$, then 
    $$|z_k|-|z_{k+4}|>r-\sqrt{r^2+4-4\sqrt{r^2-1}}.$$ Furthermore, if $\sqrt{2}<|z_k|<2$, then $z_k \neq z_{k+4}$ and $|z_{k+4}|<\sqrt{2}$.

body:
[Proposition prop:joint-system of arXiv:2507.12502, 'Quantitative Edge Eigenvector Universality for Random Regular Graphs: Berry-Esseen Bounds '] The vector process $\mathbf{X}(t)$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
\mathrm{d}\mathbf{X}(t) = A(t)\mathbf{X}(t)\mathrm{d} t + \Sigma(t)\mathrm{d}\mathbf{B}(t) + \boldsymbol{\mathcal{E}}(t)\mathrm{d} t
\end{equation}
where:
\begin{itemize}
\item $A(t)$ is the drift matrix with entries $A_{ij} = -\frac{1}{2}\delta_{ij} + (1-\delta_{ij})(\lambda_i - \lambda_j)^{-1}$
\item $\Sigma(t)$ is the diffusion matrix with $\Sigma\Sigma^* = \text{Cov}(\mathrm{d}\mathbf{X}/\mathrm{d} t)$
\item $\mathbf{B}(t)$ is a $K$-dimensional Brownian motion
\item $\|\boldsymbol{\mathcal{E}}(t)\| \leq C_1 K^{1/2} N^{-5/6+\varepsilon}$
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Joint Overlap System

[Theorem of arXiv:2412.04284, 'Approximately jumping towards the Origin'] For each dimension $d \geq 2$, the random variable $\|x_n\|$ has a unique, invariant measure $\pi_d$ on $[0, \infty]$. This invariant measure $\pi_d$ has expectation 
$$ \int_{0}^{\infty} x ~d\pi_d(x) = \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2} \frac{ \Gamma(\frac{d+1}{2})}{\Gamma(\tfrac{d}{2})} = \sqrt{\frac{\pi}{8}} \sqrt{d} + o(\sqrt{d})$$
which is asymptotically $(\sqrt{\pi/8} + o(1)) \cdot \sqrt{d}$.
The invariant measure $\pi_d$ has faster than Gaussian decay: for every $\alpha > 0$
$$ \int_{0}^{\infty} e^{\alpha x^2} d\pi_d(x) < \infty.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma calcdim of arXiv:2505.11721, 'Variational principles for Hausdorff and packing dimensions of fractal percolation on self'] Let $\mu$ be a positive and finite Borel measure supported on $[0,1]^d$. Let $(\mathcal G_N)_{N\ge 1}$ a sequence of finite families of closed parallelepipeds included in $[0,1]^d$ and such that for all $N\ge 1$ two elements of $\mathcal G_N$ are equal or have disjoint interior. 

Suppose that for each $N\ge 1$ and each $Q\in\mathcal G_N$ one has $\mu(\partial Q)=0$ and  the elements of $\mathcal G_N$ form a covering of $\supp(\mu)$. In particular, $\mu$-almost every $z\in \supp(\mu)$ is contained in a unique element $Q_N(z)$ of $\mathcal{F}_N$ for all $N\ge 1$. 
 
Let $\epsilon_1>0$, $\epsilon_2\in (0,1)$, $\delta_2\ge \delta_1\ge 0$ and $\Delta_2\ge \Delta_1\ge 0$. Let $(N_j)_{j\ge 1}$ be an increasing sequence of integers. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item Suppose that  for $\mu$-almost every $z$ one has $\liminf_{N\to+\infty} \frac{\log(\mu(Q_N(z)))}{-N}\ge \delta_1$ and for~$N$ large enough the sides lengths of $Q_N(z)$ are larger than $e^{-N(1+\epsilon_1)}$. Then,  $\underline\dim_H(\mu)\ge \frac{\delta_1}{1+\epsilon_1}$.

\item Suppose that for $\mu$-almost every $z$ one has $\liminf_{j\to+\infty} \frac{\log(\mu(Q_{N_j}(z)))}{-N_j}\le \delta_2$ and  the  sides lengths of $Q_{N_j}(z)$ are smaller than $e^{-N_j(1-\epsilon_2)}$. Then, $\overline\dim_H(\mu)\le \frac{\delta_2}{1-\epsilon_2}$.

\item  Suppose that for $\mu$-almost every $z$ one has $\limsup_{j\to+\infty} \frac{\log(\mu(Q_{N_j}(z)))}{-N_j}\ge \Delta_1$  and the  sides lengths of $Q_{N_j}(z)$ are larger than $e^{-N_j(1+\epsilon_1)}$. Then, $\underline\dim_P(\mu)\ge \frac{\Delta_1}{1+\epsilon_1}$.

\item Suppose that for $\mu$-almost every $z$ one has $\limsup_{N\to+\infty} \frac{\log(\mu(Q_N(z)))}{-N}\le \Delta_2$  and for~$N$ large enough the sides lengths of $Q_N(z)$ are smaller than $e^{-N(1-\epsilon_2)}$.  Then,  $\overline\dim_P(\mu)\le \frac{\Delta_2}{1-\epsilon_2}$. 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma calcdim of arXiv:2505.11721

body:
[Theorem rescaledmomentmethod of arXiv:2411.11085, 'Universal constant order fluctuations for the cokernels of block triangular matrices'] {\normalfont(Nguyen and Van Peski~[nguyen2024rank])} Fix a prime $p$ and a positive integer $d$. Let $(\Gamma_h)_{h\ge 1}$ be a sequence of random
finitely-generated abelian $p$-groups and $(k_h)_{h\ge 1}$ a sequence of real numbers such that the following holds:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item The fractional part $\{-\log_p(k_h)\}$ converges to $\zeta$.
\item For all $\lambda\in \Sig_d^{\ge 0}$, we have
\[\lim_{h\to\infty} \mathbb{E}\
\frac{|\Hom(\Gamma_h,G_{\lambda'})|}{k_h^{|\lambda|}}=\frac{c(G_{\lambda'},|\lambda|)}{|\lambda|!}.\]

\end{enumerate}

Then
\[\left(\rang(p^{i-1}\Gamma_h)-\lfloor\log_p(k_{h})+\zeta\rceil\right)_{i=1}^d\]
converges to $\mathcal{L}_{d,p^{-1},\chi}$ in distribution as $h\to\infty$, where $\chi=\frac{p^{-\zeta}}{p-1}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem rescaledmomentmethod of arXiv:2411.11085

[Corollary 18 of arXiv:2608.30059, 'Multihomogeneous Measures and Stochastic Polar Representations'] If  \(\nu=\nu_Z\in M_{\chi_\alpha,\sigma}(E)\), then   the following are
equivalent: 
\begin{enumerate}[\rm(i)]
\item
\(\nu\) is \(B\)-invariant.

\item
For every \(a\in\mathsf T\)
\[
\nu_{B^aZ}=\nu_Z;
\]
equivalently, every random element \(B^aZ\) is another stochastic representer of
\(\nu\).

\item
For every \(a\in\mathsf T\) and every
\(\Gamma\in\mathcal H_\alpha(E)\)
\[
\E{\Gamma(B^aZ)}=\E{\Gamma(Z)}.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:Lipschitzquotient of arXiv:2609.01557, '$L^\infty$ Variational Approximation of the Aubry Set'] Let \(v_1,v_2\) be two critical subsolutions and set
\[
    z:=v_1-v_2.
\]
Then for all \(x,y\in\mathbb T^n\),
\begin{equation}
    |z(y)-z(x)|
    \leq \delta_M(x,y).
\end{equation}
Consequently, \(z|_\mathcal A\) descends to a \(1\)-Lipschitz function
\[
    \overline z:(\mathcal A_M,\delta_M)\to\mathbb R.
\]
If
\[
    \mathcal H^1(\mathcal A_M,\delta_M)=0,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
    \mathcal H^1(z(\mathcal A))=0.
\end{equation}
In particular, \(z(\mathcal A)\) contains no nontrivial interval.

body: Ding-Lee-Peres Question 5.2 (arXiv:1004.4371, Section 5: when t_hit = o(t_cov), are the cover-time fluctuations of order t_hit?) is answered in the negative. On the clique-star G_k (a k-clique with one pendant leaf at each clique vertex; t_hit = 2k^2 + k + 1) the cover time satisfies Var(tau_cov) ~ t_hit t_cov and (tau_cov - E tau_cov)/sqrt(Var tau_cov) converges to a standard Gaussian; on the double star D_k (two adjacent centres, each with k pendant leaves; t_hit = 6k + 3) the cover time centred at 4k log k and divided by 2 sqrt(2) k sqrt(log k) converges to |Z|, a half-normal law, with t_cov = 4k log k + (4/sqrt(pi)) k sqrt(log k) + o(k sqrt(log k)) and Var(tau_cov) = 8(1 - 2/pi) k^2 log k (1 + o(1)). Centred at its mean instead, (tau_cov - t_cov)/sqrt(t_hit t_cov) converges to (|Z| - sqrt(2/pi))/sqrt(3), and the standardized cover time (tau_cov - E tau_cov)/SD(tau_cov) converges to (|Z| - sqrt(2/pi))/sqrt(1 - 2/pi), not to a half-normal law; SD(tau_cov)/t_hit ~ (sqrt(2)/3) sqrt(1 - 2/pi) sqrt(log k) -> infinity. The proofs use exact first-step hitting systems, an excursion transform f_k with mu = k^2 - k + 2 and sigma^2 = k^4 - 4k^2 + 5k - 2, stage and coupon-clock closed forms, a residual lemma (the trap is last with probability 1/(r+1)), second-order expansions with explicit error 3k log k + 5k, moderate deviations by Gartner-Ellis at speed a_k^2, an operational-time construction exact in law (tau = 2P + J - 1), and an occupation CLT with covariance (2/q) L^+.

[Definition 73 (Algebraic ancestry and analytic critical cost) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] For a cutoff \(N\ge2\), the split ancestry Rees module is
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr R^{\rm anc}_{\le N}(H)
 :=H\oplus
 \bigoplus_{n=2}^N\ \bigoplus_{r=1}^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}
 z^{-r}\operatorname{Ran}P_{n,r}.
 
\end{equation}
The symbol \(z^{-r}\) records the algebraic normal order
\(F_rL_n/F_{r+1}L_n\).

For tensors set
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr K_0^{[0]}:=\mathbb R,
 \qquad \mathscr K_1^{[0]}(H):=H,
 \qquad \mathscr K_n^{[0]}(H):=\mathfrak A_1^{(n)}(H)\quad(n\ge2),
 
\end{equation}
and, for \(n\ge2\), \(r\ge1\),
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr K_n^{[r]}(H):=
 \mathfrak W_{\rm mf}^{[r]}(H^{\otimes n}).
 
\end{equation}
Thus cost zero means trace class in every cut, while cost \(r\) permits the
critical profile \(\phi_r(N)\).  The inclusions
\(\mathscr K_n^{[r-1]}\subseteq\mathscr K_n^{[r]}\) define the analytic
critical boundary
\begin{equation}
 \partial_{\rm cr}^0\mathscr K_n(H):=\mathscr K_n^{[0]}(H),
 \qquad
 \partial_{\rm cr}^r\mathscr K_n(H)
 :=\mathscr K_n^{[r]}(H)/\mathscr K_n^{[r-1]}(H),
 \quad r\ge1.
 
\end{equation}
The truncated analytic Rees space is
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr R^{\rm cr}_{\le N}(H)
 :=\bigoplus_{n=0}^N
   \bigoplus_{0\le r\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor}
   z^{-r}\mathscr K_n^{[r]}(H),
 
\end{equation}
with the degree-one summand understood as \(H\).  The direct Rees sum carries
its product quasi-topology.  By contrast, the quotients
\(\partial_{\rm cr}^r\mathscr K_n\) are used as algebraic associated-graded
spaces; no Hausdorff quotient topology is implicit.
title: Algebraic ancestry and analytic critical cost

\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 3 (Dobrushin-Major-Taqqu in Hölder topology) of arXiv:2606.04179, 'Functional Scaling Limits of Interpolated Correlated Random Walks in Hölder Topology'] Assume the correlation function \(\rho\) is a regularly varying 
    function of index \(-\alpha\) with \(\alpha \in (0,\frac1{\hermRank})\), that is
    \[
        \tag{regularly-varying ``fat tail''}
        \rho(k) = k^{-\alpha} \slowVar(k)
        \qquad \forall k\in \nat 
    \]
    for a slowly varying function\footnotemark
    \(\slowVar\colon (0, \infty) \to \real\)
    and \(\feature \in L^p(\gamma)\) for some \(p > 2\). Then the rescaled interpolated random
    walk converges in distribution in the Hölder topology. That is
    for the variance \(\sigma^2 \coloneq c_\hermRank^2\hermRank!/(\hurst(2\hurst-1))\)
    \[
        \hat\interpF^n \coloneq\tfrac{n^{-\hurst}}{\slowVar(n)^{\frac{\hermRank}2}}\interpF^n \xrightarrow{d} \sigma Z^{\hermRank,\hurst}, \qquad \text{in the space } C^{\beta}([0,T]) \text{ for any } \beta \in (0,\hurst - \tfrac1p),
    \]
    where \(Z^{\hermRank,\hurst}\) is a ``Hermite process'' (Definition \ref{def: Hermite process}) with Hurst index
    \(\hurst = 1-\frac{\alpha \hermRank}{2}\in (\frac12, 1)\),
    and \(C^{\beta}([0,T])\) is the space of \(\beta\)-Hölder continuous functions on \([0,T]\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Dobrushin-Major-Taqqu in Hölder topology

[Proposition 2 of arXiv:2608.22112, '2608.22112'] \textbf{(Accumulating prediction errors increase the multi-step loss)}
Let $\mathrm{MAE}_h$ and $\mathrm{Loss}_H$ be defined as in
\cref{MAE} and \cref{loss}. Suppose that
\[
\mathrm{MAE}_{H+1}
>
\frac1H \sum_{h=1}^H \mathrm{MAE}_h.
\]
Then
\[
\mathrm{Loss}_{H+1}
>
\mathrm{Loss}_H.
\]
In particular, if the sequence $\{\mathrm{MAE}_h\}$ is increasing,
then extending the optimization horizon increases the loss.

[Theorem 4 (Antisymmetric maximum principle) of arXiv:2609.01403, '2609.01403'] Let $n\ge2$, $s\in(0,1)$,
\[
    H=\{x_1>0\},
    \qquad
    \widetilde x=(-x_1,x'),
\]
and let $B_r(x_0)\subset H$ and
$c\in L^\infty(B_r(x_0))$. Assume
$u\in\mathcal L^{2s}(\mathbb R^n)$ is antisymmetric with respect to
$\partial H$, namely
\[
    u(\widetilde x)=-u(x)
    \qquad
    \text{for a.e. }x\in H,
\]
and $u\ge0$ a.e. in $H$. Suppose
\[
    \mathscr{L}_su+cu\ge0
    \qquad
    \text{in }\mathcal D'(B_r(x_0)\setminus\{x_0\}),
\]
and
\[
    u\ge m>0
    \qquad
    \text{a.e. in }
    B_r(x_0)\setminus B_{r/2}(x_0).
\]
Then
\[
    u\ge\alpha m
    \qquad
    \text{a.e. in }B_r(x_0)\setminus\{x_0\},
\]
where
\[
    \alpha
    =
    \alpha\!\left(
        n,s,
        r^{2s}\|c^+\|_{L^\infty(B_r(x_0))}
    \right)>0.
\]
As above, for $0<r\le1$ the constant may be chosen uniformly in $r$,
while for $c\le0$ it depends only on $n$ and $s$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Antisymmetric maximum principle

[Defi 8 of arXiv:2609.01105, 'Obstruction to quasi-invariance of Gaussian measures under transport flows on Riemannian M'] Let $m \in \mathbb{R}$. A function $a : \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{C}$ is said to belong to $S^m$ if $a$ is smooth and satisfies for all multi-indices $\alpha, \beta$: 
\[
    |\partial_{\xi}^{\alpha}\partial_x^{\beta}a(x,\xi)| \leq C(\alpha,\beta) \langle \xi \rangle^{m-|\alpha|}.
\]
Similarly, we say that a function $a : \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$  belongs to $C_*^{\rho}S^m$ if $a(x,\xi)$ is smooth in $\xi$ and for all multi-indices $\alpha$:
\[
    \|\partial_{\xi}^\alpha a(\cdot, \xi)\|_{C_*^{\rho}} \leq C(\alpha) \langle \xi \rangle^{m-|\alpha|},
\] 
where $C_*^{\rho}$ denotes the Zygmund space \cite[Appendix A]{TaylorPDE}.

[Theorem thm:whole-plane-persistence of arXiv:2609.00645, 'Global persistence of nearly radial concentrated vortices in a bounded domain'] Fix $\kappa,M,R>0$.  Then there exists $C=C(\kappa,M,R)>0$ such that the following
holds.  For $\varepsilon>0$, let
$\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$ satisfy
\begin{equation}
  \omega_{\varepsilon,0}\geq0,\qquad
  \int_{\mathbb R^2}\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\,\mathrm d\mathbf x=\kappa,
  \qquad
  \|\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\|_\infty\leq M\varepsilon^{-2},
  \qquad
  \operatorname{supp}\omega_{\varepsilon,0}
  \subset B_{R\varepsilon}(\mathbf0).
\end{equation}
Let $\omega_{\varepsilon,t}$, $t\in\mathbb R$, be the corresponding Yudovich
solution of the two-dimensional Euler equation in $\mathbb R^2$.  Then
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})^2
  \leq C\mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,0}).
\end{equation}
If, in addition,
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,0})\leq\frac{\kappa^2}{C},
\end{equation}
then, with
\[
  \mathbf X_\varepsilon
  :=\frac1\kappa\int_{\mathbb R^2}\mathbf x
  \omega_{\varepsilon,0}(\mathbf x)\,\mathrm d\mathbf x,
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\ \sup_{\mathbf b\in\mathsf C(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})}
  |\mathbf b-\mathbf X_\varepsilon|
  \leq (1+\sqrt2)R\varepsilon.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\ \sup_{\mathbf b\in\mathsf C(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})}
  |\mathbf b|
  \leq(2+\sqrt2)R\varepsilon.
\end{equation}
In particular, for any family of initial data satisfying
(equation eq:whole-plane-initial-data of the paper) with the same $\kappa,M,R$, if
$\mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,0})\to0$ as $\varepsilon\to0$, then
\[
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})\longrightarrow0,
  \qquad
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\ \sup_{\mathbf b\in
  \mathsf C(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})}|\mathbf b|\longrightarrow0.
\]

If a_1 >= a_2 >= ... >= a_n and b_1 >= b_2 >= ... >= b_n (both sequences sorted the same way), then (1/n) sum a_i b_i >= ((1/n) sum a_i) ((1/n) sum b_i); if one sequence is increasing and the other decreasing, the inequality reverses. The integral form: for f and g both monotone in the same direction on [0,1], the integral of f g is at least the product of the integrals. This is the one-dimensional case of the Harris-FKG inequality (a product of two increasing functions of one uniform variable has nonnegative covariance), and its proof is the identity 2(n sum a_i b_i - sum a_i sum b_j) = sum_{i,j} (a_i - a_j)(b_i - b_j) >= 0.
both sequences (or functions) monotone in the same direction; opposite directions reverse the inequality
no independence or product structure needed beyond the single variable; the n-variable generalization is Harris-FKG

[Corollary 39 of arXiv:2608.25785, 'Proper Actions on Homogeneous Spaces of the Upper Triangular Matrix Group via Coarse Geome'] Let $S$ be a nonempty set, $I$ a finite set with $\# I\geq 2$, $J_1,J_2$ subsets of $I$, 
    $\{f_i\mid i\in I\}$ a family of functions from $S$ to $\R_{\geq 0}$,
    $\{a_{(\sigma,i)} \mid \sigma =1,2, \, i\in I\setminus J_\sigma\}$ a family of elements of $\R_{>0}$, and $\mathcal{P},\mathcal{Q}$ partitions of $I$.
    Assume that there exists $i_0\in I\setminus (J_1\cup J_2)$ such that $f_{i_0}$ values on $\R_{>0}$, and for each $\sigma\in \{1,2\}$ and $j\in J_\sigma$, there exists $C_j\geq 1$ such that $f_j\leq C_j\max\{f_i\mid i\in I\setminus J_\sigma \}$.
    Then the following two functions are pairwise close:
    \[
    \max\left\{\sum_{i\in P\setminus J_1}a_{(1,i)}f_i\middle| P\in \mathcal{P}\text{ with }P\neq J_1\right\},\quad 
    \max\left\{\sum_{i\in Q\setminus J_2}a_{(2,i)}f_i\middle| Q\in \mathcal{Q} \text{ with }Q\neq J_2\right\}.
    \]
    Here, $\R_{>0}$ is equipped with the LR-coarse structure. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: For the biased Bernoulli convolution at ratio 2/3 - the law of sum_k B_k (2/3)^k with B_k i.i.d., P(B_k = 1) = p - the measure is singular for every p < p* = 0.140277, where p* solves H(p) = log(3/2) in natural logarithms (H(p)/log(3/2) = 0.4896, 0.8018, 1.2341, 1.7095 at p = 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 1/2). Proof: the dimension of the measure is at most the entropy-over-Lyapunov ratio H(p)/log(3/2), and a measure on the line of dimension below one is not absolutely continuous; Hochman's theorem is needed only for the matching lower bound dim = min(1, H(p)/log(3/2)), which this does not use. Two further thresholds govern the Fourier criterion at this ratio. The biased factor |(1-p) + p e^{i phi}|^2 = 1 - 2p(1-p)(1 - cos phi) has arithmetic mean 1 - 2p(1-p) over the phase, which gives the annealed (main-term) exponent alpha(p) = 1 + log(1 - 2p(1-p))/log(3/2), zero at p(1-p) = 1/6, i.e. p = (1 - 3^{-1/2})/2 = 0.211325; and log-mean 2 log(1-p), which gives the quenched (typical) threshold (3/2)(1-p)^2 = 1 at p = 0.183503. As a calibration control for statistics on the unbiased Bernoulli convolution at 2/3 (the same ratio, frequencies and arithmetic, only the weights changed): below p* the measure is singular and a detection is expected; above 0.2113 the main term decays and a pass is expected; between 0.1403 and 0.2113 the measure has dimension one while the main term already diverges, so a reading there means nothing - controls belong at p <= 0.12 and p >= 0.35. Unlike the Pisot control lambda = 1/phi, where one localised cell forces the reading a priori, the absence of such a cell at ratio 3/2 is Mahler's open problem on ||(3/2)^m xi||, so the control's genuineness rests on an empirical extensiveness test: a flat per-step rate means one cell forces the reading, a wobbling rate means a real measurement (flat to 0.0005 at 1/phi from K = 8; wobbling by 0.028 at the unbiased 2/3).

[Definition 6 of arXiv:2605.02002, 'Glauber dynamics for random field Ising models on bounded degree graphs and MLSI'] (Approximate conservation of $\phi$-entropy) We say that a distribution $\mu$ on $\{0,1\}^n$ satisfies $K$-approximate tensorization of $\phi$-entropy if for any function $f:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$ and any $X\sim\mu$,
$$
\operatorname{Ent}^\phi[f(X)]\leq K\cdot\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbb{E}[\operatorname{Ent}^\phi[f(X)\mid X_{-i}]],
$$where we denote by $X_{-i}$ the configuration $X$ restricted to $[n]\setminus\{i\}$.

[Theorem 9 (Outlier-value and overlap laws) of arXiv:2608.19594, 'Mesoscopic Rectangular Spikes under Subspace Local Laws:\\Outlier Values and Singular Subs'] Assume \cref{ass:global-noise,ass:edge,ass:holo-SLL,ass:weighted-compatibility} and $r_n\to\infty$.  Suppose that the restricted supercritical spike measures
\[
  H_n^+:=H_n|_{(\theta_\star,\infty)}
\]
converge vaguely in probability on $(\theta_\star,\infty)$ to a deterministic finite measure $H^+$.  Then, vaguely in probability on $(b,\infty)$,
\begin{align}
  \nu_n^{\mathrm{out}}&\vague \rho_\#H^+,\\
  \omega_n^{\mathrm L}&\vague \rho_\#(\cL H^+),\\
  \omega_n^{\mathrm R}&\vague \rho_\#(\cR H^+),\\
  \omega_n^{\mathrm{LR}}&\vague \rho_\#(\cLR H^+).
\end{align}
Equivalently, for every $f\in C_c((b,\infty))$,
\begin{align*}
  \frac1{r_n}\sum_j f(\sigma_j(W_n))
      &\longrightarrow \int f(\rho(\theta))\,H^+(\dd\theta),\\
  \frac1{r_n}\sum_j f(\sigma_j(W_n))\norm{U_n^*\widehat u_{n,j}}_2^2
      &\longrightarrow \int f(\rho(\theta))\cL(\theta)\,H^+(\dd\theta),\\
  \frac1{r_n}\sum_j f(\sigma_j(W_n))\norm{V_n^*\widehat v_{n,j}}_2^2
      &\longrightarrow \int f(\rho(\theta))\cR(\theta)\,H^+(\dd\theta),\\
  \frac1{r_n}\sum_j f(\sigma_j(W_n))\chi_{n,j}
      &\longrightarrow \int f(\rho(\theta))\cLR(\theta)\,H^+(\dd\theta),
\end{align*}
where the sums may be taken over all singular values because $f$ vanishes near the edge. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own work draft; proof (unaudited), conditional reduction, no novelty claim. Let alpha>0, beta=alpha+1, p_t=A*t^(-beta) sum to one on t=1,...,n, H>0, ell0>0. Suppose comparison task losses h_t satisfy 1{s<(1-delta)H/p_t}-eta_t <= h_t/ell0 <= 1{s<(1+delta)H/p_t}+eta_t with 0<=delta<1, eta_t>=0, and actual losses satisfy sum_t p_t*abs(ell_t-h_t)/ell0<=e. Set E=e+sum_t p_t*eta_t. Then ell0*(A*T_n(floor((A*s/((1-delta)*H))^(1/beta)) clipped to n)-E) <= sum_t p_t*ell_t <= ell0*(A*T_n(floor((A*s/((1+delta)*H))^(1/beta)) clipped to n)+E), where T_n(m)=sum_{t=m+1}^n t^(-beta). If r=(A*s/H)^(1/beta) tends to infinity, n/r tends to infinity, delta tends to zero, and E=o(A*r^(-alpha)), then total loss is asymptotic to ell0*A/alpha*r^(-alpha). This supplies the exponent alpha/(alpha+1) conditionally; proving the transition and error hypotheses for a network remains open.

[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2609.03185, 'Uniqueness of tangent flows in free boundary flow'] There exist constants $C>0$ and $\epsilon>0$ such that the following holds. Suppose that $|\alpha|, |\widehat{\alpha}|, |\mathscr{R}-Id|, D_{\mathscr{T}^{\alpha,\mathscr{C}_+}_\tau}(M_{\tau_0}), D_{\mathcal{W}^{\alpha(\tau),\mathscr{C}_+}}(M_{\tau_0}), D_{\mathscr{T}^{\alpha,\mathscr{C}_+}_{\tau+L}}(M_{\tau_0+L})\leq\epsilon,$ and $ D_{\mathscr{T}^{\alpha,\mathscr{C}_+}_\tau}(M_{\tau_0})>e^{-\tau_0/8}.$
Then
\[
D_{\mathscr{T}^{\widehat{\alpha},\mathscr{RC}_+}_{\tau+1}}(M_{\tau_0+1}),\ 
D_{\mathcal{W}^{\widehat{\alpha}(\tau+1),\mathscr{RC}_+}}(M_{\tau_0+1}) \leq C\bigg(D_{\mathscr{T}^{\alpha,\mathscr{C}_+}_\tau}(M_{\tau_0}) +|\mathscr{R}-Id| +|\alpha-\widehat{\alpha}|
+e^{-\frac{(R_{\widehat{\alpha}}-1)^2}{8p_0}}\bigg),
\]
\vspace{-\baselineskip}
\[
D_{\mathscr{T}^{\widehat\alpha,\mathscr{RC}_+}_\tau}(M_{\tau_0}) \leq C\bigg(D_{\mathcal{W}^{\alpha(\tau),\mathscr{C}_+}}(M_{\tau_0}) +|\mathscr{R}-Id| +|\alpha-\widehat{\alpha}|
+e^{-\frac{(R_{\widehat{\alpha}}-1)^2}{8p_0}}\bigg).
\]
If $|\widehat{\alpha}|\geq|\alpha|$, the exponential error terms are bounded by the corresponding distance terms. Finally,
$$ D_{\mathcal{W}^{\alpha(\tau+1),\mathscr{C}_+}}(M_{\tau_0+1}) + D_{\mathcal{W}^{\alpha(\tau+1),\mathscr{C}_+}}(M_{\tau_0+L+1})
\leq C\Big(D_{\mathscr{T}^{\alpha,\mathscr{C}_+}_\tau}(M_{\tau_0}) +
D_{\mathscr{T}^{\alpha,\mathscr{C}_+}_{\tau+L}}(M_{\tau_0+L}) +|\alpha|^2 \Big).$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma of arXiv:2512.09219, 'Strong confluence of geodesics in Liouville quantum gravity'] ([GM21])
Let $h$ be a whole plane GFF and fix $s>0$.  Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\mathcal{Z}$ be a collection of $n$ points in $\mathbb{C}$ such that $|z-w| \geq 2(1+s)$ for all distinct points $z,w \in \mathcal{Z}$.  For $z \in \mathcal{Z}$, let $E_z$ be an event measurable with respect to $\sigma(h|_{B_1(z)}-h_{1+s}(z))$.  Then, for all $p,q \in (0,1)$,  there exists $n_* = n_*(s,p,q) \in \mathbb{N}$ such that if $\mathbb{P}(E_z) \geq p$ for all $z \in \mathcal{Z}$,  then $\mathbb{P}\left(\cup_{z \in \mathcal{Z}} E_z \right) \geq q$ for all $n \geq n_*$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Defn 35 ({\cite[Definition~3.6) of arXiv:2609.02561, 'NON-NEF LOCI IN MIXED CHARACTERISTIC'] {LX}}]
Let $f: X \rightarrow S$ be a projective surjective morphism of integral excellent schemes with $X$ normal. Let $D$ be a $\Q$-Cartier $\Q$-divisor on $X$, and let $v$ be a divisorial valuation over $X$.
Take a projective birational morphism $\mu :Y \rightarrow X$ from a normal integral scheme, a prime divisor $\Gamma$ on $Y$, and $\lambda\in\R_{>0}$ such that $v=\lambda\cdot\ord_{\Gamma}$ (Remark~\ref{excval}).
We define the asymptotic vanishing order $v(\| D/S \|)$ of $D$ along $v$ as
\[ v(\| D/S \|) := \lambda\cdot\ord_{\Gamma}(Y/S,\|\mu^{*}D\|) = \lambda\cdot\ord_{\Gamma}(\|\mu^{*}D\|,Y/S). \]
This definition is independent of the choice of $Y$ and $\Gamma$ by Lemma~\ref{ordaffine} and Remark~\ref{ordrem}.
When $S$ is affine, we write $v(\| D/S \|)$ by $v(\| D\|)$ since it is independent of the choice of $S$ by Remark~\ref{ordrem}.

[Lem small-frequency-abelian-estimates of arXiv:2605.13004, 'Orientation in Poisson Cluster Processes via Imaginary Bispectra'] Let $\overline H(x):=\int_x^\infty h(u)\,du\sim x^{-\alpha}L(x)$ with $0<\alpha\le2$, where $L$ is slowly varying. Write $L_t:=L(1/t)$,
\[
U(t):=\int_0^\infty \cos(tu)h(u)\,du,
\qquad
V(t):=\int_0^\infty \sin(tu)h(u)\,du.
\]
Then, as $t\downarrow0$, the following estimates hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $0<\alpha<1$, then
\[
1-U(t)\sim S(\alpha)t^\alpha L_t,
\qquad
V(t)\sim C(\alpha)t^\alpha L_t,
\]
where
\[
S(\alpha)=\frac{\pi/2}{\Gamma(\alpha)\sin(\pi\alpha/2)},
\qquad
C(\alpha)=\frac{\pi/2}{\Gamma(\alpha)\cos(\pi\alpha/2)}.
\]
\item If $\alpha=1$, then
\[
1-U(t)\sim \frac{\pi}{2}tL_t,
\qquad
2V(t)-V(2t)\sim 2(\log2)tL_t.
\]
More explicitly, with $J(x):=\int_1^x u^{-1}L(u)\,du$, the potentially larger slowly varying contribution to $V(t)$ is of order $tJ(1/t)$, and it cancels in $2V(t)-V(2t)$ because
\[
J(1/t)-J(1/(2t))\sim (\log2)L_t.
\]
\item If $1<\alpha<2$, then $\mu_1:=\int_0^\infty u h(u)\,du<\infty$, and
\[
1-U(t)\sim S(\alpha)t^\alpha L_t,
\qquad
V(t)-\mu_1t\sim C(\alpha)t^\alpha L_t.
\]
\item If $\alpha=2$, then $\mu_1:=\int_0^\infty u h(u)\,du<\infty$,
\[
V(t)-\mu_1t\sim -\frac{\pi}{2}t^2L_t,
\qquad
2V(t)-V(2t)\sim \pi t^2L_t.
\]
Moreover, if $R_2(x):=1+\int_1^x u^{-1}L(u)\,du$, then
\[
1-U(t)=O(t^2R_2(1/t)),
\qquad
 tR_2(1/t)=o(L_t).
\]
\end{enumerate}

[Defi 47 of arXiv:2603.05174, 'Regularization of the superposition principle: Potential theory meets Fokker-Planck equati'] The Markov process $X$ is called a right (Markov) process if the following additional hypotheses are satisfied:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item The filtration $(\mathcal{F}(t))_{t\geq 0}$ is right continuous and $\mathcal{F}(t)=\widetilde{\mathcal{F}}(t), t\geq 0$.
\item For one (hence all) $\alpha>0$ and for each $f \in \mathcal{E}(\mathcal{U}_\alpha)$ the process $f(X)$ has right continuous paths $\mathbb{P}^{x}$-a.s. for all $x\in E$.
\item There exists a natural topology on $E$ with respect to which the paths of $X$ are $\mathbb{P}^{x}$-a.s. right continuous for all $x\in E$.
\end{enumerate}

Induced Euclidean metric
Bijection and monotonicity are essential to this obstruction

[Theorem thm:zz_main1 of arXiv:2608.19198, 'Probabilistic Representation and Convergence of Gromov-Wasserstein Gradient Flows'] Let $\rho_0\in\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and let
$\mathsf{F}:\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}^d)\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ satisfy
Assumption (assumption:zz_main of the paper) (i) and (ii). Set $\delta_{\rho_0} \coloneqq
    \frac{\left(1-1/\sqrt{2}\right)\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_{\rho_0})}
    {2^{5/4}(\mathsf{F}(\rho_0)-\mathsf{F}_\star)},$ with $\mathsf{F}_\star = \inf \mathsf{F}$.
For any $\delta\in(0,\delta_{\rho_0})$, the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)]
The piecewise-constant
IGW--JKO interpolant
$\bar\rho^n:[0,\delta]\to\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, with time step
$\tau=\delta/n$, converges pointwise weakly to a $\mathsf{W}_2$-continuous curve
$\rho:[0,\delta]\to\mathrm{Dom}(\mathsf{F})$, and the limiting curve satisfies the continuity equation
\begin{equation}
    \partial_t\rho_t+\nabla\cdot(\rho_t v_t)=0,
\end{equation}
in the distributional sense on $\mathbb{R}^d\times(0,\delta),$ i.e.
\[  \int_0^\delta\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \partial_t g(t,x) \, d \rho_t(x)dt=-\int_0^\delta\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \left\langle\nabla_x g(t,x), v_t(x)\right\rangle d  \rho_t(x)dt,  \ \  \forall g\in C_c^\infty((0,\delta)\times\mathbb{R}^d),
\]
for some velocity field $v_t \in L^2(\rho_t;\mathbb{R}^d).$
\item[(ii)] If, in addition, Assumption (assumption:zz_main of the paper)~(iii) holds, the aforementioned convergence can be lifted to
uniform $\mathsf{W}_2$-convergence along a subsequence, and the corresponding velocity field $v_t$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
v_t\in-(\mathcal{L}_{\rho_t}|_{\mathcal{I}_{\rho_t}})^{-1}[\partial_{\ell}\mathsf{F}(\rho_t)] \quad \text{$\rho_t$-a.s. for a.e. $t \in (0,\delta)$}.

\end{equation}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu)$ be a probability space (a finite or even $\sigma$-finite measure suffices here), $T: X \to X$ measure-preserving, $f \in L^1(\mu)$ real-valued. Write $S_n f = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f \circ T^k$ and $F_N = \max_{1 \le n \le N} S_n f$. Then
$$\int_{\{F_N > 0\}} f\,d\mu \ \ge\ 0 \quad \text{for every } N \ge 1,$$
and consequently $\int_{\{\sup_n S_n f > 0\}} f\,d\mu \ge 0$. The maximal inequality follows: for $\alpha > 0$, $\mu\big(\{ \sup_{n} \tfrac{1}{n} S_n f > \alpha \}\big) \le \tfrac{1}{\alpha} \int_{\{\sup_n S_n f / n > \alpha\}} f\,d\mu \le \tfrac{1}{\alpha}\|f\|_1$ (apply the first statement to $f - \alpha$; for the last step in infinite measure one needs $f \ge 0$ or $\mu$ finite, since $\int (f - \alpha)$ over the set is where $\mu$ finite is used). This is the only analytic input needed for the pointwise ergodic theorem. It fails if $T$ does not preserve $\mu$.
T is measure-preserving
