[Theorem 33 (Approximate-interpolation weighted SRM) of arXiv:2608.26516, '2608.26516'] Let $\psi:\Hc\to\R_{\ge0}$, let $\lambda_m>0$, and suppose that the weighted objective attains its minimum on every realizable $m$-sample.  Assume that for every such sample $S$ there exists $g_S\in\Hc$ satisfying
\[
    \emp_S(g_S)\le\eta_m,
    \qquad
    \psi(g_S)\le r_m.
\]
Set
$
    R_m:=r_m+\frac{\eta_m}{\lambda_m}.
$
If
\[
    \eta_m+\lambda_m r_m\to0
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \Gdim(\Hc_{R_m})\log(m+1)=o(m),
\]
where $\Hc_R:=\{h \in \Hc:\psi(h)\le R\}$, then every minimizer of
$h\mapsto\emp_S(h)+\lambda_m\psi(h)$ PAC learns $\Hc$.

[Corollary cor:mb-observable-distance-eb of arXiv:2608.25551, 'Beyond Optimal Rates in Stochastic Optimization: Trajectory-Adaptive Stopping Rules'] Suppose Assumptions~(assump:strong-convexity of the paper)--(assump:stepsize-bound of the paper) and~(assump:bounded-minibatch-stochastic-gradients of the paper) hold, and suppose~(equation eq:eb-integrability-condition of the paper) is satisfied. Let $R_0$ be an $\mathcal{F}_{t_0 - 1}$-measurable quantity satisfying $R_0 \ge Z_{t_0}$ almost surely. Then, for every $\alpha \in (0,1)$, the recursively defined process $\{\widehat U_{t+1}^{\mathrm{dist,EB,MB}}(\alpha)\}_{t \ge t_0}$ is well defined and fully observable from $R_0$ and the minibatch SGD trajectory. Moreover,
\[
    \mathbb{P}\left(
        \forall t \ge t_0:\
        Z_{t+1}
        \le
        \widehat U_{t+1}^{\mathrm{dist,EB,MB}}(\alpha)
    \right)
    \ge
    1 - \alpha.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary subseq-symmetric of arXiv:2507.01406, '{\Large On Iterated Lorenz Curves with Applications: The Multivariate Case }'] Assume the hypotheses of \textit{Claim~\ref
{An-vanishing}}. Let $\{n_{k}\}_{k\geq 1}$ be any sequence of integers with $
n_{k}\rightarrow \infty $, and suppose that 
\begin{equation}
L_{n_{k}}(x)\longrightarrow L^{\ast }(x)  
\end{equation}
uniformly on $[0,1]$. Then 
\begin{equation}
L^{\ast }(x)+L^{\ast }(1-x)-1=0\qquad \text{for every }x\in \lbrack 0,1].

\end{equation}

In particular, under any of the sufficient hypotheses on the starting law $F$
given earlier in this appendix for which the one-sign regime holds from the
start, Claim~(An-vanishing of the paper) applies with $N=0$. Hence, by the
compactness result \textit{Claim~(AA of the paper)}, every subsequential limit of $
\{L_{n}\}_{n\geq 0}$ in $C([0,1])$ is symmetric.
title: Corollary subseq-symmetric of arXiv:2507.01406

c_k(F_\phi)

[Lemma 37 of arXiv:2506.10494, 'Geometric Jensen-Shannon Divergence Between Gaussian Measures On Hilbert Space'] Let $\alpha \in [0,1]$. Let $S,T, \{S_k, T_k\}_{k \in \Nbb} \in \SymTr(\Hcal)_{< I}$ be such that
	$\lim_{k \approach \infty}||S_k - S||_{\tr} = \lim_{k \approach \infty}||T_k -T||_{\tr} = 0$. Then
	\begin{align}
		&\lim_{k \approach \infty}\det[(1-\alpha)(I-S_k)^{-\alpha}(I-T_k)^{\alpha} + \alpha(I-S_k)^{1-\alpha}(I-T_k)^{-(1-\alpha)}]
		\nonumber
		\\
		&= \det[(1-\alpha)(I-S)^{-\alpha}(I-T)^{\alpha} + \alpha(I-S)^{1-\alpha}(I-T)^{-(1-\alpha)}].
	\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.29486, 'Cabled braids and their crossing matrices'] Let $N=\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$. 
An $n\times n$ matrix $A=[a_{ij}]$ is the crossing matrix of a reducible pure $n$-braid if and only if $A$ is a zero-diagonal symmetric matrix and 
there exists a partition $N_1\amalg N_2\amalg \dots \amalg N_m$ of $N$ with $1<m<n$ such that for any distinct $k, l\in \{1, 2, \dots ,m\}$ and any $(i,j),\ (i',j')\in N_k\times N_l$, $a_{ij}=a_{i'j'}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Prop Hurwitz-unstable of arXiv:2507.09421, 'Stability of randomly switching stochastic reaction networks with asymptotically linear tr'] Let $M=(m_{ij})$ be a $d\times d$ Metzler matrix. Then the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[(i)] There exists some nonzero $v\in\mathbb R^d_{\ge0}$ such that $(vM)_i$, the $i$-th entry of the vector $vM$, is strictly positive whenever $v_i>0$.
    
    \item[(ii)] There exists a principal submatrix of $M$ which has an increasing direction.
    
    \item[(iii)] There exists a principal submatrix of $M$ which is Hurwitz-unstable.

    \item[(iv)] $M$ is Hurwitz-unstable.
\end{enumerate}
title: Prop Hurwitz-unstable of arXiv:2507.09421

body:
[Prop quotient-we-global of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $\alpha\colon G\to G'$ be any homomorphism of compact Lie groups, and let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a $G$-global weak equivalence in $\cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}$ such that $X(V)$ and $V$ are $\ker(\alpha)$-free and Hausdorff for every $V\in\textbf{\textup{L}}$. Then $\alpha_!f$ is a $G'$-global weak equivalence.
    \begin{proof}
        Picking functorial cofibrant replacements in the $G$-global level model structure yields a commutative diagram
        \[
            \begin{tikzcd}
                X'\arrow[r,"f'"]\arrow[d] & Y'\arrow[d]\\
                X\arrow[r,"f"'] & Y
            \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        where $X'$ and $Y'$ are cofibrant and the vertical maps are $G$-global level weak equivalences. By 2-out-of-3, $f'$ is again a $G$-global weak equivalence, and hence $\alpha_!f'$ is a $G'$-global weak equivalence by Lemma~(lemma:restr-right-Quillen of the paper). To complete the proof we will show that $\alpha_!$ sends the vertical maps to $G'$-global level weak equivalences; it will then follow by 2-out-of-3, that $\alpha_!f$ is a $G'$-global weak equivalences.
        
        We argue for the left-hand map, the argument for the right-hand one being analogous. By Lemma~(lemma:orth-spc-ev-lrQ of the paper) each $X'(V)$ is $\mathcal G_{{\textup{O}}(V),G}$-cofibrant, and hence in particular $\ker(\alpha)$-free and Hausdorff by Lemma~(lemma:G-CW-Hausdorff of the paper). Applying the previous lemma levelwise therefore shows that $\alpha_!(X'\to X)$ is a $G$-global level weak equivalence, as desired.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop quotient-we-global of arXiv:2608.28504

body:
[Thm main of arXiv:2609.03751, 'Sparse bounds for maximal rough singular integrals'] Let \(d\geq1\), and suppose that
\(\Omega\in L^1(S^{d-1})\) satisfies
\[
    \int_{S^{d-1}}\Omega(\theta)\,d\sigma(\theta)=0.
\]

\begin{enumerate}
\item
If \(\Omega\in L^\infty(S^{d-1})\), then, for every
\(1<p<\infty\) and every pair of bounded, compactly supported
functions \(f_1,f_2\), there exists a \(1/2\)-sparse collection
\(\mathcal S=\mathcal S(f_1,f_2,p)\) such that
\begin{equation}
    \left|
        \left\langle T_\Omega^\ast f_1,f_2\right\rangle
    \right|
    \lesssim_d
    (p')^4\|\Omega\|_{L^\infty(S^{d-1})}
    \sum_{Q\in\mathcal S}
        |Q|\langle f_1\rangle_Q\langle f_2\rangle_{p,Q}.
\end{equation}

\item
Let \(1<q<\infty\). If
\(\Omega\in L^{q,1}\log L(S^{d-1})\), then, for every \(q'\leq p<\infty\)
and every pair of bounded, compactly supported functions
\(f_1,f_2\), there exists a \(1/2\)-sparse collection
\(\mathcal S=\mathcal S(f_1,f_2,p)\) such that
\begin{equation}
    \left|
        \left\langle T_\Omega^\ast f_1,f_2\right\rangle
    \right|
    \lesssim_{d,q}
    (p')^4\|\Omega\|_{L^{q,1}\log L(S^{d-1})}
    \sum_{Q\in\mathcal S}
        |Q|\langle f_1\rangle_Q\langle f_2\rangle_{p,Q}.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Here $\tau$ is such that the $(\mathcal{U}(\eta),x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)$ is conformally equivalent to $(0,\tau,1,\infty)$.

OWNER RESULT DRAFT, proof (unaudited), T336-w727-C015 v1. Under all C013 raw-input cube RBF hypotheses (d>=1,n>=0,ell,s,epsilon>0,B>=0, contexts of length <=n and labels bounded by B), the exact C004 cone encoder with feature bound 1, coordinate Lipschitz constant 1/ell and gating bound 2, followed by C002 Chebyshev attention at feature bound 2, has every Q,K,V, residual-MLP matrix and final selector entry bounded by W_star=(n+1)max(4,s,2/s,1/ell). The fixed parameter-independent input encoding has coordinate bound K_input=max(1,B,s). In the shared-register attention head, the combined coefficient beta-eta*s has absolute value at most 3, eta<=2/s, 0<=beta<=1, and there is no token-count factor in that head. Cone grid coefficients are at most one, individual slope entries are 1/ell, and role-gating entries are at most two. Thus this predictor belongs to C014 parameter cube with W=W_star, K0=K_input, A=5 and P=L(15D^2+2DH)+2D, for the fully counted D,H,L of C013. Conditional on C013 scalar error bounds, fixed clips mean [-U,U], U=nB/s+sqrt(s epsilon)+1, and variance [s,1+2s] leave the comparator unchanged. No KL monotonicity of variance clipping for other class members is asserted. C002 and C004 are accepted ground; C013 approximation composition, C014 cover and the present membership bridge remain unaudited. This is not the full prior-averaged ERM theorem, a finite-bit theorem or a novelty claim.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:fd3502bad36abbd92203b2cd72bf3b62af0f4fa0c92e72077c36e91abc4d0ef5","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/fd/fd3502bad36abbd92203b2cd72bf3b62af0f4fa0c92e72077c36e91abc4d0ef5.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:0f46a58b01ff5a7514ba5971c7348f809809fc95597fb843aabc40328056e327","bundle_entry_key":"t336-w727-c015","bundle_id":"population.w727-t336-comparator-parameter-bound-010","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Transformer approximation and generalization; Gaussian-process inference","draft":"w727/bundle_010.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.transformers:draft-raw-rbf-transformer-comparator-parameter-bound","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C015 v1: explicit bounded-parameter membership of the raw-input RBF predictor

Kind: bound. Target: none. Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty claim.

## 1. Statement and dependencies
Use exactly the hypotheses, dimensions D,H,L, grid and truncated Gaussian features of C013 v1: raw inputs in [0,1]^d, d>=1, n>=0, ell,s,epsilon>0, labels bounded by B>=0, and normalized bidirectional ReLU attention followed by tokenwise residual ReLU MLPs. The Gaussian kernel has diagonal one and noise variance s. Use the C004 v1 cone encoder with feature bound R=1, gating bound S=2, and coordinate Lipschitz constant K=1/ell, followed by the accepted C002 v1 Chebyshev solver with feature bound 2. Both accepted constructions are ground; the present task only bounds their displayed individual matrix entries. C013's approximation composition and C014's parameter cover remain unaudited.

Put N=n+1 and

    W_star = N max(4, s, 2/s, 1/ell),
    K_input = max(1,B,s),
    U = n B/s + sqrt(s epsilon) + 1,
    v0 = s,  v1 = 1+2s.

All trainable Q,K,V matrices, both MLP matrices and the final two-coordinate linear selector of this particular C013 predictor can be chosen entrywise in [-W_star,W_star]. Its fixed affine input placement is parameter independent and entrywise bounded by K_input. The construction therefore belongs to C014's bounded parameter class with A=5, W=W_star, K0=K_input and P=L(15D^2+2DH)+2D. Unused heads/MLP units are padded with zero weights.

Moreover, conditional on C013's stated approximation bounds, fixed output clipping to [-U,U] for the mean and [s,1+2s] for the variance leaves this comparator unchanged for every permitted context. This does not assert that variance clipping decreases KL for other predictors.

## 2. Encoder entries
C004 Section 4 lists every nonzero encoder operation. Gaussian feature projection has norm at most one, hence each grid coefficient phi_j(a) has absolute value at most one.

* Absolute-value layer: rows read x_r-a_r or a_r-x_r from raw coordinates and the preserved constant. Since 0<=a_r<=1, input entries have absolute value at most one. Output sums use entries one.
* Cone layer: the hidden map copies nonnegative absolute-value registers and the constant, with entries one. The output writes phi_j(a)+K sum_r |x_r-a_r|. Its individual entries are K or phi_j(a), bounded by max(1,K). The sum over d registers does not turn K into a matrix entry Kd.
* Minimum tournament: each hidden row reads u-v and the output subtracts its ReLU from the u register. All entries are zero or plus/minus one. Unused registers pass through the architecture's fixed identity residual.
* Role gating: ReLU(f+2(r-1))-ReLU(-f+2(r-1)) uses entries of absolute value at most two, including both the role coefficient and the coefficient on the constant register. Output entries are plus/minus one.

All encoder attention matrices can be zero, and all unneeded MLP entries are zero. Thus every encoder entry is bounded by max(2,1/ell). Counts J,p,d may grow but do not enlarge an individual entry.

## 3. Solver scalar coefficients
In C002 with the feature bound 2 and n_plus=max(1,n), set

    L_spec=s+4 n_plus, c=(L_spec+s)/2=s+2 n_plus,
    d_spec=(L_spec-s)/2=2 n_plus, a=c/d_spec>1.

Here L_spec is a spectral endpoint, not the network depth L. At the first solver step eta_0=1/c and beta_0=0. At all later steps C002 gives

    eta_j=2 C_j(a)/(d_spec C_(j+1)(a)),
    beta_j=C_(j-1)(a)/C_(j+1)(a),
    eta_j c = 1+beta_j.

For completeness, if t=log(a+sqrt(a^2-1))>0, the recurrence C_0=1,C_1=a,C_(j+1)=2a C_j-C_(j-1) gives C_j(a)=cosh(jt) by substitution and induction. These numbers are positive and nondecreasing with j. Consequently 0<=beta_j<=1, 0<eta_j<=2/c<=2/s and eta_j s<=2 for every step, including step zero.

## 4. Literal solver matrix entries
C002 Section 4 uses selector Q,K matrices: their entries are zero or plus/minus one. Its initial broadcast head has V entry N. In the solver's first four heads, each nonzero V entry is plus/minus N eta_j, hence at most 2N/s in absolute value.

The fifth head has Q=K=one and NO N factor in V. It writes

    beta(w-w_old)-eta s w          into w,
    beta(u-u_old)+eta(qbar-s u)    into u,
    w-w_old                      into w_old,
    u-u_old                      into u_old.

The combined coefficient on w (respectively u) is beta-eta s, not two different entries. Its absolute value is at most beta+eta s<=3. The other entries in this head are -beta, eta, one or minus one, bounded by max(3,2/s). The fixed residual identity is not a learned parameter. All vector coordinates are separate registers, so no additional merging of the displayed coefficients occurs.

The four readout heads use selector Q,K and V entries plus/minus one or plus/minus s. The final linear map selects mout and vout with entries zero or one. The initial vout=s is fixed input data; it is included in K_input. Solver MLP matrices can be zero, and zero extension into the encoder's larger register space introduces no new nonzero entries.

Combining Sections 2-4 bounds every matrix entry by

    max(2,1/ell,N,2N/s,3,2/s,s) <= W_star,

because N>=1. Also W_star>=4, as required by C014's W>=1 hypothesis. No operator norm bound or finite-bit description bound is asserted.

## 5. Fixed encoding and output clips
Input coordinates consist of raw x in [0,1]^d, labels of absolute value at most B, binary flags, the constant one, the initial variance s, and zeros. Their bound is K_input and does not depend on learned parameters. C014 is applied to the whole encoder-plus-solver class, so its fixed encoding does not silently include learned feature computation.

For an m-point context, m<=n, the exact Gaussian posterior mean is k_*^T(K+sI)^(-1)y. Positive semidefiniteness and unit diagonal imply |k_*(i)|<=1, hence ||k_*||_2<=sqrt(m), ||y||_2<=sqrt(m)B and ||(K+sI)^(-1)||_op<=1/s. Thus |mu|<=mB/s<=nB/s, including the empty context by mu=0. Its noisy variance satisfies s<=v<=s+1.

C013's separate scalar bounds are |muhat-mu|<=sqrt(s epsilon), vhat>=s, and |vhat-v|<=min(s/2,s sqrt(epsilon)). They imply |muhat|<U and s<=vhat<=1+3s/2<1+2s. The fixed interval clips therefore leave both comparator coordinates unchanged. For other members of the class the same clips enforce bounded outputs and are nonexpansive for the parameter-cover argument only.

## 6. What remains
This supplies an explicit comparator parameter radius and output ranges for the C014 deterministic cover. It is not the full prior-averaged ERM theorem. To obtain that theorem one must compose the appropriate task-law concentration argument with the original Gaussian context law, including context clipping and its bias, and retain all unbounded Gaussian query-tail terms. C006/C007, C013 and C014 still require their own independent review. Inscribed polygonal approximations to a semicircle are finite unions of straight segments with uniformly bounded length, while their limit is a smooth arc and is not a jagged route made of straight segments. Let (X, B, mu, T) be an invertible measure-preserving system on a standard probability space with T ERGODIC. Let G be a compact metrizable group with normalized Haar measure m, let phi : X -> G be measurable, and let T_phi(x, g) = (T x, phi(x) g) be the associated group extension of (X x G, mu x m). Then:

  T_phi is ergodic  <=>  for EVERY nontrivial irreducible unitary representation pi : G -> U(d_pi), the functional (transfer) equation
        F(T x) = pi(phi(x)) F(x)      for mu-a.e. x
  has no nonzero MEASURABLE solution F : X -> M_{d_pi}(C).

Equivalently, ergodicity fails exactly when some nontrivial pi admits such a nonzero F. A nonzero solution can always be normalized so that its Hilbert-Schmidt norm is constant, because ||F(x)||_HS is then a T-invariant function and T is ergodic.

Abelian case (the form most often used). If G is abelian, the irreducible representations are the characters chi in the dual group, and the criterion reads: T_phi is ergodic if and only if for every nontrivial character chi there is NO measurable h : X -> S^1 with h(T x) = chi(phi(x)) h(x); i.e. no nontrivial character of phi is a measurable multiplicative coboundary. For G = S^1 and phi written additively this is: for every nonzero integer n, the equation u(T x) - u(x) = n * phi(x) (mod 1) has no measurable solution u.

SHARP EDGES. (1) Ergodicity of the BASE T is a hypothesis, not a conclusion: if T is not ergodic then T_phi is not ergodic either (invariant sets of the base lift), and the displayed equivalence is false as stated without it. (2) Compactness of G is essential -- the proof uses the Haar PROBABILITY measure and the Peter-Weyl decomposition of L^2(G); for noncompact G (e.g. G = R, cylinder flows) the natural invariant measure is infinite and ergodicity is a genuinely different problem. (3) 'Measurable' cannot be weakened to 'continuous': a cocycle can be a measurable coboundary without being a continuous one, so verifying that the equation has no CONTINUOUS solution does not certify ergodicity. (4) Every nontrivial irreducible pi must be tested, not one convenient one. Example: G = S^1 and phi taking values in {+1, -1} with the induced two-point extension ergodic. Then for the character chi_1(z) = z the equation has no solution (that is exactly ergodicity of the two-point extension), yet chi_2(z) = z^2 satisfies chi_2(phi(x)) = 1, so h identically 1 solves the equation for chi_2 -- and indeed T_phi is not ergodic, since phi lives in the proper closed subgroup {+1,-1}.
(X, B, mu, T) is an invertible measure-preserving system on a standard (Lebesgue) probability space
T is ergodic with respect to mu
G is a compact metrizable group with normalized Haar measure m
phi : X -> G is measurable and the extension is T_phi(x,g) = (Tx, phi(x) g) on mu x m
solutions F of the transfer equation are required only to be measurable (matrix-valued), not continuous

[Lemma of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] \label[lemma]{lem:psd_diagonal_dominance}
Let $A = [a_{ij}] \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}$ be positive semidefinite. 
Then, for all $i, j \in [d]$, 
\begin{equation} \@ifstar{\oldabs}{\oldabs*}{a_{ij}} \le  \frac{1}{2}(a_{ii} + a_{jj}) =  \frac{1}{2}(\@ifstar{\oldabs}{\oldabs*}{a_{ii}} + \@ifstar{\oldabs}{\oldabs*}{a_{jj}}). \label[ineq]{ineq:psd_diagonal_dominance} \end{equation}
Moreover, for $i \ne j$, the following conditions are equivalent: 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item Equality is attained in ((ineq:psd_diagonal_dominance of the paper)). 
\item  The $2 \times 2$ principal submatrix $A[\{i,j\}]$ is not positive definite. 
\item The $2 \times 2$ principal submatrix $A[\{i,j\}]$ is not full rank. 
\item $a_{ii} = a_{jj} = \@ifstar{\oldabs}{\oldabs*}{a_{ij}}$. 
\end{enumerate}

\begin{proof}
We first note that for all $i \in [d]$, $e_i^T A e_i = a_{ii} \ge 0$ 
(with any equality implying $A$ is not positive definite), 
so $a_{ii} = \@ifstar{\oldabs}{\oldabs*}{a_{ii}}$. 
We compute 
\[
0 \le (e_i - e_j)^T A (e_i - e_j) 

= a_{ii} + a_{jj} - 2a_{ij} 
\]
and similarly
\[
0 \le (e_i + e_j)^T A (e_i + e_j) 
= a_{ii} + a_{jj} + 2a_{ij} 
\]
so that $2\@ifstar{\oldabs}{\oldabs*}{a_{ij}} \le a_{ii} + a_{jj}$. 

Finally, when $i \ne j$, equality in (equation ineq:psd_diagonal_dominance of the paper) implies $(e_i - e_j)^T A (e_i - e_j) = 0$ or $(e_i + e_j)^T A (e_i + e_j) = 0$, hence $A[\{i,j\}]$ is not positive-definite and therefore not full rank. 

Then, $\det(A[\{i,j\}])=0$, so that $\@ifstar{\oldabs}{\oldabs*}{a_{ij}} = \sqrt{a_{ii}a_{jj}}$. 
In turn this forces $2\sqrt{a_{ii}a_{jj}} = a_{ii} + a_{jj}$, which is to say the vector $(a_{ii},a_{jj})$ attains equality in the arithmetic-geometric mean inequality.
Therefore $a_{ii}=a_{jj}$, and in turn $\@ifstar{\oldabs}{\oldabs*}{a_{ij}} = \sqrt{a_{ii}^2} = a_{ii}$ as well. 

That (iv) implies (i) is obvious. 

\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered lemma of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'

PROOF FOR THE EXPLICIT FAMILY; independent audit pending. For rate-one continuous-time simple random walk on G_d=(Z/2Z)^d x Z/m_dZ, m_d=max(2,floor(2^d log(d)/4)), with generators (e_i,a) for a!=0 and (h,0) for h!=0, the spectral gap is asymptotic to 2/d, t_mix(1/4) is asymptotic to d log(d)/4, and t_mix(3/4)/t_mix(1/4) tends to log(4/3). Thus this simple unweighted Abelian Cayley family satisfies the spectral product condition and lacks total-variation cutoff. For integer d tending to infinity, put N=2^d, m=max(2,floor(N log(d)/4)), and D=d(m-1)+N-1. On the Abelian group (Z/2Z)^d times Z/mZ, use the symmetric generator set

S={(e_i,a): 1<=i<=d, a!=0} union {(h,0): h!=0}.

The sets are disjoint, have no identity, contain no repetitions, and are closed under inversion. They generate the group: all (h,0) are available, and (e_i,a)+(e_i,0)=(0,a). The resulting graph is simple, connected, undirected, unweighted, and D-regular. Consider its continuous-time simple random walk with rate one.

Write alpha=d(m-1)/D and gamma=N/D. The cube projection is the sum of independent coordinate-flip dynamics at total rate alpha and jumps uniformly to a different cube point at rate (N-1)/D. The latter generator equals gamma(Pi-I), where Pi is uniform averaging, and commutes with coordinate flips. Consequently

Law(cube at t)=exp(-gamma t) Q_(alpha t)+(1-exp(-gamma t)) pi_cube,

where Q_u is rate-one coordinate-flip walk on the d-cube from the origin. Its distance from uniform is exactly exp(-gamma t) d_cube(alpha t).

The auxiliary coordinate changes only at coordinate-flip events. Conditional on their number k and on every cube increment, its k increments are independent uniform nonzero elements of Z/mZ. For k>=1 the distance of their sum from uniform is (m-1)^(1-k)/m <= 1/m; this follows by Fourier inversion, since every nontrivial auxiliary Fourier coefficient equals (-1/(m-1))^k. For k=0 its distance is at most one. Since k is Poisson(alpha t),

0 <= d_full(t)-exp(-gamma t)d_cube(alpha t) <= exp(-alpha t)+1/m.

The lower bound is projection; the upper bound compares the joint distribution with the product of its cube marginal and auxiliary uniform law, conditioning on the entire cube event history. This handles possible dependence between the two coordinates.

For a cube character of Hamming weight k and an auxiliary character j, the eigenvalues of I-P are:

* 0 for k=0,j=0;
* [2k(m-1)+N]/D for k>=1,j=0, multiplicity binomial(d,k);
* dm/D for k=0,j!=0, multiplicity m-1;
* [dm+N-2k]/D for k>=1,j!=0, multiplicity (m-1)binomial(d,k).

These exhaust Nm characters. The nonzero minimum is asymptotic to 2/d; the auxiliary eigenvalues tend to one. Therefore t_rel is asymptotic to d/2.

For coordinate flips, each spin has mean exp(-2u/d), independently. Its chi-square distance is (1+exp(-4u/d))^d-1. Thus at u=s d log(d)/4 it tends to zero for s>1. For s<1 the magnetization has mean d exp(-2u/d) and variance at most d, while its stationary mean is zero and variance d. Chebyshev's inequality at half its mean gives d_cube(u)>=1-8/(d exp(-4u/d)), which tends to one. The same conclusions hold with u=alpha s d log(d)/4 because alpha=1-O(1/(d log d)).

Put T=d log(d)/4. Then gamma T tends to one and alpha T tends to infinity. The full distance therefore converges to exp(-s) for 0<s<1 and to zero for s>1. No value at s=1 is needed. Monotonicity and bracketing on either side of the thresholds show

t_mix(3/4)/T -> log(4/3), and t_mix(1/4)/T -> 1.

body: [Definition of arXiv:2601.20502, 'Optimal matching under size priority'] For any weighted graph $G=((V,E),w)$, a matching $M=(V,E')$ on $G$ is a subgraph of $G$ such that $E' \subset E$ and  every vertex of $V$ belongs to at most one edge of $E'$. \[

\]
Furthermore, $DG_{\alpha,\varepsilon}\in C^{0,1}_b(L^{\varsigma_q}(\mathcal O);\mathscr{L}(L^q(\mathcal O),\mathscr{L}^2(H,H)))$ 
and 
there exists a constant $C>0$,
depending only on $\alpha,\delta,\sigma,d,q$, such that 
\[
\sup_{z\in H}\norm{DG_{\alpha,\varepsilon}(z)}_{\mathscr{L}(L^q(\mathcal O),\mathscr{L}^2(H,H))}

\]

[Lemma 15 of arXiv:2608.29585, '2608.29585'] The ring $\cO_d$ is a DVR with uniformizer $\pi_d$.  Its completion is a
complete DVR with residue field $\Q(\zeta_d)$.  The maps
$R\hookrightarrow\cO_d\hookrightarrow\widehat\cO_d$ are injective, and
$\Bbbk$ embeds in $\operatorname{Frac}(\widehat\cO_d)$.  Every nonzero
integer,
in particular $2$, is a unit in both local rings.  For $m\ne0$,
\begin{equation}
 \val_{\Phi_d}(\{m\})=
 \begin{cases}
 1,&d^\sharp\mid m,\\
 0,&d^\sharp\nmid m.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
For every $\xi\in\Bbbk^\times$, the valuation of its image in
$\operatorname{Frac}(\widehat\cO_d)$ equals $\val_{\Phi_d}(\xi)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:crt of arXiv:2609.02041, 'Sparse $k$-AP Covering Sets and the Arithmetic Kakeya Conjecture'] There are infinitely many positive integers $Q$ 
for each of which there exists 
a function $f : \ZZ/Q\ZZ \to (0,\infty)$ such that 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item $0<f(x) < Q^{\frac 1{100k}}$ for all $x\in \ZZ/Q\ZZ$.
\item $\mathbb E_x[f(x)] = 1$.
\item for any $a\in \ZZ/Q\ZZ$, we have
$$\mathbb E_x[f(a-3x)f(a-4x)f(a-5x)] > 100^{k^2}\log Q.$$
\end{enumerate}

body:
INDEPENDENTLY CHECKED FINITE COUNTEREXAMPLE (w362-R001). On a square with four independent edge weights uniform on {1,2}, select the cheaper path between opposite corners, breaking ties toward the upper path. Conditional on upper selection, its two costs have covariance -5/121: the probability both equal 2 is 1/11, but the product of marginal probabilities is 16/121. The unconditional two selected costs have covariance -9/256. Their sum has variance 23/64; dropping covariance terms gives 55/128. Disjoint raw inputs therefore do not ensure independent costs after path selection. This is a finite obstruction, not a claim about planar fluctuation exponents.
Finite square graph with two two-edge terminal paths
Four independent uniform {1,2} weights
Upper path wins ties
title: Selected geodesic costs can be dependent

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2603.28093, 'Random Stability of Random Variables'] Under the condition~\eqref{eq:ln-N}, any Gaussian $N$-stable $X$ is symmetric: $X \stackrel{d}{=} -X$. It satisfies $\mathbb E[X^2] < \infty$. Taking $Y$ the standard $N$-stable random variable, with Laplace transform $L$, we can represent $X = \sqrt{Y}Z$, where $Z \sim \mathcal N(0, \sigma^2)$ is independent of $Y$. The characteristic function of $X$ is given by 
$$
f(u) = \mathbb E\left[e^{\mathrm{i}uX}\right] = L(\sigma^2u^2/2).
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let B_1, ..., B_N be finitely many open balls in R^d (or in any metric space, with the caveat below). There is a subcollection S of pairwise DISJOINT balls such that every B_i is contained in 3B for some B in S, where 3B denotes the ball with the same centre as B and three times the radius. Consequently the union of all the B_i is contained in the union of the dilates 3B over B in S, and in R^d with Lebesgue measure |union_i B_i| <= 3^d sum_{B in S} |B|. The constant 3 is what makes the greedy argument work; 2 + eps also works for any eps > 0 with a slightly more careful selection, but 2 does not. In a general metric space the same greedy proof works for a finite family; for infinite families one needs either uniformly bounded radii (the 5r covering lemma) or a Vitali-type fine-cover hypothesis. [standard; e.g. Stein and Shakarchi, Real Analysis, Lemma 1.2 of Chapter 3]

\[
\ker(\cA_\Omega+\Lp(\Omega))=\operatorname{span}\{\phi_\Omega\}.

and, after normalization at one fixed interior point, the corresponding eigenfunctions are locally compact in $C^1$ and converge along subsequences to a positive eigenfunction associated with $\Lp(\Omega)$.

Let $M,N$ be two independent standard normal random variables.
Then, conditionally on the event $\{\deg_n(a_1)\geq d(n)\}$
\begin{equation} \begin{aligned}

[Definition Diagrammatic graphs of arXiv:2506.06559, 'Bi-infinite incipient cluster in high dimensions'] A diagrammatic graph ${\bf G}$ is a triple  $(G,S, \ell)$ where 
\begin{itemize}
\item $G$ is  a multigraph with a finite number of edges { without self-loops},
\item $S\subset V(G)$ is called the set of labelled vertices,
\item $\ell\colon S\to \mathbb{Z}^d$ is an injective function that encodes the labels of the vertices in $S$
\end{itemize}

If $V(G)=S$, we say that the graph is fully labelled.

We denote by $E(G)$ the set of edges of $G$ and  $E^*(G)$ the set of pairs of endpoints of the edges. For any ${\bf e}\in E^*(G)$  denote  $n_G({\bf e})$ the multiplicity of ${\bf e}$, i.e.~the number of edges in $E(G)$ whose endpoints are given by ${\bf e}$  (with the convention that $n_G({\bf e})=0$ if ${\bf e}\notin E^*(G) $). 

We denote $\mathfrak{G}$ the set of diagrammatic graphs.
title: Diagrammatic graphs

Let 1 <= p < infinity. A subset F of L^p(R^d) is relatively compact in the norm topology if and only if all three of the following hold: (i) F is BOUNDED, sup_{f in F} ||f||_p < infinity; (ii) F is uniformly continuous under translation, sup_{f in F} ||f(. + h) - f||_p -> 0 as h -> 0; (iii) F is uniformly TIGHT, sup_{f in F} integral_{|x| > R} |f|^p dx -> 0 as R -> infinity. Conditions (ii) and (iii) are each independent of the rest and cannot be dropped: the family {n^{d/p} 1_{B(0,1/n)}} is bounded in L^p and tight but not uniformly translation-continuous, since for |h| >= 2/n the translate is disjoint from the original; and the family {1_{[n, n+1]}} is bounded and uniformly translation-continuous but not tight, and has no L^p-convergent subsequence. Boundedness is listed as a separate condition here for safety - some treatments observe that it can be derived from the other two - and stating it explicitly costs nothing. On a bounded domain condition (iii) is automatic and the criterion reduces to (i) and (ii). The criterion is FALSE for p = infinity, where the analogue is Arzela-Ascoli on compacts plus a suitable equicontinuity. This is the L^p analogue of Arzela-Ascoli, with translation-continuity playing the role of equicontinuity. [Kolmogorov (1931), M. Riesz (1933), Frechet (1937); see Hanche-Olsen and Holden, 'The Kolmogorov-Riesz compactness theorem', Expo. Math. 28 (2010)]
1 <= p < infinity
all three conditions (boundedness, uniform translation-continuity, uniform tightness); on a bounded domain tightness is automatic

Owner research draft; status proof (unaudited), claims T368-w734-C001 v1 and C002 v1; no novelty claim. For any integer m>=1, let H(z)=0 for z<=0, z^2/2 for 0<=z<=1, and z-1/2 for z>=1, and phi(z)=z/2+H(z)/8. This C1 activation has 1/2<=phi prime<=5/8, Lipschitz derivative at most 1/8, and |phi(z)-z phi prime(z)|<=1/16. For f(a,w;x)=m^-1 sum_j a_j phi(w_j x), the separable datum (x,y)=(1,+1), logistic loss L=log(1+exp(-f)), and simultaneous GD training BOTH layers with actual step m, every initialization a_j=r_j=-w_j>0 stays on that anti-balanced manifold. Its loss remains >log(2) and tends to log(2). This refutes the literal all-initialization extension of Cai, Wu, Mei, Lindsey and Bartlett (arXiv:2406.08654v2), Theorems 3.2 and 4.1, whose output signs are fixed. If all 2m initial a_j,w_j are iid N(0,1), for each integer T>=0 and epsilon<log(2) the first loss-hitting time satisfies P(tau_epsilon>T)>=q_T^m, with q_T=[Phi(sqrt(2))-Phi(1/sqrt(2))][2Phi(3^-T/(2sqrt(2)))-1]>=[exp(-2)/(4pi)]3^-T. The event is d_j=a_j-w_j in [1,2] and |s_j=a_j+w_j|<=3^-T/2 for every j, and has squared initial parameter norm <=17m/8. The update diagonalizes as s_j prime=(1+c)s_j, d_j prime=(1-c)d_j with c=sigmoid(-f)/2 in (0,1/2). Only initial Gaussian coordinates are independent; the trajectories are coupled. This gives finite-horizon delay, NOT positive-probability infinite-time failure. Gaussian high-probability convergence remains open. The missing general step is controlling output-weight nondegeneracy or saddle escape throughout the large-step trajectory.
Mean-field normalization m^-1; both layers updated simultaneously
No biases; scalar input and one linearly separable datum (1,+1)
Exact anti-balanced starting manifold for the nonconvergence claim; iid N(0,1) coordinates only for the finite-horizon tail claim
No independent audit; finite recurrence checked with 6640 exact rational assertions; Lean attempt timed out
title: Cai et al. burn-in with trainable output weights: anti-balanced smooth-leaky obstruction (T368, unaudited)

[Definition 27 of arXiv:2605.02430, '\textbf{Scaling limit of the range of tree-valued branching random walks in random environ'] Let $\zeta\ino (0, \infty)$. We denote by $\bC ([0, \zeta]^2, \bbR)$ the space of continuous 
functions from $[0, \zeta]^2$ to $\bbR$ that is a Banach space when equipped with 
uniform norm $\lVert \cdot \rVert$. 

\smallskip

\noi
$\textbf{(a)}$ We denote by $\MMM([0, \zeta])$ the subspace of $\bC ([0, \zeta]^2, \bbR)$ of \emph{continuous pseudometrics} on $[0, \zeta]$. Namely, the functions  
$d (\cdot, \cdot) \ino  \bC ([0, \zeta]^2, \bbR)$ such that for all $s_1, s_2, s_3\ino [0, \zeta]$, 
$$d(s_1, s_2) \! \geq \! 0, \; \,  d(s_1, s_1)\! = \! 0, \; \, d(s_1, s_2)\! = \! d(s_2, s_1) \; \, \mathrm{and} \;\,  d(s_1, s_3)\! \leq \! d (s_1, s_2) + d(s_2, s_3). $$
$\textbf{(b)}$ We also denote by $\MMT([0, \zeta])$ the space {of continuous real tree pseudometrics}. 
Namely, the functions $d (\cdot, \cdot) \ino \MMM([0, \zeta])$ such that for all $s_1, s_2, s_3, s_4 \ino [0, \zeta]$, 
\begin{equation}

 d(s_1, s_2) + d(s_3, s_4) \leq \max \big( d(s_1, s_3) + d(s_2, s_4) \, ; \,d(s_1, s_4) + d(s_2, s_3) \big) \; .
\end{equation}
We easily check that $\MMT ([0, \zeta])$ and $\MMM ([0, \zeta])$ are closed subsets of 
$(\bC ([0, \zeta]^2, \bbR), \lVert \cdot \rVert)$. \cq
title: Definition 27 of arXiv:2605.02430

[Lemma 17 (\textsf{Polynomial growth of the Brownian paths}) of arXiv:2609.02064, 'Coalescence and fluctuations of O'Connell--Yor polymers\\ via the free-energy correlation '] Fix $\theta\in(1/2,1)$ and define
  \[
    M_\theta
    =1+\max_{0\leq i\leq n}
      \sup_{t\in\R}\frac{|B_i(t)|}{1+|t|^\theta}.
  \]
  Then $M_\theta<\infty$ almost surely,  and for some constants
  $c,C>0$ that depend only on $\theta, n$, 
  we have 
  
  \noi
  \begin{align} 
    \PP(M_\theta>u)\leq C e^{-cu^2},
    \qquad u\geq1.
  \end{align}
  In particular, $M_\theta$ has moments of every finite order.  If
  $\supp(\phi)\subset[-R_\phi,R_\phi]$, then, after changing a
  deterministic constant,
  \begin{align}
    \sup_{0\leq\eps<1}|B_i^\eps(t)|
    \leq C M_\theta(1+|t|^\theta),
    \qquad t\in\R,
  \end{align}
  simultaneously for $0\leq i\leq n$.

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Compare with the a in (3/2, 2) proof via first-passage percolation and with the recurrence criterion via degree growth. Result: For a < 2 the source proves transience through a finite-energy flow built from the fpp-distance structure, using that face degrees along the peeling are heavy-tailed enough (the dual has vertices of huge degree, giving 'highways'). For a >= 2 the degree of the dual's root is lighter tailed and the map is 'dilute'; the known results are: the primal map is recurrent for all a (bounded degrees, Gurel-Gurevich-Nachmias), and the dual is transient for a < 2. For a in [2,5/2) the dual has volume growth exponent (a - 1/2)/(a - 3/2)... the volume of balls in the dual grows polynomially with degree 2 x (a-1/2)/(a-3/2)?? at a = 5/2 the dual is the UIPQ-type map with quartic volume growth, known recurrent (Gurel-Gurevich-Nachmias again since the dual of a map with bounded degrees is... no: the dual of the UIPQ has unbounded degrees but is recurrent by Lee's or by Gurel-Gurevich-Nachmias's extension to exponential-tail degrees). So at the endpoint a = 5/2 the answer is recurrence, provided the dual's root degree has an exponential tail, which holds for the UIPQ. At a = 2 the degrees have a tail of index 1 (heavy), suggesting transience persists. Hence the conjectural picture is a transition inside [2, 5/2), and the open question as stated (transient for all a in [2,5/2)) is likely FALSE near 5/2 and true near 2; the right question is the location of the transience threshold a_t in [2, 5/2]. Recorded as a partial obstruction with a proposed refinement. Key identity: At a = 5/2 the dual is recurrent (exponential-tail degrees); at a slightly above 2 degrees have tail index near 1, favouring transience; a threshold a_t in (2, 5/2] is expected. Obstruction: The tail index of the dual root degree crosses the Gurel-Gurevich-Nachmias regime inside the interval; the threshold is not located.

[Corollary cor:ordinal-metric of arXiv:2605.02104, '\textbf{Chart-Generated Probability Geometry\\and Kolmogorov Expectations}'] All probability charts preserve the order on $I$:
\[
x<y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad G(x)<G(y).
\]
Hence rank statements and purely ordinal summaries are chart-invariant. In
contrast, metric constructions such as $d_G(x,y)$, chart midpoints
\[
m_G(x,y)=G^{-1}\!\left(\frac{G(x)+G(y)}{2}\right),
\]
Fr\'echet barycenters and variances, as well as boundary distances, are
generally chart-dependent. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let X_1, X_2, ... be iid discrete random variables drawn from a pmf p(x) with entropy H(X) = -sum_x p(x)*log p(x) < infinity. Then -(1/n) * log p(X_1,...,X_n) converges in probability (in fact almost surely) to H(X) as n -> infinity, where p(X_1,...,X_n) = prod_{i=1}^n p(X_i). Consequently, defining the typical set A_epsilon^n = { (x_1,...,x_n) : | -(1/n) log p(x_1,...,x_n) - H(X) | <= epsilon }, for every epsilon > 0 and n large enough: Pr( (X_1,...,X_n) in A_epsilon^n ) > 1 - epsilon, and (1-epsilon) * 2^(n*(H(X)-epsilon)) <= |A_epsilon^n| <= 2^(n*(H(X)+epsilon)).
X_1, X_2, ... are iid draws from a pmf p(x) on a discrete alphabet
H(X) = E[-log p(X)] is finite

body: [Corollary 15 (Law of Robustness for Infinite Function Classes) of arXiv:2603.02806, 'The Price of Robustness: Stable Classifiers Need Overpar'] Assume (H1) and (H3), and fix $\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1)$. Consider the $0$ - $1$ loss $\ell_{\text{0--1}}$. There exists an absolute constant $K>0$ such that, if 1. the minimal risk $R^{*}:=\inf_{f\in\mathcal{F}}R_{\text{0--1}}(f)$ satisfies $R^{*}\geq\varepsilon$, and 2. the sample size $n$ is large enough so that (i) $\tfrac{K}{\sqrt{n}}<\tfrac{\varepsilon}{3}$ and (ii) $\sqrt{\tfrac{2\log(2/\delta)}{n}}<\tfrac{\varepsilon}{2}$, then with probability at least $1-\delta$, for all $\tilde{\varepsilon}>0$, the following holds uniformly for all $g\in\mathcal{G}$ and $f_{g}=sgn\circ g$: $\hat{R}_{\text{0--1}}(f_{g})\leq R^{*}-\varepsilon\;\;\implies\;\;\frac{S^{*}(g)}{L(g)}<\max\left\{\frac{3K}{\varepsilon}\sqrt{\frac{p}{nd}}\sqrt{c\log\!\left(1+60WJ\tilde{\varepsilon}^{-1}\right)},\;\sqrt{\frac{8c}{d}\log\!\left(\frac{6K}{\varepsilon}\right)}\right\}.$

body:
[Proposition prop:poisson_explicit of arXiv:2601.09976, 'Stochastic Calculus as Operator Factorization:\\ An Operator--Covariant Derivative and Uni'] For $\mathcal{F}_T^N$-measurable $F \in L^2(\Omega)$, the operator--covariant derivative is
\[
(D_{\tilde{N}} F)_t = \mathbb{E}[\mathcal{D}_t^+ F \mid \mathcal{F}_{t-}]
\]
$d t \otimes dP$-a.e., where $\mathcal{D}_t^+$ is the add-a-point operator~(equation eq:diff_op of the paper). In particular, $D_{\tilde{N}} F$ is the predictable projection of the discrete gradient. This identification is well known in the discrete Malliavin calculus~[Privault2009,DiNunno2009]; what is new here is not the operator itself, but its characterization as an instance of the general adjoint construction $D_X = \delta_X^*$.

[Mainthm of arXiv:2411.11345, 'Real Gaussian exponential sums via a real moment map'] Let $\mathcal{E}, \mathcal{E}'$ be Gaussian exponential sum and let $\mathcal{E}\odot\mathcal{E}'$ be their Aronszajn multiplication. For any tuple of independent Gaussian exponential sum $\mathcal{E}_1,\ldots,\mathcal{E}_{m-1}$, write $\mathrm{E}:=(\mathcal{E}_1,\ldots,\mathcal{E}_{m-1}):\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}^{m-1}$. Then, for every open set $U\subset \mathbb{R}^m$, we have:
\begin{equation}
  \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(\mathbb{E}\#\mathcal{S}\left\{\mathcal{E},\mathrm{E};U\right\}+\mathbb{E}\#\mathcal{S}\left\{\mathcal{E}',\mathrm{E};U\right\}\right) \leq \mathbb{E}\#\mathcal{S}\left\{\mathcal{E}\odot\mathcal{E}',\mathrm{E};U\right\} \leq \mathbb{E}\#\mathcal{S}\left\{\mathcal{E},\mathrm{E};U\right\}+\mathbb{E}\#\mathcal{S}\left\{\mathcal{E}',\mathrm{E};U\right\}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop generator_continuous_process of arXiv:2411.13964, 'Long-time analysis of a pair of on-lattice and continuous run-and-tumble particles with ja'] Let $\mathcal L$ be
  the generator of the continuous process. Its domain $D(\mathcal L)$
  is the set of bounded measurable functions
  $f : E_D \rightarrow \mathbb R$ such that
\begin{itemize}
\item for $\sigma \in \Sigma_+ \setminus \Sigma_-$ the function
  $f( \cdot, \sigma)$ is absolutely continuous on $[0, \ell)$ and
  $\lim_{x \rightarrow \ell} f(x, \sigma) =
  f\left(\ell,*_\sigma^\ell\right)$,
\item for $\sigma \in \Sigma_+ \setminus \Sigma_-$ the function
  $f(\cdot, \sigma)$ is absolutely continuous on $(0, \ell]$ and
  $\lim_{x \rightarrow 0} f(x, \sigma) = f\left(0, *_\sigma^0\right)$.
\end{itemize}

For $f \in D(\mathcal L)$ one has that
\begin{itemize}
\item in the bulk $\cup_{\sigma \in \Sigma} E_\sigma$ the generator
  comprises a transport term and a jump term
\begin{align*}
\mathcal L f(x, (\sigma^1, \sigma^2)) = &\underbrace{(\sigma^2 - \sigma^1) \partial_x f(x, (\sigma^1, \sigma^2))}_{\text{\normalfont transport term}} \\
&\quad + \underbrace{\lambda(x,\nu) \int_{E_D} \left(f(\tilde x, \tilde \nu) - f(x, (\sigma^1, \sigma^2))\right) dQ\left((x, (\sigma^1, \sigma^2)); (\tilde x, \tilde \nu)\right)}_{\text{\normalfont jump term}},
\end{align*}
\item whereas for boundary states
  $(x, \nu) \in \cup_{\nu \in \partial K} E_\nu$ the generator is
  given only by the jump term
$$
\mathcal L f(x, \nu) = \lambda(x, \nu) \int_{E_D} \left(f(\tilde x, \tilde
  \nu) - f(x, \nu)\right) dQ((x, \nu); (\tilde x, \tilde \nu))
$$
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Generator of the continuous process

body: For a weighted sum S = sum a_i x_i of independent Rademacher signs with all |a_i| >= 1, the probability that S lands in any interval of length 2 is at most C n^{-1/2} (Erdos's sharpening via Sperner's theorem: for an open or half-open interval of length 2 the sharp bound is the middle binomial coefficient over 2^n; a closed interval of length 2 can carry more, e.g. n = 2, a = (1, 1) and [0, 2] has probability 3/4). Inverse Littlewood-Offord theory (Tao-Vu, Nguyen-Vu) characterizes when the concentration probability is large - the weights must have rich additive structure (generalized arithmetic progressions) - and powers the least-singular-value and universality results for discrete random matrices.

[Theorem 1 (Main a priori estimate) of arXiv:2608.29726, '\LARGE A Priori Estimates for Singular Fractional Stochastic Burgers Equations'] Let \((\alpha,\gamma)\) satisfy
\eqref{eq:admissible-alpha-gamma}, fix \(T>0\), and let \(m\) be a smooth
transformed solution on \([0,T]\), associated with a smooth enhancement in
the class of \Cref{prop:fractional-enhancement} and obtained through the
Da Prato--Debussche, linear response, and Zvonkin transformations of
\Cref{sec:enhanced-zvonkin}.  Initialize all stochastic coordinates at zero
and assume that \(m(0)=u_0\in C^\infty(\T)\).  Then
\[
 \norm m_{L^\infty(0,T;L^1)}
 {}+\norm m_{L^\infty(0,T;L^2)}
 {}+\norm m_{L^2(0,T;H^{\gamma/2})}
 {}+\norm m_{L^3(0,T;B^s_{3,3})}
\le C_{T,s}
\]
for every \(0<s<1/3\).  At \(\gamma=2\), the Besov term may be taken with
any \(0<s<1/2\).  The constant depends locally uniformly on \(T\), \(s\),
\(\norm{u_0}_{L^2}\), the enhanced-model norm, the uniform norm of the resolvent family,
and the resulting coefficient and Zvonkin norms.  If the resolvent parameter is
selected locally uniformly as in \Cref{prop:zvonkin}, the bound is therefore
uniform over bounded families of enhanced inputs.

[Theorem 12 (Jacobian master identity) of arXiv:2605.26107, 'Radial Extremality for LRU Caching and the Fill--Holst Conjecture'] Let $N\ge2$, $1\le C<N$, and let $q\in\Delta_N^\circ$ be nonuniform.  Put
$\lambda(\theta)=u+\theta(q-u)$ and
$\mathcal H(\theta)=H_C(\lambda(\theta))$.  Then, for $0<\theta\le1$,
\begin{equation}
        \mathcal H'(\theta)
        =
        \frac{1}{\theta}\left(H_C(\lambda(\theta))-\frac{C}{N}\right)
        +
        \frac{1}{N\theta}
        \sum_{1\le i<k\le N}
        G_{ik}(\lambda(\theta))
        (\lambda_i(\theta)-\lambda_k(\theta))^2.
\end{equation}
In particular $\mathcal H'(\theta)>0$ for $0<\theta\le1$.

[Lem properties_of_the_discrete_continuous_coupling of arXiv:2411.13964, 'Long-time analysis of a pair of on-lattice and continuous run-and-tumble particles with ja'] Let $X$ and the sequence of stochastic processes $(Y^L)_{L \ge 2}$ be
  as in definition~(def:discrete_continuous_coupling of the paper).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] Each $Y^L$ is a DITP (resp. DFTP).
\item[(ii)] Let $0 = T_0 < T_1 < \cdots$ be the jump times of the
  couple $(\sigma^1, \sigma^2)$. For all $t \ge 0$ one has
\begin{align*}
\left| i_L(y^L(t)) - x(t) \right| \le &\left| i_L(y^L(0)) - x(0) \right| + \frac{1}{\gamma_L} \sum_{k = 1}^{n(t)} \left| D_k(t) \right|
\end{align*}
where $n(t) = 1 + \sum_{k = 1}^{+\infty} 1_{\{T_k \le t\}}$ and
$$
D_k(t) = \sum_{i = 1, 2} (-1)^i \sigma^i(T_{k-1}) \Big[ N_i^L(T_k \wedge t) - N_i^L(T_{k-1} \wedge t) - \gamma_L \left( T_k \wedge t - T_{k-1} \wedge t \right)\Big].
$$
\end{itemize}

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] We have the following formula,
$$\sqrt{1+t}=1-2\sum_{k=1}^\infty C_{k-1}\left(\frac{-t}{4}\right)^k$$
with $C_k=\frac{1}{k+1}\binom{2k}{k}$ being the Catalan numbers. Also, we have
$$\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+t}}=\sum_{k=0}^\infty D_k\left(\frac{-t}{4}\right)^k$$
with $D_k=\binom{2k}{k}$ being the central binomial coefficients.

body:
[Lemma 14 (Interpolation bounds for the cubic Besov functional) of arXiv:2608.29726, '\LARGE A Priori Estimates for Singular Fractional Stochastic Burgers Equations'] Let \(1<\gamma\le2\), \(1-\gamma/2<\beta<1\), and let \(m\) be smooth
with \(\sup_{t\le T}\norm{m(t)}_{L^1}\le M\).
Let \(E_T\) and \(Z_T^\beta\) be as in
\Cref{prop:energy-cubic}.  For every \(\varepsilon>0\), the following
bounds hold with a finite constant \(C_\varepsilon\), whose value may
change from line to line and may depend on \(T,M,\gamma,\beta\), but not on
\(m\).
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=*]
\item If \(\beta>2-\gamma\), then
 \begin{equation}
 Z_T^\beta
 \le\varepsilon E_T+C_\varepsilon.
\end{equation}

\item If \(1<\gamma<2\) and
\(1-\gamma/2<\beta\le2-\gamma\), then there exists
\(s_0\in(1/12,1/3)\), depending only on
\(\gamma\) and \(\beta\), such that
 \begin{equation}
 Z_T^\beta
 \le\varepsilon\bigl(E_T+K_T^{s_0}\bigr)
 +C_\varepsilon.
 \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

body:
Nam-Fonseca-Lee-Mingard-Louis Lemma1: exact balanced gradient-flow skill dynamics. Use the finite fixed-basis noiseless model in the companion definition, with f(i,x)=sum_{k=1}^N a_k*b_k*g_k(i,x), target amplitude S>0 and 1<=N<=n_s. Fix D>=1 training examples and let d_k be the number whose task is k, so sum_{k=1}^{n_s} d_k=D. The source samples them iid from its task/bit distribution; the identity below holds conditional on any realized sample. Run continuous-time gradient flow with eta>0 on empirical half squared loss L_D=(1/(2D))*(sum_{k<=N} d_k*(S-a_k*b_k)^2+sum_{k>N} d_k*S^2). For each represented k assume a_k(0)=b_k(0) and 0<R_k(0)=a_k(0)*b_k(0)<S. Then for every T>=0, a_k(T)=b_k(T), R_k(T)=a_k(T)*b_k(T)=S/[1+(S/R_k(0)-1)*exp(-2*eta*S*(d_k/D)*T)], and L_k(T)=(S-R_k(T))^2/2. In particular d_k=0 leaves R_k constant; d_k>0 gives R_k(T) increasing to S. Omitted skills k>N retain conditional loss S^2/2. This is a continuous gradient-flow identity for trainable scalar factors of fixed skill functions, not a convergence theorem for feature learning or finite-step stochastic gradient descent. Without balance the scalar product derivative is eta*(d_k/D)*(a_k^2+b_k^2)*(S-a_k*b_k), which does not generally reduce to the displayed logistic equation.
Same fixed-basis model and empirical half squared loss; D>=1 and eta>0.
Equal scalar factors at initialization with product strictly between zero and S; continuous gradient flow.

body:
[Theorem T:Markov-process of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] For $\rho \in \mathbb{R} \cup \{-\infty\}$, take any half-space pre-landscape $\mathcal{M}^\rho$, continuously extended to $\mathbb{H}^2_\uparrow$.
 Consider a function $f \in \operatorname{UC}_{0,+}$.
For each $t > 0$, define the process
$\mathfrak{h}^\rho_t f = f \diamond \mathcal{M}^\rho_{0, t}$, and set $\mathfrak{h}^\rho_0 f = f$.
Then $(\mathfrak{h}^\rho_t, t \ge 0)$ is a time-homogeneous Markov process on $\operatorname{UC}_{0,+}$, whose law does not depend on the choice of pre-landscape. Moreover, for almost surely $\mathcal{M}^\rho$, $(t,f)\mapsto \mathfrak{h}^\rho_tf$ is continuous on $\operatorname{UC}_{0,+}$, and $\mathfrak{h}^\rho_t f$ is a continuous function for each $t > 0, f \in \operatorname{UC}_{0,+}$. Lastly, for any finite set $Y \subset \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}, t > 0$ and any function $f \in \operatorname{UC}_{0,+}$  satisfying
\begin{equation}
    
    \limsup_{x \to \infty}\frac{f(x)}{x} < \infty,
\end{equation}
the marginal
$
(\mathfrak{h}^\rho_t f(y) : y \in Y)
$
is given by Theorem (T:half-space-fixed-point of the paper). 
The Markov process $(\mathfrak{h}^\rho_t, t \ge 0)$ is the \textbf{KPZ fixed point in half-space} with parameter $\rho$.

Let $x_1,\dots,x_N$ be random points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose joint law is invariant under reflection of any subset of them through the origin, and which are almost surely in general position. Then the probability that all of them lie in a single open halfspace whose boundary contains the origin, equivalently the probability that the origin is not in their convex hull, equals $2^{-N+1}\sum_{k=0}^{d-1}\binom{N-1}{k}$. In particular this probability is $1$ whenever $N \le d$. Note that symmetry alone does not suffice: general position is needed, since for instance two points i.i.d. uniform on $\{\pm e_1\} \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ are symmetric yet give probability $0$.
the joint law of the points is invariant under reflection of any subset through the origin
the points are almost surely in general position (every d or fewer are linearly independent)
independence of the points is not required

\EE\cH^d(Z_o)^2\!
=\! \frac{\gamma^3 \pi^{d-2}}{32} \Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^2\!\!
G_{10, 10}^{5, 5} \left(
1 \middle| \begin{matrix}
	1-a,\,1-a,\,1-a,\,\frac{5-d}{4},\,\frac{3-d}{4},\,a+\frac{d+1}{2},\,a+\frac{d+1}{2},\,a+\frac{d+1}{2},\,0,\,\frac{1}{2} \\
	a,\,a,\,a,\,\frac{d-1}{4},\,\frac{d+1}{4},\,\frac{1-d}{2}-a,\,\frac{1-d}{2}-a,\,\frac{1-d}{2}-a,\,1,\,\frac{1}{2}
\end{matrix}
\right)\!,
\]
where $a = \frac{1}{4} \big( \frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{\pi}} \frac{\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)}{\Gamma\left(\frac{d+1}{2}\right)} - d + 1 \big)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 2 of arXiv:2608.27634, 'Curvature-Aware Radius Shrinkage for Adaptive Nearest Neighbor Classification'] Let $x_{(1)}, x_{(2)}, \dots, x_{(k_{\mathrm{base}})}$ denote the
	$k_{\mathrm{base}}$ nearest training neighbors of $x$, sorted by increasing
	distance $d(x, x_{(1)}) \le d(x, x_{(2)}) \le \dots \le d(x,
	x_{(k_{\mathrm{base}})})$, and let $r^{(0)}(x) = d(x, x_{(k_{\mathrm{base}})})$
	be the reference radius of Eq.~(3). Then restricting the voting set to the
	$k(x)$ closest neighbors, as in Eq.~\eqref{eq:ki}, is equivalent to voting
	within the closed metric ball of radius
	\begin{equation}
		r(x) = d\big(x, x_{(k(x))}\big) \le r^{(0)}(x),
		
	\end{equation}
	i.e., $\{x_{(1)}, \dots, x_{(k(x))}\} = B(x, r(x)) \cap \mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{train}}$
	(up to distance ties), with $r(x) = r^{(0)}(x)$ exactly when $k(x) =
	k_{\mathrm{base}}$ (i.e., $s(x) = 1$).

body:
[Proposition 19 (R\'enyi spectrum of a test martingale) of arXiv:2608.20337, 'Information on trajectories:\\ martingales and random times'] Let $(M_t)$ be a nonnegative martingale with $M_0=1$.
Taking the single factor $\Pi=M$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:pathspace} gives the wealth cumulant $\Phi_T(s)=\log\E_P[M_T^{\,s}]$, convex in $s$, with
\[
  \Phi_T(1)=0,\qquad
  \Phi_T'(0)=\E_P[\log M_T]=-\KL(P\|Q_M),\qquad
  \Phi_T'(1)=\E_P[M_T\log M_T]=\KL(Q_M\|P),
\]
for $\dd Q_M/\dd P := M_T$.
The separation between the typical value and the mass-holding one is $\Phi_T'(1)-\Phi_T'(0)=\KL(Q_M\|P)+\KL(P\|Q_M)$.
For a likelihood-ratio stream $M_T=\prod_{t\le T}R_t$, at any $s$ where the conditional one-step cumulants $\log\E_P[R_t^{\,s}\mid\cF_{t-1}]$ are all deterministic --- independent steps being the canonical case --- the spectrum is their sum, $\Phi_T(s)=\sum_{t\le T}\log\E_P[R_t^{\,s}]$, evaluated term by term without simulating a single path. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: R\'enyi spectrum of a test martingale

[Definition def:cavity-interpolation-planted-sk of arXiv:2605.03718, 'Potential Hessian Ascent III:\\ Sampling the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick Model at $\beta < 1/'] {cadel2010sherrington}}]
    Consider the Hamiltonian of the planted model (with the functions of the last site isolated):
    \[
        \beta H(\sigma) = \sqrt{\frac{(n-1)}{n}}\beta H_{n-1}(\rho) + \frac{\beta^2}{2n} + \frac{\beta}{2}A_{nn} + \sigma_n\left(g(\rho) + (y_t)_n\right)\, , 
    \]
    where $\rho = \left(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}\right)$, $(y_t)_n \sim \mathcal N(t,\beta^2 t)$, $A_{nn}\sim\mathcal N\left(0,\frac{2}{n}\right)$ and 
    \[
        g(\rho) := \frac{\beta^2}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\sigma_i + \beta\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}A_{i,n}\sigma_i\,.
    \]
    The interpolation that smoothly decouples a $(n-1)$-dimensional configuration $\rho$ and a $n$-dimensional configuration $\sigma = \rho\cdot\sigma_n$ for the Hamiltonian $H_t(\sigma)$ with magnetization $m \in [-1,1]$ and overlap $q \in [0,1]$ is defined as
    \begin{align}
        \beta H_t(\sigma) := &\sqrt{\frac{(n-1)}{n}}\beta H_{n-1}(\rho) + \frac{\beta^2}{2n} + \frac{\beta}{2}A_{nn} +\left\{g_t(\rho) +(y_t)_n\right\}\sigma_n \nonumber\, ,
    \end{align}
    where
    \begin{equation}
        g_t(\rho) := \beta^2\left(\frac{t}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\sigma_i+ (1-t)m\right)  + \beta\left(\sqrt{t}\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}A_{in}\sigma_i + \sqrt{1-t}\sqrt{q}\,h\right)\, ,
    \end{equation}
    for $t \in [0,1]$ and $h \sim \mathcal N(0,1)$.

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2608.30178, '2608.30178'] Assume that the model $(X, Y)$ in \eqref{eq:noimm-system} is
source-conservative.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If \(r_1\ge0\), then \(\Pp_{x,y}(\tauX<\infty)=0\).
\item If \(r_2\ge0\) and \(\theta_2\ge1\), then
\(\Pp_{x,y}(\tauY<\infty)=0\).
\item If \(0\le\theta_2<1\), then
\beqlb 
 a_2(1-\theta_2)\E_{x,y}\int_0^{\tau_0}X_s^{\kappa_2}\dd s
 =a_2(1-\theta_2)\E_{x,y}\int_0^{\tauY}X_s^{\kappa_2}\dd s \le y^{1-\theta_2}.
\eeqlb
In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \left\{\int_0^\infty X_s^{\kappa_2}\dd s=\infty\right\}
 \subseteq\{\tauY<\infty\}
 \qquad\text{almost surely}.
 
\end{equation}
Moreover, for every \(T,L>0\),
\beqnn
 \Pp_{x,y}\left(
 \tauY>T,
 \ \int_0^T X_s^{\kappa_2}\dd s\ge L
 \right)
 \le\frac{y^{1-\theta_2}}{a_2(1-\theta_2)L}.
 \eeqnn
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2506.15736, 'Coming down from infinity for coordinated particle systems'] Suppose that a coordinated particle system $(X(t))_{t \geq 0}$ on a finite set of sites $V$ with no reproduction. Suppose $(X(t))_{t \geq 0}$ stays infinite. Then the following three conditions must be met.

    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)] There exists a site $v_1 \in V$ with $X_{v_1}(0) = \infty$.
        
        \item[(b)] There exists a site $v_k \in V$ such that the $\Lambda_{v_k}$-coalescent does not come down from infinity. 

        \item[(c)] There exist sites $v_2, \ldots, v_{k-1}$ such that for every $i = 1, \ldots, k-1$ either $M_{v_iv_{i+1}}(dz)$ or $R_{v_iv_{i+1}}(dz)$ is $\Lambda_{v_i}$-strong.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 44 (Uniform lifted linear Schauder estimate) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Fix \(m\geq2\) and \(\sigma\in(0,1)\).  Let \(s(t)\), \(a\leq t\leq b\),
be a Ricci flow satisfying \(\PBG_m(s;\Lambda;[a,b])\) for some \(\Lambda\geq1\).
Let \(E\) be a fixed finite-rank tensor bundle and consider,
on the universal cover and in the charts of
Lemma~\ref{lem:uniform-parabolic-atlas}, a system
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal P U
 =\partial_tU-a^{ij}\nabla_i\nabla_jU-B^i\nabla_iU-CU=F.
\end{equation}
Assume that the second-order part is diagonal in the bundle components and
uses the same coefficient matrix \(a^{ij}\) on every component.  For fixed
constants \(0<\lambda_-\leq\lambda_+<\infty\), suppose that
\[
 \lambda_- s^{ij}\xi_i\xi_j\leq a^{ij}\xi_i\xi_j
 \leq\lambda_+ s^{ij}\xi_i\xi_j,
\]
and that the local
\(C^{m-2+\sigma,(m-2+\sigma)/2}\)-norms of \(a,B,C\) are bounded by
\(A_0\).

Every smooth bounded solution on the universal cover satisfies, for
\(\theta>0\) with \(a+\theta\leq b\),
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 \|U\|_{C^{m+\sigma,(m+\sigma)/2}_{\mathrm{uloc}}
          (\widetilde M\times[a+\theta,b],s)}
 \leq C_\theta\bigl(&
       \|U\|_{C^0(\widetilde M\times[a,b],s)}\\
       &+\|F\|_{C^{m-2+\sigma,(m-2+\sigma)/2}_{\mathrm{uloc}}}\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
For the global estimate, assume in addition that \(\mathcal P\) is
deck-invariant, equivalently that the coefficient fields \(a,B,C\) descend to
\(M\).  If \(U\) and \(F\) are deck-invariant and descend to tensors \(u\)
and \(f\) on \(M\), with \(u(a)\in C^{m,\sigma}\) and
\(f\in Y_s^m[a,b]\), then
\begin{equation}
 \|u\|_{X_s^m[a,b]}
 \leq C\left(
      \|u(a)\|_{C^{m,\sigma}(M,s(a))}
      +\|f\|_{Y_s^m[a,b]}\right).
\end{equation}
The constants depend only on
\(m,\sigma,\Lambda,\lambda_-,\lambda_+,A_0\), on \(\theta\) in the interior
estimate, and on an upper bound for \(b-a\).  The interior and initial-face
estimates are based, respectively, on Lieberman's interior Schauder theorem
\cite[Theorem~4.9, p.~59]{Lieberman} and his Cauchy--Dirichlet Schauder theorem
\cite[Theorem~4.28, p.~77]{Lieberman}.  All atlas-radius, overlap, and cutoff
constants, fixed-coordinate ellipticity constants, localized initial-face
boundary-chart constants, and coefficient H\"older constants are uniform over
the admissible family specified by \(\PBG_m\) and the displayed bounds.  In
particular, the constants are independent of collapse of the compact quotient.

The transductive covariance-penalty criterion of the label-free blend selects by the cross-validated relative squared loss, while the pools score by the mean per-row ratio. On the benchmark corpora the two orderings part on pkanrtm (24,000 calibration rows, a near-zero-target tail): the squared-loss criterion picks the simplex, the worst vertex, on every cell. The same criterion written in the score's own metric, R_1(w) = mean_i sqrt(max(r_i + delta(w), 0)), repairs it. Measured 2026-09-06: P39 (a) REFUTED: the ratio-metric blend vs the best vertex on pkanrtm = -0.93 (within 0.3); (b) REFUTED: vs the registered blend on the other corpora = advection -0.02, darcy +0.40, burgers -1.74 (within 0.2); (c) HELD: it beats least squares on 48 of 55 cells (87 pct); falsifier (worse than the registered blend by more than 0.3 on any corpus, or worse than the best vertex on pkanrtm by more than 1.0) TRIGGERED. On the pools the blend was built on (EMIT, OCO-2, both splits): P40 (a) HELD: the R_1 blend vs the registered blend = B-emit +0.48, B-oco +0.14, C-emit +1.52, C-oco +0.16 (within 0.2); (b) HELD: wins over least squares R_1 vs registered = B-emit 38/39, B-oco 30/30, C-emit 40/36, C-oco 30/30 (at least the registered count less three); (c) REFUTED: the two selections coincide on B-emit 3 of 40, B-oco 0 of 30, C-emit 0 of 40, C-oco 0 of 30 cells (at least half); falsifier (R_1 worse than the registered blend by more than 0.3 on either corpus on either split) not triggered. P43: the metric on the third family, fresh split (P43): P43 (a) HELD: on the fresh split the registered blend reads -46.02 vs the best vertex on pkanrtm (the P38 falsifier fires again); (b) REFUTED: the R_1 blend vs the best vertex = advection -0.02, darcy +0.80, burgers -0.98, pkanrtm -0.28 (within 0.3 everywhere); (c) HELD: R_1 vs the registered blend on the other three = advection -0.02, darcy +0.56, burgers -0.13 (within 0.2); (d) HELD: the simplex-vs-least-squares signs by corpus match the first split; falsifier (R_1 worse than the best vertex by more than 1.0 on any corpus) not triggered.
the score is the mean per-row ratio ||e|| / max(||y||, floor); the criterion's cross-validated loss is the mean squared ratio; the transductive variance shift delta(w) = V_ev(w) - V_cal(w) is estimated by the pairs bootstrap of the fitted predictor at both row sets
measured on the benchmark corpora (advection, Darcy at four betas, Burgers at four viscosities, pkanrtm and pkanrtm-lowfi) with the three vertices simplex / least squares / pool heuristic and the 0.1 barycentric grid; the EMIT / OCO-2 check is P40

Write rho_i = ||f(x_i) - y_i|| / m_i for the per-row ratio. Then S = mean rho_i and Q = mean rho_i^2 = (mean rho_i)^2 + var(rho_i). Two estimators f and g with the same S can differ in Q by the difference of their ratio variances, and an estimator with the smaller Q can have the larger S whenever its ratios are less dispersed but larger on average - the ordering by Q is the ordering by S only when the ratio dispersion is comparable across candidates. On a corpus whose ratios have a heavy right tail (near-floor rows, where a fixed absolute error is a ratio of hundreds), the dispersion term dominates Q and the candidates are ordered by their tails, not by their mean ratio. The ratio criterion R_1(w) = mean_i sqrt(max(r_i + delta(w), 0)), with r_i the out-of-fold relative squared residual of candidate w at calibration row i and delta(w) the variance shift of the scored rows over the calibration rows, is an estimate of S under the same transductive correction, since E||e|| ~ sqrt(bias^2 + variance) row by row; it reduces to the cross-validated score when delta = 0 and to the same ordering as Q when the ratios are homoscedastic across candidates.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:ef75b230c5d868157d3a3f1951176d5c0d43d12f8c53d6fe40b4f866e828f2e7","revision_digest":"sha256:56366f50180f11ea42ef50cdc3da5ab7798148284956f092920ed76a1246a859","source_id":"measurement of 2026-09-05/06 (ens_rmt_bench3.py, analyze_bench3.py); RMT_ENSEMBLE_THEORY.md 6ao / 6ap","source_revision":"as-read-2026-09-05","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":["claim_78ede5727d3ca5ff1b9ac9270c2fa52c0f165ec6857efe2847021006a1c90698"],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body: [Lem count-long-edges of arXiv:2411.14336, 'Finding the root in random nearest neighbor trees'] This algorithm satisfies the property that, for all $\varepsilon > 0$ sufficiently small and all $n \in \mathbf{N}$, $\mathbf{P} \{ 1 \in H(\varepsilon,n)\} \geq 1 - \varepsilon \text{ and } |H(\varepsilon,n)| \leq {2^{d}}/{\varepsilon}$. The algorithm runs in $O(n)$ time. Furthermore, there exists $c > 0$ such that with probability at least $1 - \varepsilon$, $|H(\varepsilon,n)| \subseteq \{1, \dots, \tau\}$ for $\tau = \exp(cd)\cdot (1/\varepsilon)\log(1/\varepsilon)$.

[Defn 5 (Good sequence of initial data) of arXiv:2510.22155, 'Random walks in space-time random media in all spatial dimensions: the full subcritical fl'] We say that the deterministic sequence of measures $\mathfrak m_N(\dr x)$ on $\mathbb R^d$ is a \textbf{good sequence of measures} if $$\sup_N \mathfrak m_N(\{a\in \mathbb R^d:|a|\ge M\}) \leq Ce^{-c M}$$ for some $C,c>0$ independent of $M\ge 0$, and furthermore there exists $\e>0$ 
for which one has the estimate uniform over $t\in (0,1]$ and $N\ge 1$: $$\sup_{a\in \mathbb R^d} | (\mathfrak m_N, G_t(a-\bullet))_{L^2(\mathbb R^d)} | \leq C(t\vee N^{-1})^{\e-1}$$ for some $\e>0$. Here $G_t(x) = (2\pi t)^{-d/2} e^{-|x|^2/2t}$ is the $d$-dimensional heat kernel.

[Lemma lem:singularinvariance2 of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] Let \(T\) be a ladderpole tube.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If more than one components of \(F_{\tau}\cap T\) meet \(v_{i}\), then between two adjacent components, a product annulus connects them near \(v_{i}\).
\item If \(v_{i}\) and \(v_{i+1}\) have opposite coorientation, then there is an edge connecting \(v_{i}\) and \(v_{i+1}\).
\item If \(v_{i}\) and \(v_{i+1}\) have same coorientation, then no edge connects \(v_{i}\) and \(v_{i+1}\).
In this case, let \(S_{i}\) be the component which meets \(v_{i}\) and is closest to \(v_{i+1}\) and let \(S_{i+1}\) be the component which meets \(v_{i+1}\) and is closest to \(v_{i}\). Then, a product annulus in \(T\) connects \(S_{i}\) and \(S_{i+1}\).
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2608.29427, '\small Positive mass and rigidity \\ for asymptotically flat tangent bundles'] Let $(M,g)$ be a contractible AF manifold. Suppose that $g$ is weakly trace-majorizing, has decay rate
	\[
	\sigma\geq n-2,
	\]
	and has nonnegative integrable scalar curvature. Let $\widetilde g$ be an admissible metric on $TM$. Then the connecting metric $\mathdutchcal g$ is flat and
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item[\small \textbf{\textsf{(a)}}] \emph{\small \textsf{\textbf{Positivity of mass.}}}
		\[
		0\leq
		\underline{\m}(TM,\widetilde g,\zeta)
		\leq
		\overline{\m}(TM,\widetilde g,\zeta)
		<\infty,
		\]
		for any set of preffered coordinates $\zeta$.
		If, in addition, $g$ is weakly trace-rigid, then the ADM mass of $\left(TM, \widetilde g\right)$ in the preffered coordinates exist and
		\[
		 \m(TM,\widetilde g, \zeta) =
		\frac{(n-1)\omega_{n-1}}
		{(2n-1)\omega_{2n-1}}
		\m(M,g).
		\]
		\item[\small \textbf{\textsf{(b)}}] \emph{\small \textsf{\textbf{Rigidity.}}}
		If in a set of preferred coordinates,
		\[
		\underline{\m}(TM,\widetilde g,\zeta)=0,
		\]
		then
		\[
		(M,g)\cong_{\mathrm{isom}}(\mathbb R^n,\delta).
		\]
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

For a measurable f on a measure space (X, Sigma, mu), the distribution function is d_f(t) = mu({x : |f(x)| > t}) for t > 0; it is nonincreasing and right-continuous. For 0 < p < infinity the weak L^p quasi-norm is ||f||_{L^{p,infinity}} = sup_{t>0} t * d_f(t)^{1/p}, and weak L^p = L^{p,infinity}(mu) is the set of (a.e.-classes of) measurable f with this quantity finite; by convention L^{infinity,infinity} = L^infinity. It is a quasi-norm: ||f+g||_{L^{p,infinity}} <= max(2, 2^{1/p}) (||f||_{L^{p,infinity}} + ||g||_{L^{p,infinity}}), from d_{f+g}(t) <= d_f(t/2) + d_g(t/2). Chebyshev's inequality gives L^p contained in L^{p,infinity} with ||f||_{L^{p,infinity}} <= ||f||_p, and the inclusion is strict in general: on R^n, |x|^{-n/p} lies in L^{p,infinity} but not in L^p. For 1 < p < infinity, L^{p,infinity} admits an equivalent norm; L^{1,infinity}(R^n) admits none.

[Proposition 31 (Response completion of the central skeleton) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Let $L=(L_A,L_Q)$ be admissible.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.4em]
\item The finite-rank product
\[
 (x,a,q)\star(y,b,r)
 =\bigl(x+y,a+b+\Anti(x\otimes y),q+r\bigr)
\]
extends uniquely to a continuous two-step topological group law on
\begin{equation}
 \Gito_L(H):=H\times E_A[L]\times E_Q[L].
\end{equation}
This group is the completion of the common finite-rank central skeleton in the
response norm $\|x\|+\|a\|_{L_A}+\|q\|_{L_Q}$.

\item The evaluation maps
\[
 a\longmapsto(\lambda(a))_{\lambda\in L_A},
 \qquad
 q\longmapsto(\mu(q))_{\mu\in L_Q}
\]
extend isometrically from $E_A[L]$ and $E_Q[L]$ onto the closures of their
finite-rank images in the corresponding supremum-norm function spaces.  Thus
the completed central topology is exactly the initial topology generated by
the bundled probes.

\item Suppose $\mathfrak I(H)$ is a separable rank-one-normalized Banach
operator ideal in which finite-rank operators are dense, with
$\mathcal S_1(H)\hookrightarrow\mathfrak I(H)$, and, on
finite-rank skew and self-adjoint operators, the probe norms satisfy
\begin{equation}
 c_A^{-1}\|a\|_{\mathfrak I}
 \le\|a\|_{L_A}\le C_A'\|a\|_{\mathfrak I},
 \qquad
 c_Q^{-1}\|q\|_1
 \le\|q\|_{L_Q}\le C_Q'\|q\|_1.
\end{equation}
Then the identity on the finite-rank skeleton extends to a canonical
bi-Lipschitz group isomorphism
\[
 \Gito_L(H)\cong
 H\times\mathfrak I(H)_{\rm sk}\times\mathcal S_1(H)_{\rm sa}.
\]
For the complete dual unit balls the identification is isometric.
\end{enumerate}

For t>0, the normalized tilt exp((1-t)x-tx^2/2) has variance (1-2/pi)/t: X+1 becomes half-normal with precision t. These laws are log-concave, and both variances can be arbitrarily large compared with the original variance 1. These deterministic examples do not refute KLS normalized with the current covariance, or an averaged localization estimate.
Dimension one
s<1 for the linear tilt
t>0 for the quadratic tilt
Normalized deterministic tilt family
title: DRAFT: exact exponential tilted covariance obstruction

[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2604.07207, 'Mixing times of step-reinforced random walks'] Given $\F_{t(k)}$ for some $k \leq \lfloor L/40 \rfloor$. On the event $E_{1}(k)$, for any $j\in \mathscr{I}_{t(k)}$, one has 
$$
\EE (|\CalC_{j,n}| \mid \F_{t(k)}) \mathds{1}_{E_{1}(k)} = \frac{a_n}{a_{t(k)}} \mathds{1}_{E_{1}(k)}, \quad \text{where } a_m:=\prod_{k=1}^{m-1}\left(1+\frac{\alpha}{k}\right),\  m\geq 1.
$$
Moreover, there exists a positive constant $H_0=H_0(\alpha)$ such that if $H\geq H_0$, then for any $k \leq \lfloor L/40 \rfloor$ and any $j\in \mathscr{I}_{t(k)}$, one has
  $$
 \PP\left(|\CalC_{j,n}| \geq \frac{L}{2k} \mid  \F_{t(k)} \right)\mathds{1}_{E_{1}(k)} < \frac{\mathds{1}_{E_{1}(k)}}{8},   \quad \text{and} \quad \PP\left(|\CalC_{j,n}| \geq \frac{L}{96 k} \mid \F_{t(k)}  \right) \geq \frac{9}{32} \mathds{1}_{E_{1}(k)}. 
  $$

[Lemma 44 (Common finite-rank approximation on the intersection branch) of arXiv:2606.29292, 'Intrinsic Gaussian Tensor Geometry and Random Operator Spectra'] Let $2\le r<\infty$.  For $1\le j\le m$, let $R_{j,n}$ be increasing
finite-rank orthogonal projections on $\cH_j$ converging strongly to the
identity, and let $C_n$ and $E_n$ have the same properties on $\cC$ and
$\cE$.  Define on algebraic kernels
\[
 \Pi_nK
 :=(R_{1,n}\otimes\cdots\otimes R_{m,n}
    \otimes\conj{C_n}\otimes E_n)K.
\]
Then $\Pi_n$ extends contractively to $\mathfrak T_{m,r}$ and
\begin{equation}

 \Prof_{m,r}(\Pi_nK-K)\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad K\in\mathfrak T_{m,r}.
\end{equation}
With fixed real forms, the stochastic projections may be chosen as
complexifications of real orthogonal projections.  Using one such sequence
in every stochastic leg preserves symmetry and yields the analogous
convergence on $\mathfrak W_{m,r}$.

[Theorem thm:extremal of arXiv:2608.11931, '\texorpdfstring{Nonlinear parabolic characterizations of stochastic completeness at infini'] Let $u_0\in\ell^\infty(X)$.  Choose constants
\[
    A\le \min\{0,\inf_X u_0\}
    \qquad \text{and} \qquad
    B\ge \max\{0,\sup_X u_0\}.
\]
Then, there exist global bounded pointwise solutions $u^A,u^B$ of
the (eq:GPME of the paper) with initial datum $u_0$ satisfying
\[
    A\le u^A\le u^B\le B
    \qquad\text{on }[0,\infty)\times X.
\]
For every $T>0$, the restriction of $u^A$ to $[0,T]\times X$ is minimal
among all bounded pointwise solutions on that time interval lying above $A$
while the restriction of $u^B$ is maximal among all bounded pointwise
solutions lying below $B$.  In particular, if $v$ is any bounded pointwise
solution on $[0,T]\times X$ with $A\le v\le B$, then
\begin{equation}
    u^A\le v\le u^B
    \qquad\text{on }[0,T]\times X.
\end{equation}
If $u_0\ge0$, the choice $A=0$ gives a global minimal positive solution $u^0$
satisfying
\[
    0\le u^0(t,x)\le \|u_0\|_\infty
    \qquad\text{on }[0,\infty)\times X.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:extremal of arXiv:2608.11931

[Thm 23 of arXiv:2603.27433, 'The $k$-cycle shuffling with repeated cards'] Let $(n_N)_{N\ge 1},(m_N)_{N\ge 1},(l_N)_{N\ge 1},(k_N)_{N\ge 1}$, and $(t_N)_{N\ge 1}$ be sequences of positive integers that satisfy the following:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $n_N=m_N\cdot l_N$ for all $N\ge 1$.
\item $\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}l_N=\infty$, but $\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\frac{l_N}{\log n_N}=0$.
\item $k_N\ge 2$ for all $N\ge 1$, and $\limsup_{N\rightarrow\infty}\log n_N k_N\le c_0$, where $c_0\in[0,1)$ is an absolute constant.
\item $t_N=\frac{n_N}{k_N}(\log n_N-\frac 12\log l_N+c)$ for all $N\ge 1$, where $c\in\R$ is an absolute constant.
\end{enumerate}
Then, we have
$$\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}d_{TV}(\sim_{l_N}\backslash P_{n_N,k_N}^{*t_N},\sim_{l_N}\backslash U_{\S_{n_N}})=2\Phi(\exp(-c)/2)-1.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 23 of arXiv:2603.27433

body: In the mathematics of chaos theory, a horseshoe map is any member of a class of chaotic maps of the square into itself. It is a core example in the study of dynamical systems. The map was introduced by Stephen Smale while studying the behavior of the orbits of the van der Pol oscillator. The action of the map is defined geometrically by squishing the square, then stretching the result into a long strip, and finally folding the strip into the shape of a horseshoe.
title: Horseshoe map

[Lemm 17 of arXiv:2609.01105, 'Obstruction to quasi-invariance of Gaussian measures under transport flows on Riemannian M'] Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth boundaryless complete Riemannian manifold. Assume that the flow $X_{t,t_0}$ of a vector field $u \in L^1_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R},\mathcal{C}^{1,\varepsilon}(M))$, as defined in \eqref{eq:defX}, satisfies the following property: for all $t_0 \in \Rr$ and all $x \in M$ there exists $\delta=\delta(t_0,x)>0$ such that for all $t\in \Rr $ satisfying $|t-t_0|\leq \delta$, 
\[
    \Jac X_{t,t_0}(x) : (T_xM,g(x)) \longrightarrow (T_{X_{t,t_0}(x)}M,g(X_{t,t_0}(x)))
\]
is an isometry. 
Then, for almost every $t$, the vector field $u(t)$ is a Killing field, namely: 
\[
    	\nabla_i u_j(t)+\nabla_j u_i(t) = 0.
\]
Conversely, if for almost all~\(t\), we have 
\[
    	\nabla_i u_j(t)+\nabla_j u_i(t) = 0,
\]
then for all~\(t\in \Rr\) and all~\(x\in M\), we have that~\(\Jac X_t (x)\) is an isometry.

A finite irreducible Markov-modulated Poisson process can have time-stationary forward-wait SCV below one, although its event-stationary interarrival SCV is at least one. On a unit-rate directed n-cycle with uniform stationary phase, arrival rate h>0 at one phase and zero at all others, m=E[X]=(n-1)/2+n/h and SCV(X)=1-(n-1)(n-5)/(6*m*m). Hence SCV(X)<1 for n>=6. For n=6,h=100 it equals 21451/24576. With rates (100,1/1000,1/1000,1/1000,1/1000,1/1000), exact arithmetic gives about0.8740277570. Across all finite irreducible MMPPs with nonzero nonnegative arrival rates the infimum of time-stationary SCV is1/3. This is a mathematical derivation with novelty unverified; it refutes the time-stationary proposal in He2021 section4.3, not his proved event-stationary theorem.
Q is a finite irreducible continuous-time Markov generator
D is a nonzero nonnegative diagonal arrival-rate matrix
Time-stationary initial phase is pi; event-stationary initial phase is pi D/(pi D 1)

[Theorem Main 4 of arXiv:2609.02871, 'Estimating the number of real zeros of linear combinations of radicals of polynomials'] Let $a_k, b_k$ and $c_k$ be real numbers.  Let $\alpha \in (-\infty, -1/2)$. If the function
\[
f(x)=\sum_{k=1}^{n}c_{k}[(x-a_{k})^{2}+b_{k}^{2}]^{\alpha}
\]
is not identically zero, then $f$ has no more than $4n-2$ critical points. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Method: Martingale estimates for the axis-switching walk Result: The axis of the next step is predictable from the past, while its sign is fair. Obstruction: Zero speed and a diffusive second moment do not imply recurrence. The occupation-dependent balance of the two coordinate clocks remains uncontrolled.
