STATUS: proof (unaudited). For the regularized Gaussian/ReLU reciprocal-angle transition, fixed K>0, bounded C5 tests with bounded derivatives, sufficiently small fixed theta_star>0 and theta=1/(nu)<=theta_star, 0<u<=K, the complete C032 operators A,B obey |n(P_n f-f)-Af-Bf/n| <= C_K[(u+sqrt(u))/n^(3/2)+(1+1/u+1/u^2)/n^2+n exp(-cn)]. The same bound holds for the exact killed kernel with bounded cemetery test value. The permitted u interval extends down to 1/(n theta_star). Independent Gaussian rows, zero-bias ReLU, width n sufficiently large; A=(2u+a)D+u^2 D^2 and B=(10u+6a/5+b/u)D+(11u^2+12au/5+a^2/2)D^2+(4u^3+au^2)D^3+(u^4/2)D^4, a=1/(3pi), b=1/(6pi^2); regularization is C032 normalized-Gram self-loop off a small concentration box. Construction: use n iid rows (x,y)=(max(g,0),max(cos(theta)g+sin(theta)h,0)), g,h independent standard Gaussians. The output angle is the angle between the two n-vectors; kill if either norm or the angle is zero. For regularization, self-loop when the sample averages of (x^2+y^2,(x-y)^2/theta^2,(x^2-y^2)/theta) leave a sufficiently small fixed box about their population mean. Constants may depend on K, theta_star, the test derivative bounds and bounded cemetery value. Depends on unaudited C032 estimates. The pointwise remainder is not an occupation estimate. Uniform stochastic control of inverse u along early entrance and matching to the semigroup sensitivity remain open; no global network rate is claimed.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:b090c632f1e5de1c6f7ad4f40b7bbe00f61c62942e72d69d83ad2b46c530c819","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/b0/b090c632f1e5de1c6f7ad4f40b7bbe00f61c62942e72d69d83ad2b46c530c819.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:a439b634a9bb55f65381a01fac0ee04abcb05fa30d364c04315eee7cbb214e93","bundle_entry_key":"relu-two-parameter-weak-remainder","bundle_id":"population.t244-entrance-uniform-local-remainder-013","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; random neural networks","draft":"w691/bundle_013.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.randomnetworks:t244-relu-two-parameter-weak-remainder","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C036: a two-parameter weak remainder extending the compact calculation

Version 1, 20 October 2026. Target 1, kind moved, proof (unaudited).
This is a local estimate, conditional on the constructions and moment
calculations proved in the unaudited C032. It is not a finite-horizon rate.

Put a=1/(3pi), b=1/(6pi^2), and define

    A=(2u+a)D+u^2 D^2,
    B=(10u+6a/5+b/u)D+(11u^2+12au/5+a^2/2)D^2
                          +(4u^3+au^2)D^3+(u^4/2)D^4.

Fix K>0 and a bounded C^5 function f on [0,infinity) with bounded derivatives
through order five. There exist theta_*>0 and positive constants C,c,n0,
depending on K and the derivative bounds, such that, for n>=n0 and

    0<u<=K,   theta=1/(nu)<=theta_*,

the C032 regularized transition satisfies

    | n(P_n f-f)(u)-Af(u)-Bf(u)/n |
       <= C[(u+sqrt(u))/n^(3/2)
                         +(1+1/u+1/u^2)/n^2+n exp(-cn)].       (1)

The same estimate holds for the exact transition killed at degeneracy,
with any fixed bounded cemetery value for f. Constants may depend on this
value. Unlike C032, the lower endpoint of the permitted u interval depends
on n and tends to zero. The bound becomes large near that endpoint; this
is explicitly retained rather than suppressed in a compact constant.

## Proof: retain the factors lost in compact notation

Use C032's normalized row coordinates Z_theta, means mu_theta and fixed
concentration box, with T_theta the reciprocal angle multiplier. All
coordinate derivatives of T_theta through order five are bounded there,
uniformly for 0<=theta<=theta_*. The same is true of the smooth coefficients
in its theta expansion T_theta=T0+theta^2 H+O(theta^4).

Each nonzero coordinate derivative of Phi_theta(z)=f(uT_theta(z)) has at
least one factor u. The remaining powers of u are bounded using u<=K.
Consequently each of its derivatives of orders one through five is bounded
by C_K u, not merely by an unspecified compact constant. The fifth-order
Taylor remainder for the sample average is at most C_K u n^(-5/2).
Polynomial terms deleted outside the concentration box have exponentially
small expectations, by uniform normalized Gaussian moments and Holder;
bounded transition terms have error at most C exp(-cn). After multiplying
by n these errors are bounded by C[u n^(-3/2)+n exp(-cn)].

For clarity, the resulting sample-average expansion, separating the
deterministic, covariance and higher centered-moment terms, is

    n(P_n f-f)
      = n[f(uT_theta(mu_theta))-f(u)]
        + Q(theta) + H0(u)/n
        + O_K(u n^(-3/2)+u sqrt(theta)/n
                                      +u theta^2+n exp(-cn)).   (2)

Here Q(theta)=Sigma_theta:D_z^2[f(uT0)](mu_theta)/2 and H0 is the
third-moment and paired fourth-moment coefficient at theta=0. The factor
u sqrt(theta)/n follows from the O(sqrt(theta)) variation of those row
moments and the factor u in each test derivative. Variation in the means
and coordinate derivatives is O(u theta/n), which is smaller. Replacing
T_theta by T0 in the covariance term costs O(u theta^2). The O(n^-3)
fourth-cumulant term before scaling is also absorbed by u n^(-3/2).

These estimates use no reciprocal moments of the unregularized chain.
The O(sqrt(theta)) moment bound can be verified by telescoping each product:
the differing factor has L2 norm O(sqrt(theta)) on the Gaussian sign-flip
strip and off it by Taylor expansion; all other factors have uniformly
bounded joint L2 products. Cauchy-Schwarz then bounds each difference.

The theta=0 coefficients Q(0)+H0/n are precisely the baseline terms C030:

    2u f'+u^2 f''
       +(10u f'+11u^2 f''+4u^3 f'''+u^4 f''''/2)/n,

up to O_K(u n^(-3/2)+n exp(-cn)). Alternatively the sample Taylor expansion
at theta=0 gives these coefficients directly, including this u factor.

The C032 covariance expansion sharpens to

    Q(theta)=Q(0)+theta[(6a/5)u f'+(12a/5)u^2 f''+a u^3 f''']
                                                    +O_K(u theta^2). (3)

Indeed Sigma_theta=Sigma0+theta Sigma1+O(theta^2), mu_theta has a uniform
second-order expansion, and differentiating the smooth test Hessian twice
in these deterministic coordinates costs at most C_K u. Bounded fourth
derivatives of f suffice for this step.

Finally the deterministic reciprocal map has the uniform expansion

    uT_theta(mu_theta)=u+a/n+b/(n^2 u)+O(1/(n^3 u^2)).

For theta<=theta_* its displacement is O(1/n). Taylor expansion of f to
order two, keeping the displayed linear and squared terms, therefore gives

    n[f(uT_theta(mu_theta))-f(u)]
      =a f'+[(b/u)f'+a^2 f''/2]/n
                             +O_K((1+1/u+1/u^2)/n^2).          (4)

The remainder includes the deterministic-map remainder, the mixed term
in the displacement squared, and the cubic test remainder. Substituting
theta=1/(nu) in (2)-(4) gives

    u sqrt(theta)/n=sqrt(u)/n^(3/2),
    u theta^2=1/(n^2 u),

and proves (1). The killed exact kernel differs only off the concentration
box, at cost at most C n exp(-cn) for bounded tests, completing the proof.

## What this does and does not pay for

If a path obeyed u_k comparable to k/n after an entrance layer m, the
singular part of the one-step remainder in (1), after division by n and
summation over k>=m, would be O(1/(nm)), since sum_(k>=m) k^-2=O(1/m).
This is a conditional arithmetic observation, not a proved path estimate.

The unresolved stochastic step is to obtain the appropriate occupation
and tail estimates for 1/u_k and 1/u_k^2, including rare slow entrances,
and then to match the early chain contribution to the semigroup
sensitivity. Compact containment alone supplies no such inverse bounds.
Thus (1) does not turn C034 into a network log(n)/n rate theorem.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:c3e2e521d8f6568c73d76b296f77bd4f1ce193dcca84e2457de51eb037ede795","revision_digest":"sha256:5657ba7b19a2724a945e569a0e6f575b6eea6169a5e5cbc305fbd47d8322bd6d","source_id":"own-work:T244-w691-C036:v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20-v1","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body:
[Lemma 22 of arXiv:2606.11994, 'Sample Path Properties of the\\ Fractional Wiener--Weierstrass Bridge II'] Assume $H>1/2$, and put $p=1/H$.  For step functions $f,g$ on
$[0,1]$, the inner product on $\calH$ has the concrete
representation
\begin{equation}   \left\langle f,g\right\rangle_{\calH}   =   H(2H-1)\int_0^1\int_0^1   f(x)g(y)|x-y|^{2H-2}\,\dd x\,\dd y .   
\end{equation}
Moreover, $L^p[0,1]$ embeds continuously into $\calH$: there is a finite
constant $C_H$ such that
\begin{equation}   \norm{f}_{\calH}   \le C_H\norm{f}_{L^p[0,1]},   \qquad f\in L^p[0,1].   
\end{equation}
Under this embedding, \eqref{eq:calH-inner-product} remains valid for all
$f,g\in L^p[0,1]$.  Finally,
\begin{equation*}   \norm{f}_{\calH}=0,\quad f\in L^p[0,1],   \quad\Longrightarrow\quad   f=0\text{ Lebesgue-a.e.}
      
\end{equation*}
In particular, the embedding $L^p[0,1]\hookrightarrow\calH$ is injective.

body: [Lemma 6 (Polynomial entropy implies a local bound) of arXiv:2602.20971, 'Does Order Matter : Connecting The Law of Robustness to Robust Gener'] Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a measurable class of functions bounded in $[0,b]$, where $b>0$. Assume that for some $p>2$ and $A>0$, $\sup_{Q}\log\mathcal{N}\left(\eta,\mathcal{G},L_{2}(Q)\right)\leq A\eta^{-p}\qquad\text{for all }0<\eta\leq b,$ where the supremum is over all finitely supported probability measures $Q$. For $r\geq 0$, define $\mathcal{G}(r)=\{g\in\mathcal{G}:Pg^{2}\leq r\}.$ Let $\bar{A}:=1\vee A$. Then there is a constant $C_{p,b}>0$, depending only on $p$ and $b$, such that $\mathfrak{R}_{n}(\mathcal{G}(r))\leq C_{p,b}\left(\bar{A}^{1/p}n^{-1/p}+\sqrt{\frac{r}{n}}\right).$ In particular, if $A\geq 1$, then $\mathfrak{R}_{n}(\mathcal{G}(r))\leq C_{p,b}\left(A^{1/p}n^{-1/p}+\sqrt{\frac{r}{n}}\right).$

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2609.03243, 'Weighted Ces\`aro type operators on the weighted Bergman spaces in the unit ball'] Let $\alpha>-1$, $\beta>0$ and $\mu$ be a positive Borel measure on $[0,1)$. 
Then the following assertions hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)]   For $0<p\leq1$, the operator $\mathcal{C}_{\mu,\beta}^{\xi}: A_{\alpha}^p(\mathbb{B}_n)\to H^{\infty}(\mathbb{B}_n)$  is bounded if and only if
  \[
    \sup_{0\leq r<1}
    \frac{\hat\mu(r)}{(1-r)^{\beta+(n+1+\alpha)/p}}<\infty.
\] 
\item[(ii)] For   $1<p<\infty$, let $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{p'}=1$.  Then $\mathcal{C}_{\mu,\beta}^{\xi}: A_{\alpha}^p(\mathbb{B}_n)\to H^{\infty}(\mathbb{B}_n)$ is bounded if and only if $\mu$ is finite and
\[
    \left\{\frac{\hat{\mu}(r_k)}{\delta_k^{\,\beta+(n+1+\alpha)/p}}\right\}_{k\geq 1}\in \ell^{p'}.
\]
\item[(iii)]   The operator $\mathcal{C}_{\mu,\beta}^{\xi}: H^{\infty}(\mathbb{B}_n)\to H^{\infty}(\mathbb{B}_n)$  is bounded if and only if
  \[
    \int_{[0,1)}\frac{{\rm d}\mu(t)}{(1-t)^{\beta}}<\infty.
\] 
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 3 of arXiv:2609.03243

[Proposition thm:GeoBM of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Let $M = \{M(x)\}_{x \in \mathbb{R}^d}$ be a non-negative, real-valued random field on $\mathbb{R}^d$ having fast $\mathbb{B} $-mixing correlations as in Definition~(d.omegatmixing-field of the paper)(i.B-mixing-field of the paper)-(i.mixing-field-fast of the paper).
Assume that $M$ is bounded by some constant $R$, that is,
$\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}^d} M(x) \le R < \infty$.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a simple point process on $\mathbb{R}^d$ having 
fast mixing correlations  as in Definition~(d.omegamixing of the paper)(i.mixing-ground-fast of the paper), bounded reduced  Palm intensity function~(equation bdedreduced of the paper),
 and independent of the random field $M$.
Consider the  edge length measure $\sigma_{n}^{\textnormal{}}$ of the geostatistical graph $\Psi(\mathcal{P}_n, M)$ as in (equation e:Geo-edges of the paper).
\begin{enumerate}[wide, label=(\roman*), labelindent=0pt]
\item 
A central limit theorem holds for the family $\big(\sigma_{n}^{\textnormal{}}(f)\big)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$; that is, as $n \to \infty$,
\[
  \big({\rm Var} \, \sigma_{n}^{\textnormal{}}(f)\big)^{-1/2}
  \Big( \sigma_{n}^{\textnormal{}}(f) - \mathbb {E}  \, \sigma_{n}^{\textnormal{}}(f) \Big)
  \stackrel{d}{\Rightarrow} Z,
\]
for all $f \in \mathbb{B} (W_1)$, provided ${\rm Var} \, \sigma_{n}^{\textnormal{}}(f) = \Omega(n^{\nu})$ for some $\nu > 0$.

\item 
Further, if the random field $M$ and the point process $\mathcal{P}$ are stationary, with $\rho$ denoting the intensity of $\mathcal{P}$,
then the expectation and variance asymptotics
hold for 
$\big(\sigma_{n}^{\textnormal{}}(f)\big)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$,
as stated in Proposition~(expvar of the paper). 
\end{enumerate}

[Definition 34 (Common accessibility) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Call $\tau=(\eta;\mathfrak I,\mathcal S_1)$ an
\emph{accessible operational type} for $\cP$ if there is a single Borel
$\cP$-causal group-valued state
\[
Z_\tau:\Omega_H\longrightarrow
 \mathsf Z_{\eta;\mathfrak I,1}(H)
\]
whose canonical chart satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{ch}_\tau(Z_\tau)
 =\bigl(X,A^P,\qv{M^P}\bigr)
 \qquad P\text{-a.s. for every }P\in\cP,
\end{equation}
where $M^P$ is the continuous local-martingale part of the canonical process
and $A^P$ is its It\^o area.  The same map serves all models.  Part~I is
conditional on this common-realization hypothesis; Part~II proves it for
$\Smax$ by a law-independent raw-causal selector whose lawwise semantics are
verified afterwards.

[Definition 84 ($\widehat U,\widecheck U$) of arXiv:2605.26664, 'Mixing times for Glauber dynamics of lozenge tilings of the hexagon'] For $j\le k-1$, let $(x^\pm,\bar y^{\pm,j}_{a,b,c})$ be a point in $\mathbb T_N+(0,1/(2N))$ at minimal distance from $(x^\pm, y^{\pm,j}_{a,b,c})$. We
  let $\widehat U=\{\widehat U_j\}_{1\le j\le k-1}$ denote the Bernoulli path ensemble
  with endpoints given by
  $\{(x^\pm,\bar y^{\pm,j}_{a,b,c})\}_{1\le j\le k-1}$, conditioned to
  the event that the top path $\widehat U_{k-1}$ is weakly {below}
  $\mathcal U^{k/N}_{a,b,c}$ and that each $\widehat U_j,j\le k-1$
  is weakly below $ \mathcal U^{(j/N+N^{-1+(6A+R)\delta})}_{q'}$.
  Similarly, we let $\widecheck U=\{\widecheck U_j\}_{1\le j\le k-1}$ denote the
  Bernoulli path ensemble defined like $\widehat{U}$, but without the constraint
  that $\widecheck U_j$ is below
  $ \mathcal U^{(j/N+N^{-1+(6A+R)\delta})}_{q'}$.
title: $\widehat U,\widecheck U$

body:
[Lemma lem:green-form-inverse of arXiv:2608.02459, 'Response Calculus for Spectral Simplicity\\ and Joint Eigenvalue Densities'] Fix $x\in\Omega_{\rm op}$ and $\theta\in L^2(M_x)$.  The potential
$u:=U_D(\theta M_x)$ belongs to $V_x$ and is the unique solution of
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal E(u,v)=\int_D\theta\widetilde v\,dM_x,
 \qquad v\inV_x.
 
\end{equation}
Its $L^2(M_x)$ representative and its energy are given by
\begin{align}
 \widetilde u&=G_x\theta\quad\text{in }L^2(M_x),
 \\
 I_D(\theta M_x)&=\langle\theta,G_x\theta\rangle_{L^2(M_x)}.
 
\end{align}
Equivalently,
\[
 G_x\theta\in\operatorname{Dom}(A_x),
 \qquad A_xG_x\theta=\theta.
\]

body:
[Lemma lem:fixed-power of arXiv:2608.30779, 'Some uniform estimates for K\"ahler--Ricci Shrinkers'] For every \(D<\infty\), there are
\(C_D,c_D,r_D>0\), depending only on \(n\) and \(D\), such that the
following holds for every
\(X\in\overline{\mathcal{KRS}(n)}\).
For \(k\geq0\), \(x\in B(p,D)\), and \(0<r\leq r_D\), every
\[
 s\in H^0(\mathcal R,-kK_{\mathcal R})
\]
with finite \(L^2\)-norm on \(B(x,C_Dr)\cap\mathcal R\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{B(x,r)\cap\mathcal R}|s|_{h^k}^2
 \leq
 \frac{C_D(kr^2+1)}{((k+1)r^2)^n}
 \int_{B(x,C_Dr)\cap\mathcal R}|s|_{h^k}^2\,
       \omega_{k+1}^n.
\end{equation}
At \(\rho_k=c_D(k+1)^{-1/2}\), one also has
\[
 \sup_{B(x,\rho_k)\cap\mathcal R}
 \left(|s|_{h^k}^2+
 |\nabla s|_{\omega_{k+1}\otimes h^k}^2\right)
 \leq C_D\int_{B(x,C_D\rho_k)\cap\mathcal R}|s|_{h^k}^2
       \omega_{k+1}^n.
\]
Moreover, \(|s|_{h^k}\) extends uniquely to a locally Lipschitz function
on \(X\).

[Corollary 33 of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Assume $(x_i)_{i\leq n}$ satisfy the hypotheses of
	Proposition~\ref{prop:light-tail-quotient}, and $n/d^2 \to \alpha\in (0,\infty)$. 
    
    There exists an absolute constant $\mu>0$ such that the following holds. For every fixed $L\geq 2$ and $\eps\in(0,1)$, there exist $
	K_0=K_0(\alpha,K_x,L,\eps)>0$ and $C=C(K_x,L)>0$ such that for every $K\ge K_0$,
	with probability $1-o(1)$, the following holds: for every
	$\ell=2,\ldots,L$, every $\mathcal I\subset[n]$, and every
	$t\in\R^n$ supported on $\mathcal I^c$ satisfying
	$\|t\|_2=1$ and $\|t\|_\infty\le(Kd)^{-1/2}$, let
	$\mathsf V_{t,\ell}$ be the span of the eigenvectors of
	$\Sigma_{t,\ell}$ whose eigenvalues are at least $\mu$, where
	\[
    \Sigma_{t,\ell}\equiv\sum_{i\notin \mathcal{I}} t_i^2 u_{i,\ell} u_{i,\ell}^\top,\qquad m_{t,\ell}:=\dim\mathsf V_{t,\ell}.
    \]
    Then for every such $\mathcal{I}, t$, the $\mathcal{F}_{\ell-1}^{\mathcal I}$-measurable event
	\begin{equation}
	\mathcal G_\ell^{\mathcal I}(t)
	:=
	\left\{
	\max_{i\le n}\|u_{i,\ell}\|_2^2\le Cd,
	\quad
	m_{t,\ell}\ge(1-\eps)p_\ell
	\right\}
	\end{equation}
	occurs, and $P_{\mathsf V_{t,\ell}}\Sigma_{t,\ell}P_{\mathsf V_{t,\ell}}
	\succeq\mu P_{\mathsf V_{t,\ell}}$ holds.

body:
[Lemma 1 of arXiv:2608.17493, 'Integrals of some compound processes'] Let $X, Y$ two stochastic processes on $\mathcal{D}[0,\infty)$. Assume that $X(t)\stackrel{d}{=}Y(t), \ t\ge0$. 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[($i$)] If both $X$ and $Y$ have independent and stationary increments, then $X\stackrel{d}{=}Y$ on $\mathcal{D}[0,\infty)$.
		\item[($ii$)] If both $X$ and $Y$ have independent increments and $X(t)-X(s)\stackrel{d}{=}Y(t)-Y(s), \ t>s\ge0$, then $X\stackrel{d}{=}Y$ on $\mathcal{D}[0,\infty)$.
	\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact conditioning, spectral integral estimate, deterministic graph comparison or order-statistic asymptotics Result: One spectral step only needs finite mean. Put g2(x)=exp(-x)*sum_(j>=2)P(j)*x^(j-2)/(j-2)!, and consider Kf(x)=integral min(x,y)*f(y)*g2(y)dy on L2(g2 dx). Tonelli gives integral x*g2(x)dx=sum_(j>=2)(j-1)P(j)=E[K_degree]-1. Since min(x,y)^2<=x*y, the squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm is at most (E[K_degree]-1)^2. Thus finite mean already makes this symmetric integral operator compact. The kernel is also positive semidefinite because min(x,y)=integral_0^infinity 1_(t<x)*1_(t<y)dt. This removes an exponential moment from the compactness step, while leaving the stronger population conclusions untouched. Check: The gamma integral of x^(j-1)*exp(-x)/(j-2)! equals j-1. For compactly supported test functions, Fubini expresses the quadratic form as integral (integral_(x>t) f(x)g2(x)dx)^2 dt; continuity extends positivity to L2. Obstruction: No assertion that every source growth/extinction theorem survives under finite mean. Identifying the branching eigenfunctions, integrability of the spine, and uniform integrability of martingales still require proof.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0453-weaker-degree-tail-hypotheses-for-erlang-weighted-tree-growth

 (II) Let $f \in C_0({\mathbb R}^d \times {\mathbb R}^d)$. Then $\lim_{t \rightarrow 0}\| \hat {\mathcal P}_t^\varepsilon f - f \|_\infty = 0 $.

[Corollary 8 of arXiv:2604.24392, 'Numerical approximation of Markovian BSDEs in infinite horizon and elliptic PDEs'] Let $p\in (1,+\infty]$. 
Assume  \eqref{as:generatorf}, \eqref{as:b:sigma} and \eqref{as:int:X:nablaX}.
\begin{description} 
\item [(case $p=+\infty$)]: Assume \eqref{as:suprho}, $a>\theta$, $\ta>\ttheta$,  $\kappa_\infty < 1$ and $\normr{\Phi(0)}<+\infty$,
then there is a unique continuous function $v: \bR^d \to \bR^{d'}\times \bR^{d'\times d}$ with  $\displaystyle\sup_{x\in \bR^d}\dfrac{\norm{v(x)}}{{\rho}(x) }<+\infty$  satisfying  $v=\Phi(v),$
i.e. solving \eqref{prop:eq:u} and \eqref{prop:eq:baru}. Moreover the solution $v$ satisfies the following bound: $\displaystyle\normr{v}\leqslant \frac{1}{1- \kappa_\infty} \normr{\Phi(0)}$.
\item [(case $p \in (1,+\infty)$)]: Assume that there exists a probability measure $\meas$ on $\bR^d$ satisfying $\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} |x|^r \meas(\dx)<+\infty$ and such that \eqref{eq:condition:stability:rho} holds. Assume also  $\kappa_p < 1$ and $\left(\displaystyle\int_{\bR^d} |\Phi(0)(x)|^p \meas(\dx)\right)^\frac{1}{p } < +\infty$.
\end{description}
Then, there is a unique measurable function $v: \bR^d \to \bR^{d'}\times \bR^{d'\times d}$ with   $\left(\displaystyle\int_{\bR^d}\norm{v(x)}^p \meas(\dx)\right)^\frac{1}{p }<+\infty$ satisfying  $v=\Phi(v)$, i.e. solving \eqref{prop:eq:u} and \eqref{prop:eq:baru}.
Moreover the solution $v$ satisfies the following bound: $\displaystyle\left(\int_{\bR^d}\norm{v(x)}^p \meas(\dx) \right)^\frac{1}{p }\leqslant \frac{1}{1- \kappa_p} \left(\int_{\bR^d}\norm{\Phi(0)(x)}^p \meas(\dx)\right)^\frac{1}{p }$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Lemma lem:shape of arXiv:2510.05850, 'Three-point connectivity constant for $q$-state Potts spin clusters'] For a loop $\eta$ sampled from $\widetilde\SLE_\kappa^\mathrm{sep}(\mathcal{C})$ (resp.\ $\SLE_\kappa^\mathrm{sep}(\mathcal{C})$), there is a unique decomposition $\eta = \eta^0 + \mathbf{t}$ with $\eta^0 \in \mathrm{Loop}_0(\mathcal{C})$ and $\mathbf{t} \in \mathbb{R}$, and there exists a probability measure $\widetilde{\mathcal{L}}_\kappa(\mathcal{C})$ (resp.\ $\mathcal{L}_\kappa(\mathcal{C})$) on $\mathrm{Loop}_0(\mathcal{C})$ and constants $\widetilde C,C>0$ such that the joint law of $(\eta^0,\bf t)$ equals $\widetilde C\widetilde{\mathcal{L}}_\kappa(\mathcal{C})\times dt$ (resp.\ $C\mathcal{L}_\kappa(\mathcal{C})\times dt$). Moreover, $\widetilde C=(\mathbb{E}[\log \mathsf{R}_{R\to B}]+\mathbb{E}[\log \mathsf{R}_{B\to R}])^{-1}$ and $C=(\mathbb{E}[\log \mathsf{R}_{R\to B}])^{-1}$.

[Lemma lem:Ri-in-Seg-implies-boundary-pruned of arXiv:2605.16086, 'Loop pruning and downward deviations for maximum local time of discrete-time simple random'] Fix \(1\le i<j\le k\). Assume that \(k\le M_\infty\) and that the boundary step
\[
(S_{\tau_i-1},S_{\tau_i})
\]
is not pruned in \(\mathsf{Prune}(S[0,\tau_k],E)\), and that
\[
\mathcal R_{i+1},\mathcal R_{i+2},\ldots,\mathcal R_j\in\mathsf{Seg}(E).
\]
Then every subsequent boundary step
\[
(S_{\tau_r-1},S_{\tau_r}),\qquad i+1\le r\le j,
\]
is pruned in \(\mathsf{Prune}(S[0,\tau_k],E)\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:Ri-in-Seg-implies-boundary-pruned of arXiv:2605.16086

[Prop prop coefficient functional of arXiv:2512.20338, 'Up-down chains and scaling limits: \\ application to permuton- and graphon-valued diffusio'] There exists a unique bounded linear functional $ [  h _ \varnothing ^o ] \colon C(  E  ) \to  \mathbb R  $ satisfying
    \begin{equation}
        
        [  h _ \varnothing ^o ]  d _s^o
        		=
        			 M _{ | s | }( s )
				,
					\qquad
					s \in   \mathbb S  
				.
	\end{equation}
	\noindent	
	Moreover, this functional is contractive, positive, and satisfies the following conditions:
    \begin{enumerate}[ label = (\roman*) ]

		\item
		
		$
			[  h _ \varnothing ^o ] f^o
    			=
			[  h _ \varnothing  ]
			f
		$
		for $ f \in  H  $

        	[  h _ \varnothing ^o ]  h _s^o
        		=
        			 \mathbbm 1 ( s =  \varnothing  )
        $
        for $ s \in   \mathbb S   $),

        \item

body:
[Prop 9 of arXiv:2607.06745, 'Regularization and asymptotic behaviour of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck evolution operators in infin'] Let $-\infty<s<t<+\infty$. The image
of the operator
\[
P_{s,t}:L^{p}\left(X,\mu_{t}\right)\to L^{p}\left(X,\mu_{s}\right)
\]
is contained in $W^{1,p}\left(X,\mu_{s}\right)$ and $P_{s,t}$ is
continuous as an operator with values in $W^{1,p}\left(X,\mu_{s}\right)$.
Consequently, $P_{s,t}$ is compact as an operator with values in
$L^{p}\left(X,\mu_{s}\right)$.

\vspace{1mm}

In particular, the continuity estimate for the gradient has the form:
\begin{equation}
\left\Vert \nabla P_{s,t}f\right\Vert _{L^{p}\left(X,\mu_{s};X\right)}\leq C_{p}\left\Vert \Lambda\left(t,s\right)\right\Vert _{\mathcal{L}\left(X\right)}\left\Vert f\right\Vert _{L^{p}\left(X,\mu_{t}\right)}\quad\forall f\in L^{p}\left(X,\mu_{t}\right),
\end{equation}
where $\Lambda\left(t,s\right)$ is the operator defined in Remark
$\text{\ref{rem:def Lambda}}$.

Furthermore, relation $\text{\eqref{eq: formula grad C1}}$ also holds
for $\varphi\in W^{1,p}\left(X,\mu_{t}\right)$ and for $\mu_{s}$-almost
every $x\in X$.

Suppose that A is a subset of V satisfying 0 < |A| < |V |. Let W be the set of all vertices of the embedded graph of X. Then, there exists a subset B of W that satisfies the following conditions: |E(B, W \ B)| ≤k(n + 1 −k)|F(A, V \ A)|, 1 ≤|B|, |V \ A| ≤n|W \ B| δmin .

[Theorem 2 (Cameron--Martin formula) of arXiv:2608.02417, 'A Bismut--Elworthy--Li formula for linear stochastic evolution equations in Banach spaces'] Let \(R\in\gamma(\scrH,E)\), let \(W\) be an \(\scrH\)-isonormal Gaussian
process, and let \(X_R\) be the centred \(E\)-valued Gaussian random variable
canonically associated with \(R\). Then, for every bounded Borel function
\(g:E\to\R\), every \(h\in\scrH\), and every \(\varepsilon\in\R\),
\begin{equation}
    \E g(X_R+\varepsilon Rh)
    = \E\Bigl[ g(X_R)\exp\Bigl(\varepsilon W(h) -\frac{\varepsilon^2}{2}\|h\|_\scrH^2\Bigr)\Bigr].
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cameron--Martin formula

[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2609.01498, 'A Tight Erd\H{o}s-Stone Bound for All Graph Densities'] For every $0 < \eta < 1$ and $n > 4/\eta$ the following holds. If $\epsilon < 1/2$ and $G$ is a graph with $n$ vertices and
$(1-\epsilon){n \choose 2}$ edges, then $G$ has a subgraph $H$ with $p > (\eta/2)^{1/2}n$ vertices and with minimum degree at least
$(1-\epsilon-\eta)p$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let $(X, d)$ be a compact metric space. A homeomorphism $f: X \to X$ is expansive with expansivity constant $\varepsilon > 0$ if whenever $x \ne y$ there is some $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ (positive OR negative) with $d(f^n x, f^n y) > \varepsilon$; equivalently, $d(f^n x, f^n y) \le \varepsilon$ for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ forces $x = y$. A continuous map $f: X \to X$ (not necessarily invertible) is positively expansive (forward expansive) with constant $\varepsilon$ if $d(f^n x, f^n y) \le \varepsilon$ for all $n \ge 0$ forces $x = y$. Positive expansiveness is much stronger than expansiveness: a positively expansive HOMEOMORPHISM of a compact metric space exists only when $X$ is finite (Schwartzman; Keynes-Robertson), so for an infinite compact space the notion is meaningful only for genuinely non-invertible maps such as expanding maps and one-sided shifts. On a compact space the property (with some constant) does not depend on the choice of compatible metric, though the constant does. Expansiveness is preserved by passing to $f^{-1}$ and to $f^k$, $k \ne 0$; positive expansiveness is preserved by passing to $f^k$, $k \ge 1$.
X is a compact metric space
for the homeomorphism notion f is invertible; for positive expansiveness f is only assumed continuous
title: Expansive homeomorphism; positively expansive map

[Conjecture conj:tao of arXiv:2609.00399, 'Shannon's problem on the monotonicity of entropy and a Conjecture of Tao'] For every fixed integer $n\geq1$,
\begin{equation}
 H(S_{n+1})-H(S_n)\geq b_n-o_{H(X_1)\to\infty}(1),
 \qquad b_n=\frac12\log\frac{n+1}{n},
\end{equation}
where the error is uniform over the torsion-free ambient group and the
finitely supported law of $X_1$. (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Tao's conjecture
Weibull-tail moment-matching counterexample

[Proposition 32 of arXiv:2609.02169, '2609.02169'] Let $(A,L)$ be a complex abelian surface polarized of type $(1,6)$.
There exist a degree-two \emph{\'etale} isogeny
$\pi:B\to A$, with kernel generated by a nonzero point $b\in B[2]$,
and a line bundle $M$ of type $(1,3)$ on $B$ such that
$2c_1(M)=\pi^*c_1(L)$.  If
\[
 E:=\pi_*M,\qquad W:=H^0(A,E)=H^0(B,M),\qquad Q:=\det E,
\]
then
\[
 \operatorname{rk}E=2,\quad \dim W=3,\quad c_2(E)=3,
 \quad [Q]=[L]\text{ in }\operatorname{NS}(A),
 \quad \pi^*E\simeq M\oplus T_b^*M.
\]

body:
[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2604.13819, 'Convolution, cumulants and infinitesimal generators in the formal power series ring'] The $t$-deformed cumulants $\{\kappa_{i}^{t}(A)\}_{i \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}}$ are unique maps satisfying the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (i)]
\item $\kappa_{i}^{t}(A)$ is a polynomial in $p_{1}(A), \dots, p_{i}(A)$ with leading term $\frac{t^{i-1}}{(t)_{i}} p_{i}(A)$. 
That is, there exists a polynomial $F_{i}$ in $i-1$ variables such that 
$$
\kappa_{i}^t(A) = \frac{t^{i-1}}{(t)_{\underline{i}}}p_{i}(A) + F_{i}(p_{1}(A), \dots, p_{i-1}(A)).
$$ 
\item Homogeneity: $\kappa_{i}^{t}(D_{r}[A]) = r^{i}\kappa_{i}^{t}(A)$ for any $r \in \mathbb{R}$ and $i \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}$.
\item Additivity: $\kappa_{i}^{t}(A \boxplus^{t} B) = \kappa_{i}^{t}(A) + \kappa_{i}^{t}(B)$. 
In other words, 
$$
C^t[A \boxplus^{t} B](z) = C^{t}[A](z) + C^{t}[B](z).
$$ 
\end{enumerate}

body: [Thm 78 of arXiv:2608.26068, 'All once-extended 3D TQFTs are Reshetikhin--Turaev theories'] For any positive integer $t$, symmetric monoidal functors $\mathbf{Bord}_{1,2,3}^{t\mathrm{sig/2}}\rightarrow\Vect$ are classified by finite direct sums of modular tensor categories whose anomalies are equal, along with a single choice of $t^\mathrm{th}$ root of this anomaly.

body:
[Lem mobius-primitive of arXiv:2607.00311, 'Thermal Concentration and Poisson--Dirichlet Edge Statistics for Random-Lattice Gibbs Ense'] Let $\mu:\mathbb N\to\{-1,0,1\}$ be the M\"obius function. 
Thus $\mu(1)=1$, $\mu(d)=0$ if $d$ is divisible by the square of a prime, and
$\mu(d)=(-1)^r$ if
$$
d=p_1p_2\cdots p_r
$$
with distinct primes $p_1,\ldots,p_r$.

The elementary M\"obius inversion identity is
$$
\sum_{d|N}\mu(d)=
\begin{cases}
1, & N=1,\\
0, & N\ge2.
\end{cases}
$$
Consequently, for every nonzero vector $\bm q\in\mathbb Z^n$,
$$
\chi_{\mathbb Z^n_{\operatorname{prim}}}(\bm q)=\sum_{d|\bm q}\mu(d),
$$
where $d|\bm q$ means that $d$ divides every coordinate of $\bm q$.

[Lemma 29 of arXiv:2608.28991, 'Jigsaw-CRL: Recovering Global Latent Causal Order from Fragmented Multi-Client Interventio'] Fix a client $k\in[K]$. Let $\cI\subseteq \cC_k$ be a collection of blocks that is closed under block ancestors, namely
\[
C\in \cI,\ C'\in Anc_k^\rblk(C)\quad \Longrightarrow\quad C'\in \cI.
\]
Define
\[
W \;\triangleq\; \Big\langle [\bQ_k]_{\rho_k(i),:}\ \Big|\ i\in \bigcup_{C\in\cI} C \Big\rangle .
\]
Let $j_1,\dots,j_\ell$ be intervention indices such that
\[
C_k(j_r)\notin \cI,\qquad r=1,\dots,\ell,
\]
where $C_k(j_r)$ denotes the block in $\cC_k$ containing the target $t_{j_r}$. Define
\[
\cS_{\cI}
\;\triangleq\;
\Big( \bigcup_{r=1}^\ell Anc_k^\rblk\big(C_k(j_r)\big)\Big)\setminus \cI,
\qquad
S
\;\triangleq\;
\rho_k\!\Big(\bigcup_{C\in\cS_{\cI}} C\Big).
\]
For each $s\in S$, let $[\bar{\bH}_k]_{s,:}$ be the projection of $[\bH_k]_{s,:}$ onto $W^\perp$, and let $[\bar{\bH}_k]_{S,:}$ be the matrix formed by stacking these projected rows.

Then
\[
\Pi_{W^\perp}\!\left(
\row\Big(\{\bTheta_k^{(j)}-\bTheta_k^{(0)}\}_{j\in\{j_1,\dots,j_\ell\}}\Big)
\right)
\]
is contained in
\[
\Big\langle
[\bar{\bH}_k]_{S,:}^{T}
(\bI-[\bA_k]_{S,S})^{T}
[\bSigma_k]_{S,S}^{-1}
[\be_{\rho_k(t_j)}]_{S},
\ 
[\bar{\bH}_k]_{S,:}^{T}
\Big(
(\bI-[\bA_k]_{S,S})^{T}
[\bSigma_k]_{S,S}^{-1}
[\bu_k^{(j)}]_{S}
+
[\bd_k^{(j)}]_{S}
\Big)
\ \Big|\ 
j\in\{j_1,\dots,j_\ell\}
\Big\rangle .
\]

[Theorem Thm2.1 of arXiv:2602.23124, '\textsc{ Necessary and Sufficient Conditions for the Lacunary/Hereditary Laws of Large Num'] {\bf Sufficiency/Necessity in the  Lacunary/Hereditary SLLN for General Sequences:}
  
  On a  probability space $\,(\Omega, \mathcal F, {\mathbb P}),$  consider  real-valued, measurable functions $f_1, f_2, \cdots$. 
  
  \smallskip
  \noindent
  {\bf (i)} Suppose that for some subsequence $\,f_{k_1}, f_{k_2}, \cdots\,$    and   sets $\, A_1 \subseteq A_2 \subseteq \cdots \subseteq A_j \subseteq \cdots \,$ in $\,\mathcal F$ with $\,\lim_{j \to \infty} {\mathbb P} (A_j ) =1\,,$ the condition (equation A1 of the paper) holds.  

There exist then a measurable function $f_* : \Omega \to \mathbb R$ and a $($further, relabelled$)$ subsequence along which, and along whose every subsequence, the \textsc{Ces\`aro}-mean convergence in (equation 2 of the paper) holds   $\, {\mathbb P}-$a.e. 
 

   \smallskip
 \noindent
  {\bf (ii)} Conversely, suppose that along some subsequence $f_{k_1}, f_{k_2}, \cdots\,$   and  each of its subsequences, the \textsc{Ces\`aro}-mean convergence (equation 2 of the paper) holds $\, {\mathbb P}-$a.e.\,for some measurable $f_* : \Omega \to \mathbb R\,.$   There exist then    sets $\, A_1 \subseteq A_2 \subseteq \cdots \subseteq A_j \subseteq \cdots \,$ in $\,\mathcal F$ with $\,\lim_{j \to \infty} {\mathbb P} (A_j ) =1\,,$  such that (equation A1 of the paper) is satisfied.
  
  \medskip
\noindent
  {\bf (iii)} The validity of (equation A1 of the paper) for some subsequence $f_{k_1}, f_{k_2}, \cdots\,$   and for  sets $\, A_1 \subseteq A_2 \subseteq \cdots \subseteq A_j \subseteq \cdots \,$ in $\,\mathcal F$ with $\,\lim_{j \to \infty} {\mathbb P} (A_j ) =1\,,$ is equivalent to the existence of a probability measure $\,{\mathbb Q} \sim {\mathbb P} $ on $(\Omega, \mathcal F)\,$ with the property  that some      subsequence $\,f_{k_1}, f_{k_2}, \cdots\,$   is bounded in $\, \mathbb{L}^1 ({\mathbb Q})\,.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma lem-decomp-cone of arXiv:2411.19810, 'Radial conformal welding in Liouville quantum gravity'] Let $W \in (0, \frac{\gamma^2}2)$. Let $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa^\mathrm{wp}(\rho)$ denote the law of whole-plane $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa(\rho)$ from $0$ to $\infty$. Sample $(z, \psi_0, \eta_0^\mathrm{wp}) \sim \mathcal{A}_{\psi_0}(dz) P_W(d\psi_0) \mathrm{SLE}_\kappa^\mathrm{wp}(W-2)$. For each connected component $B$ of $\mathbb{C} \backslash \eta_0^\mathrm{wp}$, let $p_B$ and $q_B$ be the first and last points of $\partial B$ hit by $\eta_0^\mathrm{wp}$. Let $\tilde \mathcal{W}$ be the collection of all quantum surfaces $(B, \psi_0, p_B, q_B)/{\sim_\gamma}$, and  endow $\tilde \mathcal{W}$ with the ordering where $(B_1, \psi_0, p_{B_1}, q_{B_1})/{\sim_\gamma}$ precedes $(B_2, \psi_0, p_{B_2}, q_{B_2})/{\sim_\gamma}$ if $\eta_0^\mathrm{wp}$ hits $q_{B_1}$ for the last time before it hits $q_{B_2}$ for the last time. 
	
	    
	    Let $B_\bullet$ be the connected component of $\mathbb{C} \backslash \eta_0^\mathrm{wp}$ containing $z$, and let $\mathcal{B}_\bullet = (B_\bullet, \psi_0, z, p_{B_\bullet}, q_{B_\bullet})/{\sim_\gamma}$. Let $ \mathcal{D} \subset \tilde \mathcal{W}$ (resp.\ $\mathcal{W} \subset \tilde \mathcal{W}$) be the ordered collection of elements that come before (resp.\ after) $(B_\bullet, \psi_0, p_{B_\bullet}, q_{B_\bullet})/{\sim_\gamma}$. Then the joint law of $(\mathcal{D}, \mathcal{B}_\bullet, \mathcal{W})$ is $(1 - \frac{2W}{\gamma^2})^2 {\mathcal{M}}^\mathrm{disk}_{0,2}(W) \times {\mathcal{M}}^\mathrm{disk}_{1,2}(\gamma^2 - W)  \times \mathcal{M}^\mathrm{wed}(W)$.

[Defi def:stochasticcontrolledroughpaths of arXiv:2412.05698, 'Controlled rough SDEs, pathwise stochastic control and dynamic programming principles'] {FHL21}}]   
A pair \((Z,Z')\) is called \textit{stochastic controlled rough path} of $(p,q)$-integrability and $(\kappa,\kappa')$-H\"older regularity if 
\begin{enumerate} \renewcommand{\alph{enumi})}{\alph{enumi})}
\item \(Z=(Z_t)_{t \in [0,T]}\) is progressively measurable such that

\[
    \|\delta Z\|_{\kappa;p,q} := \sup_{0 \leq s < t \leq T} \frac{\|\|\delta Z_{s,t}|{\mathfrak F}_s\|_p\|_q}{|t-s|^\kappa} < +\infty;
\]
\item \(Z'=(Z'_t)_{t \in [0,T]}\) is progressively measurable such that
\[
    \sup_{t \in [0,T]} \|Z'_t\|_q < +\infty \quad \text{and} \quad \|\delta Z'\|_{\kappa';p,q} := \sup_{0 \leq s < t \leq T} \frac{\|\|\delta Z'_{s,t}|{\mathfrak F}_s\|_p\|_q}{|t-s|^{\kappa'}} < +\infty;
\]
\item writing \(R^Z_{s,t} = \delta Z_{s,t} - Z'_s \delta X_{s,t}\) for \((s,t)\in\Delta_T\), we have
\[
    \|\mathbb{E}_\cdot R^Z\|_{\kappa+\kappa';q} := \sup_{0 \leq s < t \leq T} \frac{\|\mathbb{E}_s(R^Z_{s,t})\|_q}{|t-s|^{\kappa+\kappa'}} < + \infty.
\]
\end{enumerate}
We write \((Z,Z') \in \mathbf{D}_X^{\kappa,\kappa'} L_{p,q}\); and also \(\mathbf{D}_X^{2\kappa} L_{p,q}\), \(\mathbf{D}_X^{\kappa,\kappa'} L_p\) if \(\kappa = \kappa'\) and \(p=q\), respectively.

[Thm 1 of arXiv:2606.29132, '\bf Local Well-posedness of General Mean Field Game Master Equations'] Under Assumption \ref{assum-0},\footnote{ The locally uniform continuity \reff{rhoR1} is needed only for  the time regularity in \reff{rhoR2} and the representation of $Z^{x,1}$ in \reff{randomFK}. In particular, it is not needed for the representation formula \reff{paxrep} of $\pa_x u_0$.}  there exists a constant $\e_0>0$, depending only on the dimensions $d_{01}, d_x, d_y$, and the bounds $L_\Phi$, $\Phi = b, \si, f, g$,  such that, whenever $0<T\leq \e_0$:

\no(i) The FBSDEs \reff{FBSDEx}-\reff{tdFBSDEx} are well-posed; and for any $p\ge 2$, there exists $C_p>0$ such that
\bea

\|\td_x \Pi\|_p^p:= \dbE\Big[ \sup_{0\le t\le T} [|\td_x X_t|^p + |\td_x Y_t|^p] + \big(\int_0^T |\td_x Z_t|^2dt\big)^{p\over 2}\Big] \le C_p |\D x|^p<\infty.
\eea

\no (ii) There exists an $\dbF^0$-progressively measurable random field $u: [0, T]\times \dbR^{d_x}\times \O\to \dbR^{d_y}$ such that $u$ is  differentiable in $x$, $|\pa_x u_t|\le R_0:= L_g+1$, and  $\pa_x u$ is  locally uniformly continuous in the sense that, for any $R>0$, there exists a modulus of continuity function $\rho_{R}$ such that
\bea

\left.\ba{c}
|\pa_x u_t(x^1) - \pa_x u_t(x^2)| \le \rho_{R}(|x_1-x_2|), ~ \mbox{a.s. on $\{I_t \le R\}$, whenever}~  |x_1|, |x_2| \le R;\\
|\pa_x u_{t_1}(x)- \dbE_{\cF^0_{t_1}}[\pa_x u_{t_2}(x)]|\le \rho_{R}(\sqrt{t_2-t_1}), ~\mbox{a.s. on $\{I_{t_1} \le R\}$, whenever}~  |x| \le R, t_1\le t_2.
\ea\right.
\eea
Moreover, it holds that
\bea

Y^x_t = u_t(X^x_t),\q \td_x Y_t = \pa_x u_t(X^x_t) \td_x X_t,\q Z^{x,1}_t = \pa_x u_t(X^x_t) \si^1_t(X^x_t, Y^x_t).
\eea
In particular, $u_0(x) = Y^x_0$ is deterministic and we have a representation formula for $\pa_x u_0(x)$:\footnote{In \reff{tdFBSDEx} we consider the directional derivatives of $\Pi$, and thus $\td_x \Pi$ has the same dimension as $\Pi^x$ itself.  Alternatively we may consider $\hat \td_x \Pi^x = (\td_x \Pi^{x, e_1}, \cds, \td_x \Pi^{x, e_{d_x}})$, which does not depend on $\D x$ anymore. In fact, $\td_x \Pi^{x, \D x} = \hat\td_x \Pi^x \D x$. Then $\hat \td_x X^x\in \dbR^{d_x\times d_x}$, with $\hat \td_x X^x_0$ the $d_x\times d_x$ identity matrix,  and $\pa_x u_0(x) = \hat\td _x Y^x_0\in \dbR^{d_y\times d_x}$. The results are actually more clean in this way, however, the notations will become a lot heavier, especially when we discuss the higher order derivatives. }

[Proposition propclassbd of arXiv:2604.07227, 'Transition probabilities of step-reinforced random walks'] Let $S$ be a generalized SRRW on a countably infinite $G$ with parameter $\alpha \in [0,1)$ and step distribution $\mu$ being a class function. We denote its law by $\mathbb{P}^{(\alpha)}$ to indicate the dependence on $\alpha$. Let $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ and $m \in \mathbb{N}_+$ be such that 
$$
\max_{x\in G} \mathbb{P}^{(0)}(S_n=x) \leq \varepsilon, \quad \forall  n\geq m.
$$
Then there exists a positive constant $\rho \in (0,\alpha)$ depending only on $\alpha$ such that
$$
\max_{x\in G} \mathbb{P}^{(\alpha)}(S_n=x) \leq \varepsilon + 5\rho^{n}, \quad \forall  n\geq \frac{8 m}{1-\alpha}.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own work draft; proof (unaudited); no novelty claim. For every finite positive d,n,m and sigma>0, iid Gaussian data/control weights and hidden biases have probability at least rho^m of producing a permanently dead biased two-layer ReLU network on all controlled Boolean inputs, where rho=Phi(-(d+2))*(Phi(1)-Phi(-1))^d*Phi(1)^n. For nonempty uniform parity targets every conditional half squared loss is then at least 1/2 forever, including when the output bias is trained. Thus an onset guarantee needs a failure probability at least rho^m; this does not refute a growing-width or intermediate-time high-probability theorem.

Independent N(0,sigma^2) data/control weights and hidden biases, sigma>0
Finite positive d,n,m; fixed positive network normalization
Ordinary gradient updates, without external parameter perturbations or resets; output parameters arbitrary

body: Let Y(b) = sum_k b_k w_k with w_k = (2/3)^k / 3 (so sum_k w_k = 1) and b a sequence of independent fair bits; its law mu is a Borel probability measure on [0, 1] with mu([0, 1]) = 1. Its Fourier transform muhat(xi) = int e(-2 pi xi x) dmu is the limit of the finite products prod_{k<n} of the factors (1 + e(-2 pi xi w_k))/2, with |prod_{k<n} cos(pi xi w_k)| -> |muhat(xi)|, and satisfies the self-similarity muhat(xi) = ((1 + e(-2 pi xi/3))/2) muhat(2 xi/3) = e(-pi xi/3) cos(pi xi/3) muhat(2 xi/3), hence muhat(3m) = muhat(2m) for every integer m, muhat(0) = 1 and |muhat| <= 1. These identities are derived from the definition of the measure alone and assume nothing about its density or dimension.

body:
Let Omega = {0,1}^E for a finite set E (the coordinates e in E are 'edges' or 'bits'), and let P_p denote the product measure under which the coordinates omega_e are independent Bernoulli(p_e) variables, p = (p_e) in [0,1]^E; write P_p also for the case p_e = p for all e. For an event A (a subset of Omega) and a coordinate e write A^e = { omega : omega^e in A } and A_e = { omega : omega_e in A }, where omega^e and omega_e are omega with the coordinate e set to 1 and to 0 respectively; A^e and A_e do not depend on the coordinate e. The coordinate e is PIVOTAL for A at omega if exactly one of omega^e, omega_e lies in A; Piv_A(omega) is the set of pivotal coordinates and its size |Piv_A| is the number of pivotal coordinates. THEOREM (Margulis 1974, Russo 1981). For every event A, p |-> P_p(A) is a polynomial in the p_e and, for every coordinate e, d/dp_e P_p(A) = P_p(A^e) - P_p(A_e). With a single parameter p, d/dp P_p(A) = sum over e in E of ( P_p(A^e) - P_p(A_e) ). If A is INCREASING (closed under raising coordinates) then A_e is contained in A^e, A^e minus A_e is exactly the event that e is pivotal for A, and the formula reads d/dp P_p(A) = sum over e of P_p( e is pivotal for A ) = E_p |Piv_A| = sum over e of I_e^p(A), where I_e^p(A) = P_p(e pivotal for A) is the influence of e on A under P_p. In particular an increasing event's probability is nondecreasing in p (and in every p_e), and its derivative is the expected number of pivotal coordinates. The formula holds verbatim for an event on an infinite product space that depends on finitely many coordinates; for a general increasing event depending on infinitely many coordinates the right-hand side is only known to bound the derivative from below in the appropriate one-sided sense, and the finite-dimensional form is the one used in practice (finite boxes, then limits).
E finite (or the event depends on finitely many coordinates of an infinite product space)
the measure is a product of Bernoulli(p_e) coordinates; the single-parameter form takes p_e = p for all e
the pivotal (influence) form of the right-hand side needs A increasing; the general form P_p(A^e) - P_p(A_e) holds for every event
the sharp-threshold consequences are cited, not proved

[Proposition 22 of arXiv:2608.30752, '2608.30752'] Let \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{id}}\) denote the marking-preserving homotopy class
of Lipschitz maps \(v:X_0\to Y\). In a \(q\)-natural coordinate
\(z=x+iy\), define
\[
  H_q(v)
  :=
  \frac12
  \int_{X_0\setminus Z(q)}
  |v_x|_{u_0^*h}^2\,dx\,dy,
  \quad
  V_q(v)
  :=
  \frac12
  \int_{X_0\setminus Z(q)}
  |v_y|_{u_0^*h}^2\,dx\,dy.
\]
These quantities are globally well-defined because the transition maps
between \(q\)-natural coordinates are of the form
\(z\mapsto\pm z+c\), and \(Z(q)\) has measure zero. Set
\begin{equation}
  \mathscr V_q(Y)
  :=
  \inf_{v\in\mathscr H_{\mathrm{id}}}V_q(v).
  
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
  e^{-2t}E(t)
  \searrow
  \mathscr V_q(Y)
  \qquad
  \text{as }t\to\infty.
  
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
  \lim_{t\to\infty}
  \frac{E(t)}{e^{2t}}
  =
  \mathscr V_q(Y),
  \qquad
  E(t)
  =
  \mathscr V_q(Y)e^{2t}+o(e^{2t}).
  
\end{equation}

Suppose, in addition, that \(q\) is Jenkins--Strebel and that its vertical
foliation is the contracting foliation of the ray. Write the complementary
components of its vertical critical graph as maximal flat cylinders
\(
  C_i
  \cong
  (0,h_i)\times
  \bigl(\mathbb R/c_i\mathbb Z\bigr),
\) \(
  i=1,\ldots,r,
\)
where \(q=dz^2\), \(z=x+iy\), the vertical trajectories
\(x=\mathrm{constant}\) are closed, \(c_i\) is their \(q\)-length, and
\(h_i\) is the transverse height of \(C_i\). Let \(\delta_i\) be the core
curve of \(C_i\), and put
\(
  M_i:=\operatorname{Mod}(C_i)=\frac{h_i}{c_i}.
\)
Then
\begin{equation}
  \mathscr V_q(Y)
  =
  \frac12
  \sum_{i=1}^r
  M_i\,\ell_Y(\delta_i)^2
  =
  \frac12
  \sum_{i=1}^r
  \frac{h_i}{c_i}\,
  \ell_Y(\delta_i)^2.
  
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
  \lim_{t\to\infty}
  \frac{E(t)}{e^{2t}}
  =
  \frac12
  \sum_{i=1}^r
  \operatorname{Mod}(C_i)\,
  \ell_Y(\delta_i)^2.
  
\end{equation}

[Lemma 17 of arXiv:2607.16502, 'Asymptotic Behavior of Path Functionals for Vector-Valued Gaussian Processes at High Level'] Let \( \bm{W} ( t ), \ t \in E \) be a continuous stochastic process, \( G :
  \R^d \to \R_+ \) a Borel function bounded on compacta and \( \mu \) a finite
  capacity on \( E \). For a Borel set \(A\subset E\), denote
  \begin{equation}
    
      S(A)
      \coloneqq
      \left\{ 
        s \geq 0 :
        \bm{g} \mapsto \mu \{ t \in A : G ( \bm{g}(t) ) > s \}
        \text{ is discontinuous at } 
        \bm{g} = \bm{W} - \bm{x}
      \right\}.
\end{equation}
  Let \( F \) be defined by~\eqref{sojourn F3 def F}. If either of the following
  conditions holds:
  \begin{enumerate}[a)]
    \item 
    \( 
    \pk{ \lambda ( S(E) ) = 0 } = 1
    \)
    for almost all \( \bm{x} \in \R^d \),
    \item 
    \( \mu \) is null-additive, \( 
    \pk{ \lambda ( S(F) ) = 0 } = 1
    \)
    for almost all \( \bm{x} \in \R^d \) and condition~\eqref{F4_G_condition} is
    satisfied,
  \end{enumerate}
  then \( \Gamma : C ( E, \R^d ) \to \R \) defined by the Choquet integral
  \begin{equation*}
    \Gamma(\bm f)=\int_0^\infty \mu\{t\in E:G(\bm f(t))>s\}\,ds-L
  \end{equation*}
  satisfies condition~\ref{F3}.
  \smallskip

  A simple sufficient condition for the requirement involving \(S(E)\) is the
  following: if \(G\) is continuous, then \(\lambda(S(E))=0\) for every
  realization of \(\bm W-\bm x\), and the resulting Choquet functional is
  continuous at every path in \(C(E,\R^d)\). More generally, the same conclusion
  about \(S(A)\) holds on any Borel set \(A\subset E\) whenever
  \(G(\bm g_n(\cdot))\to G(\bm g(\cdot))\) uniformly on \(A\) for all
  \(\bm g_n\to\bm g\) in \(C(E,\R^d)\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:int-3 of arXiv:2510.06891, 'Multivariate CLT for L\'evy processes: convergence rates without moment assumptions'] Let $\bm{X}
$ be a genuinely $d$-dimensional L\'evy process and $\bm{Z}$ be a $d$-dimensional standard Gaussian random vector with $\mathscr{A}$ equal to either $\mathscr{K}$ or $\mathscr{C}$. Assume there exist measurable functions $\bm{A}:[1,\infty) \to \mathbb{R}^{d}$ and $\bm{B}:[1,\infty) \to \mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ such that
\[
t \mapsto t^{-1}d_\mathscr{A}(\bm{X}_t-\bm{A}(t)), \bm{B}(t)\bm{Z} )\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(+\infty).
\]
Assume also that $\bm{B}(t)$ is invertible for all sufficiently large $t$ and that the limits $\bm{e}_j^\intercal\bm{B}(t)^\intercal \bm{B}(t) \bm{e}_j \to \infty$, for $j\in\{1,\ldots,d\}$, and
$\bm{B}(t)^{-1}\bm{B}(f(t))\to \bm{I}_d$, for any non-decreasing function $f$ with $f(t)/t\to 1$, hold as $t \to \infty$. Then $\mathds{E}[|\bm{X}_1|^2]<\infty$ and $d_\mathscr{C}(\bm{X}_t-t\mathds{E}\bm{X}_1, \bm{B}(t)\bm{Z} )\to 0$ as $t\to\infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:int-3 of arXiv:2510.06891

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, Maximal flow through thin boxes with heavy-tailed capacities (October 2026), addresses Question 36 of Auffinger, Damron and Hanson, 50 Years of First-Passage Percolation: does the limit of Phi/(kl) for the maximal flow from bottom to top of a box in Z^3 exist without Kesten's finite exponential moment assumption? It need not. For every height function m(N) with liminf m(N)/log N = 0 there is a capacity law with no atom at 0 (and infinite mean) such that the maximal flow through [0,N]^(d-1) x [0,m(N)] in Z^d, d >= 2, satisfies limsup Phi/N^(d-1) = +infinity almost surely, and Phi/N^(d-1) exceeds N^(1/2)/2 with probability tending to one along a sequence of N; the heights may grow like (log N)^(1/2), inside Kesten's range. For m(N)/log N -> infinity, Rossignol and Theret (Electron. J. Probab. 23 (2018), paper 99) proved convergence for every capacity law, so for these laws the limit depends on how fast the height grows. The argument counts vertical columns whose edges all carry a very large capacity. Finite-mean and finite-variance laws are not addressed. Paper and code: https://github.com/yspennstate/maxflow-thin-boxes (commit 4ebcec43a73a). Not refereed.
title: Maximal flow through thin boxes with heavy-tailed capacities need not have a limit, answering Auffinger-Damron-Hanson Question 36 (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/maxflow-thin-boxes)

[Thm 23 (Self-adjoint linearization) of arXiv:2507.00346, 'The strong convergence phenomenon'] Let $\boldsymbol{X}^N=(X_1^N,\ldots,X_r^N)$ be a sequence of $r$-tuples
of self-adjoint random matrices, and let $\boldsymbol{x}=(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ 
be an $r$-tuple of self-adjoint elements of a $C^*$-algebra $\mathcal{A}$. 
The following are equivalent.
\smallskip
\begin{enumerate}[a.]
\itemsep\medskipamount  
\item For every $D\in\mathbb{N}$ and self-adjoint
$P\in\M_D(\mathbb{C})\otimes\mathbb{C}\langle x_1,\dots,x_{r}\rangle$
of degree one,
$$
	\spc\big(P(\boldsymbol{X}^N)\big)
	\subseteq
	\spc\big(P(\boldsymbol{x})\big)
	+ o(1) [-1,1]
	\quad\text{with probability}\quad 1-o(1).
$$
\item For every $D\in\mathbb{N}$ and self-adjoint
$P\in\M_D(\mathbb{C})\otimes\mathbb{C}\langle x_1,\dots,x_{r}\rangle$
$$
	\|P(\boldsymbol{X}^N)\| \le 
	\|P(\boldsymbol{x})\|+o(1)
	\quad\text{with probability}\quad 1-o(1).
$$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Self-adjoint linearization

body:
[Definition of arXiv:2512.06640, 'Existence and sharpness of the phase transition for the frog model on transitive graphs'] Let $(X_{1},d_{1})$ and $(X_{2},d_{2})$ be two metric spaces. A map $f: X \rightarrow Y$ is called a \textbf{quasi-isometry} if there exists $K>0$ such that 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item For all $z,y \in X_{1},$ we have that 
        $$ K^{-1}d_{1}(z,y) - K \leq d_{2}(f(z),f(y)) \leq Kd_{1}(z,y) + K \, . $$
        \item For all $x_{2} \in X_{2}$ there exists some $x_{1} \in X_{1}$ such that $d_{2}(x_{2},f(x_{1})) \leq K.$
    \end{itemize}
We say that $X_{1}$ is quasi-isometric to $X_{2}$ if there exists a quasi-isometry $f:X_{1}\rightarrow X_{2}.$
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2512.06640, 'Existence and sharpness of the phase transition for the frog'

  where $W_\bot$ is upward closed with respect to both $\leq$ and $\sqsubset$ (i.e. $\forall x,y\, (x \in W_\bot \mathrel{\text{\&}} (x \leq y \mathrel{\text{or}} x \sqsubset y) \mathrel{\Rightarrow} y \in W_\bot)$)
  and is $\sqsubset$-serial (i.e. $\forall x\, (x \in W_\bot \mathrel{\Rightarrow} \exists y\, (y \in W_\bot \mathrel{\text{\&}} x \sqsubset y))$).

\begin{equation}
\mathscr D(t)
\geq
2\mu\mathscr E(t),
\qquad
\mu>0,

and, for every \(i\in\mathcal I\),
\begin{equation}
q_i(t)
\leq
K_i\mathscr E(t),
\qquad
K_i>0.

Then
\begin{equation}
\mathscr E(t)
\leq
e^{-2\mu t}\mathscr E(0),
\qquad
q_i(t)
\leq
K_i e^{-2\mu t}\mathscr E(0),
\quad
i\in\mathcal I.
\end{equation}
The same conclusion holds with \(q_i\) replaced by a localized gate defect
whenever the corresponding error bound is available.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:12bd1edd458d5d7301f42a505804cb17cb6f183f325af9b0fcc29849f7626a49","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/12/12bd1edd458d5d7301f42a505804cb17cb6f183f325af9b0fcc29849f7626a49.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:50b71a2b97a91700a978fbe3db5e49857c75eebc4c22afc59d8fa65412cc5bd6","bundle_entry_key":"tanh-arbitrary-inputs","bundle_id":"population.t250-tanh-random-products-and-arbitrary-input-gp-003","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"critical tanh Gaussian neural network chains; quantitative Gaussian-process approximation","draft":"w712/bundle_003.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.neural_networks:critical-tanh-multi-input-gp-explicit-depth-rate-w712","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C007 v2: removing the initial-Gram restriction for critical tanh chains

Status: proof (unaudited). Kind: moved. Target: T250(a), finite-input critical tanh chain family. The elementary linear-independence argument below is not claimed as a novel identifiability theorem. Novelty of the quantitative combination remains unverified.

## Theorem

Consider the model in C006, but allow any positive semidefinite initial covariance K_0 with diagonal in [0,1]. Factor K_0=V V^T, with row vectors v_j. Delete zero v_j, and retain one representative from each equivalence class v_j=+-v_k. Let m be the number retained and d the largest class size. If m=0, all trajectories vanish and the approximation error is zero.

If m>0, let K_0^red be the reduced initial covariance. Put F(q)=E tanh^2(sqrt(q)Z), and define the deterministic first postactivation covariance

    (bar K_1^red)_{jk}=E[tanh(v_j.Z)tanh(v_k.Z)],

where Z is a standard Gaussian in a factor space for K_0. Its diagonal entries F(||v_j||^2) are positive. Let rho_1 be the smallest eigenvalue of its normalized correlation matrix. Then rho_1>0. With

    A(m,rho_1)=10^7 m+48*10^24 exp(384+80m)m^2/rho_1,

the joint L-layer preactivation trajectories of all original p inputs and their GP limit admit the normalized squared coupling bound

    E sum_{l=1}^L ||h_l-bar h_l||_F^2/n <= d A(m,rho_1)L/n.

Each single preactivation layer has squared cost <=d A(m,rho_1)/n uniformly in depth. Including postactivations gives twice the joint cost. This holds for every width n and finite L, in particular L<=n^(1-epsilon). The constant is explicit in the deterministic first-layer correlation stability parameter rho_1; no uniform lower bound on rho_1 over input configurations is claimed. Identical, opposite, linearly dependent, and zero input vectors are all allowed by the reduction.

## 1. Linear independence of tanh features

Let v_1,...,v_m be nonzero real vectors with v_j != +-v_k for j!=k. Suppose sum_j c_j tanh(v_j.Z)=0 in Gaussian L2 for a standard Gaussian Z on their finite-dimensional span. The sum is a continuous function and the Gaussian has full support on this span, so this identity holds at every real point z.

Choose a real vector w outside the finitely many proper hyperplanes perpendicular to v_j, v_j-v_k, and v_j+v_k. Such a w exists: a finite union of proper hyperplanes does not fill a positive-dimensional real vector space (for example each has Lebesgue measure zero). Then b_j=v_j.w are nonzero with pairwise distinct absolute values. Restrict the identity to z=tw:

    sum_j c_j tanh(b_j t)=0 for every real t.

Taking t to positive infinity gives sum_j c_j sign(b_j)=0. Subtract this constant identity. Let b_* be the unique smallest |b_j|. The exact formula

    tanh(bt)-sign(b)=-2 sign(b)/(exp(2|b|t)+1)

implies that multiplication by exp(2|b_*|t), followed by t to infinity, yields -2 c_* sign(b_*)=0. Thus c_*=0. Repeating the argument on the remaining finite list proves every coefficient zero. For m=1 the same argument applies directly; no separation hyperplanes between pairs are needed.

Consequently the Gaussian L2 Gram of these m tanh functions is strictly positive definite: for nonzero c, its quadratic form is E(sum c_j tanh(v_j.Z))^2>0. Diagonal normalization preserves positive definiteness. This proves rho_1>0 without requiring the initial linear Gram to be invertible. The elementary feature argument is included only to justify this spectral-gap hypothesis in the quantitative theorem; no literature novelty is asserted for it.

## 2. Quantitative estimate after the first activation

C006 v1, proofs/multi_input_tanh.md, is an unaudited dependency. In its proof, initial positive definiteness is used only in section 3 to obtain a lower spectral bound for the deterministic correlation matrices used in section 6. All relative-moment, noise, and adapted-product estimates in sections 2,4,5 require only positive marginal variances and an initial correlation matrix, which may be singular. They start from identical actual and deterministic initial covariances, so e_0=0 regardless of rank.

For the reduced system, the first activation correlation bar C_1 has smallest eigenvalue rho_1>0 by section 1 above. The same orthogonal-feature decomposition from C006 gives, for every l>=1,

    lambda_min(bar C_l)>=rho_1 exp(-2*(20/3) sum_{j=1}^m sum_{t=1}^{l-1}s_{j,t}^2)
      >=rho_1 exp(-80m).

Indeed sum_{t>=1}s_{j,t}^2<=6q_{j,0}<=6. At state l=0 the actual and GP Gaussian frames coincide exactly, even though they may have singular covariance, so the first preactivation coupling error is zero. At all states l>=1 the displayed spectral bound supplies precisely the gap used in section 6 of C006, with rho_0 replaced by rho_1 and p by m. The early-depth estimate, late-depth signal bound, and small-width bound therefore give A(m,rho_1)/n per layer and A(m,rho_1)L/n for the joint reduced trajectories. This is an application of the proof with its unique use of the original hypothesis replaced, not an assertion that the literal initial assumptions of C006 hold.

## 3. Reinstating sign duplicates and zeros

For v_j=0, that input's preactivations and activations are zero at every layer. For v_j=sigma v_k, sigma in {+1,-1}, shared linear weights and oddness of tanh give h_{l,j}=sigma h_{l,k} at every layer, exactly. The deterministic GP covariance recursion has the identical constraints, so the comparison process can be chosen with those same sign relations.

Extend the reduced coupling by copying each representative column with the appropriate sign, and by adding zero columns. Each representative column's squared error is counted at most d times. Thus the full Frobenius squared error is at most d times the reduced squared error, layer by layer, proving the theorem. This includes n<m, since empirical Gram matrices were allowed to be singular throughout C006.

## Scope and audit focus

This removes the initial-Gram restriction for the finite-input tanh chain family, assuming C002 v2, C004 v1, C005 v1, and C006 v1 are correct. It does not address shared or transposed matrices, general critical activations, or arbitrary Tensor Programs. Review the transfer in section 2, especially that no other use of initial invertibility occurs in C006. No numerical estimate is used as a bound, no independent audit is claimed, and no exhaustive novelty finding is claimed.

Version 2 makes the m=0 branch explicit in the compact claim/card statement. The analytic proof and assumptions are unchanged from version 1.


# C006 v1: critical tanh chains with a positive definite input Gram

Status: proof (unaudited). Kind: moved. Target: T250(a), a restricted multi-input chain family. Novelty has not been established. This does not settle general Tensor Programs, transpose programs, or non-Lipschitz activations.

## Statement and model

Fix p inputs, initial covariance K_0 positive definite, and 0<q_{j,0}=(K_0)_{jj}<=1. Put D_0=diag(sqrt(q_{j,0})), C_0=D_0^{-1}K_0D_0^{-1}, and rho_0=lambda_min(C_0)>0. There are n neurons in every layer, activation tanh, no biases, and fresh independent weights N(0,1/n). The first preactivation layer consists of n independent N_p(0,K_0) rows. Define the empirical postactivation covariance K_l=n^{-1}sum_i tanh(h_{l,i})tanh(h_{l,i})^T for l>=1. Set Q_{j,l}=(K_l)_{jj} and C_l the corresponding correlation matrix. These diagonal entries are strictly positive almost surely. K_0,C_0 and Q_{j,0} are deterministic initial states. The deterministic GP recursion is bar K_{l+1}=E[tanh(Z)tanh(Z)^T], Z~N_p(0,bar K_l), with bar K_0=K_0. Denote its diagonal by s_{j,l} and correlation by bar C_l.

Let B=10^12 and

    A(p,rho_0)=10^7 p +48 B^2 exp(384+80p) p^2/rho_0.

For every n>=1 and L>=1 there is a coupling of the L preactivation layers and their joint GP limit with

    E sum_{l=1}^L ||h_l-bar h_l||_F^2/n <= A(p,rho_0)L/n.

The cost for any single preactivation layer is <=A(p,rho_0)/n, uniformly in depth. Adding all corresponding postactivations multiplies the joint bound by at most two, since tanh is 1-Lipschitz. Thus normalized joint W_2 is at most sqrt(A L/n), in particular for L<=n^(1-epsilon). The covariance normalization is per neuron, with all p inputs retained in the Frobenius norm. Constants are explicit but deliberately very large. Singular initial Gram matrices are excluded.

The hardest step is controlling stochastic correlation errors with adapted random sensitivity products. Section 5 handles this using a predictable normalization and Holder's inequality, without independence of future sensitivities and past noise.

## 1. Inputs from earlier saved lemmas

C002 v2 (proofs/tanh_depth_uniform.md), C004 v1 (proofs/tanh_correlation_stability.md), and C005 v1 (proofs/tanh_random_occupation.md) are used as unaudited dependencies. Their needed statements are reproduced here to make the dependency explicit; this file does not confer independent verification on them.

F(q)=E tanh^2(sqrt(q)Z) is increasing and concave, F(0)=0, q/4<=F(q)<=q-q^2/6 for 0<=q<=1. Each scalar marginal satisfies E[Q_{j,l+1}|past]=F(Q_{j,l}). Its deterministic iteration s_{j,l+1}=F(s_{j,l}) satisfies E Q_{j,l}<=s_{j,l}<=6/l for l>=1, and sum_{l>=0}s_{j,l}^2<=6q_{j,0}. For R_l=Q_{j,l}/s_{j,l}, E(R_l-1)^2<=192l/n when 96l/n<=1. At every depth E(sqrt(Q_{j,l})-sqrt(s_{j,l}))^2<=1152/n.

For standard jointly Gaussian (X,Y) of correlation c, put

    H(q,r,c)=E[tanh(sqrt(q)X)tanh(sqrt(r)Y)]/sqrt(F(q)F(r)).

For q,r in (0,1], H is increasing in c and is Lipschitz in c with constant 1+8(q^2+r^2). Finally, P_L=product_{l<L}[1+8(Q_{j,l}^2+Q_{k,l}^2)] obeys ||P_L||_4<=exp(96(q_{j,0}+q_{k,0}))<=exp(192), provided n>=27648. This is an unconditional moment estimate; no independence from propagated noise is asserted.

## 2. Relative fourth moments in the early window

Set N=400000. For 1<=l<=n/N we prove

    ||Q_{j,l}/s_{j,l}-1||_4<=125 sqrt(l/n),
    ||Q_{j,l}-s_{j,l}||_4<=750/(sqrt(n)sqrt(l)).             (2.1)

Condition on the full network past at layer l and abbreviate q=Q_{j,l}. The n next scalar neurons are independent, Y_i=tanh^2(sqrt(q)Z_i). Let W_i=Y_i/F(q)-1 and xi=n^{-1}sum_i W_i. Then E[xi|past]=0, E[xi^2|past]<=48/n. Since |W_i|<=4Z_i^2+1, E W_i^4<=31025. Independence and centering give

    E[xi^4|past] <=37937/n^2,
    E[|xi|^3|past] <=1400/n^(3/2).

Write delta=R_l-1, S=F(Q_{j,l})/F(s_{j,l}), a=S-1. Concavity, monotonicity and F(0)=0 give |a|<=|delta| and 0<=S<=1+|delta|. Since delta_next=a+S xi, expansion of the fourth power and conditional centering yield, with x=|delta|,

    v4(l+1)<=v4(l)+(288/n)E[x^2(1+x)^2]
       +(5600/n^(3/2))E[x(1+x)^3]
       +(37937/n^2)E[(1+x)^4].

Use x^2(1+x)^2<=2x^2+2x^4 and (1+x)^4<=8(1+x^4). For the cubic-noise term use x/n^(3/2)<=x^2/(2n)+1/(2n^2), 3x^2/n^(3/2)<=3x^2/n, 3x^3/n^(3/2)<=(3/(2n))(x^2+x^4), and x^4/n^(3/2)<=x^4/n. The resulting coefficients of v4/n, v2/n and 1/n^2 are respectively 318072, 28576 and 306296, each <=N. Therefore

    v4(l+1)<=(1+N/n)v4(l)+(N/n)v2(l)+N/n^2.

For l<=n/N, v2(l)<=192l/n. Unrolling from v4(0)=0 gives v4(l)<=N e*193 l^2/n^2<240000000 l^2/n^2<125^4 l^2/n^2. Multiplying by s_{j,l}<=6/l proves (2.1). All statements concern scalar marginals conditional on the full past; independence between different inputs is unnecessary.

## 3. Sensitivity to variances and deterministic spectral gap

Put h_q(z)=tanh(sqrt(q)z)/sqrt(q), h_0(z)=z, and u_q=h_q/||h_q||_2. Norms here are in standard Gaussian L2. For q in (0,1], differentiation and integration of the derivative of t sech^2(t)-tanh(t) show

    |partial_q h_q(z)|<=|z|^3/3.

Indeed that numerator has derivative -2t tanh(t)sech^2(t), whose absolute integral from 0 to t is at most 2|t|^3/3. Also ||h_q||_2>=1/2 by F(q)>=q/4. The derivative of a normalized Hilbert-space vector is its derivative projected onto the orthogonal complement and divided by its norm. Consequently

    ||partial_q u_q||_2<=2sqrt(15)/3=:b<3.

Polynomial Gaussian domination justifies these derivatives and the L2 extension at q=0. Cauchy-Schwarz, applied under the joint Gaussian coupling, gives the uniform bound

    |H(q,r,c)-H(s,t,c)|<=3(|q-s|+|r-t|).                (3.1)

Let a(q)=E[Zu_q(Z)]. It is positive and at most 1. Since sqrt(F(q))<=sqrt(q) and tanh(t)>=t/sqrt(1+t^2) for t>=0, weighted Jensen with weight Z^2 gives a(q)>=1/sqrt(1+3q)>=1/2. Also ||u_q-Z||_2<=bq, so 1-a(q)<=b^2q^2/2. On [1/2,1], -log(a)<=2(1-a), whence -log a(q)<=b^2q^2.

For a standard Gaussian vector of correlation bar C_l, decompose u_{s_j}(Z_j)=a(s_j)Z_j+v_j(Z_j). The v_j are orthogonal to Z_j. Gaussian conditioning implies E[Z_j v_k(Z_k)]=0 for every j,k. Thus

    bar C_{l+1}=A_l bar C_l A_l+V_l,

where A_l=diag(a(s_{j,l})) and V_l is a positive semidefinite covariance matrix. Iteration, or multiplying minimum diagonal factors, gives

    lambda_min(bar C_l)>=rho_0 exp(-2b^2 sum_{j,t<l}s_{j,t}^2)
      >=rho_0 exp(-80 sum_j q_{j,0})>=rho_0 exp(-80p)=:rho. (3.2)

This spectral gap is deterministic. An empirical correlation matrix may be singular, which causes no problem below.

## 4. Conditional empirical-correlation noise

Fix q,r in (0,1] and c in [-1,1]. For n iid standard Gaussian pairs (X_i,Y_i) with correlation c, let U_i=u_q(X_i), V_i=u_r(Y_i),

    A=n^{-1}sum U_i^2, D=n^{-1}sum V_i^2, T=n^{-1}sum U_i V_i.

Then E A=E D=1 and E T=h=H(q,r,c). The next empirical correlation is T/sqrt(AD), and |T|<=sqrt(AD) almost surely. U^2<=4X^2 and V^2<=4Y^2. Each centered one-sample coordinate among U^2,V^2,UV has variance <=48 and fourth moment <=90747. For the product coordinate this follows from |UV-h|<=2X^2+2Y^2+1 and (x+y+z)^4<=27(x^4+y^4+z^4); for square coordinates the sharper fourth bound is 31025. Thus each centered sample mean has fourth moment <=97659/n^2<100000/n^2.

Let E be the event A,D in [1/2,3/2]. Markov gives P(E^c)<=3200000/n^2. On the line segment from (1,1,h) to (A,D,T), on E, the gradient coordinates of phi(A,D,T)=T/sqrt(AD) are bounded by 3, and Hessian entries by 9. Hence

    E[|T/sqrt(AD)-h|^4;E]<=3^4*27*3*100000/n^2
      =656100000/n^2.

The complement contributes at most 16P(E^c)<=51200000/n^2, so the full fourth moment is <10^9/n^2. For the bias, Taylor's remainder on E is bounded in expectation by (9/2)*3*(3*48/n)=1944/n. The mean linear Taylor term on E equals minus its mean on E^c, since the full centered sample means have expectation zero. Cauchy-Schwarz bounds its absolute value by 3*3*sqrt(48*3200000)/n^(3/2)<120000/n^(3/2). The actual error on E^c has expectation <=2P(E^c)<=6400000/n^2. Therefore, writing beta=E[T/sqrt(AD)]-h and zeta=T/sqrt(AD)-E[T/sqrt(AD)],

    |beta|<=B/n, E zeta=0,
    E|zeta|^k<=B n^(-k/2), k=2,3,4, B=10^12.          (4.1)

For the last line use E zeta^4<=16*10^9/n^2 and Lyapunov's inequality. Denominators are positive almost surely even when n=1 or c=+-1. The estimates are uniform in q,r,c and therefore hold conditionally on the full network past.

## 5. Adapted correlation recurrence

Assume n>=N, fix j,k, and put e_l=(C_l)_{jk}-(bar C_l)_{jk}. Conditional sampling, sections 1,3,4 give

    e_{l+1}=A_l e_l+d_l+zeta_{l+1},  e_0=0,
    0<=A_l<=a_l=1+8(Q_{j,l}^2+Q_{k,l}^2),

where A_l is the difference quotient of H in its last variable (zero if e_l=0), and d_l=H(Q_j,Q_k,(bar C_l)_{jk})-H(s_j,s_k,(bar C_l)_{jk})+beta_l. All these coefficients except zeta are past measurable. For 1<=l<=n/N, (2.1) and (3.1) give

    ||d_l||_4<=4500/(sqrt(n)sqrt(l))+B/n,

and ||d_0||_4<=B/n. Let P_0=1, P_{l+1}=P_l a_l, gamma_l=A_l/a_l in [0,1], y_l=e_l/P_l. Then

    y_{l+1}=gamma_l y_l+d_l/P_{l+1}+zeta_{l+1}/P_{l+1}.

P_{l+1} is measurable before sampling the next layer and is at least one. Split y=z+w, starting at zero, with z_{l+1}=gamma_l z_l+eta_{l+1}, eta=zeta/P_{l+1}, and w_{l+1}=gamma_l w_l+d_l/P_{l+1}. The eta retain the conditional centered moment bounds (4.1). Since gamma in [0,1],

    E z_l^2<=Bl/n.

Fourth-power expansion and conditional centering give

    E z_{l+1}^4<=E z_l^4+(6B/n)E z_l^2
       +(4B/n^(3/2))E|z_l|+B/n^2.

Summing and using E|z_l|<=sqrt(Bl/n) yields E z_L^4<=12B^2 L^2/n^2, hence ||z_L||_4<=2sqrt(B)sqrt(L/n). Pathwise |w_L|<=sum_{l<L}|d_l|, so Minkowski and sum_{l=1}^{L-1}l^{-1/2}<=2sqrt(L) give ||w_L||_4<=9000sqrt(L/n)+BL/n. For L<=n/N, altogether ||y_L||_4<=2B sqrt(L/n). C005 and Holder now imply

    ||e_L||_2<=||P_L||_4||y_L||_4<=2B exp(192)sqrt(L/n). (5.1)

This is where random future products must not be treated as independent of the noise. The normalization is predictable at every increment; only the final unconditional Holder step combines its product and remainder.

## 6. Joint Gaussian coupling and all depths

At each layer use a fresh n-by-p matrix G_{l+1} of iid standard normals, independent over layers. Define frames C_l^(1/2)D_l and bar C_l^(1/2)bar D_l, where D_l=diag(sqrt(Q_jl)). Set h_{l+1}=G_{l+1}C_l^(1/2)D_l and bar h_{l+1}=G_{l+1}bar C_l^(1/2)bar D_l. Conditional covariance of each actual row is K_l; its conditional law is exactly that of the network. The GP frames are deterministic and the G are independent over layers, so the entire GP trajectory has the correct joint law. This is a coupling of laws, without claiming it reconstructs original weight matrices.

For PSD C and positive definite bar C with lambda_min>=rho,

    ||C^(1/2)-bar C^(1/2)||_F<=||C-bar C||_F/sqrt(rho).

Proof: X=C^(1/2)-bar C^(1/2) satisfies C^(1/2)X+X bar C^(1/2)=C-bar C. Frobenius inner product with X is >=sqrt(rho)||X||_F^2; apply Cauchy-Schwarz. This holds for singular C.

Decompose the frame difference as C_l^(1/2)(D_l-bar D_l)+(C_l^(1/2)-bar C_l^(1/2))bar D_l. Since C_l has unit diagonal, its first squared Frobenius norm is exactly sum_j(sqrt(Q_jl)-sqrt(s_jl))^2. Thus the expected per-neuron squared coupling cost is bounded by

    2304p/n +2 max_j s_{j,l} rho^{-1} E||C_l-bar C_l||_F^2.

At early states 1<=l<=n/N, insert (5.1), s<=6/l, and (3.2) to obtain

    [2304p+48B^2 exp(384+80p)p^2/rho_0]/n.

State l=0 has identical frames and zero error. At late states l>n/N, use the elementary frame bound cost<=2E[tr K_l+tr bar K_l]<=24p/l<24pN/n. For n<N, all diagonal variances <=1, so cost<=4p<=4pN/n at every state. Both are covered by 10^7p/n. Summing the single-layer costs proves the joint claim. No independence of errors across layers is required for summing expected squared costs.

## Sources, limitations, and review focus

Primary context: Agazzi, Mosig Garcia and Trevisan, Quantitative Gaussian-Process Limits of Tensor Programs, arXiv:2607.06290, Theorem 1.2 and Section 4.1; its fixed-program constants are not substituted for a depth estimate here. Gaussian covariance differentiation used by dependency C004 is sourced there to Voigtlaender, arXiv:1710.03576, Theorem 1 and Corollary 2. The present proof is own-work, unaudited, and its novelty needs literature review. Review especially the conditional empirical-correlation bias estimate, the fourth-moment recurrence, and the predictable-product argument in section 5. with $a \in \mathcal{H}^{\beta,\theta}_K(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R})$, $\beta>0$, $\theta>1$, $K>0$
and $u$ satisfying Assumption (assum:u of the paper).
     Then, there exists $T\in C^{\lfloor \beta \rfloor+1}(\mathbb{R}^d,B^d(0,1))$ such that  $ T\in  \mathcal{H}^{1}_C  (\mathbb{R}^d)$ and $T_{\#}\gamma_d=p$. Furthermore, for all $\epsilon\in (0,1)$, the restriction of $T$ to $B^d(0,\log(\epsilon^{-1}))$ belongs to $ \mathcal{H}_{C\log(\epsilon^{-1})^{C_2}}^{\beta+1}\Big(B^d(0,\log(\epsilon^{-1})),B^d(0,1)\Big)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:MGG of arXiv:2608.19198, 'Probabilistic Representation and Convergence of Gromov-Wasserstein Gradient Flows'] For  $\mu_0,\mu_1,\mu_2\in\mathcal{P}^{\mathrm{ac}}_2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, let $\pi_{01}$ and $\pi_{02}$ be optimal IGW couplings for $(\mu_0,\mu_1)$ and $(\mu_0,\mu_2)$, respectively. Suppose that $\mu_1, \mu_2$ are already rotated w.r.t. $\mu_0$ in the sense of (def:PSD_transform of the paper), so that both optimal couplings have symmetric positive definite (uncentered) cross-covariance matrices $A_1 \coloneqq \frac 12 \int xy^\intercal d\pi_{01}(x,y)$ and $A_2 \coloneqq \frac 12 \int xz^\intercal d\pi_{02}(x,z)$. Consider
    \begin{equation}
    
    T_t \coloneqq \Bigl((1-t)(8A_1)^{-1}+t(8A_2)^{-1}\Bigr)
    \Bigl((1-t)\nabla \phi_1+t\nabla \phi_2\Bigr),
    \end{equation}
where $\phi_1$ and $\phi_2$ are convex functions such that $T_i\coloneqq (8A_i)^{-1}\nabla\phi_i$ is a Gromov--Monge map from $\mu_0$ to $\mu_i$, for each $i=1,2$ (cf. (lem:gromov_monge of the paper)). 
The \textit{modified generalized IGW geodesic} between $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ w.r.t. $\mu_0$ is defined by $\nu_t = (T_t)_{\#} \mu_0$ for $t\in[0,1]$.

[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2607.11773, '2607.11773'] Suppose that ({\bf H1})-({\bf H4}) hold.
   Then for any $\tau \in \mathbb{R}$, $T > 0$, and $R > 0$,
   there exists a constant $C = C(\tau, T, R) > 0$ such that 
   for all $t \in [\tau, \tau+T]$ and $\varepsilon \in (0,1]$,
   \begin{align*}
      \sup_{\varphi \in \mathbb{K}_R}
         \mathbb{E} 
                \left[ \| u^\varepsilon_{t}(\cdot; \tau, \varphi) 
                             - u^0_{t}(\cdot; \tau, \varphi) \|_{\infty}^2 
                \right]
      \le C \varepsilon,
   \end{align*}
   where

body:
Let m denote Lebesgue measure on R^n, let B be the Borel sigma-algebra and let L be the Lebesgue sigma-algebra; recall that (R^n, L, m) is the completion of (R^n, B, m). (i) SETS: if E is in L then there are Borel sets B_1 contained in E contained in B_2 with m(B_2 minus B_1) = 0; consequently E = B_1 union N with N contained in a Borel set of measure zero, and every Lebesgue measurable set differs from a Borel set by a null set. (ii) FUNCTIONS: if f : R^n -> [-infinity, +infinity] is Lebesgue measurable, then there is a BOREL measurable g : R^n -> [-infinity, +infinity] and a Borel set N with m(N) = 0 such that g(x) = f(x) for every x outside N. One may take g with the same pointwise bounds as f (if a <= f <= b a.e. then a <= g <= b everywhere, and if f >= 0 then g >= 0). (iii) The same holds verbatim for the completion of any measure space: an M-bar-measurable function on the completion (X, M-bar, mu-bar) of (X, M, mu) agrees mu-almost everywhere with an M-measurable function. WHERE IT FAILS: (a) 'almost everywhere' cannot be strengthened to 'everywhere': let N be a non-Borel subset of the Cantor set (such subsets exist since the Cantor set has cardinality the continuum and carries continuum-many subsets, while there are only continuum-many Borel sets and all subsets of the Cantor set are Lebesgue null hence Lebesgue measurable); then the indicator of N is Lebesgue measurable but not Borel. (b) 'Borel' cannot be upgraded to 'continuous': Lusin's theorem only gives continuity of the restriction after deleting a set of arbitrarily small measure, not a continuous function agreeing almost everywhere (the indicator of [0,1] is a counterexample). (c) The distinction is not cosmetic in compositions: if h is continuous and f is Lebesgue measurable, f composed with h need not be Lebesgue measurable, whereas g composed with h is Borel measurable whenever g is Borel; this is the standard reason to replace f by its Borel representative before composing or before invoking a change of variables. (d) Statement (i) uses that Lebesgue measure is sigma-finite and Borel-regular; for a general non-regular measure there is no such inner and outer Borel approximation.
m is Lebesgue measure on R^n and L is its completion of the Borel sigma-algebra B
f is Lebesgue measurable with values in the extended reals
for part (i): Lebesgue measure is sigma-finite and outer regular, which is what supplies the Borel hull and kernel
for part (iii): (X, M-bar, mu-bar) is the completion of a measure space (X, M, mu)
the conclusion is equality off a null set, not everywhere

body:
For any random spanning forest on a countable graph with trivial edge-tail sigma-field, the event that it has infinitely many components has probability zero or one. Finitely many edge changes alter a finite component count by at most finitely much and cannot change finiteness. For every finite edge set K, the infinite-count event can therefore be computed after making all edges in K absent, so it is measurable outside K. In particular FUSF on an infinite connected locally finite network has either infinitely many components almost surely or finitely many almost surely. In the finite case the argument does not make the component count constant.
Countable underlying graph
Tail-trivial forest law
For the FUSF corollary use Lyons-Peres Theorem 10.18
title: The finite-versus-infinite component dichotomy is a tail event
