[Definition 3 (Random clock) of arXiv:2604.11434, 'Maxima of stationary systems of randomly time-changed L\'evy particles'] Given a L\'evy process $(L_t)_{t\ge 0}$ and a bounded function $\alpha:\RR \to (0,\infty)$, we define
\begin{align*}
  A_x(t)
  \ = \
  \int_0^t
  \alpha(L_r+x)
  \,\mathrm{d}r
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  T_x(t)
  \ = \
  \inf\{s\ge 0 \mid A_x(s)> t\}
  \,,\qquad
  t\ge 0 \,, x\in\RR\,.
\end{align*}
  We call $(T_x(t))_{t\ge 0}$ the random clock, $(A_x(t))_{t\ge 0}$ the inverse random clock, and $\alpha$ the mass function.
title: Random clock

[Lemma lem:smoothcontrol of arXiv:2608.05089, 'Correlation decay in area-tilted line ensembles'] For any fixed $\alpha > 0$ and $\lambda_0 > 1$, there are some constants $H > 0$ and $C, c > 0$ such that
the following statement holds for all $\lambda > \lambda_0$, all $\Delta \geqslant 1$, and all large enough $T > 0$.
Let $\mathbf{X}$ denote the $\lambda$-tilted line ensemble.
Then there is a random smooth function $\Phi : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}_+$ satisfying the following three properties:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Almost surely, we have $X^2(t) \leqslant \Phi(t)$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$. 
    \item Almost surely, we have $\Phi''(t) \leqslant \frac{1}{2}$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$. 
    \item Defining the event
    \begin{equation}
        \mathcal{H} \coloneqq \mleft\{ \# \mleft\{ j \in \mathbb{Z} : |j \Delta| \leqslant T \text{ and } \Phi(j\Delta) \leqslant \tfrac{H}{2} \mright\}
        \geqslant \frac{\alpha-2}{\alpha} \mleft( \frac{2T}{\Delta} - 1\mright) \mright\},
    \end{equation}
    we have $\mathbb{P} [\mathcal{H} | X^1]  \geqslant \mleft( \frac{1-\Delta/2T}{\alpha} \mright)^2$ almost surely.
    
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem 15 of arXiv:2608.13976, 'Boundary Harnack principle for diffusion with jumps on metric measure spaces'] Suppose ${\bf (\wh{EP})} _{\leq , r_0, \gamma}$ holds  with  $r_0>0$ and $\gamma>0.$
  Then there is a constant $C=C(r_0, \gamma)\geq 1$ such that
  for every ball $B$ with radius $r_0$ and  $\overline B\subsetneq \sX$,

$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 74 of arXiv:2607.10486, 'Weak martingale solutions to stochastic Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system with transport '] Assume that  $\rU$ is a topological vector space and $\rU^\prime$ its topological dual.

A function
\[
Q: [0,\infty) \times \Omega \to \mathscr{L}^+(\rU,\rU^\prime) 
\]
is said to be  a strongly predictable process if and only if for every $f \in \rU$, the new process 
  \[
[0,\infty) \times \Omega \ni (t,\omega)  \mapsto  Q(t,\omega)[f] \in \rU^\prime 
\]  
is predictable in the sense of the previous Definition \ref{def-precictable}, i.e.  for all $f,\, g \in \rU$ the process  
    \begin{equation*}
      s \mapsto \duality{f}{Q_s g}{\rU^\prime}{\rU} \mbox{ is } \mathscr{P}(\mathbb{F})\mbox{-measurable}.
   \end{equation*}

[Lemma 15 of arXiv:2608.14802, 'Dynamical Gibbs-non-Gibbs transitions for finite-alphabet models on trees'] Let $t>0$ and $\theta>4$. Denote by $\Delta := \{ (x,y)\in (0,1)^2 : x=y \}$
the diagonal of the strictly $p_2$-dominant chamber. The map $\widetilde{g}_t^{[2]}$
satisfies $\widetilde{g}_t^{[2]}(\Delta)\subseteq \Delta$ and is componentwise
increasing on $(0,1)^2$, that is,
\begin{equation*}
    \widetilde{g}_t^{[2]}(x,y) \leq \widetilde{g}_t^{[2]}(x',y')
\end{equation*}
componentwise whenever $x,x',y,y'\in(0,1)$, $x\leq x'$, and $y\leq y'$.
Furthermore, let $d_t:(0,1)\to(0,1)$ be the map induced by $\widetilde{g}_t^{[2]}$
on the diagonal, i.e., $ \widetilde{g}_t^{[2]}(x,x) = (d_t(x),d_t(x))$.
If $d_t$ has a unique fixed point $\rho\in (0,1)$, then every discrete trajectory in
$(0,1)^2$ under $\widetilde{g}_t^{[2]}$ converges to $(\rho,\rho)$.
title: Lemma 15 of arXiv:2608.14802

[Lemma 39 (Uniform parabolic atlas from bounded geometry) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Fix \(n\), \(m\geq2\), \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), \(\Lambda\geq1\), and
\(L>0\).  Let \(s(t)\), \(a\leq t\leq b\), be a Ricci flow with
\(b-a\leq L\), and suppose that the inequalities in
\eqref{eq:bounded-lifted-geometry} hold with this \(\Lambda\).  Then there
are \(r_*>0\) and \(A_*<\infty\), depending only on
\(n,m,\sigma,\Lambda,L\), with the following properties.  For every
\((\widetilde x_0,t_0)\), there are harmonic
coordinates for \(\widetilde s(t_0)\) on
\(B_{\widetilde s(t_0)}(\widetilde x_0,4r_*)\).  Keeping the spatial
coordinates fixed, they remain valid on
\[
 B_{\widetilde s(t_0)}(\widetilde x_0,4r_*)
 \times\bigl([t_0-(4r_*)^2,t_0+(4r_*)^2]\cap[a,b]\bigr).
\]
Parabolic estimates may therefore be applied on backward, forward, or
endpoint-truncated subcylinders contained in this set.  In these coordinates
the coefficients of \(\widetilde s\), \(\widetilde s^{-1}\), and the
Christoffel symbols have the finite parabolic H\"older bounds through order
\(m\) needed below, all bounded by \(A_*\).  On overlaps, the transition maps
and their inverses have uniform finite-order parabolic H\"older bounds through
the same order.  Radius-\(r_*/4\) one-sided or truncated subcylinders can be
chosen to cover space-time, while the radius-\(2r_*\) cylinders have uniformly
bounded overlap and admit spatial cutoffs with uniform derivative bounds.

body: [Theorem 1 of arXiv:2605.25323, 'Slow Convergence of Ising and Spin Glass Models with Well-Separated Frustrated Vertices'] Let $\Lambda$ be a square lattice region with fixed $+$ sites on the boundary of $\Lambda$ and a fixed ferromagnetic interaction $J_{ij}=1$ on each boundary edge $(i,j)$. Suppose $\Lambda$ has exactly four frustrated faces, $f_{1},\dots,f_{4}$, that are symmetric around the center of the lattice region under 90 degree rotations and are well-separated (i.e., the shortest lattice path from $f_{i}$ to $f_{i+1}$ has length $2n$, $i=1,2,3$). Then there is a universal temperature $T$ such that the Glauber dynamics ${\mathcal{M}}$ for the spin glass model on $\Lambda$ with $f_{1},...,f_{4}$ the faces with frustration has mixing time $\tau({\mathcal{M}})\geq e^{cn}$, for some constant $c>0,$ whenever $t<T$.

Author-checked lemma; a parent-agent counter-check identified the mechanism, but the full proof has no independent review. Let theta be an invertible measurable measure-preserving transformation of (E,P), with measurable inverse, and n:E->Z measurable. The law of theta^(n(Z))Z for Z~P has density g(y)=sum over k in Z of 1_{n(theta^(-k)y)=k}. Consequently g is integer-valued and finite P-almost everywhere. An arbitrary noninteger target density requires additional randomness or a projection to a marginal.

[Definition of arXiv:2608.22159, 'Optimal Mixing of Glauber Dynamics for the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick Model at \(\beta < 1 /'] Let \(P\) be a Markov chain on a finite state space \(\Omega\). We say that \(P\) is reversible with respect to a probability measure \(\mu\) on \(\Omega\) if the detailed balance condition holds:
    \[
    \mu\left(x\right) P\left(x, y\right) = \mu\left(y\right) P\left(y, x\right), \quad \forall x, y \in \Omega.
    \]
    Equivalently, \(P\) is self-adjoint on \(L^2\left(\mu\right)\).

body:
[Proposition 11 of arXiv:2607.26564, 'Stochastic Scalar Conservation Laws on Moving Hypersurfaces'] ($L^1$-contraction)
Let Assumptions \ref{Assumption1} and \ref{Assumption2} hold. Suppose that $u_1$, $u_2$ are two generalized entropy solutions to the stochastic conservation law \eqref{eq74} with initial values $u_{1,0}$, $u_{2,0} \in L^{\infty}(\Gamma_0)$, respectively. Then there exists a positive constant $C_{1}$ such that $\mathbb{P}$-a.s.
\begin{eqnarray*}
    & & \mathrm{ess\,sup}_{t\in [0,T]}\|u_{1}(t) - u_{2}(t)\|_{L^1(\Gamma_t)} \nonumber\\
&\leq& C_{1} e^{C_{1} (1+ \|u_1\|_{L^\infty(Q_T)} + \|u_2\|_{L^\infty(Q_T)})}\|u_{1,0} - u_{2,0}\|_{L^1(\Gamma_0)}.
\end{eqnarray*}
In particular, the generalized entropy solution to \eqref{eq74} is unique.

body: Let X_1, ..., X_n be independent random variables with E[X_i] = 0 and |X_i| <= M almost surely for every i, and let sigma^2 = sum_{i=1}^n Var(X_i). Then for every t > 0, P(sum_{i=1}^n X_i >= t) <= exp(- t^2 / (2 (sigma^2 + M t / 3))), and the same bound holds for the lower tail by symmetry. When sigma^2 is much smaller than n M^2, this improves on Hoeffding's inequality, which does not use the variance. [standard, e.g. Boucheron, Lugosi and Massart, Concentration Inequalities]
title: Bernstein's Inequality for Sums of Independent Bounded Random Variables

Let lambda<=n(lambda)<=poly(lambda), and let m,N and the seed length be polynomially bounded positive integers with N>=(n+1)*m. Let F_s:{0,1}^n->{0,1} be an efficiently evaluable noisy weak-PRF family at a fixed q in[0,1/2), in the sample-oracle sense of Definitions3.1–3.2. Choose one uniform seed S, one independent uniform N-bit pad Z, and one independent uniform permutation Pi of N coordinates as the secret key. Each encoder call independently samples m uniform X_j in{0,1}^n, m independent Bernoulli(q) bits E_j, and a fresh uniform filler R of length N-(n+1)*m; it returns Pi applied to(C xor Z), where C concatenates the pairs(X_j,F_S(X_j) xor E_j) and R. For any probabilistic polynomial-time distinguisher making at most Q polynomially many adaptive encoder calls, there is a polynomial-time weak-PRF sample-oracle distinguisher making at most M=Q*m calls whose advantage bounds the encoding-oracle advantage up to min(1,binom(M,2)/2^n). Here the reference encoding oracle returns a fresh independent uniform N-bit word at every call. Thus the encoder is undetectable under the noisy weak-PRF assumption. Locality of F_s and decoder robustness are not needed for this claim.
A noisy weak-PRF family with uniform random input samples; polynomial parameter lengths and n>=lambda.
One shared independent seed,pad,permutation; fresh sample inputs,noise and filler per encoding.
At most polynomially many calls,with a fixed polynomial upper bound Q.

\[
 Y(w)=b+cw+\int \left( \frac{1}{\lambda-w} - \frac{\lambda}{1+\lambda^2} \right)  {\rm d} \mu(\lambda),

for some $b,c\in {\mathbb R}$, $c\geq 0$, and $\mu$ being a Borel measure on ${\mathbb R}$.

=& -2g_\ag(A_\alpha,A_\beta)

body:
[Corollary 5 of arXiv:2608.01516, 'Nondegeneracy and regularity of polynomial pushforwards'] Let $a,b\in(0,+\infty)$, $\eta>0$, $k,d\in\mathbb N$, and $d\ge2$. There exists
a constant $C:=C(a,b,\eta,k,d)>0$ such that, for every
$X=(X_1,\ldots,X_k),Y=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_k)\in\mathcal P_{d,k}^{\rm lc}$
satisfying
\[
a\le \operatorname{Var}(X_j)\le b,
\quad
a\le \operatorname{Var}(Y_j)\le b
\quad
\forall j\in\{1,\ldots,k\},
\]
and
\[
\det \Sigma^d(X)\ge \eta,
\quad
\det \Sigma^d(Y)\ge \eta,
\]
one has
\[
d_{\rm TV}(X,Y)
\le
C d_{\rm KR}(X,Y)^{\frac{1}{k(d-1)+2}}.
\]

In particular, if a sequence
$X_n\in\mathcal P_{d,k}^{\rm lc}$ converges in distribution to an
$\mathbb R^k$-valued random vector $X_\infty$ whose distribution is absolutely
continuous, then the convergence holds in total variation and
\[
d_{\rm TV}(X_n,X_\infty)
\le
C d_{\rm KR}(X_n,X_\infty)^{\frac{1}{k(d-1)+2}}
\]
for some constant $C>0$ depending on the sequence and on the limiting
distribution. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary 5 of arXiv:2608.01516

[Definition QFCLT of arXiv:2411.06861, 'Quenched invariance principle for random walks in random environments admitting a cycle de'] Set $X_t^{(n)}:=\frac{1}{n}X_{n^2t}, t\geq 0$. We say the \textit{quenched functional CLT} (QFCLT) or \textit{quenched invariance principle} holds for $X$ if for $\mathbb{P}$-a.s. $\omega$ under $\Prob_0^\omega$, $X^{(n)}$ converges in law to a Brownian motion on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with covariance matrix $\Sigma^2=\Sigma \cdot \Sigma^T$. That is, for every $T>0$ and every bounded continuous function $F$ on the Skorohod space $D([0, T], \mathbb{R}^d)$, setting $\psi_n= \Mean_0^\omega[F(X^{(n)})]$ and $\psi_\infty= \Mean_0^{\text{BM}}[F(\Sigma \cdot W)]$ with $(W, \Prob_0^{\text{BM}})$ being a Brownian motion started at $0$, we have that $\psi_n \to \psi_\infty \mathbb{P}$-a.s.

As our main result we establish a QFCLT for $X$ under some additional moment conditions.

[Lemma rho of arXiv:2411.07878, 'Bernstein-type and Bennett-type inequalities for unbounded matrix martingales'] Fix $\lambda > 0$, $\alpha > 0$. Define the function
    \begin{equation}
        \rho_{\lambda, \alpha}(x) \coloneqq \left(\phi(\lambda x) - \frac{(\lambda x)^2}{2}\right) \exp\left\{- x^\alpha \right\}.
    \end{equation}
    Then for $x > 0$ it holds that
    \[
    \sgn \rho_{\lambda, \alpha}'(x) = \sgn\left(\upsilon(\lambda x) - \alpha x^\alpha\right) ,
    \]
    where
    \begin{equation}
        \upsilon(t) \coloneqq \frac{t \phi(t)}{\phi(t) - t^2 / 2} .
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, full calibration, paired). Given that the long-only gain is the estimation variance the constraint removes at the rows the stack is scored on, the amount of constraint was chosen with the evaluation inputs: a blend w(t) between the simplex and least-squares stacks with t minimising the cross-validated calibration error plus the excess bootstrap variance of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows, and a per-row version t_i = 1/(1 + kappa v_i/median v) that leans to the simplex where least squares is uncertain. P24 (a) HELD: on EMIT the per-cell blend reads +0.08 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 39 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 t* is at or above 0.5 on 30 of 30 cells and the blend reads +0.66 vs least squares; (c) REFUTED: the per-row blend vs the per-cell blend is +0.70 on Y2 and -0.14 on EMIT overall; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Fresh-split replication (P25, split C, SPLIT_SEED 11, the criterion uses no evaluation targets): P25 (a) HELD: on split C the EMIT blend reads +0.63 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 35 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend reads +0.84 vs the simplex (wins 30 of 30) and +0.65 vs least squares; (c) HELD: t* averages 0.34 on EMIT and 0.67 on OCO-2; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Bootstrap-size stability (P28, B = 16 against B = 8 on split B): P28 (a) HELD: t*(16) equals t*(8) on 86 pct of the 70 cells and is within 0.2 on 100 pct; (b) HELD: the blend's mean gain against the simplex moves from +0.08 to +0.06 on EMIT and from +0.83 to +0.83 on OCO-2, and the both-endpoints win count on OCO-2 is 30 of 30 at B = 16; falsifier (agreement below 50 pct or a gain moving by more than 0.5) not triggered. Break test: a fixed midpoint t = 0.5 matches the criterion on OCO-2 (+0.96 / +1.01 against +0.83 / +0.84 on the two splits) but loses 1.6 and 4.4 pct on EMIT where the criterion stays at +0.08 and +0.63 - the criterion's value is knowing, without labels, when not to leave the simplex; the EMIT shortfall against the hindsight-best t is the bias-shift term of the risk identity. Scarce calibration (P30, 240 of the calibration rows per cell, split B): P30 (a) HELD: at n = 240 the simplex beats least squares by +14.10 on EMIT (full calibration +8.83); (b) REFUTED: t* averages 0.22 on EMIT and the blend reads -2.61 vs the simplex; (c) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend beats both endpoints on 30 of 30 cells and the simplex reads +2.27 vs least squares (full calibration -0.18); falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT) TRIGGERED. The observable part of the bias shift (P31): adding t^2 (D_ev - D_cal), the shift in the two bases' mean squared disagreement between the evaluation and calibration rows, to the criterion - P31 (a) REFUTED: the R'-blend reads -0.71 vs the simplex on EMIT split B (R-blend +0.08) and +0.71 on split C (R-blend +0.63); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the R'-blend is -0.11 vs the R-blend on split B and -0.12 on split C; (c) REFUTED: mean t** 0.39 against t* 0.33 on EMIT, share of the hindsight optimum 0.07 -> -0.62; falsifier (R'-blend worse than the R-blend by more than 0.3 on any corpus or split) TRIGGERED. Per-output mixing weights (P34, the criterion decoupled across outputs): P34 (a) REFUTED: the per-output blend reads -0.41 vs the per-cell blend on EMIT split B and -0.53 on split C; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 -0.02 and -0.08 on split C; (c) REFUTED: on Y2 the share of outputs at t_d = 0 is 0.20 and at t_d >= 0.5 is 0.34; falsifier (per-output worse than per-cell by more than 0.3 anywhere) TRIGGERED. A nearest-neighbour proxy for the bias shift (P35, the simplex's out-of-fold residuals at the nearest calibration rows standing in for its bias at the scored rows): P35 (a) REFUTED: the full-shift blend reads -0.69 vs the R-blend on EMIT split B and -0.12 on split C; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 -0.08 and -0.14 on split C; (c) REFUTED: cross-only vs full on EMIT -0.05 vs -0.62 (split B); falsifier (either variant worse than the R-blend by more than 0.3 anywhere) TRIGGERED.

body:
[Theorem thm:dilation of arXiv:2608.01253, 'The pseudo-quantum representation of \\finite reversible Markov chains'] The generator $K=\sigma^y\otimes A$ of (equation eq:K of the paper) satisfies

\begin{equation}
K^{T}=-K\qquad\text{and}\qquad K^{*}=K,

\end{equation}

that is, $K$ is antisymmetric for the transpose and Hermitian for the conjugate
transpose. For $z\in\mathbb{C}$ set $W_z:=e^{zK}$. Then $z\mapsto W_z$ is an entire
homomorphism from $(\mathbb{C},+)$ into $\OO(2M,\mathbb{C})$, with

\[
W_{z+w}=W_zW_w,\qquad W_0=\mathrm{I},\qquad W_z^{T}W_z=\mathrm{I},
\]

and it has the closed block form

\begin{equation}
W_z=\begin{pmatrix}\cosh(zA)&-i\sinh(zA)\\ i\sinh(zA)&\cosh(zA)\end{pmatrix}.

\end{equation}

[Proposition 4 (Optimality) of arXiv:2605.13107, 'Discrepancy and Fisher information'] Let $\e_1,\ldots, \e_n$ be independent Rademacher random variables. 
	Consider any discarding algorithm\footnote{Here, an algorithm can be any function that maps a sign string $\e_1,\ldots, \e_n$ to a subset of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ of the terms to be discarded.} (online or not) that maintains, for each $k$,
	$$
	\abs[\Bigg]{\sum_{j \le k \text{ accepted}} \e_j} \le T
	\quad \text{deterministically}.
	$$
	Then 
	$$
	\E \#\{\text{discarded}\}
	\ge \frac{n}{2 T + 1} - T.
	$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:rows of arXiv:2608.30254, 'Exact Recovery Thresholds for Weighted Data Selection\\ in Vector-Valued Linear Regression'] Write $w_j^\top$ for the $j$-th row of $W$ and $y_{ij}$ for the $j$-th entry
of $y_i$. Then
$F_c(W)=\sum_{j=1}^m\sum_ic_i(\langle w_j,x_i\rangle-y_{ij})^2$ and
$\lVert W\rVert_F^2=\sum_j\lVert w_j\rVert^2$. Hence the minimizer set of $F_c$ is the
Cartesian product over rows of scalar weighted least-squares solution sets,
and $A(F_c)$ consists of the minimal-$\ell_2$-norm scalar solutions row by
row --- \emph{with the single shared weight vector $c$}.

[Lemma sde.unique_solution of arXiv:2605.17725, 'Limit theorems for random walks with spatio-temporal drift'] For every initial law on $\mathbb{R}^d$, the SDE (equation eq:sde_critical of the paper) admits a
non-explosive global weak solution, and its law is unique. Let
$(P_t)_{t\ge0}$ denote the corresponding Markov semigroup. Then there exists
a unique stationary distribution $\pi$ for this semigroup and there exist
constants $C,\lambda>0$ such that
\begin{equation}

|P_t f(x)-\pi(f)|
\le
C e^{-\lambda t}(1+\|x\|^2)\|f\|_\infty
\end{equation}
for every bounded measurable function $f$, every $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and every $t\ge0$.

body:
[Lemma lem:mean-bias-On-1 of arXiv:2605.03718, 'Potential Hessian Ascent III:\\ Sampling the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick Model at $\beta < 1/'] Fix $t\in[0,T]$ and $0 < \beta < 1/2$. Let
\[
\delta q_n:=\nu(R_{12})-q^*,
\qquad
\delta m_n:=\nu(M_1)-m^*.
\]
Assume the hypotheses \textbf{(H1)--(H3)}, and let $Y^*$ be the cavity field and set
\[
\mu_r:=\mathop{{}\mathbb{E}}[\tanh^r(Y^*)],\qquad r\in\{1,2,3,4\}\,,
\]
and
\[
\mathbf M:=
\begin{pmatrix}
1-4\mu_2+3\mu_4 & 2(\mu_1-\mu_3)\\
\mu_3-\mu_1 & 1-\mu_2
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then, the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[itemsep=0.3em]
    \item The deviations satisfy the stability equation 
        \begin{equation}
            \begin{pmatrix}\delta q_n\\ \delta m_n\end{pmatrix} =
                \beta^2\,\mathbf M
            \begin{pmatrix}\delta q_n\\ \delta m_n\end{pmatrix}
                \;+\;O(n^{-1}),
         \end{equation} 
        where the $O(n^{-1})$ is uniform in $n$. 
    \item Furthermore, if  $\rho(\beta^2\mathbf M)<1$, then
        \[
            \delta q_n=O(n^{-1}),
            \qquad
            \delta m_n=O(n^{-1}).
        \]
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Proposition 14 (Second-order smooth consistency) of arXiv:2609.00673, '2609.00673'] Let \(\gamma\in C^6(I,\mathbb R^3)\) be a unit-speed space curve.
Assume that, on a compact subinterval \(J\Subset I\),
\[
\kappa(s)\ge \kappa_0>0,\qquad |\tau(s)|\ge\tau_0>0.
\]
Sample it uniformly by
\[
P_i=\gamma(s_i),\qquad s_i=s_0+ih.
\]
For the quotient indexed by $i$, call $C_i=[s_{i-1},s_{i+2}]$ its associated four-point cell. All quotient estimates below are uniform whenever $C_i\subset J$; estimates for the defect $D_i^h$, which involves two consecutive quotients, are uniform whenever $C_i\cup C_{i+1}=[s_{i-1},s_{i+3}]\subset J$.
Let \(\theta_i^h\) and \(\phi_i^h\) be the turning and signed torsion
angles of the chord polygon and set
\[
x_i^h=\tan\frac{\theta_i^h}{2}.
\]
There exists $h_0=h_0(\kappa_0,\tau_0,J)>0$ such that, for $0<h<h_0$ and all cells under consideration,
\[
0<\theta_i^h<\pi,\qquad \phi_i^h\notin\{0,\pi\}.
\]
Hence the sampled polygon lies in the generic Frenet branch and all quotients below are well defined.
With $m_i=s_i+h/2$, the midpoint convention compatible with the chord tangents gives the
asymptotic expansions
\[
x_i^h=\frac h2\kappa(s_i)+O(h^3),
\]
and
\[
\phi_i^h=h\tau\left(s_i+\frac h2\right)+O(h^3).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\frac{x_i^h+x_{i+1}^h\cos\phi_i^h}{\sin\phi_i^h}
=
\frac{\kappa}{\tau}\left(s_i+\frac h2\right)+O(h^2).
\]
If
\[
D_i^h:=
\frac{x_{i+1}^h+x_{i+2}^h\cos\phi_{i+1}^h}{\sin\phi_{i+1}^h}
-
\frac{x_i^h+x_{i+1}^h\cos\phi_i^h}{\sin\phi_i^h},
\]
then, uniformly on such cells,
\[
\boxed{
\frac{D_i^h}{h}
=
\left(\frac{\kappa}{\tau}\right)'(m_i)+O(h)
},
\qquad m_i=s_i+\frac h2.
\]
Thus the finite-step conservation law approaches $(\kappa/\tau)'=0$, equivalently \(\tau/\kappa=\mathrm{constant}\) on intervals where \(\kappa\tau\neq0\). The scalar quotient itself is second-order accurate, whereas its normalized finite difference is first-order accurate. If the underlying smooth curve is a general helix, then
\[
D_i^h=O(h^3).
\]

[Definition 7 of arXiv:2606.20948, '\textsc{Slot decomposition of\\ continuous Box-Ball Systems}'] [The slot diagrams of a positive point configuration]
 \rm  Let $\sN\in\cN_+$. Proceed recursively. Denote $\sN_0 \vcentcolon =\sN$, $\su_0\vcentcolon = 0$, $\sM_0\vcentcolon = \emptyset$, and a function $\sg_0(y) \equiv 0$ for all $y> 0$. 

Recursive step. Suppose that $\sN_{k},\su_{k},\sM_{k}$ are defined.
See Fig.~\ref{Mk}.
 For $k\ge1$ let $\sg_k\vcentcolon =\sg[\sM_k]$,  the right boundary of the slot diagram $\sM_k$, as defined in \eqref{sca7}. Then, use \eqref{sc12} to define
\begin{align}
 (\su_{k+1}, \sM_{k+1})&\vcentcolon = (\su[\sN_{k}], \sM[\sN_{k}]),  \\
 \sN_{k+1} &\vcentcolon = \Bigl\{\bigl(u-\su_{k+1}-\sg_{k+1}(\ell), \ell\bigl):(u, \ell)\in\sN_{k}\setminus\sM_{k+1}\Bigr\}. 
\end{align}
A point $(u,\ell)$ in $\sN_{k}\setminus\sM_{k+1}$ is shifted leftwards to a point in $\sN_{k+1}$ having the same vertical coordinate~$\ell$, and horizontal coordinate $u-\su_{k+1}-\sg_{k+1}(\ell)$. 
Note that given a finite set $\mathcal T(y+\su_{k+1})$ that verifies \eqref{eqRy} for $\sN_{k}$, once we shift it as in \eqref{sc111} we get a finite set $\mathcal T(y)$ that verifies \eqref{eqRy} for $\sN_{k+1}$.
Therefore we inductively get that $\sN_{k}$ is $\mathcal T$-finite.

Iterate the recursive step to obtain a map from $\sN\in \cN_+$ to a sequence of slot diagrams and insertion points 
\begin{align}
  \sN\mapsto  (\su_k[\sN], \sM_k[\sN])_{k\ge 1}.
\end{align}

body:
[Lemme 26 of arXiv:2604.00635, 'Large deviations of the periodic Toda chain'] Let $\mu$ be a probability measure such that $I[\mu] <+\infty$.
Then there exists a sequence of probability measures $(\mu_p)_{p\ge 1} $ so that
\begin{enumerate}
    \item For every $p\in \mathbb{N}^*$, $d_{\mathrm{BL}}(\mu,\mu_p)\le 1/p$,
    \item For $p$ large enough, there exists $\kappa_p>0$
    \begin{align*}
        &1+\frac{2}{\ell}\int\ln|x-y|\mathrm{d}\mu_p(y)\ge \kappa_p \, , &  &\forall x\in \mathbb{R} \; .
    \end{align*}
    \item $\mu_p$ is compactly supported.
    \item If $\int x \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x)=0$, then $\int x \, \mathrm{d}\mu_p(x)=0$ for every integer number $p$.
    \item $\mu_p$ has bounded density with respect to Lebesgue measure.
    \item $I[\mu_p] \longrightarrow I[\mu]$ as $p \to +\infty$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemme 26 of arXiv:2604.00635

[Theorem thm:probe-stability of arXiv:2608.21561, '\textbf{Loss-Parameterized Fisher Width Along Learning Trajectories}'] Let $T\subset\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty and compact. For any linear maps
$A,B:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$,
\begin{equation}
    |w(AT)-w(BT)|
    \leq
    \gamma_dR_T
    \|A-B\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
    
\end{equation}
Consequently, if
\[
    a_T
    :=
    w\!\left(\overline G_\star^{1/2}T\right),
\]
then
\begin{equation}
    \left|
        \frac{w_F(T;\theta_t)}{\sqrt{s_t}}
        -
        a_T
    \right|
    \leq
    \gamma_dR_T\varepsilon_t.
    
\end{equation}
If $a_T>0$, then
\begin{equation}
    \left|
        \frac{w_F(T;\theta_t)}
        {a_T\sqrt{s_t}}
        -1
    \right|
    \leq
    \frac{\gamma_dR_T}{a_T}\,
    \varepsilon_t.
    
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 202 (Pointwise estimates for inhomogeneous terms tied to the modified quantities) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Let $N = \Ntop$.

\medskip
\noindent \underline{\textbf{Estimates tied to the fully modified quantities}}.
Let $\tander^N \in \mathfrak{P}^{(N)}$ where $\mathfrak{P}^{(N)}$
is the set of order $N$ $\ell_{t,u}$-tangential commutator operators from Def.\,\ref{D:STRINGSOFCOMMUTATIONVECTORFIELDS}. 
Let $\mathfrak{X}$ be the term defined in \eqref{E:MODIFIEDQUANTITYINHOM},
and let $\mathfrak{A}$ be the term appearing on RHS\,\eqref{E:RICCICONTRACTEDLANDL}
and enjoying the schematic structure \eqref{E:AINHOMRIC}.
Then the following pointwise estimates hold on 
$\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}$:
\begin{subequations}
\begin{align}
	\begin{split}
		\left| 
		(\muX v^1) \tander^N \mathfrak{X} + 2 (\Lunit \upmu) \muX \tander^N v^1\right|
		& 
		\lesssim 
		  \fundbootsmall \left| \newuL \tander^{[1,N]} \velocityarray\right| + \fundbootsmall \upmu \left| \tander^{[1,N+1]}\velocityarray\right|  \\
		& \ \ \ \ + \upmu \left| \tander^{\le N}(\vortrenormalized,\GradEnt)\right| +  \left| \tander^{[1,N]}\controlvars\right| +  \left|\tandersmall^{[1,N]}\badcontrolvars\right|  
	\end{split} \\
	\begin{split}
		\left|\tander^N \mathfrak{X} \right| 
		& \lesssim 
		\left|\newuL \tander^N\velocityarray \right| + \upmu  \left|\tander^{[1,N+1]} \velocityarray\right|
		+ 
		\left|\comdersmall^{[1,N];1}\velocityarray \right| \\
		& \ \ \ \ +  \left| \tander^{\le N}(\vortrenormalized,\GradEnt)\right| 
		+
		\left|\tander^{[1,N]}\controlvars\right| 
		+ 
		\left|\tandersmall^{[1,N]}\badcontrolvars \right|,
		 
	\end{split}  
			\\
	\begin{split}
		
		|\tander^N \mathfrak{A}|
		& \lesssim \upmu\left| \tander^N(\VortVort,\DivGradEnt)\right| +  \left| \tander^{\le N-1}(\VortVort,\DivGradEnt)\right| + \left| \tander^{\le N}(\vortrenormalized,\GradEnt)\right| +  \left| \comdersmall^{[1,N+1];1} \velocityarray\right|  \\
		& \ \ \ \ 
		+ \upmu \left| \tander^{[1,N+1]}\velocityarray\right| +  \left|\tander^{\le N} (\vortrenormalized,\GradEnt)\right| + 	|\tander^{[1,N]} \controlvars | 
		+ 
		|\tandersmall^{[1,N]}\badcontrolvars|.
	\end{split}
\end{align}
\end{subequations}\medskip

\noindent \underline{\textbf{Estimates tied to the partially modified quantities}}.
If $\tanderY^{N-1} \in \mathfrak{Y}^{(N-1)}$ 
and $\widetilde{\mathfrak{X}}$, 
$\partialmodquantinhom{\tanderY^{N-1}}$,
${^{(\tanderY^{N-1})}\mathfrak{B}}$
are as defined in \eqref{E:PARTIALMODIFIEDQUANTITYINHOMZEROORDER},
\eqref{E:PARTIALMODIFIEDQUANTITYINHOM} 
(with $\tanderY^{N-1}$ in the role of $\tander^N$), 
and \eqref{E:PARTIALMODIFIEDQUANTITYINHOM} (with $\tanderY^{N-1}$ in the role of $\tander^{N-1}$) 
respectively, then the following pointwise estimates hold on 
$\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}$:
\begin{subequations}
\begin{align}
\left|\partialmodquantinhom{\tanderY^{N-1}} \right|
& \lesssim 
\left| \tander^{[1,N]} \velocityarray\right| +  \left|\tander^{\le N-1} (\vortrenormalized,\GradEnt)\right| + \fundbootsmall \left| \tander^{[1,N-1]} \controlvars\right|, 
 
		\\
\left| \Lunit \partialmodquantinhom{\tanderY^{N-1}} \right|, 
	\,
\left| \Yvf{A} \partialmodquantinhom{\tanderY^{N-1}}\right| 
& 
\lesssim 
\left| \tander^{[1,N+1]} \velocityarray\right| +  \left|\tander^{\le N} (\vortrenormalized,\GradEnt)\right| + \fundbootsmall \left| \tander^{[1,N]} \controlvars\right|, 
 
		\\
\left|{^{(\tanderY^{N-1})}\mathfrak{B}} \right| 
& 
\lesssim 
\left |\tander^{[1,N]} \controlvars\right|. 
	
\end{align}
\end{subequations}

[Lemma 30 of arXiv:2609.03332, 'Singularity Models of Finite-Time K\"ahler-Ricci Flows'] Suppose $T = T_F' < \min_{k \geq 2} \{T_k^0, T_k^\ell\}$ so that $L (t) = 2 ( m + 2 ) ( T - t ) \to 0$. Then there exists a constant $C > 0$ independent of $t$ such that on $\widehat{M} \times [0,T)$,
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)]	$0 < \frac{1}{C} \leq f_k^2 \leq C$, \;$k \geq 2$,
\item[(ii)] $h^2 \leq Cf_k^2$, \;$k \geq 1$,
\item[(iii)] $\big| A' \big|_{g (t)}^2 \leq\; C$, and
\item[(iv)] $|K_{g(t)}(X,Y)| \leq C$ \text{ for any two-plane $\textrm{span}\{X,Y\} \subset \mathcal{H}'$}.
\end{itemize}
Here $\mathcal{H}'$ denotes the horizontal distribution and $A'$ denotes the O'Neill's $A$-tensor of the submersion $\widehat{\pi}' : \widehat{M} \to N'$ with respect to the metric $g(t)$.

[Lemma 5 of arXiv:2604.15152, 'The Multinomial Allocation Model and the Random Box Load'] For $0\le r\le n$, $n\ge1$, define $\varphi_n(\cdot)$  by
\[ \frac{n!}{(n-r)!}=n^r (1-n^{-1}\varphi_n(r)).\]
Then
\[ 0\le \varphi_n(r)\le \binom{r}{2},\]
and moreover, $\varphi^*_n(r)$ defined by
\[ \varphi_n(r)=\binom{r}{2}-n^{-1}\varphi^*_n(r),\]
satisfies
\[  0\le \varphi^*_n(r)\le r^4,\quad 0\le r\le n.\]

body:
[Lemma 4 (Scaling of the spectrum) of arXiv:2603.29473, '$\chi^2$--cut-off phenomenon for Galerkin projections of Fokker--Planck equations with mon'] \hfill

	\noindent
	Let $u:\R \to \R$ be a solution to $\mathcal{L}_1 u = f$ for a suitable smooth function $f$. Then the function defined by $u_\varepsilon(x) = u(x \varepsilon^{-\frac{1}{1+\gamma}})$ satisfies
	\begin{equation*}
		\mathcal{L}_\varepsilon u_\varepsilon = \varepsilon^{\frac{\gamma-1}{\gamma+1}} f\left ( x \varepsilon^{-\frac{1}{1+\gamma}} \right ).
	\end{equation*}
	In particular,  any eigenfunction $u$ of $-\mathcal{L}_1 u = \lambda u$ with an eigenvalue $\lambda$ can be transformed into the eigenfunction $u_\varepsilon$ of $-\mathcal{L}_\varepsilon$ with eigenvalue $\lambda \varepsilon^{\frac{\gamma-1}{\gamma+1}}$.

	Furthermore, the following relation holds true $\|u\|_{L^2(C_1 e^{-V})} = \|u_\varepsilon\|_{L^2(C_\varepsilon e^{-V/\varepsilon})}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Scaling of the spectrum

[Theorem 10 (Predictive coincidence decomposition) of arXiv:2608.20337, 'Information on trajectories:\\ martingales and random times'] Let $\alpha_i \geq 0$ for all $i$ with $\bar\alpha := \sum_{i=1}^W \alpha_i
\geq 1$, let $Q_t^\alpha(\gamma) := \prod_i
P_t^{(i)}(\gamma)^{\alpha_i}/Z_t(\alpha)$ be the Gibbs law on prefixes, and let
\begin{equation}
  \kappa_t^\alpha(\gamma)
  := \sum_{x\in S} \prod_{i=1}^W
     P\bigl(X_{t+1}=x \mid X_{0:t}=\gamma; P^{(i)}\bigr)^{\alpha_i}
\end{equation}
be the one-step predictive coincidence kernel.  Then
\begin{align}
  Z_{t+1}(\alpha) &= Z_t(\alpha)\,\E_{Q_t^\alpha}[\kappa_t^\alpha],
    \\
  \cC_\alpha(t+1) - \cC_\alpha(t)
    &= -\log \E_{Q_t^\alpha}[\kappa_t^\alpha] \geq 0 .
    
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Predictive coincidence decomposition

Let $m\in {\mathbb N}_{\geq 1}$ be such that 
$$
N^{-1}\eqsim \eta^{m-1} L_0^{-1} \qquad \text{(more precisely,\  $\eta^{m}L_0^{-1}<N^{-1}\leq \eta^{m-1}L_0^{-1}$)}.
$$
Then for all $\ell\in \{1,\dots,m\}$, it holds that:
\begin{align}

\Big({\mathbf E}\Big\|v^N-\fint_{\eta^{\ell} B} v^N\Big\|_{\underline{L}^2(\eta^{\ell} Q)}^r \Big)^{1/r}
&
\leq \eta^{\ell\gamma_0}\Big({\mathbf E}\Big\|v^N-\fint_{B} v^N\Big\|_{\underline{L}^2( Q)}^r \Big)^{1/r}\\ 
\nonumber

[Definition d:ext of arXiv:2508.21658, 'Infinite-dimensional stochastic differential equations for Coulomb random point fields'] \thetag{i}
A non-negative symmetric bilinear form $ (\E , \mathscr{D}_0 ) $ densely defined on $ \Lnu $ is called closable on $ \Lnu $ if, for any $ \E $-Cauchy sequence $ f_n\in \mathscr{D}_0$ such that $ \lim \| f_n \| _{\Lnu } = 0 $ as $ n \to \infty $, 
it holds that $ \limi{n}\E (f_n , f_n ) = 0$. 

\noindent \thetag{ii} 
If $ (\E , \mathscr{D}_0) $ is closable on $ \Lnu $, then there exists 
a closed extension of $ (\E , \mathscr{D}_0) $. 
The smallest closed extension $ (\E , \mathscr{D} ) $ is called the closure of $ (\E , \mathscr{D}_0) $.

        \exp\left[
        -\left(\pi^2(\log(d-1))^2+o(1)\right)

\]
where
\[
        \rho_d=\frac{2\sqrt{d-1}}{d}
\]
is the spectral radius of simple random walk on $T_d$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 43 (Glauber dynamic) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Consider the square lattice graph $\Z^d$ (also denoted $G=(V,E)$).
    Let $\mu$ denote a stationary measure on $\Pi_G$.
    For any $u\in V$, let $G_u$ denote the subgraph of $G$ induced by the vertices $V\setminus\{u\}$.
    A \emph{Glauber dynamic} for $\mu$ is a function
    \[
        R:\Pi_G\times V\times\Sigma \to \Pi_G,
    \]
    with the following properties.
    \begin{itemize}
        \item\textbf{Local update.}
        For any $\tau\in \Pi_G$, $u\in V$ and $\iota\in\Sigma$, we have $R(\tau,u,\iota)|_{G_u}=\tau|_{G_u}$.
        \item\textbf{Consistency.}
        For any $\tau\in \Pi_G$ and $u\in V$, the distribution of $R(\tau,u,\iota)$ in $\diff\iota$ is $\mu[\blank|\tau|_{G_u}]$.
        \item\textbf{Equivariance.}
        For any $\tau\in \Pi_G$, $u\in V$, $\iota\in\Sigma$ and $\theta\in\Theta$, we have $R(\tau,u,\iota)\circ\theta=R(\tau\circ\theta,u\circ\theta,\iota)$.
    \end{itemize}
    We shall also write $R_{u,\iota}:\Pi_G\to\Pi_G,\,\tau\mapsto R(\tau,u,\iota)$ for any $u\in V$ and $\iota\in\Sigma$.
title: Glauber dynamic

Let (Omega,tau) be a probability space and phi_1,...,phi_Z real orthonormal functions in L2(tau), with Z finite. Assume that for every fixed real q>=1 there is a finite C(q) such that ||f||_L2q(tau)<=C(q)||f||_L2(tau) for every f in their linear span. Let lambda_1,...,lambda_Z be real numbers and define the finite-rank positive kernel U(theta,theta_prime)=sum_k lambda_k^2 phi_k(theta)phi_k(theta_prime), using these same representatives on its diagonal. Then for every q>=1, ||U||_L2q(tau x tau)<=C(q)^2 ||U||_L2(tau x tau), and ||U(theta,theta)||_Lq(tau)<=C(q)^2 E_tau U(theta,theta). Here ||U||_L2(tau x tau)=(sum_k lambda_k^4)^(1/2), E_tau U(theta,theta)=sum_k lambda_k^2, and all noninteger moments use absolute values. If the assumed C(q) are uniform over a dimension-indexed family, these conclusions are uniform over that family. This is Lemma6, equations78-79, printed p36, of arXiv:2101.10588.

[Lemma lem:finite_set_pointwise_tail_bound of arXiv:2609.01576, '\normalfont Pointwise Majorization for sub-Weibull and Mixed Tail Processes with Applicati'] Suppose that $K\subset T$ is finite and $t_0\in K$. Let
$\cT=(T_n)_{n\ge0}$ be an admissible sequence of nonempty subsets of $K$ such
that $T_0=\cbr{t_0}$ and $T_n=K$ for all sufficiently large $n$. Define the pointwise
chaining cost
\begin{align*}
G_{\cT}(t)
:=
\sum_{n\ge0}2^{n/\alpha}d(t,T_n),
\ t\in K.
\end{align*}
Then, there exists a finite constant $A_\alpha$, depending only on
$\alpha$, such that, for every $u\ge1$, with probability at least
$1-e^{-u}$, simultaneously for every $t\in K$, we have
\begin{align*}
\|Z_t\|
\le
A_\alpha
\left[
G_{\cT}(t)
+u^{1/\alpha}v(t)
\right].
\end{align*}
title: Lemma lem:finite_set_pointwise_tail_bound of arXiv:2609.01576

ATTEMPT RECORD (SUPERSEDING REVISION 2026-09-07 12:4x after the Codex holder's review), author-checked only. CORRECTION of C0004-A001. The sentence 'the naive guess rho^D proportional to r_D(x)^2 fails unless Z^D(D) is a.s. constant' is too strong: if Z^D = xi mu with xi a random scalar and mu deterministic, then Z^D(dx)/Z^D(D) = mu(dx)/mu(D) is deterministic and E[Z^D(dx)/Z^D(D)] = E Z^D(dx)/E Z^D(D) although Z^D(D) is random. The correct statement: since E Z^D(A) = E[M P(A)] with M = Z^D(D) and P(A) = Z^D(A)/Z^D(D), rho^D equals the normalised intensity E Z^D(dx)/E Z^D(D) (when E Z^D(D) is finite) exactly when M is uncorrelated with P(A) for every Borel set A; independence of the mass and the normalised measure is sufficient, not necessary. For the DGFF extremal measure the mass and the shape are coupled through the Gibbs-Markov structure, which suggests that rho^D is not r_D(x)^2 dx normalised, but nothing in A001 or here proves it and the question stands. Key identity: rho^D(A) = E[Z(A)/Z(D)] equals E Z(A)/E Z(D) for every A iff Cov(Z(D), Z(A)/Z(D)) = 0 for every A; independence of the total mass and the normalised measure, and a constant mass, are special cases. Standing obstruction: see the earlier attempt; the correction above replaces the flawed step only.

body:
[Thm Inverse2 of arXiv:2609.01350, 'New classes of trace-form permutation polynomials and their compositional inverses'] Let $q=2^m$ with $m$ odd, and let $f_1$ be as above a permutation
polynomial of $\mathbb F_{q^2}$. By Theorem~(Result1 of the paper), one of the
following holds, and in each case the compositional inverse is:

\begin{equation}
f_1^{-1}(x)=
\begin{cases}
x, & \gamma=0,\\[8pt]
x+\left(\dfrac{h_1(x)}{{\rm Tr}_q^{q^2}(c_2)}\right)^{q/2},
  & \gamma\in\mathbb F_q^{*},\ c_3=1,\ {\rm Tr}_q^{q^2}(c_2)\neq0,\\[12pt]
x+\dfrac{\gamma\,h_1(x)}{1+\gamma{\rm Tr}_q^{q^2}(c_1)},
  & \gamma\in\mathbb F_q^{*},\ c_3=1,\ {\rm Tr}_q^{q^2}(c_2)=0,\\[12pt]
x+\dfrac{\gamma}{A}\Big(B(x)+\big(B(x)^{3}+A^{2}h_1(x)\big)^{1/3}\Big),
  & \begin{array}{@{}l@{}}
      \gamma\notin\mathbb F_q,\ A\neq0,\\[2pt]
      {\rm Tr}_q^{q^2}(\gamma^{2})=(c_3\gamma+\gamma^{q})^{q+1},\\[2pt]
      A\big(1+{\rm Tr}_q^{q^2}(c_1\gamma)\big)={\rm Tr}_q^{q^2}(c_2^{2}\gamma^{4}),
    \end{array}
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
where $A={\rm Tr}_q^{q^2}(c_3\gamma^3+\gamma^{q+2})$,
$B(x)={\rm Tr}_q^{q^2}\big((c_2+c_3x+x^q)\gamma^2\big)$, and $(.)^{1/3}$ denotes
the unique cube root map of $\mathbb F_q$ (a bijection since $m$ is odd).

The last two components have the same sign, so P_t(2,3)>1/3 for sufficiently large t. Label intensities f(1)=1,f(2)=0,f(3)=2. For g=1{f>=1},h=1{f>=2}, covariance at lag t is -(P_t(2,3)-1/3)/3<0. Hence the image process does not satisfy the supermodular time-slowing order, whose infinite-lag limit would require this covariance nonnegative. Check: The eigenvector sums to zero and direct multiplication by the symmetric generator gives eigenvalue -(3-sqrt3). The remaining nonzero mode decays at rate3+sqrt3, so it cannot cancel the eventual positive transition overshoot. The covariance formula uses g=1-1{X=2} and h=1{X=3}. Obstruction: This blocks transferring the established sufficient supermodular-order argument through arbitrary f. It does not produce a queue-workload reversal. In fact same-observable covariance under a reversible environment is a nonnegative mixture of exponentials, so the simplest light-traffic coefficient remains monotone. Higher-order queue effects or a different comparison method are needed.

body:
[Theorem TC of arXiv:2510.12480, 'Cyclic and alternating $U$-statistics'] With notations and assumptions 
as in Section~(Sprel of the paper),
the following holds for the cyclic $U$-statistic{} $U^\circ_n(f)$ in (equation Uc of the paper).
\begin{romenumerate}
\par
 \refstepcounter{thmenumerate}\textup{(\roman{thmenumerate})\enspace} 
We have
\begin{align}
  \operatorname{\mathbb E}{} [U^\circ_n(f)] = n \floor{\tfrac{n}2}\mu
=\tfrac{n^2}{2}\mu +O(n),
\end{align}
and, as \ensuremath{{n\to\infty}}, we have the weak law of large numbers 
\begin{align}
  \frac{2}{n^2} U^\circ_n(f)\overset{\mathrm{p}}{\longrightarrow} \mu.
\end{align}

\par
 \refstepcounter{thmenumerate}\textup{(\roman{thmenumerate})\enspace} 
As \ensuremath{{n\to\infty}},
\begin{align}
n^{-3}\operatorname{Var}[U^\circ_n(f)]\to
  \sigma^2&:=
\tfrac{1}{4}\operatorname{Var}\bigl[f_1(X)+f_2(X)\bigr]
\notag\\&\phantom:
=\tfrac14\bigl(\operatorname{\mathbb E}{} [f_1(X)^2] + \operatorname{\mathbb E}{} [f_2(X)^2] + 2\operatorname{\mathbb E}{} [f_1(X)f_2(X)]\bigr)
\end{align}
and
\begin{align}
  n^{-3/2}\lrpar{U^\circ_n(f)-\tfrac{n^2}{2}\mu} \overset{\mathrm{d}}{\longrightarrow} N(0,\sigma^2),
\end{align}
Furthermore, $\sigma^2>0$ unless $f_1(X)+f_2(X)=0$ a.s.

  \par
 \refstepcounter{thmenumerate}\textup{(\roman{thmenumerate})\enspace} 
If\/ $f_1(X)+f_2(X)=0$ a.s., 
and thus $\sigma^2=0$, 
then
\begin{align}
  \operatorname{Var}[U^\circ_n(f)] = n \floor{\tfrac{n}2}\operatorname{Var} [f_{12}(X_1,X_2)]
=\tfrac{1}{2}n^2\operatorname{Var} [f_{12}(X_1,X_2)] + O(n).
\end{align}
Moreover, there exist
finite or infinite sequences of real numbers $(\lambda^{\mathsf s}_r)_1^{R}$ 
and $(\lambda^{\mathsf a}_q)_1^{{Q_+}}$ 
such that
\begin{align}
n^{-1}\left(U^\circ_n(f)-\operatorname{\mathbb E}{}[U^\circ_n(f)]\right) \overset{\mathrm{d}}{\longrightarrow} 
W:=\sum_{r=1}^R\tfrac12\lambda^{\mathsf s}_r(\zeta_r^2-1)
+\sum_{q=1}^{Q_+}\lambda^{\mathsf a}_q \eta_q
\end{align}
where $(\zeta_r)_1^R$ are  standard normal variables and $(\eta_q)_1^{Q_+}$ 
have the
stochastic area distribution (equation area of the paper), and all are independent.
The coefficients
$(\lambda^{\mathsf s}_r)_1^R$ in (equation tc2 of the paper) are the nonzero eigenvalues (with
multiplicities) 
of the self-adjoint 
integral operator $T_{{f_{12\mathsf s}}}$ 
on $L^2({\mathcal X},\nu)$,
where, recalling (equation fsa of the paper),
${f_{12\mathsf s}}:=(f_{12}+f^*_{12})/2$ is the symmetric part of $f_{12}$.
Similarly,
the coefficients $(\lambda^{\mathsf a}_q)_1^{Q_+}$ 
are the positive numbers such that the imaginary
number $\mathrm{i}\lambda^{\mathsf a}_q$ is an eigenvalue of the 
anti-self-adjoint operator $T_{f_{12\mathsf a}}$ on $L^2_{\mathbb C}({\mathcal X},\nu)$,
where ${f_{12\mathsf a}}:=(f_{12}-f^*_{12})/2$ is the antisymmetric part of $f_{12}$.
We have
\begin{align}
  \sum_{r=1}^R(\lambda^{\mathsf s}_r)^2&=\operatorname{Var}[{f_{12\mathsf s}}(X_1,X_2)],
\\
  \sum_{q=1}^{Q_+}(\lambda^{\mathsf a}_q)^2&=\tfrac12\operatorname{Var}[{f_{12\mathsf a}}(X_1,X_2)],
\end{align}
and                    
\begin{align}
\operatorname{Var} W&
=\tfrac12 \sum_{r=1}^R(\lambda^{\mathsf s}_r)^2+  \sum_{q=1}^{Q_+}(\lambda^{\mathsf a}_q)^2
=\tfrac12\operatorname{Var}[f_{12}(X_1,X_2)].
\end{align}

\end{romenumerate}

[Thm 8 (The Hausdorff--Young Inequality on $a+h\mathbb{Z}$) of arXiv:2608.16144, 'Central limit theorem in R\'enyi divergence for lattice random variables'] Suppose $1\le p\le 2$ and $1/p+1/q=1.$ If $f\in \ell^p(a+h\mathbb{Z})$, then 
$$
\widehat f\in L^q\left(\left[-\frac{\pi}{h},\frac{\pi}{h}\right),\frac{h}{2\pi}\,dt\right),
$$ 
and moreover
\begin{equation*}
\left(\frac{h}{2\pi}\int_{-\pi/h}^{\pi/h}|\widehat f(t)|^q\,dt\right)^{1/q}\leq\left(\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}} |f(a+kh)|^p\right)^{1/p}.
\end{equation*}

[Theorem 5 (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck limit) of arXiv:2607.23640, '{\sl Non-equilibrium fluctuations of a two-species exclusion process with slow boundary }'] Assume that the sequence of initial fluctuation fields $ \left\{\bm Y_0^n\right\}_{n\in \mathbb{N}} $
 	converges, as \(n\to\infty\), to a mean-zero Gaussian field \(\bm Y_0\) on
 	\( (\mathscr S^\dagger)'\), whose covariance is given by
 	\[
 	\lim_{n\to\infty}
 	\mathbb E_{\mu^n}^n
 	\left[
 	\bm Y_0^n(\bm f)\bm Y_0^n(\bm g)
 	\right]
 	=
 	\mathbb E
 	\left[
 	\bm Y_0(\bm f)\bm Y_0(\bm g)
 	\right]
 	=:
 	\sigma(\bm f,\bm g),
 	\qquad
 	\bm f,\bm g\in\mathscr S^\dagger.
 	\]
 	Then the sequence \(\{\mathbb Q_n\}_{n \in \mathbb{N} }\) converges in
 	\(\mathcal D([0,T],(\mathscr S^\dagger)')\) to the generalized Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process \(\{\bm Y_t:0\le t\le T\}\) characterized by the
 	martingale problem
 	\[
 	\mathcal M_t(\bm f)
 	=
 	\bm Y_t(\bm f)-\bm Y_0(\bm f)
 	-
 	\int_0^t
 	\bm Y_s(\mathcal A^\dagger \bm f) \,\mathrm ds,
 	\qquad
 	\bm f\in\mathscr S^\dagger,
 	\]
 	where \(\mathcal M_t(\bm f)\) is a continuous centered Gaussian martingale with
 	quadratic covariation
 	\[
 	\left\langle
 	\mathcal M(\bm f),\mathcal M(\bm g)
 	\right\rangle_t
 	=
 	\int_0^t
 	Q_s(\bm f,\bm g) \,\mathrm ds.
 	\] 	
 	Equivalently, for every \(0\le s\le t\le T\) and every
 	\(\bm f,\bm g\in\mathscr S^\dagger\),
 	\[
 	\mathbb E\left[
 	\bm Y_t(\bm f)\bm Y_s(\bm g)
 	\right]
 	=
 	\sigma(S_t\bm f,S_s\bm g)
 	+
 	\int_0^s
 	Q_r\left(
 	S_{t-r}\bm f,
 	S_{s-r}\bm g
 	\right) \,\mathrm dr.
 	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Compare with known dimensions of LQG geodesics and of the LQG metric ball boundary. Result: If the continuum path were an LQG geodesic its Euclidean Hausdorff dimension would be that of LQG geodesics, which is strictly greater than 1 and below 2 and only known within bounds for general gamma; the energy support, if concentrated on a fractal set, would have dimension between the geodesic dimension and 2. I could not do better than these bounds because the object (C0015) is not constructed. A rigorous discrete statement is available: the discrete energy of the minimising current between opposite sides of [0,N]^2 is bounded above and below by constants times the effective conductance, whose growth exponent is the same as that of the resistance in C0014, so the energy is not carried by a set of full dimension 2 whenever the resistance exponent is non-trivial. Obstruction: Continuum object not defined; only the discrete energy scaling is accessible.

It follows that all moments converge to the moments of the exponential law of parameter $1$. 

In particular,  $$
\lim_{K\to\infty}\frac{ {\mathds E}^{(K)}_{\nu_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}}(T^{({\scriptscriptstyle K})}_{A}) }{ M_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}(A)\, \eta_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}(A) }=1\;,
$$
and
$$
\lim_{K\to\infty}{{\mathds P}}^{({\scriptscriptstyle K})}_{\nu_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}}\big(T^{({\scriptscriptstyle K})}_{A}>t\,  {\mathds E}^{(K)}_{\nu_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}}(T^{({\scriptscriptstyle K})}_{A}) \big)=e^{-t}\;.

body:
[Lemma 2 (Canonical solvability of the metric Hodge system) of arXiv:2609.01093, 'Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold'] Let $X:\Real_y^n\to\Real_x^n$ be an orientation-preserving global
bi-Lipschitz map with $d\mu=J dy$.  Fix $1<p<n$ and put
\[
 p^*:=\frac{np}{n-p}.
\]
For every $q\in L^p(\mu)$ there is a unique vector field $F=F^i\eframe_i$ along $X$, whose Cartesian components belong to
$L^{p^*}(\mu;\Rn)$, satisfying \eqref{eq:invdiv} in the conjugated
distributional sense: equivalently, $u:=F\circ X^{-1}$ satisfies
\[
 \partial_{x^i}u^j-\partial_{x^j}u^i=0,
 \qquad
 \partial_{x^i}u^i=q\circ X^{-1}
 \quad\text{in }\mathcal D'(\Real_x^n).
\]
The solution is
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal P_{\gmetric}q
 :=\mathcal C_X\nabla\Delta_x^{-1}\mathcal C_X^{-1}q, \qquad \mathcal{C}_Xf=f\circ X,
\end{equation}
and it satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \|\mathcal P_{\gmetric}q\|_{L^{p^*}(\mu)}
 \le C_{n,p}\|q\|_{L^p(\mu)}.
\end{equation}
In particular, for
\begin{equation}
    r_{\mathrm{HLS}}:=\frac{4n}{n+4},
\end{equation}
one has $1<r_{\mathrm{HLS}}<n$ for every $n\ge2$ and $r_{\mathrm{HLS}}^*=4$; hence
every $q\in L^{r_{\mathrm{HLS}}}(\mu)$ has a unique solution
$\mathcal P_{\gmetric}q\in L^4(\mu)$ which we refer to as the canonical Hodge vector field along $X$.

[Defi 2 (\Adam\ optimizer) of arXiv:2606.21433, 'Central limit theorem for\\ the averaged Adam optimizer'] Consider
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item an innovation $ ( X, U ) $,
\item $ \alpha, \beta \in [0,1) $, $ \epsilon \in (0,\infty) $ with $ \alpha < \sqrt \beta $ (the \emph{damping factors}),
\item $ n_0 \in \N_0 $, $ \theta_{ n_0 }, m_{ n_0 } \in \R^d $, $ v_{ n_0 } \in [0,\infty)^d $ (the initialisation), and
\item a decreasing $(0,\infty)$-valued sequence $ ( \gamma_n )_{ n \in \N } $ (\emph{sequence of step-sizes}).
\end{enumerate}

An $\R^{d}$-valued stochastic process  $(\theta_{n})_{n\in\N_0\cap[n_{0},\infty)}$ is called \emph{\Adam\ algorithm with damping parameter $(\alpha,\beta,\epsilon)$ and step-sizes $(\gamma_{n})$ started at time $n_{0}$ in $(\theta_{0},m_{n_{0}},v_{n_{0}})$} if and only if
for every $ n \in \N \cap ( n_0, \infty) $, $ i \in \{ 1, \dots, d \} $ it holds that
\begin{equation}
  \thetai_n = \thetai_{ n - 1 } + \gamma_n \, \sigmai_n \, m^{(i)}_n,
\end{equation}
where for all $ n \in \N \cap ( n_0, \infty) $, $ i \in \{ 1, \dots, d \} $ we have
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item  $m_n=\alpha \,m_{n-1}+(1-\alpha) \,X(\theta_{n-1}, U_n)$,
\item  $v^{(i)}_n= \beta \,v^{(i)}_{n-1} +(1-\beta) \,(X^{(i)}(\theta_{n-1},U_n))^{2}$, and
\item  $\displaystyle \sigma^{(i)}_n= \bigl[ \epsilon + ( v_n^{(i)}/(1-\beta^{n}) )^{ 1 / 2 } \bigr]^{ - 1 } $
\end{enumerate}
and where $ ( U_n )_{ n \in \N \cap( n_0, \infty ) } $ is a family of independent copies of $ U $.
We call the sequence $(t_{n})_{n\in\N_{0}}$ given by
$
  t_n = \sum_{ k = 1 }^n \gamma_k
$
the \emph{training times} of the \Adam\ algorithm.
title: \Adam\ optimizer

\begin{equation}
S_{n,u}^{k,\epsilon}(f_k;\delta):=\sup_{j \in J_{k,l}}\left[ \mathbf{1}_{\{ |J_{k,l}||{\mathbf R}^{k,\epsilon}_n(u;j)| > \delta \sqrt{n}\}}\left| \int f_k \, {\rm d}  \mathcal O^{k,\epsilon}_{n,u}[j] - \int f_k \,{\rm d} \big( \widehat{\Theta}^{k,\epsilon}_{n,u}[j] \otimes {\rm O}^{k,\epsilon}_u\big) \right| \right]\overset{\mathbb{P}}{\longrightarrow} 0

[Definition 29 (Competitor) of arXiv:2603.27940, '\Large \bf Stability of supermartingale optimal transport problems'] Let $\pi$ be a finite measure on $\R^2$ with finite first moment, and let $\pi_1$ be its first marginal.
Fix a disintegration $\pi=\pi_1\times\kappa_x$.
Let $M_0,M_1\subset\R$ be Borel.
A measure $\pi'$ is an \emph{$(M_0,M_1)$-competitor} of $\pi$ if it has the same marginals as $\pi$ and if,
writing $\pi'=\pi_1\times\kappa'_x$, one has
\[
\int_\R y\,\kappa'_x(dy)\le \int_\R y\,\kappa_x(dy)\quad\text{for }\pi_1\text{-a.e.\ }x\in M_0,
\qquad
\int_\R y\,\kappa'_x(dy)= \int_\R y\,\kappa_x(dy)\quad\text{for }\pi_1\text{-a.e.\ }x\in M_1.
\]
title: Competitor

[Proposition prop:combined-persistency of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] Let $\mathfrak{F} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset)$ be an f-frame.
  $\mathfrak{F} \in \FrameClass{\Box\text{-p}} \cap \FrameClass{\Diamond\text{-p}}$ iff $\Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M}$ is persistent for every $\mathfrak{M}$ based on $\mathfrak{F}$.
  \begin{proof}
    ($\Rightarrow$)
    Take any $\mathfrak{M} = (\mathfrak{F}, V)$ and $\varphi \in \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$,
    then we use an induction on the construction of $\varphi$.
    We shall only consider the cases with modal operators.
    The case when $\varphi = \Box \psi$ is proven similarly to Proposition (prop:extrinsic-persistency of the paper) (1 $\Rightarrow$),
    and the case when $\varphi = \Diamond \psi$ is proven similarly to Proposition (prop:extrinsic-persistency of the paper) (2 $\Rightarrow$).

    ($\Leftarrow$)
    For any $\mathfrak{M} = (\mathfrak{F}, V)$,
    $\Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M}$ is persistent by the assumption,

[Lemma 30 of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] Let \(A\) be a trace-class operator. For \(|\theta|\) sufficiently small, define
\[
        H_A(\theta):=\log\det\left(\operatorname{Id}+(e^\theta-1)A\right),
\]
where the logarithm is the holomorphic branch near \(0\) normalized by
\(H_A(0)=0\). Then, for every integer \(n\ge1\),
\begin{equation}

        H_A^{(n)}(0)
        =
        \sum_{m=1}^n
        (-1)^{m+1}(m-1)!S(n,m)\operatorname{tr}(A^m),
\end{equation}
where \(S(n,m)\) is the Stirling number of the second kind. Consequently,
\begin{equation}

        F_{a,L}^{(n)}(0)
        =
        \sum_{m=1}^n
        (-1)^{m+1}(m-1)!S(n,m)
        \left(
        \operatorname{tr}(T_{a,L}^m)-\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde W_{a,L}^m)
        \right).
\end{equation}

[Theorem eq:cross-moment-decomposition of arXiv:2608.23860, 'Revelation Control'] Assume square integrability, a shared conditional mean across banks, and $c_{\mathscr X}\ge0$ almost surely.  Then
\begin{align}
M_\times(f)
&=
\mathbb E[(\mu-f)^2]+\mathbb E[c_{\mathscr X}] \\
&=
\mathbb E[(m_{\mathscr H}-f)^2]
+
\mathbb E[\operatorname{Var}(\mu\mid\mathscr H)]
+
\mathbb E[c_{\mathscr X}],

\end{align}
and therefore
\begin{equation}
\boxed{
V_B(\mathscr H)-\mathcal V(\pi_f)
\le
\sqrt{M_\times(f)}.
}

\end{equation}
Consequently, for any policy $\pi_G$ measurable with respect to a refinement $\mathscr G\supseteq\mathscr H$,
\begin{equation}
\mathcal V(\pi_G)-V_B(\mathscr H)
\ge
\bigl\{\mathcal V(\pi_G)-\mathcal V(\pi_f)\bigr\}
-
\sqrt{M_\times(f)}.

\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Replicate-denoised Bayes-regret bridge

[Theorem thm:dbm-conv of arXiv:2411.10829, 'Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble and its Laplace transform'] For fixed $\beta>0$, let $\{Y_i(\tau)\}_{1\le i\le N, \tau>0}$ be the $N$ dimensional DBM of (Definition_DBM of the paper) started from zero initial condition.
As $N\to\infty$, the process
\[
(\boldsymbol{\tau}, i)\mapsto 2N^{2/3} \left( \frac{Y_i(2N/\beta + 2\boldsymbol{\tau} N^{2/3}/\beta)}{2\sqrt{(N + \boldsymbol{\tau} N^{2/3})N} }-1 \right)
\]
converges to the Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble in distribution in the topology of uniform convergence over compact subsets of $\mathbb R$ for $\boldsymbol{\tau}$--variable and jointly in finitely many $i$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition of arXiv:2602.04303, '\Large\textbf{Strong solutions to SDEs with singular drifts driven by fractional Brownian '] Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P},(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t\in[0,T]})$ be a complete filtered probability space and $B^H$ be a $\mathcal{F}_t$-fractional Brownian motion.
			\begin{itemize}
				\item Weak solution: We say that the triple $(X,B^H)$ is a weak solution to (equation sec1-eq.1 of the paper) if $X$ solves (equation sec1-eq.1 of the paper) and is $\mathcal{F}_t$-adapted.
				\item Strong solution: A weak solution $(X,B^H)$ such that $X$ is $\mathcal{F}^{B^H}$-adapted is called a strong solution, where $(\mathcal{F}^{B^H})_{t\in[0,T]}$ is a filtration generated by $B^H$.
				\item Pathwise uniqueness: We say that pathwise
				uniqueness holds if for any two solutions $(X,B^H)$ and $(Y,B^H)$ defined on the same
				filtered probability space with the same fBm $B^H$ and the same initial condition $X_0\in\mathbb{R}^d$, $X$ and $Y$ are indistinguishable, i.e. $\mathbb{P}(X_t=Y_t,\forall\;t\in[0,T])=1$.
			\end{itemize}

[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2606.25494, 'A functional central limit theorem for kernel gradient flow and infinitesimal gradient boo'] Assume that $\P_n$, $n\ge 1$, and $\P$ are deterministic elements of $\ell^\infty(\mathcal{G})$ such that the convergence
\begin{equation}
G_n[\varphi]=\sqrt{n}\,(\P_n[\varphi]-\P[\varphi]) \longrightarrow G[\varphi],
\qquad \varphi\in\mathcal{G},
\end{equation}
holds in $\ell^\infty(\mathcal{G})$ as $n\to\infty$. Then there exist functions
\[
\Gamma_i=\Gamma_i(\bar\xi,v,F,\P)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\Gamma_i'=\Gamma_i'(\bar\xi,v,F,\P),
\qquad i\in\mathcal{I},
\]
uniformly bounded for $\|F\|_{\mathcal{H}}\leq M$, such that
\begin{align*}
\sqrt{n}\big(\Psi(\bar\xi,v,F,\P_n)-\Psi(\bar\xi,v,F,\P)\big)
=
\sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}}
\left(
\frac{\Gamma_i\,G[\varphi_{A_i^{\bar\xi}}]+\Gamma_i'\,G[\varphi_{A_i^{\bar\xi},F}]}{\P(A_i^{\bar\xi})}
+\frac{o(1)}{\P(A_i^{\bar\xi})}
\right),
\end{align*}
where we use the notation
\[
\varphi_A(x,y)=\1_A(x)\quad \text{and}\quad \varphi_{A,F}(x,y)=\partial_1\ell(F(x),y)\1_A(x).
\]
Furthermore, given a sequence $\varepsilon_n\to 0$ such that $\sqrt{n}\varepsilon_n\to+\infty$, the $o(1)$ terms are uniform for $\|F\|_{\mathcal{H}}\leq M$ and $\bar\xi$ such that $\min_{i\in\mathcal{I}} \P(A_i^{\bar\xi})\ge \varepsilon_n$.

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2606.06231, 'Sensitivity of SDE Solutions to Perturbations of the Diffusion and Drift'] In addition to Assumptions \ref{assump:main_assumptions_1}, \ref{assump:PDE}, \ref{assump:main_assumptions_2}, and \ref{assump:sigma_invert},  assume the following:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $T>0$, $u_T(t,x)$ be a $C^{1,2}$ solution to \eqref{eq:Feynman_Kac_pde_intro}, and $v_T(t,x)$ be a $C^{1,2}$ solution to \eqref{eq:Feynman_Kac_pde_intro} but with $F$ replaced by $G$ and $\sigma$ replaced by $\eta$. 
\item   Suppose $u_T(t,x)$ and $v_T(t,x)$ are both polynomially-bounded in $x$, uniformly in $t\in[0,T]$.
\item   Suppose $f$ is $\sigma_f$-sub-Gaussian with respect to $\mu_X^*$.
\item Suppose that for all $t\in[0,T]$, $h_t$ is $\sigma_{h_t}$-sub-Gaussian with respect to $\mu_{X}^*$ for some $\sigma_{h_t}\in(0,\infty)$ and $\sigma_{h_t}\in L^2([0,T],dt)$.
\end{enumerate}

Then for all $t\in[0,T]$  we have
 \begin{align}
&\|v_T(t,\cdot)-u_T(t,\cdot)\|_{L^1(\mu_X^*)}\\
\leq& (  (T-t) L_h + L_f)\frac{(1+1/\epsilon)^{1/2}\|\sigma-\eta\|_{F,\infty}}{K_{\kappa,\epsilon}^{1/2}}+2 \left(\sigma_f^2   + C_* \int_0^{T-t}\sigma^2_{h_{t+r}} dr\right)^{1/2}\notag \\
&\qquad\times\left(\int_t^{T} \int\mathbb{E}\left[ \left\|\sigma^{-1}(\tilde{X}^{t,x}_{s})\left(F(\tilde{X}^{t,x}_{s})-G(s,\tilde{X}^{t,x}_{s})+\kappa(\tilde{X}^{t,x}_{s}-Y^{t,x}_{s})\right)\right\|^2\right]\mu_X^*(dx) \,ds\right)^{1/2}\notag.
\end{align}
 

If, in addition, $F-G$ and $\sigma_{h_t}$ are bounded then
\begin{align}
&\|v_T(t,\cdot)-u_T(t,\cdot)\|_{L^1(\mu_X^*)}\leq (  (T-t) L_h + L_f)\frac{(1+1/\epsilon)^{1/2}\|\sigma-\eta\|_{F,\infty}}{K_{\kappa,\epsilon}^{1/2}}\\
&+2\sqrt{2}  \|\sigma^{-1}\|_{2,\infty} (T-t)^{1/2} \left(C_*(T-t) (\sup_s\sigma_{h_{s}})^2+\sigma_f^2   \right)^{1/2}\notag \\
&\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\times\left(\|F-G\|_\infty^2+\kappa^2    \frac{(1+1/\epsilon)\|\sigma-\eta\|_{F,\infty}^2}{K_{\kappa,\epsilon}}  \right)^{1/2}\notag\\
=&O(\|F-G\|_\infty+\|\sigma-\eta\|_{F,\infty})\,.\notag
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 24 (Oliveira coalescence--hitting comparisons) of arXiv:2607.13183, '2607.13183'] Let $(X_t)_{t\ge0}$ be a finite irreducible reversible continuous-time chain with
generator $\mathcal L=P-I$, where $P$ is a reversible transition kernel. Let
\[
        t_{\rm hit}^{\rm ct}:=\max_{x,y}\E_x\tau_y .
\]
For the standard continuous-time coalescing process driven by this chain, write
$C_k^{\rm coal}$ for the first time at which at most $k$ particles remain,
started from an arbitrary finite initial configuration. There is a universal
constant $C_{\rm Oli}<\infty$ such that, for all $k\ge1$,
\begin{equation}
        \E C_k^{\rm coal}
        \le C_{\rm Oli}\left(\frac{t_{\rm hit}^{\rm ct}}{k}+\tmix\right).
\end{equation}
In particular, for the process started with one particle at every state,
\begin{equation}
        \E\coal\le C_{\rm Oli}\,t_{\rm hit}^{\rm ct}.
\end{equation}

body:
[Thm of arXiv:2412.05746, 'Hyperbolicity, slimness, and minsize, on average'] Given a geodesic metric space $(X,d)$,
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item if it is $\delta$-hyperbolic, then it is $3\delta$-slim~[alonso1991notes].
        \item if it is $\delta$-thin, then it is $\delta$-hyperbolic~[bridson2013metric].
        \item if it is $\delta$-slim, then it is $4\delta$-thin~[ghys1990espaces]. The bound is tight. 
        \item if it is $\delta$-slim, then it is $2\delta$-hyperbolic~[soto2011quelques]. The bound is asymptotically tight.
        \item if every geodesic triangle has minsize at most $\delta$, then it has insize at most $3\delta$ as well~[ghys1990espaces]. We note that the original reference uses $4\delta$, but we can easily improve the bound.
        \item if every geodesic triangle has insize at most $\delta$, then it is $2\delta$-thin~[ghys1990espaces].
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: For a positive finite Borel measure mu on R, its STIELTJES TRANSFORM (also Cauchy transform) is m_mu(z) = integral (x - z)^{-1} mu(dx) for z in the open upper half plane C^+. It is analytic on C^+, maps C^+ into C^+ when mu is positive, and satisfies the a priori bound |m_mu(z)| <= mu(R)/Im(z). INVERSION: for a < b continuity points of mu, mu( (a,b) ) = (1/pi) lim_{eta decreasing to 0} integral_a^b Im m_mu(x + i eta) dx, so the transform determines the measure. CONTINUITY: a sequence of probability measures mu_n converges weakly to a probability measure mu if and only if m_{mu_n}(z) -> m_mu(z) for every z in C^+; convergence on any set with an accumulation point in C^+ suffices, by analyticity plus a tightness argument. In random matrix theory the transform of the empirical spectral distribution of a Hermitian matrix H is m_n(z) = (1/n) tr ( H - z I )^{-1}, the normalised trace of the RESOLVENT, which is why resolvent methods and Stieltjes-transform methods are the same method. Sign conventions differ across the literature: some authors define the transform with (z - x)^{-1}, which flips the sign of the whole calculus; the convention must be checked before importing a formula. [standard; e.g. Anderson, Guionnet and Zeitouni, An Introduction to Random Matrices, Section 2.4]

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2606.16487, 'Logarithmic Large Deviations for Heavy-Tailed Sums'] In the setup above, the following large-deviation bounds hold on $E_\alpha$,
with speed $\log n$ and rate function $I(y)=\alpha\log y$.

\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)]
For every open set $G\subset E_\alpha$,
$$
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\frac{1}{\log n}\log\mathbb{P}(Y_n\in G)
\ge
-\inf_{y\in G}\alpha\log y.
$$

\item[(ii)]
For every set $F\subset E_\alpha$ that is closed in $\R$,
$$
\limsup_{n\to\infty}
\frac{1}{\log n}\log\mathbb{P}(Y_n\in F)
\le
-\inf_{y\in F}\alpha\log y.
$$
\end{itemize}
Moreover, for every $x>c_\alpha$ one has
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}
\frac{1}{\log n}
\log\mathbb{P}(S_n\ge a_n n^x)
=
-\alpha x.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2606.09691, '\textsc{Degenerate Diffusions on Continuum Percolation and Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Equatio'] Let $(B,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a probability space and let $L$ be the generator of a symmetric Markov process $(X_t)_{t\geq0}$ taking values in $B$, with invariant probability measure $\mu$. Let $P_x$ denote the law of $(X_t)_{t\geq0}$ starting from $x\in B$ and let
\[
P_\mu(\cdot):=\int_B P_x(\cdot)\,\mu(\d x).
\]
For a function $f$ in the domain of $L$, define the Dirichlet energy by
\[
\mathcal E(f,f):=-\int_B (Lf)(x)f(x)\,\mu(\d x).
\]
Then, for every $T>0$ and $\ell>0$,
\begin{equation}
P_\mu\bigg[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}|f(X_t)|\geq \ell\bigg]
\leq
\frac{\e}{\ell}
\sqrt{\|f\|_{L^2(\mu)}^2+T\,\mathcal E(f,f)}.
\end{equation}

body:
[Theorem 1 (Uniform high order factorial bound) of arXiv:2608.04799, '2608.04799'] Fix \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\), let \(p_n\) be given by
\eqref{eq:pn-intro}, and let \(\Xi_n\) be given by \eqref{eq:Xi-intro}.
For every compact \(K\Subset E\), there are constants
\(C_K,c_K>0\), depending only on \(K\) and \(\lambda\), such that
\begin{equation}
  \mathbb E[(\Xi_n(K))_q]
  \le C_K^q e^{-c_Kq^3},
  \qquad q\ge1,
\end{equation}
uniformly in every \(n\ge n_\lambda\).
Moreover, if \(|\lambda|\le L<\infty\), then \(n_L\) can be chosen so that
for every compact \(K\Subset E\) there are \(C_K,c_K>0\), depending only on
\(K\) and \(L\), for which \eqref{eq:main-uniform-bound} holds uniformly in
all \(n\ge n_L\) and all \(|\lambda|\le L\), with \(p_n\) and \(\Xi_n\)
carrying the parameter \(\lambda\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Uniform high order factorial bound

[Lemma 5 of arXiv:2606.22656, 'Fluctuations of Point Vortex Ensembles\\ at Small Negative Inverse Temperature'] Fix $\beta_*<8\pi$.  There exists $C_{\beta_*}<\infty$ such that, for
all $\beta\leq \beta_*$, all $N\ge2$, and all $2\leq n\leq N$,
\begin{equation}
    B_{N,n}
    :=
    \binom Nn
    \sum_{\Gamma\in\ipi(n)}|A_N(\Gamma)|
    \leq 
    Cn^{-1/2}\rho^n,
    \qquad
    \rho:=C_{\beta_*}\beta.
\end{equation}
As a consequence, denoting by $\K_N$ the complete graph with $N$ vertices, if $\rho<1$,
\begin{equation}
    \sup_{N\ge2} \sum_{\Gamma\subseteq \K_N}|A_N(\Gamma)|
    \leq \exp\pa{C\sum_{n\ge2}n^{-1/2}\rho^n}<\infty.
\end{equation}

[Corollary Coro:Martingale_inequality of arXiv:2604.07497, 'The Three-Dimensional Stochastic EMHD System: Local Well-Posedness and Maximal Pathwise So'] Let $\epsilon, \kappa > 0$, if $M_t$ is a continuous local martingale as in (equation Thm:Burkholder-Davis-Gundy Inequality_1 of the paper), then we have that 
\[
{\mathbb P} \Bigl( \sup_{t\in [0,T]} |M_t| \geq \epsilon \Bigr) \leq \frac{C}{\epsilon} {\mathbb E} \Bigl( \Bigl( \int_0^T |\sigma_t|^2 dt \Bigr)^{\frac{1}{2}} \wedge \kappa \Bigr) + {\mathbb P} \Bigl( \Bigl ( \int_0^T |\sigma_t|^2 dt \Bigr)^{\frac{1}{2}} > \kappa \Bigr),
\]
for some positive constant $C$.

body:
[Cor 31 of arXiv:2507.00346, 'The strong convergence phenomenon'] We have
$$
	\mu_0(\boldsymbol{w}) =
	\lim_{N\to\infty} 
	\mathbf{E}\big[\ntr U_{w_1}^N\cdots U_{w_q}^N|_{1^\perp}\big]
	= 1_{g_{w_1}\cdots g_{w_q}=e}.
$$
Moreover, if $g_{w_1}\cdots g_{w_q}=v^k$ for a non-power $v$, then  
$$
	\mu_1(\boldsymbol{w}) =
	\lim_{N\to\infty} N\,
	\mathbf{E}\big[\ntr U_{w_1}^N\cdots U_{w_q}^N|_{1^\perp}\big]
	= \omega(k)-1,
$$
where $\omega(k)$ denotes the number of divisors of $k$.

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2603.00353, 'Aldous-type Spectral Gaps in Unitary Groups'] Let $n\ge2$ and consider the hypergraph $\Gamma=([n],w)$ where $w_B=c_{|B|}$ and $c_\ell\ge0$ for $\ell=0,\ldots,n$. 
Then\footnote{We use the convention that $\binom{a}{b}=0$ when $b<0$ or $a<b$.}
\begin{equation} 
    \min_{\triv\ne\rho\in\irr(\U(n))} \lambda_{\min}(\Gamma,\rho) = \lambda_{\min}(\Gamma,\rho_{(2,0,
    \ldots,0,-2)}) = 
    \sum_{\ell=0}^n c_\ell \frac{n+1}{\ell+1}\binom{n-2}{\ell-2}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Thr thrLineCorrelations of arXiv:2607.29423, 'Schwarzian Field Theory at High Temperatures'] For $N\geq 0$ let $\big\{\obs{f}{s_{j}}{t_j}_0\big\}_{j=1}^{N}$ be a set of non-interlaced observables, and $\{l_j\}_{j=1}^N$ be a set of positive integers. 
Let also $\{k_m\}_{m=0}^{N}$ and $\{\tau_m\}_{m=0}^{N}$ be as above.
Then 
\begin{multline}
\int\limits_{C^1_{0,+}(\mathbb{R})} \prod_{j=1}^N \obs{f}{s_j}{t_j}^{l_j}_0\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\mathscr{M}_{\varkappa^2}^{\infty}(f)
=
\int_{\mathbb{R}_+^{N}} 
\prod_{j=1}^N \frac{\Gamma\Big(\frac{l_j}{2}\pm i w_1(j) \pm i w_2(j)\Big) }{2 \pi^2\, \Gamma(l_j)} \cdot \left(\frac{\varkappa^2}{2}\right)^{l_j}\\
\times
\left.
\prod_{m=1}^{N}\exp\left(-\frac{\tau_m \varkappa^2}{2}\cdot k_m^2\right)  \sinh(2\pi k_m)\, 2 k_m \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} k_m\right|_{k_0 = 0},
\end{multline}
where the integral on the right-hand side converges absolutely.

[Definition Def_Slice of arXiv:2609.02848, 'The universal moduli space of non-degenerate $\Z/2\Z$~harmonic spinors'] A set of \defined{normal data} for a codimension two submanifold $Z_0 \subseteq X$ consists of:
  \begin{enumerate}[label=\rm{(N\arabic*)},ref=N\arabic*]
  \item
    a rank $2$ subbundle $N \subseteq TX|_{Z_0}$,
  \item
    a Euclidean metric $h$ on $N$, and
  \item
    
    an $I \in \Gamma\paren{Z_0,\Hom\paren{\Lambda^2N,\End(S|_{Z_0})}}$ such that
    $I(\mathrm{or}) \in \End(S_x)$ is an orthogonal complex structure
    for every $x \in Z_0$ and $\mathrm{or} \in \Lambda^2N_x$ with $\abs{\mathrm{or}} = 1$.
  \end{enumerate}
  
  Every ${\mathbf{p}} = (g;\gamma,\nabla) \in \mathbf{Dir}$ defines normal data for a codimension two submanifold $Z \subseteq X$ by declaring
  \begin{equation*}
    N \coloneq TZ^\perp, \quad
    h \coloneq g|_N, \quad\text{and}\quad
    I \coloneq \gamma|_{\Lambda^2 N}.
  \end{equation*}
  
  The \defined{slice} associated with a ramified Euclidean line bundle $(Z_0,[{\mathfrak l}_0]) \in \mathbf{Ram}$ and normal data $(N,h,I)$ for $Z_0$ is the tame Fréchet submanifold
  \begin{equation*}
    \mathbf{Sl}
    \coloneq
    \set[\big]{
      ({\mathbf{p}},[{\mathfrak l}_0]) \in \mathbf{Dir} \times \mathbf{Ram}
      :
      {\mathbf{p}} ~\text{induces the normal data}~ (N,h,I) ~\text{for}~ Z_0
    }
    \subseteq
    \mathbf{Dir} \times \mathbf{Ram}.
  \end{equation*}
  These slices foliate $\mathbf{Dir} \times \mathbf{Ram}$ in the sense that every $({\mathbf{p}},[{\mathfrak l}]) \in \mathbf{Dir} \times \mathbf{Ram}$ is contained in some slice.

		\[
			K_r\coloneqq \{y\in\mathbb{Z}^d: |y-z|\leq r\text{ for some }z\in K\}\, .

			\leq 2|K|\exp\{-c\min(a^2r^{d-4}, ar^{d-2})\}\, .
		\]

[Definition of arXiv:2605.03718, 'Potential Hessian Ascent III:\\ Sampling the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick Model at $\beta < 1/'] The Bregman divergence of $\psi:Q\to \mathbb R$ is $D_\psi:Q\times Q\to \mathbb R$ defined as 
\[
D_\psi (x,y) = \psi(x) - \psi(y) - \ip{\nabla \psi(y)}{x-y}.
\]
    We say that $F:Q\to \mathbb R$ is $c$-strongly convex with respect to $D_\psi$ if for all $x,y\in Q$,
\[
F(x) \geqslant F(y) + \ip{\nabla F(y)}{x-y} + cD_\psi(x,y).
\]
We say that $F:Q\to \mathbb R$ is $C$-smooth with respect to $D_\psi$ if for all $x,y\in Q$.
\[
F(x) \leqslant F(y) + \ip{\nabla F(y)}{x-y} + CD_\psi(x,y).
\]

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Limit constant for common random two-dimensional partial orders structural calculation Result: Partition each square into m-by-m cells, m=floor(n^(1/3)). Keep a label when its two points occupy the same cell, and retain it only if no other kept label shares that row or column. The retained labels have identical comparisons in both posets. For a fixed label the match probability is1/m^2; conditional on its cell, another label is a conflicting match with probability(2m-1)/m^4. Therefore the expected retained number is n/m^2*[1-(2m-1)/m^4]^(n-1), asymptotic to exp(-2)*n^(1/3). Check: Two retained labels have distinct row and column indices, so each of their coordinate orderings is determined by cell indices in both independent samples. Independence over labels gives the exact no-conflict probability. The bound is liminf E C_n/n^(1/3)>=exp(-2). Obstruction: The isolated-cell matching discards many usable labels and supplies no matching upper constant. Optimizing a local grid construction does not establish existence of the global optimal limit.

body: For jointly distributed discrete random variables X and Y with joint pmf p(x,y) and marginal pmfs p(x), p(y), the mutual information is I(X;Y) = sum_{x,y} p(x,y) * log( p(x,y) / (p(x)*p(y)) ). Equivalently, I(X;Y) = H(X) - H(X|Y) = H(Y) - H(Y|X) = H(X) + H(Y) - H(X,Y) = D( P_{X,Y} || P_X times P_Y ), the KL divergence between the joint distribution and the product of the marginals. I(X;Y) >= 0 always, by nonnegativity of KL divergence, with equality if and only if X and Y are independent.
title: Mutual Information

[Corollary 13 (Posterior thresholds) of arXiv:2607.20373, 'Embedding martingale diffusions as binary posteriors in sequential inference'] Let $0<\alpha<p<\beta<1$ and $\tau_{\alpha,\beta}$ be the first exit time
    \(
        \tau_{\alpha,\beta}
        =\inf\{t\geq 0:P_t\notin(\alpha,\beta)\},
    \)
    where $P$ is the posterior for a binary experiment. Assume $P$ is an autonomous win-martingale with $P_0=p$. Then $\tau_{\alpha,\beta}<\infty$ a.s.~and
    \begin{equation}
        \widetilde{\mathbb P}(P_{\tau_{\alpha,\beta}}=\beta)
        =\frac{p-\alpha}{\beta-\alpha},
        \qquad
        \widetilde{\mathbb P}(P_{\tau_{\alpha,\beta}}=\alpha)
        =\frac{\beta-p}{\beta-\alpha}.
    \end{equation}
    If the decision is $1$ at $\beta$ and $0$ at $\alpha$, then
    \begin{align}
        \widetilde{\mathbb Q}^0(\textnormal{decide }1)
        &=\frac{1-\beta}{1-p}\frac{p-\alpha}{\beta-\alpha},
        \qquad
        \widetilde{\mathbb Q}^1(\textnormal{decide }0)
        =\frac{\alpha}{p}\frac{\beta-p}{\beta-\alpha}.
    
    \end{align}
    The expected decision time under the marginal law is
    \begin{align}
        \widetilde{\mathbb E}[\tau_{\alpha,\beta}]
        =2\bigg[&
        \frac{\beta-p}{\beta-\alpha}
        \int_\alpha^p\frac{y-\alpha}{\sigma^2(y)}\,dy
        +\frac{p-\alpha}{\beta-\alpha}
        \int_p^\beta\frac{\beta-y}{\sigma^2(y)}\,dy
        \bigg].
    
    \end{align}

[Theorem 14 of arXiv:2608.26692, 'Many Facets in Random Polytopes from Product and Log-Concave Measures'] There exists an absolute constant $C>0$ such that the following holds.  For
every sufficiently large $n$ and every full-dimensional log-concave
probability measure $\mu$ on $\R^n$, there exist $T\in[n,2n]$ and
\[
 N=\left\lceil e^Tn^{3/2}\right\rceil
\]
such that, if $X_1,\ldots,X_N$ are independent with distribution $\mu$ and
\[
 P_N=\conv\{X_1,\ldots,X_N\},
\]
then
\[
 \E f_{n-1}(P_N)
 \geq n^{n/2}e^{-Cn}
 \geq(cn)^{n/2}.
\]

[Definition 6 of arXiv:2609.02850, 'Canonical-row Chern flow on Bott--Samelson towers:\\ realizable-volume models for Schubert'] Let $\kk$ be a field.  A homogeneous polynomial
$f\in\QQ[x_1,\ldots,x_n]_d$ belongs to $\RV$ if
\begin{equation}
 f(x)=\frac{q}{d!}\int_X\left(x_1D_1+\cdots+x_nD_n\right)^d
\end{equation}
for some $q\in\QQ_{\ge0}$, an integral projective $d$-fold $X/\kk$, and
semiample Cartier divisor classes $D_1,\ldots,D_n$ on $X$.  The case $q=0$
includes the zero polynomial.
title: Definition 6 of arXiv:2609.02850

OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). For critical percolation on Z^d, d > 6, show that the empirical measure of the cluster of the origin, rescaled by n^{-1/4} in space, conditioned on |C(0)| = n, converges in distribution to integrated super-Brownian excursion (ISE). Source: Heydenreich and van der Hofstad: Progress in high-dimensional percolation and random graphs, author version with open problems, Open Problem 15.1, p. 218. Status notes: Hara and Slade proved convergence of the r-point functions of the critical cluster to those of ISE for spread-out models in d > 6 (2000); convergence of the conditional measure itself and the nearest-neighbour case were not verified as resolved.
Posed in Heydenreich and van der Hofstad: Progress in high-dimensional percolation and random graphs, author version with open problems
Current status unverified as of 2026-09-07
title: Open problem: ISE scaling limit of critical high-dimensional percolation clusters of fixed size

[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2608.26300, 'Coordinate-Deletion Bundles from Composition Algebras: Hopf Defects, $KO$-Classes, and Rea'] On $\partial B_i\cong S^{d-1}$, the clutching map between the local
	$U_i$-frame and the punctured-space trivialization is represented by
	$M_i=L_{q_i}$. After radial normalization it is homotopic through
	$\GL_d^+(\R)$ to
	\[
	\lambda_D:S^{d-1}\longrightarrow\SO(d),
	\qquad
	u\longmapsto L_u,
	\]
	where $N(u)=1$.
	
	For $D=\C$ and $D=\Hh$, this is the underlying real clutching map of
	the complex and quaternionic Hopf line bundle. For $D=\Oct$, it is
	the standard octonionic Hopf clutching map associated with the fibration
	$S^7\to S^{15}\to S^8$; this is a clutching description of a real
	rank-eight vector bundle and does not make $S^7$ into a structure group.

Let (Omega, F, (F_k)_{k=0}^n, P) be a filtered probability space. A sequence of random variables (D_k)_{k=1}^n is called a martingale difference sequence adapted to (F_k) if each D_k is F_k-measurable, integrable, and E[D_k | F_{k-1}] = 0 almost surely for all k in {1, ..., n}.
(F_k) is a filtration
D_k is F_k-measurable and integrable

body:
[Theorem thm:main2 of arXiv:2411.03512, 'Ergodicity and Mixing of Sublinear Expectation System and Applications'] Assume that  $\{X_k\}_{k\geq 1}$ is a $d$-dimensional $\alpha$-mixing identical sequence on a sublinear expectation space $(\Omega,\mathcal{H},\hat{\mathbb{E}})$ for some $\alpha>0$ with $\hat{\mathbb{E}}[|X_1|^{2}]<\infty$. Let $t_k=\lfloor P(k)\rfloor\vee 1$ for each $k\in\mathbb N$, where $P(x)=a_mx^m+\cdots+a_1x+a_0$ is a real-valued polynomial with $a_m>0$ for some $m\geq 2$, and 	$\Gamma:=\{\mathbb{E}[X_1]: \mathbb{E}\in \Theta\}.$  
		Then there exists $C>0$ such that for any $\phi\in C_{lip}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with Lipschitz constant $l_{\phi}>0$ and for all $n\in \mathbb{N}$,
		\begin{equation*}
			\left|\hat{\mathbb{E}}\left[\phi\left(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=1}^n X_{t_k}\right)\right]-\max_{x\in \Gamma}\phi(x) \right|\leq C  l_{\phi}n^{-1/2}.
		\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:main2 of arXiv:2411.03512

Author-derived auxiliary statement, awaiting designated referee review: for a ray measure mu with finite I_r, the averaged signed ray traversals form a unit flow f from o to infinity with sum_e f(e)^2 <= (I_r-1)/(r^{-1}-1). For pairwise edge-disjoint boundaries D_j of finite vertex sets containing o, I_r >= 1+(r^{-1}-1)sum_j 1/|D_j|. Therefore no subgraph of the nearest-neighbor square lattice supports such a measure with I_r finite for r<1, since square boundaries have 8j+4 edges and the reciprocal sum diverges.

0 < E(s) - \bigl(E_N(s) + L_N\,\mathbb P_s(A_N)\bigr)
< (U_N - L_N)\,\mathbb P_s(A_N),
\]
where $L_N$ and $U_N$ are defined in Proposition~\ref{prop:overshoot}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
For a population process X_t with state space the nonnegative orthant R_+^d, the extinction time of the i-th species is the stopping time tau_0^i = inf{t >= 0 : X_t^i = 0}. The species is said to go extinct almost surely if P(tau_0^i < infinity) = 1 or if lim_{t -> infinity} X_t^i = 0 almost surely.
Nonnegative sample paths
title: Stochastic Extinction Time and Boundary Hitting
