[Lemma 22 of arXiv:2506.11707, 'Fluctuations of two-dimensional determinantal processes associated with Berezin--Toeplitz '] Let $B$ be a self-adjoint operator and let $\Pi$ be an orthogonal
projector on a separable Hilbert space so that $\|\Pi B(1-\Pi)\|_{\tr} \le {\rm C}$.
One has, for $t\ge 0$,
\[
\|\Pi\mathcal U_t(B)\|_{\rm tr} \le {\rm C} t.
\]
Moreover, if $\Delta$ is a bounded operator such that 
\begin{equation} 
\| \Pi B(1-\Pi)\Delta\Pi\| \vee  \| \Pi \Delta (1-\Pi)B\Pi\| \vee \|[\Delta, B]\| \le \varepsilon  \, , \qquad 
\|\Pi\Delta \Pi B(1-\Pi)\|_{\tr} \le \varepsilon , 
\end{equation}
then for $t\ge 0$,
\[
\|\Pi\Delta\Pi\mathcal U_t(B) \|_{\tr}   \le \varepsilon (1+\tfrac 32
{\rm C}t).
\]
title: Lemma 22 of arXiv:2506.11707

Established criterion stated by Ruodu Wang in arXiv:1411.6190v3 Section 2.2(e), equation (7), p.9, attributing Wang-Wang Joint Mixability (doi:10.1287/moor.2015.0755): Let n>=2, and let F_i all have increasing densities on finite essential intervals [a_i,b_i], or all have decreasing densities there, with means mu_i. The tuple is jointly mixable if and only if sum a_i+max_i(b_i-a_i)<=sum mu_i<=sum b_i-max_i(b_i-a_i). Increasing/decreasing is nonstrict and includes step densities and uniform laws. Joint mixability here means a coupling with marginals F_i and sum equal to sum mu_i almost surely. This card records the exact author-survey statement; it does not claim the original long proof has been independently checked. Publisher access to the original theorem was blocked in this round.
All densities monotone in the same direction on their finite essential intervals
n>=2
a_i<b_i finite
title: Source note: Wang-Wang joint monotone-density mixability criterion

body:
[Lemma G-CW-Hausdorff of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $G$ be a compact Lie group and let ${\mathcal{F}}$ be any collection of closed subgroups of $G$ closed under conjugation. Then any ${\mathcal{F}}$-cofibrant $G$-space $X$ is Hausdorff, and every isotropy group of $X$ is contained in ${\mathcal{F}}$.
    \begin{proof}
        By Lemma~(lemma:restr-equiv-lQ of the paper), the underlying non-equivariant space of $X$ is cofibrant, hence Hausdorff. For the second statement, note that the collection of all spaces with isotropy groups contained in ${\mathcal{F}}$ is closed under coproduct, pushout and transfinite composition along closed embeddings, as well as under passage to subspaces. As moreover the source and target of any generating cofibration for the ${\mathcal{F}}$-model structure have isotropy groups contained in ${\mathcal{F}}$ (here we use the closure under conjugation), the lemma follows.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma G-CW-Hausdorff of arXiv:2608.28504

body:
[Lemma 33 (KL bound using regularized large gaps) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{lem:KLhive}
Let \(h_n\in H_n(\lambda_n,M_n;N_n)\) be the hive obtained, via
Proposition~\ref{gt-rem}(iv), from the large-gap construction applied to the
deformed GUE minor process for \(X_n\).
 Conditionally on \(h_n\), attach three
independent uniform Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns with top rows
\[
\lambda_n,\qquad M_n,\qquad N_n.
\]
Let \(q_n\) be the resulting density on the triply augmented hive space
\(\mathbb A^3\).

Let \(p_n\) be the maximum-entropy triply augmented hive density from
Theorem~\ref{thm:gaussian1}, with the same expected quadratic boundary
moments as \(q_n\):
\[
\mathbb E_{p_n}|\lambda|^2=\mathbb E_{q_n}|\lambda|^2,\qquad
\mathbb E_{p_n}|\mu|^2=\mathbb E_{q_n}|\mu|^2,\qquad
\mathbb E_{p_n}|\nu|^2=\mathbb E_{q_n}|\nu|^2.
\]
Then
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(q_n\Vert p_n)=O(n\log n).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: KL bound using regularized large gaps

[Definition of arXiv:2605.15066, 'The critical activation density in graph bootstrap percolation'] Let $S\subset F$ be graphs and suppose that 
$V(F)$ is ordered. 
Let $S'\subset F'\subseteq G$ be some other graphs, where $V(G)$ is ordered.  
Then we call $F'$ an {\it $(S,F)$-extension}
of $S'$ in $G$ if  there is an isomorphism of the graphs $F\setminus E(S)$
and $F'\setminus E(S')$ such that 
the $i$th largest vertex in $S$ is mapped to the $i$th 
largest vertex in $S'$, for each $1\leqslant i\leqslant v(S)$.

[Theorem th:mlsi of arXiv:2608.19358, 'An optimal Poincaré inequality\\for the complex Ginibre log-gas'] For every symmetric $f\in\mathcal{C}^1(\mathbb{C}^n,\mathbb{R})$ such that
  $\Phi_f(G)=f(\lambda_1(G),\ldots,\lambda_n(G))\in
  H^1(\gamma_n^{\mathrm{mat}})$, we have
  \begin{equation}
    \operatorname{Var}_{\mu_n}(f)
    \leq
    \frac{2}{n}
    \mathbb{E}\left[
      a_f(G_n)^*\mathcal{O}(G_n)a_f(G_n)
    \right]
    \text{ and }
    \operatorname{Ent}_{\mu_n}(f^2)
    \leq
    \frac{4}{n}
    \mathbb{E}\left[
      a_f(G_n)^*\mathcal{O}(G_n)a_f(G_n)
    \right]
  \end{equation}
  where $a_f(G)$ is the random vector of $\mathbb{C}^n$ given by
  $(a_f(G))_j=\partial_{z_j}f(\lambda_1(G),\ldots,\lambda_n(G))$. Moreover the
  quadratic form on the right-hand sides is independent of the labeling of the
  eigenvalues. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title:
Functional inequalities from the matrix lift and eigenvector

[Lemma 18 (Hypoelliptic propagation control from a non-characteristic boundary layer) of arXiv:2607.19752, 'Weak Equilibrium Measures and Capacity--Hitting Identities\\ for the Hypoelliptic Third-Or'] Let $\lambda\in(0,1/2)$.  For $\alpha>0$, define
\[
    C_{\alpha,\lambda}
    :=
    \left\{z\in\calD\setminus\calC:
        \dist(z,\calC)\le \alpha^\lambda,\quad
        |r|\ge \alpha^{\lambda/4}
      \right\}.
\]
Then
\[
    \sup_{z\in C_{\alpha,\lambda}}
    \Pbb_z\left(\tau_\calC>\alpha^\lambda\right)\to0
    \qquad\text{as }\alpha\downarrow0,
\]
and
\[
    \sup_{z\in C_{\alpha,\lambda}}
    \Pbb_z^\alpha\left(\tau_\calC^\alpha>\alpha^\lambda\right)
    \longrightarrow0
    \qquad\text{as }\alpha\downarrow0 .
\]
The same estimates hold for the adjoint processes.

[Theorem thm:trichotomy of arXiv:2609.02155, 'Exact Limits of Random Projections for Preserving Geometry:\\ Distance Recovery, Nearest-N'] Let $Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I_d)$, let $T\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d}$ be a fixed known map
of rank $r$ with nonzero singular values $s_i$, and write
$D=\left\lVertZ\right\rVert^2$, $Q=\left\lVertTZ\right\rVert^2$, and $M=T^\top T$.
\begin{romannum}
\item \emph{Best-possible inference is governed by rank alone:}
$\rho_{\mathrm{HGR}}(D;TZ)=\sqrt{r/d}$, so for every $f\in L^2$,
$\Var(\E[f(D)\mid TZ])\le(r/d)\Var(f(D))$.
\item \emph{The unwhitened squared-norm estimate is governed by the spectrum:}
\[
\Corr(D,Q)=\frac{\tr M}{\sqrt{d\,\tr(M^2)}}
=\sqrt{\frac{r_2(M)}{d}},
\qquad
r_2(M)=\frac{(\tr M)^2}{\tr(M^2)}.
\]
If $\kappa=s_{\max}/s_{\min}$ over the nonzero singular values, then
\[
r\frac{4\kappa^2}{(\kappa^2+1)^2}\le r_2(M)\le r.
\]
The lower bound is asymptotic to $4r/\kappa^2$ as $\kappa\to\infty$.
\item \emph{Recovery under additive noise is governed by the spectrum near
zero:} if $x\sim\mathcal N(0,I_d)$ and
$\eta\sim\mathcal N(0,I_m)$ are independent and
$y=Tx+\varepsilon\eta$, then
\[
\tr\Var(\E[x\mid y,T])=\sum_{i=1}^{r}\frac{s_i^2}{s_i^2+\varepsilon^2},
\qquad
\MMSE(x\mid y,T)=d-\sum_{i=1}^{r}\frac{s_i^2}{s_i^2+\varepsilon^2}.
\]
\end{romannum} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Trichotomy

[Thm operator_bdd of arXiv:2604.10446, 'Least singular values of shifted sparse random combinatorial matrices'] There are absolute positive constants $C_1$ and $C_2$ 
such that the following holds. 
Let $1\leq m\leq n$, $\gamma\geq 4$, $\beta \geq 1$, and let $d$ be an integer satisfying $1\le d \le n$.  
Let $M$ be an $m \times n$ random matrix with entries in $\{0, 1\}$, where each row is independently and uniformly 
sampled from the set of all vectors in $\{0, 1\}^n$ containing exactly $d$ ones. Let 
$$N= \max\big\{ 9 \min\{d,n-d\}, 2\gamma\log m \big\}.$$
Then, with probability 
    at least $1-n\cdot m^{-\gamma} -2n^{-\beta}$, one has 
    \[
     \|M-\mathbb{E}M\| \leq \frac{2 \min \{d,n-d\}}{\sqrt{N}} + C_1 \beta \sqrt{N}
     \leq C_2 \beta \left( \sqrt{\min\{d,n-d\}+ \gamma \log m} \right).
    \]
In particular, taking $m=n$, $\gamma=4$, $\beta =2$, and $\log n \leq d \leq n- \log n$, we have 
\[
 \|M-\mathbb{E}M\| =\|M^{T}-\mathbb{E}M^{T}\|\leq C_{(thm: operator_bdd of the paper)}\sqrt{d}.
\]
with probability at least $1 -3 n^{-1}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm operator_bdd of arXiv:2604.10446

body: In mathematics, the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture describes the set of rational solutions to equations defining an elliptic curve. It is an open problem in the field of number theory and is widely recognized as one of the most challenging mathematical problems. It is named after mathematicians Bryan John Birch and Sir Peter Swinnerton-Dyer, who formulated the conjecture in the 1960s with the help of machine computation. Only special cases of the conjecture have been proven.
title: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture

[Lem Varadhan of arXiv:2604.23751, 'Large deviation principles for pattern-avoiding permutations, and limit shapes for constra'] For any $n\ge 1,$ let $\mu_n$ denote the distribution of $X_n$ and assume that $(X_n)$ satisfies an LDP at speed $a_n$ with good rate function $I.$ Let $F:E \rightarrow \mathbb R$ be a bounded continuous function. Let the distribution $\nu_n$  be defined as follows:
 \[ \mathrm{d}\nu_n(x) := \frac{1}{Z_n} \textup{e}^{a_nF(x)} \mathrm{d}\mu_n(x),\]
 where $Z_n$ is a normalizing constant such that $\nu_n$ is a probability measure.
 Then we have
	\[ \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{a_n} \log Z_n = -  \inf_{y\in E} (I(y)- F(y)). \]
	Moreover, if we let $Y_n$ have distribution $\nu_n$,
the sequence $(Y_n)$ satisfies an LDP at speed $a_n$ with good rate function $J$
 given by
 \[ \forall x\in E, \quad J(x) = I(x) - F(x) - \inf_{y\in E} (I(y)- F(y)).\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem Varadhan of arXiv:2604.23751

[Lemma of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] \label[lemma]{lem:Zp_symmetrizer_space}
For $f \in_R \mathbb{Z}_{2q+1}$ ($q \ge 1$),
\[ \Sym(f) = 
    \{ g \in_R \mathbb{Z}_{2q+1}
    \mid \forall x \in [q] \quad
    \sum_{i=-q}^q (f(x-i) - f(-x-i)) g(i) = 0 \}.
    \]
In particular, $\dim(\Sym(f)) \ge q$. 
\begin{proof}
We identify the elements of $\mathbb{Z}_{2q+1}$ with $[-q,q] \cap \mathbb{Z}$ so that inverses are obvious. 
By direct computation, $\Sym(f)$ is the set of random vectors $g  \in \mathbb{Z}_{2q+1}$  such that for all integers $x \in [-q,q]$, $(f * g)(x) = (f * g)(-x)$, i.e.
\[    \sum_{i=-q}^q (f(x-i) - f(-x-i)) g(i) = 0 \}.    \]
But the condition corresponding to $x=0$ is vacuous, and for all $x \in [q]$ the conditions produced by $x$ and $-x$ are identical. 

To see the dimension, note that the simplex of probability measures on $\mathbb{Z}_{2q+1}$ has dimension $2q$, and we have imposed $q$ linear constraints. 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered lemma of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'

\item{\rm(Continuity)}   As an $\mathbb{R}^4 \to \mathbb{R}$ function,  $(x,s;y,t) \mapsto W^{\xi {\scaleobj{0.8}{\boxempty}}}(x,s;y,t)$ is  continuous. 
 \item {\rm(Additivity)}  For all $p,q,r \in \mathbb{R}^2$, 
    $W^{\xi {\scaleobj{0.8}{\boxempty}}}(p;q) + W^{\xi {\scaleobj{0.8}{\boxempty}}}(q;r) = W^{\xi {\scaleobj{0.8}{\boxempty}}}(p;r)$.   In particular, \\ $W^{\xi {\scaleobj{0.8}{\boxempty}}}(p;q) = -W^{\xi {\scaleobj{0.8}{\boxempty}}}(q;p)$ and $W^{\xi {\scaleobj{0.8}{\boxempty}}}(p;p) = 0$.
    \item {\rm(Monotonicity along a horizontal line)}
     Whenever $\xi_1< \xi_2$, $x < y$, and $t \in \mathbb{R}$,
    \[
    W^{\xi_1 -}(x,t;y,t) \le W^{\xi_1 +}(x,t;y,t) \le W^{\xi_2 -}(x,t;y,t) \le W^{\xi_2 +}(x,t;y,t).
    \]
    \item {\rm(Evolution as the KPZ fixed point)} For 
    all $x,y \in \mathbb{R}$ and $s < t$,
    \begin{equation}
    W^{\xi {\scaleobj{0.8}{\boxempty}}}(x,s;y,t) = \sup_{z \in \mathbb{R}}\{W^{\xi {\scaleobj{0.8}{\boxempty}}}(x,s;z,s) +
 \mathcal{L}(z,s;y,t)\}.
    \end{equation}
    \item  {\rm(Law and asymptotic slope)} For fixed $\xi \in \mathbb{R}$, $W^{\xi} := W^{\xi +} = W^{\xi -}$ with probability one, and for each $t \in \mathbb{R}$, the random function $x \mapsto W^{\xi}(0,t;x,t)$ is a two-sided Brownian motion with variance $2$ and drift $2\xi$. Furthermore, on a single event of full probability, for all $t \in \mathbb{R},\xi \in \mathbb{R}$, and ${\scaleobj{0.9}{\boxempty}} \in \{-,+\}$,
    \[
    \lim_{|x| \to \infty} \frac{W^{\xi {\scaleobj{0.8}{\boxempty}}}(0,t;x,t)}{x} = 2\xi.
    \]
    \item {\rm(General Busemann limits)} for all $\xi \in \mathbb{R}$, $t \in \mathbb{R}$, $x < y$, and sequences $\mathbf v_n = (x_n,t_n)$ with $t_n \to -\infty$ and $\frac{x_n}{|t_n|}\to \xi$,
\begin{align*}
W^{\xi-}(x,t;y,t) &\le \liminf_{n \to \infty} \mathcal{L}(\mathbf v_n;y,t) - \mathcal{L}(\mathbf v_n;x,t) \\&\le \limsup_{n \to \infty} \mathcal{L}(\mathbf v_n;y,t) - \mathcal{L}(\mathbf v_n;x,t) \le W^{\xi +}(x,t;y,t).
\end{align*}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:Buse_basic_properties of arXiv:2505.09604

[Definition 8 (Minimal set) of arXiv:2607.20838, 'Long-memory Markov chains with power-law intensities'] An invariant set $M$ is called a minimal set if it contains no proper closed invariant subsets. 
	That is, for any closed invariant set $E \subseteq M$, we have $E = M$.

[Propo oo of arXiv:2412.01673, 'Spatial SIR epidemic model with varying infectivity without movement of individuals'] The system of equations (equation sy of the paper) admits a unique solution  $\left\{\left(\overline{\mu}^S_t,\overline{\mu}_t^{\mathfrak{F}},\overline{\mu}_t^{I},\overline{\mu}_t^{R}\right),\ t\ge0\right\}$   which is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure, with the densities\\ $\left\{\left(\overline{\mu}^S(t,.), \overline{\mu}^{\mathfrak{F}}(t,.), \overline{\mu}^{I}(t,.) ,\overline{\mu}^{R}(t,.)\right),\ t\ge0\right\}$ satisfying for all $(t,x)\in \mathbb{R}_+\times D$
	\begin{equation}
	
	\left\lbrace
	\begin{aligned}
	\overline{\mu}^{S}(t,x)&= \overline{\mu}^{S}(0,x)- \int_0^t\overline{\mu}^S(s,x)\int_DM(x,y)\overline{\mu}^{\mathfrak{F}}(s,y)dyds,\\
	\overline{\mu}^{\mathfrak{F}}(t,x) &=\overline{\lambda}^0(t)\mu^I(0,x)+\int_0^t\overline{\lambda}(t-s)\overline{\mu}^S(s,x)\int_DM(x,y)\overline{\mu}^{\mathfrak{F}}(s,y)dyds,\\
	\overline{\mu}^{I}(t,x)&= \mu^I(0,x)F_0^c(t)+\int_0^t F^c(t-s)\overline{\mu}^S(s,x)\int_DM(x,y)\overline{\mu}^{\mathfrak{F}}(s,y)dyds,\\
	\overline{\mu}^{R}(t,x)&= \overline{\mu}^R(0,x)+\overline{\mu}^I(0,x)F_0(t)+\int_0^tF(t-s) \overline{\mu}^S(s,x)\int_DM(x,y)\overline{\mu}^{\mathfrak{F}}(s,y)dyds,\\
	\overline{\mu}^{S}(0,x)&= \overline{S}(0)\pi_S(x),\ \overline{\mu}^{I}(0,x)= \overline{I}(0)\pi_I(x),\ \overline{\mu}^{R}(0,x)= \overline{R}(0)\pi_R(x),
	\\ \overline{\mu}(x)&=\overline{\mu}^S(t,x)+\overline{\mu}^{I}(t,x)+\overline{\mu}^{R}(t,x),\ \forall t\ge0.
	\end{aligned}
	\right.
	\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Propo oo of arXiv:2412.01673

[Corollary 84 (Orthogonal and gap-diagonal Pfaffian certificates) of arXiv:2606.29292, 'Intrinsic Gaussian Tensor Geometry and Random Operator Spectra'] In Theorem~\ref{thm:local-to-global-tensor-pfaffian}, two-sided orthogonal
blocks may be treated with
$\mathsf E_N^{\rm dec}=\mathsf E_N^{\rm W}=\ell^2$ and reconstruction
constant one.  Dyadic blocks partitioned by the scale gap may be treated
with
$\mathsf E_N^{\rm dec}=\mathsf E_N^{\rm W}=\mathsf{Gap}_\sigma$ and
reconstruction constant one; fixed finite overlap inserts only the uniform
coloring factor from Theorem~\ref{thm:matching-gap-reconstruction}.  Thus
local square-summable and gap-diagonal certificates are instances of the
same spectral theorem. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Orthogonal and gap-diagonal Pfaffian certificates

[Cor second-localized-testing of arXiv:2609.03751, 'Sparse bounds for maximal rough singular integrals'] Let
\(\Omega\in L^{q,1}\log L(S^{d-1})\) satisfy
(equation eq:Omega-global-cancellation of the paper), and let \(q'\leq p<\infty\).  Then,
uniformly over all stopping collections and bounded measurable
truncation functions,
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
    \bigl|
      \mathcal Q_{\Omega,t_1}^{t_2}(h,b)
    \bigr|
    \lesssim_{d,q}{}&
    \|\Omega\|_{L^{q,1}\log L(S^{d-1})}\\
    &\times
    \|h\|_{\mathcal Y_\infty(\mathcal Q)}
    \|b\|_{\dot{\mathcal X}_p(\mathcal Q)} .
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
In particular, this testing condition introduces no \(p'\)-dependent
loss.
title: Second testing estimate

$z(t)=\sqrt{\alpha_{t}}u+(1-\alpha_{t})\alpha_{t}^{-1/2}G_{0}(u)$, so
(equation eq:burgers of the paper) has a unique solution in the class of Cauchy transforms of
probability measures with $\mu_{t}|_{t=0}=\mu_{0}$, namely (equation eq:marginal of the paper).
